reviews.comment: Abby is really nice and genuinely cares for her students. I struggled pretty heavily in Calc 3 near the end, but her lectures were always great and extremely helpful. She is very passionate about what she is teaching and always go over tips and tricks to simply things that our professor didn't do the greatest job explaining. Only positives to say.

If you have the option to choose your TA, take Calc 3 with Abby.  I have nothing but amazing things to say about her.  She clearly explained all content and was very accessible for her office hours.  If I ever had any concerns prior to exam day, she would clearly detail any practice problems I needed.

GOAT Calc 3 TA. She has a website with past exams for all the tests that are great study resources. She goes over the exact kind of question that will be on the quiz right before you take it. Also very knowledgeable and can explain basically all questions.

Abby was an amazing TA - always welcoming and patient. She explained tough topics clearly and made sure everyone understood. Her relaxed, supportive environment made it easy to engage or just take a brain break by listening or chatting. One of the best TA's I've ever had - I wish I could have her for more classes!

Abby is genuinely one of the best TA's I have ever had for a class, she explained topics so thoroughly and made concepts so much clearer while also being the sweetest person ever. I truly looked forward to going to her office hours every week, sometimes just to chat and give myself a short break from studying. Highly recommend her!!

Not a bad option if you can't get Crane. If you go to class you wont have any problems getting a good grade in the class. The assignments are locked by a code but you just need to know someone who went to get it from them and just watch the lecture videos he posts. Passing the CSWA exam isn't hard, and assignments are doable.

He is the goat, super smart IIT MIT graduate. He goes through the solidworks with the class, TA office hours are useful, and overall the class is very easy despite maybe not leaving a solidworks pro. You can get certified in solidworks even if you are bad at it.

A very, very straightforward professor, follow what he says during lectures or watch the recordings and you'll be fine. He explains everything youll need for the CSWA and a section of that class is a prep period. There is a final that's worth like 5 percent of your grade, but the real final is the final design project which I really enjoyed.
just go to class and you'll be fine. Pretty free class if you do all the work

Super chill dude. If you go to class and pay attention this class is so free. I totally get if learning a new software is more difficult for some people. But Kumar teaches well if you follow along and prep before hand when he tells you to (which is uncommon). The notation stuff at the end of semester is a little boring but fine.

Really enjoyed the final design project, especially considering some of the other profs just have a written final (which for a CAD class is lowk silly). Passed the CSWA with ease by following his recommendations. He gives you everything you need to succeed in the class.
Is he the most enthusiastic prof? No, but he's a pretty good one.

Kumar's lectures are disorganized and move very slowly, but the short recordings on Canvas explain the same material much more clearly. Class time isn't very helpful, save your time and skip. Homework is a large part of the grade but manageable. Working with friends and self-learning makes the class easy to pass.

Overall he's a fine professor. He goes through the lectures very quickly, which makes him hard to follow, but there's videos of the lecture material you can watch after at your own pace. There's homework once a week, which are graded pretty lightly.

Kumar was a good professor. The class activities are where you learn how to use Solid Works so don't skip class. The homework assignments aren't difficult but use TA office hours if you're stuck. The final project is tedious and takes a long time so don't do it last minute. Make sure to study for the final quiz.

To say his home works are difficult would be an understatement. He provides no guidance and I've never seen an assignment graded with such a fine-tooth comb. He zips through the classwork at a speed not even experienced students can keep up with and belittles students that dare to ask questions. gl getting an email response. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

CAD is an easy class, so a great professor is not essential to your success. Professor Kumar teaches you everything you need to know for the CSWA exam, but sometimes I felt like he went too fast or didn't go through certain topics deep enough. The GD&T section was taught pretty bad, I watched Crane's videos and understood the content a lot better.

First several lectures require a lot of focus to understand how to use SOLIDWORKS, then you can kind of watch them online and figure it out on your own. Did not prepare us very well for the exam, I did my own prep and got a perfect score on it. Grading depends on TA and can be unnecessarily harsh sometimes. Really cool content though.

His teaching style does not prepare you for future courses (mech e ppl). Yes he's easy & you can get an A and pass the CSWA no problem, but you WILL NOT be prepared for DML or other classes when you get to it & you'll have to relearn everything & teach yourself. Do yourself a favor & take a professor who will prepare you. CAD is easy with any prof.

He's just a funny little guy that knows his stuff and as long as you follow him in class you'll make an A. Just make sure you have a windows laptop and get a mouse and the software set up by the time he tells you. Don't miss class. The lectures are crucial.

Prof Kumar was good when it came to Solidworks. He knows his stuff and will go through the class activities in class. However, when he lectures not about solidworks (drawings/tolerances) it is so boring and draining I struggled to pay attention. The certification is pretty easy but his "final quiz" is terrible especially due to his lectures.
Decent professor and its easy to pass the CSWA exam if you do the class activities and homework well. Boring class after the CSWA, and the information after is very boring.

Using solidworks isn't the bad part (even CWSA), if you do the class activities & homework properly. Problem is how everything is he does is vague. And the topics at the end of the year (GDT, tolerance/allowance, & screw readings - important topics for DML), he doesn't mention until last 2 weeks of school and does a half effort job of teaching it.

Kumar is a good professor. He's fine. Yes, he moves fast in lectures, and sometimes it's difficult to keep up when you're making parts. Best advice: don't fall behind, and find a small group of people to sit with during lectures. The Solidworks certification exam was fine, felt prepared - great resume builder. This class was very helpful and fun :)

Moves too quickly in in-class lectures but his recorded ones are better. Funny in person. I did not feel prepared for the certification exam at all. Super homework heavy with a big final project at the end. Not very lenient with grading. TA's were more helpful than him in office hours. Not bad, overall kind of meh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is SO BORING. If you have any experience with SolidWorks or CAD this class will be a breeze if not its probably a pain. The class is structured around getting you to pass the CSWA exam towards the end of the semester you learn about tolerance (def need to pay attention). Assignments are easy but time-consuming and graded by TA's

Lectures are very boring and sometimes hard to understand. The GDT lectures after the CSWA Exam are not the best as he pretty much reads straight from the slides. Homework is very doable and the TAs will walk you through it if you don't understand. Do well, on the HWs and you'll basically be set with an A.
Overall easy class. Lectures are boring but easy to understand. Sometimes it is easy to fall behind when he is lecturing but he uploads all lectures so you can catch up after class.

Easy class, Kumar pretty easy to follow along in class. Total grade is 50% homework. The CSWA exam easy very similar to class. His lectures aren't the most entertaining but tells you all the info you need. He always stays after class to answer any questions. GDT is worst part about the class but the final quiz for it is not worth very much points

Professor Kumar is a cool guy. His lectures are very boring. However he posts all the PowerPoints he uses and records his lectures. It is not the end of the world having him as a professor. It is not a hard class even if you don't pay much attention, you can get an A.

Dr. Kumar is a great teacher. Fast in lectures but always has time after class to talk. Sometimes I had to skip but he always posts recorded lectures in canvas making it easy to catch up. Try not to skip but always have someone to help u just in case. The exam wasnt hard and grades are light if u make sure ur right and dont turn in sloppy work.

Dr. Kumar himself is very knowledgable about his field, but here is how you pass. 1) KNOW your TAs, they will help you with everything related to the course material. 2) Use YouTube to find *very* similar practice problems for the CSWA exam (do not freak out for a month like I did, you'll be fine). GDT was simple (5% of total grade), go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is always available after class to ask questions, and he has online lecture videos which are very helpful since he does go fast in class.

Kumar himself is hilarious sometimes because he's kinda blunt. Just keep up with his lectures in class, and if you fall behind, just go up to him and he'll help you after class. Other students in class were also extremely helpful in catching up on work/ understanding any mistakes.

Easy homeworks, boring lectures. Heavily weighted final project was due over thanksgiving. Certification was also easy. Prof is chill. Graders were very strict. GDT and tolerance lectures were very boring and not clear
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: overall boring lectures but the class isn't hard. homework is easy to get good grades on and if you show up to class, you should pass the certification exam. second half of the class is especially boring bc its all about tolerancing and gdt and theirs a surprise honorlock quiz at the end. still not to hard though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class consists of following along as he builds parts on SolidWorks then doing similar HW, which is 50% of your grade. The latter part of the semester is spent on tolerance, but he explains it well. Attendance is not mandatory but highly recommended, since you need the access codes he gives out in class to complete the daily quizzes.

He is a very straightforward and respectable professor as long as you pay attention during lectures and copy what he does in solidworks the class is a breeze. They only way you can get behind is if you skip lectures/don't make them up on canvas. Overall he was great and would take his class again.

He doesn't go into depth of how to do certain things in CAD, so you have to self-teach that part. But one piece of advice is to GO TO CLASS. The in class exercise utilizes a specific tool that will be used for your hw. Only about 1 hw assignment per week too.
His lectures were often times really dull and not interactive. However, his class was an easy A, he assigned a very reasonable amount of work, and you do learn a lot from his class.

If you ask an answer that's common sense he will get aggravated which I found funny, some of his homework is difficult but overall not too difficult. The final project sucks and so does the final unit so make sure to do well in the first part of the class.

Professor Kumar is not a great professor. His teaching in class is very limited and certainly does not prepare you in the slightest for the certification exam. You learn very little, only reason you get an A is by doing homework (which tends to be very tedious and time consuming). I would recommend the other professor for this course.

Dr. Kumar has been one of the best professor that I have met. He makes every concept very clear in class and designs the study process that has been very helpful for students to catch up. He doesn't give hard time to student and the difficulty level is appropriate. The quiz he give  helps student to review the materials that covered in class.

Pretty easy class once you learn the basics but be prepared to teach yourself everything and be completely unprepared for the cert exam unless you've taught yourself a bunch of stuff. You'll get a good grade but you'll also learn nothing. Heard Rubiano's class is hell though. Apparently you learn a lot but his class structure is horrible and hard.

Professor Kumar is not a great lecturer. The majority of the class is learning Solidworks, and I would recommend not going to the lectures live but watching the recordings later so you can pause them and work on the stuff in class at your own pace. It is easy to get an A, but study hard for final because it is weighted high and on honorlock.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very dull lecture style but will help you if you ask the right questions. Helps to have prior CAD experience but its not necessary. You have to teach yourself the basics of the program but that's not bad. Some of the easiest 3 credits you'll take here if you know what you're doing. If you're looking for an easy class take him.

Dr. Kumar is really good at teaching and explaining exactly what you need to learn. He goes through the practice problems with you, and never makes you do something harder on your own than he has already done with you. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Solidworks section of the class is pretty easy if you are somewhat good on computers. Prof. Kumar does class activities pretty much every day until the Solidworks exams that are really helpful in learning how to use solidworks. After he starts teaching GDT. Do well on the Solidworks exam and do all of the class activities and its an easy A.

Kumar doesn't teach well, and the hw's are difficult. Tests have at least one question on them that covers an obscure topic barely discussed. If the class is still online due to Covid, you will have to type all hw's and exams. And don't ask questions during class/office hours because you'll only get rude and condescending replies.

He is the absolute worst instructor I have ever experienced in my entire academic career. He just turns his back to the class during the lectures and read from the slides with his laser pointer. Lectures are 3 hours long and boring as hell. You will have to memorize almost every slide. Every week you will have quiz, homework and lab report.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The homework is pretty easy if you figure out the basics of CAD. GDT can be pretty confusing especially since Kumar can sometimes be a tedious lecturer.

Ashok V. Kumar is the reason why I stayed in Engineering. He is a great man that has galvanized and enboldened my view on Engineering. He has made me more of an inquisitive human being and has solely developed my mastery of Solidworks. 10/10 would take again.
worst class at uf by far. this guy doesnt know how to teach
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Kumar's lectures are boring. I learned mostly from friends who have taken the class already, and only watched the lectures for the access codes for quizzes. He doesn't care if the quizzes and in-class activities are late. HW is most of the grade. Follow the HW instructions step by step and you'll pass this class. The one test is brutal though.

Not the most interesting of classes, but Kumar walks you through most of the assignments. Lectures are recorded, but make sure not to get behind (esp later on). Reasonable amount of work, and you can get certified in the class as well. He's pretty understanding regarding technical difficulties, but it can be hard to reach him by email.

Professor Kumar is a very solid professor. His lectures are cut and dry. He doesn't make it very interesting, but he makes sure you are able to do well. He answered all questions and was very accessible. There are many homeworks and quizzes, but only two exams. With this class, just put your head down and get through it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kumar's talents may lie in research instead of teaching. His lectures are confusing and do not adequately cover the course's contents. Kumar prefers to hire TA's that grade unnecessarily harshly. If available, take Prof Crane's course, if not, take Kumar and prepare for a rough semester. Kumar's rating is inflated due to his cult following.

Professor Kumar is an awe-inspiring man. He is an incredible leader and professor who is gracious enough to bestow upon us his knowledge and teach us three times each week. I would recommend taking this course over any other course that I have taken and I believe you would be doing yourself a great disservice if you were to not take it as well.

Ashok V Kumar saved my life. I took EML2029 as a requirement, but I wish I could spend every day there. There is no experience better than attending one of Kumar's lectures. He ensures that if you have a question, comment, or concern, it is heard with an open heart and an open mind. Mr. Kumar is the best teacher you can have. Money back guaranteed.
he is a god, through and through, don't let anyone tell you otherwise

Completely adequate. Most acceptable professor Ive ever taken. I would neither try to take his classes or try to avoid them. I probably wouldnt risk my life for the man but if he was a beggar on the street Id spare some change.

Clear and straightforward professor and class. Makes his class simple as he can. Helpful during class but had at responding to emails. Was surprised by his bad reviews considering his class is pretty well structured

I thought Kumar would really disappoint after reading some awful reviews, but he's actually a very good professor and lecturer. You don't even have to go to class on Fridays if you don't want to. He goes kind of fast in lecture but as long as you're paying attention you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Poo quality teacher. Writes small, works far too fast, doesn't prepare well for exams or showcase the material well. Make sure to buy the book for the examples it gives, or you'll be lost throughout. Quizzes almost every class ensures that you attend, not that they are in any way relevant to the material at hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: At first the class may seem overwhelming but once you get the hang of it, it's pretty easy. Attending class is a must because he gives short quizzes at end of almost every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Pretty monotone, but not as bad as reviews often say.

Gives super stupid quizzes for attendance. Later in the semester, he started making this quizzes have more points, and if you miss any points whatsoever, your grade will drop a whole point. The content is not hard but The way the class is treated is super annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Kumar is one of the most insufferable people I have ever had the displeasure of knowing, he doesn't care for or about his students, his lectures all feel like he doesn't want to be there, his TA's grade unnecessarily harshly. The material for this class is relatively easy and passable with minimal effort but having to be around Kumar ruins it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is the most condescending professor I have ever witnessed, I would avoid skipping class because if you miss one thing good luck sorting it out with him. An absolute chode who only cares about his research rather than his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall, Prof. Kumar is not bad. But, he does not teach the class with the solidworks certification exam in mind. The certification exam was not part of the class, which can be taken as good or bad since it is not part of the grade either. Lectures on tolerances are quite dull in my opinion. Tests are easy if you put your effort in on the hw.

Worst professor possible to teach EML2023. Barely knows how to use a computer (once spent 20 minutes trying to figure out how to open a PDF). Likes to give quizzes at the end of lecture for points so you *have to come*, and gives pointless exams on things he has made up to test on that are not actual parts of the course or the content for EML2023.

Terrifyingly awful. No Solidworks Certification, doesn't actually teach anything because he expects full knowledge of topic. Poorly created and difficult homework and exams, even for someone who has noted experience with the craft. DO NOT TAKE FOR THIS CLASS.

Not meant to be a hard class. 50% of grade is homework. You get a week or more to do the homework. You HAVE to do it the day before the TA office hours bc you will most likely encounter something confusing and you can ask all the questions you want and you will get 100% on homework. The 3 tests are 30% final proj 20% and they are not graded tough.

Course comprises of : 3 exams 1 project 7-8 homeworks Class was too slow at the beginning of the semester. Spent half the semester teaching SolidWorks ( good thing if you don't know the software!) . He's slow ,but good in class but doesn't care about students when you ask him something outside the class (Things like grades). Mixed feelings !

Dr Kumar is a nice guy if you actually talk to him but from emails he seems stuck up. Solidworks involves a lot of trial& error on your own part. He puts up videos for some assignments which are helpful. He doesn't grade the hw, it's assigned graders which is difficult sometimes. exams suck and aren't always relevant
Kumar will teach you not only how to construct the shaft but how to lay it the right way as well.

The course was easy, but if you had to ask something over email or office hours you were not going to get any help.  I brought my laptop to demonstrate the problems I was having with the software and he just said "you must not have the right software" and turned back to working on his laptop.  Just have good friends to help you out.
Excellent professor.
The class is fairly easy if you just attend and work at SolidWorks. I suggest taking him. You can get an A relatively easily. He is pretty boring in class but he is a friendly/nice guy overall.

Easy class but from a few emails I've sent, he really doesn't care about his students. Explains things very poorly and at bad paces. Takes too long to explain easy things, breezes over harder concepts. Watch his lecture videos on faster speeds and you'll be fine.
Easiest class ive taken at UF. He puts up lecture videos on how to do the homework and all the assignments are easy. Exams are graded lightly but there is a big project at the end of the class
Not a very hard class, but he isn't a good teacher. He's pretty arrogant and doesn't care about the students. Take a different CAD professor if possible.
Just an awesome teacher and a very good, balanced human being. :) :) Dr Kumar.. Live long and prosper..
Very good teacher, so nice, and give a good grade

Dont know why he has such a low rating. He goes through all the homeworks in class and the tests arent hard, plus the final project isnt nearly as bad as other professors. Just go to class and bring your computer to remember subtleties of solidworks.
Good teacher, goes through how to do all of the homeworks in class.
Not a very good teacher, but the material in the class is sometimes interesting.

I took graduate Finite Elements and thought Dr. Kumar was a very good teacher.  He presented a lot of information during the class period, but always did examples in class that directly related to homework and tests.  I recommend this class with him.
Pretty horrible teacher. Goes to quickly in class and doesnt care abouit students. He is not nearly as bad as his counterpart Snider though. Be prepared for a horrible class.
Goes to quickly in class and often isn't clear. Doesn't seem to give a****about the students.  You have to go to TA hours if you want to figure out the homework.
Pay attention to the way he makes the computer models or you will never be able to do it on your own! Boring class and TA's grade harshly but it's interesting.
not one of my favorites
CAD professor. If you can understand part histories, you dont have to go to his lectures.

I personally don't find the accent hard to understand, but cannot stand his teaching style. You won't see a single number on any of slides and he spends most of class deriving given equations. On days where he was teaching I would watch the other professor's videos during class and would just do the iClicker for the extra credit.

this dude has the thickest russian accent of all time; he's impossible to understand. he only derives equations in class and rarely does sample problems. even when he does sample problems, you can't understand what he's saying. I watch the other professor during lecture. he teaches 2/3 of the class as well, more than yelton does.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance is not technically mandatory, but the iclicker is worth a 5% extra credit. He has a very strong accent that is very difficult to understand, especially in the large lecture hall with the microphone.

Nice professor but he is very bad at teaching. He has a thick accent making it hard to actually understand what he is trying to explain, so I personally had to teach myself using the textbook and other resources. Took him with yelton who is actually good, but he also has pretty disorganized notes.

Nice guy, but insanely difficult to understand. He has a thick accent that makes understanding nearly impossible. His lectures were mediocre, it seemed like he bounced between topics and there wasn't much organization. I just went for the iClicker (extra credit!). He was one of three professors and I'd say he was the hardest to understand.

PHY2049 is not difficult, but his lectures are quite boring. I came to class for the iClicker extra credit and just did homework/classwork for other courses during his lectures. You can honestly do this course with just the e-textbook, his lectures don't make a difference in your learning imo. Sometimes does demos, but Dr. Hershfield does more.

He frequently skips steps when showing his work most of the time it is unreasonable to expect us to follow him. I am a lazy mf so I never showed up to class and just watched the online lectures but they are terrible. I would heavily recommend attending the lectures just for the extra credit. What he teaches is enough to get by, but not by much.

Accent makes it impossible to understand what he is saying. His lectures do not provide relevant example problems and he skips over large amounts of topics when he runs out of time. I wouldn't even bother going to class unless you want extra credit from iClicker. Hershfield saved this class.

Korytov is a good professor who does have his shortcomings going too indepth on topics and getting off track but he is passionate about teaching physics and will explain something to you until you understand it.
Chop chop chop-Korytov

Dr. Korytov is a passionate professor and always ready to share physics principles and demonstrations to students. In my experience, he is favored by actual Physics Majors as he goes much deeper into theory and mathematical proofs than is needed for the class. He did occasionally go a couple minutes over time, so don't book a back to back.

Good guy but his accent and teaching style makes the lectures really not worth going to. StudyEdge will teach you this class and get you prepared for the exams way more than actually going to lecture.

He isn't a terrible lecturer but he'd often go over the same thing over and over and would make simple concepts 10x harder. When he'd lecture I'd give up on learning and just try to find youtube videos or learn from the HW

His lectures feel like they slap you in the face and say learn it. Sometimes I can understand it all and sometimes I get nothing out of the lecture. He likes physics and cares but the class can be a struggle sometimes.

If you can absolutely avoid him! While he's intelligent and knows what he's talking about he has no idea how to teach. Inconsiderate making the iclicker AFTER class time!! He wastes class time talking about foreign physics concepts and avoids things that will be relevant. Exams are brutal, forcing you to remember the smallest physics 1 concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He has a very thick Russian accent and tends to mumble all the time; most of his lectures are incomprehensible. The class had two professors and the other one was fine, but since they traded lecture days at random, walking into class felt like playing Russian roulette because attendance was practically useless if Korytov was teaching.

Dr. Korytov definitely cared about us and tried to make classes interesting and engaging. That being said, he was a bit hard to understand and a bit all over the place. I liked the other prof better. Very knowledgeable, but didn't translate well into learning for many of us. I recommend a tutor.

nice man, bad teacher. final had 2 questions where the correct answer was not an option. whole class in uproar. gave everyone credit for 1 but people who picked 12 or 24 for other (answer was 18). not sure if hamlin or korytovs decision... quizzes are made by TAs, so not everyone takes the same quiz. final reflected class fairness (or lack thereof)

He's nice, but his teaching is a little lazy. He won't finish problems in class and leave us to assume how ot find the solution. Also he mumbles a lot and doesnt ever explain his steps so you're left lost. I can tell he cares about his class, but i do think he needs to work more on how to be a good professor.

The worst lecturer I have had. He rambles and never finishes the problems. He skipped a giant chunk of important things to talk about random physics stuff. You'll do fine if you have any background, but if you don't, your TAs will be better than the prof, and find online videos to watch. A guy on youtube teaches the same textbook.

Professor Korytov is so sweet. His demonstrations are good and you can tell that he cares about your learning. The class is pretty challenging but support is always provided if you need it. While it can be a little hard to understand his accent, you get used to it and it's easier if you understand the context of what he's saying.
Very thick Russian accent and hard to understand. Good thing he only teaches for 1/3 of the semester, but definitely the worst of out the three professors in this class.

He had good jokes but was otherwise a bad professor. He mumbled into the mic and went off on tangents during lectures; I only went to class for the 5 percent extra credit. He would probably be better in upper-level physics but couldn't bring himself to care enough to be a good prof for an intro course.

Uhhh good luck. Korytov is a rough instructor. Cant read his writing, cant understand him well, and he refuses to show any math past the physics when doing examples, making lectures extremely difficult to follow. He lectures for 1/3 of the course and that 1/3 is not easy. No effort outside of lectures/office hours
Teaches 1/3 of the course and is by far the worst of the 3. Exams are difficult with around an 11.5/20 average.

If you are taking PHY2048, Korytov teaches for 1/3 of the year. He has a thick Russian accent that makes it almost impossible to understand what he is saying. Your best bet is to get studyedge or teach yourself.

Korytov is a cool and knowledgable guy, but I didn't learn anything from his lectures and he tends to be quite hard to follow. He seems like I professor I would take for higher level physics courses that demand more understanding and I would avoid him for physics 1 or 2 by any means.

He has a very thick Russian accent which made what he was talking about very hard to understand. The content itself isn't hard but I couldn't follow what he was talking about in lectures. I didn't even go to any lectures during the last unit because I learned better on my own. I'd avoid taking this professor if possible.

This man was an AWFUL lecturer. By the end of the course, I stopped going to class when he was teaching and just relying on study edge, the textbook, and past exams. Very difficult to understand and talks about the concepts in such a round about way where I would get confused almost immediately. Avoid if you can.
Good professor. Explains examples while keeping things less monotonous with stories. Chop chop chop.

He was often difficult to understand in lectures and he tended to meander and rant about back-stories about physics and things that were unrelated to what we were learning. It was frustrating because his powerpoints were extremely confusing compared to the other lecturere (Yelton) that we had. Whenever Korytov taught, I always had to read the book.

chop chop chop

he doesn't explain things very well

study the textbooks and past exam solutions if you want to score high

Professor Korytov is such a nice, funny person.  Whenever he takes an integral, he likes to say "chop chop chop" which is the highlight of physics 2.  However, his lectures put me to sleep as he would focus too much on derivations of formulas that were already on our exam formula sheets.  I did not learn a single thing from him.

This was a challenging class and Korytov did not help with much clarification. It would be difficult to understand his teachings in pretty much every class, and I only did well by using StudyEdge. I kept up with in-class lectures by watching StudyEdge sessions that taught it the best.

Professor Korytov is very funny (chop chop) and is a very nice person, but a terrible lecturer. He is very hard to understand, and will spend the entire lecture talking about the derivation of formula and give very bad examples of its applications. Not even worth going to class when he is the one lecturing, spend the time going over it yourself.

He says that he actually wants his students to succeed.  However, everything about his teaching style goes against that sentiment.  His lectures are convuluted and difficult to understand.  Some of his exam questions are based on things he briefly mentioned in lectures, others are still impossible.  BUT he does say "chop chop chop," it's adorable.

I wish he had done examples with actual numbers instead of a bunch of proofs. He expected us to understand every part of his lectures even if something was mentioned only once. The "chop chop chop" thing he does is funny, but it's not enough to redeem him as a professor.

Hard to understand with the mask and his accent. His examples don't use numbers and are more conceptual, so it's hard to tell if you're doing the problems right. It's satisfying when he says "chop, chop, chop" and he sometimes says wholesome things. Overall, he's a nice person, but it's hard to learn physics from him.
Much better lecturer than Bartos, and made exams that reflected course content.

The lectures and his explanations of concepts aren't organized well and tough to get on your first or second watch. The reviews are pretty concise and match the exams well. Exams are all reasonable. Weekly quizzes are single question, so missing those can really damn your grade. EC & 85+A should help though. Readings & TAs are your best friend.

He's much better than Bartos but that doesn't mean he's great. You can't understand him at all and his lectures are hard to understand with just one watch. The only good thing about him is that he sticks to his word when writing exams and he's much more reliable than Bartos. Avoid taking physics 2 at UF at all costs unless you're amazing at physics

Professor Korytov is an extremely kind person. However, he is so difficult to understand with his Russian accent. I could only make out one out of every three words during most of his lectures and explanations. The material is very difficult to grasp anyway, so this makes it even harder, which is a shame because Korytov is a very sweet person.

Korytov taught material for 2049 that was on exam 1. afterwards bartos stepped in. Korytov prepared us for the exam very well, whereas bartos threw us to the wolves and made an absurdly difficult final exam. Korytov reviewed questions that were later on the exam. Knowing concepts is useless for exams. Do practice problems over and over and over.
Focused more on deriving equations than actually using them to solve problems. The exams were extremely hard and many questions on them were never covered in class. Was hard to hear at times.

Physics in general is awful at UF. The professor usually knows how to do the problems but cannot communicate it well to students. Often a lot of theory explaining rather than helping prepare for homeworks, quizzes, and exams. Exam's are hard with an average of 11/20 on each. You get a formula sheet which you have to use to save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Physics 2 is probably just a hard subject. Teachers do their best to explain it, but I mostly used study edge to pass the course.

Very confusing lectures, mainly due to the powerpoints the professors use, but he does do a pretty lackluster job at explaining very complicated Physics 2 concepts. You can get through the class by self-studying, but it is VERY difficult imo. Take at CC for an easier time. I've heard PHY2060/1 is better for learning the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He can be very difficult to understand, but he was the better of the two professors present in the course. Exams were kind of difficult, but not impossible. Most questions reflect past exams, so study those.

I took this class during an all online semester due to COVID-19. Physics 2 is a very challenging class and professor Korytov did not make it any easier. He is a horrible lecturer and is hard to understand, the tests he makes are nothing like the ones from the past so its very hard to study. Hell also include questions on things you dont learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I liked this professor, but it was very difficult to understand through his accent. He also teaches the topics well and is very passionate about them. The issue is sometimes the lectures are boring and he spends too much time fiddling with iClicker quizzes, even if they are extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is a genius, which is what I would deem as his only drawback. He does a good job at explaining the concepts but he does sometimes forget the level to which he is teaching. He also lacks energy so his lectures can be pretty boring, but he does a good job at teaching.
lectures were a useless waste of time; you have to teach yourself everything, and the content does not follow the textbook much.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst prof I've ever had. Can't teach or speak English. Starts every lecture saying "This chapter is very simple." Like dude, this is one of the hardest classes offered at UF. Definitely use StudyEdge for this course. I paid no attention when he taught our class. Could not even learn how to tie my shoes from this guy.

Korytov is an average lecturer, but his slides are available on Canvas and they generally follow the textbook (also available on Canvas) pretty closely. In my opinion, the hardest part of the class is the discussion quizzes, which depends entirely on your TA. Overall, the class is easy to pass if you commit to it (and maybe use StudyEdge).

Class itself was doable if you use Study Edge or are committed to reading the textbook (highly recommend Study Edge). Lectures were almost useless, usually just spent the entirety of the 50 minutes deriving a formula that was barely used. Usually went easy on giving extra credit clicker questions though which was nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: had to drop the class once him and mueller started switching after the 1st exam. Homework assignments or type questions are not at all on the exam. you need to really grasp the theory and concept before attempting to even understand the problems on the previous exams. He's a great person but not a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Simply put this guy can't teach. He doesn't explain anything well, his speech is unintelligible, and he doesn't prepare you well for the exam; you basically have to teach yourself everything. He told our class that he had concluded with material for our second exam, and then still tested us on it after telling us not to study it. Nice guy, bad prof

Strong Russian accent and loves to mumble into the microphone. Honestly, I'm lucky I even hear every 4th word. I only go to class for the clicker points and to write down the equations he puts up on the powerpoint. The course is hard, and tests are fair, but still expect a low score. (the whole class is curved).

This class is really difficult, and Korytov's lecture's aren't great, usually difficult to follow. The tests are really hard, but fortunately the grading scale is adjusted accordingly. I was able to get an A, relying almost completely on Study Edge to learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class with Korytov is insanely hard but having Study Edge saves your grade, even though the class is barely curved.

Great teacher. Don't miss lecture. Make sure to always finish your homework as that will help a lot for discussion quizzes. Homework, clicker questions, and discussion quizzes should be freebie since there's a lot of grade forgiveness. If you get all of those points, you only need to average a C- to get an A in the class. His accent isn't a problem

Expect to work really hard for a good grade. His accent makes him nearly impossible to understand. I went to class every day for the first exam and didn't do well. I started just using study edge and ended up doing way better. No matter what you'll work hard in physics but you have to be in your A game with him.

he has an accent that makes understanding him difficult with difficult material. DON"T FALL BEHIND! my friend got sick and miss a few days and was completely lost. Study edge helped me keep up with the class and understand the material he didn't explain well. Go to class

While some profs are really technical and boring, he teaches by making analogies to the real world. This makes topics super easy to understand and easy to remember for quizzes. I also like that he actually starts off some topics by saying "This is really easy" ... One of very few profs I've had to be encouraging and make things simple for students

On the first day of class I thought I was still hungover from the previous night. Turned out that it wasn't just me. His "English" is the worst I've ever heard. People in foreign countries speak way better English than this guy. I maybe understood 10 words total in the month he taught the class. Avoid. At all costs.

I thought his test (2nd exam) was easier than Avery's (they teach together). He took questions straight from the homework for his test, whereas Avery was more inventive with his test questions. Hard to understand in lecture; I would recommend an outside study outlet (TutoringZone, etc) for physics 2 in general.

AVOID him at all cost,guys !He teaches along with Avery this semester and these professors are mostly there for researches and not for teaching. He's not a good lecturer at all. His accent is REALLY thick that makes him so hard to understand in lecture .Exams are ridiculously HARD! StudyEdge and good TA might help. No curve!

Strong accent makes understanding him difficult sometimes, and he doesn't know how to really explain the material. He mostly presents it in the same way a textbook does. If you fall behind at all you are done for.

DO NOT FALL BEHIND! He will run through the material like you'll definitely understand it the first time you hear it. He's a brilliant guy, but he has a problem dumb'ing it down for the rest of us. And he likes to talk about his Higgs Boson research. Alot.

Overall I thought he was a great professor.  He doesn't do the usual boring power point lectures, he actually teaches using on the black board and does examples.  I hated physics but he made the topic a lot easier to understand and learn.
slightly below average

Overall I don't like him myself. He is always doing Calculus even though he is teaching Physics.... It seems all he knows about teaching is write down the formula and do the calculus. the other professor is so much better...... he makes his class really boring.....PHY 2049 as a whole is kind of hard.....the quizzes are easy but the exams are not.

Dr. Korytov was a great professor, this was the hardest class I had at UF, but he was invested in his students understanding the material and doing well. If you had questions and just not enough time during office hours, he would spend his own time explaining them to you to make sure you understood everything
Study hard, tests are all over the place. Also had Korytov/Hirshfield right after Walsh, and that was quite the trip.  Drop the class! Wait theres no other choices, guess you gotta deal...

Funny guy, good background. His language just gets in the way. Would understand better if it wasn't for a microphone projecting his voice over 600 heads. I would come to his class straight after having Walsh for Calc 3, yes, pitty on me
You'll learn more by reading the book when you go to class.  He's a good guy and helpful, but I just didn't learn too much from his lectures.
He's not a bad teacher...really nice guy...very helpful in office hours...he's hard to understand in lecture because of his accent...the exams are not hard if you study

Decent teacher.  Only real issue is the language barrier.  I learned from Physics 1 it was better to study from the book than use lectures.  His syllabus is a little on the hard side with little room for error.  He curves generously, so don't worry about low test scores.  He helps in office hours too as well as very enthusiastic.
I can't understand a thing he says. The best way to learn is to do as many practice problems as you can.
Prety freaking hard teacher... Yet he is very motivated with a positive attitude.  You will learn your physics and he is a genuinely nice person.
Very hard tests!!!! Makes class seem so simple and gives easy quizzes in class, and then you get to the test and don't recognize how to do any of the questions. He sucks
very good TA makes class easy and understandable
He is very lively and enthusiastic. His energy and positive attitude make him very easy to follow and to learn the information.

Take this class! So long as you show up once a week and do all her assignments that take about an hour a week to complete you're virtually guaranteed an A. The only thing you have to study for is the Excel certification exam which doesn't require a lot of studying. Dr. M herself is very enthusiastic about the course. Take this instead of CGS2531.

Easiest class you will take. Only one exam (on Excel). 90% of the grade is assignments ~2 hours max per week. Meets once per week for max of 1 hour and the Prof is as enthusiatic as you can get about Excel and Access.
Do not take with her, absolutely abysmal experience with her.
Too much work for a 2 credit class and daily quizzes, projects, and assignments.

Easiest critical tracking class you will ever take. Meets once a week for a project you do with a partner. If you're stuck she'll help you through it. No exams, only play posits and the excel certification/final exam. Definitely chose the excel certification its super easy. Please take this and not CGS trust me.

Most of the class is assignments with unlimited attempts and step by step instructions. Only somewhat difficult thing is the excel certification midterm but that's relatively easy too. Professor mostly just lets you learn through the online textbook and doesn't really teach herself, but its easy to get an A.

Very light class, hardest part was the Excel Certification Exam, but that wasn't even that bad. Some of her lab instructions were confusing and there was some busy work, but overall not bad at all. Only one lab a week.

One of the easiest classes I've taken. Study early for the Excel Certification exam and attend every class. The in-class projects make up a big part of your grade. She's a good professor, but be on time for class because if you are more than 5 minutes late, she won't let you do the project. No extensions, so don't turn things in late.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy class. Spent about an hour a week on this and got Excel certified.

I recommend this class! Dr. M gives step by step instructions for the labs each week in person that don't even take the full two periods. I passed the excel certification with minimal studying. The only other assignments are play posits on canvas.

The class was a very easy A. All of the in-class assignments were done in partners and the TAs and her will help with anything you may need. There was about an hour of work per-week to do outside of class, but there was nothing to stress or worry about.

The class is set up so that there are lectures due outside of class and projects completed in pairs during class. If you finish the project early, which is almost all of the time, you can also leave early. The projects and lectures are both very easy, and the professor and TAs will help if you have trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy A. Don't need prior knowledge for the class. Couple extra credit

This class was extremely easy. The online assignments take about half an hour each to complete and the weekly in person assignments take about half an hour to an hour to complete. If you show up and do the work you will get an A in this class.

Super easy class that I would take again. Online IS assignments are very easy and can be taken as many times as needed. In class assignments are also easy and have hint videos if you get stuck. You also have an opportunity to get Excel certified. 10/10 class.

This class was very straightforward and it was very clear what to do. I don't love working with excel, but it was still made very easy to do well. Also you get the opportunity to become excel certified which is really cool!
Great class and professor! I learned a lot and it was not stressful. I would 100% recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The class was relatively easy. I had to watch PlayPosit lectures and complete the computer lab with a partner every week but they're all step-by-step. If you take the Excel certification, buy the practice test and it should be easy.

Professor is super nice and passionate about the material. Grade is mainly based on the activities you complete in class with your partner and easy video lecture assignments. Hardly any work you have to do outside of class. Really recommend this course over the computer program option.

Dr. Aditi is just one of the best professors at UF. She is caring and tries to make her lectures clear and fun. I appreciate her effort to make lectures as personal and interactive as possible and her humor is always on point. Although exams and projects can be harder than average, she makes sure to give you enough practice to do great in her class

Lots of assignments, but you can get 100 on all of them. 5 Tests and 1 gets dropped, they aren't too difficult. Very easy A, and you learn a lot of useful skills. Professor is funny, but I would speed up her lectures.
Nothing to complain about, assignments are straightforward and not too difficult. Only thing to watch for is some tests have content that isn't covered in the review notes. Great and funny professor.

This class can be hard. My suggestions are 1. Watch the lectures and take notes 2. Before the exams re-watch the lectures and note down ALL the examples she uses (they are mentioned in the exam) 2. Don't do the final project. Take the excel certification. Good Luck.

Dr. Mukherjee, although challenging, is an amazing and rewarding professor. She makes guidelines clear at the start of every course I've taken. Exams can be very difficult, so be sure that you understand the ins and outs of the material. The best thing about her classes is that due to the workload and practicality, you really learn the material.
This was a great course to take, there are a lot of assignments that you are graded on which spreads the grading scale making it easy to score very high. Overall great class and professor.

Hands down one of the best professors I had at UF! She is caring, she tries to make classes fun, she goes out of the way to make sure everyone understands the material and exams are more than fair. Projects can be a bit hard but they'll prepare you for the exams. She also does exam reviews where she explains what you can expect on the exam.
All the assignments are straightforward and there are TA's in the lab to help you. Great way to learn excel and access and get a certification.

Dr. Mukherjee was great! She provides "hint" videos with each assignment which make assignments straight forward. You can resubmit assignments before the deadline for a better score. Lectures are less than one hour per week, tests every two weeks. She drops your lowest test grade. This course is not as hard as people make it out to be!

ISM 3013 was so easy. I litterly finished all the assignments besides the tests in October. The excel projects are extremely easy and she litterly makes a video on how to do it exactly. There are lectures and the test which are also fairly easy. They are a little boring but this class is easy

This class is chill and great to balance out a schedule with other hard classes. You learn a lot of valuable Excel & Access concepts and also get Excel certified, which is great to put on a resume. Quizzes are lowkey hard but are only worth 20% of your grade and one gets dropped. I recommend taking this class over CGS for sure.

Idk what any of these other reviews say. This class is pure, unadulterated cake. Super easy class and with some useful excel concepts for those who are looking at and excel heavy job like investment banking.

This class is a breeze if you just complete the assignments on time. She talks very fast in the lectures, so make time to pause. 40% of your grade is IT assignments with a video walking you through the steps. The quizzes could be very specific and challenging but reread your notes and take the practice quizzes for each chapter and you'll do fine.

Her lectures were SO boring. However, it's an easy class and you get excel certified. Just watch lecture on 1.5x and take notes - the exams are actually really hard (I got C's on each). She drops one exam & they take like 7 min to take but they are just super specific (don't count for much though). Assignments are SO easy if you watch the video.

Very easy class as long as you do your work. Quizzes are kinda trivia but it doesn't matter because they aren't worth that much. Personally I'd take the hybrid version rather than the completely online version.

This class is very easy! I took CGS also, and enjoyed this one much more. The quizzes were very easy and the exams were not too difficult if you do the practice quizzes. All the excel/access assignments have videos showing exactly how to do them so those were very easy as well. The only thing I don't like is how quickly she spoke in the lectures.

Dr. M was my favorite teacher. Her lecture vids are a little fast-paced sometimes so it takes a while to watch them but she gives you plenty of time to complete assignments. She provides hint videos for all of the Microsoft topics which literally show you how to do the assignment and get a good grade for it. She is nice and replies to emails fast.

Very easy to get an A if you just complete all assignments on time. Every assignment is posted w/ a "hint video" that literally shows you exactly how to do it. Quizzes are not proctored and questions are straight from lecture. Exams are a bit difficult but are exactly like the quizzes. Dr. M is nice & understanding, just talks fast in lecture.

This class is definitely harder than its CGS counterpart. The class is 50% following directions on excel and 50% exams that are vocabulary. Our class wasn't offered excel certification but I heard it's useful. Use quizlet for the quizzes and watch all lectures and fill out Dr. M's note guide a week before exams and you should be good.

Is very clear on what needs to be completed for her class. The video lectures were not that great. Talked too fast, randomly skips or repeats. Also not that engaging, often zoned out and had to re-watch. Assignments were relatively easy to complete in the given time frame. Should study for the exams.

ISM3013 mainly focuses on Excel learning, which is very applicable to real-world problems. Dr. M is very clear about her expectations - do the Excel/Access assignments (with her hint videos), take the weekly quizzes (fairly easy), and relate real-life examples to the concepts taught in the lectures, then you'll do well on the 3 exams and in class.

Your grade is heavily dependent on the three tests. Watch. the. videos. They are a pain but if you plan it right you'll be grateful that you watched it. Also, the quizzes are easy enough to do well. Group projects in class those are easy, the TA's are nice. For the excel certification, get g-metrix, you'll get to practice the excel tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures and exams for the IS topics were horrible. It takes so long to take notes because she talks so fast, and the exams you kinda have to wing it. The Excel topics were not difficult at all. For Excel certification, I definitely recommend GMetrix. It was helpful! We didn't do Access bc of online transition, but I'm sure it wouldn't be hard.

Professor Mukherjee is honestly a great professor. I like how she tells you what you need to know to do well on the exam. It doesn't feel like she's trying to trick us (which is refreshing). She explains concepts well in lecture and answers emails fast. The projects helped me prepare for her tests. Put in the effort you can get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you take the practice quizzes for the exams she gives and take VERY detailed notes from her lecture videos then you can make A's on exams. I recommend making quizlets for them. Her lecture videos are very boring and take forever to make notes but it's doable. Use geometrics for the excel certification, and quiz answers are on quizlet.

The easiest class I've taken at UF. Just come in weekly to do projects which if you follow her steps exactly will be an easy A every time. The day of every exam I would watch all the lectures which would take about an hour and a half and then take the exam right after and get an A. Quizzes are common sense and easy points.
Aweful!

I had Dr.M for ISM4113, ISM4210, and QMB4702. She was an amazing lecturer for all three classes and I felt that she had clear grading criteria. I emailed her with a ton of questions for those classes and she was very responsive. Although those classes were a little test/project heavy as long as you pay attention, you'll be fine.

This professor first and foremost tries really hard and does seem to care, but her expectations of every student to be entirely committed and deeply passionate about the subject as she is is very unrealistic. She regularly gets angry at the class for not being enthusiastic and takes it out on our grades and how hard she makes and grades exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The only thing about this class that requires actual effort is prepping for the Excel Cert Exam, since the lab sessions prior to the Cert exam are little to no help. Consider the exam review resources she recommends in the module for it. For the exams and quizzes, just watch the concept videos and use Quizlet as needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Excel and Access projects are free A's so make sure you don't skip any. Exam questions are fairly similar to quizzes and reuse questions sometimes. The Excel certification is tricky and includes things that weren't taught in class so be sure to prepare well for it.

Excel/Access assignments are a breeze. Make sure to always go to lab because these seriously help your grade. the Information Systems portion of the class, however, is a lot trickier. The pre recorded videos aren't very helpful when it comes to quizzes + tests. Questions on exams come out of nowhere, and you need a good understanding of concepts
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't know if there are any better choices for this class. Good part was being able to get Excel certified, and that assignments you did with a partner and basically always get 100's. Bad is tests are very hard. Very hard to pull an A in the class.  Unclear of where to find material that will be on the test. Only 30 questions, 4 wrong that's a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The tests are stupid hard for no rhyme or reason and the content is downright silly and useless. Plus, she puts questions on the test out of nowhere. Overall terrible class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Honstly one of the worst structured classes I have ever taken. The lectures aren't even in person and the videos she puts up have absolutely nothing to do with her quizzes. Overall really bad class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: If taken online, her project lectures are only a bit helpful. Had to look up a lot online. As for her IS topics, its a lot. The lectures are long and you need to watch those along with taking notes from the book. She helped me out when I needed a grade bump though. I like her as a person but her class is a hard one for something that could be easy.

She makes it mandatory to have Microsoft 2013 but it's not available for Mac... I had to use my roommate's Windows computer to do all of my weekly projects. The projects are very difficult and she barely explains half the instructions with her lectures. Her lectures for the textbook info is also vague and does not help when taking quizzes/tests.

I've actually taken 2 different classes with Dr. Mukherjee. While I find that most of her classes are a waste of time.. in one of them we just played with legos and playdoh.. I find that she gives a ton of extra credit. While I do say sometimes I think she pulls things out from thin air. However, she will help your grade! And is very funny

Okay, she was so unhelpful.. my grades ranged from a 94 on the exam to a 66 on the second. She literally would tell you what to study and then pull these random questions out of no where.. It was so frustrating because I had no idea what to study. The certifications are super easy, basically everyone passes. She offers exams curves but not enough.

She's fun and spunky. There's a curve on every test that bumps your grade up by a whole letter grade generally. She also helped me get a nearly perfect score on my Microsoft Excel and Access certification exams too. Pay attention in class, take notes, google quizzes, and skim over the textbook to get an A
Awful teacher

I loved this professor, she is very quirky and nice. Sometimes i struggled through the mandatory lab, which you had a project. So I'd suggest watching the videos ahead of time. Other than that if you watch the lecture, study for the tests and exams you can get an A, A-. Not a bad class at all and its very useful (but expensive)

She's honestly hilarious, her Access/Excel videos on Sakai are EXTREMELY helpful and an A/A- is very easy if you just go to Discussion class and read the book/take practice exams on Connect before exams. Just don't be an idiot and she'll usually help you if you're strugging. I'd say this class was extremely useful (albeit expensive)

NO PATIENCE, Not helpful in office hours, extremely rude, very sarcastic and tries to make you look stupid, very unprofessional, her assistant is extremely nice and helpful. The online exams are harder than they should be. Silly material
hard to communicate
Great teacher! She explains every excel and access chapter very well. Just read the chapters for the in class exams. Class isn't mandatory. Quizzes are easy. :)

Had her for a different class than others on here. Was a fairly straightforward and mostly easy class. Some lectures were on the boring side. Exams were straightforward from lectures and she was overall pleasant.

While it was very difficult to pay attention in class, the times that I did, she was funny, nerdy, and really wanted her students to do well. Many mix ups with when quizzes were due, but they were decent if you used the texts. Study for the exams and you will pull off an A if you do all the work. Most students passed Access/Excel exams the first ti

Really easy class; just do all the assignments/read the textbook & STUDY. Class isnt mandatory (skip Monday's, come to Wednesday lab). Certifications were a little tough, but I easily passed both 1st time around. Curves the grade at the end & drops 3 quizzes, assessments, hw assignments. Ending semester before curve w a 97%.

One word describes this two semester experienced professor: unprofessional.  Stop trying to be everyone's friend and teach!  While you are at it, how about some objective grading and control over compulsive cheating during tests?  Ready to finish this class and move on.

Dr. Hale is kind, but she teaches very fast and expects us to have a deep background in the material. Many people I know have dropped because of this. Mini-exams are heavily weighted and can hurt your grade, while practice exams don't match the actual tests. To succeed, I definitely recommend using StudyEdge.
the goat, grades based off exams but she has lots of padding built into grading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: is she annoying with her singing? yes. is the class hard? yes, but every chm1 class is hard. in my opinion she is the best professor for chm1. the difficulty of the mini exams + exams is going to be the same across all chem profs. everyone rating her poorly on here is just rating based on self projection. shes good, im taking her again for chm2
Expect to put 10 hours a week into Chem2045 with any professor if you want to succeed. Dr. Hale is extremely bubbly and makes it fun to attend lectures.

PLEASE AVOID THIS CLASS!! Dr.Hale is very kind but between her mini exams (which weigh you down and no other professor does) and her singing in class, your only hope to passing is subscribing to StudyEdge on the first day of class. had to drop the class because not even passing those progress exams could save my grade thanks to the mini exams.

You're better off just teaching yourself everything, she's inconstant with what she teaches in different lectures depending on the time of day, and generally explains almost every concept poorly. Chem 1 has relatively very easy material, but she still finds a way to explain it bad enough and jump around topics enough you'll leave lecture confused.

Dr. Hale is a nice person and tries to be helpful when students reach out, but her lectures are virtually incomprehensible, and she frequently glazes over topics. Exams make up almost your entire grade, despite the HOURS worth of HW assigned each week on top of studying. Definitely recommend Study Edge!

She tries to make lectures entertaining by bursting out into song (often Taylor Swift), but when it's finals season, and you're spending every day studying and stressing about classes, it can get grating. Her lecture style made me grateful for my high school AP Chem teacher. She overcomplicates explanations; definitely recommend YouTube instead.
The professor is standardly unhelpful, but is better than no instructor. She often bursts out into song during class. This professor is not accommodating.

Absolutely amazing lecturer does her best to keep it engaging while getting through all the content. Class can be hard, but doing the recommended practice problems in the textbook helps a lot. Explains everything very well in the lecture and during her office hours.

Dr. Hale was a great professor and cared a lot about science. It is very hard to teach students so much material with such little class time. I used Study Edge for a lot of additional learning after going to her lectures as they can be kind of hard to keep up with. Overall, she is very enthusiastic about chemisty (and Taylor Swift).
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had a great time in Dr. Hale's class. Her lectures were engaging, and actually explained why things occur the way they do. She is an inspirational teacher. Her exams, however, were insanely difficult. Attending and participating in lectures, completing practice exams, reviewing slides, reading the textbook, and going to office hours helps.

idc what anyone says, i loved dr. hale. she is by far the best professor for 2046. she actually teaches in class (when she isnt singing) but i think it makes it so engaging. she is super approachable, and her class genuinely helped so much. you do not need study edge at all, just pay attention in lecture, and DO PRACTICE TESTS!!!

Professor Hale is very passionate about what she teaches, but I found that it often got in the way of her lectures and made her hard to understand and she would often go on tangents that weren't that relevant to the course. The course is very test heavy but study edge was definitely helpful.

She's overall a decent lecturer, but you need to put in more effort than just showing up to lectures. She is sometimes hard to keep up with because of her singing, but rewatching the lectures posted online 100% helps. If you do ALL the practice exams, review the textbook & practice questions, you'll be okay. Study edge helps, but isn't needed.

She just reads off slides and does not teach anything. You basically have to learn the entirety of the material by yourself. She also thinks she is funny by dancing and singing when no one actually cares. If I didn't have a baseline for this stuff before I took the class def would not have done good. Do not take her.

I see why people would complain about her teaching style because it is quite ... "extra" BUT it is still really effective while being engaging. I feel like her class made me understand chemistry in ways my high school teachers never could. She likes to build a foundation from the theoretical to further understanding (and tests on these concepts!).

She sings which is endearing at first but grows old quickly. You can tell she really is passionate about chemistry but often skims over exam content to rant about some random chem topic she finds interesting. Exams were tough, and practice exams are nothing like actual exam. Overall doable if you put time into reading textbook + practice problems.

She's not bad, that's important. Her lectures are insightful and she's enthusiastic (sometimes too much, be ready for singing). However, the exams make up pretty much all the grade and they are very very difficult. Lectures and studying are pivotal. Make use of the TAs and office hours. You'll likely get frustrated or annoyed, but it's still Chem.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not sure why she gets good reviews. Lectures were rushed and disorganized, and she spent too much singing and not enough time on lecture content. Made it impossible to focus on the actual chem and was honestly kind of rude.

She can make things more difficult than they need to be. I recommend her if you've taken AP Chemistry because she helps you understand things on a deeper level. Biggest tip: take past exams and start studying 3 days before (longer if you missed lectures). Expect lower quiz grade than exam grade (but please study!!!). Also, she sings in class.
The professor is unaccommodating, even in extreme situations.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She does not thoroughly explain the PowerPoints and goes really fast. Also, if you ever decide to say an answer out loud in class and you get it wrong, she genuinely will give you so much shame in front of the entire class. It is pretty discouraging. Also in her emails, she is not compassionate and makes it pretty difficult to be vulnerable to her
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Just sings every lecture instead of teaching you. Exams are worded to just trick you instead of test you, and they also consist of content she mutters under her breath and is in a corner of her PowerPoints. Very rude to some students

Hale has bad lectures that can be confusing when she starts singing or making obscure references. She lacks communication skills and often times doesn't go over material that shows up on exams or quizzes. Attendance not mandatory and not needed since her lectures are hard to follow and don't help. Study edge needed.

The only material to really help you in the class is the lecture and the homework assignments. Do not expect to do well without attending. I missed the 4th of July week and I felt like that definitely played a role in my final grade. The lectures are recorded, but Dr.Hale moves a lot so don't expect the best quality recordings.

Dr. Hale was great, very enthusiastic about chemistry, and she had office hours 3 days a week, and even more before exams. 
Full credit on homework as long as you finish it, no quizzes, 3 midterms + a final, which are difficult but if you're taking this class you should expect that.

She's passionate, energetic, & good at explaining. StudyEdge is great. Go to her office hours! The quizzes and exams are difficult, but she gives you the resources to succeed. You need to dedicate lots of time % effort, but I got an A in chm 1 & 2 with her. She sings and stuff which I get not everyone likes, but it makes the class more engaging tbh

Very very (VERY) enthusiastic professor; Kind, but sometimes a little too excited to teach to the point where what's on the test is not emphasized. The tests are hard but the practice tests, quizzes, and homeworks are mostly helpful. Super sweet and loveable professor though!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hale's lectures are mediocre at best .Her exams and quizzes are way more difficult than they need to be and often are setup for you to do poorly on rather than succeed. She loves chemistry, but expects her students to love it and dedicate hundreds of hours a week to her class. Study edge will make your life easier. Study hard for quizzes/exams

Professor Hale is very energetic and passionate about her class. She does genuinely try to help any students if issues come up. Her office hours helped a lot to expand on certain topics. Chemistry is hard, but she does a good job at teaching it. She does sing and bring up off topic/tangential stuff in class sometimes though.

Enthusiastic but didn't go in detail to help ppl understand topics, felt rushed & had to go past the end of class, get study edge to make your life easier. Exam questions are similar to concepts/ topics study edge talks about + past exams. Soooo much busy work: hw(2-3),pla(3), quizzes(1), worksheet quizzes (1), worksheets(1) each every single week.

Be prepared to absolutely die in chemistry at UF. She's not flipped style learning, but she might as well be. I would suggest taking another prof bc she is kinda disorganized-everyone was confused when our grades dropped and the canvas grade was false the whole sem. Failed the class before even taking the final bc 60% of our grade was exam scores

Hale is not everyone's cup of tea, but I found her lectures very engaging. I would recommend reading the textbook before class because it's hard to keep up with the lecture if you don't have a background. You don't need study edge, just do all the textbook questions and the practice exams. Exams are hard but plenty of practice will get you an A.

I loved Dr Hale. Her exam questions are kind of tricky and conceptual, but she is very approachable if you go to her office hours. Some people call her "crazy" cause she will randomly start singing Taylor Swift in class, but honestly, it helped me remember some material better (I am a Swiftie). Definitely do the practice problems from the book!

This class genuinely took everything out of me. The content is not that bad but the exams are extremely hard!! Quizzes depend on if you have a strict TA or not. Definitely need studyedge for this class to do well.

Professor Hale comes to class excited to teach and full of energy. If you plan to take Hale, be ready for a lot of singing/musical references and a Harry Potter obsession. The grading for quizzes depends on your TA, but exams are all multiple choice. She responds to emails, but is a little passive aggressive in her responses. Overall ok.

Hale sings a lot and it can be a bit annoying and distracting but other than that her lectures are good. I recommend having study edge on the side because some things can be explained better. But overall if you attend office hours do the  homework and make sure to watch lectures (they are recorded) you should be fine.
