He's difficult, with multiple papers/exams making up the bulk of grading, but the discussion makes up for it. As long as you're able to write, it's fine. Exams will only cover what he said in class, so notetaking makes them easy to prep for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Classes have a reaction paper due every Monday and Friday that must be 500 words, be prepared to read. However, the readings are discussed in class and feel like they have a purpose in the class overall, rather than just being busy work. He genuinely cares about the class and encourages discussion. Very nice teacher and would definitely recommend.

soooooooo many reaction papers. i had him for a caribbean class and every week there were 2 500 word reaction papers due. one due monday one friday. and he randomly grades  5 out of the 20 due. lectures would turn into tangents so he wouldnt even answer a question if u asked. a great guy but holy cow would not take him again if i could choose.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Very nice, friendly professor. Classes are very discussion-oriented.

However, I do feel that it is a lot of work at times. You have to write two 490-500 reaction papers on a reading per week, and doing these papers were often time-consuming
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Good teacher, big lecturer, assigns a lot of readings but if you pace it out it's not too bad. I took him for Politics of Puerto Rico and I enjoyed it. I could've gotten a better grade if I turned in the essays on time + enough words.

Professor held very engaging lectures and encouraged discussion. He respects everyone's views and examines all angles of a topic. His TA was fairly specific on some aspects of the reaction papers and essays, but not overly harsh. Overall an interesting class with a professor who cares about the topic and his students.

Suarez is the best lecturer I've ever had. You can tell he cares deeply about the art of teaching and engaging a classroom. He is an easy grader if you know what he is looking for, but he is very particular. Exams are all written, and 2 major papers are written with novels to be read outside class. He is flexible, but takes a while to grade things.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly, it was a super interesting class. Attendance really matters in terms of participation, as you can fail very easily if you miss multiple classes. His TA was not great with grading or reading papers thoroughly enough. Overall, only take this class if you're committed to not missing more than 3 classes, and if you're interested in it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Graded on attendance, participation, 5 randomly selected 500 word reaction papers, 2 papers, a midterm, and a final. All are pretty easy. He is a passionate lecturer and really cares about the topic. One thing to note is that you have to write a 500 word reaction paper every M and F, but otherwise there is not a lot of work. Fairly easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is a good lecturer and the content is very interesting. You are graded on two exams, 4-5 randomly selected reaction papers out of 15, two short papers, attendance, and participation. You get a failing attendance grade after 3 absences so do not exceed that limit. I wish I knew that and to do all the reaction papers no matter what.
i liked the class but not the professor. instructions were unclear on most assignments. takes off points for simple thing like double space. do not recommend.

I personally loved this class. We read 2-3 research papers a week, wrote 2 reaction papers a week, 2 short papers, and took 2 exams. Attendance and participation are both graded. The readings he assigns are interesting and reaction papers take an hour to write. I thought his lectures were fun and relevant, the tests are easy too if you study.

I did not have a problem personally with him but I would never take another one of his classes. Readings are way too long and there are three a week. You'll write 1,000 words weekly and he only grades 6 out of the 15-20 that we do in a semester. The class is easy to pass, I got an A with minimal effort, but I truly feel like I learned nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Suarez is probably the best professor I have had so far. He is super passionate about the classes he teaches which makes lectures even more interesting. He is always willing to help or clarify with any material you might have trouble understanding. Overall phenomenal professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: class makes you think about lots of important topics. lots of papers. exams are easy and open-ended

Professor Suarez is a great professor and he is very passionate about the material he teaches. I took two classes with him because he is pretty straightforward. His classes have a lot of reading and writing assignments, three reading and two writing each week, but if you go to class and pay attention the class is pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a good choir director. Pretty chill and relaxed but also can offer some really intense feedback that builds your skill as a singer. If you have experience in a choir before he's about what you would typically expect.
He is the chillest professor I have ever had. Some musical experience is required, but he is very helpful with any problems you may encounter and will stick around after class if needed.
Super chill guy, fun to work with. You kind of have to have some background knowledge of singing/sightreading but at this point in school most people in chorus have already sang before.

Great choir director, really chill guy. Doesn't provide many resources for beginners unless you ask, but I found most of what we sang was relatively easy to pick up with practice even without being able to sight read.

Less experienced students aren't helped much with performances. Often criticizes smaller things in comparison to glaring problems with performances. For a class marketed towards students of any experience level, it's not clear how much that is considered. Overall, seems like a chill guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cain conducts the Choral (treble choir) and the Glee Club (tenor-bass choir), and his good personality makes learning about music and performing it fun and relaxed. I have been in Glee Club for 3 semesters now, and each semester has at least one concert to perform at, and Dr. Cain frequently looks for more performance opportunities.

explains concepts very clearly. her lectures are very engaging, and they were never boring in my opinion. I loved that she did two days of review before every exam and I found that, because of her reviews, I didn't have to study for any of the exams to succeed in the class. the extra credit in this class is also very abundant.

Extremely flexible and caring about students. The honors section was easy, given that I had already taken calculus in high school. Her lectures mainly just go over example problems; I rarely felt lost, but the videos from Dr. Streese that she links in Canvas were helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took her for Calc 1, and she's a good instructor. Answers questions in class, and would circle around whenever we'd do practice questions. Gives lots of resources to study for exams, which I found so helpful. She really shines during office hours, though, so definitely go to those even if you're retaking the credit!

I took the honors section of calc 1 and had a great experience. She provides so many resources and had efficient, effective, and well structured lectures. the exams were all very fair and easy to prepare for. strongly recommend, she definitely has a very deep understanding of mathematics and is an excellent educator.
Honestly I watched Stresse's videos that she posted more than her own, but she was not bad. She clearly went over the topics in the packet, however, sometimes she moved quickly and skipped around

Some days her lectures were very clear and helpful, others I left more confused than anything. Definitely watch Dr. Streese's lecture videos and get Study Edge. Extra credit for exams was very helpful. Weekly homework felt very tedious, but was very helpful with unlimited attempts.

She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She provides a lot of study resources for the tests. The extra credit helps a lot, especially for the final. Her lectures are also helpful.

She was really nice and cared about all the students. I would watch Dr Stresses lectures for more help. Definitely get StudyEdge because it teaches you in a different way so can understand the material better and extra practice is always good. Do all old practice exams before tests because test is almost exactly like practice exams!

Was a very sweet prof and she was a great teacher. If you had any questions she would always answer them. Was in the honors section and when we did practice problems she would circle around the room to see our work and if we were doing it right or if we had questions and she would guide us accordingly. Pay attention to her reviews for exams.

As someone who's already taken calc 1 before, she's honestly pretty good at teaching it. Sometimes her lectures are kinda scattered and sometimes she doesn't explain things as well as she probably could but  she's still pretty good at what she does. She's also always willing to help so definitely reach out to her.

The lectures are kind of fast-paced, and the accent makes it a little hard, but she is very caring and walks around the classroom to see whoever has any questions. She also includes a 5% curve and offers 2% credit for all the exams.

Thick accent that takes time to get used to, but she is good at explaining the problem-solving steps. MAC2311 is weird in the way it is set up because the actual teaching of the lesson is through videos on Canvas. Class is just practice with more problems (not a fan of this structure).

Awesome professor for diff eq. Made the class enjoyable and her activities do well to prepare the class for exams. Writes her own exams and each type of question has been covered in either the lectures or review packet. Would 100% take any math class with her again.

Took Dr Gamage for Calc 1 and had such a good experience I chose to take Calc 2 with her as well. She takes her time explaining topics, offers extra credit through discussion boards, and goes through the effort of printing out packets and exam reviews for every student.

I had Calc 1 with Professor Gamage and decided to take Calc 2 with her again because she is a great professor who cares a lot about her students.  She makes workbooks and exam review packets that are very helpful.  In Calc 2 I ended about .5% away from passing with a C, and I emailed her and she helped me.

This class was well structured and the professor explained clearly. There were opportunities for extra credit in discussion boards as well as in exams which gave a boost to the grade. The  grade also depends on homeworks and quizzes .
Prof Gamage really cares about her students, and her lectures are pretty easy to follow and relate a lot to what's on the test.

If you need a calc teacher, CHOOSE HER!!!! Can't say enough good things about her. She creates packets for each unit with a large amount of practice problems, and always gives extra exam review that other teachers don't. She is also so helpful during office hours- she will work through any problem you need from the homework or quizzes.

Took her again for Calculus 2. I had personal family issues the semester I took it, and she was very understanding and helped me a lot during office hours to catch up with assignments and content. Passing with an A relied solely on her and my TA's help, which also reflects how good Calc 2 with her is as a course

Calculus 1 with Gamage was heaven. Amazing lecturer, caring, flip classroom style so you could ask questions. You can rely on Dr. Streese online lectures for review, and they are just as great. Not only you will learn, but you will have a caring professor trying to make you succeed. I took Calc 2 with her and my experience was even better.

I took Gamage due to the review that someone left that her Calc1 class was great and then came back to write another review because her Calc2 class was great as well. I can not recommend her more highly, her packets are on another level as she is as well. She genuinely cares about feedback and tries to give the best tips. I'll be back after Calc2!!

Amazing Calc 1 professor! Her packets made it so easy to stay organized and study. Make sure to do past exams to prepare for exams! I took AP Calc in High School, but I was nervous to jump to Calc 2 in my first semester. This class helped me feel confident for Calc 2. Lectures aren't mandatory, but the habit of being present will keep you on track

Had her for her honors calc 1 section and she was super attentive during it! Went out of her way to look at our papers and help us if we went the wrong direction. Honestly easier then regular calc 1. TA quizzes a bit brutal during Unit 1 but the rest were fine. Exam was a little scary but the multiple choice was 80% easy with 2-4 brutal ones only.

Lectures are good except the majority of content and information provided in lecture note packet comes from Streese and is the preferred lecturer. Past exams are extremely helpful in preparation for exams as this course is more of a review of calc 1 and self study is needed.

Took her for Calc 1, loved her so much I'm taking her again for Calc 2. Explains clearly, and she will always stay a after class to see if anyone has questions. She always followed my DRC accommodations. Seems like easier of a class than calc with another prof. Just know that a lot of your grade with come from your TA bc they grade your stuff.
Gives a good curriculum to succeed, her texts can introduce concepts in a more complex matter than they need to be explained, but she is great at explaining and making Calculus concepts accessible

Very clear and organized professor, gave lots of good materials (including past exams which were very helpful). However, much of the course material must also be self-taught and it is easy to fall behind. The exams were worth most of our grade and easy to do poorly on despite knowing the material well due to the nature of the questions.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's nice, and her unit packets helped with note-taking. Her lectures were good, but I preferred Dr. Streese, whose video lectures she also posted. I watched those and attended her class for clarification. She shares many resources and wants students to succeed. Focus on practicing past tests she provided—they were key to my success.

She covered all of the content and was open to questions. Has a bit of an accent but there was never a time I couldn't understand her. It was nice that she printed out note packets and made review sheets for all of the exams. If you took calculus in high school and did pretty well I would jump up to calc 2. I wish I did.

I would go to her offices hours asking her to explain problems she would be very off putting and often ignored my questions to regarding the process of the problem. During lectures she often glazed over problem that she felt were easy even when questioned she would just say this is something you should know. Not helpful take someone else.

She is very nice, but make sure you're doing most of the learning on your own as her lectures usually are best for reviewing because they are fast and it's hard to process everything she goes through each lecture if you don't already understand the basics. You need to do as many practice tests as you can, because your grade is mostly tests.

Wasn't hard, just annoying. I took calc in high school and this was the same thing with a few more concepts stacked on top. HW and quizzes are in Canvas (kinnda aggravating tbh), tests are MCQ and FRQ. Lock in on those exams and it shouldn't be too bad. She's a good prof, I was just never that engaged bc I've taken calc before.

If you go to lectures and do the homework it is almost impossible to do poorly in this class. The homework problems and the practice done in the discussion session is exactly what will be on the test.

Professor Gamage is honestly an amazing option for Calc. She explains the topics very well and has everything laid out so you could figure out the schedule of lectures and what is happening every time you come into class. Grading scales are very clear and she is always willing to help in lectures as long as you are willing to ask questions.

I thought this would be a relatively easy class haven taken calc in high school and having an A all year, but I was wrong. Worst class on my schedule. The exams are very hard and if you think you understand a concept after studying for days, you still won't know it on the exam because the most outrageous versions of a question are asked.

Overall, she's a great professor. There is a good amount of homework, but it is manageable. Homework assignments are usually harder than the tests. The tests are hard but not outrageous. Moves very quickly, so don't take this class if you've never taken Calculus before.
AMAZING!! I love this woman.

I took Dr. Gamage for DiffEq Summer B. Going in, I was scared because it was a 6 week course, but she made the experience amazing. She gives you the notes at the beginning of class, making understanding lectures easier. She is very understanding and always open to questions. Lots of hw but manageable. Tests are fair. Would definitely take again!

Diff eq can be a tough subject but Dr. Gamage made the class a lot more manageable! (This is coming from someone who finds math really difficult) She requires mandatory attendance but her lectures are very informative and better than any youtube video you'll find online. If you're taking diff eq at UF, take it with Gamage.

Dr. Gamage was an excellent DiffEq professor this summer! It was her first time teaching the course but she made a difficult topic very easy. I never felt like the exams were designed to trip me up and I always felt the questions were fair.

Gamage is an amazing calc 2 prof. I was nervous but you can ask her any questions you have and she will be extremely helpful. The content is tough but she will help make sure you do well. The exams can be tough but the review packets she puts together are amazing in helping you prepare. cannot rec her more.

I took Gamage for calc 1 and 2 and completed both with an A. Her lectures were very useful and straight to the point. She provided review packets for exams that covered everything needed, so if you did the homework,  review packet, and a practice exam or 2, the tests should be a breeze. Gamage also linked videos for further explanations. Take her!!

I had heard horror stories of Calc 2 but she made it easier and fun. She is so understanding and kind but also is just built for teaching, her style is so clear and easy to learn from. I had some external issues the semester I took her and only got the C I needed to pass but no doubt in a typical semester would done so much better thanks to her!!
Took Gamage for calc 2 and it was great even thought it was a really tough class. Probably wouldn't have done as well if I wasn't taking her. Her lectures are really helpful and the best way to pass

i had her for calc 1 and loved her so much i took calc 2 with her and again, she was amazing!! she's so patient and really cares about the class and her students. quick email responses and understanding if u need an extension. genuinely my favorite prof, i wish she had a calc 3 class for next semester. TAKE CALC WITH G

YOOOO same person who called her a goat last semester and let me tell you... ONCE AGAIN A GOATT!!!! Calc 2 was such a breeze with her absolutely recommend! She gives you so material to study, and all you have to do is go to class. Also, her TAs are pretty good as well (idk if this changes). GOAT ONCE AGAIN!!

Gamage is a new professor at UF. I took her calc 2 flipped class. Even though its "flipped" I never watch the online lectures because she basically just teaches it in class. She is very caring and ready to answer any question. Good lecturer and in a much better environment than a huge lecture hall.

I took this professor last semester for calc 1 and this semester for calc 2. She is amazing and puts a lot of effort for the class!! She brings workbooks every class which contain everything that's on the exam. The sweetest and most caring professor I took at UF.

I had professor Gamage last semester for MAC2311, and signed up for her MAC2312 course this semester, because she's simply that great. She hands out several packets weekly which contain EVERYTHING you need to know, and will not continue class without clearing up any miscommunications or confusion. The exams are very class-related (no curveballs).

Let me tell YOU about the goat Professor Gamage.  I took her last semester with calc 1 and she was genuinely one of the best professors I have EVER had. She hands out packets with literally everything you need to know on them, you do not need to print out ANYTHING or buy any books at all. I'm taking her for Calc 2 now, literally love her. GOAT.

Prof. Gamage is extremely kind, I'd recommend her to anyone looking to take this course. 

This course is difficult, but that's the fault of UF coursework rather than her. Gamage puts a ton of effort into teaching and creates a workbook with relevant material for everyone each class. She puts a TON of effort into teaching. 

I recommend her!!

Her classes consisted of quickly covering topics in a packet she gives out followed by practice problems and individual problems where she will walk around and help out. Its helpful to watch the lecture videos before class but not entirely necessary as she does a good job of explaining. Her teaching style made it super easy to succeed.

printed out all the lecture material for us ahead of time, making taking the class super easy. if you are struggling i highly recommend using Study Edge as a supplement . although i got a c+ in the class, I account it to this being my first ever experience with calc as i did not come in taking any ap or aice classes in it before.
Amazing professor

Took her for a flipped MAC2311 course and she provided packets for each unit that directly relate to the exams. She reviews all the material in class. TA was not helpful and he made it more confusing but overall a good class

For this course she goes on tangents and inserts herself and her experiences in every situation even when it doesn't apply. Her criteria for the core questions makes zero sense. Gives grade deductions for work being "too clean." Refuses to acknowledge actual world events in ethical discussion.
Take the online version. She doesn't actually teach she just goes on tangents in class and never stays on topic. Class is a waste of time but attendance is mandatory.

Professor Morton was a really great professor for this course. She really took her time to explain things and made Zoom University a little more enjoyable. Her quizzes and exams are a little annoying just because the class is mostly discussion based but just try your best and you should be fine!

Dr. Morton is one of the most incredibly professors the university has. If you ever have the opportunity to take ANYTHING with her, do it. Just completely full send it. She teaches in a way that inspires and really cares about all her students. A true wonder woman- 10/10.

Dr. Morton is the type of teacher who tells you one thing is the correct answer for a test, then makes it incorrect. Her teaching is inconsistent, her answers are relative from person to person, and she gets upset when you question her in any form. Find another teacher if you can, she doesn't do you any favors.

I'm so glad I chose Dr. Morton for strategy! She does her best to keep lectures interesting by being animated and using current campaigns to help teach the material. There is a lot of group work, but that's normal for this major. Dr. Morton was an excellent professor and a very caring person who wants the best for her students. Highly recommend.
Shes a great professor! She teachs you how to start talking and thinking in a professional way. 100% recommended.
Fun class but you have to pay attention and do well on the projects. No tests.
She is great! She is so fun, and she gives good grades.  I have learned a lot from her class.

"Difficult," in every sense of the word. Grades very thoroughly, but to the point of being overly critical. She is also very helpful, but ONLY in one-on-one setting. She will review your work, but will not tell you everything she doesn't like, then mark it off for the grade. Notorious for not giving straight answers; won't allow laptops in class.

Try to stay on her good side. She definetly shows favoritism and you'll know if she doesn't like you. She beats around the bush with instructions for all the assignments and answering questions. She teaches the majority of the material after the assignment or deadline is due. She's very sarcastic and tries to be funny, but she's not.
Great teacher.  Very informative.  You will learn a lot, but you must do the work.  Dr. Morton is top notch.
She's a nice lady, but very vague when answering questions. Not an overly hard class, just do exactly what she wants you to do...as vague as it may be.

She is really nice and kinda reminded me of Oprah.  She has real world experience but is sort of ambiguous in answering questions.  On quizes she will give you two correct answers if you prove one may be right.  The problem is she doesnt go over her tests in class so you have no way of proving your answer was right.  tests are definetly tricky.
If you want to get the best out of UF's Advertising Dept., take a class with Morton. She knows her s***, and you'll thank her later for the hard work you'll put into the course.

I have had Morton for three classes, ADV3000, ADV3001, and ADV3203.  She is who you want if you really want to learn and produce something.  That being said, you will have to work for it.  The thing that I love about her classes is that she does as much work as she expects you to do.  She is a very through grader and is always around to ask for hel

morton is tricky...which means that sometimes she doesn't know what she is talking about...but she is goin to do the best she can to clarfify course material. exam 1 is the easist, while the rest have some trick questions, that if quickly read leads you to the wrong answer...take your time and you will get an A.

She is pretty funny although has her quirks (she won't talk to anyone before class) Tests are OK but can trip you up if you don't know your stuff (not the easiest but not the hardest by any means). Overall an easy class though.. (though, boring). If you need an elective that is 3000 or up this is a pretty good choice.

I thought she was pretty cool in the begining.   Tells some jokes, the material didn't seem too hard..but by the end..god it was so boring.  She gives a lot of extra credit.and she seems all nice, but was kind of **** when I had to makeup a test due to a car accident.  She's a little fake, but it wasn't a bad class..I learned a little.

she's alright. energetic and really nice, but she never really gives a straight answer. she says SOMETHING that sounds like she knows what she's talking about, but it doesn't answer your question.  other than that, the class is pretty painless.
I thought she was so funny! I really liked the material too.
its boring

If you want to learn, take another teacher. She doesn't seem to have alot of knowledge about this class. I'd ask her questions & it seemed like she made up the answers or if its on the book she'd have to look it up. The class isn't hard, I'll probably get an A, but taking this class makes me want to change my major which makes me sad.
Nice teacher, she's funny and gives alot of examples, gives extra credit, if I had bought the book for the class I woulda got an A.

It honestly feels like the structure of this course is designed to hurt GPAs or push students to drop. I do not understand how this is allowed at a school like University of Florida. 0 out of 10. Do not recommend. Avoid this class and this professor if you have any choice. If getting an A or B matters to you, this is not a class you should take.

DO THE COURSE EVALS. Extra credit is only useful up to a C. Get ready to study for several hours a day, especially for the first exam. Second exam is easiest. Hardest class I've done.

I'm sorry, good luck

Study Edge is a must. Get any ACPs you can. He cares about students but sticks to the rules no matter what. Very Gen-X in approach. Attend class or watch the recordings. The material is tough, but he ensures the grade is earned, not easily given. Protects the value of our degrees.

reviews.comment: listen this class is hard, it is so gd hard!! but Banko is a really caring professor. Show up to lectures, and buckle in!
Consistently study and ensure you are comfortable in excel, and you'll do fine.

reviews.comment: In order to succeed, especially accounting majors, DO STUDY EDGE! Review the mini videos given along with the quiz answer keys and exam reviews. reviews.comment: its not that bad. he only uses excel now, so its easier for exam 1! do the study edge mocks, his review & real deal, and each module/chapter review packets. review review review and review some more. study edge sucks at the final topic imo (M&M world & redoing MVE/stock prices) - his explanation is better tbh! you got this!

UF should be ashamed of how this class is ran.

Not nearly as bad as people say. Use the resources on Canvas to learn and practice the material. If you put in the time and effort to learn the material you will do well. Be prepared to have no life and GET STUDY EDGE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

This class is really really hard, he just made the class completely excel based so no calculators on exams. If your not a finance major, just take the C and move on with your life, its not worth putting hours and hours into this class. If you want the B though, you need to work your ass off

The fear of this class is overrated if you're not a finance major. Yes it is time consuming but if you use his content and use study edge and do all of the assignments you'll be okay. Just take the D or C and stay focused on your other classes because it's easy to get caught up in this class.
Do you think God stays in heaven because he, too, lives in fear of what he's created here on earth?

I needed study edge to teach me the material for this class because he didn't. I had to watch the recording of lectures, as there are over 1400 students enrolled in this course and the lectures are in a maybe 50 person sized classroom. Lectures were also mostly problem solving as the slideshows were prerecorded from Covid and horribly out of date.
Not too bad, I hear a lot of people think this class is hard, I just skimmed the lectures and got high 90s on all exams. Mostly just common sense if you are a finance bro

This class is known to be super hard and it is. However, I would not attribute it to the way Dr. Banko teaches, all exams have at least 3-4 questions that resemble his lectures and the TA's do a great job at preparing you for success. I didn't use Study Edge, I tried, but it was confusing and easier than exams. Med-Hard course but I learned A LOT!

This was last class to graduate - by far the worst teacher I've ever had. Insanely smart however he purposefully makes this class as difficult as possible for no reason besides weeding out finance majors. He doesn't teach much of anything.

Imagine dedicating 200 hours for a D because of how hard the material is. Thank the stars for study edge.

reviews.comment: Put in the bare minimum amount of effort and barely scraped by with a D, thank God for extra credit. If you are not finance/do not enjoy finance this class will make your head hurt, and if you are you will have to grind like hell for a B. Awful experience, thank God it's over.

reviews.comment: get the study edge and actually put the work in. Banko is actually a good person and he's willing to help his students when possible. reach out. test 1 is the hardest and it's very important. study hard for it. test two is much easier and test 3 is even easier. it seems super intimidating at first but if you just put the work in ur fine.

This class was unreasonably difficult for an intro to finance course. You need to be doing study edge as soon as it comes out and do every. single. problem. at the end of the packet. This course is ridiculous and you need to deticate your life to it to do well. These comments are not exaggerating.

As a finance major you need to be ready to put in the work, and accept the fact that even doing that you may still not get what you wanted. Just keep doing problems and get study edge for extra practice. How you do on exams 1 and 3 depends highly on his mood since some of the twists he puts may make or brake your grade.

This class is absolutely beyond what should be expected at undergraduate level. Be prepared to memorize 100s of formula variations & ratios and how they interplay with each other. Exams are taken with zero formula sheets and are purposely designed to trip you up. I do work full time but even if I didn't this class would be a NIGHTMARE.

I am a Student in his Fin4128 Financial Plan Development class.

reviews.comment: if you werent religious before, pick a religion and start praying because this class will have you begging every god known to man. just yesterday i found myself praying to God, Buddha, Jesus, AND Allah for mercy because of this class. i lost two dear friends of mine this semester because i kept turning them down to study for this class.
Legendary professor. Very knowledgeable. Class gets a bad rap but only because there is a lot of content. Put the time in and you'll be fine. Wish I could take him for more classes.

People tend to overhype how hard Bifi is, in reality yeah it sucks but def manageable. I think getting a C is definitely really attainable, getting B's and A's requires lots of studying and id say anywhere from 12-20 hours outside of class a week working on the content. you guys need to chill. this class is not the bane of your existence, just do study edge and learn how to manage your time. i could have easily passed with an a or maybe a+ if i devoted an organized two hours a day

Professor Banko is by far one of the worst professors I have ever encountered.

reviews.comment: I'm re-reading the reviews of Banko and this class for laughs currently. AWFUL AWFUL AWFUL. Avoid if you can, do Study Edge otherwise.

i simply cannot put into words how much this classed pissed me off. i am a comp sci student and this class was harder than some of my higher level comp sci classes. i put my all into this class and barely got a C+. so upsetting.

Memorize the Desai end of chapter questions, they are the 'conceptual' questions on the exam. DO STUDY EDGE AND BANKO'S PRACTICE EXAMS. Exam 2 is easy, 1 is a bit difficult, but 3 ipo was the worst. Plus he just started doing exam 3 using excel no calculator so study extra hard. An A is doable but you have to dedicate 90% of your time to this class

Way too much to do for intro class... Weekly quiz, weekly discussion and response, two big projects and a final exam. Most of us still get an A but I read online that you should get A just for logging in and doing the syllabus quiz and nothing else. It's not that easy.

Easy A if you follow all the instructions and submit assignments on time. If you don't, you might be in slight trouble. I think almost everyone will get an A with the extra credit 10 points at the end of the semester.
It's okay. I didn't get inspired or irritated. Just did this class and will probably get an A.

premed senior here and I need all As. I took this class thinking it's an easy A. Very strict grading I had to spend a few hours every week. it impacted my grades in this class and other class. About 40% of grade is after withdraw deadline. Not sure if I will get A or A-

He is alright. I saw reddit and other places this class was a pushover but not really. You gotta do everything on time to get full points - possible but annoying. Didn't interact much but some students are angry for some reason. Not that serious. Not that bad. It's just a class lmao
Wasn't the easiest course. But wasn't too bad.

So many problems and glitches but swift response to emails and questions. Read everything he sends..he sends lots to read. New videos will help the course. Don't take this thinking too easy. Easy but not too easy.
The class was okay. Many improvements needed and the professor said he will do it next time. It didn't help me this time. Seems like there is a transition of teachers. Very average.

So I went into this course not really knowing what to expect but it honestly turned out way better than I thought. The instructor takes time to make sure you understand the material and the grading is fair, nothing comes out of nowhere. Me and my friends all felt the same way about it. Would recomend, easily one of the better courses I've taken.

Agree with most people on here that he's a pretty tough grader, but the grading was fair in my opinion. Pretty interesting course and communication was way better than other professors I've had in the past since there were regular announcements and he was quick to respond to emails and had regular (online) office hours

he sends lots of announcements and can be confusing. I reached out via email several times and he was helpful. but  he also gives bonus points at the end for participating. hopefully my grade gets rounded up. he also gave me some exception when asked otherwise strict with deadlines

reviews.comment: Vague rubrics for assignments, with harsh grading. Old lecture videos that didn't answer all the quiz or discussion questions. Poor communication of expectations.
Jus wanna give good rating since few people in class chat groups hate this guy for no reason. He is alright. Slow and tough grading though.
Tough grader but he once explained answers in detail when I emailed him.

If you expect to do nothing and get an A. This isn't the place for you! If you put in the work, I think Dr. Haarith was fair in grades and had clear expectations. He responded to emails and was available for office hours. This was a great course!

I heard this course was an easy A. This new professor doesn't think it should be. There are so many deadlines to get through. He is very strict and expects you to submit everything on time. He sends many announcements, but gets irritated sometimes and asks you to read the syllabus again.Not sure why he doesnt use his own videos

Grading can be very harsh, and guidelines are unclear. Lectures were all recorded by a different instructor, and they are extremely difficult to follow. The lowest few quiz and discussion grades are dropped to help you out, but considering the big projects receive heavy criticism, this doesn't do very much to balance out your overall grade.

Lectures were pre-recorded by a different professor before COVID and were unrelated to the quizzes or discussions. Project grades are released late and with no feedback or indication on the rubric. Class could be interesting with an engaged professor, but Dr. Haarith was uninvolved in any lectures or assignments.

Very tough grader, lectures are vague and difficult to understand. There are also few assignments, making it difficult to recover. Weekly quizzes and discussion posts, with two major projects, also graded incredibly harsh.

The discussion posts are more harshly graded than other courses so make sure to actually put some effort into them. Some quiz questions aren't specifically covered in the lecture. The lectures can be very confusing. If you're like me you'll be googling different words every 5 seconds. With some effort though you can get an A.

Contrary to “popular” opinion, Dr. Deardorff is not an adequate instructor. His pretentious teaching style erodes individual thinking, and any opinion he disagrees with is labeled as lunacy, making him very dislikable. His  course workload is not bad, but I think a different professor would have made the class more enjoyable.

Professor is very nice and passionate about teaching. I think overall grade is determined mainly by what TA you have, but the class was fairly easy aside from the final. Deardorff gives great feedback though.

Insane amount of reading. We had to buy 3 books in addition to readings on canvas. I took it over summer and sometimes had 60+ pages of reading required in one night. Tons of content. reviews.comment: he is very passionate and knowledgeable in lectures! always helpful when answering questions too. the discussion sections were fun but participation is graded kinda harshly. just contribute everyday and you'll be fine. lots of readings that i stopped doing by the end of the course. study guides for midterms and finals that match them exactly!

reviews.comment: Colonial Latin America is a great general course for people who want to learn about the Atlantic World from 1450-1750! reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed taking Professor Deardoff's class in Colonial Latin America. There are weekly readings with discussions, which aren't detrimental to your grade. Professor Deardorff was amazing! This class was the first Ive ever taken with him, and I was very surprised by how interesting the course was and how nice Deardorff is. reviews.comment: Dr. Deardorff is the man! Idk about non-history IDS classes but as a History professor he is the cream of the top! He is just a cool guy and super understanding. Inquisition Research Seminar. Dr. Deardorff is an excellent teacher. An expert in the subject matter and passionate about what he does, and he cares a great deal about his students. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

Professor Deardorff loves his craft. To any student who shows even a little interest, he makes sure that they are where they need to be in class as in a very chill guy. Although Dr. Deardorff was a very pleasant and agreeable man, the class was so intense that my TA thought that Quest courses were supposed to be one of the hardest levels of courses available. DO. NOT. TAKE. PIRATES AND POWER. This is the worst possible quest course! I have to drop it and it absolutely destroyed my GPA. The TAs were harsh for no reason. reviews.comment: Prof. Deardroff is a super nice guy! The lectures drag on and can get a little exhausting, but they're still really informative and interesting. Amazing, knowledgeable professor. He expects a lot from his students but he guides them and helps you along the way. Very accessible and interesting lectures.

One of my favorite profs this semester. I came out of this class with a good understanding of a topic I previously had no knowledge of. He's such a great guy and loovees lecturing (I'm pretty sure if he could talk about Latin America and Spanish history for 6 hours straight he would.) Awesome Professor, really relaxed. Doesnt really respond to email so its better to go to office hours for any questions. Gives extra credit and exams are open note. Do the work, get an A.

O'Neill is absolutely fantastic. He is knowledgeable, a great lecturer, and clearly passionate about the subject. That being said, he makes it exceedingly clear that if you do not do the readings, you will not get an A. However, the readings are the only thing expected from you and he breaks them down wonderfully in lecture. Highly recommend!

The GOAT!!! O'Neill is one of the best professors at UF. You will def need to work for your A (do ALL the readings, take good lecture notes, and use your office hours!), but O'Neill's iconic lectures and clear passion for political theory will also def inspire the same in you. Prof O'neill is such an amazing professor. He clearly loves and understands the topics presented which makes the lectures super engaging. Grades are weekly discussion attendance,  3 exams, and weekly paragraph reading responses. I highly recommend Billsborough as a TA!

He is so smart and loves what he teaches. As long as you attend class, take notes, and study, you'll do well in the class. Three written exams, super straight-forward and easy to ace. Timmy Stolz is the best TA and is always willing to help answer any questions.

Dr. O'Neill is an amazing lecturer and I highly recommend you take him for an intro level class. His lectures are extremely engaging and although attendance is not mandatory, I recommend going. I don't think its necessary to purchase the textbook to succeed as his lectures pretty much cover all the material you need to know for his exams.
very passionate about political theory and overall engaging lectures. most of your grade consists of 3 written exams throughout the semester and depending on your TA they can be graded quite harshly.

reviews.comment: You can tell the professor enjoys the subject, and not only engages with the material very well, but also with the students. His lectures were very engaging, and he explained the material very well, if you have the option to take his class, please do! You won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Essay driven and your grade is pretty dependent on your TA. I had Timothy and he was the GOAT. O'Neill is poli sci royalty and it definitely shows in his entertaining lectures.

Daniel does a great job at making the political theorists studied interesting and engaging. What TA you get does make or break your grade, as they are the ones that actually grade the papers worth almost your entire grade. I had Timothy Stoltz who was hilarious but a bit strict on grading unless you visit him for office hours.

Your TA will make or break this class (avoid Wallie). Only graded by a few papers and two in-class tests, but all tests are essays, and you can bring a page of notes. Very lecture-heavy. No required attendance, but his lectures give you all the information. Don't bother reading, you can rely on his slides. Really interesting and engaging lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer, engaging and funny. Doesn't waste your time. Presents content in an unbiased and knowledgeable (yet approachable) manner. Lecture notes are stellar at guiding you through long, often dense readings, but he doesn't post them online. 4 papers, 5-7 pages, a week to write them, all graded by TAs. Get Timmy Stolz if you can.

O'Neill was great at breaking down the important concepts and even gave us page #s for textual evidence to write the papers. He's charismatic during lectures and gives you exactly what you need to know--enough so that I didn't do any readings. Grade is heavily based on TA. Paper questions are clear and concise. Take good notes and you'll be fine!

Dr. O'Neill was a gold tier prof. He took complicated material and made it easy and fun. The papers were easy as long as you went to lectures and read. He also remained neutral the whole time, which is so hard but he handled it perfectly. My TA Tim was great and was a big help. I'll be taking POT4053 with O'Neill next semester, super excited!

Interesting lectures by prof made boring material interesting, but entire grade rides on the TA. Mine was incredibly unclear during discussion, gave vague feedback, wasn't helpful when asked questions to improve, and was a really harsh grader (barely gave out As, RIP to you if Wallie is ever a TA again), but others had fair TAs and did well.

reviews.comment: Prof. O'Neill makes the lectures very interesting, however books are needed, there is a lot of reading/research, and 4 papers are the only assignments. Prof is funny, and manages to make confusing political philosophy clear and interesting. Grade does depend on the TA and they all look for different things - plus some are tough graders. reviews.comment: Loved O'Neill's lectures he did a pretty good job at explaining things. His act where you don't know what political opinion he is is also pretty entertaining as well.

A great professor. You never know what his personal beliefs are and he does a great job explaining the material when it gets hard. POT2002 is 100% essay based and the discussion sections are very helpful if you get a good TA. I recommend Walker if he is available

Overall Prof O'Neill was a great lecturer and made the readings easier to understand. But if you want to do well, make sure you meet with your TA to make sure you know what they are looking for when it comes to papers.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor O'Neill is a great lecturer and makes understanding and breaking down the readings super manageable. The TA's in the class are honestly what your grade comes down to though. I think Murad and Glen are the most reasonable graders from what I've heard.
ONeil is a great lecturer! I took this class online and still loved it

reviews.comment: He is an excellent lecturer who has a true passion for political theory. However, the TA's are key. I got a C on my first paper but once I went to office hours I got my grade down to a B because they helped me a ton.

Professor O'Neill's class is challenging and your grade will heavily depend on the TA you are assigned. My advice: begin your outline/papers early (you receive the paper topics in advance), visit your TA's office hours often, pre-write your exam essays EARLY (ques. also given in advance), and I suggest creating a study group to survive together.

reviews.comment: Enthusiastic, knowledgeable and funny, Professor O'Neill is a great guy and lecturer. There is a lot of reading to do (6 books) but his lectures help you understand it so much better. Love that he doesn't use Canvas. Papers are just you and the book, no outside resources, so do read. He gives you the midterm q's to plan ahead. Learned a lot.
Loves to hear his own voice. Bring earbuds and read on your own.

Professor O'Neill is one of those admirable professors that actually loves what he does. He gets super into his lectures and is out of this world knowledgable on the topic. reviews.comment: He's incredibly passionate about Political Science. He really makes you feel good about asking questions. If you prove that you read by asking specific questions, he'll openly admire you in class. He's deep, philosophical, quirky, funny, and really personable.

Dr. O'Neill is one of the best, if not THE best professor I have ever had. He cares so deeply about Political Theory, and he lectures in such a manner that is reflective of his love for the subject. I left this class with a massive knowledge base--and I absolutely loved every second of this class. Get ready to read, but it is so worth it.
Professor O'Neil is clearly passionate about what he teaches and wants his students to get enjoyment out of the class. You'll leave his class wishing he was your cool uncle.
Super interesting to listen to, he keeps things fun and upbeat. I would definitely take another class with him.

O' Neill is by far the EASIEST Good Life professor. He told us what to focus on for the midterm and final exam (definitely made studying A LOT easier). Although the material is all over the place and for the philosophically minded, O'Neill has a subtle sense of humor that makes lecture more enjoyable. Take good notes and READ, quiz questions are more or less directly from material and their lectures.
Usually very clear.  Needs to use a mic though.  Interesting material for the most part but way too many reading and BS assignments.  Be consistent with doing work and reading and you should be fine.

Phenomenal teacher. Energetic, enthused, and all around best professor I have ever had. Hilarious. Loves his topic and students. I imagine the history of grass growth would be fascinating under his tutelage. Take at least one class by him before you graduate.

Dan O'Nel is the best lecturer I've ever had.  He is clear and concise, and helps you to understand the works of some very tough authors.  If you have any interest in politics or philosophy, I highly recommend this class for you.

DAN THE MAN. God I loved this professor. He literally made me obsessed with Political Theory. He's an intelligent man. TAKE HIM.

Dan O'Neill.  I love Dan!  You can't get any better than Dan!  I'm about to finish my PhD and in all my years in school I have never looked forward to, enjoyed, or learned from a class the way I did in Dan's.  Without a doubt, Dan's the best.

I have abosolutely no interest in Political Theory but he managed to make this tedious and boring topic somewhat interesting. O'Neill is the BEST poli sci prof that I've had at UF. It's a fast paced class, and if you don't like writing you'll hate the course. However, it is extremely interesting and O'Neill is engaging and downright hilarious.
He's hilarious

Professor O'Neill is the best professor I have ever had in college. Turns a somewhat boring subject into an exciting one. Looked forward to going to his class every day, and learned a lot. Do the readings and go to section if not the lectures. HIGHLY recommended.

O'Neill is very enthusiastic about this subject and it comes across in his lectures. His jumping around keeps you awake. He cites the texts in lecture and those quotes are very helpful when it comes to writing the essays. Gives you paper topics beforehand

Great professor.  Engages the class and makes the material interesting.

Hist. of Am Pol Thought. Awesome class taught by an interesting professor. You must read the text to understand and get involved in discussions. Don't be afraid to speak what you think and give your point of view even if its different. He likes to question and pick on your mind to make you think. Overall great professor and class. Highly recommend.
Dr. O'Neill is brilliant.  He engages the class and brings dusty old texts to life.  History of American Political Thought was really interesting.

O'Neill is by far the most engaging and helpful professor I've had at UF. Though the reading might not always be simple, after going to class you WILL understand the material. He makes political theory incredibly interesting to learn, and applies the things he teaches to practical examples in government and society. He has a great sense of humor!

Best professor ever. I changed my major to political science because he was so interesting and fun to learn from. Hilarious. Hopped up on diet coke. He follows his outlines precisely- TAKE NOTES. Such a nice guy, too. I cannot WAIT to take more of his classes.

O'Neill was one of the best poli sci professors I've had. His lectures break down complex material into understandable theories. Extremely helpful in office hours. Was willing to just sit there and talk out the material. Overall, if you write well and go to class you should get an A. Two papers and a final. Great guy!

I have had 2 classes with O'Neill. He is exciting and really into what he's teaching. He doesn't seem to have much of an ego that some profs has. POT2002 was easy, his other class wasn't. If he grades the papers personally, it is a lot tougher and the reading is more "mandatory". He has common sense and doesn't take himself too seriously. Nice guy.
make sure you take real good notes. he knows his material
I liked him alot. if you come to class, you can write the papers and the tests without worry. He explains everything you need to know.

Professor O'Neill was the most animated professor I have had at UF. His enthusiasm is contagious; people listened intently to his lectures early in the morning. Two essays were required (graded by TAs). The rest of the grade was determined by a mid-term, a final, and section participation. If you have the opportunity to take this class, do it!

His lectures were very informative and even if you miss a day of reading, or dont understand what you read, his lectures clear everything up.  His ability to make the concepts relatable is amazing and very helpful. To any poli sci undergrad, take this class!
Great class!  O'Neill is a really good professor and knows how to communicate the material in an interesting and unbiased way.  One of my favorite courses at UF.  A lot of reading though.
Hated the class. Opinion of him is slightly better. Seems better if you don't cross him. Make your life easier and just agree, at least until grades come out.

Professor O'Neill is a great teacher. He brings the subject material to life with his energy for the subject and his occasional jokes. Energetic, helpful, really encourages participation.

A great professor.  The class isn't easy, but it's not hard.  You just have to be there every day, read the material, and listen to him.  He'll tell you exactly what you need to do for papers and tests.  He's hilarious and really knows how to keep you interested.  Only negative is that his writing is terrible and drawings often don't make sense.

Professor O'Neill is incredible. I just completed summer b as a freshman and I could not have asked for a better classroom experience. O'Neill is engaging, witty, and extremely well informed of the material he teaches. Lots of reading, takes notes in class everyday, go to his office hours if he assigns a paper, and you should be alright.

this guy is amazing. as an incoming freshmen, i feel uber fortunate to have this guy so soon! i definitely thought UF kept their good teachers under lock and key, but definitely not o'neill.  this guy does not hold back and that's what political theory is about. and get ready to read!

This man was amazing. He is able to engage you in learning. The TAs he chooses want to help you learn and are always there to guide you. I suggest going to class, listening, writing down pages numbers and talking to O'Neill and your TA. Plus, he's freaking hysterical!!!

There are those really rare, great professors who have the charisma and personality to teach, in addition to being articulate and knowing their subject area to a fault. O'Neill is one of these professors. He's pretty much my hero.
HIS CLASS IS AMAZING, take it! lectures were a complete and total joy, he makes arduous political theory texts really come to life. I LOVE DAN O'NEIL!
amazing! take this class!
If you're not in love with this guy by the second week of class, you might want to check your pulse.
He is very knowledgeable however very hard and teaches his Intro classes at a much higher level. His lectures can sometimes be very boring... you MUST do his assigned reading, do not blow it off!

Dan is by far the best professor I've had at UF.  He is extremely knowledgeable, funny, and interested in what you have to say.  GET TO KNOW HIM.  I also found the readings extremely versatile so it encompasses differing views.  Great class.  I learned a lot and am a better student after taking his class.  But make sure you read and take notes!

GREAT PROFESSOR!!! Best i have had so far. He is extremely insightful, you can go to office hours whenever you wnat and he'll stay there til whenever to help you. He has somewhat high standards but if you just re-write your notes you'll get an A. It's theory so just go to class everyday, write down pg. numbers, and try to read to books. LOVE HIM!!!

go to class (you cant skip this one!), write down EVERYTHING he says (page numbers specifically) and you won't have to read the books, tough grading (just write everything you have on essays and tests) but funny and entertaining! really likeable. would take another class with him.
this guy is freaking awesome. he's incredibly wise and really funny. an amazing professor. the essays are difficult, but just keep up with the reading and ask your ta's questions.

he's awesome. he makes you want to come to class. in lecture he covers and explains the material very well while keeping you interested. he is extremely funny and animated. i would definitely reccommend this class, even though it is an intro class you have to be ready to work!

Great professor!  The subject material and the subsequent essays are challenging, but class and lecture are very much enjoyable.  I highly, highly recommend.

O'Neill is not easy, but his course is tremendously rewarding.  I have learned so much this semester!  He is very enthusiastic with the material, which makes you want to come to class and learn.  Excellent professor!

Dr. MacDonald is amazing! Conduct of Inquiry is a tough intro to grad school heavy on theory and method but he truly cares. Super available, gives thoughtful feedback, and wants you to succeed. Easiest grader I have met at UF, and even his hard end-of-semester assignments are graded with understanding/good communication. VERY easy to talk to in Office Hours and find what he wants.

David as a lecturer was OK. The content is not particularly engaging but the class is an easy A for those with poli sci tracks. Tests are a little oddly worded but he usually curves by a question or two to reflect that.

Honestly, none of us knew our grades in the class until quite literally the last day to turn grades in. The TAs were lost too. Barely any prep for the exams. The homeworks did not help at all. The only thing that helped was Kim Brehm on YT. beware!!

reviews.comment: The project, divided into several parts, is the bulk of your work for this class, and until you don't wait until the last minute to start working on it, you should be fine. Sometimes, the lectures aren't super helpful for the programming project, but still useful for the quizzes, which are not much to worry about.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is very hard to study for, i felt like i knew the content good and still was unprepared for every exam (no previous ones to view). He also never responded to my email about seeing my exam answers and waited until the last day to release exam 4(so that no one could dispute...). If you're good at discrete he's fine but i lost my 4.0 here

Honestly, Peter Dobbins is incredibly knowledgeable about Discrete Mathematics, but he's not a good professor. The grading criteria was unclear without knowing my grade the entire semester, not have enough resources to study adequately for the exams, and the lectures provided are usually not the best for learning the material. I wouldn't bother.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are good. Quizzes are kinda annoying. The programming project can take a while but if you start early you should be fine. I just wish the lectures had a bit more connection to the programming project.

Everyone complaining probably waited last minute and didn't bother looking at the linked textbook once. Dobbins taught this class clearly and is an awesome guy, at the end of lectures he sometimes talks about his dog or daughter like a friend to a friend. Follow the linked textbook sections, watch lectures for the specifics and you'll be just fine.

* Unorganized course
* tests two weeks apart
* Pre-Lectures are more useful than actual lectures
* Programming 2 with this class can be very difficult, due dates for prog almost ALWAYS overlapped with tests.
* Study guide for each test (w/ answer key)

Very disorganized lectures that are difficult to follow. His handwriting is terrible as others have mentioned. Homework and lecture problems are not good preparation for the exams. I did well, but taught myself pretty much everything through youtube and the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are disorganized and unhelpful, with sloppy/unclear work. You are not adequately prepared for exams at all. Lectures don't help and the study materials do not prepare you well at all. I learned the whole course through youtube.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is disorganized. Professor is not accessible outside of classroom. Office Hours accessibility is just as tight. Dr. Dobbins speaks in run on sentences with few pauses. Difficult to understand and follow. Instructions intentionally very vague. Vagueness is not a problem if adequate help can be received. However, that is not the case.

His lectures were hard for me to follow and understand. He talks very fast, has messy, unorganized handwriting, and gets off-topic sometimes. Concepts were hard and took a lot of practicing to truly understand it. Exams have written portions and more complexity than just multiple choice. I got really bad exam grades but still ended with a B though.

Took him last year, and he is a good guy but isn't the best for lectures. He sometimes went off topic and wouldn't focus on having a clear explanation. I understood alot more from self teaching. BUT he was super good during his OH cuz no one attended them. His exams are alright, not that difficult is you clearly know the information.

Terribly disorganized class. Exams are 70% of your grade (of which is locked so you're unable to tell what you have in the class until the end of the semester), and next to no preparation is provided. Lectures are ultimately useless as well, and examples for problems are practically unexplained, forcing you to work backwards from the answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dobbins's COT3100 class is highly challenging due to disorganization. Confusing and overly long lectures, absent professor, and minimal exam prep make it frustrating. Lack of a course calendar and practice exams adds to the difficulty. Resorting to YouTube or online resources for clarity is common. Would not take this class with Dobbins again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
- Class is extremely unorganized
- Lectures are useless
- Your grade hinges on exams

DONT TAKE THIS CLASS,very disorganized test heavy,70% of grade was exams which there were no previous exams to study. Also, no clue how the exam was formatted, he was trying to be mysterious or something.Lectures are pretty much useless,uses flipped format for teaching.The lessons don't reflect the level of difficulty, he doesn't go over examples.

The class is somewhat unorganized but you will learn a lot that will help you in future CS courses. Exams are tough, but practice exams are usually tougher. Not a class you can slack off in, but simply doing your work is enough to make you pass.

Lectures were really good bedtime stories. I legitimately fell asleep every single lecture I went to, and it might not be his fault because the content just feels so boring and useless. Sometimes the more he explained the more confused I got. I would say the class's content isn't exactly "hard," it's just weird and strangely structured.

He is a terrible lecturer, but likeable otherwise (he's nice but can't teach). Look at the powerpoints because there are things mentioned there and not in the book. Watch Kimberly Brehm's videos. Attend discussion and the test review by the TAs. IMO tests weren't that bad. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it will give you extra credit!

DSA with Prof. Dobbins was one of my better experiences in CISE. The key to success in his class is taking good notes of his lectures + pre-lectures (which are both recorded) so you can make a good reference sheet for his exams, which often have extra credit. HW and readings never take more than an hour max. Would take Dobbins again in a heartbeat

Dobbins was one of the worst profs I have ever had. Class is very exam heavy, but he doesn't tell you the layout of exams or give practice exams, just review questions which typically do not help. On top of that, he is not a strong lecturer, so I found myself turning to Kimberly Brehm on Youtube to teach me everything. Take a dif prof in a dif sem

Dobbins has great material to use for the class (lecture videos and the text book). His lectures however were confusing and hard to follow along. My recommendation would be to watch the lecture videos, do the RE and the HWs, and go to office hours. Attendance was mandatory but was recorded through zoom so there was no need to go in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture attendance is mandatory. Lectures are confusing, handwriting is messy, and don't teach all content thats on the exams, so read textbook if you want to be prepared for them. most of grade is from 4 exams and attendance.

Dobbins lectures aren't particularly good. I learned the entire course through the textbook and youtube videos. With that being said, the homework is easy and the exams are relatively fair. As long as you study a decent amount the class isn't too bad.

Professor Dobbins was one of the best teachers I've had at UF. Very clear grading rubric, but to be honest, his in-person lectures are not very helpful. However, this is massively made up by his great pre-lectures that cover everything. Just go over your notes from pre-lecture and do the practice exams and you'll be fine.

Professor Dobbins is very smart but his lectures were almost always confusing and I struggled to grasp the concepts. Thankfully, this class is easy to pass with high marks thanks to the TAs and Kimberly Brehm's Discrete Mathematics playlist on YouTube. Physical attendance was not mandatory; you only needed to join his Zoom meeting for credit.

Class itself is not hard, had four exams but if you just either read the book or study well they are extremely easy. Dobbins lectures are him speaking like he is trying to meet a word count for an essay, but logging into the zoom earns you extra credit. TA's are awesome and crucial to success. Kimberly Brehm on YouTube is key, you are welcome.

Don't attend lectures for this class. I attended all lectures in person (I'm a Doblin), and only paid half attention because his lectures actively made me understand the material less sometimes. The course content itself isn't inherently difficult, but his explanations are so confusing that the course seems very hard. The tests were fair though.

Dobbins is a very knowledgeable professor but he makes this class extremely boring.The lectures(which are a extra credit grade) are useless and consist of him rambling on some random stuff most of the time. The exams arent necessarily hard just require a lot of studying so don't take him with an already heavy course load. If you can take other prof

Dobbins is admittedly a nice person, but his lectures are difficult to follow and rather useless. He spends lots of time talking about things unrelated to the course material, which itself is already hard to understand. You're better off skipping lecture and relying on videos. Fortunately the tests were easier than the convoluted homework.

Class had a lot of exams, but all are very easy if you either study hard or just read the book. His lectures are extra credit if you go to them all, but just joining the zoom and doing other work fine. Lectures themselves aren't helpful since he doesn't really breakdown anything into normal people language, just watch youtube videos instead.

dobbins seemed like a nice prof but he did tend to complicate generally simply info, which was a bit frustrating for the 3 quizzes we had and the lectures were not necessary overall for the class. The main thing was a project which I overall found to be very enjoyable and well-structured (better to work with a partner and start the work in advance)
Professor Dumbbins is the worst lecturer I've had at UF. Somehow, he managed to turn an interesting class into a boring and repetitive topic. Don't take him if you prioritize learning!

Professor is very knowledgeable about the material and wants students to succeed. Altered the way material was presented based on student feedback, making it easier to follow along. All presentations and class notes were uploaded to study from, and exam reviews are made from previous exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dobbins was alright. The test are not the hardest thing in the world either, if you do the reviews he post you will be fine. The class lectures are not that helpful, the most helpful ones are the pre-recorded videos and youtube (TrevTutor & Kimberly Brehm).  You do not need to do the lecture problems at all, they take too much time, just  hw.

Dobbins was overall a really good professor. He was extremely caring and does what he can to make the average for the course relatively high. There are quite a few exams, but the exams are fair and go over the content discussed in pre-lecture videos. His main lectures can be confusing but are supplemental. Very organized class. Great experience.

He was... Rather bad. Generally avoid him, take Resch or just wait for Resch. The professor grades on participation, homework, and tests - And those tests are difficult. Very difficult and not based on his lectures.

I liked Dobbins in previous class but this class is ridiculously hard. The material is very challenging and the grading isn't clear because you're not given all the test cases. When you go to OH with him, all questions are answered with a riddle. Take with a very little class load. Says 3 credit hrs, feels like 9 credit hrs.

The class is entirely proofs and logic-based math. Many things are common sense but others are barely explained properly. Lectures, as you can tell by every other review, are utterly useless. Dobbins speaks like he's trying to teach an alien English. Tests make up a huge majority of the grade. Easy to pass but hard for an A. Class sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: worst lectures and the exams are stupid hard. When the class was fully online people 100% cheated their way through but with us who had exams in person, we were absolutely miserable. You know the class is bad when everyone's encouraged to do course evaluations to get 1% added to our final grade because anything will benefit us at this rate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class destroyed my mental health. The exams are really hard and worth most of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dobbins is a nerdy, good guy. He is very passionate but you have to study for this class. Learning this material is not easy and you got to set time for yourself to study and learn the material. This is not a class to procrastinate (unless you are a god at logic and proofs). If you are taking this class and Prog2 DONT PROCRASTINATE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dobbins' lectures make little to no sense. There are pre-recorded lectures for the main content of the class and in-person lectures for exercises. I stopped going to the in-person lectures and the pre-recorded lectures never stopped being confusing. I got an A only because I put in a ton of hours googling and figuring everything out on my own.

Dobbins is the type of god you fear rather than love. The 8 people who actually show up to lecture are called Doblins (Dobbins + goblins). I named my homemade brew after him (Dobbins juice). You need the Dobbins juice to cope with the Microsoft Word lectures. If it wasn't for Dobbins, I wouldn't know how terrible lectures could be.

All the resources offered in this course combined were probably 2% of all the material I had to review to barely pass. I relied on youtube and stack overflow for a vast majority of this course. Watching youtube videos and then attending lecture was like taking a step forward and 2 steps back. Don't go to lecture, don't take Dobbins

Imagine a bee gets in your ear - you can't tell what it's doing, you just hear a noise and know you're going to get stung. That's this class.
Dobbins is a nice guy and will help you out if you ask, but this is admittedly a tough class, and the lectures make absolutely no sense. Be prepared to work long hours and neglect all else for this class.

Very early on you'll likely realize that there is no point in attending lectures, in person or virtually. Watch the pre-lecture videos, read the textbook, search on youtube and stack overflow. Dobbins' lectures are useless for learning. Discussion sessions are more likely to be helpful, if your TA is good. Exams are most of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dobbins is the only professor I have had at UF that doesn't even do the bare minimum when teaching. All he does is poorly explain practice problems (working out the math in Microsoft word). The TAs carry this course and the exams are ridiculous.

Awful teaching. Lectures are useless and he spends most of his time talking about something else rather than the course material. Also makes things so difficult for students. No point in going to campus to take exam if it’s going to be on our laptop anyways
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I'm crying again

THE BEST! Top quality teacher. You don't find teachers like Dobbins at UF. He is just top quality. Treats you like a friend and makes the class super easy with his grading schemes and teaching pattern.
this class is 2x harder than phy2048 if you want a good comparison. exams are harshly graded and not based on stuff we learn
Worst professor I've ever had! Most students are confused and overwhelmed by the material

Hands down the worst professor I have ever had. Useless lectures, confusing material, doesn't care about students learning. I could go on and on and on. Do NOT take classes with Peter Dobbins you will in fact have weekly breakdowns
Useless lectures, material is made to confuse you, and way too much homework
