He cares about his students and is very organized, but I would recommend against taking any of his courses if possible because you will end up teaching yourself if you want to pass. Not difficult, but inconvenient

Dobbins seemed like he was yelling a lot of the time. We were in Carleton, but he had a mic on so this wasn't necessary. I personally really didn't like his teaching style. It was a flipped classroom, which was another negative for me but others may like this. Overall discrete is pretty hit-or-miss in my experience.

As I type this, a a spec for a homework is being changed about 6hrs before the due date. Every specification has been either extremely vague or poorly written. Grading is often unclear. While an interesting subject, I regret taking this course :(

Dobbins was stubborn and unprofessional in his NLP course. The spec sheets for assignments were extremely unclear and Dobbins was unwilling to improve them and take any feedback. The exams were disorganized and a technical nightmare which he acknowledges but refuses to take action on. On teams chat, questions were ignored & responses were unclear.

You can learn everything in this class by going through the free nltk book yourself in a couple weeks. The hw specifications are generally poorly written, and exam q's have included regurgitating part of the nltk api and memorizing regexes. I like dobbins as a lecturer and person, but take him for discrete/plc, both are better than this course

When I took Dr. Dobbins for CIS4930 Natural Language Processing, he was possibly one of the worst professors I have encountered at UF. Dr. Dobbins himself cannot complete the assignments assigned to the class as he cannot answer basic questions about them. There is no clear grading criteria, you kind of have to guess what the grader wants. Avoid.

Homework and Online quizzes were due weekly and very easy - unlimited trys. Lectures were almost worthless - pre-lecture videos were the actual content, actual lecture was unreadable and went over questions that hardly pertained to class. Exams were graded leniently

Professor Dobbins gave clear explanations, but his lectures were extraordinarily slow. During one of his lectures, he gave announcements for 40 minutes. I ended up just watching the lecture recording afterward at double speed.

Dobbins is the man! This class was honestly a great balance of being informative and fair, and I never really felt stressed due to the way he and the TAs worked the projects. We were given test cases to test our projects, and checkpoints where we could see how our project would be graded beforehand so we could fix it. Cool course material too!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dobbins is a pretty good prof, he is clearly very knowledgeable. His lectures are semi-useful. Best way to get better is to do all the extra assignments he gives/textbook problems/practice exams. Dobbins clearly cares and will try to help you in office hours.

reviews.comment: it was a flipped classroom in a class of several hundred students which is just foolhardy at best I stopped going to lectures and read the textbook instead which is what I recommend if it's still a flipped classroom; lectures were a waste of time

reviews.comment: I had Professor Dobbins for COT3100 and I really enjoyed his class. I think his lectures are supplemental to the textbook and I recommend reading the textbook alongside the lectures.

reviews.comment: I had Dobbins for Discrete Structures. His lectures in class were a bit hard to understand. reviews.comment: I took this professor for COP3502 which was quite a bit more messy than COT3100, so I'm writing another review because COT3100 has been a much more positive experience. While his lectures are often unnecessarily complicated, the textbook and homeworks can be used to learn, and the discussions and exam reviews really prepare for the exams.

reviews.comment: Had Prof. Dobbins for "Discrete Structures" and for "Information and Database Systems." He was very passionate, and easy to reach. Sometimes his lectures could lose focus, but overall were informative. Class attendance is optional.
Really bad. Don't expect any grades until 4 years after you've graduated.

I was in COP3502 for spring 2019 and I don't see why there is so much bashing against Dr. Dobbins. Sure, his lectures were kind of a drag and disorganized, but they weren't mandatory. You could get by using the notes he posted on the course website and going to office hours with him and the TAs. Grading was pretty easy with +2% EC. I recommend him.

Compared to my previous programming professors, hes a major improvement. But the class is disorganized and theres too much emphasis on attending virtual office hours to get information you need. Grades slowly trickle in weeks and even months later than expected. Assignments and quizzes are close to what youll find on the exam.

Had dr. Dobbins for discrete and databases, and he was alright. His class was pretty easy. I dont understand why so many people complain about him. His not the best professor, but definitely not the worst either.

Taking Databases with Dobbins changed my perspective on what field of study I wanted to pursue with computer science. I never thought that I would like handling data, but the way he teaches and his ability to help students right after lecture was a real godsend. He structures things to be just hard enough to make sure you learn, without killing gpa
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If I hadn't coded before, I would've been lost. Doesn't follow syllabus nor lecture notes. He is clearly knowledgeable, but not good at teaching for beginners. Very disorganized in lecture (useless!) and online. Just do the practice problems and get an A. The textbook is helpful, but no one reads. The TAs are lost bc of miscommunications.
Pete's alright, but the focus of the class was odd - why have us use a BlueJ-related textbook if you're going to drop that specific program a few weeks in?

Prof. Dobbins was overall a pretty good professor and has a lot of potential, BUT: Course is not well organized, presentations need a lot of improvement, Exams are entirely computational and not conceptual (normally a good thing but... not here), syllabus and assignments are very poorly named and laid out.
This has been the worse class I have taken at UF. The class is so unorganized and unclear that it is hard to learn anything when you do not even know what they are asking you to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Had him for Programming Language Principles. He cared deeply about the subject and made it interesting. Projects were very tough but were good at learning the material and were well planned out and fair. He definately cares about his work and students more than most professors I've had. would definitely recommend!

Professor Dobbins does not explain things in a clear way. Very minimal access to course materials. For example, were given problems to practice for our quizzes yet were never given the solutions to those problems so you have to try your best and just hope you did it right. The most disorganized class I have ever taken, would not recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is poorly structured and extremely hard to access without previous programming experience. Lectures are meandering and taught to the students as if we already understand the material. The textbook isn't referenced so it is incredibly difficult to find resources to learn from, and the grading fell far behind.

I am so lost in this class right now that I do not even know the right questions to ask! I took this class last semester & that Prof started small & built his way up. I feel as if this Prof is on shuffle skipping around complex topics before he's even explained the basics of Java. Def not a good class for someone with barely any coding experience

I know it's only been two weeks, but this class has been a nightmare. His lectures are extremely confusing and he doesn't teach from the book or provide any notes or resources, making it challenging to teach myself. He goes off on weird analogies about Arctic ecology and convoluted tangents that eventually muddy any point he was trying to make.

Professor Dobbins was not very good at explaining the topics. I was confused the majority of the semester, so I was struggling in this course. The TAs weren't any better. I did like that the lowest quiz was dropped and 5 points extra credit was offered along with extra credit on many of the quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Fairly easy class, 2 exams, 5 quizzes(lowest dropped), no homework. I only studied the day before exams and quizzes and did well on them. As long as you do the practice exercises on the book, you will do well in this class. He is nice, but his lectures are kinda boring.

Dobbin is definitely one of the good professors in the computer science department here. He is nice and very helpful. The only drawback is that he can really over-complicate the chapter sections sometimes.

He seems to care a lot. There are few grades to contribute to your overall grade so its scary if you bomb one quiz but its okay because he drops a quiz anyways. He's pretty loud too so it can be annoying but overall he's a pretty good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dobbins is a really nice guy and accessible during office hours. He is always happy to explain concepts and homework problems you have trouble with. His TAs were HORRIBLE at getting quiz grades back quickly (he recognized that he didn't ask for enough TA help- shouldn't be a problem for future classes). Study the textbook and the quizzes are doable
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures are complete nonsense. HW makes no sense at all and there is no real project in the class. Complete waste of time in going to lectures as they lack organization and content. Many students probably like him because he is easy but, you won't really learn as much taking aa course with him.

Pete was the shining light of the classroom. Once he started talking databases everyone was stuck in awe admiring his profound knowledge on the subject. He is definitely one of the best CISE teachers in the department and if you need help he is super easy to reach. He constantly reminds you of his office hours if you have any questions, I love him
One of the better cise department professors at UF, instructions are always super clear and exams are straightforward.

He makes the class very easy and is very supportive to those students who struggle. However, you are extremely ill prepared for a future in computer science if you assume this man is the norm or that this is the level of difficulty you'll face in software engineering or development. I wish he would scrap the pointless work in BlueJ!!

From my experience, Peter is by far one of the best professor in CISE. He explained thing clearly. MOst importantly, he doesn't just talk, he showed you what he was talking about in class. That to me make understanding programming a lot easier.
PETE IS THE MAN

Pete was a great teacher! He actually did coding in class to show you what he was talking about. Subject material was easy and so were tests. 10/10 Hope he teaches more CISE classes so I can take them.

Pete was a good teacher but he was lousy at explaining things. Honestly, I would suggest to take Pete but you'd have to learn the concepts on your own. Your grade is determined by the quizzes and the exams and the homework. Take him but be prepared to do work.
Pete is a grade teacher and one of the best in the computer science department here.

Pete was a great teacher. He talks quickly but is very clear with what he's saying. He makes things easy to understand. Quizzes/exams are all very fair and quite easy. Homework was all easy and very fair. Grades were always fair and reasonable. Class was overall enjoyable.
Pete is way too chipper. He's okay. Don't buy the BlueJ textbook. Attendance is not mandatory. Grade in COP3502 depends on TA anyway.

If this class was relived in Star Wars, Pete would be the wookie cuz while your programmer peers might understand, if you have no programming experience, you are screwed. This man uses so many analogies, your head will spin. Simply put, do not take this class unless you are ok with understanding chinese movies without subtitles.

Pete Dobbins is a nice guy but a bad teacher. He goes out of his way to use confusing wordage, and makes simple concepts overly confusing. The TA's are hit or miss, mine was absolutely terrible. If you are new to code, do not take this class lightly because you will fail.

Pete is very friendly and sincere but he's not a good teacher. He talks fast, often makes confusing analogies (sometimes his analogies are very helpful, but mostly they are not), and goes off on tangents about material that isn't part of the class. However, his tests and quizzes aren't too bad, if you have a good TA. Lia is fantastic!

Class was very easy, but he  uses way too many analogies.  All the comments say the TA's are awesome, but it depends on the year; mine were terrible.  The pace is ridiculously slow, I ended up reading the textbook ahead of the class because I got bored of lectures.  If you have prior prog. exp. bring something to lecture to entertain yourself.
He is a good professor, he explains everything well and gives good examples. The discussions were not hard

Definitely the easiest class ever. Attendence is not necessary. I did not go to a single lecture, and the discussion sections were more than enough to learn the material. You seriously aren't into Computer Science if you score less than an A. So much extra credit on tests and drops with an optional final exemption.
He is poor in teaching and explaining things in lecture. I got A's on all exams, but he still gave me an A-.
Lectures are practically pointless. Follow his online lecture notes and let the TA's explain things during discussion periods. I made A's on all the Exams and was on Reddit all semester..

Great teacher. I thoroughly enjoyed his class. I had little to no programming knowledge before taking his class, and I can say I learned a great wealth of knowledge. Just make sure to do the discussion questions he assigns a week in advance, and you'll be fine. Also, make sure to pay attention during his lectures. Laptop in class is a big help

This class is basically for learning how to work in a group. You'll be assigned to a group of 8-10 to work on an open sourced program for the entire semester. Relatively easy, but there is a lot of tedious work involved.

This class is very time consuming class, because it's beginning of class for the programming. His first test is easy, and second test is hardest. To be success this course, you need to meet TA alot, and need to study after every class. Not very easy class.

Dobbins is a good teacher. However, I wish he could have conveyed information better to help those with no prior programming experience. He talks loud, pronounces his consonants to the max, and sometimes stares at the class for questions rather than asking for them. If you need help, go to the TA, Tony! He's awesome and knows his stuff really well.

Professor Dobbins has a fun personality but rarely shows it in class. This is a difficult class, and you MUST do the homework. The assignments are assigned it seems a week early, without much information given. Go to TA office hours, GET TONY, he is awesome. The class is difficult, but managable.

He was a decent professor.  His notes from class were useful, but his ability to convey the information to students was not great, and it took a learning curve to understand the notes from class.  The TAs in the discussions were really helpful and clarified nearly everything I didn't understand in class.  All in all, a good intro to programming

Dobbins is a great teacher! One of the better teachers in the CISE department! The tests aren't hard if you study practice/past tests and understand the discussion practices. There is also A LOT of partial credit given on the tests. I wish I could have had him for CIS3023.

He's not horrible, but not great either.  He knows his material, just does not know how to convey it to students with no program experience.  Doing projects help the most for exams. Go to TA office hrs, they help A LOT! If you don't do the projects, it will bite you in the end.  Exam are fair and a lot of partial credit...2nd exam was ridiculous.

Dobbins is nice guy and really helpful in office hours, but I found his lectures to obtuse and hard to follow. You'll get the most of this class by doing the projects, discussion problems (Go to discussion! It really helps and counts towards your grade!), and practice tests. Overall challenging and time consuming, yet very interesting and engaging.

I had no prior programming knowledge going into this class. At first, his teaching seemed a big overwhelming. Actually, his practice tests are almost identical to the real tests, so I suggest you study those. Discussion helps A LOT. I made a mediocre effort and earned a 'B' for the semester. PS, second test is hardest. I suggest you take the third.

It is a crime to say Dobbins is a bad teacher. He is one of the best instructors at the CIS Department. He projects very clear and knows his stuff. In my opinion, those who hate him are the ones that got the bad grade they deserved. There's a lot of programmers-wanna be, but be careful, this is not for everybody. Excellent professor though!

Taking this class with no prior programming experience was a mistake.  Dobbins makes abstruse analogies during lectures and his TAs are very difficult to understand (and they can't understand you either!).  Overall, the lectures are boring.  I recommend going to his office hours.

Not an amazing lecturer, but not bad either. He's extremely helpful in office hours and a cool guy all around. Give yourself ample time to work on the projects (This is programming, folks, it takes time) and you'll do fine.
This class was particularly easy but his Java students struggle a bit at first. It takes a while to get used to him but the class is fair.

I had him for CIS3022 and 3023.  Personally, I really enjoyed his classes. A couple time consuming projects, but most of them weren't bad.  May not be the best teacher, but definitely one I'd try to get classes with rather than take my chances with someone I don't know.

I had him for CIS 3022, 3023, & COT 3100.  I'll take him for Intro to Soft Eng as well.  He's a great guy, & a wonderful teacher.  I had no prior programming experience.  The class had no required textbook so I got all of my information from lecture notes that I took in class.  I worked diligently on the projects & tests and got A's in 3022 & 3023.
He repeats himself about 30x per lecture, but the tests and projects are easy. Also, you can learn everything just by going to discussion and asking the T.A.'s. Easy class, pretty good professor.

He really does know his stuff. In his class you get out what you put in. He may be somewhat hard to understand at times but just starting early on projects and seeing him in his office hours makes it an easy A. Don't believe the bad reviews. They obviously didn't go to lectures.
Great Lecturer.  He gives numerous examples and his projects are fun and great ways to learn the material.  Very willing to help students inside and outside of class.
CIS 3022 & CIS 3023  It gets harder as the class progress but it is doable. I don't know what some people is talking about, I guess is the lazy people.

Both lectures and projects are excessively boring, redundant, and unclear. Helpful and nice guy, but just not up to the job. If you don't know the material already or don't have friends that do, you will have a hard time.
he's young and tries to relate to us but the metaphors are too much, hard to pay attention to. However I would take his other courses because he tries hard and I have learned a lot.

Pete is a nice guy who explains things very clearly and precisely. However, he WILL go off on tangents during lectures. Some people don't go to class and do fine. I wasn't one of them. Pete was the first guy who taught me how to program.

A very good teacher. In CIS 3022, he really wants everyone to succeed and be interested in java so the tests aren't too hard and are very similar to the practice test and the discussion sessions. The class is easy in the beginning but gets a little hard towards the end if you have never programmed before.

This guy is terrible.  He doesn't go over nearly what he needs to in class in order to do the projects.  The projects get too hard at the end.  I eventually dropped the class before it got too bad...oh yeah...and the TA's are foreign so they barely speak and English and are of no help at ALL!!!  I changed my Major because of this class, BEWARE!

Dobbins is one of the worste teachers at UF. He is responsible for many students despising programming because he teaches it so poorly.  His classes are easy to get good grades in, but he won't teach you a thing. He'll just babble and tell horrible jokes.

When you ask him a question, he tells you the answer again but louder....His tests were fairly easy, but his lectures border on ridiculous some days. Towards the end of the course i couldnt even pay attention to him anymore because he talked about random metaphors that didnt make sense. It almost seems like he is Trying to overcomplicate it.

Class was easy for 3022 and 3023. The tests compose a good portion of your grade, so they're really helpful. Other students complain about this class because they can't manage their time when creating the projects, and they end up waiting until the last minute. 10 points of bonus per test. Dobbins is funny and usually understandable.

For CIS3022 he was not a great lecturer and typically over complicated the topics when discussing them.  For cis3023 I've found his lectures to be a lot better, though still a little unclear at times.  He is a really nice guy, and if you talk to him outside of class, he answers questions better.

Good lecturer, helpful at explaining things. I didn't have any problem understanding him until the end of the course, with private and public properties. You definitely want to attend all the discussions, though. The class seemed overwhelming in the first week, but then it became my easiest.

Dobbins isn't a horrible teacher. He tends to overexplain what doesn't need a lot of explaining, and fly over complicated material that he expects you to know. Things got really complicated at the end of 3022 and you're expected to bring that knowledge with you to 3023. Go to discussion because the TA's are helpful, and you get bonus points for it.

I had professor dobbins this last semester and he did not see that bad at first.  What I ended up doing was using this really great java for beginners website which helped explained things like recursion, classes, and 2D arrays which is the most difficult part of the class

I think the comments here are really harsh. He's a slightly below-average teacher but he's not THAT BAD. I have no Java experience (although I do have programming experience) and the class is not that hard for me. The class is boring but better if you can bring in a laptop to practice programming or whatever while there. Take good notes.
Very ineffective at teaching. He just doesn't seem to have the charisma and teaching skills necessary to do the job. I ended up dropping the course and changing majors.
changed my major because of this guy. the end.
Vague notes, vaguely written homework assignments and not very easy to follow his lectures but is very wordy when lecturing and answering questions.

It almost seems as it his lectures are from a script. Someone will ask a question, he will **** a response. 10 minutes later, you're more confused and your question is still unanswered. His online notes are unbelievably vague and his project specs are written like a riddle. They arent hard, but he words them so poorly, you dont know what to do.
He uses as many words possible to say relatively simple things. You have to filter out what he says... it takes the TA 1 hour to explain 3 of his lectures.
I've had plenty of bad profs but this is the only one whom I've regarded as just downright stupid.  Tests are easy but don't expect to learn much.
No Comments

Took two classes with him. I totally agree with the other comments. He made me doubt whether programming was right for me. I only showed up for lectures because that is my principle, but you really do not get anything out of it. Class is dead and material is hard to absorb and confusing. I managed good grades but still learned very little.
Quite possibly the worst teacher I have ever had.  Avoid this man like the plague
Well..what Can I say? I enjoyed the lectures, and the tests were pretty easy. I needed an extra 50 minutes to sleep...his variable pitch, polyphonic voice does the job.

Dobbins is the worst excuse for an instructor.  He was horrible in class and would lecture on about useless crap and test on stuff he'd never even covered in class.  The TA's are useless because they dont speak any English.  One of the worst classes I've ever taken
No Comments

Easy class but Dobbins tends to make it so boring. He lectures on and on about useless stuff and that at random times breaks off to talk about other random ideas. Tests are long and very detailed. Always show up late. I dont think many teachers are better, so take it with him. You will just have to really work for the A.

I think he is a good professor, the only complain I have about this class "software engineering" is that we waited one month and a half in the class without doing anything, at the end of the semester it got really busy because we had to catch up because of this waste of time.

OK, I thought he was a lackluster teacher for Programming 1 and 2. Now, I have no doubt that he's completely inadequate for teaching this class. Very easy, but I have learned ZERO and yet I'm probably going to get an A. We barely made it to Chap. 4 FCOL. take it with Dr.Banerjee--he's really great.
Like a lot of ppl already said, Dobbins does not know how to teach Java programming to the students who dont know****.  whoever said this class was intro needs to get their head checked
He doesn't commit to helping his students learn the material. He also relies too heavily on his TA's to grade work and does not monitor their grading methods .

This class is so bad I got depressed. If you study on your own you will be fine (TA's help). Even thought this is an introductory class he expects you to be on top of everything - no slack. The lectures do not help at all in understanding the material, but let you know what's going on in the class.

I came into the class not knowing anything about Java programming and I know just as much now as when I started. Unless you know all about Java before taking this class make friends or else you will be dropping the class. The way he talks  in class makes you want to shoot yourself. I hate Dobman.
he doesnt teach****, he lectures about crap. just learn the stupid classes comparator, comaprable, learn your projects, you will learn something, analsysis & design, **** that

Worst CS teacher ever.  Seriously, I hate this guy  and he's a complete joke.  Always late to lecture, does absolutely no work whatsoever, no idea what he is teaching (you cant lecture an intro java class).  If you want to or are even thinking of majoring in CS you wont be after you take this class.

Like others have said, Dobbins is a waste of time. If you know the material already, then you're fine.If you don't know it,you're screwed cuz he sits at the podium rambling. I know quite a bit about programming and he often had mistakes in his lectures. I didn't take a class next semester cuz of him

I got an A out of Dobbins, but he's the worst prof I've ever had.  The class was essentially divided into two strata: those like me who already knew the material and could do easily without needing to work hard, and those who needed to learn, but couldn't because Dobbins can't teach, and bombed.

I just don't know what to say.  It's unfortunate that you can have a fantastic CIS teacher in high school for C++, and then come to a prestigious university and find such trash behind the podium.  I just wish the United States as a country would invest more money in the teaching profession...

Good teacher, considering he has to use a lecture format.  Tends to ramble, but is willing to help students who need it.  Tests are easy if you actually do a little bit of studying and listen in class.  Could do a better job in selecting his TA's though.
and Soft Eng.  Dobbins comes in and doesnt look like he has a plan to teach His lectures basically suck but he does give easy tests/quizzes. He will try to help out of class if you dont understand

His lectures are horrible. He's very boring and dull. But his classes and his tests are very easy. If you know how to study on your own with your book, you'll get a good grade. If you rely on his lectures, you'll be in trouble.

class is not so hard if you practice long enough. Good thing about tests are that there is a lot of partical credit. TAs do a good job, dobbins isnt very good at helping out with projects. Very generous on curve!!

Worst teacher i ever had.  All assignments and tests are extremely vague and you have to guess at what he wants. First test had a huge typo in it that screwed up the first half of the test. Third test arrived 20 minutes late for us. AVOID HIM!!!!!!!!!!!!

His tests are fair, but the idea of making the homeworks revolve around a single project is flawed. Practicing java requires solving problems of different/unrelated nature to gain a better perspective on the subject...

Knows his stuff and does a good job teaching it.  Does the best job he can trying to teach something in a lecture that really needs to be done in front of a computer.  He is always late for class though (5-10 min).  Tests are very fair and not too hard.

To put it simply: You get what you put in. If you complain about the professor and slack off through the course, you'll do bad.Actually listening to Dobbins and practicing a little Java in your free time will get you a B at least.TAs could improve though.

Nice guy, tries hard, but his teaching methods are terrible.  Maybe it's just me, but learning to program in Java in a lecture class just doesn't work.  His tests are awful, not because they are hard, but because they are written in about 5 minutes.
He is the worst teacher we have ever had.  Avoid taking a class with him at all costs.  This message should be considered a public service announcement.  Run...and run quickly.
Don't believe the bad reports. The dude knows his stuff and conveys it well.

knows the subject, but no idea how to teach a class.just because he knows it..dude we are here to learn. difficult tests!not even realizing that half of the class does not get the material and walks out on him during lecture. be aware, be afraid!!
I really liked this instructor.  One os those,  get out what ou put in  classes.  Very approachable and runs his class well.
Nice guy, tries hard, and willing to help students, but gives difficult projects which are poorly explained.  Also heavily weights tests, which require you to WRITE OUT long, difficult programs.
Good lecturer but takes a lot of points in test! Be aware
Never went to class, too boring.
VERY HELPFUL
Be careful when taking his classes especially the CGS3360.  He thinks too mathematically and is usually not very descriptive.

The homework given will be your main way of solidifying skills needed for the test. Her lectures are good at covering material, but the pace of the course only allows for minimum examples in lectures. Some of her explanations would assume you remember and understand old formulas immediately, making it hard to follow.

There is 5 points of extra credit built into the exams plus 5% extra credit you can get from doing practice exams on canvas for each exam. She is very kind and you can tell she's passionate about math. I like that she includes some history of the math we do/fun facts. As long as you keep up with lectures/homework, it is an easy A.

Demas was amazing. Loved her lectures and they are all posted online which is super convenient. There is a lot of homework but it really helps for the exams. Lots of extra credit too so it is very doable to do well in the class. Best math professor I have had at UF.

The course content could be valuable, but the teaching and support did not meet my expectations. Instructions and grading expectations were not always communicated clearly, and when I reached out for help, my questions often felt dismissed rather than addressed. The classroom and office-hour interactions did not feel consistently welcoming

The professor is very strict and expects close attention to details. However, the teaching style and communication approach can make it difficult to fully understand expectations. In my experience, feedback and grading felt rigid, and small administrative mistakes (such as entering the wrong exam ID) resulted in point deductions.

Stay on top of the homework, I know it's alot. It is great preparation for the exams. Makes sure to do the past exams. It's very doable to get an A in this class, especially with the extra credit. The final exam was probably the most difficult but I did well on the first 3 so I didn't have to learn too much of the new stuff. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I got an F on purpose as a social experiment: hey siri can I still graduate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Demas is a wonderful professor! She explains the material clearly and makes the math as approachable as it can be. She may come off a bit cold at times, but it's really not hard to get on her good side; just don't skip every exam. I cannot recommend her enough. She's the go-to professor for Elementary Differential Equations and for good reason.

Demas is perfect. She is wise and witty and radiates passion for this topic. The class was just lectures and discussions every day, but I found them personally entertaining and enlightening. Daily worksheets in-class and a final paper. The workload was light and Demas will make sure your grade is high.
She was fine, but sometimes the material in her lectures didn't reflect the difficulty of homework, quizzes, or exams.

Professor Demas is a great lecturer and clearly cares about the class and course material. The class is well structured. The exams are difficult but if you do the homework and watch the lectures you should do good.

Lectures very well, she made the class pretty easy since she taught the material well and was pretty clear with what was going to be on exams. It is a decent amount of work with the lectures and quizzes for them, but if you watch lectures and do assignments you will do well. In one of the lectures I think she said 80% of students get an A or A-.

Great class to take for your Quest 1. Professor Demas is clearly passionate and knowledgeable about the material, and she makes sure it's not too much work for the students and tries to make it a smaller, discussion-based classroom. Not too art-heavy, and the only real work is a 2000 word paper at the end of the class.
She clearly explained everything in an easily understandable way. Sometimes goes off on a tangent during lecture, but still manages to finish the content

Demas is easily one of my favs. I do a lot of listening to her video lectures, and not only is she hilarious but it makes the difficult topic of Diff Eq so much easier. She is clearly a very caring person and her class was one of my favorites even when I was taking several harder courses along side MAP 2302. Definetly choose her.

Definitely take Demas!. Her homeworks are harder than the exams, but they're unlimited attempts and prepare you very well for the exam. During lecture she talks about what to expect on exams. Very interesting lectures. Every exam has had extra credit points, and she gives 2% in extra credit assignments. You'll walk away knowing content very well.

Professor Demas' lectures are great, she delivers content in a concise manner and her lecture notes have everything you need. Each lecture has multiple examples for each topic so you are completely prepared for the exams. I appreciated that Demas taught the content so well that I didn't have to do work outside of her class to learn the material.

Professor Demas is extremely passionate about Italian Renaissance art and this passion shines through in her lectures. She loves when students ask questions and her exams are also easy (you have access to the in-class PowerPoints). Anyone who shows up and puts some effort in should get an A. However this class is much more art heavy than math.

I had Carol Demas as my instructor for Elementary Differential Equations and loved having her. Her lectures were clear and straightforward, exams were easy if you prepare, and there were many extra credit opportunities. I would definitely recommend taking!

In Williamson section, didn't step foot inside that lecture hall after the first day - watched Demas videos and they got me easily through the semester. I had to make up the final exam (it was probably harder than the original) but my 102% gave me plenty of leeway to keep an A. Prob the easiest grading math class at UF.

Demas is a great professor. diffeq isnt that hard imo, but she explained it clearly for those with not much previous background. Theres extra credit, lots of hw, similar to calc 3 amount (shabazz). Hw isnt too hard tho. I made a careless mistake regarding the final (cant say for legal reasons) but she was very understanding which is why I got an A+

Pretty decent lecturer, you don't have to go to class since she posts all the lecture videos on Canvas. No mandatory participation requirements. The tests are pretty easy, most of the questions are relatively basic but there 3-4 on each exam that's slightly harder. Should be a walk in the park if you are somewhat decent at math.

I didn't love Demas's lectures or way of teaching but at the end of the day, since she is the class coordinator and writes the exams, her lectures are the best of all sections. Her exams can be ridiculously mean though (much harder than the practice exams) however no matter who you take it with, the exams are all the same.
Demas is a great teacher, except she probably needs a mic. Just do the work, and if you passes Calc 2, there is no reason not to get an A in this class.

I think that she hates when students give excuses, because so often they give fake ones, but that kind of does not give her the way to act like that. I think that her lectures are engaging and funny thought, she has storytime every 2 lectures which is actually really nice. Mean person, cool lecturer, thats all

If you are good at math and dont want to show up to a lecture, just take the lecture class instead of the online one.  The grade disparity between them is immensely unfair, with a friend who got the same amount of questions wrong in the lecture getting a grade 9 points higher .  Prof. Demas is known for being rude to students who ask her questions

Dr. Demas is clearly extremely passionate about her Quest 1 class on math in Renaissance art. The homework is not strenuous at all, and above all else the course material is extremely interesting, which makes this class one I'd recommend to anyone looking for Quest credit. Show up and engage in discussion with the class and you'll be better off.

Demas is the goat. She makes the concepts easy to explain and goes over steps very well, you just have to watch the lectures and I think you'll do well in the class, she even goes over extra examples based on homework problems that people might find difficult. There is a bunch of extra credit, people complaining likely didn't put in the work.
Towards the end the class got a but wonky but if you put in the work and do your practice tests you should be fine.

Dr. Demas is passionate about what she teaches and just hopes you leave with an appreciation for art. The class is easy—4 discussion posts, a presentation (no need to present), and a 2000-word final essay, graded fairly leniently. I 100% recommend taking her Quest 1 class.

Best prof you can take at UF for DiffEq

Clear explanations, Hilarious deadpan humor, gives lots of examples, open to questions/feedback.

Lots of homework to do, but if you do it, you'll be prepared for the exams. If not, the exams will be hard. Put in the time, because no other prof will be easier.

Inconsistent exams. Some are very easy, some are very hard. Free response grading criteria is unclear. Her lectures are very monotone and can be hard to follow. Sometimes does not explain concepts well or goes too fast. Not great, but unfortunately the best option.

Definitely the best diff eq professor that UF has, try to get into her section if you can but if not all her lectures are posted on canvas and better than the other professor's lectures. She's also pretty funny which makes the lectures easier to pay attention to.

Demas is on of the best professors I've had at UF. She's such an understanding woman, if you go to office hours after an exam she will give you some points back and gives extra credit for doing practice exams. Lectures were so engaging and she's hilarious!! If you can TAKE HER SECTION!

She has a good sense of humor which makes otherwise boring content not so bad. All exams are out of 105% and you get 5% extra credit for doing practice exams. There's a lot of homework, but if you actually do it all and understand it you'll probably get an A.

Have never been met such a great professor, humorous, smart, caring, kind. She always wants students to actually learn stuff, instead of being a tough teacher. I supper love her lecture, super clear! She's just like a caring mom of all of us honestly.

Super super good professor. Clear about instructions and office hours and the Canvas course is really easy to navigate. The homework is awful but it makes the exams so much easier. However, it's easy to fall behind if you don't adhere to the due dates that she has. Overall, lectures are pretty interesting and I would recommend her
She can be a little weird at times (especially when fantasizing over Euler) but over a good lecturer who explains quite well and gives us plenty of practice. Don't get behind or you're cooked
Very rude if you have any questions.

I can't be explicit or my rating will be removed, but this lady is a bad***. She is absolutely hilarious and I find her humor to be underappreciated. As an instructor she is very clear and tells you exactly what you need to do to succeed. She is also very knowledgeable of the history of the things she's teaching you. A very well rounded instructor.

Love this woman, actually had her for my humanities quest course and developed a great relationship with her. Very passionate and had a dry, sarcastic sense of humor which I enjoyed. The class was a great freshman quest course with few assignments, easy exams/final paper, and options for extra credit.

I loved this class. She was an awesome lecturer. If you do and understand the homeworks, you'll probably do fine on the exams (the homework problems were harder than the exams). She also gave practice exams. Lectures are recorded. Very fair in terms of due dates and she gave extra credit that she explained how to do at the end of the semester.

Excellent professor. She teaches the material in an easy-to-understand way as long as you also put in an equal amount of effort in your own time. All the classes are recorded so you technically don't have to attend. She is also not dry and can be funny sometimes. Her lectures do have to rush sometimes but that's not her fault (lots of content)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great lectures and course format. Four exams, homework and quiz for each lecture, and lots of extra credit/grace on exams. Professor Demas' humor made lectures entertaining and she's excellent at breaking down really complicated math into steps that make sense. Definitely a class you can succeed in if you put in the effort.

I love this woman so much. Its a shame that she teaches so few classes. The homework she assigns helps you prepare for her exams, which are very fair. She puts many study resources on her canvas, she records her lectures, is very helpful when answering questions and she has a silly sense of humor. If you have the chance to take her, don't miss it!

I love her so much she has a dry and witty sense of humor and I watch her recorded videos and i'm literally laughing out loud anddddddd she's a rlly good lecturer. the homework's are spaced fairly and they're never as hard as the lecture problems she does and the tests r also on par with previous years 🫶🫶🫶🫶

She teaches the class decently well, but all the rest of the professors available are horrendous. The homework is kinda hard and takes time, but prepares you well for the exams. She is very rude and complains constantly during class, but you will still learn from her.

I took this class over the summer online. Didn't have her as my actual professor but we were given her lecture recordings to watch. In the prerecorded ones she just reads out what's on the sheet and doesn't actually explain anything or go into proofs. Good for students who like to memorize instead of actually learning. Also glazes Euler like crazy.

She was fine for the first 2/3 of the class, and then her lectures fully devolved into just showing examples without explaining anything. Wasn't difficult to pass the class, but she was very obnoxious about remembering precalc stuff and was rude in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Demas was an interesting, but great, professor. I found the material super interesting. I ended with a 99% and found that it was very doable as long as you do ALL the materials. She was also SUPER generous with the amount of extra credit she gave and that most of the online assignments had multiple attempts
Awful professor avoid if possible but most the other professors just play her recorded lectures. Try to find the old Dr. Manly lectures and find an old textbook to teach yourself.

She would absolutely belittle the class almost non stop if you don't remember some pre calc stuff or calc 2 stuff. Also she loves to glaze some old mathematicians and gives unrelated information on their history. She speeds through everything during lectures. Not tech savvy at all and will struggle with the projector and recorded lectures.

Great professor. She is very passionate about math. I am glad I took her. Her class structure is easy to follow. She makes witty comments which are very funny. Exams are fair and similar to previous exams. The extra credit at the end is nice. I am glad I took her. Learned a lot with her.

Demas was a very good lecturer, and made this class pretty easy to digest if you just attend lecture either in person, on zoom, or at your own time on the recorded lecture. Exams were just like the practice exams, some of the homeworks were time consuming, but you have unlimited attempts. You also get 2% extra credit. Easy 3 credit overall

Rude and accusatory. Always assumes the worst in her students. I am appalled by my personal experiences with her. She is an amazing lecturer though. If you never have to deal with her directly you should be fine. People often take another professor but watch her lectures.

Demas is great, funny, and witty. Homeworks take a while! Do them (MC with unlimited attempts) and you'll be prepared for exams, which were chill but the final was hard. Attendance is not mandatory and most people (me)  watched recorded lectures. Gave 2% of extra credit assignments and the grading scheme is fair.

I though she was a very good lecturer. She was very easy to follow even though there is a lot of information to learn in diff eq. The workload was not bad just the usual math class homework of about 15 questions. Attendance is not mandatory and all the lectures are posted online or you can join on zoom.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Attendance is not mandatory, so you can just watch her recorded lectures which are amazing. Exams are not hard, and are similar to the practice exams she provides
Amazing professor. No words. 10/10

LOVED HER! She's definitely only for certain audiences though... the way she taught was perfect for me and I enjoy her jokes and enthusiasm for what she is teaching (although i guess her voice is technically monotone it works for me). Easy A if you do the practice exams and all homework assignments
A strangely... insecure (?) professor. Makes snark comments about students in recorded lectures. Monotone lectures. Otherwise a reasonable 3 credit course.

Professor Demas can be straight-to-the-point at times, but is kind and caring. She teaches thoroughly and provides extra practice problems. Some may view her tone as condescending, but her inflections are purposely informative and with good-intention. During review sessions, she may interject people's questions to save time and teach at a good pace

The class was well-structured and organized and was very exam-heavy like any other math course. Professor Demas does a great job explaining the lessons and her lectures are helpful. She also usually sets aside two days before the exams for review, and these reviews clear up a lot of questions. You will probably end up with an A or A-
she regularly would hurt my feelings
The TA was great and very helpful but every single time i interacted with the professor she was rude and clipped and clearly does not like people with accommodations

She is the head of the department& yet she is wildly unreasonable she views everything said to her as a lie or making an excuse When the hurricane happened& class was canceled my class didnt get to finish the lesson so everyone thought the quiz was postponed No It wasnt you were expected to still do it even though my home lost power she doesnt help

Professor Demas was an amazing lecturer for elementary differential equations. She always took care to prove every formula and process that she was using, and the guided notes she used were clear and easy to follow along. Though she takes a strict no-nonsense attitude towards the course, she still finds a place for humor in her lectures as well.

While she is a good lecturer and provides plenty of resources for the students. She tends to be very judgmental when it comes to excused absences and assignments, making it hard for students to be sick or to partake in other activities. She is also therefore unnecessarily strict, preferring to place blame on students that acknowledging her faults.

You will not get a better math professor at UF! Professor Demas is a wonderful lecturer and she provides so many resources. The lecture notes are great and the past exams prepare you for exams. She is seriously the nicest professor you will meet and I enjoyed her sense of humor.
She's amazing, I love her teaching! Lectures are recorded and the homeworks really help you prepare for tests. Final is culminative so beware.

Carol Demas is easily one of the best lecturers in the math department. People will come on here and complain that she's "mean" but it's completely untrue, she just doesn't spoonfeed you answers. Her lectures are amazing and always convey the material clearly. If you truly put in effort, this class should be a straightforward.

Loved her class! She's passive-aggressive but makes up for it cause she's a good lecturer and loves to talk about her dogs. HW is not super hard, there's extra credit and easy quizzes. Stick to the LECTURE NOTES to study for exams and use past exams to practice; you should be set to do very well on the exams. Very accessible outside of class.

Aggressively average professor. Personally not a fan of her lectures; found her really hard to pay attention to. Also homework takes so long that it's demotivating and you end up needing help or answers on all of them. Not helpful to the learning environment at all and felt like I needed to cram before every exam.

I thought Demas was really funny and enjoyed her lectures. The grading is pretty tough and exams are pretty much raw scores or 1 free question. Homework is all on canvas and usually multiple choice. Use homework as practice for exams and you will be fine.

Prof. Demas' course has one homework assignment per lecture, which often means multiple assignments weekly. This adds up fast and turns the class into constant catch-up if you ever stumble. Demas is not forgiving with personal situations. The four exams are less difficult than the homework. She's v witty in lecture and is a lot of fun to listen to.

One time someone told me that they thought that Dr. Demas was "kind of evil" but I adored her this semester. I watched her online lectures for 90% of the semester even though I didn't have her as my professor. I thought that she was hilarious and really doubled down on topics and equations that were really important. Would highly recommend!
Awesome professor, she is a very good teacher. Will hold review sessions in class the day before or day of the test. Drops some of the homework, quizzes, and pretests.

Not a good professor, but given the limited choices at UF, most people don't realize how much better this course could be. Very doable class if you know your stuff or have time to study, but Carol is a bit demeaning and rude if you have questions. Most of the ratings are proportional to the grade received by people, not the quality of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Enjoyable lectures and fair tests.

For a calc class she never lectured. At the beginning of every class she would pass out a worksheet and just walk around the room or sit in front of the class and tell people to come up to her for help. Prepare to learn actually everything on your own 
As long as you do the work yourself, pretty easy to pass.

Dr. Demas was an amazing professor. She could be easily reached outside of class for any questions and help. The exams were generally fair as long as you had studied the content and gone to the lectures. She sometimes got a little bit snappy about some subject. I definitely recommend her for Diff. eq.!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: We need more STEM girl bosses in teaching positions at UF because she is the perfect representation of one. She is a harsh professor but she helps her students a lot. She is lenient sometimes and is super understanding during emergencies. She is also so funny and is passionate about the subject she is teaching.

Demas is THE BEST calc prof ever. She really knows what she's doing and provides clear lectures with a lecture note guide too. She's super responsive to questions too. Lots of HW but it helps you keep up with everything. Tests are very fair and she explains everything so well. You can tell she really cares for her students.

Professor Demas is great and explains her lectures well, although my professor was Rudyak, I didn't go to his lectures and only watched Demas's lectures. That being said, this was one of the easiest math classes I have taken at UF. There is alot of homework, but it really prepares you well for the exams.

She explains the topics clearly and gives plenty of examples. As long as you attend lectures and do the work, you will do well. She also has a unique dry sense of humor which is fun. The exams are very fair and you have plenty of time to complete them.
Really good at explaining the topics in the pre-recorded lectures. Exam reviews are a must for a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Demas was really passionate about calculus but had difficulty conveying the basics of calc 1 to her students. We did packets in class and she would often skip and not explain steps when working through problems. She would be probably be good for upper level math and calc but at a lower level she assumed we knew things that we didn't.

Overall, the material was fairly easy but she taught and explained it very well. She really wants her students to succeed and gave many hints on what was on the exams. The homework can get a bit annoying as there is a lot of computation involved. Would definitely recommend.

I've had Demas for Calc 3 and Diff Eq. She's a really caring professor and wants all of her students to succeed. She has a monotone voice sometimes but that's because she does 4 lectures in a row for the same class. She makes the exams and lets you know exactly what to expect. If you watch lectures and do the HW you will get an A.

Professor Demas is a good professor. Not bad, not great, just average. She's a nice woman who cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Her lecture style is boring, but the content isn't terribly difficult to grasp. She writes extremely fast during lectures so it is critical to pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Diff Eq isn't a hard class w/Demas as course coordinator. She does a really great job coordinating exams w/hw, so put in the time and you'll be fine. Her lectures are... different. I ended up switching to Ian Manly's zooms bc he's more on-topic and doesn't complain about class engagement. A lot of students love her, it's just a matter of preference

By far one of the best lecturers I have had at UF. Its one of those where you either love her or hate her because her lectures are quite fast paced and she has a... particular sense of humor. But she cares deeply for students, no textbook, homework format lets you practice/study while getting a good grade. Exams are what you would expect.

Had Demas for Calc 2, Calc 3, and Differential Equations. Always extremely clear, professional, and constantly communicating with students. Although she might come off as intimidating, she is very accommodating and always willing to help. Very knowledgeable professor and always tries to make lectures interesting with cool facts. Awesome prof!
She's an angel. She's funny and knew exactly how to teach the class in a way that kept up interested (which is hard for diff eq). Take her if you can

She gives exactly what she expects from you. you just have to watch the lectures and understand the LQs and the exam will be fine. The study guide is usually very similar to the exam so makes it easy to prepare.

I had Demas for calc 3 and diff eq. I really enjoyed having her for both classes. Calc 3 is pretty standardized so it probably doesn't really matter who you have for that class. Diff eq isn't as standardized, her lectures were easy to understand and her homework was easy as long as you had your notes to refer to. Exams were always straightforward.
For diffyq, Demas is the bomb and has a great class structure. Lectures are clear, easy to follow, and she is just a cool person overall. Highly recommended.

Demas was a very average professor for Calc 3. Went over on time for a large majority of zoom lectures, even though they were very fast paced. Exams were difficult but manageable if you dedicated tons of time to preparation. Graded through a points system, so it was very difficult to gauge your grade for the first portion of the semester.

Professor Demas was SUCH a great professor for Calc 3. Her lectures are a little fast paced but she always recorded them and posted them so we had access to them later. She was very responsive to questions asked and she was super nice and helpful if you tried in the class. I highly recommend her for calc 3
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ms. Demas is a great lecturer. Some lecturers this semester had troubles with going over class time in Zoom lectures, and Demas' were by far the most succinct. At the end of every lecture, she worked out two warm-up questions that are very similar to exam questions. Almost a full letter grade of extra credit available, but you have to work for it.

Professor Demas was very helpful and always willing to answer questions. During lecture if anyone had questions or was confused she would never hesitate to take a second and explain. The discussion board was also open for student questions with quick replies on problems. She held NUMEROUS review sessions before exams during her OH. Really caring.

If Carol Demas was an ice cream flavor she would be vanilla. Not your first choice but you wont complain if you get it. Completely adequate in terms of lecture quality but was always willing to answer questions.

Professor Demas was such a sincere professor who really cared about her students. She taught the material in a clear manner and her lectures were entertaining. She assigns a lot of work, but if you do the work, it really shows in your final grade. The exams are very straightforward if you do the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Carol is your best bet for MAP2302. There's never any surprises as to what will be on a quiz/test and she makes sure you know any type of question that could show up. She definitely knows what she's doing, and if you get her you'll be set. She's also considerate and pretty funny, which made her lectures enjoyable.

We would spend half the lecture discussing examples from the previous lectures and we would have to rush through new concepts. I bombed the first exam and my grade never recovered even with StudyEdge and countless office hours. I had to change my major (from math) because of this class, and I had always been good at calculus in high school.

Ms. Demas is an amazing choice for MAC2313. Her zoom lectures this past semester would often go over, but she is willing to give extra time to ensure her student get some extra practice with warm-up questions at the end of each lecture. There are enough extra credit opportunities and review sessions to be able to succeed while putting in the work.
Gives one example and moves on without showing steps

Professor Demas was extremely essential to my success in calc 3, she was always available and would respond to any question I had at any time. She gave extra credit that bumped many people up by 2-grade letters and the course was very clearly outlined. Be sure to post on the wall with any questions way before the deadline.

She is a great professor, and you can tell she really cares about her students. Her lectures are very easy to follow and understand. She assigns quite a bit of homework, but it's worthwhile. Overall if you attend class and do the HW you'll do fine.

As far as calculus courses go, the online secation of calc 3 that she headed was well structured and easy to follow. The only reason I'm giving her 3 stars is that she can be a little rude when responding to questions. Sometimes I found she tack on snide remarks to emails after she answered your question. Not a huge deal but something to note.

When everyone said Calc 2 was impossible even with an amazing prof such as Chui I decided to take it online so I could go slowly and watch lectures 30x to understand stuff. Demas holds online office hours twice a week and thoroughly explains ANYTHING you ask her, and you can send questions the night before!! 2+ tries on every assignment and quiz
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: From my understanding, Demas was the coordinator/grader for this online class, while Dr. Christodouloupoulou did the lecture videos. Regardless, the class isn't difficult, as long as you keep up with the workload. There are discussion boards on Canvas to post questions, and either prof replies very quickly. Both also offer in-person office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor! Explains everything clearly, and genuinely cares that entire lecture hall understands the material. Very willing to stay and help after class. Attendance isnt mandatory because lectures are available online, but her teaching style is great.
Great teacher, lectures are helpful but you can watch online if you dont like her style.
Such a good teacher! I was really glad I had her section. Very clear with teaching the material, even the tougher concepts, and she genuinely cared about the students.

Carol is the greatest! Her lectures go with the homework, and if you understand the homework; you will do great on her exams. She hates when people skip class though, so never miss class without telling her if you want to stay on her good side. She gives lots of extra credit opportunities and is a very fair grader. She's also subtly hilarious.

Had Carol as a TA and lecturer, amazing woman. Super nice and fair grading. Be nice to her and she will help you out with whatever you need. Calculus is still hard, but she makes it more bearable, ask her to tell you some jokes.

She clearly demonstrates the harder concepts and gives amazing real world examples when something is difficult to conceptualize. Overall is one of the best professors I have had for lecturing here at UF.

my favorite professor ever- but don't underestimate the content because it builds overtime and the final is really tough. go to office hours, get to know her, she's the most helpful resource for learning the content. 

can't recommend her enough, truly a joy to learn from!
Amazing professor, I found the class pretty hard but she was great at explaining things and very helpful in office hours!

Professor Davison is the best professor I had during my time so far at UF. She explains topics in detail with analogies that helps connect ochem to everyday topics, class quizzes and tests are fair and reflect lecture topics well with some reasonable additional challenge. It is critical to attend classes, her office hours are also extremely helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Davidson is the best professor I had at UF. She makes a hard topic easy to understand. She is extremely nice, willing to help if you reach out, and is an overall very positive person that makes lectures very tolerable. Would highly recommend with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: First, Dr. Davidson is a lovely person. She cares about your success, especially so if you put in sufficient effort. Her lectures are the best I've attended in my college career. She uses real-world analogies for a lot of the concepts she explains. This can be a notoriously difficult class, but you can succeed if you're proactive and attentive.
Lab practical grading is obfuscated and is practically luck based.  You will never interact with the professor and you need to hope for a good TA.  She also makes you buy her $50 lab notebook.

Most of the class is doable including the practical after thorough review of its procedure. The final is more of a challenge. Despite some difficult personal situations Dr. Davidson has been extremely accommodating. Orgo is always to be hard but Dr. Davidsons compassion made the class more bearable.

Dr. Davidson is one of the best professors I have had thus far at UF. She is super transparent about the material. She knows it is difficult and will help you if you are having trouble. She does a great job of using analogies to make the material more understandable and also gives little breaks with a random comedic story. GO TO CLASS! GO TO O.H!

THE FINAL LAB EXAM IS EXTREMELY HARSHLY GRADED, the experiments and class is easy and doable but the exam is horrible and you will not be prepared but expected to know the entire textbook and experiments.

The best professor I've had so far. Quizzes and tests are difficult but manageable. Makes the double-block lecture very enjoyable (even including a break in the middle). Super friendly and open. If you don't need two years of ORGO, I recommend taking Dr. Davidson's class.

davidson is a great professor and really wants you to understand orgo. the content is difficult since it is combined but she wants you to succeed. the homework is hard and takes a very long time but is doable.

this is the only prof u need for orgo1/2, best class ever. LOTS OF HW that will take hours due every 2 days, 5 quizzes, 2 exams.. study lecture notes only and use study guides and NEVER miss class. if you have time management and good study skills, you will get an A.. dont take if you hate hw or are lazy, because it gets hard FAST. WOULD TAKE AGAIN

I absolutely love Dr.Davidson!!!! By far the best professor I have encountered at UF! The class material is very difficult (obviously it's orgo 1+2 squeezed together) but if you go to lectures, study after class ... it's very doable! No matter what, do not fall behind! She's a wonderful professor but you have to study a lot and put in the hours!

I enjoyed all the labs until half way through the semester when you basically could not get a product with any of the experiments. Its enjoyable in the lab. but the knowledge checks are sneaky hard. the practical is harshly graded. and the lab exam was very challenging, harder than any of my other finals. drops about half of people out of a A.

I really enjoyed having Dr. Davidson! She is so kind and her passion for chemistry makes lectures much more interesting. The class is obviously hard because of the content, but she uses ALEKS in a much more constructive and less time-intensive way than I experienced in gen-chem at UF. I can't recommend her enough!!

SHE IS THE BEST!!!!! Easily one of my favorite professors at UF. She is the most kind professor who makes her classes fun to be in. I never feel that the 2 hour blocks are long and she makes organic chemistry very easy to understand. TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She gives great lectures, show up and focus and you shall do good. The exams were very fair, free response, with no suprises. Partial credit was given due to this. She is also very accesible for office hours and answers any question or will repeat any concept for you. Much easier then orgo1/orgo2 due to having a great professor !

I highly recommend the class CHM3217 it will be way easier than taking the organic 1 and 2 sequence. Dr. Davidson is a very approachable and entertaining professor. She really cares about her students and does her best to help you learn the content.

The lab portion of the class is pretty interesting. There is some work to be done but nothing too difficult. The issue with this class is that large of your grade is based on progress quizzes and an assembly final with very little direction on what those will cover. The TAs  are not able to help. Practical is graded too harshly.
Why does the prof make progress quizzes that hard, does she want to fail us

Bless this woman. She made organic chemistry pleasant. The class is difficult, but easier than any other organic chemistry class you will encounter. It is quiz and exam heavy, but small cheat sheets are usually allowed. So instead of just having to memorize a bunch of random reactions you do have to think mechanistically.

Dr. Davidson is not involved with the course so this is primarily a class review. The class is super TA-dependent since your graduate TA will grade everything you do. It's pretty easy overall and labs can be fun and interesting. Beware of knowledge checks, they can be difficult at times and you should prepare well. Same for final and practical.

So Dr. Davidson writes the book for the class and the exams but the TAs run the lab. I had Khoa Dang for my lab he was very sweet and helpful and a funny guy. I would take with her if you can, most the TAs are pretty chill. Only downside was the final was pretty hard but it's on 20% of the grade. If you show up to lab and do the work you'll be fine

The lab was fun and interesting. Definitely gave me a better understanding of organic chemistry. Grades depend mostly on TA. The knowledge checks and lab exam were a bit difficult. They can have significant impact on the grade. Try not to only understand what you are doing but also why. Look over the practical beforehand to do well.

The class is way more difficult than it should be. Progress quizzes make up a large amount of your grade and have little to do with the lab and what you talk about in class. It is a really poorly constructed class. It is the only lab I did not get an 'A' in. Get ready to study and do poorly on the quizzes. Most people do.

AMAZING professor! Very understanding and willing to help you! My favorite chemistry professor at UF. She made the material so much easier and allowed for us to ask questions, ask for help, etc. Genuinely looked forward to coming to class.

The class had two two-hour lectures a week, though she had a break between the hours of about 10 minutes. She is very thorough in making sure we understand concepts. There are a lot of reactions we learn, so it is important to practice writing these out. I definitely recommend taking this class who have an option.

Class taught by TAs not Dr. Davidson. I had a really good TA and I got a 100 on every lab, but the progress "quizzes" which are assembly exams determine your grade. Make sure you study a lot for them because they're short, hard, and not curved. She loves to go on about her fair grading but the weighting of assignments makes no sense.

The lab itself is pretty easy, especially if you have a good TA. Your grade consists of attendance, prelabs, notebooks (post labs), attendance, practical and two progress quizzes. The progress quizzes are content based, pretty hard and a big part of your grade. You can get 100s on everything but bomb the practice quiz and your grade will tank.

Class depends on the TA since Davidson is only the coordinator, but my TA was great. I really like the experiments (we even got to make slime) but I don't like how the two progress exams can tank your grade. The exams are very hard so make sure you study very well. The class is already curved so don't bother asking for a grade bump.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: quizzes weigh more than attendance + lab itself. study hard for quizzes bc it'll drop you bad. she does not give any EC nor cares if students are under 0.5 away from next grade. class is a joke but the quizzes are tough (lower than the BCH exam averages). way too hard for a lab. barely will learn. brags that her avg grade is a b+ for a lab class...

No clue what impact Tammy had on my understanding of orgo lab past dealing with my grades since the TAs carry the class. The lab itself is easy & kind of fun for a lab class but the exams are actually pretty hard. Do not underestimate them. Make sure you memorize all the key material. I'm smart but I barely made an A just because of the exam grades
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is SO sweet and the exams honestly arent hard. The only problem with the class is your grade is literally only 4 exams (she averages 3 grades to replace your lowest but still). She is very good at explaning things def take her

For orgo lab we never personally met w Dr. Davidson, but your fate in this class will depend entirely on your personal TA. Make sure you know everything you're doing and understand why you're doing it. Don't get complacent for the midterm, final, and practical, though. Show up to every lab on time and follow the procedures and you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: class wasnt too bad. make sure you understand WHAT you are doing in lab as well as WHY. i had no clue what i was doing up until the midterm, I literally talked to so many TAs a week before the exam and they explained everything to me so I did great. The final was a lot easier because of the switch online. ASK QUESTIONS! exams are tricky but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For orgo lab, we never met Dr. Davidson, so this is more a review of the class overall. It's an ok class, but keep in mind that the exams are designed to trick you. Also, make sure to take your time on the practical (especially melting point) and grab all of your reagents before you decolorize your starting reagent (makes sense when you do it).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The only reason I got an A is because of the switch to online. Lab is super easy and ran by TAs but the midterm and final are ridiculous in my opinion. Not so much because of the material but because they make up 50% of your grade. Even if you do great on your lab notebooks, a low grade on the exams will screw your entire grade. No curve or E.C.

Took this well after gen chem. She definitely understands how fast paced the class is, and because of that she is flexible on homework deadlines if you ask! Aside from how much homework was due, I never noticed we were going double pace. She explains concepts thoroughly; you won't need to memorize any mechanisms! Noncumulative tests and quizzes!

I never met her in person since the labs are run by TAs; the actual lab is fun and stimulating. The grading is something to watch out for. Even if you have an A the entire semester, the final + practical can easily change that. Many students had unseen "impurities" that knocked their A to an A-. The final is so nitpicky that it's hard to do well.

Took this class after 2 years of finishing General Chemistry Reqs and it was rough. She presents the material in such a good way but if you don't study/work practice problems... good luck. First quizzes not too bad then it went down hill, very fast paced and dense w concepts. DO THE HOMEWORK. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. She is a fantastic orgo Teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is very flawed in structure. This class was about six hours a week of wasted time. As someone that is into chemistry, I learned almost nothing from the experiments. The midterm and final expect knowledge far past what is covered in lab and the notebook. Luckily, they are a low percent of your grade, but an A is very difficult.

She is literally the best professor and person I have ever met. She genuinely cares about her students and the class outcome.
