If you need help, she'll be delighted to help. 10/10 would recommend her for any class. She could talk about the most trivial of things and I will give her my undivided attention.

One of the coolest professors at UF ever!! Literally made me excited about orgo. Her lectures are amazing and exams are all fair. I never had to use or felt the need to use study edge at all. All you literally have to do is make sure you know how to work out all the practice problems at the end of the textbook. All her exams are based off those.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: The labs and midterm are easy. As long as you don't get busted equipment for the practical you will be okay as well. Pretty much everyone goes into the final with an A so the quiz is designed to shake out a grade distribution. Do not get lulled into a false sense of comfort with the easy midterm and your grade before the final.

Dr. Davidson is very knowledgeable, and she makes organic chemistry easier to understand. Take advantage of the pre-formatted notes that are posted online, since she fills them out in class. That being said, the course material is accelerated, so you might feel overwhelmed at times. As a result, you must review fairly often to be successful.

Professor Davidson is an excellent teacher, a fair grader, and an overall great person. She always puts her best foot forward in lecture, and never avoids a question from her class. Organic chemistry can be tough, especially 3217, but she makes it bearable.  Also she uses lots of food analogies, so make sure you eat before class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Never interacted with Prof. Davidson, Organic lab is incredibly fun and interesting but ultimately your grade depends on your TA and how picky they are. The practical and Midterm were extremely doable but the final was pretty hard. I recommend a good and thorough understanding of spectroscopy and the lab topics to do well in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Davidson loves organic chemistry, and it is evident that she is excited to share organic chemistry with her students. She is helpful, clear, relatively organized, and understanding. I thoroughly appreciated the fact that she posts outlines for the notes that I could print out and use to follow along in class.

The lab at UF is actually fun but the grading is ridiculous. The actual hands on work that you do in lab is not worth much of your grade but the lab quizzes are worth 65% of the grade which is quite ridiculous. The midterm and practical are easy but the final will shoot your A down to a C if you don't do well. Probably done on purpose. very cunning
BEST CHEMISTRY TEACHER AT UF! Orgo was actually my favorite class I took that semester because she was so great. Extremely clear, fair tests, super helpful and overall an extremely nice person!

If you do every problem in the back of every chapter (excluding the looking ahead section) and you ask her or her TAs questions when things don't make sense to you then there is no reason you shouldn't do well. I did the same thing and ended up with a 99 average in the class. Just try not to fall behind because cramming won't get you that A.

Awesome teacher. I really liked her class outlines. Her exams were pretty fair, though she only gave one practice exam. I only spent the week of studying/learning the material and managed to get an A and two high B's on her exams. My only problem was that she treated us like children at the beginning of the class and went way too slow.
She is a great professor! Tests are fair and nothing like her sadistic husband. She doesn't try and fail you she just wants you to pass. Go to TZ and an A is def attainable.

Dr. Davidson is a great teacher. Her tests are fair and are not harder than they have to be. With that being said this class is still no walk in the park, but if you study hard an A is definitely possible. She curves the class slightly, with the lower grades getting helped out more than the higher grades. I would recommend her.

T-DOG! Tammy Davidson. She's an awesome professor. If you have the opportunity to take Organic II with her, I would recommend her 100%. She lectures extremely well, her exams are 100% fair, and she doesn't try and trick you with BS. She just wants you to learn the material and understand it. Go to class, study, TZ and you will ace Orgo II.

She is an amazing teacher. Best professor at the University of Florida, hands down. She's so helpful and is a great lecturer. She loves for people to go to office hours and her exams are fair. If you do your part in the course, you'll be successful.

Great professor, always willing to help. I've had a rough time with all chemistry courses, but she actually made it interesting for me. It's not an easy class, but if you make an effort and dedicate about a week to studying before each test then you should be fine. Go to her office hours often and do the problems at the back of the chapter.

If I took her class last year (fall 2009) I would have gotten an A. Her previous exams are used as study guides but they do not help as much as other people let on. Her exam ?s are much more difficult. Go to class for clarity, the book is long and tedious. One of the 3 exams are dropped.

GO TO CLASS. Her lecture notes are much more helpful than the textbook. Labs take a lot of time. Her practice tests are nothing like the problems given on the exam. The problems in the textbook are wimpy compared to her exams. Lowest of the 3 exams is dropped! On exam will give partial credit for showing your work!

Lab isn't hard, but the final is graded horrible. Grading scale is very unforgiving making it hard to get an A, but B is very doable. Don't stress, you will get a B for showing up but unless you devote more time to this lab than Orgo 2 itself don't expect an A.

This teacher is the best UF has to offer, especially for an organic chemistry class. I love her teaching style and her tests are totally fair. She is the best chemistry teacher I have ever had and actually understand! TAKE THIS PROF! A lot of partial credit is given and practice tests actually model the actual test! She is the best!

Excellent teacher. I came into organic a little scared and she made it so much easier and clear than most professors probably would. Very nice woman, but she lies about the difficulty of her tests. She does not curve, because her "test averages are in the 80's." My classes averages were in the 60's, and she still felt no need to curve. She gives very little extra credit, that almost does nothing for your grade. Don't take her
Dr. D. is a really nice woman, but I would not recommend that you take her because her tests are fairly difficult and there is no curve.
No curve, only some partial credit. Easy to do not so well, and very difficult to get an A. But I love love love Dr. Davidson!

The labs themselves are pretty easy, though the TAs may not have any idea what "should" happen. I think at some points I became the TA as often questions were directed at me instead of our TA. The reports are a combination of lame and pointless, and the grading on them is somewhat unclear. The class is designed so 95% get a B or better.

For Organic 2 lecture, do NOT take davidson. She is nice, but her grading isnt what you need if your pre-something. Her tests are very hard. I would much rathar take a mean prof. who curves/has easier tests than a really nice lady who doesnt curve. Ive never worked this hard in a class and not done well. I only had 2 b's in college before this clas
very clear explanations, makes learning orgo easy, always willing to help and answer questions outside of class
I took the lab, and it is pretty fun. It is easy cheesy, but be careful on the lab reports, they are graded harshly. Nothing is misunderstood, you really learn in this class.I loved it.
No Comments

The lab class is not hard.  Spec exam is really easy.  People make it sound so hard.  Study and you should be fine.  The lab reports are not hard to do if you can do high school chemistry lab you should be fine.  Her quiz were not hard, I studyed before the class and still pulled an A.  But take every point as a life-value if you want to do well.

This "new" lab format sucks, lab reports are graded harshly, make sure you know why EVERYTHING was done during the lab, oh ya and good luck with the spec. test, all you get is a 2 hour lecture on the stuff, I don't know anyone doing well in this lab. What a waste.

The lab is so pointless.  You will always do the same things over and over again.  lab grading is tough.  Lab reports are due for EVERY SINGLE Experiment done and are such a WASTE of TIME.  Not to mention that it is TWICE a week for 3 hr. each time!!!!
A Very tough teacher for Orgo II. Take Dolbier or Enholm instead. Avoid this teacher unless your only other choice is Portmess!!

Lets face it Orgo is not easy but Davidson does her best to make it interesting and she is great at explaining things! She gives more than enough time for you to see her in office hours and when the class grade drops she comes up with fun extra credit ideas like worksheets. GREAT PROFESSOR!
good teacher

She is a great teacher, but her grading is horrible.  She doesn't curve.  According to people who have taken her class in the past, her tests are becomming harder and almost as difficult as her husbands, Portmess: he at least curves.  Avg. first test: 77 second test: 65.  No curve and little extra credit.

She an amazing teacher...one of the best lecturers...very organized, and makes the subject material as easy to understand as anyone can.  The material is tough by nature, but study hard, go to class, and go to her for help (which she is always willing to give) and you should at least get a B.
She is such a mom, i love it! haha. Take her class, do what she tells you to do, and work hard. You'll get an A.

Dr. Davidson is an amazing professor. She's extremely nice and explains everything well. Class is hard, but the total grade average in the class was a 78% which is extremely high. You do not have to study everyday to get an A...but if you study hard and do all your hw, while understanding the concepts you can get an A. Go to office hours

Great orgo teacher, but still a VERY hard class to get a good grade in. She does not curve, but her tests are supposed to be easier. She gives a lot of extra credit. Study 1-2 hours EVERY day in order to pass organic with any teacher. Weekends too. If you get behind, you will be sorry. I got an A in this class because I studied day and night

first of all, it is organic so by nature is IS difficult, but not as much as ppl think - try to memorize and you'll fail for sure, she is easily THE BEST TEACHER I'VE HAD AT UF AND I HOPE TO GOD SHE TEACHES ORGO 2. take her if you can b/c her office hours are good,she really cares about us and wants u to understand -JUST DO THE HW AND PRACTICE EXAM

I love this lady!  She's such a mom.  Very helpful and exams are modeled after practice exams. Exams are still difficult.  Keep up with the homework and go to office hours! Pop quizzes (not bad if you've been keeping up with the material  on your own). She's super friendly and funny. Best organic professor to take!  Anyone will confirm.

Even though I love chemistry, the class was hard. But Dr. Davidson definitely knows what she is talking about and was very clear and helful. Her office hours are very good and she wants us to pass but she also expects us to put forth effort. She is the best teacher to have or organic.
I think you've just gotta love this soccer mom with a chemistry degree...she's a good person, explains things well, and doesn't really try to trick you on tests

dont let these people fool you.  this class is insanely hard and davidson is NOT the best professor.  portmess is a much better lecturer and if you pay attention you will be fine.  DO NOT TAKE DAVIDSON OR YOU WILL FAIL.
Great Teacher!!! Provides practice exams and is very reasonable.  Very helpful in office hours too!  Makes Organic Chemistry doable!
Her tests were pretty easy except for the final which was a pretty hard.Her lectures were very clear and she is very helpful.Best organic 2 prof.Take her!

Incredible class! My favorite one so far.
Professor Emerson knows exactly what he's doing to keep his students engaged. The lectures are all memorable but the line isn't drawn there... the supplemental videos are also incredible for learning. 
Wish I could write more, but I have to get back to reading haha. ALOT of reading. But it's great!!!

You can tell he genuinely loves the subject matter and teaching it to his class. I relied on the SN for 95% of this class, skimmed the LSB and Barrons pages, and made sure I had an index ready for each exam. I did not do the paper, BUT I did grind every single practice problem during the days leading up to the exams. DO THE PRACTICE PROBLEMS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I only used the LSB and Smokin Notes to create my index. If you do the extra credit and term paper you should easily be able to get a B, at the minimum. Do all the practice problems he gives since they're similar to the exam. Very passionate professor who wants you to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I only read the LSB and watched the lectures, no Smokin' Notes. I also did the term paper which helps a lot. Emerson is an awesome professor, you can tell he really cares about TEACHING not just memorizing. If you can go in person, please do! He puts so much effort into the lectures (about 3 costume changes/class) which is really refreshing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I listened to some of Emerson's lectures for the first exam and they are quite entertaining, but reading the LSB and Smokin Notes is enough to do well on exams. Do every practice problem to study for the exams, and DO THE TERM PAPER as it makes the end of the semester easy if you score well on the first two exams. He also curves exam grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I never read either textbook or watched the lectures. All I did was study the Smokin' Notes in the days leading up to the exam and make an index. I would only do a handful of the practice questions because I would always run out of time. DO NOT ATTEMPT THIS. Smokin' Notes and the practice questions definitely help. Can't speak to Emerson obviously.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He cares about what he teaches, which makes the material easier to digest. The more you read, the better you will do. Be warned—his final exam is markedly harder than the other exams, and the practice material does not prepare you for this. Hindsight being what it is, I should have done the term paper, so I recommend it.

This class isn't too bad if you have smokin notes. For the first exam, I would say to read the textbook and smokin notes to get the basics. However, for exam 2, I relied only on smokin notes and practice problems and I did fine. The third exam is definitely the hardest. DO THE TERM PAPER AND EXTRA CREDIT. It will save your grade.

I'm a finance major and took this at the same time as BFI (insane, I know). It's not half as bad as I was expecting. Emerson is phenomenal- he is so generous with curving every test and is so open to helping you if you have questions. DO THE PAPER & EXTRA CREDIT!! They grade it very nicely and you can slack off a bit for exam 3.

difficult but by no means impossible to do well. if you're willing to start prepping for exams at least a week in advance, and do ALL the reading, practice, and extra credit, this is a very achievable A or B. just don't take it in combination with a lot of other hard classes, as it requires so much time and focus to get through and comprehend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't listen to what other people are saying. I dont have smokin notes. All I do is read the LSB and watch his lectures, and I'll end with an A. DO THE TERM PAPER- its graded easily and will save your grade. Emerson is so nice, curves every test, and really cares about students. He's also passionate about what he teaches, which is rare nowadays.

Emerson writes his own textbooks, so if you aren't understanding his lectures, reading his textbook is going to do you no justice. The lectures never seemed to hold my attention and the reading was extremely hard to understand because it was all in his words (which make absolutely zero sense).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Emerson's class is challenging but engaging. His energetic lectures make the material interesting, though the exams are tough. Studying diligently and utilizing resources like Smokin Notes and unstuckstudy can really help. Overall, a rewarding course if you're willing to put in the work.

Extremely overcomplicated class with waaaaay too much material. People say you MUST study/prep for days, use Studyedge, make notes, etc. Well I didn't, and I passed with a D lol

Unless you love business law and want to spend many many hours just to get a b on the exam, I'd say take the GPA hit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The most difficult class I have ever taken
Awesome professor! Really fun lectures which make the subject matter a lot more interesting. Only grades outside of extra credit are three exams tho so I would do the term paper to boost my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class a lot! Really energetic professor and shows how passionate he is. Lectures are long so I used Smokin Notes to cut down study time and they really helped. Overall great course if you space out your studying 5 days before exams and do all extra credit papers.

The most important materials in this class are the LSB and BL textbook; those are all you need to pass. Professor Emerson is eccentric, but he is still an engaging lecturer that I would still recommend everyone watch his lectures. His passion is so contagious I almost tricked myself into thinking I wanted to go to law school.
This is one of the few professors here at UF who actually is passionate about what they do but also genuinely cares about the student's success.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: I love learning about law. Prof. Emerson goes out of his way to be accessible, make the content enjoyable, and to prep you for the exams. That being said, the exams are challenging, even for someone who loves law.  Study daily. Go beyond memorizing definitions to truly understand what the questions are asking you. Go to office hours and chat.

THE WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD. He dresses up for every class, plays music during his lectures, and dances around while teaching. This was so distracting that I couldn't even watch his lectures. He grades on 3 tests (which are BEYOND difficult and confusing). DO THE EX CREDIT! I had smokin notes (which barely helped). Goodluck!

The class is heavily based on the LSB textbook, which is extremely hard and complicated to read. 

He makes his tests over complicated and extremely confusing. DO THE TERM PAPER! It will replace your lowest exam score and the extra credit can boost up your grade by 2 points. 

Overall, the content was not very useful to me, but rather interesting.

The content is meaningless unless you're interested in law and he makes his exams over complicated for no reason. It is such a shame business students have to take this class because there are so many that are more beneficial.
I graduated 2 years ago and I still think about Professor Emerson all the time. He turned a tedious, boring subject into a fun class to look forward to. If you have the chance, take a class with him.

This class was a lot easier than I thought it would be. I didn't read the LSB, watch the lectures or do the optional paper and still got a B+. I read the Smokin Notes and did 300 practice questions 2-3 days before the exam. With a bit more effort, I could've easily gotten an A or A-. Every exam was curved by 8-10%.

There are ONLY 3 exams that determine your grade. The amount of work that you put in will not reflect in the outcome. By far, one of the worst classes I've had to take. His system is not beneficial and unless you are a good test taker, you will struggle in this course.
10/10 prof. Makes the class very fun. Tests are open note/book. Definitely recommend taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
This class scared me going in due to
Not being the greatest test taker. I did all the extra credit and did horrible on 2 of the exams and still passed with a D due to the extra credit. The class is doable even for bad test takers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Don't give in to the hype. This class is not as difficult as it is made out to be. 

As entertaining as the lectures are, I personally did not learn from them very well. You will be much better off reading the textbooks/smokinnotes. 

Finished with an A, and I am not usually an A student. As long as you put forth the effort, you can do it.

I'm going to be 100% honest, this is a difficult class but not impossible. GET SMOKIN NOTES, I would've not passed if it weren't for SN. DO THE PRACTICE QUESTIONS!!!! Begin studying a week in advance. I would've probably gotten an A had I not studied only 4 days in advance. DO THE EXTRA TERM PAPER. I promise it will save you!!! It is possible!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing prof, grades very leniently and really does want you to succeed. I truly don't understand why this class has such a bad reputation, I learned so much and prof is very reasonable. 10/10 would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: loved this class tbh. lots of reading yes, but manageable if you stick to a reading schedule. the material is interesting which makes it easy to remember and exam questions (open book) are straight from the textbooks. didn't watch the lectures (sorry professor) and got over 100 on every exam. do the term paper though so you can relax for exam 3
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is not as bad as it's made out to be. I didn't open the textbooks until the day of the exams and relied solely on Smokin Notes, giving myself about two days to read them prior to the tests (i am lazy). Those saying you need to read every assigned page to do well are delusional. I also did not write the term paper nor do the extra cred.

BEWARE OF THE THIRD EXAM. The third exam is nothing like the first two, WAY harder. Professor Emerson gives you the opportunity to write a term paper that replaces your lowest exam score, DO IT! He also provides 2 points of extra credit. The exam questions are very long and difficult, but not impossible. Really tough class, but doable.

3 Exams that are the only "mandatory" assignments. I'd advise that you NEED to do the extra credit term-paper, it's graded very easy and accounts for lowest test grade. He's a very enthusiastic person but the funny lectures don't really help. The reading is rough and never-ending... exam questions are confusing. The LSB is the only book needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have never met a professor as dedicated to teaching as Professor Emerson. He wears (multiple) costumes EVERY lecture to provide tons of hilarious examples to supplement the reading. The class is difficult- but there are 3 extra credit papers, and the exams are completely open note. However, you still should do the practice problems to do well.

Professor Emerson is a very-straightforward professor. His expectations for the class are clearly outlined within the first week of the semester. The course uses two primary textbooks; all exam questions come from these. He provides an extensive exam review and offers extra credit as well. The class is structured around three exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Straight up lies. Will say you do not have to take the final and give you a zero. I asked him personally to clarify that not taking the exam would not affect my grade and he told me not to worry about taking it. Tanked my grade/ GPA, putting me on academic probation. Doesn't help that he's so boring, hard to contact, and the course is old/ useless.

He is a great professor and there is no denying in that. Going to the lectures is completely optional but I would recommend for the fun. The readings are heavy, so have a very clear schedule to read every day! DO THE PAPER! It helps a lot to relax for the third exam, which is the hardest. Read the book and do the practice problems and you're good!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did Smokin Notes and worked practice problems. With term paper replacing lowest exam score made an A easily. He is funny and entertaining. I personally do not think this class is nearly as hard as its made out to be. Just put effort in the right places. Beware he will ask randomly detailed questions about what he talked about a specific lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this class. Professor Emerson is really fun. He likes to dress up and be silly and it makes the class really engaging. If you do the readings, prepare for exams, and do the optional paper, you'll do great in this class. It's really not that hard as long as you dedicate the time to learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He keeps lectures fun and unique. Tests are kinda hard but open note so I recommend marking your textbooks with tabs to easily find material. He curves exams quite a bit!

Professor Emerson is a captivating lecturer and someone who truly cares for his students. The entire class is based on 2 books he wrote, which are not easy reads. Each exam is based on roughly 300 pages of reading. Professor Emerson makes everything memorable by adding costumes and crazy scenarios to keep ideas in your head.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honest Review. Very great and understanding professor. Grading instructions were clear. Your success depends on your ability to take tests and how good you are at remembering what you read. I never read that much and this class is about 200 pages per exam. I did not do well on the exams. I did all the practice questions and term paper as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Two extra credit opportunities and one exam replacement opportunity, DO THEM! They are all graded easy. Exams are very hard. Read the LSB textbook and do the practice questions those help the most lectures arent that helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is challenging! You can't cram the material for the exam! I read the 200+ pages, watched his lectures and bought Smokin notes and did all his test practice questions and still found the exam to be difficult! The first exam is the easiest exam so do everything possible to get a good grade on that exam! Also do the Extra credit paper!

This class turned out both easier and more interesting that I anticipated. LSB/lectures are solid but not necessary. I read the smokin' notes and grinded out the practice exams about a week before each exam and got an A. DO the term paper. Its graded easy and takes out your lowest exam grade.

All you need to get a good grade in this class is a clear grasp of the LSB. The other book and his lectures aren't very helpful. Only 3 exams. Open note, so summarize the LSB into an index of topics. Dr. Emerson's lectures are interesting but aren't particularly helpful on Exam day (2-3 questions maybe). Summarize the LSB and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great class and extremely beneficial if you plan on doing just about anything in the business world. I do not recommend watching the lectures but get ready to read A LOT. Each exam is based on over 200 pages worth of reading and exams are very difficult, write the extra credit essay or you will be in trouble.

Must read the LSB to get an A. Highlight as you read and tab the book so you can find things during the exam. Do the term paper. It is very easy and doesn't even have to be that good to get a high score. Will save you from a lot of stress going into exam 3. Lectures are not important to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: WORST CLASS IVE EVER TAKEN total grade is only 3 exams. Im not a bad test taker but this professor has the hardest exams. He says he isnt trying to trick you but he is. The questions are long & hard and the answers are confusing. Do the term paper and the extra credit, even though the extra credit is only 2 points total it helps. AVOID IF POSSIBLE

Be ready to read, read, and read. His questions are oddly specific and confusing and the practice exams are just a glimpse of the actual exam, however, the real exam is way more difficult. DO the paper! I regret not doing it, scored an 88 and 91 on the first two exams and the 3rd exam is the hardest, got a 68 and ended up with a B+ :( do the EC!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He understand that this class is hard, so he gives extra credit. Honestly how all professors should be. You definitely have to read the LSB because the exam questions are tricky.

Fun professor, but the LSB and lectures were too confusing to learn from. Reading the Smokin'Notes and grinding out the practice problems about 1-2 weeks before the exam was enough to secure an A, without any extra credit. Also, he curves his exams by a RIDICULOUS amount, making it hard to fail this class, as long as you keep up with the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: My approach was to read the smokin notes several times and create an alphabetical index of important terms and topics with a brief definition and a page number for reference. The tests are difficult but building an index and then doing as many practice questions as possible is the key. Dont do the smokin notes practice questions, they wont help!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Emerson clearly knows what he's talking about, but he's so all over the place. Just use smokin notes packets to study and definitely read LSB and Barron. Those three are what is key to getting a good grade. Also do the optional term paper (replaced lowest exam score!) and EC. The EC took me from the B+ to an A-, and it took only like an hour to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lecture style is very funny, unorthodox and unique and consists of him acting like a duck, dancing in costumes and playing music. Grading is 3 conditionally-weighted open book/note exams, optional term paper and 2 EC papers. If you want to do the optional writing stuff, treat it as a 4K word class. Exams are tricky and kinda hard but he curves.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor who wants students to pass. There are 3 open book/notes exams. Your highest exam score is worth 45%, your next highest is worth 35%, and your lowest is worth 20%. Offers an optional term paper to replace a test grade and other extra credit. Mainly focus on reading the textbook (LSB) which he offers a free and youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I understand law is not meant to be easy; however, every exam has about 200+ pages worth of material and the questions are LOADED, ABSOLUTELY LOADED, with technicalities meant to trick you. Sure, he may SAY he's not trying to trick you, buuuut that's not true. The lectures? A circus. They're all smoke and mirrors. By FAR the worst class I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Whatever you do, just write the term paper. Do not walk into this course thinking you can study immensely and ace the exams. The exams are difficult, and the questions can frequently be up for interpretation. I HIGHLY recommend to take this class in the summer because I most likely would've failed under heavy course load. Term paper  peace of mind
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This teacher seems like he wants to help you until you thinkhow are you helping someone who Is a bad test taker? This class is test heavy there are only 3 exams and they are basically the entire weight of the class. The exams are 5 multiple choice and are paragraphs. There were too many lectures, and were distracting because he acts in them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really fun class!! You need to read the LSB religiously, you can skip Barron's but I would still buy/rent it so you can use it on the exams. Check every question on the exams with the LSB and Barron's. Making an index for the exam is helpful. Do the paper if you can. If you're a good writer it'll be a breeze and you'll replace an exam!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: READ. It's a very fun class, he is a great teacher but you really have to read both the LSB and Barron books. If you read the chapters before watching the lectures and do the practice exams you should be fine.

He is a very eccentric man, so what you might have heard is most likely true. All you really need to to do is read his LSB or if your lazier the smokin' notes. Do both extra credits and the term paper. You should pass and if you put in minimal effort get an A. He is a very nice guy and if you are considering law school it's a fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: at first, I was REALLY thrown-off by how... off-the-wall this guy is. but after a few lectures, I started to enjoy his lectures. read first, watch the lecture, do some practice questions, rinse and repeat. offers a term paper which can replace your lowest test score, which is AWESOME.

READ THE LSB, have an index, and do the practice questions. I honestly only watched a few lectures to clarify some topics but Emerson genuinely puts in effort to make it entertaining. Also, the content actually seems like it will be helpful in life. It is a lot of reading but I've enjoyed it. Grade is based on 3 exams and a few extra credit items.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The material can be interesting, and reading is a MUST. Lectures were over-the-top theatrical performances. Some may like this style, but it was very distracting for me. Topical lectures are a must though too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof Emerson's theatrical performances are the highlight of this class. This guy is so goofy, but that's what makes this class so great. I find law rlly boring, but Prof Emerson was just SO hilarious. He can sing, he can dance, he can teach. He REALLY enjoys his job, and you can tell. Exams are hard, but read the LSB and Barron's and it'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He teaches an undergraduate business law class but treats it as a graduate level law class. Most of his questions are based purely on technicalities, so ensure you read the question closely before rushing an answer. Do ALL of the practice questions assigned for each exam. He is a tough professor that assigns a lot of material but it is doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Truly cares about his students and gives you many resources to succeed. Read the book, use smokin notes and do the extra credit and you should get an A. All tests are open note open book but you have to read the material ahead of time because the tests are long.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dont bother going to class because he will just be putting on a theatrical performance. Get smokin notes and read the small sections of the textbook in his syllabus. Your grade is 3 exams, open book & notes, but you gotta understand the concepts to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Emerson is crazy with his costumes, but the lectures are entertaining. He is brilliant and eccentric, so it's difficult to understand what he is talking about. But if you go to class, take good notes, and read the textbook, it will all make sense! I did this, the term paper and the extra credit and I got like a 98.6 in the class. Very possible!

This class is definitely doable. Make sure you read the whole LSB and do every single practice exam question he offers. I only studied for 7-10 days before each exam and earned a B+ in this class. Skip the lectures and just read! You will not be successful without reading the whole LSB. I really did learn a lot in this class in the end. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Emerson is the best professor I've had at UF. He really loves the class and it shows during his lectures. While he is a bit eccentric, there is a method to his madness. You HAVE to read both textbooks to get an A. The smokin' notes are a good supplement but don't cover anywhere near all the material. While the exams are open note, they are not easy

His lectures are USELESS and composed of him dressed in unnecessary costumes skipping around like an elf. His textbooks have no coherency and make it exceptionally difficult to study. Don't expect to learn anything in this class. (1) Do every practice question, (2) classify trick questions by topic, (3) find similar questions on the exam.

I took this class over 10 years ago and still find myself able to mentally pull up things we learned. The content is incredibly useful in the real world (if you pursue business or entrepreneurship) and Emerson's ability to contextualize the information when I took class really has helped the material stick.

Avoid this guy. He spends lectures dancing around like an idiot instead of teaching. I had to use every ounce of strength to avoid Mike Tysoning my laptop because of his cringiness. He writes the books which are equally confusing. Must read every page and do practice Qs to get a respectable grade. Exams are tough, do the EC and research paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Reading the LSB is awful and painful to read. It's so confusing and his test are very tricky. I would not have taken this teacher if I didn't have to. He needs to re-structure his class. I feel like it could have been a great class, if it were taught by someone else. He might be a nice guy, but he's not a good teacher. Plain and simple.

Emerson is highly energetic, literally dancing around the room during lectures. There are two books to be READ, not skimmed, and you need to watch the class lectures and topical lectures to be ready for the exam. You can write a term paper to replace your lowest exam grade. Very heavy on reading, but exams are open notes, open book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Funny guys and his skits make the class entertaining, but there is little preparation for the very tough exams. No matter how much you study, knowing how to navigate the LSB is critical to passing exams. Many tricks on tests. Get ready

Don't get me wrong, he's a hilarious guy and all, but poor teacher. I would of learned nothing from this course if it wasn't for the LSB and Barron's books. Please just read the books first and if you want something entertaining after... watch the lectures. Another old teacher who goes off on tangents instead of teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is very disorganized but the Smoking Notes help a ton. The exams being open note doesn't mean that they are by any means easy. The class is interesting but if you don't need it don't take it. ALSO, WRITE THE PAPER IT WILL SAVE YOUR LIFE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. The class is extremely difficult, and the entire grade relies on exams. Watch all the lectures and read ahead, and you can do relatively well. He promises no trick questions, which I won't way I completely believe, but overall, exams are fairly written and fairly graded. HUGE curves are also a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Just read the LSB AND the Barrons. His grading scale with extra credit is very very generous. Very eccentric, but great at engaging students who want to learn the material. Read each exam question carefully bc usually there is one crucial detail that people miss. Lots of reading, but one solid read through the textbooks should be enough studying.

Emerson is an odd professor since lectures are only him dancing around the place. Don't expect to go to lectures and learn something. Exams are hard, and require extensive hours reading the LSB, and going over scenarios. He is nice, and his TA's are as well. Honestly you teach yourself in this course. Read Read Read!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: By far, the best professor I've ever had. The guy is simply born to teach, and he absolutely loves doing it. With that said, it is extremely difficult, so don't expect this open notes, open book class that's graded entirely off exams to be easy. Your likelihood of an A may be relatively low, but it is possible with reading and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: In this class, you have to read there is no escaping it! - Skim the LSB first. Then reread it. You want to read the LSB 2-3 times(sounds crazy but you have to) - Refer to the Barrons for clarification because the LSB can be a bit confusing - Do every single practice question 2-3 times - He curved our exams heavy(1st exam - 13 points; 2nd-17 points)
Emerson is a great and caring teacher. This class is reading heavy, but it's totally do-able. He's a great professor and tries to engage the class. Would definitely take again, super nice guy.

This class is easy in the sense that there is no hw, just study for tests. But this class is hard because the tests are extremely difficult to pass. Emerson does curve the heck out of the tests which is a life saver, and DO THE PAPER because you are almost guaranteed to fail at least one exam. I only used SN and finished with a C. Read LSB for B/A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Get ready to read for this class because if you read the textbook then you should do fine on your exams. There is extra credit it this class which helps. Make sure to do the paper that can replace your lowest test grade which will help with your grade. I cannot stress enough read the textbook and get Smokin Notes for the exam and you should do well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I found it really difficult to do well in the class. He is a nice guy, but his lectures are extremely hard to follow. He tells a lot of stories and dresses up in outfits that do not correlate with the material very well. I had to stop watching lecture because it was a waste of time. The tests are very difficult even though they are open notes.

Amazing professor overall. Goes out of his way to make law as interesting as possible and clearly cares about his students. Emerson is one of those people that you look at and it's just obvious they were born to teach. Watch the lectures (I watched on 1.4x speed mostly), read the texts, and do practice problems and you should be golden.

The way Emerson teaches (using props, skits, etc.) is very unconventional. It might help some students learn better but it just made it hard for me to take the class seriously. I didn't watch lectures but read the books/supplements and got Smokin' Notes. Tests are open-book and open-note which helps. Make sure to tab your books!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Emerson is not like any other professor. He enjoys the course and uses it to play dress up, yes seriously. His intention is to make the class fun. There are only 3 exams, a term paper replaces your lowest grade and two other papers for extra credit at 1 point each. No homework. Lots to read! If you work hard you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The worst professor we've had so far in the MBA program. He does not really teach during class and instead dresses up and puts on skits. He is disorganized and does not clearly define his expectations for the course even though he has a 12 page syllabus. When you email him outside of class he does not really answer your questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Funniest professor you will ever meet. Made this horrible hard boring class much better. Prepare to read the most you every had in your life. That is what it takes to pass this class. Read that whole LSB. What I did is read all the chapters, highlight important sentences, and then re-read those important sentences every single night until test.

Open book, open note exams but don't let that fool you. Exams are difficult if you don't read the books. DO THE PAPER, it replaces your lowest test score which can really make a difference in your grade. Emerson is a very... eccentric guy. Watched lectures at 2x speed. Stopped watching lectures half way through semester and just read the texts.

OK this class is difficult. If you don't like to read you won't do well. There is so much reading involved- the textbook is crucial! How to study: Read AHEAD, watch lectures only if you have time, DO the practice problems- they are very similar to the questions on the actual exam!! He offers extra credit and an optional term paper

This class has easily been the most beneficial class I have taken at UF so far. The lectures shouldn't be your priority but the "Law, Society, and Business" text is CRUCIAL. This text is actually very interesting and well written (by Emerson). Test tips: 1Read the LSB 2 Make your own detailed index 3 DO THE OLD TEST QUESTIONS 4 Use given index

Emerson is peculiar.  He has very theatrical lectures, and you honestly don't need to watch them.  Gotta have the books because tests are open book, and I got Smokin Notes and they were fantastic.  Just study the smokin notes and use the textbook indexes during the exams and you should be good.

Hate the way he teaches. Props, skits, short movies. Teaching style is not organized and hard to follow. Since he wrote the textbooks, his books are presented the way he teaches, which is scatterbrained. Ugh.

This class is pretty easy to get at least a B+ in, considering as of spring '16 he started offering extra credit (do it!), the extra credit can easily bring you up one letter grade if not two! Also like other people said, do the term paper because it really is not hard and easy to get at least an 85%+ replacing a poor exam score.

Step 1: READ THE ENTIRE BOOK. (LSB)   Step 2: Don't watch the lectures. If you do watch lectures, read the book FIRST.  Step 3: DO ALL OF THE PRACTICE QUESTIONS.   Step 4: Write the term paper. Seriously just do it, I got a 100 on it.   I got 95 on the first two exams, 100 on the term paper, and I skipped the final. Easy peasy
Long lectures, need to read the book and understand the material. Application test questions. Open book and open notes exam. Books are a must for this class if you want to pass.

He's entertaining for sure but I also stopped watching lectures after the first exam. They are just too distracting and don't relay enough info in a straightforward way. Read both textbooks inside and out, tab like crazy, definitely do the optional term paper, and you will be fine. It is absolutely possible to get an A, but you have to work for it.

Class is confusing. He uses a lot of different outfits to help us learn, but ends up being a distraction. Extra credit paper that was supposed to be helpful unless you have a bad grader. If you are able to take another class than this, DO IT.

Emerson is a very eccentric guy. I stopped watching lectures after the first exam. His lectures did not help me and all of the costumes and theatrics were kinda distracting. Just readoutline the books and you'll be fine. DO THE PAPER! The paper is an easy A and will replace your lowest test score!

The only grades in class are 3 test and there are no additional grades counted towards your average. He will drop a test with a highest paper grade for 20% of your grade. Test are almost impossible to pass. His lectures are hard to follow along because he dresses up and doesn't go in order. I was incredibly excited to take this class.
I really enjoyed the class

Make sure you read both books and listen to his lecture. That's the only way you can get an A. Smokin notes will help you understand things, but don't rely on that. His practice exams are different from his actual exam. I thought the lecture was actually interesting.
Very difficult class. You need to read a lot and study hard to pass. The professor uses multiple costumes in class, uses music and acts to provide live examples of the concepts he is teaching.

To get to the point, you HAVE to read both textbooks. He's not a bad professor, but the nature of the subject matter means that you have to read A LOT to get an A. Don't expect Smokin' Notes to be sufficient either. Do practice exams, go to class, start reading books two-three weeks in advance and you should get an A. Oh, and do the term paper!
This guy is great. Costumes master. Class was very interesting, gives you insight on various aspects of law surrounding business. Recommended.
He likes to play dress up in class and show unrelated home videos of him acting.  Final was open note but closed book and very tricky.  Better read the text multiple times.
Of my entire college experience he is by far my favorite professor

Emerson is a fantastic professor. Easily my favorite at UF. Watch/go to class he makes it extremely fun. I still go around telling Emerson anecdotes. Reading both the LSB and Barrons book is a must prior to the exam. Test questions are very specific but doable. Go to class, read LSB, read Barrons, highlight & PQs should set you up well. I got an A-
Very easy class. Got really high watched "A Few Good Men" never read the book or attended the class. Got an A-. "You can't handle the truth"

Very hard class. The exams are extremely hard. He swears the exams are not meant to trick you, but in reality thy are. Make sure you read the book, not once but several times and study, study, study it's the only way you'll pass the class. Past exam material isn't really that helpful.
Tests are way too confusing and hard. He makes it that way on purpose. You'll read and read and you even get to use your book on your exam but you will likely still fail

The test are SOOO confusing and he purposely make's it that way. Test are really hard and you have to read an incredible amount of material. Out of 160 pages each exam we read anything could be on the exam. Again, class is really hard old exam problems don't help that much you just have to read and understand the book.

Class is REALLY hard, especially if your a business major because you have law students taking this course as an elective which they have the upper hand though Emerson's grading scale is fair but class requires alot of work and you have to read about 750 pages of readings.. Very analytical test questions not easy at all.

One of the better courses I've taken in college thus far. There is no doubt that Prof. Emerson is a looney, but he knows how to teach and keep it interesting. You will need the LSB. The Barron's helps reinforce concepts if needed, and provides a strong glossary and index. Just keep up and practice with the old exam ?s.
Can't say enough about Emerson. Keeps you awake during lecture, hilarious. Study hard. You'll get a ton out of this class.

Emerson is crazy but his lectures are interesting. Read every page of the textbook if you want to do well on tests. Tests are open note and open book so be familiar with the book and organize your notes. Not an easy class but you will learn a lot and if you keep up with reading and lectures you will do well. Not recommended for lazy people.
Professor Emerson's class is fun!  His tests are open book/ open note, but do not be fooled!  You need to know the material.

He uses the books A LOT as he wrote them :p Very smart guy, but tries too hard to be kooky and I found it more distracting than entertaining. Expect a lot of reading, printing, highlighting, and tabbing.

Requires a lot of studying, but he makes the material interesting. Use a highlighter in your book and bookmark everything!   I really enjoyed his class, even though he's a Baltimore Ravens fan.  Go Steelers!

Professor Emerson is amazing. His passion for the law is contagious and coupled with this passion is his vast knowledge which he conveys to his students in an entertaining fashion. I ended up with a B+ in the class but I was also studying abroad and did not dedicate as much time as I could have. If you go to class and read the book you will be fine

Very... different. Sometimes funny, sometimes just annoying. But reading the LSB text is a MUST. Barron's book just used as a reference. Shouldn't miss the lectures! Use tabs to label things in your book!!!! Test are open book so familiarity w/ location of material is key. Overall a pretty fun class which I learned a lot from.

Prof. Emerson is arguably an acquired taste.  His style, and outlandishness, might turn some off.  But if you allow yourself get past, or even into, the theatrics, there is a vast amount of learning to be had. The tests are not easy, but if you read, keep up with lectures, and put the time in, you can perform well, while learning valuable info.

Awful professor. Really likes to hear himself talk. Does not really teach so much as tells stories to the class. Interesting material, but the professor is a clown. In a bad way. I loathe watching his lectures

Watch the lectures and keep up in the book and BAM you have at least a B. Not a difficult class (as upperclassmen we've had much worse), so no one should complain. It was a breath of fresh air to have Emerson, and I'm happy to be graduating on a high note from UF! Really enjoyed the class. It will be helpful later on in life! :)

Such a great professor and great guy! Not the easiest class I've ever taken and not a subject I thought I would have any interest in at all, but it's the first time I was actually a little bit sad to end the class. I really enjoyed this class. Take this professor!

Awesome professor, keeps you interested in lecture. The Smokin Notes did not help me at all. When I stopped using smokin notes and started watching lecture, highlighting book and reading the barrons book I got a 93 on the exam. When I used smokin notes I got a 65 and 68. Just my opinion, but look at the suggestions on how to study and use that!
Most entertaining class I have ever taken!!  Very interesting material!!  You will not be bored in this class.
Book is riddled with errors, it reads like an encyclopedia.  Random words spelled wrong in the book

This was one of my least favourite instructors.  The class has interesting information but you have to teach it to yourself because the instructor dances and acts out juvenile skits most of the class time.

Great class. You should read most if not all of the assigned readings. Exams are highly analytical, so you must understand the material. Prof. Emerson was very entertaining, I went to the live lectures.

Asset to UF. Very intelligent Harvard grad, understands the law.  His exams are much like what you will find in law school, challenging the very principles in the search for the "grey".  Would recommend to anyone up for a challenge or does not care about their grade.
Great class.  Best I've ever taken.  Puts his all into it.
WOW! WOW! Hard! Interesting Class! You will learn a lot BUT smoking notes DO NOT HELP, and the test are open book, and most people fail. HARD!

This class definitely requires effort. You should read most of the required reading prior to the test. While people mostly complain about the trickiness, you have to realize this going in - the slightest detail (left in or left out) changes the outcome of a situation. This class is do-able.

Horrible teacher(?). Vague, pompous, ostentatious, self-absorbed. Law is an inexact science and he uses it to veil his incompetence. He must be smart - he went to Harvard - gimme a break! The text is no help - HE WROTE IT - it reads like he lectures; fractured, pseudo-allegorical and purposefully disjointed (so it’s useless during open-book test).

Interesting individual, went to Harvard. Honestly, I don't think he's a good teacher because he expects us to be those in Harvard maybe. I did much better not listening to his lectures. Don't let his costumes fool you. His exams are difficult and confusing, do not listen to lectures, will confuse you more, just study notes and texts.
hmm just read the book. lectures are a waste
Great Class.  Best at UF

Excellent instructor. Honestly, if you put the effort and READ your textbooks (which you can use for tests) then getting a B should be no problem at all. Emerson is extremely interesting and I look forward to more courses instructed by him. If you sign up for this course NOT interested in the material, just don't take it. BUL4310 is for lovers.

I don't even think a lawyer could get an A. I barely made a C.  He seems nuts but is a great teacher, very very helpful more so than any other UF teacher I've had.  Tests are extremely difficult even though its open book, if you don't know the answer good luck finding it.  If you had all day to take it you might get an A.

Wonderful class.  Even gave out comprehensive notes to lectures.  returns phone calls promptly; answers all e-mails, and even sends congratulatory e-mails, while having 700 students!  Funny, interesting, informative lectures.  Wish other professors put in even 1/10 the effort he does.

Don't bother with lectures; just a huge waste of time. Pointless associations of practically everything with a legal topic. Every other test question is a trick question. Quizzes are filled with errors and trick questions.

This class was actually pretty good.  Nowhere near the difficulty these whiners say.  I'm set for an A without any Herculean effort.  I wish his lectures stayed more to the material and less to his theatrics.  Very helpful-called me back to answer questions about the material and sent emails to congratulate high scores on exams.

HARD AS HELL!!! A lot of reading, very long exams. Like the others have said, only take it if you have to. You learn a lot, but there is also a lot of stress. Everyone fails the test of gets a high D so don't get down on yourself.
Great class and prof.

dont take this class even if you wanna go to law school. he's pointless and flounces the fact that he's from HARVARD...this class (and emerson) is full of bull****. BUL-SHIT...test make no sese...but wait, he's funny?
Very tedious class. Take it only if you have to.

This class made me want to beat my face in on concrete. I wouldn't have minded the million and a half pages of reading if the professor wasn't such an arrogant jerk. i didn't do too bad in the class due to the 20 point curves since the whole class failed most of the exams. Horrible experience. just horrible. don't take it unless you have to!!!
Excellent Prof.  Has won about a dozen teacher of the year awards.
Bad class, made me want to quit college.

Overall a very good professor. Everyone knows he is a nut though. He dances and prances like a fruitcake every class to demonstrate his points. While I admire his enthusiasm, a lot of it is a bit much, and is just a waste of your time. Study hard, do the crazy ammount of papers and reading, and you'll do well and learn a lot while you're at it.
Great class!  Best at UF

Worst class I've ever taken @UF. Can't figure out what the foolishness in the lectures has to do with law. Disorganized, late with grades, always making excuses. You're held to deadlines, but the teacher and TAs never meet theirs.Have to write 6000+ words, and grade 30000+ words worth of other student's work. Avoid this class if you can.
Best Prof Ever!  Take this class and experience a unique, gifted teacher.
Best Prof I have everhad, by far!
Great Prof!

Most of the negative recommendations on this site tend to be too extreme.However in the case of Emerson they are actually pretty accurate, the man is totally consumed with himself and really an arrogant bast**d which is really something I do not say lightly. His antics get old after the first class. People used TZ notes so made the test impossible.
No Comments

The class assignments are explained clearly.I only went to class for the first part of the semester.I never watched the classes.I did all of the CWs and got a B+ in the class.His teaching methods are interesting, although not appealing to everyone.However, he told those that attended class they would get EC, but all he did was add it into the CW's.
Never watched class, bought smoking notes, getting a B in the class.  He is truly an ass, and the head TA was horrible as well.  Really nothing good to say about this class!
This guy is an arrogant idiot.  He dances around and waste student's time when he should be teaching.  The class wouldn't be bad if he weren't so frickin terrible.
class was horrible
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
i got mostly D's on his tests even though i studied my ass off. when he says open book, its like a joke. but DO THE COURSEWORK b/c i ended up with almost a B+ b/c of it
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

He's full of antics but pay attention, and follow his lectures along in the LSB text. He goes over everything, without skipping around, that he considers important and will be on your test. Do all of the assesment quizes in the Faulkner CD. They take time but most of his questions come from it. Go to live lectures, volunteer, dress up, it's fun! =)
Emerson is brilliant (and usually on LSD). The class is pretty tough and some of the test questions are ambiguous. DO ALL THE COURSEWORK.

By far one of the best professors at UF, in terms of teaching ability and smarts. A joy to watch and he is an all-around nice person. Read everything and do the coursework. He doesn't drop any tests, they all get averaged in somehow, so the coursework becomes your safty net. Watch all the lectures!
No Comments

So, it's business law- the material is pretty dry.  Despite that, he manages to entertain with his goofiness and the class (thanks in large part to a huge army of TA's) runs like a well-oiled business law machine.  Get the Smokin' Notes and do the coursework!
You either love him or hate him. Tough class but you learn a lot. Very worthwhile taking.

Do absolutely all the coursework (which is extra credit) or you'll be screwed! Lots and lots of reading. He explains things well but uses a lot of examples that absolutely have nothing to do with what he's talking about.
read read read! with open book and open note tests you think the tests cannot be that difficult but u'll be amazed.  do all the coursework!
Fantastic Prof!  Best Ever!
Excellent professor.  Keeps things interesting by effectively using humor.

decided to take his class after catching a lecture of his on tv..very interesting, very insightful, VERY DIFFICULT, TONS of work, i got a C+ as a freshman, but do NOT recommend to anyone else..it was a semester in itself, but GREAT professor, hilarious

He is probably one of the worst professors I have ever had.  Once you get past the costumes, jokes, videos, etc., you will find that he is a joke.  He is extremely unhelpful outside of class and is rude as well. Good luck, you will need it!
awesome awesome awesome teacher, but u must do all the work. u gotta read everything and pay attention and you'll do just fine.

The guy really is nuts, but I have to admit I did laugh quite a few times at his lectures and that doesn't happen to often in any UF lecture.  The material is hard and you have to work really hard, but its not impossible to make an A.
This class is a waste of time.  All of the examples are just fluff.  He could spend a lot more time actually explaining the material rather than parading around like a bafoon.
He makes a pretty boring subject interesting. Even if you don't like Business Law, he'll make you laugh just looking at his crazy costumes. I thought this was a great class!
Don't be fooled by his great teaching style and humor during lectures.  You must do the work! Great class and teacher though. Just keep reading and reading and reading...
Great Teacher - Best One at the University, By Far!
If you think he is a bad teacher you have no creativity at al!!!. Lots of work, somewhat tough material, but class is very interesting and do all the work!!
BUL is an okay class -- easy B if you do the course work -- but if I ever see another skit with his daughter in it I think I will scream!
Horrible man, he is soo rude if you want to speak to him outside of class. He seems really nice but he is really mean and nasty.
My favorite professor ever in college.  This guy knows how to teach.  Wish they were all like him.
unique style and he entertains while teaching LAW, give him credit where credit is due
No Comments
If you think this guy is a bad teacher,then drop out of school.You are an idiot.
Good class, easy B,B+, but alot of work
he is crazy- in a good way.  He dances every year in the Cracked Nut. Wears different costumes EVERY day.
Best teacher at UF, enjoy the class while you are in it and keep up!
Easy A with good work ethic.  Innovative teaching style.
Outstanding teacher.  If you do all the coursework, you just can't get below a B
Makes learning interesting but loses students on random tangents
No Comments
Lectures were long, but she explained the concepts well. The test was more difficult than I thought it would be, but was not impossible. Make sure to study the slides and know all the concepts.

One thing I forgot to mention in the comment that I wrote below is to definitely started studying at least a few days out or a week or 2 out if you're behind in lecture and just focus on the big picture stuff

Didn't read the textbook nor did I pay attention to any of the lectures. Although from what I heard in the background she seemed good. I only used smoking notes and just read it a bunch before the exam and was able to succeed.

Her plants unit is known to be the hardest out of the 3. However, her slides have everything you need to do well on the exam. She explains the concepts well, but it is a lot of information to digest so you will need to study to score high. While she posts the slides, attendance is technically required and you will learn a lot more by attending them
Unfair professor.

I thought she was good teacher, I found her easy to follow along and study for but there was a cheating incident in my test room and she had us all retake the exam and I truly belive it was harder and included questions from topics we were not told to study and blamed those of us who did nothing wrong. She also is not clear when asking questions.
there was a cheating situation and she punished the students that didn't do anything.

Dr. Davis is amazing and very passionate about plants! Clear learning outcomes make it easy to study for the exam, and lectures do a great job of covering all the material needed. Smokin'Notes not required for this part of the course and no need to read the textbook, just look at the lecture slides. Exam was very fair and easy :)

dude if there wasn't smokin notes, I would have been cooked. Her lectures were very long-winded and would not be clear AT ALL. if you have no plants knowledge before this class, just do yourself a favor and get smoking notes, esp because her slides were very minimal in words. Not too tricky of an exam though!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Davis was amazing. If you take detailed notes during her lecture you will be all set for the Plants unit, so you should attend! Don't bother reading the DENSE, OVERCOMPLICATED textbook, her lectures are great. She answers questions very gracefully and always provides great explanations and videos for concepts. Wish I could take her again :)

Listening to Dr. Davis talk is like listening to one of my peers, which is surprising considering what she teaches and how long she's been doing it. She's really great. I love how passionate she is while simultaneously knowing when to sneak in a laugh or two. Material is pretty difficult but that's par for the course in biology classes.
Plants are sooo boring but Dr. Davis is pretty good. I used smokinnotes and was glad I did. Don't bother reading the book.

Bio 2 is divided into 3 segments with an exam for each. No final. Professor Davis taught the first segment of Bio 2. She was the best of the 3 instructors in my opinion. She offered a 2 point extra credit and the curve on the exam was very fair. As long as you study the lecture power point you will be fine.

Dr. Davis did a great job with the plants unit. She emphasized points that were going to be on the exam and gave us good practice materials. I got a C on her exam studying on my own and would recommend smokin notes if you want to nail it. She made plants interesting!

Professor Davis made the plants unit SO MUCH easier. I love how you can tell she's very enthusiastic about plants and explain the concepts really well. Everyone said Plants is the hardest unit but Professor Davis made the content so much more digestible.
Plants is a lot of information and memorization, but Dr. Davis made it manageable. I definitely recommend using smokin notes, especially for the processes and diagrams!

I personally really liked Dr. Davis. She had good lectures and was very passionate about plants. Everyone told me that plants was the worst unit for Bio 2, but it ended up being my favorite. The information can be hard to grasp at first, but turns out to be very interesting. Her exam was moderately difficult.

I thought that Dr. Davis was great! She taught the plant sections of biology 2, which is a notoriously hard section, but she presented the material in a way that made it fun and easy to understand. Dr. Davis gave learning objectives, which was helpful when studying for the exam. The exam was straightforward, so if you study, you should do well.

Very unorganized. Textbook, assignments, and lectures do not line up. Quizzes will ask info that is literally not in the textbook or not in any of the lectures (literally recorded lectures and searched through transcript, no mention of multiple questions). 

Expectations unclear. Assigns homework based on textbook reading, doesnt want us to read.

Dr. Davis was a decent professor. We didn't take her exam due to the hurricane, but the material she taught was quite boring, and she didn't make it very interesting. She was a kind person, but it took her and the TA's months to grade our exam make up assignment. Overall, would not take again, but I just don't like plants and she was boring.

It is difficult to speak in regard to the exam since there was a hurricane and we were. assigned a makeup assignment. Her slides are very heavy with examples and are difficult to look back on since there is minimal text. Smokin notes was definitely helpful for organizing information and integrating information from the textbook which is needed

Dr. Davis is an amazing women and actually cares about students. The plant material is very hard and boring but if you have Smokin Notes you should be fine. Our exam got cancelled due to the hurricane and we had three assignments instead, They took a while to grade but she would give points back if you went to office hours

She is a great teacher and really loves her field. The class was mainly taking notes in lecture and easy homeworks. I didn't take her exam due to hurricane and we had a really fair make up assignment. Went to her office hours and she was super nice and helpful. Overall, she is great the material can just be annoying .

The lectures weren't that helpful, and she didn't explain the material in a very easily understandable way. If you have SmokinNotes you'll probably do fine, but probably attend the office hours unless you've learned this before. Our first test got canceled and turned into three assignments, but three months later it's still not graded.

Her lecture ppts weren't great study tools as they were mostly photos with little information. She was at a disadvantage because of the hurricane this semester but still was not great with communicating or getting grades back. She's nice, but she's not the best professor.

This professor is OK at best. It's impossible to study from the slides because it's literally just pictures of plants, minimal words. She is obviously very passionate about what she does but that is not indicative of a good lecturer. She goes on long tangents about little rabbit holes and if the lectures were recorded I would've never went to class

Lecture is useless and slides are filled with pictures and irrelevant videos. She is passionate about plants and that shows through the excessive number of examples that she includes in her slides. SmokinNotes was a MUST for me and allowed me to pass the exam with an A.

Skip lecture. Join the groupme to find when the Learning Catalytics are and do them during the class time from your dorm. She is a horrible lecturer and wastes a lot of time. Just get the Smokin' Notes and study that. She makes the plant section v confusing. I attended all lectures but only studied Smokin' Notes for the exam and felt more prepared.

I really appreciated Dr. Davis as a person. She could better organize her lectures, but she taught us what we needed to know and made her lectures available to us online. I'd buy smokin' notes because they refresh everything she discussed. Her exam was extremely easy and straightforward, no tricks. Study well and you'll do well.
Great professor, makes the boring plant information quite interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The most convoluted, confusing, unorganized prof I have ever had. This lady would fly through the concepts we NEEDED to know for the exam and would instead spend 30 minutes talking about the largest tree in the world. cherrypicks the info from the book to teach which makes it hard to keep up. Exam was sort of straightforward, but tricky.

Horrible Lecturer. Was a waste of time. If I didn't take AP Bio in high school, I would be screwed. Taught more about plant life than actual biology in plants. Feel unprepared for future. Spends more time trying to be relatable to students than trying to teach.

Her test was completely different than what I would expect. The majority of the class she talked about irrelevant information about various Gainesville plants and the things that she found interesting that weren't on the exam. She would skim over info that was heavily tested on exam and go in depth about various plants because she was interested.

Dr. Davis taught the plants portion of BSC2011 and I felt that she taught it well. Yes, she often went very in depth with examples, but she clearly loved what she taught. The exam was somewhat similar to the clicker questions and overall was reasonable. I would recommend Smokin Notes just to help solidify everything taught; it was a huge help.
Very very nice and responsible professor!!

I had Dr. Davis for the cells portion of the course. Overall, not too bad. I wish she posted her Powerpoints before class so I could print them out beforehand. Her exam was pretty straightforward, but she did have a couple tricky questions that you had to read carefully.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved her. Her lectures were easy to sit through and her learning catalytics questions were really similar to what she put on the test. Our of my three professors her test grade was my best. Her test is very straight forward. Smoking notes helps a lot though, don't think it would'v been this easy without it.

I loved having Dr. Davis for the first part of BSC2010, and am excited to take her again for BSC2011. Her lectures are informative and entertaining. She makes it clear what is expected of us. Just be sure to study because it is a lot of material, but she is very helpful, and genuinely cares about her students. Very nice and smart lady.
Her lectures are decent, but sometimes she talks about stuff that is not related to the course. Overall good professor.

I loved Prof Davis! She taught the cell portion of bio 1. Her test did have a few random questions about stuff that she only mentioned once but there still should have been enough questions on topics that she warned us about to get an A. Very kind and accessible outside of class. Reading the textbook is good supplemental material
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Terrible lecturer. She talks so monotonously and with so much wandering that it is nearly impossible to glean what is meandering, distracted filler, and what is actual information. Things are phrased and rephrased dozens of times but somehow you can't understand anything. Must read and take exstensive notes on entire chapter to survive.
Dr. Davis is awesome! She is considerate of her students and very consistent with lecture material and exam material. Great teacher who loves what she does.
