Really sweet professor with a well organized Canvas. Material was mostly engaging aside from some dense additional readings, some of which would show up on exams. Overall had a good experience with this class.

Dr. Wang is a fun and caring professor. She always sent out announcements for updates and it is obvious she is passionate about the topic and caring. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: interesting class and an easy A as long as you do assignments. assignments are easy and everything is open-book and open-note so you don't really have to study. additional readings show up on tests but you can use canvas on tests so answers are easy to find

Dr. Wang is the SWEETEST! I loved taking Abnormal Psychology. She treated all topics with the appropriate care and nuance. However, beware that the discussion posts are essay-length. The "additional readings" in the modules are not optional and do appear on exams. That being said, I would love to take a class with Dr. Wang again in the future.

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this professor. The class was well-structured with clear expectations. reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wang is really great and the class is super easy and really interesting. The only reasons I don't rate the class 5/5 is because the readings are so long and definitely necessary. Exams are open note and can be tricky, so make sure to prepare well.

The course is very easy and the professor is nice. My only issue is Neo-marxist derivatives such as DEI being widespread throughout the course. My first encounter with this at UF online. Disappointing to have to be subjected to Neo-marxist teachings without any counter arguments.

DO THE READING IF YOU WANT AN A. The lectures do not go over all of the material needed to be successful on the quizzes so make sure you read and do well on the quizzes.

reviews.comment: This class was fine, the material was interesting, but it definitely took a long time to read and take notes on the chapters. Most interesting course material I've had. Professor is really nice and tests are open book. I loved this class and the textbook was super easy to read. Definitely take her class if you have the chance!

reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

I highly recommend her as a professor!

Very easy course, and all the quiz answers are online. The tests are open textbook/open note and very easy to complete. The hardest part of this class is parsing what her grading structure means, and writing discussion posts. All in all very boring but easy course.

reviews.comment: Dr. Wang is amazing. Her weekly assignments consist of a warm up, enrichment lecture, textbook reading with powerpoint slides, and a quiz that is open note and open book. Her tests are tricky but they are also open note and open book. I wish I could take another class with her.

i put minimal effort in this class and got an A. I didn't read the textbook the entire semester, but instead I just read the smokin notes (briefly tho). homework + lectures (2 hours each) are rlly long and lecture is not engaging but she tests on lectures + reading together. I'm a good test taker but I wouldn't take this prof again.
This class was not bad at all. Use SmokinNotes and you'll get an A. Class is just Smartbook assignments, quizzes, and exams. Stay on top of Smartbook, use SmokinNotes, and this class is easy.

As a 1st year professor the lectures were disorganized. A majority of the exam questions were disorganized as well. Difficult to maintain composer during exams as the questions wording seemed incorrect or misleading. Hopefully she progresses as a professor to better serve her students.

WARNING! This class will take your full attention on a daily basis. Smartbook assignments might take up to 2-3 hours to complete. There is no room for mistakes or missed deadlines. Every point counts, so complete the extra credit study. She is quick to dismiss objections or appeals for exam questions.

The TAs were quite erratic. altering or canceling hours frequently. After exam 2, your commitment to this class may lead to burnout, so take caution. Exam questions are intended to deceive or confuse you.

Nice person, but no grade curves or appeals have been granted. Tons of time wasted in lectures on current topics that have no impact of assignments or exams. Exam questions are open to interpretation, so she is determined to find a reason to deny an appeal. This is a disservice to the students.

The exams are worth the majority of your grade so put a major emphasis on studying. Utilize smoking notes! Do the extra credit it can make a difference in a C+ or B-. Devote a lot of time and effort to this class to obtain a solid grade.

The most difficult course I have taken. Wonderful person but her lectures will put you to sleep. Students would chime in often during the lectures about outside topics which provide no benefit to the exams. Do not miss an Smartbook assignment, quiz, or extra credit points because you will need all of them to pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a 1st year professor with tons of experience to offer. You must watch her lectures and read the chapters to obtain any success. Do the extra credit because you will definitely need the points. Doesn't provide clear material so ask questions if you feel mislead.

This was her first semester teaching so lectures were kinda disorganized at times, so I stopped watching them and read the textbook instead. She has tons of real-world experience and seems to genuinely care about her students! Got an A with very minimal effort. Do the extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your grade will rely on how well of a test taker you are. Some exam questions were lengthy. Exams are 56 questions but by question 35 your brain will be fried. This class requires maximum effort everyday to earn a passing grade. I will forever hate Marketing due to this class!

Not entirely a bad class but definitely not smooth. Throughout the chapters so many terms were alike you can get lost in the mix. Tough to follow along in lectures. Assignments have virtually no impact on your grade.

Exam heavy class! If you earn a C on the first exam, you're out of the running for an A in the class. Students' feedback frequently broke the flow of the professor's lectures. This was her first year of teaching, and she can improve in the future. This is a really difficult class.

Dreadful lectures. I had the impression she would look for any reason why the overall class exam average grades were so low. She seemed to be losing the class more and more as the semester progressed. Exam heavy class. There is very little room for error, if any at all.

Odile is a fantastic person with excellent qualities outside of teaching, but her class is challenging and difficult to get through. Sometimes even studying lectures and taking notes is insufficient. Disliked my experience.

She has a lot of experience, but I didn't think her teaching skills matched that experience. incredibly disappointing, to put it kindly. She won't round up to an A even if you have an 89.99%. Happy that it is over. It's difficult to sit through the lectures.

Where to begin with this course. Everything appeared to be disorganized. Pay attention to all details, no matter how minor you believe they are, because that will almost certainly be an exam question. She's too proud to acknowledge that her exam question was poorly worded. Don't expect an appeal granted.

200 points with 168 of those points coming from tests which means if you get just 17 questions wrong the entire semester you are already out of an A assuming you did all the other assignments. Also has math questions in which you cannot use scratch paper. Overall not a fun professor to deal with and wouldn't take the class if it wasn't required.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not the most exciting class to take. I felt like in her lectures she overly spoke instead of driving home the concept. Felt mislead at times. Just an awful experience.
I felt professor Guinot struggles to clearly explain important topics. She comes across as always being right. Very nice person but the quality just wasn't there.

Worst professor! Exam questions are basically riddles designed to trick you. Exam reviews are just topics that are no on the exams. Don't expect for any exam question appeals to be granted no matter how badly written. Do not waste your time trying! She doesn't thoroughly explain topics. Best of Luck!

This Professor has amazing lectures that keep your attention! She has real-life experience with the topics, adds a lot of fun to the topics, and provides relevant examples. The Professor also has interesting guest speakers that are relevant and insightful. Overall, I really enjoyed taking this class and would highly recommend it!

Professor Guinot is an incredible professor. I strongly recommend taking marketing with her in the spring instead of Professor Cooke. You don't need to go to her lectures, but I recommend it. She is an excellent lecturer and uses lots of real-world examples. However, you can easily pass the class with Smokin Notes.

Great professor. Used a lot of real world examples to try and teach the class and had previously worked at Apple, Google, and Motorola so you could be confident in what she was teaching. She also acknowledged that the previous exams were way harder and made hers much easier. Overall, great teacher.

I love Professor Guinot! She was super nice and the exams contained very little math. Tbh I did not watch a single lecture, except the exam reviews. I crammed studying 2-3 days before the exam by watching the exam review and doing a ton of practice problems from the past exams. Take this class with this professor!!
Such a kind teacher who wants students to succeed. Reformatted exams to include less math and less complicated questions. Very easy class and different from past teacher.
Odile doesn't try to trick you on exams, and everything is straight forward. If you watch lecture videos its hard to understand her at times due to her accent but overall Shes a great professor.
Odile is a great professor and have great characteristics but her class is very hard and tough to get through. Even studying lectures and notes is still not enough at times. GOOD LUCK!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Her lectures were entertaining and it really shows that she knows her material because of her real-world experience. Exams used both smartbooks material and lectures so you have to watch them. Exam and hw was straightforward. Really loved this class!

Very knowledgeable and passionate about her lectures. She has over a decade of experience in the marketing industry and it shows. The smartbook assignments are a lot of work, but for a 4 credit class it is a reasonable workload overall. I would definitely recommend taking one of her classes on marketing.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He teaches history as if it is your major and you are a grad student. Even if there are no prereqs, you NEED extensive background knowledge on his lessons. You will not keep up otherwise, especially because he assumes you know all the context and does not elaborate, talks fast, and all your grades are based on pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It surprises me how teachers like this stay with universities when they are contain so little knowledge of whatever they profess to have. There is nothing of substances he could impart on anyone for anything. Don't waste your money on credit hours with him.

Prof. Curta was clearly very passionate about the field of study but make sure you have at least a background in the time period. I had none, and struggled because of it. His lectures are very quick and if you don't keep up with the information he's giving, you'll be very confused on the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Curta was very knowledgeable about what he taught, but his lectures were a bit disengaging and I often found myself zoning out. He is an extremely kind person who is willing to help. I LOVED my TA and really enjoyed her lectures. Participation only matters in discussions, from what I experienced.

This entire class is basically graded on 3 written assignments and a discussion post. His lectures were not engaging, but I loved the TA's lectures. Attendance isn't mandatory but TA's take a participation grade at the end of the semester? He would also only reply in discussion posts to correct people which I thought was very strange.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Curta is very passionate about history and loves talking about it. If you talk to him 1:1 at the end of class or during office hours he is incredibly approachable and nice, good guy overall. If you like history you'll like the lectures, if not you might be a little bored. Assignments were light and not graded harshly, really liked him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Curta has a genuine love for the topic he is teaching. The lectures are fun and interesting. You spend more time with your TA. But the TAs are amazing. Definitely would take another class with Dr. Curta.

Great teacher. You talk to the TA more. Lectures every class, the whole time. SO many things to read for hw. Lots of discussion posts, 3 writing assignments, NO TESTS! Funny dude, just (in my opinion) boring topic/class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: VERY easy quest class. Super chill TA's, and lectures (objectively) don't feel and aren't mandatory to succeed. If you show up, note the key definitions and use them in your writings. No tests, quizzes, midterms or finals. only 4 assignments in the course and they are self-explanatory. He knows what he is talking about for fs. He posts his lecture.

This has been the most boring class I've ever taken; I do not recommend it. The topics of Migration and Identity are really touched on, but the class primarily revolves around historical examples, which, by providing background context, half of the class has already passed. The work is easy to do, and the history is not very necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am a first year freshman and this class is definitely a culture shock for me. He definitely knows what he's talking about, but the lectures feel unengaging. I respect the knowledge, but the admin of the course isn't my cup of tea. If you take this class, take notes on the key terms and do not take notes on all of the examples. No tests. Show up.

I took multiple classes with Dr. Curta and honestly love him. Although he is a tough grader, he genuinely cares for his students and will happily offer help and sometimes extra credit if you meet with him during office hours. He is so passionate about history and education, and was by far my favorite professor from UF.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Curta is knowledgeable and demands a lot of attention from students. I've taken Early Medieval Italy + Byzantine History, and neither is beginner-friendly. Lectures are dense + fast. He's condescending. History dudebros fill his classes. But if you can read and think with a critical, historical mind, it's a good challenge/skill-builder.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DO NOT take any of his courses unless you have 15 hours of free time daily for the readings :) Half of the time lectures were incoherent and very hard to follow as Curta loves to ramble about things that do not really relate to the topic at hand. Only take his classes as a last resort. Please save yourself from the unnecessary stress!!:)

Easy grader, but one of the worst Professors you can have in History. Lectures are rambling and incoherent, will frequently demean and belittle students, does not believe in teaching anything that doesn't already gel with his particular, super-Christian worldview (he WILL force it on you), impossible to get in touch with in-person for office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You can read every on the 4 books he assigned (despite saying you only need one for the quizzes, which itself isn't true), attend every one of his ramble lectures, and you still won't do well in the class. A complete waste of time to have so much information thrown at you and not having more then 4 quizzes to actually pass his insane grading scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Curta does as little as possible and expects to be feted for it. He claims to have office hours and then makes it extremely difficult for students to actually see him. How such an inaccessible individual could still be employed at UF is troubling.

This professor is incapable of empathy and proper instruction. He thinks he knows everything and will insist that he is always right, even when confronted with his own mistakes in writing. The only person he respects is himself and this lack of respect is despicable.

Dr. Curta made me feel like a stupid baby that doesn't know anything at all. Quizzes are impossible, exams are pretty easy tho. He's a nice guy and I like him as a person, do not take this class if you dont care abt medieval history.

What to say about Florin Curta? Every email I've ever received from him is coated in condescension. Reading back his emails to me has literally brought me to tears. Every question I have ever asked in class or in email has been met with disregard and blatant disrespect. He teaches because he likes the sound of his own voice.

This professor makes the case for abolishing tenure. I don't know why but he always responds to emails in a sarcastic or mocking way, going out of his way to belittle those who are trying to learn something or ask a question. His lectures are also very disorganized.

Never underestimate his ability to respond rudely to an email. Never underestimate the attention to minuscule detail that the quizzes require. More importantly, never take the course. He is the epitome of the stereotypical college professor in ways that are unceasingly negative.

For his seminar EUH4903 it was a easy in terms of grading. There is a lot of reading and writing, but as long as you do it you will get an A. There are weekly essays until around Halloween he stops giving hw and you just work on your research. It was a great class to learn the research method and how to use UF libraries effectively, great overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Dr Curta is wonderful! 
He is knowledgeable and his interest in the topics covered truly carry his courses! Some lectures can be lengthy & complex but never fail to captivate! some courses have difficult and info specific pop quizzes but they are passable! With interest in the topic and participation in readings and lectures you will do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curta is knowledgable about anything. I had him for Medieval Germany and it was based on lectures. Reading journals before every class and a research paper. You will read a lot. If you are interested in the subject you will love his classes. They allow you to actually learn the material. He also offers one extra credit assignment.
Professor Curta is very knowledgeable but seems to not be able to translate it to his students. His accent makes it hard to understand and his lectures are very dense. I do not suggest you take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Curta is a very knowledgeable person, almost to the point of being a walking encyclopedia. That being said, he quite literally never put in any grades. I only discovered my grade after the semester was over. His criteria for grading are completely unclear and it felt like a lot of the readings weren't actually necessary for the class.

He changed the number of assignments mid-semester. The majority of the reading contributed nothing to the class (as well as the books), and his inability to record and input grades, made this class far harder than it needed to be. On top of this, he was not very helpful or willing to meet with students unless it suited him the best way possible.

Dr. Curta is a tough professor, his classes are centered on his lectures, as well as the readings he assigns which are a bit heavy but doable. His in-class assignments are difficult if don't you have a really good understanding of the class. He wants you to come to him, so ask questions/for help if you need it. Ultimately, a good professor.

You are expected to read a good amount, but his weekly reading expectations were fair. Your grade is based on tri-weekly journal entries based on readings (you can pass the class with a 70% just doing these) and 5 in-class assignments (doing well on these boosts your grade). He's a walking historical encyclopedia, definitely recommend his classes.

This class was definitely tough but he intended it to be that way. Dr. Curta's lectures are pretty interesting and it's obvious he's passionate about history. He definitely sets his class up as a challenge to his students but offers extra credit and fairly clear guidelines. The quizzes are surprises but the exams you know ahead of time.,
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Average professor lectures cover a lot of material but and with so many names you can get bogged down in the details. Your grade is made of 4 quizzes, 10 points each all MC and 2 exams with a few MC a few definitions but mainly an essay with no word count each worth 30 points. You need to go to lecture to learn, reading and presentation are lacking
Has favorites in class. I wouldnt take this professor for anything else
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Curta for the Viking Experience. The class was different due to COVID and everything was online. We had 200 word reading journals everyday and 5 in-class assignments that were akin to take home tests. They were hard. The class was hard. But if you love history, take a class with him because its truly rewarding. You will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have taken 3 classes with Dr. Curta and I wish I had taken more before graduating. Dr. Curta is very passionate about what he teaches and really does care about his students learning. Though his class is difficult if you come to class and listen to his lectures and reading of the primary sources you should be able to pass the class with no issue.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Curta is enthusiastic about what he teaches and has good lectures. Attendance is not mandatory but if you skip class you won't do good on the quizzes. He gives pop quizzes so read the assigned chapters and pay attention in class. He's a reasonable grader and gives good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I would avoid if you can. I went to every lecture, but learned far more, if not everything, from the readings. Lectures are too full and he talks so fast it is hard to understand him sometimes. There were 4 quizzes that were impossible to do well on, weekly journal entries, and the midterm and final are essay questions.

Very rarely would you find a professor as knowledgeable as Dr. Curta. He's smart to the point that it's intimidating sometimes. He is kind and easy to talk to in office hours. Readings are reasonable in length, but can be extremely difficult to understand. I wish he would use more time for discussion and interacting with the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a fantastic lecturer, definitely one of my favorites at UF. Just as a lot of people have already said, he is a very intelligent and talented individual. In my experience, he can sometimes come off as a bit rude in emails, but he is genuinely very kind and helpful in person, and is always happy to discuss things in his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Curta is a great teacher that I would definitely take again. The grade for this class was based on 4 pop quizzes and 2 tests (midterm and non-cumulative final). The quizzes are based on the primary readings, so I definitely recommend keeping up with the readings every week (theyre not that bad) or else you will do poorly on the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He is a brilliant individual who loves history, but he moves way too fast and does a poor job at putting things in perspective, which is necessary for such a dense course. His pop quizzes are impossible and his attendance policy is unreasonable. I slowly lost interest in this class as the semester went on because his teaching method is chaotic.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Most of the reviews don't seem fair to him. This dude is smart and knows what he's talking about, however it was difficult for me to keep up with his course when combined with my other courses. He doesn't set unrealistic expectations, but at the same time he expects us all to work. And his accent is actually easy to understand. Try and he'll help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Curta is very knowledgeable and impressive in his field, but I found his class very challenging. Quizzes were extremely specific and seemed to come from no where
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: While Professor Curta is extremely knowledgeable and intelligent, his class was extremely intensive on reading and his pop quizzes seem to be based little on the reading at all. Format for the entire class was pop quizzes, a midterm, and a final. Hard to understand his accent and follow his powerpoints at times especially as he moves very fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This professor is awesome at what he does. He knows EVERYTHING! He is very passionate about what he teaches, which can make him excited at times and go quickly through the lectures. His accent is a bit difficult at first especially if he rushes, but he can definitely be understood if you pay attention. No final, just little tests.  Awesome teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: To everyone complaining about Dr. Curta's accent--he speaks eight languages, and is perfectly comprehensible. He is truly one of the most brilliant people at UF, and any history major would be lucky to learn from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: To everyone complaining about Dr. Curta's accenthe speaks eight languages, and is perfectly comprehensible. He is truly one of the most brilliant people at UF, and any history major would be lucky to learn from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Curta is one of the best teachers I have encountered at UF. He has such a deep passion for history that it really shows in his lectures. The class wasn't the easiest I've taken, but certainly not difficult. He really pushes his students to learn something, and as long as you remained somewhat interested.. You will learn A LOT!

Rather than teach about What Is The Good Life, he complies a list of things that he finds interesting and teaches about that instead. This course is terrible, and Dr. Curta doesn't make it any better.

Curta's lectures put me to sleep beause they were primary based on history and I am not a fan. Clicker points are used for attendance, primarily history based, and the answer is usually all of the above... Besides that, my TA was great so the weekly discussions were what I got the most out of. Good luck!

Dr. Curta knows what he is talking about...regarding history. But he is a very bad professor for Good Life, all of his lectures are just history-related and can't help you with the midterm or final. I still can't answer the question, "what is the good life?" Hope you have a good T.A

Dr. Curta is a very good professor,  just not for Good Life. He uses Tophat so attendance is kinda mandatory. All the clicker questions are history related, only a few of the many we've had so far were actually related to the readings. Smokin' Notes helped me pass the midterm.

treats good life as a history class, so maybe half of the information in lecture is actually relevant. I stopped going after a few weeks. he seems very nice though and I can imagine he is an excellent history professor
He cannot make up his mind as to the type of answer he wants on tests and quizzes. He thinks he is teaching a history class to history majors.
Brilliant professor and a nice man.
Professor Curta is by far the best history teacher I had at UF. Brilliant teaching, exciting topics, never got bored in his class. He changed my views on history.
Amazing professor! The best history teacher! He has amazing lectures and goes out of his way to help students.
Very smart!  By far one of my favorite teachers at UF.  Have to attend his classes all of the exam questions and quizzes come from his lectures.  Very helpful if you go to office hours.

A very knowledgeable and intelligent professor who gives disorganized lectures and follows them with difficult quizzes and exams. This is not a casual class. I would only recommend him to serious history buffs.

He is obviously a brilliant scholar and I had a lot of respect for him in that way. What he lacked as a professor was structure. He gives pop quizzes that are based largely on lecture and can be very detail oriented, so take good notes.
I took a few graduate courses with him and he is a very good teacher and brilliant scholar.
Great professor.  One of the smartest people in world.  If you work hard and go to class you will really enjoy it and do well.

Great course! Those folks talking crap about him obviously weren't serious about his class. He is a wealth of knowledge and offers help to ANY student who asks him! All he asks is that we do our part--which requires EFFORT and HARD WORK! Too many folks want an  easy "A". Well this is not that easy "A" it's a challenging course but so worth it!!!
He is the best professor ever. Very well informed and considerate. You guys don't know  anything when you label him as rude. He is an amazing person and a wonderful professor.

As stated before, Curta rejected extra credit papers and added a question to the exam MERE DAYS before it. His teaching his no coherency, his method of grading (random quizzes that have questions that simply speculate on the reading - if you get it wrong, one point off your final grade) is terrible, and his class has little substance. Awful prof.

First do not bother giving your precious time to this Professor. Curta is rude and self absorved. I feel  sorry for him because the highliht of his life is HIS DEGREES. As a human being this life he failed.

Very unprofessional, at end of semester had rejected extra credit papers that were to his credentials but were approved by TA's and not him.  The day before the final added subjects to study.  Avoid class's taught by this teacher
He is the best teacher ever. You do have to work in his classes. He has high standards. Check out his website and CV. Is absolutely impressive.
Horrible professor. He is pompous,and inconsiderate. Very unclear in both speaking skills and expectations. I give him an overall grade of: F.

He is a very good teacher. Truly enjoyed his class. One of his TAs acted in a very unprofessional way giving away the questions for the exam. No wonder he had to clarify things a few days before the final. He asked us to study all the questions provided to us three weeks in advance. Some people were unhappy but it was really not his fault.
Dr. Curta is very unprofessional as he has recently changed an extra credit assignment and exam with less than three days to go before it is due.  If you are smart, AVOID THIS CLASS!!!
He is the best teacher ever.
The best history teacher at UF. If you love history take his classes. He is absolutely brilliant.

Really good history prof.  His accent was almost never an issue.  Extremely knowledgeable about what he's teaching.  He's really more of an archaeologist than a teacher, but you can tell that he loves what he teaches.  He didn't give us quizzes/tests, just bi-weekly journal entries and a final paper.

The greatest history professor I had. He personifies what history should be at the collegiate level. After class, he was always available to clear up any questions regarding subject matter.  His grading is much simpler than most students realize. He gives ample readings, however, they far surpass the level of the testing. Prepare to learn a lot!!!

A brilliant man, no question, but in my opinion whether or not you do well depends on whether or not you can understand his accent.  He requires a lot of reading, and his lectures are separate from the reading assignments, so you really do have to keep up in all aspects to do well (he took attendance in my class).  I agree with others in that his quizzes were oftentimes very "out there".  Very interesting class though.

Terribly hard to understand at times during class, but the real problem comes with his astounding lack of clarity. It's never clear just what you need to study and his readings are ridiculously long. No one warrants an undergrad class with a 1200 page cous

he's a really interesting teacher, and his class is fast paced and he knows his stuff. i think its hard to take notes for b/c he talks about EVERYTHING related in the slightest bit AND he speaks incredibly fast. however, the material is intersting because he is very into his job. The exams were easy, he told us 6 essays for them and chose one for t

I don't think I've hated a class more than this one.  I couldn't understand what he said and when I would go to his office hours, it seemed that he would always brush me off and never answer any of my questions.  I definitely don't recommend him.

He is Amazing!You will learn in his class what you should know in history at college level.His tests are hard, so I sugest u review every week!Quizes are not that hard. I love this class, and I am lucky to the opportunity to be in there, and his acent is sexy, very diff and attractive!!;)!!

He is a brilliant man - he really knows his stuff.  The quizzes are difficult and the readings are long, but he puts as much effort into teaching as he expects his students to put into learning.  The class is fascinating.

oh gosh!!! im soo disappointed and upset. i was psychd to take this class but i had to drop it b4 spring break! his accent deters one's learning. quizzes are completely ambiguous. hard to pass even if u try to learn the info urself. it couldve been a great class =(. he lectures TOO FAST and ALL OER
I never knew someone could make learning about the Vikings so boring.  Don't go to his office hours unless you want to be talked down to.

VERY BRILLANT MAN.  Please take his classes only if you want to, he requires a good bit of reading, but never attendance. Don't waste his time, he won't waste yours. He's a great lecturer, does go a little fast sometimes and with a slight accent can blur together. DESERVES A LOT OF RESPECT!
Very hard to understand.  Pop quizzes are ambiguously-worded at times and always very difficult.
Very hard course, but taught very well.
It's not his problem if you have trouble with the accent.
The reading requirements for his class is big. Difficult to understand his accent.
Very smart; he knows his stuff, and speaks 7+ languages.  Unfortunately, he is very difficult to understand at times.  He is tough, but very fair.  Make sure to attend class.
A fantastic, spellbinding, leanient, clever, knowledgeable professor.  He knows everthing!!  Incorporates funny anecdotes and stories into the readings.
Very knowledgable.  I learned a lot in his class.
Excellent Professor! You have to be an honest student who does the work but overall the experience will be good! Knows his history like no other I have seen
hard to understand sometimes with his accent.
Outstanding teacher who is very effective in presenting needed Information.

Engaged, passionate, and extremely caring. Fell in love with this topic and ended up taking the minor. Homework is consistent, clear expectations. GO TO CLASS even tho attendance is optional because she'll give pointers to what is on the exam. Clearly cares about her students
Great class! Her lectures are engaging and she doesn't ask for much in terms of grading, just that you walk away with an open mind. It's clear that she cares about the topic and her students a lot!

Professor Gonzalez is AMAZING!!! She is so sweet, passionate, and caring. She is very open-minded, and she will help you with whatever you need! She really cares about people with disabilities and her passion has truly inspired me to partake in things that help the community!

Wow, what can I even say about Jenna? She is a one-of-a-kind teacher who has an unmatched passion for what she does. Not taking a class with Jenna is a missed experience, please take a class with her if you can!!!

Such an amazing class, Jenna is super passionate! You learn a lot that you can take and start seeing in your daily life. Two weekly assignments due but they are super simple. Exams are easy if you show up to lecture and use the PowerPoint to study (make sure to check the study guide for some topics that may be mentioned in the additional readings).

I loved her class. Attendance not mandatory but she was so passionate about what she taught that it made me want to show up every class. Its a 2 hour block once a week but she usually only lectures for 45 minutes - an hour and then lets you out early everytime. Gives study guides before the exam that basically goes over everything.
This class was so enjoyable, and that was all due to the professor. It is clear that she is passionate about what she teaches and cares for her students.

Jenna is amazing! Took this class summer b for the diversity credit but I ended up loving it. Jenna is so sweet, funny, and truly cares about her students. Minimal assignments and exams are really easy if you just review your notes and sometimes the readings. There are some quizlets online that really help too. Take this class!!!

Jenna is an amazing professor that truly cares for her students and the topic of disabilities. She is extremely knowledgeable and is an expert, as she is also the Director of the Disabilities Resource Center at UF. There are weekly assignments and recommended reading resources that are sometimes on the exams, so just be sure to spend time to learn.
Jenna was awesome and truly has a passion for what she does. Class was super easy and interesting. As long as you pay attention and take minimal notes you will pass. She's also hilarious!

Jenna is an incredible professor and honestly just an incredible person in general. She is very genuine and teaches valuable lessons in her lectures. The class itself is easy in my opinion, but you gain so much knowledge. She really opened my eyes to a lot of things. 10/10 recommend her :)

Jenna was so sweet, I took this class over summer B as my first semester at UF and she was so understanding and kind. Assignments were so easy, some took a little time just because they were associated wuth long movies/documentaries but don't let that dissuade you. Exams were so easy so don't stress that either

Jenna Gonzalez was my favorite teacher during summer B. She is a great professor and you can tell she cares about her craft. My class was lecture style but she taught the material like we were having a conversation. The class was engaging and I enjoyed it. I think we had three exams total and discussion posts. Definitely recommend

she is a very passionate professor! she cares about her students and she will teach you a lot about the course from a different perspective. the ta's might be picky while grading your work, but i highly recommend taking her!
I would recommend this teacher a hundred times over, she is awesome.

This class is incredibly easy! Jenna is super caring and passionate about the subject, so the class is really interesting. I only took this for a diversity credit, but I ended up learning a lot. EASY ASSIGNMENTS. It's like 2 assignments a week but they aren't graded harshly. Exams are based exactly off the powerpoints, and they are open note.

Super easy. Lectures are posted so you don't need to go to class. Exams are open note and are basically word-for-word from the notes. Its a 3-credit class, but you only meet once a week for 2 hours, but you always get out an hour early. There's an assignment due Thursdays, it takes 15 minutes to complete and a PackBack assignment on Sundays.
The best professor I have had and makes lectures very interesting. She is an amazing person and is very passionate about what she is teaching and cares very much about the subject and her students.
Very nice professor, content is super easy. No final, the only assignments are discussion posts and three movie analysis assignments that are very simple. Really hard not to get an A in this class.

This professor is quite incredible. Aside from being an amazing human being, she clearly cares about us as students and our knowledge of the topics. Her main goal is to educate us about disabilities. The exams were extremely easy, average for the first one was a 99. Great experience!

Jenna is such a great professor! She is very passionate about the subject and makes it clear that her main purpose is to help students learn rather than worry about grades. She offers some extra credit, however most people won't need it because she makes her exams pretty easy. Overall, really enjoyable class to go to. Definitely recommend!

Take this class! It is a diversity gen-ed and you will learn so much and gain a new perspective! Jenna is an amazing lecturer and makes her students passionate. Her exams are very easy as she gives a study guide. She's the best!

She is an amazing professor and very passionate about this topic. She knows her stuff and has dedicated her life to those with disabilities. She is very kind and accessible outside of class and a great person. The content isn't hard and she makes the exams and assignments very easy so don't stress. I got something out of this class and enjoyed it.

Professor Gonzalez was amazing and all her lectures were truly enjoyable. I took this class on a whim but im so glad I did because I learned a lot of practical information. Textbooks were not used but I would not recommend missing lectures because she goes info that is on the exams in lectures that is not on the PowerPoints she posts on canvas.

Such an interesting class! She cares so much about her students, clearly incredibly passionate about the subject. Your grade is made up of a couple homework assignments that were usually very simple, just watching a video and answering a couple of questions, and three non cumulative exams written entirely based off the lectures. Easy & interesting!

I took this class as a gen ed course and loved it! She is an amazing teacher and the class is easy. The class is mainly lectures, and all she wants is to make sure the students get something out of the class instead of just being stressed about grades.
A GEM! All she cares about is that her students leave the class with a new perspective on humanity and people.

Jenna is literally one of the sweetest people ever. She's so passionate and knowledgeable about all things related to disabilities and creates such an easy and engaging class. Basically one easy assignment per week and a couple short projects. Easy A and amazing class. Take her if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Gabriel is the best! He's honestly so kind and genuinely has a passion for the topics he teaches. I actually took ARH2531, but he really is the best. His exams and quizzes are easy, we have class trips to the Harn and a Buddhist Temple, and he brings items to allow us to try the style of art that we're learning about. I highly recommend!

Douglas is an amazing professor. I took his sci-fi art class and it's definitely one of my favorite classes I've taken at UF. Lectures + content are engaging, he's all around a really awesome professor that cares about his students too. Attendance + discussion posts matter, so make sure you show up to class. Take a class with him if you can!

Douglas Gabriel is kind, thoughtful, funny, and truly cares about the material and his students. He makes a point to ensure that we are prepared. His jokes are always unproblematic and respectful. He gives detailed, thorough feedback. He makes lectures fun and engaging. He discusses the unserious AND serious art and holds both to the same regard.

Sooooooo great! He is such an engaging lecturer; my major is not ARH, but he makes the content so exciting, he is truly passionate. He (or the TAs) will give you a lot of feedback on your work, so you know how to better articulate ideas in future work, but the grading was relaxed, making each task less scary. Mostly a few papers and discussions.

Professor Gabriel has really engaging lectures and is very passionate about what he teaches. The midterms/exams have clear instructions and he provides insightful feedback on what he is looking for. Overall its very manageable I definitely recommend taking him.

I took this class mostly for credit, but also for interest in the topic of modern art, and I was beyond pleased with how much I was able to gain from this class. Professor Gabriel is an excellent lecturer and is so clearly knowledgeable in what he teaches. There was a great amount of humorous moments and kindness exhibited throughout. Very caring!
Good lecturer, very obvious expectations grading and work-wise, work is not that heavy of a load. Very manageable class and Professor Gabriel is a professor who I would love to have again.

Lowk did not go to class at all even tho attedence was graded but I still got an A bc I did good on the exams. Exams are easy and he gives practice questions. He was a kind teacher and his lecture was interesting the one time I did go
Another professor who just rambles off a PowerPoint in an unintelligible accent. Nice enough guy but I would take anybody else who can communicate in an acceptable way.

Awesome class and the content is actually interesting to learn about! Weekly assignments include lecture videos, textbook readings, discussion posts, and quizzes. VERY textbook heavy when it comes to the quizzes and exams, so thats all you really need in terms of studying. Only 2 exams which are weighted pretty heavy, all multiple choice questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Ghadge is nice and understanding. The class was easy and straightforward. The grading was not strict. I took this class for Quest 2 and highly recommend it. It is not a very time consuming class. There were easy reading quizzes once a week and super easy attendance quizzes for class to promote discussion and a group project for the final.
Professor Ghadge was a great professor; he was incredibly understanding to students' situations and other class workload. Class merely comprised of discussion and 1-3 easy group projects.

Dr. Ghadge has a clear passion for the course, but he was a hypocritical & unsympathetic professor. After dealing with serious medical issues and an ER visit the day of my first exam, Dr. Ghadge failed to answer any of my emails and continued to blame me for my lack of follow up with him- he did not let me makeup. DON'T EXPECT SYMPATHY OR A REPLY.

Professor Ghadge is SO SWEET! He's honestly so caring and understanding about things that you're going through. I would most definitely take any of his classes if you  can. I took transnational sociology with him, and it was great. LOVE HIM!

I have taken Ghadge multiple times now and I love his classes. He is very kind and understanding as long as you talk to him. Some of his classes are group projects which are hit and miss but not his fault, it just depends on your group. He is a very easy grader and as long as you do as the rubric says and try your best you'll do well in the class.

BEST PROFESSOR FOR SYG2010! Loved every second of the class and actually liked showing up to the lectures. Did have a book, but honestly his slides cover everything that is on the exams for the class. DEF TAKE!! If you show up you will pass. He did have pop up assignments, but the TAs gave everyone 100s, even if you were not there. I LOVED!

He is so sweet, wholesome, and funny. There are 3 in class tests, 1 quiz a week, 2 papers, and a some surprise attendance assignments. He drops 2 quizzes and attendance assignments. He lectures from the textbook but the tests are so easy you could not read. Test answers are based off of hw and slides he posts, and frq questions are posted ahead too

Literally one of the nicest people on the planet. The course hasn't ended yet but we're done with assignments aside from the final project.There really wasn't a lot of work or reading (esp. compared to other social science classes). Very accommodating, sometimes if a lot of us were confused he'd extend the deadline for everyone after explaining it

Attendance is not technically mandatory, but he does random in class assignments and only one gets dropped. He's a great teacher though, and he makes sure that the space is inclusive and safe (in the sense that you don't have to be afraid to say something wrong), which is nice when discussing controversial topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easy class, nice guy, really progressive topics so don't take if you're pissy about anti-capitalist themes. Grade based on unproctored quizzes on textbook readings, 3 in-class tests, and in-class assignments (ICA) that are randomly given as attendance. Try to come to class because missing an ICA drops your grade about 1% which you need to buffer.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very nice and cares about his students. The quizzes are extremely easy and right from lecture material and sometimes the textbook. He also posts the slides but its necessary to go to class because he randomly does 12 in-class assignments throughout the semester for about 24% of your final grade.

Weekly quizzes on Canvas are all found on Socratic. The lectures are kind of boring, it is all straight from the textbook. The exams are also all straight from the textbook but a majority is common sense. The in class assignments are given at random so attendance is important. The exams are in person and weighed heavily.

Super easy class that takes minimal effort and time. Loved the topics we covered and Professor Ghadge's lectures were fun and engaging... he often wraps up class early too. Easy/repetitive multiple choice tests and in class assignments make up your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's very knowledgeable and enthusiastic. The readings are digestible and interesting. The lectures are based on summarizing the readings with discussion. There are short writing submissions every week, very easy and doable. Final essay and class book are also very doable.Hes very caring & understanding, the sweetest professor. You'll learn a lot!

I took him for social inequality and the class was pretty easy, just be prepared to do a few readings a week (they usually did not take very long) and write a reflection. He is a very understanding and accommodating professor and I am glad to have taken his class this semester! I highly recommend him to anyone who is looking for a sociology class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof gives really boring lectures and sometimes hard to understand. He's very nice though and encourages the class to participate. Tests are in class, but all quizlet questions, so I recommend finding quizlets and studying those. Random pop quizzes for attendance so if you don't wanna go to class, you gotta try your luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He was very enthusiastic about the things he was teaching but i found that his lectures were a little monotonous, luckily it was based on the textbook so if you read it you were ok for the test. He was very understanding and good at communication. Attendance is nor fully mandatory but he does give ICA's randomly.

asked her to round my grade bc it was an 89.65. she never answered back  and it lowk ruined my perf gpa. She also got mad when we would not read what she assigned when we had other important classes to worry about

This teacher is no bueno. She is grading everything I submit very harshly, and giving essentially no reason as to why(or what I did wrong on the assignment). I once sent a very formal email asking about an assignment, but mistyped "Mrs." instead of "Ms." and received a very snippy email in return. BE WARNED. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ms Gruver is very knowledgeable and clearly passionate about the subject. The course is intellectually engaging, but it can be demanding, especially if you're not used to the pace or reading expectations. Lectures are well-structured, though sometimes dense, and participation is important. Grading is fair but requires strong attention to detail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tough but great! Makes you think.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Incredibly tough grader, rubrics aren't detailed enough for such a high standard that Ms.Gruver seems to have. Inputs her own biases into her grading on subjective topics. I am personally not neurotypical so my answers tend to be more in-depth and nuanced, which is apparently incorrect. She mostly doesn't explain the grading on your assignment.
Tough grader indeed, but to be honest she is very understanding and accommodating, as long as you show effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Grades a bit harshly, pop quizzes on weekly readings, and very few grades with somewhat vague rubrics. However, readings didn't take too long. As long as you tried on the assignments properly you'd do fine, content was interesting and she understood many were taking her class purely out of a QUEST req. Lots of free points near the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough grader, but absolutely worth taking her class. She pushes you to think critically and genuinely helps you grow as a person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I was surprised by the complaints I saw on this page. Honestly, the hardest thing she asked us to do was read the assigned literature—which is the whole point of the class. Overall, I think she did a good job.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Ms. Gruver is one of the most inspirational instructors I have had at UF. She brings fresh perspectives to classical readings and genuinely cares about helping us make the most of this class.

Takes the class way too seriously and can be pretty rude to students. She grades with an iron fist for no reason. Even though the material is mostly pretty easy she makes it so much more difficult than it needs to be. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class was not too difficult and not too much work but the main topic of the class is unclear. Professor is nice but a little difficult to reach sometimes, and grades can entirely depend on her mood when grading. READ THE BOOKS. She makes sure you read them, so just read them. Grading criteria can be unclear and not a lot of assignments.
Terible teacher, thinks her quest class is so important that she is willing to give you a failing grade becasue you missed the lecture one time. would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Really nice professor but mostly boring class. Only fun parts in my mind were learning cad and arduino circuits, rest of the class is kinda dull. Its very easy though so I recommend.
She's really nice the class is just pretty dull and boring. One homework assignment a week and a lot of them are done with your group. Culminates in a final group project that's really easy.

If you are between professors for EGN2020c, go with Goncher. Her section has reasonable coursework that did not take up too much time during the week. The class is 5% of grade homework assignments and then a final project worth 25% at the end. It's not too difficult if you split up the tasks. Overall good professor.
one hw assignment a week isnt bad, class was very easy and she is a very nice professor
The class was easy but was full of busy work. Prepare to do a lot of projects. Professor was really nice but there isn't much else I can say.

this class was easy, but it sucked. it was just so boring and full of unnecessary work. but, every engineering student has to take it. goncher is nice, but doesn't really give any useful feedback for any questions or assignments

I took this class on a flipped format, we had to watch very long lectures before class which seemed pretty redundant as the professor would jus go over the content in class. She cares about her students and was approachable during office hours. Offered plenty of extra credit through extra exam questions, turning projects early, and by participating

Prof. Goncher was nice overall, but her lectures were really boring and I zoned out a lot. The assignments did not have clear criteria at all, so my group was always asking why we lost points on assignments. Don't take this if you don't like circuits or group projects.

Shes a nice person but she doesnt know how to teach. Lectures are on meaningless vague concepts, and she expects you to already know how to interpret C++ coding, work with solid modeling software, and use circuiting kits even though its an introductory class. Youre graded on a few homeworks that are supposed to be easy but have no guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a really nice lady, but the grading rubric isn't clear, so ask questions. Lectures are boring, but projects are interesting.

Many of the in-class meetings consist of group work. Class largely revolves around the Arduino Uno starter kit. I found the final design project to be a great learning experience, very satisfied with the class overall along with the professor!

Took this class 100% online and it was great! Prof was organized and helpful, and she really cares about her students. Definitely recommend, and it's one of the more chill engineering classes, which made it enjoyable. Love Goncher!
She is very enthusiastic about the teaching material. Lots of group work, but that's given in this class. Some classes are rather lecture-heavy though, even if you are not tested on the material.

Dr Goncher is great! Baby circuits is already a pretty easy class, but she prepares you well for exams and is generous with grading. She provided SO MUCH extra credit at the end of the semester, and I couldn't recommend her enough for EEL3003.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you take her for Engineering in Design and Society she is very nice and the class is mainly project based and hands on. I took it online because of corona but if you submit all the assignments on time you should get an A.
Lectures are confusing and hard to follow. Minimal resources given for studying. Quizzes and exams do not reflect the problems done in class or the homeworks assigned. Would not recommend

Tough exams, but pretty fair. Final was much harder than expected and he curved grades. His lectures are engaging and he does his best to explain concepts simply. If you go to office hours he will really try to make sure you understand. Homework due MWF so its a very time consuming class. One of the better MAE professors.

This class is like buying a ticket to a Broadway show three days every week. His lectures are absolutely incredible. As long as you pay attention in class you will do well, and frankly its hard not to. He is incredibly funny and engaging with constant cracking jokes. He is also very caring and understanding and wants the best for his students.10/10

Great character, which makes lectures engaging and his office hours are extremely accessible. Homework was due M,W,F each week which meant a good amount of time invested into the class, but work was manageable. Showing up to class each day is important, he will repeat things several times if they are on the exams, which weren't extremely difficult.

Prof. Subhash is a decent professor. Though in class he is so loud and slams on the tables to get students attention, I feel like I leave with a headache every class. Though, you have to go to because his notes are not posted online. Outside of class he is so rude in emails and just won't respond half the time. Also, so much homework.

This is hands down on of the best professors I've had. Really caring and wants you to succeed in his class. He explains things very well and no matter how many times you ask him, he is always positive and willing to help. He makes funny jokes and his office hours are the best thing to go to. If you go to his OH, you are guaranteed good grades

One of the most important things about a professor is enthusiasm for the subject. Dr. Subhash is one of the most enthusiastic professors I've had. His accent can take a bit to get used to but once that's done his lectures are amazing. Lots of example problems, physical demonstrations of concepts, etc. Also, go to his office hours, they're great.

Subhash is an amazing professor and his lectures are very enjoyable. Make sure to do your hw and ATTEND HIS OFFICE HOURS!! They helped a lot and by going it forced you to study and understand the material better.

Subhash is a decent professor. Homework was strenuous, with 2-3 assigned homeworks /week, you could NOT fall behind. Attendance is not mandatory but is basically required to pass, as his exams are very heavily conceptual based. I could not stand the lectures personally. He is nice, and somehow I ended up passing even though the final killed me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor is incredibly neglectful. HE lost one of my quizzes, and when I approached him (multiple times) about him he'd only say stuff like "if you're a better student you wouldn't have to worry about it". I got a 90+% in both of the midterm exams, and he graded that quiz 1 as a 50%, and that took my grade from an A- to a B. Awful professor.

Difficulty is 4 because of 2-3 weekly assignments, with frequent cases of finishing material on the associated homework's due date. That being said, you will find yourself in a MOM groove quickly and the homework is absolutely manageable with a good group/OH. Subhash is a star in his lectures and I'm so happy I was able to learn MOM from him.

Ghatu Subhash is a fantastic professor. I have loved his class and it has been nothing but a pleasure to be a student in his class. He was incredibly helpful in office hours and overall, I have nothing but good things to say. 
Advice: Attend lecture, do homework, go to office hours, and understand the basics (as every exam stacks). I

Subhash's lectures are very well-taught and helpful. I think he did a very good job of teaching mechanics of materials. My only issue with the class was that there was no way to make up the lecture notes if you were absent, even if it was excused. The tests were fair, and he was very good about partial credit. Would definitely recommend his class.

Very knowledgeable on class subject matter, and his passion comes through when teaching. Makes himself as accessible as possible for office hours and is always willing to re-explain topics. Wants to see students putting in the effort, and can come across as intimidating if he doesn't see you as often. Many former students wanted to TA for him.

Professor Subhash is the first professor that has helped me understand physics/mechanics material clearly. His lectures are engaging and clear, and his office hours help even more. He is willing to teach you anything, but only after challenging you to think individually. Plus, he has a good sense of humor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are great as long as you pay attention. He  tells you what concepts quizzes/exams are on them and does not try to trick you. He is always extremely accessible outside of class and will go above and beyond to make sure you get the grade you deserve. Go to his office hours, it greatly helps.

Subhash is pretty good. He often prioritizes practice examples over actual lecturing material, so be prepared to open the textbook if you don't understand every single decision he's making, because he will quiz you with basic principle questions. He adjusted to online teaching very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Subbash is a great lecturer and makes understanding all the concepts in this lab class easy. Going to his lectures really helps write the reports and makes the exams easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is a good professor, passionate and ready to help. Funny is his most significant characteristic, which make students relax and easy to focus. Just a little Indian English.

Stated that he did not want to teach this course to the class. Spoke too fast. Handwriting is illegible. About 50% of grade material was covered by a guest lecturer. Rude to students. TAs did not like him. VERY disorganized. I hear he is good for mechanics of materials... but not mech design!!
A good professor who explains things well.  First two tests were easy but the final was terrible.  I guess I didn't do so well because I didn't study enough, not because he was a bad teacher.
The best professor I have ever had in college. Keeps you engaged all the time and completely lays it out for you. He will make it clear for you but you need to go to class and keep up with the work.

Great professor. He really wants everybody in the class to understand and do well. He wants  you to come to his office hours to show you are trying in the course. Make sure you participate in class so he gets to learn your name.

Great new professor. Teaches the concepts very well. He is very enthusiastic and seems to really like what he teaches. Helpful during office hours. Exams are very straightforward and relate to his lectures. Make sure you know the concepts for the exams; they are a large portion of the test.

Prof. Hershfield is a great lecturer and he is quite passionate about physics. You can tell in how he teaches how much he loves the subject. PHY2049 under Prof. Hershfield has probably been one of the best college classes I have ever taken.

Professor Hershfield was very kind and would take the time to explain problems to you individually at office hours until you understood the concepts. Just a hard class but great professor who offered a lot of resources.
He's very passionate about his lectures

The class is very organized, which is great because there is a lot of content to get through. It will be difficult if you fall behind. Make sure to genuinely complete the homework and in-class demos as they often closely resemble exam content!

He does lots of engaging demos to make things more interesting and show real-world applications to the math being taught. A good lecturer tends to at least give some help if not fully work out without numbers the harder homework problems for the week. Funny guy and super nice and helpful during office hours.

He was the better professor out of the two who taught the class this semester. He reviewed some homework examples during lectures and performed cool demos in class. Exams are tough, with averages between 50-70, so you have to study a lot if you want a good grade. There's a 5% iClicker extra credit.

He's nice and always encouraged us to ask questions. Created an extra study session on wednesdays for the students who wanted to do better for 2nd exam. Talks at a pretty decent rate though some say it's slow but I like how clear he is. FYI to anyone taking him, he likes to put hw examples (or similar) on exams. Has more "understanding" than others

I kinda failed all exams and am not good at test-taking in general lol but Hershfield lmk that I in fact passed(C)! Don't know how but literally do all iclicker hw & quizzes. No matter what professor you get physics will be horrendous - Hershfield made it more bearable bc he was nice, always eager to answer any questions, and held extra studyseshs

Great guy, seemed passionate about the subject, and explained everything well imo. He was funny, loved his in class demos. Weekly quizzes during discussion section that weren't bad, but exams were a little more difficult. Good grade is very doable, extra credit through iclicker and homework/quiz grades divided by 0.9.

TAKE HIM!!!!! He's an awesome lecturer and has lots of demos. Exams are tough with averages in the 60s but quizzes help pad your grade, plus the cutoff for an A is low (85% or above). Put in the work and you can get an A.

This class was the Physics Journal Club, supervised by Dr. SElman and run by a great TA. In it we would read a physics paper a week, and a group would give a presentation on the paper. It was a great introduction to science communication and reading papers!

Classic SElman, would 100% take a class with him again. Finished our two hour lecture block in an hour and then had an "exit ticket" participation credit at the end of class which took 10 minutes max and was a great learning experience. Best part of course is being in the SElman Room, which is the best classroom in NPB, and his hat game!

Great professor, makes the physics easy to understand and comprehend. The homework's can be time consuming but if you go through the lecture notes all the material is given. Also the exams are fair and he does good reviews before them
Light work class, great professor. Highly recommend for an easy A
Great lectures

Dr. Hershfield is great at giving clear and concise information paired with practical real world applications for what he's teaching you. Physics 2 is a hard class, but instructors like him make things a lot easer, especially since he dedicates a lot of lecture to walking through sample problems from past exams or current HWs.

Solid professor but what's really difficult is how the class is taught in general. Way too much conceptual lecture and not enough time spent solving problems and getting us ready for the exams which are a massive percentage of the grade.
Really cared about teaching and made the class way easier to understand. Basically only learned while he was lecturing
He gives one of the best physics lectures you can find. He will also show you how to start the homework problems which is super helpful.

Hershfield is great, I just wish he was the only professor teaching my class since the second professor who swaps with lectures with him was wholly awful. Physics is a tough class and hardly being able to understand half of the lectures made it much harder, but Hershfield's lectures and exam reviews at least helped me pass.

Awesome lectures, good sense of humor, and he curves your homework grade at the end of the semester. 75% of your grade is determined by 3 exams (25% each), but problems are very similar to homework or in-class worksheet in terms of content. If you do the homework, nothing on the exams will surprise you.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fantastic lecturer, explains everything you'll need to know for the exams, and wants to see his students succeed. If you can take PHY2049 with Hershfield (or PHY2060), you should do it.
I was scared for physics two after physics one, but taking it with Hershfield is the right move. He gives practical lectures that help with homework and teach the concepts so well, and the exams

Hershfield is amazing! His lectures are straight to the point and he explains concepts in a way anyone can understand. Physics 2 is notoriously a very difficult class but it was much more doable with him as the professor! Wish that he was the professor the whole time instead of switching off!

He's the goat. Easily the best physics instructor I've ever had. I loved his exams; they were so clear and simple. He made the class enjoyable and straightforward. He does everything he can to make you succeed. I highly recommend taking any class with Hershfield.

A blessing after having bad physics 1 profs. I never thought physics could be enjoyable but somehow Hershfield does it. Great, clear lectures, very sympathetic about how difficult the class content is. If you did bad in physics 1 and are nervous about physics 2, make sure to get Hershfield as your professor.

He is easily the BEST physics professor here for physics. For the first time I feel that I actually understand the content and his lectures made perfect sense. His exams so far have been very similar to previous exams and very great class. I WOULD TOTALLY RECOMMEND!

Wonderful professor, and incredible lecturer. He makes one of the most notorious weedout courses at the university enjoyable. His lectures are always relevant to homework and exam material and incredibly clear.

Hershfield is a great professor. He's everything you could want in a professor, teaches well, has humor, good office hours, and the class has a nice grading scale. The class is still difficult but that's just how physics is.

This dude was awesome and I felt like I really understood everything he taught, but he was almost never there. I swear this guy only taught like 25% of the course and left the rest to the other professor who was not as good.
Made physics 2 easy to understand. Very fun and interesting lectures.

Very good lecturer, covers all the material in less than 50 minutes while still having it make sense. Skips all the fluff and just tells you what you need to know. He is funny at times and is just good at what he does. Only reason I got a B is because physics is really hard but that's not his fault.

Professor was very knowledgeable and made the quest class surprisingly interesting. We learned a lot of about energy and applying it to the real world.Tests are a mix between MC and FRQ, but there are no trick questions and he is a very fair grader. There is a final paper at the end, but it is very open and was easy to write.

Physics is a hard class. He is a good lecturer but can be very dry at times. Wish he taught the course all semester rather than splitting it up between three professors, the other two were not nearly as good as him.

Note: this rating is for Hershfield ONLY, not the other PHY2048 professors.  His lectures were easy to understand, and he makes it clear that he cares about student success.  His exam questions are easy to spot, because they're actually fair and doable.  Great professor, wish I could have had him the entire semester.

He was my favorite professor out of the 3. He went through how to approach homework problems, explained problem solving steps & went at just the right pace. He taught the kinematics, statics, fluids & waves units & those were the best explained. He also went out of his way to upload an exam review & 'skills for the final' so you can tell he cared.
The only good physics professor at UF. Physics is by no means easy, but the first part of the course with Hershfield actually made a lot of sense to me. After that though...

Best prof I've ever had. His lectures actually make sense, and they keep you engaged. He's funny, respectful, and very helpful. Go to his office hours! He's always willing to help. Better than McGill or Korytov. He makes sure to make the material understandable, and shows you problem solving strategies. I wish the whole class was taught by him.

Out of the three professors this semester, he was my favorite. He makes the information you have to know very clear and does sample problems during his lectures that are actually helpful for the HW and exams. If you can have him as one of your physics profs i highly recommend him

There are iClickers during class that marks whether you attended the class or not and it's kind of optional, but it somewhat helps your grade, so it would be dumb not to do it. Exams are made by 3 professors so it really depends on how the exams go. Hershfield alone would have probably made the class easier. He gives hints on the homework a lot.

He is a great professor. Always makes sure to go into depth about why something is the way that it is instead of just saying that's how it is. Only issue was that I needed more practice, so I made sure to get Study Edge for this class.

Professor Hershfield is overall a nice guy with pretty clear expectations, good grading, and a caring attitude. Some lectures in the class felt boring, but I won't blame him since it was a Quest class(Energy and Society). You'll do very well if you do the homework, study a bit for exams, and show up to class.

Dr. Hershfield taught my UnCommon Reads class, and I enjoyed it more than expected. Even when discussing a subject outside of his expertise, he was very knowledgable while still allowing students to lead discussions.
