The class consisted of weekly discussions on book chapters and presentations at the end led by students.
I preferred Hershfield to Yelton. Hershfield lectures were a lot more clear. He is very caring and always willing to answer questions you may have. Lectures are very clear and organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a great professor for Phy2048. He taught alongside Yelton and I 1000% learned more from him than Yelton. He explains well, has fun demos, and moves at a reasonable pace considering how much there is to teach. Overall, recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: chillest professor ever. if you have a solid background and understanding in physics the exams and quizzes will be easy. homeworks can be difficult but it's not hard to get help figuring out the solutions. will have participation points in class sometimes.

Great professor. Explains concepts in a way applicable to everyone, and makes sure to answer everyone's questions after class. I learned a lot from him, and on top of that none of the tests or quizzes were difficult. Highly recommend him for 2060 if you plan on taking it.

Hershfield was a great professor.He was very accommodating in office hours and seemed to genuinely care about his students.Lectures were very clear, made great use of examples and diagrams.Often helped on difficult homework problems and always took questions.The class was rather difficult, but fair overall.Highly recommended.
Significantly better than Pektova, but regardless I received a B+ in the course strictly through the use of Tutoring Zone.
Had a very clean, methodical way of explaining some difficult concepts. Funny, enjoyable lectures.  Wish he would have been the only teacher, bc the other lady (Petkova) was awful.
Great at teaching and helpful when preparing for exams. What more can a student ask for.

Dr. Hershfield is a great professor. I really enjoyed actually listening to his lectures and he teaches the useful material and how it applies to problems, unlike the other professor. Very clear and helpful outside of his class.

Dr. Hershfield does a great job teaching the concept sof physics that are extremely hard to grasp.  Goes at a slow pace, DOES NOT DO POWERPOINT!!!  He prepares you for the clicker question that is about to happen, and he is nice enough to write solutions to the previous exams, which makes studying for the exams significantly easier.

Didn't have him as a teacher, but he was the course coordinator for 2049. Tried to talk to him in his office about a test. He was very condescending, spoke over me mid-sentence, treated me like an idiot (made an A, for the record). Glad I'll never have to deal with him again.
Dr. Hershfield is very good at explaining things and is very helpful and patient outside of class.  I would definatly recommend him.
If you have any prior physics experience the class is a joke. Very easy, minimal effort required.
Best professor I've had so far in college. Physics is not meant to be easy and Hershfield's class is not necessarily easy BUT he's the best you could possibly expect. Take him if you can!
I thought Hershfield was a fairly good teacher, and his tests were very fair and easy. If you have the opportunity to take this guy for physics 1, I definitely would.
Good teacher, engaging with demos and stupid jokes, if you don't do well in his class you have only yourself to blame.
Tests are hard (average on the final was around 50%) and his lectures are worse than Acosta's.. who is at least amusing in a nerdy/awkward way. Demos are cool tho.

This guy is smiling all the time and pretending to be a very "good" person. Let me tell you why: Smiling all the time because he does not know anything about physics. He is trying to hide his deficiency by smiling. He just copies the textbook into his notes, and from his notes onto the blackboard. Social engineer! Useless and nasty!
Outstanding

Um, if you just do the homework and study a bit and memorize some formulas and pay attention in class, you can get an A.  His demos are cool.  And it really helps to have taken some physics course beforehand...or you may get lost early on.
Great teacher
No Comments
Very knowledgable man.  Very clear on his expectations of the students.

Has trouble correlating questions with the book. Alot of poorly written ambiguous questions as well. Somewhat interesting material taught by someone who doesnt seem too interested in it.  HITT forces you to go to class, but count as a full test grade.
This class is not easy at all. Not easy A. He helps you out in class with the hitt responses yet his tests cover alot of material. Take it if u like to learn not for slackers.
No Comments

You have to be involved in her class. I had many questions throughout the course, but she was very kind, responded promptly, and clarified all of my concerns. There are exams every other module, but if you listen to the lectures and complete the assignments for each module, you should pass. If you put in the effort, she's not the worst professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Be aware of this professor. She has an AI detector and uses it on discussion boards. Do not even put it in your own words as it detects that too. The only somewhat strenuous assignment is the discussion boards as you have to include 2 concepts from the textbook, something that surprised you, 2 questions, and maintain it all within the word count.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I liked that Dr. Mawdsley was very organized and gave clear expectations, but I did not like the structure of the class. She gives 6 exams, and they are only available to take over the weekends (Friday to Sunday). The exams were pretty difficult and would likely be better quality if the questions were free response instead of MCQ.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: ~1,000 words total for discussion posts (300 word min for responses). Exams make very direct references to the reading. For example, a question might ask about a specific wording that was used in one of the readings. Exam every other week only available on weekends. The lecture videos are not particularly helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As a middle school teacher with MDCPS, I can say Dr. Mawdsley's young adolescent class prepared me for my classroom job. Importantly, her methods on teaching growth mindset helped me encourage my students (who went months without a teacher before I arrived) improve their confidence and state test scores! Class & professor 100% worth taking!

1 reading guide/wk. Sometimes reading was too much but you can just read specific sections. Easy quizzes/exams w study guides. Simple material but not boring. She's good at telling if you BS something, likes students who participate. Super knowledgeable lady. Sometimes makes comments on annoying little things, but it doesn't impact grade.

Dr. Mawdsley wants you to write the definition of things word for word on her tests. I feel like I didn't learn anything beneficial in the long run. The feedback she gave on assignments wasn't helpful. Once she took off points for something she didn't include in the rubric. Her rubrics aren't clear and she'll take off points for random things.
Dr. Mawdsley is by far the best education professor I had in my time at UF! She's super helpful and her class gives you practical experience great for any teaching job! Take her class!
Instructor grades based on her criteria in her head. She was not nice and I do not suggest taking her class. Everything was based off the textbook and it does not even seem like she has read it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Mawdsley is my favorite professor I've had at UF; I also ended with a 100 in this class. Content is interesting, and so are lectures/discussions. Work is easy, as well. One reading guide is due per week, and a study guide is given a week before every quiz/exam; the questions are the exact same as what is on the real thing. Great class/prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I absolutely love her. Do not let the bad reviews scare you; she is a phenomenal professor who makes very applicable lessons meant for future educators. She is understanding and tells you exactly what you need to do to succeed on her tests. 5 stars, would take again.

By far the best professor I have had at UF she knows her stuff really well and is always encouraging regarding feedback. Taking notes was not super necessary because she is very thorough in her lectures and if you are passionate about adolescents and teaching then you will not be bored. TAKE HER CLASS

Dr. Mawdsley runs her class in a very accessible way. She made efforts to connect with each one of her students to advance their learning opportunities. Although I am only an education minor, I gained a lot from her lectures and the practical experience which accompanied her class. Put in the work, study, participate, and you will be rewarded!

So rude. Ironic that she teaches about teaching and does the opposite of what her lessons say. Prepare to regurgitate exactly what the textbook says or get questions wrong. Super harsh on attendance too. Honestly, my worst prof at UF so far. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures are feel boring and endless 99% of the time. Your only salvation are those sweet 5 min you get to spend in group discussions. Attendance is mandatory; you only get 1 unexcused absence. Participation matters. There is 1 group project. Regurgitate info from the readings verbatim on quizzes/ exams or face the consequences. Take only if req.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Mawdsley isn't the best lecturer, but her class is pretty straightforward. She's clear in her expectations, and as long as you follow them, you'll do fine. Not my favorite class I've ever taken, but not the worst either. A lot of reading and writing.

Does not teach how she says we should. Is honestly just rude. I expect a lot of myself, but she all but requires exact sentences to be repeated from the readings in short answer questions on tests. Her lectures take forever, and does not respect that you have a life. So many readings, and you better remember every word. Glad its over!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: By far the meanest and least understanding teacher I have ever had.

She is a tough grader and forces students to take exams on weekends. She literally only opens exams on Sundays, and refuses to open them earlier. If you have church AND work doubles every Sunday like me, youre screwed.
Rude, cold, and does not care about her students. By FAR the worst professor I've had at UF.

Dr. Mawdsley and I got along fine. The workload is manageable if you have time management skills. Her exam and quiz reviews are clear and specific, but beware, her papers are confusing to complete (model yours after the sample papers she uploads.) I have an A in her class because I studied a LOT, so be prepared to do that. Very harsh grader!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's OK. Volunteering is required by the department. I wouldn't take this class unless it is required for your major. She can be a tough grader and tests count for 60% of the grade. She makes it clear what will be on the exam and is willing to help clarify.

I was surprised to find Dr. Mawdsley did not have any reviews. She is a great, very down to earth woman, who wants you to truly succeed. You have post chapter quizzes due at the end of each week, which are chapter heavy. If you get the online textbook as well it makes it easy to do well. Tests then use these questions. Also a group project & paper.

I took COM1000. Definitely take that for a chill and easy A class. Dr. Harmon is very sweet and gives amazing feedback for written works. The course has/uses Packback, discussion posts, quizzes and exams. Everything is super easy to do, quizzes and exams are open note. You would have to try to not get a good grade in this class.

I loved this class (Instagram and Empathy). The assignments were straightforward with lots of group work and the class is very engaging. To get the most out of this class I recommend you do the readings and viewings before class. There aren't many with only a few that surpass 10 pages.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very easy Quest 2 course that you can finish with little-to-no stress. Information from the course is valuable too, and you get regular feedback from your TAs on the assignments you submit. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took this as a quick Quest 2 class that I could finish before my internship started, and lucky for me this is one of those online classes that you can finish in two weeks if you want to. Harmon is a very enthusiastic lecturer, but all grading is done by a TA, and mine was very lenient.

This is not only one of the easiest classes I have taken but the information is relevant and important. All grading criteria is very clear. Most of the time as long as you make an effort to answer questions & meet word count, you get full credit. Do the extra credit it boosts you grade so much! One late assignment allowed (take advantage of this)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very nice professor and the lectures are engaging. The workload was very manageable and the material was interesting. Overall easy class I recommend!
Just show up to class, do your speeches, and you'll get an A.

Dr. Harmon is a good professor who is really passionate about what he is teaching. There is only one big group project where you make a skit and there are two easy papers. The assignments are either easy or just interesting! His lectures can get boring sometimes but overall, I recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Harmon is a very nice professor who cares about his students and their success. His lectures can get boring but most of it is just common sense. He grades your speeches pretty easily and his exams aren't very difficult either. The only graded assignments are your speeches, exams, and points for attendance.
She's a good professor and is good at explaining the topics but her exams are HARD. They are much more complex than the practice problems.
Just watch the pre-recorded lectures/read the textbook and do the homework. Pretty easy if you pay attention.
Put the work in and you'll do fine. Just get ready to dedicate a lot of time and effort to the class if you want an A.

There is not much to say because you learn just about nothing from her and everything from studyedge. There is no reason students should feel like they must pay extra for outside sources (like studyedge) in order to just pass the class. The teacher should be doing more, or formatting things differently. Disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests questions are nothing like the practice she gives. Talks super slow in lecture videos so notes take forever. Honestly just a bad formatted class. Makes it near impossible to get an A ethically with current format.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Goslinga. She gets too much unnecessary hate just because her class is difficult. She cares a lot about the class and her students and is an amazing professor. I would recommend using all of her provided materials and Study Edge to get a better understanding of the material!!

I genuinely believe Professor Goslinga is overhated. The class does require a good amount of effort; however, it is definitely doable (no study edge). I relied on the textbook to learn the material and watched her lectures to check my work/for her material overviews. Do all the practice problems she provides and get used to her wording for exams.

Prof Goslinga explains the material pretty well and sets clear expectations, but can sometimes rush through the material, leaving some students confused. Make sure to stay on top of hw, lecture videos, and practice tests to make sure you're prepared for the tests. As long as you do that, you will not need study edge. DO NOT PROCRASINATE.

Dr. Goslinga gets such a bad rap purely because her class is difficult. You have to put in a lot of time and effort into this class in order to be successful, but it is doable. I highly recommend talking to Dr. Goslinga because she is amazing and very helpful. Also, do Study Edge.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly, this class isn't that bad considering how everyone talks about it. Just watch her pre-recorded videos and the study edge, and you should be fine. Professor Goslinga is actually a pretty good professor and seemingly a really fair person.

She expects you to watch an average of two hours of pre recorded lecture videos before every lecture in addition to the two hour lectures she records on Tuesdays and Thursdays! Make sure you have plenty of hours a week to dedicate to this particular class. In my opinion she also overcomplicates most of the lecture material.

Goslinga as a professor was okay, although her videos on Mediasite did little to nothing to help students. McGraw Hill is required for this class and requires hours upon hours of poring over to understand the material. The exams are difficult, studied 7+ hours a day for a B. Prepare to dedicate >50% of your study time to this course.
Ugh FML :((

Goslinga is an amazing professor. The class itself is not hard just follow her calendar and stay on top of the work. I had Study Edge for the first exam but canceled it for the second. The Study Edge tutor sucks for this course. Just rambles, curses, and doesn't want to be there. Just use Goslinga's extra practice. Would take her again.

Unpopular opinion: this class wasn't terrible. She is a good teacher, but it's obvious that she knows this class is a weed out course and therefore makes it seem all tough. The content isn't the craziest, but it takes some adjusting (haha) to get used to it. Get Study Edge just to have the extra practice exams, it helped me.

This class is extremely hard. There are resources available to assist, but it doesn't help that everything is online. Don't take unless you have to. The tutor for this class' study edge sucks btw don't waste your money.

Professor Goslinga is an amazing professor teaching a difficult class. Attend the lectures in person and don't be afraid to ask questions. Then you will do great! There was a concept I was seriously struggling to understand and I asked her questions about it after class and she patiently explained it three different ways till I understood it!
exams were hard

Goslinga is a great instructor. She goes through every single concept that is covered in the exam and also goes through homework questions with you, if needed. The exams were difficult, but you have plenty of time to complete them (her motto is do the test twice, so she gives you time enough to do that).

Professor Goslinga is an amazing professor! You MUST follow her schedule in the syllabus or you will not have time to study before exams. She explains things very clearly and is open to questions. She explained a difficult concept to me three times when I did not understand it. Follow the schedule, go to office hours, and you will succeed!

She knows this material very well, and I always appreciate when a professor gives a lot of review time and practice problems. Your performance in this class will be reflective of the effort you put in, but Professor Goslinga makes sure you have what you need. I really enjoyed this class.

Professor Goslinga is just fine, however, this course is intense. I took it as a 6-week course over Summer A. There is so much material and so many lectures to watch. Especially with it being over a period of six weeks, I had absolutely zero free time. Don't take it during the summer unless you want to lock yourself in your room 4 days a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pay attention to every detail and make sure to keep up with the class. It isn't an easy class but she's a very fair professor, and is willing to explain things to you if you're confused. Watch all her pre-lectures and go to lecture in person.
She knows what she's talking about. The class isn't that difficult if you take the time to learn the material properly. Very test heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is very fair and clear in her grading criteria. She does not have minus grades, and she has an optional final exam to replace the lowest grade. Exams are 30 questions online, so the best advice is to do ALL practice exams and ALL connect. Study Edge is super super helpful. GO TO OFFICE HOURS AND LECTURES!

Exams are tough but doable. Pay attention to her lectures and the practice problems and make sure you got those down. I didn't use study edge and I was more than prepared for exams. I would highly recommend attending office hours. I attended towards the end of the semester, and wish I'd attended earlier. She's super approachable and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Goslinga is nice and helpful during office hours.The practice problems/notes from lectures are great. Review the practice exams multiple times/rewrite ur notes and you'll be fine. This class is not that difficult, ppl exaggerate for no reason. Just make sure u keep up w the work and know you'll need to study. Study edge is not needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tests are extremely difficult. Get study edge and do practice problems and try to get all homework and quiz points. Failed this class by .5 for a B and was extremely frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very difficult course, I did well on homework, but it did not equate to good grades on exams, no matter how much you study it comes down to whether the information comes to you or not
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Everything you've heard about this class is true or honestly worse. Getting a B is doable, an A is possible but hard. YOU NEED STUDY EDGE. The exams are weighted heavily, which makes it so hard to get a good grade. The exams are tricky & unnecessarily hard. If there's a small detail somewhere… it'll probably be tested. Her voice is annoying af too.

You can use study edge, textbook, pre-recorded lecture, and/or live lecture. If you put in the effort and use the resources depending on how you learn best, an A is doable. She goes through the content quite quickly, so use the TAs or older students if you have questions. VERY exam-heavy, definitely do practice problems and practice exams to study.

She's good. Exams are a bit tough, but the optional final at the end of the semester is easier than all of the other exams and really boosts grades. Make sure to get all the Connect points and do all of the optional work on Connect. She pulls some exam questions right from those.

Exams were rough and unapologetic. As a lecturer she's covers the information well but each lecture is agony to listen to as she's just plain boring. Not a professor you are excited to go to class and learn from.

I started only using study edge lectures halfway into the course but I still think she is a decent teacher. People overrate the difficulty of this class in my opinion. Put the time into actually understanding the material, and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly probably don't need study edge unless you want more practice problems. I don't think you need to read the textbook as long as you really pay attention to the lectures and do the homework on your own, it's good practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very frustrating to learn how many people cheated in this class. Makes me feel better about not getting an A, though. Her lectures are thorough and she gives you the types of questions you will see on exams.  But the class is way too exam heavy. I have 95% on homework and quizzes and 3 B's on exams. I have a low B in this class. So frustrating.

The class is difficult but very manageable if you put in the work. The professor provides a lot of optional practice problems that I recommend doing in addition to the homework/quizzes. With some variation, each chapter probably took around 3 hours for the lectures and textbook, 2ish for the homework and quiz, and 3 hours for the optional practice.

Goslinga is a knowledgeable teacher and teaches topics thoroughly. There is no need for Study Edge since there is so much practice between the book questions, the in-class problems, and the practice exams. One can easily spend the recommended 10-14 hours a week studying with those resources alone.

Very manageable class, most people say it's hard because they don't put in the work. She is a good lecturer, and goes through practice problems at the end of every lecture that are similar to exams. Watch the pre-lecture videos and the lectures and do the work. Also, she is very nice in office hours if you have questions.

This class was not as bad as it was told to me by many other students. If you do the work, it's easily doable. Read the textbook, watch the pre-lecture videos, and watch the lectures. Review the practice problems she does at the end of class, there are very similar questions if not the same just different numbers on the exams.
You know that one scene from Mean Girls where Regina George writes in the Burn Book, that is how I feel about her and this class

She is a good lecturer, and the course is organized well. The tests try to trick you, but she warns you to look out for tricks on the test. This class is not nearly as difficult as it is made out to be.

The content can be difficult and there is a lot of information to know for the exams, but it's not bad if you put the work in. Don't fall behind. Watch out for trick questions on exams. This will probably be your hardest class up to this point in time (have fun with FIN3403).

The class is a tough entry level business class, but if you do all the work you can at least get a B. She's a good teacher but the class is very test heavy. If you use the Study Edge for it, it makes the class a million times easier. I only did Study Edge and didn't watch lectures and got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class is tricky because of all the different ways that you can be tricked on the exam questions. Do as many practice problems as possible to do well. I recommend using study edge to get extra problems to just keeping hammering home.

From the beginning, she makes it clear what is expected of students in the class and definitely makes you work for your grade. The tests are pretty difficult; you can't just wing it. Your grade will depend on how much time and effort you put in to learning and practicing the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: On the bright side, she always curves final grades so not everyone fails. On the downside, if she didn't, everyone would fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Class is designed to make you fail, even if you do all of the work and practice that is available to you. Goslinga teaches well and designs her lectures and assignments so you feel like you are doing well, but then the exam is full of curveballs and tiny tricks that can make you fail even if you know everything by heart. Take it somewhere else.

Very easy class if you're mathematically oriented. Watched lectures once, reviewed practice exams right before the exam, and got a B in the class. Total of approximately 3-4 hours per week of work for me for that grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: This class is really hard in of itself, but I think that the professor explains the concepts fairly well, and going to office hours for extra help is a good idea. Even though homework isn't graded, it's definitely a must. The exams are really straightforward, without any trick questions, and the TA's are willing to go over the problems.

This class is really hard in of itself, so I think that the professor explains the concepts fairly well, and going to office hours for extra help is a good idea. Even though homework isn't graded, it's definitely a must. The exams are really straightforward, without any trick questions. I didn't use Study edge but I heard that it helps.

Professor Goslinga's teaching style wasn't the best. She lectures off of powerpoint which did not help me understand the material. Study Edge definitely broke down the material in a more logical way. The key is to do multiple practice problems to she how different questions can be worded and Study Edge gives you hundreds which helped me do well.

I started the class watching lectures but I found that what she taught and what she actually asked on the exam were a little bit different. I ended up using Study Edge every week and only watched her lectures when I had nothing else to do. Study Edge gives you lots of practice questions which is pretty much the only way to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Goslinga is a very challenging professor. Her exams are very difficult, cumulative, and make up 90% of the course grade. I strongly recommend getting study edge for this class as they give plenty of practice problems that replicate what you will see on the exams. The textbook homework assignments are not indicative of what exams look like
Goslinga is a really good teacher but the class is impossible. Definitely use Study Edge if you want to pass. Don't bother watching lecture all you need to do is go to the Study Edge weekly reviews.

Prof. Goslinga teaches the class well and is specific on what she wants to you to know for the tests.  The tough part about this class is being prepared beyond measures about the material on the test so any questions can be answered.  I used Study edge as a supplement to this class and have done very well because of it.

I think she is a pretty fair teacher. Her lectures are well done and she usually tells you all the information you need to know. That being said, she is overly fond of trick questions and the practice that you receive online through mylab is pretty ineffective . Using Study Edge practice questions helps as they simulate the test more accurately.

Currently, I am on track to get an A in the class. Best way to phrase her is as hard, but fair. Most of your grade depends on 3 tests, so just don't get behind on work. Study Edge's weekly videos helped ensure that I fully understood the material, since the practice problems she gave were more surface level and I would recommend it for the course.

This class is super difficult and totally a weed out class. They make the exams super hard and I had to start studying well prior to exam time. The only reason I passed this class was because of Study Edge. Study Edge offers chapter review sessions and exam review sessions with tons of practice problems. The practice problems are super helpful.

I never read the textbook or used Study Edge and I pulled an A simply by watching her lectures and doing MyAccountingLab. The lectures are extremely dry but to the point. She doesn't waste a minute of classtime. The exams are hard but managable. Everyone knows it's a hard class, just put in the time/effort and you'll be fine for a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Goslinga is a good professor, in the lecture she explained things clearly.  I think this course is not as hard as some students said. If you watching the lecture and try to understand how everything work, it is a really easy class. I got an A just by watching the lecture before exam and doing the practice exams which she give us.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Very tough class; takes time and effort but you can do it. Prof knows what she is doing, but the lectures and reading can be a lot to handle. Whether you have a tutor or Study Edge (I didn't use SE), practice until you're confident. Read the book, print the lecture slides to write on, practice ALL the optional homework, and study long in advance.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is and should be a "Weed out" class. It is a good place to begin telling if students are willing to work since the work itself is easy but it is a lot of busy work where details are essential. Nonetheless, the Professor makes it unnecessarily more difficult than it has to be. She herself is an inadequate Professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Definition of a "weed out" class, but for a ton of majors here at UF. If you MUST take it at UF, Study Edge will be your saving grace. Watch lectures, use every Study Edge tool possible,  and work your tail off by doing practice questions and old exams and you can manage a C and move on. May the force be with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: There is a clear gap between the information provided by Professor Goslinga and the textbook, not to mention what is presented on the exams. The professor does at best a mediocre job at attempting to explain the concepts in this course, and completely fails at properly communicating and providing the students any real foundation in accounting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This is one of the first difficult classes you take within the business school. She makes the tests unclear and very vague. The only reason that I was prepared for any of the exams or quizzes is because I used STUDY EDGE!!! STUDY EDGE is a MUST they saved my life and my GPA!!

C+ is the only C and lowest grade I have ever received. For the first exam, I relied solely on watching lecture and reading the book, which resulted in a D. For the next exam, I started using Study Edge and the practice exams they provide, and I did a ton of practice problems and got a B+ on the exam. GO TO CLASS AND USE STUDY EDGE!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a very clear lecturer. It definitely helps if you read the chapter before watching or attending lectures.

I took this with no prior knowledge about the accounting and I didn't use Study Edge or TZ at all.  If you watch each lecture thoroughly (write down everything) and do ALL of the MyAccountingLab questions you should be okay.  This class is difficult so schedule a lot of time for it. Don't get behind on the lectures!  STUDY STUDY STUDY FOR EXAMS!
She explains basic accounting well enough, but she makes the subject more dry and boring than it needs to be. Read the textbook, make outlines, and watch every lecture if you want an A.

Definitely a tough class. Do not underestimate this class going into it and be ready to put time and effort into it. If you are comfortable and somewhat knowledgable with accounting then don't get study edge, if not then get it. Be prepared to study for over a week for each exam and don't be afraid to drop the class. Do not rely on the curve.

The class is definitely one of the toughest classes I've taken here at UF. Although the tests are hard, Goslinga is a good professor. She knows what she is doing. My tip would be study at least a week in advance for every exam. Also, get good grades on the quizzes and group projects. If you do them, you will be fine.

This class is extremely difficult because it is a weed out class and it is designed for students to fail (too many business majors). If you go into the class with this mindset then you will likely pass. You'll need to study for at least two weeks for exams and definitely use Study Edge because they want you to pass while Goslinga does not.

Professor Goslinga is a very knowledgeable and really cares about her students. If you really try to understand the material, you will do well. Do not use StudyEdge or TZ  because they are not needed, it's a waste of money. I got an A in the class without using either of these services.

This professor is great. Yeah, the class is hard, but if you are a UF student you should be able to handle that. School isn't about finding really easy A's. It's about actually learning the material so that you can be useful to the world after college. Easy A's don't make you useful to the world. Professor Goslinga does.

Horrible excuses of a professor.  Exams are ridiculous and the difficulty gap between practice problems provided and what's on the tests is massive.  Unless you're an accounting major, do NOT take her class.

The class is exactly what it's said to be. Very very tough and a lot is weighed out on the 3 exams throughout the semester. Her lectures are hard to get through so I used study edge to help me pass the class. Ended up with an A

Pretty much knew what I was getting into when taking this class - it's not fun and definitely not easy material. I struggled a lot as the class was getting started, but ended up doing okay in the end. Big shoutout to Study Edge because relying on Goslinga alone won't help out your GPA.

My first piece of advice is take this class at a community college. I promise you the   stress and anxiety from Goslinga is NOT worth it. If you are dumb enough to take it at UF (accounting majors) make sure you get Study Edge because you're crazy if you think you can do it alone.

Professor Goslinga herself knows what she is talking about. She is clear cut in her explanations. The absolute biggest advice I can give-DO NOT assume your grade will be similiar to old practice exams! The real thing is much harder. One is not even a real exam the other is a summer exam. Stay on top of it, do weekly if you can at TZ or SE

She really knows what she's talking about, and does a pretty good job of getting it across. The hw is not mandatory but honestly of you do it and understand it you'll be fine. Just make sure you read each question on the exams really carefully because they do get tricky.
Goslinga knows what she's talking about, no doubt about that. The material isn't individually difficult but it's a lot of material and really to mix up if you don't do the work.

DO NOT TAKE AT UF! I studied diligently for weeks leading up to the exams, using TZ, old exams, practice problemseverything. I could teach the concepts I had them down so well. Taking the second exam, it was blatantly obvious she was trying to trick us. She makes this intro class unreasonably difficult. Unless you're an accounting prodigy, beware.

Don't take it over summer. It was the one and only thing I did for summer A. The practice exams she gives you are from THREE YEARS BACK how are you expected to prepare for the exam with those? The exams are beyond tricky.  I read every chapter, did all the pre and post HW, the quizzes, the tests,everything. I barely passed. Take it somewhere else.

This is a deceptively hard class. Just when you think you understand the material she actively tries to trick you on the tests. She sometimes curves exam grades but do not rely on that. I used TZ for the second and third exams and it helped significantly.

Class really isn't as had as its' reputation would have you believe. Just watch the gorram lectures and read the book and you'll be fine. I watched every video and read every chapter and got an A. No TZ or studyedge, I didn't even do that many practice problems. You guys need to stop complaining!

So she is a nice individual outside of class but for class (and particularly tests) she is a pain. The only way to survive is with TutoringZone. The concepts are easy but the tests are a pain in the rear.

Goslinga sets you up for failure on the exams. I suggest going to the lectures, doing all the homework, reading the textbook, and definitely get the full semester reviews at TZ. Eat, sleep, and breathe this class and its possible to pass. The quizzes are easy, but make sure you do them to get the points, you'll need them!

You have to work for the grade. The majority of the class gets a C. You need a B for Accounting Majors. Everyone else needs a C to pass. Read all chapters, go to live lecture so you are not distracted watching it online. TA's are very helpful and TZ as well! Quizzes straight forward, and tests are tricky.

As long as you read the book, watch the lectures, and do the homework problems, you should definitely get an A. People who say this class is extremely difficult probably didn't do the homework, because it isn't graded; however, the homework problems are almost exactly like the questions on the test.

I got a C in this class at UF over summer C. Weekly quizzes are worth 10% of your grade with each test being 90%. She doesn't curve heavily, about 40-50% of the class gets a C but only the top 15-20% get A's or B's.

I really enjoyed the class. I am an accounting major and it prepared me for my high level classes. I would not suggest people to take it at UF unless they're accounting majors, you don't need the depth that Goslinga requires you to learn in the material.

Goslinga goes out of her way to make the class hard, but it's not impossible to do well. You really need to practice old problems over and over again. The book wasn't helpful. And definitely go to TZ, they know what they're doing.

Very hard class. It is a weed out class so be prepared for hard exams. Tutoring is HIGHLY recommended. She is boring, but the subject really isn't interesting. Homework is not graded but it helps. 3 exams are 90% of the grade, so do bad on those and you are screwed!!!

This was a very difficult course but it's very useful. I read each chapter in the textbook before watching the lecture and then I printed out her lecture notes and wrote on them as I watched her lectures. If you're not an accounting major I recommend you take this class elsewhere. But is is manageable if you put a lot of time towards it.

I took this class as a Political Science major as a part of my Business minor. I got an A on my first 2 exams, and I'm waiting to hear back about the final. Just read the chapters, watch the lectures, and actually do all the homework assignments and you will be fine. This class is completely manageable as long as you make sure not to get behind.

VERY, VERY, VERY DIFFICULT. Highly recommend not taking this class at UF unless absolutely necessary. It is way harder then it needs to be. You will feel prepared for the exams and then go in and she will trick you in any way possible. Have never worked so hard or studied so much for a class in my life and will be lucky to get a B.

Not a good teacher at all. Hardest class I ever took and she purposely makes the tests hard. I read the book and did the online my accounting lab and did great with those two things and bombed every exam and failed the class.

I took this class last spring and got an A without TZ or SE. You just need to read the chapter prior to lecture and make sure to actually watch the lecture. Do all of the homework problems. An A is definitely possible.

Goslinga is certainly one of the least lively professors I've had in the business college. Do not try to get through this class without TZ or SE. The textbook is next to worthless and the lectures will only help your understanding a little.

I took this class in the Spring and it did require a lot of time. I studied for it every single day, read every chapter in the text book, went to all of her lectures, took notes in class and I was fine.  Prof. Goslinga was very helpful I met her in office hours and asked her questions. She was quick to email back and always willing to help.

Currently taking the class and I must admit it is very demanding. I wouldn't say it's hard but it requires ALOT of time to prepare yourself for so much new information. If you spend adequate amount of time a B isn't impossible. An A requires substantial time. Might want to go easy on the amount of credits if you take it fall or spring.

Very difficult class.  For the final alone I did all homework, did very well on quizzes, did over 200 practice problems, watched every lecture, and did tutoring zone. Failed the final and got a C in the class.

People make this class out to be terribly hard. Yes, it requires a lot of time and studying, but as long as you do that, you will do fine. Her tests are fair, especially if you prepare properly, and she is always willing to help. The more practice problems you do, the better!

This class is do-able, by every means. Don't wait until last minute and you'll be fine. It's a class you do actually have to study for, so just be prepared for that. Do the homework, read the book, re-do problems in class. Use office hours if you need, she's a really great professor and always willing to help. You can do this. :)

Do not slack off in this class or you will fail. Tests are tricky and you must be prepared for anything. Print off the powerpoint slides and take notes on them. Exam 1 is the easiest and make sure you do well on it to offset your grade on Exam 2. Make sure you do the practice exams multiple times to familiarize yourself with how she asks questions.

DO NOT TAKE AT UF!! I watched all the lectures, did all the online problems and practice in accounting lab. Read the book. Made a D on Test 1. Studied for two days straight and just bombed test 2. The questions are nothing like the practice exams.Her wording is tricky and misleading. I have to drop the class! Hardest class I've ever taken!!!

Class is not as difficult as the entire UF population makes it out to be. READ THE CHAPTERS before lecture and somewhat understand them. Also, pay attention during lecture and do EVERY practice problem in the slides.  The MyAccountingLab problems can help tremendously as well. Constantly keep up with the material and an A is easily attainable
The class is hard, but not impossible. Do every single problem available, including all of the study plan. If you do all the study plan, you will get no less than a B.

My hardest class. Harder then chem and calc combined for me. Take a printout of the powerpoint slides. take notes from her lectures on those printouts. Just review those notes and slides for her tests. Book is only useful for background information.3 exams including final. 2nd exam is hardest. final is just lots of material. DONT mess up first exam

Honestly, many people complain about this class, but she is a very good professor. Her lectures are easy to understand. If you have trouble she may not make exceptions for you. But I think she is very fair. You just can't treat it like a normal class and actually apply yourself since this is probably the 1st time you come into contact w/accoounting

This class is not hard to pass with a C. Watch lecture, do MyAccountingLab H/W and practice problems before taking the online quizzes. If you're looking for something better than a C you really HAVE to apply yourself. She curves D's and F's on exams so that they are in the C range. Her questions are tricky & hard, accounting is a foreign language.

DO NOT take this class lightly...start strong, and end strong. I made the mistake of slacking off after my first test, and now I have to retake this class. Not an easy class, and her questions are very tricky. Do alot of practice problems!

Terrible class! If you are minoring in Business, you only need a D to pass the class, but after watching every lecture, taking notes, going to tutoring zone, doing all practice problems, I failed the first two exams. I have never failed a class before! I had to drop it and now enrolling into the class at Santa Fe. She is extremely tricky and unfair

Yeesh! The only good business professor out there is Mark Rush. Goslinga has joined the club of people that can't teach business classes. They just go on like it is all common sense. Professors need to realize that their students are new to the subjects they teach. Otherwise they wouldn't be taking the class in the first place.
Hard class mixed with a bad teacher means take this class anywhere else if you can. Teacher/TAs are unhelpful and tests are very hard.

Very poor teacher. Tests are extremely hard and questions are on stuff she barely went over. Final is cumulative, yet you can only review the tests for 1 week after her grades are posted and ONLY by her TAs which have poor office hours, and are crowed. Accounting is hard to begin with, and then you have this teacher. Take anywhere else if you can.

This class is further evidence that UF could care less about their students.  I learned absolutely nothing and this class was extremely difficult for no reason.  Be prepared to put in 30+ hours a week to work toward a C.  Teacher is horrible and makes this class harder than it should ever be.

I thought Professor Goslinga was great. She's really thorough and she goes over all the intermediate steps so you always know what's going on. She talks really slow tho so I recommend watching lectures at a faster pace. I would say all u need is to watch lectures and write notes when watching, read, and do the hw. And you should be fine. Not so bad

Run Run Run if you can.  Teacher curved the 2nd exam from a F to a C since basically everyone FAILED.  I want UF to give me my money back from this sham of a "teacher."  Also, exceeding difficult to almost impossible to get a good grade with this useless teacher.  Thanks UF.

Professor is terrible.  If you need help, you can go to her TA office hours where 1 TA helps 10+ students.  Ridiculous.  Her tests are impossible.  Only 3 tests and yet they are over 5+ chapters?  That's impossible.  I even got a tutor and she said she never heard (except at upper level) of an accounting class being this difficult.
This class is a time consumer! I suggest definitely going to class and doing all the practice problems. Her exams can be harsh  but TZ was decent prep.

Like the others have said there's a lot of work you need to put in to do well in this class. I did all the practice problems and went to TZ and did all of those problems, it sort of brought it all together for me which was great.

The class isn't too hard but the key to getting a good grade is putting in a lot of time. Skim the book and do LOTS of practice problems. TZ was a good review but should only be a supplement. Teaching is good but goes slowly at times. Do quizzes with a friend.

Really tough class but an A is definitely possible. TutoringZone is a waste of time and money. Read the book and do the practice questions in MyAccountingLab.  Don't just copy the practice questions from lecture.  Pause the lecture, try it yourself, then write it down- you'll learn much more! First test is easiest, second is a lot harder.

Bad lecturer, she isn't even a teacher.  She only reads off the powerpoint's in class, the ones she didn't even create to begin with. Not surprising when you ask a question and she doesn't know the answer.  All her stuff is from pearson. This is a grad level course, and she teaches it like her undergrad one. Online quizzes? Seriously?  Insulting.

This class is not a "blowover" business class. I'd equate it to the orgo of business, so if you're going to take it, you have to go in with the mindset that this class is going to be your focus, because you have to know the material as if you were taking the CPA. I couldn't swing it in the midst of sciences, so I'm taking it at home over summer.

Professor Goslinga is VERY FAIR and is ALWAYS willing to help! The reason why many students do not do well is that they do not put in the time. Exam 1 is the easiest and then it gets more difficult. Very possible to get an A. I never went to Tutoring Zone and did geat. Do practice problems, ask quesions, and go to class! Good luck!

This class requires 100% of your attention and people do poorly b/c they are used to doing well w/o having to try hard.  Whenever she does a problem PAUSE & do it yourself first!  DO NOT MEMORIZE!  U have to use the material learned from the book/text and know how to apply it.  Only way to survive.  Got an A on all exams: IT'S POSSIBLE! good luck!

Goslinga is hard. This class is an "Easy A" anywhere but at UF, so I recommend taking it somewhere else. TutoringZone is basically a MUST to pass the course. The tutor can explain the material better than Goslinga. You can tell she is proud of her low pass rate. Especially because she does not curve until the end of the semester.

I feel bad writing this review, b/c she's a nice lady, but my gawd her voice will make you want to slam your head in a door! She's slow and your brain can't help but tune her out. So do the study plan in my accounting lab or you'll be screwed.

First, TZ is not helpful so don't waste your money. The first exam is pretty easy, just pay attention in class. The second exam was ridiculously hard, so don't fall behind and study like crazy. The final was pretty easy, as long as you studied for the first two you'll be fine. Watch lecture at double speed and look to the book, not her,for answers.

Okay so this class really is NOT that difficulty, at least the material isnt.. I could probably tell you all of the basics of accounting. Her exams aren't that difficult eaither, just really tricky with the wording of the questions. The quizzes are what really screwed me in this class. She doesnt clearly specify when they're do and she only leaves

goslinga talks slower than anyone i have ever met.  i put her on 1.75 speed while watchin lectures and she still bored me.  i watched all the lectures, read the book, and did most practice problems and still got a C.  her curve does not even make sense.  good luck!

This Class is so over rated. Everyone is going to tell you how hard it is, but it?s really NOT!!! You have to have to; have to study like crazy for the exams. But if you study (watch lectures and read the book) you will be fine. I easily got a B in the class.  The material is not that hard, and she is a great teacher.She does lots of examples!

Goslinga was a surprisingly good teacher. She went slow and stuck mostly to the book, but she presented the material in an easy-to-understand manner and tried to ensure that everyone was up to speed before she moved on. Staying on top of your work is essential for this class; don't leave everything until the end, or you'll screw yourself over.

Intelligence alone won't get you the A in this class. If you want a B, you'll have to read the chapters and keep up with the class weekly. If you want the A, do every single practice problem of every chapter. TZ has and will be useless for this class. I'm a 4.0 ECON student that read every chapter and ended up with a B. No curve on our final either

Outlined every chapter, went to every class and did every single suggested problem. i'm going to get a B+. She reads off the slides and is essentially useless. i was lucky and had a GREAT TA who explained things really well but he's leaving now. the most time consuming class i've had. be prepared her exams are rough.

Never went to class only to Friday labs (she reads off the slides?!??!). MUST READ BOOK. I outlined the chapters; did most of the problems in the back of the chapters; took the practice exam. I should be getting a B or B+. First exam ok, SECOND EXAM a KILLER, third exam in the middle ish. Study hard... it's an A minusable class but with hard work.

If you put in the time to study, and understand the concepts and how the transactions work together, you can get an A. You have to read the WHOLE textbook, TZ doesn't seem to help much. The teacher is nice, and she's open to questions before, and after, class. Not the hardest class ever, you just have to study A LOT.

She read off the slides but did clarify many things and did a lot of practice problems. She was very helpful and even answered questions in the large lecture. Quizzes are always easier than exam but necessary points to do well. Study for the quizzes as you would for the exam, and you'll do well on both! Tough class but manageable with preparation.

The lectures are boring; she just reads off the powerpoint slides.  But she does practice problems which are a big help.  READ THE BOOK AND DO ALL THE SUGGESTED PROBLEMS. First test is easy, second and third are killer.  I went to all the lectures, outlined all the chapters, and did the suggested homework and squeaked by with an A.

Goslinga is a nice lady, but don't be fooled by her Southern Charm. Tests are challenging, especially test 2! Read the book BEFORE lectures (yes, attend class) - it makes the lectures much easier to comprehend and absorb. Do well on quizzes and study hard for tests! I worked my butt off and got an A minus. Its annoying she uses minus grades.

Class was my most difficult one. Happy to get a B, but spent 2-3 days straight studying for each of the 3 tests, going to TZ, going to lectures everyday, doing Ok on weekly quizzes, reading the book. There wasn't anymore I could have done, stuff is hard. Not a class you can put off studying for the last minute

Hard class, requires a lot of studying. I would recommend just going to class even though she pretty much read off the slides. The more you hear something, the more it sinks in. Also, you MUST read the textbook if you want any chance of doing well. Quizzes are easy, don't miss points here. Tests are pretty hrad. I ended up with a B in this class.

This was professor Goslinga's first semester teaching. Her teaching technique is basically reading off the lecture slides. Class test averages were either low C's or D's, but that might not entirely be Jill's fault. Accounting is a hard class. Quizzes can be easy, just study! TZ didnt help much. ended up with a C in the class.

i think this is one of her first times teaching this class so that may contribute to the difficulty of the class. the lectures are straight off the powerpoints she puts online and the tests are a mix of the lectures, the book, and whatever other impossible questions she can think up. this was a hard class and the second test killed half our class.

matlab is annoying (with AI traps like others mentioned) but other than that if you do the HWs and exam review + past exams (which give extra credit) exams are pretty easy and even if you do poorly the grading scale is so lenient its hard to fail, a C is 68%. i didnt get flagged for AI but seems like theres many others with false positives so YMMV

Reads slides and moves on. Ask a question and she makes you regret it. Learned every topic from YouTube. She embeds hidden traps in MATLAB assignments that flag students for cheating even when they did their own work. Hundreds reported. Her syllabus has a 48-hour plea clause because she knows innocent people get caught. Take someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dont take this class. take the proof based one, the content is slightly harder but it is much easier than having to deal with this "professor"

This woman is painfully obsessed with AI and finding students who use AI. The harmful part is that she wrongfully reports students who she believes use AI, causing numerous issues for them, and then has zero sympathy whatsoever.

Professor is obsessed with catching students who are using AI, to the point of a high false positive rate. An extremely stressful experience despite never cheating in the class, and I've learned significantly less then my peers in linear algebra (not computational). Take the other linear algebra the proofs based one if you can.
Really good grading policy. I bricked the first exam and still got an A comfortably.
Lots of work

I'd give a negative rating if possible. Lectures are unclear and exams are extremely hard. She seems to focus more on reporting people to the DSO and planting "AI traps" in assignments than actually teaching or helping students succeed. If you want a professor who cares about your learning and provides clear instruction, look elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: My complaint is about her obsession on catching cheaters for Matlab. She wastes DO's time and had them come in lecture to talk about the importance of not cheating. She reported 80 students for the first assignment and 50 for the second. I wish her focus was more on teaching than catching cheaters. It stresses me out. She puts AI traps too.

Her lectures are extremely boring, she just gives theorems for you to memorize. That would be fine but she reports kids left and right. In class she announced in class she reported 80 kids to the DSO for ONE assignment, notorious for false accusations. Very stressful experience
I LOVE being reported to the DSO!!!!!
I am a dog.

This class could be SO much easier, but the anti-AI fear mongering and hidden "gotchas" mixed with an abysmally inaccurate exam when compared to any practice material, PLUS the inability to see the results of your exam without going to IRL office hours makes for an extremely unpleasant experience. I'm sure I'll pass, but I can't wait for it to end.

She could focus on improving the bad lectures and tests, but instead wages an obsessive war on AI use. Expect hidden 0-pt AI trap prompts, gloating about "catching cheaters," and mass emails about students being reported. Some poorly-placed traps(like within instructions to search online) may catch innocent copypasters, causing needless anxiety.

This was the most stressful course experience I've had. The professor discourages independent self-learning and focuses heavily on policing rather than teaching. I am a student who has never had an academic integrity issue in any previous course, yet I was referred to the DSO in this class, which caused significant stress and anxiety.

Her lectures were alright and I found them useful to understanding the material. Matlab didn't really help me learn much though and wasn't important to the class. Be sure to not use AI because she uses prompt injection to catch students and report them.

She needs to start focusing on providing more content to learn the difficult software she wants us to use (math and coding tg) rather than being so paranoid and reporting half of the class to the DSO for looking how to use the software. Very paranoid woman, even if you don't cheat you'll be accused. Requires side recording for tests too which alr.

She is bad. She expects us to know everything about a software that is for math and coding for really long assignments and just rely on a discussion board for questions. Gets you reported “for cheating” even if you truly dont and does it at the end of the semester where now you have to wait till spring to know what will happen with your credit

She's notorious 4 reportin way too many people to the DSO so watch out. Even if you're innocent expect there's a chance u'll get reported. Plus the DSO's notorious 4 not takin the student's side on things from what I've heard too. I thought I was done w this class only to get reported in December 4 an assignment from mid semester. This' ridiculous.

There is no way 3.4/5 is accurate this teacher is the worst she doesnt teach well, doesnt answer questions and in general doesnt care about her students. if the rating was based on enthusiasm she would have a 3.4 i give her that but if you dont have a religion then get one to pray for this class

I want to take the time to write this because the programing assignments in this class are ridiculous. If you dont have previous matlab experience then expect to suffer, she expects you to complete the assignments with no previous knowledge of Matlab and is so focused on cathing you for cheating if you look up stuff in google.
Shes enthusiastic for the class but has no regards for teaching well. Goes to fast and doesnt explain well.
The teacher doesnt know how to teach. when she explains something leaves no room for questions and completley ignores people with their hands up.

This teacher is the worst and if you dont have coding experience and search up something in google which was in the instructions of the coding assignment she will still catch you for cheating and report you to the DSO. The school should kick her out and assign someone who makes sure their students are understanding the class

Overall, great professor. Class is very straightforward with lectures, lecture quizzes, MyLab homework, exams, and MATLAB coding projects. Exams are a bit conceptual but she offers plenty of opportunities for success. Attend her MATLAB Q&As as she gives some of the solutions and even tells you how to write the code. Do all the extra credit offered.

Very nice lady and teaches linear algebra very well. One homework plus an LQ per lecture, very manageable. Holds a review lecture before each exam and gives plenty of study material. MATLAB is annoying but doable. Lots and I mean LOTS of extra credit! Overall, I enjoyed her lectures and thought she gave us lots of opportunity to pass with an A.

Class content is easy as long as you follow along with her in-person lectures (available on canvas). Assignment in MATLAB are difficult, especially if you don't have a coding background, but review sessions and TAs largely give you the answers if you show you've tried. Explains difficult concepts well, but can speed through some content for time.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Her lectures were great and really helped me understand the material, she had a short Q&A section at the end for students who had questions, as well as plenty of study materials prior to each exam. She also dropped the lowest exam grade of the semester, essentially making the final (cumulative) exam optional.

The lectures are just fine, the matlab assignments are super annoying but overall i thought the 3 tests were fair. She is super paranoid about cheating and requires a side-view camera angle for all the tests.

I like her strategy of teaching the class by bringing printed notes to class and annotating them with her. She provides a lot of extra credit opportunities, and the final exam is optional to raise your grade. MATLAB assignments are a bit difficult, but she walks us through a lot of it.

Lectures are very difficult to understand. You're better off looking online for alternative lectures. There are multiple resources for studying for exams, but NONE of them are remotely similar to the actual exam. She requires a tripod setup for exams and constantly accuses students of cheating. EC and curved grading scale are nice, but that's it.
Genuinely debated jumping off Century Tower every time I went to an exam.

Terrible professor as I am going out of my way to write abt how terrible she is. Cares more about catching cheaters than helping students understand content. Accuses students of cheating when there is no evidence. everything does not prepare you for the test. Took a lin alg course in high school and still struggling w her content.

genuinely one of the worst professors I ever had. hw and lectures do not help you prepare for the exams as much as they should. she can also be very unempathetic towards students when it comes to understanding the material. matlab assignments are helpful to understanding a bit of the coursework but overall very time consuming

She seems nice. I just don't like the way her tests r designed. It's testing ur memorization ability rather than whether u actually understand & know how to solve certain problems. I wouldn't mind her testing on terminology & thm stuff if she allowed a cheat sheet on tests. MATLAB is cool to learn, but it can also be a pain. Ec is nice though.

3.5/5.0 is really an overestimation on the quality of the class. Rather than hosting traditional office hours for academic support, this professor holds one-to-one academic interrogations on a regular basis via Zoom. She also reported nearly half the class to the dean for mass "academic dishonesty" on open-book assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lecture material critically lacks detail and context, making comprehension nearly impossible, reducing it to rote memorization. Prof. Huang's dismissive or sarcastic response to student questions creates a toxic atmosphere. This behavior discourages students from seeking necessary clarification, creating a climate of fear and anxiety.

Kind person, but lectures were fast and confusing. Many students likely used AI because they were lost, not dishonest. She still reported nearly half the class to the dean. Notes didn't match exams, and the course felt disorganized and stressful.

Professor Huang seems like a nice person, but is not a good instructor. Her notes do NOT prepare you well for the exams, and her lectures just aren't good. She's not very good at explaining things and moves very fast.

The class itself is very manageable, I did bad on every exam besides the optional final and came out with an A. The notes and assignments are incredibly easy and not on par with the exams, she does not prepare you well. You really have to understand linear algebra conceptually to do well on the exams

I took Comp Linear Algebra over the summer and it was honestly pretty easy. Just watch lectures as they are assigned and do all the review and you'll be good. Yes, the exams are only 10 questions, but they are very similar to review material. Only big annoying part is the MatLab assignments imo. Make sure to watch her Q&As for those.

professor was okay her explanations and lectures were fine. PLEASE do the matlab assignments early they are the bulk of the work for this class and similarily take up the most time. there are weekly qa sessions for them if needed. TAs can often grade pretty rough. exams are all mcq about 10-15 questions. lots of ec oppurtunity.

I think Professor Huang is a very nice person, just not a great educator. The lectures and exam review didn't prepare me for the actual exam content. Half of the exam review content never even appears on the tests. Very abstract at times and since exams are such a big portion of the grade, it is really punishing. I'd take anyone else if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is cake except 4 extremely tedious MATLAB assignments that are a huge portion of your grade. (If youre having to hold q&a sessions every week for a type of assignment, maybe the students arent the problem!!) TAs are strict graders and Dr. Huang is a terrible teacher. She takes AN easy class and turns it into a huge waste of time.

This class is very poorly designed. The lectures are abstract, mostly proofs that Huang doesn't explain very clearly, and usually half the homework question types aren't covered. Half your grade is based on exams, but the review content just doesn't cover everything on them. You're better off watching YouTube lectures to make it through this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her accent is so hard to understand youre better off watching the lectures on mute. She and her TAs spend all their free time trying to catch cheaters instead of helping us. Even if you dont cheat, odds are you will be accused of it multiple times throughout the semester. I swear I spent more time trying to prove my innocence than the classwork.
Worst professor in UF. Never respect students. Never reply to email

Her lectures are not amazingly helpful for the test content, it's quite abstract proofs that don't necessarily  teach HOW to do the problems. She tends to rush through the problems. You are given weekly homework problems to do which actually teach you how to do problems you will be tested on. A is very doable for this course b/c of extra credit.

I took Dr. Huang online and she was great. She has excellent online lectures and the class was run very well and grades were posted in a timely manner. The class wasn't difficult at all and I would highly recommend it for those who want to learn linear algebra without memorizing the proofs.

The lectures are pretty abstract (talking about multiple dimensions), and she never tells you what the math actually is. She just goes through proofs of what you just need to memorize. I can't see you how you would apply this in the real world.

The exams had only 10 questions with no partial credit, making it tough to score above 70 even if you understand most of the material. The class also has a terrible TA.She does offer extra credit, but even though it doesn't make this class any nicer.

Honorlock exams are proctored using a side-angle camera, which isn't working properly all the time, making it super hard to stay focused on the exam. If you don't set it up correctly or it's blurry/stops working, you get points deducted. You need a clarification on the score from MATLAB, and the TA has to re-run your assignment; you get deductions.

This professor is the best for Linear Algebra. If you go to lecture, and you do all the assignments and do the practice material for the exams you will get an A. Lectures are extremly clear, and even have extra credit for showing up. She is enthusiastic and knowledgable, and taking this course was both interesting and fun.

Really responsible professor. Took it online. Video letcture is enough for everything. Easiest math class taken. Matlab takes abou 4 hours each and there are 4 Matlabs. The only annoying part about this course is the Matlab and the side-camera requirement for the test. Lot's of EC. Chill class.

Dr. Huang offers SO MUCH extra credit on MatLab, practice exams, and discussion forums, as well as having an optional final exam replacing your lowest exam score. If you do all the homework and MatLabs on time, you can get an A quite easily even if you don't do that well on the exams. Exams are not weighted enough to make or break your grade.

Great lecturer, explained the topics well. If I was ever confused I went to the textbook which was surprisingly good for a math class. MATLAB assignments were frustrating, but other homeworks were not so bad. Focus on learning the concepts and you'll do good. She provides a LOT of bonus opportunites, including iclicker in class.

PROS: Grade is curved, Huang also offers a decent amount of extra credit, so DO IT
CONS: Exams are 10 multiple-choice questions online each question being worth 10 points so it's easy to tank your grade, MATLAB assignments are TIME CONSUMING, very focused on catching cheating which makes taking Honorlock exams stressful, youtube better than lecture
Comp lin alg is a very straight forward class, if you pay attention during lectures and do the homework you'll do fine
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Huang is kind, but she teaches quickly and often skips steps. The first half of the class was difficult, so I always went to office hours, but help was sometimes limited. The MATLAB assignments were tough, and the TAs weren't very helpful. The makeup exam was surprisingly easier than other exams, and I recommend taking the course online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Huang has well designed lectures and the exams will not waste your time with unnecessary arithmetic. If you take the time to fully understand the concepts you will do well, just know that the topics in this class can get pretty abstract, so do your own research and attend office hours when the lectures are not enough.

I've had a *lot* experience with AI/mathematics and this class is one of the best classes that I've ever had.  If you can't cut this class, you can't do AI.  Period.  EVERYTHING is relevant.  Professor goes out of her way to make excellent typed notes *for you* and videos which distill this down.  It's work, if you can't do it, get out thank you.

Dr.Huang's lecture are abstract to understand in person, the online version of her lecture is much better. Take the comp linear class online because she won't post all of the online lecture for in persons.

Ppl say this class is easy, but I disagree... The lectures are pretty abstract (talking multiple dimensions), and she never tells you what the math actually is. She just goes through proofs of what you just need to memorize. I couldn't tell you how to actually apply this in the real world. The grading is curved so very manageable but not a breeze

I feel like they were more concerned with catching students cheating than actually teaching. The lectures were hard to follow, and the exams had only 10 questions with no partial credit, making it tough to score above 70 even if you understand most of the material. The class also has a terrible TA.

Hard to understand in lecture. The class is fast paced but not difficult. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and a redo exam at the end of the semester so it is not hard at all to get an A. Do the weekly homework for practice and you'll be fine.

Overall experience was pretty average, best advice is to just do the homework and it would hard not to pass. Math is more conceptual style, average of about 3 HW and LQ per week, 4 Matlab assignments throughout the semester and 3 exams with an optional final that replaces lowest exam grade. Did not have to attend lectures, available to watch online

Professor Huang is slightly hard to understand, but I was still able to understand her lectures. Exams get harder as class goes on, but there's no final which is nice. This class has a bunch of weird terms and confusing questions, really the only way to do good is just practice problems and the exact same stuff will be on the exam.

Lowkey a fake class. Very easy and it's very well organized, just don't leave all the LQs and MyLabs accumulate or it'll be very tedious to get through. Practice exams and review sheets are very helpful! Professor Huang is really nice, but TA Robert is a little annoying.
