The only reason I was able to succeed in this class was thanks to Study Edge. Professor Harris is amazing, but the concepts were super difficult for me to grasp and Study Edge helped to simplify it all.

The homework and quizzes are good because they are like the tests. I think it's just the right amount of homework. I highly recommend going to office hours if you have questions about anything or need help on hw. You get multiple attempts on hw (it's on canvas). He explains stuff pretty well in his lectures.
Didnt watch many of the lectures and still got a C+. But he is a really good professor and clearly teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Harris was very kind and he well explained the material. Despite this, his lectures were vague for being 30+ minutes each. Wish he wouldve used more practice problems so taking him requires a good amount of work in your own time.

Lectures vague, and it was really hard learning online with no in class stimulation. Tests were 30 questions and mostly free response, which was ridiculous considering everything going on. He is a kind man who seems to care, but in terms of learning, there was not really much to it. StudyEdge and practice is key.

I honestly didn't interact with Harris much due to it being a flipped classroom, and his lectures weren't always worth watching. He was super nice and knowledgeable in office hours, but if my TA weren't great I don't know how I would have survived this class. I taught myself most of the material and definitely wish I got Study Edge.

Did not really interact much with Dr. Harris, but he communicated with students about exams and the homework assignments were very helpful in preparing for exams. StudyEdge is always a great resource, I did not really watch lectures.

Class started very rocky because Professor Harris didn't post homework or quizzes to one of the chapters before it was tested on, so all parts of the Chapter went virtually un-studied for the test. After that, however, the class got back on schedule and everything went well. Class is hard, but grunt work will get you a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Harris is a really kind professor. I thought his tests were fair and similar to the homework and worksheets. Get StudyEdge though to do well. I came in without chemistry background and got an A, but I worked for it. Its really not as bad of a class as everyone says. Dr. Harris is very accessible and willing to help. Expect lots of work though.

Dr. Harris is very kind and understanding, however, his lectures are vague and there were issues in prompt responses, posting grades by deadlines, accurately posting due dates etc. We were always behind the other classes which made studying rough. After investing in StudyEdge and not wasting time watching lectures, I started to improve immensely.

Dr. Harris is undeniably the best professor the chemistry offers for CHM2045. With that being said the course is difficult and you cannot fully rely on his lectures for preparation for homework and exams. It is best to do several practice problems before the exam. His lectures are not bad and certainly better than other chemistry professors at UF.

Dr. Harris made a stressful course even more stressful by posting lectures and pre-lecture assignments late. We always seemed to be a chapter behind other CHM2045 classes and were still expected to test on the same day. We usually had to cram a chapter before an exam. Overall, a cool guy not the best professor. TIP: GET STUDY EDGE

This class can be extremely time-consuming and challenging. There is quite a lot of homework but it does help prepare you for exams along with other practice assignments. Dr. Harris' lectures are not enough to do well on the exams and are not all that helpful. I would recommend keeping up with assignments and doing a lot of practice to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Harris really is a good professor, and cares about helping his students. Chemistry is a hard class overall, but he does a pretty good job of explaining most concepts. Homework/quiz wording is a lot like test wording. Tests aren't curved and there's no extra credit. Study Edge definitely helps

The questions on the exam are similar to the topic of the homework and worksheet questions, but are worded COMPLETELY differently on the exam to confuse you. Exams are difficult (not 100% multiple choice anymore), and I didn't find the lectures to be that helpful as time progressed. Read the textbook and get study edge if you're not a chem genius.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Having Dr. Harris as a professor was refreshing because he seemed to actually care about his students and help them out where needed. The tests are hard (that doesn't change no matter which professor you take) but Dr. Harris is the best option out of the other UF chem professors.

Dr. Harris is a nice guy but just like other chem professors (at least online) his lectures suck. They are just basic introductions and as the semester went on he didn't even give examples. You will need to teach yourself a lot. The class is designed to be a weed out class so be prepared to study a lot. Ive heard he is the best they have though.

There are no past exams, but that's because all of the exam questions are going to be variations of all the questions in the homework, worksheets, pre-lecture assignments, quizzes, practice assignments, etc. Even if you don't know the material that well, know how to answer the questions by practicing or writing down the steps.

Dr. Harris is the best CHM2045 professor at UF. His lecture videos this online semester were fairly helpful and he provides many practice homework and assignments so you can succeed on the exams. The class is a weed-out and is test-heavy but he makes it as enjoyable as Chem 1 possibly could be.

His lectures were easy for me to understand. I did not read the textbook much, I mainly used YouTube videos and his lectures. He is really sweet and understanding of your situation when you reach out to him through email. His homework and quizzes are similar to what is on the tests. Highly recommend him as a chem 1 professor!

Dr. Harris seems to genuinely care about his students which is why I specifically chose him as my professor. My laptop broke down during one of my exams and after I explained to him what happened, he let me take a makeup exam on the date of my choosing. He's an amazing professor who will work with you if you're struggling. Still, get study edge.

This is just a very difficult class for a lot of people in my opinion. Dr. Harris makes the course bearable though and he really does seem to genuinely care about his students. He tries to make the lectures as engaging and funny as possible. The tests are very hard though; you will need study edge if chem is not your strength.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I had Harris for Chem 1 and again for Chem 2. My CHM2046 was split between two professors and I had Harris for the first half. I thought his exams were very fair based on what was included in his lectures, but if you don't study or do practice problems you may not do so well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I took CHM2045 in the spring of 2020 and I thought that most of the information in class and exams were very fair. I will add that some of the HW questions seemingly came out of nowhere so I bought a chegg subscription for $15/mo (because study edge is damn expensive) and was able to pass with an A without dropping a small fortune on study material
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Harris is a pretty good professor for CHM2045, although most of the time I felt that his lectures were not enough to apply knowledge from his lessons to homework. He would teach the basic lessons at first, which were easy most of the time, I just wished he did problems that applied the basic lessons to questions that are similar to the exam.

Never responds to emails. I didn't think he really knew how to teach. Office hours were pretty useless. Survived by going to office hours and practice question from the textbook and previous exams. He has no idea what is on the exam. His teaching got worse once corona hit, which is why I didn't get an A.

Professor Harris is an awesome professor! CHM2045 is a hard class, and he was able to help significantly before the class transitioned online (I had him spring 20 when covid-19 moved the rest of the semester online). Exams are very difficult, and I'd highly recommend study edge. The course became much tougher online, but Prof Harris is the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Harris is the best professor for chem 1. His class is harder though in some regards due to how it is set up. For the exams given though, he is the best professor to have. He is a really cool guy, and he will make your time less miserable. The course itself takes a lot of work. Expect to put more time into it than most courses at UF.

Prof. Harris is currently the best Prof. at UF for CHM 2045. This class is quite a challenge, and if you don't put in the work you will fail. That said, I really enjoyed Prof. Harris. He is funny and really cares about his students. Go to his office hours - they are a big help. I would gladly recommend Harris.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is a tough corse but Dr. Harris was pretty good at explaining things. just takes a alot of practice and studying
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Harris is probably one of the best professors I've had so far. He's enthusiastic about chemistry which makes his lectures much more appealing. He also does not give much homework, but his exams can be challenging; exam 2 especially. Going to lectures, doing practice problems, and keeping up with the content are your best bet.

Dr. Harris is great. I think he is a wonderful professor. He is entertaining and genuinely cares about the students. I am just not good at chemistry so my experience was not the best. From what I've heard, Dr. Harris is the best chem teacher so if you are able to, take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Harris is probably the best chem 1 professor teaching the course. This is a tough class and you can't count on a curve as students make perfect scores. He has an average replace policy that can save you from one bad exam. Study edge is helpful for this class and will definitely help you learn tougher material that he may not cover in lectures.

Compared to other Chem 1 professors at UF, Dr. Harris is the best option. He goes fast but covers all the material and he's accessible outside of class and through email. Not as work heavy as Sumner and cover all the material unlike Lopez. A lot of self studying/learning is required, but stay on task and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Loved him. Super helpful and funny. His class was not too hard but still allowed students to learn the material. I would definitely recommend.

Good overall teacher and person. Cares about students but the chem dept doesn't give much leeway for curves and dropping assignments. AWFUL AT RESPONDING TO EMAILS so if you need something go to him before or after class or during office hours. CHM2045 is definitely a weed out class so prepare to put in a lot of work with no curve
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: What makes him better than all other chem professors at UF is that his HW and discussion worksheets are extremely close to the exams, as long as you do the work you won't find the exams difficult. I think he's a mediocre lecturer, study edge is EXTREMELY helpful in terms of learning content but doing his WS and HW is essential to pass the class.

Makes you buy a textbook then reads from the textbook for lectures. Doesn't explain the topic fully but expects you to be able to solve the highest difficulty problem of a concept as soon as the 25-minute lecture is over.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The best professor for chem 1! it's a weed-out so obviously it's gonna be harder than it needs to be but Harris is very fair. keep up with the material; Study Edge isn't necessary but does help a lot to study for exams. his office hours helped a lot, too. he's a great professor & a nice guy; I would take him for all my chem classes if I could!

I had professor Harris for chem 1, and he was great. He was easy going and did not give too much homework. I definitely recommend getting study edge for this course. While Harris does a great job teaching, study edge reinforces the material, teaches things Harris left out, and provides extra practice. Definitely make sure you keep up w the material

I LOVE Dr. Harris!! He is so amazing, caring, and funny. He knows what he is doing-- don't listen to the other reviews on here saying otherwise. He is BY FAR the best chem professor teaching Chem 1 right now. He gives homework that represents what will be on the exam, but don't underestimate the exams: they are tough and will try to trick you.

It was easy to follow along with the lectures as he posts the powerpoints and lecture videos on canvas. He also allows you a decent amount of time to work out the sample problems and Top Hat. The worksheets completed in discussion prepare you for the exam as they had similar or harder questions. Overall the workload was easy to manage.

Professor Harris comes across as a really enthusiastic guy, but as the semester went on, I realized that he can't explain anything. I went to his office hours once to ask a question and his response didn't make any sense so I ended up at another professor's office hours. Take Korolev if you can. If you have Harris, Study Edge will be your BFF. GL!

Dr. Harris is a decent teacher, however I must admit I never used my notes from that class to study. To get an A in CHM2045, Study Edge is a must. The workload was very doable and class was interesting enough.
Very enthusiastic and made the lectures more interesting and easier to understand. Tophat questions in class everyday mean attendence is required. Probably the best Chem 1 professor here.

Be aware that the chemistry department at UF is trying to fail any students going through it. That being said, regardless of the professor you have for Chemistry you need Study Edge to pass with a good grade. Harris uses powerpoints written by the book and has no idea what is on the exam because he does not make the exam. Quizzes/HW on chegg.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His enthusiasm and ability to lecture enabled me to do very well! By far the best professor for chem 1 considering the homework, which definitely helped with the exams, engaging lectures, and flexibility. I got sick prior to one of the exams and he helped me schedule a retake; he also opened up a past due assignment for a friend. Loved him!

Harris is by far the best Chem 1 professor at UF. Sumner assigns mountains of homework and quizzes that students can't keep up with, and Lopez doesn't teach test material until the day before the exam. Harris assigns maybe one or two homeworks a week, and is really helpful in office hours. On top of that, he's new, so he still cares about students.

Coming into chem I was terrified and it was Harris's first time teaching at UF so I didn't know what to expect. Honestly, he's the best because we had way less homework and quizzes and he was so nice throughout the semester. The tests are the same no matter what teacher you get so just READ THE TEXTBOOK and you'll be okay. Practice makes perfect.

I had Harris for Chemistry 1. Although he makes the material easier to learn, the class overall is hard for students at UF. Get 2 questions wrong on the exams and you already have a solid B. I found his lectures exciting. I would prefer Harris over the other professors in the Chemistry department. He is very social and engaging in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's really chill. The class requires a lot of work.

I absolutely loved his class. He is a great teacher and makes it easy to follow his slides in lecture. He is always willing to help clear confusion and prepares students for the tests. I also did study edge weekly to keep up with the material, but overall the class is very challenging but if you put in the effort you will succeed.

Dr. Harris is the lesser of two evils. I would take him over Dr. Sumner any day. He assigns less work than Sumner. Regardless, be prepared for weekly homework assignments that each take 2 hours and the same thing with quizzes. Also, sometimes his TAs don't even know the answers to his HW or quizzes. He probably will never respond to your emails.

This class is genuinely an easy 100%, but it is A LOT of work. The only reason why I didn't give her a five-star rating is because I do not like her flipped-classroom way of teaching, as there are way too many pre-lecture videos to watch over the weekend,. Other than that, she is super nice and knowledgeable.

Mrs. Amie is the sweetest! She was the lab instructor for Intro to Animal Sci and extremely qualified and knowledgeable about the animal agriculture sector. She brings much experience teaching high school agriculture and running her own livestock operations to the classroom, which enriches the student experience. I recommend getting to know her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Homework isn't too bad, just frustrating if you have a lot of other classes. Labs itself were fun! Loved this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Pretty good. Her Career's class is a lot of busy work. You do get a full drop for a speaker if you can't show. A couple of the large assignments feel random but it's an easy A.

The class itself is fairly easy. However, be aware that attendance is mandatory. Class is normally given at 7:25 or 8:30 (in the ANS building which is FAR from main campus). Every week, you must watch around 2-3 hours of pre-recorded lectures because she DOES NOT lecture in class. The assignments are easy, but it is a lot of busy work.
There is a lot of random assignments but they're simple. If you're pre-vet, save this class for junior/senior year!
Very interesting and useful course, I recommend it to anyone considering veterinary school.
Best professor ever, never hesitate to take one of her courses!

This class was very fun. A lot of the assignments were VMCAS sections to complete to prepare for the vet school application so I would not recommend it to freshmen with little college experience, but it is doable. Grading is done fully by the TAs. Class time consists of presentations from different veterinary professionals, so it is very helpful.

Pre-labs prepare you for class well and the quizzes/assignments are simple. We go on a lot of field trips so transport can sometimes be an issue, but usually there are people willing to carpool. I would recommend this course and instructor to anyone, it was truly my favorite this semester.

Amie is AMAZING! This course has lecture videos to watch before attending class, which can be a bit time consuming, but if you watch them and do the in class assignments (which are very easy) you will succeed. "Quests" are every two weeks and there is a quiz about lectures every week, both of which are easy! Just watch lecture and study a bit!

Amie is amazing! I have her for ANS3006, ANS3006L, and ANS2934. We have to watch recorded lectures and class time is used to discuss and do activities. There is no reason you should not pass any of her classes. If you need help, talk to her or email her, she is very eager to help students succeed.

This woman saved my life, I was struggling with another tough class and missed some assignments. She worked with me and allowed me to submit stuff for some points taken off. She even allowed for exam corrections for half points. Ans3006 is a medium difficulty class but doable. She is also an advisor for internships and is very helpful!

Amie is literally the sweetest professor ever! I would take this class ten times over if I could. Class is super early, but you have to go because there is a quiz on Monday, activity on Wednesday, and a test every other Friday. I would say there is a lot of material but it's nothing super difficult. I would highly recommend taking Amie's class!

Amie was a great professor! The class is taught mostly through prelabs videos, TAs, and different professors that specialize in a certain area. This lab was by far the most fun lab I have ever taken. She does make you do more work than necessary, but you learn a lot about livestock animals.

Amie is amazing. I love the way she teaches makes you engage on the topic even more. For exam she drops your lowest grades and they're not hard either . I'm taking lecture along with lab and lab is more hands on deck with her and you learn alot of things with different livestock animals. The only thing I didn't like was the "how much water" project

Im not done taking the class yet, but it's an easy A! Currently have over 100% due to extra credit on the quests. Basically a discussion class and gives a 2 hour prerecorded lectures every week. 10 assignments are given but are evenly spaced out and theres 7 quests given (one is dropped). One quiz per week but are fairly easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The labs were usually very interesting. You need to go to lab to pass the quizzes. Understand the prelab content bc you discuss it during lab as a group.

Class is focused only for pre vet majors. Teacher gives too much work and waste class lecture time with useless group breakout rooms. Her reviews barely line up with tests maybe half the stuff might me sked of you. not willing to work with students

Overall not helpful to me as a student. I thought she was bad at covering information with her lucture times and wasted them with group breakout rooms. I felt I would have gotten more out of the course with a more seasoned professor. I do not suggest this professor at all, pick another if you want a better class experinece.

Amie was an awesome professor! If anyone is thinking of taking this course, you should take it if you are interested about the different career paths of veterinary medicine, the financial aspect of it, how to get into vet school, and how to maintain your wellness. I am so happy I took this course. Best course I have taken at UF through two years.

Takes forever to grade and forever to respond emails, 2 hours of recorded lectures each week, has 6 major tests that do not line up well with reviews she gave, not willing to work with students or be flexible at all, still seems like it is her first or second year teaching, very cold, take someone else for Animal Science lecture (or lab)

An amazing teacher! I truly loved showing up to her classes. They were very interactive and hands-on. The quizzes and homework are extremely easy as long as you show up to the class. Would recommend 100 times over.

She's a great professor, I really enjoyed taking her class. She actually cares about her students and is willing to do what is best for them. Her lectures are interesting and you need to attend them in order to do well in the class. Her tests aren't difficult but you do have to study for them a few days in advance. Overall, it is a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a great professor and her labs are engaging. The lab quizzes are easy if you paid any attention, though the discussion posts could be a little long and less interesting, but overall it isn't a difficult class. There's a lot of material on each test but the reviews are incredibly helpful! Attendance is mandatory but she drops your lowest lab.

Amie does a fantastic job of keeping her lectures fresh and engaging. I learned so much from this class; it's been my favorite course at UF so far. Amie is readily available to help out or answer any questions and gives great feedback on assignments. I went to her after multiple exams to clarify lingering questions and she always answered them all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I think this was her first semester teaching on a university level. She has a lot to learn, but for the most part was okay. Gives random QOTDs that are ultimately relatively important for grade. Tests can be difficult if you don't go and pay attention to lectures. Takes a while to grade and reply to emails. Can be very dry with you sometimes.

Imler is a great professor, her lectures are not recorded so you must attend and there are sporatic Question of the Day problems which act as attendance points essentially. Great class with lots of qualified guests that lecure on areas in the animal science industry. Must work to earn an A, very interesting introductory class overall!
Could not recommend RUT3443: War and Peace enough as an elective. This course changed literally everything for me.

Prof. Kleespies is a great lecturer! She is very knowledgeable on the topic of the Cold War, and you will learn something new every single time. Get ready to read and watch a couple of American, British, and Russian books and movies. Engaging in class discussions is important, but also super fun. As long as you show up, you will get an A!
Best language instructor I've ever had, extremely helpful. As long as you go to class and put in effort you will easily get an A and actually learn in the process

Dr. Kleespies is a great professor! She really care about her students learning. She makes sure you get to practice pronunciation a lot. There are vocab quizzes for every unit(6 units) and a test for each. The tests are open book and she is pretty lenient on grading. I learned a lot from this class and definitely would recommend taking her.

I took beginning Russian 1 with Dr. Kleespies. She was an amazing professor to have. She kept the integrity of a language classes with exams and quizzes, but graded in a way that was understanding. Russian is a very hard language to learn, but she made it fun. She even planned a field trip to the Russian store in Gainesville!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Kleepsies is easily my favorite professor so far in my college career. The online format of my classes made them all a bore to come to, except this one. This class made me genuinely excited to attend. Though there is a lot of reading involved, you will love this class if you are interested in the subject matter.

Dr. Kleespies is genuinely a good person. She was very attentive to all or class (which was less than 30 people), and made sure EVERYONE participated. As mentioned prior, there is a lot of reading if you don't want to sound like a doofus in class discussions. Stay on top of the papers by writing them in advance. Just be proactive and participate.

Dr. Kleespies is a very kind professor and truly an expert in her field. The class involved about 50 pages of reading per class period, but it is very manageable if you enjoy literature, and she makes the class discussions very engaging and interesting. This was one of the best courses I have taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Kleespies for beginner Russian 2 and she is amazing. Because she is American and learned Russian in college, she went through the same process that many of us are going through and knows how to teach to our demographic and get rid of bad habits. Actually was excited to attend class every day and ask many questions.

Extraordinary professor. Incredibly passionate about russian language/literature and so knowledgeable. Very fair grader as well. Lets students learn at their own pace. Very accessible outside of class and through email. Lots of room for extra credit improvement. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Best professor ever. Dr. Kleespies is smart and caring. She really wants her students to learn. You can tell she loves teaching! I decided to take two classes with her this semester and I was constantly thinking and practicing. That being said her classes take a lot of work, but if you are willing to put the effort in you will be just fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved this class! It's hard enough reading War and Peace, but she made the class so interesting that I would gladly read it again. It was difficult reading 50 pages every two days, but completely worth it. She is very knowledgeable on Russian history and literature.

Dr. Kleepsies is phenomenal, certainly one of the best professors I've had at UF. She made Russian lit accessible and enjoyable, but also encouraged discussion and free thought. She cares so much about the subject, and that is evident in the way she leads class. Take her if you can!
Best language teacher at UF!
Single handedly the best professor I've ever had. Absolutely amazing clarity, helpfulness, interest in the subject...Kleespies is an angel among bad professors.
Prof. Kleespies is phenomenal. she really knows what she is teaching and encourages indepependent creative writing. TAKE THIS CLASS!
wonderful professor.  Very open to talking about anything Russian in her office hours.  Have taken 2 of her classes & i cant get enough!!!
Great teacher! Very involved and passionate about the material! Easy and fun classes with a lot of discussion! Kind of like a high school teacher/class but I loved the course. Take her!
Very Nice! Always willing to help and doesn't make you feel stupid when you say something wrong. She was the nicest person ever and I really miss her now. Very very kind. She is very smart too!
Professor Kleespies is awesome!!! Take her if you can!

Dr. Kleespies is an AWESOME teacher, you really do learn a lot, and she helps you begin to think about various aspects of Russian history and contemporary issues. A hard class with a LOT of reading but worth it! She is very enthused with the material and has a tremendous wealth of knowledge. Be prepared to work, but it will pay off!

Great teacher! The class had a LOT of reading, but professor Kleespies is phenomenal, relaying ideas and getting you to think outside the box. Really looked forward to class every day. The research project was a bit daunting, but she gives you the tools and is always willing to help you out with ideas and strategies.
Dr Kleespies is a great teacher. Her grading is fair, and you'll learn a lot in her class. It's also not terribly difficult to get an A in my opinion.
Oh my God. Sweetest, nicest professor ever. Crystal clear, and extremely well informed. Definitely take her class!

professor kleespies is an awesome professor who's always more than willing to help students out, but her class special topics wasn't very interesting. if you want a russian lit class, this is perfect, but it's not for students who want to better their russian skills.
LOVE INGRID!!! You will truly enjoy her expertise and passion about what she teaches. Though it may be some more work than you are used to, she is a fair grader and a great person.

Amazing! She understands both english and russian very well, which is rare in the department. She makes every lesson fun. As a tip she loves the show LOST, so find a way to slip that into conversation and you'll be on her good side. TAKE HER CLASS!
she's really passionate about russian. easy class. i liked that we got a lot done and she was pretty lenient about stuff.
One of the best professors I have ever had.  Extremely clear and very fair in terms of grading.  Enjoyable class.
The best teacher I've ever had.  Whatever the subject is, just take her.
Awesome.
Great quest 1 option!

obviously very very smart and super sweet (gave us cookies at the end of the year 😭) 

loved the lectures and I thought the reading selection itself was very well rounded/fun (cried ALOT at the short stories/novels we read) 

KEEP ON TOP OF READING! you WILL fall behind on easy tests and lectures that you should not fail if you don't read
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: (comedy and citizenship) Prof. Ingram is sweet and an easy grader. Her lectures and activities can be kinda boring or drawn out at times but the overall material is interesting. Readings every class but no reading checks or anything, just class discussions. Bit of writing but nothing crazy. Pretty solid option for an Honors Quest

Dr. Islam is incredibly knowledgeable of the course topics and has plenty of industry experience to make him a wealth of insight for the field of robotics and RTOS, which increased value of the class even further despite challenging assignments. One of the best professors I've had the pleasure of being taught by. Absolutely goated with the sauce

Good lectures with plenty of industry insights, though they can be slow at times. The course structure relies heavily on the lab section. Be prepared to spend a massive amount of time on the G8RTOS to do well. Grading consists of 2 lab quizzes (10%), 1 midterm (only 10%!), 6 labs (60%), and a final project (20%). TA-driven course.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't like his teaching style. Unorganized slides, randomly writing stuff on the chalkboard. Exam questions do not correlate well with what he teaches in class. Examples shown in class are very few. The final exam and projects simultaneously.

I took EEL4745 (uP 2) with Dr. Islam and very much liked that class. Only later did I realize that the TA's carried that course. I dislike his teaching style where he rewrites things from the slides on a chalkboard and "solves" problems. He arrived late for most lectures (~5 mins) and 20 mins late to his own Final exam w/o giving us an extension.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Puts a lot of effort into teaching, and you'll learn a lot through the assignments. However, he's somewhat strict with grading. He once held a paper-based midterm quiz without allowing much time to complete it, and he has high expectations for project outcomes. Overall, though, he's friendly, and I enjoyed the course.

Prof Infante was okay. If you do all the work and put just a little bit of effort in you'll be fine. Only downside is that their too sensitive about this whole academic misconduct stuff and feel like every little thing is considered academic dishonesty even if you think it isn't.
I you told me you had a worse Spanish professor I would call you a liar.

I was a SPN1130 student, so my experience might be different. Profe Infante was super chill.  There were a lot of assignments on the Voicethread and the Contrasena platform, and the TAs were awesome. The course is super easy, just participate with your coach, do assignments, and put effort, and you'll pass. Oral project and 2 exams included.

I could've gotten an A in this class if 1) The professor showed up for her classes and 2) She wasn't so harsh at grading a beginner-level course. I want to stress that her classes were awkward, cringe-worthy, and mostly boring. In those periodic times that she actually showed up to teach, all I thought was "only 50 minutes left until I get out."

Tough grading on homework assignments and tests. No leeway for small mistakes regardless of assignment. Expected you to be very proficient at the beginning. Would regularly show up late or never show up at all. Felt like the substitute was there more than she was. No extra credit. Learned more from the online homework than her lectures

Maria Infante is super hypocritical about her policies. She stresses that participation matters and to try your best then berates you if you mess up in her class. She also requires you to immediately get to work and only speak in Spanish in her room even if you are 20 minutes early. She will dock you for coming in late but will come in late herself

Iman is a wonderful and personable professor who stands out as the highlight of UF's film program. She's consistently engaged and wants all of her students to succeed, no matter what. She pushes people and cares more than just giving us a basic grade.

She's an amazing professor! She's very knowledgeable in her craft and what she does. She cares about her students a lot! Go up to her and engage, ask her questions. Don't be afraid to engage extra to get more advice etc. she's the type of professor you'll remember throughout your career.

Wonderful teacher, who cares about her students' success. She is always approachable and informative when answering questions. Her support has made an incredible learning experience, and her teaching will last me a lifetime.
Iman Zawahry has little if any professional experience.  How disappointing.

Iman is an incredible professor. She really cares about her students and will do everything in her power to ensure their success. She clearly communicates expectations and will give honest feedback so your work demonstrates the best of your abilities. She never lets you settle for less than what you're capable of. Her class is more than worth it!

Iman is a brilliant professor and Industry Professional. She only wants the best for every student so there might be some tough love shown occasionally, but I promise it's just because she knows your true potential. Highly recommended all of her courses!
Islam in Media & Pop Culture. Participation is the biggest thing. She's an amazing professor and super easy to talk to. I had fun doing most of the assignments even though some were heavy topics.
Odd choice to have a person with few credentials and little experience teaching a course like this. She is very nice but I didn't come here for nice.

EFP is a great class with Iman! There's a lot of assignments but all of them are catered to teach you about the camera and different lighting. You get out what you put into the class so make the most of each assignment and try to make them good! Iman has a ton of industry experience & if you participate in the class, you'll learn so much from her.

Iman is one of the most amazing professors in the Jschool. She truly cares about her students & wants them to succeed. I've learned so much from her and actually feel prepared for a career in the film industry. The class is very intensive but Iman guides and helps you along the way. I can't recommend taking her classes enough & wish I could again!!

NCF is also one of the best classes I have ever been a part of. If your dream is to go into filmmaking then this class will be a dream come true. Iman gives you a lot of room to experience things on your own, but she is only one call/text away and she genuinely cares about all of her students. She is one of the best professors I have ever had!

RTV3320 was a really fun and impactful class. You get to learn how to use professional camera equipment and make some great videos. You definitely learn how to work in the industry and the creative process behind filmmaking. Iman is very positive and encouraging, making it a joy! I would definitely recommend taking it with her!

Iman allows and encourages creativity in every aspect of this class. She's there to help and guide you in implementing your vision for your work or you and your classmate's work. Highly encourage taking one of Iman's courses!

Iman is one of the best professors I've had the pleasure of learning from and working with. She's incredibly knowledgable and truly cares about her student's progress and growth. If you have the chance to get to know her, do! Her passion and laugh are contagious and although the grading can be tough sometimes, the amount you'll learn outweighs it.

NCF is an amazing class that throws you in the deep end in a good way. In this class, you have many roles mirroring a film crew and are trained in these roles both in the technical and the creative aspects. Iman will always be there to help but won't hold your hand the entire time. The class does a good job of making you more responsible! Recommend

This class is pretty easy-going if you're looking for something that's fun yet insightful. You learn so much about Islam in the media and Iman brings in awesome guest lecturers. It was one of my favorite classes at Uf!!

The best class at UF if you want to go into narrative production!! It really pushes you to think about how you can be a better storyteller and Iman gives great feedback. She really cares about the students and wants them to make films of the best caliber possible. I highly recommend taking this class, it's a great portfolio/resume builder.

The best class I've taken at UF. I really appreciate all the effort Iman put into creating this class. We made 3 short films as a class and also got to have a different role for each film. This class requires dedication and a lot of work but it's so fun and a great way to build your portfolio! 10/10 recommend this class.
This class was so fun and Iman was always there to help with any questions I had. She provided great feedback which was really helpful for the assignments!

Islam, Media and Pop Culture was such a great, informative class! We got to do really cool things like talk to prominent writers and comedians who are Muslim, and ask them about their journeys navigating the media landscape. Pretty easy, but very important in the modern day to be learning about! Also, Iman is hilarious and a joy to be around!

Narrative Collaborative Filmmaking with Iman was probably the most important class I took all throughout college. Its a ton of work, and involves a lot of time outside of class (we film 3 weekends during the semester) but if you want to make films, its totally worth it. Iman teaches you everything you need to know to get started working on set.
EFP with Iman is such a fun easy class to take! As long as you go to class and participate, youll probably get a good grade, and also learn a lot! Definitely recommend

I took Iman's Islam Media and Pop Culture class and it was very easy! There aren't too many assignments and they aren't graded very hard. There's a lecturer in almost every other class and they are all very interesting people. Iman is also very positive and energetic, making the class more fun.

Iman is one of the most caring professors I've met at the University of Florida. She is accessible outside of class and is knowledgeable in what she teaches (just look at her credentials!) The coursework for this class isn't too difficult, but you definitely need to put in the effort. I can't recommend her enough.

Much like most of the classes under the Telecom Film Production major, this one blows. The lectures are less stimulating and require less critical thinking than you could expect from an 8th grade English class. Imans advice is inconsistent and doesnt elevate your writing. The only helpful part of the class was creating the mock industry pitch.

Professor Munoko was one of my favorite UF professors. Her flipped classroom approach encouraged collaboration and made it easy to ask questions. She covered many useful topics, and although only two exams made up most of the grade, they were fair and reflected the material.

Munoko is quite possibly the best professor in the accounting department. Pay attention to her lectures, read the textbook and do the practice questions she gives to prepare for the exams. Definitely not a free A, but most of the class gets at least a B. Classwork was annoying cause she doesn't drop any assignments so you have to go to every class.

Not bad! I just made quizlets of everything she says in the pre-class lecture videos and I got a B on exam 1. Exams are 70% of your grade, so do the +2% extra credit. Assignments are easy A's if you don't miss any classes class since they're done in class and hard to complete alone. But she is accommodating and helpful if you must miss.

Dr. Munoko is a very nice person, but her exams are worded strangely and material will be presented in a strange manner that is not introduced at any other time in the course. There are only two exams which make up 70% of your final grade. Despite this, she might be the "best" professor to take for BP.

I really liked Munoko, she cared about the students and pretty much all of the non-exam grades were easy 100s. Beware of the exams though, they were brutal and it was really easy to think you knew more than you did. I ended up doing poorly on the first exam and hustling to raise my grade on the final, but there was a nice curve.

BEST professor I've ever had. Very organized and knowledgeable, clear instructions, practice tests, potential curve. Group work is easy. Great feedback, makes a point to speak one-on-one with every student. She truly cares about her students and even let us take the final exam a day early to avoid doubling up with the FAR1 final on the same day.
Old man yelton was the goat. Just save your questions for office hours since he's not trying to waste time on them in class

he's pretty funny during lecture; he has a dry sense of humor. he explains concepts well and does relevant sample problems during class. there is also iclicker 5% extra credit. do practice exams and understand the concepts discussed in class. if you just know how to do the math and don't understand the conceptual aspect, you will not do well.

Attendance is not technically mandatory, but the iClicker is worth 5% extra credit. I found the class very difficult, as the lectures weren't very organized or helpful. The iClicker extra credit, StudyEdge, and textbook are what saved me.

1/3 professors I had for phy2 w/calc, he was easily the funniest. He taught the fundamentals so the difficulty of his lectures vs the other two is not fair to compare. The 3 exams in this class are extremely difficult and worth 25% of your grade each. Hours studying left me with slightly above avg results, despite my pretty strong understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is really hard, and he doesn't really help that much through his lectures. Office hours are good, but his lectures aren't that great. Better than Takano though. Make sure to understand HW's to the tee, and study hard for the exam.s
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best lecturer out of the three I had. He's very funny and engaging while also managing to explain the topics clearly.
Professor does teach according to his own methods. However for neurodivergent students there is some inflexibility I noticed. Accommodations from DRC were not taken seriously by him.

This class was tough, but he was the best lecturer of the three that rotated. Taught better than the other two professors. Read the book, and do practice exams. There is an iClicker in this class. No curve on exams, and very little extra credit.

Yelton is a fairly good lecturer. He's pretty funny which helps make lectures less boring. If you pay attention in lecture and understand the homeworks, you should do pretty well on the exams. The textbook is actually very useful and understandable for this class.

All three of the professors for this class were awful. I came into this class with an excellent background knowledge in physics, but their complex way of explaining everything made me worse at physics than before I came in. Once we got into the final unit which is not covered in high school physics, I was lost and went from A to B+ with the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The GOATT. Professor Yelton helped me so much in this course. He is undoubtedly the best one out of the three. He explains things well and helps you really understand the topic not just memorize the solution. Consistently go to his office hours, and you will pass. I'm speaking from experience because I would definitely have failed without him.

Best professor compared to others but that isn't saying much. He at least goes over more practice problems that are useful for the awful HW. I have never taken physics before so this class was terrible, but your best bet is teaching the content to yourself. Class is curved enough that even I could get an A-, but every exam average was about 60.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was ridiculous. Taking AP Physics in high school was the only reason I did well because the lectures were super confusing and a bunch of time was spent deriving equations instead of teaching you how to use them. Luckily they give a bunch of practice exams, and you better do them all if you want a decent grade.

Professor Yelton was great. This was a big lecture hall, but he managed to make it funny. Physics is difficult, but he explained the topics pretty good. He also cracked a joke or two in the class and made the atmosphere overall better.
Not a great professor, but to his credit, it is hard to be a good professor for physics 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: yelton is the better lecturer of the two. still difficult topics and you will not do well without doing extra outside of class and homework.

Dr. Yelton does a good job explaining the topics. Physics 2 is pretty boring, but he's pretty funny so that makes it easier to pay attention. As with most professors, Dr. Yelton is a genius so sometimes he struggles to understand what makes certain concepts hard for students, but as long as you're getting help outside of class you should be fine.

I had Yelton for PHY2048 as well, and this class is difficult, but Yelton's lectures were infinitely better than Korytov's. He's funny, easy to listen to, and fairly good at explaining the class content. I did rely on StudyEdge heavily for this class and found I scored better when I did. Good luck!

Funny British professor. Lots of dry and sarcastic humor, but he explains the material very well and keeps things real (drops many hints about what will be on the exams and how to do well in the course).
Lectures were very clear and easy to follow, he genuinely seems to care about the class and the students, going above and beyond to make complex topics easy to understand.
If he doesn't think your question is good he simply wont answer it(but in a roundabout way), a mid teacher but very funny lecturer, not all that helpful, but not a worse case scenario either.

He is very clear in his lectures and answers questions well, but the sample questions he gives in class are much easier than the ones on the test. He writes hard test questions, but the basic concepts are the same for what he practices and what he adds to the tests.

Yelton is a solid professor. His lectures get confusing at times, but he's insanely funny. Physics sucks at UF, but Yelton makes it more or less bearable. However, he hates using actual numbers for questions, so be prepared to leave answers in variable form.

Yelton is a really funny guy but again not the best teacher. Be prepared to go through the material super fast and have to teach yourself most of the content. His jokes kept me awake but I was often lost in the lectures and had to spend lots of time out of class to reteach the content to myself.

Dr. Yelton is a very engaging professor to listen to. However, his lectures, alongside the other professors we've had this semester, are incredibly fast-paced and barely provide any meaningful information in class. I don't dislike these professors as much as I dislike the curriculum they teach (it's very poorly structured); so, keep that in mind.
Only thing that got me through this class was Study Edge. 10/10 recommend getting it if you are taking this class! Exams are very hard and Study Edge prepares you for them.

John is a great lecturer since he 1. cares about individual students performance, 2. offers targeted explanations in his office hours and outside, 3. considers individual hurdles and accommodates special needs, 4. listens to and incorporates feedback in his teaching. He focuses more on conceptual understanding than maths, which I disliked.

I would strongly recommend taking Physics 2 at Santa Fe instead. Professor Yelton works best for students who are strong in physics, and not ones who need need more help. He moves too fast through material and covers very basic problems for examples and then the homework is much harder. I was able to pass this class only because of Study Edge.

I had never taken a physics class before. Yelton is not a good introduction to it. I did so poorly on the first exam before I turned to tutors completely. Physics is probably gonna suck no matter who teaches it though

Yelton is funny but the material in the lecture doesn't resemble the material tested. The homework would take 3-5 hours minimum without any outside help but it only weighs 5% of your grade. Since tests make 75% of your grade, it's better to just study for the exam and ignore lectures since it's so superficial.

Yelton/Hamlin duo is one of the greatest combos to ever exist at this institution. Yelton goes through examples fairly quickly, but attending the lectures and reviewing lecture notes after class will make the material easier to understand. Graded on HW (each week, dont wait til last min to start), weekly quizzes (simple), exams, and some EC.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Very entertaining yet informative makes jokes and has demonstrations for a lot of things so you can visualize what you are learning. If you do the work that is required, which isn't too much, you can get a good grade.
I love Yelton's class. He makes physics interesting and easy to understand. The exams are fair enough, definitely do the practice exams. Do the work and you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Yelton, while not the better professor in my opinion for PHY2048 was still very good at what he did. He definitely made things a lot more complex than they needed to be many times. I had to use StudyEdge to get a better grasp content. He can be a little pretentious but overall still very good, just be prepared to put in a lot of your own work.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Yelton is a pretty good teacher given the circumstances. He is surprisingly funny (ask to hear his British accent) and good hearted. He can be a bit hard to ask a question, but lectures are okay. When it gets too confusing you should really read the textbook before class. Grading is fair, overall not the hardest class you will take.

Yelton taught alongside Hershfield when I took Phy2048. Yelton goes through complicated problems very quickly right after introducing the concept. He essentially throws you in the deep end while copying the work from his second monitor and says "mhm" while trying to explain it. If you can pick up Physics quick, he's for you, otherwise I Wouldn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Yelton is a good professor but he goes pretty fast through the material. Make sure to stay on top of studying and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Yelton explains the actual concepts very well and he has a great sense of humor. His lectures are my favorite this semester. He does go fast on algebra, but if you take notes and review them later you'll be able to think through the steps he takes. I've never taken physics in my life, but I have been able to do well in this class so far.

I'm currently in his class and he is the worst at teaching. All of us students are confused, and when we ask questions during lectures, he gives the most vague explanation. He doesn't explain why and how to solve the problems. He just writes it out, as if we've had years of physics experience when many of us have basic knowledge of the material.
Didn't do anything all semester. We watched videos from another lecturer from years ago. If you didn't already have a solid background in physics, I would not have passed.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He basically only sent passive aggressive emails to us, made his TAs grade the weekly quizzes, and had us watch old boring lectures by another professor instead of teaching the course material to us. I recommend watching Aplusphysics videos and learning the hw problems inside out to do well !
Difficult class but if you watch the lectures and do the homework you should be OK. The grading scale is very generous, and there's a bit of extra credit too.
Doesn't actually teach the course, instead the TA's do all of the work and he gives us recorded videos from 3 years ago
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Kinda mean but good teacher. Weekly homework assignments (1-2 hours). Exams are hard, first and second exams had averages in the 60s.

This man scares me. I went to office hours once and he just rudely said "what are you standing there for" So yeah I don't like him. He bases his tests mostly on his lecture questions and even though the answers are posted online they're not explained very well so you better go to lectures. His half of the exams tend to be harder. Exam 2 made me cry
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor I've ever had at UF. I hated physics in high school, but after taking his class I'd consider taking more physics classes at UF. No textbook required, but make sure to attend class. His exams are fill in the blank (which sucks) but he curves the whole class so I still got an A with an 89. Super funny guy!

This is the only physics class I have to take and was pretty worried at first. Dr. Yelton is an intelligent, caring, and funny individual. Every class he will cary out demonstrations that manage to make physics fun. He will help you a lot in office hours and will even extend his hours if needed. Come to class, do the practice tests and you're set.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Okay so yeah hes a funny guy, the tests were worth 80% of our grade with 20% being the hitt clicker questions. Hes really nice but terrible at using real world examples and throughly explaining things. He often used the words works this way because I know so I am unfortunate to have him again in the fall.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: When I took Physics 1, I was faced with a major life event that distracted me from school. Professor Yelton was beyond caring. I was scared to approach him because, to me, he was just a face that delivered lectures to 600+ students. But he really listened and was willing to work with me while still grading fairly.

Dr. Yelton has by far been the best teacher I've had. It's really easy to tell he puts a lot of work into his class because of all the demonstrations he does. He's a bona fide genius, and wants to see you do well and keep you engaged. However, he does move very fast, so I would recommend not skipping his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Yelton is better than most professors in his department in that he provides generally clear, concise lectures that aren't meant to confuse you. While I primarily used study edge to navigate this course, Professor Yelton's lectures served beneficial in the long run.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Yelton is my favorite physics teacher I've had at UF. His lectures are clear and concise which never makes you feel like anything in class is unnecessary, which is a good thing because you have to go to class to answer the HITT clicker questions (for extra credit). He's funny and has a wonderful British accent. Homework and exams are very fair.

Professor Yelton might have been a good professor to some, but for me, he made it impossible to understand what was happening in lectures. He always skipped steps and didn't explain concepts with real world examples. He's a nice person though and he made the class enjoyable with his jokes. I just wish he spent more time teaching instead of joking.

Many people tend to like him because of his jokes in class, but his teaching style does not fit everyone. If you are looking for someone who will teach the material through and through to you, this is not him. You must have some knowledge on the topic or you will easily get lost as his lectures tend to skip steps and skim the "easier" concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Test average is around a 60 so dont be afraid if you do badly. 55+ counts as a C. Very hard class, Study Edge is a must.

Dr. Yelton was a crazy guy when it came to blowing stuff up In class. He made some jokes and kept class interesting but the exams are insanely hard so make sure you complete the homework and know how to throughly do every homework question and you should get atlas a B.

Yelton was awesome! He would throw in some jokes that lightened the mood of being in a tough physics class. The tests were difficult, but he would hold extra review sessions before them to give more chances to ask questions. Physics is a hard subject, but he at least made lectures enjoyable.

Yelton explains concepts well, albeit quickly (skips steps in his algebra), so keeping up can be difficult. The lectures teach everything you need to know, and the textbook is good as reference. Sprinkles in dry humor, is genuinely interested in our success, gives small yet challenging workload, and liked our class enough to throw us a pizza party.

He is very comprehensive in his lectures, doing regular practice problems will help prepare you for his exams which are all free-response, but graded very leniently. He is very willing to help, as long as you ask, and honestly he wants everybody to get a good grade.

Took PHY2020 online. He is willing to help if needed, but I found his class to be VERY hard. The tests are much harder than problems in class. However, the class is graded on a huge curve (because he knows not many people are going to do well in the class), but it really didn't seem to help too much.
Fantastic teacher! Has a fantastic and super dry sense of humor and a cool accent. The class is pretty easy, just don't fall behind

This guy is awesome, great teacher, and funny. Make sure you attend class. Any questions on the HW and he is more than willing to help. Tests are easier than the HW. So do the the HW and understand it and this class should be no problems. Must stress that going to class and doing HW is a must!!!
The test are not multiple choice, so you need to study hard! Helpful in office hours.

YELTON IS AMAZING!!  If you have to take physics at UF, try your hardest to get him.  If you have to wait a semester to make sure you get him, do it.  He makes jokes (and they're actually funny), very clear in his explanations and just makes you want to come to class when he's the one teaching.

He is very good with examples. Follows a more European method so isn't into babying you. He has a good humor and has awesome demonstrations. Go to class, and even if the book is recommended, buy it if you are not strong in physics. Quizzes are given almost right after he teaches you the concept, so stay awake.

Yelton is one of the professors I remember most fondly from UF. I thought he was hot, in a sarcastic, older teacher who studies quarks with a Scottish(?) accent kind of way. I would recommend him if you have to take physics.

Prof. Yelton's my favorite teacher at UF. He's  intelligent, humorous and has a hot accent! What more can you ask for? Don't hesitate to take his class if you get the chance! I just wish he could teach Physics 2 too!

Hes a pretty good teacher. Way clearer than Detweiller. Do the homework and the practice tests and you should be alright. His lectures are also a bit entretaining but if you have a solid physics background u dont rly have to go.

Easy class if you do the homework. Stopped going to class about halfway through the semester and instead learned from the book, which is very well written. Most people do pretty poorly, and its curved, so if you apply yourself and study, you shouldn't have any trouble.
he was standoffish.
Great class

I agree completely with the last post. Theres something about his teaching style that loosens the rigid subject matter. Granted, the class still isnt easy, but Yelton does a miraculous job at dumbing it down and keeping it interesting.
for some reason, he just kicks ass
Great teacher.

tough class, be prepared to study.  However, yelton saves the day... Detwieler sucks at teaching.. he is a mumbler and he constantly repeats and forgets.  Yelton is funny and prepared.  You will look forward to your days with the YELTZ

Yelton always seemed a lot more prepared than Detweiler. And funnier too. I liked it more when he taught the class.  The exams usually average somewhere around 8/13, but a 60% is a B, so you shouldnt have too much trouble in the class. However, if Detweiler taught the entire class, I would have been in trouble.
the man cant teach...
Funny teacher.  Very good at teaching.  He knows his stuff.  Class can be a little hard, but there is a huge curve.  So if you study and pay attention in class, an A shouldn't be too hard.
pretty good professor, pretty funny too

He has a good sense of humor, and as far as physics teachers go, he is excellent.  For someone not physics/math minded his class may be tough, but if you have experience in those areas you shouldn't have too much trouble.

Yeah hes a funny guy, but when grade time comes the last laugh is on u.. I missed a C by .5% and wouldnt give it to me. His syllabus said 50% at least a C and in class they talked about a cruve. At the end they didnt curve for a C. Class is hard but big shot teacher doesnt work with students at all so know what u get.

A very clear lecturer with good and very helpful demonstrations. I learned a LOT more watching his demonstrations than I did in the lab. Funny guy, awesome accent, take one of his classes if you get the opportunity.

Funny guy. A very clear lecturer, though he got frustrated when people didn't pay attention.  Sometimes, he went a little deeper than we probably needed to, and I feel like the harder test questions probably came from Yelton, though I can't prove it.

A lot clearer than Professor Detweiler, I loved it when he taught. He was lot easier to understand and even made jokes! Well, to be fair Detweiler tried to make jokes, but they just weren't as funny. Definately try and get Yelton if you can!!!

Very knowledgeable; firm grasp of all concepts covered, especially calculus.  Lives in my neighborhood, saw him trimming hedges.  Easy, short HW; very easy in-class quizzes  If you're smart and pay attention in class, you can get an A on tests without studying.  Only need 80% overall for an A.  I only wish there was more calculus involved.

Great guy with a funny accent. In a class with two professors, you will look forward to days when he is teaching. He is always there after session ends to answer questions. He never hesitates to add humor into lecture. Take the class if he is teaching.

Hes a really good teacher. Explains a lot and easy to understand. He's British so the accent is awesome, but its not hard to understand him. He does examples in class and his humor is funny. Some classes were hilarious, and it really helped me learn. When people asked questions he was a bit condescending, but his explanations are easy to follow.
He's a great professor, got a quirky accent but it's easier to understand than you'd think. He's pretty funny, if you enjoy physics humor, and he knows what he's talking about.
No Comments

Yelton was awsome. The class was challenging, but what could one expect signing up for accelerated physics? He will be teaching 2048 next semester, and I think he will be more reasonable than many of the alternatives. He discussed how he wanted to do away with clicker quizes to attendence optional.

He'll be teaching non-honors physics later on, so what we have said may not apply.  With that in mind, his exams and homework assignments were very challenging but ultimately rewarding.  No one has ever made a 100 on an exam in his 2060 course.  Maybe he'll be easier on you guys!
Great professor, great class, sometimes tough but completely doable and absolutely worth it
pretty funny.  I can usual figure out what he's doing.  Sometimes he could explain things a bit thoroughly.
No Comments

class isn't that hard, he helps you out a lot especially on review section maybe the reason the classs is kinda easy is because we had another professor. I didn't study for a single exam still get an A well barely an A.
Excellent teacher.  This class is hard, but it's worth taking.
He was kinda funny but made physics harder than it had to be.
No Comments

This Professor was kind but cannot use canvas to save his life. He does not respond to emails and is very disorganized. His assignments also did not make sense and seemed like they were created by AI. If you want to have a stressful semester take this class.
Genuinely cares about student's long-term success and social issues, highly recommend.

Professor Kramer is a nice teacher, but very unorganized. His HSC4558 class is extremely manageable, it consists of weekly group assignments (find a reliable group!), weekly quizzes, a midterm (prepare!), and a final group project. He does not respond to emails, but approach him in class and he will answer any question. His canvas is confusing.

Professor Kramer is a caring and understanding person who wants his students to succeed and learn more about the wide variety of healthcare careers. However, his Canvas skills are severely lacking. You don't need to read the textbook. The weekly reflections are a pain, but he's an easy grader, just start early. Start on the final paper early too.

Dr. Kramer was funny and caring, but he is so bad with Canvas. I never read the textbook and stuff and did just fine. The final paper for intro to health sucks, but it was easy. He isn't great about answering emails and his office hours are short. He didn't let us pick groups and I ended up with a bad group that never pulled their weight. Easy A.
He doesn't know how to respond to emails or use canvas. So good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Kramer is very kind and is good at organizing speakers, however, he struggles with responding to emails and with working canvas. I really enjoyed the variety of speakers he organized and I really got something out of the class. Definitely take the course if you are fine with the issues in communicating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is easy credit and has very interesting guest lectures. Overall the class is inciteful and a nice intro to health science class. The final paper is easy, just a high page count. Prof is very understanding and helpful but struggles with canvas.

Overall, great teacher. However, the class is extremely disorganized. Quizzes are all out of place and he never turns on the grades so you will have no clue what you got until days later. Pretty tough grader on reflections. Group work once a week but pretty easy.
Horrible professor, doesn't teach anything or try to learn the material before he comes to class

Professor Kramer was my teacher for Intro to Health Professions during summer b. At the beginning of the term, the class was a little dysfunctional but it got a lot better. We had some really interesting ethical discussions and got so many guest health professional speakers. The work is easy, but make sure to work on the final paper in advance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You can tell he really loves the class. As long as you read or watch lecture videos you will be fine. You do have to know the legal cases, but he breaks it down so simply. Overall an amazing professor and very funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor and the class was pretty simple as long as you do the work on time. The quizzes/ tests were open-note. There are group projects that can be stressful, but overall an easy class.

Get the book he wrote, it's word for word what you need to know about the cases in class. I recommend opting into the cold call, I always did and only got called on twice the whole sem so I basically never did work since by opting in you get points. Group projects were very entertaining and easy. He's hilarious,whoever said this class was hard lied
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are engaging even though they're slides. He does a good job of making sure the material is easily digestible and not incredibly boring. You do need both textbooks and since it is a law class get ready to read but it's not difficult. Good extra credit opportunities. His feedback is so good and helpful. Would 100% recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Rivera is just great all-around. There's a lot of assigned readings from both the textbook and other legal cases, but his lectures are incredibly thorough and everything is open-note. Super understanding about conflicts as long as you communicate. It's clear he loves what he does from the amount of effort he puts into assignments.

I've had Dr. Rivera for multiple classes and he is great. Very funny, knowledgable and seems to care about his students. Lots of reading, exams can be difficult and prepare for mandatory, but interesting group projects.

My only complaint would be there were group projects in a completely online class, but he provided group feedback surveys and offered assignments in place of the group projects in case you were worried about the group work. Unfortunately, you could only complete the replacement assignment before you received the group project grade.
Rivera was awesome very nice and funny would take again 10000% cannot stress how fun he was
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Rivera is the best professor I have ever had. He's really funny and makes his lectures straight to the point so classes are usually short. Group projects are graded very leniently, and he creates fun PowerPoint shows for them. He also gives out a ton of extra credit. You definitely have to do all of the readings though because he cold calls.

Professor Rivera is a very passionate and in-depth professor. He takes time to make his lessons creative, interactive, and easily understandable even when he's covering difficult texts or information. I'm not usually into online classes, but this one was very well-organized and straightforward. The exams were difficult but the supplemental was good
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Rivera is my favorite teach thus far in my academic career at UF. He is caring, nice, and overall an excellent professor.

One of my favorite professors! I have taken 2 classes with him & would definitely recommend taking his classes. He does cold call in class for participation, but gives the option to do a discussion assignment if you dont like speaking in class. Exams are online and super easy. cold calling isnt very difficult, just skim the case online before class

You have to go to class because he does cold calling as his attendance (very anxiety inducing). Exams were easy. 5 essays but 2 are optional. Extra credit you have to work for. Groups you with random people at the beginning of the semester so hopefully they actually do work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: You will have to read the cases to prepare and have to attend class because he randomly picks students and asks them questions for participation points. Exams were online and easy. Get the supplemental he wrote not the textbook, textbook was useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: A teacher that cares about his students and will help you out with curving grades. Be ready for group projects, though. There was 4.  Overall 10/10!

I loved Professor Rivera. Highly recommend getting his textbook everything he wants you to know is in there. There is a lot of extra credit. He is very simple and to the point. You don't need any previous knowledge. Attendance is kind of mandatory but we always got our super early. Definitely take this class he's awesome!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Funny, passionate about law

My favorite professor so far. Lectures are engaging; you will have to read a lot of cases, but they're interesting, so it isn't terrible. 2 exams, 3 group activities, and 5 papers. Overall, I definitely recommend Rivera as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved Rivera and this class, but beware, it's harder than CJL2000. No supplementary book, you actually need to read the cases. Group projects are a lot harder and require more work. 4 non-proctored exams, 4 group projects. FYI, if people in your group aren't participating, good luck, Rivera does nothing. Overall, it's still a pretty easy class.

Best criminology professor I've had thus far. 2 exams, 3 group projects. He uses the socratic method for attendance. If your name is called, you better have read the readings for the day and be there. I only got called maybe once or twice a month, but some people never got called and some got called once a week. Get his supplementary book!!

Loved this class. 2 exams, 3 group projects, module quizzes, 3 easy essays. Class participation/attendance does weigh heavily on your grade so read the cases and go to class.
