I would recommend buying his textbook over the Schubert one if you can only get one. DO ANY/ALL extra credit he offers. If you have a 85% in class, 5 extra credit points=90%!!

Kinda tough class. Lots of reading/writing. 3 group projects rely heavy on group participation. I was in crappy group who barely communicated, our submitted assignments were slapped together, we received low grade scores. If not for extra credit opportunity, I would have flunked class. 95% of Quiz/Exam answers come from lectures, almost verbatim.

His lectures keep you engaged. There are quizzes for each module, 1 individual assignment, 3 group assignments, and 4 exams. It is very spaced out so I was never really stressed. The main thing is each class, you have to read cases & submit your name beforehand to be called on. But you can do discussions instead if you don't like to talk in class.
There is a lot of reading as well as lengthy lectures. You will have to complete discussion post and quizzes weekly which he is a tough grader on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Such a great professor. Lectures were entertaining. You don't have to attend but you will have to submit a discussion post if you don't elect to participate in class (you submit your name the night before). Not a harsh grader. Offers sooo much extra credit!! Brought my grade up from an 89 to a solid A. Exam questions are word for word from the pps

I had so much fun in this class and learned so much! His lectures are witty and do a good job of explaining complex ideas. You really get to practice critical thinking and how to use logical reasoning. The class is challenging though. My group thankfully had high participation which earned us extra credit and boosted my grade to an A.

By far my favorite professor at UF. He makes law and criminology super entertaining, and you can tell he puts a lot of effort into his lectures. Graded on quizzes, exams discussions, and assignments that you complete in a group (my group was great at getting stuff done). This was my second class with him, I also enjoyed his CJL2000 course!
A lot of cases to read and I felt no need to use the textbook that he wrote himself. The other textbook I did use thou. Grades come from discussions and three papers.
Just read and understand the PowerPoints, easiest class to take for the law-driven requirement for criminology majors.
Professor Rivera was an awesome professor. Class was super easy yet informative. Makes sure to cover all the material but in a fun was.

LOVED the class and rivera. His lectures were interesting and the quizzes/exams matched so as long as you understand most of the material he's teaching its an easy A. Participation was either discussion post or put your name in the day before and risk him calling on you. Everything was straight forward and he was flexible. Would take again!

This is the funniest teacher I have had at UF. super engaging and I learned a lot. He does cold call in class so make sure that you have read all of the cases in detail and could answer questions about it on the spot. also group projects in the class but they aren't difficult and only take a couple of days. lots of extra credit opportunities also

Professor Rivera is an amazing teacher, his lectures are funny and easy to follow. Discussions are straight forward, you just have to make sure you participate in different days. The group activities are a great way to get a lot of work done in little time and he is fair in regards of giving the points to those who worked hard. Take his class!
Great professor and pretty easy class. If you read the cases and do the work you should be good!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a really great guy and teacher! Always answers emails and gives feedback on everything. Class was completely manageable work-wise and he gives you so many extra credit opportunities its impossible not to get an A. Pre-recorded lectures are short and easy to follow and all test/quiz material comes directly from them. Couldn't recommend more!!

Not a bad choice for a teacher, easy class overall. The book helps but I would not say it is fully necessary. He is a bit funky, but who isn't? Recommend this class for a GPA boost or just to maintain whatever you already have.

Professor Rivera has a unique personality that made his lectures easy to watch. You will have to read the textbook, as the weekly discussions are based on them. Additionally, you will have to post on the weekly discussion on multiple DAYS to receive full credit, so no waiting till the last moment. As long as you do what is asked, you will pass!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Rivera is probably one of the best professors I have had here at UF. Court cases are pretty easy to debrief. Quizzes are open note, so are exams except for a lockdown browser. All other assignments are really easy. Overall a great guy and i HIGHLY recommend this class. Ignore all the criticisms of him on here they are just lazy.

One of the best professors I have had at UF. Very straightforward, makes it clear what he expects out of you, and it helps that his lectures are funny. If you take any of his classes, you won't regret it!

Professor Rivera is hands down the best professor. He responds to emails quickly. He is a fair grader. His presentations are great and hilarious. He is a down to earth professor that makes learning about cases fun. If he shows up as an instructor, pick him! you wont regret it.

One of the best professors Ive had so far! There is a lot of writing with the discusions, but if you read and do the work, he is not a tough grader. Quizzes/exams are all based on the lectures. If you are not a criminology major, you probably won't like this class! Very focused on cases/case law. Very fair prof! Wish he taught all my class!

Rivera's lectures are really great! He's funny and cares about his students. You will have to read a lot of cases for the class, but most of their summaries can be found online. His quizzes/exams are online and straight off the powerpoints he posts on canvas. Beware, he will randomly call on people in class to answer questions so be prepared.

This class is not only super easy, but it's actually really interesting. He uses the Socratic method, but he's incredibly nice, even if you don't know the answer. Quizzes are straight from Powerpoints and make up a majority of your grade. Tons of extra credit and 4 easy papers. Seriously, take this class! Professor Rivera is the best!!!

The best professor I've had at UF. Required reading, weekly quizzes, a few tests, and four required activities. All are spaced out nicely, and lectures are short and relevant. Clear grading criteria. Discussions are important, but directly related to assigned material. I wish he taught more classes -- I'd definitely take him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Rivera is one of the best professors in the Criminology department. His knowledge of the law and legal system is incredible and he makes learning about the cases enjoyable. He is very understand and will help students work through issues that they are having in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really nice guy and will listen to all about problems, etc. Highly suggest

Mr. Rivera is a great professor, the class consisted of two discussions weekly (roughly half a page each) and to respond twice for each discussion. There was typically a weekly quiz which the book and his lecture gives 90% of the answers, hard if you don't understand case law. His tests are hard if you don't study. As everyone knows law is hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: His teaching methods offered little. You were not allowed to see quiz and test results because he was sure cheat sheets would be made. His activities in a hypothetical court setting were ridiculous and set up so he could say how wrong you were. I have 10 years law enforcement and never heard judges talk like he did

He's a good professor, his class is very straight forward. There's quizzes, discussions, and exams which are all the usual. If you read and take notes you'll be fine. If you need any help, he answers emails very quickly. The only negative to this class are his activities. There's one for each module and 4 modules. I couldn't stand doing them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class was useless. You are supposed to remember all cases with their outcome, one too many to even count. Tests are ridiculous and quizzes are the same. Avoid if possible at all cost.

Professor Rivera is just an awesome, caring guy! Clear expectations, great feedback. Participation is key- lots of activities, all with purpose, and they WILL help you learn and understand the law. READ THE TEXT! The quizzes and exams come from it. Entertaining lectures; awesome clip art to keep interest. Definitely would take again!
sigh I don't know it just feels tougher than it should be.

Professor McNealy is an average professor overall. I personally liked the structure of only having a few big assignments, but she did tend to spontaneously create assignments due day-of, which always felt somewhat AI-generated with how bland they were, if that makes sense. A lot of the class is self-explanatory in terms of content.

This class is much more confusing than it should be for an intro-level course. Instructions are often unclear, and it can be difficult to understand what is expected. The biggest issue is communication; emails are usually answered with very short responses that don't actually clarify anything. It makes the class more stressful than necessary.

Avoid if possible. Lectures are 5 minute videos, just definitions, then Quizzes and Exams expect deep working knowledge of concepts discussed. She can be rude when emailing her. Class structure needs to be updated too. Very unclear expectations.
Graded the first synthesis harshly and never gave a justification, ignored emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor McNealy is overall above average. She does a great job explaining concepts in lectures and in discussion, but she could definitely include more details in her lectures. There is lots of reading in the class, but I've definitely heard of classes with more. You have to do the assigned readings if you want to pass the class.

Did not enjoy my experience at all. The material wasn't difficult but taking the class with this professor was not fun. She responded to all of my emails with sass and took off points for miniscule things.
The class wasn't too bad but every email from the professor was filled with sass.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Although the curriculum itself isn't bad, interacting with the professor was a less than favorable experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cool professor. She brought in examples from pop culture that we can resonate with (like "Hotline Bling" and copyright issues). I actually enjoyed going to class and lecture.   BUT LORD HELP US ALL WITH HER EXAMS. We got a study guide that didn't cover practically anything on the exam. Read the book or you will fail. The exams felt impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: very hard professor. get ready to study for a while because the exams really are off of the book. she doesnt really review, only makes you do a project before hand that has nothing to do with the test. doesnt curve grades at all or anything.

Dr. McNealy's class took effort. The exams require AT LEAST a week of studying. There is only 3 exams, 2 law briefs and weekly quizzes before class each Tuesday that you must have read the chapter on before because they are times for 10 minutes. The whole class is basically electronic. Attendance is Russian roulette, so go to class!

He seems like a great guy, but his assignment instructions are extremely unclear. The final assignment instructions are entirely written with AI, and regular assignments typically take longer than they should.
So many assignments, bad instructions, outdated material, and long assignments.
Bad instructions and long assignments.

I took this class as a filler in my final semester. Simple tasks are made more time-consuming than it should be. If you really want to learn Excel, you're better off spending 30 minutes in youtube. This class is about how much effort you're willing to put into interpreting poorly written directions.

He is very caring and prompt, responds quickly and gives extra credit for attending office hours, etc. If you follow the videos and do the work on time you'll pass. The work takes a while, however, and the videos are outdated. You can always ask if you need help. People expect it to be an idle, zero-work online class so that's why they do poorly.

Loved this professor! His accent and enthusiasm is so fun, but would not recommend the class for non critical tracking unless you want to work on your excel skills, and word. Did not like word. 

Peer office hours are a straight shot for an A, I'd always go at the beginning of the week and get work done early. There are 2 rough weeks of work.

There's quite a few assignments but there's no reason I'd expect anybody to spend more than 4-5 hours on this class per WEEK. Almost every assignment has a set of videos you can watch where he guides you step-by-step through almost all of the assignment. He offers a lot of EC at the beginning of the course and it's all very easy to complete. Easy A

This class is fine. There are 1-2 assignments a week that take 2-3 hours max (except for the midterm and final, which take several hours each). There are usually clear grading rubrics, though sometimes instructions are still very confusing. A lot of the work is pretty much pointless busy work. I would not take unless it is required for your major.

I came in knowing little-to-nothing about Excel and other computer programs, and genuinely learned so much. The assignments are long but it's usually just one per week and I was able to complete each in under 2 hours. Some pre-recorded videos are outdated but they go over explicitly how to complete each step of the assignment and are still helpful
Lots of assignments but materials are actually practical. I learned so much things. Lots of extra credit activities too.

The course definitely requires a good bit of time, especially the Midterm and Final, so it is good to try and plan a few hours ahead of time to sit down. Some assignments suck more than others but in the first half of the class he gives step by step guides. Grading is easy so if you hit every part of the self-assessment rubric, you'll get an A

I needed to take this class because I couldn't take ISM; this was probably the worst decision of my life. The assignments are very outdated, like 5 years plus. As well, the explanation of the assignments is terrible. JMG will spend 15 minutes explaining something and just say "well thats not how you do it". Also, the assignments are so confusing.
worse class ever. Nice professor though but the coursework is terrible and SO confusing.

The assignments in this course are very poorly explained and it led to a lot of confusion and time wasting for a course that should not be difficult. The videos and rubrics that are supposed to help us are clearly outdated as well. Choose a different course if possible.

Took this class a semester ago, but I figure it's still worth writing. His instructions can be very unclear and confusing. Homework that should've taken an hour max often took an extra 30 minutes to an hour because he would ramble during the prerecorded videos. The final project came with an outdated rubric. I'd look at other classes to take.

Lots of work for summer but weekly assignments are doable in a day or two. Not hard at all, just read the rubric before you submit. I had 0 excel experience before this class and I learned so much. One complaint is that he waits until the last minute to give extensions and yaps a lot so watch vids in 2x spd. I ended w/ a 99%
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: You'll love this course if you were a fan of the teacher who assigned homework just cause in high school. This course is such a genuine waste of time it is ridiculous. Grading is entirely based upon your TA, and JMG spends most lecture videos showing you the wrong way to do something then saying "now do this instead" at minute 27. Take ISM.

This class is geniunly the worst class I could have ever chosen to take over Summer. The amount of busy work is ubsurt, the lectures are poorly recorded and old, the information being thought in the class is so outdated, and the teacher has the worst lisp and accent. Nightmare of a class.

Wouldn't be that hard in a fall or spring semester. The videos may not be on the exact same assignment but it gives a good understanding of what to do. The grading is pretty straight forward and he gives you the rubric to self-grade before submitting any assignment. Finally, he gives a lot of extra credit to help boost your grade.

Do not take CGS2531 over the summer. The workload is unbelievable and takes several hours each day, with complicated deliverables that are due back-to-back-to-back. Also, the explanation videos will have mistakes and do not always match the assignment it is posted with, so it can be quite confusing.

If you want to become a victim to corporate America but while in college, take this class. I've never taken a course with so much unnecessary busy work that is so, so horribly explained. I thought taking this class during the summer would be easy, but it was one of the worst mistakes I've ever made.

The assignments take hours to do so don't wait until last minute. The teacher has an accent and sometimes messes up steps so that was interesting. The TA's are either super chill or take off points for unnecessary reasons. There is a lot of extra credit though, so I would definitely do it!

The professor is nice, but can be difficult to understand sometimes. Assignments are ok, but as a mac user it can be relatively harder. TA's are either incredibly harsh or incredibly lenient, literally no in between. Be ready to spend hours on this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but hard to follow along with his instructions, even if you follow along with the videos, as a Mac user, you're pretty much out of luck. TAs are the harshest graders, and their grading is never consistent, and the feedback doesn't do much if you're not able to resubmit work. Be mindful if you want to take this to boost your GPA.

Dr. Mendoza-Garcia is a very nice man, but he is honestly not the best professor. His grammar is suboptimal, which makes understanding already confusing assignment directions and the syllabus even more difficult. Be ready to put in A TON OF WORK. TAs are EGREGIOUSLY INCONSISTENT graders. Don't get frustrated by the course design, or lack thereof.

This course just needs to be revamped, possibly with a different professor? He is super nice and accessible outside of class, but he has such a thick accent that even the captions fail sometimes. The whole course just felt sloppy.

Very fun and enthusiastic teacher. I enjoyed his videos and his speaking, but I will say that some elements are very confusing and inconsistent. As others have said, grading instructions vary from video to canvas instructions. I usually stick to the videos. The syllabus is a MESS lol. I do like him, though. TAs are nice.

Overall, not a very hard class at all. Pretty time consuming because of the way the class and videos are structured. Make sure you utilize TAs and take some time out of your day in order to complete the assignments. The professor definitely is enthusiastic and caring just a little difficult to follow. Was a very easy A.

Professor Mendoza-Garcia seems to be a very caring and enthusiastic professor, but this course is a mess. The assignments are relatively easy but are so time consuming due to the extremely confusing and inconsistent directions. Frustrating but not very hard to get an A due to the extra credit given.

One of the most unqualified professor's I've experienced so far at UF. Assignments are sometimes very easy and straight forward, but a lot of the times extremely time consuming and you have to watch his videos to understand what is being asked of you. His videos and instructions contradict. Makes at least one mistake every video, unintelligible

Sometimes I was confused from his videos, but utilize the TAs. They will help you if you're stuck and will make sure you did everything right. Overall, the assignments may have been time-consuming, but the class isn't too bad. He was also very lenient with dates during the hurricanes. There's also extra credit opportunities if you're worried.

The professor is very hard to understand, and video "lectures" are at many times confusing and don't match the rubric of the assignments. The TAs can be harsh or laidback graders, so assignment grading can be very inconsistent.

Overall, the class was manageable. There were no mandatory lectures, and students had ample time for assignments. However, the directions were often unclear. A 20 minute assignment would take well over an hour because written and recorded directions would contradict each other. On the bright side, Professor Mendoza was caring towards students.

This class takes some adjustment, but the professor is helpful. The assignments are lengthy, but engaging. Using tools like Unstuck AI alongside the lectures made the course more manageable. Overall, a rewarding experience if you're willing to put in the effort.

He is a caring and very enthusiastic professor. The assignments are not terribly difficult, however be prepared to spend a few hours working on them. His videos are nice, but if you are a Mac user they are not very helpful. Overall, getting an A in this class isn't hard it just requires patience and diligence.

Overall, the class isn't really that difficult. Do the assignments and follow the directions and you'll usually get a 100 or at least an A. The main issue is that the assignments can take forever sometimes, and the directions aren't always super clear. Overall easy but time consuming.

Overall, the class was not that difficult, it was just time consuming. The professor seemed very enthusiastic in the video lectures; however, most of the videos were really outdated which makes it hard to follow at times. As long as you submit the assignments and join office hours when you have questions, you will get an A in the class.

This class wasnt terrible but assignments were time consuming. He posts instruction videos for each assignment but they are hard to understand and he also makes lots of mistakes, making the videos way longer than they need to be. Overall not a bad class, I did learn a lot but could be improved in ways.

Terrible. Absolutely terrible. Although he has instruction videos for assignments, he does not speak english well (sometimes the CC can't even understand what he's saying) & he often makes mistakes in his videos which makes it even more confusing & frustrating. Directions are unclear. So many assignments that take hours to complete. SO MUCH WORK.

Prof. has lots of energy, very supportive. DO NOT FORGET TO CHECK ASSIGNMENTS!! It's very easy to miss assignments bc he does not open the modules until Monday week of. Instructions are a bit scattered: make sure to read all text, watch instruction vids, and read rubric. Not too many assignments, but can take hours to complete projects.

Assignments take forever but the professor shows you how to do it step by step. However, the professor is hard to understand and speaks broken english. Professor also commonly makes mistakes throughout lectures wasting everyone's time, when he could've easily remade the 10 minute video as he recycles them year over year. Take ISM instead.

This class taught me a great deal about extrapolating data and price prediction. It is not a difficult class, the videos walk you step by step. He grades on assignments which is nice, rather than only exams, so you leave with actual skills for future work. Mendoza-Garcia is passionate which is nice to see in a professor and gives EC. Good class.

Although I got an A in this class, I was annoyed about the quizzes he made. Many of the questions he didn't even mention in the lectures, finally made me guess the answer for all the attempts of the quizzes (he generally gives 2 attempts for each quiz; however, he made different stupid questions for each attempt that AI got wrong for several time).
This is the most disorganized course to ever exist I hate this class and I feel I am worse at excel than when I started

The professor is helpful, smart, and kind, but this is a horrible class. The structure is unclear and confusing even after reading the syllabus, and you will end up with so many assignments that may or may not actually be for credit. The lectures are incredibly hard to follow + are often outdated or not meant for mac users. So so frustrating.

The class is just hard to manage if you already have a complete schedule, assignments take several hours and seem to appear out of nowhere, and although he explains how to do each assignment step by step, his poor English and poor explanations make this less of a blessing than you would think, you will end up rewatching the videos several times.

Speaks broken English, if you have a MacBook, you're done for. All of his tutorials are on a different computer IN A COMPUTER SCIENCE CLASS. Assignments can take 8 hours. This guy should never have a job teaching American students.

Dr. Mendoza is great! He seems like a very kind person and always got back to me on questions within 24 hours. Class itself is an easy A if you follow directions. He posts videos on exactly how to do each assignment, so as long as you follow them you will do fine. Some assignments take a bit of time, so i'd recommend not waiting till the due date!

This course took a lot of adjustment. It took me a few assignments to finally understand how to complete all of the assignments. If you are taking in Summer A be prepared to spend hours a day on assignments that are so long and tedious. Professor is a nice guy but his explanations can get lost in translation and difficult to follow.

I have taken both CGS and ISM and I feel like I gained more knowledge from this class. Homework was difficult at first but you get used to it. Professor is also very nice and communicative. I've used Word/Excel/PowerPoint for years and I still learned a lot. Overall a good experience and extra credit is offered as well.

I took this class during Summer A. I don't think this class was as difficult as some people make it out to be. Yes, there were assignments that left me confused and took time, but at the end of the day, I was able to learn a lot from this class. The videos he provides in each assignment literally shows you everything you need to do.

The class is hard to understand at first, not because of the material, but mostly the way it's organized. It's confusing. Assignments are long. Don't take in Summer A. However, Prof John is a nice professor and he allowed me to complete some assignments that I couldn't do because of a family emergency. He's passionate, just needs some updating.

This class was very challenging for me, but I didn't have a lot of excel experience going in. I found it very rewarding, though considering how much I learned. Lectures and tutorials are really helpful! I spent a lot of time on these assignments so be prepared to work hard but I loved this class overall!
This is by far the worst professor I have ever had. If he is the only professor available you should wait to take this class. Extremely rude and you will not be able to understand anything he says.

This class is the most infuriating and tedious class you will ever take. Mendoza's tutorials are incomprehensible and he goes on tangents about content that does not relate to the task at hand. The directions on canvas are messy and extremely difficult to read. It will take hours to complete an assignment that should be extremely easy.

Do not take this class Summer A unless you want to spend a minimum of 5 hours a day on excel. Assignments are unnecessarily long. You will be dealing with a copious amount of data for no reason but to waste your time when you could learn the same computer functions with a normal amount of data. You learn useful skills but at what cost?

He's a nice guy but his class is confusing. I came into the class being Office certified and found that the assignments were time consuming. He does videos covering the assignments but most of the time they are lengthy cause he goes off topic and talks about other features which makes the assignments harder to do. But easy to get a good grade.

This professor effectively shows how to do the assignment. The assignments are straightforward. There is tons of extra credit and 2 discussions are dropped. Some of the assignments were long, but if you give yourself ample time it should be okay. However, some lectures are confusing and skip some steps, so you may have to figure those out.

This class is straightforward. Dr. Mendoza-Garcia filmed himself doing all the assignments with a step-by-step tutorial. The TAs can be tough graders sometimes,ensure you review the rubric before submitting things. Some assignments take a long, so start them earlier. No exams just assignments so make sure you do them in their entirety and on time.

He is extremely helpful and is the best professor I have had so far. He prioritizes student's learning meaning all the answers for assignments and homework are available in case of knowledge gaps. It's easy to cheat, sure, but with a class like his it's probably best to utilize the less stressful environment and genuinely learn.

He actually does videos for everything, but they aren't necessary if you are decent at Microsoft. Everything is graded by TAs, so it takes weeks to get back. I usually wouldn't even get feedback for assignments that built on each other until after it was all due. Instructions are not very clear, and he responds very very late to all questions.

This is one of the most poorly structured classes I have taken at UF. For a class about efficiency with computer tools, it is organized very inefficiently. The class is easy enough and you will get an A/B+ no problem, but the video lectures and assignment instructions are not clear and full of fluff and typos.

I took this class as a quantitative option for my foreign language & I learned a lot about Microsoft Excel & Word, but the assignments were lengthy & the directions were unclear. He provided videos that helped explain & were an example for assignments. They helped a lot, but they were outdated.

Each assignment worth few points so missing some makes a big difference. Videos and office hours are helpful, lots of extra credit (do it even though it seems like small amount). Weekly videos he always is excited!

- videos that go over how to do every assignment step by step (do yourself a favor and put it in 2x)
- if you have Microsoft certification in word, excel, ppt, you get out of some assignments
- must pay close attention to detail, grades explicitly by rubric
- annoying late policy, turn everything in on time or your grade will suffer
- not too hard

Dr. Mendoza-Garcia is a lovely man who really cares about his students. The lectures can be confusing sometimes but it's nothing that even a slight bit of common sense can't solve. The workload is not that much, I never spent more than 3 hours a week on this course. Do the extra credit and go to office hours if you need. Highly recommend.
he was definitely the professor for this course!!

Dr. Garcia is a very caring professor who knows what he is doing. His lectures are easy to follow and really helps when supplemented with assignments. Although, the assignments can be extremely long, so I wouldn't wait last minute when submitting assignments in this class. Take use of office hours.

If you are taking this class Summer A, be prepared to have multiple long and time consuming assignments due on the same day. My best advice is to watch the videos he provides for the assignments and do what he does. If you are looking for easy credits, I wouldn't recommend this class. This class is valuable if you want to learn Excel & Word.

Ultimately getting an A in this class is very manageable. There are a lot of assignments, and they can be tedious, but they are not overly difficult; he has explanation videos that are helpful (most of the time). A few quizzes, no exams, and he offers extra credit. Plenty of office hours. He is very enthusiastic about teaching and is caring.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you're in between this class and ISM, definitely take this one! Dr. Mendoza is so passionate and experienced in all of his videos. He offers multiple office hours and extra credit opportunities. Sometimes, the tutorial videos are confusing if they are the older ones, but if not, it's such an easy A. Just make sure to do everything on time.

Prof. Mendoza-Garcia cares so much about each student even though it is an online class and was always very helpful. This class is a lot of work and his videos are not always helpful, find a friend in the class and work together. Looong assigments. One of the kindest most enthusiastic professors I've had at UF, TA's were helpful too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 1/3 of the time spent on assignments is actually trying to understand the instructions & what you're supposed to do. In his demo videos he'll give you three wrong ways to do it or show you the way you could do it but aren't gonna actually perform the action before he shows you what you're really supposed to do. Go in w patience and you'll survive.

He cares about his students but is not a good teacher. When taking this class you are basically entirely on your own. He doesn't explain the meanings of the assignments, and the videos he gives for "help" are just him mumbling and messing up in Excel. He edits the videos when he messes up. I knew excel prior, if you don't then don't take this class

Professor is very passionate. Lots of help if you need it. Assignments are usually straightforward but not always.  Definitely a time consuming assignment based class. No exams. I found him easy to understand but I do think his instruction videos could be smoother. Extra credit is super easy and definitely worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Garcia's class is probably one of the easiest in the business school and his assignments are very clear and fair

He's an amazing person and caring professor but I wouldn't take his course past an introductory level. He is hard to follow and understand. His assignments have step-by-step video guides too so the class can be an easy A if you have knowledge on Excel/ Word.

Professor Mendoza-Garcia gave clear instructions and helpful in all his video lectures. However, a lot of the homework is pretty time consuming. It's easy to get an A in the class, but make sure not to procrastinate the homework because some of it takes longer than expected. He also offers a lot of extra credit which is nice.

You are on your own for learning MATLAB if you take him. Probably the most caring and thoughtful prof you will get at UF, but his videos are not helpful and is hard to understand with his accent. He will help you out, respond to emails quickly, and give lots of extra credit opportunities (why I got an A). Am scared for future coding classes now.

Although the content is easy, the professor is so confusing. The video explanations are all over the place and super hard to follow. He often backtracks while talking causing the assignments take longer than they need to be to finish. If he provided examples and clearer explanations the class would be way easier.
HORRIBLE VIDEO INSTRUCTIONS
This professor was terrible, never take this class. You will not learn anything and only get a bad grade. Drop the class and take ism3013 when u can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class was very straightforward. The videos he provided were tutorials on how to do all of the assignments. He was also very responsive if someone had difficulty with an assignment. It's an easy class that is sometimes tedious because they're long but otherwise, everything was great.

Some assignments can be pretty long, but I took this Summer A and it was manageable. If you ever get stuck, there are office hours and the TAs are super helpful. There's also tons of EC, but it's an easy A. I did this class with a Mac. His accent was never an issue for me and there are captions on most of the videos anyway.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class should be useful but he makes it boring, and time consuming. There are many assignments due weekly and it's just a lot of busy work that he explains so badly in the videos. Some assignments are easy and some take 3-4 hours. Use the rubrics because sometimes what he does in the videos is not what is in the rubric. Easy A but lots of hw!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Mendoza-Garcia has good intentions but the way he executes them is simply awful. He decided to mandate in-person lectures despite saying a remote option would be offered throughout the semester in the syllabus. Calls on people during lectures, embarrassing them. Long homework due two days after lecture despite needing the lecture to complete.

Amazing professor, offers tons of EC! There are closed captions on all of his videos so don't worry about not understanding his accent. I had never used Excel before, but he gives step-by-step videos on how to complete the assignments so they're easy to do. Some are more time consuming than others, so don't start them an hour before they're due!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is nice and probably means well, but he is awful at teaching the class. It felt as if he didn't even understand the content himself, as he would get confused frequently during lectures. Assignments are pointless and long. Guidelines, expectations, and lectures are confusing and old. This class seriously needs to be updated.

This man's lectures are simply painful to listen to. He's very motivated, but impossible to follow. Nice guy, but there's a difference between knowing what you're doing and having the ability to teach it. I often believe he has neither
All the assignments are very tedious and very difficult to understand. Didn't really learn much at all from this class either, other than how to deal with doing confusing assignments.

Professor is a great and caring guy. The class is online and can be tedious but every assignment has a video of him doing exactly what you have to do. Sometimes assignments get tricky and can be tedious but he's super willing to help. I felt the class was useful and I learned a lot in excel and word

This class is just so annoying. Professor Mendoza Garcia is the kindest you'll ever meet, but this class is disorganized and so time consuming. It's a worthless major requirement what can I say. I don't know if there's a better option.
His accent makes it hard to understand the classes, especially for topics related to computers.
Doesn't give correct directions. Can't complete assignment without it. Sell.

Lots of extra credit (probably 18% of final grade). BEWARE: Garcia has a larger scale project than some of the other professors but if you take the time to do the iterations it is easy. My advice is to complete as many of the assignments as humanly possible and attend class for extra credit activities. This should boost your grade up at the end.

This class is an easy A if you give yourself time to complete the assignments and watch his videos. The grading criteria is clear, and although his videos may not be the best quality sometimes, no assignment takes more than 2 hours. If it does, there are office hours all day long. Fair grading, manageable workload, highly recommend. Ended w/ 102%.

This class can be tricky to navigate. The professor provides you with crystal clear instructions for every assignment. However, it is still challenging. Do all of the extra credit, go to office hours to ask questions, and put in effort. I greatly struggled in this class and managed a 102%.

The professor is extremely caring and is definitely passionate about the subject, although I feel like I was struggling to learn half of the time in this course. The recorded lectures are hard to understand, disorganized, and sometimes give me a headache. Getting an A in the class is easy though, the work just takes a while to do.

A LOT OF PEOPLE ARE EXAGGERATING HOW BAD HIS VIDEOS ARE. PROF MENDOZA'S ASSIGNMENTS ARE SUPER EASY AND THE RUBRIC IS SUPER SPECIFIC. HIS VIDEOS LITERALLY WALK YOU STEP-BY-STEP THROUGH EVERY SINGLE ASSIGNMENT, AND YOU CAN COPY MOST OF WHAT HE DOES IN THEM FOR AN EASY A. PEOPLE WHO SAY THEY ARE DISORGANIZED/HARD TO FOLLOW JUST AREN'T PAYING ATTENTION

This class is absolutely awful. It teaches Excel techniques that have no real world application at all for most humanities students. Assignment take a very long time to do, and the instructions are very confusing. He has videos to help you but they are unorganized and extremely confusing. DO NOT take this class unless you are already good at Excel.

Mr. Mendoza is a very caring prof, but doesn't know how to teach at all. He wants you to succeed in the class, but his videos are extremely disorganized, make no sense half of the time, and you can barely understand any directions he gives. His videos don't consider students who use macs and the format of his windows is completely different.

Has clear rubrics for each assignment and in the beginning has videos that walk you step by step. Participation in the discussion boards are important. The TAs aren't tough graders. Office hours are super helpful if you need some clarity. There is a ton of extra credit as well. He wants you to do well and is extremely understanding.
Very nice man that basically goes over how to do the assignments for you. You end up learning a lot about excel and word in this class, and he is very enthusiastic about it.

Very easy class, work can all be done day of. If you submit your work early you get bank time which allows you to turn in an assignment late later on and he gives a lot of extra credit. Watch the lectures and he literally goes through every step of each assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This course was helpful for learning the basics of Microsoft Office. Later on in the course, some of the assignment directions got a bit confusing so be sure to go to Office Hours (there are plenty throughout the week) and pay attention to the rubric, and you should be fine.

Very easy class and shouldn't really give you any trouble, but on the other hand you won't really learn anything if you know the basics of excel, word, and power point, so you should probably take the ISM3013 class instead

Dr. Mendoza-Garcia teaches this course well. Every assignment and discussion has a well-defined prompt and rubric, so it's crucial to follow it closely to get a good grade. Participation is also important in the class, especially discussion posts because they make up a big part of the final project in the end. Just stay on top of your assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Mendoza-Garcia's class. You definitely will walk away with more knowledge than you started with. He gives a lot of videos to help with assignments and tons of office hours. Sometimes his accent can make it hard to answer so be sure to go to his office hours and speak with TA's. He gives tons of extra credit!

He is an awesome professor. Class is very easy and low work load. You can complete all assignments based off of rubric and if not, he has a video that walks you through all steps in every assignment. Just double check rubric before turning in and youre good! Complete all assignments and discussion on time because they are brought up in the future.

Professor Mendoza-Garcia may be the most caring professor I have had at UF. 350 characters are not enough to describe how caring, efficient, and well-spoken he is. He really does care about his students and their learning. The amount of help he provides is astonishing. He is a great guy and knows what he is talking about.

Unbiased review: He is a very good professor. His lectures tell you exactly what to do and guide you through all the steps so that you can complete the assignments. The class is easy and simple if you watch his videos with the steps. Plus, you learn A LOT in this class, especially in Excel. He is a nice, enthusiastic guy who cares about his class

I'd rather ask a guy who can logically lay out class contents in Spanish to teach this course tho I know nothing about Spanish. Doubt he did not pass any language proficiency test at all. This guy just randomly says something in his recorded videos that have nothing to do with HWs. Avoid this guy for better college life. Please!

This guy was hyper disorganized in his videos, which confused me a lot. He never made clear rubrics for HWs and failed in explaining everything in his video. He hopes everyone can excel in his course but that def is way far beyond his ability. The content itself is a cake but with his instructions is another story.

This guy is incredibly disorganized in his videos and has no idea what he is talking about. Although he really cares about his students, his teaching quality is so poor. His videos are so vague, which confused me a lot. Go to TAs office hour and you will be fine. He hopes you can excel in this course but that's the way far beyond his ability.

I agree this class is easy but also confusing at times. Most of the lessons could be fit into 1 lecture but for some reason he makes us watch 4 lectures all about the same topic just for 1 assignment. His accent made me want to throw my computer at times and his audio quality is trash. That being said I ended the class with a 100% thanks to the EC.

Easy A. He is an amazing person and ironic fave professor. Recorded videos are super easy to follow and get 100 on assignment. He cares and is quick to respond to any questions/issues. Ignore the bad reviews, glad I took him even if I didn't learn much. Very understanding of students and there.

John Mendoza Garcia is a fantastic person, however his teaching style was not my favorite. He is the most confusing professor I've ever had ( including high school) and makes simple tasks difficult because of his lack of communication and failure to explain things decently. He is very encouraging and is very open to speaking with students.

This guy is pretty useless. He is not organized, doesn't know what he's doing, and can't actually teach. The videos that he uses to "explain" the assignments are terrible. The quality is awful, he seems like he is doing these things for the fist time in his life, skips important steps, and makes mistakes. It's an easy A, but you're on your own.

Dr. Mendoza-Garcia seems to genuinely care about all his students. He gave lots of opportunity for extra credit. As someone who didn't have any previous background in Excel, I had trouble following along with some of the videos to complete assignments. We typically had 1 assignment per week and would take me 2-6 hours depending on the difficulty.
Extremely detailed assignments for a lot of points and it doesn't help that he doesn't speak english very well. Hard grader but manageable class would recommend for a sum a or b sesh
This is probably one of the easiest classes I've taken at UF. You can complete the assignments by watching his videos. He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities so take advantage of it.

This was a very easy class as long as you followed the instructions and asked for help when needed. While Dr. John-Mendoza was not good at explaining assignments and often left instructions out, he was very caring and tried his best to answer questions. The class can be frustrating at times, but there is usually only 2-3 hours of work each week.

Prof Mendoza Garcia is great. He always gave me good feedback and he seemed to really care. There's no textbook which is nice cost wise. Assignments were due on fridays so I always did them the day they were due and I got 100s. Sometimes the assignments were a little difficult but I didn't always watch the lecture videos so thats probably why.

Class requires one project and a discussion post a week. Budget out five hours. Would recommend starting at least four days before the deadline. He will release tons of videos that show how to do the assignment so make sure you watch them all. Very quick with response and lenient grader. Always check project with the rubric he gives you!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. John gives a pretty straightforward online class. Do the assignments and get the A. As long as you meet the criteria for the assignments, you will get a 100, and usually, Dr. John releases videos that you walk your through them. There are no tests and the quizzes are very easy. You should expect to spend 2-3 hours a week on the class.
I don't know why Dr. Mendoza is reviewed so harshly. While the class is kind of boring all of the assignments were extremely easy. If you need a math gen ed credit this is the easiest one at UF!

Pretty much an assignment and discussion post a week. Dedicate three hours to it and you should get an 100%. He serves more as a facilitator than a teacher, but he will tell you how to do the steps of the project in the video. Can be stressful with so much on a rubric, but just make sure you hit every step ON THE RUBRIC.

WATCH HIS VIDEOS!! there isn't a textbook for this class so you get all information from the videos he posts. sometimes they are confusing and indirect but he provides the rubric for each assignment, so as long as you figure out how to do what's on the rubric you will do well. 1 or 2 assignments/ projects due every week plus some discussion boards

The hardest part of this class is reading the instructions. You have to swift through it several times and really pay attention to just understand the task. Nothing is made clear and you often have to ask additional questions for clarification. The course isn't difficult, but it is frustrating just figuring out what to do for each assignment.
Well organized content. Nice professor. Dr. Mendoza cares about his students. I felt like a human taking this class.

This class is easy if and only if you work really hard on the projects and make sure that everything is perfect. He does basically nothing to help you and it is a lot of self teaching. However, this class is easy if you work really hard.
His videos are completely related with assignments and he is very fast answering questions. You can get the certifications.
Great teacher!
Fantastic teacher. I learned very much. Detailed instructions are provided in his videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Mendoza is a very enthusiastic and nice guy!!! He answers questions very promptly!! The only thing I did not like is when uploading files in canvas. The files can become corrupted. You ALWAYS need to open and verify the assignments after they are uploaded.

He has been one of the best teachers Ive ever had at UF. This is my first online class at UF and It was clear to understand. He gives written instructions and provides answers in his videos and offices hours.

The class was mostly easy Office functions from high school. The assignments were overcomplicated by the fact that the instructions often had important parts left out and were poorly worded. The instructor would also change or add to the assingment instructions very close to the deadline. Some of the data files were so large they would crash Excel.
Easy class. Lots of assignments, but extra credits.

He cares about students. He answered all my questions and Im getting an A. If someone is reading this, be careful with the participation points, you must participate on time in the forums and peer reviews, that will be your evidence. Professor repeated that many times. Friend might not get an A, because she forgot to do it and forums were closed
Nice teacher! Recommended
Good and respectful teacher. Advice: watch all videos. Take advantage of the office hours and extra credits.
Dr. MEndoza is always willing to help and answer emails and questions in the forum quickly.

This is the most stressed I've ever been in an easy class. It takes hours to piece together the lectures and instructions, which are presented scattered over multiple pages with no organization. When asked for clarification, Professor Garcia often further complicates things. He often forgets to include essential parts of the instructions.

Class is badly designed. Some of it is him and some of it is probably UF. The course basically consists of hs level busywork where you just have to follow his exact directions to do basic Office functions but with extra work added. You don't learn anything useful at all. It's time consuming but should be an easy A

Prof. Garcia seems to care for students, but his videos are extremely unclear and hard to follow along. Lynda videos are way too long just google up the stuff you don't know how to do. Missing a few small details can cost heavily on assignments. Also this class doesn't cover Access so I'm wondering whether I should've taken ISM instead...

All learning relies on outside tutorials, and instructions aren't specific. The teacher isn't assessable and isn't of much help. If you're in the Business School, take the other option--this one isn't worth it, even if it is online.
Easy class
Instructions don't make sense and the data we use is terrible.
So heavy homework.
Do not take this class if you don't have to. Anyone who hasn't given this course a 1 out of 5 is lying to themselves, there are so many better options that taking this class with this professor

It took this class in spring, the course was awful and I drop it. I retook it in summer and I got an A. There was a big change! The instructions were more specific and if you watch his videos you'll find lots of tips for quizzes and assignments.

reviews.comment: I absolutely hate this class. The only way to find the actual requirements for the projects are to read the many paragraphs of vague instructions, watch hours of vague videos, and look at the useless rubric which doesn't always line up with the rest of the instructions. Also, I haven't learned much because the projects are mostly 9 pages of typing.

I was actually looking forward to this class as I've dabbled in Excel and Word and found both programs interesting. However, it is safe to say that this course may have ruined all interest. The prof. has a really difficult time explaining instructions for assignments and his instructions are ALL OVER THE PLACE. You will find yourself super confused

reviews.comment: I wasn't sure about taking this course in summer. I guess things have changed. Long instructions, but very well detailed and explained with videos. His videos give tips to succeed in the assignments.

Terrible professor for an easy A class. I only have solid A's in college, but this CGS class was the first B. Never take this professor... No instruction and everything we did all harshly graded busy work!

reviews.comment: His instructions are poorly worded and unhelpful. Missing parts on one or two assignments can ruin your grade. Easy quizzes and extra credit barely saved my grade in what should be an easy required class. TAs grade the 5 assignments, quizzes are graded automatically, and the course relies entirely on Lynda videos, no reason for a professor.
