reviews.comment: Uses a flip classroom style that leaves you with more questions than answers and while Dr. J is knowledgable and accessible for questions, he tends to make you feel dumb for asking and won't give you a direct answer. Orgo 2 is already hard, just take a different professor.
This guy is a joke

This class changed me for the better. It taught me how to work hard. It taught me that even if I work hard, I still might not get the result I want. That's an important life lesson, especially for those interested in science. Dr. J puts so much effort into this class and he definitely expects the same from his students. I recommend this professor!

Probably the worst teacher I have ever had. You will definitely pass the class however, his teaching style is unorganized and his questions are extremely difficult. He is the worst. The way his class is set up makes zero sense. He is not helpful in the slightest when asked any question at all related to the course.

I think Dr. J gets way too much hate. He is a good, funny, caring prof for an admittedly CHALLENGING class. You must stay on pace and do things his way in order to succeed (for the most part). My advice is to study very hard for first exam (easier content) so that carries your grade when it comes to the final exam (harder content). You can do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr J prepares us for orgo 2 but makes this class harder/more stressful than it should be. The basics/key points of many topics are not thoroughly explained enough in LTPs, but are doable. If you can nail the topics and THEN go to every class, participate in the MANY practice questions he offers, you'll do well. Stay on LTP pace, and listen to him!

Organic chemistry is a very hard class and Portmess style of teaching made it even harder for me to understand. He is a bit all over the place during his lectures and online videos which made it hard for me to follow along. The extra help I received from Study Edge and the massive curve on the exams are what helped me to pass this class.

Dr. J has a flipped approach where you watch lectures at home and come to class to do practice questions. Pacing assessments, supplemental materials, and class questions all VERY accurately reflect the tests. His grading style is a bit confusing and not quite transparent, this can be frustrating, as most of the time you are unsure of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truthfully, I am not a fan of this professor's teaching style. You watch lectures before class and class sessions are treated like discussion periods. A lot of reviews will say that your grade is a huge question mark until halfway through the semester. This is true, BUT as long as you perform on average with the rest of the class you will pass.

I got a B and still genuinely felt like I learned NOTHING. The only reason people pass is because of the curve. His teaching style is impossible to follow because he expects all of us to inherently know everything about organic chemistry. The exams, lectures, and textbook seem like they are all trying to teach us different things.

I cannot recommend this professor to anyone. I was forced into taking his class since he was the only professor available for orgo 1 since I was a transfer. His grading is based on class ranking and because of that,2 weeks from finals I do not know if I am passing or failing. This class has given me so much stress and I feel I have learned nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is extremely disorganized. When problems are explained in class you are rarely able to get a direct answer. With hard material, and no option to go back to previous questions the exam grades are pretty much randomized. TA sessions are the only useful course resource and a 50 minute session is more informative than hours of lectures.

Dr.J is incredibly cryptic and disorganized. He teaches organic chemistry as if it is a review for a grad student. He is also absolutely resistant to any feedback and seems to enjoy instilling fear in students. Unfortunately, he is also incredibly funny and charming in person and available to contact online almost 24/7 making him hard to hate.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Everyone genuinely has it backwards, Dr. Portmess is the BEST organic professor this school has to offer. He is honestly hilarious and is so real with all of his students. He genuinely just wants everyone to become the best student they possibly can and wants to see us all succeed. Highly recommend him, would give anything to be back in his class.

His lecture style is rambling and difficult to follow. His lecture videos aren't much better. I've been learning more in 45 mins with an UGTA than an entire week of lectures. It would be better if he actually taught the material in class instead of going over "practice problems" and talking about his pedagogical method.

Portmess claims the difficulty of his class prepares you for medical school. I can report after 3.5 years of medical school to this point, I've yet to take a more ambiguous/unnecessarily ridiculous course in my life. Every course in med school I told myself - no matter what this won't be as difficult/ridiculous as Portmess Orgo 2. I was right...

You will pass but he is so cryptic and tells students they aren't trying hard enough even when they're doing all they can. You'd think when the entire class is failing he might realize its time to look in the mirror. Good luck. Get 100 on all the OWLS. Undergrad TAs carried this class on their backs

Its orgo 2, its gonna be hard no matter the professor. That being said, Portmess is good if you learn from lectures where he emphasizes the smaller, background pieces of a problem, then you apply it to harder problems. VERY active on his discussion board for any questions/concerns, UGTAs are angels descended from above and their notes will save you

Do not take Orgo 2 with him if you can, you will feel lost and confused and will not receive any help from him. He does not teach during the lecture times and forces you to watch his LTPs, which are mostly rambling. The only thing that helped in this class was the UGTA sessions so if you do take this class I would recommend doing that.

I never met him personally, so I cannot speak on how nice or caring he is as a person. As a professor, though, he is not the best. Don't expect good communication with him by email because he will not respond promptly and by the time you reach out again don't expect him to be considerate/fair. Confusing LTPs, ridiculous exams, no actual learning.

Worst class and prof. at this school. Nothing more I could've done to study, I played by all of his rules and did terribly on his nonsense exams anyway. First grade lower than an A at UF (got a 96 in orgo 1) and not a reflection of who I am as a student. Terrible instructor, I don't know anyone in the class that actually learned this semester.

No one said orgo 2 was going to be easy, so if you blame Dr J for doing bad then you were doing something wrong. Yes, his LTPs might be hard to understand but if you try watching them a couple of times they'll start to make sense. Dr. J is a great and caring professor who wants everyone to do well so as long as you put in the effort you'll get an A

Despite the rumors you hear, Dr. J is genuinely such a kind, nice man who genuinely wants everyone to succeed. Although his teaching style was not for me, his UGTAs were my savior and I would not have gotten an A without mine. His exams were fair, and he is ALWAYS on the DB wanting to help. Just put in effort and you will be fine I promise.

Portmess is kind of overhated. Yes his class is difficult and it can be confusing at the beginning BUT, he has the class set up in a way where if you just do what he says you'll get an A. His class does take up a lot of time so if you're taking another difficult pre-med course, I do not recommend taking his class. Enthusiastic and caring.

He's a incredible person and wants students to pass. his exams are impossibly hard. I don't really think i learned anything in this class, but i passed somehow.. which isn't a good thing considering i need this knowledge for the mcat. take it with someone else. ik he's a great person, but it's hard to adapt to his teaching style.

Absolutely avoid if you can!! I know I am a great student, but the way Portmess structures the class sets students up for failure. Grades are based on the top percentages of the class, which creates a terrible environment for learning. I could write a whole essay on the things that made no sense or were frustrating about this course.

By far the worst professor at UF. His class invites you and holds you hostage in his twisted world full of impossible-to-follow lectures, a really weird discussion board platform, SODs, MOWs, Non-graded's, OWL HW, etc. Covers material most schools don't, impossible exams (guessed on over half the questions), and he's rude to students. AVOID

I did not like the structure of this class whatsoever. I was able to hang on with the pacing, but the exams were on a different level compared to practice problems and lecture videos. Portmess cares about his students, and it is easy to pass the class, but it crushed my perception of myself. Take this for an easy pass but not to understand.

I've heard Portmess is better than other orgo 2 professors. He's a fun guy who knows a lot and has AMAZING TAs. Didn't attend a class but did fine. His LTPs did not teach me well, so I had to learn most of the material elsewhere. The OWL assignments were super helpful. His assessments are very difficult and scarce, but he grades on a MASSIVE curve!

He knows his stuff and cares. but god damn this class was not it. orgo 2 is hard, but he made it 1000x harder with his class structures. take it with literally anyone else and you'll be fine. i don't like his lectures online and with only 2 exams... yea never again.

This class ruined my life. I lost friends because of how much time this class requires. YES you WILL pass. But never in my 20 years of living have I ever been so depressed and felt like a failure. I watched every lecture, did every supplement material... still could not do well. Very discouraging on me...Just push through and do everything you can!

I'm honestly so done with crazy science courses at UF.  This class was the last straw.  You barely have time to finish anything, and all of his "helpful" resources are just cryptic.  Maybe I would have passed, but my mental health just couldn't take it anymore.  I was already behind in week one.  Portmess is so hard to understand in lectures.

This class will definitely be one of those defining classes of your academic career. The class is difficult and requires a lot of work, but you will walk out of it feeling very prepared and proud. Dr. J is funny, caring, and just wants to see you succeed. The class may seem daunting at times, but it is absolutely doable. Thank you Dr. J.

Participate in everything especially not graded assignments and OWL homework. They will buffer your exam grades. Lectures were hard to understand, so make sure you watch LTPs. Even if you get a 30 to 40 on the exams you will pass. If you want to pass take him. If you want to learn all of the material take a different professor.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Your success in the class is not dependent on your understanding of organic chemistry, but rather your understanding of his esoteric question style. You must teach yourself with his pre-recorded lectures, because the in-person lecture is just rambling nonsense repeating what the online videos said. Thank goodness for the UGTAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: worst experience of my life. if you want to pass orgo 2, this man is the professor for you. just know your mental health will be sacrificed in the process. get a 100 on all the OWLs, it'll save you. participate in anything and everything, he rewards effort. i knew i'd pass from all the rumors, but this class still destroyed me. good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr.J isn't an inherently bad professor but his style of teaching is hard to follow along. I have gotten As in previous chemistry classes, but have never felt as helpless as in this course since you cannot rely on any outside sources or go back on exam questions. His class felt like preparing for the nature of his exams rather than organic chemistry
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely the worst professor at UF. The chem department here sucks, but he truly is the worst of the worst. Not straight forward, way too many additional problems. Makes the exams so wordy; this is chemistry, not English class. I don't wanna read a whole poem every time I solve a synthesis. AVOID WITH YOUR LIFE! IF YOU DARE, BEWARE!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Idk how I ended with a B-, but I won't complain. I took this for Summer C and man was this an overwhelming experience. We only had 2 exams, and the OWL acted as an "exam grade" buffer. Exams are difficult just bc of how he's not straightforward. Ik ppl who got 30s on the exams but still passed with a C. Passing is possible, but it's tough with Dr J

What a rollercoaster of emotions this class was. I was super convinced I was going to fail at first but ended up with an A. Overall, he's a nice guy and a caring professor. He just has super hard exams. Try your best and you will succeed!!

Absolutely amazing. Yes, this class is hard, no doubt about it, but Dr. J cares SO much. Stay on pace, do all the problems (at LEAST the ones in the pre/post LTP guide), SODs, MOWs, and FUs, and post on the discussion board too! Genuinely grew to love orgo so much because of this man, and feel very prepared for biochem and the MCAT.

Professor portmess is not a bad professor but his teaching styles is MOST definitely not for me. Its not impossible to pass the class, I barely passed any of his exams but the OWL homework does give a significant boost to your grade, so do well on them. Do any extra credit given and try to at least improve your score for your second exam

Took him over the summer a while ago, honestly I didn't really participate + spent most of my time just watching kdramas that summer. Learned nothing and had to reteach myself the content, but I passed the exams despite failing all of them + barely paying attention. This is a class you can pass if you work hard, but you'll probably pass regardless.

Portmess cares about his students and makes sure most people pass his class, he makes it very hard to fail. I had him for both orgo 1 and 2 and his format is very specific but very important to master, it will ensure your success. You will want to give up but I promise you will survive this class. SIGN UP FOR A UGTA IT HELPED ME SO MUCH.

He is a caring and passionate teacher who is patient and open to questions. He spends all hours of every day on the discussion board answering any questions you have as well as staying overtime for office hours every time. LOT of work to do outside class (reverse style, lecture vids at home) but they help. O1 exams extremely hard but O2 were fair.

Professor Portmess has been extremely helpful in my learning of organic chemistry. his class was a solid foundation for biochem. Workload was not easy, but it was totally doable if you put in the effort. In addition, his class really prepared me for the mcat. I highly suggest taking this professor if you want to succeed in biochem and the mcat.

Very difficult to maintain the pace of this course, he provides an overwhelming amount of material. He is a very caring professor, and you will most likely pass the course as he is fair about grading. I just feel like I spent the whole class learning how to prepare for his exams rather than the actual course content. Super passionate about chem tho
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had him for Orgo 1 and 2 and could have not imagined it with anyone else. We had a flipped classroom so attending class was "optional", but attending is important for a good grade. The class was very chaotic, especially in regard to grades, but Dr. J is very, very caring and knowledgable. Everyone's grade was definitely inflated

One of my favorite professors, made learning Orgo 2 pretty interesting and gave kids lots of opportunities. Sign up for an undergrad TA session, do all of the follow ups and pertinent practice problems, stay on LTP pace, use rogue chem as a supplement. By doing these things I was able to achieve over a 100 in this class with a reasonable study plan

Words can't describe this class. Nothing can prepare you for this roller coaster of emotions. If you have the option, don't take it. If you are forced to take it, buckle up. I somehow was able to stumble my way into an A. In my opinion, I don't deserve it and it was out of sheer luck. Outside resources are useful IMO. Good luck to all.

The best professor I've had. I learned a lot and feel proficient in orgo. Very nice and funny in office hours. If you want to do good, apply yourself. It's challenging, but doable and rewarding. Don't pay for extra help - go to class, office hours, and post on discussion board. Let him help you because he's a great teacher and wants you to succeed.

Maybe it's Stockholm syndrome, maybe I'm burnt out from this emotional rollercoaster of a course, all I know is that this man is a wonderful professor. Had him for orgo 1 + 2, and honestly I just can't imagine learning o-chem with anyone else.  10/10, two spongebob thumbs up.

Portmess' class is a rollercoaster of randomness that only exists in the brain of he; however, Portmess is pretty self aware of his mind games so he gives students a curve if he sees fit, but no one really knows what the criterion is for that curve. If you want a good lecturer don't take him, but if you want to pass though, he's prob the best shot.

You will succeed in this class if you follow the steps and advice Dr. Portmass outlines in the beginning of the semester. The material is inherently difficult, but Dr. Portmass is very knowledgable and puts in the time and effort to help students. If you put in effort and are decently smart - an A in this class is very much within your reach!

Very smart man, very sh*t professor. Prepare to teach yourself organic chemistry. Memorize 60 molecules by structure, common name, iupac name, and characteristic/function. Know everything for every question and dont second guess yourself or your screwed. If your a nervous test taker prepare to have a panic attack. God help you, Jason Portmess wont
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The biggest issue with this class is that you literally never get to see your grade. Also, he bragged about how no class has broken an eighty average on an exam in the twenty years he has been teaching. That is probably the best way to express how bad this class is. And he is currently the only orgo two instructor at UF. But at least he curves.

I took this class during summer & I would recommend to avoid taking it during this term as we only had 2 exams (midterm & final). Dr portmess values effort & is aware that his class is difficult, so effort goes a LONG way in his class. If you want higher than a C then make sure you score average/ above average on every exam.

I took this class over the summer which is why it was so hard. The lectures confused me for a good 2 weeks, and had very easy examples. The exams were way harder than what we practiced too. If you do everything he says, I think it's possible to get an A, but it's unrealistic to do list when you have other courses to go along with it.

This class is difficult. Most of your grade is exams and a bit of homework. Exams are tricky and hard to predict. However, it is not difficult to pass the class. Dr. J is a great guy and will work to help you out. I would try not to worry about your grade as it will likely be higher due to curves and bonuses.

Dr. Portmess is the most difficult professor I have had yet in school. Make sure to stay on pace with the LTP's, as that is the only way going to lecture will be useful to you. Otherwise you're going to be largely on your own for gauging your understanding. If you stay on pace, class will be an important opportunity to reinforce and ask questions.

As long as you keep up with EVERY little thing, you will be okay. You would need around an average of 55% on every exam or higher to pass. There were tons of oppurtunities to boost your grade so always keep an eye out for those. 
Make sure to be assigned to a TA because they will help you out the most!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stay away from this man at all costs. He is conceited, unfair, and a HORRIBLE teacher. The amount of time and effort you have to put into this course is absurd. I let people convince me he was worth it in the end with his magic grading but he single-handedly made me want to drop out of UF. I have never disliked a professor like this.

Exams are short and sweet but man he is an awful lecturer. Walking in from day one, he jumped into the deep stuff that honestly didnt make much sense. I only learned because of the UGTA sessions. He also didn't seem happy to teach orgo 1. IDK ... Maybe he is good for orgo 2? But now that Peterson is gone, it worries me for the future kids

What I hate about this class, you have absolutely no clue what grade you have in the class. I had to drop because I couldn't tell if I was failing or passing, and I just did not want to take a risk. Its extremally stressful when your gradebook has N/A and some strange grading criteria for the exams. Its unfortunate we have to take him for orgo2.

Dr. Portmess is...an experience. You will pass the course, but getting a great grade is exceptionally hard. I never fully knew what was going on in his course. The average grade in the class is a B-. It is certainly one of the toughest classes at UF. Dr. Portmess is an interesting guy, and he cares about you, but he doesn't. Take it if you dare.

Orgo with Dr. J was tough but he gives us so many different opportunities for practice and extra help that although his lectures are convoluted and hard to follow, you still at the end of the day learn a lot. As long as you get above the average on exams, you will pass.

Exams were ridiculously hard. People who studied hard ended up with similar grades to people who didn't/barely studied at all. Impossible to get an A, you have to study the subject all day/everyday in order to get even close. If you are the kind of person that wants to pass (C/B-) without studying, you can still pass though.

Dr. J definitely is one of the better chemistry profs I've ever had, he provides plenty of resources to make sure you can keep up and pass his class, also there's plenty of extra credit opportunity as well. His class is really test heavy so you absolutely have to study well for the exams and definitely use the practice exams too.
Got a 27 on the final and still passed with a B-. Absolutely love this man
Didn't study, didn't show up to class, was failing all year until grade curves hit and I passed. He's a certified g
Thought id fail but I got a B- which ended up being the class average, I wont take him again because of the stress but I recommend him if you need to at minimum pass orgo
I had to retake orgo 1 and this time around I was scared until he curved everything and I somehow went from failing to a B+ by the syllabus standard. Definitely rewards hard work

Do every single thing he tells you to do and the exam will be similar. Be active on the discussion board, a lot of insight on there and show up to all TA sessions and office hours. Not an Easy A but still doable if you try

For not showing up a single day and just studying a few hours for exam, I should have failed but he curves the grades at the end and I ended up passing because of extra credit. Recommend if you don't cream yourself over an A or A-
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly thought I would fail but I passed with a B-, everyone says he's bad but he's just tough and he cares a lot of you make the effort to show up and participate.

Really tough exams but doable. You wont fail the class if you try your best. Get a 50% on one exam and do 80% of the homework and you'll pass with a C. Study a lot and utilize every resource he gives and you'll be okay. A lot of extra credit opportunities.

You have to devote yourself to study a lot and effectively. Study the material he gives you, all of it. First read the book chapters relevant to a lecture, then watch the lecture, pause to work our problems, do follow ups, then do the post lecture book problems. Do everything and be in a TA session, they're really helpful. Good professor, hard work
Good and funny guy, hard exams. Attend TA sessions, they help a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Exams are extremely difficult and unreasonable. His lectures are very hard to follow and goes out of his way to ensure his exams are completely different than supplemental study resources such as study edge. Majority of students fail the exams and he ends up doing major damage control at the end of the semester. Overall, no student should take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. J provides tons of resources for students after previous feedback and is constantly on his discussion board answering questions. Super knowledgable guy as well. It's unbelievable that people still find ways to complain about him. It's not an easy course. You need to put in a lot of work, but it's in preparation for future, tougher courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orgo is a hard class but Dr. J sets you up with everything you need to succeed. Trust the process. Do all of the FUs, MOWs, SODs, and attend the UGTA session. Not an easy class, but you can succeed if you put in the effort.

Professor Portmess is a nice guy but his teaching methods are confusing and frustrating. His lectures are mostly recorded and you have to wacth it which makes it even worse. His exams are extremely hard, I always get 30s-50s on them because its based on his own questions. His does give extra points at the end so do every homework. AVOID him.

Dr. J isn't a terrible professor, but his exams are very difficult especially since I took them online (cannot go back to a question). Teaches very weirdly and leaves a lot of the work on you; if you learned the material his way through the book and his discussion forums you'd likely do well. I didn't apply enough effort and passed with solid B
If you can, avoid this man at all costs. He does not have your best interests at heart, no matter what he may try to say.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Expectations were very unclear, constantly shifted the grading scale without telling us, everything was prerecorded for the online section but he doesn't have office hours even though he doesn't make new content. ridiculously difficult. The more I studied, the worse I did. Ended up passing but seriously just take it at community college

This class was incredibly challenging to follow along with the structure and content. If it wasn't for Study Edge, I don't think I would have understood anything. His exams were huge curveballs, but Study Edge helped me prepare for that.

The hardest class I've ever taken. Dr. J was a good teacher and had a lot of resources to help but the only thing that got me to pass this class was Study Edge. I did not understand any of the concepts in the lectures but study edge cleared up a lot of things for me and got me to at least understand the basics so I could pass the exams.

Portmess does a great job at preparing you for biochem and med school, but his exams are awful. He says not to use outside resources, but Study Edge helped me so much with just knowing what to study. He likes to say practice until you can't get a problem wrong, so definitely recommend Study Edge for more practice.
He was so bad, I want to give him a zero. But thats not possible, so I give him a one.

He's a really nice guy, but his lectures are absolute garbage. I felt super confident in my orgo knowledge going into this class and afterwards I felt like I actually unlearned orgo. Scored 40-50 on each exam, did all hw and EC, and ended up with a B, so it's definitely doable even if the class feels like a waste of time. Get rouge chem.

dont listen to the people who not to use study edge. I used it didnt watch lectures for the last exam and it was the best I did. Yea if you want an A in the class your going to have to work on it but I had nothing memorized by heart, averaged forties on the exams and passed the class with a B-. If you do all the assignments you will pass.

I'm not gonna lie, I despised him and his ways & I still do to an extent; but I don't doubt how overqualified he is to teach this subject. Simply, his exams are too hard (but you get reworks for bonus points). Try to do everything he says and you will at least pass. SE helped me, I honestly didn't find RC very helpful.

Honestly, hardly put in any effort for this class but I would not recommend doing the same because I definitely got lucky... I only really studied for the final and my exam score was 15 points higher than the first two. If I ha tried that hard on the first two I probably could've ended with a B+ at least. Dr. J is tough but a good guy.

Dont take him if youre not willing to do everything to know your stuff: LTPs, supplements, UGTA sessions, FUs, MOWs, SODs, tb probs, OWL, his DB. Hes a great guy but the content is a lot & not clearly defined, so people fall behind & go to Rogue Chem. Rewarding class if you try, frustrating if you dont. Chances are you will end up with a B or C

Dr. J's the best prof I've had at UF! Orgo is definitely tough with him, and he writes hard exams, but his improvement bonuses are generous (failed the first exam and got an A in the class) and the way he explains concepts is very unique. Work hard though- go to his office hours, UGTA sessions, and use the discussion board! Honestly a great guy.
just avoid him and his class its not worth the headache and tears you will shed

avoid at all costs. portmess' exams are nothing like what he teaches. do EVERYTHING he assigns and then hope to get a decent grade. on the bright side he randomly gives a lot of bonus points if you improve from one exam to the next.

Yeah, I did bad in this class and this was my worst grade to date at UF. My problem with Portmess though isnt just that his exams are really difficult, but that he doesnt give practice material or anything to his students to help prep for the exams. Also, I have heard from people who attend his office hours that he is condescending and rude.

If you like to take shortcuts for every class and/or pay for notes, you'll have a bad experience. Only take if you genuinely want to push yourself through hard work, you'll find it a fun experience at the end of everything. Don't take with another difficult/time-heavy course. 50% chance you will experience Stockholm Syndrome.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I am so glad he wont be teaching organic chemistry next semester

Portmess is one of the best, if not the greatest chem professor I have taken at UF. Ive taken Lopez and Sumner For gen chem and they were both terrible but Portmess was a surprising break from the difficult chem professors. Other reviews should be taken with a grain of salt, Study edge is helpful but not needed, his lectures are very thorough.

These reviews bamboozled me when I took the course. I decided to go against popular opinion and take Portmess based on these reviews, which was a terrible decision. He makes the hardest college course (as per Google) 10x more difficult for no reason. He has an unorthodox method of teaching that involves not giving you half the material. Stay away!

Dr. J is truly a wonderful professor. His class is hard, nobody can deny that, perhaps it is even harder than what it needs to be. This is not done for his advantage, instead, he's preparing students for bigger challenges (like biochem). Don't let his reputation cloud your appreciation for such a great professor. ps; watch ALL lectures.

Easy to pass and get a B-. Will have to put in a lot of work. Watch all LTPs, use Rouge Chem and Study edge. Attend UGTA sessions. Post on DB and make your name known to him. Redo all assignments reopened and try to get higher scores on round 2. Take dr j on a semester where this is your ONLY hard class (ie no physics etc). Go above and beyond

Worst professor I've ever taken. I took his online classes and they were super messy. No grade scale. Homework was totally different from the tests. Exams were HARD and TAs helped but not enough. If you can, avoid taking him.

Most professors do not come remotely close to the nuance and depth of instruction Portmess provides. He is unique, idiosyncratic, and truly passionate about organic chemistry. Do everything he tells you to do, as soon as he tells you to do it. If organic chemistry is not currently your favorite subject, Portmess will ensure that will be.

He is by far the worst teacher I've ever had, His exams are long and complicated, and the lectures and notes are not helpful. I feel as though he talks about the information rather than explains through it. If there's ever a way to make his class more difficult, we will do so. Has a huge ego that seems to be fed through belittling his students and making them feel inferior. Made a point to emphasize that even though his class consists of mostly non-chemistry majors, he would teach advanced orgo not necessary for students

I recommend watching his lectures even though they don't make any sense, then watch the study edge videos that correspond to those lectures, then use rogue chem for practice. Watch a lecture a day so you don't get behind cause it sucks catching up. Do all of the MOW, SODs, and FUs as soon as they are assigned, and read over ur skeletal note.

reviews.comment: Those that think Dr.J is a good professor... have Stockholm Syndrome from this man. Some of his lectures make great sense, others will have you replaying it 3-4 times. AVOID! please... for your mental health!

He knows that learning is not necessarily about the grade you get instead the knowledge you receive. Best professor I've ever taken in my life. He will make you work for it but if you like orgo take him, he cares so much about the subject and his students. If you don't care about learning take someone else, but he will inspire you more than anyone.

His exams were not straightforward. I studied so much for his final and after taking it, I realized I might as well had just done something better with my time (not saying you shouldn't study, but no one knows WHAT to study). Everyone will try to scare you and say he is the meanest guy ever but he is truly the best professor I have ever had at UF. The only thing he really cares about is organic chemistry applications and you showing effort. Read the textbook, go to SI sections, listen to all lectures, ask questions on the DB and you will do fine. So thankful I had him.

Literally awful. Portmess provides vague lectures and expects you to learn from that and be able to practice yourself. You will most likely pass the class, but with a C or C+. Its extremely hard to get anything above that. Get Rogue chem if youre taking it!! It saved my grade so much and theres no way I wouldve gotten above a C without it.

Dr. J is a pretty hard teacher, and he bases his approach on learning Orgo 2 reaction patterns rather than memorization. worst professor hands down. I got an A- and I still think hes the worst prof Ive had. Disorganized, talks chemistry to fill his ego and is the most unapproachable prof Ive had. Honestly, an extremely difficult class to get an A but an extremely easy class to pass. I didn't watch a single lecture or really learn anything besides what happened in the OWL homeworks. worst professor I've had... does NOT teach.. only fills his ego by talking about chemistry and not actually teaching... has NO office hours (which is probably against UF policy btw) and is condescending even through online communication... thinks his class is your world and universe... Dr. J is a great, enthusiastic professor however his class in disorganized. His passion for organic chemistry makes you want to learn it as well and he has been one of my favorite professors at UF. His class has been the hardest class I've taken at UF so far, however it has been the most rewarding.

Dr.J really does care about his students and wants them to learn. Start studying day 1! I recommend that you go to class and listen to what he says. He sidetracks sometimes but those are important too. Overall he's a nice guy but his class needs to be your priority and requires a lot of time.

Great professor, his class isnt the easiest but with some dedication its totally doable and you learn a ton of material. Study edge was a great supplement to use with this class to help review material as well.

I tried so hard, went to office hours, had tutoring, but had to drop. Orgo is difficult, but he makes the course much more intensive than it needs to be. Unless you LOVE the subject, take an easier prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Unnecessarily difficult & confusing teaching style. His lesson plans are a mess. How is your grade calculated? That's a mystery. I got an A in Orgo 1 but could not succeed in this class no matter what I tried (I ended up dropping). He sends 15-20 emails per WEEK. His tests are extremely tricky and unreasonable. I hate this man.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: By far one of the hardest professors I have had at UF. No class has ever been this hard, nor has been this hard. But YOU WILL LEARN. Dr. Portmess is a little all over the place, but he makes himself available to students in office hours and arranges SI sessions. Get all the help you can. Practice, practice. He gives extra points for PR on exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The biggest piece of advice I can give you regarding this class is WAIT for next semester if this is the only professor available. It is honestly worth delaying graduation to take a manageable organic chemistry class. This class is unnecessarily difficult and quite frankly requires a ridiculous amount of work. Genuine pre-med weed out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This is the most difficult class I have taken thus far despite being a physics major. You must work hard to earn an A in this class, but there is LOTS of extra credit. Get involved with SI, post on his discussion board, and attend everything that is offered, because you will earn extra credit points for it if he sees you care.

This is the hardest class I have taken to date. However, Portmess was an amazing professor. Yes, you feel like you are drowning the whole semester, but it pushes you to have a really really good grasp of the material. If you are going to need this stuff in the future, Portmess will make sure that you know it by heart.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Worst class I have ever taken in my life. Makes it unnecessarily hard to do well just so that he can keep up his reputation of being the hardest professor at UF. Doesn't care if you learn, he just wants you to know that his knowledge of orgo chem is omnipotent and he will never dumb it down for the his students sake. Wait for another prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This. Class. Is. Time. Consuming. He gives you everything you need, meaning you have to do everything he gives you if you want to do well. The result? A class that is a nightmare for anyone who isn't motivated by organic chemistry (me). I can't say this class isn't fair, because it is. Just beware if chemistry isn't a passion or at least enjoyable.

He is a kind person, but I felt confused a majority of the time in this class. I didn't understand him during lectures so TA sessions are VITAL! I would do all of the homeworks, FU's, TA sessions, practice exam sessions, MOW, SODs, butterflies, but I would get the test and feel like I didn't know anything. Magic curve helps.

It's not as bad as people say. I really enjoyed this class and he prepared us for the MCAT so well. I wish my other professors cared half as much as portmess does. Excellent lectures and office hours. He does talk fast so I recorded the lectures and listened to them before the test and I got A's on all the exams before the curve so it is possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class requires time. You actually have to STUDY. Do the FU's, SOD's, MOW's, heck even do study edge. Do everything you can to learn the material and DO NOT CRAM. I recommend studying at least a week ahead of every exam. Pay attention and write down exactly what he says in class. Office hours and TA discussions help a lot too! Good luck! lol
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Honestly, amazing prof that really wants you to learn--and you do. He just doesn't have to make his tests SO hard. The first one broke me, I studied so much and got a 41% (average was 50) but then he gives you improvement points and does weird magic grade stuff so I got a 67, 62, and 67 on the rest and ended up with a B- because of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: DO WHAT HE SAYS. He gives you the map to an A. It's like treasure hunting. It doesn't come easy but I know I'm going to kill the MCAT's because I took this class serious Follow along with that class instead of cramming or rushing ahead. If you want to get your money's worth and actually learn the material take Portmess.

Dr j is one of the best teachers i've had. He's funny and keeps lectures interesting. Orgo isn't super easy and he wants you to learn it well. He provides more than enough material to succeed so Study edge is not an option. It does take some hard work but if you put in the effort you will succeed. Tests are very fair, not impossible at all

I took Professor J for orgo 1 and 2 in one summer. Read before class and come prepared to pay attention so put away any distractions. He is one of the best lecturers and really puts effort into teaching you. He is a professor that I will always remember for his passion teaching. I didn't go crazy studying and passed without any worry.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: At the beginning I did not like Portmess but I began to respect him as the semester went on. He really does care about his students will do anything he can to help. His tests are indeed insanely difficult though. An A in the class requires an insane amount of effort. Utilize UGTA sessions. Study Edge won't save you in this class.

Dr. J is very knowledgeable and passionate about orgo. He definitely expects a lot of his student. The way I see his exams , they are like the flu virus. They take on new forms every time and tend to b unpredictable. When you take his class get ready to think outside of the box and work harder than you ever had. " Who wants it most will do best."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Portmess definitely makes this class harder than it needs to be. Orgo is difficult enough as is, and he does very little to make it feel more manageable. It is certainly possible to do well, but a ton of effort is required to keep up with what his disorganized style. His syllabus is incomplete and he is not transparent about grading at all. Avoid!!

I passed orgo 1, but I didn't understand orgo until I had Dr. J. He is a great lecturer and he knows his stuff. You need to work in his class to do well. Go to office hours. Sign up for TA sessions. He has a lot of resources for you to do well. Do the SODs and MOWs. Put in an honest effort. It's hard, but it's a great experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fall '14: You need passion (many daily hours) to pull an A in Portmess's class. His tests are challenging but fair if you attend every lecture; all the salty premeds below say otherwise, but they simply didn't put in the hours. Go to class, office hours, and TAs. Live and breathe the class. This is the only way to an A. Amazing person and lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Portmess is THE hardest professor I have ever taken. He makes the class harder than it needs to be. His tests are extremely hard and outside the scope of the class. He makes you memorize "star molecules" and is very unorganized. Do not take him unless he is your last choice. I only passed because of the "magical" curve & extra credit at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I had him for both orgo 1 and 2. This was the worst class I've ever taken. It's almost like he talks in riddles. He makes the material harder than it needs to be. Do all the MOW's and SODs as well as the textbook problems. His tests are ridiculously difficult. Orgo is hard, but if you put in all your effort you can get a good grade. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Portmess is by far the best but also the hardest professor I've ever had. You learned a lot about chemistry in his class. However, if you are just you want to do well,  DO NOT TAKE HIM. If you love Chemistry, take it with him !!! He is the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Orgo is just a difficult class no matter what, but Dr. J does make the topics more complicated than it actually is because he uses his own language. I took him for  Orgo 1 and 2 and I can honestly say that he pushed me far beyond what I thought my limits were. Long story short, it's a challenging class, but hard work does pay off a lot in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: With Dr. Portmess you will get a very deep understanding of orgo, but most importantly  he will show you how to think critically, refine your study skills, and be accountable for material in a difficult course. These are skills that will be beneficial no matter what field you are going in to.
He's a great teacher but hard. Take if you want to learn a lot about chemistry. You will definitely need study edge and attend lecture. A lot of work but can be worth it in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I honestly only have good things to say about Dr. J. I had him for both orgo classes and wouldn't change professors if I could go back in time. Enjoyable lectures and he really wants people in his class to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Portmess is easily the worst professor/instructor I've ever had the displeasure of having. The class is unnecessarily difficult and did not help for Orgo II at all. I only took him for Orgo I but I was told he punished his Orgo II class for having a good exam average. Don't let him fool you with his bs "stats" at the beginning, they're skewed.

Dr. J is passionate about Organic Chemistry. He makes the material feel important. However, his tests often focus on fringe scenarios, straight up trivia, and questions you've only seen 60-70% of the material. I am pursuing acceptance to Med School and wish I had taken someone else for Organic I and II. He goes way farther in depth than necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Portmess is an excellent instructor and lecturer. For those who aren't interested in chem, especially pre-meds just trying to make it through, don't take it with him, especially  if you're doing it "just to look good." Dr. Portmess makes you work for his class. His exams are difficult. But if you're passionate about Chem, take it with Portmess.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Portmess is an excellent professor teaching an extremely difficult course. It is important to attend class as well as take detailed notes. However, I used Study Edge reviews and practice problems, which made the course feel much more simple in studying for the exams. I highly recommend taking Portmess and using Study Edge for his material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was definitely one of the most difficult courses I've taken at UF, but it helped me be more disciplined than I have ever been. Dr. J truly does care about getting to know his students and helping them. Even if you don't perform optimally in the class, it does not imply that you will be incompetent. No mistakes ... just opportunities!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I like Dr. Portmess, but he is tough. His exams are hard (besides the level of difficulty of Orgo). He gives a lot of extra credit and improvement points + curves at the end of the semester. A lot of people dropped the class (around 50%) and still 10% failed. It was hard to decide, but I'm taking another prof for Orgo2. Never got a B/C before

The amount of delusion in these reviews is unreal. People with bad grades rate low, people with good grades rate high. I'll be a tiebreaker. I got a B-, which means I should give him a 3... but no. His lectures are all over the place, and he tests on trivia rather than the big picture.  He's only worth taking if you're CheE or some such major.

I have mixed feelings about his class, my work ethic has increased significantly , but he has such a unique way of doing things that he makes orgo harder than it needs to be. Study edge helps because they simplify it, but practice and office hours is key. You can get by easy with the other professors but you will truly know orgo by taking him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: In this class you need to not only do well, but stay ahead of the curve, aka be one of the best. If you don't like competition or very hard work, stay away. You need to perform well and also be better than others. I like it this way but if you're not a stellar student... if you're average you won't enjoy and will see your grade being curved down.

Dr. J taught me a lot about organic chemistry but it was not easy. I learned a lot through practice and going to lecture. I would highly recommend study edge because they give you a more in depth understanding of the material and extra practice which is vital. I would recommend being very active in the class and doing orgo at least once a day.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Portmess is the hardest orgo teacher at UF. And unfortunately you don't find this out until you're already signed up for his class and can't get out of it. He makes you memorize "star molecules" that you wouldn't have to know in different sections, and tests you on concepts that don't come until orgo 2! If you struggled in gen chem do not take Dr J

Portmess doesn't teach you Orgo 1 he prepares you for Orgo 2. I took Orgo 1 with him last semester and Orgo 2 with one of the harder professors this semester. The Orgo 2 material is far harder but because of Portmess' class it was joke. His Orgo 1 students did better than those from other professors. If Orgo 2/Biochem  is in your future, TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Difficult class, but nobody said orgo was easy. Don't listen to the angry pre-meds, some people actually need this for their major. It's doable if you do EVERYTHING, assigned and optional and go to TA office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. J is pretty diggity darn arrogant about his teaching style... which is a lot worse than he thinks it is.  The new MCAT requires only the basics of organic... there's no reason to receive the excessive minutia Portmess tries to force down your throat. Don't take an unnecessary ding to your GPA, avoid his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jason will make you hate yourself. I am now changing my major and altering my life goals because I apparently am not scholarly enough to be pre-med. He made me realize this. All of my hopes and dreams are crushed and it's because he expects you to absolutely live and breath what he teaches. Unless you are a chemistry major, DO NOT TAKE HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Portmess is a very tough professor. I wouldn't recommend taking him unless if you're majoring in chemistry. He does give a lot of EC and practice HW. His lectures is all over the place and fast paced. It's hard to keep up with him if you can't multi-task. I wish he would give students times to fill in the notes before explaining the materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Day 1 Dr. Portmess is VERY honest about the difficulty and work ethic you will need has tons of office hours and supplemental aids But I don't think he (his lectures) prepare you at all for his exams. He is very knowledgeable but doesn't convey material in a way for you to understand if chem isn't your strong suit. I like him. I HATE his method.
Portmess is a great but challenging professor. He will challenge to work in a way that you probably never have before. Get ready for a challenging but enlightening class.

Worst. Prof. Ever. Get ready to study what you do in lecture and way more, and miraculously know what random things he'll ask in his tests. The practice tests, other than the multiple choice part, is NOT representative of the actual tests either. He's a nice person and wants you to succeed, but ultimately doesn't teach well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. J seems like a cool guy and is passionate about orgo, but his teaching style isn't the best. His lectures are all over the place and very confusing. I read the chapters in the book before going over them in class and sometimes I still didn't know what was going on. His examples are not very clear. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Portmess was my favorite teacher at UF. Very difficult class, but if you put in the effort its easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. J is passionate about orgo, but his style was not fantastic. Although he does provide skeletal notes, he speaks a lot of fluff which can make the material hard to understand. READ THE BOOK. GO TO TA OFFICE HOURS. He has a bit of a god complex. Do the homework and read the book and you will survive. He does give a lot of extra credit at the end.

Portmess is an interesting character, but a good chem professor.  Go to the lectures, do all the synthesis and follow up problems he assigns there, it will help prepare for the exams, which are tough, but not impossible.  Make sure you do all extra credit assignments, it will bump up your grade for sure.
Great professor

Dr. J is a good professor, he makes me appreciating orgo more than any other class. Practice is the key. Participation with purpose matters. You learn new things every single UGTA session, UGTA peers' successful strategies help me to do well in this class.  MOWs, FUs, SODs should be your friends to hang out with in this course.

The most challenging class I have ever take, but also the best. Tests are tricky and even the tiniest of details can appear. Take the timeo understand the concepts and not just memorize and it will pay off. Go to office hours, do ALL FUs, MOWs, and SODs, attend UGTA sessions and do all practice problems. Great class!
Rumors are just rumors. Reality is when you get an experience on your own. Dr. J is amazing.

I was told my life would be over once I got stuck with Portmess for Orgo 2. But they were all so wrong. Dr. J cares more about his engaged students than any other teacher, and offers every ounce of help he can to allow you to pass... Just do literally everything he gives you and you'll be fine... It's a lot of work, but oh so worth it!

Originally I had heard how terrible his class was and was very scared. It was one of the hardest classes I've taken and the hardest I've worked, but Dr. J is probably the best professor I had at UF. Now I am studying for the MCAT and realized how much more I retained thanks to Portmess compared to other students with different professors. Worth it.
Great! Great! Professor!!! Really helpful especially at office hours! :)

One of the hardest classes I have ever taken at UF. He was a very good teacher and helped the students more than other teachers I have had. I wanted an A though so I got study edge because I thought Portmess couldn't always explain things in a way I needed, so sometimes I was left quite confused.

Professor Portmess was a great teacher. His lectures were great and I felt that I learned a lot! But, his tests are pretty rough. Lots of practice questions are the best and make sure to redo his questions in his lectures. I used Study Edge to help me out and they had more practice questions which is always helpful. Make sure to go to class!

THIS CLASS TAUGHT ME MORE THAN CHEMISTRY. Jason taught me self discipline and how to examine my self. I despised this man the first month, but later I realized that it was my work ethic that I was despising. Jason is a great teacher as well as a great guy. You need to be fully engaged when you take this course, and the return will be much greater.

Genuinely cares about his job/students & knows ALOT about orgo. Tests are the hardest tests Ive taken at UF, but the class if more than passable if you go to EVERY class & do every extra credit assignment, and memorize all mechanisms/his SODS/MOWs/FUs. Every extra credit attempted lowers percentage point required to pass, & theres a curve @ the end

Excellent teacher with a thorough knowledge of the material he presents. Do book problems and everything he gives you in class (MOWs, SODs, and FUs). If you put in the work, it's not too hard to get a B or B+, but getting an A is very difficult.

Apart from being the best professor I've had, not only in terms of learning the material but making me realize that I don't have to pay for tutoring services to do well in a class. In a nutshell, take orgo with Dr. J, do well and you will come out of the class with a whole new outlook of tackling future obstacles.  An A is possible if you commit.

Dr. J is an amazing teaching and I recommend him for everyone taking Orgo 2. He really knows the material. If you go to office hours, you can ask any questions you want and he's super helpful. He gives you a guide to do well in orgo and if you follow it, you will be good! Yes, you have to put in a lot of work but it's so worth it! TAs are alsogreat

He talks a lot without breaks in his lectures so it is hard to know what is important. Expects you to be able to be at his level by putting in your own work. Not a fan of his notes. Shows random slides during class that are not provided in skeletal notes then appears on exams. Seems took down on health professions.

Go to his classes. With each pop quiz you take your percentage required to pass lowers. Do all SODs MOWs and FU's. Supposedly won't let you fail but i don't think thats true. Tests were very hard. You need to study on a regular basis, not a cram a few days before kind of class.

This man's class taught me a whole new level of work-ethic. His lectures are to be treated as review session. For the most part he expects you to already have a grasp on the concepts before coming to class. DO ALL OF THE FUSODMOW's or you will regret it. I learned so much in this class, and I would recommend him, just be prepared to work hard!

He is a good person, but he exams were way too difficult. I learned a lot of material from his class, but his tests were so outrageously difficult that i truly couldn't test my knowledge. He put too much biological chemistry on the exams, last time i checked, we were in Organic chemistry 2 not biochem.

Dr. Portmess is a great lecturer, and he makes it clear that he has extremely high expectations for his students. I learned a lot in his class, but his exams were so tough that I could not prove that I knew the material. He has lot of biologicalbiochemical applications on exams. Study every day, go to every class (extra credit is offered)!

I wouldn't recommend taking this class unless you are prepared to memorize his notes word for word. He will put the most obscure thing he barely mentioned in class and it will be a large portion of your exam. Be prepared to attend all office hours and read your book religiously. This is the only way to even pass the class, forget about a good grade

Dr. Portmess is the best professor I've had at UF. Orgo is NOT easy by any means...work hard and GO TO OFFICE HOURS. He explains things very well, and if you apply yourself, he is very willing to help you. He even knew my name by the end of the course.
His amount of knowledge is STUNNING.  Expect to study, as echoed by all other students.  But, this is college people, and more importantly, ORGANIC CHEMISTRY.  It aint easy for a reason!

Dr. J is an incredibly awesome person. Best professor I have had so far at UF. He's always willing to go the extra mile to help his students. He actually makes Orgo fun and addictive! Expect to study a lot! Orgo is definetly not a walk in the park, doesn't matter who you take. Also, I did not have him for Orgo1 and I did fine!

Had him for both Orgo 1 and Orgo 2. A phenomenal professor! Definitely a VERY challenging class, requires a tremendous amount of effort and time. This class made me think about orgo ALL THE TIME. After the orgo2 final, I literally had no idea what to do with my life.. Portmess made this class FUN! He's a great lecturer and is very funny. Take him!

Everyone on campus will say not to take him. I'm really glad I didn't listen to them. He puts more time into his class than any professor I've ever had. Not going to lie I made myself a slave to this class as much as possible. Honestly, I feel really lucky to have taken orgo with him. Might not get the grade you want,but the experience is worth it.

I had Portmess for both orgo 1 and 2 and it was a very hard class, but very doable if you studied his notes. I had him a couple years ago and was wondering if anyone knew his office hours this semester?

His class becomes very manageable once you learn that you HAVE to do his FUs, SODs, and MOWs. I recommend reading parts of the book he goes over to fully understand the concepts. His curve is weird and I ended up with an A-.

Portmess is by far the best teacher I have encountered. He is extremely helpful in lectures and in office hours (his TAs are awesome too). His tests are hard, but many questions come from "FUs" and "MOWs" that are given in class. If you study the way he tells you, you'll do great He also doesn't fail anyone, everyone gets at least a C if you try.

Dr. J is an excellent and helpful professor. Exams are tough. Study advice: be very comfortable with trends and practice lots of problems, especially ones from class (they can show up on tests). Don't look at the solution until you've tried the problem. Seriously! Finally, attend class. There are pop quizzes, and you will want those extra points.

A truly wonderful professor that is interested in the success of his students. You have to want it! Attend office hours. Do the FUs, the SODs, and the MOWs. Check the discussion board often. ATTEND CLASS. He makes orgo as easy to understand as possible. Definitely one of my favorite teachers thus far at UF!

The best advice anyone will ever give to you with Portmess is study his FU's, SOD's, and MOW's like CRAZY! These always show up on exams. Don't get behind, you'll just screw yourself over when it comes exam time. The exam average is around a 65 but he curves and gives extra credit in class so make sure you go, especially the day after the exams!

I love this guy. I don't understand how anyone could hate him; his exams are doable with studying, not impossible. After Orgo 1 I lost all interest in chemistry but Dr. J makes it interesting. He's very clear, and very helpful. Best professor I've ever had. Wish I could take him again. If someone didn't pass, it's only because they didn't study.

BEST professor at UF! Pay attention during class, read the book if you don't quite understand, and GO TO OFFICE HOURS. Use the teaching center and TAs, they are his previous students and are also FANTASTIC! You don't really need to practice outside of the F.U.s he gives you (quiz yourself with them before getting answers in office hours). Got an A

Excellent teacher. Very helpful. If you like puzzle solving, you'd love this class. Not very hard, but requires lot of practice. Do the problems in the book and the FUs from his notes and an A is very much possible.

This is the hardest class I have taken at UF I took it in 6 weeks and I honestly think the only way I made it through was because how much Dr. J cares about his students. He offers so much time and help to make sure that you can do the beat you possibly can in his class.  It def wasn't easy but it sure was worth it in the end

Dr. J is the best teacher I've had at UF so far. Get to know him and go to office hours!! You have to work for a good grade but it pays off. He actually wants you to do well, unlike many other UF chem professors. Don't take it with anyone else! Also studying in groups helps for ths class.

I was scared about failing this class before the semester started. Ended up doing very well. Great lecturer and tests are mostly CRITICAL THINKING. Be able to apply knowledge to things you haven't seen. He gives out extra credit too. If you're just looking to pass, it's 60% or even lower depending on the average. TZ > StudyEdge for this class.

Hard class. Don't bother with the book problems unless he specifically tells you to look at them, or if you don't understand something. Tests are super unpredictable. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS! He is super nice and willing to help. Also do TZ or StudyEdge if you want more practice/help.

Dr. J is by far the best professor I have had at UF. He teaches organic chemistry so well, but don't be fooled by this. His class is very difficult and requires alot of studying. I used the textbook nonstop to study for the exams. This is what ultimately got me the A I needed. Make sure to also do his posted past exams! They help immensely!

How to survive Dr J orgo: never miss class, if you go to class he will help you. Go to office hours, it help a lot! Do NOT fall behind! Do all book problems and find more! Memorization will not serve you well, understanding concepts will. Get TZ with Lauren and do the packets.Exams are hard, but lots of partial credit. You can get a A/B w/hard work

I wish I had more space. To the guy who "made his worst decision of his career" sounds like orgo was a wake up call. If you are willing to put in the work and learn the material, you will be fine. Go To Class! Dr J will help those who put in the effort. Miss class and you are on your own. Best Orgo professor at UF!

Best teacher I've ever had, and that's coming from someone who struggled through his class. Dr J pushes you to your limits but you learn so much about Orgo and yourself along the way. If you hate Portmess I'd argue that it's because you didn't invest the effort necessary. Not easy, but if you want to be proud of yourself when you pass, take him.

He is absolutely awful. Do not take his class. Some people say it's worth it because he "knows what he is talking about and forces you to learn." This is not true. He has absolutely no regard for students and literally tries to fail you. He makes every exam much more difficult that the other professors'. Worst decision of my college career.

Great lecturer with tough exams. Well worth it, but the book problems will only get you so far. His TAs are great, and Tutoring Zone helps a lot, too.
