Portmess does emphasize going to his office hours.  The thing is, not everyone can go to office hours and wants to. He gives hints to quizzes and tests for those that do go to office hours.  It's unfair to those that absolutely can't or don't feel the need to.  So when he throws hard questions sometimes, the officehours students get the benefit. :(

I think everyone will agree that Portmess is NOT in any way, shape, or form, an easy teacher.  You want an easy A? Find someone else.  But he is really good at what he does.  He definitely knows his stuff and is always willing to help you out.  Despite the struggle to do well, I'm actually really glad I got stuck with him. :)
If you are a hardworker, remotely intelligent, and want good grades try to get another prof. I have had him for two semesters and have mixed feelings about him.
Difficult yes, but personally I would find another OChem professor. Tests are difficult.
He is a hottie ;)

Everyone that is complaing needs to SHUT UP!!! You didnt work hard, you didn't study enough, go cry by yourself. Organic chemistry isn't easy, but at least you have an instructor that focuses only on teaching, not research, and offers more office hours than you can probably attend. He gives u a minimal mechanism list for each test, come on guys...
eh, he needs a pepper for his efforts. he's fair-ish, and has a good sense of humor.
Worst teacher EVER.  Avoid this guy like bird flu, because he will act like a chicken.  I studied 3 weeks for an exam and still bombed, it makes me want to protonate his FACE.

Dr. J is a good professor, always there to help, offers several office hours.. The key to Portmess is to go to his office hours, do the study problems in the book, and as he says PRACTICE PRACTICE PRACTICE! Orgo is a hard subject so do not take it if you are not willing to make the time commitment.

He is a difficult teacher, probably more difficult than a lot of the other orgo professors at UF, BUT he is extremely helpful and FAIR.  You learn so much in his class.  Everyone that says he is impossible just lazy or didn't have the time to put more effort forth.  You can't study the night before and expect a decent grade.
Tests are extremely difficult and hardly relate to the material covered in class. You can find a better orgo teacher, get out if you can.

His class was ridiculous. He seriously tried to come up with the hardest tests possible just so that the kids that went to **** would fail. He's a jerk. I ended up getting a B but I have never worked so hard in my life. The material he teaches in class is never on the test and you have to go to his office hours to find out the real materia

He teaches well and the class seems easy enough, except for the exams. The exams come out of nowhere and there are no practice tests. You might end up being better prepared for his exams if you randomly selected problems from OTHER teachers, than if you studied his class notes.

He is a great teacher....teaching wise he only teaches the basic fundamentals, an analogy i can make is this: He teaches basic additon and subtraction BUT when it comes to the exams he expects you to know how to do advanced calculus- he is very helpful and has many office hours but his exams are next to impossible- on the final there were completel

Hardest tests I have ever taken.That said, he is a great teacher and is by far the most accessible professor I have ever had.He added office hours half way through the semester to help out.Hard tests dont make you a bad teacher.He is a great teacher who gives hard tests.He says he doesnt curve, but he does with quiz pts.He also tosses out   bad que
Studied till I thought there was NO way i could not get a 100. Took the tests, walked out thinking I aced every single one and failed them.
ooooh crap stay away! This guy's tests are VERY VERY HARD! His final WAS INSANELY HARD, I studied my butt off and flat out failed I mean wtf
good luck
Portmess sucks donkey d***.  Studied till I made myself sick (literally) and still got a 'D.'  Hate him and his tricky, out of this world-impossible tests.

Although during class he seems like a great teacher, onc eyou see his test, you will hate the man for life.  He is satan.  He appears so friendly on the outside and then screws you on his out of this world tests.  Do not take his classes ever.

okay... so my first test i got a 71 on... worked by butt off... got a 143/150 on the final and ended up with a 94 in the class. don't lose hope because it can be done. two things to remember 1) office hours will save your gpa and sanity. 2) never ask the TAs questions during the test... they lied to me and they will lie to you

His tests are extremely difficult. You'll have no idea what to expect for his tests and his practice tests do not help.  There is no curve and he expects you to teach yourself.  If you have to take him just be prepared to take it again next semester even if you work hard.

do not take this class if you want to pass the first time. the tests are impossible and there is no curve. although he's a funny guy he makes this class so much harder than it should or needs to be. nice guy but terrible teacher.

Dr. J is very nice and helpful but tests are super hard! Make sure u know how to work all problems in book! He also goes thru material fast so make sure u read the chapter ahead of time, it will help you out alot!!

the class is ridiculously hard. please listen to us when we say don't take Portmess if you want to pass organic the first time. he knows what he is talking about but his exams are RIDICULOUSLY HARD and his class has NO CURVE!!! but if you are capable of teaching yourself then go ahead.
Three words: Devil in disguise. You cannot run fast enough, take him if you want your gpa to head-dive.

He sure isn't the easiest professor, but certainly not ridiculously hard.  This is my 2nd time in orgo, 1st time with portmess, and I can say with ease that portmess is a GOOD teacher.  If you know your stuff, you will get no less than a B!  He doesn't trick you - you just need to study hard, go to office hours if needed, and focus on the test.

To say the least Portmess's tests are rediculous! I took this class with 4 other friends, 2 of which had already taken the class, and we all had to drop it! From what he tells you the class seems like it will be a breeze, he says his tests aren't that hard and his quizes b4 the test are simple. But when test time comes prepare to be brutaly raped!

Portmess will make you wish you were on the streets being a bum rather than persuing the medical field. his class is ridiculous. he lectures well and he says all this bull about how tests aren't tricky.... but they are.. and unfair. the second test covered cht 4,5,6 and my version of the test had a chpt16 question on it... yah..... i know.

what everyone else's saying is true...he's a nice guy, brilliant chemist...but can't teach for crap. His tests are impossible...I studied for them for days straight, esp. before the exams, and nothing. Find out if you even need ochem, and if you do, take someone else...book & class: a waste of money and time. Don't do drugs.
Just prepare to be tested on super extensive, natural 2nd hand knowledge of organic chemistry that you're "expected to know" and will never learn in class or reading...nice guy, IMPOSSIBLE tests
His class gave me clinical depression. Take it with another professor!!

ewwwww, run away from this teacher. he's terribly hard and his tests suck balls. Take Davidson or even Battiste(curved grading scale). He's nice, but you can tell he gets a kick at making you suffer during his exams.
Portmess's class gave me clinical depression. Take it with another professor!!
Saying his tests are an abomination to mankind is an understatement. Cool guy, but bardest ochem teacher at UF..will try to trick you and test on stuff youve never seen or heard of before.

Portmess is quite a character--funny, witty, but TOUGH! His first test wasnt bad, but then it all goes downhill. Kids were dropping like flies all semester. I was about to, but stuck it out. I thought for sure I'd get a D or F after that last test and the final, but I ended up with a C--VERY SURPRISED! Study hard, get extra help, but dont freak out

I recommend taking his wife Davidson instead.  I did all the book problems and attended offics hours, but his tests suck, are not straightforward, and his TA's make many grading errors.  I also think he has a spil personality b/c at any moment me make make a fairly rude comment.  Other than that, he's a nice guy.

This guy is such a great teacher, really drills the information in your head.  While you're going through his class it seems like torture, but once you finished you realized it wasn't so bad.  If you do practice problems and attend office hours there is no reason you should get anything lower than a B.

I had my dropped papers signed and everything in teh beginning of the course, but I stuck with it, went to office hours religously, went to class, did **** (which helps immensely!) and wound up with a 93% in the class. The class sucks but if you're willing to put forth the effort it's definately doable.
Dr. J is the best chemistry professor that I have had so far at the University of Florida.
Portmess will leave your gpa in a mess..

His tests are VERY DIFFICULT.His lectures are straightforward and he is a very good teacher, but the tests will suprise you. My advice is to go to the lectures and study for the pop quizzes (he tells you half of the time when they are..) Although there is no officual curve, the pop quizzes are extra credit (they have brought my grade up 5% points)

these people are all slackers.  portmess is a great teacher and his exams arent bad if you just go to class.  he gives plenty of extra credit quizzes which serve as the curve.  people who are taking orgo spring 2005 should definitely take portmess over battiste-the-beast and davidson-will-make-you-her-slavidson.

His exams are so much harder than any other organic teacher.  Great lecture, but tough class!  If you really want to learn, I would go to his lecture ontop of a DIFFERENT organic teacher.  I studied for 75 hours and still failed my exam.

I had Portmess for two consecutive semesters, for the Orgo sequence. He gave me the first C's in my life. There was no curve whatsoever. He is a really nice person and lecture is not boring, but he doesn't care about students' grades, which is the one thing students do care about! Do not take his class, especially during summer A or B.

This already has to be the hardest class offered by the school, and Dr. J doesn't make it any easier. His lectures are decent, and he talks nice, but his tests <all of them> are an abomination to mankind. Read the following carefully: THEY'RE UNBELIEVABLY HARD WITH NO CURVE!!! It's looking to be my first W. Sorry guys, but do not take his class.

He is a good teacher and he knows his**** but he can not relate to the students...what teacher refuses to curve when the average is like 60 something on a test? There's a reason 40 percent of his students drop the class.

Dr. J is awesome. Of course its a really hard subject and you have to do insane amounts of studying, but he makes it as bearable as possible. he is sweet, funny and always willing to help you, no matter what it takes. I strongly suggest going to office hours. I'm getting an A right now because of it.

Tests are extremely hard (its orgo) & long.  You either know it or you don't.  Doesn't curve, a 70% is a C.  The average on the last test was a 58% and there is no curve.  I hear Dolbier is the best orgo prof to take...  AND dont take Brendan Tutoring Train downtown!  He is not organized and all he care is getting the 400$ out of your pocket

i switched to him sum b.it worked out, i got an A.quizzes were extra credit and hes really helpful.go to his OH, study ~1 hr a day and do all the assigned probelms and ull be ok.has random ?s on tests no one knows(what does allegra look like etc)but not too many.whoever put up the fake ratings saying port easy/enholm hard so ill drop enholm, THANKS

He is a very good teacher in that he's always available to help.  He isn't condescending and will answer all questions...however...his tests are ****es. The first test not so much, but the second one was just ugly, granted it is organic chemistry so no one expects a walk in the park.  BUT, he doesn't curve, and the OTHER teachers do.
Interesting lectures.  Tests are much harder than the practice tests, however.

His lectures are great and hes always there to help you. However, the practice tests are not nearly as hard as the real test and he throws in random questions. No matter how much you study you will still be caught off gaurd come test time.
He's my hero
No Comments

just took his first exam. sucked. he gave 50 minutes for a test that should have had a 2 hour time limit. it was really hard because you dont have enough time to think about what youre doing. half the girls in the classroom were crying. it took all i had as a man to hold back my own tears. i could have aced Wagener's test. :kills self:

Hes a nice guy who is very willing to help you outside of class.  Test aren't too bad if you study, only bad part is he doesn't believe in curves. If you take him just do the homework and go to his office hours and you'll be fine.

Very nice and helpful man. He does an excellent job of teaching the material, but his tests are hard and his grading policy hurts the slightly above average students. I had to drop the class because I was going to get a C when I deserved a B.

I had Scriven(easy), took 1/2 the class dropped the whole semester.Started over with Portmess(his 1st semester), he was awesome till test 2, 1/2 dropped. He had no curve. I got D+. Started again with****nstein(mean) but she is waaay easier. I have an A. Portmess is an awesome lecturer, cool guy. tests suck, very tricky, not straight forward.

Great teacher... really lays out his expectations from day one. Very willing to help you if u help yourself. go to his office hours like he begs you to you'll learn things you didnt even know U didnt know. Highly Recomended!

he is one of the nicest, most helpful profesors i ever had. his lectures were really clear and covered everything on the exam. he actually understands how stressed we are about organice and helps u through it. go to his office hrs, he might even put something u ask on the test...it happened to me a lot.
he is god

TAKE PORTMESS. ESPECIALLY FOR ORGO 2. ONE OF THE EASIER SCIENCE CLASSESE I HAVE TAKEN AT UF. TESTS ARE PRETTY EASY IF YOU GO TO HIS LECTURES AND STUDY MINIMALLY ON YOUR OWN.  AFTER TAKING DOLBIER FOR ORGO I, PORTMESS'S TESTS WERE A BREEZE!
Good lecturer, but the class moves very quickly. If you get behind you are screwed. Tests are fairly hard, mostly because little mistakes cost you big time, so you have to be perfect.
GREAT TEACHER!!!!  The course material is difficult, but he definately helps get you through it.
Good lecturer but gives very difficult tests.  He's definitely a "people person" though.  Go to his office hours -- he loves to help.

1st semester at UF. Apparently had something to prove to the other faculty and made tests very difficult (avgs 50-60%). Was ALWAYS willing to help in office hrs and lectures were good but not great. Do problems AND read the book (for tricky true/false). Got better towards the end. give him a chance.
No Comments

lenient late policy, pretty easy assignments but the minimum word count for some are way too high and i ended up just writing fluff for them. still got As on all of them but there was often slow grading and not great feedback on some. overall pretty easy and would take again.

Matt is a great professor who has a clear deep knowledge of film and the material he is presenting. The class is graded on a variety of mostly easy work, but the essays take some attention. He grades them fairly and provides good feedback, but do not expect an 100% on an essay unless it is earned.
He is very passionate about film, you just have to ask the right questions. I really enjoyed his class and hearing his perspectives. If you like film you'll love this class!

Professor Knudsen is really laid back! He's super sweet and taking his Technical Writing class was beneficial to my professional communication, but super manageable with a full schedule. Homework is once a week and he is really great with feedback, grading is mostly fair. Overall, he has clear guidelines to follow and it's a great 3 credit class!
Saw him on the island. Really can't get past that

Put a lot of work towards teaching the course material and then some. He was very accessible for feedback through discord and office hours. Unfortunately overambitious, the work was unorganized, overbearing, and stressful at times but he made it very doable to get a good grade by dropping the lowest test and assignment grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He should be allowed to teach

The class is a mess. Lectures dont teach you anything. The culture is off. Prof speaks like a child, fearmongers and has a I know it all and you should have known this attitude. Class consumes loads of your time. I second a previous comment that there is a cultish feel exhibited by some.

He cares, but he comes to class under-prepared. The exams and labs are broken to the point of it being detrimental to the class. His fearmongering is worse than Professor Schwartz, The lecture material does not prepare you for the exams, There are people who display culty behavior when talking about him. Pls avoid his class unless u knw wht u doin.
Impossible to understand cause he made everyone talk in child like voices. Weird.
Worst professor I've ever had and bizarre that he's in the Don files texting Ep about his thoughts on teaching and making an analogy to a certain performance.
Objectively not a god professor but legit makes me sick now thinking about some of the things he said or laughed about in class.
He's legitimately the worst professor I've ever had. He's also on the list and had been to the island.

Legitimately one of the best professors I think I will ever take throughout my entire time in higher education. There is no one who cares more for his students than Michael does. He will go out of his way to spend HOURS of his own time to help any struggling student. That being said, his exams are very tough, but they are also fair.

Exams are actually wild since he gives us unlimited time. Personally took an exam from 8:20pm to 7:45am the next day but very few people stayed that long because you're completely free to leave whenever you want. I just sucked at coding and needed to get an A on the exam. 10/10 class though
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The course felt unorganized (see other responses), but comprehensive. The course is fairly difficult with minimal prior programming experience, but it is very possible to get an A due to many extra credit opportunities. I believe the majority of the class got As. Definitely take this over COP3502 and COP3503 if you think you can handle it.

Professor Link seems well-meaning, giving extra credit, extending deadlines, bringing food, and being active on Discord, but the class is chaotic and stressful. Exams run past midnight, content is overloaded, grading is extremely slow, instructions constantly change, is constantly fear mongering about AI, and students are left constantly anxious.

He means well. Weird student fans that sees no problem with 6+ hour exams. Impossible to reach outside of class for anything important. Constant stress over AI and the honor court, even if you did nothing wrong. Canvas is so messy and retakes are so disorganized you can't keep track. Everything takes months to get graded, even if it's auto-graded.

Hands down the most generous and caring professor, buys us food for exams (which always go past midnight). However, the class and canvas are disorganized with many extraneous assignments and categories, MOST of which are optional but not marked as such. Exam dates and deadlines change frequently and you need to be active on discord to know anything

Pretty good guy, cares a lot about his students and put a lot of work into the class. He spread himself thin adjusting for the class, the retakes/extensions helped students but it also made the class more unstructured and slow. Hard to get him to post practice materials/readings/activities/class slides/projects/grades (anything) remotely on time.

idk why ppl complain about grading when they KNOW he dealt with health issues and fell behind on grading. he literally takes care of your grade so ppl just complain over nothing. what other professor constantly gives you retakes if you do bad on an exam and gives extensions like candy? it honestly pisses me off how ppl don't see this

oh this class is TOUGH, it combines prog 1/prog 2 + mini DSA in ONE semester. but his exams are 2h but he GIVES you UNLIMITED time. tons of extra credit (170 pts available, out of 100 pts), and 35% exams, which is EXTREMELY generous... if you struggle, he won't fail you; he'll set up 1 on 1 with you and PERSONALLY help you. TYSM professor link

With Link, you will be thrown into an incredibly hard class (20hrs/wk) with an immense workload by an interesting, well-meaning, involved, caring person. Curves are great, deadlines are extended many a time, and the conversations are fascinating. Warning though, the Canvas page is messy, and tickets/messages are frequently not seen or ignored :(

Class size was a bit too large this semester, but to no fault of the professor. As a result, class learning, grading, moved more slowly, communication was a bit harder, etc., but still not very difficult and greatly preferential to spending several semesters taking the other programming intro courses.

Extensions, retakes, and extra credit are common, but the exams are tough as nails. AI = Honor Court. Can reach him through Discord ticketing system, but after class works best. Congenial, friendly and tries to relate with Zoomer culture. Tries to create fun demonstrations like with inflatable bubble suits.

Very knowledgeable. A is doable.

The GOAT of UF. Puts a lot of care into his students ensuring every individual understood the content and would pass the class. Not only did he put care into his course, but he even hopped online on weekends to give hours long lectures to help students with other classes like discrete. He gets to know all of his students very well. Don't cheat tho.
he's a cool guy

Difficult class (covers Prog 1/2, and a third of DSA in one semester), but he puts in SO MUCH effort to help you. Exams are very hard, but offers retakes if you don't do well, and does daily exam review. There's also "unlimited extra credit". Class is so flexible to the point it's kind of disorganized but you'll finish the class knowing your shit!

His class was disorganized yes, but he was also incredibly kind, cared about every single student, and had us actually LEARN. He would stay up with students debugging code until 2 am, do optional review sessions all the time, and do everything he can to help you succeed. Yes its hard but if you put in the work he takes care of your grade.

Highly recommend to take any class with Professor Link if you can! He truly cares about his students, is super easy to talk with, and will adapt his teaching to help everyone succeed. I failed COT3100 with Dobbins, but retook it with Link and finally understood the material. Attend class and office hours—he'll support you if you put in the effort!

listen, the ppl writing bad reviews for grades being late r somewhat correct. yes its unacceptable that grades were late but it was also his first time teaching the course & he dealt with so many health issues. he went ABOVE AND BEYOND for his students regardless of that & i cant believe people dont see it. if ur reading this professor, thank u.

I took his class after failing Dobbins, he was SO MUCH BETTER. granted he did get behind on grading, but that was because he was dealing with some health issues throughout the semester. his lectures were very easy to follow and I felt his exam questions were fair. he is extremely kind and caring and helped students with their other classes.

Michael is my favorite teacher that I've had in my academic career. Loved his teaching style. I always knew what expect because the course always followed the same outline (guided notes from textbook, homework, quiz, exam, in that order). Can't wait to take him again. Wish he taught everything.Absolutely made it up to ppl for finishing grades late.

He was very flexible with his students and honestly wanted to see us all succeed. Is open to feed back and is always responding to messages and questions in discord. The class was disorganized but I honestly think it was a result of him being so flexible with his students.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy but is very unorganized. Literally for the whole class he was very behind in grading so you will never know your actual grade. The next semester has started and he is still putting in grades which is very unacceptable.
pretty unorganized in canvas and sometimes even in lecture and grading is months behind. fall semester is already going and final grades are still yet to be posted.

Sigh...I had such high hopes at the start of class but over time his teaching just went so downhill so fast. He would assign so many quizzes and homework sets but was very disorganized and it would take weeks for those to get graded and not to mention that for the exams so much content was not covered which made exams very hard to study for.

Good teacher, but didn't finish summer grades until the fall. Very lenient in grading and in general, but finishing grades 2 weeks after they are due shouldn't be acceptable for a professor just as it wouldn't be acceptable for a student. Often doesn't post assignments and notes on time or at all, lectures can be hard to follow without notes given.

Best professor I've had in college. Very approachable, encourages participation, and very understanding. His grading is perfect; makes sure you get the grade you deserve. He's also very easy to reach out in case you run into any issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Fantastic at what he does. Can't wait to see everything he will do at UF.

Although listed as an in-person class for the summer he allowed ppl to take it online. He goes above & beyond for his students & I can't praise him enough. He dropped at least 1 quiz & dropped more than 1 HW assignment too. He even volunteers to help ppl w other classes they're currently taking like Prog 2. He truly wants his students to succeed.

most caring person ive ever met. hes literally a superhero. shows up and goes above and beyond for his students. he deserves an insane raise. best professor in cs department without a doubt 100%. i wish the best for him in life. he makes discrete (arguably one of the more complex classes in cs) doable and even enjoyable. no one else can do that.

the semester hasn't even ended yet but i had to leave a review anyway. this man is the BEST professor i have ever had in cs in my entire life. he is so lenient, extremely understanding, and is so attentive. u can text him outside of class and he responds within a minute, hes more like ur friend than a teacher. he has a special place in heaven

Take him. He gives food for everyone for exams and there are many extra credit opportunities. You'll have a lot of fun. Everybody loves him. The class is very informative and helps to prepare you for future classes and the real world(technical interviews). He drops the final or lowest test grade. He drops the 2 lowest quizzes.

100% recommend Professor Link. He is very organized, a quick grader & quick to respond to requests, flexible, approachable, empathetic, & friendly. CIS 4715 with him has an extremely organized Canvas and is very easy, definitely worth taking if you're a PM or want one easy credit. Regardless, Link would clearly be a great teacher for any CS course.
Incredibly funny and engaging speaker, helped me fully understand content so much better, very caring and genuinely wants to help students. 😎😎😎😎😎😎😎😎

the best professor i've ever had. i learned so much in one hour and 30 minutes than i ever had in my college life. enthusiasm and connection with students is unparalleled. i am jealous of the future generations that get prof link as an instructor.
She is such an amazing professor, and fosters an amazing environment to practice Spanish. Loved this class, wish I could have her again!

The amount of Revista homework was pretty annoying since it did not help much with comprehension. The attendance policy is kinda whack but that was not her decision. I wish there had been better questions to talk about in class because it was so hard to talk for long periods of time about the really basic questions we were given. Easy overall.
So much homework in this class and it's due at 8am half the time so you think you have until 11:59 and end up missing it. She is really good in class, though.

Took her class in Valencia for Summer B study abroad and it was alright. She was very patronizing and I had no issues with her but many of my peers did. Not very accommodating and we did a lot of pointless activities. Did not grade exams harsh but we had a lot of homework.

Very sweet teacher! Had her for SPN2240 so I was excited to have her again. Class might sound scary but its not that bad. She does lecture Mondays, group work Wednesdays, and cancels class every Friday. There are 2 IPAs and a podcast like SPN2240. I wish she had more lectures or exercises because there are a lot of rules to learn, but overall easy.
Very nice professor who is understanding and compassionate. The learning environment she fosters is non-judgmental which is very conducive to improving language skills.

Prof. Lee is a gem, she is so nice and understanding and makes class comfortable and interesting. There is little work in the class, to the point I was actually a little disappointed because I'm trying to learn Spanish and I don't feel like I learned too much in this class. Nonetheless, class is interesting and an active space
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Sweetest teacher Ive had! Really caring and positive about the topics we discuss in class. As other classes she follows the curriculum set up by the department and does a good job enforcing the assignments and giving feedback. Course is easy, and Prof Lee is really good at communication

She is a great Spanish prof, very approachable and friendly. Tests for this class (IPA assessments) are based less on grammar and more on application, which is very nice. As long as you do the assignments on time and attend class you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great Spanish professor!

I absolutely loved Sra. Lee! I came in with AP credit so the class was a bit easy, but it's great for practicing speaking, as you do a lot of small group discussions. Señora cares a lot about her students, shown by learning all of our names within the first couple weeks. She is always in a good mood and has fair exams. 100% would take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Very easy class, professor is really nice. Obvious she gives quite a few sh*ts about her students. If I had her for all of my credits for my spanish minor I wouldn't mind one bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Very nice lady, definitely cares about her students. Attendance is something that she really stresses, so make sure that you show up! If you don't understand something, she'll make time to work with you on it. However, her lectures could be somewhat boring at times.
Super nice teacher. Make sure you go to class, exams aren't too bad. You will learn a lot. Easy going and always in a good mood. Would take her again.
She's nice, but I didn't learn a lot and I wanted to. The busywork gets annoying- don't miss deadlines. VERY EASY!!

Nicest professor at UF. Always in a good mood, always smiling, a breath of fresh air. Her class includes online homework, in-class small-group discussions, tests, quizzes, and 4 blogs. The class is easy if you put forth the effort so you'll have no problem getting a good grade. Take her! I hope to get in more of her classes in the future.
i had to work very hard to get my a in this class. she's difficult to understand, the tests are HARD. but, you can do it if you want the a.
Very nice professor.  Always in a good mood.  The class is really easy.

Very interesting as a person--she was born in Korea and lived in Argentina-- and very nice. Speaks easily enough to understand and helps if you don't. The class is taught entirely in Spanish but she will speak to you in English afterward. The class is similar to high school Spanish and there are a lot of little homework assignments. Good overall.

She is a great professor! Extremely friendly, helpful and always smiling. She grades compositions easily. Her quizzes and exams are easy. Not hard to get an A as long as you put forth a little bit of effort. I definitely recommend!

Very easy class. She is very nice and if you know Spanish, easy to understand. She's willing to help and her exams are extremely easy. Don't miss more than 3 classes, you'll lose participation points. Memorize everything in the book and make sure you translate the stories for the exams.
she isn't even Latin.  she fails miserably at trying to explain the conjugation of verbs.  definitely do not recommend her.

The exams are quite difficult, and the lectures don't always prepare you for what is tested on them. The final is also a different format from the 4 other exams in the class. The lab is easy, though, and will carry your grade as well as the extra credit opportunities provided.

Great class. Smokin'Notes is great for lecture exams. Lab attendance is graded. She offers lots of extra credit, take advantage! For lab exams, go to the help center to study the models. Filling out blank versions of the lab ppts also helps. Exams are very fair, there's just quite a few of them. Study a couple days in advance and you'll do well.
She is a great lecturer. Exams are tough and are very detailed but if you study the slides repeatedly, an A is doable. Lots of extra credit is offered which brought my grade up at least 3%.

She provides a lot of useful resources to study from, just make sure to do the extra credit bingos. Taking a lot of detailed notes during the lectures and then using smokin' notes practice exams are really helpful for the lecture exams.

I think Dr. Nguyen's lectures were very easy to follow and set you up very well to take the exams. One thing I recommend is watching the lectures early and doing any problems in the book that are assigned. I also think the SmokinNotes were awesome for this class and the practice exams given by SmokinNotes were very similar to the test.

Almost all content comes from lectures. Be ready to take notes & learn a lot. The class and information is fun and Dr. N doesn't get very technical. Her exams are mostly about broad concept and there's very little trick questions. Would recommend!

Dr.N cares abt her students but the class itself is so hard. Hybrid worked better so I could pause & take notes throughout the lectures. The exams were in person. DO ALL THE EC OFFERED YOULL NEED IT! Go to help center as early & frequent as possible. Got smokin notes & was lowkey not worth it in my opinion, quizlets are just as good. HW helps a lot

Dr. Nguyen gives you everything you need to succeed in the class. Everything that's tested comes directly from the lecture material. Take good notes and utilize Anki. Make sure to not fall behind on lectures, and you will do fine. There is a huge grade boost with the EC opportunities and HW's.

Her modules are super clear and organized, and she explains everything in a way that makes the material easier to understand on your own. The exams are fair and match the lectures if you pay attention carefully and take good notes during the videos. Extra credit opportunities and online homework helps to buffer exam grades.

Dr. N is an excellent professor! The class is fast-paced though and sometimes overwhelming. Read test questions closely and study the student learning objectives. APK2105C is honestly what you make of it; if you are interested in the material and take time to study, you'll do just fine.
She's a great teacher who explains concepts well and provides very fair exams. Some of the exam questions can be designed to trick students who don't study enough.

Overall this course was great but definitely takes effort. It takes lot of time outside of class to learn the material as it goes in depth. The exams were difficult but as long as you do a little bit everyday it will workout. Smokin Notes was very useful when it came to the lecture exams.

This professor doesn't care about her students and takes pride in watching them fail. She gives no support and punishes rather than teaches. She makes students feel inadequate with overly complex assignments (even the syllabus quiz) meant to confuse, not teach. Her teaching approach is condescending. Easily the worst academic experience I ever had.

If you're an APK major I recommend taking Dr. N for anatomy. Her online lectures, although long, explain every thing you need to know for exams. Lots of EC opportunities and fair exams if you study well. Take detailed notes and you will do fine. Super nice and helpful in office hours and responsive via email. One of my favorite professors at UF!

Dr. N is nice as a person but her exams were definitely harder than the other physio professor. If I could do it all again I would have taken the other professor, their exams were only on two chapters and ours were anywhere from 3-5 chapters. We had way too much content and it was taught all the way until 2 days before the exam.

SO MANY EXAMS; u feel like there is an exam practically every week; lab exams are almost weighed 2x lecture exams, so make sure u do better in those, which are pure memorization of slides; also do EC, as it is lowk very clutch; lecture exams are lowk hard, and lectures are boring and long online; final is not worth a lot; 90 is an A thankfully

There is a LOT of material for this class, but if you put in the effort, it is manageable to get an A. I thought Dr. N's exams were fair, and based on the learning objectives she gives. Studying for the lab exams was the most time-consuming part of the class. I loved the material we learned, and Dr. N responds quickly to emails.

7 exams for one class, all unnecessarily difficult (will ask u a question about a figure and then on a later question say that that figure is labeled incorrectly). lecture videos are so long. so much minor information on tests. rude professor. she's a good lecturer if you can sit through her videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Nguyen was simply amazing.  She was able to explain every test question in office hours in a relatable manner.  Anatomy help center is crucial to doing well in the class also.  Also, do the study guides because my test scores jumped twenty points after completing those.

Dr. Nguyen was a great professor! The lectures were online for me and taking detailed notes on them is super helpful, a lot of the tests were heavily based on them. The practice tests and textbook are great resources as well. She also gives extra credit which is useful. If you put in the effort to study for her class you will do well.

Really hard for me, but did well.  I've never had a class structured so well before: assignments were awesome.  Wanted more content-oriented feedback on papers.  Ch. 19 (performance factors) and 20 (training) should be in course: read outside of class. Respiration lectures (visiting professor) were challenging: gave up and studied clear textbook.

Dr. N is a great professor who makes a challenging course manageable. The lectures are engaging, and she offers plenty of extra credit opportunities. Studying the SLOs and using resources like Unstuck study can really help you succeed in this class.

Great prof, loves what she teaches, pay attention and go to lectures, study a lot and use PRACTICE TESTS. exams are difficult but definitely passable. easy work load, HW before exam date and some easy assignments. I mostly used her lectures and some youtube. just make sure youre comfortable with the content, record lectures and you'll do fine.

Dr. N is extremely knowledgeable and wants to see her students succeed. Extra credit is offered and it helps you study for exams. You have to stay on top of the lectures and do a LOT of studying for this class. If you know everything on her slides, you'll do fine on exams. Review videos and study guides posted before each exam. Little homework!

APK in general is a difficult subject, but Dr. N does exceptionally well at providing resources, materials, and lectures that make learning the content easier. She clearly cares about her students and is a great professor to work with. To pass the exams (which are difficult but fair) you have to study A LOT and take the time to learn the content.

I love Dr N. Easily the best professor I've had so far. Class is definitely lecture heavy, but if you go every day and take notes based on how she explains the slides, you'll be fine. Exams are difficult and detailed but fair. First professor I felt comfortable enough to go to office hours and she was super helpful. If you can take her you should.

Exams are pretty straight forward if you review the lecture slides, but they can get really specific. Go to lecture because of the pop-quizzes AND the info will stick better! She can be blunt at times, but that's just her personality. She genuinely wants students to do well, so don't get intimidated lol. Definitely pull up to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take her for Anatomy! I was in her online section and i've never had a course laid out so accessibly. It is not an easy class, sorry. But the resources provided just on the canvas page are plenty to get you thru it. Plus there is significant extra credit (which i did not do and very much regret). do 2 hours/week out of lecture and you'll be fine

you NEED to attend lecture if you want to do good in this class. If you know you skip often, don't take in person section you won't do good. If you attend lecture and pay attention this class is quite easy. Exams are not a major part of the grade, so you can still do plenty good even without the best exam scores. Very fun class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a very passive-aggressive teacher who doesn't understand or empathize with her students at all. it seems like she tries to trick you on every exam, and doesn't want what's best for her students. I would never take anatomy with her.

If you're planning to take her hybrid class, dont. Take an inperson class instead. The lecture videos are long and you won't really feel like watching them all, but she doesn't put everything you'll need to know ON the slides (a % of it is verbal).Her exams are almost set up like she's trying to trick you imo. Not horrible but there's better.

Dr. N's lectures are okay, and she is understanding regarding hurricanes, which is why she would push back the lab exam, however, her exams are tricky, and lab exams are the worst nightmare imo, she also doesn't have (-) grades so if you are below A, it is automatically B+ which is very annoying, if u have to take anatomy, don't take it w/ her

Exams(lecture and lab) are pure memorization of her slides. Not that much application-questions. Don't bother reading the textbook. Smokin notes practice quizzes/tests are FANTASTIC and recommend. Easy A if you study and keep on top of lectures. Do have to go to lectures since adds a ton of info there.

I loved P. Nguyen! She is incredibly passionate and organized, and she wants to help you comprehend the material and grow in her class. SLOs have what you need for the exam, and go to the anatomy help center!! I liked using Smokin Notes for extra exam practice too.

Dr. N is the best professor I have had at UF so far. Her class is very difficult and requires a lot of time and attention, but she prepares her students well. I did very average on the exams but I was still able to finish with a great grade because she offers so much extra credit. The curriculum is challenging but she gives numerous helpful tools.

The class itself was not too bad. Actually pretty interesting. However she can be incredibly cold and distant if she doesn't like your vibes. I can't really explain it, if you ask her a question about the content she'll just roll her eyes and give you a funny look. She did prepare us well for the exams Ill give her that, just bad vibes though.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Nguyen is an incredible professor and surely knows much about anatomy/physiology. Her lectures and powerpoints were very clear and although exams could be somewhat challenging, they were not impossible. She is a great lecturer and drills down on key concepts and points that you need to know for exams. Overall a wonderful experience.

I love Dr. N! Absolutely take her. Gives so many opportunities for extra credit and her SLO's exactly outline what's on the exams. Study based on the SLO's and you'll do fine on the exams. Her lectures are so interesting and she explains hard concepts in a very easy way to understand. Hard content, but she made it very manageable :)

LOVE Dr. N. I took her for both Anatomy and Physio. Gives so much extra credit and room for opportunities. Amazing lecturer and really tries to engage with the class. She gives SLOs that are exactly what you need to know. Tests are very much application based but it helps absorb the material better. Best professor ive had at UF so far.

Dr. N is a great professor. Her recorded lectures are great for the hybrid section, she explains things thoroughly and easily. This class alone is very hard, but if you put in the effort it's very possible to get an A. Mostly just graded on exams, but there's tons of extra credit opportunities. She seems to truly want her students to do well.

I took Dr. N for both APK2100 and 2105. She is an amazing professor who is easy to reach out to, has great lectures, and so many opportunities to succeed. Do the extra credit, go to the help center / office hours, and an A is absolutely feasible. Material can be difficult and exams are application-based, but I still recommend taking her class.

While it was hard to pull off an A in this class, Dr. N was super helpful along the way. She always had office hours to review exams, which was helpful, she gave lots of extra credit, and her lectures had depth. My only issue with the class was that the lectures were very time-consuming, and the tests were application-based.

Dr. Nguyen is a good lecturer who clearly cares about the subject matter, but her exams are incredibly difficult. They are heavily application based, so even with a good understanding of material, you will barely pass them. I would recommend taking another professor if you can.
Lecture material does not correlate to exam material.

Professor Nguyen is the best professor I've had at UF thus far. Yes, it is a difficult class- but if you put in the time, an A is extremely manageable. All of the exam material is given in lectures and each study guide given highlights exactly what is on the exam. Definitely take advantage of the extra credit through lab too.

Dr. N is a great professor! As long as you stay on top of all of the content, you will do fine in the class. The exams are more application base so make sure you thoroughly know the content. I recommend getting Smokin Notes as it supplements what you learn in class and helps you to further understand the content.

Dr. N is a good prof, but this isn't a walk in the park. Start your studying a week before each exam and space it out if you want to do well. Try hard on the homework and lab quizzes because those are a great buffer. DO THE SLOs for studying and I would recommend going to lecture + recording it to re-listen later. An A is hard but attainable!!

Dr. N's class is extremely difficult. Even if you study for weeks, it is hard to get a good grade on the exams since they are all application. I never had enough time to finish the in-class exams because it was 40 difficult questions in 50 minutes. If you miss something in lecture, you are basically screwed because she does not record them.

Very detailed in lectures and gives examples to help you understand the material. Her exams are tough but very straightforward- she tells you what she wants you to know. Homework is weighted a lot and there is 25 points of extra credit available to every student. Her exams are easier than Dr. A.

She's a really nice person and super helpful! She explains things really well and I would definitely recommend her for this class. Her course is very content heavy but if you stay on pace and study using the study guides with the student learning objectives she provides, you will do well. And do the extra credit!!
Dr. Nguyen is lecture heavy for exams. I would listen carefully to her lectures and use the learning objectives to study for the exams. Learning objectives are key for this course.

I highly recommend Dr. N for APK2100C. The course has 7 exams (4 lecture, 2 lab, final), and homework + EC to help your grade. Take good notes on the lectures and fill out the SLOs! For lab exams, go to the help center & use the models! The material is definitely difficult, but Dr. N. teaches it well. Getting an A is possible if you study VERY hard
Really not a difficult class, homework is weighted almost as heavy as exams. Extra credit offered for both lab and lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: easiest class taken as a premed senior. 7 exams incl lab ones. 25 points of EC available if done and easy online hw. literally just memorize the slides word for word and you will actually get a 90%+ on every lecture exam. lab exam is worth more points (second one is easier) but rly take adv of the help center. TAKE HER OVER ALGHREN FOR ANATOMY !

Dr. N was a great professor! Very clear, detailed lectures and lots of resources given (extra credit, SLOs, practice exams). The material is certainly a lot and very complex but getting a good grade is doable if you put in the study hours. Use the homework and labs (+ lab exams) to your advantage! Don't procrastinate on watching lectures/ studying!

This class is extremely hard and content heavy. plus, the lectures were administered from 3 different teachers (not just her). but, the class is doable and the homework/quizzes are easy! study for like 2 weeks for 25 hours because it is so much knowledge. get smokinnotes and study like crazy and then it will be an easy A. she offers exam reviews!

Dr. Nguyen is the best! This class is challenging and requires a lot of memorization, but if you study in advance and do spaced learning (I would start studying 5-7 days out), you'll be fine. I focus on the lecture slides and supplement them with Smokin Notes, and have gotten As on all the exams. I would definitely recommend!

While her exams can be difficult, Dr. Nguyen's lectures were straightforward and useful. If you answer the student learning objectives based on the lectures, you should be fine. The class is a lot of memorization, but if you rinse and repeat and keep up with the lectures you'll be fine.

Great professor who is knowledgable and explains concepts well. Success in this class results from studying early and using the STUDENT LEARNING OBJECTIVES. Trust me when I say this, I got a 75 on the first exam because I didn't know the SLO's existed. I got a 93+ on the other 3 exams when I started using them while doing everything else the same.

Dr.Nguyen as a whole is a nice professor and is passionate about the course, but her lectures and the exam don't line up well. It is an anatomy course, so it is a lot of information at once, however, her teaching of such info is super basic and dry, whereas the exams are very detailed and created to catch you messing up.
Lectures were recorded and were very detailed but easy to follow. Labs were taught by TAs. Gave lots of extra credit. Watch the lectures and you'll do fine.

The hardest class I have ever taken. I have never gotten below a B and I had to drop her course. I studied for hours on end and failed the exams. Her tests are not testing your knowledge. The questions are very, VERY tricky. She is rude and passive aggressive. The material itself isn't hard to grasp, just the way she tests you on it is insane.

I have a different professor for this course overall, but she supplies the online lab portions for learning both bones and muscles. Her muscle pdfs are USELESS for the actual exam. There are images with choices different from what the packet says for muscles. Sometimes, she gets terminology wrong or doesn't explain locations well.

Only has 40 questions on the exam. I study for hours on end and still have failed every one. I know that I know the material but she tricks you on the exams. The hardest class I have taken. I am the type of student that studies a lot and takes the time to learn the material and I still have failed. Never got below a B in a class before.
She is literally just so rude and passive-aggressive for no reason.

Dr. Nguyen really made me fall in love with Anatomy. Her class is lecture heavy, but she gives you everything you need to know to get an A on exams. Take good notes and take advantage of extra credit. Her grading system is forgiving and fair. She is an awesome, clear lecturer! One of my favs!

Dr.N is highly organized and her class course is set up very clearly. If you skip class you will not pass. Do not read the book (she mentions this from the beginning) and study every day or you will be overwhelmed with your notes. Utilize office hours as she is great at helping you understand confusing concepts. The key is not procrastinating.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Nguyen for hybrid class. Lectures were pre-recorded and labs were in person. Dr. Nguyen was always available to meet with you. You are able to review your exam after it has been graded. Honestly this class was one of the hardest I have taken, but ended with a 90.9%. You have to work for your A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love learning about anatomy and physiology but not from her classes. Exams SUCK. I feel like I study a good bit and I know the material but then she kills you with the "select all that apply" or "A and B, B and C, A and C, none of the above, or all the above" questions. It's ridiculous. Her exams aren't a test of knowledge, they're to trick you

Literally she does not care about her students. She literally is making us take an exam after thanksgiving break. Her lectures don't even add up to her exam questions. I love anatomy but she made me not like learning.

Average professor. Didn't really make the material exciting to learn. Speaks kind of fast in lectures. Exams are "applied" memorization of lecture material (no need to read textbook, but take REALLY good notes). Homework and pointless labs help with grades. Thought I would enjoy the class but it was kind of boring. Get ready to hear "okay?" a lot.

This course isn't too bad, and Dr. N is very nice and a good lecturer. Lectures are helpful for the exams, but not necessary (I just read the book and have done decently on the exams). Online labs were a pain sometimes, but after COVID this probably won't be an issue.

Dr. Nguyen is a good teacher for physiology. The tests are not obvious in their answers but if you study you should be able to get good grades. Her lectures are helpful and should be used as the main study tool for the exams, as all the material from the slides is fair game.

DR. N is a kind person, but a very difficult professor. She is not involved very much as a teacher because she uses the head professor's lectures for you to watch and then she will summarize them. You will not interact much. Use the lab exams and homework in your favor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Nguyen is great! Her exams are based off of her lectures, so if you do not watch them you will do poorly on the exams. It is a lot of material to learn but it is definitely doable if you keep up with it. Lots of other grades go in to help balance out the exam grades too.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She tends to have a condescending attitude when students ask questions which is frustrating but other than that she is a pretty good teacher. She's passionate about physio which makes her lectures interesting. WATCH LECTURE!! as someone who always relies on smokin notes her exams heavily stem from what she says in lecture! !!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easily my favorite science class at UF. Dr. Nguyen made physiology concepts easy to understand. She also sent out personal emails if you aced her exams, which I thought was nice and unique. I highly recommend taking her class if she's teaching!

Everything you need to know for the exams are in Nguyen's lectures, but her explanations in her lectures could be a little clearer. The homework is worth almost as much as the exams, which is a great buffer for your grade. Make sure you actually understand the material though because the exams are not just about memorization.

Most lectures were delivered online by another professor; Nguyen released summary videos that clearly covered the most important material for each chapter. To do well, she expects you to know everything in the lecture videos. Pay attention to clinical examples.

While Dr. N. is enthusiastic and generally a nice person, the exams in this class are very difficult. Her tests are extremely specific and mostly unfair trick questions. but her tests are ridiculously hard. Be prepared to thoroughly study for days and still barely pass the exams. Other than the exams, the class is 100% manageable and pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: These people are wrong... Her homework (which you can find the answers to VERY easily) are worth almost as much as the exams!! Very easy to make an A in this class if you watch and study her lectures. Don't bother with the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you don't watch her lectures, you will have no idea what is going on in the class. She is very engaging, knowledgeable, and willing to help. Exams are not rote memorization but application which is necessary for higher education (ie grad or med school). She has been recording her lectures for fall 2020 for study purposes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I highly recommend Dr. Nguyen if you want to master and be proficient in anatomy. Yes, the exams are challenging and full of application questions (hence the course name, APPLIED Anatomy). However, this forces you to study in-depth and really learn the topic. Lab exams, homework, and EC are grade buffers (in my opinion), so take advantage of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. N is an amazing anatomy professor. I took her APK 2100c course over Summer B, and I had a very enjoyable experience in the class. Dr. N was always super helpful in terms of answering questions and very accessible for questions. Overall, if you would like to learn anatomy and don't like reading textbooks for hours on end, I would recommend Dr. N

Dr. N is really great and she genuinely cares about her students. Her lectures are not mandatory, but they are very helpful. The lectures can get boring, and it you fall asleep smokin' notes helps a lot. The labs aren't that bad, and if you have a good TA, can actually be helpful. The homework and online labs are a great buffer for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. N is awesome! Don't be scared by other reviews. Her lectures are great and she answers questions really well. The tests are difficult but fair, as long as you take good notes during lectures and study them well you'll be fine. Record the lectures if you have trouble keeping up, she doesn't mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. N isn't always the best at explaining the material but she gets the point across. She cares a lot about her students and if you go to office hours or email her questions she'll answer any you have. If you show up to class and use Smokin' notes it's not hard to do well in. Her exams are very applied which benefits you in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nguyen is a passionate professor, but is not great at getting the material required to do well on exams across in lecture. Smokin' notes are almost 100% necessary for this course as not much study material is provided. The exams do not affect your grade as much as other classes are structured; if they were, her class average would be much lower.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Overall she's a great professor! Exams are tough and have many applied questions. As long as you pay attention to her lectures, take good notes, and use smokin notes it is doable. Homework grades and lab grades are easy A's and account for a lot of your grade, so if you do badly on an exam it will compensate. She is awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Nguyen is a very caring professor who wants her students to succeed. Her exams are notoriously difficult, but if you apply yourself and understand the material rather than just memorizing, the exams aren't bad at all! Also, the exams are only worth about a third of your grade, so doing poorly on a few won't wreck your GPA.

I had Nguyen for APK2100 online and APK2105 in person. I would not recommend taking the online option unless you really like online classes. I enjoy her in person class much more as I have been learning the material better and it is more personal. She is a very understanding teacher and is an incredible help in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took online and thought the class was more than do-able. Anatomy in general is a lot of material and can be difficult, however Dr. Nguyen's exams were very fair - a few questions were tough but majority were straight forward and simple, so if you studied the online lectures, you're fine. Lots of extra credit. overall, loved her!
She is very tough in her exams. Lectures don't cover many questions on her exam. She gave me a zero for a reasonable excuse. Does not care about a person's issue.
She seems like a nice person but the tests are nothing like the lectures, homework, book, or anything we are given to prepare. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. N teaches literally everything you would ever need to know for exams, but you need to GO TO CLASS!! She gives away test questions during lecture a lot so write down what she says. The way things are weighted allowed me to get an A in the class despite never scoring an A on an exam. Doable class just have to put in the time to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Nguyen does a perfectly fine job at teaching the course. She offered online review sessions before each exam and encouraged students to go to her office hours. Her exams are definitely more difficult and require you to know specific details, but, combined with a lot of outside assignments, the final grade is fair. I learned a lot from it!

Class is truly not that bad if you watch all of the lectures proactively, take notes, and review your notes 3-4 times. You don't need to spend money on Smokinnotes, it's all in the lectures Algren gives. Nguyen does not teach the class. Get all the extra credit you can from lab quizzes. 1st lab exam is tough, you need to go to the help center.

I took her "hybrid" class where I watch Alghren's lectures online, have lab in person, and take Nguyen's exams. If you stay up to date on the lectures (which don't take a long time) and use smokin notes, you will do fine in this class. It's not a walk in the park, but it's definitely doable. 10/10!

She wants her students to succeed. A lot of people struggle with her exams since they are application based, but it forces you to learn more than the base of the material. She is a wonderful person and will take time to review exam questions that you missed. (I overslept and missed an exam and she let me take it in her office hours for full credit)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: I went into this class thinking it would be really hard and unfair because of these reviews, but halfway into the semester I have to say that it's actually not bad at all. Don't let the reviews scare you. If you put in the work to really understand the lectures and know how to APPLY them, you'll do fine. It's a shame how bad these reviews are.

her tests do not align with the material presented in lecture because she does not take the time to create her own lectures. The class is disorganized, and she is easily flustered and offended by questions from students. If you want to actually learn in this course avoid this class.
Just no. Avoid at all costs.

Dr. Nguyen is a decent professor. The lectures for the online class are not taught by her, but the material is consistent with the exams and is taught well. You can do good in this class if you read and watch all of the lectures. Make sure you give yourself time to study and ask questions if needed. There is also 15 points of extra credit offered.

If you're naturally a genius, you'll probably do fine. If you're kinda smart, good luck. no amount of studying that i did helped. and i mean weeks. She's very nice; however, she can't find more than one way to explain. if you have to take her, print out every slide and take notes. Read text before and after class. combine notes. go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Nguyen is a very good professor. She doesn't do her own lectures for this class but doesn't test you on anything outside of the lectures. Her tests are hard, but she is very fair. You have to be fluent in the material. She lets you review your exams with her after and ask for as much clarification as you want. There is no curve on the exams.

Easily the worst professor I've ever had. The lectures aren't even her own lectures, there's somebody else teaching the class, so there's a complete disconnect between what is being taught and what is being tested. Her exam averages are always between 60-70, meaning that her students learn less than 3/4 of the material and she doesn't curve. Awful.

I took her for live classes and she often emphasized material that would be in the exam. Its called applied anatomy for a reason. ITS APPLIED. I think people leave a low rating because they dont do well in exams. If you UNDERSTAND the material and know how to apply it youll be fine. Just go to lectures, pay attention, and go to UGTA reviews.

I had this professor for two semesters only. We never watched her lectures and she did not feel the need to make exams relevant to the information on our virtual lectures. She is terrible at making exams because she cannot communicate her thoughts in person during office hours or on the exam. Aside from her lack of teaching skills she is rude.

Probably one of the worst professors I've ever had. When you go to office hours to ask questions about exams she treats you like you are an idiot for not knowing the answer. She uses a different professors lectures and then makes the exams so often times they're totally different. The exams are IMPOSSIBLE but you still can pass if u do well in lab

Dr. Nguyen's class, although very challenging, is doable. She is very attentive to students and always encourages students to come into office hours to ask questions. Her exams are challenging , but I am much more knowledgable in the long run than merely regurgitating the information. Study the lectures, use the textbook, and study every day.

her first three exams were styled completely different. the first one was doable, and they've gotten gradually harder to being impossible. she takes down lectures so students dont procrastinate but makes it harder to go back and study material for the exams if they like rewatching them. doesnt care about her students. would never recommend.

This class is so frustrating when you take it with her because she is not even technically the professor, she is a facilitator so she uses the other professors materials but make her own exams, the first one was super easy and gave me a false sense of security, the second one was surprise! way harder with no warning and totally changed.

uses lectures that aren't her own and then makes the exams extremely hard. She is very rude and does not help the students what so ever. I DO NOT recommend this professor!

Very helpful and kind, responds fast to emails/discord and always on the side of the student/helping the student. Exams and projects are open note.

Very easy class to pass if you put in an average effort.

Great introduction to programming in Python. Pretty light workload overall but some assignments were trickier than others, so I recommend getting them done earlier in the week. reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Coming in with 0 coding experience, up until the first exam this course was challenging. But after I finally started to get it and do better. Castro has feedback form mid course and makes changes based on feedback.

I felt like I was actually learning something that will matter. It was well paced, and lots of practice. I really like the last project, and I think I will use what I learnt in the future. Watch the demos, they are very important.

The class is really easy, and the assignments are fairly straight forward if you look at all the demo videos. Tons of extra credit offered in the class and everything was open notes, so it made it easy. Would definitely recommend to anyone. She made the class fun, probably the only fun class that I took this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's amazing! I took Python for CS majors before, and this class is way better. It's well-structured, with lots of practice, and the exams are super practical. You'll learn what you need — 100% recommend! Just make sure to pay close attention during the first few weeks and you'll be fine.
Good, understandable lectures. Projects can be tricky so get to work on them early so you have time to ask TAs questions. Exams were easy and relevant to course material.

Professor Castro is very understanding and for being the first time she taught this class was able to teach and still organize the class in a fair way. Exams are tough but she allows you to retake for a small boost to the original grade if you make videos explaining the process. Two projects which were fairly difficult but fun to see results.

As a person, Professor Cruz great. She seemed very knowledgeable of coding and programming. Unfortunately, I feel as though the labs, projects, and exams don't match the level of difficulty we are used to on the quizzes or the supplementary works (Codio) we are given. 
I wish we were given more to work with before given the difficult stuff before.

This class is heavy on projects and labs, be ready to devote lots of time. You'll also have to teach yourself some stuff but that's pretty normal for CS. Prof lectures are great for overview, but you'll definitely need to do your own codio lessons to learn the material. Codio is the online textbook ($50 ish) they have you buy, its very useful.

You really can't get much better than Prof. Cruz.  She is passionate about the material, explains it well, has PM/TAs that make themselves available at every hour of the day, and everyone is only a quick Discord message away from getting help.  The projects take time but other than that the class is pretty smooth sailing.  Just stay on top of it.

she is super nice even though i dont enjoy coding and will switch majors she is super talented and dedicated she is very kind. She is lenient and gives many extra credit opportunities attendance is optional and if you go its extra credit same thing with labs and some opportunities. exams are 20% but projects are like 40% so becareful with projects

Great professor. Class is very well organized and she is very willing to make adjustments as needed. The class discord and office hours system is amazing and super helpful. Gives funny, engaging, and informative lectures. Overall, amazing class.

She is nice and makes this difficult class a better experience by giving extra credit opportunities and offering help and changes that students say they want. When there was a miscommunication with DRC that delayed our exams, she ended up taking off way less points than normal for any questions we got wrong. She clearly cares about her students.

It's def a tough class and prop one of the most heavy classes I've taken, but it's def great tho. Lots of people don't do well cut they get humble due to how easy Programming 1 is. Start early, the TAs are amazing, and just have fun

Cruz is a passionate, caring, and overall amazing professor! Everything that was tested in exams, quizzes, and projects was covered completely in her lectures. She made it very easy to learn C++. There were extra materials via Codio's online textbook, but I didn't find this very helpful. Taking notes on the lectures was more than enough.

can relate:

she just reads off the slides which have lot of text & poorly organized code. She tries to teach, but can't convey the topic on a deep level. Professor Cruz is the best professor I have ever had. Instantly responds to feedback and is very active online  outside of the class. Respects all her students equally and is very funny. I really would take this class again if I had to.

Professor Cruz is one of the best professors I have had so far at UF. She is always available answering questions on the class Discord and constantly is changing the course in response to feedback. She is very fair with grading and will push back dates. Her lectures are also very engaging and entertaining. Plenty of extra credit too!

She is extremely passionate and wants to help you learn the subject. She knows what she is talking about and has a great system for TA/peer help (class discord with question boards, office hours, etc.). Just be sure to get work done on time and give yourself time to debug and you will do great (this is especially true for the final project).

She CARES so much and is extremely accessible for help. The class is time consuming bc of labs/projects but if you keep up with content and utilize OH/the discord you can and will succeed. Her lectures are a tad simple but they are good for basic knowledge. The discussion sections will help so much with labs/projects. Best professor at UF.
She is cool.

Professor Cruz is amazing. The type of person will reply to you at 11 p.m. when you are stuck. The class is hard, but it is worth it. You will be a different student before and after the class. You will learn a whole lot. It is worth it, but be prepared to work hard.

Professor Cruz  will answer anything to you as long as you start working early on. The labs are very well organized and the demonstrations are very helpful. Class is a waste of time bc she just reads off the slides which have lot of text & poorly organized code. She tries to teach, but can't convey the topic on a deep level. Professor Cruz has been phenomenal. Her energy is great! and the course is well organized.

Having a Professor like her is a rare and incredible experience that I highly recommend you take.

I loved her class! She cares a lot and it shows. Her tests were not the best, they were hard and there was A LOT for relatively little time. Projects were better. She gives you a lot of time, explains the necessary things, and is flexible with deadlines when a lot of students are struggling. Very understanding and caring, skilled teacher.
Dr. Cruz really goes above and beyond to make sure everyone learns the content. Her energy has been an enjoyment. It is a lot of work but I feel very motivated to continue taking programming classes.

Professor Cruz was an extremely caring professor. Prof Cruz Castro has been one of the greatest professors I've had at UF! She provides feedback and listens to students, gives good lectures and answers questions, and is always looking for a way to improve the course. Prog 2 is a project heave course so start early and you'll be fine!

Professor Cruz Castro is a really nice professor who is quite understanding. She understands your circumstance and is understanding if you ever needs extensions. great prof

Every week I would look forward to her class, as they weren't lectures at all, instead, thought-provoking discussions. There are only a handful of discussion posts and very few projects, light work only. If you need a Quest 1, please take Professor Clark's, you won't regret it.

Loved this professor and the way that she handled considerable topics that could be boring. There is a lot to read with her course, which is not entirely her fault, but she made it more palatable. She also stood up for me when there was another student who was not considerate of me. If you want to take Good Life, make sure she is your professor.

She was the sweetest professor. I hated class discussions in high school and would never participate in them but she made me comfortable enough to share what I had to say. Some weeks the workload is a lot but nothing you can't manage.
