i love professor clark! she's very funny and engaging in her lectures. however, this class is a TON of writing. there's weekly discussion board posts and multiple essays and writing assignments. she gives great feedback on all the assignments, and will review your work and give you notes on your rough drafts if you email her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: this teacher starting hitting on my bf and it was very rude. i do not appreciate that at all. her work load is so ridiculous i would not recommend taking this teacher at all. please stay away.
Shes really nice but you have to write (I don't like writing)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: For good life only the TA you get matters so I don't know how Clark actually is. The course itself is fine but slightly more work than I expected.

No one likes Good Life but Mrs. Clark makes it a little more manageable. Her class didn't have a TA and she is good at leading discussion. The readings suck but you have to do them or else she will be able to tell in your discussion posts. Do the 20 point extra credit to give yourself some room for error in the final paper.

Overall, there is nothing particular challenging in this class, just a lot of little assignments. The hardest part is probably the short essay midterm (which is hard to study for, I recommend smokin notes). The weekly discussions are easy, but very tedious in my opinion. There is a 20 point extra credit assignment, DO IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Never met her myself so class is very dependent on TA. Participation matters-weekly discussion with 20 students. one discussion post a week based on readings/videos that's easy (just do it and get the points). A couple of longer essays. There is an in person essay midterm that is easy as long as you know what the weekly readings are about. No final

Weekly discussion posts (take 1-2 hours). Weekly small discussion periods with 20 other students. Make sure to talk as participation is credit. Attendance is credit (10% of grade). Lots of writing, as midterm is multiple essays and last two projects are essays.

Just take this class, it's a good way to get this humanities credit out of the way, and Clark seems to be the best Good Life professor. There's weekly homework, but they are just discussion posts that you can B.S. and the final essay prompt is easy.

Lynne Clark is one of the best What is the Good Life professors. The homework was annoying but it wasn't hard and the prompt for our final essay was relatively easy. Her lectures can be a bit boring but they were easy to follow and you can tell she is passionate about the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class as a whole is not hard. Definitely a good amount of homework, but the exams are on the easier side. Great professor
This teacher makes me want to turn myself into a vegetable.
You need to study to do well on the exams. I did not watch the live lectures and did the  bare minimum to get a B. It's pretty easy if you're good at stats

She does do a good job at explaining most concepts in the lecture videos on Canvas, the production quality of the videos is laughably bad and could be much more concise. While using StudyEdge for the exams, it became clear how much better the class could be taught.

Prof. Mocko was a fine professor who gave pretty easy assignments and exams. If you keep up with the lecture content and do the quizzes, you don't have to study that hard for the exams. The group projects were an absolute pain but she grades them easy. She was lenient with me when I forgot to submit an assignment at the beginning of the semester.

Mocko is a great professor, clear and detailed, good for students who struggle with math/stats. Inverted schedule, all notes are online vids 1-2hrs worth, and optional in-person lecture is just example problems. I do not like the online format, couldn't stay on top of notes enough to go to optional lectures but prepares well for exams.

I struggled a lot in statistics in college but somehow in business stats with Mocko I did really well. Mocko explains everything super clearly and her study guides are what is exactly on the tests. I never went to class or listened to lectures since her wkly module videos were all I needed to succeed in her class. Nonetheless, you do have to study!

Professor Mocko explains things well enough, and provides a pathway to pass a difficult class if you put the time in. In my opinion this class would be much easier if it was a full term and not an accelerated version in the grad program modules. There's way too much information. Be prepared to put 15+ hours a week in for this class alone.
Exam 1 is the worst. Study her 100 question document. Used teachmezach for extra help.

One of the most caring professors I've ever had, and one of the best teachers. She breaks down material well and puts effort into teaching her students. I honestly just didn't care much about the material, so I checked out halfway through. First exam was the hardest one. Exams count for 3/4 of grade. Only one chance for extra credit (5 points max)

Seems like a nice lady but is very clear she does not have sufficient knowledge in this subject. Confusing lectures and difficult to understand the content. This shouldn't be a hard class but she makes it one. A form of torture would be to make me take this class again.

What are we even learning. I'm only a couple weeks in this course and none of what she has said makes much sense AT ALL! I've been confused since Day 1 because she doesn't explain content clearly whatsoever. Not a good teacher. Statistics doesn't have to be a hard class, however, this is like getting put through the wringer.

Professor Mocko was confusing in lectures. She does answer very quickly when you have any questions or concerns. However, your grade is majorly based on 3 exams (75% of your grade) which are difficult if you do not do ALL of the note shells, the reviews, and practice questions.

The class itself is set up in a way that it is very test heavy, around 70% of your final grade. She posts lecture videos for each module with a notes shell. Overall decently covers everything on the each exam and gives a pretty rounded 100 question review. Only complaint would be the test weightings.
War criminal

Overall class is amazing, and teacher is good besides her lecture videos are sometimes messed up. Exams are most concepts which messed me up due to me focusing on the math portion of this math class the most.

- LOTS of homework
- ec opportunities
- exams = whole grade
- annoying voice in lecture videos, but does a good job explaining
- she gives a 5 day grace period on most assignments
- 1st exam is harder than the other 2
- provides note outlines/videos = no textbook/readings :)
- honestly not a bad class but it is a bit of work
- 3 attempts on hw
It's not a particularly difficult class; it just requires some time to study and comprehend the material. Also a lot of lecture content does not show up on exams.
It's difficult to follow because she teaches by example rather than with steps. Also, her video quality is severely lacking, especially the audio in the later modules.
The grading scale is a bit odd (90% = B-) and the audio quality of her lectures is not that good, but she does a great job explaining the content.
Class difficulty was average but the lectures are unbearable, mostly due to the audio.

This class mostly busy work. This review will not influence you to not take this course with Prof Mocko since it is required for business majors, but be warned. BUSY WORK! So much work. The course includes an international activity that will make you pull your hair out. Instructions are vague and difficult to find. Includes groupwork. Good Luck!

Took her both at the undergrad and grad level and didn't enjoy either. She teaches through examples, not by steps, so its hard to follow. She also treated the grad class like first grade by using all these random "show me how you know it" activities that were essentially busy work. Would not take again.

To pass this class it is extremely necessary to be able to recognize the type of question asked and apply the concepts. You can know your way around JMP backwards, but if you don't understand what concept to use with the question its a waste! Try your hardest to do your best on Exam 1 & 2 (Exam 2 is easiest, 3 is hardest). 
Study edge did not help.

Professor Mocko's lectures render Study Edge unnecessary for this class (although practice material is good if you're struggling). Her lectures and hws are more than sufficient to get an A. Be sure to do her 100 problem practice questions before each exam (and master them). The last exam is the hardest so be sure to do well on Exam 1 & 2

Really not too hard of a class but just takes time studying and understanding the concepts. Do not need to watch the live lectures but need to watch module videos. Study edge can be helpful for exam review but not a necessity.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Mocko is BY FAR the best professor I've had in my life. No matter the difficulty of the subject, the class feels like a 4th grade class where she baby feeds you the material! She is very soft spoken and a kind soul. Prof Mocko truly does go the extra mile in ensuring that everyone is digesting the material as they should. 11/10 recommended!!
She was super clear in her lectures and never once was I confused on a topic. She made it a super easy class.

Her lectures were more engaging than average. I studied the smokin notes for 2 days before the exam and did well on it. Also, studied all the lecture slides which covered all the content that would be on the exam. The test wasn't anymore difficult than average and she gave out extra credit.
Honestly such boring lectures test was easy tho
She is not very helpful and doesn't explain things well. Her lectures are long and boring. Her exam was not too difficult but I would not want to take a class with her ever again.

Her overall teaching was okay. Everything you needed to know on the exam were on the slides, but she would go through them rather quickly and tended to oversimplify. The exam was very fair but no practice tests were given out. There was a curve, but it was almost as minuscule as the amount of time she gave us to answer her iClickers

I didn't listen to any of the lectures and read the smoking notes a week before the exam during spring break and got an A on it. Her lectures weren't helpful to me, and you don't need to read the textbook. If getting the smoking notes is a problem, re reading the slides a bunch of times should suffice. Exam wasn't tricky and covered broad concept

The animal unit has a lot of content covered in a short period of time. Exam was easy, but definitely need to know literally EVERYTHING in the slides to do well. Not clear on what exactly we needed to study, and overall professor seemed to not really care. Lectures not very helpful yet mandatory, and slides are really only study material provided.

This professor covered the animals unit for exam 2. Although I really enjoyed the content, the exam was nothing like the practice she'd given and did not reflect the minimal amount of material she gave us to study with. This professor seems to be more occupied with her amphibian research to put time and effort into helping her students succeed.

She's not as bad as everyone says. She did go over a lot of content, so it was hard to know what to focus on for the exam. Don't expect to just go to the lectures and be prepared for the exam. You will have to put outside time to learn the material. However overall, she was not a bad professor.

I think she teaches way too much content to turn around and only test you on 35 questions. She goes through her iClickers fast, so be prepared because those do affect your grade. Overall, just not a very nice person who doesn't seem to care about her students.

This professor is definitely enthusiastic about the content she teaches, but she can not explain things in simpler terms. I liked the slides because I could go back, and know that everything I need is on there. She really tried to make things fun, but due to lack of participation, failed. I also hated how she barely gave us time for iclickers.

Generally, the worst quality professor I have taken thus far at this school. I highly doubt she understands the material she is attempting to teach us. Doesn't prepare you for the exam at all--uses the "your college students" excuse. Extremely dense powerpoints that has lack of elaboration (somehow) on some slides. Clearly there for the paycheck.

Lectures are okay, not particularly interesting and not the MOST informative; Test wasn't terrible if you really studied (Would HIGHLY rec smokin' notes for this course); Kind but tended to rush certain end of lecture; Ridiculous asks for readings

To be successful on the exam, you need to memorize everything in her slides, which are almost 80 slides per lecture. She said there would be a curve on the exam, but she gave us a curve of a 0/0 so take that as you will. Worst section of BSC2011 imo, and she goes way too fast over slides to actually take good notes.
All I learned from her lectures were that she loves frogs. She was a boring lecturer and did not prepare me well for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her slides have a lot of information, which is nice if you miss a lecture, but not when studying for the exam, since her questions are very specific about the material on her lecture slides. A lot of the exam questions purposely tried to trick you. She didn't give us a curve. She spoke very fast, and her lectures were full of too much information.

She was your average college professor, she was there to read the slides but ultimately left us on our own to learn and study everything. Smoking notes not necessary for this exam but you need to memorize all of her slides to do well on her exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is probably the worst of the 3 bio professors (Dutton and Douglas being the others). She has a lot of content packed into her lectures and had some trick questions on the exam. Additionally, she gave no study resources or curve on her test.

Lectures are either too fast paced or too long, course deviates from syllabus so attend class. iClicker closely follows lectures and not very tricky. Her exam (animals) felt surface level compared to the depth of content in class, but it definitely covered all of the topics. If you have HS bio/physiology experience, class is way easier
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures were rough, she tried to pack a lot of information into each session with not nearly enough time. Her iClicker questions were the hardest, and while the test wasn't too bad, there were questions that were actively trying to trick you. Some questions on the exam were material she had quickly gone over the day prior.

Her lectures were hard to follow through and the slides were poorly organized. She's a tough grader, does not have a curve and overall was the worst professor of the three professors for this course. Beware of taking her exam, you really want to do well.

Dr. Longo was a fun professor who is clearly very passionate about amphibians and I really liked her unit on Animals. The lectures are very dense and I used smokin notes to help study for the exam and that worked out pretty good for me. But as long as you show up to class and take/review notes, you should know everything you need to.

Her lectures are DENSE, and her delivery doesn't make it better. However, she'd usually tell us what graphs/tables we'd need to know for the exam and what we didn't need to memorize. The exam was almost entirely based on the PowerPoint slides, so there weren't any real surprises. The avg score was a 75, so we didn't get a curve. Not the worst.
She is your average professor when it comes to lecturing. Many of the questions on the exams were worded poorly and she tries to trick you. I would not recommend.
Did not give a curve when the exam was insanely specific and class did not do well. She lacks compassion for her students and was not interested in how they did.

There was no curve and everyone did horribly. Smokin notes was very helpful but not enough to do well on the exam. Worked so hard over spring break because this exam was the tuesday right after and did not do well. Wasted my time, money, and energy for no reason.

If you want a decent exam grade use Smoking Notes, the amount of info each lecture went through was far too much and the exam itself asked tricky questions just to mess with you. Also unlike other semesters where there was a plentiful curve, there was no curve even after the professor herself said not to ask her because there will be one. AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Longo taught us more information than required. It was beyond what was in the textbook. When it came to the exam, she used the things she emphasized against us to trick us with very subtle differences in the wording which is hard to discern when she emphasized a topic specifically. Do not take it with her.

Dr. Longo is very efficient with lecture time—she starts right on time and jumps straight into the content. However, she covers a lot of material in each lecture, making it hard to know what to focus on for exams. She doesn't clearly specify what to study, so I found resources like Smokin' Notes much more helpful in narrowing things down.

I actually loved Dr. Longo for the animal section. Her lectures are informative and fun;If you attended class and studied the slides, that's literally all you need for her exam. It was very fair and had biology jokes at the end to ease nerves. She is not nearly as difficult as her RMP makes her out to be, just put in the work, and you will be fine.
Dr. Longo has a clear passion for animal physiology and made the lectures very detailed. The exam questions were pretty specific so using smokin notes to study was the most useful thing.

Study her lecture slides. Memorize every word on those slides. The entire exam is just her slides. She's very organized and to the point. Easy extra credit, although its only 2 points. Manageable if you memorize everything on her slides. Did I mention her powerpoint slides?

I had her for the second segment of BSC 2011. Her lectures made me feel like I was listening to a med school physiology lecture - way too much information for an introductory biology class!!! Studying for this exam was a pain, but doable if you're willing to memorize nearly everything on the slides.

Bio 2 is divided into 3 segments with an exam for each. No final. Professor Longo taught the 2nd segment. She was my 2nd favorite. She was a really good instructor but she put a lot of extra info on the slides, so it was difficult to know what to study.

Dr. Longo was a fairly good lecturer, but could definitely slow down to enhance understanding. Her test was specific and challenging. I got a high C with smokin' notes. iClicker questions were unnecessarily hard, but I still got all those points. Overall not bad, but could be better. You'll be fine if you pay attention and participate.

Awful lecturer, would go through around 60 slides a lecture and spoke so fast it was extremely difficult to take notes. Her exam wasn't awful but definitely had questions that were oddly specific. Gave us a bonus question on the exam she promised would be super easy so many people got it wrong that she had to give the points to everyone.

She's not that bad for bsc2011, it was her first time teaching and the average was not bad (plus there was a curve). She was a little fast at the beginning but ultimately slowed down when asked. Her Iclicker questions were the hardest but the test was all from the powerpoint so just study that and you'll be fine.

Professor Longo is not a bad lecturer but she doesn't know how to make it easier for students. She covered so many unnecessary content for the animal unit that's not useful for the exam. She also talks way too fast in the lecture, making it impossible to follow and actually learn anything in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was fine for the animal unit. Her lectures are very fast paced that I stopped going to class and just took notes off the powerpoints she posted and participated in the learning catalytics. Exam was moderately difficult, but had a generous curve and easy extra credit question. Overall, if you put in the work, an A is very attainable.

She really wasn't that bad. Sure, her lectures were information heavy but that's just how it is at UF. I felt that she respected her students and cared about our learning. Honestly, people were complaining more than was warranted as the exam was quite easy and the median score was 80, plus a generous curve and 2 points of extra credit.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: dr longo was very passionate and had a lot of care for her students. she is great at responding to emails and discussion comments. her lectures were very informative, albeit a little fast paced. the animals unit is itself fast paced so cant blame her too much. if i had one critique it would be i wish she explained concepts a little more in depth
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She often misspeaks without correcting, giving varying info to people. She IS easy to contact. She doesnt answer questions well, saying read the book / ignoring the difficult part of the question. She didnt set reasonable expectations for her unit, never once finishing lecture / giving four times the amount of learning objectives as the plants
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Longo can't teach. The only contribution she made was reading off slides. Posted an exam review a day before the exam. When students asked questions on the review day about a topic she just said to go back to the slides that were already confusing enough. Too much information, and not enough explanation. Was vague about the exam content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: fast paced, goes through a lot of information in a single lecture and has learning catalytic questions in between so it is very important to pay attention the whole time,

Dr. Longo definitely constructed her section of the course in a way that I was not used to. There wasn't a linear flow to things, and the content was pretty much scattered from random topics that shared a loose connection to the general topic at hand. I had to memorize the most minute of details from her lectures, as that was what was tested.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Longo does such an amazing job at making this class very engaging and interesting. She is clearly very passionate about the subject and I genuinely learned so much from this class. Class grade is made up of occasional assignments, quizzes, and a final project, all of which were very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Out of the three BSC2010, I actually liked Dr. Longo the best. She taught us like adults and was thorough with lectures. For the test, you MUST know the lectures in and out. The questions were straight from her lectures. If you go to her office hours, she can sometimes be confusing when explaining things. I recommend forming a study group.

Really nice lady who knows her stuff, but she has a bit of a hard time explaining it in a way for others to understand. Lectures aren't as long as they were for unit 1, but still take some time. Rewatched all of her lectures and studied for her exam, and despite feeling good about it, I ended up bombing. Questions were much harder than expected.

In all of BSC2010, Dr Longo was the hardest professor. She graded harshly with little feedback and never offered extra credit unless required by administration. Her exam was poorly worded and there was no curve. She is very clearly a researcher who teaches solely for funding.

Dr. Longo is not a bad professor in terms of lecturing but I do think her exam was poorly written. We were not provided with any study materials other than a summary video which was just a repeat of the lecture slides. This is unfair considering the other two professors provided these materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Longo doesnt get the credit she deserves. Yes, some of her questions were specific, but it was all in her slides and as long as you fully understand the material, look/listen to the lecture slides, read the book you will be ok. I got my best grade in this exam. Smokin notes helped drill the info, asking her questions helped clarify anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Longo is not compassionate for her students who recently were forced to endure a 15 week semester with no break during a global pandemic. Her exam was not reflective of the material emphasized during the lectures and the average was below a 65% with no curve.

Don't be scared off by the negative reviews following the 2021 spring exam 3. Dr. Longo had detailed lectures, lots of reading (as did the other three profs) and a difficult test but overall not too bad if you studied the learning objectives. Ppl retaliated bc they got a bad grade, doesn't reflect the prof. If u can't handle bio1, hope ur not STEM.

Very disappointed in this professor. Unfair treatment and lack of empathy. I would not recommend having a class with her for anyone. How are you not going to give a curve to the last exam when the average was a D?!

Final exam was worded terribly. The questions were very wordy and hard to read. We were also given about 50 minutes for 30 questions, which is typically a good amount of time, however 30 questions with about 100 words each can be a bit daunting to look at on a final. Teacher did not curve the exam, even though she said she would about 30 min before

People are being very harsh to her as a direct result of the Spring 2021 exam. I thought her lectures were really interesting and her teaching style was easy to follow. That being said, the exam was poorly worded and when the TAs predicted a 10 point curve, we got nothing. She does not care about students' success, but hey, welcome to college.
Avoid Dr. Longo at all costs. She clearly does NOT have her students' best interest at heart and does not care about teaching material.

Her lectures are terribly boring, and the exam is unreasonably specific to minor points mentioned in passing. She is very unhelpful and so are her slides. She provided no study material other than a brief video (which just said to rewatch the lectures), so there was no way to prepare for her question types other than outside resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: horrible teacher, she said she would curve exam 3 and then she didnt. The average was a 64 (that says something about her teaching). She gave no review material/study guide for the exam and her exam questions were extremely specific and some of the things we didnt even go over in lecture.

I really enjoyed her lectures; they were concise and interesting. Her exam wasn't standardized though. The honest truth is that even most who got As on the first two exams did much worse on this one. The few exceptions to the rule don't change that fact. Entitlement is not the root of people's concerns. That aside, getting an A overall is possible.

Terrible. Didnt curve the exam even though the syllabus said she would because she was pissed about all the bad reviews on ratemyprofessor. She shouldnt be teaching at UF. Im convinced she wrote the positive reviews herself. Would give 0/5 stars if I could.

I personally thought evolution was the most interesting topic in bio, however Longo's exam didn't correlate with her lectures or what I studied in the book. I got an A on the first two exams, and failed Longo's exam despite studying for a week. Very upsetting since I enjoyed this topic the most and one badly written test ruined my grade.

She is not considerate of her students. She does not teach in her lectures, and even if you read the textbook and do the learning objectives it is hard. She pulls the exam questions out of her butt. The exam average was a 66 and she is not going to curve it. Not a good professor. Dont take her if youre going to take bio!

As far as day to day work goes this class isn't difficult. Compared to the other lectures in this class, hers were pretty good. However, her exam was extremely vague, and had ambiguous questions with multiple technically correct answers. I studied a lot, but the class average was a 60, and she refused to curve even tho its in the syllabus
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures were okay but were not representative of her exam as evidenced by the average which was a D. She also did not provide any practice questions or study guide, and her exam was full of vague questions and grammatical errors. She is unwilling to compromise and provide any kind of curve, despite her exam average being the lowest of the three.

Ok besties I take back what I said before. I still think her lectures were the easiest, but she refused to curve exam 3 even though the average was terrible thanks to its poor wording and ridiculous specificity. Still not the worst since the class was easy overall, but the exam was ridiculous and she's unwilling to compromise with her students.

I think many reviews here are unfair to Dr. Longo as people posted them after being upset about the exam. I found the exam to be very fair and lecture-based. I watched lectures on 2x speed the day before, studied 5 days in advance, and did very well. Dr. Longo is available in office hours which I recommend if confused, and is overall a good person.

She is not giving us a curve even though her exam was the lowest average out of the three (66.1). Her reasoning was that it was because people got perfect scores, but in one of her sections the highest was a 93 and she is not going to give them a curve either so her logic does not add up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Despite exam 3 having the lowest average, Dr. Longo did not provide a curve. The exam had oddly specific questions many of which were worded poorly. In one of the class sections, the highest grade was a 93 and she said that "we got perfect scores" so there would be no curve. Avoid her at all costs.

Despite exam 3 having the lowest average, Dr. Longo did not provide a curve. The exam had oddly specific questions many of which were worded poorly. In one of the class sections, the highest grade was a 93 and she said that "we got perfect scores" so there would be no curve. Avoid at all costs.
easiest material but provides no study guide or practice, then refuses to curve the exam
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Longo seems like she has her students best interests at heart, however her final exam didn't really show that. The topics she told us to study were barely covered, and instead she quizzed you on random facts of knowledge, like who Darwin's favorite scientist was. Her lectures were informational but they were not set up for the exam.

I honestly enjoyed learning from Longo. Her lectures were to the point and I liked the small jokes and memes she included. However; her exam was oddly specific and the wording was confusing; it did not reflect what we had learned that well. If you study you should be fine, but if you don't pay attention to detail you won't do well with her.

I personally thought Dr. Longo was a pretty good teacher who was passionate about the material. I just rewatched her lectures, reviewed the notes I took on lecture slides, & memorized the few things she told us to know for the exam. The exam was very specific, but everything you need to know is in her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She seemed passionate about what she was teaching, but her exam was extremely confusing and worded oddly: a lot of the possible answers sounded more opinionated than factual, which confused me greatly. I studied hard for her test and didn't do as well as I hoped. A lot of the questions were "most correct" instead of only one being correct

The exam was very specific to her lectures and poorly worded, and she didn't provide a study guide. Still, all I did to study was rewatch her lectures at 1.5 speed near the exam and I got an A, and that's w/o a curve. Her lectures were by far the easiest and fastest to watch. She's not great, but also not as bad as people are saying.

Professor Longo was a fair professor and gave us everything we needed to pass the class. We literally had 8 lectures for the last exam and I didnt watch 3 and still did well on that exam and got an A in the class. I also enjoyed the animal crossing references she put in the test lol, but yea a pretty normal bio class dont know why ppl are trippin

I got high A's on the other two exams, but for this exam I did awful. I studied about 2x as much for this exam as the other two exams and was 100% confident with the material, but the test was NOT representative of the material. Even the people who studied for weeks didn't do too well. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

While the evolution material in itself is not difficult, this professor makes her exams impossible to study for, and impossible to understand the questions. She wants her students to study from the learning objectives, and makes her final exam a history test about Darwin's life. No matter how much you study, be prepared to not get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Longo is a teacher who only puts in the minimal efforts. Asking her questions and help clearing up concepts is difficult, and she does not seem to enjoy supporting her students. The concepts are not terrible, but her level of commitment is lacking in helping her students understanding. Just make sure that you truly understand before taking exam

Dr. Longo's exam was by far the hardest out of all 3 professors. Do well on the first 2 exams and you will be fine. I got a C on her exam and very high A's on the prior 2 so I did end with an A, but her exam was very tough. The material was not hard, but the way the exam was written made the content harder than it actually was. Good luck!

Her lectures were extremely important and should be reviewed. I didn't review as much as I should've, so I got a B on the test, however, I got an A overall. The test had some oddly specific application questions but it wasn't as bad as people say. It isn't super easy, but she was passionate. Take the low score with a grain of salt. It's college.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: People may give her a bad review because they did not do well on the final exam but the reality is she is a good teacher. Everything she covered in lecture was on the exam. I did study a good amount for the final and did well. I know many students did not and have reflected that on their reviews of her. Realistically, she is a pretty good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: People on here failed her exam and are giving her awful ratings that she doesn't deserve. Honestly I liked her lectures and her exam was not hard. She doesn't help you prepare though. The learning objectives are literally everything that's on the exam. Study those and you're fine.
Studied very hard for the final biology rxam and the test was not reflective of the material learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There are many other reviews on this page that are not fair to Dr. Longo. Students flooded Rate My Professor after failing the exam, which is more a way for them to express their anger than honestly evaluating the professor. Dr. Longo taught evolution very well, there werent too many assignments or lectures, and it is totally feasible to get an A.

There are a lot of reviews here that may be over exaggerated. Dr. Longo strengths include 1) easy to follow lectures 2) organized materials that coincides with the reading 3) not very difficult homework. On the other hand, her weaknesses lie in her ability to 1) answer questions and clarify points of confusion 2) evenly test lecture material.

I watched every lecture, took notes, went to basically every one of her office hours, even had smokin notes. Her exam was unrepresentative of what she taught, and she provides little resources to her students

The evolution material was relatively straightforward. I dedicated time each week to reading the textbook, going over my notes, reviewing her lectures, and working to understand the material. Yet, it didn't matter because Dr. Longo's exam was IMPOSSIBLE and did not reflect much of what we learned. The questions were ridiculous and unfair.

Dr. Longo is not a terrible professor. Her lectures cover everything you need to know, but her exam is not representative of her lectures. Her exam focused heavily on the first few lectures, and had almost no content regarding the last 2-3 lectures. I recommend reading the textbook, especially the pages she discusses in the textbook.

Her test did not compare to the lectures she gave. I studied way harder for this test than the other two in hopes to get an A in this one but no. It didnt lower my grade too much only b/c of how I did on the other tests. When asked for practice tests, study guides etc, she said knowing the learning objectives were enough. Clearly not.

Her lectures are about as worthless as she is, but she'll make sure that you go into the exam thinking you know something, and then flip the script. Your grade is basically only based on the exams and half her tests have nothing to do with her lectures. stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Test not representative of the material, good luck studying for the exam!!!

This lady makes the weirdest evolution exam for bsc2010. I studied hard, did well on the other exams from the other two professors, and got a 60 on her exam. I think the class average was around there. Why not just make a fair exam? Especially when we're all learning online in a pandemic. The questions she writes are ridiculous.

Here lectures were not bad (and her accent isnt bad or her fault either), she even included some memes, but her exams were nothing like her lectures. They were poorly written and very confusing. She is not teaching because she wants to, she is teaching because it funds her research... In other words, shes a researcher, not a professor.
Test is absolutely nothing like any lectures or homework. Avoid longo at all costs if you can

I didn't find Dr. Longo's lectures to be too bad. I actually liked how visually engaging they were. However, her exam was really not that reflective of the content that was taught. The wording was confusing at times and the averages were in the mid 60s across all sections. **Tip: Use the first two exams as your buffer!!!

Dr. Longos exam was a nightmare. I studied and felt confident. The exam had weirdly worded questions with deep application expected. There was also a significant amount of history questions. Just weird. Do not recommend Dr. Longo if you have a choice.

Loved the unit, leading to the exam I was confident on my knowledge of evolution... then I took the exam. The exam was not an assessment of knowledge but more of your ability to understand the question and look past the abundance of grammatical errors. Would never take her again and I am so glad to be done with Bio.

Honestly, I enjoyed her lectures the most out of all of the professors from Spring 2021, but she provided so little preparation/guidance for the exam. The questions were incredibly random compared to the major aspects of evolution and was not a good representation of what we were taught (class average around a 65), even with help from Smokin' Notes

There is a great disparity between Longos lecture and exam. She does not truly teach us how to apply the concepts as she expected us to on the exam. Some of the greatest mysteries of life include the existence of god, the meaning of life, and, of course, how one could prepare for Longos exam. The last mystery is the hardest to solve. Good luck...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was an OK lecturer, but her exam absolutely did not reflect what she taught. Even though the material was easy, the questions were confusing and did not fairly test our knowledge. If you are taking BSC2010, be very wary of her! Make sure you do well on the other profs' exams, as Longo's tests are very unfair. You have been warned!

The other two professors were by far better than Professor Longo. She failed to prepare us for the last exam and omitted most of the information that you would learn by reading the book, which means that most of the questions I would have not known even if I studied harder. The exam was confusing and poorly written. WOULD NOT RECOMMEND HER.

One of the worst professors that I have ever encountered. Study for three weeks? That doesn't matter on the exam. You will spend most of your time rereading the questions trying to decipher what it is saying than actually answering the questions. She clearly demonstrated a lack of care for her students and was extremely lazy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: never again

Other reviews are too harsh on her accent, which was not the issue. The issue was the questions that she elected to put on the exam, which represented a history course more than a biology course. Questions were worded poorly and overall super confusing. If the whole class does poorly, it is more reflective on the professor than the students.

She sucks. Her lectures contain little information. Her sentences are grammatically incorrect which information hard to learn when you can't figure out what she is trying to say as this is unfamiliar information to students. She goes over stuff in lecture that are not even relevant to exams. Be prepared to be asked obscure & arbitrary information.

Other reviews are too harsh, her accent is fine. She understands the subjects and is easy to contact about questions, but her exam/adherence to the textbook do not make sense. The questions on the exam did not cover many of the modules/skills we learned through the textbook. The questions were almost entirely lecture-fact based.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: BSC 2010 is separated into three sections, all taught by different professors. After just finishing our last section (evolution) with Longo, I believe she should not be teaching evolutin. She does not even come close to the other two professors, and we were tested on things that were never spoken about. She has a heavy accent, and bad grammar.

Dr. Longo was easily the worst Bio prof of the three. Her exam was poorly written, and the questions were oddly specific and not really relevant to biology as a subject. Her lectures were pretty useless, and I stopped watching them pretty early on. Unfortunately, you can't avoid her if you need bio so just plan on doing well on the first 2 exams.

I really do not understand how the test was so hard compared to the content she lectured on. By far the worst out of the 3 profs I had for this course. Her exam was significantly harder than the rest.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst of the three. I studied for 3 weeks and got 100% on all smokin notes quizzes consistently and got a C on the exam. The exam did not represent what was taught and was horribly written. Avoid at all costs.

The information she covers about evolution is so easy and simple, yet she somehow found a way to make the test hard. The wording was bad, the grammar was bad, and the questions were overall vague. She gives you no study guide or practice test, and she's good at lecturing, but the depth of her material isn't laid out like the tests you on.

I really enjoyed disease ecology & evolution w/ Dr. Longo! She makes the course engaging and interactive. The content is interesting and she doesn't assign too much work but you do participate a lot in class with group activities but it's low stress and you end up learning a lot. No exams when I took it, just quizzes, HWs, and a final project.

Although she was a caring professor, her exam did not reflect the information in her lectures or activities. After listening to all of her lectures, finishing her posted activities, and the LC from the class, the exam was 10x harder. For such an easy unit, she created a monstrous exam. The exam curve was so high that people passed, but still unfair

Dr. Longo was my favorite lecturer of the 3 units. She explains everything clearly and concisely with many examples. However, her exam was poorly written with questions different from anything we'd seen in the class before. The exam ended up being curved so everything turned out alright. Her lectures and SmokinNotes were the best study sources.

Very nice and caring teacher during the pandemic. Evolution test for bio1 was awful - had a 15% curve since people did so bad and it was unrepresentative of the content she taught. She meant well but didn't prepare us well. Great at responding to emails and a genuinely nice person.

Professor Longo is super sweet, but her exam for the evolution portion of bio 1 was surprisingly specific. Though her lectures were short, she specifically referenced lots of material from the lectures in her exam that she did not emphasize, so it is important that you know EVERYTHING that she talks about. Do not underestimate this exam!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Longo is clearly a good person, but her lectures does not match the exam at all. She teaches the Evolution portion of Biology 1 and while her notes and powerpoints was very general, the exam was so specific. There's no study guide and clearly doing the notes and getting smokin notes didn't help either.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. Don't need to go to class because online lectures are posted which are both shorter and better prepared. Homework and quizzes are fair and the exams are very similar (VERY) to past exams. Easy class compared to Calc 2.

this class is very easy. the material is simple, and her exams are written very easily. I did not have to study for any of the exams in the class, and the final is noncumulative as well. I just don't think she's a very great lecturer; she explains concepts poorly, especially compared to the other math professors I've had.
She is a wonderful professor and explains the concepts very well. Nothing in this course is super difficult, so if you pay attention/watch the recorded lectures and do the homework its pretty easy.

Firsrt off, she is a great and funny person. However, it terms of your grade, it might be better to watch her lectures online. In-person, she goes through the lectures pretty quickly which can make them hard to follow.
She has great online lectures. A lot of opportunity for extra credit and exams are very similar to the practice exams.

Dr. Shabazz is a really good math professor, with clear lectures and plenty of resources to study for exams and be completely prepared. The class itself had plenty of extra credit provided, if anything a little too much. The examples in lecture can be a little quick, but they are all still explained quite well.

Explains everything in the lecture so well and always takes time to answer questions. She will hint at what types of problems are on the exam during lecture. The lecture before exams, she works out an entire past exam that isn't posted in the canvas, and then lets everyone take pictures of another past exam that isn't posted.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Shabazz is a decent professor. I preferred watching the lecture videos rather than going to class, so that option is available if you can manage to stay on top of things. And make sure to do the extra credit!

Dr. Shabazz is a good lecturer. She takes questions from students as she works through questions which is very helpful. Sometimes lectures are fast paced, but the notes are very helpful to look over if you get confused doing hw. While this class is test heavy, she has posted many materials online that are very beneficial to help prepare for exams.
Dr. Shabazz is a very good lecturer and the class is very manageable as long as you put in the work. The grade scale is also very lenient and she provides extra credit too.

My calculus professor was Jesse Kim, but I found that I learned much better with Shabazz's lecture videos. She gives extra credit opportunities other than the 3% added to your grade. There are also ~3 practice exams provided for each exam, which help tremendously.

I had Jesse Kim as my professor but I went to Shabazz's lectures instead because I like her better. She goes at the right pace during lectures and cares about her students. She explains the lessons really well. Also if you can't get her she also has online videos you can watch online which are also helpful.

Class is very organized, and her lectures make the content accessible & easy to understand. The online resources (past tests, lectures, practice problems) make preparing for the exams and quizzes painless. As long as you stay on top of lecture due dates, this class has very lax grading. Exams have gotten easier compared to the older ones in Canvas.

Dr. Shabazz is by far the best calc 3 professor in the UF math department. Although I can understand some negative reviews saying she sometimes skips basic steps, making it hard to follow along, that is the nature of the course and you will not find a better lecturer. We always finished on time; she gives 3% extra credit and partial credit on FRQs.

I honestly skipped Dr. Keeran's lectures and just watched Shabazz's online lectures. She is the course coordinator, so she gives useful information about the exams. The modules really ramp up in difficulty as you go but there's a lot of extra credit.
No matter what lecturer you're assigned for calc 3, Shabazz's online lectures are always available and very helpful — I did well in this class by just watching those.

Taking calc 3 w Shabazz is the play.  She is extremely intelligent and a good lecturer, and will always explain extra if you have any questions.  Abundance of practice available if you need it, and the extra credit is a great padding to your grade for the semester.

Missy Shabazz is the professor that knows too much. Explains lecture material decently but often skips steps or uses shortcuts that she does not mention, making lectures very hard to follow. 3% Extra credit is nice but homework are significantly harder than lectures, tests are okay, practice exams do not prepare you well. module 4 is really hard.
I think she may be the best professor to take calc 3 with here. She writes the tests and gives hints about what to study as they "may" be on the test ;)

Harder than calc 2. Took online which was a mistake. Honestly the course material wasn't hard, but learning math online is. Take the quizes seriously and that will help bc then grade is only tests. Tests aren'y like practice exams. All exams are curved nicely also. Only gripe was that it was hard to learn online and weren't many outside resources

I have someone else for lectures, but just started to watch prof Shabazz lectures online, which were much easier to understand. She is pretty clear for the most part, and going to office hours of my TA also helped clear up any confusion. Would recommend for this class.

This is who you want for calc 3. she's the course coordinator so she writes the tests and literally tells you what half the test will look like during lectures. Extra credit for practice exams and discussion posts helps boost your grade. Module 4 is by far the hardest, but if you do your extra credit every unit you wont have to worry abt it.
Module 4 is lowkey rough. Professor is very caring. sometimes her lecture might feel rushed but if you attend them everything at the end makes sense and the exams are very easy too
Didn't have Shabazz but her lecture videos were a lot better than my professor's in person lectures.

try to take her for calc 3 because the tests literally mirror the lecture examples and arent bad. the canvas is super organized and i recommend just watching her lectures online bc sometimes she goes fast in-person. there is a discussion board for every module where u can ask for homework help and contributing counts towards ec. i highly recommend.

This professor clearly understands the material but cannot teach it effectively. Their explanations are too advanced, skipping basic steps that beginners need. The lectures are hard to follow and it's easy to get lost quickly, making it more realistic to learn externally.

The professor seems knowledgeable about the subject, but their explanations are often unclear and overly complicated. Generally are better off waiting for the online lectures to skim through what's actually necessary for the homework assignments.

Shabazz is great, She is very accessible and the online lectures are like a cheat code for the class. First 2 tests are easy, try to get really high grades. The 3rd and 4th are hard, with the 4th almost guaranteed to bring down your grade

Stay caught up, watch the online lectures and an A is certainly feasible.
Just spewing math with no explanation of the concept.

This class was very doable over summer C 2025. Every module had the same structure, making it easy to follow along and know what you were expected to do. this class is much easier than calc 2 but still harder than calc 1 in my opinion so you will have to study a lot. my recommendation, do lots of practice problems, even a little per day still works

This class and the lectures were fine. The homework could be a lot because there's homework every lecture. But the quizzes and exams were evenly spaced out and not too difficult. There's extra credit for responding to a discussion board with homework help and doing practice exams.

Amazing professor! She explained concepts clearly, and you were able to ask questions. Lectures were quite helpful. Extra credit was given. Assignments weren't too bad. Content does get difficult as it goes on, so studying is needed. However, for difficult content, she was a great lecturer. Recorded lectures.

I found calc 3 to be harder than calc 2, but not really her fault since content is more difficult. Lectures are fast and often lack much needed explanation. Practice exams (pretty old ones) and review sheet given, but they lack worked out solutions. Compared to in-person grading, FRQs have no partial credit. Exam point curve and extra credit given.
Lectures aren't great but exams are very similar to the exam practices provided. Use the online free textbook and actually do Xronos to pass the class.

Shabazz was a fairly good professor. Each lecture she just filled out the lecture notes (it helps to have a copy of them yourself). Sometimes the lectures would feel like she was spitting out information and not leaving you time to process things. The last module in particular felt like this but overall it is manageable to end with over a 100.

I found Calc 3 to be way harder than Calc 2, but I do not believe it was because of her. Her online lectures are way better than in person, but her lectures are her just solving problems without explaining what is going on. For the most part I did well in the class, but being underprepared and bombing an exam or two is hard to recover from.
Took this class under York's section, but after the first exam, switched to watching her wonderful videos. Got an A because of it. Be warned, the last exam is the most difficult.

Her lectures were fine, but sometimes it felt like she was rushing through them to get done as fast as possible at the cost of thoroughly explaining what was going on. Make sure to prepare well for the tests as doing bad on any one of them will make it hard to get an A.
Dr. Shabazz cares a lot about her students. Her lectures are alright, but the grading scheme is very forgiving. Definetely make sure you study for your exams / quizzes properly, and you'll do fine

Shabazz moves quick through lectures, so it's often hard to keep up or fully grasp the concepts during class. I highly recommend using Study Edge for this class, it really helped me understand the material more clearly, especially since the class involves a lot of 3D visualization and spatial reasoning.

She was a pretty alright professor. She gives hints as to what is on the FRQs in the lecture before each exam. She could definitely go a bit more into depth on how the problems work conceptually rather than going straight into solving them. I found this class easier than calc 2, but now by much. Be prepared to study.

Lectures are fine and mostly focused on solving example problems. It would have been nice for her to mention old techniques she is using again in new scenarios rather than glossing over them. I found it a bit difficult to remember old material in later units. The actual math is not very difficult once you can conceptualize the problems in 3d.

Dr. Shabazz, or should I say Dr. Shabadass, was a great professor! I learned a lot in this class and while her video lectures had mistakes, and some other lectures like those of Ian Manly might be better to watch, I still ended with a super high grade due to the plentiful extra credit she provided both on tests and with small extra assignments!

I will admit, Shabazz tries to be a good professor, but she knows the material too well that she can't teach it. Lectures are just her doing math without explanation of what she's doing. You just have to pickup trends. No worked out solutions for any homework or practice exams. Makes it difficult to study. Quizzes & exam are tough so study hard.

HW/Lecture Quiz difficulty is very close to test difficulty. If you want to do well in this class, just trust me and do the NYTI(In the back of each guided lecture note) and do every practice exam at least 1 time and honestly more than that for every single exam. Unit 1 is the hardest by far if you've never taken a higher level algebra class.

I don't reccommend her lectures. She doesn't really explain what she is doing and goes really quickly. Watching the recorded lecture or online videos is definitely better than attending in person lecture since you can slow her down and pause. Overall, it takes a lot of time and energy to understand Calc 3 when it wasn't explained clearly.

MAC2313 was one of the most time-consuming math courses I have taken thus far at UF.  Homework is very tedious and lectures are not substantial at all, only providing the basics of each concept. Extra credit does help, but only adds 3% to your grade. I am grateful that I ended the class with an A-. Study Edge helps for this class.

Shabazz is in my opinion the best Calc 3 professor at UF. Her lectures will leave you confused for unit 4 since unit 4 is very hard to understand off the rip, but on units 1-3 she is the best. This class is very conceptual, and students who can understand what is actually going on behind the scenes rather than just the calculations will succeed.
I'm sorry but she did not teach well at all, none of her lectures helped. She was funny but that was about it. I'd say the best thing about the class was her extra credit.

Calc 3 is a bit tricky to understand. However, if you understand how to do the problems and do all the practice exams you can get an A in the class. The exams are easy in the sense that if you understand how to do the concepts that were in the practice exams youll do just fine on the actual exam. study and youll be aokay!
Easy exams and easy to get a good grade. Her online videos are great and you don't even need to attend lecture if you watch them online. I'd recommend her to anyone taking calc 3
She did not round me after missing the cutoff by .01 points, felt like walking onto a freeway populated by nothing other than semi trucks
Shabazz does a good job with lectures. Overall, class was not too hard if you put the time in and actually study. Do practice exams she gives and you should be good for the test.

Not a difficult class, but her lectures make zero sense sometimes. She jumps from one thought to another without clearly explaining what she did or why she did it.  Its tough to keep up a lot of times because I get lost, but with study edge, I have been doing well.

Lecture can sometimes move fast, but she posts videos on Canvas of a recorded lecture with the same material. If you keep pace and do your work on time, you should be fairly well prepared for the exams.

Dr. Shabazz is a pretty good lecturer and the class has a good amount of extra credit. The exams are difficult, but fair. I would suggest doing well on the first 2 exams because the 2nd half of the course is significantly harder than the first. The recorded lectures and practice exams are super helpful for understanding material.

Prof is knowledgeable,  gives a lot of extra credit work. At the end 3% added to actual grade for extracredit. Extracredit doesn't make any difference.  If a student gets 80% ,extra credit adds up 3% to give 83%.Still the student grade is B.Extra credit is not helpful as mentioned in all post.

She wasn't terrible but definitely a professor that might not work for everyone. Her classes can feel a bit fast at times but watching lectures back really help. Although doing the homework gets tedious at times, they are really helpful especially since some questions could be word for word on exams. Your TA also plays a big role in this class.

Overall a pretty average professor. Sometimes spends too much time on easy concepts early in the lecture and is forced to rush on more complex topics. Many of my friends who had other professors for this class had an easier time with it.

Shabazz is definitely not a perfect professor but her lectures were pretty good and the exams are very fair. The class is very conceptual and sometimes Shabazz does not explain all the concepts well but it is usually fine. Definitely go to office hours or put in more effort to understand the challenging concepts.

I took this course online over the summer and felt that her lectures were generally very helpful! The homework was good practice and the Canvas page was one of the most well-set up I've seen. There were also lots of opportunities for extra credit.
She provided practice exams and some previous year exams before each exam, which made it a lot easier to know what to expect for the exams.

Calc 3 isn't the easiest class, but her lectures while not the best, do help, the extra credit given really helped in the class, she is funny and lets class out early a lot. Overall, I think she is the best of the calc 3 teachers with a lot of resources for studying.

Very difficult class, but lots of extra credit. The practice exams are the best study material for the exams. Shabazz's lectures are as entertaining as a math lecture can be although sometimes she moves too fast.

Just an ordinary calculus 3 course, nothing too special about this professor. A lot of extra credit. Usually one 40 min online lecture every other day and 40 min homework when there's no lecture. Calculus 3 is supposed to be a time consuming course. 4 tests in total and not cumulative which is really nice. Definitely harder than calc 1 and 2.
I didn't even have Shabazz for Calc 3 and her lectures actually made me understand what was going on. If you have Calc 3, make her your priority.
The online lectures are very helpful. She gives a good amount of extra credit and the exams and quizzes are fair and will not try to trick you with weird questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Grading is light with tons of opportunity for extra credit, dropping lowest quiz/homework scores, etc. Both the recorded lectures and discussion boards are incredibly helpful, and the Xronos homework is more difficult than exam material. If you put in the work, Calc 3 is an amazing course.

Dr. Shabazz's lectures are very helpful and she is great with communicating in Canvas and getting us our grades quickly. Homework is designed to help you succeed and it feels like she genuinely cares for your learning. Calc 3 is nothing to be scared of at UF especially with all of the grade cushions like bonus questions and quiz drops.

While I didn't particularly enjoy the class, I enjoyed her lectures. I had a different professor, but went to all of Shabbaz's lectures because she explains better and frequently she'll tell you what problems will appear on the exam. I definitely recommend her over any other calc 3 professor.

Shabazz is a great teacher, but she does sometimes make mistakes and skip/rush over steps which is something to be wary of. Her Office Hours are very useful for getting assistance and also to get useful materials like practice exams. If you go to lectures, she often points out certain questions that will be on exam.

Very nice and forgiving. Average at teaching in lectures. Makes mistakes often, and doesn't explain her thought process going through problems most of the time. Do the Xronos for practice because they're the most accurate to exam questions. Online lectures are helpful, but don't rely only on them.
She gives a good bit of extra credit and you don't need to go to the lectures. The exams are not bad if you study.

A lot of people like her, but personally I'm not a fan. She gives lectures as if they are reviews and skips over a lot of steps. However, she posts every lecture online well in advance so don't even bother going to class. Also, GET STUDYEDGE, it makes this class extremely easy.

Lectures consists of her droning on and on while skipping certain steps. Thankfully she posts all recorded lectures on Canvas so you don't need to go to class. Use the class discussion board for help. GET STUDYEDGE! Alex from Studyedge is the best, she's the reason why I have an A.

Super well setup course, lectures are not mandatory and have online video versions as well. Many of my classmates watched both the in person and recorded lectures, but only necessary if you're uncomfortable with the material. Only mandatory attendance is the weekly quizzes in breakout. Tons of resources available, and fair grading.

Good lecturer and explained concepts pretty well. As easy as a calc 3 class gets. Class is fast-paced, with lecture quizzes, homework due after each lecture, and a weekly break-out section quiz. Just use the resources offered (TA, office hours, practice exams), and its easily passable.

Calc 3 with Shabazz is not a crazy difference from Calc 1 or 2 with any professor. She's a good professor that will get you all the info you need for the exams but does it really really fast. She usually ends class 20 minutes early because she speeds through the notes so fast. Good professor with a good personality, success will be up to you.
She is the gold standard for mathematics professors at UF. I'm sure you'll get tired of the coursework at times, but get over yourself, because in the end you'll realize how good she did her job.

Dr. Shabazz was not the worst professor, but she was definitely better than the other MAC2313 professors. The class itself is not difficult, but it is important to attend or watch the lectures as the content is obnoxious. The discussion period depends on the TA, and some are better than others, nonetheless, the quizzes are straight forward.

Great professor with great knowledge of the subject, and will answer questions in lecture if you ask. Homework assignments and a short quiz come after every lecture, but not super hard. The class is a bit fast, but the lectures are recorded. Her office hours were helpful, but have specific questions. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT, it really helped!!

I came with prior knowledge so I can't comment on difficulty, but comparatively, Shabazz's lectures are weak. They're dull with only a few examples, and I feel like it's hard to grasp the concepts from her. You're better off watching Professor Leonard on YT and doing the HW. On the bright side, HW and LQ grades were easy, and there was easy EC.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 34 ~40m lectures, with a lecture quiz and homework for each. 4 exams worth 15% each that always have questions that aren't on past exams, and 8 quizzes worth 15% total, all proctored with Honorlock. Sometimes there will be strange due dates, and if you have questions, they are mainly answered in a large discussion post by other students.

Teaching style is very fast paced because of the amount of course content but she explains it well regardless. Lectures are very helpful and full of example problems. Definitely does her best to prepare you for the exams between the lectures and the pre-recorded videos. Would definitely recommend for calc 3.
shabazz is not even my professor and i use her lectures because they are so helpful. i think she is clear and she is willing to help. her exams are usually very fair also.

Professor Shabazz has a style of teaching that a lot of people don't like, myself included. The class itself is what you expect from a UF math class with 4 total tests (the final is not cumulative!). The TAs (at least the one I had) are very nice and will give you all the points they can for the work you do on the FRQs. Watch Ian Manly's lectures.

Lectures are clear and go over the course content well. There are lectures on canvas made for the online version which are shorter and more concise. Very easy to ask for help and personable in office hours. Has office hours before exams where I got extra copies of old exams that werent on canvas, and she explained what would be on the exam FRQs.

My favorite class I've taken at UF and I don't even like math like that. Genuinely made Calc 3 easy to learn and the way the course is set up in canvas is perfect. I didn't even go to class I just watched all the online lectures on my own time. Also hella extra credit. Goated professor.

As with math classes at UF, don't fall behind and get ready for tough exams. Shabazz did have plenty of extra credit that can give you a good boost at the end of the semester, and the online course is well organized and incentivizes helping other students out through the discussion boards which also count as extra credit. Overall, more chill than 2

Shabazz was a good professor and she was easy to understand. The course content is very difficult. A lot of studying it required to do well and I believe that I didn't pass this class because I underestimated how much time I should have studied before the exams. I recommend using Study Edge for some extra outside help in understanding this class.

Shabazz just teaches off the notes, so you can watch the videos and get the same information. I think the material is slightly harder than calc 2 but the tests were extremely simple if you put any effort into reviewing past exams. HW after every lecture isnt difficult but is tedious
She is very nice and gives extra credits. Office hour helped me a lot! It is pretty manageable if you put effort in!

I loved Dr. Shabazz. She was a great professor and my grade in this class is solely due to my negligence in the class. I really enjoyed calculus I just wish that I put more effort into this class as the A is very much doable. Lots of assignments but honestly worthwhile as they do help you to understand the material.

I loved Dr. Shabazz and calc 3, she made the class super fun. I felt like one of the main benefits from attending her lectures was that she would tell us what the FRQs would be on the exam. Doing all of the materials provided ensures a good grade on the exams.

The online course isn't ideal. The lectures while informative are slow & not really engaging. The homework assignments were simple & tedious but some of them contained problems that weren't addressed on the lectures with the exams. To pass you should also engage with the extra point discussions & if needed use StudyEdge.
Stephen Adams is the G.O.A.T.

Dr. Shabazz is a very kind person, and is very understanding and willing to help you understand things. Class is relatively straightforward, do the practice exams and you should be fine on the regular exams. Dr. Shabazz does make a lot of mistakes while lecturing, which can cause confusion, so you may have to go to office hours or figure things out

Funny and energetic lecturer. SO many extra credit opportunities. Attendance mandatory which is super annoying but she was an easy to follow lecturer. Calc 3 in general is hard and there is a lot of homework involved. But Shabazz as a teacher, would recommend.

Dr. Shabazz is clearly the best Calc 3 professor in the department (other classes use her lecture videos). Her office hours are extremely helpful and she offers many chances for extra credit. You can tell she wants her students to succeed.

You can tell Dr. Shabazz cares about us students.  She takes questions in class and gives hints on what's going to be on the exam. She's the best Calculus 3 professor.  You should definitely try to get her. She's fun too.
I do not suggest taking this class online. Calc 3 is already a harder class and when you're online you have less materials and practice in comparison to the in-person classes.
Out of the other calc 3 profs, shabazz is the most loud and clear during lectures. She takes notes digitally while the others use pen and paper.

Shabazz is by far the best professor for Calc 3. I took the class with Chui but I learned everything through the online lectures that Shabazz makes. The videos are very high quality and if you make sure to understand them you will do great on the tests. She also offers a significant amount of extra credit assignments so make sure to do all of them!

I don't understand the negative comments. Dr. Shabazz was great. Her lectures are good and engaging. You always knew what to expect on exams.  She also gave plenty of extra credit.  She is the best Calculus 3 professor.

Lectures were too basic compared to questions on quizzes (TAs make them) and exams and Xronos HW was a pain. Online is a lot harder than in person. Workload is tedious and do prepare yourself by practicing multiple problems.
Shabazz was one of my favorite professors. She helped me understand the concepts and was fun to have in class. You should try to get her.

Professor Shabazz is a fun person but not the best lecturer. Calc 3 is extremely easy so it didn't really matter much, but she makes a lot of mistakes during lectures and often won't finish them during the class period, so then you have to go watch the rest of the lecture on your own.

Horrible class. She made you buy TopHat even though iclicker free for UF students. Lectures were a mess. I hated the fact that attendance was mandatory(2.5% of your final grade). I believe that if you do not get any value from a lecture you should not attend. The class blurred and overcomplicated the topic... just watch MIT Calc 3, Prof Leonard.
I took this class online and she was very active on the discussion page and let us watch old lecture videos that were really helpful.
For the online section of this class, you just watch other professors' lectures. Just keep up with the material and practice example problems. Otherwise the class is alright.

Class was easy for me, but I didn't like shabazz at all. She would always mess something up on her example problems, have to go back up, and change it. Also missed a bunch of notations on variables making it more confusing than it should be. She's not detail oriented at all.

This class was mostly watching lectures, taking little mini quizzes, doing online homework, and then discussion boards for extra credit. I would recommend staying on top of things because getting behind will get stressful. I believe if you do all the extra credit, it should add 3% to your final grade.

Prof Shabazz is pretty straight forward in what she expects, and is pretty decent at teaching. She also cares and will be super accommodating with things. Quizzes were impossible, but TAs wrote those. The exams are relatively fair, sometimes a little hard. Just a bit annoying is that she just changed the way she grades, so it's harder to get an A.

Overall fine; nothing special. Probably the best option UF currently offers. She offers a ton of extra credit which saved me. I was able to get through the first 3 exams pretty easily using just her lectures (no study edge). The last exam is awful but I could get a 30% on it and still keep my A so overall a fair class with all the extra credit ops.
Dr. Shabazz is a great lecturer for Calc 3 she does her best to keep the class engaged and provides ample opportunity to ask questions during the lecture if needed.

Great teacher. Posted lectures online and made the content fairly simple to understand. She was the course coordinator so she wrote the exams and often gave us hints to a couple questions that would be on the exam. Also gave out 3% extra credit that was very easy to get. Only downside is that the MC sections on exams are disproportionally weighted.

Great professor all around and the best professor for clac 3. This is the professor everyone comes to when they skip the other professors' classes. I you don't get her for clac 3 you are doing yourself a disservice.

Lectures posted in modules were not very helpful and did not go into enough depth, I found it more beneficial to watch old in-person lectures. Exams were hard, also because the course was fully online they were all multiple choice and there was no partial credit for free response questions.

If you pay attention, you will pass. 3% EC was clutch. Unit 1&2 lectures are good, but units 3&4 lectures were a little confusing because the content got harder (she did give FRQ hints in lecture, so pay attention). Some quizzes were hard, but the TAs wrote them. Exams are very similar to notes and past ones. Use the discussions and Groupme!
