Once a week discussion section attendance and participation is graded but not bad. Designs course for student success
Fantastic professor. Engaging, thought-provoking lectures and interactive discussion sections. Papers are graded well.

Dr. Ross clearly loves her job. It is clear that she is passionate about philosophy. Her lectures are interesting and she tried to make a boring topic as fun and engaging as possible. Grading depends a lot on your TA but overall this class was a good introduction to the field of philosophy.
Dr. Ross was a great professor. Her lectures were topical and interesting, she also makes an effort to offer further thinking.

If you have her for a huge lecture-style class, your experience will definitely be shaped more by which TA you have. However, Dr. Ross structures her class and readings in a way that is very intuitive. The readings weren't too intensive and the general grading for her class was quite easy as long as you did your work (papers, quizzes, disc posts).
Only complaint is the readings. There's so much reading - at least two new ones per week, which were usually around 20 pages - and I'm a very slow reader so that really sucked for me.

She's a fun and easy choice. Your grade really relies on a small number of writing assignments but there is normally extra credit and if you show up to discussion sections or an office hour or two they don't end up that hard. She is also really passionate about what she teaches and can make the vaguest philosophical argument make sense.

I loved taking Metaphysics with Dr. Ross, so I signed up for another class with her this semester. She really enjoys what she does and likes class discussion. She is pretty good at fostering discussion, and it never feels cumbersome. One thing to keep in mind: your grade will be based largely on essays and large writing projects.
I really liked the course structure; he explains everything well and is helpful with clarifying information if needed!

Best professor at UF. Super kind and knowledgeable, taking every class I can with him. Fair difficulty, won't kill you but treat his classes with respect and use the opportunity to learn from a great writer and mind.

Amazing! The topics of writing are not superficial and useless, he brings purpose into them, where I can learn about public health and updated articles to be aware of what's happening in the real world to then apply it into papers and projects. He is very entertaining and funny, focusing on the student's comfort and participation. Highly recommend

Summer b class is a little time consuming/content heavy as I wrote an essay almost weekly, but that's expected in a 6 week course. It's doable if you're on top of your assignments, and the workload isn't too hard. professor was understanding, quickly responded to emails, and isn't a harsh grader if he sees that you clearly put in your best effort.

This class for an introductory writing course had so many useless and unnecessary assignments that not only was just straight busy work but also felt like didn't help my writing whatsoever. Useless class, don't take him for 1102 if you don't need to.

Dr Thompson was easily the most enjoyable professor for any writing course ive done at UF. Lectures are genuinely interesting and fun, he gives lots of feedback and is approachable for help outside of class. Really fun course and even more enjoyable professor.
Guidelines for papers were clear and he was super willing to help us along the way. I certainly recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Thompson is honestly one of the better professors I've had. He was a super chill grader and fun guy to talk to. While some the readings he assigned were kind of boring, the class itself was not that hard considering grades consisted of three essays and a presentation.

I took Dr. Thompson for environmental writing, and enjoyed him so much I registered to have him in medical writing as well.  Everything is a 100% or near that, and you can always send your writing in early to get feedback and revisions.  Citations and references are most important.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Got rid of a major paper and then crammed more words into the last two papers with little notice which caused unnecessary stress towards finals week.  Sent out sign ups for the final presentation with no notice and some people were allowed up to an extra two weeks to prepare. Must read nightly readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took Writing in Environmental Science with him and I don't like writing, but this was one of the only writing classes I've ever actually enjoyed taking. 5 main assignments (you choose your own topic) with a few smaller ones and 3 small presentations (not harshly graded), slightly research-heavy. You can miss up to 6 class periods with no grade hit.

Love love love Scotty T. He was the best professor I've ever had, and it's been a year since I took his class. If anyone ever asks me who a good writing professor is, I always recommend him. Attendance matters, but its not a painful class. There's a bit of work, but if you need an extension he'll always say yes, just ask.

Really nice guy. I took Prof Writing in Public Health and I feel like he actually did make me a better writer. The papers were pretty time-consuming, but they were worthwhile. He gave clear feedback and wasn't a tough grader. Also very flexible and understanding. I'd recommend any class with him.
Very easy class! Very straightforward of what you need to do once you get used to the canvas page. He is a very nice professor too, really helps on resume and stuff.
THE BEST ENGLISH TEACHER AT UF!!! If you're not taking him you are doing yourself a disservice, he is fabulous, superb, 10/10 would recommend to a friend!

I took Analytical Writing and Thinking in Crime and Punishment with Dr. Thompson. Some of the readings were a bit boring but, overall I was engaged with the material and learned a lot about crime and punishment. Dr. Thompson is a great lecturer, accommodating to students, and a fair grader. If you are considering it, definitely take this class!

By far the best English professor I have had at UF. Genuinely cares about his students and is willing to adapt the syllabus as necessary. Grades easy bit gives really good feedback. Take this course even if your major isn't plant related.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: He has been one of my favorite English teachers across the board. He's super caring and genuinely helps his class with progressing in their writing skills while simultaneously not being harsh. He helps you develop skills without being scared of getting a bad grade. Wants to help us be successful.
He is a nice guy, who knows latin and is willing to help. He is new to teaching but is willing to try new things and get feedback. The class is clear in structure and obligations.
If you're motivated and used to independent study, you'll be fine, but don't expect to be guided step-by-step. Grading is fair.

On a typical week, we would read a new Wheelock chapter over the weekend, discuss it in class, do practice from the textbook for homework, and then review it in class. We did not practice speaking much and I felt the textbook was my primary teacher. There were quizzes every few weeks which were graded fairly + a final we could use a cheat-sheet on.
Extremely harsh grader on assignments, so you genuinely never know what to expect. The lectures are not helpful whatsoever in understanding the material. TA's do mostly all the work.

I did not think the class was that hard. Yes, the exams take an extensive knowledge of the textbook, but if you focus on learning the information and completing the discussions, it is very doable. She also drops lowest test and discussions. I thought she was very fair.
This professor put me back on antidepressants.

Professor is SO condescending, rude, and makes zero exceptions. Accused me of using AI (I did not). When confronted she implied I cheated my way through HS to get into UF. As a freshman taking this course I lacked some skills, but when I asked for help she refused because "I should already know it and shouldn't be in the class." Poorly structured.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I thought the course was set up to be super easy to follow and very student friendly. I took this course during the Summer A semester so it was definitely fast paced, but it wasn't difficult. Reading the textbook was your friend for the exams. Her grading policy was very generous as there was at least one drop for each type of assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bad ratings are mostly from people caught cheating—she's strict about it. Just study a bit and you'll be fine. Readings are graded for completion, discussions are easy, and while exams require knowing the book, they aren't weighted heavily so you don't need an A. Drops allowed me to finish course a week early. Lectures aren't very useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AVOID AT ALL COST.  do yourself a favor and take ANY OTHER PROFESSOR I had to take her for 2 required classes as a Psychology major and it was the biggest mistake of my life. She was extremely condescending and passive aggressive in announcements and emails. Only looked to punish students instead of help them and was nitpicky over ridiculous things

RUN! RUN! RUN!

This will be the most upsetting, discouraging class you take, not because of the material, but the professor is quite literally the worst, unmotivating professor

I took an exam in my car and now am under investigation. I had 7 credits till graduation. This course wasn't even required for my degree. i thought it would be fun..

Awful professor who makes 0 exceptions and does not truly care about her students. I asked her respectfully if she could unlock the assignments for the semester (6 weeks) they were all through a program that would cost $150 after the two week free trial so I asked her if she could unlock it all bc I couldn't afford and she said I sympathize but no!
The class was super interesting, the lectures were casual and chill, overall pretty easy.

Terrible structuring for anyone who is neurodivergent. The first class I'm considering withdrawing genuinely because of how distressing I find it. Discussions are due Sunday at 11:59, but if you don't do part one by Thursday 11:55 (specifically 55) you will get 20% off your grade. I genuinely was excited for this class, and spent so much money alr…
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I wish the instructions were clearer. Also, assigning a heavy workload in the first three weeks isn't helpful when adjusting to her teaching style. I usually perform well regardless of how challenging the class or professor is, but I had to withdraw from this class.

I did not have a bad experience at all with this professor as some others did. The expectations were clear and I would say the work load was fair. You have to read quite a bit from the online text and definitely watch the lectures. I didn't find her difficult or rude at all, but I never had to ask for an extension on anything. She was pretty fair.

Online course super chill, just have to do McGraw hill every week and discussions here and there. Exams aren't too hard and she drops the last one. Very straightforward  and so easy to get an A. Not to mention during the 2 hurricanes we had she excused all of our work for that week and gave us 100.

Class itself is minimal work, wont take much time out of week. There are 4 exams, lowest dropped, and then an easy discussion assignment and reading assignment every week (literally a completion grade). Bless her for just giving us 100% on all the assignments that were supposed to be due during the two hurricanes instead of pushing due dates back
Strict on deadlines, doesn't provide proper feedback on exams. Not a very ADHD/neurodivergent-friendly structure in her courses.

This class was a rehashing of intro to social psych applied to a specific topic. It provided little novel information and most lecture material, videos, and readings had discrepancies between them. Also the class relies heavily on the buggy canvas video embedding tool so expect to spend a few hours troubleshooting uploading discussion videos.

She has very clear expectations for class, but at least she is consistent. Make sure your APA citations are done well- use the Citation Machine website. Exams are honorlocked, and there are several discussions that primarily make up your grade. She offered a lot of extra credit for us, so be sure to check the announcements!

This professor has a lot of negative reviews so I was hesitant when the course began, but it ended up being a positive experience. Normally in the past there were no exams and a big group project, but there was no group project and exams instead. She offers several chances for extra credit and drops your lowest test and assignment grades.

Dr. Shwartz genuinely cares about her students. She offered 5 exams (one of them she gave us the answers to) and she dropped the lowest two test scores. The exams are very straightforward. There are a few small assignments but she gives a clear rubric and grades fairly. This class is also very interesting.

Disregard the negative reviews! Class was very interesting, multiple lowest grades are dropped (exams, assignments, and discussions), exams are fair and very straight forward, Dr.S is more than understanding and available, extra credit, and she even gave freebie assignments (didn't have to complete and got 100%). 10/10 recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor at all costs! I have her for two classes this semester, my final semester at UF, and she is making it miserable. She's condescending, has unclear guidelines, sends out class messages that are extremely rude, and blames students for mistakes she makes. Do yourself a favor, take a class with literally anyone else.
Warning! Avoid!!! Don't listen like I did and you'll see why this professor has a 2.8/5.

I don't understand how she is still at UF considering so many students have bad experiences with her very passive-aggressive, micromanaging demeanor. She's on a huge power trip. Being a harsh grader is one thing, but I will never take a class with her again purely because of her attitude, which is a shame because she teaches interesting topics.

She is a very tough grader and unwilling to negotiate grades. I felt very discouraged after I received a 75 on a group paper that made up 15% of the grade, but after putting full effort into all of the other assignments and completing all of the extra credit, I managed to get an A. Do all of the extra credit in this class; it goes a long way!
Smooth semester as long as you don't ignore syllabus and rubrics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. You better hope your randomly assigned group members are competent otherwise you won't pass the mandatory group project. Terrible communicator. Buy a few APA rule books and study them because if you mess up even just one citation, you'll drop a whole letter grade. Very nitpicky and loves to take off points. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, class content is not difficult. However, 50% of your grade is based off a randomly assigned group project. For this reason, you better hope the draw works in your favor. Extremely tough grader when it comes to proper APA citation style and dos not provide much feedback in this department.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough grader, but if you reach out and communicate with her, she's very reasonable and caring. She also genuinely cares about the subject and wants each student to leave the class feeling fulfilled. I would definitely take this class again.

She definitely cares about what she teaches; her students...not so much. She's a VERY tough grader. Most of your grade is based on a group project where she gives very little direction and follows the rubric TO THE LETTER. Mess up a citation? Drop almost a full letter grade. And it's a group paper. Awful. She's also pretty passive-aggressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This teacher was the worst! She tried to blame her students for her mistake! Assignments are unclear, which makes them harder and when grading doesn't follow what it says. She is not accessible out of class and if you do get to go to her office hours, she doesn't help and is rude to her students. Avoid the class if you can!

Cried a few times. Rude, accused me of cheating. please DON'T TAKE IT ! But if you do end up in it: assignments have very unclear instructions - she's a VERY tough grader; follow the rubric point by point and include absolutely everything it asks for (even if it seems optional) and make sure to take advantage of extra credit assignments.

She was extremely rude throughout the entire course and refused to answer basic questions about assignments when you emailed her or went to her office hours. She gave very unclear instructions for the paper we had to write this semester and for the final project she made us record a video presentation that HAD TO BE between 9:45 and 10:00. AVOID!!

She made the class unbearable and way more difficult than it needed to be. Discussion posts were fine but final project and paper were awful. Her guidelines on the paper were so unclear and final project had to be recorded and meet time limit of 9:45-10 minutes otherwise points would be deducted. Took me hours to get the time right AVOID HER CLASS!

Has an inflated ego. Her infamous "no arguing about grades" rule is ironic considering she's teaching a class on how to foster positive work environments. Personally, I did well in this class but it was because I went way beyond the standard grading criteria to make sure I satisfied her vague wants. Take this class with a different prof if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class itself is easy, but she takes forever to grade and doesn't really communicate with students

Just no. She is condescending and outright rude. Her TAs do all of the work for her, and then she is rude when you have a question about grading. I've had more pleasant interactions with chemistry professors than with Schwartz. Do yourself a favor and avoid at all costs.

Doesn't teach anything, just tells you to read the textbook. Takes forever to grade assignments. Some assignments have unclear instructions. The course itself wasn't bad - I thought it was easy and straightforward, and you will too if you are good at report-style writing. But the professor's strict attitude doesn't help facilitate learning at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Schwartz is rude, uncaring. I was a TA in this course, and now I know why she begs for TAs, no one wants to TA for this professor, as she is rude and has a God complex.  If you plan to TA for Dr. Schwartz you better be ready to work and work hard. She is a nightmare as a person and as a professor. Stay away from anything related to Dr. Schwartz.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: she is extremely vague and unclear in her directions. assignments take weeks to get back grades. if you need any extension or accommodation she does not care.
I actually really enjoyed this teacher! Few assignments and no exams! Just papers in which if you follow the guidelines, you'll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: 50% of your grade is dependent on group papers. It may not sound bad but it is. Your groups are randomly chosen based on the topic you want to write about. She was very unreasonable when I had technical difficulties with an assignment and I ended up losing a ton of points for submitting it late. Interesting material but this class sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She doesn't really require much. The lectures are short 10 minute videos at most and then you just write a post or do a video discussion post. It's been a really easy class just use citethisforme website for APA format help and put in the work and you should be fine.

I enjoyed Professor Schwartz and her course. For Mini A, weekly discussions, midterm paper, and final project. Fair amount of work for a mini course. Midterm paper difficult, but do-able. Final project was much easier. I would take the prof again!

Took this class for Mini A, enjoyed the professor and topics. 1 or 2 discussions a week, 1 midterm paper, 1 final project. Slow grading, but gives specific feedback. 1 extra credit opportunity. No quizzes or exams. Would take prof again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took I/O psych w/ Professor Schwartz & loved her! Caring & a pretty easy grader. There's a few quizzes & 2 papers, we also had a few extra credit opportunities. Directions are sometimes vague but the directions for most of the assignments are the same so it's easy to catch on. As long as you stay on top of your work & do the ec youll get an A.

Overall workload isn't bad and discussion topics are interesting, but you had better make sure you do everything she tells you to and not screw anything up. She takes no excuses for anything, and she (or her TAs) grade severely. I'm still waiting for my final project grade and terrified she'll give me a ZERO on it b/c I was shy of the word count.

I didnt really learn much through the class. Every week theres a 50+ topic ALEKS style quiz that usually takes around an hour and a half. Some weeks had over 100 topics. A huge part of your grade is a group paper with little direction. Our file somehow corrupted, and she didnt reach out to tell us, just gave us a horrible grade. Unprofessional.

Dr. Schwartz was a phenomenal professor! The class was set up in an easy to understand format. Her lectures were interesting and incorporated stories from her career which I enjoyed. The group case study and lit review paper was easy when the work was split evenly. No tests/quizzes, just easy reading activities. Overall fun class and not difficult.

After spending 5 days writing a literature review paper, one of our group members accidentally submitted the wrong document. After submitting proof and evidence that we didnt work on it after the due date and followed every step in the rubric, she refused to regrade and I dropped 2 letter grades. Easy assignments just unreasonable professor.

Dr. Schwartz was a fine professor, but making a group project worth 50% of our grade is totally unfair, especially for an online class in a pandemic. She made one lecture per week, and everything else graded by TAs, so she did not do much.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Half the assignments are due 3 days before they say they are due. They are easy, though. Most of the grade is writing two article critiques. It's a small amount of work, but the due dates are not the date they are due.

You have weekly assignments but nothing difficult. The case study paper isn't bad if you're a good writer and get a common disorder. Dr. Schwartz is understanding especially during a pandemic. The reading activities are tedious but doable. Overall a really interesting class.

She's okay. I wasn't expecting the weekly discussion posts and textbook reading assignments to be as much work as they were every week. The group project directions were often disorganized, incomplete and hard to make heads or tails of, and I entirely ignored her lectures because you have to read the book anyway, but at least there were no exams.

Read the textbook and keep up with work and you'll be fine. Dr. Schwartz was more than understanding during the pandemic, the tropical storm, and even the election. She willingly extended deadlines and lessened the workload. No exams, but 50% of your grade is dependent upon a group project.

I am taking this prof for a 3rd time. Each time I've taken her it has been a different set up to the course. The first time I took her for Pseudoscience all assignments were due by sunday, the 2nd time, assignments were due throughout the week. Not many assignments for grading so you must do well on everything. She was understanding during pandemic

NEVER take Shari Schwartz. I got a 98 in this class and it was not worth the frustration and headaches. She is rude and condescending in emails and her assignment instructions are not clear at all. She uses voice memos instead of normal announcements and she doesn't believe DRC accommodations should apply to her class. DON'T TAKE HER!!!!

Industrial/Organizational Psychology with Professor Schwartz was a lot more enjoyable than I originally anticipated. The material is applicable to any job you might have and Professor Schwartz is very responsive if you have any questions. There are quizzes based on the readings and lectures but the two paper are the bulk of your grade.
No empathy. Difficult. Quizzes, midterm, and final are tough. UF should look into other options.

The quiz questions are very difficult and crytic. The pictures associated with the questions, offer little to no assistance and she is a very difficult grader when it comes to discussions and essays. Students with 4.0 GPA's have failed her course, and she offers no sympathy for life events. This proffesor should be reviewed to protect students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The questions for these quizes are very cryptic and the pictures are very difficult  to see and offer very little context for the question. As a full time parent, student, and employee, I was given very little grace and she has little to no understanding of the challenges we face in day-to-day life. Students with 4.0 GPA's have failed this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Utley is a very knowledgeable professor and is a very understanding. I was shocked to see all of the negative reviews. This course is difficult, but it is a difficult area of study so that was to be expected! Read the textbook, watch YouTube videos on anatomy, study for the quizzes, and you will be just fine. You get what you give!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bad. Barely interacted with the class, no actual teaching performed. Read the weekly readings, read the vague modules full of typos, and get punished on vague quizzes because the "prof" refuses to actually teach. Quizzes poorly worded, based on single-sentence minutiae from textbooks. Quality papers given 10% off seemingly arbitrarily. Disgraceful.

The modules do not match the quizzes and the images that are on the quizzes could be numerous things w/out knowing context. Don't let the extra credit fool you -not worth the effort as it was also graded harshly. Sherry took points off for things she said were not in my papers that were in fact IN MY PAPER which tells me she blindly graded my work.

Utley & TA Sheri should be fired and banned from working in the state university system. Test questions/assignment details are pulled straight out of....the air. Then, her minion, Sheri, clearly has some type of learning/reading disability because she blankets assignments with a poor grade and the same "not adequately explained" comments.

Extremely difficult class. The professor did not interact with the class in a positive manner at all during the semester. The module content is bare bones and the quizzes don't match what you read. Her grading criteria is awful and she comes across as snarky and rude.  TA Sherri is terrible as well and will bash every paper you write. DO NOT TAKE!

Worst class I have ever taken. Quizzes don't match module content and are beyond unreasonable. The amount of reading required is more than triple what other grad school courses require. The assignments are graded unfairly. Would absolutely never pay to take this class again - I learned nothing b/c of the extreme amount of stress this class gave me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Her quizzes are not based on the module information and in the photos that are on the quizzes, they are information that the student will have no idea about. For the assignments, you are required to have 500 words but you are going to find yourself writing over 1,000 words. If you miss a specific topic from the module, you will lose a full point.

Dr. Utley is an absolute clown show who puts zero effort into her students or her class. The course itself is an egregious waste of time, money, and effort solely because of her. This class is a complete circus.

The so-called professor is condescending, unresponsive, and dismissive toward students' concerns. You will never not worry about this class. Do you think you got it? Think again, you don't. You forgot one small detail about this topic you had to read/learn alone? Half your points are gone. You will rue the day you started this class. Seriously.

Unresponsive to emails. Very harsh grading focused on what is missing and not what knowledge is shown (1/2 points automatically if missing ANYTHING). Quizzes are not based on modules. 200+ pages a week to read. Quiz answers might only be in a single sentence in all that reading if that. Does not care about students learning the overarching topics.
Terrible. Would never take again.

This course is ridiculous, if I were not set to graduate after the semester I would have dropped the whole program because of this class and professor. She does not teach and when concerns are brought up they are not addressed only dismissed. It's a horrible class and a horrible example of a "professor."

Trauma Analysis class she "teaches". If it weren't a core class, I would've dropped out within the first few weeks. The module notes are a joke. Copy/paste from outdated textbooks. Assignment prompts are very broad and the quiz questions aren't even related to the module text. The grading for this class is just comical. Avoid her at all costs.

She is by far the worst professor ever. Granted you have to do more work as the class is online, but she did absolutely nothing. She never lectured or taught in anyway. She never engaged with students or added to class discussions. She never replied to emails. Her notes are very basic and never helpful. Quizzes and exams were impossible to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The modules and pictures provided are the only references available for the class. The quizzes are supposed to be based on the modules which is continually incorrect. There are multiple grammatical errors in every single module as well as spelling. Answers to quiz questions are unclear and extremely wordy for the time provided to take the quizzes.

AVOID HER! Impossible class. I cannot stress that enough. The class is called gross anatomy but all the quiz and test questions and assignments ask either about histology, pathology, or making a diagnosis from two or three symptoms. She does NOT teach about histology or symptoms. So you have to teach yourself everything. Many students fail!

I cannot say much about Dr. Utley as her TA does everything for her. Dr. Utley doesnt teach through live or recorded lectures. Her notes are pretty much straight off of the internet and are not at a graduate level. Her assignments are very broad and open ended. I am sure she would be okay in person, but she doesnt know how to do an online class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It is very clear that she loves what she does. Makes the material fun and I learned a huge amount.

First she gave us assignments on spring break. Guess after complaints she gave us the next week off. Then she moved up the final project date to sooner a week before it was due. Also said that this was due to grades being due on the 26th but had the final exam due on the 28th? Absolutely will not take her again.

Awesome class! She was one of the best professors I ever had, knows this field, and I learned so much in this course! She really cares about students and wants them to do well. Gives lots of time to finish exams and discussion questions and gives extra credit for participation. Not bad to look at either! Too bad she only teaches online.

She didn't go to meetings about her work and now grad students working under her are forced to do double the work. Her response was that she was sorry but she should really resign. A shameful professor

Professor Ulanowicz is awesome. She put a lot of background information about the text into the lectures and really encouraged conversations, especially with different perspectives. There could probably do to be a few more assignments but overall super enjoyable class and obviously very smart, engaged professor
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Ulanowicz is AMAZING! Take her class if you're genuinely passionate about the subject, and I promise it will be one of the most rewarding educational experiences you can have. Her lectures are information-heavy, and you'll fall behind quickly if you miss class, but she is a phenomenal lecturer. Also a very quick and very fair grader!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One novel per week. With audio books, it wasn't hard. If you can do that, then absolutely take this class. There is nothing about her teaching style that makes anything harder than it should be. There were two 3pg papers and one 8-10pg. Keep up with the reading, don't wait until the last minute to do the papers, and you'll do well and enjoy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof U was great! Be prepared to read all the books she assigns because you go over them in depth, and sometimes there are pop quizzes on them! Every Friday, there are written exams on the stories you covered that week. She likes detail, so you really can't BS them! And if you miss class during the week, you'll be hurting during written exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She's a great professor who facilitates conversation and lectures well. However, she is a very tough grader and will make you work for an A or B. She's incredibly nice and will help you in office hours. She also offers some extra credit along the way to help you out, although she also gives quite a few pop quizzes and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Ulanowicz is one of my two favorite professors at UF (The other being Carolyn Kelley)! Her classes are informative (I have been in several) and she makes your writing better, while still maintaining humanity, unlike other professors that I have encountered. She cares about your education and is willing to help you.
She is awesome!

An amazing professor. I've taken five courses with her - both children's literature and outside the department - and each time, I learn a great deal. She can be a tough grader, so make sure to do the reading and know what you're talking about. She gives tons of extra credit opportunities and she's a really understanding person.

I truly can't say enough positive things about Prof. U. She is incredibly smart, and in studying children's lit, she teaches you to think in new ways. She is approachable and funny. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! She will help you with assignments and talk through papers. I haven't met a student who didn't adore her. Take her classes if you get the chance!

Professor U is an amazing teacher! I loved the material we went over! Don't be fooled by the fact that it is Children's literature, though. She expects a lot from your essays. She wasn't very good about responding to emails, but if you go in for office hours and show that you want to put in extra effort to do well on your essays you'll do well.

English major or not, if you like reading and analyzing details you might not have ever noticed on your own, you will love her classes. She knows everything, and the discussions get really interesting as they cover everything from literature to sociology to art, psychology, and history. You will learn so much, but you will need to work. Must take!!

She's great. She knows quite a lot about children's lit. I feel like I learned a lot and had a fun experience while reading texts like Peter Pan, Winnie the Pooh, the Secret Garden, and The Wind in the Willows.

Really interesting class, I learned a lot about analyzing childrens book. Prof. U is very knowlegable and she is really sweet and loves teaching and her students! Not too much work but you need to pay attention to details in the books you read and be willing to participate and share your ideas in class discussions. I definitely recommend her!

childhood and film class. good selection of films.  you really have to think  in this class when writing the essays (three and a shorter final). hse is very intelligent, and I learned a lot about film (this was my first film class)

One of the greatest classes and professors ever!!  She is sooo amazing and really cares about students!  She is incredibly intelligent and will give amazing insight into all of the novels you read. I really can't say enough great things about her.

I took Lit for the Adolescent and Childhood and Film with Anja--she is incredible. LOVE HER! You'll learn a ton! But don't take her class because you think it'll be easy to read children's books. Her classes are best for English majors, because you need to have the ability and desire to stretch your mind & analyze the material in new ways.

She is amazing!! I learned so much in her Childhood in War class. I HIGHLY recommend taking her. She is extremely knowledgeable about the subject matter but is very interested in what students think. This class was an "open forum" where we could express our ideas freely and without judgement. Oh and for all you guys out there- she's beautiful!
I had the biggest crush on her ever. Nicest lady.

i agree with the other person. the teacher is really cool, but you should not bass a class off that. liking the subject helps. it is not just looking at pretty pictures. it is a class you have to use your brain in. i thought i knew enough, but my lack of adding to class discussion was not smart. she didnt make it difficult to try, but i was laxy.

This class was challanging. I should have left the first day. I am not an English major and it hurt me. Although the teacher was helpful I would have left this class up to those majoring in it. If you do not like to read do not take this class. You have to read and be able to talk about it.

this class is hard. the teach is way cool, and i learned so much, but i had to work hours and hours on stuff. i worked very hard to get my b. take her if you want a challange and do not mind using your brain.

dude. i tried so hard in this class. you actually have to do the reading and she gives you papers you actually have to think about. yhis is not an easy "A'. i learned a lot, but noy do those kids who want to learn really miss out on stuff cause i am taking up the room.

Do not take her class if you are looking for an easy A. You need to be able to participate and add something to the class. Quizzes are given without notice, and in-class essays call for you to use your intellect. If you want an easy A class with little to no effort to be made, than taking her class is no recommended. Take Floral Arrangement instead

A few of these comments are off-base in regard to the ease of the course. You can  do well in this class, but don't expect an "A" for laziness.  Dr. Ulanowicz is actually a pretty tough grader. So if you're taking this for an easy "A" do everyone a favor and take another class. Don't sit there and take space away from people who need the class.

Excellent class with a wonderful prof.  She is helpful, fun, and interesting, and I really feel that I learned something here rather than just regurgitating info.  Take a class with her if at all possible!

(Children's Film)  Had her before, and yet again she has proved to be an excellent professor.  Disappointed that she's not teaching anything new next semester, but still, I highly recommend her.  One of the most intelligent professors and just really sweet and funny.  Very approachable, creative, interesting.  Don't leave UF without taking her.
(Holocaust Literature)- Very nice teacher. She is extremely helpful and passionate about the subject. She is also willing to help you out whenever you need it.
Very intelligent woman. She really gets you thinking. Ulanowicz is one of those professors who just wants you to learn something from the class. She's very understanding and nice. Great teacher!

(Rep. the Holocaust)  I loved this class and the professor.  The topic was extremely interesting and the prof is one of the most intelligent and insighful teachers I've had.  There are weekly journal assignments (easy) where you just record your thoughts, 3 formal essays (you choose from a list of topics), and a final essay.  Highly recommended!

She's a great teacher. You have to write ten short papers and three formal papers. The short papers are graded on completion and aren't too difficult. Speak up in class and DO THE reading. A lot of times, you don't have to do all of it, but try to do most of it. The readings aren't too difficult.

This is for EAS4810C. This class is atrocious. Prepare to spend 30+ hours on each lab just to get in the 70-85 range. I'm convinced that Dr. Ukeiley instructs the TAs to grade as hard as possible because there's really no other explanation. Ukeiley's structure for this class will wear down your mental health, so be ready.

He gets the job done, no complaints. Bit tough to reach him outside of class but really approachable after lecture. Gives a solid review before each exam and the long answer questions (+-50% of the exam) are either explicitly told to you in class or can be predicted from prior hw. Nothing great, nothing horrible, pretty average (not a bad thing).

Takes getting used to
1st half lots concpts Second half more application
Lots of time to do HW, I would procrastinate, do NOT recomend

Felt unprepared for exams, easier than expected
Past exams useful
introductory true/false to warm you up
short answer to get you going
long question at the end
long Q like HW, easy to predict with HW and past exams

Do you love derivations? Do you love memorizing formulas (there's no formula sheet) AND useless derivations for exams? If so, Lawrence Ukeiley is the professor for you! Have any questions? Don't bother emailing him unless you want a condescending response.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof complicates almost every example in lecture. Pulls numbers out of nowhere. Class is almost Thermo II, with textbook tables with countless values. First exam had a typo that cost 30 points. Didn't fix the issue. Proceeded to warp the grade scale multiple times. Final exam was ok. He can get annoyed at lecture questions very easily.
Past exams given and were useful for study material, homework was applicable to exams the majority of the time.

Not a bad course at all. Hes a good lecturer and he curves, averages on all the exams are 68-70. but with a curve and assuming you do all your HW its an easyish A. The Material can be tough and there's no way around it tbh. He teaches aerodynamics from the VERY basics and builds it up. VERY theoretical at many points in the class. Very good course!

Took him for comp flow, material is pretty cool. He's very straightforward and the class is "good" once you figure him out. Just read the textbook and know the material rather than just  regurgitate it. Homework is mostly completion based. Make sure you have at least a week 2 work on final project. his exams are fair, overal good course

He sucks. People say he's nice but can snap back at you if you ask a question he doesn't like. Makes you do useless derivations that will NEVER appear at a work place. He needs to make this class more practical - final exam covers too much material. It seems that he thinks aerodynamics is the only course his students are taking.

He is huge on doing long meticulous derivations that no one is paying attention to in class and rarely works out actual problems.  This class is made to be difficult, on exams be prepared to apply complicated formulas that you haven't worked out a problem with.  If you have applied a formula before, he likes to ask you to derive it from scratch.

This guy is horrible. All he does is copy the derivations from the book (except he makes tons of mistakes). Because of this, going to class is completely useless; however, it's technically required because he gives unannounced quizzes. Unfortunately you have to take his class if you're an aero student. Just be warned, and be prepared.

My purpose for this rating is not for Ukeiley directly. Ukeiley is a half-way decent professor. My warning is that Aerodynamics at UF IS A WEED OUT COURSE. He/they/whoever makes this class artificially hard. I could write an essay on the things done to this course just to try and fail students, but for the sake of this review, be warned!
Nice prof! ok course. a lot of aero stuff. But good experience.

Ukeiley's a really nice guy, he's not a bad professor, either. He's a numbers guys, which isn't necessarily bad, but I'd like to a see a bit more explanation of derivation--but you can't have it all I guess. You'd be fine with taking him and you'll learn a good amount, too. He finished the curriculum 2 weeks early!

Professor Stingl offers fair grading, minimal homework, and well-prepared quizzes for four exams and an optional final. Balanced coursework, respected teaching, and adeptness with online tools define his approach.

Professor Stingl was a joy to have. His lectures aren't Hollywood worthy, but they get the information across. His study guides highlight everything you need to know for the exams. If you study them thoroughly, you will surely get an A. Will offer extensions if needed.

Professor Ulrich Stingl is not the best professor around. Although he does have a ppt, he does not make any effort to explain the concepts. He just reads the slides( really boring!!) Do not let this professor diminish your interest in Microbiology!! To get an A, just watch youtube microbio videos, read textbook, and study the quizzes

Very easy class but still informative! Straight-forward, no BS. Watch the lectures and study a little and you'll be fine. Modules are very short and exams don't cover much material at all. Unless you don't try at all, there's no reason you won't do well in this class. Class could probably be made a little harder but I'm definitely not complaining

Awesome professor! Study ahead of time, do study guides, watch videos and you will do fine. I learned so much from this class. I would definitely take him again. You will see quiz questions again on the exams.
Dr. Stingl is one of the best professor! He respects his students and gives a lot of help when needed. It is an easy A class as long as you study for it!

As long as you watch the lectures, you will do fine on the quizzes. Make sure you understand the quiz questions because the exams are very similar to them. Overall, he is very fair and will clearly tell you what you need to know for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: took Quest 1 Comida & Conflicto and even though the class itself is not hard there is a lot of work involved. about 2 quizzes a week about articles that can be more than 10 pgs long and videos that you have to submit on friday's about a particular topic. I honestly thought it was a lot for a quest, but she doesn't have exams so that's good
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took SPN3930 and SPW3030 with Paola and they were my favorite classes I've taken at UF. One of the most knowledgeable/interesting professors I've had. Classes are reading heavy, but she is always excited to help during office hours. Essays have loose prompts, and she encourages thinking creatively & giving our interpretations of the topics/texts.

Interesting lectures but she barely provides a space for students to share their knowledge on the topic. So keep your knowledge to yourself, she knows more than everyone else. The good thing is that you do not need to be creative or original in this class, as long as you write the final paper that she wants you to write, you will get an A.

Fantastic professor. There's a lot of reading in this class, but that's to be expected, it is a literature class. She was always very available outside of class, and really wants her students to be successful. Great feedback on all assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He was confusing and not a good teacher. Avoid.
Throughout this course, I found purpose in what I was doing. He inspired me, encouraged you and then challenged me. I loved his deadpan style of speaking symbolically.

He is the sage when hes on the stage and hes the guide when hes on your side. I never imagined I would come across such a professor. I experienced the breadth of his knowledge and depth of his care. God give him long life.
I just enjoyed him throughout the semester :)
Really approachable guy . Would recommend
I scheduled an one-one-meeting with him and that made a whole lot of difference. He was a great listener and he addressed my needs.

He used piazza for course website, which was super easy! He brings uncommonly wide range of international and interdisciplinary perspectives, which may easily confuse you to death, specially when you don't see the connection. Here's your bet: Keep calm and tell him you're confused. He will explain it for you. Super crazy trill professor :)

He frequently checked with each individual student to make sure we were on track for our final project. He knew it was tough but he was intentional; but he did have empathy. I would have dropped this class in the middle without the support. He kinda sensed that I was too anxious about my project and provided examples and tips to be successful.

Gaulee is an exceptional teacher except that I hated  the  way he put us through a tough group project. You had to identify and call university leaders and make reports. Even though it eventually turned out pretty well, working in the group was a pain
He was certainly a calm haven when I was going through a storm of chaos. Accommodated me and provided me some really useful resources. I liked his anecdotes and unique perspectives

Hard class but great prof. Exams are worth a lot but extra credit is given & the grading scheme is forgiving. Didn't make it to many lectures bc I couldn't wake up, but they're recorded and he's a decent lecturer. Get started early on the project & devote some good time to studying and you'll be fine.

Lectures are succinct and helpful. Course consists of 3 quizzes, 3 exams (all open note with lecture slides), and a semester-long project, each with 20% bonus points. Homework is optional. Grading is very lenient.  It's possible to get an A with minimal studying, but the professor is very knowledgeable if you want to learn beyond what's required.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ungor is fine, however the structure of the class itself is incredibly dense and textbook heavy. Don't expect that going to lecture is at all a substitute for the textbook, as the ideas covered in class are basically a summary of the textbook. Also, you only are graded on 3 quizzes, 3 exams, and 1 semester long project. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fun lecturer and gives 20% bonus on every assignment because otherwise averages would be low. Content is "difficult" but you'll be fine if you actually watch the lectures. Most of the course stems from DSA but adds extra fun stuff like network flow

I think this class and the professor is amazing. If you enjoyed the proofs in the algorithm analysis, I 100% recommend this class. Materials are not easy but it will make sense if you put some time. He also grades the projects very leniently. He is willing to interact with students and gives good feedback. I can't recommend the professor enough.
This class is no joke - the exams are brutal. But the professor really cares about student learning. Use all the resources like office hours, textbook, and tools like unstuck ai to succeed.

All around solid course structure and content. It can be difficult, but comes with forgiving grading scales. I'd only dock Prof Ungor because grading took/is taking absurdly long (my grade received is a best estimate). He can definitely be arrogant, but it's in a strangely endearing way that made me respect him more lol

Professor Ungor is a great lecturer; he keeps students engaged and is really knowledgeable. The content might appear tough, but if you read the book and engage with the material you should be fine. The class gave A LOT of extra credit. Basically, you can gain 120/100 points on every assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ungor is an amazing instructor whose deep understanding of the subject comes through in his teaching. He keeps students engaged during lecture, and checks for understanding along the way. He kept me coming to lectures. From the level of communication and organization in this course, I can tell Dr. Ungor cares about the success of his students.

One of the best professors I've had. He cares about students and is passionate about what he teaches. His lectures and amazing and crystal clear. The content is hard. Anyone who gave him a bad rating probably looked for an easy A. Work hard, read the slides and you will get an A. He gives a lot of extra credit to help students.
Weekly quizzes, a large project, and 3 exams. Good course, I know much more than I did previously. Helped me to conceptualize algorithm analysis. I recommend.

You can tell he is a very smart guy and the material was very hard. He was SO generous with partial and extra credit though. On every quiz there was a 10% curve and on the exams it was around a 30% curve, and partial credit for exams and projects. Be aware, our grade was 33% final project, 33% quizzes, 33% exams. All HW was optional.

Dr. Ungor's lectures are honestly really engaging, and you can tell he genuinely cares that his students learn the material. The tests are tough for sure, but he also gives a generous amount of extra credit on them. Do the problems in the textbook and make use of office hours and you will do well.

The course was very difficult but the instructor was very interesting. He truly understands the student's difficulties and listens to the student while giving the necessary help (in dues and grades). Good instructor.

I don't get these other ratings. The class was hard, but curves and grading were extremely lenient. Office hours were helpful even though lectures were a bit confusing.

For context, on the final project NONE of my code worked, but they still graded it 100%. Max grade was like 140% on that. Similar curves on exams
Very difficult course. If you want to study a lot and ultimately fail in class, this is the perfect course.

Some professors enjoy mentally challenging students, and unfortunately, this falls into that category. He seems to relish seeing students struggle, crying, torturing, and rushes through lectures using slides from other universities. Grades are released right before midterms(hours before),creating pressure.Luckily, the course is no longer mandatory.

He is not a bad teacher but super tough exams. He has only 3 exams and no assignments except 2 projects during our time, projects are 40% and exams 60%, at least when I took it. And there is no curving, In first two exams, my scores were above mean and median and in or under upper quartile, he didn't show marks of third exam, and just gave a B+.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor has made the course unnecessarily hard. Feedback was not provided properly. Grades are not released on time at all. The course was very overwhelming and there was a lot of pressure throughout the semester. Disconnected from reality.
If possible don't take his course. Never answer questions after class.

Unlike the popular opinion, I didn't find the AoA course as difficult. The professor teaches really well and has well-organized slides. Attending and understanding all his lectures are enough to succeed in his course. To score well in the course prepare from the beginning of the semester and solve all the exercise problems in the textbook.

COT 5405 is one of the most difficult courses in Computer Science at UF. The 3 midterm exams each 25% weighted are one of the most difficult exams and hurt GPA. Questions are framed from standard books CLRS or Kleinberg-Tardos, and cover a LOOTTT of Math. Take this course if you are good at Discrete Math and have a history of doing good at exams.
The class was okay. They rushed the end of the semester. He presents a lot of material but it's manageable if you don't have any other super tough courses in the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have taken two classes with Dr. Ungor, and he consistently has EXTREMELY difficult exams. The average is usually like 50% and has to have a massive curve. However, I do think he is a pretty effective lecturer, and besides the exams, there is not too much work. If his exams were even in the realm of reasonable difficulty he'd be a 5/5.

He is not a bad teacher, his previously recorded lectures in the chalk board are amazing. I found much harder to follow algorithms and proofs through slides, so it is unfortunate that has become the norm. The tests usually have lots of EC that one can take advantage of. If the class means are low, he will assign even more bonus points to remediate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His exams are difficult and constitute 80% of the grade. You can do well, but you will need to spend a lot of time reading the textbook and doing practice problems (possibly sacrificing other classes). It is an important topic, but you basically need to treat it as a full-time job unless you already have solid understanding on the subject
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clear lecture, detailed notes, in-time response, hard exam (only if you don't spend enough time on this class).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is brutal with the grading methodology. When the semester started there were only 3 seats left for the class and before the drop-off period 81 people dropped. Just messed with most people's grades. You can get good grades still, but only if you sacrifice all things else (including other courses).

Easily the worst class I have had at UF. By far the worst and hardest COT3100 professor. I also received my worst grade at UF in his class (I'm a senior graduating with a 3.94). His lectures were at 7-8am in the morning and were terrible, and your entire grade depended on 4 test grades (all of which were extremely hard). Worst experience ever.

He use the textbook *Introduction to Algorithms*, which was a great book that not only teach you algorithms, but also design principles behind them. Do take this professor's! You'll find yourself mastering algorithms and have no fear with job interviews after taking this course. A lot extra credits in exams, I got A even missing the term paper.
His way of teaching is amazing! And exam questions, although tough, test our understanding of the concepts and are interesting to solve

Ungor is one of the better lecturers at UF as I've been in the department for 5 years now. If you make sure to study each lecture, study old exams, and make practice exam problems for yourself to do a couple times per test, you should at least pass, Partial grading system is rough, its very "all or none" grading. Go to Ungor's office hours!

You would really learn a lot in this class. His teaching style is amazing. He gives non-mandatory homework that I found very useful. If you are good at maths and problem solving, you would do good. This class is mostly based on logics with some methodologies and concepts. I definitely recommend it.

This professor have clearly gudiance and wonderful lecture. He always show example when make the statement about algorithm. Exam is difficult so you should take 120% effort to study if you want to get a high grade.

He's not necessarily a bad lecturer, the course is just a really difficult topic. He's very nice and gives a huge curve, but his tests are just way too hard. Even if you understand his notes, that doesn't imply you will understand the questions on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class made me cry like no other. People seem to have mixed reviews on Ungor and personal grades seem to drive one's opinion. In this class working hard is not equivalent to scoring high. I don't believe Ungor sets his students up well for success with the hard material. Homework/lectures review easy questions and tests are insanely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Maybe he is a decent teacher on campus, but that was not the case for the online class. Zero interaction with student and no online support what so over. No lectures what so ever. He did not even assign a TA for the online class. Felt like he left his students high and dry. You have to read on your own and take 4 tough exams. Stay away!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Taking Discrete with Dr. Ungor was definitely challenging. The course grade was based on only four exams (which included bonus points), which I found to be quite challenging. However, I do not think the class was unfair. You have to put in your effort, but Dr. Ungor and the TA's were all caring and wanted to help students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take the online version of COT3100 from him. Grade is based on 4 tests; literally no support is given in terms of lecture material to students: its heres a digital textbook and the dates for your tests (and a bill for more than $1500). YouTube is a better resource; University is also to blame: multiple complaints were ignored by admin!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I felt robbed by the university and the professor. Professor did not do his job in my opinion. Rather than teaching and helping, all he did is inform the class when the exams are up and when the exams have been graded. He assigns homework but does not bother to explain any of the problems. Final score is based on 4 tough exams only. Stay away!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take Discrete Math with him. His class was at 7:25 AM, and I learned nothing from his lectures. He gives us a curve, but he kept changing it after every exam. I thought I would get one grade in his class, but he changed the curve at the last minute and bumped me down a letter grade. He is also rude and condescending in class and over email.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take Discrete with him, just dont.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Basically just lectures from powerpoint slides that narrow down the textbook. The man knows what he's talking about but more/real examples would help for a class that has such difficult content.

Lectures were alright, but most of the material needed to be practiced and studied myself. Definitely did not make this course easy. However, I learned that his exams are HEAVILY based upon the practice problems he assigns in the homework (at like 25-50% are taken straight from them/twisted around a bit). TA office hours were also VERY helpful

Professor was not ready to teach this class. Do not expect much help and be prepared to learn on your own. Final grade is based on four exams only. Outdated short videos that do not cover the examination material. Exams are difficult and not enough time is allotted. Grading criteria kept changing with time. By far the worst educational experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is yet another class that needs a lot of improvements in the CISE department. I was graded on only 4 tests which the TA's would hash points off for any minor mistakes. Each test was 100 points out of 110 or more and the average was still in the 70's. In the end I got an alright grade for my work, but this course was just disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ungor is a good lecturer, but teaches the basics of Discrete and expects you to be able to do much more difficult things on the exams. There is non-mandatory homework which is basically the questions in the textbook that he makes his slides from. There was very little facilitation of learning and exams are extremely difficult.

Tests students on material that doesn't appear/reflect the primary study material provided. Aims to make up for his lack of effort in course structure by assigning a plethora of problems (about 150+/exam) and showering students with extra credit. Possible to get good grades but an intuitive learning experience is not achieved in my experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grueling class. Hes a decent teacher, but the material is covered at an insane pace and the exams are incredibly difficult. The whole grade is from the four exams, with averages on each hovering around a 60 (a C was a 47 by the end of the class). The upside is that you learn lots of very useful material, but prepare to put in tons of work to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The online course was an assign and forget course. He does not have office hours, he did not participate with the students and the material online is not enough to use to prepare. This was a time for everyone to learn on their own. There were only 4 grades, which included 4 tests. Each of the tests is much harder than the online text.

Dr Ungor has very high expectations from the students but his teaching does not keep up with it. Lectures are straight from textbook, with very easy examples, (maybe for us to understand the concept) but the exams are unbelievably tough. No preparation is ever enough. I would avoid unless I want to face a great great challenge.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures are simple and go over a lot of material very quickly. Going to class and reading the lecture powerpoints does not prepare you for his exams whatsoever. Grades are only based on very difficult tests using very difficult questions, when he lectures on very easy examples, 48% was a C. Worst college course I've ever taken in four years.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He spent a ton of time going over the easy concepts and flew through the hard stuff. His lectures are straight from the textbook (examples are even the same) and the discussions do not help at all. I would avoid taking this class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I would definitely like to encourage you to take Analysis of Algorithms if you would like to study computer science. The lectures of Dr. Ungor are pretty clear and vivid. It is a wonderful experience to take this course. Also, you will learn a lot of algorithms in this class.

The Professor ensures you have a deep understanding of Algorithms and its ANALYSIS. There were certain moments where he tries to make students appreciate the beauty of certain algorithms. This class was totally worth the challenge it presented. The feeling of accomplishment after getting a problem right in the exam is truly rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Passion for teaching is clearly visible in his lectures. Interactive lectures make his lectures fun. He would inspire you to think in various ways which is required in a subject like this. Be ready to work really hard and one would be able to learn a lot during this course.

Over past years, he has lost enthusiasm to teach. (I also saw his lectures from a year back). Covers topics in a very fast manner, therefore teaching a select few in a class of 120. Even though I scored the highest possible grade in this subject (Thank you CLRS), his lectures are more like revision material after studying CLRS not vice versa.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Tests are totally random, not a t all what should be given at Masters level. Needs to teach much better. Pretty rude and doesn't teach well.
I just loved this course and I believe it has a lot to do with his teaching.
The class is taught with great enthusiasm, which is communicable.

All I want to say is that though this course is a little bit harder than an ordinary class, because this one requires a lot of thinking, you will surely get good grades if you work hard. Homework is a good practice. Besides, this course is really useful for job interviews.
Amazing lectures and is really clear with his concepts. Recommended!

Decent lecturer (skips a lot of material, doesn't explain everything). Exams are pretty difficult. Terrible grader (even if you get part b right, if part a is wrong you get no credit at all). Exam averages were roughly 45, 70, and 55. He curves at the end but not many students get As.
The professor is quite reasonable; simulates your interest in the subject and motivates and challenges you to imply your own thinking.

Dr. Ungor is one of the best CS professors at UF (there aren't that many great ones). He's really passionate about algorithms and can really inspire the computer scientist in you. You may not have an easy time, but I promise you Ungor is teaching you to become a world class computer scientist. If you want to be average, don't take Ungor.
Bad grading
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is an excellent teacher. He will not spoon feed and make you work hard to understand things clearly. I leaned a lot in this course.
He teaches with passion, and gives amazing lectures and challenging mid term questions.

His lectures are amazing. I usually hated the amount of homework he gave each week, but it helped me to prepare for exams. Exams are a bit tough tough. Some questions he gave are not solvable in polynomial time during exam. Despite the tough exams, he is very generous in grading.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It was an amazing experience to analyse algorithms with Alper. He is an excellent professor who infuses so much of enthusiasm for the love of algorithms. And he knows his work so well that he answers almost all questions himself.
He is an excellent professor

Albeit he was an amazing lecturer who always delivered highly entertaining and interesting lectures, I really didn't like it when he gave extremely long quizzes and basically undoable tests in terms of difficulty. I feel like he needlessly challenges us,while we're still learning the material. Try to avoid, or get ready to be tested every week.

The professor is very knowledgeable in the field of algorithms, that greatly helps whenever we have questions or we don't understand something. It was a great experience. For people who like algorithms and geometry, it's an excellent course.

Excellent lecturer. Really wants his students to succeed which is a rare quality of distinguished professors. Office hours were helpful. I always knew what my grade was. He was always up to date with his lectures and assignments. Graded frequently. Excellent guy all around. Textbook is essential. Course itself is solid. Very necessary for Comp Sci
Tough class, but very clear expectations and plenty of opportunities to bring your grade up.

He is one of the best professors I've had at UF. The material is difficult and the class is super demanding, but if you put in the work, you will do well. Lecture slides and even discussion section slides are posted online. You should complete all of the suggested problems (even though it's not graded) if you want to do well. This is NOT an easy A.

Even though I did not do as well as I wished I would have done in the course, I do not blame the professor at all. He is very intelligent and explains everything in detail. Most interesting class I have taken so far.

Expects a lot of his students but gives plenty of extra credit. Do the homework he assigns and study hard. One bad thing is that he gives quizzes that are about as hard and long as the tests. Makes it feel like there's always a big exam coming up. Fair and very kind professor. Clearly passionate about the subject and teaching it.

The course is challenging but also stimulating and overall a great course. Don't take it if you want an easy grade though. Great professor, best I have had so far. The professors enthusiasm and understanding of the material made me want to go to class and learn about the subject.

This is a very difficult course. Dr. Ungor did make many attempts to make our success easier. However with such a hard class I don't think he could have handled it better. He speaks clearly, presents topics and concepts in a logical manner, and asks relevant questions throughout lecture to keep the students engaged.

I honestly enjoyed going to class.  He made lectures entertaining and they were pretty clear.  The discussion section for this class was also very helpful.  I went to his office hours before an exam and he did a detailed review of all the questions that were asked but only 6 people showed up.
Interesting class on Geometry Algorithms. Expert professor with deep understanding. Clear lectures and slides.

Ungor is a great prof, smart, inspiring and occasionally funny. Tests are hard but gives some bonus points on each exam. HWs are optional but excellent way to prepare for the exams. hoping to take more classes with this guy.

Quizzes were basically tests in terms of difficulty.  Only 6 grades in the class (3 Quizzes and 3 tests) which it pretty difficult, but each test had bonus points, and most of the problems were similar to home works.  Overall pretty nice class.
One of the best professors I came across. Amazing lectures. Keep up with classes and H/W's - papers should not be tough!
Tough in grading but have clear expectations.
Amazing teacher I gained so much from his classes. He explains each topic very nicely. The exams are hard be well prepared.

The one main thing I say about Professor is his explanation in class. What an amazing lecture  videos we have! Mainly P vs NP, and approximation topics, I  wouldn't have understood so clearly with out his explanation.

He is a very good teacher, explains really well. He has a well defined course structure ans is very specific about the course. He makes sure the tests and assignments are challenging for the students. Only take his course if you have interest in the subject otherwise his course will be very tough to clear. He is very helpful in general.

Awesome and extremely professional teacher. His work ethic and class definitely changed the way I view academics; I used to think all that mattered in school was getting an A's but he helped show me value of the material and that has resulted in me having increased interest and dedication to all of future classes and academic endeavors.

I liked the lectures. The topics are interesting and the professor is enthusiastic about the material. He encourages participation and often asks leading questions to help students feel engaged. You should attend this class, and definitely do the homework. The tests are a bit of a time crunch and you will need to have had the practice.
Great teacher. Test were hard but exactly what should be expected. Taken from homework problems and practice problems.

His lectures were Concise while still covering all the topics in a healthy enough depth to gain an understanding of the material. If it was clear that the students weren't understanding the topic, he would take time out of the lecture to make sure it was understood.  The Homework wasn't graded, but it was very necessary in order to do well on test.

Great teacher, hard exams. he's one of the most professional lecturers I've had, he comes to class prepared. The homework isn't for a grade but you wont pass unless you do it well and understand the concepts.
Solid Teacher

Dr. Ungor is a great professor. He uses powerpoint slides as a base, but expands on them a lot so it is very helpful to go to class. Very clear in his explanations and helpful. If you do the homework and understand it tests aren't that bad. Definitely recommended!
Hard demanding but Worth it

I heard bad rumors about him prior to taking the course, but let me tell you he is the best professor you could have for this course. The other professors make the class more difficult than it needs to be (it's already difficult enough) and are much more strict on grading. Yes, the material is difficult but he tries to make it understandable

Very interesting course, but tries to cover too much. Always compares progress against previous semest. and will gloss over material if we're "behind." Exams hard. Grades by "clustering," but I would say fair. The book is great. Sometimes he uses too many pronouns/idioms in lecture - makes lecture confusing. EDGE students could have hard time.
