reviews.comment: Overall I really like Dr. Keeran. He is patient and really helpful during office hours and class(he always walks around and will help you). If you put in the work in Calc 2 it really is not that bad but it does require effort. The flipped classroom holds you more accountable and I think it helped me so I still recommend taking him
75% of grade is midterms and final exam rest is in class and discussion quizzes. No extra credit.

Best professor at UF in my opinion. He genuinely cares about his topic and his students. Was the class itself extremely difficult? Yes. And his grading scale (no A-) did not help. But he is definitely willing to help and is in general just a funny and sweet guy.

Keeran "teaches" by linking you to online video lectures of someone else teaching (which is very fast paced and hard to grasp) and doesn't really "teach" in class. Class time is used to work on problems about the lectures you were supposed to watch online. It requires a lot of self studying *every* week, so be prepared for a lot of work.

Keeran was honestly a really sweet professor and gave helpful feedback on proofs without just outright giving you the answer. The class itself is extremely difficult imo but Keeran really doesn't want to see you fail and will definitely help you out during office hours. The lectures can get a bit boring but they're vital to passing the class.

Great one on one help provided during office

I really like Dr. Keeran as a person. He's a very cool guy who's obviously smart and knows his stuff. His lectures at the start of class always greatly clarified the online lectures (flipped classroom). Calc 2 is what you make of it; redo worksheets, homeworks, and past exams a week before the midterms and you'll do fine.

His class was flipped, so we would watch lectures beforehand (I didn't bc I already knew the material), then he would do a brief summary at the beginning of the period and we worked together in groups on worksheets. I didn't spend much time on this class. You need to know the material well for exams. Funny and helpful, but not always understanding.

Keeran is a solid lecturer and decent professor. His class (at least when I took it) was exam heavy, but the exams were similar enough to the homework problems that I felt prepared without having to study a whole bunch.

While Keeran is not the world's best Calc professor, he's not bad either. Keeran is a perfectly fine professor who cares about his students and the subject he is teaching. He may not be the most enthusiastic, but he is always available to answer questions, especially in his flipped environment.

Keeran teaches a flipped classroom setting, and his brief lectures are perfect for if you had already taken calculus at high school. Very test heavy class so study, and Keeran himself can be funny at times

Look: Calc is going to be hard no matter who you get. Keeran might not have the best lectures (especially if you're in his flipped classes) but ultimately he's not that bad for calculus and together with the TA's they'll answer most if not all of your questions.

reviews.comment: Professor Keeran's class itself was not terribly difficult. It was a flipped classroom style class so mostly everything was completed at home. However, the time spent in class was mandatory and quite useless. He was super unpleasant and rude most of the time and always in a bad mood. Honestly don't recommend.

Professor Keeran was frustrating. I was in a flipped classroom setting so we would  watch lectures and then go into class for review and he would just give a worksheet and walk around. If someone asked for help, his explanations were minimal and he didn't provide a lot of practice exams. Attendance was mandatory and it wasn't even worth it.

I took the flipped version of this class but the professor does small recap lectures at the beginning of class which was helpful for reinforcing the material. I used Study Edge for the tests in this class; the tutors do a really great job at breaking down the topics so that you really understand it and know how to apply the knowledge.

Took this class as a flip classroom. However, he would still give mini lectures that were useful to understanding concepts. If you have questions, he is able to explain well. Make sure to do previous exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nice guy, really good at explaining the material in a short time. Flexible for office hours, and the exams aren't terrible if you do the review worksheets and previous exams.

I had Professor Keeran for linear algebra and calc 1, and he is by far my favorite math professor. His lectures are very clear and concise with plenty examples. I would highly recommend taking any of his classes.

Keeran is a pretty chill guy. He makes an effort to learn your name and help you with any questions. Doing well on the tests are really dependent on understanding the worksheets handed out in class. (if you don't finish them in class, I would go to the math tutoring center and work through the rest).

Professor Keeran uses a flipped-classroom so you watch your lecture at home and do worksheets with partners in class. The video lectures aren't very good but he gives a brief summary in class which is extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: In my opinion Professor Keeran is a great choice for students at UF. He is a really nice guy and even made an effort to learn everyone in my 100 person class names. There's a fair amount of homework but nothing too crazy. Professor Keeran is also very helpful in office hours.

reviews.comment: You'll learn how to write proofs to his liking or you will fail this class. His grading is brutal. There is no gray area/forgiveness. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't let the other reviews scare you away from taking Professor Keeran. In my honest opinion, he is a great teacher. I highly recommend this teacher.
Never curves anything, extremely tough grader on homeworks too.

Do not recommend. reviews.comment: Dr. Keeran is extremely knowledgeable, he makes calculus 3 seem easy. "Seem" being the operative word. Keeran is a pretty spicy fella, but if you can make it past the rough exterior, theres golden melty goodness inside. Dont expect him to bring you soup when youre sick, but he gives EC on every test and drops a bunch of quizzes/homework grades. Class was easy and doesnt require outside resources. reviews.comment: The calc 3 series at UF is pretty standardized. I had him for lectures and he was great at answering student questions. His hitt questions are pretty easy. Plus he would always talk about the alligator!

Great lecturer. Personally, I did not attend class much but still received a 98% with high grades in every test. If you choose to skip class like I did then be prepared to watch the lectures online and study the homework.
He's a great professor who knows how to teach the material and keeps you engaged throughout the lecture. Overall works with you to make sure you know what you're doing.

Keeran was a very great teacher, however, his exams are VERY HARD and if you bomb one that's pretty much it for you. On my exams I got an 80, an 86, a 60 and on the final I got 100. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easy class but there's a clicker question every lecture so attendance is kinda mandatory.

Dr. Keeran is tough, but fair. He's strict but has a dry sense of humor that makes class more bearable. The exams are tough but doable if you put the time in to study. I would pick Dr. Keeran over flipped-class for sure.

reviews.comment: Keeran is a great Calc 1 professor. He is much better than the other calc professors who teach a flipped classroom style calc. Keeran is the best calc professor you will have access to, even though he is the toughest. He makes a big portion of the exam, so being in his class is being the main test maker. He seems like he hates teaching and is always in a bad mood, but that might just be his personality because he is super sarcastic. He also kind of looks like the food critic from Ratatouille. He writes faster than I can think and is pretty bad at explaining most things. If you have taken calc before you're fine. If not, don't take his class.

Keeran's a good and funny lecturer. However, exams are tough and will test heavily your high school math. If you are any type of nontraditional student who took high school many years ago, you need to review that stuff and be sure to do it quickly on exams, because it will appear in many questions even if it doesn't appear on lecture or homework.

Keeran is a solid choice of a professor- fair exams, not a lot of homework, and pretty helpful all around. He stops lectures frequently to make sure students are following along and answers any questions that come up during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Keeran is a great professor who makes sure you are going to class and doing your work. However, if you want to truly succeed in his class I would strongly recommend using Study Edge to heighten your performance. I used study edge and got an A in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best math teachers I have ever had. He explained things making sure his students understood the concepts. His tests were not easy. He is not an easy A. reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His dry and sarcastic jokes definitely make the class more bearable. However, don't expect an easy A in this class. Do all the practice homework and memorize the theorems. He'll say don't but if you want to pass, you should.

I do not recommend Keeran. He is not very nice at all, and is demeaning to the students. Make sure you attend class, as the clicker questions are every class and you can only miss certain ones. Take someone else for calc if you have to take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is not that bad if you go to the lectures and actually pay attention, since his tests are basically based off of his lectures. I never did any of the additional homework aside from the webassign and I did fine.

Keeran is a decent professor. There's no real ambiguity about how he grades and what he expects of you for exams. reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures are great and concise. He is pretty funny and I loved his newspaper stories. There are a decent amount of clicker questions, so go to class. Go to class, do your homework, and do practice exams and you will pass. He is a really great professor, I would definitely take him again.

Keeran is a real simple guy who likes to make jokes. He truly does care about his students and tries his best to explain the math the best he can. Attendance is mandatory with clicker points and there is homework due every week but the class was very manageable and straightforward.

He's a cool guy and makes his lectures concise. If you like math like me, this class is not a problem and should only take you no more than a couple hours a week of homework and studying. If you don't like math, than it is probably the class that that is going to be hard, not the teacher.

Keeran is honestly a good math professor. He knows what he's teaching and tries his best to get a lecture hall of 500+ students to understand an already hard subject. Study Edge is also a great supplement for this class as it gave me extra practice and clarified chapters that I was confused on. If you show up to class and learn you'll be fine.

Keeran is a great professor. He definitely knows the material and teaches it well. Expectations are VERY clear and the class is well organized. Exams matched the lecture notes. Do not waste your time with study edge. Studying the lectures will get you an A.

Keeran really cares about his class and his students. This class taught me a lot and you have to keep up with the class to get the best grade possible. Study well before each of the exams. At first, I was worried Calc 1 would be too difficult since I had only taken Pre-Calc prior to coming to UF, but Dr. Keeran does a great job at teaching the material. reviews.comment: Keeran doesn't overcomplicate calculus and the exams were very easy. There is every discussion, but they are only two questions and they mimic examples from the lectures. He takes the time each class to crack a joke and makes math a little more interesting.

Keeran's lectures are helpful and relate to the homework assignments. He gives a reasonable amount of homework and he's always open to answering your questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Would take again

reviews.comment: Keeran thoroughly explains all concepts and gives solid answers to even the most basic of questions. His exams stick to what has been taught and he will let you know specific concepts and problems that are important. As a bonus he is rather amusing too.
He is very straightforward and reasonable. The exams cover stuff that you actually learn in class; if you know the material, you should do well on the exams.
Just show up to lectures and do your homework and youll be fine
Please look inward.

Worst experience in a class ever. Calc 3 in and of itself isn't difficult, but Keeran makes it  1000% more difficult than it needs to be. HIGHLY DO NOT RECOMMEND.

I didn't even have Keeran as a lecturer, he was just the main professor for calc 3. He puts multiple tricks into one question just to try and trick you. Keeran takes Calc 3 and makes it more difficult than it has to be. Be prepared to work for the grade you want. He only gives you one practice test and it's always much easier than the test you actually  take. I would take someone else if you can

reviews.comment: I love his lectures. They're super clear and easy to follow. Sometimes he goes a little fast through the examples, but if you ask him to clarify anything he will. Take the homework seriously!! It can really bring your grade up if you do well on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: if you do work youll pass 100%
Be ready to work for an A. Exams make up 70% of your final grade and are very conceptual. He moves fast during class, so you have to stay on top of the material. Overall, he's a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He gives hard tests. There is no dropping test grade which is why some people do bad (including me). I did good in 2 of the three exams. The final was my worse exam though but I didn't prepare for ir.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The subject matter is not complicated but it's important to understand concepts if you want to pass. Study Edge is a great source for establishing the concepts as well as for computational review. Also, don't underestimate his multiple choice, one question can change letter graded significantly.

GREAT Prof!! Lectures are super fast, so don't worry if you don't get it right away. Expect to work for an A, this is Calc 3, after all. I took notes on the book and made study guides for the exams and ended up with an A. He's super helpful during office hours, even if you ask vague questions about larger concepts. Love his dry humor. 10/10

Keeran is a good professor and I love his dry humour. Just keep up with homework assignments and do practice exams before exams and you should be fine. Everyone else who rated him as awful are just salty because they made the class harder for themselves.

He made calculus III harder than it needed to be. He forces his students to learn the theory and definition of calculus. Most of the  exams were on the theory, almost  65%. As for his TA, he was condescending and rude. He did not respond to email. It took many trips to his office hrs for his peer to tell him to set a schedule.
Horrible. Condescending. I did not find him fair. Hard tests. Lightly touches upon topics.

Professor Keeran is very knowledgeable and explains the process needed to solve each problem in an understandable manner. For exams,  pay special attention the concepts as they will be heavily tested on exams. He is by no means a bad professor and if you have good study habits and put reasonable effort  into the homework, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Keeran is a funny man and has a lot of knowledge on the subject.  The class and test is hard, but if you study, do the practice problems, and have an extra source such as Study Edge to supplement the material, you should be fine. If you are having trouble understanding the lectures, I definitely recommend Study Edge.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Would rather play in traffic than take this class again
One of the worst calc teachers at Uf.   He's absolutely terrible.   His tests are made to trick you and are very difficult.   And stupid
I really did not like professor Keeran. He is nice but monotone and does not teach very well. His tests are very difficult and concept based. They are made to trick you which is frustrating.

Keeran is the kind of teacher where you will need to do example problems over and over again. He does not truly go in depth in lectures rather he just gives the overall lesson but then moves on. You must go to class and keep up. I got through this class with Study Edge because of the endless problems they gave us.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: so hard, so helpless, so disappointment
Great teacher, keep up and you'll have no problem

This was my first exposure to Calc. 3.I ONLY ever did recommended textbook problems & WebAssign & only used the lecture notes & got a solid A.  Keeran was clear since day 1 about staying on track, so I did just that. This class is 50-50 on calculations and concepts, so study both. Calc. 3 is what it is, & Keeran did well in teaching the material.
He doesn't explain concepts very fully. Rather, he gives you the formula and explains the theory behind it quickly. Office hours are somewhat helpful, but I wish he would give more practice problems.

Overall, great lecturer, frequently adds humor to make the class more interesting, but be sure to pay close attention to the concepts word-by-word since they will show up on exam MC+FR. Try to find extra resources (StudyEdge + past exams) since only one practice test and some supplemental book problems are given in weeks prior to exams.
Really self-absorbed, very unhelpful, and extremely unaccommodating
very standard calculus course, and you can get through without having to recall equations from older geometry courses
Great Prof, amazing lectures, clear and straightforward exam which test knowledge and not trick.

He is a really great professor. I always understood the professor in class but I never felt like I had enough examples to be able to pass the exams. I used study edge for extra practice and ended up with an A.

Preparing for exams can be annoying. He is clear but the material gets tougher as the class goes on.  taking it right after MAC 2312 helped.  Study edge made a helped when i was preparing for exams and gave a lot of extra problems to do.

I was always good at Calc in high school, both in practice and conceptually. I took Calc 3 fall of freshman year and I thought it was easy to get an A, but conceptually Calc3 is a bit tough, and I didn't make an effort to understand it. Only cared about the A. Keeran was a good lecturer but I never went to class. Tests are easyfair.

Dr. Keeran teaches very clearly and evenly-paced. I took Calculus 3 with him right out of high school and though testing was harder, I moved right into his lectures without skipping a beat. He teaches high level material using a high school-comparable method.
tests are definitely fair

Initially, I had a different view of how this class was. While it is still challenging to a degree, the course got better as the year went on, although the material got tougher. After the first exam, after gaining insight on proper studying methods for exams, things gradually improved, although still, one must make an active effort on hisher part.

Calc 3 is a relatively challenging subject but Keeran is really clear and answers questions well. The class is fair and he's got some of the greatest dad jokes I've ever heard. Seriously, worth taking for your chance to hear a dad joke in between trying and failing to understand vector fields.

Keeran's lecture are a bit dull, but they are very clear and straightforward. He gives tons of opportunities to ask questions during lectures as well. He has super dry humor which I personally loved. The tests can be difficult if you don't properly prepare for them and really understand the definitions of the material. Overall Dr. Keeran is the man

Taking him this semester and he's upfront about how the class (starts easy, gradually gets harder). Haven't made it to all the classes and still do very well on exams, despite there usually being a conceptual question on an exam where he can try to trick you with his wording. Went to his office hours once and he's very inclined to help.

I took one exam and I'm already incredibly flustered with how things have gone. He tests hard, but during lectures, he says things will be very easy. Plus, he doesn't offer a lot of extra credit, so it's hard. Coming from a student who loves and has high interest in Calculus, this class was made difficult by him.

The BEST math teacher I have ever had. Lectures are super clear-- highly recommend buyingprinting his lecture notes before hand. Tests are very fair & similar to the practice ones he posts online. Go to class for the notes & clicker questions, do all the webassign, go to discussion and you're almost guaranteed an A with little effort.

Straight forward professor, go to class and take notes. Definitely recommend getting a copy of the notes he uses from targetcopy. The class gets much harder as the class goes on, study hard for the final.

The lectures can be somewhat boring but he makes the content very clear and easy. Tests aren't hard if you do the homework and many of the test questions are similar to the ones in the book. He kept the class very entertaining and interesting. Overall a great professor.
Very clear and organized lectures. Enjoyed his humor and kept me interested during lectures. Very straight forward exams and not too bad if you pay attention and put a little time in.

Dr. Keeran is the best! He actuall cares about his studentsand he's not a pretentious jerk like other upper level math professors are. He will help you with writting your proofs and he's not a grading Nazi.If your confused about any of the material, he's excellent during office hours.

I am not the best at math, but taking this class with Keeran made me feel as if I was. He made each concept extremely simple to understand. Be sure to do all of the homework prior to attending class and when studying, use the book! A lot of the test questions are similar to those in the book.

I took Calculus in high school so I did not find the material hard. Class is mandatory because there are clicker points. I went to class and didn't take notes, I only went for the participation points. If you have Study edge its extremely helpful.
Very clear lectures! Very approachable in office hours. Show up for class, take notes, and the tests are very straightforward! Loved him!!

Overall Dr.Keeran is approachable. I did not anticipate to receive the grade I got. The final took me by surprise. There are no curves and no drops. The first exam was fluff, but the level of difficulty will change dramatically. Study edge is useless for this class. Best advice, study and read the book. He's not the best, but certainly not theworst

I heard that this used to be a good class, but there was a new professor this semester and he was super disorganized. There should have been a curve in the end to compensate for the quality of instruction, but he refused to curve so a lot of people got below a C. Take this class at community college if you need it for critical tracking!

He has been one of my favorite teachers here at UF so far. He is a very straight forward guy and will not pull any dirty tricks on tests. Linear algebra can be a bit dry (although really easy) but he is entertaining with his corny jokes. Just go to class and do the homework and you will get an A without much effort (for this class at least)

Linear Algebra is a pretty dull subject, but he does his best to make lectures at least somewhat entertaining. The subject material is not very challenging, it just takes consistency. Lecture attendance is not necessary: read the book, do the onine homwork, review all before the test. Oh, and start the Matlab projects early. Good luck!

He'll probably tell you this on the first day, but it's true: Go to class and do the homework. Exams were mostly variations of homework problems and MATLAB assignments. Easy class as long as you don't slack off, and if you like bad jokes he tells A LOT of them.
He's fine but can't keep his eyes open. Really tries to make funny sarcastic jokes. I go for clicker questions, do SE and Tutoring Center and get As.
Professor Keeran is a great teacher and is very helpful. His lectures are very thorough and as long as you go to class, you shouldn't have a problem getting an A.

He has a clever sense of humor, however, he goes really fast through lectures. One is always ahead of an exam by at least one extra lecture. One needs to be able to write quickly too in order to keep up with his notes.

I took Calc I with him here at UF and he was great! The lecture notes were all from Smith, but he only went over the important examples during class and skipped the theory that could potentially confuse people. He's very nice and helpful, as well as encouraging. Also he's funny! Take him!! Easy class.

Professor Keeran is a really good lecturer. His notes are very clear. You just have to make sure you attend class regularly (or you'll have to go to office hours and get the notes there). Do the homework regularly even if it's not mandatory; it helps you stay on track when preparing for the exam!

Didn't go to class and barely pulled a C with using Cramster and his answer solutions he has online. The times I did go to class the notes I took never really seemed to help me. Not a terrible option for a teacher but if you can choose someone different I would.
GO TO CLASS. or else you will most likely fail. It is impossible to cram for his test 2 or 3 days before it.
In college it's rare to find a professor who can actually teach. Keeran is a great teacher. Do the HW, GO TO CLASS, and you will have an A. Explains everything very well. Take him.
LOVE HIM. he was definitely the reason I got an A.
Awesome professor. One of the best in the math dept. Show up, do your hw, do the practice test and you are pretty much on your way to an A. Brilliant!
Fair but pretty easy. Just pay attention and show up to class.

Willard is the bomb! He is actually a secret super hero at night.  But seriously he is a great teacher. To do well in his class all you have to do is show up and do the homework. And he is really funny during lectures sometimes.

He's legitimately a super hero. He's the epitome of a math professor: giant glasses, lanky, chalk all over his hands...but what most people don't know is that he transforms into a superhero at night. And he cracks hilarious jokes during class. Seriously, TAKE THIS CLASS.
You can't ask for a better teacher, he is extraordinarily cool and only asks that you pay attention in class and do the homework.

Keeran is a champ. Uses plenty of examples, is humorous, and genuinely knows his material. Effecient: won't waste your time. Definitely the reason why I did so well in calculus 2. Practice problems are a necessity as well.

He is actually a really good teacher. He has a bit of theory to lectures at times, but it's not that important to note. When he actually goes into detail about how to do the problems, he's great. He is very detailed and does lots of practice problems. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS IF YOU EVER NEED HELP!!! He is actually a  great guy outside of school.

Keeran teaches like a boss and uses lots of examples. All the scathing reviews here can be explained by the stupidity/laziness of the posters and are unwarranted. Keeran no longer gives multiple choice exams, and he gives partial credit. His test ?'s came from easy homework problems and lectures. Go to class, do the homework, and you'll be fine.

I was a little afraid to take this professor after reading some of the postings, but he is very good. If you listen and do the homework problems, you will be fine. I even took him for another class. He teaches by examples which is a good way to learn math.

Before taking Keeran's class I read this website and was afraid. There is nothing to be afraid of though. I got an A in the class and never did any of the homework, Keeran himself prepared me for the tests. He teachers through example, and that is exactly how I learn best.

I had to take this class twice, the 1st time in a lecture hall 2nd time in a small class. You have to do the homework if you want a chance of passing this class. It is easier to pass in the smaller setting cause the tests are not multiple choice. If you dont get a small section, change sections or teachers!

Believe what most people are saying. Keeran makes the subject harder than it needs to be. He is a straightforward lecturer, despite being dull, but his lectures don't give you a good feel for what's on the tests. Study from the book a lot, doing practice problems from there. That will best prepare you. If you can, take with a different professor.

Great lecturer, this guy knows his stuff. He gives great examples and you really understand the material. Problem is his tests are ridiculously tricky, not hard, tricky. Go to class, office hours, and do all the homework/practice test. I scraped a C+. Work really hard, you'll be ok. Final was nearly impossible. Only 4 tests, 25% each. Good Luck.

Awesome teacher. Love this guy. Tests are tough but fair. Great jokes making fun of diff eq and math. Ended up getting a C+, thought I was on track for a B+ or even A- but oh well. This class was very enjoyable despite it being diff eq (diff eq in general = boring). Love this guy. Almost want to be a math major to have him again.

This class is very difficult, but if you do the homework, go to class and office hours you'll be okay. He posts the homework solutions and answers, as well as reviews and past tests online, which help A LOT. Unfortunately, he wont be teaching this class next semester, and he said that the next person is using web assign. Good luck!

WORST MATH TEACHER EVER! I hate this class. I have never done poorly in a class until this one. This teacher is terrible. His tests are extremely hard and don't have a good format for a math test. My advice would be to wait until he is out of here to take this class because there is no way he will stick around with such low class averages.
Will never understand why he gave a majority multiple choice exam in a math class. Is a bit of a jerk, too.

He is a good prof. and all you have to do is appreciate his dry sense of humor and dont be fooled by his monotone voice. His tests werent bad but math is one of my stronger subjects. If math is not your thing do the HW and go to TZ and you will be fine. The only bad thing about this class is you grade consists only of tests.

This class is not hard if you go to his lectures and take notes. His tests start out easy and then get harder as the semester goes on. He is very helpful if you need help and go in during his office hours. I went to class and did the homework and had no issues

His test are extremely hard. He's extremely boring and hard to listen to. On one of the test, our class had a 57% average and he didn't care. I ended up dropping the course and definitely don't want to take it with him again!.

Keeran's class wasn't easy by any means. He speeds through lectures, shows little to no emotion, and is always extremely serious and borderline rude to his students. However, the real "professor" for this class (Zach from TZ) knows his stuff and he helped a whole lot on the exams. A's are possible if you work hard enough/took calc in high school.
Hardest tests I've taken at UF. I understood the material inside and out and still did poorly because the multiple choice exams were so tricky.

Keeran is an absolute disaster as a teacher. This was his 1st semester at UF. He was previously employed at the prestigious Santa Fe Comm. College. Dont let that fool you, he tries to prove himself at the big boy school by being unreasonable. He refuses to use Elearning, and had no office hours during finals week. BEWARE

Terrible class which is made far worse by the professor.  The lectures are impossible to get through, and every test question is aimed to trick you.  This paired with the incapacity to reply to  student's emails, and general disregard for them made this class hell.

This guy is worthless.  Let's see, where do I begin?  He has no TA's, his classes are overcrowded with 350+ students.  You can't contact him by email and he is hesistant to help students.  I am an honors student taking this class for grad school admission.  You will not do well in his class.  I've passed rock hard turds easier than this class.

A very fair teacher.  The first 3 test were reasonable and he was helpful if problems stemmed during exams.  I thought the final would be on the same level as the previous test, I have never been so wrong in my life. Study efforts for final should be tripled!
His exams are designed to make you fail. The material is easy but he makes tests impossible to finish in one hour. Do NOT take him if you can!!
Great lecturer, explains the material very well even though he is a very boring/droll teacher. His tests are multiple-choice and EXTREMELY difficult. I do NOT recommend him.

DO NOT TAKE HIM... take this class the following semester but do not take it with this guy! Although he teaches very well and his lectures are just flawless, his exams will make you regret you stayed in the class. The material is easy but the exams are designed so you fail. (your exam scores will go down exponentially as the semester advances)

completly nuts and paranoid about cheating! one of the driest and most boring styles of lecturing i have had at UF. His tests are very tricky with no room for error b/c they are multiple choice. One missed ? drops u a letter grade on a test. Study a lot to be sure u know the material! I would avoid taking him and get someone else if possible

GREAT teacher! very clear and doesn't go to fast or too slow. the only thing that's difficult are the exams. make sure you practice a lot to get your speed up or else you won't finish in time. 7 MC and 2 FR for each of the 3 exams and then the final is all MC. if you need diff eq's, take keeran!

Knowledgeable, thorough, fast, organized, and not prone to mistakes. Wrote out solutions to all problems and posted them the first day of class, which was immensely helpful. He obviously cares about teaching and is very aware of his mannerisms (too aware?). Tests are mostly multiple behind the methods, and if you miss class you'll be lost.
Had him for diff eqns. Good lecturer. Exams are extremely difficult. Had to drop the class. Don't take a class with him unless you plan on devoting a ton of time to it. Otherwise you will fail.

Summer class, everyday. The programming assignments were killer, and took way too much time to figure out, but MATLAB is a hard language. The lessons he taught were very easy to understand. His tests are harder, but I definitely learned a lot in this class. Definitely a teacher you want to take if you want a challenge.

He is an amazing teacher and can actually make you learn the subject. Unfortunetly, his tests are not something that show you know it. The only grades in the class are 4 tests, and that includes the final. Test are majority multiple choice and have 7-9 questions per test. Something as simple as an alegbra/sign mistake can lower your grade.

Clear and to the point. But takes his time to make sure all tricky problems of a concept are covered in the lecture. Multiple-choice tests can be both a blessing and a curse depending on how well you study for the material. Relatively easy tests. It's a great class if you like to slack off and then study your @$$ off a week before the tests.

Good lecturer, easy to understand, but kind of boring sometimes. He is very helpful, willing to stop in the middle of class to answer students' questions. HW is optional but helpful. Tests are really hard but not impossible, and they're difficult to study for too. Teaches the material well, but the tests are killers.

Don't let the small number of questions your grade is based on frighten you.  He knows its a small number of questions so they are all generally easy, but do overstudy for each exam because one mistake brings you down a letter grade on multiple choice.  Nice teacher, cares if you do well or not.  Calc 2 is a breeze with him if you keep up.

I like his teaching style. Very straight forward and knows what he's doing. Very boring tho. Only talks monotone and never jokes or smiles. Only grades are tests and multiple choice so no room for error at all. You mess up your grades screwed. Tests are way harder then the practice ones and hes the most paranoid guy I have ever met about cheating.
Dry
Go to class, take advantage of office hours to get questions exam grades, and study the problems he assigns. Difficult class, but good professor.
my advice to all those who plan to take his class: be able to do all problems he assign, and be able to solve them QUICKLY!!! otherwise the exam is very straight forward.

Not a bad lecturer, but tests were extremely difficult.  The questions were often presented in a confusing way and most of them where multiple choice (no partial credit) and the tests were too long to be taken in the hour given.  Keep in mind your grade is based only on the tests.  He's not impossible, but try to get somebody else if you can.

Don't listen to the negative comments. I tried to go out of my way to figure out which diffyq and calc3 class he was teaching after taking him for calc 2. He is awesome, especially since many mathematics profs have somewhat of a language barrier. He is crystal clear in lecture (very prepared with many examples) and his tests are exactly like them!!

Took him for both calc 3 and diffEQ and both times I had to drop the class.  He's not a bad guy but his tests are terrible.  Multiple choice test means working 15 minutes on a problem and getting 0 points because you either made a small error, or you couldn't decipher his cryptic answer choices in the short time given.  Avoid if possible.

Do not take this man. He is a nice guy and all but is extremely paranoid. Assumes the class cheats, even before first exam. Muliple choice tests, no partial credit, promised homework, quizzes, and curves to help grade, never did any. Makes answer choices on tests look exactly the same on purpose. ok at teaching, testing style will hurt you severly.

for the most part this was an very easy class. all you need to do is know the material. you cant BS the tests. test averages around 72 74 64 and not sure about the final. Most people however did not know what they were doing going into these tests. if you know the material everything on the test is extremely straight forward nothing tricky
Awesome guy. He goes through the material pretty quick but makes sure you understand. Tests are just like the practice problems he goes over in class and HW. Take this class!

Keeran's amazing, probably the best math teacher I've ever had. He goes fast, but he has to to cover all the material. He's willing to explain anything even if only one person in the class needs it. His tests and quizzes are just like the homework. He also has a rather dry sense of humor.  Take him if you can!

Keeran was an okay guy overall.  At times spoke very fast, but always clarified things and stopped to answer questions.  Keeran crams the curriculum during the summer semester making the class very difficult!
He covered a lot of material, which made the class very hard.

Scott Keeran is an amzing calculus teacher. He is always avaible for help and office hours. And though things can get a bit awkward when someone angers him he usually has good class demeanor and a random joke thrown in here or there. His test are straight from the homework. Take him if you can!

Scott is the best! He is not exciting to listen to although he has a couple jokes up his sleeve. The tests come straight from the homework and are not tricky. If you do the homework (which isn't that much) you'll do great in the class.

Calc 3 was not my thing so obviously I'm biased. As far as teaching, Willard has the personality of a doorknob and completely fails at trying to captivate the interest of students. IMO a good professor can take a dry subject and make it palatable. Willard pretty much gives it to you straight whether you like it or not.
Great teacher.  Its as easy as a math course can be.  Direct, precise, and fair.  Not interested in busy work or working more than necessary.  Take him if you can.
if you have a choice, take any and all your math classes with him. he's the best!

His teaching is very direct and precise. It's easy to follow evewn though a little fast. He does examples and explains as much as possible. His tests are pretty straight-forward - from the HW and fair. He helps out as much as possible. One thing I didnt like though was that he collects homework randomly and gives quizzes randomly (although easy).
great teacher! if you do the homework, you'll ace the tests and quizzes. he's also very helpful during his office hours, so dont hesitate to go to him for help!
he explains the material  very clearly and is very willing to take any question from a student. great math teacher.
He gives lots of examples and his tests are direct and not tricky.

He is quite literally the best instructor I have ever had. He gives insightful feedback for my poems, and he is such a caring instructor that can be reached out to even after the course ends. He is just a wonderful human being who happens to be a great instructor.

This class gave me hope that my semester would be okay. Yes, it is an easy credit, but it's also so fun, inspiring, and a great time. The class goes by so fast every time, and the professor is one of the bests I've had. He is extremely kind and is extremely knowledgeable that it was admirable. He clearly loves what he does!

I ended up having William for both CRW1301 and CRW3310, and he is truly one of the best teachers I've had. The classes aren't hard. You get out what you put in, so if you want to become a better writer, put in effort. The papers are simple too. William creates a relaxed environment and is eager to help you. Go to office hours to talk to him!

He has a deep love for poetry that shines through all of his lectures. He is fun and passionate and brings the joy of poetry to his class. Taking creative writing with him is an enriching experience that has helped my creative abilities, and for that I am forever grateful.
Amazing class!!

William has absolutely been a pleasure to study under. He has done a wonderful job of creating a safe and fun class environment. He has a completely unserious disposition, but is incredibly passionate about writing, reading, and analyzing poetry. He will critique you honestly and effectively, and is genuinely driven by helping you be a better poet!

William was an amazing professor! Even while busy with graduate school, he made time for me and my peers. He is genuinely interested in the thoughts of his students and shows a real passion for poetry. I'm delighted I took this class and recommend him as a professor for all students looking to take a useful course in introduction to poetry.

Mr. Littlejohn-Oram is an incredible teacher who is enthusiastic about what he does. He made me feel comfortable in sharing my work and left great feedback. I learned so much about writing poetry, and he made the three-hour lectures very fun and stimulating. We did writing workshops and went over famous and unique poetry works during the classes.

This man genuinely cares about his students. You can bare your heart and soul into a poem, and then the critiques you get back will be genuine, thoughtful, and delicate in their delivery. He makes jokes and gives a short break in the middle of class if it's long. Genuinely wants to get to know you as a person, and overall very understanding.

My first B in college. The exams were all trick questions with little time to truly grasp what she was asking. She however gives you plenty of opportunities to better your grade. I felt the powerpoints and lectures were not helpful for the depth of knowledge we had to know to do well. The textbook was easier to understand (surprisingly).

The class was very straightforward. Your grade is dependent on 4 midterm exams and 1 cumulative final exam, but your lowest exam score is dropped. Exams are all multiple choice. She is very knowledgeable about the material, but her accent can make her difficult to understand. Content is only delivered via in-class lectures. Limited extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you pay attention in lecture, study the slides, and review the quizzes, you will do well. The content can get a bit boring at times, which may make this difficult. She offers iClicker extra credit and other random opportunities.

Very nice lady. Has a tick accent, but it didn't bother me too much. First 2 exams you will do well if you understand the material. The last 2 exams were very math-heavy and you had to understand application more. Uses iClicker for mandatory participation and attendance. No homework, only quizzes online that are timed. You get a free exam drop.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: nah fade her. At first I thought accent was bad, but thats not the problem. The only problem is the fact that she gives very little explanation of content, but when you ask a clarifying question about a topic she will just explain it the exact same way. Nice lady but fade fade fade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Wang is great at lecturing and communicating with her students what information we are expected to know and what is coming up in the course schedule. There are plenty of small extra credit opportunities and optional textbook practice problems. There is a lot to learn, but she cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

Dr. Wang is just amazing. Her lectures are so clear to understand and her exams are very fair. This is certainly not a breeze of a class but if you study her lectures well you will do just fine. She genuinely cares about student success and makes an effort to get to know everyones' names. She gives some extra credit and the final is optional.

Summer A: SUPER fast-paced. Prepare to study for hours every day (use quizlet, STUDY QUIZZES, create study guides). Exams are pretty fair. Attend her lectures for extra credit. Very responsive to emails, and gives help. I took the optional final, and found it easier than some of the exams we took! I got a B, but an A or B+ is doable.

Dr. Wang is easily one of the best professors I have had. The course material itself is not easy so you must study and put time in outside of class, but her lectures are pretty straight forward. The exams are not too bad as long you study the lecture slides. TONS of extra credit. Feels like the first time I actually learned material in a long time.

Super fast paced - there is lecture every single day for all of summer A. Attendance mandatory, there are T/F questions that show up word for word on the each unit exam. Quiz every day following lecture (good study tool for exams). Exams challenging but not impossible - know the PowerPoints well. Offers a ton of EC. I did not open the textbook once
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Wang is one of the best professors for a STEM class I have ever had at UF. She gives an insane amount of extra credit for going to class and participating in discussion boards. Her exams are very straight forward and come directly from her powerpoints, quizzes, and t/f questions. I wish Dr. Wang was my professor for all my classes tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is a gem. Very passionate and caring, there are very few professors like her. 10/10 person. Take this class its a very manageable A.

Very sweet prof, but the class itself is insane for Summer A. Usually an exam a week. It is easily the fastest paced class I have taken at UF. I had to study several hours a day just to make sure I understood the information. Lectures almost always go over class time. We will have a brand new lecture one day and have to take the unit exam the next.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wang is really sweet and caring, but she never finishes lectures on time and tends to fly through the lecture/ppt. You need to study and read the textbook because the lectures are fast paced and confusing.

Extremely caring is really understanding, we don't deserve her. She is sometimes confusing, but honestly I've never had a problem understanding the material. I've never opened the textbook, just focused on her slides, in class T/F questions, lecture quizzes, animations, and got an A on all of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: People who complain in this class clearly have a hard time finding time for the course. This is genetics, a UF STEM course, expect to put in some time!! Study the T/F (on exams), study lecture quizzes (similar to exam questions) and ask questions if you need to. Textbook is helpful to reinforce

She is sweet and caring for her students, available for questions. Yet, when material gets tough, she is hard to understand, and confusing as a lecturer. However, her straightforward exams (almost from lecture quizzes) make up for this deficit. Overall, not the best lecturer, but straightforward class if you study DAILY (summerA forces you to)

Nice prof, passionate about subject and really cares that students are able to learn it. Can be a bit of a confusing lecturer, but available for questions. Not many assignments, but gives optional replacement final & several extra credit pop quizzes. In your best interest to show up, a must for paper discussions days. Exams not easy, but not awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Take her! Best genetics professor at UF. Her course is straight to the point. Dr. Wang provides students with a lot of extra credit opportunities in the form of pop quizzes, so always attend class. If you study the lectures and go to class, an A is doable. Taking biochemistry before this class was a huge help.

Take her class! She gives so much extra credit and really cares about her students. Her exams are very fair and come straight from the power points. Expect to go to every class in case there is an extra credit pop quiz (only two questions) and also to take pictures of the T/F questions that will show up WORD FOR WORD on the exam.

She was great. Show up to class to get the T/F questions that are gonna be on the exam. She cares about her students and is always looking for improvements in her teaching. Lecture Quizzes online, study those they are on the exam. PPts are on the exam word for word (Multiple Choice) . Optional final to replace a test and it was super easy.

So caring, she reaches out after every exam to each student to discuss ur test grade. Her lectures are the ppts w/ blanks but u have to pay attention to fill in the blank. She makes it red and bolded so u can't miss it. Bonus pop quizzes: u get 0.5 even if u get the 2 q's wrong. Lecture Quizzes mimic the exam. Study the T/F. Easiest optional final.

Lots of extra credit, very caring professor. Go to class+ pay atention+ read power points and book (if you want) and very likely you will get an A. T/F questions given in class come in exam word by word (16 pts/exam of T/F). I read the book+ power points, T/F questions, and quizzes, but a friend read ppts without reading the book and got an A too.

Although the class was a Summer A Genetics course, I thought Dr. Wang did a pretty good job at teaching. She is generally regarded as the best AGR 3303 prof. The class moves fast and there usually is a test each week. I found the tests to be reasonably difficult but the lecture and attendance pop quizzes do help a great deal in the long run.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hard to understand. Blanks out the most important word of the powerpoint. Tests are all multiple choice with trick questions.

Stay up to date with all lectures daily, attend class for pop quizzes, and get ready to use YouTube and ultimately teach yourself. Her exams are extremely tricky, and you are expected to know every single thing in the textbook and her lectures. She sometimes does not show to office hours so beware of that, also. Poor experience.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took her class in Summer A, and although it was a fast-pace class, it was manageable. Grade consisted solely on tests, but she gave a lot of extra credit through pop quizzes. Also,  she asks T/F questions every class, which show up word for word on the exam, so make sure you go to class. All around, Dr. Wang is the best professor at UF.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This Professor is very niceand she gives out a great deal of extra credit if you attend class. The extra credit questions are usually her practice questions online and she always uses practice questions or very similar questions on her exams. If you study the slides and do her practice questions you should do well on the exams.

Class isn't mandatory but I recommend going because she gives T/F questions (some of which are word for word on the exam) and extra credit pop quizzes. I read the book to help clarify her notes and just looked over her powerpoint slides a few days before each exam. She isn't the best teacher but it's pretty easy to get an A in the class.

No complaints say about her teaching methods, the class was too fast paced & early in the day for my liking. Attendance is important (but not mandatory) because the PPTs on Sakai are not completely filled out & don't have the in-class T/F questions that go on the exam,  & she gives 11 extra credit pop quizzes which add up in the long run.

I took her Summer A course, and she's probably one of my favorite professors I've had at UF so far. Very kind, passionate about the subject, and she's so helpful in office hours. Just read the slides, her follow-up questions, and don't skip the extra-credit quizzes, as they'll be on the test. Getting an A really isn't hard if you don't slack off.

If you have to take genetics, take it with her.  The most fair class I have ever taken at UF.  I had to go to class, and I had to study, but I learned the material and got an A.  She really cares about students and her teaching.  Great class.  Helped a lot on the MCAT too.

Such a great teacher! She gives bonus pop quizzes if you attend class (33 bonus points!) She gives outlines for exams. Read the book and go over the outlines and review questions and you will do great! Very helpful and responds to emails within the hour. Has an accent but tries so hard to get you to understand. Overall great teacher! Take her!
Really kind and sweet professor! Lots of quizzes though so make sure you study

Without exaggeration, possibly the best Chinese professor in the country. Hard to imagine such a demanding and rigorous course taught in a better way by a better instructor. Waking up at 7am every day for the class was challenging and the persistent quizzes keep you working, but she is so nice and removes so much anxiety that you don't even notice.

Xu Han is an amazing and very understanding professor.She is a great teacher and I learned so much from her. You can tell she really loves her job and she makes me excited to go to class in the mornings. Hopefully I am able to get into her intermediate chinese class next semester. There are a lot of quizzes.

Best professor ever! want to minor in Chinese now :D
live laugh love xu laoshi

Professor Han Xu or Xu Lao Shi in class was the best Chinese professor I've had and I am taking her again this semester with an earlier time because I wanted her specifically. She is incredibly caring and truly values what is best for the student more than anything. Expect weekly homework and vocab quizzes that aren't overly difficult.

Xu laoshi was an outstanding professor and is one of the main reasons that I now want to pursue a minor in Chinese. She keeps the lectures light-hearted and fun, promotes class participation in a way that does not induce any anxiety, is extremely understanding, and whole-heartedly wants her students to succeed. I highly recommend this class.

This was my favorite class during my time at UF & its solely thanks to the teacher. She was such a good person to be around that it made the class significantly better. Both as a teacher and especially as a person, she's the best at UF. Very caring & passionate person, both about the class & students. She'll likely be my favorite undergrad teacher.

Xu Laoshi is incredible. Even if you have a background in Chinese, you will still learn something. Homework assignments every week with two quizzes per chapter; however Xu Laoshi is very accommodating.  If I could, I would take the class again with her.
Literally everyone agrees, best teacher hands down.  Makes a difficult language easy and goes at a comfortable pace.  If your considering her, stop, just get a seat.

Hands down the best teacher I had this semester. She wants everyone to succeed, and if you show you care, she'll help you. Got to office hours, show up to class, and participate. I can't wait to take her again next semester. Her lectures are always entertaining, and even if you have prior knowledge, you'll learn something new.

Amazing professor. Very very understanding, very lenient. The class is pretty difficult if languages isn't your thing, but she gives lots of resources to learn Chinese. Attendance is rly important if you want to do well, but only because the course material is pretty rigorous. No complaints about Xu Laoshi, would absolutely take her again!

Easily the best teacher I had all semester. She was very understanding of personal situations and almost always accommodated them. The course itself is a bit intensive since it's a language course, but she offers many chances to learn and exercise Chinese. Tests are rly important, and so is the HW (it counts for a good amount in the end).
Xu Laoshi is amazing! She is so nice and understanding! She is very clear about the quiz and test material. If you put in the effort, you will excel.

An absolute gem of a professor and human. Chinese is naturally a hard language but Xu laoshi makes the class enjoyable and as stress-reducing as possible. Not enough words I can say to describe how much of a star she is.

Xu laoshi was a wonderful professor for beginning Chinese. She is incredibly kind and always makes class fun to attend. Though her grading is not too tough, you will need to attend class, do the work, and practice Chinese--but that's always necessary for languages! If you are interested in taking Chinese, don't hesitate! She's amazing.

Although it was my first class every single morning, I find myself not minding waking up early to attend. The vocabulary may seem overwhelming at first, she makes it workable for any beginners. The tests are straightforward and content is well discussed. Xu Laoshi is a respectable individual.

Absolutely love her! She's extremely enthusiastic in class and really tries her best to engage her students. Also flexible with her teaching schedule so if the class asks for homework/exams to be pushed back, she is willing to adjust it for us. Most importantly, she is very caring. Super easy to talk to and not intimidating at all!

Absolutely love her. She genuinely cares about students and is an excellent teacher. She only speaks Mandarin in class and speaks juuuuuust above the students' level, which is exactly what you need to make you feel relatively comfortable while also pushing you forward. Best Mandarin teacher at UF.

I've had 5 different Chinese language teachers and Xu laoshi was EASILY the best. She's very caring and wants you to pass, but she will also challenge you to get better. You will be challenged, but class is very structured and she is very clear about her expectations. She's super personable and just an overall lovely person. I miss her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Would take again

reviews.comment: I had her for Intermediate Chinese and Advanced Chinese last semester, she has by far been my favorite Chinese teacher, just make sure to show interest in the class and she'll return the favor for you. She's was always very helpful with my questions.

Great teacher. Very stubborn so don't expect to get points back on tests or homework. Tests are fairly easy and there are plenty of opportunities to earn points elsewhere. Always go to class and try to get on her good side by participating often.

Xu Laoshi is the best!! She is really  nice, funny, caring, and helpful. She is an awesome teacher, she speaks only Chinese which is great for learning and somehow we all understand her too. I wish I could have her for all my Chinese classes, she's awesome
You need to read the book, exams are easy if you prepare and read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Might be the worst professor at UF. This guy still being allowed to teach is the worst thing to happen to UF since the shoe throw. In all my life, I've never seen a teacher just not grade the course. Both the final exam (40% of the grade) and semester-long project (another 20%) that we all spent time studying for and working on were just ignored.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CSE senior here, Xia was easily the worst. The final exam and project (65% of the final grade) were never released, only the final grade after the semester was over. The prof reads off slides and exams are needlessly difficult. Tip for survival: Jim Kurose (textbook author) videos on youtube. Kurose lectures better in half the time and he smiles.

Honestly, I found this class quite interesting, but mostly because of watching the textbook author's lectures on YouTube and reading the textbook. Professor Xia's lectures are dry and drawn out which make them hard to get through. The test questions are easier than the complex homework, but many felt like “trick questions” based on unclear wording.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Xia is very knowledgeable about computer networks. This class is a lot of reading and homework, but his lectures essentially go over the textbook with slides created by the authors. There are 6 homeworks, two exams, and one semester-long project. Start homeworks early and study several days out from exam and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, but the subject (Computer Networks) needs a lot of reading, and he evaluates a lot of things so requires doing a lot of work.

I took CNT5106c this year and was super scared the entire time,because of rate my professor reviews. He tells you what to expect upfront.If you read textbook,do the work,it's not that hard to get an A.He curved the grade quite a lot. My stats : 10 marks above the avg in the 1st exam , 5-6 marks below avg in 2nd,almost full in assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I tried to concentrate and listen to him, but he teaches so uninterestingly that you won't be able to get what he is trying to say. He gave a project on canvas without even giving proper guidance on it. He is very strict on deadlines for homework. He is not very interactive, and his way of teaching is very boring.

So I tried my best to do well in the class. I did really well on every hw, midpoint project, and in the upper quartile for the midterm score. He likes gatekeeping information as he never told us how he scaled the course grade, didn't show us our final exam grade (saw cheating), and final project grade. he curves base on others without transparency.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor's lectures are not good; I preferred the YouTube videos of the textbook's author. Homeworks aren't too bad if you don't wait until the last minute to start them. Exams are tough, and the project was very difficult and no guidance was given. He luckily curved a lot at the end of the semester, but you don't know what it will be.

Horrible. Final project is impossibly difficult with instructions that confuse more than explain. Other networks professors make the class 100% easier while Xia just copies stuff from the graduate version of the course. Unbelievable that UF allows this bad of a person to each.
Worst professor I have ever had the privilege of taking a class with. Class is entirely based on a project and two exams.

Easily one of the worst professors in the entire UF curriculum. The project is the most difficult I'd ever done, and you're given practically no guidance, like if you were dropped in the middle of the Amazon jungle and had to crawl your way back to civilization with one hand tied behind your back. Just sad, disparaging, and outright dreadful...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I have ever had. Does not teach well you have to read the book to do the homework. The project is a literal nightmare no guidance whatsoever. Good luck trying to design a P2P file sharing system from scratch without ANY help. Do not take. Hard avoid. Run. It's not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely boring and ultimately useless; most content for the homework assignments and exams comes from the textbook. Exams are worth 65% of the final grade, made specifically to trick you, with no practice exams or study guides. Final project is 25% with no guidance at all and poor instructions. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CNT4007 is a class is made up of 6 homework assignments that barely matter and suck to complete, a giant project you are not taught anything about (which has iffy and poorly-written, inconsistent instructions) and two exams on topics that videos on youtube explain better than the teacher's lectures. And it's a required course. Isn't that fun?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is decided by two exams and a few homework assignments that make zero sense. The one project done in this class was a grad-school level project and was given to undergraduate students. The material is vague and hard to understand and I pray nobody else has to take this class with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you haven't already noticed from the other reviews, this guy blows. He gives no guidance for the semester long project and you are probably gonna get grouped up with people you've never worked with before which makes it 10x harder. Lectures are useless. Avoid at all costs, the other guy who teaches this course seems wayyy better.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are basically useless and hard to watch. There are only three components to the final grade, none of which have any relevance to the lectures. 6 homeworks, which are time consuming and difficult. 1 group project thats more difficult than all the OS projects together, and 2 exams with irrelevant questions. Least favorite class so far at UF.

WORST professor I have EVER experienced at UF. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. The whole class is 2 exams and 1 project. He gives ZERO direction on the group project so you're completely on your own. Assigned homework ON THANKSGIVING. Also the lectures are completely useless. You will want to commit SIGKILL if you take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Group project, two exams, few homework assignments, currently in the class right now and breezing through it, professor can barely be understood, class is super easy but the way the assignments and lectures are presented can make it super hard for other people.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Makes no attempt to make the content even remotely palpable to students. Lectures consist of monotone readings of hundreds of slides filled with small details. Just avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Entire class was graded off of 10 assignments (6 homeworks, 2 exams, and 2 project submissions). If you stumble on anything, you'll be struggling for the rest of the semester. Final grade was curved, but Prof. Xia never said by how much, so prepare to have no clue how you're doing until final grades are in (context: my 79 got raised to an A-).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor does next to nothing with regards to feedback and lecturing. Avoid taking if possible.

This professor is extraordinarily boring. Lectures are simply unwatchable. Just use the textbook author's youtube videos to learn the material. Exams were very difficult and homeworks were useless and no feedback given - seems like the TAs just slapped a random grade on each assignment. Start the project in advanced since it is decently challenging
hard asignment, boring lectures

Very knowledgeable professor. It's not an ML class and he told us that during the first week. It's a probability class where he brings in examples from ML every once in a while. Homeworks can be really tough but he is very willing to help you get to the right answer during office hours. Every class is very information dense, I wouldn't skip it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Super boring lectures. 
Very bad grade curve... (got a B+ at 95+ percent)

Painfully boring lectures, but the textbook is pretty good, so if you read it thoroughly you'll do fine on the exams. Project is hard and you get no guidance. Homeworks are annoying and you get no feedback.

Pretty good, seems to care and know his stuff. Exams are entirely true/false and written however and the true/false are intentionally misleading. That doesn't really test student knowledge.... also many could be argued either way if you were allowed to write an explanation why you chose true/false. Pretty annoying when there's so much material
Material is a bit dry and there's a lot of it, but Professor Xia is knowledgeable and good at explaining. He is also very accommodating and understanding.

The lectures are just TOO BORING. He speaks very monotone and quiet, leading them to not be engaging. The class isn't too difficult, but it is an absolute snooze-fest that likely requires a fair amount of reading to do well in the course.

The professor has fantastic knowledge of Computer Networks and tries his best to convey the course material. Course is rather bookish and requires lot of reading to do well in the exams, grades are given based off 2 exams, a few homework assignments and a group project. None of them felt overloaded and they're all doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had him for Prob. for CS and ML. ML was barely talked about. He does nothing to make the lectures interesting. Few examples, few real world applications, not even color is in his slides. Just pure math. He speaks in a slow, monotone voice. I could not force myself to watch his lectures. To his credit, he was pretty helpful in office hours.

Good class, but lecture and homework is math-based, while exams are physics problems. It makes the homework not very useful to study from. Use previous years' exams to prepare. Take mech 1 if you want an easy A, take theoretical if you want to learn more physics (...or math, really).

We had two professors for this course. I enjoyed Prof Xue's lecture style much more and his exam questions reflected the lecture content very well. His organization of the class was understandable and he did not over-assign reading sections (unlike the other prof). Attend class, the iClicker gives a lot of extra credit.

Tests ranged from difficult to straight-forward, but Prof. Xue gives tests from previous years to study. Homework made up 40% of the grade, but extra credit is given throughout the semester. Class sometimes diverged from the lecture notes, but he overall adhered to the structure of the notes.

Very difficult course, as expected... Introduction to theoretical physics is the first course in the undergrad physics curriculum really introducing you to the formalism. I don't think prof. Xue did a good job explaining the content well. A lot of the math, although meeting the prerequisites for the course, was glanced over with no explanation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend taking this class without prior Calculus experience. The class is intended for business majors, yet it has a group project (which feels impossible since this is a huge lecture class and you can't find your group members) in a coding program. The past exams are good study material, but be ready to teach yourself calculus.

She is a sweet lady, but it is absolutely irresponsible for UF to put her as the professor of a core math class. She is hard to understand when speaking fast and does not explain things well. I had to learn the course content entirely by myself.

I would guess she's a researcher who was told she has to teach a class. Her accent is hard but not impossible. She never finished notes in class. Matlab project is pointless but P0 lets you get over 100 on it. Tests are difficult but not impossible, but you HAVE to understand the concepts. If you know some calculus going in you should be fine.
I can't understand her. She does not teach well I end up having to teach myself everything. In her lectures she skips over her notes. Going to class and watching her lectures only confuses me more.

The professor speaks quietly, fast, and has a thick accent that makes lectures hard to follow. There is a coding group project using MATLAB. I highly recommend completing the extra credit project 0 assignment, which allows you to practice using MATLAB. If you buy Study Edge, their packets can teach this course alone in a much simpler manner.

She kinda just mumbles incoherently for the whole lecture and then is confused why you are lost. If you need to take the class, just take it with Demas, she's a way better teacher. The class itself is kinda difficult but not the worst. There's a lot of homework and weekly quizzes you have to do, and definitely be prepared to study for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is a sweet lady but so hard to understand because of her accent and she rushes through lectures without explaining anything. The projects were graded harshly and some tests seemed unneccessarily hard.
Just dont. Save urself bro.

Absolutely terrible professor. You cant understand her at all which means you will have to teach everything yourself. Homework and quizzes are straight bs and her notes dont explain anything at all. She is no help at all and graded one of my exams wrong and was adamant on not rounding up my grade less than 0.1% so I could get an A.

Class with her was relatively easy, the tests and homework were very manageable, grading scale was extremely fair about 50/50 tests to out of class work/participation. As long as you attend class and are studying, doing the guides she posts it's very easy to achieve an A.

Lecture heavy but mostly just reads the notes, good grading percentages since homework and lecture attendance are weighted pretty well compared to the exams and quizzes. Quizzes are online and so is homework. Wouldn't take again but if necessary for class fine.

GET STUDY EDGE it is the only reason I learned anything. Attendance is mandatory but you can log on and do it from anywhere. Lectures are her filling in blanks on the lessons. There's a lot of homework which helped me learn but it's a no calculator class and there are questions that make you use one. Also a CODING group project….. good luck!!

Take it online. Attendance mandatory but could do LC at home. Random coding project. And lock in for midterms or u might get cooked. Final has no overall practice but question are similar from year to year. Not difficult class as long as u know how to manage without a teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Strongest accent ever, you can barely understand her, her tests were honestly nonsense (coming from someone who doesn't like math), but they don't weigh much as long as you do the homework and projects. We had a coding project that made zero sense. Wouldn't recommend

Take this online, or learn the whole course on your own anyway. Attendance is mandatory, but you can open the LC at home. Lectures are her speed-filling in lecture shells. You won't get the concept. The homework is atrocious and time consuming. The final has no practice test and cumulative. Lock in on midterm 1 or no chance of an A. Oh, and CODING!

Appalling class. Beside the useless yet insanely time consuming CODING project in a CALCULUS class, and awful lectures, Williamson simply seems to care very little about teaching.
