The class only has a few assignments though (5 discussion posts, 2 exams, attendance grade, and an essay). In my opinion, it is an easy A class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hard to understand, atendance is mandatory. She'll be no help in learning the material but she gives helpful tips for what will be on the exam. Know how to do the homework problems and the practice exam. She gives 10 point extra credit for every exam so that's helpful. She is a blight on the engineering department
She knows the subject very well.

Lectures were basically pointless other than getting attendance credit. She was very hard to understand, spoke fast, and had pretty bad handwriting, so you would actually gain nothing trying to listen during lectures. Only hope is to read the book and learn yourself. She does give exam redos for extra points which does help out a lot.

She was very hard to understand during lectures. In addition to her accent, she started wearing a mask about halfway through the semester which made understanding her twice as hard. Otherwise, she is a decent teacher. Exams are graded lightly with an additional 10% added on to each exam if you do the extra credit. Cares a lot about students
not hard to understand, vibes is just that way. it was alright
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Understanding her in lectures was extremely difficult. Her exams would often have the same questions she did as examples in class, so it's great to have paid attention during lectures. She allows a formula sheet during exams that you can write anything on. Write class examples. Homework was tough for sure. She allows exam corrections for points tho

makes mistakes during lectures that confuse everyone, including herself. Has a habit of putting derivation questions on exams, but you are allowed to make your own formula sheets so just put the derivations on in small font and you should be fine. Id recommend taking the other prof if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her class may be easy to get an A, but as a professor???? She does not understand/listen to anything you attempt to talk to her about and has taken points off tests if you go to her asking about your grade. Handwriting is barely legible. She also does not grade fairly; you could have the same answer as a classmate and get different grades.

She is very caring toward her students. She went over concepts and did not go over very many practice problems. She would rush through using the software, and confuse herself, and thus confuse the rest of us. But the extra credit on each exam was very nice.
She is awesome. Just go in person she is the sweetest professor I've had

i must admit that quite possibly she is one of the most useless professors at UF. she talks when writing on the board with her back to the class and half of the board covered behind her. she only has eye contact with students she is familiar with. Exactly the same HWs can be found online with nothing changed. Project and exams full of wired quest

To preface, she's super nice and caring, and this is my second course with her. You'll have to read the textbook or other source to piece together what she's teaching because it wasn't clear, but it's doable. She's a nice grader and gives lots of partial credit. Super into what she teaches, it's just that she's not that effective at conveying it.
Nearly illegible handwriting in a subject with lots of subscripts and superscripts and variables that need to be distinguished.

Quite possibly the most useless professor at UF. Not only does she speed through lectures to the point where it's impossible to keep up, she doesn't prepare well enough for lectures to adequately answer questions when students ask them. Her exams and final project are also ridiculous, as she's just as unclear about how to approach them.
The lectures are very helpful
The class was very useful.  I enjoyed the class very much.

Can be VERY hard to understand at times (sit up front).  The material wasn't too bad, lots of math though.  Towards the end of the course the equations get a bit crazy, but she gives formula sheets that really help to study for the last exams.  Exams were hard to finish in time, though.  I didn't finish like 2 of them.  She's nice and helpful.

Seems to have gotten harder than just bringing HW in for the exams. Impossible to understand in class, rendering lectures useless. Depend on the book. HW problems are much simpler than the exams, which are crunched for time. Would not recommend her.
Sometimes when she talks it literally does sound like she is talking Chinese. Hardest teacher to understand I have ever had. She nice though. Homeworks are long even with solutions manual.
Cannot understand her speech or her writing.  She made mistakes often.  Relied entirely on the book and the HW.  Good Luck and may God have mercy on your soul.
Not easy understand much, but give good grade and tests. Not often she want help.

Very delightful and nice lady. Cares for students, wants to help whenever she can. Helps with homework if having trouble, exams are similar to homework, and homeworks are time consuming but helpful. Wonderful woman, recommend.
very helpful teacher, learned a lot in the class. exams and class were very easy. homework counted as an exam and took about 10 hours each to finish (5 hw assignments all semester)
I got many deep understanding about engineering science from this class!

Haha, Chen's a joke, she's a new professor so I should give her a break, but the class was useless. The tests were just homework problems that you were allowed to bring. The day-to-day lectures were incomprehensible and unnecessary to succeed. She really needs to rethink her "teaching" style, if you can call it that. Nice lady though!
hard, was not really helpful, tests were too hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. York is a great professor. He is confident, gentle, and easy to understand. You can tell that he's very passionate about math when he's lecturing. He encourages participation and is supportive of students. One thing I didn't like as much was the fact that he writes extremely quickly during lectures; it's hard to keep up sometimes.

By the first exam, we were almost 2 lectures behind - I received a C+ on that first exam. I then stopped showing up to lectures and watched Shabazz lectures the rest of the semester, got a solid A because of it.
great lectures and a good professor overall. didn't love going through the derivations of the equations first all the time, but it was occasionally helpful.

Dr. York was okay. I'd say the biggest disadvantage to his teaching is that he writes the notes instead of following the guided ones. At first, I attended his lectures but in the 4th exam, I started going to Demas like everyone else. Dr. York is very familiar with the material, so there is nothing you can't ask him. Overall its easy but boring.
He gives a good lecture and if you don't like it you can just watch the videos. He will sometimes do cool applications of the math with is nice too.
Dont take York, Streese is so much better its not even funny.

Dr. York was a solid professor!  He primarily focuses on conceptual things rather than examples but he is thorough with his explanations.  Attendance not required, but is necessary!  I Could've very easily made an A but I skipped nearly every class (lazy semester) so I barely passed with a C.

He was horrible. I never went to his class but instead I went to Shabazz. She isnt better either because every time I went to her office hours she was so stand offish and weird. York will take forever to email you back and then want to have an attitude because he doesn't want to teach. Also, the tests are impossible to study for and are very hard.

This professor wasn't the class coordinator, so he tried to copy the lectures of Dr. Shabbaz, but didn't do a good job explaining and frequently fell behind. When he fell behind, he told the class to watch Shabbaz's online lectures because there would be material on the quiz that he didn't cover in class. I ended up to Shabaz's lectures.

Overall solid prof. Good lecturer and really helpful explaining concepts, calc 3 itself I found harder than the other two but he made it a lot easier. York and Shabazz gave 3% of extra credit this semester which really helped out. The exams are worth a lot though, I had an A for the whole semester until exam 3 so make sure not to fall behind.

York worked together with Strusse on the course's canvas page - and thank goodness for Strusse, I would not have been able to survive without him! I used Study Edge throughout the whole semester. An A is definitely possible you just have to practice over and over again!
Great teacher but try and take Strese over him as Strese runs the whole class and makes tests/hw.

Nice guy, but spends entire lectures going over WHY things are a certain way instead of just teaching them and showing examples, makes everything more confusing. If you have him, just skip his lectures and either use Stresse's video lectures or go to Stresse's class.

Dr York was a great lecturer who made sure we actually understood the material and why we were learning it. Sometimes we did fall behind lecture schedule so examples were skipped. Overall great professor

York is great with lectures. Calc 3 in general is straight forward. Pay attention, keep up with your assignments as it is a 4 credit class, and you'll do fine. He's easy to follow and understand, and takes his time to thoroughly explain; I'm taking his diff. class next semester.
Did not learn a single thing from lecture, had to teach myself every topic, even went to office hours and he was unfriendly.
He doesn't record lectures and honestly half the time they aren't even helpful. Discussion periods have a quiz and the TA's were harsh graders (he didn't grade anything) all homework was on Xornos

I stopped going to class early on because he confused me even more. Studyedge saved me for this class. Homework isn't reflective of exams, do ALL the practice exams. Discussion is easy if u get a good TA. Got either an A or A-. Extra points on exams!
Horrible!! DO not take he is AWFUL!!

He is a good lecturer. Show up to the lectures, ask questions if you need help, and you will do fine. The exams were pretty hard and sometimes it felt like they covered the material in a more abstract way than was done in the examples, so you need a really thorough understanding of the topics if you want to do well on them. I learned a lot.

Dr. York is a really good lecturer and goes in depth with the concepts. I had already taken Calc 1 previously, and I think he did a good job going deeper and he gave good explanations. Sometimes he was a little wordy and went too deep but it was mostly a good review. Do the practice exams from previous years to prepare for the exams.

I took the class online but preferred that format as I always find myself just learning the material from YouTube if I take it in person anyways. Lecture quizzes can be retaken 3 times and are untimed. Timed quizzes are 4 questions around 45 mins I believe. Had no calc experience and didn't use study edge, but I did spend lots of time on this class
Standard huge lecture class. You can just skip the class and learn from youtube. Not much homework.

I took Prof York online for Calc 1 and he isn't as bad as other people are making him out to be. Simple lecture quizzes and Xronos HW given out each week. The first two midterms were a piece of cake, but Exam 3 was the toughest!!! Overall, I did well on the final and the tests were usually easier than the extra credit reviews he gave us.

This class is just a standard college class with a huge class size. No recordings but you can just learn from random youtube videos without going to class. Do the practice exams. Exams are almost identical to them.

His class was huge with a LOT of students. Lectures were given in a good pace, which I thought were fine to understand. However, the quizzes every discussion period kind of kills the vibe, and I often did not go to those, making my grade drop significantly.
Not the best lectures, I'd recommend looking into Study Edge. Tests are doable though, not too difficult if you put in the work and study.

York is a very standard college lecturer. He discusses the topics theoretically which makes them hard to grasp, and goes through examples that somewhat enforce the topics. Realistically, you could not show up to lectures and rely on outside material to teach you and pass. He does provide a lot of past exams as practice though, which is nice.

While Professor York's lectures could sometimes be excruciatingly long, I would say this is mostly based on the organization of his lectures rather than his teaching ability. He's a very caring professor that will work with you and is easily accessible outside of class, but he writes down every word for lectures. Grade is HEAVILY dependent on TA.

Professor York's written notes during lectures are excruciatingly painful to sit through as he writes almost every word he says down and the way he teaches concepts is very confusing. Almost 75% of your grade is based on exams and the other relies on ur TA's quizzes. My TA gave extremely difficult discussion quizzes, so pray u get a good TA.
I really did not interact with Mr. York too much, but he is very accessible and loves helping student during his office hours. Would take him again!

York has a very conceptual way of teaching, the exam material are clearly outlined in the homework and past exams are posted for review. I would not take him again for calculus personally. Study edge etc. is not necessary to get a good grade in the class. Exams will make or break your grade, expect half conceptual and half technical applications.

Despite what others say study edge etc. is not needed to pass this class. You have Dr. Yorks and TAs office hours. As well there is free math help in little hall and UF posts mac2311 exam study guides and solutions. Easy to pass just use your resources. As well email Dr. York he is a very reasonable professor. Homework is quick and easy.

This man talks SO SLOW! I had to wait until his lectures were posted on Canvas so I could watch them in 2x speed. I was not a fan of how he taught material and explained concepts either. His exams had some material that were never covered in class. Studyege is the only reason I passed. Make sure you have a strong trig background.

He is a great teacher but of course the content is no fun. Some of the exams were MUCH harder than the practice exams he posted. My best advice is to get private tutoring with the tutoring center that UF offers for free. I owe my life to my tutor there.

Dr. York was a pretty good professor overall. I didn't get to interact with him much because the class was huge but I still managed to do well in the class. Part of your grade is up to the TAs so make sure you get one that grades easily.

Like any other Calc class, you need to prepare for it. Dr. York was an encouraging, supportive, and helpful professor. First time taking Calc and passed it first try! Attending office hours, taking notes during lectures, and practice exams are recommended. Do not slack on any exam, your grade will depend on one or two mostly likely.

York was an average professor. His exams weigh a lot towards your grade, but even if you do badly on one, you can still get a good grade. Unless you were taking a make-up exam or quiz, you didn't have much interaction. He was kind to students who went to him for help. Some advice: get a good TA, and do his old exams before the actual ones.

Professor York is arguably one of the best calculus professors @ UF. He genuinely cares about your learning and understanding of the content and will answer any math questions. While the Xronos homework is tedious, the TAs will help during office hours. Get StudyEdge if you want extra practice, but it's not necessary. I wish he taught Calc 2!

His lectures are often full of proofs you don't need to know. Assigns homework that is nothing like the test questions. How good your TA is will heavily effect your grade. I never took ap calc in high school and I felt so lost. I had to retake this class and got an A the second time. Study edge/ practice exams are a necessity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. York is very sweet and caring. I took calc 1 online and definitely recommend doing it online. He responds to emails and you can just tell her genuinely wants the students to succeed.

Prof York was OK. His lectures contained good information, but a lot of the time he would go through a proof/long explanation, only to say at the end that we didn't need to know how to do it. You could probably not attend lecture and only use study edge for this class, and pass with flying colors, especially if you have a solid math background.

Professor York definitely cares about students - he gives ample resources and is incredible at assuring that the needs of students with accommodations are met. However, his lectures were not helpful for exams (75% of grade). He often deviated from the main topic by going over proofs that were not relevant to exam topics, which wasted time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: this class is ridiculously unfair. the exams do not represent the homework, each TA section is run differently so some curve your exams and some don't. his office hours are useless because he is unwilling to help you pass the class. all he does is nod his head and say mhm to your complaints. save yourself the trouble and take it at Santa Fe.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was very easy and all the exams were very straightforward. Make sure you do the practice exams to prepare for the test rather than reviewing homework. In lectures, he spends a lot of time slowly writing stuff down word for word which is annoying but when he gets to the content he makes it very understandable.

Best advice: get 100% on HW and Test so they can help your grade. Got a B on pretty much all of my exams, and got a C for my final. As able to pull through with a A- since I had a 100 on everything else. Offers 5 extra points for exams if you do the exam review sheets. DO IT! Will help your grade a lot. Really easy work, really hard exams.

This was one of the most streamlined classes I've ever taken. The workload was relentless with assignments due daily and many taking many hours to complete, but putting in the work every day secured me an easy A. Dr. York was extremely helpful both in the lectures and in office hours, making learning content simple if you just reach out for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor was condescending and impatient with student questions/concerns. Pulls very vague impossible details from books on quizzes and tests every/every other week. Office hours did not help, email gets you no where. Accused students of cheating with no basis. Multiple students withdrew mid-semester from distress. It's not worth it - AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests consisted of key terms from lecture/textbook (he gives you a list of them in advance) and analysis of primary/secondary sources that we went over in class. The lectures can be fast and dense, if you get the big picture it's alright. Lot of readings, but they were really interesting! Slow grader, but a good lecturer that wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: professor will not answer questions, accuses multiple students of cheating to be proven wrong, gives 0 guidance and will tell you to figure it mout when asked for help. rather than helkping you he will tell you to drop the course. should not be teaching at the University of Florida
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: worst professor in the entire history department you should stay far away, refuses to give guidence or even teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Worst class i have ever taken. Does not give clear instructions. NO TECHNOLOGY ALLOWED. Good luck on the quizzes, they are the most obscure terms and questions you'll ever see. Lectures are almost obsolete and does not matter to any of the essays or quizzes. Everything graded is on the textbook or the two books you read for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is a friendly professor, but he takes forever to grade and frequently does not provide feedback for why he is grading you as harshly as he is. Unless you are physically in his office for office hours, he will not respond. Ignores emails, grades harshly, and does not teach the material that you are expected to master.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
His tone when talking to students bordered on disrespectful. His criticisms were often cryptic and contradictory, with him sometimes refusing to outright call out a problem until the very last minute.

His behavior constantly edged on harassment, and his treatment of certain other students in regards left much to be desired.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easily accessible class and a professor who is very lenient. Many difficult readings but just go to office hours if you're lost. He's a "Nobody's Perfect" professor so he doesn't give out 100s, but it is relatively easy to get a 90-95 if you do the readings and have good writing skills (which you should have if you've made it this far.)

I had Gerien-Chen for Quest 1: Global Asia and loved him. You could tell he was passionate about the material he was teaching and I learned a great amount in the class. The class was graded based on a few assignments and the T.A. and Gerien-Chen are tough graders, but going to office hours helped tremendously. He is a kind and caring professor!

The professor seemed very knowledgeable and genuinely passionate by Asian history. The professor is a nice guy but is a tough grader and you have to put a really good effort to maintain an A in the class. The professor and TA grades your papers and gave good feedback but your grade is based on like 5 assignments. Avoid this class for Quest 1 id say
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Gerien-Chen for global asia. He taught about interesting topics I had never learned before, so I liked the material. However, he's a fast lecturer and expected a lot for a quest class. About 2 long articles to read per week, and the class only has a few grades total which can make it hard to keep a high grade. Attendance is mandatory.

Dr. Gerien-Chen genuinely cares about what his students will take away from the class, both in knowledge and skill sets. Although he is a tough grader and it can be difficult to maintain an A, I much became a better writer and thinker after only one semester. He is very understanding and helpful during office hours, so definitely connect with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Professor Chen is friendly and approachable. I just finished the final paper which was open ended prompt and 7-10 pages. The lowest grade was always an 80%.

My advice: read regularly throughout the week, and base your final paper around questions you want to find answers to!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A very tough grader with lots of reading. While he is an enjoyable teacher to have there are better options in the history department. Your grades is determined by several writing assignments varying in length but it is incredibly rare to get higher than a 90, in a class where a 93.3+ in an A. If you interested take it, if your worry about GDP dont
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Chen is obviously knowledgeable about his subject, but the class was horrible. The grading was the toughest Ive ever seen at UF, and Im a senior. There is no way you can get an A in this class. The feedback was often times confusing or contradictory, and he refuses to give out anything higher than a 90, even if you did all of the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He made it impossible for anyone in this class to get an A this semester. Would love for him to give us examples what A work looks like because it's never enough. Also, he should talk to the others profs here who have taught longer - he's the most difficult professor in this department for no reason. Very vague instructions don't help either.
Professor makes an A impossible to attain. Great lecturer, but no leeway with grades
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As a professor, his strengths are definitely in his knowledge and his lectures. He also cares for his students and is accessible outside of class. However, his classes are the hardest history courses to earn an A in, and often times, it feels like he makes things too difficult for no reason. He's also a bit condescending during lectures/feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. James Gerien-Chen is by far my favorite Professor at UF. I took him for my Senior Research Seminar and he was very helpful not only with content, but with writing and researching as well. He understood the past 2 years has been hard on students, and genuinely cares for you. He gives great lectures and grades fairly, couldn't recommend him more.

Overall, his subject matter knowledge is great and he teaches well. In terms of grading and managing the class, he seems overwhelmed. He put much of our grade in charge of an algorithm that punished us for doing what he originally told us to. He expressed his regret at that but did nothing to reverse it. He gives very good feedback though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Gerien-Chen is by far the best professor I've ever had. He is extremely concerned about his students and has no problem helping out in office hours or extending deadlines due to personal issues. He is very knowledgeable in his field and very good at making his students think for their own responses. Definitely take one of his classes!

Dr. Chen is very kind and caring. He is a young professor so he is still figuring things out but he more than makes up for that with his ability to have great lectures. Dr. Chen is not a light grader and he will make you work for the A, but as long as you put in the work you should be fine. Be warned that he also takes a bit long to get grades in.
She is extremely kind and one of those few teachers who enjoys her job. Her class was low stress and fair exams and assignments. I wish she was my teacher for every class.

Professor Zori was one of the kindest teachers I have ever had. Her class was fairly easy with weekly group assignments, one individual paper, and one group presentation. She had two exams, both with extra credit and open-note quizzes.
Great professor. She is very knowledgable on the topics she teaches. She cares about her students and wants to see them succeed. It is an engaging, debate-structured class.
Dr. Zori's expectations for assignments were very clear and she is a very fair grader. The class is structured as a debate with 500 word reflections afterwords.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Zori is one of the best professors I have ever had!! She loves to teach, and it really shows, she is very knowledgeable, understanding, and helpful. She wants you to succeed. I cannot say enough good things, take any and every class of hers you can!

Dr. Zori is awesome. Her expectations for assignments were very clear and she is a very fair grader. The content of the course is interesting and thought-provoking when considering various topics in public health. She is very accessible outside of class and gives great advice on advancing in the public health field.

Assigns a hefty amount of work. Puts up 4 hours of lecture per week on top of reading/quizzes/projects/assignments. Quizzes do not align with lectures or textbooks and waits a week until after you've taken the test to release results. Had to take this class as a requirement in my last semester (so very unfortunately).

Prof. Zori's class is what you make of it. She doesn't lecture and instead class time is devoted to debates and group work. She is not a strict grader though and the work load is quite manageable. Nothing super difficult and she provides detailed rubrics of what she expects on projects/papers so an A is very attainable. Exams are based on textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Zori is very caring and understanding. The class is not too difficult and covers interesting topics. Weekly assignments that do not take too long. Exams are straight forward and studying the tophat material will suffice.

Dr. Zori is so sweet and so understanding of her students. Her class is not hard, but there is some work you have to do (group project, a paper, discussion posts, and prep for debates). The weekly quizzes were not bad the book was easy to read. The exams are you either know it or you do not. Kritik grading is wonky so hopefully she changes that.
His lectures were fine. Nothing outstanding.

For calc 3, Professor York was great as his lectures were very comprehensive and would go into detail on the derivations of some of the more complicated multi-variable expressions. His lectures helped a lot with the class as he would point out things essential to doing well on the exams.

His lectures were great, just follow along and even the difficult material makes sense. A lot of the time I would be in lecture, have no clue what was going on, then looked back at my notes later while studying and it made total sense. His style of doing practice problems in class was great. Also was really nice and answered questions

His lectures are amazing. His lectures can sometimes be long, but 2x speed makes it better. The homework takes a while, but you won't need to study after because of how comprehensive it is. He's very lenient in the quizzes and homework due dates. His lectures are so good that I feel like he is personally explaining it to me face to face.

There are about 2-3 lectures per week, and each lecture has a 10-20 question homework as well as a quiz with 3-5 questions. The tests are exactly like the quiz questions and are pretty easy. I never had to interact with the prof during the course because it was online and I had no technical difficulties. The beginning of course is easy, end is meh.
I took Dr. York for Calc 3 and liked him enough to take him for Diffeq! His lectures are clear, straightforward, and easy to comprehend.

He's a whatever lecturer but the course is very easy to follow along with and the lectures are super missable if you're a good math student and so I rarely ever went and was still able to get a very easy A.
I've never said something remotely similar but I seriously hope this guy tears both of his ACLs

This course is very organized. Lecture videos are great but long. 30 lectures total. 4 tests heavily weighted at 70% but are really easy to get 100 on if you study, and is the same question type as the practice test. This course is conceptually easier than calc 3 but much more time consuming due to heavy computaions. 1 hour studying per day likely.
Honest person, goes through examples in class, and is willing to work on any number of questions with you during office hours.

Bang average professor, long boring lectures he zips through without much explanation half the time. Homework takes a ludicrous amount of time to do for what the content is. That being said, the class concepts are not hard. Just be ready to spend 3 hours on one unit between the lecture/lecture quiz/hws.

The lecture videos were good means of learning, but they were monotone and boring especially with the long lectures at the end of the course. The exams are weighted heavily, but the exams are easy if you take the time to study and do practice exams that are provided.

Busywork, busywork, busywork!! Next to zero extra credit, exams are weighted heavily. Homework is incredibly time-consuming. His Summer C lectures were disorganized and sometimes quite long. Expect a fairly straightforward but time-consuming class. Exam content is straightforward, but this class feels more like applied precalculus than calculus.

This was a great class! The lectures are kind of boring and the homework takes a long time, but I think this class works really well being online. Spend maybe 2 or 3 hours a day (including the 1hr lecture) and you should be fine. Exams are very fair and straightforward, but be weary for tricks!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: tbh bad lectures and they get very long for summer C. I didn't like how he would mess up during the lectures and didn't explain his train of thought. Diffeq isn't hard but it got confusing with his lectures

Dif EQ is easiest course in Calc1-DifEq progression. Plenty of extra credit; I ended up needing a 7% on the final for an A in the class. York's lectures are totally fine, he's a clear lecturer, but I really only went to class to see if he'd ever change his shirt (he did twice throughout the semester). Exams are carbon copies of practice exams. Easy

This teacher graded fairly and was what I expected for a survey calc course. It is a bit of work, but if you takes notes and study you should be able to get a decent grade in the class. Nothing crazy stressful, but takes sometime to finish the homework.

I had Dr. York for an online section of differential equations and I can only say positive things! The lectures were from Dr. Demas and were great, and his testing and grading criteria was straightforward! I ended the class with a good grade and have no complaints!

I took professor York for MAC2313 (calc 3) idk why that isnt an option for course code but hes not a good lecturer and very slow. Hes a nice guy and will help you individually as he's pretty good at math, just not good at teaching. The online shabazz lessons are what helped me pass but im a math major so im a bit biased on the difficult of course.
Decent guy, bad lecturer. Just don't put off studying.

Put good instead of OK because of minimal HW. Guy comes 5 mins late and free-writes on printer paper as his way of teaching. The class wasn't hard, but he overcomplicated basically every lesson, so I usually watched Streese's videos after class. TA is hit or miss, fortunately mine was very helpful. As long as you can do the HW yourself you're fine.

This professor wasn't the class coordinator, so he tried to copy the lectures of Dr. Shabbaz, but didn't do a good job explaining and frequently fell behind. When he fell behind, he told the class to watch Shabbaz's online lectures because there would be material on the quiz that he didn't cover in class. I ended up to Shabaz's lectures. (MAC2313).
Lectures are really hard to understand. If you want to do well in his class, you have to get Study Edge or watch Streese's video lectures.

Very skilled mathematician but a somewhat poor lecturer. Supplementing his lectures with either the online ones or Study Edge is a necessity to do well. Expectations are mostly clear but tests had a few curveballs. Grind practice problems if you wish to do well on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly he's pretty good. You're not gonna get too personal with him but it's also a large lecture hall. He explains concepts very well I would say if you take this class it's good to also watch the lecture videos from the other professor on canvas. If you can't get stresse get York over any other calc professor
They really do be hiring anyone at this point
If you want to keep your 4.0 don't take him as your professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I recommend the other professor or even taking the course online over taking it with York
Does not know how to teach
Bad at lecturing.
Whatever you do don't take York as your professor!!!!

Alex York is the type of professor no one should have in their time at UF. He is as unenthusiastic as they come. Comes in to class with 1 minute to spare and acts like a robot. Not helpful at all!!! Just watch the video lectures on canvas and you'll be fine, but going to watch this "professor's" lectures will just be a huge waste of time!
I enjoyed his lectures his way of taking was easy to understand

Alex does not care about if you are learning in the class at all. Man walk in 2 minutes before class starts and has no personality. I heard that the other professor it much better, so try and get him if possible. Overall, the lectures are useless unless you already know the course as literally all he does it copy from a sheet dosen't explain.

York was kind but lacked in helpfulness and informativeness. His lectures were written out but never recorded, making it difficult to review and comprehend the material if you did not attend class. Study edge became a necessity to pass the class. Overall, the experience left much to be desired. Also, your TA will make or break your experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: York was a very solid math professor. His style of lecturing got tedious at times because he just writes on a piece of printer paper that's projected onto a screen, but generally they were bearable. The exams cover material covered in class and there's no surprises. As long as you show up to lectures and do the homework, you should be good.

Professor York is organized and his lectures are clear and easy to follow. In order to succeed on exams, emphasis should be put on homework and other outside-of-class materials. Weekly discussion quizzes can be challenging, studying for these will help students to be more successful.

Professor York had a clear guideline of expectations/grading for the class. The practice tests were representative of the actual exams, and the homework was a good practice tool. However, the lectures often overcomplicate the concepts tested, so I found Study Edge to be useful in providing clear explanations.

Spends too much time in class explaining why certain theorems work, but not on different ways to do the problems. Doing the previous exams help, but make sure to try on the homework because that is where most of your learning will come from not the lecture.

For each thing he taught, he would give at least one example applying that thing. Also, you have access to past exams, which usually resulted in the same grade that I would get on the actual exams. He did move pretty quickly at times, but it is part of the curriculum and his teaching was good.

Class is primarily based on exams. Homeworks and discussion quizzes barely matter unless you heave through exams. Lectures are heavy; most times, York offers a long, winded explanation instead of a to-the-point methodology. Confusing and unengaging, made it difficult to learn material during class. Exams are ridiculously hard. Not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor York is clearly passionate about math. however, his explanations are often confusing and long winded. he explains basic theorems by first completing the long proof. he focuses too much on conceptual ideas and proofs rather than providing example problems and showing actual application.
His style is not for everyone, but as long as you watched the lectures and actually do the HW, you will be fine. The HW questions are so much harder than the tests
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
York was pretty good. I had never really been excited about math until I took York.

His lecturing style isn't great for taking notes so watch the lectures without taking notes in person then immediately afterwards review the recording and take notes on that.

The class has a free online textbook. It is good, use it.

Average calc 1 professor. He was pretty accommodating for the most part. Nothing special. Highly recommend actually putting effort into the Xronos homeworks and using the available past exams when studying for exams

Professor mainly teaches things on a conceptual level and doesn't show many examples. I used Studyedge and the lecture material was used as review if I needed it. Get studyedge for this class or you'll struggle when it comes to discussion quizzes and exams, as exams count for 70-75 percent of your grade!

Took the class online, was the easiest calculus class and I ended with a 114%. You could earn 90 points on each test, but was only graded out of 80, and he offered 5 points extra credit if you did some questions from previous exams. He was in literally none of the lectures, but he was nice to me whenever I asked him (sometimes stupid) questions.

I wasn't the biggest fan of his lectures, but they were good enough! Exams were very tough and unless you have a strong calculus background, this class can be very hard. The best thing you can do is study the past exams, study edge was great too.

Having been familiar with most of the material before I started, the class was quite easy. The structure of the class, both the lectures and Canvas was very organized. The discussion class is mandatory but lecture are not as you can just watch the recorded lecture videos or go via zoom.

Spends a large proportion of each lecture on proofs that aren't on the test at expense of practice problems. HW is usually pretty lengthy and is graded on correctness by the glitchy Xronos platform. Lectures cover 75% of what's needed for the HW, which covers 85% of what's needed for the exams. You'll need to do some outside learning to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: York was an alright professor. Not the best but definitely not the worst math teacher Ive had. Sometimes he would spend time doing proofs and then at the end say they wont even appear on the exams. His lectures were pretty clear and straightforward most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Did a lot of proofs which didn't really help much. He's an alright professor, but I'd want to get someone else next time. He's nice, and funny sometimes, but I just didn't "click" with him, idk.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall good professor. The lectures usually are easy to follow and recorded, no clicker questions participation is graded by an easy post-lecture quiz. The tests are usually harder than the homework (which is accuracy with unlimited attempts) and the lecture problems, but I managed to get an A with past exams. Study Edge helps but not necessary

York's style of teaching is LOTS of writing. He goes pretty slow so I honestly just rewatch the lecture recordings and take notes like that. Make sure you study the past exams before the test because the same themes might be repeated. The TAs are pretty nice but can be confusing to understand sometimes. Overall, a decent professor but not perfect.

Dr. York is a very nice guy who makes things very clear for you. If you do not understand something, I recommend immediately using other resources to gain a better grasp of the subject. The one thing I did not like about Dr. York is that he would sometimes spend excessive amounts of time explaining proofs which did not really help on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor York is a very good professor. I had him as an online lecture course and he was very sweet and made sure to answer all of my questions. His class relies heavily on tests and discussion quizzes. Make sure to look at previous tests. Those helped me a lot on all the exams. Also, I recommend looking at harder problems than what he goes over.

Calc is a tough class, but really the TAs are always open to help and York explains things super well. Going to the lectures is not mandatory, but there is attendance plus you will understand the content better if you go. DO THE HW, it is your most important resource in the class. Also, past exams are really helpful. York is a wonderful prof!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. York is very good at explaining the basics of what you need to know for Calculus. It is very easy to follow along with his lectures. If you want to do well in this class make sure to do the Xronos HW assignments as well as the problems provided in the textbook. Study edge is also very helpful in this class but not necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. York! Even though I hated learning about Calculus, he made the class bearable. He was funny and put content into ways that students could understand. He was very transparent about grading and tests. Though, I had to use Study Edge as this class is just notoriously hard.
calc 2 is one of the hardest classes ever but dr. york made it possible. his lectures are very clear and helpful. take calc with him
Super nice and Great At explaining concepts during office hours
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. York was a great calculus teacher. Every lecture was easy to understand and was actually in the given exams. Not that much homework was given. There's a quiz after every lecture but they were easy. Of course, you still need to review and study just a bit for the exams though. You could get a good grade if you just put in a little effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. York is the best professor I've had so far and definitely the nicest professor for Calculus. He gives great lectures and won't kill you with extra work. MAC2311 and 12 inherently very test heavy classes no matter the professor so I don't think that can be held against him

Dr. York is my favorite professor so far! Everything you need to know for the exams are given to you in the lectures. He is super responsive to the zoom chat and also stays after class to answer more questions. I got A's on all the exams with minimal studying: I would only take his practice exams and review questions I got wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. York was a very good professor and his lectures were very informative. Very helpful if you bring questions to office hours, however expect to wait a bit before being let in. The exams are definitely challenging compared to practice exams and lecture examples, so this class will probably be tough if you dont come in with past calc knowledge
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although I got a mediocre grade in the class, Dr. York helped me so much in the end. The class very tests heavy and you have to start studying weeks in advance. Do not solely rely on study edge, although it is very useful I think it is easier than the exams.

Professor York is entertaing and funny however the problems he explains in lecture are significantly easier than the questions on the exam. I recommend him if you already have calculus knowledge and just need to retake the course.

The level of difficulty of Dr. York's lectures compared to the actual exams are nothing alike. When it came to the exams, I did poorly with a weeks worth of studying. The department creates the tests and I think York needs to include examples that are the same level of difficulty as showcased in those exams. No test grades are dropped and no curve.

This class was hard and takes time to study and understand the material. I think the exams weren't similar enough to the material we learned so you should use outside resources to pass as well. The professor is nice but there are so many other students that it's easy to get lost. The TA's are in charge of the weekly quizzes that get harder.

Loved York for MAC2311! He's a funny guy and has great lectures. His format is super clear and concise and he knows what he's doing. He has plenty of office hours through your TA's and himself. Be wary, exams and final make 75% of your grade. He has plenty of resources to study for exams and with some prep, this class is very manageable.

York is a cool dude who makes calc seem relatively easy. However, the class is weighted heavily based on tests that aren't even made by him. The tests themselves are absurdly difficult in comparison to the practice exams and past exams. If you've taken AP calc before, you'll be fine. Wouldn't take again since he doesn't drop anything meaningful.

Dr. York definitely knows what he is talking about and made calculus seem a lot more approachable. my only complaint is that for a few topics he made them seem a bit more difficult than they could have been. Get studyedge and put in some work and you'll get an A

Professor York is a good person but not the best professor. While a class like this comes with the expectation of a lot of studying, York does not provide the best materials to study. Lectures and homework are too easy while exams are difficult. It would be helpful if York did harder problems in class and gave questions similar to exam format.

Dr. York explained everything very clearly, but he often made things more complicated than things needed to be. Despite that, he made sure that everyone had a chance to ask questions and answered things on a timely manner. Overall amazing dude, just do your homework and attend lectures and you got it.

Dr. York did a great job at caring for his students during COVID. Even though his tests are pretty hard, he offers many resources and past exams for you to study from. He also responds to emails very fast! Overall, he is a fun and helpful professor. Online school has been tough on everyone, but his class is very doable with some extra help.

Such a good professor, especially when dealing with COVID. A professor who seems like he actually cares about you and your wellbeing. Attend office hours as soon as you don't understand anything so you don't fall behind. Grade heavily weighted by exam scores but that's to be expected. Take this class with him, I am so glad I did.

I feel that York did a great job. I took the class online and he was available after class and during his office hours if you need additional help. If you actually pay attention in the lectures and do the homework, you will do well. Also, I was shocked that this was my easiest class considering I didn't even take pre-calc in high school.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: York was a great professor to have for calc 1 freshman year. He was funny, knew the material and was willing to go back and explain for anyone who was confused (even through zoom). Over all great professor and good dude. Watch out for trick questions on tests tho.

Is a decent professor but would not choose to take it again with him. Why? Because his lectures do not really cover exam questions and sometimes he will spend 30-40 min over two questions and rush the important bits. If you want an A with him tho, just read the book, do all the practice exams, and do good on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of extra credit, exam questions are tougher than homework but theres a bunch of extra credit on all the exams that more than makes up from it. Theres so much extra credit on the exams its impossible to fail. Lectures werent that helpful but just do your homework and youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Although he means well, Professor York was a horrible professor. He rushed through material and his exams were nothing like work done in class. His tests were also very weirdly graded but weighed so much.

His exams were way harder than past exams. I did great in every aspect of the class except the exams because they were brutal. He mad them way harder than past exams. Don't be fooled by how easy things are compared to his exams.
Such an amazing professor, I would take his class over and over again. He made things so easy to understand and was so fair in his exams!

I found questions on the exams to be quite harder than any of the ones done in class. I only did well in this class with the help of study edge and immense studying. Math is not my thing and I found York to be good for learning the basics of the lesson but had to work on my own to understand the difficult questions that would be on the tests.

Before the pandemic he was an excellent professor during lectures, however, when we switched over to all online, he just uploaded old lecture videos that were so unhelpful! Everyone seemed to be lost, but this could have been prevented if the pandemic didn't happen. GET study edge, it's the only reason why I finished with an A.

York is a great teacher, he thoroughly explains everything and goes slowly to make sure he solidifies the concepts. His lecture notes are very helpful. Math is not my thing, but his lectures helped me understand it a lot better. Exams are basically your entire grade though, so definitely starting studying and practicing for them days in advance.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Don't take this class with him. You'll be alone in terms of understanding the material and trying to get help in office hours. It won't help and you will only be more frustrated in the class. He'll just help with a particular question, but is not good with helping you understand the material/concept beyond lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Doesn't give good feedback when you ask. Grading criteria on exams is unclear on many occasions. Like for FRQs you'll get points off for something that you didn't even know you needed to include in your answer, lazy test-making that will only mess you up. Discussion classes were pointless; it was a more confusing experience.

Actually, he doesn't give good feedback. If you go to his office hours and ask him about your concerns (understanding the info) he'll just provide you with a brief, unhelpful suggestion. Maybe he's good for students who are comfortable with Calculus previously and can teach themselves the material, but if you aren't, I wouldn't take him.

Although everyone here says he is great for flipped (well as long as you can teach yourself) you will get the opposite experience in traditional. The homework (Xronos) and especially quizzes were "busy-work" and were generally not useful for exams (which is your whole grade basically). And he doesn't give you the tools to succeed.

If you're considering having him for a traditional class experience, I would consider someone else. His teaching approach is more "hands-off" than other math professors I've had at UF. After taking his class, I don't believe that he had a want for his students to succeed, and it showed throughout the class. I will never take a class with him again.
Great professor, really cares about his students!

Hes a good teacher and goes very slowly on all concepts. Its very helpful for getting the basics of all his lectures. That being said, he never gets to any hard problems that would be on the test so discussion section or study edge is the only way to figure those out. But getting the basic principle really helps with the hard ones, so good overal
York is the best professor I've had at UF so far. 100% recommend taking calc with him.
The nicest and best teacher in the math department

Best math professor and one of the overall best professors I have ever had. If you need to take calculus at UF TAKE IT WITH YORK! His class is so organized and he is so patient with his students. Explains calc in a way that actually makes sense. He actually cares about his students and he will work with you if you need help.

By far the best math professor and maybe the best professor I have ever had. He cares so much about his students, so approachable, and explains calculus in a way that is so easy to understand, he makes his class so organized which makes learning calc so much easier and enjoyable. I am not a math person but he makes math make sense.

I had a great relationship with York in flipped Calc 1 and I absolutely loved him! He was very attentive to student's questions and I could really tell he was passionate about Math. Next semester I heard he will be the Main Lecturer; he will do great! He lectured for about 15 minutes in my flipped class and was always able to explain things well!!!

Math has always been my weakest subject and I was dreading having to take calculus, especially after only taking pre-calculus in high school. I know for a fact I wouldnt have passed if it wasnt for Dr. York. He genuinely cares that his students understand the material and wants them to succeed. This c+ was my biggest accomplishment this semester!

Prof. York is by far one of the worst professors i've encountered so far. It doesn't help that this is a flipped class. You'll show up, get a worksheet, and turn it in next class. He gives the occasional weird cat book or worksheet (news flash, they're his REAL cats). This class is a waste of time and unbearable if you don't have study edge.

Dr. York is an excellent teacher. He explains calc so well and if you pay attention when he talks you'll benefit immensely. His class is flipped and the online lectures are not by him (they're not helpful) but his short in-class notes make up for it.

I took this class flipped. I had lectures online and had to attend class for a 5-7 minute lecture and spend the rest of the time doing a worksheet (basically for attendance). The online lectures are not done by Dr. York and it shows because they're awful. Dr. York is a phenomenal professor, but honestly, all you need for this course is study edge.

Dr York is amazing!! I loved having him for calc 1, my class was flipped style so we watched videos and home and in class we would do problems and dr york reviews important things from the lecture. I liked that sm more than traditional style its a lot easier to understand the material and dr york explains everything rlly well!!
Really nice guy. You should go on the field trip, pretty fun. The class is way more difficult than needed though. You need to actually dedicate quite a bit of time to study.

Took this class for my gen ed science course, and it turned out to be much harder than expected. Tests were basically your entire grade, and they were hard. Make sure you look over provided practice test, and rely heavily on in class practice questions. Extra credit was given to raise grade 2%.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class for my gen ed for science, and it turned out to be way harder than expected. His lectures are very important to pay attention, and only some of the information you need to memorize is given on the study guide. You should really memorize the practice questions given in lectures and the study guide questions.

He's very passionate about what he teaches, which makes lectures engaging. In my opinion, the class was difficult, but he is a good professor, which made it tolerable. The exams are pretty much your whole grade so be sure to study for them and definitely do the extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truly, he is a great guy, but this class was the worst class I've ever taken. I wouldn't recommend this class.

Don't take this class. I needed something for my Science credit and expected a class called Oceanography to be manageable at the least, but it's unexecpectedly (and unecessarily) hard. Professor Zimmerman does not seem to understand that most students are only taking the class to fulfill a credit, and the class seems to be overly hard. Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams are just sm harder than you would think for a class titled, "oceanography." I went to almost every lecture and just still did not do well. He offers extra credit but like idk. Take something easier, it is not worth it.

Exams are 72% of your grade. Very hard to get full credit on exams. Extra credit of 2% offered for going on field trip. I studied for hours for the first 2 exams and it will be hard for me to get an A with only one exam left. Discussions and exercises are easy and quick to do. I would not take him again because of the grading scale, but nice guy.

Definitely my favorite class that I took fall semester. He is available outside of class and is willing to go over any questions you have. Take pictures of any questions in the lectures, as those are likely to appear in exams. The textbook extra credit helps, but isn't necessary. If you go to class and take notes, the exams should be pretty easy.

I do not suggest taking this class for Quest, there is a lot of busy work. Professor Zimmerman is clearly smart and passionate, but he constantly criticizes his students for every little mistake they make. Sometimes it feels like he expects his students to know as much as he does, and nothing ever satisfies him

He is great, but sometimes is too passionate about a topic and makes it hard to understand what is on the exam by going more in depth than necessary for an introductory course. Pretty much a combination of AP Enviro and basic physics topics taught in high school. However, he always makes class fun and loves student interaction.

Professor Zimmerman is entertaining in class and honestly loves his work. He's always excited to share his knowledge with us. Pay attention to lectures! Tests make up about 72% of your grade (split between 3 exams) and the rest is between small quizzes and discussion posts. Really good class if you're interested in the ocean, NOT MARINE MAMMALS

Class overall was super doable but lots of work like most quest classes. He liked to argue with groups for fun and was overall very argumentative during project presentations as well as in class/in general. With 2 extra credit opportunities an A is more than doable. If you don't like group work, you should probably find a different quest class.

Loved this man. He's very inspired by what he teaches for this course. He curves every exam to make the mean an 85 so if you are above the average you're ensured to get higher than an 85 on every exam. He also plays music before class which is fun, but make sure you know what songs he plays and by whom because it's his last question on every exam.
Very chill dude, lectures are easy to follow. OCE1001 is really just like a difficult high school science class. Exams aren't too bad, but Canvas exercises are deceptively tricky.

Professor Zimmerman is very passionate about his teaching and his students. Do not be afraid to talk to him. You have to go to class in order to get the notes. Make sure to take pictures of the in class questions because those will be on the tests. Do the extra credit and you should be fine. An A is possible if you study and do the extra credit.

I will be honest. I took this class to fulfill my GenEd Science requirement, and it was definitely more difficult than I expected. However, it is possible to earn an A. You have to go to class everyday to get the material that is on the test. Do the extra credit and go on the extra credit field trip!

DO NOT TAKE IDS2935 WITH ANDREW ZIMMERMAN. You will thank me later. Save your time and some brain cells. He makes this class much harder than necessary and loves to argue with students for fun. One of the most annoying classes and professors that I've ever had.

Super helpful professor and he always made the lectures interesting. The class is super lecture heavy and you have to go to class to get all of the material for the exams. The exams are the majority of the grade for the class and they are deceptively hard. If you study a lot you will be okay but you can't really slack with this class.

Prof. Zimmerman is clearly passionate about what he teaches. His lectures were fun and interesting to listen to. Exams are pretty difficult- I would recommend doing the extra credit- makes the difference between an A and a B. He's a pretty laid-back professor but don't underestimate the difficulty of the exams.

Fun professor and lectures were engaging. Exams were pretty hard but he always curves them. Offered helpful study guides too. Also offered extra credit which was vital in getting an A in this class. As long as you study & do all the assignments & extra credit then you'll definitely pass. I recommend memorizing all practice problems in lecture.

Unless you're required to take it I wouldn't recommend, especially if you're balancing weed-outs at the same time. I'm in engineering, and I just did not have the time needed for this class in addition to Calc 3 and Physics 2. Exams are tough unless you've spent a lot of time studying, and his lecture style is interesting to say the least.

Very passionate about the material and pretty quirky. Makes the class super fun and interesting. Almost no homework but make to attend the non-mandatory lectures, as the exams can be kinda challenging.

I took OCE1001 as a 100% online class. Not much interaction with the professor at all. There were so many lectures (pre-recorded) to watch that it was overwhelming, but the quizzes were difficult if you did not watch the lectures. Discussion posts and homework were easy. The final exam was tough but curved a lot.

Professor Zimmerman is very passionate about the topics, but the lectures were very confusing and some material is difficult to grasp All quizzes and exercises were open source, but the final became really stressful because it was closed note. Quiz and exam questions are incredibly specific, and most info was found in the lectures. Do extra credit.

I took this class just to get a general requirement out of the way so I didn't really care too much about the material. He was really nice and understanding of some situations. Expectations were clear and none of the assignments were too hard. Do what you're supposed to and you'll get an A

I absolutely loved this class! Dr. Zimmerman is so sweet and so passionate about anything and everything ocean-related. My class was all online, so it was a little weird. You do have to do well on all the assignments as there are no tests, so your grade is really dependent on quizzes and homework. If you watch the lectures, you will be fine.

The lectures aren't too boring and Zimmerman is actually really nice and charismatic. I didn't read a single page of the textbook and passed with an A. (You need it for the extra credit assignment which I HIGHLY RECOMMEND if you take this class.) There are a lot a pre-made decks on Quizlet to help study for the exams and quizzes too.

Great class! Hes super passionate about the subject and always kept my attention during lectures. Theres extra credit opportunities to earn up to 6 points added to your final grade and he also curves exams to a class average of 85. If you do the assignments and keep up attendance, theres no reason that you shouldnt pass with an A.

He clearly loves the material which can be boring but tries to make it interesting. Never worried about this class bc there's only 6 homework quizzes. Most of your grade comes from the exams in class. study tophat questions(there are lots)bc a good amount of them are on exams. Lots of extra credit (field trip &online). No need to buy the textbook.

Memorize the slides that he posts to Canvas (I personally found them more helpful than the in-class slides), study the study guides, show up to class for the TopHat points, and review TopHat questions before the exams. An A is possible but you do have to put in some effort for it; know the details. Cool professor, passionate about the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I never had to worry about this class, There is like 4/5 homework assignments spaced throughout the semester that are 10 questions. He uses TopHat and puts 8-10 of those questions onto test so study those. Goes over everything on the test, no trick questions so study and youll get a good grade (exams r curved). dont buy textbook, and DO THE ex cred

Learned a valuable lesson taking his Oceanography class. And that is to never assume a course code of a class ever accurately reflects the difficulty of the class. This was one of the most demanding classes I have taken at UF and it was only for elective credits. You will have to spend most of your time watching his lectures and writing notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Do not take his summer OCE 1001 online. Took what should be a straight forward subject and muddied it with long/boring recorded lectures that you couldn't download powerpoint from. Test were all based on these recordings, not flexible or dynamic in his approach, etc. Don't waste your time, find someone who knows how to run online course content.

This class wasnt bad but is only interesting if you enjoy the subject. Definitely manageable and you can find answers to hw questions online. You do have to attend class because he has clicker questions that'll help your grade in the end. Offers ec but you have to buy a $100 textbook. Ec did help a lot and you have the chance to go on a field trip.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you miss a lecture you basically missed what is going to be on the test. He does post the slides but will leave information out of those slides to make you come to class. You have to answer TopHat questions everyday in class so you have to show up. If he didn't curve the test grades I'd be failing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a good teacher, but contradicts himself a lot. He grades very tough and specifically, even after feedback. Follow his examples as closely as you can.
He is a cool guy.

Extremely helpful if you go in and talk to him. DO NOT BE AFRAID TO ASK FOR HELP. He is always willing to help! Exams are hard but he basically gives you answers if you pay attention to in class questions. Those are on the exam and can only help your grade. Don't expect to get an A if you don't pay attention in class and only cram before exams.
Online lectures are long and boring, you won't pass his quizzes even if you think you understand the material. Definitely not an easy 'A'. Wouldn't recommend.
study extra hard for tests

Zimmerman was a great professor, very passionate about his topics.  You must go to class! Easy pop quizzes every week or so. As long as you thoroughly study the power point lecture slides you should be fine for tests.  Also, DO NOT buy the textbook.  Had an A in the class and didn't open the book once.

The tests are fair and he is clearly very knowledgeable on the subject, but his criticisms for group projects are really rough and sometimes quite rude. He has high expectations that you understand what it means to "be a scientist" without bothering to clarify. Overall a pretty easy class, but be prepared to get frustrated.

This is absolutely the worst class I have ever taken.  Not only are his tests atrociously hard, but he is so unclear it is insane.  Before his exams he holds Q&A sessions, half the time he asks the class for answers because he doesn't even know what he taught us.  His teaching strategies are ridiculously hard, misleading, and unorganized.

Very intellectual professor, not a super interesting dude though and lectures are slow and fairly boring. Super fair grader, fun reading topics and very helpful in terms of feedback. Understanding, forgiving and nice guy, class was very straight forward you'll get a good grade with any amount of effort.

He is smart, but as smart as he is, he is twice as boring. Also, if you're a conservative, he will like you more. It is not super noticeable, but he tries to have some gotcha moments if you lean more liberal on the topics we're discussing. But he does foster good discussion, and I never felt super uncomfy giving my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The readings are a lot. Though they weren't too bad in and of themselves, I often found the quizzes to be more based on memorization of the texts rather than comprehension. That said, Dr. Zubia is an amazing professor and very intelligent. He works to make himself available outside of class, and there is extra credit later on that really helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class had the highest amount of readings and the most difficult ones of any class I've taken. There are also quizzes every week. That being said, he cares about his students. If you go to office hours and engage respectfully in class, you can get a good grade. It will also GREATLY prepare you for any high-level poli-sci course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Zubia is an excellent professor. He not only cares a lot about the course material, but also his students. The course involved a lot of reading with a quiz associated with it every week, but if you can keep up with the texts, this course isn't too difficult. Lectures can be long, but engages a lot with the classt o make up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wouldn't recommend this class. Very reading-heavy and you will find yourself getting more work from this class than any other (quizzes, reflections, etc). While Dr. Zubia is funny and knowledgeable, he doesn't provide any kind of clear grading rubric & the material is unorganized, so students often have to remind him to upload the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He very clearly knew what he was talking about and could talk endlessly in lectures. However, the reading was too excessive and guidelines for rubrics and grading were unclear. He was very smart, but the structure of the class is weak.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Zubia is a very knowledgeable and personable professor, but this class is a lot of work. Reading is necessary to do well in this course. If you listen and participate in the lectures, you should do fine on the quizzes, but he is a very picky grader, so it can be difficult to do well on the reading reflections.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Zubia, while a very knowledgeable individual, is extremely vague with every assignment given as well as giving an exaggerated amount of course readings. Truthfully this class is not worth the level of effort needed to excel in it, and Dr. Zubia does not facilitate understanding and applying the content of the course. Truly disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Makes you buy a $90 dollar course subscription to get all your homework, quizzes, and tests on top of the tuition you're already paying and converted some assignments to harder, in-person versions to make "grading easier", even though all the homework, quizzes, and exams are automatically graded. Just making things harder for students ultimately.

Yary is truly the best professor I've had at UF. Her enthusiasm and energy created an environment I genuinely looked forward to every day. Even when attendance wasn't required, I still chose to go because I enjoyed the class so much. ASL 1 isn't a difficult course when you put in the time and effort. So grateful I took ASL with her!!!!

Professor Santiago's lectures are very fun and engaging. Classes are canceled fairly often and attendance is not mandatory. Everything is accessible online if you miss class and she's really easy to reach through email or office hours if you struggle with anything or have any questions. I had a great experience and plan to take ASL 2 with her too!

Professor Yary is by far one of the best professors I've had at UF. I had her for both ASL 1 and 2, and her care for the language is evident through her teaching. She is great at explaining signs and will always take the time to answer any question you may have. You can tell she loves what she teaches.

Dr. Santiago fostered a welcoming environment to something that can be quite intimidating. She is hilarious and I looked forward to going to her class every morning. She did a lot of engaging activities and encouraged us to immerse ourselves in the deaf community. She is always willing to help a struggling student!

As someone who had never taken any ASL in high school, I took both ASL 1 and 2 back-to-back with this professor. I found that she moves very very quickly and will make you feel stupid if you don't know something in front of the class. If you have extensive knowledge of ASL already, great, but if not, maybe rethink the professor you choose.

Don't take this course with this professor if you suffer from ANY anxiety. The professor was rudely snapping and groaning at me because I had struggled to sign my name during the first week of class and that behavior continued throughout the semester. So many days I left embarrassed and on edge due to her teaching style.

Yary is such an awesome professor! She loves teaching ASL and you can really tell. I loved being able to learn from her. There are a lot of assignments, but they are very short and easy to get done quick. If you go to class and participate, you will do perfectly and definitely get an A.

I really liked Professor Santiago - she was a good instructor and absolutely hilarious even with my limited knowledge of ASL. It's definitely a valuable class to take to both learn a new language and learn about a unique culture.

Yary is amazing! Since ASL is a visual language be prepared to attend class and practice as much as possible.
