Getting involved in Signing Gator helped me do better in ASL as it allowed me to more frequently practice ASL with other students at my level. Yary is very specific about how to communicate in ASL. She always guides her students to success.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Yary is the best professor that I have ever had. She values her relationship with each of her students and makes learning ASL enjoyable. Yary represents the deaf community beautifully and I have learned a lot from her. ASL1101 is not hard as long as you go to class and participate.

By far the funnest class I've taken here at UF. There are a lot of assignments each week, but with good time management on your part, it won't be too bad. Material is not too hard to grasp. Put in the effort and you'll pass with an easy A and with a new skill. I wish I had more semesters here so I could take her for ASL 3 when it opens.

This was my less stressful class for the semester. It is a fun class to learn about, and the Professor really wants you to understand. There is a few assignments due each week, but they are super easy. I wish I could take her next semester!

easy A class. wants you to learn. but you can easily learn yourself off youtube and never need to go to class. quizzes and exams are super easy and very caring teacher. she is very flexible and loves to make people laugh. good if you want an easy A and foreign language credit.

She wanted everyone to come to zoom class but it wasnt for any points so I didnt always go. You have to purchase a subscription to a website to be able to access the assignments and vocab. Theres a lot of quizzes (sometimes 9 in one week) but theyre easy and you can use vocab vids to help, same with the exams. With some effort youll get an A
Love this class and love professor Yary. As with any language you have to practice outside of class, but she really makes it easy to learn and you can pick it up pretty quickly.

I really enjoyed having Yary, she was a good professor and I felt like she was an easy grader. She offered multiple attempts on worksheets with no time limit and I've never gotten less than an A on an assignment, she also grades fast.

An amazing woman and an amazingly funny professor, she adapted so well to her first semester at UF. There were hiccups for sure, but her expertise and passion is evident throughout the class. You get out of ASL what you put in, and if you're willing to commit to learning ASL (correctly) Yary will help you with some tough love.

Yary, which is what she likes to be called, is a fun and energetic person. The first day I was incredibly nervous because she is teaching ASL as a deaf woman, however the class is easy and fun. I enjoyed her class and I hate that her ASL 2 classes are full next semester because she is one of my favorite professors I've had so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Makes lectures and content pretty digestible and generally easy to understand. Follow along with the textbook and make sure you can do lecture and homework problems on your own. He provides one sample exam for each of the midterms and the final, pretty realistic in difficulty level to the actual exams. Witty guy + keeps it interesting. Fair grading
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fun course

Prof Zapletal is alright... your grade is based off three exams and six homeworks, so its very easy to quickly drop to a low grade. His lectures arent very clear, and some complicated proofs that dont show how to complete basic proofs using the theorem. Personally, the textbook didnt help me much either, so I had to rely on outside sources.

Attendance not mandatory. Personally didn't find his lectures helpful, but some did. Harder to develop intuition for proofwriting as a noob cus the logic behind his methods was at times unclear.
Has a sense of humor, reasonable grader, and offers an opportunity to do a presentation that drops 3 hws. 
Overall fine, I won't avoid him in the future.

The guy is genuinely super helpful, and his lectures are pretty good. There were a lot of "ums" but honestly it helped slow down the lecture so I didn't mind at all. The textbook and lectures are both vital for you to do well, but it is a time consuming class especially if you haven't done proofs before (I hadn't). Cool guy, would recommend.

You get so little graded assignments that if you mess up on one you are guarenteed to be going down in grades, especially since his grades does not seem to follow any rubrics. This is worsened by the fact that you could almost never understand his lectures through his ughs and umms.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Zapletal is such a clear lecturer and he makes difficult concepts seem super easy. Homework is easy and he gives plenty of feedback and an opportunity to make it up for full credit if you miss parts. The tests are hard, but fair and make up the majority of the grade. His office hours are helpful and he is an understanding and helpful guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zapletal's lectures are very confusing. I feel lost during lectures and have to read the book/watch videos on each topic just to somewhat understand them. He gives 3 tests and 6 homework assignments, so if you do poorly on one exam, you're pretty much done for. He doesn't answer questions clearly and doesn't explain topics or teach well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quite literally the worst prof ever. He didn't follow any of the material on the homeworks or exams at all. I felt like he was speaking a different language even after trying to read the textbook beforehand. He would ramble on and on about things that didn't matter and didn't directly answer any questions asked by students. Do not take this class.
Confusing lecturer - many stop attending class

He is an okay professor but does not teach well. He sits there and drones on and rarely follows the notes put out by the course coordinator, Shabazz. If you can take Shabazz you should, but if not you can take whoever and then just watch Shabazz's lectures since she records them. This is what I did and then I went to discussion, and I was fine.

His lectures are extremely confusing. It often feels as though he's unprepared for lecture and just winging it as it goes on. I stopped coming to class after 3 classes and just watched recordings of a different calc professor it was that bad. Do not recommend!!!!!

Not a lot of requirements - usually just a few tests, which typically are not difficult, but you really need to be able to learn on your own because of the confusing/unprepared lectures. The teaching style is seemingly influenced by an ancient mathematical philosophy somehow aware of but stubbornly adverse to modern discoveries and advancements.

Dr. Zapletal is definitely a great professor who knows what he is talking about. Lectures were a little slow at times, but that gave us plenty of time to properly understand the concepts being taught, which was especially necessary towards the end of the course. The most important thing I learned was probably to never forget the Jacobian.

Honestly, I had him for MAC2313 and he wasnt good. It was a huge lecture hall and he would get really nervous. BUT with the small classroom size and with him being able to make the course material, he was a really great lecturer for Diff Eq!! The homework was optional, and the exams were open note and based on hw. He made a hard class managable :)

Dr. Zapletal is probably not the best choice for calculus, but was excellent for DiffEQ. Yes he does have a stutter, but it does not make him difficult to understand. His lectures covered everything you need to know for exams, and he went over concepts multiple times to make sure students understand. Oh, and exams are open notes too, which was nice

He is the absolute worst professor Ive ever had in my entire life. He is extremely hard to understand and doesnt care about his students. He will ignore people with questions. I had to watch the lecture videos for another professor to get by in the class. I would steer clear of him if at all possible. I would give him a zero if possible.

This guy cant talk to save his life. You get lost after trying to understand the lectures through all the uh and ums. Just went and did the clicker at the end of lecture and watched Huangs lecture. Only thing that saved my grade. But the exams were very similar to practice exam online and the review sheet they give online.

Pretty bad lecturer, stutters a-lot and sometimes even did lecture problems incorrectly. I ended up watching another professors lectures during my lecture time, which is honestly how I passed the class. If you can try to get another professor, but if you are stuck with him just watch someone else lectures.

At the beginning of the semester, I was nervous beyond belief for my first class at UF. Zapletal seemed like a harsh grader who gave boring lectures. But I couldn't be further from the truth. He was interesting as a speaker and generous as a grader. I couldn't be happier taking his section and would recommend him to anyone.
He seems to be very knowledgeable about what he teaches and is very enthusiastic in class. It's obvious that he has a passion for math and it shows.

Literally worst professor I've had here at UF. Constantly stuttering during lectures and extremely poor time management. Only reason I went to class was for clicker points. If you're stuck with him just watch Huang's taped lectures. I'd suggest buying a Chegg subscription if you need help with this course. Honestly nothing positive to say about him

He is extremely hard to understand. I had to watch Huangs lectures to actually learn the material. The only reason I came to class was for the hitt clicker points. If possible I would try to switch to Huangs lectures but if not then just be prepared to have to watch her lectures instead of listening in class.

By far one of the worst professors I have had. Please switch out and try to get Huang. His class lectures were a waste of time and he could not clearly convey the topic we were learning that day. Constant stuttering and skipping over important parts of the lecture to save time gave me a hard time in this class. JUST TAKE HUANG!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I don't understand why he is even lecturing at all. Most students either skip or only show up for the HITT clicker points because you can barely understand a word that he says. Every class I see kids with headphones in listening to Dr. Huang's lectures instead of his. Don't waste your time, take Calc 3 with Dr. Huang.

Legitimately the worst lecturer i've ever heard. You could put a third grader with a stutter up at the front of the class and it would be more intelligible than what Zapletal spits out. Either get studyedge or watch the online lectures from the other teacher, and then show up at the end of lecture to get the hitt clicker point.

Dr. Zapletal seemed as if he absolutely hated having to teach students. I recently discovered that he is tenured and that helped to explain his attitude. I'm not sure if he had an accident of some sort or if he genuinely has terrible public speaking skills but he stutters like it is his job. It is very difficult to understand him in lectures.

A lot of vocal pauses ("uh"), but not too bad of a lecturer. However, he rarely finished the notes, I would have to watch Huang's taped lectures to catch up. Homework can be difficult, but the exams are easy as long as you master the basic concepts from the WebAssign. Always extra credit points on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class isnt too bad, for what it is, considering the other lecturer provided all other resources and information. Zapletals lectures were, however, awful. I couldnt focus on anything through his speech impediment, and often left feeling more confused about the subject matter.

I have never heard the word "ah" more times in my short existence on this earth before entering into this man's lectures. I would strongly recommend against taking any class of his, as you will be on your own as far as the material goes.

He is a pretty boring professor. The book is pretty boring. Unless you want to do the HW problems ad nauseam and be at office hours every single week, I would get Study Edge. They just teach you what's on the exams and it's a lot more entertaining than actually paying attention in class.  Go to class for clicker points or you'll be on the verge.

He's a very funny guy and you can tell he's passionate about math and a little physics sometimes, but it just sucks that it's kinda hard to understand him sometimes. His math jokes are actually slightly amusing sometimes, and you'll learn that ONLY A FOOL WOULD FORGET THE JACOBIAN! You'll more than likely need videos to enhance your understanding.

Dr. Zapletal is clearly well-versed in the material, but he is quite difficult to comprehend overall. Whether you are good at Calculus or not, you WILL have to learn the concepts on your own. If you have him, figure out a way: read the textbook, find a mentor, check out OCW MIT's online lectures, but make sure you do something and you will succeed.
Hilarious guy. Best teacher you could get in calc 3. As the other person said, DON'T FORGET THE JACOBIANNNN!
Lectures are very slippery, need to be nimble to solve many of the problems.  You must not forget the Jacobian.
Very nice professor. Loves math. Is patient in office hours. Provides sample tests. Students can use notes on exams.

I loved him as a professor. He can be difficult to understand at times, but he repeats himself a lot. Test are open book, open note. People even brought solution manual's and he didn't care. Only 3 test though, so if you screw one up you are screwed. He gives sample tests, very similar to the actual test. Some test questions are homework questions.

Don't take this class. I've been an A student especially in math all my life.  got an A in calc 2 no problem. I couldn't understand anything from his lectures and I ended up teaching myself. I still think I understood the material but his tests didn't correlate to the homework. He did give good partial credit though. I got an A-. Don't expect an A.
Pretty impossible to understand. Very nice man but a very bad speaker. Class wasn't too helpful but his open book/note tests saved me.

Pretty good teacher.  Tests open book and open note, so paying attention and taking notes will help but is not 100% necessary.  Is willing to help students outside of class.  A pretty nice guy and professor.

Took his class last spring for Honors Calculus 3.  Great class.  Open book/open note tests.  He also likes to randomly smile at his work while writing on the board, which is funny.  "It IS continuous!"
Hard to understand, but open book and note tests make life easy.  Hardest part is strict grading scale.  Grade consists of 100% of tests.  Good class if youre good at calc and/or studying for calc

He's a good honors calc3 teacher.  I went to class because I liked his lectures, but I had friends who didn't go to class and they did well.  He can be awkward to talk to alone, but definitely is a great teacher.  Tests open note and open book.

Great lecturer and explains things thoroughly...he's awkward if you try to talk to him one on one, but otherwise he grades fairly and as long as you do the assigned practice problems, you will not have any issues with the class

DR. Z is the MAN; he is extremely knowledgeable. I would highly recommend taking him for Calc 2. His grading is amazing! Somehow a 2 out of 5 became a 92. His partial credit is the best I’ve seen. His practice tests are nice too.
Pretty easy teacher, just be prepared to teach yourself as well. If your not an independent learner, dont take his course. Nice guy though.

I can't speak for his ability to teach calculus, but prof. Zapletal was a great logic teacher. While I might like to see a bit more formality in some proofs, the intuitions that he gives behind proofs is awesome. Also, if you ask a question, he often seems to understand the point (or your misconception) behind it and directly addresses it.
He was disparagingly easy, but he couldn't really explain himself when it came to... anything.
Dr. Z is pretty cool.  He doesn't bog you down with lots of sill yproblems or anything, he just shows you how to do the calculus.

The above review is exactly right. You're on your own to teach yourself, but he give a sample test before the actual exam. The difference is only a few number changes. So learn how to do the sample test (you don't even have to memorize formulas!)

Get in this class if you can. He cant teach but his tests are sooo easy. Just go the class before the test and he'll do the review sheet which is a replica of the test with different numbers. oh and his tests are also open book! Get this teacher, hes easy

Lectures are meaningless; I went to class. I believe one would've done better self-studying the entire class than listening to him. Originally had 6 homework assignments, but reduced it to 5, leading to less buffer for grade. Talks more about research than the actual class itself. Had extra material to go over, so he had class during reading days.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zeng's lectures are just screenshots and snippets of the book read out, which are not at all helpful.  His grading is very inconsistent, with points being deducted on homeworks for no discernable reason.  There was a large amount of extra credit at the end of the course.
Doesn't have office hours himself & sucks.

Dr. Zeng is a very kind professor and was very responsive via email. Grades are based off 2 midterms + 1 Final, which is primary based on chapters 20-26. His lectures were informative but really had no benefits to me doing well on the exams. If you're passionate about chemistry take him. The final exam at the end is challenging but fair. Good luck!

A very boring class all-in-all. There is not much engagement going on. Lack of homework means very little practice with the content unless you force yourself to do textbook problems. Very easy to get lost in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Zeng didn't explain material clearly. It felt like it was a better use of time to skip lectures and read the textbook instead. His material was mostly about statistics and a deeper dive into chem 2 topics with a small section on chemistry instruments. Your grade is based on  3 exams and the final, but 1 of them can get dropped.

Half of the material overlapped with statistics and gen chem, but I often left class feeling confused. He's kind but doesn't explain content well--definitely read the textbook. Grade is only based on four exams, each with 20 MCQ and sometimes a short response, and you get to drop your lowest exam grade. Few useful practice questions are given.

Her lectures are hard to understand, her grading is so strict, definitely not beginner friendly. However she is available a lot after class but beware of the queue. Take this class if you started coding in the womb. If not, do yourself a favor and skip

Took this class in Fall semester 2024. Overall, the class was relatively easy. It definitely helps to have prior coding experience coming in as the first few weeks were essentially teaching you how to use an IDE and how to code in python. Labs are easy, exams are kinda hard, and don't procrastinate on projects. They are really long.

This review is for CDA 3101--wasn't an option in the RMP drop-down menu.   Prof. Zhou is easily one of the most caring and responsive professors that I've had.  She goes far out of her way to make learning comfortable and enjoyable for everyone.   I will absolutely take a course with her again if I have the opportunity.  Inspirational!

The professor is very helpful and wants you to succeed, but the lectures can be dry. Watching recordings at 2x speed and using resources like Unstuck study helped me prepare for the coding-heavy projects. Overall, a manageable class with a lenient grading policy.
There are not any materials for practicing before any exams, and the exams have different styles of questions. (Read all the answers carefully)

Professor Zhou has a thick accent that makes it difficult to understand her lecture material. Quizzes were difficult to score 10/10 on because of confusing questions that take off points for input errors. Also, study guides are not enough to pass quizzes and exams.

workload is insane for a intro class. she doesn't curve bc the average on the tests is around a 70%, but she doesn't consider that most people already have prior experience, and the people who don't get screwed. projects take forever, there's a lab every week, and you don't get a moment to rest and catch your breath.
I really liked the way she explained concepts and how she draws out diagrams for a problem, it made things much easier to understand. She definitely wants you to pass and is willing to help you.

Had no experience with Python yet found it very easy to understand her lessons during class. She follows the e-textbook so even if you dont watch the lectures you should be okay, but she does go over alot of helpful examples very slowly so that anyone could understand
Hard class for students with no experience, good and lenient professor. Complete every lab/project ahead. Would recommend.

Lectures were not mandatory, but she is a wonderful person. She is always caring for you to succeed and learn everything very well from her class. I would 100% take this class again. There were many labs, assignments, projects that could take a lot of time if programming is new to you.

Very smart teacher and really wants you to learn, but her lectures are boring so it's easy to fall behind (especially in the online section). You really need to listen to the lectures and take good notes. The weekly quizzes were straightforward with a great study guide, but you really need to study for the coding part of the exams. LOTS OF PROJECTS
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her lectures are so good and she gives so much extra credit you can earn up to 3% on your final grade. The tests are similar to her practice tests, and the labs and projects can be hard sometimes but her walk-throughs in class help so much.
be prepared to spend alot of time on coding projects, however, coming into the class with prior coding knowledge was helpful, I watched the lectures I needed to watch on zoom. Not bad class.

Lectures are unengaging. Professor takes a very slow pace and it's hard to stay focused. Halfway through the semester I stopped going to the lectures (attendance is not mandatory) and started watching the recordings at 2x speed. I had limited coding experience going in and that made the course easy so far.
Lots of confusing projects, does not lend itself to people with no past programming experience.

If you have no coding experience, its HARD. Very very hard. I was required to take this for DAS and had no interest in programming but was willing to learn. I went to lectures for the first month or so then realized it didn't help all that much. She seemed nice, but classes were majorly unengaging. She does offer EC for zybooks so that's cool.
There are chances to get extra credits.

She's nice and a great welcome to UF CS. READ THE TEXTBOOK AND DO ITS ACTIVITIES. Everyone I know who succeeded had high As near or over 100%, and they read the book. Most struggling to pass didn't read the book and assumed lecture would be sufficient. They're great supplemental material, but read the book for an easy A. Great class, GL!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The textbook explains things really thoroughly. It's a good resource if you're confused about anything. The lectures can be a bit dull if you have prior experience, but the projects and labs are fun. Make sure to allocate a lot of time for them though, especially for the last project.

I was honestly nervous about this class going in as I wasn't that great at coding, even after fundamentals. This class was pretty good though, there were a lot of ways to practice in each section, tests were fair and curved, and projects were actually easy than the fundamental classes.

Skipped lectures and used Zybooks which was more helpful imo, but watched the lectures where she helped with labs and projects. She's there to help you out and wants you to pass. Easy EC opportunities. The last project was a bit of a pain, but doable. If attending on Zoom, she usually ignored the chat and people who turned their mics on completely.

This was my first time taking a programming class so it was very hard at the beginning. I just watched lectures at home because I didn't find any worth going in person. You have to buy the online textbook for submitting stuff which is somewhere around $70. I had no experience so I felt behind compared to the other people I encountered in the class.

She normally spends a lecture showing us how to set up when we have a lab or project which is good. Quizzes are a bit difficult but exams are usually well-prepped for, though the coding questions on them are tough. Zybooks is helpful for learning, it's just a lot to stay on top of. Prof is nice, and there's lots of office hours if you need help
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Decent lecturer but project criteria often does not match the exact zybooks specifications and vice versa

Not the worst, but I've seen better. Not engaging with lectures and her TA's are even worse. Grading and feedback from them is horrible and don't bother asking why because you'll be waiting till finals to hear anything back.

I didn't love Prof Zhou, but I didn't hate her either. I honestly just don't think she's a strong lecturer. She isn't super engaging, but she is really great at helping set up the projects during lectures. The stuff is hard though even though it is Python, so be ready to spend a lot of time coding. She also gives lots of extra credit opportunities.
Extremely good professor. Zybooks is a bit expensive but her lectures are great. Recently moved the course to Python which made it relevant to the modern day

Prof. Zhou is fantastic. I thought the course was very well structured and she taught everything with crystal clear clarity. I really enjoyed learning more about Python and as a first time programmer appreciated how in depth everything was. All quizzes, exams, and labs were very fair. This is by far the best intro level course I've taken at UF.

Overall a decent professor. She can be cold and abrupt, but reasonably so because the class is HUGE. I think her projects/labs are more than fair. Her exams can be a little challenging, but they're only worth like 1/4 of the class. She offers like just over 3% of EC for your overall grade, which is very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very easy class, especially because it was python. If you have any previous experience this class will be a breeze. I did all my projects/labs the day of. You don't have to watch the lectures but they are very helpful if you do watch them, professor explains stuff for labs/projects/quizzes/etc. Online textbook was meh.

Professor Zhou is really caring & the class is structured well. Just stay on top of your projects, start them early and you should easily be able to get an A. People who are complaining probably waited last minute to do projects which you can not do in this class. Programming takes time to think about problems so tryna to cram just doesn't work.

Course consisted of quizzes, projects, stepik exercises, and exams. The quizzes and exams could be a little tricky so make sure you know your stuff, but other than that it was fine. Just make sure to properly test any projects before you hand them it. There were plenty of materials listed for you to access, read, and learn from as well.

if u dont have coding exp prep to be overwhelmed+ struggle to understand the logic of coding but dont worry bc it can take time. if ur new to coding put in time to study and truly learn whats taught bc the moment u get behind and scrape by in class, u will struggle to recover. start projects early, the pakudex proj will kill u.

The class set up makes it impossible to fail because there are so many assignments and extra credit opportunities. That being said, unless you have prior coding experience it is very time consuming and you'll want to work on the projects early so that you can see TA if needed. I never went to class or watched the lectures and still made a B.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Entertaining teacher, who explains the material very well. Very easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The lectures were just reviews of material, while the actual material was pre-recorded by other professors. The assignments are fairly simple, with a lot of extra credit opportunities. I had virtually no coding experience and the class was easy, if you don't understand something the interactive textbook was a great source to see how concepts work.

The class is well organized and will force you to learn what is necessary. The in-person lectures were eh--good practice for exams but not very helpful otherwise. TAs are almost always available. Start projects early so you can ask them for help if needed; they'll basically fix your problem for you. Do all the EC available.

Lectures arent needed that much, its a flipped class and watching modules before and going to the discussions and live coding sessions are better, also can be a little hard to understand and if you watched videos you are good tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I think Prof Zhou is a sweet and caring person, but I never found much use going to lectures. Zybooks (the interactive textbook) will teach you everything you need to know. Office hours for coding help takes a min. of an hour on the weeks before a project is due. If you have no programming experience this class will be a challenge. Time is the key

Prof Zhou is a very nice and patient prof. Answers any questions and explains anything. The class itself is structured very nicely. It's flipped, so you watch lectures before. 3 days of meeting in a class - basically kahoot, live coding, lab. Attendance is only mandatory for the lab. The class isn't that hard, and there is a lot of extra credit.

It was a flipped class, so we watched lectures on our own before class. And in class, I really liked the idea of the Tuesday quiz competitions because that motivated us to be 100% focused on the questions, thus preparing well for the weekly online quizzes (through Honorlock). I also liked some of the labs and projects we had.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's okay, not great but definitely not the worst. Lecture is not mandatory but lab is. Lecture is okay but there are too many people, Lisha has an accent, and she isn't very organized when it comes to explaining. Your TA will be more important than the professor. However, class is well organized and there is a lot of ec! DONT PROCRASTINATE!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: As someone with absolutely no programming experience, this class was HARD and took a lot of time. I found watching the lecture videos better than the textbook - they're mostly easy to follow! Playing the kahoot games in class also helped prepare for quizzes/exams. Plenty of EC (up to 8 points). Not hard to get an A if you just put in the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: They call it an introductory course but you need a background in programming if you want to pass this class. The lectures are just kahoots, you learn from reading the textbook. The projects/labs take hours each and you are teaching yourself. Awful class if you like to actually be taught the content, but if you like self-teaching then go for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I expected this to be a normal in person class however 90% of the material you had to learn on your own and we played Kahoot during the lecture periods.

Very easy and fun! Lots of EC, which you can copy from the live coding sessions. Weekly quizzes are taken directly off of menti from lectures (post-lecture recordings available). Projects and labs are time-heavy but you shouldn't have a lot of problems with them given the resources and how some project/labs are literally walked through.

She is very hard to understand. You have to teach yourself the entire courseload through zybooks -> online textbook. If you don't have previous programming experience, this course will give you a run for your money.

I absolutely adore prof Zhou. The class is hard, but learning how to code will always be hard. However, she makes this hard learning entertaining by assigning fun labs and projects. She is also always in office hours and is very accessible outside of class. She really helped me a lot and I would definitely take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Honestly, this class isn't too hard if you understand the basics already, if you don't it'll probably be more difficult at first. I don't like the flipped classroom style so beware of that, might as well not show up for class although problem-solving on Thursday is good. The prof is very hard to follow when explaining questions though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Lisha definitely tries her best but she's hard to follow along with sometimes. As of Fall 2021, we had a flipped classroom with practice problems on Tuesdays and live coding on Thursdays (although I skipped Thursdays lol). Not a super hard class but I would definitely make use of discussion bc you'll def be lost the first few weeks.

I didn't rely much upon her teaching abilities, but the class structure is excellent. The projects and labs blend together the material quite well. As long as you are able to keep up it is manageable and even easy. Plenty of extra credit.

Can't speak on her teaching abilities but doing Zybooks and watching the problem solving sessions before quizzes helped a lot. The class is project-heavy but the TAs are very accessible. Do the extra credit throughout the semester and you can easily end up with over a 100 in the class. The exams are just like the practice exams

Can't say much about Dr. Zhou's teaching ability. However, the class is excellently structured/organized. TAs are amazing, accessible, and leave you meaningful feedback. Watch the lecture videos instead of the problem solving sessions. Bulk of your grade comes from the individual projects and exams which are easy if you don't procrastinate.

Prog 1 has a lot of projects, starting early is pretty much a requirement in order to do well in the class. Zybooks was a huge help as a complement to lectures, some people just skip lectures and only do Zybooks (you also get extra credit if you do enough Zybooks).
She's a solid prof and cares about her students/the structure of the class.

A really good professor goes over everything. Really suggest going to the problem-solving sessions as they are really helpful for quizzes and labs. if you pay attention you will be good for this class. She also offered extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof Lisha is helpful, answers quickly and wants her students to succeed. Go to the problem-solving-sessions. Do all the extra credit (bumped me from a B to an A-). I had no coding experience so it was rough but ask the TAs for help, they're great. Start projects EARLY. Labs take a few hours, projects take days. There are only 2 exams. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I think that Zhou's teaching ability is better expressed through her design of the class rather than through her lectures. There's so much practice with each concept that it's hard to not understand the material. The course heavily utilizes the TA's as the primary source of help. Zhou definitely cares about her students and provides a lot of EC.
Class is pretty easy if you've programmed before, if you haven't, it can be difficult. Most of the grade is based on projects and labs.

Easy A if you do your work and have some prior programming experience. If not, Zhou is accomodating through office hours. Lot of work but also a pretty good amount of extra credit. Make sure to start your projects ahead of time, especially for 2 and 3. Her lectures are kinda worthless though, only her problem solving sessions matter for quizzes.

Lisha Zhou gives you all the materials to succeed. She is generally helpful in office hours and offers enough extra credit to get an A even with a couple of bad exams or quizzes. The only thing to remember in this class is to start your projects early. TA and Zhou will help those students a lot more than students doing it right before it is due.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you have prior programming experience, you are good, easy A. If not then good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Zhou is the main course coordinator and she truly cares about her students. The lecture videos, Zybooks, the multitude of TA office hours, and problem-solving sessions allow you to master the material pretty well. Easy A with prior programming experience and a learning curve without, but you can still succeed if you keep up with the workload.
helped me alot as a beginner

Had her for COP3502 over the summer which was all online due to covid but her zoom lectures were informative and helped a lot during the projects and exams. She would elaborate on concepts that were kinda hard and she would answer as many questions as she can during lecture which further helped my understanding of the concept(s). A very nice prof.

Always would answer my emails and answer my questions clearly, not sure why her rating is so low. definitely one of the better professors i have had here. The class is easy and interesting if you dont fall behind on material.

I took her twice for COP3502. The lectures aren't the most exciting and sometimes out of sync with the labs/projects (which were KEY), but they were very helpful for exams. She was also eager to help outside of class. And the Coronavirus response/shift to online was pretty seamless. I'd join the all female class if you can/like smaller classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Zhou cares about your success in the course and gives ample opportunity to consult her outside of class. I took the course online and found I had good support from her and the TA to clear up any questions on content or projects. Highly recommend her class and would take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Super sweet! Her lectures are easy to understand, and as long as you actually put in work for the projects you'll be fine. But start early because those deadlines creep up.
Solid Professor
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I had her for programming 1 in the Fall and she has significantly improved as a professor. She is always available outside of class to help and will go above and beyond for you.

So I thought she was the worst professor ever, but I later found out there were some extenuating circumstances where she got super late notice about teaching the class. Lectures are worthless but you dont need them so dont show up. Zybooks is solid and the exams are stressful but easy to study for. Use your TA for projects.

Lisha Zhou does her best to help all of her students and ensure they understand what is going on in the class. I definitely recommend doing zybooks before class because it makes the content easier to understand, but overall Lisha does a great job of teaching Java fundamentals. If you're really confused, I definitely recommend her or using TAs!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: By far the most unorganized professor I have ever had. She seriously waited until the last five days of the semester to put in the majority of our grades, meaning we are blindsided with no time to fix it. The entire course revolves around online txtbook, Zybooks, enabling her to sit in the background of a 500+ person class without teaching anybody.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lisha Zhou piles on weekly labs and multiple projects that require an immense amount of time and effort, but offers zero help throughout the course. She pawns you off to one of her many TAs, who seem just as clueless to what's going on as the students. If you are interested in computer science, I would advise you to find a different professor.

As someone who has coding experience the class started off fine, but after the first exam I felt like they were implementing concepts we never learned into projects and labs. Had us constantly downloading different software and it felt like I was trying to figure out how to use programs than actually learning the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Rough class.

I've never taken a programming class before this one and I had no coding experience and this was a ROUGH experience. Lectures were completely useless, Prof had a heavy accent and the material covered was either confusing or irrelevant. The only way to learn was through the (mandatory) textbook, struggling through the labs and projects, and the TAs.

I took her in fall 2019, it was her first semester teaching, so you cant expect perfection. She seems to want to improve as a teacher, asking for all the criticism possible to get better. Almost never went to lectures, read all of zybooks instead to teach myself. Be prepared to do the labs and projects since they are a big part of your grade.
great

Took this class Fall 2019. Was very simple (but I did have prior programming experience). The few times I went to office hours, I was able to be helped by the TAs. Zhou is a good lecturer, but I didn't go to class all too much.

Prof. Zhou seems a little unorganized in her lectures, but she helps a lot before the test. There are not many practice exams and some of her TAs do not do much help. This class is extremely difficult for students who do not have experience or background in programming.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The TA's weren't that helpful explaining much. I felt like the TA's were more confused than I was the whole semester. Some TA even cursed in the mic during a midterm and it was really unprofessional. The only TA you can trust is Josh cause he was my TA. Class is heavy with projects
Not a fan. There is extra credit but its a group project. Class is very unorganized since she is a new teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable and resourceful.
Very unorganized

The professor is very nice and she really did try to help but it seems th explaining wasn't sufficient for me. I think the curriculum was very good. Mind you I had not programming experience, the class was difficult in terms of time commitment and material, and studying as the slides weren't self explanatory. Coming out of I did learn A LOT.
Lots of extra credit. I felt like the teacher's personality was different than what was on the slides, though she is really good.
Good for people with prior programming knowledge.

Lisha is a good professor but nothing was curved when having averages in the 50s and 60s. Luckily exams rent weighted as much so I still got a good grade and was able to enjoy myself when taking the course as the projects are fun and the last one was an optional group project.

Shes a caring professor who emails back quickly and gives extra credit, but sucks as a teacher. She just reads off of lecture slides and doesnt explain topics enough for you to understand them for projects or exams. Even with the textbook the class makes little sense. Projects make up most of the grade but are too complicated.
Very helpful and inspirational.

i really struggled with programming initially, and while Mrs Zhou did not make the class very easy, the increased difficulty made it worthwhile as i feel like i learned a lot. Zhou is an extremely nice woman and very smart as she's already lecturing at such a young age. unlike any other professor i had, she always would answer messages immediately

For a first semester programming class, I found it to be quite accessible. I initially struggled through the first half but was able to find my footing in the second half. Zhou is a good professor, and explained difficult concepts in a manner in which I could easily wrap my brain around it. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She was fantastic for her first semester teaching such a big class!! I loved her so much she is so nice and willing to help

I happen to be one of those having previous programming experience, and do not feel like the course is too hard. If you want to get good grades, you need to read the online book. Class size is too big though.
Very nice prof and accessible outside the classroom. You can drop the lowest quiz and project. Final exam only contains multiple choice questions. My TA is awesome BTW ^-^.
Prof. Zhou is very nice, hilarious, and smart. The course is challenging and requires significant effort and commitment. But I learned a lot.

Your experience in this class will come down to how much precious coding experience you have. I took AP CS in 12th grade so I was mostly familiar w the material but I still had to work for the A. Her lectures are useless, she reads off the board. Time consuming projects and weekly labs. I found the textbook very useful though, read that & your good

This has to be one of the worst classes ever. If you have no programming experience, this class is setting you up for failure. Projects are difficult and if you ask for help on them it is considered cheating leaving students frustrated and office hours flooded with students. Not to mention you can't understand anything she says in the lectures.

You really should have experience before taking this class. Zhou is very nice, but she strikes me as not having much experience-Slack is used for course communication but it is often an area of confusion. I felt that the course was disorganized, there's heavy reliance on TAs. Some TAs were awesome and really tried to help, other TAs were lazy/rude.

COP3502 at UF is supposed to be an introductory programming class. However, it felt like anything but. There are labs due every week as well as projects that are worth 40% of your grade. Exams are pretty tricky, and the free response section was difficult. Her lectures and slides aren't helpful, and can be confusing.

There are only two types of people in this class, which are people with programming experience and people who have had none. If you are in the first group of people then this class should be easy. If you are in the second group, then this class wil most likely be very hard due to lack of teaching from professor. Use the textbook, it will teach you.

Zhou certainly isnt the best lecturer, but shes very understanding and nice. I found the class manageable by staying on top of my stuff (and that is with years of previous programming experience). Make sure to read the online book, it will help you tremendously in the quizzes. The labs and projects are fun, and graded by the TAs.
A lot of these intro classes have grad student or just graduated PHDs that either don't want to be professors or it's their first year. For a first year teacher, she's fine.

She reads from slides of powerpoint and doesn't explain anything. They say you don't need programming experience to take this class, but only the kids that did were doing well. If you need help, go to office hours, which are packed every hour of day with 20 kids min. She drops lowest quiz and project, but exams are impossible. No curve(that I know)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great professor. Very kind, always willing to help. Bit of an accent but she is definitely suited for her job

BEWARE of her flipped classroom-style class with mandatory attendance. However, she was a really sweet and caring professor. Provided notes corresponding to each lecture and study guides that I relied on to study for exams. Preferred her over the other professor that teaches this class and is prominent in HUN.
The SWEETEST most caring professor I've had. Her exams are very fair, and the material is interesting. Take her if you can!!

Such an amazing human aside from teaching. Very caring and makes material so interesting and helps students without making us feel bad. I think if I paid attention more during class instead of cramming I could've gotten an A. Exam averages were literally 95%, she's amazing
I love Dr. Acosta she is very caring and understanding. I would recommend taking this course with her. She is awesome.
She is the nicest and her exams and 100% fair. Take her if you can!

Dr. Acosta was very nice. She genuinely cared for her students. However, the course was too easy. Every exam, the average was A. Easy A is not bad, but at upper level course, I was expecting more challenge.
The professor was nice, and cared for her students. Her lectures were fine, not super great. She was very clear about grading criteria, which was nice.

Dr. Acosta truly cares about students. She is extremely receptive to questions inside and outside of class, provides study guides for every exam, as well as optional in class reviews. All exam averages were A's. You'll learn in this class and also do well. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Acosta was such a wonderful teacher. This was an Honors Uncommon Read course, and I honestly didn't know what to expect, but Dr. Acosta was warm and genuine from the start. She demonstrated true respect for students to speak truthfully in her classroom and always seemed understanding of everyone's different perspectives.

Dr. Acosta inspired me to major in Nutritional Sciences. She was genuine, truly caring and kept me interested during lecture. I wish other faculty were as engaging as her! I'll try to take as many classes with her as possible. Off topic, but I love her fashion sense and wish she would give me a makeover!
Pro. Acosta is an amazing person and teacher. She is extremely passionate about the material. You will love it!!!

Professor Acosta lectures so well that it makes you NOT want to miss lectures. She is kind, approachable, and is by far the best professor I have had at UF during my three years here so far. I would highly recommend this class. It does require studying, but nothing out of the ordinary. You will not regret taking this class with Dr. A. Loved it!

Professor Acosta is an awesome lecturer.  She is very energetic and passionate about what she teaches! She is such a cool person and is VERY straightforward on her exams.  If you put forth the effort to learn and memorize the material, you will do well.  Best class I have taken yet.

Amazing professor! Great lecturer, keeps it interesting with lots of visuals. Always trying to engage the class in discussion, even though there are a ton of students. Very available outside of class, and provides lots of study materials for exam. I would highly recommend taking her class! The textbook is optional.

A nice guy, but a horrendously bad teacher. Demonstrations are cool, but can you focus on teaching instead? I don't know how the Rice Physics department manages to hire low-quality professors. The only person who is worse than this man is Jared Stetson.

Easily the most enthusiastic prof I've had. Lectures are posted beforehand, but you have to attend online class to take live mini-quizzes. Material can be tough, but everything is kinda breezed over so the quizzes and exams are practically out-of-the-book. Acosta will be hand-wavy with the math, which just means you often just plug numbers in.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Probably the hardest course I've taken, but that's advanced physics for you. Charming and intuitive presentation makes even math-heavy slog lectures at least somewhat bearable, while more fun topics make you actually interested in what you're learning. Make time for it, and stay on top of the weekly lectures, you're quizzed (very lightly) on them.
Had him for phy2049 online, lectures were focused and funny at times. Lots of great demos. Broke down the concepts well and showed the derivations but did not require them.

Professor Acosta is a really sweet guy who cares a lot about his students and the material he teaches. He is so passionate about Physics and wants you to be passionate too. The material for PHY2048 was a nightmare, but Prof Acosta does his best to get you through his sections.
He's a really nice guy. He knows the content and teaches it really well.

The coolest dude ever! He made physics much more manageable for me to learn. Although he teaches it with Hamlin and Hagen I would definitely say that he is the best and that I learned the most from him because he takes the time during lecture to make you feel confident about learning physics . It is a hard class and you definitely need to study.
If you want to feel truly inspired by a physics 1 lecture, TAKE THIS GUY. Simply the best. He also works on the super collider at Cern in his freetime which is dope.

Took PHY2048 when it was taught by Acosta, Hamlin, and Hagen. I'd say Acosta was the second best prof. He gives decent lectures, but spends too much time deriving formulas that are given on the exams, so it's very boring in class at times. He's very nice and approachable. Gives very easy clicker questions. Go to class for the clickers. 5% EC.
Dr. Acosta is amazing! He explains the material very well and also is quite humorous during lecture. He is very fair on his exams but this does not mean its easy, still have to work for it!

I didnt take physics before this class but did well because there were so many resources available (old exams, additional videos, etc). Class demonstrations were super helpful for visualizing concepts. Sometimes, during exams Id think wow this is a really good question for testing our understanding. Favorable grading scale. Very thorough prof.

Professor Acosta explains concepts slowly enough to follow, but deeply enough to truly understand the material as well. He makes attempts to make the lectures entertaining (although not all of his jokes are winners). He films videos online that can substitute for lecture attendance if necessary (clicker points are extra credit).
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Acosta is a genius when it comes to physics, and teachers the material well, but not well enough in comparison to the exams. For PHY2048 Spring 2017, he taught the class until the first exam. I needed to use Study Edge as a supplement to the lectures. The tutoring offered made the difference in my test grade. I don't know one person who didn't SE.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Physics is already a hard class and even though Acosta tried to make lectures worth going, he did not go into depth about topics on exam  or give any example problems for what the exam would be like. He is very enthusiastic but not a great teacher. I used Study Edge to help me because lectures were not helping and got an A- in the class.

Overall, I believe that Dr. Acosta was a good professor, but the subject was hard. He seemed very enthusiastic about teaching and overall, watching his online lectures in addition to coming to class and participating overall did help. This class was very hard, but I liked him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Acosta is very excited to teach us physics, and he can clearly convey the information of the course. He is a good professor that explains his demonstrations and the concepts of physics well. He leaps and bounds better than Dr. Rinzler and Dr. Matcheva, with whom he taught this course. I don't like physics, but he made this class doable.
Class is by no means easy, but doable. Lectures can be long and all over the place. Use Study Edge and don't cram for tests.

Passionate about class. Lectures can get confusing. There is a lot of information that tends to be harder than most classes. I used Study Edge and found that without it, I definitely wouldn't have gotten an A.

Physics is a tough subject overall. Exams are difficult, but not impossible. They made the class this semester a flipped classroom where you watch lecture videos at home and then do example problems in class. In my opinion, this was somewhat annoying but the videos were very decent at teaching the subject. I recommend going to class for clicker pts

Very knowledgable about the material and will help you in any way possible. Definitely more approachable than Woodard. Exams were very fair and problems will mostly be based off of your hw and problems he does in class as well as ones from the book. Overall, probably the best physics prof I've ever had.

He is the physics professor you would be lucky to have. Even though the class is awful and he still writes impossible tests, he is a very good professor. Unfortunately, he is usually not the one lecturing, but when he does, it is very clear. He is well liked, and I wish the course lent itself to be more engaging.
Nice guy, class is hard but if you work hard and are smart you'll do fine. Everything on the test is explained in class, you just have to manage to pay attention.
:))) Laughing always symphatetically. But that is his only "quality" :)))))
Overall a good teacher, class is boring but you get points for attendance (HITT points).  Much more interesting than Rinzler who is the other professor.
Good teacher and easy to understand. Dry at times, but hey, this is physics. Helpful outside of class too.
Very kind to students, willing to help - class is difficult, but attempts to make it manageable.
Excellent teacher. Very fair grading and tests. Very good at getting students to understand the material. Quite possibly the best Physics teacher at UF.
No complaints.  Explained proofs well, easy and fair homework.  Easy and fair tests.

he is great, clear, organized and the best physics teacher i had so far. exams were mostly based on homework and the grading had rediculus curves 82 was an A but with the extra point he gave for quizes and one of the exams it was more like 78!
Best professor in the physics department! (not that there is much competition for this distinction)

Acosta is the better professor as opposed to Stewart. He teaches better, and he is more adept to responding to students' questions. He sounds like Kermit the Frog, but his lectures are very structured.
Neat and organized notes. Good speaker and can teach really well. He looks like a smart guy and cracks some good jokes. I would recommend him.
Haha, I agree with Acosta being the lesser of the two evils. He's pretty good, too bad I hate physics.
Good speaker.  Sometimes he can be funny too.
(Honors) Very well prepared, exceptionally smart, and truly interested in having his students learn
Dr. Acosta is the lesser of two evils when learning Physics w/calc. two.  But then again, anything beats having to deal with Avery.
No Comments

Really smart guy, knows his stuff, great lecturer, clear examples, and grades very fairly. As long as you put in the work he asks of you, you will learn so much and get an A. Acosta makes physics fun and simple, which is not easy.

TA Acaro is a great reinforcer for the knowledge tought in Calc 2. At the begenning it may be hard to differientiate between his 4's and his 9's but it will get easier with time. He also is very clear on the grading criteria, and grades very case-by-case basis, potentially leading to you doing very well on exams. His lectures are elite!

He was a very good professor and explained each concept pretty clearly. Everything for the course is explicitly stated and he gives practice tests for each exam that are identical to the exams but with different numbers. Overall a great teacher and very easy class.
He was an incredible TA. He was able to make difficult concepts easier to understand and he always helped us with any problems that we had.

He was my TA for Calc 2 alongside Prof Chui. He always worked out problems well for us and was a big part of my earning an A in the class. His grading gave feedback on what we did wrong, and he is such a great person to talk to. Big Ecuador soccer fan!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Rubiano will ensure you're prepared for the rest of your engineering classes. His lecture videos are dense and incredibly useful. As long as you do the homeworks, you'll be well-prepared for exams. Cares about his students, could schedule OH with him whenever and gives helpful feedback. Learn Excel - you'll be using it for the rest of your life.

Worst experience I've had. The professor is disrespectful in emails and the TAs never reply. Lectures consist of old YouTube videos that only cover the basics, but the exams are incredibly advanced and feel completely disconnected from the teaching material. It feels like being taught addition and then being tested on calculus.
Bruh idk I just got cooked.

The exams are as fair as they can come, and your final grade in the class depends on them only. Quizzes and HW are for practice. Dr Rubiano's lectures are fast-paced and to the point. You learn everything you need in minutes. Really organized online resources and he's always available to meet over Zoom.

Lectures are "short" but so dense you pause every second if you actually want to understand the content. Excel calculators he made us create were just time wasters, since only the first exam had us using them. Hardly communicated with us and gave zero feedback. Easy exams if your work is done, but overcomplicates how he wants us to prepare for them
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Rubiano's thermo is by far the best class I've taken at UF. It is tons of work, but his online lectures are really good. They are short and like his channel's name, they are not boring. Would've killed for this format in highschool when covid hit. I wish he taught more classes, in person or online.

TA was awful all semester. You had to beg for getting feedback on exams. Dr. Rubiano was great tho. He is very caring and shows it during office hours. His youtube lectures are really good. No dillydallying. Sucks that his grading TA was so bad.

The class resources were very clear and easy to follow. Your final grade is calculated from 4 exams. The exams are easy if you have taken all the practice quizzes. Exactly what I was expecting from a solidworks online course.

Makes thermo so annoying. Does these awful 10 minute YouTube videos cause I guess he's too important to record real lectures/needs to monetize them cause UF doesn't pay him enough? Such a poorly designed course. IDK how he is in other classes but don't take him for this.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are concise but 4 years old,
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst class I've taken at UF. Lectures were shallow 8-12 minute, 4 year old yt videos that didn't have enough detail. Assignments were not graded but expected to be 100% correct on exams. OH were practically mandatory which defeats the purpose of being online. The professor and TAs severely neglected the course material and structure. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Possibly one of the most miserable experiences I have had at UF thus far. Quizzes do not show up on the canvas assignment page, little to no feedback on submissions or exams, the grading scale is way too harsh given that the class is graded solely by 4 exams.

Took Thermo asynchronously with him. Tons of work, but the class is very well organized. Canvas is clean and everything is easy to follow. His youtube lectures are the best: short and sweet! Not an easy A, but you learn torrents of concepts with him

Dr. Rubiano's video lectures were very helpful and it's easy to go back and relearn from scratch when needed. I also liked the expansive amount of example problems, especially with a complex course like this. Canvas was really well put together. Nothing I would improve! Really nice in person when helping during office hours.

This was one of the most enjoyable classes I've taken. Dr. Rubiano is the brightest professor I've had. I've taken online classes before and they were all awful, but this one was better than any in person courses. He has lots of office hours and they are exceptionally helpful. Wish I had taken any of his other classes before!

Dr. Rubiano's class teaches you unimaginable levels of self-accountability. His first exam asks you to go back to homework and quizzes problems. You quickly realize how much work you missed. And once you start doing the work everything seems much easier to understand. Probably the only class I've taken where working hard really pays off!

Best professor I've had in 4 years. had him in person for Solidworks and I learned a lot. Wanted to go into CAD myself for a job. But even his online version of mech 1 was amazing. His lectures are really good and he has unlimitted office hours. He's unbelievably smart and he'll know the answer to anything you throw at him.

Like any other Rubiano class, they're time consuming and difficult but you learn a lot if you dedicate the necessary time. Honestly, I wouldn't take mech 1 with him if you haven't taken a different class with him before. I already knew the expectations of excel and the workload. Otherwise, it would become overwhelming quickly.

The other comments regarding his workload are accurate. Prepare to sacrifice free time if you want to succeed. Rubiano is clear that this class requires a large amount of time, effort, and responsibility, but that doesn't change that you'll think about this class so much that you'll age 5 years. He does curve pretty hard if you improve.

Rubiano has a particular style in regard to his online classes... For this class, it does not really work. You are expected to make excel sheets for every problem, those of which are really tedious and unecessary for this type of course. For learning Solidworks, Rubiano is great, for mech design his class format isn't the best.

Amazing and understandable lectures. Helpful TA. DO NOT GET BEHIND! I repeat: DO NOT FALL BEHIND! Expect 3-4 hours of work 3 days a week. Check canvas everyday for quizzes that do not show up on to-do list. Grade is only exam based.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This online class was by far the worst format I have ever seen. Only exams count towards the final grade. He doesn't announce when quizzes or homework will be posted, and they are posted for 12 hours (!!!) only. The exams are insanely long and you need to write everything in hand and then write it in Excel. Do NOT take this class online with him.
Not very clear sometimes, slightly unapproachable, but overall, not a bad professor.

Despite the many homeworks and hard, time intensive, exams, Rubiano is a great professor who only wants you to succeed! He gives a lot of extra credit if you do your work and improve throughout the course.

Rubiano was very accessible, offering unlimited office hours to anybody who reached out. His classes are certainly difficult, but for good reason. By the time you leave his class, you will KNOW the content inside and out.

Decides final grade completely subjectively based on what he thinks you deserve. Only graded by 4 exams and one project, so your grade will be really low until the end of the class when he makes his decision. Great lectures, but unclear rubrics on difficult exams. Expected to do all homeworks and quizzes for "just practice" and no credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Conducts class in a way that I think all professors should, or at least try to. Good at explaining stuff during lectures. Also allows people to ask plenty of questions during class or explain a problem themselves which I think is great for a course like this. This has easily been the best and most interactive online course I've taken.
He forgets about his own exam days

Honestly, I felt like this class taught me the concepts not only thoroughly, but really efficiently. I think a lot of people complained about having to adapt to the style and relying on excel, but personally I think it was super useful. This was a really enjoyable class.

This is the second class I have taken with Dr. Rubiano. His classes are amazing. I would take anything he's teaching. If you fail a quiz, he'll know exactly what to recommend and point out where you went wrong. He offers unlimited office hours outside of the scheduled ones, and is always quick to set them up when you shoot him an email.

This is the only class I've taken where the syllabus tells you exactly what you need to do to succeed. The lectures are to the point and really well explained. Homework and quizzes help a lot to prepare for the exams. Somewhat of a learning curve, but I wish all professors set their class like Dr. Rubiano. He's also very helpful during office hours

No rubric, no assignments listed in gradebook, no assignments on calendar. Grade is based on exams. Attendance, weekly quizzes, and recorded homework are mandatory yet ungraded. No feedback on recordings, assignments, or quizzes to improve. EOC "subjective" grade given not on syllabus. Email response hit/miss. Needs restructuring to be good course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Entire grade is exams, so homework is ungraded, but you NEED to do the homework to do well in the class. If you watch the lectures and do the homework you won't really need to study. Tests are open notes so having your work done is key. He will help you out with your grade if you put in the work and participated. Otherwise, I wouldn't expect help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very organized and very clear. His exams make you think out of the box. No complaints. Best professor I've taken so far

My biggest takeaway from his class was that grades shouldn't matter as much as they do. Dr. Rubiano teaches everything so well that it's hard to blame anyone other than yourself when you don't get the grade you wanted in an exam. However, you learn sooooo much in his class, that it's hard to care about the grade not helping your GPA.

It takes time to really understand what he means about learning vs performance in a class, but you really end up caring a lot more about how much you will remember when you graduate and how prepared you are for a job. Dr. Rubiano is a tough grader but it is what it takes for you to understand that. Learned more than in any other class.

Professor Rubiano was difficult but amazing. You will hate him at first then will love him more and more. There is a lot of work, but push to stay on top of it and it will taper off about 2/3 of the way through the semester. Especially near the end he has made a genuine effort to connect with everyone and to be understanding of student situations.

Great professor, very knowledgeable. Lots of work at first with homework and lectures, and can seem very fast paced especially with no CAD experience but makes an effort to communicate and understand students. Availability and grading standards clearly communicated. Stay organized and proactive, and you will definitely learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: Rubiano is upfront about how to succeed, that is spending 15+ hours a week on homework and mastering all materials the day they are presented. You can succeed in this course if you put in the amount of effort equivalent to two normal classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: After reading the reviews I was scared to take him but after being in the class I am so glad that I did. There is a-lot of work and no homework grades, all just pop quizzes which can either be submitting old homework or doing a regular quiz. He is a great teacher and I learned so much. 10/10 recommend. He is also very caring and understanding.

Do NOT take this professor. He makes thermodynamics way harder than it should be. This class is very demanding and not rewarding. The quizzes and exams are very difficult and seem to test how to use Excel to solve problems rather than actual understanding of thermo. His grading is very unclear and he makes up new rules when it is convenient for him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I ended up getting a C+ in this class and tbh, I'm not even mad. I complained a lot about having to adapt to the amount of work and using Excel for every quiz and exam, but I learned a great deal about self discipline. Once I got the hang of it, this was a very enjoyable class. Will be taking a class with Rubiano again if offered.

This is my first time reviewing a professor, I thought Dr. Rubiano was a very good professor, he taught the subject very well and cares a lot about his students. That being said, the class is a lot of work and he grades tough but fairly. Do the work and you will be fine, and an A will definitely be doable in the class.
Clear. Fair. Very smart. Really cares about his students. So far best prof in MAE

I came in to the class hearing that Rubiano was the hardest professor in MAE. It's really not that hard or that much work as people say it is. Or maybe it seemed easier because his class is well organized. And you learn a lot, so I would recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots of students write off Rubiano as too strict and a harsh grader, but if you put in the work you will find great value in this course. If you're looking for an easy A, do not take this course. But if you actually want to learn, Rubiano is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this professor. It takes at least 10 hours of work a week to earn an A, and he requires that you record your screen for all assignments. He cares about his students and is very knowledgeable, but he has no grasp on how difficult the class is for those with no CAD experience. I would only recommend him If you have an easy semester ahead.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Most people will automatically write off Rubiano since he assigns a lot of work and is somewhat harsh when it comes to quizzes and grading. However, he is extremely knowledgeable when it comes to what he teaches. If you are willing to put effort into the class and not just expect an easy A, you will be rewarded and prepared for the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
This professor is the one who tries to teach by "teaching you a lesson."
Tons of homework. Working on SolidWorks every single day. Checks to see if a random part out of everything you have made is correct as a quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Rubiano is the smartest professor I've had. His thermo lectures were amazing, and his Canvas page was a reflection of the what he teaches us to be: detailed, organized, hard work, and effort. Course rules are clear and quizzes and exams, hard but fair.

I just got my first promotion at work. Everything my boss congratulated me for I owe to what Dr. Rubiano taught us while taking his class. Hard work and passion for what you do really does make you stand out.

I was so mad for getting a C- in this class. So much work and no leniency with grades or missing deadlines. Today after 2 years I can't thank dr Rubiano enough for teaching me what hard work and focus can do with all my other classes. My GPA has dramatically gone up after taking solidworks with him.

If you want to learn SolidWorks, take this professor. You will learn very well but only if you put in the effort. Practice by doing all homework and classwork and you will do well in his quizzes. He makes it very simple to understand the subject. One important note is that he grades too harshly on the quizzes, but can be made up by extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do not take Rubiano for EML2023. Your plate will be full of homework all week, every week. Take anyone else at UF for the class.

EML3100 - Thermodynamics (Summer 2022). His lectures are amazing. He has a YouTube channel "Less Boring Lectures." The lectures are just his videos. I watched them for other classes before I knew that he is a prof at UF. He is a tough grader, but he explains the material well, and the exams are what you expect.

This is one of the hardest classes I've taken simply because of the work load. Lectures outside of class with about 5-8 parts to make a week. I've heard he is the hardest professor that teaches this class but teaches the best. I learned a lot but for feedback go to office hours often.
