Took him in the spring of 2021. I found his grading overall to be far too harsh. His quizzes were difficult, and he had an assignment almost every class plus homework. He is certainly challenging, more so than the other EML2023 professor (who I am taking now). If you want to take a class that's harder than it needs to be, you're at the right place.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Graded harshly and the lectures where not very comprehensive.

Had Dr. Rubiano for thermodynamics. His Youtube lectures were good but his class and assignments were terrible. Frequently messed up grades (even the automatic ones on canvas) and wrongly claimed students would get high grades for trying their best. Final exam was impossible. TA is the only reason I got an A. No idea how he's so high rated here.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He teaches far more than just the course he's teaching. Truly shows a whole other side to learning abt engineering and good earned work. Take dr rubiano for learning about communication, collaboration, responsibility, and overall good work ethics. Best professor I've ever had.

A lot of people complained about his class, but just  watch & understand the lectures. The quizzes should be easy 100s. The class is time consuming if you've never used SolidWorks. If you need help, reach out, he always responds to emails & is willing to meet with you outside of OH. If you REALLY want to & HAVE to know SolidWorks, take Dr. Rubiano.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Rubiano cares about his students and he pushes them to be their best. The class was a major pain for me because I didn't enter UF as an engineering major so I used a MAC-M1 instead of a PC computer. Make sure to have a PC. This class is not taught as a 2000-level course. I have never put in so many hours of work for such mediocre results.
Worst prof I've ever had. Worked 10 hours plus each week for things that never got graded. Makes the class a million times harder than it needs to be. take with anyone else
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The material can be frustrating to learn sometimes so be prepared to put in extra hours. He does grade pretty harshly sometimes but if you put in the work your grade will be fine in the end. Overall, he seemed to really care about how well his students learned and I feel like I actually learned the material well.

Professor Rubiano may come off as mean or that he just wants to drop your grade but he is a person that genuinely cares about not only your academic future but you as a person. He will hold you to a very high standard which may seem awful at times but if you put in the work and take his hints in class you can easily get an A
He's pretty good. I had over summer B so I think EML2023 was a little easier. Both his online videos and in-person lectures are helpful but he's almost impossible to get ahold of outside of class.

I had to drop this class, almost no grades go in and the only things that do are graded very harshly. I tried to set up a meeting to discuss my grade a few times and he ghosted me every time. Rubiano makes this class a lot harder than it needs to be and it is flipped with lectures that aren't helpful at all. I would recommend any other prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He makes short videos for each lecture that are concise and helpful. However, it would be better to take this class with another prof because he makes the class much harder than it needs to be. Quizzes have insane amounts of time pressure and are graded harshly, and his final project is far more complicated than for other professors.
Got a concussion so I didn't finish the course, but I learned more in about a month of Dr. Rubiano's summer c course than I have during the entirety of this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: He gives out weekly quizzes which are super stressful. Also a lot of homework assignments which he doesn't even grade them.

As you get into the more specified engineering courses you find that the easy way is not always the right way. Dr. Rubiano is probably the hardest Mech 1 teacher, yet after going through it I would say I am thankful I took him. He is extremely knowledgeable as well as accessible outside of class. He really prepares you for future coursework.

Great Prof with very good lecture videos. Always willing to help before/after or outside of class (even if you are asking questions about another class). Biggest flaw is that he is a tough grader but he does it "so that we can be better engineers." If you can show him you do the work and are learning the material, he will not let you fail.

Professor Rubiano is a great professor. He is very clear on expectations for the course from the beginning and his lecture videos are great. However, his class (EML3005) is difficult. There are 18 min of lecture videos to watch every MWF which have homeworks attached. Every Friday there is a quiz. If you skip homework, you will fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gives multiple weekly quizzes in a one hour time span, which is super stressful. Will give credit to his lectures, which are well put together and concise. Gives a group project but it's quite ambiguous. His office hours are hit or miss (by appt). Overly harsh on grading, and told people to drop despite knowing they could still pass. So here I am.

Was easily accessible after class or during office hours for any questions. Made use of pre recorded shortened lectures for review or instruction outside of class. Genuinely felt like he cared that his students were learning the curriculum of the course. Nice guy, great professor, just be respectful and do your homework and you will be fine.

Although the class was hard, the professor cared that we learned the material and was always available to help. He gave pop quizzes but you felt prepared. There was a big project at the end on top of two finals which requires you to put a lot of hours into it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's great! Don't expect the grade to just be given to you. He makes it very clear that he does everything in his power to help you but you have to be willing to put in the work. Don't be afraid to ask for help. Grades are based on quizzes mainly and require you to be diligent and efficient with your time.

Although very tough to learn the majority of SolidWorks in six weeks, Professor Rubiano made the class incredibly enjoyable. We had one pop quiz a week, and although unannounced, I always felt prepared due to his lectures in class. Sometimes the TA graded in a way that was not fair, but if you reach out to professor, he will fix it accordingly.

reviews.comment: Dr. Rubiano makes you work to get a good grade. You will learn a lot IF YOU WANT. He cares a lot about students. tons of exercises to practice and master your abilities of SW. 5 quizzes (no drop), one final divided in two parts and the final project of whatever mechanism you want to do, be sure to start working on with TIME. Quizzes similar to HWS
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 1s and 2s, oof! Its so simple tho. Wanna learn more than any other class ever? Take Dr. Rubiano. Not just abt engineering btw. Youre lazy and want As you dont deserve? Avoid him, theres other options. This guy is a 6 rating.

Clearly has a chip on his shoulder, makes the class much harder than it needs to be. Avoid taking at all costs.

reviews.comment: Dr. Rubiano is devoted to deliver fantastic lectures and life lessons. He legitimately cares about his students and their future. Incredibly knowledgeable! I just got my first big promotion and I know I owe it to how hard he pushed us. 1's here must be from people that wanted easy A's: he will fail you if you don't work hard. The best of UF!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best professor at UF! He makes you give 100% of yourself to become a better professional. His lectures are amazing. I learned a lot! Just as it should be, you need to put the work and time to get the most out of this class. At the end, you get the grade you deserve. He provides all the resources for you to stay motivated and to learn and practice.

Theres no room for procrastination in the course, but you eventually get the grade you deserve for all the hard work (its easier than MoM lab or DML, imo). I learned A LOT from the lectures, which are basically short and sweet 10-min YouTube videos Dr. Rubiano makes himself. Definitely one of the best professors at UF!

Dr. Rubiano has been one of the best professors I have had. He actually puts his students first over anything else and wants them to succeed. You are required to put in a lot more work than other professors but you will learn the most about Mech Design 1 in this class. Would highly recommend taking his class!

Dr. Rubiano is an incredible professor. He focused on teaching us Mech 1 and helping us retain the information, not memorize it. The bad reviews are from people who took the class wanting an easy A. If you want to learn Mech 1 and have a good foundation for the future, take Dr. Rubiano. He has amazing Youtube lectures and helps outside of class.

Not a man of his word, either intentionally or because he forgets. Says one thing in class and then says another in office hours/ emails. Could be very rude and condescending. Avoid taking him if you have another option. Says he rewards hard work but was very rude when trying to show it. Get everything in writing from him

Dr. Rubiano is an awesome professor, he has amazing flipped lectures on his youtube channel and is super approachable and helpful in class. That doesn't mean you don't have to work for it, we had homework for every class and many pop quizzes. He is a reasonable, fair guy and I definitely recommend taking him and getting to know him.

One of the best at UF. Dr. Acosta is extremely knowledgable and very good at communicating his knowledge to students. The production quality of his lecture videos was fantastic. He keeps track of participation and rewards effort in the class. This class may be much easier if you take it with a different professor, but not nearly as rewarding.
Really great professor! Very invested in your individual success. This class is essentially a flipped class, so take it if thats your style.

Dr. Rubiano is the bet professor you'll get for Mech Design 1. He really focuses on you learning the material and his lecture videos are really high quality. His class is definitely the most difficult as well, but he does care about his students if you run into any personal problems. Would recommend taking him, but not with a heavy semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Definitely requires more work than other profs but genuinely always willing to meet and discuss any topics (homework, project, etc). Always considerate about any personal issues someone might be having. Your grades in the class might suck at first but if you put in effort and he knows you put in effort, your grade will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Rubiano is tough on his students but he really wants you to learn something in his class. Even though I didn't do the greatest in this class (took it during covid fall semester), you could tell that he cares.

reviews.comment: Dr. Rubiano is a gem in the engineering college. He's not easiest professor, he expects you to WORK and to try to learn, that's his priority. Definitely was never condescending, and overall has a heart of gold and great passion.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. The production quality of his lecture videos was outstanding. From talking to other students, this class will be much easier if you take it with a different professor, but not as rewarding. He cares very much about the success of his students and rewards participation and effort. Take him if you can!

Probably the best professor I've had at UF. He really makes you work for a good grade, but more than anything he cares that you learn the material even more so than other professors teach. It's a tough class but he prepares you very well as long as you are consistent throughout the semester.

There's effort that you need to put in but he seriously guides you through it.

Such a great professor! I knew once I got on here I would see complaints. The complaints are from students who want easy A's and no concern to understand the material. The guy is extremely sarcastic, laughs at students when they ask questions in class/ office hours. Probably the most annoying/ unpleasant professor Ive had in 4 years. First off I would rate the difficulty as a 4.2. reviews.comment: As the other reviews say, she advocates for mental health. She canceled our final essay because she figured it added undue stress. Bless her soul. I devoted, on average, 1.5-2 hours a WEEK for this class, and it should be the easiest A ever.

took her last semester. she's very unorganized and often says one thing and does the other. she's confusing and her classes are dull. take another professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Aceves is a queen. She is so empathetic and understanding especially during the pandemic. She cares about her students and is a very fun and nice person. I learned a lot in her class about writing in my industry that I will carry with me forever. She is one of the only professors at UF that truly cares about students mental health.

Professor Aceves is one of the kindest, most caring professors I've had at UF. From the start, she was a vocal advocate for mental health and treated us accordingly. The class isn't difficult at all. She's understanding about extenuating circumstances, willing to meet with you to help you do your best work, and wants all her students to succeed!

Her class is dependent upon three essays you write, three group projects, community service, and attendance, so go to class and make those papers good!  Her class is super easy.  There is a lot to read, but no busy work.  You can get by with Sparknotes for your readings.  However, she never gives clear rubrics for her assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I had him for the section Writing About Summer. He asks questions that open up to interesting discussions in class. He takes his time to thoroughly explain writing assignments and rubrics and if that's not clear enough, he is happy to explain further and answer questions after class. He gives a lot of helpful feedback on papers.

By far my favorite teacher when it comes to a writing class at UF. He provides interesting discussion and as long as you show that you care during discussions and go to office hours to go over your papers, he will help you do very well in this class. Definitely try to get any of his sections because I know he teaches multiple writing courses.

Acheson is a very clear and engaging professor, and he gives excellent feedback which you can then use to earn some points back in revisions. The Ways of Reading textbook is essential at the beginning of the semester because there are passages in there that you will write papers on, but he only assigned reading from the other textbook.

Kendall Ackley was the best TA I've ever had. First of all, she's a genius. Second of all, she's a genius that is easy to understand. She really knows her stuff. I would definitely recommend her! She is very good at explaining stuff and really helped me out with everything. Hands down the best at UF!
Very helpful and laid-back. She tries to help you understand the material and do well in the course.
Pretty cool TA, lets us call her by nicknames. Definitely would recommend her lab to one of my bros.

Can't recall the course names, but I had her for two.  The type of teacher and person that reminds you of your own personal responsibilities!!!  You MUST want to be outstanding if you want to rise to her expectations.
She is a very amazing person.  I took two classes with her and loved both of them.

This class is useless.  The material is covered with minimal effectiveness.  The material is rum through quickly to meet EAS requirements but there is no knowledge gained.  Professor Ackerman is extremely helpful.

She is a fine teacher, but she quizzes on material before she goes over it in class.  The quizzes count for a good part of your grade.  This is why I did not get an A in her class.  The material on the quizzes changes as well so be careful.  Other than that she was fine!

Requires a lot of reading, often about the same subject in many different articles.  She's not a bad teacher, but she stresses developing a repitore with students and then makes her students use name tags throughout the semester because she won't learn names.  Not the greatest of classes, but you do learn the law and you'll get through it fine.
she treats students as if they were 5 years old, she lectures right after tests, and she will not help you during class time.
This teacher is great to have for your first semester in Proteach.  She is helpful and knows a lot about the field she's in, which makes it fun.  If you have the option- Take her!!!
people exaggerate how hard this class is. chill class and prof

The stats class with Dr. Munson was amazing. He was clear on grading and was fair on everything he did. He used a book that taught the key basics of a very difficult topic. His lectures and methods of working out problems helped students succeed. You should easily get an A if you do the homework and quizzes and study those concepts for the exams.
understanding professor very laid back. material isnt that easy and u have to put time into learning it. the capsim is hard if ur trying to get full points. only grades r capsim and 3 exams.
Used Studyedge, but the material is quite hard and not the easiest to get a high grade in. Had to put in lots of hours studying and practicing all his problems.

For the last core business class, this class was very doable especially with Study Edge. Lectures are useful for conceptual questions but doing quizzes and Excel definitely gets you there. The professor was very quick with emails and understanding. Would recommend getting SE to make the class easier especially as a senior.

Professor Munson's lectures were long and helpful, especially for the conceptual questions on the exam. He lost me several times when going through the Excel but nothing that a specific tutoring service did not help. The Excel stuff is not hard, it just takes a few times to understand, so go through several problems. His quizzes help with exam prep
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gave me an extention/make up for an exam no questions asked. Very laid back and not that hardcore of a professor which is really nice as a senior. If you are failing at the end of the course he gives you extra credit so that you don't fail which is really nice especially since people take this senior year to not delay graduation.
Emails back very fast unlike most professors. Very understanding and willing to accommodate. Not that difficult of a class. Lots of extra credit opportunities.

Average difficulty business class. Very understanding and very lenient. Not that engaging of a class but he genuinely cares about helping you succeed. You do have to put time into the capsim simulation but as long as you don't do it last minute like a lot of people, you're fine and he walks through it in class. Overall just a good professor.

Professor Munson is very engaging & one of the most agreeable professors I had all 4 years. You get 1 makeup exam no questions asked which is amazing as a senior. As long as you at least use study edge you'll be good. But, I would recommend study edge's practice exams over his quizzes 100%. His lectures are still a good listen.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is well structured and there is a reasonable amount of content for each exam. It's a doable class, especially if you get Study Edge. He does have good resources on canvas, but Study Edge helps with the individualized question videos. Munson is a smart guy with lots of experience

You can tell Dr. Munson is very intelligent and highly respected in his field. His lectures are not too long and often include fun stories about his personal experience in the field. The tests are not difficult if you pay attention in lectures and study hard- and he gives you ample study material to do so. Study Edge is not necessary.
If you dont know how to use excel in a good way, don't take this subject. The professor is good, the minimum grade in our class is B, so overall the subject is okay.
Munson is so kind and fun to talk to! He is very helpful when you need extra assistance on a concept. You definitely need to put in the work for operations management but Munson makes it very doable!

The class is challenging and requires a lot of studying. I did learn a lot about operations management and its applicability, however, he does not prepare students well for the exams. The questions are pretty tricky and require a lot of practice, in lecture he tends to rush through them. I highly recommend getting study edge!

Dr. Munson was extremely helpful and caring everytime I reached out to him this semester. For the last class in the business school it is no surprise that it is challenging one. Exams are very difficult but the rest of the assignments you should have 100%.
I love this man to death, he is a legend and a king. Would not have had half as great of a time without his many personal anecdotes that are highly entertaining, if off topic. Great experience.

The class is not bad at all. I would't even bother watching his lectures, instead just do Study Edge and you can easily get an A. Lots of excel and lot of content sometimes, just make sure you don't try to cramp studying for the exam 1 day before. Leave 2 days to study for them and 3 would be optimal. Exams are a combo of MC and short answers.

reviews.comment: Watch his lectures if possible and use Study Edge to supplement his problems. Since taking Linear Programming out of the material, it's gotten way better. reviews.comment: Good professor. Appreciate that he doesn't spend more time in class than needed. The final was a bit tricky. He asked some questions that we didn't really cover. He's also laid-back. Good class overall.

Dr. Munson is hilarious. He makes class really entertaining and is a very understandable person. He's usually fine with switching due dates and accommodating schedules so long as it makes sense. However, he's a little too smart for his own good. This class is insanely difficult, and if you don't mesh with the material, it'll be a huge struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I personally like Dr. Munson's method of lecturing. He talks a LOT, but I think his way of explaining concepts is more clear than almost any other class like this one I have taken. It's easy to follow along and understand the materials if you pay attention.

Take this class seriously. Munson provides clear criteria for what you need to do to do well in his class. His lectures are interesting and he makes sure students have chances to practice tons of relevant problems before each exam. 3 exams so do yourself a favor and start off strong by taking enough time to study before each exam.
Interesting stories and explains things very well. Goes of on tangents sometimes but they relate to the material. Very accessible. I wish more professors cared this much.
Professor Munson is a really nice guy. The class isnt hard. I probably watched a total of 2 lectures and just used study edge for the exams.
Took ops man and its very hard. I recommend study edge or smokin notes, you dont even need to watch lectures. He lets you do test corrections and is very flexible in terms of due dates if you ask!
Great professor! Hard topic. You must keep yourself motivated.

reviews.comment: 3 exams, Capsim, and a couple of homeworks assignments online. All lectures are recorded and put on online, but I definitely recommend just using Marty at StudyEdge and you'll be able to get an A with no issue.

reviews.comment: You don't need to watch lectures but you will need study edge to pass in order to get the material dumbed down a bit. Not many assignments besides the exams. You get a whole sheet of paper for notes to use during exam so just fill that with everything you need. Very nice if you go to his office hours and usually curves final grades.

This class was pretty simple. I didn't find it too difficult and actually got a 100% in the class. The textbook is not necessary. I used Study Edge and watched the lectures, but lectures aren't really necessary. He does drop hints on what will be on the exams though. The homework is simple but annoying. He does seem to care about his students! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Munson is the man! You get out what you put in, for sure. I watched every lecture and used skoolers to help nail stuff for the test. They helped me put together my formula sheet, which was nice. Go to office hours if you have time  he's really fascinating! I'm really going to miss Munson.

Definitely recommend using Skoolers. Munson even speaks highly of them during lecture and is friends with the tutor. You definitely have to put some time in, but you can easily start studying a week before the exam and still get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Munson is the best. Wonderfully caring guy who just wants you to do well. He even speaks highly of Skoolers which is nice as some professors tend to dislike the outside help. Make sure your cheat sheet is comprehensive. That was a real life saver for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Test were a little tough but he grades based on curve. If the test was too hard he will adjust. Listen to the lectures and study the main points. He will tell you in the lectures "you will probably see this on the test". If you only study those stated "test" comments; you'll make a "B" all day. Want better???study more.

reviews.comment: This class is supposed to be relatively easy and he keeps it pretty similar year after year. I used Study Edge and will pull off an A- without having watched any lectures. Just beware he does do "in lecture we did X" questions on his exams so if you just do Study Edge you might miss those ones!
This is really not a hard class. The hmwk and yellowdig requirements are easy. I used Skoolers for this class, and it helped a lot. Dr. Munson is a caring professor. One of the best I've ever had

Not really a hard class, but now he has switched to type in the answer rather than a multiple choice format on his tests. There were a lot of issues with test questions, like how to round, and questions being worded wrong. Besides that, the hw and yellowdig stuff is easy. I did tutoringzone (skoolers) for this class, and it helped a lot.

Nothing against the guy, he obviously knows his stuff; BUT, this class is not what I expected. I didn't expect to spend most of the time doing math problems when he could have taken this course in a different direction. The class is titled Operations and Supply Chain Management. At no point did I learn about the logistics in the supply chain.
Study Edge is a lifesaver for this class. Get Study Edge and you'll easily get an A/A-.

Dr Munson understands how this is a senior class. He can be pretty flexible if you need to work out schedule conflicts too. Material is mostly math with a few definition questions. Do the Study Edge review a couple days in advance and they even give you a cheat sheet you just re handwrite onto a piece of paper that Munson lets you use for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is very math heavy. Although the professor does his very best to be fair, exams sometimes incorporate subtle nuances that some students might not pick up on. I definitely recommend using Study Edge in this class to help pick up on anything that the professor tests on that he does not explicitly mention in class.

Munson cares about what he is teaching is willing to help, however, the homework and other problems can get to be a bit much and be time consuming and the exams are tricky. I used Study Edge for this class which helped me to condense the material and taught me ways to avoid being tricked on exams. Hard work and extra tutoring got me a good grade.

You don't ever really read the textbook, even though you get a free online version with your OMLab subscription  you pay for it with your class finances :( He is a funny guy, who wears the same white button everyday. His classes aren't really helpful, the homework is, and the OLD TEST QUESTIONS! Boring content and math heavy, but not hard math.

Class was hard for me. Have got Mostly A's in Finance ended up with a C+ -- tricky exams. Time to complete all problems is also rough for exams. Tough class. Homework's are time consuming, but it's a good way to learn the material.

Ops Man with Munson is not difficult at all.  He's a great guy.  Experienced in industry before switching to academia, Dr. Munson's class is very straightforward.  Lectures can be viewed online, online homework (a la WebAssign) is due thrice, before each of 3 exams.  TAs and Dr. Munson are always available.  As long as you watch lectures, Easy A.
Great class

Munson's not a bad guy, but the problems just drag on way too much. You start to lose interest quickly and since there's so many simple calculations to be made, there's a great chance you made a mistake along the way. Tests are kind of tricky. Definitely possible to get an A, the class is just kind of a pain.

Dr. Munson obviously knows a lot about the subject and is always really eager to help students understand. The lectures are based on slides from the book, so they can be a bit repetitive. The class itself is very straightforward - 3 exams, online homework (which can get annoying), ETS business exam.
The class is pretty easy but the tests can be a little tricky, tutoring zone helped with that.
I actually really enjoyed this class, but I definitely needed to go to Tutoringzone to get A's on the tests.
Ops man with him is fairly easy but the final was ridic.  Class is math intensive for the last 2 exams...  If you study and get smokin notes and do TZ you will be fine.
Great professor, even with donuts for breakfast on quiz and test mornings.

lectures were more conducive to catching up on sleep, than to learning statistics.  confusing presentation of material and error prone in dictated lecture & distributed ppt slides.  VERY easy grader. not the best professor but very nice guy..would probably be great to go to the bar with or head to the gym for a quick karate sparring session.

The course content was very interesting, but the grading and readings assigned were way too serious for a Quest 1 course. I would say take a different course for quest, but definitely consider Lebowitz for future classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took ISS 1684, What is Democracy? Professor Lebovitz is a very eloquent speaker and challenges you to think deeply. Lectures are great, and I recommend going to office hours as he loves to engage with students. Not much work other than the readings. Class participation matters so make sure you engage in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: [ISS1684: What is Democracy?] Cannot recommend this professor enough. The course does take some time and critical thinking, especially during discussion where he makes sure you know what you are talking about. However, he's probably my favorite professor this semester: gives amazing feedback, is clearly very knowledgeable, and makes the class fun!

ISS 1684: He is SUCH a great lecturer and really understands how to pick your brain. Participation is a large part and it can sometimes feel very difficult or intimidating to engage. Overall, SUCH an interesting course. Don't take if looking for an easy quest class you can sit through. It requires a lot of engagement, but I felt it was worth it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I cannot recommend this professor enough! I'm taking his Quest 1 this semester ("What Is Democracy?" / ISS1684) and it's the most interesting class I've ever been in. By the end of each class, you'll be convinced that democracy means one thing & by the next, he'll flip that over and you'll be convinced of the opposite..11/10 professor!

Take this class if you enjoy engaging with your peers and thinking critically. The professor may be intimidating at first because he expects the students to be engaged, but he is incredibly well spoken and knowledgeable about the subject matter. Good for those interested in pursuing a degree within the Hamilton center too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Lebovitz crafted a masterful, thought-provoking course examining democracy's trajectory throughout history. The class style is interactive, and he gives tremendous feedback on written assignments. In this course, you truly get out what you put in; while the readings are difficult, he frames them well and directs insightful conversation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Lebovitz is way too overqualified for this. It's a discussion based course with a lot of reading (no quizes though). Grade depends on a few writing assignments and class participation. He will play devil's advocate and grill you on everything you say. Fun if you like debate, history, or politics. Do not take if you want an easy quest.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Lebovitz is very erudite and has an unimpeachable understanding about the most seminal texts influencing today's western parliamentary democracy, of which he will teach the excerpts drawn from 18 authors spanning from Ancient Hellas to the contemporary age. Classes are highly engaging and assignments are distributed and graded fairly.

I would not recommend this class and  professor. For being a Quest 1 class, it was extremely difficult. There are heavy readings for each class, only essay grades, and participation in class is a large part of the grade. (He is more concerned with embarrassing you in class than he is with a good response)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He assigns too much work, especially for a Quest I. Classes are repetitive and he makes you feel stupid, no matter how much effort you put into preparation. He does give good writing advice and he's passionate about the subject, but then again, its a Quest course and its not worth the stress. Don't take unless you're really interested in democracy.

He is VERY knowledgeable and clearly cares about the material he teaches but way too demanding for a Quest. He assigns a lot of reading and the class is extremely repetitive with no variety. I participated a good amount, but he would sometimes make me feel unintelligent. If you are a poli sci major, I can see how it could be more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Though monotone, his lectures are very easy to follow and are relevant to the exams. I'm personally a calc 2 fan so I didn't find the coursework super difficult but I do believe his lecture style helped. BUT, some of my friends had chui who wrote the exams and would hint at whats on it while he did not.

this dude is the GOAT. I had him last semester and he explained concepts clearer than any other professor, teacher, or youtube video ever has for me. the lectures can be boring sometimes since he's generally monotone, but he has a dry sense of humor that brightens the mood every once in a while. best math professor i've ever had.
Attendance is graded by an attendance quiz on canvas with questions from the lecture from that day, so it can be done at home. He explained material well and was very helpful with any questions.
Calc 2 is hard. Uh try your best. Teach is chill.
His lectures are very thought out and he explains the materials and notes thoroughly. He also cracked some jokes and his class was overall enjoyable! You'll be okay with him as your professor

Every type of problem that could show up on a test is in his notes. He's very detailed and goes at a good pace. Lectures are recorded, homework is tedious (as with all math) but incredibly doable with unlimited attempts. I like math, but even if you don't I think he makes the subject accessible and comprehensible to anyone.
decent professor but the exams were SO hard. probably took years off my life. no extra credit. if you aren't a super strong math student don't take unless you have to

Although attendance isn't mandatory, Dr. Adams goes over many examples in his lectures so I would recommend going. There are many previous exams that he posts to help you prepare for exams. He explains concepts really well and relates them to real life examples which is helpful.
Amazing lecturer! Makes all the content easy to absorb and provides lots of resources to help you succeed. Definitely recommend.

He's a good lecturer for most people but I couldn't grasp the content and struggled. Adams & Calc 2 just isn't for me I guess. The exams are brutal. Study ahead of time by using the past exams and resources on canvas. Don't forget to do homework or particpation quizzes. The TAs are helpful. Set up 1 on 1 meetings with them if you are struggling.

Amazing math professor that made Calculus 2 bearable. He has in-depth lectures that explain not only how certain techniques work but also why they work. The Xronos assignments are annoying sometimes, but understandable for this class, and even if the tests are difficult he properly prepares his students for every question within his lectures.

Calc 2 is a hard class but with Adams it went pretty well (for me at least). Xronos can be buggy sometimes but usually fine. Lectures are straightforward. Those + past exams + Xronos + extra problems are all you need to do well on the exams, plus there's extra credit on them. Take advantage of office hours if you need them.

Adams is very organized and professional, and he applies a pretty rigorous treatment to calc 2 topics. At times I was confused by his explanations, so I found Chui's lectures to be slightly more helpful, but overall he is clear and communicative. Exams are challenging so make sure to do a lot of problems and practice taking the past exams.

Calc 2 is horrendous (especially for the 2nd time since I have to retake lol) but I feel like if you genuinely keep up and practice the homework every single day, you'll do fine. It just moves extremely quick and I was always behind. Felt like the other prof (Chui) gave more shortcuts/tips on her notes/office h, I ended up going to her to learn tbh

Dr.Adams makes Calculus II easy and understandable. Each lecture starts off with an introduction to a new topic followed by several practice problems which he goes over in detail. I found the homework problems to be much harder than the actual exams. Practice exams are much more useful for studying which are posted on canvas.

This guy is amazing. Made a notoriously hard class like calculus 2 enjoyable and genuinely has one of the most impressive teaching styles I've ever seen. He is also funny and cracks a couple knee slappers every once and a while.

Amazing lectures, especially with having an outline for each lesson provided on Canvas. Homework is manageable, and exams are also pretty straightforward if you look at past exams and practice, which is also provided on Canvas!
He is a very organized lecturer and follows guided notes which he uploads to Canvas. Very manageable workload and exams are a breeze as long as you prepare

Adams is such a kind, funny, caring individual who I love having as a professor (please be my father). He makes the material feel natural and go by quickly, and I didn't struggle in this class because of him. I highly recommend going to lectures to not fall behind, but it goes by quickly and the homework is short. 10/10 teacher, would take again.
Steve is an awesome teacher. He has a great sense of humor and keeps the class engaging. His lectures are straightforward and the class is setup very well. Highly recommend.
He is actually a good teacher but his class is very test heavy with them being worth 75% of your final grade and his test are pretty difficult aswell

Very capable professor with clear grading and great resources. All the lectures and lecture notes are available on canvas along with past exams and solutions. If you care to prepare for the exams you'll be able to. 1 quiz per week in your discussion period, and that's the only time attendance matters.

Adams is great for calc 2. His lectures were productive, and they were recorded to review for exams. As he taught, he would let us know what was expected of us on exams for that lesson. Attendance was just a couple questions from the lecture, and it was due at midnight. The homework helps to prep for exams.

I genuinely don't understand people who leave bad ratings for Professor Adams. Calc II is generally just a hard class, and everyone knows it. Professor Adams explains difficult material in an easy-to-understand way.

No textbook, just lectures and notes, and some homework; the main thing is spamming practice problems and practice tests.

idk why there's so many 5 star reviews this is by far the sleepiest I've been in a class. Guy is fine but monotone voice and if you don't ask questions it can be hard to understand why he does things sometimes. I don't think he breaks it down in a way someone completely new to topics would understand. dude is just not for me ig

I hate this class with all my being. With that being said, he is an awesome lecturer. Very clear explanations and the class is structured very nicely. PLEASE DO THE HOMEWORK. I didn't and my grade isn't what I would like it to be. 
10 quizzes (2 dropped)
3 Exams (SOOO hard)
Class participation (3 dropped)
Tip: add schedule to calendar w/ reminders

Dr. Adams is an outstanding lecturer! Very clear explanations in the thought process for solving problems. He might be following a personal outline (or notes on talking points) when going through a lecture, so it seems very structured but he occasionally throws in some jokes. He is helpful with additional questions after each lecture.
The professor knows his material and is generally easy to follow. Do practice outside of class.

The lectures were tedious and monotone, but the class does not have a lot of homework or busy work. The class is exam heavy but there are many practice exams that you are able to take for good practice. With the extra percentage opportunity on the midterm exams and with how easy the final is, you can earn a good grade if you apply yourself.

Such a great professor. He made a notoriously difficult class into something understandable. The lecture structure is incredible with him going over one topic a day. The exams are difficult but that's expected from a hard course. Make sure you do the participations at the end of the lecture, though, those are easy points that are easily forgotten.

Calc 2 is by no means easy, but if there's any professor to take it with I would choose Prof Adams everytime. He has participation quizes that are due by the end of the day that are just problems he went over in the lecture so he literally tells you the answer. He's has a math professor sense of humor which adds to his charm.

For a difficult calc class with lots of content he does an amazing job teaching the subjects. Lectures are recorded and posted quickly after the lecture took place. Lots of practice exams are provided which are a good tool for the exams he gives. Weekly quizzes and HW are given but are helpful for making sure you are on track with the class.

Very clear lectures; I had no calc 2 background and really felt good about what I was learning. My TA was great too. Exam questions can definitely be misleading and are meant to trip you up, but the concepts themselves are fine if you study and do a lot of past exams to prepare. He cares about the students, but it is also a difficult class.

Dr. Adams' class was tough but I enjoyed it. I went to almost all office hours, took a lot of time on the homework, and used StudyEdge, all of which were very helpful. Dr. Adams makes it clear what you'll need to know for the exams. Midterms are taken out of 100 points with 105 available and the final has 110 available.

I took him after not passing Calc 2 last semester. He was great. I loved the way he explained concepts because he knows how to take very complicated topics and explain it in a very easy way to understand. His workload is also a lot more manageable than other professors, but it prepares you for the exams. I would recommend to anyone.

Professor Adams was great! In lecture, he explained things really well and made it easy to understand. It was Calc 2, so it was hard, but he made it easier to understand by explaining each step thoroughly. I would recommend going to the lectures because he makes it worth it, but attendance is definitely not mandatory since he posts all the lectures

Professor Adams thoroughly explains topics during lectures and is very open to any questions you may have. I will say the homework can be hard, but it prepares you well for the exams. Just make sure to do practice exams and problems, and you will do fine on exams even if you think you won't.
Great professor! Makes you actually understand calculus!
you can print out all the lecture notes in the beginning of the year and follow along with the math during lectures. it's a good system and his lectures are really well paced

Super great course! Dr. Adams' lectures are very organized and well-thought-out to teach each concept. Lectures + practice quizzes (w/ explanations for the right answers) were easily accessible online. Attendance isn't mandatory except for discussion quizzes. Made calc 2 seem simple and easy. Exams weren't difficult (abt. equal to course content).

As someone who was not motivated and did not do well in Calc AB, Dr. Adams helped me understand a lot of the content well. Thanks to Dr. Adams I now understand calc well. Exams were fair and he gave extra 5-10% extra credit problems. He also dropped 3 lowest weekly quiz. A+ professor. One of those classes where studying is key!

Dr. Adams is such a funny guy and an amazing professor. I struggle with calculus and definitely felt that other people were grasping it a lot better, but neither Dr. Adams or my TA was to blame. There's lots of resources and practice, even I ended up passing, but I could have spent more time on studying…

Adams covered all notes during lectures, although it was monotone and boring to me. I ended up watching the recordings of Prof Chui instead because her lectures were more engaging to me. Past exams were provided for us to review, there is ample material to study.

Dr. Adams was an incredible professor! He broke down the concepts really well and went through plenty of practice problems. The Xronos assignments could be tedious at times but were good practice. The exams were very fair and the final was very easy.
Amazing lecturer, he makes a difficult class very digestible. Workload is pretty light and most of the final grade is exams.

Dr. Adams provides many online resources, gives easy homework, and explains concepts very well so it's honestly difficult to not do well. He's funny in class and shows how to do different problems related to a topic while in class. As long as you either pay attention to the lectures in-person or keep up with them online you'll get a good grade.
Concepts can be a bit difficult, but a lot of resources are given to study and prepare for tests. Professor Adams was funny in his lectures and i liked the structure of the class.

Dr. Adams is an amazing professor!! Even though the content of this class is difficult, he explained it really well. There was a lot of homework, but it was the best thing to help me understand and practice the material. There are also a lot of resources (recorded lectures and past exams) to help you prepare for the exams.

Tests are not that hard, do as many as the previous exams as you can (all of them) as they are very similar. If you sit down and do the Xronos by yourself and understand them you will get an A. He records all his lectures so you can watch them later in the day. If you're struggling study edge really helps, I used them for exam 3 and the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Legit the GOAT. He explains concepts so well, provides note packets for every single lecture on canvas, and publishes all past exams as a study resource. The math itself might be tricky at times, but your grade is so padded with homework and you have so many study resources that it's almost impossible to get a bad grade in the class.

Just a goat professor. Calc 2 is pretty hard but Adams gives you the best chance you have to do well, he has teaching this class down to a science. Just actually do the hw and review past exams and you'll be good. One of my favorite professors ever

Great professor! The class is super organized, the notes are really helpful, and the discussion quizzes are managable. I would recommend doing a lot of practice tests before the exam if you want to do well as I found the bonus problems to be a waste of time.

Dr. Adams is a funny guy and a model professor at UF. Calc 2 is a hard class no doubt, but if you go to his lectures and are disciplined with practicing the concepts, an A is very achievable. For exams, get study edge and if you think you can get away with not fully understanding something, chances are its going to be on the exam.
He's a great professor and does a really good job explaining everything, just the content in calc 2 is really difficult.

The lectures were very clear, there's extra credit on exams, and tons of practice exams available. The weekly quizzes were quite simple. If you do a few practice exams before each test you should be able to get a good grade.

Great teacher and definitely a must take professor. The lectures provide a solid first glance at the topic, and he ensures that you understand the material. The weekly quizzes are usually easy if you review your notes and offer good practice. The tests are fair, and if you study your notes and review the previous exams, you should do well.

Stephen Adams is the GOAT. Great guy, excellent lectures, very clear guidelines, and is available MWF at office hours and really wants to help you out. The catch? Very tough tests. Do not underestimate, they're not easy. Extra credit is available on them but don't rely on it. Weekly quizzes but 2 of them are dropped.

Excellent lecturer who gives you literally everything you need to succeed in the course. Records every single lecture in an accessible format.  If your willing to put in the effort and time, you will do well in this class despite its difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There is a reason Dr. Adams is rated so highly. His lectures are perfect, perfect timing, perfect note template, perfect humor. He is great at explaining concepts, and the organization and structure of his class are so well thought out. He WANTS you to pass and provides all the resources you need to do so.

Calc 2 is a hard class in terms of material however Adams made the course manageable. Lectures were recorded and posted. The course is heavy on three exams and the final however there are past exams provided and the material is covered in depth in the lectures and homework (Xronos).

The best math professor I've had! His lectures are incredibly thorough, and they're recorded for you to look back on if you miss class or need to review. He is very respectful in his office hours and will never make you feel dumb, no matter the question. Tests make up 70% of your grade, but plenty of practice exams are provided.
Took Calc 2 with Professor Adams, his respect for students is so natural in and outside the lecture hall. Goes through learning materials in just the right pace. Thank you!
Had great notes and lecturing
Incredible professor

Dr. Adams is by far the best math teacher I have had. The last time I took math was 3 years ago in high school and calc 1 was not too bad. I took it for summer B so it was very high paced and would probably not do that again but I think if you're good with maths you would be great in his class. He is very accommodating and understanding. Take him!

Adams was a great lecturer and all of his lectures are posted online. His exams were fair and free from errors. There are practice exams to look over. The lectures are definitely material dense, but they can be rewatched.
Really good professor for how hard this class was. Easily the hardest math class I've taken at UF. Dr. Adams' lectures were more than enough to get me through it with an A.

Dr. Adams was an amazing Calc 2 professor for such a naturally hard class. He made the concepts very easy to understand, practice exams were very comparable to the actual one, and the questions you got tested on were very fair. Lectures were recorded so attendance wasn't really mandatory but there was a lecture quiz due 11:59 PM the day of lecture.
Doable but this class is hard as hell!!! Study those practice exams relentlessly. Good guy though and lectures are recorded which is a plus.

Currently have an A, class structure and lectures were thumbs up. Lectures follow the textbook (which is free) and co-written by him. Does a really good job explaining the proofs and helping you understand them. Goes over hw and exams briefly after they're graded and open to questions. Caring and approachable, teaches well.
amazing professor who cares about students. everything that can be on the test will be shown on lectures, elaborates more if someone requests, and explains very thoroughly.

Dr. Adams was great! His lectures were clear, engaging, and easy to follow. HW, attendance, and quizzes (2 lowest in each category get dropped) make up a decent portion of the grade, so it isn't too hard to get a good grade in the class. I wish he could've been my teacher for all of my calculus courses!

Calc 2 was a hard class but Adams explained all concepts in a way that made it easy to understand. Very rarely confused in this class. Adams also has a dry math teacher sense of humor that keeps class entertaining. Best professor I have had so far at UF.

Adams is a great professor, lectures very well and is knowledgeable. He makes everything so easy to understand and easy to follow along with. Records all his lectures and is very kind. Always stays after class for students with questions. Knows how to get through the lectures timely as well. Material is difficult but he makes it seem easy.

Adams was the best math prof at UF I've had, im taking calc 3 right now with a new professor and the class is easier content wise but so much more draining because it isn't taught as well. Adams taught calc 2 amazing, if you put the work in there is no reason you don't get an A

He moves pretty fast through lectures and doesn't always do examples of the harder applications of a topic. Explains basic concepts in class but then relies a lot on TAs to get more in depth and specific with the applications. If you pay attention and do the Xronos though, you can pass.

Dr. Adams is a great lecturer. I did not go to his office hours, but I heard he is caring when you ask for help. I mainly used the tutoring center in the little hall for extra support. The content itself isn't difficult to learn if you put in the time and space out your learning. Study Edge also helped but provided bad practice problems.

This guy does an amazing job at making Calc 2 a bearable class. He always finds the perfect analogy to explain a concept. He's also pretty damn funny and some of his jokes will catch you off guard in a good way. Obviously this class is gonna be tough but as long as you ACTUALLY watch/go to the lectures and do practice problems you'll be fine.

Easily one of the best math professors I've had, and that is saying quite a lot when the class he teaches is calc 2. He somehow manages to keep a class of hundreds of students focused on what he says, and he is not afraid to make a joke just for fun or to get students to pay attention. He also only puts content on exams that has been in lecture.

His lectures are clear and coherent to the material that we are expected to learn. I didn't have tot use any outside resources to learn the materials because of how he was able to get students to understand his lectures. Exams aren't too bad, but the final is HARD!

Calc 2 is a really hard class but Dr. Adams makes it as easy as it can get. He explains all the concepts pretty clearly and can answer even the most obscures questions as if he already had an answer prepared. Make sure you study cause the exams are HARD!

Easily one of the best math teachers I have ever had. At the beginning of the year Calc 2 was heavily hyped up as the hardest math class at UF by all the preview people, but Professor Adams has his lectures refined down to such a perfect science that I'd almost say Calc 2 was easy.

Dr. Adams is a great lecturer! For such a tough course, he explains everything thoroughly and is ready to answer questions during lectures. Attendance is expected for lectures (class participation assignments for each lecture; answers are given in the lecture) and mandatory for discussion groups (quizzes each week). His lectures are recorded, too.

Very nice guy and good professor but felt like he over complicated a lot of the material which made already difficult calc 2 even worse. Moved through lectures fast but he had to in order to cram in all of the material in a short span of a semester. Exams are pretty difficult but definitely study the practice exams in depth.

- 3 lectures/week (w online recording)
- 1 TA period (avoid Zhao if possible)
- funny, gives grandpa from Up vibes but when he was still married to Ellie
- fair amount of homework, weekly quizzes
- great job explaining hard topics, does good review of calc 1 topics
- in high school they tell you that profs won't care, he's the anti-example of this
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were thorough and easy to follow/understand. Homework is short but covers all the important topics, and he gives more than enough time to complete it. Lecture recordings were nice for review. Best professor at UF so far.

Idk the class was really hard for me for some reason and got a C. And then I took calc 3 and got an A. Professor is really good though. Super intricate in his explanations and has a good attention to detail.

Adams is easily the best math professor I've had at UF. Calc 2 is a difficult class, but Adams makes the material very approachable. His lectures are great and he's always prepped for questions. His exams are hard, but they cover the material in class and there's no real surprises. The TAs are a spotty, but that's always the case in math classes.
Professor Adams is a great lecturer who explains concepts of calculus extremely well. Even though Calc is somewhat difficult in general, I would highly recommend taking Adams.

Awesome teacher, explained concepts very well and was super nice and funny. The class was very difficult for me even though I went to every class period, the exams were crazy difficult and I almost never had time to finish them.

Adam's lectures are like step-by-step tutorials. His explanations are simple and concise. However I found them more engaging when I watched them at 2x speed. Calculus isn't easy no matter who you take, but I feel Adams made me it much easier!!

Dr. Adams is an amazing lecturer who clearly knows what he is talking about, yet explains content in a way that is simple to understand. Although the content of the class is hard and you will have to put in the work to do well, Adams is always eager to help both online and in person.

Dr. Adam's lectures were clear. He answered questions well and cared about the students. The course was structured fairly and the grading scale is forgivable. Would take the professor again, but not the class. The content wasn't fun.

Dr. Adams is basically all you can ask for from a professor, since his lectures are clear and consistent, he shows a desire for students to understand the material rather than memorize it, extra credit opportunities are given, he's flexible and always willing to answer questions, and is generally likeable. Would recommend for calc 2.

I have already taken Calculus BC in High School and passed it, but my advisor had me retake it for some reason. I already understood most of the material and felt he sometimes overcomplicated concepts. But when I didn't understand, I would go to his office hours which he had a lot of and was very helpful. Also a really nice guy!

Dr. Adams is a great professor. I had taken calc 2 in high school but Dr. Adams helped me understand the topics so much more than I had before. The material can be difficult at times and if you actually do the xronos assignments it will be very time consuming.

I loved the class. It was flipped and I thought it would be hard but it wasn't that bad. I will say that he has a lot of lecture videos that are long and sometimes he would confuse me. However, I had StudyEdge that had short videos and taught me the same thing that he did in an easier way. He also cracked jokes to keep you engaged. Would recommend

Although I came into this class with a previous foundation of calculus, the flipped manner of this class definitely helped me succeed. This class is perfect for those who like to work in groups to solve problems and watch lectures as homework.

I did withdraw from this class because calc 2 is a different breed. However, I liked Professor Adams because he was caring. I felt like there wasn't enough time in lecture to cover examples. The hw was hard  because I never knew how to start. He gave us days off after exams that I would have preferred to go class so that I could learn more.
Professor Adams was very good. He has very clear lecture notes and problems to work through. The exams are reasonable as long as you do the Xronos homework.

professor adams gives great lectures, and moves through the content quickly enough so i never got bored or distracted. he also posts a TON of resources on canvas to help you get extra practice if you need it. calc 2 is probably the hardest class i've ever taken, but professor adams made it doable
Professor Adams was very friendly and engaging, though he often moved through material very quickly.

Topics are paced very well and lectures tie together well from lecture to lecture making them easier to follow. Although missing a lecture will mean you'll be completely lost, they're always posted online and very easy to access so in-person attendance is not mandatory but definetly encouraged.

The lectures were always great, engaging, and thorough. The class was a bit difficult, but having him as a professor made it easier. He always did a great job answering questions during and after class.

Great professor who is funny and personable, but not a fan of the course or its material. This is quite a difficult class and merely focuses on the mechanics of calculus rather than its applications. I would strongly recommend that business majors with no intention to switch to engineering, etc. opt to take MAC2234 instead.
great lecturer & clarity in calc 2 :)
Absolutely amazing professor with great teaching skills.

He is an amazing professors and possibly one of the most organized professors I have ever had. His lectures are perfectly organized and he always gives great feedback when students have questions. His grading is very clear and he allows for 5 extra points on the exams: i.e. if you got 95 points on the exam you would get a 100%. Highly recommend.
LOVE THIS ABSOLUTE LEGEND
Great professor, the best math teacher I have had to date.

Although this was a flipped class (watch lectures outside of class and do a worksheet in class), Dr. Adams briefly explains the material at the beginning of each class. He has no problem answering any questions you have in or outside of class as well. Great professor but make sure you are willing to put in work outside of class if you take him.

Professor Adams was amazing! I took the flipped class, and the lectures weren't amazing but he always did a wonderful job of re-explaining the concepts. He was always thorough in his explanations and willing to help. There are also opportunities to help your grade like extra credit and extra points on exams. Wonderful professor!

Dr. Adams is a fantastic professor. I have taken Calc 1 & 2 with him and he is extremely consistent and really knows his stuff. Ask him an obscure question in class and he'll answer it as if he had the full answer prepared beforehand. He also has great humor. Calc is hard, but Adams certainly makes the class doable. Highly recommend.

Dr. Adams is a great professor, I took him for MAC2311 and MAC2312. He was very helpful in class, and was always willing to stay after class to answer any questions we had. He does a good job at explaining how to find the answer to a question, and his thought process behind his work. Both classes are difficult but he wants you to succeed.
One of the best math teachers I've had, so patient and thorough with explanations. I had the flipped class and I really liked it, I also definitely recommend his office hours they're super helpful.
I accidentally took MAC2311 flipped classroom but I ended up liking it because of Dr. Adams. Very solid teacher; gave excellent feedback when asked questions.

Adams is honestly great. I didn't like the flipped structure of the class but he was always available for office hours. He's really approachable and doesn't make you feel dumb when you don't know how to do something. This class is definitely difficult (you have to put in the work) but I think that's just how the class is set up.

Prof. Adams is a nice, funny guy and always helps when its needed. If you don't have calc experience, his recorded lectures aren't the best imo. However, if you put in the effort in the class, you will be fine. Extra credit is offered on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Adams is great, he is very funny and very clear on how the class works. Make sure to stay on top of things and do as much practice as possible, including the practice test. However do be aware that sometimes the practice tests are like the tests and other times completely different. Make sure not to miss class, as it is flipped
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It is a flipped course, and participation is mandatory. Dr, Adams is very clear on the course material, and lots of practice exams are offered. If you actually put an effort to get an A, there is no way you will end up with anything else.

Dr. Adams is a cool guy. I took the flipped classroom calc 1, and I thought it was okay. Math is pretty ugly in my opinion, but if you have to take math, Dr. Adams is approachable, patient, and funny, and he is always willing to help students who ask for it. His jokes can be pretty epic, too

It's a flipped-style classroom, which I think benefitted me. Adams is super reasonable in terms of attendance, work, grades, etc. All exams had possible extra credit. It's a class where if you actually try, you'll be fine.

I was initially hesitant about the flipped classroom style for Calc 1 but I learned to like it. Adams is a pretty good teacher and this class style helped prepare me for tests. Very very nice guy, pretty funny, and very approachable. He's a great option for calc.
Calculus 1 is awful, but the awful parts are usually department-controlled (The exams and review options). Adams is the best you'll get.

Great guy, not so great professor. I would not take his class if this is your first calculus class. Overcomplicated super easy subject material to the point where getting good grades on tests felt impossible. Test questions were so difficult, it almost was like they weren't even testing you on the concepts, but just wanted you to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Adams was fantastic. Good humor, but just the right amount. He gives great lectures, and was very adaptive to the new online learning environment. Before each exam, he would make announcement in Canvas listing each old exam and which specific problems would pertain to test. Highly recommend!

Just loved Stephen; was always super nice and funny in class and great at explaining concepts. I would highly recommend him for Calc 1, the pre-lecture quizzes are always simple and he's great at letting you know when something is important or not for exams.

Compared to other teachers lecture videos they are much better. I took calculus in high school and this class was so easy. Dr. Adams is also super understanding if you email him about missing class ahead of time.

Dr. Adams is a kind man who is clearly passionate about math and teaching. He is very understanding and willing to help. Has some funny jokes as well. Your grade will be primarily tests, but exams from previous semesters are provided to study from - study those and you'll be fine!

Dr. Adams is a really great calc professor. His lectures are really helpful, and he always explains problems if you need help. I went to office hours to review a test and he explained each problem I got wrong. I'd definitely recommend him. Make sure you get a good TA, though
Highly recommend for Calc 1. The flipped class style is super helpful, and Dr. Adams himself is super funny and caring. He made math a bit less painful. 10/10 Recommend.

Great lecture videos! It's a flipped class, so you watch lectures at home and then do assignments "in class" (also at home this semester). Tests are challenging but not ridiculous if you have done all the online homework assignments and understand how you did them. Provides practice exams and past exams to study for the test. Very funny dry humor.

Dr. Adams was a very accessible professor and made calculus bearable. I would say he was very fair and always made an effort to make himself available outside class. He always gave useful feedback and was overall a very good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amazing professor and truly cares about his student's success. Available outside of class and actually works with you through questions and gives you tips and tricks. Also summarizes lectures before class begins do that's cool.

Dr. Adams is an amazing calculus professor who will answer any and all questions you have. If you create regular interactions with him, it makes MAC2311 so much easier as he explains things in ways that just make sense. I cannot recommend him enough.

Dr. Adams is a genuinely outstanding professor. Calculus can be difficult at times, but his exams are extremely fair and accurately measure your knowledge. Go to office hours if you canthey're super helpful.

Dr. Adams does make an effort to present material to help, but the lecture videos that he uses are almost entirely unreliable and do not benefit you so whatsoever. That being said, he takes time to explain the material in class which does in fact make it seem more like a traditional setting rather than the flipped method that it is classified as.
My B does not reflect his teaching. Amazing teacher.

Lots of readings each week but they're interesting. The class uses team-based learning and you'll be with the same people all semester. Quizzes and the midterm are straightforward. Other assignments were generally graded pretty leniently. Put in effort and you'll be fine

SO MUCH READING but at least it's usually pretty interesting. She makes us read so much but spends almost no time on the readings. Her lectures are kinda useless but it's ok because the content is easy. She is good at clarifications and is willing to leave room for discussion over specific questions. The class was structured as team based learning.
Great professor and person, cares about students and is always open for conversation on any number of topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: absolutely the best professor at uf! Dr. Strong is brilliant, funny, interesting, and accommodating. She always gives great feedback and I have learned an immeasurable amount from her and her classes. do not miss the opportunity to learn from her!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She does not take into consideration that students are taking other courses, and assigns entire books to read by the next class. Unreasonable professor, unwilling to discuss attendance or grading matters, and brings her own political opinions into the classroom, which I believe is unnecessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you are looking for an easy quest class, do not take this. It is definitely attainable to get an A but there is a lot of work. There is a lot of writing and papers for a class that does not give any words. Additionally, the class was entirely based on doing group work. For the most part assignments are graded easy, but it is annoying.

Overall, pretty easy class. Lots of reading from the textbook & other 3 books that are part of this course. Other articles are assigned. Lectures are boring because she just reads from the slides. This class is Team-Based learning so if you are assigned good partners this class provides an opportunity to make friends. IRAT quizzes average 60%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took Making Babies because the name of the course really made me curious as to what the class entitled. While it wasnt what I expected it to be, Dr. Strong was a great prof. I was a terrible student and she was still always super nice and understanding. The class has a lot of reading and writing but overall shes an easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I liked the class, but Dr. Strong was sarcastic and sometimes arrogant. She was especially picky on quizzes (class averages were always around 60%). DOES NOT GIVE ENOUGH TIME ON QUIZZES/TESTS. This was the biggest complaint students had the entire semester!! She only read the powerpoints for lecture and wasn't very consistent with extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I hate this prof. He repeats himself in lecture SO much it makes u feel like u are going insane. He always runs out of time bc he shows up 5-10 minutes late. His online lectures are more useful in 2x speed because he actually covers the LO's. Use Smokin' notes to review and u will be fine but I would suggest taking the online section if offered

HORRIBLE organization and time management. Would always show up to class 3-5 minutes late, sometimes canceled class after it already started.Said he would put in extra credit and never did. NEVER answers emails so if you need to reach him outside class good luck.Repeats himself so much in lecture. Misplaced our last exam and APK dept had to step in

A MESS!!! his lectures always start late, and sometimes even cancels class AFTER it started. He repeats himself SOOO much and is so monotone and boring. he's also IMPOSSIBLE to reach and never answers his emails. our f25 exam 4 got cancelled because he "lost" it and apk department had to get involved.
Not much to say.. If you study / attend lecture you will get an A. If you don't attend lecture you can still get an A using Smokin' notes.

Dr. Adolphs' learning objectives are very clear. I would definitely watch the YouTube videos as they are very helpful. I also used Smokin' Notes, and the practice exams they put out are very helpful!!

He rambles a bit in his lectures but it makes things pretty clear. Over summer he skipped many many chapters because his time management is a bit off but it made the tests that much easier. He shows up to class late everyday (to be fair it was an 8 am everyday). Tests were very fair, if you pay attention and take notes you won't need to study much

Dr. Adolphs has a way of explaining the material in a way that made complete sense to me. He repeats and drives home the important points during lecture. I looked forward to his lectures and this class. The exam is also fairly easy if you know your stuff.
He was straight forward and taught this course very well. Focus on the learning objectives, it was very helpful for the exams. Smokin notes practice questions were also very helpful.

Lectures start 5–15 mins late, often rambles and repeats- sometimes helpful, but often confusing. Smokin Notes was essential to keep material clear. He's impossible to reach, cancels class last minute, posts double-length videos instead. Never graded my exam, responded to emails about it, and class ended without a grade for it- wildly unfair.
He will not answer emails, will not be at his office hours, and is impossible to reach so it's hard to get your content questions answered. He is also always upset.

I loved taking this class with Max Adolphs. He is a great lecturer and repeats lecture information to reinforce subjects. I used Smokin' Notes to help make the complex subjects simple when working through the learning objectives for the exams.

Adolphs sets clear expectations for what content will be on the exam. Definitely attend the lectures even tho there's not attendance. Smokin notes also helped me a lot in brushing up on the content before exams
