He shows up 5-10 mins late to class almost every day. A few times, he has emailed the class 1 hour before lecture to cancel lecture for that day and posted videos for us to watch instead. He cancels office hours last-minute. Exam scores take forever to come out. He doesn't respond to emails. Lectures are longwinded, vague, and not engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attend class, doesn't post online materials so you must attend to get the information. Doesn't start class on time or end on time, goes way over and starts late. Rambles a ton.

he's nice but not understanding at all. exams are like the lectures but super specific so make sure to know the tiniest details. i literally got an A in biochem and almost failed this class so idk what that says about his exam format.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Adolph's has been one of my favorite professors at UF. He is super enthusiastic about the class and is a passionate teacher. He truly wants students to learn and I enjoyed the class a ton. smokin notes was also helpful and helped keep me track each week as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Adolphs is very caring for his students, I took this in the Summer and he was very understanding that it was an accelerated course. Go to lecture everyday he repeats big concepts that will be on the exam so take good notes. I used Smokin Notes for a different perspective and it helped me to fully comprehend the content.

Loved the course! Adolphs is a great lecturer with a clear passion for the content. You need to pay attention and take good notes. The Smokin Notes do a good job of having everything from lecture in clear writing. Otherwise, Adolphs will answer any questions you have after class/take a look at your notes to ensure you're on the right track!

Adolphs was a great lecturer and explained the content very well. Used lots of visuals which helped to understand the processes/ content. Class isn't mandatory but it's super easy to fall behind if you don't go. Since there is so much content, I would recommend Smokin Notes so that you have all the info in one place.

I really liked Dr. Adolphs for this class. He explains things in a very logical way. His recorded lectures can run long, but everything said in lectures is reflected in his exams. As long as you keep up with the lectures and take good notes you will do good. The only bad thing is that he doesn't really show up to his own office hours lol.

Dr. Adolphs is an amazing prof. You really need to rely on his lectures to do well on his exams, what he says during lectures is word for word what appears on the exam so make sure to write it down. Didn't use textbooks at all. He also doesn't give out extra credit so make sure to do well on the exams since those are graded heavily.
Adolphs is the professor you want for physio. He is clearly passionate and knowledgeable, and I found the material and the way he explains things
Lab quizzes are so annoying and unnecessarily hard. He is a fantastic professor and exams are very fair.

I liked this course. Dr Adolphs explains everything so well, although a little time consuming. Basically just take really good notes on his videos and then just use the learning objects. do this and you will be good. Lab was annoying tho

Ngl, he be yapping a lot. Some weeks, we would somehow have 8 hours of recorded lecture. But I have to give him 5 stars bc he is quite good at explaining content. I wish I took his class earlier as it is foundational for a lot of other courses and the mcat. Very reachable and puts in time for his students. Some his questions I found were misleading

Professor Adolphs is very knowledgeable and explains concepts thoroughly. His lectures can be long and repetitive, but they give you a great understanding of the concept. He makes practice exams for each exam that are really helpful. There are 4 exams, but no cumulative final. I definitely recommend Professor Adolphs.

This professor is my goat. If you study all the lectures well and take good notes, you will get an A in the course. If a concept is hard, reaching out to him or his TAs is easy and they are happy to help. Your effort in the class translates 1:1 to your grade. The tests cover everything in the lectures but are completely fair. Cannot recommend more.

He is honestly one of the best professors I have ever had. His expectations are very clear and his exams are very straightforward. Does a great job explaining tough topics to get you to understand the bigger picture.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, online lectures can be lengthy but it is because he is emphasizing the concepts for understanding rather than flying through the material. Exams are not meant to trick you and he is very straight forward. Can't recommend enough.

He is an amazing lecturer although a bit repetitive. His lectures are long so be wary of that. His exams are based completely on learning objectives and are very fair. How I got an A was watching the lectures on 2x speed, taking good notes, and then doing the learning objectives right after. Overall, I learned alot from him.

Dr. Adolph was great, his lectures although long, were really in depth and helped you understand the material, make sure to keep up with them since they can pile up. there are lecture quizzes at the end of the week but its really easy and less than 10 questions. labs are 1 a week and end about an hr early if you have an online lab that week
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had here. The online format is not unbearable, but they can pile up some weeks. He repeats himself throughout the lectures which can get redundant but it is typically a clue of what is on the exam. Great class

I absolutely loved Dr. Adolphs. He is a grade professor and always thoroughly explains each concept. As long as you go to class, you will do will in this class. I supplemented my lecture notes with Smokin Notes which helped to further my understanding of the topics and get an A in the class!

Dr. Adolphs is the best professor I've had. He's a great lecturer and explains things really well. Lectures aren't mandatory but I strongly recommend attending all of them because his exams are based off what he talks about in class. The exams are easy & straightforward. No trick questions or anything complex. Loved his class so much!

Amazing lecturer. Hardly had to study because of how effective lecture was. If you go to class and pay attention you will get a good grade
Super nice guy and willing to help outside of class
TAKE HIS CLASS

Dr. Adolphs is the best professor I've had at UF and I TA'd for him for two semesters. I love the way he lectures and ensures every student clearly understands the material before each exam. He answers emails promptly and encourages all students to attend office hours (TAs and his own). Attendance isn't taken, but you MUST go to lecture to do well.

Very good professor. Lectures are very easy to understand and test material come directly from them. For one exam, I crammed all lectures the night before and got an 88% for that exam. If you care about GPA then definitely take physio with him - test are super easy!

One of the best professors by far at UF. You can tell he truly cares about the students and wants to see all of us succeed. His lectures are incredibly useful, and he explains things many times to make sure the concept is really understood. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!
He makes very detailed lectures, goes over the important content again and again, really helped to understand the content. Tests are easy if you follow and understand the lectures.

Dr. Adolphs is one of the best professors I have had here at UF. He is super cool and a chill guy, as well as a great lecturer. There were times when he would take a whole class to talk about one powerpoint slide, but he made sure the information was ingrained into us. Exams based of the SLO's. Amazing experience, amazing professor.

Dr. Adolphs is one of the best professors at UF. TAKE THE CLASS IN PERSON! He is such a great lecturer and his exams are actually really straightforward. It's a difficult course but he gives you all the information you need to do well and as long as you put in the effort you will be fine!

At the start of the year, I was a little intimidated because Exam 1 was harder than I expected but Dr. Adolphs is really a great professor. His lectures are very easy to understand and he bases his exams right off of that. You HAVE to go to lecture or else this class will be impossible for you! If you are able to- take Dr. Adolphs!
Dr. Adolphs was amazing, by far the best lecturer! His lectures were crucial for exams, but he explains everything so well.

Professor Adolphs is great, he is always very attentive during lectures and explains the material several times to ensure that the students understand. Study the SLOs for his exams and attend UGTA office hours. The class material can be difficult but ensure you are actively studying before the exams. Not previously taking Anatomy is okay! Very nice
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Adolphs is the BEST professor I have ever had. He is an AMAZING lecturer and this class is easy to pass as long as you come to class and studying the learning objectives (they are literally a study guide). I know the online format is tempting since this class is so early but the online is much harder and Adolphs is worth it!! Seriously!!

Dr. adolphs is genuinely one of the best professors I've had at UF. His lectures are really all you need to do well on his exams. I personally, just rewatched his lectures and did the learning objectives to get A's on his exams. His exams are also straight-forward and great

The best APK teacher I have ever had. Exams were about learning objectives and were difficult but fair. Probably the only class I have taken where I actually understood the material. Teaches in thought trains but somehow it all makes sense.
Attending his lectures is a must !! This course was very fair as well as his exams . If you study the SLOs thoroughly and ahead of time  you are bound to get an A. Textbook is not necessary.

Dr. Adolphs is the best APK professor I have ever had. He knows the material so well and is able to explain it perfectly, he draws out every single pathway and explains it so well. Weekly quizzes help your grade a lot and group discussion is a great way to understand the material. His class is very interesting and the exams follow the objectives.

Dr. Adolphs is the best professor I have had at UF. His lectures are extremely helpful and all you need to do well on exams, he also makes learning physiology so fun. Go to his office hours!!! He explains everything in so much detail and makes sure you understand and are ready for exams.

Amazing professor!! He is super open to questions, and during his lectures he tends to ask the class questions that keep you in the conversation. I was kinda surprised by the difficulty rating for this course...because you definitely need to stay on top of the work and study a fair amount. Overall, would definitely recommend!

Max Adolphs is the best prof I have ever had at UF. He does teach fast, as there is a lot of material, but he isnt afraid of taking almost a whole period to review if he thinks we need it. Tests are fair and not worded to trick you. He wants students to truly understand and be interested, not regurgitate useless information.

Studying his class this semester. Not being partial because he is my crush, but he is the best at explaining each topic with absolute dedication. It gets little difficult to score full points in the quizzes right after the class. He is respectful with any doubts and questions. Wish he had virtual office hours as it is hard to reach him via email.

Professor Max Adolph's Physiology class is essentially a very light survey of the material. He does not go overly in depth and his test questions are not written to confuse you, they are very straight forward. I enjoy his lectures, but it is pretty clear the material is dumbed down in this class compared to other physiology courses at UF.

My favorite APK professor by far. It is obvious how well he knows the information and he tells everything like a story so it's so easy to put two and two together. Quizzes at least once a week and the exams are not cumulative. Study the learning objectives and you'll get a for sure A.

Dr Adolphs is great. He demonstrates that he knows the material like the back of his hand. Entertaining lectures that make the material easy to understand. You have to show up to every class for an easy quiz based on that lectures material but its basically just an attendance checker. The exam is easy if you study the learning objectives.

She didn't grade anything for a month, then gave very bare feedback for each submission and then took off 20% of my final paper just saying it wasn't specific enough. Don't take with her if you can help it. Material was fine otherwise, really just her.r

Do not take this class. She grades super late and you don't know your grade up until the middle of the semester. She is not lenient at all and doesn't tell you what you did wrong. You can only contact her throughh Canvas and even then, she takes a while to respond. I had an A+ the last week, and she gave me a C on the final with no feedback or help

She was a TA for my Art of Identity and Health class and was great! You have to work for your grade, just as you should in any class. She provides beneficial feedback on assignments so that you are able to improve in areas that were lacking before. She contributes insight into discussions and provides so much knowledge into the course! I recommend!

She was a TA for my Arts & Identity of Health class. She is very passionate about what she does and it translates into what is taught in the course. Although her grading can be tough, it isnt hard to come away with good grade. Highly recommend her for any class youre taking!!

Professor Addie is one of the best professors out there! She really cares a lot about her students and she always responds to emails and questions very promptly. She has so much knowledge about the world and society and Im very thankful for everything shes taught me. I highly recommend her!
Yewande was very passionate about the course and cared about the success of the students. Was a lot of fun taking the course.

Professor Yewande Addie was an assistant professor in the class IDS2935 (synchronous online). In the discussions, she was well versed in a range of topics and her commentary was offered more depth/individual relevance to the topic. While completing group projects, she was very easy to reach and offered feedback that helped raise our grade.

Yewande was my TA for my Quest class and she was so sweet and insightful. The class encouraged expressing ourselves and that often came with a lot of vulnerability, but Yewande was always supportive. My only complaint is she grades a bit harsh and her feedback can be vague. She'll comment praises but not explain why points were taken off.

Yewande was the TA for my Art of Identity and Health quest course fall of 2020. The class was online but attendance was mandatory for two lectures a week over zoom. Overall, I felt like I had to really put in effort to get an A but it isn't unattainable. She notices who participated and who doesn't, so use that to your advantage.

She posts work at 3 am on Monday mornings and makes assignments due at noon that day. I have more work in this class than all three of my other classes combined. She won't respond quickly. There is extra credit but not enough. The assignments are also very time-consuming. Shes honestly rude when you reach out for help. Has said, "its okay to fail."
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class was misserable
Dror is awesome and really cares about his students. 10/10.

I took beginning Hebrew 1 and 2 with Dror this year and he was amazing! I had no basis in Hebrew but I learned so much. His class is hard but he is very helpful and wants you to succeed. I highly reccomend taking his classes because he is one of the best professors I've ever had!

I completed my year of Intermediate Hebrew with Dror, he is a really great Hebrew professor! One of the most patient dudes I know. After finishing our textbook, we read a short novel in Hebrew and dialogued to improve our conversational skills. Definitely recommend!

This is an online class with long readings every week and 3-4 weekly assignments. There are 2 major papers, and the rubrics and instructions are really vague so the average tends to be low because you don't know what you're doing, and he grades very harshly but doesn't give any feedback. Easy exams. A lot more work than I was anticipating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dror is great! I found his class to be super easy and at times fun. Highly recommend if you have a pretty good foundation for Hebrew and are looking to keep it up/improve.

I am taking Intermediate Hebrew with Dror and I very much like his teaching style. He's very knowledgeable on teaching tactics and gives students plenty of opportunities to work on their speaking, writing, and reading skills. He is incredibly patient! I would recommend studying with him simply because of that! His corrections have really helped me
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I had a rude awakening with this class. The discussion assignments and quizzes are easy. However, there are two critical analysis writing assignments that have a very vague rubric that he graded INCREDIBLY harshly. The class average for the paper was below 50%. he also gives no feedback on what you did wrong so you have no clue how to improve.

Prof. Abend is one of the best professors Ive had at UF! He is so caring, and although the class is a bit tough, he is very supportive and always eager to help. Anytime I messed up speaking Hebrew, he would always say stuff like it is a new language, take your time, youre doing great! and so on. I cant wait to take another class of his!

I took Yiddish 1 with Dr. Abend and I highly recommend it! I have learned so much in just a semester and I am so fortunate to have been able to take such an uncommonly taught language. Dr. Abend is very kind and patient--taking his class is a joy. If you get the opportunity, absolutely take Yiddish with him!

I took Yiddish Language & Culture. The class was easy, especially if you already know the Hebrew alephbeth (or alefbeys), or any German. The lessons are taken directly from the textbook (can be found as a PDF). There were only 4 other people in the class (!!!) when I took it, so you could choose to accelerate your studies almost one-on-one, or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a great guy and a great professor. Makes learning a foreign language fun. If you are considering taking this course, do it.

Dror has mandatory attendance, which is necessary as the only way students would attend his dry lectures. He likes to stand up front and talk the entire class, with the occasional calling on students or pairing us into groups. Despite the heavy lectures, you won't feel particularly knowledgeable when you leave. The essays are vague but graded easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This lit class is very unpredictable.  While I do have a relatively high A in the class, the grading scale is often varied and the prompts are vague.  He gives you a list of 10 or so novels to buy and those are your textbooks, but I've only read one of them in full.  Sparknotes and Shmoop have been my main "textbooks."

His Lit class is very  easy if you've taken AP Literature before. It's more of a glorified book club w/ papers. Personally I am not a fan of his lecture style for the class. It's very him-controlled and students don't get to participate much. I've not read any of the many books we've had to read and yet have a very high A. Sparknotes is your friend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I've taken three classes with Dror throughout my college career. The first as a first semester freshman and the last as a spring semester junior. He has taught me in and out of the classroom very important lessons about life. I enjoyed going to his class and participating. I have the utmost respect for him as a professor and as a person.

AVOID this class at all costs! The coursework is completely irrelevant-all we did was study poetry. I can honestly say I learned nothing about Israeli culture from taking this class. The professor almost seemed anti-Israel at certain points. His grading system is ridiculous-very picky. This class was by far the most disappointing class I took at UF

Harry Potter and the Holocaust with Dror-Abend David is my favorite class! You learn so much, and honestly there is barely any work! You can definitely get by without reading anything besides the two mandatory Harry Potter novels (which is awesome). Really, your only work is two short papers, and he's a tough grader, but they aren't bad.

I have taken several classes with Dror before this one. This class was Harry Potter and the Holocaust. Honestly, the class sucked. It was just irrelevant and annoying and everyday I would be upset that I had to go to class. I got an A-. As if it wasn't bad enough my transcript said Harry Potter and the Holocaust, I didn't even get an A. DON'T TAKE!

Dr. Abend is a really nice person, and his Shakes on Trial class was interesting!  I was on one of the legal teams, and it was enjoyable.  He often lacked clarity in terms of the charges, punishments, and court proceedings.  His lectures were also rather dull.  Overall, you'll get an A, but there are better Honors Reads classes available!

disorganized, no lesson plan,class time is wasted with games that has no pedagogical reflection,deducts large grades for innocent mistakes, never accept grades negotiation even if all class agreed he is wrong. ask us to prepare no. of pages and the next day he teaches other pages,a very easy course was converted into a hard and stressful.

Very cool teacher, doesn't stick to the syllabus really but you end up learning something. Grading is a bit weird but if you listen in class it shouldn't be hard at all to get an A. Would definitely recommend.
Dror is the best teacher! I am taking all his classes
Such a great teacher. The best.

Adams has good knowledge about the subject and uses it to make the lectures interesting. He gave quizzes that were easy if you just paid attention in class. I know he and someone else were grading assignments, and most of the time, there was good feedback.

I had Dr. Adams three years in a row and took four classes with him. I can't recommend him enough. The lectures are engaging, his grading is clear and helpful, and overall a super understanding guy. He gives feedback on all papers, of which there are usually 3 major ones and several mini ones. The class grade is mostly those, and attendance.

Dr. Adams is awesome. Extremely interesting class with amazing lectures. 5 ~500-750 word short responses with 2 drops and 3 ~2000 word essays. There isn't enough room to say everything but Dr. Adams is extremely understanding and always fair. He even stayed 10-15 minutes extra after every class to talk to students and answer questions.

LOVE THIS PROFESSOR! Super informative and engaging lectures (don't skip the class!!) and gives great feedback on essays. Not a super harsh grader, but pushes you to do your best and expects you to use the feedback he's given on your next essay. Is incredibly fair and holds himself to same standard of deadlines and professionalism. 100% recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Phenomenal professor & one of my favorite classes at UF so far! He's very passionate about what he teaches but lectures in a way that does not bombard you. There's a total of six assignments: all writing, but there is a fair rubric of what he looks for. Fair grader, offers meaningful suggestions. He cares about you and understands his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lots of reading. Easy essays and very entertaining and informative lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a review for AMH2020. Great lecturer, tries (and succeeds) to make the material interesting. Not much hw (weekly one page double spaced papers), easy grading. Exams and essays are very straightforward. Did not expect to actually enjoy this class but it was great! Take him if you can or need the history credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really engaging lectures, makes history very fun to listen to. Testing is subjective which is really nice, not much focus on memorization which I enjoyed. I would take this class again, just make sure you take notes!

Dr. Adams had really entertaining lectures that directly related to the papers we had to write. He would always give feedback on papers and explain why points were taken away on assignments. He was responsive to questions and rewarded people who put in the effort to learn.

Dr. Adams' class is the best class I have taken at UF thus far! He is so awesome, and makes his class very interesting. At times, history can be boring, but Dr. Adams' was great. I would definitely recommend one of his classes.

Very rewarding class; prof. is super chill dude. Grading gets harder as the class goes on... no one got higher than a 95 on assignments. Lectures very engaging, time goes by quick. Attendance is randomly checked. Gives great feedback during office hours on assignments, and general advice on the His. department. Wants to help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Adams has a truly unique style and complete command over the topic. Took the practicum on TR and was fascinated. He is a down-to-earth professor and always makes expectations clear. Very good person and would recommend!!

I really enjoyed taking History Practicum with Dr. Adams. His lectures are great, and he set very clear standards for what he expected throughout the course. I really appreciate how he naturally fostered discussions and how he incorporated examples from his own research into lectures and course material. Great prof, I highly recommend!

Dr. Adams is one of those professors who will go above and beyond for a student. I will say his essay grading is tougher than I'm used to, but he kindly looked over my papers before I turned them in so I could improve my grades. He's really friendly, organized, extremely knowledgeable, and a great storyteller. Just a great professor.

This class is great- I'd highly recommend taking it! No quizzes or tests- just weekly 250 word assignments and two longer papers, but so long as you listen to the lectures, substantiate your work with evidence, follow Chicago manual style, and write well you should be fine. Professor Adams is awesome and happy to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Adams is a very engaging lecturer. While teaching a history practicum, he starts off grading easy and advises students on how to score higher, as the grading gets harder. Pay attention. Read the small books he assigns! You have weekly assignments but they're mostly reading-heavy, and the assignments themselves are easy. Just a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is an Honors book class on Hamilton by Ron Chernow. The class consisted of reading roughly 60 pages per week of the book and then discussing it during the weekly class. There were also 3 papers due throughout the semester, which are graded pretty toughly, and make up about 80 percent of your grade. It wasn't too bad of a class, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: We were assigned 3 300+ page novels to read, so be prepared for that. A lot of brainstorming ideas. Only 2 essays and no tests. He was a really great lecturer though, and he cared a lot about his students success.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor, I would absolutely take classes with him again! He's super helpful outside of class and if you play your cards right, it's totally possible to get recommendations out of him. And since he's the department chair, that looks pretty awesome. He has a genuine interest in the students that surpasses any other professor I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: If you're looking for an easy A don't take this class. However, if you really want to learn do take this class. His lectures are easy to sit through and are very engaging. Dr. Adams is the department chair so he knows what he's talking about and it shows in his lectures. Powerpoints mostly  have photo examples so don't skip lecture.

This is not the easiest class, but it's one of those where you look back and are glad you took it. Adams was very helpful and passionate about history. He really pushes you on the writing component, but this helps prepare you tremendously for other classes you take down the road. A lot of reading (up to 100 pages/week) but I'd take this class again
Great teacher if you absolutely love history. Once you understand what he likes in writing, the class is a breeze. I would absolutely take him again.

Professor Adams makes me enjoy history! I absolutely loved this class because I had to actually read to pass.  He always helps when you need it and gives great feedback on every assignment.  Increased my ability to write as well!  Take him!
BAE. Had him for American Capitalism. Inspired me to want to do business stuff and make tons of money. Literally bae. If you have a chance to take his class, do it!

You must read the textbook to do well in class. There are pop quizzes in both lecture and discussion. They are easy as long as you've read the chapters. I Dr. Adams makes the lectures fairly interesting. You can tell he is very passionate about the subject! I recommend this class.

I've seen many professors who have had the little chilly pepper next their names and it completely wrong. But in this case, it is very true. Not only is he physically attractive but he is an amazing professor that really knows the subject. I would recommend for everyone to take a class with him!. Just read and pay attention & you'll do great.

Your grade is based on 3 papers that require a lot of references to the books we read in class. I didn't read a thing until a paper was due and did fine grade wise, however. He is a really nice and intelligent person who makes the course information very interesting.
Very helpful outside of class, a fair grader, and always engaged and organized for class.

I took History of American Capitalism with Adams and can definitively say that he was the best professor I've had at UF. I was already interested in the subject but he made every lecture engaging by prompting discussion and asking questions. He's an fair grader and clearly articulates the goals of the class. No political bias in his presentation.

He is a wonderful teacher. He makes every subject interesting, even in a morning class. You're expected to do all of the reading and participate in class discussions to make a good grate. If you don't mind writing papers (two major ones and a few short responses), then you'll love the class! Tough, but completely fair grader. RECOMMEND HIGHLY!
Practicum.  Good lecturer.  If he taught things other than AMH I'd be all over it, but that's not really my focus.

Slavery&Abolitionism. Really nice guy, really good lectures. Makes things really interesting.A lot of reading but oh well. Makes boring subjects fun. Very approachable in his office. Grades papers a little rough but with effort you can overcome. Grades rewardingly on improvment. If you make the effort it will insure your A. I def. rec. him.
It made the industrial revolution something that could be talked about.  The class was boring because of the material, but Adams was able to get past the boring material.

Adams is my favorite history teacher I've had. He's a great lecturer and is very clear about what he expects. I'm in AMH2020 now and find myself wishing to be back in his well-organized and interesting lectures. If you need 2010 or a humanities credit, take his class...you won't be disappointed.
Can be dull at times. Can also be anal and vindictive. Seems to know his stuff but can be boring. He is however always willing to help.
Professor Adams is amazing! He is energenic, funny, and very knowledgeable. He made me interested in history and I never minded going to class! I wish he taught AMH 2020!

Adams made American History come alive. He was fantastic. His lectures are important, try not to miss them. An A is very possible as long as you are on top of things. Make friends with your TA, thats the most important part
He is a really great teacher. The lectures are so interesting, and an A is very possible.

He is an AMAZING lecturer.  I find myself wanting to go to class because he makes the material incredibly interesting...also has a real good sense of humor.  Tests aren't too bad: just read, go to lecture and discussion, and pay attention- you'll do great!
He is a great professor. He makes lecture interesting.
No Comments

Love Kane! He was always understanding and easy to reach outside of class, and also passionate and well-versed in what he taught. The class is reading heavy. I skimmed most of them. Weekly is question actually a lot of ur grade. Grading is subjective, and based on TA. The TA was Ryan Cousins was cool and funny, but don't expect a free 100 on them!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: No final exam, just an essay and a presentation. Few other essays but grading was free. Every week was a reading you could skim and you had to come up with a question for the discussion on Fridays. Reading was dense but you didn't need to know much. Lectures were kind of boring so I did work for other classes. He is passionate and talks a lot.
Really cares about this class. Not afraid to tell a joke. You can tell he really just likes talking about the class, but never in a way that makes you bored.

Becoming Black is absolutely one of the easier Quest 1 classes, considering the horror stories I've heard from others. The readings aren't anything crazy, but you are expected to submit thoughtful questions for discussions. Lectures are nothing super special, but you can tell Dr. Kane loves what he does.

Great class. Workload is super light. Prof is so willing to help his students and his passion for his work really shows. Wonderful readings. If you happen to not be able to do them then the lectures summarize them. There's only one exam and he's a super lenient grader. Otherwise, it's pretty much a paper, presentation, and small quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Abdoulaye's class was very easy, and he's definitely knowledgeable about what he teaches. I'd recommend Becoming Black to anyone looking for a very easy Quest 1, apart from the mandatory attendance.

The lectures didn't have much to do with the assignments we had to do, but attendance was mandatory. There are some short response papers and at the end of the semester there was a very open essay and group project. It seemed like if you did it, you would get a good grade. It is evident he cared though and was thoughtful during lectures.

Pretty chill class.  Decent amount of writing but nothing crazy.  Assignments took me about 2 hours to do max.  Attendance is mandatory but you can work on other work in class.  Discussions once a week but its chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Easy class, not a lot of work other than readings here and there, 3 150 word assignments, 3 500 word papers and one final project. Very easy to pass and get a good grade. If you are genuinely interested in this topic then would recommend. Attendance is 'mandatory' but you are given 4 personal days for the semester, after that your grade will drop.

I took Becoming Black as my Quest 1 class, and it was incredibly easy. Attendance is mandatory for a grade but to be honest you can do other work in the class. No exams, grades consist of readings and weekly questions, essays, and short writing commentary. There are experiential learning activities that require you to walk off campus sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Becoming Black as a Quest class. Pretty easy, definitely a good amount of assignments but if you do the bare minimum you will be fine. The TA is nice too so.

I took his quest class and it was very straightforward and interesting. I liked how I got five free absences from lectures so I could have some more flexibility if I needed to study for a test or something without my grade suffering. Also our TA was really great and grades were always done in a timely manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For Becoming Black, this class is super easy. He kinda just rambles during class so I get work from other classes doe during that time. Every Sunday there is a reading which I just skim then write 3 questions about it to "prove your read it" There is also a 1000 word essay then 4 experiential learning activity commentaries which are like 150 words.

This class was an elective on anthropology of religion. He is knowledgeable, but cannot teach well. His lectures are essentially just quotes from the textbooks. Attendance is taken by 5 unannounced pop quizzes. He is disorganized and puts grades in late. There are two papers, each 3 pages. Study hard for the midterm and final!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nicest human being on the planet! I'm not exactly the most organised person in the world so have a tendency to hand things in a tad late but he is very accommodating and understanding. The class itself is also very interesting. 20/10 would recommend to a friend.

Quizzes and discussions are due the day they open, so if you can't get to a computer you're out of luck. Set up a discussion board for course questions and then never responded to anybody. Tons of due dates were wrong online. I got an A but he told the university I did not complete the course and it took him forever to fix his mistake. Bad prof.

All Quizzes and Discussions open the day they are due. If you can't get to a computer that day you're screwed. HIS QUIZZES ARE TIMED 10 MINUTES FOR 10 QUESTIONS. He likes to do fill in the blank questions but only allows for two options to be correct, lower-case and upper-case, I made the word plural and got it marked wrong.

LOTS OF READING!5 books plus online articles.You have to read for the quizzes and tests.The quizzes and tests were all written,i think there was one MC for the final.You also have to write 1.5page essay for midterm and Final.Attendance and discussion questions every week are mandatory.7-8 page research paper.Nice guy though.Need to like ANTHRO

Very good professor as long as you are interested in what he is teaching. Do not take his class if you are looking for an Easy A because it is Anthro or African Studies. If you are interested in the topics, his class is very interesting and not too difficult to get an A or B in as long as you read the texts.

His lectures are full of tangents. He makes you go to class by enforcing a strict attendance policy, but class is a waste of time. You have to do the assigned reading if you hope to pass the tests. If you have read the tests are really easy. Very strict when it comes to make up for quizzes. You better have a documented reason.
Very interesting class. It opened my eyes on a lot of things. The teacher is very nice and respectful.

Super boring class! He does do attendance however you could just sign the sheet and leave(like i did). Lectures are useless, but sometimes he does tell you valuable information. He is nice though and gives out LOTS of extra credit opportunities!
He's a nice guy. He will help you out if you let him know you have a problem with the class.
This guy is totally hot.
hes really understanding when you have a problem and really wants you to do well in his class. not the clearest on everything but then again my attendance was less than great.
He's really nice. Attendance is important to do well. Hes also pretty understanding when you have a problem.
Great teacher.
I enjoyed his class. He knows a lot! Great discussions.
knows alot but fairly dull. Great with office hours, willing to help.

His classes were great - i took the freshman level and the africans abroad - he is very fair on his tests, lots of reading but with a little interest and work, you can get a good grade and you can talk it out wiht him too -

The class was somewhat boring, but Dr. Kane is a very nice, quiet man who is willing to help you when you're confused or have a problem. It's also pretty amusing when he says the wrong word for things, & he has a sense of humor about it :)

I couldn't understand a word this man was saying, so I ended up dropping the class for fear of failing a Freshman-level class. The material was very interesting, but be prepared for 90 people fighting over how the United States hate African (on a daily basis).

Actually, I found Dr. Kane's class to be rather enjoyable. The information was interesting and he exercised several techniques for presenting it. At the beginning of the semester, it was a bit trying to get past his accent. That was about the only setback to taking his class. Aside from that, everything was just peachy...
No Comments

Review for SUR3641 - survey computation class. Very fair grading and curves class. If you show up, show your work, and have understanding of the problem the grades will reflect that. Gives credit for coherent attempts. Fast grader and will provide extra time and feedback if needed. Homework is heavy and lots of spreadsheets. Good exp. overall.

Grading scale is so biased toward not getting an A from this course, as if, the aim is not to learn, but to get any grade less than A. Assignment rubrics are not in detail and you get your points deducted for something that was not asked in the assignment.
Overall, I do not recommend this course.

The professor is very knowledgeable and helpful. The course can be demanding at first, but once you advance in the course you just follow the system smoothly. The professor answers students' questions efficiently and quickly. I also learned GIS! I recommend taking this course with Dr. Amr.

His lectures consist of 3 PowerPoint slides that he scribbles all over while trying to write words with his mouse. Then he demands that the students jump through hoops to submit their work cleanly. This is the worst course I've ever taken, I would have dropped the class if it weren't required and he's the only one teaching it.

Great teacher! Very helpful.  He is a long distance teacher, at least for my course, and he was always available to take calls, emails, etc for GIS questions!  Slight accent, but better than almost all other professors at UF.
Is extremely thorough when teaching, takes an unnecessarily long time to explain things. Classes have alot of work but you can get help easily.

The one thing you gotta understand about Professor Rock, is he's very descriptive on each energy development module of the class. He teaches in a way that made us feel like he was guiding rather than lecturing, unlike many other professors in this department. 

He also uses a lot of Lord of the Rings memes and references 

10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved Rock!  He was clear about instructions and always took time from his day to help when we had questions.
Rock was the best TA I have ever had! During office hours he would always be available to help with readings and even met with me outside of class many times.

MCB3020 with Asghari was the best class I could've chosen to take alongside Orgo 1 in terms of manageability. I used Smokin Notes to study and I think it was CRUCIAL to my success. There's weekly homework and quizzes on McGraw-Hill which are busy work (imo they're not helpful, just something you have to complete). W/ extra credit and 90 is an A
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Asghari was a great professor! All the lectures are online, and he posts slides to accompany the videos. I used Smokin Notes to study for the exams, and it helped me do well and understand the content.

Honestly really loved the lectures and material in the class. I did not have SmokinNotes and did not feel that I needed it. The class is pretty similar to genetics in terms of content but just in less detail. I think it's obvious the professor cared about the class and he was quite knowledgable about the content.

The lecture content was interesting and well-presented.
Sometimes the lectures, readings, and exams were not very well connected.

Dr. Asghari uploads all of his material ahead of time which makes it helpful for studying ahead. The grading scale is also not too lecture heavy which makes the grading scale manageable, plus extra credit. I found the Smokin Notes study guide suggestions useful when studying for the exams.
Extremely caring professor with an extremely manageable class!! I would recommend to anyone to take for microbio. Stay on top of homeworks (completion) and quizzes and you will do great!

Super nice professor overall, and you could tell that he definitely cared about what he was teaching. His lecture videos were a bit confusing, but the study guides helped a lot. The exams were pretty straight forward, and I barely used SmokinNotes.
His exams were very fair and straight forward, everything you needed could be found in the notes from lectures or in the smokin notes packets.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Asgharis lectures can be a bit confusing but nonetheless says everything you need to know. He has multiple study guides and lecture reviews. He also gives extra credit that can help bring your grade up a couple of points. An A is definitely attainable as long as you put the work in. I did not use Smokin Notes either and was able to get an A.

Definitely recommend. Dr. A is very kind and really cares about his students. An A is a 90 and grades go up to 108%, so it's very attainable. His lecture content was a little unclear/confusing so I used Smokin Notes (fantastic btw). The McGraw homework (just a completion grade) is a lot harder than the actual exams, which were very straightforward.

This online version of MCB3020 with Dr. Asghari is SUPER chill. Assignments were super easy and the quizzes were super easy to complete. The tests were off of the lectures he gave off. If you listen well and understand what he's saying, then the tests will be easy. Exams are online and do have honor lock. Extra credit was given (+20 points).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was so kind and caring. 1-2 quick and easy assignments per week. Exams covered a lot of content but were very similar to practice exams and he goes over everything you need in the exam review. He grades based off 108% rather than 100, so it's easy to get an A. He even provides his personal phone number so you can reach him whenever you need.

The class is difficult as it covers a lot of material however there are a lot of resources such as quizlet and the study guides he creates where if you complete there is no reason you shouldn't do well. There was also 3% of extra credit that is easy to get with all quizzes and homeworks being open-note.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Asghari was a really good professor and super enthusiastic about the course. This class is mostly based on his video lectures so be prepared to watch and take notes. The best way to study for his exams are with his study guide and using smokin' notes to help you.

Make sure to watch all the lectures and take good notes! The professor can get sidetracked or repeat things, but most modules have three videos under an hour each, so they're easy to manage. Smokin' Notes is a great resource for practice questions and extra videos to clarify key concepts. It's super helpful for exams!

Asghari is a super nice prof. He is accessible, is passionate about what he's teaching, and encourages questions. His lectures are a bit confusing, so be ready to spend a lot of time taking notes on them. You don't NEED smokin' notes (isn't a terrible idea), just use the study guides he gives you (super important). Extra credit is available at end.

Test grades weigh heavy. There were 4 exams, none dropped, and they were NOTHING like the practice exams he gave you. He has lectures for you to watch but even watching everyone there were topics on the exam we did not cover. Super exam heavy and the department took away all extra credit. There were quizzes and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Asghari was kind and accessible, and the class was organized. However, the content itself was VERY unclear - lectures didn't cover 75% of tested material and doing the homework was impossible without the internet or careful reading of a big textbook. An A is attainable without studyedge, but I'd highly recommend it to make your life easier.

I took this class summer A so it was definitely rushed but very doable. I did not watch any lectures as I felt they were repetitive and long and I only studied smokin notes. He made the class out of 102% with the extra 2% being the homework/assignment section which helped. It was a lot of memorization because the exams were very specific.

Take this class in the summer if you can. He condenses everything. Most if not all the exam information is in the study guide, a handful of questions are directly from or reworded the practice he gives. His lectures tell you the information straight up that will be tested. VERY kind and caring about your well-being. Responds very quickly. Keep up!

I took MCB2000 over the Summer A semester so at times it often felt very rushed, however, the professor allowed optimal time to learn all the lecture information and multiple practice exams and assignments so I could understand the material. However, I suggest getting Smokin Notes for this class. It helped me summarize and learn the material.

Taken during summer A, so everything felt rushed. The lectures were extremely long to sit through, but highly recommended if you want a good grade on exams. Study guides provided that were helpful in preparing for exams! A lot of homework assigned every week as well, but not too difficult. Manage your time properly and getting an A is possible!

Long lectures, sometimes 8-10 hours of lectures per week. Homework was ridiculous, sometimes 200 questions for one assignment with several due every week. Readings took hours upon hours to complete. If you don't watch all his lectures, or spend ridiculous money on smokin notes, you absolutely will not pass this class.

Asghari was a great professor that's very reachable. Watch certain parts of his lectures a couple of times because it's easy to miss something, but the class is very manageable. Smokin Notes is a good resource because it provides the possible answers to the study guide and has flashcards that help you study whenever you get the chance.

Class was online. 3 lectures a week with an occasional McGraw Hill homework and quiz. Really know the study guides he posts, they very much reflect the exams. I used smokin notes study guide answers to study, and those were pretty representative of the exam questions!

Tbh I didn't watch a single lecture and just read the Smokin' Notes and went through the study guide and I was fine. There were never any surprises on his exams. There's also an insane amount of extra credit that can bump you by an entire letter grade. It's a pretty standard online bio class, so as long as you prepare you'll be fine.

Get smokin notes! it was really fast pace in summer a, recommend taking it in fall/spring. skim over his lectures and do the smoking notes. FOCUS ON THE STUDY GUIDE, someone questions are on the exam. 4 exam not cumulative. stay on top of content, and don't fall behind

Never watched a single lecture and only used Smokin Notes. He gives a lot of extra credit so it's not too difficult to get an A. His tests are specific but if you do the practice exams (smokin notes and also the practice exams the professor provides) you should be good. The study guide is also very helpful and covers everything on the exam.

It is evident that Professor Asghari has a deep passion for the subject matter and a wealth of knowledge to share. However, the heavy focus on tests and assessments seems to overshadow the true essence of learning. The quality of the recordings leaves much to be desired, making it challenging to follow allow along and grasp the concepts effectively

This class is not an easy A! Lectures can be hard to understand and he tests on very small details. His test includes lots of questions that are all of the above none or various other combinations. You will have to put a decent amount of time into this class.

The lectures and powerpoints were honestly useless. I've sat through some amazing lectures over the years, but his just ain't it. Avoid this class if you can; material is interesting, but the exams aren't squarely based on lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only grades are four exams, non-cumulative. Two extra credit quizzes per exam add up to 10 extra credit points to exam grade. There's like seven lectures per exam, don't bother reading the textbook. He gives a lot of hints as to what will be tested on the exam, do study guide and practice tests and you'll be fine. Easy A if you're a good studier!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lectures aren't great, use smokin' notes. complete the study guide- it's pretty much the exam. offers a good amount of extra credit (10% per exam) so it's easy to get through. graded only on exams- no hw or assignments other than extra credit. you won't interact with or hear from asghari much. he makes exams a bit difficult but it's doable.

Unintelligible professor who jumps around from topic to topic in lecture and is very vague when explaining what is/isn't important. Watch vids at 2x speed with CC, then use the textbook to fill out the study guides. DO ALL EXTRA CREDIT. There are only four exams and you're not allowed to review them. They are HARD if you don't fully prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Asghari is one of the most caring and approachable professors I've had, he is always accessible without the need of TAs, he gives A LOT of EC. Most of the grades are more tests but if u pay attention to lectures, it's an easy A, take good notes. He takes the time to explain concepts & apply real-world examples to them,doesn't rush his lectures.

Dr. Asghari is a great professor!! Complete the extra credit quizzes, take detailed notes and read the textbook (if you have time; just read over the topics you maybe unfamiliar with) you can earn an "A!" He does care about his students/replies in a timely manner any questions or concerns you may have. I wish he taught more graduate level courses!
Your grade in this course is solely based off of exams, so prepare accordingly. Yes, exams may be slightly specific but he gives generous extra credit. Just read questions carefully!
Just exams and extra credit and his lectures are so bad. Not impossible at all his exams are just super specific and from a question bank

As others have said, he jumps from one topic to another sometimes. Tho I took this class online so I assume lectures might have been recorded a while ago. Retaking the practice exams helped me reinforce what I learned, 2nd exam is the hardest imo. Extra credit makes up for the only grades being exams. Took notes during e/a lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were very mediocre - he seemed to bounce around a lot. Sounded like a nice guy but I don't think I learned much from his teaching. Exams were a bit annoying (question bank - repeated questions, some grammar was confusing), and the entire grade. He offered a lot of extra credit, which was nice (equivalent to ~10% per exam).

The class is just four exams and then extra credit quizzes. Pretty easy to get an A if you study for at least a few days. Exams are very specific but not impossible. Super easy class if you've already taken biochem. I got an A on the first exam, B on the second and Cs on the rest and ended with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a challenging course. Exam grades are the only grades. If you don't need a micro course, maybe skip it. Lots of studying and do the study guides! He's passionate about this course so that's a big plus! The course is actually pretty detailed and the material is great! You'll just need time to really study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Asghari is knowledgeable and a decent lecturer. I relied on watching the online lectures and using the practice exam as a study tool. I did all the extra credit quizzes and scored mid to low 80s on three out of four exams. He clearly explains what's important for exams in lectures. I didn't use Smokin' Notes nor did any optional homework.

Never watched his lectures. Smokin' Notes for everything. Read the study guide he provides and the answers Smokin' Notes has. Extra credit quizzes as it's the only other grade you have aside from the 4 exams he gives. Exam questions have weird wording and can trip you up. Practice exams and extra credit quizzes are through the textbook (McGraw).

He is very passionate about the topic. There are 7 lectures (50 minute) per exam and 4 exams total. He gives 10 points of extra credit per exam and usually curves them. If you take notes and pay attention to the exams it's really not hard you will be fine. Usually 2 days of studying is enough and everyone can get an A or high B.

I want to preface this rating by saying that I took this class online, so I have never met Dr. Asghari in person.  His lectrures were long and, honestly, not very interesting, but that could have just been the online format.  A full letter grade of extra credit is available, but his exams are ROUGH if you don't memorize everything.  I've had worse.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grading is very unfair on the case study in the end of the semester. It can lower your grade by the whole letter in the very end (beware). Questions on the quizzes have mistakes in them (not being proof read at all). Boring and long lectures. A lot of tests.

don't bother with the textbook, but do take the online practice exams. some questions end up on the exam. the extra credit quizzes buffer your grade a lot more than you would think. he also does curve the exams by a few points. his questions are kind of tricky, so be careful. use smokin notes' study guide and you're good to go.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Asghari is wonderful and the reason I am pursing a career in biology. He is passionate about the subject so the lectures are interesting. He gives a very useful study guide, if you do it and watch all the lectures that class is great and you learn a lot! I would take this class again if I could.

He was absolutely wonderful! The exams were easy if you read the textbook and paid attention to the lectures. They can be difficult if you don't prepare enough. He is willing to help any of his students and is very caring and understanding of personal situations. I wish I could take this class again!
Amazing professor and is always available if you need any help. His exams are very straightforward.
He gives so many extra credit quizzes! The lectures can be very tedious and arent really necessary if you use smokin notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lots of extra credit up to 10 per exam (4 exams). Easy class all you need to do is study and do the practice questions on mastering microbiology. Get Smokin notes if you have to but it is not necessary.

I honestly thought his class was really easy. I got about an 80-90 on the exams. My mistake: not doing all the extra quizzes. They are really easy and straight worded from textbook. I calculated it, and if I had done all the extra quizzes I would've gotten an A.

Professor Asghari is a really nice professor, he extended exam deadlines for the class, and provided extra credit opportunities. His exams were not too difficult but the formatting, ProctorU, and a few grammar mistakes did make them a bit challenging at times. Informative class that is not too difficult, just make sure to grind before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hands down my favorite professor at UF! I enjoyed his class and learned a lot during his thorough lectures . He gave LOADS of EC you could find the answers too on quizlet. Make sure you do his study guide and you are almost guaranteed to get an A on the exam which is very straightforward! He really cared and was always accessible on his phone. TAKE

Avoid this man at all costs. His lectures are from 2015 and are completely useless. Textbook reading doesn't help too. He does respond to emails fast, but when you ask for help, he tells you how bad you did compared to other students. I enjoyed the information from the class, but he made me hate learning it because he lectures and tests were awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is straightforward. I watched the lectures and made quizlets from the content and the questions asked on the study guide. For the exams, you need to know a bit of detail but it is all in the lectures. The textbook is not necessary at all to get an A. Make sure you do the extra credit and the practice exams because they help a lot.

Definitely watch the lectures and take good notes (Id write on the slides and add things hed write down/say). DO the extra credit quizzes, they help a lot! Try to fill out the whole study guide and review it a couple times. You can call/text him and he answers almost always. He tells you everything you need in lectures and explains things well.

I'm online and you will not pass if you do not watch all of the lectures. 4 exams 400 points and 9 Extra Credit Quizzes 45 points. I got an A just by watching the lectures and paying REALLY close attention plus all of the extra credit quizzes. Take DETAILED notes, do the readings, and I heard smokin notes helps A LOT with Asghari.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ashari was probably the worst professor I have ever had. I had a stomach ulcer and had to go to the hospital. He didn't care at all and made me take the exam anyways. He genuinely does not care about his students. Also without smokin' notes, there is no way you can get an A. I got a B cause I didn't use smokin' notes for 1/2 of the class.
HE IS THE WORSE TEACHER EVER. I HAD COVID AND HE DIDNT CARE ABOUT MY WELL-BEING AND MADE ME TAKE THE EXAM WHEN I WAS IN THE HOSPITAL IN ICU

Dr. Asghari does have some challenging exam questions but overall they are well-balanced and the class is not too difficult as long as you complete all of the lectures and assigned reading. He definitely tests on details he mentions out loud but that are not on the slides, so you must take notes on his oral lecturing, not only the slides.

I enjoyed this class and feel that Dr. Asghari did a great job of conveying all of the information. My main issue is that the test questions are truly worded in a misleading way, and multiple answers sometimes apply depending on how you read the question. I attended all lectured, did all reading, and took notes, and received a B in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: extra credit is everything!! lectures are very long and tough to get through but super useful in exams. DONT RELY ON SMOKIN NOTES! exams are based on random textbook info so make sure you do required readings. however, he is really nice, responds quickly to questions over email, and does extra credit quizzes that boost your grade so much :)

This professor sucks. His exams are crazy hard and his lectures don't teach the material well at all. Reading the powerpoint slides and textbook is useless. I had to get smokin notes to even score decent. His questions are so tricky and way more difficult than the practice exams. I had an A until the final then my grade dropped to a B bc of final
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really terrible class. Graded only on exams and extra credit, nothing else. Exams are extremely tricky, lots of questions in short time, and practice exams don't prepare you for it. Wrote tons of notes and still did terrible. if you can take ANY OTHER CLASS, do it. If you HAVE to take this class, prioritize lectures and smoking notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Asghari is a great professor! His tests are not hard but can be very tricky to see if you actually studied the material. Watch lectures, do the required readings & smoking notes & you'll be good. He also gives A LOT of extra credit. Word of advice: don't skip lectures and rely heavily on smoking notes, I made this mistake and it cost me my A

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR FOR GENETICS. She made this class 10x more difficult than it needed to be. First, she gives a final which not all professors do. The exams, except the final, were multiple choice AND short answer. The short answer was extremely difficult (ie. one question asked to draw transcription, like tf???). Very nice women though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment:
Read straight from the slides.  When I asked her to explain test questions she essentially restated what the answers were without adding any other information.
After publicly stating on canvas that the test scores were far worse than she wanted or expected, she just said "oh well" and submitted grades.  No curve, no extra credit, nothing.

Class wasn't difficult material wise, but it's a lot, and receiving an A is nearly impossible. Prepare to STUDY. LONG textbook. You need a 94 to obtain an A, which meant small wiggle room in this exam heavy class. Hated the group project; graded harshly by TAs, which I felt was unfair. This class caused me a lot of stress. But very nice professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely bad lecturer, she does not even seem interested in the topic she is teaching, and lectures for two hours in a monotone voice. I was not even going to bother writing a review but even after being a horrible professor and claiming that grade curving was up to her discretion, she would not give me .5% to bring my grade to an 80.

Here's the strat:

1. 10/20 lectures for 1% of the grade, up to you to allocate your time.
2. Have the self-discipline to make sure you understand the material
3. iClicker and past test questions make up the exams
4. Textbook and slides are more than enough to gauge what you need to know
5. 94% is an A but it's manageable
6. Do homework, it's light
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are 3 exams total, each of which are 20% of your overall grade. The average on 2 tests was a D and she refused to curve them. Lectures are not the best and tests focus on very small details. If you think you can memorize 500-600 slides of information per exam, you will do well. She also refused to bump grades up 0.1% because it's "unfair".

I know the other professor for this class has bad ratings, but take him instead of her. He asks more math questions. Her tests are very conceptual and be ready for 600 slides of material per test. She is a terrible lecturer. If you can spend half of your time on one class and memorize every slide then you will do alright.

Not a great lecturer to be honest but mangable. Her lecture slides will have all the material you need to do well on exams. Exams are multiple choice and written response. Homework is worth 30% of your grade and there is a group porject thats pretty chill. Easy to get near 100 on every homeowork assignment. Study well and show up to lecture

You can tell Professor Held is passionate about chemistry but she lacks organizational skills. She often gets off topic during class leading us to fall behind in the lectures. Tests are not too hard just complete the her assigned work. Do go over your tests to make sure there are no discrepancies because she can make mistakes grading.

This class was more difficult than I imagined it to be but once you get used to the class it becomes easier to understand. The lectures were fine but sometimes very unhelpful when the professor rushes through. But if you put in effort you will get the grade you want

Overall, take this class for what it is. It is most people's first chemistry class at a University level. There are a fair amount of assignments and the class only meets twice a week, so you need to study on your own time. Learning from the lectures is hard, so go to office hours. This class was hard work, but I do feel prepared for CHM2045.

Abby seems like a really nice person, but lectures could be disorganized and rushed at times. Sometimes topics seemed confusing, but office hours help a lot! Lectures were also recorded and posted so you could go back to rewatch them which was very helpful! If you understand the homework and problem sets, I think you will do fine on the exams.

Abigail as a person is great and caring, she gave me an extension when I had family issues. You can get an A in this class if you attend office hours and attend lectures. The material itself is hard just like any chemistry course so be prepared to study. There are 3 exams and a final. Problem sets and homework are all due by each exam day.

Made the material a lot more confusing than it needed to be and I didn't feel well-prepared for the exams. Honestly if you have the option definitely take the online version for CHM 1025, I've heard it's much easier.

The way she explains certain topics can make things more confusing as you're first learning the topic but over time, its alright. The software she uses to write notes on lectures is hard to read once they post online after. Would recommend going to the lectures and doing problem sets when they released instead of all at once.

They pretty much rushed through the slides and gave you aleks and problems sets to do for homework. For an intro to chem class the material was really difficult (strongly recomend having taken chem in high school before taking this class). I pretty much had to get study edge which costed me extra money bc their material wasn" enough
Concepts are not too difficult if you have a prior chemistry background but the exams are very tricky. The homework, practice problems, and lectures do not prepare you for the exams.

Not a great lecturer. Made a lot of mistakes while teaching and most of the time made concepts seem more confusing than they actually were. Provides many practice problems before exam, however, many of the exam questions are way harder than the practice problems.

I absolutely loved Professor Held! She is so passionate about teaching and it truly shows! She wants all her students to succeed plus she's funny! Furthermore, her problem sets and homework quizzes are a big help in understanding the material covered. Do them as you go through each lecture. Don't leave it for the last minute! Highly recommend Held!

This course was definitely tough. Exams are weighted 60% of your grade but the lowest is dropped by the average of the 3 exams. Aleks is used about 1/week in a summer course. Overall a lot of work but take advantage of redoing the problem sets and homework quizzes.

Professor Held is a nice person but not a great professor. Her homework is really difficult, especially for a 2 credit intro class. She does not have the best way of explaining concepts and overall just makes the class more difficult than needed. Her exams are really hard but fair. She is accessible outside the class. I would not take her again.

She was very good at teaching during her lectures. Going to lectures was key in order to do well on exams. Also, it is important to do well overall on homework quizzes and problem sets because they all add up to a good chunk of your grade. Start assignments early because there is always a lot due right before the exam.

Overall good teacher. Classes are very lecture-heavy with simple slides of definitions and practice problems. At least she isn't boring to listen to and can be funny at times. Office hours are great! Wish I had started going sooner.

She is a very likable person, but class is awful. All exam grades were very low. Lectures were so unorganized. Every exam had topics not covered. Test questions built on each other so getting one thing wrong cause you to get the next 5 wrong.Tests on small details instead of big pictures.Homework is nothing like the test material. Take another prof

No point in going to lectures, they make it more confusing. Talks in circles and has no idea if we can apply material. Makes plenty of mistakes and lectures are chaotic. Be prepared to buy study edge. Assignments are on multiple platforms, but content does not go together. On every exam, there was something brand new never taught in class.

Her lectures were very casual and I liked that they included practice problems. This class was a basic review of chem, so I didn't use Study Edge. I took notes off her lectures & did pretty well on exams. Do the optional worksheets!! She literally pulls questions from them. It was just annoying when she had the TA lecture for some days.

I thought this class was pretty challenging considering it is only an intro level chem class. Professor Held was very caring but often times I got confused during her lectures. Truthfully study edge is what got me to fully understand the material.
She was nice and a relatively good teacher. Lectures were pretty easy to understand and studying and practice is important for the exams. Not too bad!

Don't let CHM1025 stress you out if you took high school chem, it's mostly a review. Ms. Held helped me refresh my chem knowledge and learn a few new topics. The ALEKS is pretty annoying, especially if you do bad on the initial test and the following knowledge checks. Her exams aren't killer, the time window is two hours for around 30-30 questions.

I only took honors chem in HS before this class and it was alright. There arent any practice tests she gives out before exams so you just have to figure out a way to study for the 3 exams and cumulative final. HW was mostly ALEKS (takes multiple hours), practice sets on each lecture and optional worksheets (due before each exam). Overall: mid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: In reading some of the other reviews, I think some people direct their disdain for chemistry towards Ms. Held. Ms. Helds lectures were educational and efficient. She emphasizes important points well and provides multiple avenues to understand the material. She is relatable and was great at controlling a lecture hall of a hundred or more kids.

It's not a hard class but it was Held's first time teaching it which made it a little unorganized. There is ALEK homework but that's not her fault that UF's fault. One of the relatable professors I've had and office hours with her was extremely helpful.

Approachable and kind. She did great, considering it was her first time teaching. People are blaming her for how bad ALEKS is, but they dont realize that she only uses it since UF requires it. She provides good resources such as practice problems, and her office hours are a great resource. The students giving a low rating are just irresponsible

She was just okay. I dont think I got too much homework, but learning from lectures were hard. Sometimes it was just the TA and it was hard to hear at times. The homework (ALEKS) was a waste of time. She didnt give out any practice exams to study from so for the 4 exams it was hard to study.

ALEKS isn't helpful, and her homework doesn't match up well with her exams. she offers no extra credit and has a hard time explaining things in more depth. This was her first time teaching this course though, and with more experience, I think she'll improve. super kind, and understanding in correspondences.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class is not treated like an Introduction course, it is extremely unorganized and you are learning one thing from the lectures, and a complete different topic on ALEKS. There are 0 resources for students to study for the exam, besides some illegible lecture slides. I would not recommend if you are trying to build strong foundations in Chem.

Grad students should NOT be professors for an intro to class... period. Horrible teacher, she would say one thing, erase the work then say forget about that I did it wrong then do something new. You will have tons of ALEKS to do and NOTHING on that is on the exams.
