reviews.comment: He did a great job teaching MATLAB and showing students how to problem solve and think outside of the box. Office hours are always available and the TA's will be a tremendous help with any trouble you're having. The exams are fair and the final project is fun and rewarding. I loved the class.

Professor Ahlgren is intelligent and caring. APK2100C, however, is extremely demanding. Exam questions are so obscure. Even after days of studying, I would still score Cs and Ds on exams. The only way I got a B in the class is by pouring myself into the extra credit. If you're hoping for an A — good luck!!!

Doctor Alhgren is a great professor. Her lecture videos are crucial to obtaining a good exam grade, but she presents the material well and highlights the areas in the lectures from which she generates the questions. She provided up to 5 points of extra credit per exam and up to 10 points of extra credit for engagement. Highly recommend her course.

Dr. A is a fantastic professor who really cares about student success. The exams are challenging, but with diligent studying, using unstuck study, and taking advantage of extra credit, an A is very doable.

Honestly, this class is extremely difficult. Be prepared to dedicate hours of studying because her exams are extremely detailed. She is a nice professors and has many opportunities to redeem yourself so take advantage of resources. Lectures exams can be dreadful but lab exams are manageable. Dont underestimate this class if you want a passing grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: An absolute gem of a professor. Although Physiology is expected to be a tough class, Dr. A gives some of the best quality education UF has to offer.

Doctor Ahglren is an amazing lecturer and genuinely cares about her students. She will give you every opportunity possible and breaks things down so well! She really knows her stuff and is super passionate about teaching! Her exams are extremely difficult and requires you to know your stuff, but a good grade is possible if you put the work in:).

Truly cares about her students and will give every opportunity for you to succeed. Despite this, her tests are pretty difficult. Everything is extremely specific so you have to know your stuff. She is great at answering any questions you may have and really knows her stuff. She is an amazing lecturer and makes tons of jokes the whole class:).

Doc A is my favorite professor at UF. It is obvious she cares is much about her students and the material she teaches. 
The extra credit is incredibly generous. The exams are tricky so its important to focus on the questions on the slides and the learning objectives.

Doc A is amazing. She explains the material so clearly, and attendance is important to doing well on lecture exams. 7 exams is a lot for a class, but the 2 lab exams were very straightforward. The lecture exams are manageable, but they can be very involved. There is a TON of extra credit. I did not have to go to the final and still got an A.

This truly has been one of my favorite classes at UF. It is very manageable to get an A. With that being said, her midterm exams are difficult and require a lot of studying but you do not need to do great on them. They are not worth a lot and she gives TONS of extra credit. Make sure to use the help center and do well on the lab exams.

TAKE DR. A!!!! She is a great professor and knows so much about this subject. She wants you to succeed in this class and provides many extra credit points. Her exams are pretty tough, just study hard for the lab exams and the final and you'll be golden.

Dr. Ahlgren is an amazing professor! Super dedicated to teaching anatomy and incredibly caring. However make no mistake her exams are BRUTAL. Teaches lectures very quickly and teaches a LOT, so much so it is difficult to learn everything, then on exams the most obscure questions are asked. DO THE BINGO CARD as it will save you later down the road.

Dr. Ahlgren is funny, helpful, and a caring person. However, her class is INSANELY hard. I have aced most of my classes at UF, but this course was my first major hiccup. I would take her again because I do think that you can get a good grade if you are strategic with it. Be sure to utilize ALL extra credit, and use lab exams as a grade boost.

I love her as a person, but not so much as a professor. She knows her stuff well & was in the group me & was easily accessible outside of class. Exams are REALLY hard. Go to lab center often and review models constantly. DO WELL ON THE LAB EXAMS AND START ON THE EXTRA CREDIT (w/stamps) EARLY. I would've ended with a C if it wasn't for extra credit.

Doc. A is one of the best professors I've ever had! She's so passionate about teaching anatomy, I actually switched my major to APK. The exams are detailed, but there are no trick questions, and everything she tests you on comes only from her lectures (textbook is available, but not required). Ahlgren is so sweet and caring, HIGHLY recommend!

One of the best lecturers I've had at UF, super accesible and caring too. Very challenging class but definitely doable if you put in the work. Exams aren't exactly tricky but you have to really master the content to do well.

Doc A is an amazing professor for anatomy. She is very passionate about it and loves teaching her students, which truly shows. Her exams are hard so you really have to study but she provides a lot of opportunity to make it up. Also lots of extra credit. I highly recommend her!

Doc. A is incredible. There were honestly a ton of exams (7 total): four lecture, two lab, and one final. Lab exams are extremely easy if you study the material. Lecture exams are difficult, but if you study you will do fine. She is such an amazing person, and she makes learning the material fun. Take this if you're at all interested in anatomy!

Ahlgren is a great professor, she's funny, caring but her exams are way too difficult. Once you fail an exam its impossible to bring your grade back to what it was before. She does offer lots of extra credit which is helpful but other than that this class was difficult for just a level 100 class. One of the hardest classes I've taken. Avoid!

This was the hardest class I have taken at UF.Although she is a nice professor, she makes her 4 Lecture exams extremely hard (majority of your grade) and there are constant exams every week, 2 LAB exam & Final (culminative). Her test are application based,and not based off her lectures.Also, she phrases all her exam questions weird. Stay away.
Dr. Ahlgren is a great person and professor. Her exams are challenging because it relies on application but the lab exams and final exams serve as an opportunity to bring your grade up.

Dr. Ahlgren is very passionate. The exams however are quite difficult, so be prepared to really study. The questions ask intricate details and really make you think. Be prepared to study really hard and just as hard for the final exam. One of the hardest classes I have had at UF.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Ahlgren was one of the hardest but most comfortable professors I've had. I've aced physiology, immunology,however, I had to not only study hard for her class but change my dynamic and be able to adapt. Her online class provides video lectures in which she explains the content very nicely; however, it is necessary to listen for specific details!

although her lecture exams are pretty tough, the lab exams are quite easy to memorize for and the homeworks really cushion your grade! on top of that, she gives a generous amount of extra credit and is always available to help during office hours, so overall a wonderful professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I am a graduating senior and Dr. Ahlgren is hands down the most dedicated and caring professor I've ever had. Are her exams hard? Yes. Is this a difficult weed-out class? Yes. If you want to have the best possible experience regardless of these factors, you need to take it with Dr. Ahlgren. If you put in the work, you will do well.
Although her exams are tough, Dr. Ahlgren is a wonderful professor. Her passion is obvious and admirable, I would sign up for her course before anyone else's.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I went into this class not knowing anything about it and did not take anatomy first. It was MUCH harder than I expected and a lot more work too. She is a great lecturer and I learned so much, but her exams are tricky and focus on small details, which I did not like. Study super hard and you should be fine. Also there was no A- grade offered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She gives amazing lectures and Im sure her class is fantastic for APK, however, for BSC - her exams are horrible. They ask trivial/minute details that are nearly irrelevant. She tests you on so much information to distill it all down into 35 trivia question. Her questions are poorly written and extremely vague. First time not getting an A.

The sweetest and most passionate person I have met to date. She cares for her students and it is obvious. Amazing lectures that really are beneficial for learning, and more importantly understanding, the material. Does not test on anything outside of lectures, so while the book helps, it is not necessary to read. You can get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her exam questions are deceptive and focused on trivial details. Had a 4.0 before this class- never studied this hard, yet I'm doing poorly (though way above the average) Also, she was "busy" so she didn't even upload BSC lectures for the last unit, just APK ones that were very basic and useless. Everyone I've talked to regrets taking BSC with her.

Dr. A is the best professor I have taken at UF. She is super passionate about anatomy and that made me love the subject even more. She is super detailed with her explanations, but don't be fooled she likes to give detailed tests as well. 100% recommend taking her!!

Dr Ahlgren is AMAZING. She is caring, funny, intelligent and passionate about what she teaches. By all means this is NOT an easy class and she expects you as a pre-med/pre-health student to obviouslywork hard for your grade. Reading the textbook and lecture slides are most helpful for exams, not smokin notes in my opinion. Learned a lot from Dr. A!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. You do have to study to get a good grade, however, her tests are fair and help students to retain the information that they are being taught. She is super funny and kind, and you are positive she cares about her students and job deeply. I'm hoping I can get her for physiology!

Dr. Ahlgren is amazing! I have had the pleasure of having her for both anatomy and physiology! It's true that her exams expect you to thoroughly understand the material but you learn SO much, from an extremely intelligent and passionate person! Utilize the snowball study method and you'll do fine! She is also hilarious and I'll miss all her stories

Doc A is awesome even though her classes are very hard. I've taken a few of her courses and if you put in the effort and attend class, you will be fine. Hard exams are balanced by homework and extra credit. She like you to remember specifics so make sure you memorize graphs, charts, numbers, categories. Passionate and friendly in office hours.

Dr. Ahlgren is by far the best professor I've had at UF. She is very intelligent and so passionate about what she teaches. The lecture exams are tough but if you study a lot you can do well on them. The lab exams help your grade a lot as they are straight memorizing. Take her if you can!!

Dr. Ahlgren is an amazing lecturer. I struggled on the exams because they are very tough and have to know your information. Probably an easier A in other courses but I learned a lot from Doc A. Exams are extremely difficult but not weighted highly. The lab exams will carry your grade so study! It is possible to get a B if you do well besides exams.

If it weren't for the fact that exams are only worth 25%, this would be an incredibly difficult class. Points from labs and collaborative exams make it a lot more manageable to get a good grade. Dr. Ahlgren is a solid professor who you can tell truly has a passion for what she does. She also offers several extra credit opportunities for students.

Dr. Ahlgren is, by far, the BEST professor at UF. She is so enthusiastic, is always smiling and excited to teach, and really cares about the wellbeing of her students. Do not underestimate her class though. While she is an amazing professor, the material can be difficult to grasp and requires a decent amount of studying, but is so worth it. :)

Dr. A is, by far, the best lecturer I've ever had the pleasure of taking. Her enthusiasm for teaching is unparalleled. So personable! Her exams are not that bad. Lecture exams (2) are relatively low stakes (60 pts) while lab exams (2) are more important (100 pts). In my opinion, the lab practicals are easier anyway; mostly identifying the models.

One of the best professors I have ever had and I learned more in her class than most of my undergrad. Exams are difficult, but if you go to lecture, take notes, and supplement with the textbook, it's easy to pass. I would recommend her for any class she teaches, she's amazing!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Ahlgren really cares about her students and is so excited to teach them. Her energy in class makes learning enjoyable, which is lacking in a lot of classes. Her exams are tough, but you can still manage to get As if you put in the effort. You will learn so much in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: She is absolutely amazing ! Her exams are a bit tough but she lectures so well that you shouldn't have a reason to do bad. Usually exam averages are either a C or B but she offers lots of extra credit and also gives out HW that helps your grade a ton. probably the best professor i have had by far. HIGHLY RECOMMEND ! YOU LEARN SO MUCH FROM HER !!
Her exams are meant to trick you and are almost all questions that student are usually confused or get wrong.

Loved her! This professor tested my critical thinking but she was always amazing at office hours and she holds a lot of them. She is tough but you will come out with a very good basic medical understanding. It made nursing school seem like a breeze in some senses. I took both anatomy and physiology with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved her!!! She is the most amazing professor, and the best professor that I have had at UF!!! Amazing lecturer and really interesting material! I would definitely recommend reading the textbook and taking some notes on the chapter that she is lecturing about in class during the time that she is teaching that material, it helped me a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Doc A was the best professor I've ever taken at UF after 4 years. Super good at her job, cares about the material, and gives fantastic lectures. Her exams are tough but that's why HW and lab exams boost the grade. They're also super fair so getting an A is doable. Definitely recommend her.

GREAT lecturer but the hardest tests I have taken at UF so far. Although you can bring up your grade with lab and homework, if it werent for that I would be failing so bad. she is such a great teacher but the tests are super hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ahlgren is probably the best professor I've ever had. She cares a lot about the students and the course material. Her exams are hard, but incredibly fair. If you read and keep up with the material, it's not bad at all.

If you're taking this class alongside another science, be warned, this and it's inclusive lab is a lot of material and extra work. I took it with orgo2 and found myself drowning in work. Ahlgren is AWESOME though, LOVE HER. She makes it so fun and interesting. You get what you put in for sure. Taking her physiology next semester!

She is one of the best lecturers I have ever had at UF, and also one of the most enthusiastic and caring. She makes you work for your grade, but if you go to lecture, take notes, and follow her advice on studying, you will be more than prepared for the exams. Homework and extra credit are definite grade boosters, so make sure to do those properly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Terrific lecturer and always available to answer questions or explain concepts. I took this online, so completing the dissection portion of the lab was challenging but worth the effort

Really well done lectures. Really hard tests. She expects alot because she knows that she's good at teaching. The labratory components of this class are annoying, but will end up bringing up your grade. I learned so much, and I'm glad I took her and this class.

Doc A was absolutely awesome. Even though the lectures were online she was always stimulating the subject matter through her enthusiasm, anecdotes, and humor. Her grading criteria is extraordinary clear and as long as you keep up with the content and make sure to go over the learning objectives you will thoroughly enjoy the class and get the A.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had! So caring and enthusiastic about the subject. Very helpful and attentive to her students. Extremely hard class though- I studied weeks in advance and would average C's on exams. HW and lab saves ur grade! Great class, u learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had. It's an extremely tough class but I would not have wanted to take it with any other teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Her enthusiasm for the material makes for great lectures but they totally aren't necessary to get an A in the course. Smokin notes does a great job of teaching you the material for her exams. Her exams are ridiculously hard but the homework, extra credit points, and lab exams inflate the grade. She is seriously the best!!

Dr. Ahlgren is a great professor. The class itself is extremely challenging, but her lectures are very informative and she makes it clear what she expects you to now for the exams. The exams are mostly all application, so you really have to know the material well. Utilize her virtual office hours and the TAs. Make sure you READ the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Ahlgren is the best teacher I've had at UF so far. She is extremely knowledgeable and her lectures are interesting. If you are in a major where knowing anatomy/physiology is important (ie. APK), definitely take this class. You will learn a lot. Her exams are challenging and make you apply your knowledge, which is a useful tool to have.
If you want to be successful in this field you MUST take her for Anatomy.

Highlight of my undergard. She's not "evil" & exams are not "impossible" if you take the NECESSARY TIME to study. You can't memorize/regurgitate, it's APPLICATION. To any pre-health people: take this class if you want to actually LEARN! She is MORE than helpful if you just ASK. DON'T be afraid to ask questions IN CLASS, and GO TO OFFICE HOURS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor. Exams are extremely difficult, and I heard the online version is easier, but Dr. A keeps class entertaining and fun.

Dr. Ahlgren is a fantastic lecturer and really cares about her students. If you like to skip class or aren't motivated to study, then don't take this class because you will probably fail. If you are truly interested in the material and want to remember what you learn to help you in future classes then this is the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: If you're pursuing a career in health, this is the prof. to inspire you to learn to dig deeper and think critically. She gives you a foundation of information and expects you to expand on it. She's an awesome teacher and is ready to help (as are her TA's). Just apply yourself. Those who complain just weren't giving this course their all!
Tests do not at all reflect the material taught or what is in the textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best Professor I have had at the University of Florida. Extremely intelligent and articulate. Knows the human body inside and out. Tests are difficult and application heavy. You WILL learn physiology well if you pay attention. Passionate and enthuastic about the subject. You can tell she loves to teach and cares about her students.

Amazing Anatomy lecturer! She speaks really fast and there is a lot of info you need to know for her test (very tricky and specific qs). I loved this class and think it is worth taking w/ her because she cares about the success of her students. Clear about grading and there is HW to buffer a little if you have a bad exam grade.

I used to love anatomy but now I hate it. Anatomy is a fun course but she makes it so unnecessarily hard especially for a 2000 level course. The test is nothing at all like the homework so its basically pointless. There are no study guides so you basically have no clue whats on the exam but just know it will be hard VERY hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her class is made to challenge you but you will benefit SO much from it. Her teaching methods are made so you can retain the info long term & they work. Her enthusiasm for the subject, for teaching, and for her students is encouraging & makes the difficult course easier to do. Take lots of notes during her lecture, go to open lab, & snowball study!

Doc A is so great at what she does. You can tell she loves teaching. She makes confusing things seem so much less confusing. You do have to put in a lot of work for this class, but it's totally worth it because you'll remember it long-term and enjoy her lectures immensely.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: -Textbook: is useful when referencing her lectures or if you miss a key point during lecture, but it's best to try and write down almost everything from lecture. (Some of the info in the textbook is extensive and unnecessary) -Lecture exams: study EVERYDAY (or as often as possible); follow her "Snowball" tip -You may not pass EVERY exam (DONT QUIT)

Dr. A is an amazing professor. Although she talks fast, she is an entertaining lecturer who enjoys teaching. She is always willing to help, and has fair grading policies. However, this is NOT an easy A class. You have to study hard and keep up with the notes. This is a challenging but worthwhile professor to take!

Dr. A's lectures are amazing. She's extremely passionate about the material and gives meaningful examples of how the material is applicable. Her exams are difficult because they are application based. She doesn't wants students to just regurgitate the information since there is no value in this. Highly recommend taking this professor. She's a gem

I feel like she's super passionate about her field but this really doesn't translate to her teaching... I feel like she is unwilling to help if you have questions and frequently makes you feel stupid for asking. She also assigns homework that has nothing to do with tests, so it's basically busy work that should really be prepping you for exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is an AMAZING lecturer, one of the best professors I have had so far here. But her exams are extremely hard. Going to office hours and study lab helps A LOT though. I took her live class, but I highly recommend taking the web class, as she talks very quickly and you need to catch everything she says as it could be an exam question.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very hard exams, but a very good teacher. You will learn so much. The exams aren't work that much so you will still pass even if you fail an exam (most people hate the first exam).

One of the best professors that I had at UF! She is very passionate about anatomy. Her grading system makes the whole class doable so that even if you don't do well in the exams; you still have hw and the lab portion to bring it up. I love going to her lectures and it seems that she has a story for everything :) You will truly learn a lot from her!
reviews.rating_tags: CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took her "flipped" class (all lectures online, class meetings once a week) and I loved it! It's a clever way of teaching imo. The only drawback is she makes it mandatory to attend the group meetings (if you miss class you get %'s  of your WHOLE grade deducted. Yea.) Her lectures were very clear+thorough, make sure you watch them all!

Doc A is an amazing professor! Her classes cover a lot of material and the tests are tough but you learn A TON! She's funny, interesting to listen to, and genuinely cares about her students! Take her classes whenever you can and you'll be much better off for the future!

Great professor. Took her online Anatomy, students were struggling with online lab due to simply not being good at cutting things! No Problem! Doc A completely revamped the grading criteria mid semester, making it doable. Very flexible, helpful, passionate, Take her class.

Ahlgren is an awesome teacher and is super helpful during office hours. however, her exams are very tough and tricky ; they usually focus on small, tiny details in the lecture so you need to know the material well. Have to study a lot for this class, but lab and hw grades will bring your grade way up.

Had her for anatomy and physiology. Doc A is very enthusiastic about the subject, which made lectures fun to watch. However, her tests are pretty difficult because they are all applied questions based on small details. The homework and lab scores help your grade tremendously, so do those and study hard and you'll make it out with a B or higher.

Dr. Ahlgren is very enthusiastic while lecturing and in her office hours. The only negative thing about her that I've noticed is that she gets upset when being asked a question during lecture. Sometimes she would respond in a passive aggressive manner and make the student feel bad about asking in the first place. I doubt this was intentional though

Dr. Ahlgren is by far my favorite teacher at UF! She is so incredibly knowledgeable and a great lecturer. I had her online so you need a bit of discipline to complete her videos on time, but REALLY WRITE DOWN EVERYTHING SHE SAYS! Her exams are all application so make sure to understand the material. She is fantastic and I would highly recommend her

Dr. A is one of the BEST professors I've had at UF. She is just so incredibly passionate about the material, super accessible during officehoursappts, and is SO amazingly knowledgeable. The physiology lab portion and hwk were very helpful in balancing your grade. I'm a stickler for details and application, which is why I loved this class so much!
Do not take. Very strict and makes courses unnecessarily hard
Dr. A was a great teacher, her exams is set up to apply the knowledge so cramming will not do you justice for exams. Lab is awesome sauce ! Josh Crowe is one of the BEST GTA's ever.

Dr. Ahlgren was incredible! By far my favorite teacher so far at UF! She was extremely helpful in her office hours and her lectures kept me so engaged that I would look forward to watching them. I'd take this class online since she does go fast and it's very helpful to stop and pause her lectures.

Ahlgren is an amazing lecturer who is incredibly knowledgable in human anatomy. She's very passionate about anatomy & her students' success! I found her lecture exams EXTREMELY difficult, but I also took this course for gen-ed, & have no interest in a medical career. With the lab portion, hw, and extra credit, your grade can be saved I promise!

Dr. Ahlgren was an amazing professor! She is incredibly clear and helpful! Don't get me wrong, though, this class will take a good bit of effort. Grading is very fair. Tests are application based and make you think. As long as you put the effort in, go to class, and get help when you need it, you should be fine for a good grade.
GO TO CLASS AND TAKE NOTES ON WHAT SHE SAYS! know her lecture notes and what she says really well. Don't read the book

Best professor ever. Not difficult if you try despite what other's say. If you actually show up and do what she says, you won't have any problems. She cares a lot about her students too. I've had her for multiple classes and she's simply amazing.

Incredible teacher, but HARDEST exams I have ever encountered. I would study weeks in advance, I came to class every day, and STILL did terrible on the exams. I am an extremely hard worker, I go to UF so I obviously have a brain, but WOW were her exams hard. But her lectures are amazing.

Freshmen BEWARE!! You must be very disciplined to take this course. The labs require a lot of memorization and you WILL fail if you do not dedicate at least 20 minutes to being in lab every day. Yes, every day. So if you have a problem with that then you are too immature for this course. Do yourself a favor and take it as a junior.

She is fantastic both as a person and lecturer.  I saw her every OH and she is so inviting.  She also writes LOR's from scratch.  I took this course in six weeks while volunteering at 3 clinics, and tutoring some students on a weekly basis. got an A. Sit down and learn. Lets be honest this isn't orgo, this class isn't weedout, its RELEVANT.

Dr. Ahlgren has taught me more in 6 weeks (took it over Summer B) than any other science professor has taught me in a whole semester. If you really listen to her lectures and take good notes, you'll be fine. Grab a coffee, pay attention. Go to study hours if needed, she's so sweet. Go to study lab hours. Don't cram. Got a high A. Love Dr. Ahlgren.

Dr. A is probably the best professor I've ever had at UF. She always has tons of energy, and it shows through her teaching style. This class is HARD - you could definitely get a better grade with less work with another professor, but if you love anatomy, I'd recommend taking Dr. A. Tests are tricky but you get used to them.

First off, yes I got a C+ in the class. However, that had nothing to do with Dr. A. She is an amazing lecturer and I actually enjoyed going to class. Her test are extremely difficult. They arn't impossible if you're properly prepared. Just dont slack off if you do good on the first one. Oh and Study for the lab practical, it's the easiest part!
I would highly recommend purchasing the Smokin' Notes in addition to attending class everyday. Not a good class to take with other difficult classes.

Dr. Ahlgren is an amazing prof, one of the best I've had at UF. When she says her exams are based only on her notes, she means it. Don't overstudy by reading the textbook, unless something is unclear. Her exam questions are straight from her notes/lectures. REALLY try to take the class online, that way you can rewatch and rewind the lectures.

Had her for both Anatomy and Physio. Awesome professor. I recommend taking her online since the exam questions are based off lecture and you can watch the videos as many times as you want. It’s not impossible to get an A her courses if you put in the effort. Rewatch the lectures as many times as possible and start studying a week or so in advance.

I loved Dr. Ahlgren, she knows what she is talking about and lectures very well.  However, the tests are difficult, I spent 3 straight days studying for each exam.  It's not impossible, but it requires a lot of effort.

Dr. Ahlgren is a very knowledgeable woman but her class is so difficult! Be prepared to put a lot of time and effort in her class. Getting an A is extremely difficult. Her tests are so hard and she doesn't curve them. Go to lab and maintain your lab exam grades because thats the only okay/doable part of this course. Study everyday for this class.

My absolute favorite teacher at UF so far! She is a great teacher although lazy students might tell you otherwise. Its not an easy class but if you go to lectures and office hours you'll do just fine. Her exams usually always have a handful of tricky questions, but just make sure you understand all of the notes.

I guess if you like her for her personailty she's great. Her syllabus has the required book readings that don't cover what she's really testing. She goes over the broad points of each chapter. If you're taking hard science classes along with this, you don't really want to take this class. It's simple if you're still doing easy A classes with it.

While the course is very tough, Dr. A makes it so interesting. She gets so excited about the material that she sometimes stops to marvel at it. Her excitement is contagious. I have never had a professor who's attitude and spirit was so overwhelmingly positive. Don't take this class for an easy A but take it if you want to learn something cool.

Very, very difficult to get an A in this class. Do not take Anatomy or Physiology with Ahlgren if you care about your GPA. Going to class is a waste of time, and reading the 'required' textbook is a waste of time. Her exams are either convoluted questions from the notes, or completely random. She thinks a "70 average" is ideal...
NOT an easy class but very DOABLE. She is approachable and willing to help anyone that shows up in her office. She does use in-class  references on the exam so GO TO CLASS.
Very difficult teacher. Exams were very hard and some material presented in class was not on exams. Very APPLIED human anatomy.

She is a wonderful teacher, she tells stories to illustrate points and REALLY knows the subject.  It does take effort to do well on the exams, but it definitely isn't impossible.  She is very nice and enthusiastic. I plan on taking her for anatomy as well (:

Dr. Ahlgren is an amazing professor. She knows Anatomy like the back of her hand and she knows how to communicate that information to her students.  That being said, she talks extremely fast because all of the information that is given; I recommend typing every single word that she says and making flash cards out of everything.

Two words guys... OFFICE. HOURS. I love Dr. A. I took her for both anatomy and physio, but it took me a while to figure out her exams. Office hours are the best advice I can give! She goes over things time and time again, and you begin to understand her logic if you go. Understanding her logic and way of explaining things is KEY to her exams!

Study her lectures (record it with your iphone/computer/recorder and play back. Then study those notes solely (smoking notes = unnecessary), you WILL pass and depending on how good of notes you take can get an A very easily. She buffers by adding homework + labs/quiz = 200/540. She does not curve, but tophat 5 pts extra credit. No minus grades.

One of the best professors ive had. Possibly my favorite. Definitely forces one to learn the material and the class gets you stressed out but in the end it is very possible to get an A. Exams are a big part of the class but other points can be earned to offset a bad grade. Tough but very helpful just get to know her. If youre pre-health take her.

My biggest advice for anyone taking the class is to record her lectures and GO TO CLASS. Everything you need to know for her exams come strictly from what she discusses in lecture. Recordings are helpful because sometimes she speaks fast. Before exams, listen to recordings. It refreshes the material and makes things more bearable.

She is one of my favorite teachers at UF! Her Physiology class was challenging but if you put the work in, you could definitely get an A. Your grade isn't based solely on exams, you also have lab, HW, and quiz grades to help raise your grade. I definitely recommend Dr. Ahlgren, she's so enthusiastic about physiology and always available to help!

Difficult but definitely doable. Attendance is not mandatory but you should go. The lecture notes are fill in the blank, and the tests are based solely on the lectures (w/ some information you'd only get in lecture). During my semester she randomly took attendance twice and gave 2 points extra credit each time to whoever attended.

She is really passionate and energetic for a 7:25 am class. They lectures are interesting but exams are harder than they need be.  Study really far in advanced and you can pull of a decent grade. A lot of stress with lab exams on top of lecture exams. She is helpful when you go see her but usually there are a lot of people.

SHE IS ONE OF THE BEST TEACHERS I HAVE EVR HAD AT UF. She is a phenomenal lecturer and is super passionate about the subject matter. For exams, study her lecture slides and you will get an A. Go to office hours because she is really helpful. She gives a lot of chances to boost your grade such as homework and lab work. Hard work=A!

Not an easy class. She is extremely knowledgable and helps a lot during office hours, but I personally thinks makes this class harder than it needs to be. Got a B on the first test and D's on the next 3 and I studied A LOT. To me her tests were really hard. I ended up with a B due to lab, 4 extra credit points, and hw. Extremely stressful.

Really great teacher! She's extremely enthusiastic about physiology and is very helpful during her office hours. The exams are hard but they are very true to the material and require a deep understanding of the material. Best teacher I've had so far at Uf

I LOVE DR. AHLGREN!!! I thought I'd hate having the "hard" anatomy teacher, but she's so enthusiastic and helpful that it made going to class at 8:30am bearable. :) STUDY HER SLIDES for lecture exams, and the lab exam grade will save your grade so go to study lab!!

Ahlgren is a very good teacher. I did studied quite a bit for her exams, but I thought her questions were always completely fair. I would read the chapters (except the stuff she didn't go over) for clarity, and then do quizzes/labelling online on the website that's required for the course, and read my notes a few times. I really enjoyed her class.

Very good professor but the exams are very difficult. Most professors will ask you direct questions but Dr. Ahlgren really makes you apply what you know when taking the exams. Provides plenty of resources like study lab, and office hours . Smokinnotes help a great deal if you decide to purchase them
Her exams are a little tricky, but if you go to class and study her lecture notes they're not too bad! She is very enthusiastic about the subject and explains things very well, overall a great class!

She is very excited to teach and will help anyone. Yes her exams are tricky and you really have to read it well but they are doable. You need to go to the class and going to her office hours is always helpful. I would recommend her to anyone that was willing to work hard because that is something you will have to do. She is wonderful!!

I was nervous to take this class because of all the comments, but it is do-able! Go to class, and take detailed notes of what she says. I recommend studying almost a week prior to the exam. She's one of the teachers who claims they dont want to trick us...but she does. You also have many more point opportunities from lab, webassign, and key errors.

Very intelligent professor. Her class is a bit difficult but manageable. She does not do minus grades nor does she round any grades. She doesn't offer extra credit but she does add points if there was a exam key error. SmokinNotes were helpful. Attend class! It helps!! Grade based on exams, labs, participation, and homeworks. An A is attainable!

I can only say good things about Doc A. She really loves what she does and it shows. All you have to do is go to class and really listen and write down everything she says because her tests are word for word from her notes and what comes out of her mouth. I learned so much about the human body, and she really sparked my interest in the subject.

I had her for both APK2100 and 2105. Like previous comments you have to keep up with her material all the time, every day. She is so intelligent and very helpful if you go see her during her office hours. The book helps only a little for an extra resource but all of her test questions come straight from her notes. Going to class helps a lot too!

Truly unintelligent teacher. Extremely insecure, always picks an early morning class and attempts to sabotage those who don't come to class (LoL my PowErpoiNts Got missIng woRDs im so clEVer)-syndrome. Tests aren't difficult material-wise but suffer from being vague and poorly worded. So, you can't ace exams unless you get lucky.

She is a very brilliant professor who loves teaching. GO TO CLASS and take detailed notes. Use the textbook only for clarification. She is extremely helpful, go to her office hours!! I got an A. You will not get one if you start studying 4 days before the exam. The exams are very tricky, so know your stuff and keep up with studying from the start!
Great lecturer! Attendance is not mandatory but highly recommended (fill in the blank notes). A lot of information and memorization.

Dr. A is a great teacher and I learned so much from taking this class more so than any I have taken at UF. Her tests are pretty difficult though and you'll need to study a couple of weeks in advance. DO NOT slack off in this class

This class was pretty easy....Didn't use smokin notes...didn't use the book..just went to class and listened..studied off her notes..and have an A in the class just by getting high and takin the exams!

LOVED her class! Doc A is a great teacher, and she keeps it interesting! She tends to cover material REALLY quickly, though, and her tests are tricky, so I always had to rely on other materials (Smokin' Notes) to get what I had missed because she was talking so fast.

INCREDIBLE PROFESSOR!! Her tests are tricky but are not at all impossible. I have made 95% on each exam thus far without even opening the textbook. She is very easy to talk to and answers any question during her office hours.

She's really nice about answering questions but evil about exams. The labs are pretty easy but you lose all your points during the lecture exams. She wants the class average to be a "C". This is her first semester teaching physiology, so maybe her technique will change over time.

Best lecturer by far at UF- Great enthusiasm. Knows her info very well & is super helpful. Exams are NOT impossible, you just have to study for them and be prepared. Lots of info to memorize but it can be done since it is super interesting. I got an A so it's not impossible

Her tests are not impossible, contrary to popular belief. You just have to work a little harder for this class because of the amount of material and memorization involved. However, by no means is the material over the top difficult and impossible to learn. She is very passionate about anatomy and physiology and is very willing to help when asked

Really only passed this class because i got A's on both lab exams. Couldn't get higher than a 75 on her exams because the questions are so hard. Basically have to memorize the notes and go to class because she adds extra stuff and even still the exams are dang near impossible.

I didn't mind the 7:25 class period but her tests were HORRIBLE!!!!! She was perfectly nice and really helpful as far as study hours go but i honestly studied so much and only got a C+. Take Dobson if you can

She is a nice person and entertaining. I did learn a lot in her class, but her test were IMPOSSIBLE! I honestly felt that all of my studying was not enough, and I studied! I feel like her tests are for practicing physicians. I wouldn't take her if you are not the type of person that likes to study. I had to retake the class.

She was a GREAT teacher! Very entertaining and passionate about the subject. I do have to admit that her tests were definitely tricky, but if you study her lecture notes and read the book you should be fine! Overall I enjoyed taking her class!

Ended up with a B. Not a bad class. Some of the questions on the exam consists of answer choices such as: all of the above, none of the above, 2 of the above. Overall, her exams are not hard, but only if you study her notes AND textbook. She gave 26 extra credit points this semester, so that is pretty damn generous.

ABSOLUTELY DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER!! Her tests are tricky and unnecessarily difficult. Also, nothing is worse then listening to her drone on at 7:25 in the morning. Save yourself the trouble and take Tillman.. this class is horrible.

Not so easy class, if you enjoy memorization and TRICKY exam, this is the class for you. Not so hard to get a B with all the extra credit. Her lectures are engaging ,yet not helpful when you get the exam. Overall had to work a lot and not get the grade I wanted.

The best professor I have had at UF. She makes lectures enjoyable through her humor and stories. Print out her lecture notes, read the book for clarity, and STUDY HER POWERPOINTS. The tests are not DIFFICULT, they are just TRICKY. You must pay attention to the answer choices. I absolutely loved this class and would definitely recommend this profess

This class was one of the easiest science classes I've taken at UF. A lot of people don't like Ahlgren and say she's unfair, but of course, they're just too lazy to open their books. I read every single chapter, and studied her notes (which have extra info not covered  in the book) and now have 91%. Final should be good as well, just study!

Doc A. is a good teacher. Her tests are hard but doable. Just memorize her lecture notes and pay attention to the answer choices on her tests! I averaged a 75 on tests. Go to class and make sure you listen and take notes on her ppt slides. I advise reading the book as well bc it helps. Lab exams are easy just go to the study lab. Id take her again!

She is extremely difficult.  Take another teacher unless you just enjoy studying your butt off.  The other people who says she gives extra credit must have caught her on a good day because our test averages were barely passing and she attributes the fault to the students.  she doesn't give enough information to make things as hard as she enjoys to.

It's not so bad. For her exams: Just study the book along with her notes. She's able to keep the class awake especially at 7:25am. You ask questions, and she answers. Lab exams are also easy too. Go to study lab once or twice a week before each exam and you'll do good. You gotta work for this class, but it will be worth it at the end.

The class was tough like all college level anatomy courses would be. Ahlgren made the class interesting and fun (even at 7:25am!!!!) She is EXTREMELY helpful and nice if you go to her office hours. I recommend taking Ahlgren.

She is not as bad as everyone makes her out to be. Her exams are hard, but not impossible. When you take her exams, READ the questions CAREFULLY. An "A" or a "B" can be doable if you study from the book and notes. She gives extra credit. I zone in and out during her lectures, but as long as you study the material, you are fine!!
Don't take her I have never done sooo poorly on a college test than I have done in her class clearly there is something wrong with her tests!!

Good teacher but Do Not Take this class unless you want to work your butt off. Class was interesting and she kept my attention but her exams are impossible. I read everyone's warnings on here but thought I could do it. I was wrong. listen to people and take another professor! her exams are tricky and she knows it.
She's a hard, but good teacher. She tells you what she wants you to know and focus on, so if you go to class you will do fine.

Dr. A knows everything there is to know about anatomy. But on the contrary she is not a good professor.  The concepts she put in her tests are very difficult and the test questions she puts are not simply memorization. She is not good at explaining the concepts she puts on her exams.

Dr. A is definitely enthusiastic about anatomy, and by the end I really came to like it too. However, her exams were tough-extremely detailed. To do well you literally must MEMORIZE her slides and go to class to get the notes on things not explicitly stated in her ppts. Simply understanding concepts AREN'T enough. Ended w/ an A but it was rough!

Her tests may be quite difficult, she balances that out with her generosity. By that, I mean she gives out many extra credit points. Also, she emphasizes on the first day that the class is about APPLIED anatomy. Critical thinking is involved, which helps you to learn the material effectively and not just memorize. Great teacher to get to know too!

Covers immense amount of info each lecture & expects you to have thorough background knowledge. Her exams are EXTREMELY difficult & she is aware of that. She picks the tiniest details from lectures and creates an in depth, tricky question. Shes knowledgeable but shes yet to learn how to transfer her knowledge to her students. TAKE TILLMAN.

Took her class last spring, have to agree with everyone who says she's ridiculously difficult.  Comes off like she'll be easy, but the tests are the work of the Devil.  Had to retake her class with Tillman this semester--TAKE IT WITH TILLMAN!  He is an awesome and fair teacher, far better than Ahlgren.

Every one complaining obviously didn't try. All you have to do is memorize the slides and go to class where she'll hint to what's on the test. I got a B+ because I barely studied for the final but for the other tests I just crammed the night before. HER TESTS ARE FAIR AND UNDERGRAD APPROPRIATE! If you got into UF you can handle this class.

I started out this class excited and thinking an A would definitely be attainable. WRONG! Dr. A is very narcissistic and uncaring when it comes to students' concerns. When the class average on exams dropped to a 66% she blamed the class and took no responsibility that her exam was too advanced.  Save yourself and take Tillman.

I actually thought Dr.A was awesome! I really enjoyed the class and I actually didn't mind it being at 1st period because she kept my attention. Her test are pretty fair and it is possible to get an A if you work for it. In the end we even got a butt load of free points!
Extremely hard. Tests do not reflex on lectures and don't compare with other anatomy teacher. Do not take her.

She's a nice professor and comes off as very sweet but her tests are TERROR. She asks so many unclear questions that makes you second-guess what the answer is and she feels as if those questions are acceptable for the undergraduate level. The LAB actually saved me in this class or else I would have gotten my worst grade ever.

I don't know where all the ratings went, there were many of them yesterday when I looked.  Extremely difficult tests, unrelated to lecture material at times.  Treats students like recalcitrant children instead of adults who are trying to learn something.  Ruined many careers.  Class avg on one test was 66%, she wouldn't curve.  Super early class.

Extremely difficult; I might not pass the class, and I got a 98% A in high school anatomy and loved it.  Tests are ridiculous.  If she actually tested on the stuff she lectured about they might be managable.  No curve, super difficult test questions, doesn't listen to students and makes you feel really stupid for doing bad.  3rd test avg only 66%!!

On a positive note, Ahlgren is very enthusiastic about the course and is able to keep my attention (which is a must for 7:25am). However, she is a new teacher who thinks she needs to "prove" herself by making overly difficult, uncurved tests. She is unreceptive to feedback, almost as if she assumes students are taking advantage of her inexperience.

seemed easy at first, but got harder as the semester went on; tests are difficult and a lot of times do not pertain to lecture notes; not willing to listen to students' opinions; if you're absent you may miss some info left out in notes since she never updates them or informs those who missed class about the mistakes

Ahlgren was a horrible teacher. She seemed nice at first but don't be fooled. Her tests are hard and she doesnt help much if you go to her office hours or email her. She wont even answer questions the last ten minutes of a test. I would definitely recommend taking Tillman or even Siders.

I'm with the other person I thought this class was going to be easy at first because she seemed like an easy going lady. But she is a new teacher so it seems like she hasn't quite gotten the hand of it yet. I got an 94% on the first exam and then on the next two I recieved a C I would suggest that anyone wanting to take Anatomy  should take Tillman

At first I thought this class was going to be easy, but when it got to the 3rd exam I knew I would have to drop the class. The class average on the 3rd exam was 66%! Since she just got her PhD and its her first year teaching, I think she tries to make tests with questions that are graduate level. Make sure you study really hard or take Tillman!

Dr Leslie's Lectures are fun and extremely engaging; however, her grading criteria is not clear, which ended up costing me my grade in the long run. She would mark points off for criteria explicitly listed in the rubric, but often the expectations were too vague. Even after completing extra credit, I ended the class with a B+.

Cannot recommend Dr. Leslie enough, seriously the most interesting class and her lectures are wonderful. She is an absolute wonder to have as a professor, and super accessible if you have questions. If you are thinking about taking her, please do!

If you respect your time do not take this class because Dr. Leslie will not. Readings can exceed 150 pages a week and then won't even be referenced during the long droning lectures but will feature on exams. The guidelines are inconsistent and unclear and Dr. Leslie is more then content to hold you accountable for her mistakes and risk your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Dr. Leslie. She is so passionate about her class, always smiling, and has a positive attitude. She does a lot of class discussions and assigns readings, but they are really interesting if you pay attention. You get out what you put into this class. Easy A, but I learned a ton.

He truly cares. Passionate. He extended deadlines, the work was really not difficult. In-class Canvas quizzes every 1-2 weeks, discussion post, some writing assignments, in class paper midterm exam, and a group final project. The midterm is mainly from the textbook. He gives study guides. Small discussion style class. So understanding and funny.

Dr. Agoes was very disrespectful and I felt talked down to when asking for help. He was extremely unresponsive to emails. I was very frustrated all semester taking his course. I normally see the best in everyone, and maybe he was going through something, but I have never felt more disrespected by a professor before. My classmates felt the same way.

He is kind and takes time to get to know his students. There is minimal work, and instructions are clear. The midterm was kinda random and took a bit of studying, but it wasn't too bad overall. Attendance is mandatory, and the class is discussion based. Discussions got oddly political a few times, which was weird, but overall I would take it again.
Dr. Agoes is an amazing professor, definitely one of my top 3 here at UF. I highly recommend him for any communications course as he's extremely caring of his students.

Dr. Agoes is one of the best profs I have had at UF. He cares about the success of his students and is extremely accessible for help. Extremely understanding! Clear syllabus and grading structure. Grades fair and quick. 10/10 would take another class with Dr. Agoes. Really remarkable as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy class in itself, has very clear deadlines and very manageable work load. My only complaint is that he doesn't grade papers to a 100 because "no paper is ever 100 because that would mean its a perfect paper" so if you get a B on any of the papers then the max you can achieve is an A-. Overall not bad, but just don't slip up on a paper.

I would 10/10 take a course with Dr. Agoes again. He is such an easy grader and really makes it difficult to fail his class. He is very strict on deadlines though, so just make sure you have your work in on time and don't ask for any extensions and you should be good to go.

The absolute best professor I've ever had. She made learning a new language so easy to digest and understand. She's also an incredible person, and was accessible outside of class for help and questions. Not a tough grader, and explains where you messed up. The absolute kindest professor ever. Will be taking her again and I recommend you do, too!

1 exam and 4 quizzes. Multiple extra credit opportunities. You create a research project that you do throughout the semester. Don't have to show up to class for most lectures, but there are a few classes where you must be in class. Overall, great prof, cares about her students, passionate about the topic, and not a harsh grader by any means.

This class sucks. If you want an easy Quest 2 DON'T take this one. All of the exams are very specific and difficult. The class focuses highly specific nutrition science stuff for the first half and the second is designing a research project. You barely learn about Europe. Would never take it again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An amazing and kind professor. She makes the class interesting with fun facts. Quizzes on each chapter, in class. 1 exam and 1 final project. I think she was a bit tough on grading for some assignments but then not as tough with the ones that cost a lot of points. Take notes! I think this class is easy to get an A, just put in effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kowalewska is a phenomenal professor! Do not listen to other reviewers, as she has been nothing but incredible both times I have taken a course with her. She cares about her students, is easily accessible, offers a variety of assignments that are not very difficult, and the lectures are genuinely helpful. I cannot recommend her highly enough!

Lektor Kowalewska is an amazing professor who cares for teaching and the polish language and culture. The class is hard, not because she makes it but because learning a language, especially Polish is very hard. If you are in anyway interested in learning Polish or taking any of her classes. Do it, you wont regret it.

This professor was very kind, sometimes funny, and overall a good teacher. Lectures are kind of boring but she can make it fun from time to time. There's a quiz every week that's on like 30 pages of reading + maps so get ready for that. You only really need to read the summaries at the end of the chapter to prep. Every week there's discussions too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this professor and felt that she was very approachable outside of class. She was also very passionate about the topic and tried to make it very enjoyable for the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Kowalewska is an awesome teacher, and after having her for POL1130 I was convinced to take Europe's food. She is a very personable professor and will match the energy and effort you give her. Her classes are designed to be easily digested. She always asks for advice on how to make the classes better for future students and the current class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She graded on very few things, so one bad grade would greatly impact your final grade. The lectures are soooooo boring. There were lots of quizzes based on the readings that asked very specific questions which became both difficult and frustrating.

Dr. Kowalewska is a super kind professor, do not be swayed by old reviews. She is super accommodating and is the reason I have continued so far into learning the Polish language. Do your work and you'll be fine.

I took her Food Production and Sustainability course in the Spring. We had a very small class which was really nice because there was a lot of participation/interaction. The content was a bit all over the place but that's partially because she was open to changing the content based on our interests. She was a very kind lady with many fun stories.
Boring lectures and did not help when we lost a student from our group. Said student dropped the class and took much of the group work with him at the last minute and she did not give us any leeway.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: not an easy class but you can still get an A without too much work... just keep up with the assignments and get Smokin'Notes to study for the exams.

Not a difficult class - IB classes in high school were much harder. Grading criteria is SO clear - only one assignment I missed a point on. Space out work because they're a decent amount of reading and lectures. Don't skip anything early on because weights of each category (quiz/exam/assignment) might change later. Easy A if you don't slack.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've taken on UF online and I've taken 5. Unless you ready to really ready to work your ass off for a decent grade. SKIP THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: AVOID FOS2001. It had a reputation as an easy elective, but was reformulated into something else entirely . Frustratingly complicated assignments with confusing instructions. Weekly quizzes with a very short time limit, and the exams are administered with ProctorU, an invasive proctoring program. Do NOT take as an elective, you have been warned!!

Horrible! Lots of reading very long lectures. Like other reviews say lots of typos in the exam questions! Had to work real hard for the grade received. Exams are closed book closed notes and through proctor u! The syllabus quiz was even proctored and closed book for that! This is not an easy class!

Weekly quizzes only worth 3 points and all the answers are online. However, you do have to read and watch the lectures for the exams. A "study guide"/key concepts list is provided prior to every exams. There are a few assignments worth about 28 points each. They aren't too complicated and a clear rubric is provided. Overall, easy A.
Lots of busy work, but super easy A if you just do the work. Tests are Proctor U now!

Make sure to do all the assignments because there is no drop. The second exam was very specific and made difficult so make sure to study well even though it is an easy A. The professor is very helpful and caring but the syllabus is strictly followed. She responds to concerns from students.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Nice prof. Responds to student's concerns. Make sure to do the assignments early and follow syllabus. There are no drops, so make sure to submit everything or else you may lose your grade. Second day submission 50% off.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved this class! Although her accent is a little difficult to understand at times and certain instructions can be confusing I found the corse to be very interesting and fairly simple if you're actually interested in nutrition. Just do the work on time and send her an email if you're confused about anything and she will get back to you

Please... please. Dont take this class with this professor. You are on an island for the entire class. You are expected to be able to read 60+ pages and at least 3 hours of video lectures for a timed (3 min- 3 qs) weekly quiz. Take age of dinosaurs or something else. The professor makes the class unlikable. STAY AWAY!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class can be fun but the exams are ridiculous. Some of the things on there were never even taught. There is multiple typos and the exams are created to trick you with wording. The professor seems nice but the way she speaks to students makes them feel dumb. Lectures are painfully long, assignments are irrelevant and unnecessarily long. AVOID!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is not the joke class it used to be, it is simply now what one would expect from an actual class, it is not hard it is just not bs. Assignments are not hard but they are lengthy and a nuisance. Do the assignments and get smokin notes for an A. I do not recommend as a joke sci gen ed. As a STEM major, probably easiest sci that I will take

Distrust and micromanagement. The exams are ridiculous; they are riddled with typos and incoherent. If you know the material and study your tail off, there are  still obstacles to spite you. The assignments are irrelevant with scattered and time-consuming instructions. There is no reason for any of this. She does offer some bonus points though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: It's honestly not an easy class, however it is passable if you put in the work. The second exam is harder than any exam I've ever taken so far at UF. Nonetheless, she is very understanding, nice, and open to hearing your concerns. You'll definitely need the book since 95% of the questions on the exams will come from them, and not her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is unnecessarily hard. The lectures barely cover the subject and even if you do all the readings assigned, it doesn't matter because the exams are so specific. I regret taking this class. DONT TAKE! ITS NOT WORTH IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: As I am getting close to completing her course, I came to the conclusion:  1. Lecture videos are painful to watch. 2. Quizzes cover modules from the textbook almost every time 3. Exams are tricky, and sometimes seem that were written by someone who wants the student to fail. Mostly, they are not based on her textbook, rather on a mix of books.

Assignment instructions were a mess and never clear. Class always posted roughly 25 questions per assignment to which she and TAs would say: read instrcutions carefully but would not rephrase instructions. Also, when tech difficulties arose, absolutely no sympathy. UF's tech dept is slow and students have limited to get stuff done. Avoid this prof.

This class supposedly isn't what it used to be, but it was still very easy. I never purchased the textbook and only used the smokin notes for the exams and still did fine. The activities were weird (i.e. dissolving a multivitamin in vinegar while filming it), but easy nonetheless. She curved the class very generously, but only at the end.

Beware of proctor U.  Class is easy enough to get an A if you follow the grading criteria and submit the work on time.  Exams are a breeze if you listen to the lectures posted once online and then read through smoking notes a couple of times.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Curriculum changed this semester, it's not the easy class everyone used to talk about. Assignments have virtually nothing to do with the modules. Exams are passable just through the study guides she gives. Curved both exams heavily at the end of the semester.

I took it because everyone said it was easy & it totally changed this semester. There are so many readings & lectures. I watched & read EVERYTHING & still ended with a B, even bought Smoking Notes. The homework is absolutely pointless and doesn't even relate to readings or lectures so you learn nothing from doing them. Do NOT take for GenED

I took this class because I needed an biological science credit for my degree. This class was far from easy. It is essentially a bio/chemistry class in one. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU ARE LOOKING FOR AN EASY GRADE. It is not that type of class. The professor does not communicate well and expects far too much in such little time(summer B). Horrid

Do not take this class.  I received an A, but it was a lot of hard work for a Gen Ed class...  I thought this class was going to be an easy A, but it was the absolute worst.  So many useless assignments and very broad study guides.  Do not take this class.

THIS CLASS IN NOT THE SAME MAN'S FOOD ANYMORE. There are many lectures, time consuming assignments, and very detailed exams. Kowalewska is a very nice lady but has a thick accent and can be hard to understand. Her lectures are very long, stretched out, and boring. Possible to get a good grade but a lot of time and energy for a simple gen ed.

Summer was the first semester that this class changed and it is no longer an "easy" class. The class if now very difficult with a lot of assignments that have nothing to do with the exams. You are given a "study guide" but it's not helpful at all. This is not a class I would suggest you take especially during a summer semester.

Lots of homework that have nothing to do with the material that students are tested on. Study guides are rather broad whereas the tests themselves are very detailed/specific, so don't rely on on the guides either. Beware of ProctorU. If you're just looking to satisfy a gen ed credit, I strongly recommend looking elsewhere.

Easy class? Not anymore. You have to read a lot of pages and watch a lot of videos. Just took my first exam and it was really nit picky. I watched and read everything but ended up getting a D on my first exam. Memorize details and scientific terms.

Lots of readings 200+ pgs. 15 modules with at most an hour of videos and an hour and a half of reading. Skipping videos are not suggested because some are not covered in the book. Gives extra credit that's already provided to you. Exam is multiple choice and T/F with detailed questions. You have to work for a B unless you pick things up quickly.

Summer B was the first time this course changed.  It is no longer an easy class.  I took this class because I wanted to take a break from my other classes, but I am ending up doing more work for this class than my other two classes combined.
Agata really cares about success. She forms the class to be super simple and ready to go. Never watched a lecture the entire term. Gives extra credit. I hate science and got an A. ( :
The easiest class I've ever taken. Didn't even do the last assignment and I still ended with an A.
The class was super easy, there wasn't much contact with the teacher unless there was a problem with the online site.
Great professor. You have to study, but she's a fair grader and her tests aren't too bad. She posts all of her powerpoint online, but she's a great lecturer and worth going to class for.

Very sweet lady, welcome to help students. Really focuses on making sure the students understand. Powerpoints are all online and if you memorize them, you should do fine in her class. Couple assignments, but they were essentially grade boosters. Exams are fair game.

Great professor that kept the class very easy. Only four essays, all under 1000 words, and the weekly discussion of 250 words, which was pretty easy. One group project that doesn't take long. Very easy to work with and has a 24-hour grace period for submitting assignments late but has accepted later assignments and still gave me 100%.

Great Professor, don't have one negative thing to say about her. Very accessible outside of class and very understanding when I missed an assignment (still got full points). Very simple ppt group project. Discussion post and quiz once a week. Short papers about once a month. Whole class was organized well and assignments were well outlined.

Took this as my 6,000 word class and it was easy! Probably 1 or 2 hours of work per week depending on that week's assignment. If you took APHG in high school, it will be a breeze. There's discussion posts weekly, a few bigger papers (~1,000), other random assignments, and a group project. Didn't feel like a burden at all and prof was very nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of work, but very easy

Don't take this class over a short summer session. There is a lot of work due every week and I felt I could not keep up even with how lenient she is with on time. 2 discussion posts, 2 annotations, and an essay/ other writing intensive assignment is common per week. Taking 6 credits and working 40 hours a week with this class is not possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: A queen. Seems intimidating at first but she allows a 24-hour grade period and does not grade harshly. She is very accommodating and kind. I definitely recommend the professor and course!

This class is not as easy as previous comments suggested. The textbook is dull and you have to comment while reading to receive credit. There are weekly 250 word discussion posts, 4 papers with MLA formatting, and a group project. The grading is fair and the content is easy, just don't expect to sleepwalk through this class and get an A.

I took this course for the 6000 word writing requirement and thought it was very organized and easy to follow. Textbook annotations due each week along with a discussion on those readings. There are three small papers (600-800 word minimum), a final paper, and a group project. She takes off minimal points as long as you follow the rubric given.

I took this class since I needed 6,000 word credit class. However, I found that the # of words we had to write was WAY more than 6,000. We had large projects (1,000+ word essays, presentations, etc) and discussions due each Monday. They were relatively easy/she is not a tough grader, but I would not recommend to anyone just looking for word credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: would take again!

If you need words, take this class. Super easy A. About 1 - 2 hrs of work a week max. I took this class while taking other science intense courses and it was very manageable. Easy content as well, don't need any prior knowledge. Don't doubt it haha just take it.
Easy writing class. About 2 hours of work a week. If you do the assignments (which aren't hard) you'll get an A. No need to worry about 'syntax' and all the other bs of writing classes.

While she doesn't grade anything until the last minute, she is a really fair grader. I received a very high A in this class without much stress. Turn in your assignments on-time, but don't expect them to be graded until the very end of the semester.
It's a writing intensive class so lots of papers, but love her! She's super chill and a very fair grader. Highly recommend taking her class. Easy A if you do all your work.

Such a nice professor who genuinely cares about her students. The class is content-heavy but so manageable. Minimal homework besides studying for exams which are straightforward. Would definitely recommend this class and professor

Loved the professor and class. There is a lot of material, but the exams are straightforward, and she gives extra credit opportunities. Super interesting topics, and she is very passionate about what she teaches. I would 100% take this class again

Great professor. Extra credit opportunities for tests, in class test review, no final exam (final project that is broken down throughout the semester). You can tell she is passionate about teaching and loves the subject. Easy A class.
I would highly recommend this professor. The class itself is content heavy so it is fast-paced but absolutely manageable. Interesting topics and exams are very straightforward.

She knows what she is talking about and delivers the material in a concise and targeted way that makes it extremely digestible. Never read the textbook, just participated in class. Her problem sets are not difficult at all and she is also a very lenient grader and wants her students to succeed. I would take her class again!

Professor Agarwal is a very nice lady and is super passionate about economics, but she is a terrible teacher. I attended every single lecture in fear of getting behind and 90% of the time I had no idea what she was talking about ever. She goes way too fast so it's incredibly difficult to take organized notes or understand anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There's nothing necessarily wrong with Professor Agarwal, but I won't take her classes ever again. Her lectures were boring and hard to understand, so I stopped attending at some point and just read the textbooks. Now don't get me wrong, she is a nice person. If you go to her office hours, she will try to be as helpful as she can.

I attended every lecture in the beginning and could barely understand her.  Additionally, she treated us like high schoolers and would call us out for being on our phones/talking.  Mid semester, I stopped attending class because I quite honestly found it pointless.  I got the same score on my second exam as I did on the first, proving my point.

Professor Agarwal genuinely care about the success of her students, and want them to learn as much as possible in her class. However, her lectures are very confusing and it is periodically difficult to understand her. I feel like she over-complicates an already complicated subject. She is very accommodating in grading as she curves the grades.

This class was way too hard for a quest class. There were many miscommunications between the professor and the TA and I was confused on expectations for this class for pretty much the entire semester. Its possible to get an A but save yourself the stress of this class.
