Dr. Agunbiade is very friendly and the TA, Nicholas Martin, is awesome. There are academic review papers that need to be read and write a reflection every week. You also need to work as a group to study one chosen disease over the semester as in many projects. It was an interesting class and not as hard as I thought. It's a good Quest 2 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and avoid it if you can. Assignment/exam instructions are unclear and misleading; too many different assignment types, quantity also too heavy for such a technical course. TA was also not responsive at all and I didn't receive a single bit of feedback all semester.

This class was not only an overall waste of time, it was a difficult waste of time. Exams make up over half your grade, while at the same time there are weekly quizzes and discussions. There is is no extra credit.
If you are looking for useful information, don't bother. The class consists mainly of factoids and hasn't been updated since 2013.
AVOID. There's no resting time at all in this class. She cancels her office hours during breaks but doesn't cancel any assignments. She's out of touch as to the workload we get from other classes.

Agunbiade was such a sweetheart, with a passion for entomology. I'm a crim/psych major, I could care less, but she tried her best to make the content interesting. However, semester started off easy, slowly got harder and more disorganized. 4 proctored exams (HARD), review paper once a week, 4 group projects, 2-3 papers.

Exams are on Honorlock, mostly free response, and graded very harshly. The professor takes awhile to get back to students and assigns quizzes/discussions over holidays. Also, the grading scale is harsh for this course and the exams are very difficult. I did not enjoy my experience at all. Please do not take this class, 10/10 would not recommend.

Don't take this class, its gotten so much harder. Exams used to be open note and now they're not. Long response, and goes super specific into articles that she links. Doesn't even attend office hours. Took a month to grade 2nd exam, which could've made the withdrawal deadline but DIDN'T.

This class was HORRENDOUS!! DO NOT TAKE. I had her for the Quest 2 course and she made exams so difficult for no reason. She also pushed deadline after deadline back which you make think is nice, but actually it just means she's going to make you have 15 assignments due in one week at the end of the semester. SO DISORGANIZED. Expectations not clear

Dr. Agunbiade was very disorganized and left the class extremely confused at times. For a quest 2 course, there was an extreme amount of work and time that needed to be put into it. The exams were lengthy and detailed. She is nice, but had way too many assignments. Overall, would not recommend unless you are desperate to complete a quest 2 course.

Dr. Agunbiade wasn't very good at laying out her expectations for the class which caused a lot of chaos and confusion for students throughout the entire semester. Reading heavy, minimal guidance on exam prep, contradictory rubrics/syllabus, and more. I would advise NOT taking this course unless it's absolutely necessary.

This class is verging on ridiculous. For an entire week of material for the online class, there is usually 15-20 minutes of actual lecture (pre-recorded) provided by the instructor. Most of the material comes from the textbook and peer reviewed articles that are required reading. Professor is resistant to making changes that will benefit students

Agunbiade is very passionate about subject and funny. Real world experience + expertise in the field. As other reviewers say, course VERY disorganized but helped by the fact that she is understanding + kind. Deadlines extended constantly and weekly readings were participation credit. Very little time commitment, enjoyable experience and easy A.

This class is very unorganized. You have a quiz each week that you only get 5 minutes to answer 5 questions and these quizzes dont follow the syllabus. The term paper is graded on two different rubrics we got little guidance on. There have been many times where the modules werent uploaded in time. This class is stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: An amazing, concise lecturer, super eloquent. Her work challenges you to think in higher order, which is amazing. She's one of a kind, helpful, understanding and clear with her expectations. All assignment due dates are nicely laid out on Canvas. Can't get any better!!

To the person that said "they're not ready for a UF education if they complain about Dr. A", I have a 3.8 GPA. But pop off I guess? Dr. A isn't TERRIBLE. She's just disorganized and sometimes goes back on what the syllabus says in terms of exams and quizzes. It's an annoyingly tedious class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There are exams and weekly quizzes. The class is a decent amount of work so be prepared to put in a few hours. Dr. A is a nice person, but her class is unorganized. However, she is willing to work with students and hear you out.

Anyone who complains about DrA isnt ready for an education at UF. This is the real world people theres gonna be deadlines to adhere to and expectations to meet. Get used to it. DrA does a solid job with the course and provides clear expectations. No complaints

DocA is a GEM! She is so clear with her expectations in the course, quickly responds to everyone's emails and is so ready to help!! Her Term Paper Topic rubric is straightforward and concise. She provides amazing feedback and will go ABOVE AND BEYOND to help you!! Super sweet and specific with what she wants, no ambiguity whatsoever!! A GEM!

HORRIBLE, AVOID. She litreally does not have an idea of how to respond to emails for feedback. She first said I will respond to emails asking for feedback, then later sends an even vaguer email to the entire class which confused more than it helped. Her TAs are useless, take off points for no good reason, INCOMPETENT!!!

Although the class seemed a little disorganized, I found it pretty easy as long as you follow rubrics and complete all assignments. She responds quickly to emails, but doesn't give much feedback. Overall, this class was actually interesting and I'd recommend as one of the biology electives.

Not sure why she has bad reviews. She always responded quickly to emails and was understanding when it came to late submissions. The class itself was very interesting too and I enjoyed the papers and videos for each module. There is a term paper, but if you find an interesting topic to write about it's pretty cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class is very disorganized. This professor is never 100% clear with what she wants out of the class. There were several times I reached out to her for clarification and she would give me even vaguer responses. The coursework itself is not bad at all, but navigating the class is awful and not worth it. Get your elective credits somewhere else.

Do not take this class ! The course itself is very disorganized. Sometimes the quizzes and assignments do not appear on Canvas and the communication is not there regarding that. Also, she is a very tough grader and takes points very easily for the most minimal things. There are 4 exams, one term paper, and discussions posts.
its genuinely not a good class and the professor is no help but asks for a lot. I have no idea what I am doing, no help.
dont do it, not worth it, run away

There are 4 assignments that all added up to 100 pts, so missing one pt was like missing one pt in your final grade. Please schedule a meeting. It's the only way you'll get a thorough examination of your questions and advice for your research papers. He is willing to help and communicate. Turned in an assignment late and still got full pts.
grades slowly and gives no instructions. hell class.

Professor King is very understanding and kind to his students. However, I have no idea what I am doing in this class. I feel like I have no guidance or advice on how to write the papers, which are the only things that make up your grade. I would avoid taking this class, especially during summer terms.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor King isn't the best at communicating. Your grade is determined by 2 papers in the summer term and instructions seemed very confusing and refused to answer any emails about clarifications. Office hours are the only way to reach him and get feedback on work, if not he takes forever to grade. Doable but lots of writing and research needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Slow grader, nitpicks all of your essays, 4,000 word final paper that he gives you little instruction on. If you expect a student to write a 4,000 word essay, at least communicate more. Would not recommend taking the summer term, he has a TA grading mostly everything and will not respond to requests for advice.

Takes forever to grade and doesn't give feedback, so it's impossible to really know if you're doing anything right. Final paper was a 4,000 word "literature review" with hardly any instructions and midterm wasn't even graded by the time the final was due. Doesn't communicate with students at all, so can't really ask questions or anything either.

Slowest grader ever, canvas is basically useless. 4000 word case study with like 100 words of instructions is laughable. Took four weeks to grade the midterm paper. Shouldn't bother taking anything with him.

2000 and 4000 word paper make up the entire grade. King is a slow grader, hasn't even graded the mid term due 2+ weeks ago. Instructions and tedious and laborious (have to make your own graphs), won't respond to emails. Writing these papers is torture when you have no feedback. I'd stay away from taking this Summer session.

Easy class conceptually. Weekly assignments are easy. Four papers make up most of your grade, but he gives very vague instructions and no set office hours or good examples. Assumes that we know how to write a case study, and knows what he expects. Also, he is a slow grader (took 5 weeks to grade our midterm paper) and doesn't respond to emails.

Didn't respond to any emails. I haven't gotten my final grade yet in the class, but he still has to grade our midterm paper, literature review, and final paper which make up most of the points in the class. All of the writing assignments were on the same topic to make a case study. It was crazy that he made the final due before grading those.
This professor will not grade anything until the very very last day of the semester. Be mindful of this when taking one of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HES SO AWESOMEJUST EXTENDED A DEADLINE!!!!!!!!!!

Professor Karlson was a great professor last semester! I learned so much about 3D animation and enjoyed the different lectures. He's super engaging and helpful, especially during office hours. Grades were given back late in the semester, but he usually gave great feedback and was helpful if you reached out to him regarding assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you're online he waits till the very last day to grade projects and will only give feedback on assignments that require feedback if you're able to meet with him during office hours. The final is a preceded by three checkpoints he's supposed to assess and work with you on, unless you're in class you're not getting help with that.

The work is steady until the last 5 weeks, then it leaps in difficulty. He will take the time to do office hours but he constantly says go back and watch the lecture even when you explain you didn't understand the lecture.

Professor Karlson cares about his student's success and improvement more than anything else, and I've learned so much from him in both Character Animation and basic 3D animation. He listens to student concerns and feedback with genuine care and brings a lot of valuable knowledge to his classes. One of my favorite professors ever <3

Professor Karlson's class was a joy to attend every time! 3D Animation was super fun, and he made the lectures hilarious and a great time to be in. The class itself was hard, but that comes with learning Maya and animation, if you've never done it before. He was super caring and was good at feedback, so don't be afraid to reach out to him!

Professor Karlson is amazing! The level of difficulty of this class is high, but its not about him, its just the learning curve of Maya is pretty steep... make sure you attend the lectures and start your assignments ahead; animation takes time. He will answer questions super fast and gives great feedback... Again, start your homework on TIME
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mr. Karlson's first concern is the success of his students; he responds to questions promptly and with detail, no matter how trivial the question may seem at times. He also encourages students to review material on their own to improve their skill with Maya, which is incredibly helpful. He cares deeply about his students and is an amazing professor

Prof. Chadler is an absolute gem! He is knowledgeable, cares for his students, and is always available for a chat. The class is super easy; there is no homework (everything is done in class), no quizzes, tests, or a final exam (instead, one really meaningful gratitude assignment at the end). Attendance is 50%, though, so don't miss class. Take it!!

Easiest psych class I have taken. The material was very inspirational and easy to understand. Very easy A, and almost everyone ends up with over a 100% in the class due to extra credit at the end. Weekly work is very easy, and you barely have to think about the class outside of lecture. Group work and one scary presentation, but very easy. Take it!

One of the nicest and most caring professors I have ever met. Takes time to get to know every student beyond the classroom and class is very interesting and fun. The TA I had was also fantastic and so sweet. Ending with a 104%, everyone should take this class if they can. The fact Chandler doesn't have a 5/5 is shocking.

Positive psych: don't get the textbook.  This is the easiest class you'll ever take.  I found the whole thing depressing, which I know is ironic.  The whole premise of the class is how to find the meaning of life in a worldview that rejects meaning.  Take the class, it's easy, but be prepared to do no critical thinking at all otherwise you'll hurt.

LOVED HIM SO MUCH. Possibly the sweetest most caring professor ever. This class is super chill and as long as you show up and do your work you will be fine. loved this class so much i recommend it to everyone

I just finished this class, and I absolutely loved it! At first, I was overwhelmed with the papers that we had to do in class each week (simple reflection papers) but after the first week, I got used to it and I became really fast at writing. The content did become a little repeated at times but I would recommend this course to anyone!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Such a good class to take if you are like me and are taking a lot of hard science classes. This class is easy, has no exams, and is structured so that you can actually enjoy what is being taught. I highly recommend!!

Dr. Chandler is very nice but the could be different than some people's expectations. Group work every week and a paper due every week, but it is largely self-reflective and subjective so it isn't the woooorst? The midterm is a LOT. The class is definitely doable and the professor and TAs are very nice but be ready to put in the work.

There's a paper due every week, but it's mostly subjective self-analysis, so not too bad. He assigns an absurdly long midterm paper, though, so prep for that early. He's a really nice person, but seems to have trouble understanding some questions and communicating some concepts. Just a little disconnect between him and the students
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All the work in the class is done with a group that is assigned to you at the beginning of the semester. I don't do well in group projects, but this class was fine. There is A LOT of writing for this class. Each week a single spaced paper is due, and there is a 15ish page midterm, single spaced. However it is easier than it sounds- I promise!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: It's a class that makes you happy when all your other classes are draining. I loved this class. Definitely take it if you want a class to give you credits, help you become a better person, and just make you happy by giving you a break from all your other draining classes. TAs are super accommodating. Again, this class is about making you happy.

Ron Chandler is extremely knowledgable about positive psychology and he uses his own teaching method to gear the class. Most lectures are done by students and the learning is SO MUCH more effective. Lots of individual and group papers, all done in class. Very little homework, if any, outside the class making for a stress-free psychology course.

I would not recommend this class. There is so much writing and it's all about yourself -- I don't feel like I learned anything about the actual psychology of sustainability. He makes you buy his (badly written) textbook for $80. The midterm is SO LONG and SO UNNECESSARY. Please don't take this class.

Super sweet professor! Just show up to class and write an easy paragraph each time (individually one day, with your group the next) and you're guaranteed an A. The group project is easy, although no guidance is given so that was stressful. Dr. Chandler takes a backseat generally while UGTAs run the course (every TA got to guest lecture out of 12).

Chandler is nice and loves this course. You have to write a one page single spaced paper once a week and then do a group paper on the topic after. Midterm was 7-10 pages SINGLE SPACED, but it's writing about your own personal experiences so it's honestly not that bad. Final was a group powerpoint and we got to finish class a month before finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: The absolute sweetest man. He is so kind and knowledgeable! You can tell he truly cares about his students and the subject.
Dr. Chandler is honestly just great. He's so caring. As long as you show up to class and skim the readings, you'll do fine on the essays.

To take Psychology of Sustainability, you have to:
1. be able to write. a lot. 
2. be able to work in a group
Dr. Chandler is an amazing man with incredible experience, and he and the TAs really want you to succeed. As long as you follow the guidelines for writing, the class will go well. This class is a really valuable experience overall.

chandler is nice and the class isnt hard but the amount of work assigned is too much. the midterm is 18 pages long single spaced. paper due every week. the textbook is $80, all proceeds get donated to saving elephants which is nice (but it would also be nice for college students to have 1 less expensive txtbk to buy if proceeds r donated anyway)

LOVE professor chandler. he is awesome and knows what he is talking about. A lot of self reflection so not only do you learn more about yourself but the material is easier to understand bc its about you.
Dr. Chandler is such a nice man. I really enjoyed this class. There are a lot of papers to write but they require self-reflecting soooo not too hard if you like to write about yourself.

I genuinely love Dr. Chandler, he is rlly an amazing person and this class is very interesting and makes you reflect a lot. Howeverrrr, the midterm is absolutely insane, its like an 18 page single spaced paper but its just meant to make you reflect a lot so as long as you meet the requirements you should do well. Other than that its a great class!

Wonderful professor! This course was very easy as long as you showed up to class (attendance counts toward your grade). You are split into groups and have to write a lot of essays with that group throughout the semester as well as individual essays, but they're easy.

Paper due weekly, cant skip this as you collaborate with others to write another paper in class based on it. This part is involving but not bad compared to the 18ish page SINGLE SPACED midterm paper. Amount of work required is ridiculous & honestly unheard of. He's nice & tells good stories but makes enjoyable material so tedious, its unfortunate.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: No one seems to have mentioned the midterm for this class. It's roughly a 15-16 single spaced page paper, this isn't a writing class, I signed up for this believing it'd cover psychology & something worth learning related to this field. Sadly, unless this midterm is a literal social/psychological experiment about torturing students... it's useless
Dr. Chandler cares about his students and those around him. Ive learned so much from him in such a short amount of time. He is an amazing professor and a special individual at heart.

Weekly quizzes are super easy if you watch the lectures, and everything is graded by your assigned TA. Dr. Chandler doesn't really teach so that's the only downside, but I love this class; as someone who had an interest in social psych prior to taking this class, I have learned a lot from it!

Professor Chandler was very nice and I appreciated the fact that his class was structured around writing assignments rather than tests. However, I had to purchase the preliminary edition of the textbook he had written for $100. The "book" was a pile of loose paper which had obviously not been proofread - bad charts and tons of run-ons!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There are no exams. You're graded on participation and easy group assignments. I've never had a group assignment that I couldn't complete within 30 minutes by myself. With 10 people working on it, there's only 3 minutes of work.

He cares about his students learning, not just passing exams. You have to do a good bit of writing in this class but the material is very interesting. As a professor, he is always there to help and it shows that he cares about his students. This class and professor provide both a positive educational experience and aids in your well-being!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Group projects

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Chandler's class! The class is set up in groups and every other class day you have a one-paged paper where you apply the concepts to yourself and how to make the world a more sustainable place for human dignity. TA's grade and sometimes present. Overall, Chandler was passionate and I felt like I came away better after.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Group projects

reviews.comment: One of the easiest classes offered at UF. Definitely take him if you have the chance to. Assignments are straightforward and he really cares about his students.
Super easy class. One group paper (2 pgs), one individual paper (1 pg), and one quiz (16 q's) due each week. Most of the answers to the quizzes are on quizlet.

I really enjoyed taking Dr. Chandler's social psychology class. He's super nice and the class is not much work. Each week we had an individual paper and a group paper we had to complete, but it wasn't difficult. I highly recommend taking a class with him!
The most easiest and interesting class offered at UF. If you show up and complete the assignments in class, you get an A in the class. No exams!

I took Social Psych online, but even with that taken into consideration there was absolutely no interaction with the actual teacher; everything is graded and looked at by TAs. On top of that, you have an essay due every week and then a group essay due every Saturday, with groups of around 7 people. TONS of writing, and the groups are a pain.

Chandler is by far the most amazing professor I have ever had. He cares so much about the course material and makes it interesting by providing personal examples and asking the class to discuss topics. There is a weekly 1 page paper, but it is based off of the previous lecture and you are able to include personal anecdotes. No exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You'll have to attend all the classes to do well, and there's one long assignment every week. The midterm project is really hard, almost impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Professor Chandler. The class was an easy A and he cared about the success of his students. However, the lectures were short and often taught by his TAs. Everything was graded by the TAs too. Its a good class; nothing hard at all, but you hear more from undergrads than from the professor. No exams, just simple individual and group papers.

Needlessly difficult. Subject matter itself is not difficult. Lectures useless, just a sloppy summary of the textbook material. To pass the quizzes (no exams), have to read the textbook itself carefully. Attendance taken every lecture. TAs and Ron spent more time flipping through textbook trying to answer questions, rather than actually teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I would not recommend Professor Hill. While the material itself is not hard, we are graded on things such as "professionalism". I had a situation where I couldn't get in touch with any members of my Capsim team. He claimed that teammates not participating was part of the real world and deducted a full point off of my grade for reaching out to him.

This class is way harder than it should be. Lots of exam questions come from the minutiae of the expensive and very boring textbook. Very much a cookie cutter McGraw Hill class with lecture videos that are delivered robotically. Capsim group assignment was pretty good, however, I still would not recommend this class. Overall not worth the effort.

Disclaimer: I had technical issues for the first month of the semester, and it was hard for me to catch up on all my classes. That is why I gave it an average difficulty. The professor sends very thorough, helpful, and detailed weekly emails with reminders. You can tell he really cares about his students, and is a fair grader.

I found his class very straightforward, and he teaches many of the essential business concepts you may already know. There is a weekly lecture, smartbook, quiz, and group Capsim assignment (which is much harder than intl. business Capsim). There are many drops and grading procedures in your favor. I wish he had more practice material for exams.
Great and easy professor! Simple 3 online exams of 20 questions, 3 case studies, and a simulation. Can get away with dedicating only 40min a week to this class and get an A

Professor Gromoll has a lot of experience in the hospitality industry and was able to share these stories in each module in a way that related to the material at hand. The big project was a three part group project. I was able to acquire a Hospitality industry certification while going through this class, because he provided the needed materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ron is great and super helpful as you work to launch a career in hospitality. Make sure you will be able to make it to the designated class time as attendance heavily contributes to your grade.

Professor Gromoll was a great professor! The grading criteria was very clear and he graded assignments in a timely manner with constructive feedback. The class mainly consists of 500 word papers on the lectures given throughout the semester and assignments pertaining to career prep such as resume building and interview practice through Quinncia.

I was very anxious going into this semester and I'm ending the semester more confident, better prepared, and very excited for my future. While I didn't end up going the internship route, Prof. Ron's class was so worthwhile. The lecturers he brought in were amazing and it's not often you get a professor with so much job experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Ron was beyond supportive in my search for an internship. This was my last semester and it was one of my most anxious ones. It began with the uncertainty of landing a great job, but with Ron's support, I landed an amazing internship that fits me perfectly. Thank you for the support, Professor!

Professor Ron Gromoll- HANDS DOWN- the best hospitality professor at UF. I took him for LEI3360, LEI3992, and LEI4940. He gave amazing lectures and was so inspiring. He wants to see his students succeed. I recommend following him on LinkedIn, as he kept in touch with me right before his retirement and my upcoming graduation.
I had a great time in this course! Professor Gromoll is so helpful with finding you an agency to work with during your Field Experience semester. I enjoyed this class a lot!

Professor Gromoll is efficient in grading, maintains excellent communication with the class, and demonstrates flexibility. He also provides valuable suggestions that can assist students in finding internship opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Gromoll has been such a pleasure to have! I have enjoyed taking his classes. I am going to miss him!

Professor Gromoll is the best!! I was in two of his classes this semester (LEI 4540 and LEI 3360) and I am so glad I was. Both classes helped me learn without being overwhelmed. He is extremely passionate and brings a ton of industry knowledge. Easily my favorite professor at UF. I'm sad that the semester is ending. I will miss his classes!

Professor Gromoll is a great educator from the designs of the class to his inspirational Lectures and comments on assignments. He is very organized and thorough, explains everything, and participates "with" you through every assignment. Communication is on point and inspiring. Highly recommend! Greatest semester yet at the Univeristy of Florida!

This was a required course before my internship, as long as you stay on top of the assignments and turn them on time, you will have no issues with this course. The Professor is very knowledgeable and is willing to help you with any questions. He is very approachable.

Ron is super experienced in the field and is a great connection. He takes attendance very seriously and is not lenient with it at all. Small assignment every week with each tour. Nice guy but can be hard to get in touch with sometimes. 2 group projects, 2 exams not bad at all!

Field Experience. LOVED all of the guest speakers, actually so insightful so ask questions. You can make good connections with them. Surprisingly a lot quick, doable assignments along with your semester internship so don't let senioritis get to you and get behind/submit late. No one's gonna baby/remind you about assignments. Easy A, just show up :)

Pros: Prof Gromoll has a lot of experience and he provides a lot of extra credit opportunities. Very hard not to get an A with all the EC. Con: Attendance is taken the second class starts. The course setup felt heavy at the start of the semester, especially for an elective, but once you get in rhythm all the assignments are very easy.

Ron's facilities class if full of good field trips (with weekly 500 word summaries). He has the experience and knowledge to back up his lecture content and is seemingly connected to almost everyone in town. Attendance is random on 1 of the 2 days a week so don't skip. 

The class I took was an 8:30 though so I got a B for not showing up a lot.
If you show up and turn everything in on time there's no reason not to get an A

Professor Gromoll is fantastic! This course is the perfect culmination to the THEM degree program at UF. As an online student I feel like he got to know me as well as his classroom students. The networking opportunities he provides are invaluable and the coursework is practical. I highly recommend him and this program!

Ron is a solid professor, and he's more than willing to help if you ask for it. The lecture summary assignments (500 words) were a bit tedious and annoying, but other than that the class was easy and had a lot of value in the guest lectures.
Professor is very knowledgeable and friendly, but don't skip class as he does random roll-call.

Professor Gromoll not a bad person and is good prof. very passionate and uses his experiences as for application of concepts. lots of assignments and can take up lot of time from other classes which is messed up bc its an elective. hated his attendance policy. takes attendance randomly, and u get partial credit if your even a min late!

Pros: Overall very doable, extra credit was offered twice, Ron is a great professor!
Cons: Attendance is required and taken at random. Projects throughout semester are very group-based--so be choose your members if possible. Coordinating times with peers outside of class is required--can be challenging with various group members' schedules.

This is a very doable, stress-free class! Only two exams, the mid-term and the final, and the assignments basically consist of open-book quizzes, discussions, and simple group projects. He takes attendance randomly, and the lectures are entertaining. Ron is a very caring and understanding professor who wants to see his students succeed!

Professor Gromoll is a nice guy and is very passionate about what he's teaching. Almost all work is fun group projects where you have to go out and do interviews and take pictures. Only a mid-term and a final but not difficult at all. He randomly takes attendance throughout the semester but doesn't approve many excuses. Overall pretty easy
Really great Professor who offers extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Also helped me find my internship! Very nice and wants his students to succeed!

I had Ron Gromoll for three classes at UF and enjoyed having him as a professor immensely! He cares about his students' futures SO much and really does everything in his power to prepare you for life after college (interview prep, guest speakers, guidance sessions). Months after I graduated, he helped me find an amazing job within my field!

Professor Gromoll is a great professor and has been more than helpful throughout this semester. He really cares about his students success and prepares us well for our internships! This is my second class with him and he is for sure one of my favorite professors I have ever had at UF! His guest lectures are fun to watch and learn from!

Professor Ron is a great professor who is understanding and really cares about his students. His classes are fairly easy, and if you ever have any trouble he'll answer your questions! I have had him for a couple of classes and really enjoyed them. Would definitely recommend!
Ron makes interactive the classes by going to venue tours and he will always respond to your emails or in person concerns.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Gromoll is the sweetest teacher. He has a lot of experience in the industry, so he gives many real-life examples that relate to the course. Attendance was taken randomly throughout the semester. You are assigned a group at the start of the semester and you will do many assignments with them. Besides the group projects, it's a great class.

Professor Gromoll is very experienced in the hospitality industry, which translates into how he approaches this class. Because he is so experienced, he provides real-world examples and insight in his lectures. His lectures are fun and engaging, and he brings in guest speakers every few weeks. Overall was one of my favorite professors this semester!

Professor Gromoll holds lots of field experience and incorporates his personal expertise in lectures. He provides feedback, grades fairly, and makes the class enjoyable. Overall, a great guy who wants his students to do well.

Professor Gromoll has varieties of experiences in hospitality & tourism field. In this class, he conducted multiple field trips to different facilities for us to learn and experience in person and I enjoyed it a lot. He takes attendance randomly and it is a huge part of the final grade so make sure you show up to classes. The exams are easy too.

Ron has so much industry insight and really values participation. Internship class is actually well geared towards helping you transition into a career and setting yourself up for success. Lectures are super informative and he tells great stories. Guest lecturers come often so you have a chance to ask questions and make real connections.
Ron is a very nice, knowledgable guy. Major grandpa vibes. The lectures were pretty boring, but with randomized, graded attendance, we had to sit through em. The class itself is not difficult.

He is a super nice and caring guy. lectures are engaging and he shares a lot of wisdom. I only have negative comments about how many group projects there are which you could end up doing all the work for if people don't help. That is frustrating, just too many group projects. Also tough grader so follow rubrics closely. good teacher but takes time
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class would have been so much easier without the unnecessary group assignments. He also gives zero actual feedback and doesnt participate at all. Good luck if you have bad group members because he needs two people to confirm the non-participation. Had one guy do 0 assignments and still had to email weekly to tell the professor.

Professor Gromoll is a terrific professor. He was previously a hotel manager so he has a lot of firsthand experience so many topics are taught through that lens, which is helpful to understand the material. Exams are pretty much what he teaches during the lectures, but there are many assignments so they don't count for a huge portion of final grade

Dr. Molstad does his best to teach you the concepts and make sure you understand everything as you progress through his classes. I thoroughly enjoyed STA4504 and I would absolutely recommend taking it with him if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I struggled a lot with this class but Prof. Molstad was very helpful for clarifying material. Exams make up 70% of your grade but he does curve. Exams were difficult and were somewhat proof heavy which differed from the computational practice exams. Make sure you do all the homeworks and get the highest grades possible.

Teaches material well and is very helpful in OH. Some HWs are lengthy and midterm/final were 5-7 day take-home exams (it will take most of that time to do) but everything is fair. STA3032 was my only prereq which made some topics harder but its definitely doable with enough effort and I learned way more in this class than in eng stats.

Homework was fairly challenging, but about expected time consumption for a math class. Molstad cares and will help in OH and his lectures are alright. The practice exams are easier than the real exams, but the real exams were not god awful (still hard), but he curves and provides some extra credit. From this you can intuit that he is a solid choice

Homework load not huge. Lectures very full of mediocre-ly explained material. Homework problems are difficult but manageable. Gives a practice exam that is similar, if not easier. Then exams are extremely difficult and different from homeworks and practice exam. I pay attention, do homework, take notes, study, and do awful on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Molstad taught stats 1 like a champ. He clearly explains concepts and has a lot of wiggle room on exam grading. Every test was curved in some way, and he has a lot of office hours. Definitely take stats with him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Had her for "Spanish in the US". Easy class, nice but lectures can be very long and boring at times, easy group work sometimes in class. 8 homeworks were on Canvas, open-note and everything. Course has a three part project worth 50% of the grade with a presentation at the end of the semester - not bad though. Recommend if looking for light work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very kind, and certainly provides a great environment in the class. The course can be a bit dry but I think that this is more a reflection of the materials (academic articles on sociolinguistics are super long and boring) than on her. One of the easiest Spanish classes I have taken. No stress at all! Some presentations but overall not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: had her for both SPN3700 &4930. she does a WAY better job at 4930, because in spn3700 she would contradict herself or ask the TAs to clarify, but was all over the place information-wise. book helps with 3700, and for 4930 it's a lot of reading, but as long as you get jist, you'll do fine on the essays. homeworks were on canvas & open notes.

I'm minoring in Spanish and have never made below an A in a Spanish class, but I'm all but confirmed to make a B in this class. The information she provides is inconsistent, and my friend and I spent the whole semester teaching each other the info since Aaron didn't do it. Super frustrating professor for what should've been an interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The semester isn't even over and I have a lot of words to say about this. The class itself is poorly organized and most people complain that they don't ever know whats going on. Her slides are often incorrect and you end up teaching yourself from the textbook. It feels like you set yourself up for failure by taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I didnt enjoy her class at all! very unclear with what she exactly wanted from you and lots of reading. she made me dislike spanish when it should be interesting to learn. she attempts to help but it doesnt seem that shes interested in her students passing or understanding the material at all.
This class made me dislike Spanish. Her class was boring and not interactive. A lot of reading and harsh grading on exams. Don't take this class unless you have to!
Fantastic teacher!

Jessica Aaron is one of my all time favorite teachers! She is extremely knowledgable and is always looking for ways to make her class fun, interesting, and informative. However, she gives ALOT of reading, so DO NOT take her classes if you know you will NOT TAKE THE TIME TO READ.

She is a very nice teacher, and does try to help. However, if you ask something in class that she doesnt know, it becomes irrelevant. She couldnt teach certain concepts and you needed to rely on the book as your teacher. I was disappointed because I expected to learn more, she used anothers materials that she didnt always agree with, very confusing

Dr. Aaron is an amazing professor who goes above and beyond to help her students.  She was available COUNTLESS times in her office to provide help with everything from Spanish grammar to learning about academia.  She makes her class both stimulating and her  approach to pedagogy is both refreshing and pragmatic.  I'd  recommend her to anyone!

Professor Aaron was eager to help and very reachable via e-mail. She was not very clear as to what she wanted in in class activities and uncomfortable teaching a lower level class but all around, the class was do able as long as you went and kept up with what was being covered.

no very clear. when she didnt know how to answer a question asked to her, she just said "that is not very important". obsessed by numbers. apparently dedicated to students. she wasnt caring at all. she didnt know how to conduct the class. her explanations were so loose and weak. just dreaming about her former school.

She is completely unclear with what she wants from her students, even though she pretends to be helpful. She led me on all semester to believe my work was of A quality and then ended up giving me a B+ in the class. Objectively, she is not just, and don't expect to get ANY grades from her...she doesn't grade a thing!

Probably the class I was most intimidated by before actually taking it... Great person, always tries to make class enjoyable.  Lots of small group projects, lots of reading, one VERY long spanish paper, but on the topic of your choice.  LOVED HER CLASS!
Baffling professor. Completely impossible to understand and communicate in the worst way possible.
Easy class. Light grader. Very accommodating and cares for his students' success.

Clearly explained all concepts of the class and attendance was not mandatory. Fairly easy grader, complete the assignments and you'll be fine. Quiz and exam questions almost identical to the textbook.

Dr. Shanker is a great human being and he cares about what he is teaching. However, it's time to call it a day for him. The lectures were often overshadowed by YouTube video noise that he could not hear. He also does not seem very efficient while using google chrome and canvas. I like him as a human being, but he's not a good professor.

reviews.comment: Can not teach a single thing and drones on in his lectures. Gained nothing from this class. Avoid this teacher.

reviews.comment: Professor Shanker has been at Rinker for many years, he is very caring and it's honestly sad how students treat him. He gives pop quizzes to encourage attendance. When students realize there's no quiz, they walk out mid lecture. Rarely over 1/4 of the class stays. Professors used to be respected. You cant expect to pass without applying yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He often does not teach the material and is extremely hard to follow. No one knows what is going on in his class. He is also not accessible outside of the class because he does not believe in emails.
jsut really boring and cant follow him

Professor Shanker is nice and approachable, but has no teaching ability. The lectures were confusing, off topic, and incomprehensible. The only saving grace for this class is that there are no exams, only weekly quizzes. If you have taken statics or are very good at teaching yourself material, you'll pass; otherwise don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Regardless of who he may be as a person, Shanker needs to hang it up. We live in a modern world, and he has no idea how to adapt to that. His lecture are incomprehensible, quiz questions are often setup in ways we've never experienced, and his inconsistency is unmatched. The class is unorganized, and it is extremely confusing. Good luck.
