Very good teacher and intresting class.  Tests are fairly easy but hard to get an A in
One of the best classes I've had at UF. The exams were honestly some of the fairest I've taken, which made the class way less stressful. He's super approachable and really easy to talk to.

If you can take him, do it. I had him for 3120 (by chance) and now fir 4130. Easiest A I've had fr. The 4130 average is over an A rn and hope the exams stay the same lol. He's super nice and passionate but as a newer professor so he's still figuring some things out i think. but he's very approachable and tries to adjust so not a big deal

This is the worst professor I have had at UF. Multiple slides with incorrect math, practice problems with incorrect key answers, is unable to explain any of the concepts correctly, be ready to self teach and recognize all of his work is completely wrong. Grading is fine but don't expect to learn anything of value. He's a super nice guy though.

Nice guy overall and you can tell he actually cares and listens. The class is hard and the subject is kinda boring, and you need a lot of practice, like a LOT. Still, everyone I know got an A. There are a lot of bonus point opportunities. Go to office hours and do the practice problems if you want to do well.

His teaching style is great! He makes sure that everyone understands fully, and when you can't answer a question, he helps you through it so nicely and understanding. He is great when it comes to teaching, and the activities in class are never too challenging. He understands that it may be everyone's first time learning Arabic. He is a great guy!

Really awesome professor for a homework heavy class. Definitely have to stay on top of coursework, but he makes things engaging with one zoom and one TA session a week. He is super understanding and you can tell he loves what he does
Salah is a good professor. His lectures are engaging and include lots of group discussion, which makes class interesting. Also, his late policy is very relaxed.

Dr. Algabli is an amazing professor. I've learned so much about writing research papers and about Arab culture. His lectures are engaging and fun, and he is very supportive, respectful, encouraging, and always willing to help and guide students.

Professor Salah is one of the most supportive and engaging professors I've had. He creates a respectful, welcoming space where students feel encouraged to grow. His classes are well-organized and thoughtful, and I learned a lot especially in terms of technology, creativity, and thinking in new ways.

Today is my graduation day, and I feel lucky to have him as my professor throughout my time at UF. From the very first course I took with him, I was inspired to keep enrolling in his classes every semester. He was a constant source of support, especially when it came to my PhD applications. When someone says "UF," it will always mean Dr. Salah.

I love Professor Salah! He is very knowledgeable, kind, and passionate about what he teaches. His lectures are engaging, and he always makes sure students understand the material. He truly cares about our success and creates a welcoming, supportive learning environment. I'm grateful to be in his class!
Professor Salah is the best , combining expertise with innovative teaching methods. His supportive and engaging approach makes learning both effective and enjoyable.

Professor Salah Algbali is a passionate and dedicated educator who makes learning engaging and enriching. His expertise, supportive approach, and innovative teaching foster a welcoming and inspiring environment for students.

Dr. Salah Algabli is an inspiring and innovative educator. His ability to integrate technology into teaching, like using virtual reality and online learning, makes learning more engaging and effective. He genuinely cares about us and works hard to create meaningful and interactive learning experiences.

Dr. Salah Algabli has been an exceptional instructor throughout the course, particularly in guiding me through the process of writing both conceptual and empirical papers. His clear, structured approach to teaching made complex topics accessible and manageable. He emphasized the importance of a solid theoretical foundation and research

Dr. Algabli is an outstanding professor. I took Arabic Gulf Studies with him, and I learned so much. It was my first time writing a research paper, and I struggled initially, but he was incredibly patient and guided me through the process step by step. He even helped me with my application for a summer fellowship in Washington, DC.

I thoroughly enjoyed every class with Dr. Salah Algabli. His creativity made learning exceptionally accessible. I took his Intro to Persian Language and Culture course, which was incredibly informative. I regretted graduating because I couldn't continue with his classes sooner; I wish I had known about him since my freshman year.

Professor Algabli has consistently demonstrated exceptional expertise and dedication to his field. His lectures are engaging and informative, blending complex theories with practical examples that enhance understanding. His approachable demeanor and willingness to provide support and guidance have made a significant impact on students. The best
One of the best professors I've ever had! I took Arabic 1 and 2 with him and have no regrets. I was challenged by the course, but he makes an A or A- easy through extra credit and completion grades.
This class was one of the most interesting classes I have taken thus far in university, and  professor Algabli was also within my top preferences for professors. I would recommend this class.
Profesor Salah is creative, respected and very approachable
Very innovate project ideas, good at getting students to use the language in class. Really enjoyed this class with Salah.

Great language teacher. Many opportunities for extra credit. Understanding and genuinely wants you to learn. The order he teaches info about the language may seem confusing at first but he loves to answer any questions you have

Salah is seriously the best ever. Hilarious, a great instructor, and really cares about his students. He makes Arabic fun and is always more than willing to offer any extra help. If you're someone who is a big studier, I would focus on taking your own notes b/c his class is mostly conversation based. If you want to learn Arabic, this is the class!!

I was hesitant about taking Intermediate Arabic but Professor Salah made it so much fun. We not only learned the language but we learned about the different Arab countries and cultures as well. We had cooking classes together, watched movies in Arabic, and even put together a conference. He genuinely cares and is the best professor Ive had!!

Professor Salah is the best. He made sure everyone participated in class and allowed students to engage in the content every single day. He made it impossible not to learn in his class, and he serves as proof that classes on Zoom can actually be enjoyable. Definitely take his class if possible! (Btw, he gives you a PDF of the textbooks.)

My favorite class so far at UF. Salah makes learning Arabic so much fun, even if it was through zoom. I love the structure of the class, it really makes learning the language easier. He's super enthusiastic about the subject too which makes it more fun, one of the best professors I've ever had.

Professor Cole is one of those professors who values the intelligence of their students. She gives you pretty much free range to develop your interests within the bounds of her class. Can't recommend her enough.

This professor is very rude and does not reflect the rating given. She relies only on the textbook or perusal for assignments, so there's really no purpose to being a professor for this class. She's not very accommodating, and can be quite mean. I would stay away from her if you don't want to be ridiculed as a student. Harsh grader with no feedback

Alyssa Cole herself does not really contribute much to the course outside the grading, while most of the material you will have to absorb on your own time. Nothing good or necessarily bad about her teaching, just overall indifferent as she plays a very little part as far as teaching the material.

She is amazing. She is very down to earth and really cares about her students. We had three essay assignments but they are graded fairly and she is happy to provide extensions. She often mentions that she wants the class to be relaxing and carefree and she means it. I have not once stressed about her class. I highly recommend her.

Great class structure and teaching style/personality allow for some chill but really interesting and educational discussion. She is very lenient with due dates as long as you communicate your needs. Takes the time to get to know each individual student and is a great person to have a conversation with on topics you may find interesting.

I absolutely recommend Professor Cole! Buffalos and Bloods is a small, discussion-based class, and most readings can be found online. I can honestly say I wasn't super interested in modern American or military history before this class, but I enjoyed it anyway. There's a few papers, but she's a fair grader, chill with deadlines, and very supportive

Dr. Cole is a fantastic professor! Her Buffalos and Bloods class was amazing. Most of the classes are discussions about the readings, but the topics are always incredibly interesting. The readings are fairly easy to get through. There are a couple of essays and a presentation, but she is a very fair grader. She wants you to succeed!

Lectures are difficult to understand and exams are on tiny details from the lectures. Some of the questions were based on specific context of examples in the lecture, not even the science behind them. Exam questions can be unclear or incorrect and he will fix them only for the person who emails in, and only after messaging him multiple times.

His lectures and reviews are difficult to understand and his powerpoints/quizzes often have major grammatical issues. In review sessions (the only live lectures) he is very curt and often refuses to answer questions unless they are in a specific order. Exams are the majority of the grade and are based on minute details from the powerpoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: dude its so bad he is almost completely unintelligible in the lectures, literally just reads off a script right from the book, and its weighted at 85% exams, which have questions on the most tiny random details you never expected to need to know. do not do it its literally comically easy to fail a class that should be easy bc of the grading scheme
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: his lectures are very difficult to understand because of his english, and his exams are not reflective of any of the homework or practice problems. he has few study resources for exams, and the exams test on miniscule concepts and not big picture. they also have bad grammar. a difficult class and he does nothing to help you understand it.

His lecture videos are so hard to understand. He just reads off a script and does not actually explain the material. The exams are very hard and the homework is as well. Maybe if you self teach yourself a lot you will do well.

He's ok. The class isn't as bad as people on here are saying. He pulls questions exactly from the lecture slides, just read and memorize until the most miniscule detail and you will be fine. He also provides a lot of extra credit - nearly 20 points extra really helped my grade and I managed to pull an A+ despite always cramming for this class.

He provided so much extra credit, the lectures had notes that he pulled information out of for the exams (if someone couldn't understand his accent), and he hosts exam reviews where he tells you the main concepts he'll test you on. Some exam questions recycled quiz questions. Easy A honestly if you try a little and get over the accent.

Babar is awful. His lectures are just audio clips on a powerpoint where his face covers half the material.  His accent makes it extremely difficult to understand what words he's saying. Also, he consistently says wrong information and does not bother to correct it. The powerpoints consist of images from text and he provides no additional info ever.

He is too hard to understand due to his accent. His lectures are useless because of this. His transcript powerpoints are also hard to understand due to poor grammar. You have to reread things multiple times to get what he is trying to say in the sentence. His reviews do not prepare you for the exams since he does not go through practice questions.

The exams are difficult, still doable, but Dr. Babar doesnt seem to care about helping students. During my time in his class last semester, he did not reply to emails, including the email where i was asking him for advice or help with grasping material. I have a friend who complained about the same thing, but ended up with an A or B .

The lectures are useless. The professor reads straight off the slides and does not explain material at all. His exam reviews were useless as well as he would say "know everything from this lecture" for every lecture. I would take this course with another professor if possible or else get ready to teach yourself everything on your own.

Another professor where the feedback doesn't reflect the actual experience. Even though his lecture videos may  suck, he publishes the slides and the video transcript! JUST READ THE SLIDES AND THE TRANSCRIPT... All the exams can be ACED with those two materials. HW answers on Quizlet, lots of extra credit, easiest A in a 3000 level class I've taken

Dr. Babar is extremely knowledgeable about genetics and cares a lot for his students, but this is a pretty hard class. Your whole entire grade is based off of 4 exams, and a very little percentage is homework and extra credit. His exams were pretty hard but very closely related to his PowerPoint. Hard class that you mostly have to teach yourself.
Can't understand a word he says so if you aren't willing to teach yourself everything, I wouldn't take the class. Take it with Kara Casey instead.

Tries to make class more difficult and complicated than it has to be. He has lecture videos where he just reads off the powerpoint for one hour, sounds extremely robotic and it is very difficult to engage with. The homeworks are timed which is unnecessary and the powerpoints are overwhelming with information. Reviews are not helpful, do not take!

His exams were exessively difficult, leaving students feeling unprepared. The timed homework assignments added unnecessary pressure and hindered learning. The exclusive extra credit opportunities tied to attending lectures were unfair and excluded those with scheduling conflicts. He did not create his own tests, he just got questions from Quizlets.

I learned a lot in this class but it wasn't because of Dr. Babar. The lectures are long and repetitive and the exam questions are poorly worded. Additionally, there is no clear grading guidelines for lab assignments and he will take off points for wording an answer in a *slightly* different way than he would prefer. This professor is ridiculous.

I have no idea what all these negative reviews are about. His lectures and powerpoints have exactly the same material as the exams. He holds optional pre-exam review sessions that are SO helpful (lots of hints about exam material). If you go to class and review the powerpoints youll be fine. The class averages for exams are also pretty good (B).

So, this class can be difficult if you never watch any of his lectures. Everything on his lecture PowerPoints, and I mean everything, are on his exams. Also, definitely watch exam reviews. Sometimes hes hard to understand but its manageable. He takes the highest 10 homeworks and has easy extra credit quizzes. Overall, easy class imo.
This class was incredibly boring. However, it was really easy. It was memorization only, and he told you exactly what you needed to know. He also gave weekly quizzes for extra credit.
He is awful!!!! I can't understand a word he is saying. His test are so hard. Worst professor I have ever taken.

There's plenty of extra credit, which is great. The exams are entirely based on the powerpoint slides, so study those! I think he teaches what needs to be taught, but if you have no questions, he assumes you haven't studied, and if you do have questions, he acts a little condescending.

If you like learning complex math on your own with literally no help from lecture videos: Md Babar is your guy! If you like struggling to understand what hes saying in lectures: sign right up! If you want a professor who gets mad at you and your class when asking for help: youll be in heaven! Dont take this class unless you can be your own prof

Babar's is much less formal than the classes you take when starting out in university. I had a hard time understanding what and why we were learning some things and this made it difficult to remember concepts. He often got angry with students and, unfortunately, his accent made him hard to understand. Focus on slides to study!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class with him online, adapting to corona. I am not going to lie, it was a little tough to follow the online lectures. However, he personally made sure we got extra credit (bonus extra credit given every week!) and also, most of times we asked to review tests, he did it. It's not an easy class, but I learned to like and respect him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class isn't as bad as everyone is making it seem. He provides a lot of extra credit opportunities. His exams sometimes have challenging questions but all of the material is from the slides. I read the textbook for the first exam but didn't find it that helpful so I just used his slides for the next 4 which is all I needed. So study his slides!

So, I'm generally a A/B+ student and despite reading the textbook, doing all the homework assignments, attending lecture, meeting with the professor, and hiring a tutor - I still managed to fail his exams. Now, I don't know what extent of effort is needed to pass his exams, but unless you enjoy a CHALLENGE or are a genius, don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He does not have enough knowledge in genetics, get angry often, very very difficult to understand.

This sounds scary but it really isn't. I didn't put as much time in as I should have but I still did pretty good. Finish reading the chapters & give yourself enough time to read through the ppts a day or 2 before the exam you'll be fine. He's really nice and if bad weather etc. cancels class, he adjusts the exams to fit. Really nice, extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you have to take any type of genetics for your major, take this course with this professor. All the lectures are his own power points, don't need the textbook. 6 total exams but none of them are cumulative, so you don't have to study that much for each test, and they're all multiple choice. no final, and he gives SO MUCH extra credit!

Very difficult for any American to understand, and also gives extremely difficult tests. Lecture Notes don't even correspond to the exams, so reading and learning everything on your own is a must. Also gets very angry when students ask questions. Do not recommend this for anybody taking a beginning level course.

He gets frustrated and lashes out when people do not understand, he doesn't seem to comprehend that we do not understand what he is saying because of his accent. He presents the course material unclearly. Course is unnecessarily hard for an introductory level, no pre-req, elective credit. Unwilling to change exam scores even when he is disproven.

Babar is very difficult to understand. You can't understand barely anything he says. His tests are VERY though and an uneven mixture of lecture and textbook material, even though his lectures don't follow the text whatsoever.
Explained things very well in lectures, reviewed more difficult topics multiple times and made sure people understood. Exams and assignments were a direct match to the lecture content.

I took CIS4301 with him. His lectures are quite engaging, and the tests are not difficult at all. Watching the review videos before the test is really helpful. The homework isn't the most clear with grading but you can ask TAs for clarification. Overall, he's quite passionate and I would definitely take a class with him again.

This entire class could be replaced with an 8-hour YouTube video. He's very pedantic and often repeats things that are useless to the majority of the class. He comes off as rude sometimes when he tells students to be quiet even though nobody is talking. It is just a bad experience and class.

The instructions for assignments are vague and unclear. Feedback on essays isn't particularly helpful either. He's passionate, the content is interesting, but the class is unorganized, and he isn't very timely. If you need structure, he may not be the professor for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although unorganized, I have to say I did enjoy his classes. They focus more one the discussion and history behind the novels, which always took interesting turns. Many people on RMP think he's harsh and/or pretentious, but he honestly just has a dry sense of humor about him. He's a very smart guy and honestly very nice.

Apollo Amoko is engaging, kind, and values input, but his classes lack organization. He doesn't use a syllabus, and the three-hour sessions are mostly unstructured discussions. I wouldn't take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very very unorganized and lectures are often quite boring, doesn't allow for as much class discussion as he claims at the beginning. Changes books to read from the syllabus super last minute after most students have already purchased. Gives unclear/super abnormal instructions for essays, and then page-long feedback that is hard to understand.

Professor Amoko isn't universally popular among students. He's criticized as being condescending, too dense + boring of a lecturer, and too pedantic of a grader. This understandably turns off many students. But you may find, as I did, that you quite enjoy his insight and teaching style. If his class content appeals to you, I say give him a shot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very rude professor. His instructions for essays were very vague and his feedback was harsh and pretentious. He was very rude in class, cuts students off and tells them that their comments and opinions are essentially wrong. He is terrible at communication, I didn't get the syllabus from him until the third week of class. Very hard to get an A.

Do not take him! Please! I was warned, but I ignored it thinking it was just complainers who want easy A's and will complain about any professor who challenges them, but that is not the case. His lectures are disorganized, instructions unclear, and even though participation is a large part of your grade makes you want to sit in the back & be quiet.

Lectures for 3 hours straight. Cuts students off and makes the same jokes every class. Brilliant, but towards the end of the semester I resented him bc of how rude he can be. Squints eyes and looks like he's in pain the majority of the class. Argues for the sake of arguing. I said white was the opposite of black and he said I was wrong. seriously?

If you like sitting in class for 3 hours straight listening to him lecture without a break this is the class for you. He grades extra hard and is not reasonable when trying to discuss grades with him. Cancels office hours often sometimes without letting you know before hand and you're sitting there waiting.

He is a nice man and very, very smart. However, he rambles a lot and talks a lot, which can be hard to follow and keep paying attention. He is also a harsh grader and his notes are always, nice try, but you're wrong. It's as if he is the only one who can make up theories about what the authors meant.

Very intimidating professor.  He is brilliant, but harsh and sometimes a little rude. Stick to your point and stick up for yourself, stay concise, and do the reading. He will tell you how to pass, so just follow his directions and tips. I learned so much.

This guy is one of the smartest and most knowledgable professors I've had thus far at UF.  He can sometimes get boring and drag along but he is freaking great!  It's like what doesn't he know!  His essays are easy, all you have to do really is contribute to the discussion because he will help make those things that are unclear very clear.

I absolutely loved this course! At first I thought, "What the hell am I doing in Nationalism and the Novel?" But by the end of the course, I had made great strides in my writing and thinking. Professor Amoko is very kind and permitting you read and show up to class ON TIME, you'll be perfectly fine.

How can one man be so knowledgeable? It seems like this professor literally knows EVERYTHING. He can be intimidating, but he is also incredibly accommodating and kind. Be warned, however, he plays favorites. His grading is fair and thorough.

I hated this professor at first, but by the end of the class, I was doing the best writing I've ever done.  Read the books, pay attention, and voice your opinion in class.  He can be a bit rude, cutting students off and not looking at you while you speak, but he pushed me further than any professor.  A good learning experience, but somewhat painful

Absolutely hated this guy. He never lets you finish making your point and constantly picks apart parts of your argument that aren't even directly relevant to the point you were making. He's very arrogant. Also, he grades papers harshly--nearly impossible to get an A on one. Was nice enough outside of class but horrendous as a professor.
Do  not waste your time

Great class. Very thought-provoking. It challenged many conceptions that I had. He brings unique and interesting insight into the class discussion. I thought he was a fair grader but he's definitely tougher than most teachers. Read what he assigns and be prepared to defend whatever you have to say (He will make you back it up with details!)

Intimidating, not very approachable, but actually nice- really brilliant, you can learn a lot if you can tolerate his tangents and ask a lot of questions. Interrupts, has strong opinions- contradict him & it won't affect your grade but he may not let you finish your sentence. If you read & participate, ask for help on papers- you'll get B at least.

(continued) He gives back a full page of comments (good and bad) for each paper. Not a single person in my class got an A on the first paper. It's still possible to get an A in the class if you attend every lecture and he knows your name. Speak up and you'll be fine. He says there will be quizzes, we never had one. Read all of the books!

One of my favorite professors. Sometimes he doesn't listen to what you're saying or he'll interrupt. He always makes you qualify a statement and it's a little bit annoying because he keeps probing you for an answer to something that's unanswerable. Attendance is a must and you must be a strong writer to get an A. Great class. Definitely worth it!

Amoko genuinely cares about his students. He gives back a full page of comments (good and bad) on each of your papers. Don't be offput, he is only trying to help. He will help you at great lengths with predrafts of papers. Very progressive beliefs as well. I recommend him.

Amoko is definitely an interesting guy. He's really laid back and funny, although a little strange and off-putting at times...like he doesn't look directly at you when you speak, kind of glances nervously around the classroom. The class was pretty interesting, papers not too bad either.  I would recommend him--quite an experience!

Great prof. He's really helpful with your papers if you go to his office hours. You definitely have to read the books and have strong papers to get an A. He's really open minded though. He's more concerned about how you make your point than what your point is, as long as you're not totally off track.

His teaching style and intergections were off-putting to me, but he is a fair grader and gave extensions/corrections happily. Attendence,  interest in the books, and participation are a must for an A.
Apollo is reasonable. Might not sound like much, but in the English department it's a small miracle. Great reading, open minded, and extremely helpful.

amoko is one of the most personable, easygoing, empathetic people in gainesville and that's saying a lot! his class, a seminar "english and englishness" was one of the most thought-provoking and critical classes i've ever taken. what's most impor

Amoko is brilliant, his reading lists defy any previous conventions about canonical African literature.  His class was not always easy, but it challenged me to think differently, take greater content from the readings, and to write with the whole picture i

somehow one of those profs i could never quite make happy... extremely harsh responses to papers - full typed pages about how disappointed he was, etc. not a happy experience. maybe my fault for taking two classes of his in one semestre.
No Comments
Brilliant, eccentric, brash and extremely helpful. He's always organized and very good at challenging "normative" thinking.  A wonderful professor.

Do you want to succeed in this class? Show up to every lecture. Do not pay attention to the lectures. Do EVERY homework. For tests memorize the homeworks(every single one). If it is a computational test question know how to do it.

This professor is honestly a really nice guy. I'm supposed to get 75 minutes for my exams, but he always extended that to 90. Exams are literally just homework problems, and he considers you a good samaritan if you request him to go over a problem. He also gives bonus points if you never miss a class. The pop quizzes are the only annoying thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
If possible, switch out of this professor. entire grade is 3 test and 3 pop quizzes. all extremely challenging. lectures are unclear and not as intense as homework/test problems.
If stuck in this class: read the textbook, memorize the hw problems, go to office hours

He is great in the sense that he will personally connect with each student. beware
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Crashed out many times over this class. Did every hw multiple times and his explanations weren't super helpful. Lectures sucked because everything was already written and he would try to explain it but would move too quickly. Exams were so difficult and pop quizzes sucked. exam and quiz averages were in the 50s-60s range. DO NOT TAKE!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really bad teacher. No more happiness for taking him class.

Assigns a ton of homework that he does not grade, 3 tests and 3 pop quizzes that make up your entire grade. Had no social life the week before the exams to be able to study and was still blindsided on every exam. I love math and he almost had me changing my major. Will tank your GPA and spirit, take anyone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is so awful because his lectures are so rushed and he just is bad at teaching in general. The grades in the class are so unfair because 3 pop quizzes and 3 exams make up the entire grade, and all of them are insanely hard. Don't take this class it actually is miserable. Even if you study a lot, you will still fail the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely harsh grader. Can barely explain concepts. The course grade was determined by 3 quizzes and 3 tests. Although the tests were homework problems, he does not teach well enough for you to do well on tests/quizzes, so you pretty much need to memorize his homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH I HATE THIS GUY
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: None of the homework counted for credit so the only things for your grade was a minor attendance percentage with testa being your whole grade which are crazy difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take any course with this teacher. He is rude, lies about what will be on the exam, grades very harshly with little to no feedback, barely explains concepts, yells at students, is not understanding, does not know how to organize the course material, and interrupts students when students ask questions. 40% test average and an A is a 93%.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The tests are mostly just homework questions from the book. However, there are a lot of them, and you have to know each one very thoroughly. Usually, you wouldn't know how to solve the problems unless you've seen them before. Be prepared to not have a social life the week before each of the three tests if you want to do well.

***HARD TEST GRADER*** He will be extremely tough on grading. You may even have the right answer for the most part, but if he doesnt like the way it looks, then youre getting MAYBE half credit on the work. 3 tests, pop quizzes, NO CURVES. If you can avoid, do it. Your GPA will go down. I would have gotten an A otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Totally destroyed my interest in linear algebra. Details have been stated by other comments. Cannot believe that I was expecting to earn a good grade by self-studying before this semester started... Definitely one of the worst professors I ever met at UF...
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This man is the worst professor I've ever had. Unclear with every topic covered, doesn't explain anything, and has little regard for his students. Very rude. Doesn't explain proofs or proof methods for newly introduced topics. Avoid taking this professor at all costs.

WORST professor I've had at UF. So unorganized with homework. Essentially told me in order to pass the class I needed to go to office hours every single time. He is a ridiculous, rude, and sexist professor. Avoid at all costs or you'll be halfway through the semester with a D, like everyone else...

This is the first class I've had to withdraw from (even after orgo and sets & logic). The exams pull questions from the HW but he changes them slightly so it's impossible to even try to remember the HW. He said there would be quizzes but there hadn't been any by the halfway point. If you do not like proofs, DO NOT take him for linear algebra!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: No syllabus; decides exam dates a week in advance; exams are gambles if you happen to have the exact proof he uses as the solution; went to office hours and he was unable to explain why my proofs were incorrect, just told me to do it his way; literally said "I look at the proof and give it a grade" when asked about a systematic grading process
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Berkovich gets to know everyones name and has pretty interesting lectures. The class is the average of your 3 exams and the A is at a 93. Often the questions on the exams were not straight from the homework. He was helpful in office hours but not efficient. I would have 5 questions and get 2 answered. Overall decent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Berkovich cares very much about what he does. I enjoyed the course but found it difficult to preform well on the 3 tests that make up the final grade. You MUST do the homework in order to pass. I did the homework, and barely scraped by. If you want to pass you need to put in the effort and have an affinity for what you are doing.

Entire grade is based on 15 proofs (3 exams 5 each). Many of them from the HW, some of them are the hardest, weirdest, least relevant questions in the book. We didn't cover half the material (eigenvectors and much of determinants), had to learn it on my own over summer. My only non-A in math, and it was a C, yet I understood the subject well...

1) Very fair grading (only 3 tests).There is no excuse for failing this class. 2) Very nice and helpful 3) Kept the class awake by getting to know names and having everyone participate in one way or another 4) DO THE FREAKING HOMEWORK. Seriously.  5) I didn't find his accent hard to understand, but I never have issues with accents in general.

Berkovich is a good teacher, although his accent is a little rough to understand sometimes. His writing isnt always clear but hes always more than welcome to change anything to be more legible if asked. MAKE SURE TO DO THE HOMEWORK. his tests are hw problems with the numbers changed. dont skip problems on hw and youll get a B, no problem.
Berkovich is the man. Do the HW and you will get at least a B.

Very hilarious and punny professor. First day of class I was worried because of his accent but he takes his time, repeats things, and makes sure everyone in the class understands the topic being covered. He really makes sure the class is involved. Just do the homework since the exams are based straight from the book.

Dr. Berkovich is a great professor. He will not let students get by without doing the work he gives. He gives a lot of homework, and his exams are literally homework problems word for word. They are not always easy, it would be hard to just memorize the answers to the homework (too many questions) but if you learn the material then you will be fine

He's really funny, I loved his class. He's also very helpful in office hours and usually sets up extra office hours if you need them. Grades are based on only three 5-question, uncurved tests, but all questions come from assigned homework. If you do ALL of the homework and make sure you understand it, you'll do well.
He is an awful teacher. He violated UF rules by not having a syllabus and violated it again by not having a set final. If you can avoid him by all means do!!

Professor Berkovich is one of the hardest math teachers you can take here. But he is extremely helpful if you ever have any questions and is pretty hysterical in class. Just remember to do all the homework that he assigns or you'll likely be in a lot of trouble for the class.

This man is off the chain! He's hard, but its because he cares that people learn mathematics the correct way. He is more than willing to help out outside of class, so take advantage! Great sense of humor as well. I highly recommend him if you want to learn some solid math (which you should want, if you take any course that he teaches).

Well, lets' just say that it is so hard to follow anything. He is one of the most hilarious men I have met, and he really knows the material.  I just don't think he is the best at conveying that to college students.  I'm a freshman and came from high school Calc 1. I thoroughly enjoy math and thought I would be ok, but you have to work very hard!

Dr.Berkovich is fantastic.  He is one of the funniest professors I've ever had, and he is really caring and encourages people to ask questions.  His class is really challenging, so make sure to do all of the hw, and ask him if you don't know how to.  He's always willing to help.  I LOVE HIM!

If you have the desire to learn the material you will not find anyone more capable of teaching it to you. He knows both the material and the pschology of teaching. However, if you are not prepared to engage in class and put in the effort this class will not work out for you, but if you want to learn math, this is the perfect professor.

I LOVE DR. BERKOVICH! He is hilarious.  I looked forward to going to class everyday because he cracks me up.  His accent is no problem.  He can remember the name of any student he's had in recent years..so if you see him on the street a year after you've had him, he will definately remember you :).

Very strong accent.  Material covered in class is mostly proofs.  Make sure to do ALL homework.  Tests are not too difficult.  He is also very helpful if you ask.  This class is VERY challenging for non math majors because he will go pretty fast over the material and leave you on your own for the homework.

Do all of the homework, no joke. The tests questions are not too difficult (because you've seen them all before in the HW) but beware: don't make any typos and make sure to explain everything you write very rigorously or you'll lose so many points you wont know what hit you. He will go above and beyond to help his students, just make an appointment

His tests are hard and mostly proof based, but he is a great professor that will help you out if you come to office hours.  Take his class if you want a challenge, you will learn a lot, and if you go to office hours and do well, you can get a good letter of recommendation.  Also, for Linear Algebra, our tests come directly from homework problems.

He is definitely intimidating at first, but he does care about his students.  Esp. if you participate in class and go to office hours.  I took Numbers and Polynomials during Summer A, which I really would NOT recommend doing.  His tests do take longer than the allotted time.  I would recommend taking his classes if you a easy-medium course load.

Moderately hard to get an A, but tremendously easy to pass--check out his grading scale.  BEWARE:  he will give you extra time on exams, but you are not entitled to it.  Be sure not to schedule a class right after any of his classes, or your grade will suffer.  Otherwise, a great professor with a great sense of humor.  His accent is NOT a problem.

You have to get used to him, then he'll be all right. Doesn't seem to believe in giving curves, but he'll be impressed if your attendence is good. Forces you to pay attention in class. His exams are fair but take longer than he promises them to take (be careful about scheduling a class after his.) Very dry and subtle sense of humor.
He's really hard, the tests are rough. Even if you do all the homework and go to class every day, it's difficult to get higher than a C

great professor, will spend countless hours helping students if necessary, actually cares about students, very understanding, if you work hard it will pay off, challenges students to think and strive to do the best they can
he is terrible

Not bad, but not the best I've seen in the math department either.  Homework is optional, and your final grade is just the average of your 3 test grades (there's no final exam).  Grades are never curved, but the scale isn't terrible:  standard 90% required for an A, but 80% is a B+, 70% is a B, etc.  Try to do all the homework and you'll be fine.
No Comments

No Comments
No Comments

Great guy. He's challenging and a little indimidating, but a great, great guy. Really cares about his students and makes sure to get them involved in class. Only take him if you're willing to accept a challenge!
No Comments

I am a math major. I thought that math was easy until this class. I would have failed the second test, but he was very empathetic to my confusion from the course and had mercy on me. He cares about the success of his students. Excellent man. Yea, kinda intimidating, but get used to it. Peace

He does seem intimidating at first but he's always willing to assist someone during and outside of office hours. He's pretty much a laid back guy who one can joke with, which is rare among professors.
One of the best teachers i've had at UF!!!!
I thoroughly enjoyed his class and his teaching methods.  He is really concerned about his students.
Makes class challenging but students learn a lot. He likes to get his students involved in class and with each other. Good guy
No Comments

At first he may seem a bit intimidating, but he is extremely helpful and easy to talk to when you get to know him.  The tests are challenging, but fair.  I had no trouble understanding him when he lectured. In fact, I am a math grad student because of him

At first i thought the class was really hard, but when i really studied and with dr. berkovich's help during his office hours i was able to get an A in the class. He was always willing to help students, even during times outside his office hours.

In the begining I was having alot of trouble in the class and seriously considered dropping the course. After Numerous discussions with Dr. Berkovich I decided to stay in the class, and with his assistance went from barley having a C+ to passing with a B
This was the worst teacher I ever had.  His tests were impossible, he speaks pretty much in russian, not english, and is totally un-helpful.  NEVER take him.

He is a challenging professor that pushes you to excel and do your best. Makes the material very interesting. Encourages participation from class. After taking DIFF.EQ with Berkovitch I decided to double-major in Mathematics.
Horrible teacher! Tortures students, impossible tests, thick accent, bad habits, and definitely not as funny as he thinks he is.

I had him for honors calc 2. I'm not sure exactly how many people were in the class to start with, but I know not many were left in the end. He seems to make the tests as hard as he can. And no curve. Bad handwriting. And an accent, but it's not too bad.
Not very hard to get a good grade, very in-depth on problem solving and not as in-depth conceptually.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nice lady but don't take her. You don't get any useful instruction and are required to learn the topics by reading through 3 worked out problems per module. Unfortunately the worked out problems aren't well annotated + some calculation steps are skipped. Also, her method is very odd so you cant use outside resources to cross-reference the content.

The grading system is harder to understand than the content itself, but the way it's taught is way over complicated compared to the way you'd conventionally solve these types of problems on the FE this is supposed to be preparing you for. Understanding her grading spreadsheets should land me a job in investment banking.

Flipped classroom, except the material you're expected to review before helps little with the problems that you're expected to solve in class. Attendance is mandatory for homework sessions that you don't really get anything out of, and the grading system requires you to do everything her way or you'll lose credit despite a right answer.

No teaching or lectures in class, but you must attend or your grade will suffer. She grades super weird, but it is very easy to get a passing grade. I don't know any dynamics after the class but i got an A-

I have always struggled in classes relating to statics and was very worried going into EGM3520. Baisley's flipped classroom style doesn't work for everyone but really helps you to fully understand the material. She gives quizzes instead of exams so you don't have to cram for large exams rather you can pace your studying weekly and fix mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took Matlab online for Summer A (really heavy workload), and she was pretty helpful. There were some technical issues with the software we used and she was pretty accommodating. Didn't actually lecture (they were pre-recorded) but responded to questions. I guess she's worse for Statics but it isn't the end of the world if you get her for Matlab.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Baisley cares about her students, but her executation is terrible. Imagine a flipped classroom where there is no instructional material for you to review before coming to class. You will often walk into class confused. Dr. Baisley and her TA's walk around for questions. But you won't know the content enough to ask a question. Its not worth it.
Not bad but not good

If Baisley has no fans, Im dead. I retook statics after having Jackson (whos god awful) Computing projects are NOT hard, just write alot. As someone with terrible mastery until the end, it is 100% possible to end with at least an A- if you take the final. As a type A person, the mini assessments made me less anxious bc its not exam heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a nice professor, but the grading system makes the experience extremely frustrating. Even with a good grade, you can fail the class by missing "mastery" by the end of the semester. Too few outside resources to help you solve homework problems/projects that can take hours. By the end I understood the process but not the "why"
The grading system makes understanding your grade a difficult process. While she is a very kind person, do not take this class.

This is for her EGM3400 Dynamics section.

You'll have little to no intuitive knowledge gained from this course, but partial credit will pass you and 2 credit hours means minimal impact on GPA.

'Learning' is through completing homework; there's no lecturing, some notes & OH is often needed to fully complete HW because you'll easily get stuck.

Dr. Baisely's class is really easy if you learn the method she wants you to use fast. Biweekly assessments, but they are not hard. Writing projects are tedious and a waste of time, something you are just going to have to get over. Easy class, but her method of solving problems is not actually efficient or practical but you have to do it her way.

Dr. Baisley is a fantastic Statics professor. Yes, her grading system is weird, yes, it's participation-heavy, but it's forgiving and ultimately makes the class much easier than what it could be. She's kind and responsive and, really, if you show up to class and do the homework, you'll get a good grade. Much better/easier than all the other profs.
Incredbely frustrating class, you can still fail even if your grade is above a fail, if you do not reach 5 mastery points. Additionally, you will not learn enough statics for MOM.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Gives ample opportunities to get points and boost your grade. No one exam is weighted heavily and the way her grading scheme is set up means its hard to ruin your score by doing poorly. Yes, there is a lot of homework and some large MATLAB projects, but they help boost your grade. Statics is hard, but this class makes it and a good grade possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a very nice lady who cares about what she teaches. She treats the class like it is kindergarten. You get a grade multiplier for participating. There are three computing projects that do enhance your understanding of the material, but are extremely tedious with an unclear grading structure. She doesn't lecture, and you learn by doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: you are graded more on your personality than your ability to do math and physics. ive taken statics before, definitely a difficult course, she makes it more unnecessarily difficult with how she offers almost no resources. no recommended textbook, no online resources, she does provide examples and some lectures but it is only two lectures per module

Her grading style is honestly really nice. Yes there are 7 exams and a final, but they are super low stress, and if you BOMB one or two it doesn't hurt you in the slightest. I only really studied for the final. She gives grade boosts for showing up to class. The projects are annoying, probably take ~6 hours each but there are only three.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: While I appreciate Dr. Baisley's attempt to make the course more student-friendly, her non-traditional format is a work in progress. She's kind and the class is easy to pass, but the flipped classroom, complicated grading system, and difficult homework problems made the class more stressful and tedious then I think she intended.

I really enjoyed having Professor Baisley for statics. The mastery system can throw some people off but I ended up liking it. The computing projects can be annoying to do. Overall the class is very straightforward.

Avoid this professor. Every fifth class period during the semester is an exam. She grades based on a mastery scale so you won't know your grade till the final. You have to master 6 out of the 10 objectives six times each in the class to earn a minimum of a C. Each exam is one problem. If you tend to miss class, avoid taking this class.
Took online MATLAB, was very attentive and gave clear deadlines. Gave extensions when the autograder went down.

Class had no tests, instead was made up of assessments that went building up your score which was then converted to your grade at the end of the semester. There were also three projects throughout the semester that were straight forward but tedious. Take her for statics if you prefer not having tests.

Easy to mess up, but if put in work then good grades follow. Work is almost directly correlated to grade for this class, and also she gives alot of work to do.

For MOM I'd study Jeff Hanson videos before, it's pretty easy to catch up. 
I would take her again.

Because this course's format (7 "mini exams" and a final) is relatively new, it's imperfect. But those who whine about how "awful" and "stupid" this class is need some maturing to do. If you aren't a good test taker or otherwise dislike high stakes exams, this class is an excellent choice.
Lack of understanding of the content. Not very good feedback. She just look busy.

This is a class that will eat up a good amount of your time; however, she must have made changes to her mastery system, because unlike the many negative comments, I found the grading criteria to be pretty clear and she always provides detailed feedback after every assessment and project. The projects are, admittedly, unnecessarily long.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I am not the best student. I was on probation engineering and barely made it out alive. I was very scared going into this class and hearing about the mastery grading system, but I believe this is the best way to learn topics in engineering. If you frequent office hours you will do well. Great experience overall, you just need an open mind.

You don't really know your grade throughout the semester. Make sure to follow the scoring system the way she does it on her practice problems for full credit. The tests are easier than homework. The projects are kinda directionless and you just have to make something up. Make sure to come to class to get engagement points. easy class overall though

i was skeptical of her after reading reviews but after giving it a shot, I really enjoyed her. grading is hard to get used to but, it turns out to be fine. she really cares about her students and wants them to do well and explains things really clearly. I totally recommend her. shes also a genuinely nice person who wants to get to know you.
She is Bing Chilling, amazing professor and would not want anyone else to guide me through statics. She actually cares about her students.
I never thought I would love a class more than Statics with Amie Baisley. She is such a caring professor that actually cares about her student. I could not recommend her more
Baisley is a needle in a haystack. She is so underrated and I wish more people would hear her out.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The class is honestly extremely difficult, however, after looking at the quality of student sitting next to me, it is clearly a skill issue on their part. Amie Baisley is not as bad as everyone says and I would sacrifice my second born child for her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I cannot praise Dr. Baisley for the amazing work she has done creating such a great class. I would sacrifice first born child to see her live another lifetime.
Baisley singlehandedly stopped me from changing my major, definitely recommend.

I'm not quite sure what's with all the 1 star reviews on here. Her teaching style is definitely different from other professors and takes time to get used to, but she makes the grading scale and expectations very clear. If you come to class, complete the assignments, and ask questions, you are going to do well enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Impossible to know your grade until the very end, waste of time projects that only just stress you out, think your doing good because you get practically 100s on every exam then end up with just barely an A- because you didn't breath correctly while in class.
If you are willing to do the work, you will earn a solid grade and really understand Statics.

The best example of a flipped classroom. One 20 min lecture per unit (7 lectures total) then class time is working on problems in groups with TA's and professor. Put in the effort to show up to class and ask questions and you WILL succeed. Most people who don't like the class just don't understand the grading scale, but she helps you through it
If I could give her a 0 I would give her a 0
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: avoid at all costs. please.

Everyone gives Dr.Baisley a bad wrap, and it is somewhat deserved. However, looking back on the class, it was structured for us to succeed. She's very open about the unique grading scale and it kind of worked. DO NOT go into this class expecting it to be like your typical course. If you can accept that and put in the work to succeed you will.

A very nice and understanding professor. The mastery grading method she uses was very confusing at first but I kinda got a hang of it, but it'd definitely something that I was a bit thrown off by at first. She doesn't do much in terms of lectures and it's very self taught, but class time does offer a lot of time to ask questions to her or the TA's.

Get ready to teach yourself and know that there are coding projects/reports in this class. Only "teaching" is a video or two per module, and there are no lectures otherwise. Showing up to class plays a huge role in your grade.

I am a senior Electrical Engineer graduating this semester. This class does not affect me at all.

Terrible Homework Structure
Projects are a waste of time and graded subjectively
No lecture material was given other than 9 videos
Be prepared to teach yourself

Worst class in 4 years of UF by far

I would give a zero if I could

Please avoid
