reviews.comment: Horrendous professor. Doesn't even lecture, and the provided materials are abysmal. When I asked for more material or other places to look she discouraged me from any outside learning saying that everything we needed to know was provided. Gives ridiculous matlab projects that are worthless and only serve as busywork. Grading scale is inconsistent.
Really sets you up for disaster for future courses that require MOM.

Nice lady and all. Knows her stuff and responds quickly. Class is organized horribly, though. Flipped class model, subjectively graded computing projects in MATLAB (without MATLAB prereq), no makeup assessments, "mastery based" grading leaving you with little knowledge of your overall grade mid semester. Headache of a class, but not major-changing.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: The worst teacher I've ever had. The grading system is unlike anything you've ever seen. There are "computing projects" that have nothing to do with the course content or even statics at all. She relies way too heavily on format and not actually learning the material. She doesn't teach, she posts videos and notes that are confusing and useless.

Professor Baisley is by no means uneducated on the subject of statics. The issue lies in the way that her class was "taught" (you teach yourself) and her unique grading scale. There are many instances of basic concepts being very overcomplicated. Professor Baisley is very nice and helpful, but her class is definitely an acquired taste for most.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: WORST professor Ive ever had trust me do not listen to any of the good reviews. with all my heart she should get fired. she does not teach. you have to learn on your own then ask her questions like bruh JUST TEACH IDK WHAT IDK. highest grade i can get is C- and thats still way higher than the class average. take anyone else but her

This is by far the worst professor at UF. She has an extremely weird grading system, that no student is able to know their grade in the class until the end of the semester. Shes rude and offers no help to her students. She makes you do computing projects that have no value and are just busy work that is very hard to complete and do well. AVOID!!!

Taking her for mechanics of materials since I enjoyed her statics class so much. She is extremely helpful and approachable, answers emails really quickly. Her grading system is mastery based, so you start at 0 and gain points. Not for everyone, but I found it more forgiving. Class is easy if you keep up with hw and go to office hours.

You gonna learn nothing, trust! She knows what she is teaching, for sure, but she doesn't know how to teach nor give a clear and constructive feedback. She is accessible, but yet, her explanation is just her repeating herself from the 30 min lectures that she makes us watch. If you wanna learn something, not just copying stuff, don't take her class

Professor Baisley for statics was the worst educational experience I have had in my time at UF. Awful procedure for homework and convoluted computing projects that suck up time while providing no real benefit. If the course had more resources than just her examples and 30 min lectures maybe you could try and actually learn the material on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All the comments with Quality 1.0 and Difficulty 5.0 are accurate. So let me persuade you to not take this class. With this class, you will contemplate dropping out of college and you will get burnt out. The lectures you watch will be filled with jargon and the homeworks and projects will make you cry. Please don't take this class lol
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I didn't trust the professor rating and I was wrong. After taking this class I can assure you avoiding this class is in your best interest. She is nice but she makes the class itself so hard. You will never know how you are doing because there is no grade. Intense projects and you have to cater all your work specific to her liking. AVOID IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: brief 30 min video and you are left to figure out all the details of every problem on your own. No textbook. No nothing. DO NOT TAKE any of her classes

Just an awful professor. I really hate to be mean and rude, but why is she even teaching this class still. I was forced to take her EGM3520 class because there were no options available, and I am really not learning anything. The Homework is insane, I spend atleast 2-3 hours solving each problem, and she doesn't actually teach anything herself

Absolutely worst teacher I have ever had. Do not take. You wont feel like you are solving the problems, just copying her extremely tedious format and trying to apply it to something else. Computing projects are ridiculous and pointless. Expect to spend a lot of time trying to figure these problems out on your own with no help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Baisley is possibly the most ineffective instructor I have ever had. Crazy HW format, virtually no lectures, horrid 'tests', & no real grading. Expects you to learn from classmates during mandatory meetings, a huge mistake between uninspired engineering students. Luckily she is only a lecturer as she is not fit for the title of professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unnecessarily complicated class. MATLAB projects and weird grading scale were terrible. I am taking Mechanics of Materials now and I have to unlearn the excessive problem solving process she has taught.

Just don't do it. The lectures are so vague and pointless and you have to teach yourself everything. I passed by a miracle and didn't learn a single thing. She makes you do MATLAB projects even if you have zero experience with it and all my friends in other sections could confirm that she made it extremely hard for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture Vids only gave understanding of very basic surface concepts. Left to your own to actually learn anything. MATLAB projects are pointless and she expects you to turn it into an experiment - 1 semester later I still don't get it. Non-standard grading methods, never understood requirements to pass the class, much less do well. AVOID AT ALL COST

Barely any lectures and you are left to learn everything by yourself, but her way of doing problems is so specific that you cannot find it anywhere else. The workload is absurd. Take any other professor she is the worst professor I have ever had by far.

She is a nice lady but does not know how to teach. She does not teach you anything herself. She gives you examples that aren't similar to the homework she gives. Has her own way of doing problems that is so unnecessary and a waste of time. Wont know what your grade is till the end of the semester. Projects are horrible and are due along with hw.
Really?

Seriously this is the worst class I've ever taken. I'm only half a semester in and I'm going insane with the amount of assignments I get. On top of the assesment every week and 4 computing projects this semester. I probably don't know anything considering the fact that she over complicates everything for no reason.

As a tutor for EGM2511, I cannot stress enough that you should choose another professor. Her style of teaching sets the student up for failure and encourages "bashing" the problem, instead of thinking logically about it. Students who take this course are left at a disadvantage in their future courses at the University of Florida. Please avoid.

We had one lecture every two weeks where she taught basic concepts and we were expected to learn everything else on our own. Worst of all, I am in Mechanics of Materials now, and I feel severely under prepared. She made everything way too complicated so you end up learning nothing from the course. My statics skills are severely lacking now.

One of the worst professors I have had at UF so far. The class might as well be a class in Powerpoint and MATLAB but she doesnt teach you how to use them for the class. Problems take hours of setup before you can even begin the solution. Grading System is bad. I dont have enough characters left to list all. FOR THE LOVE OF MATH DONT TAKE HER CLASS.

Wanted to like the odd structure of this class, but didn't. Spent more time typing up the homework problems to get credit than actually understanding the problems I was doing. Typing up the problems was especially tedious when her method takes 3x longer to do each problem than how normally taught. She is really nice and passionate, but wouldn't rec

Prof. Baisley teaches her course very differently than any other course I have ever taken. It is a bit confusing but her teaching strategy can be very effective. The homework and projects can be very tedious and long at times but it will teach you a unique way of approaching problems, which I found very useful. Not an easy A but a great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: garbage class. Don't take her. She got her PHD about teaching statics (waste of time) and tries to force her weird grading and class setup on us. MATLAB heavy for no reason, strict deadlines, doesn't actually teach, non stop groupwork, 10+ hours of tedious powerpoint homework (most of the time is spent just formatting)

She only lectures once ever other week and expects you to teach yourself. There are 7 midterms, a final, and 4 programming projects in MATLAB with a paper. All assignments need to be typed on PowerPoint which is really tedious. Her grading is super unclear so you never know what you have in the class. I would not recommend this class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: You will have weekly homework that will take 8+ hours because she makes you turn in a powerpoint, on top of monthly MATLAB projects that will take you 20+ hours. The class is broken into modules, but she doesn't actually lecture on it until after you're mostly done with the module. There are no redeeming qualities to this course. Take anyone else.

Organized. Good, but full Office Hours. Unreasonable expectations. Expects you to know Matlab+No grades until the end of the year. You aren't going to be able to spend the 25 hours a week to finish the HW (not hard, but statics must be done on PowerPoint) + 10-70 hrs for each coding project (once a month) with 8+ page report (with proofs + words).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Tough grader--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Cancels class way too much and loads make-up work onto students

Professor Phalin is a great lecturer and makes class interesting despite content sometimes being boring. Definitely utilize the cheat sheet she allows you to have on the exam. I used smokin notes to help me figure out the most important information to put on it and it was a life saver!

This class was pretty easy, I didn't use Smokin' Notes, just went to all the lectures and participated. You get a full page of notes, so memorization wasn't an issue. She also gives you a template for this sheet which is really helpful and makes sure you don't miss anything you should have on your cheat sheet.

A white midwestern lady who studied abroad in France isn't my idea of global minded. It's definitely seen in her personal opinions and teachings of the class. Sometimes it's belittling. There was a student this semester that tried to advocate for her country and it was hard to watch. The class isn't too bad as long as you watch the content well.

Professor Phalin gives you everything you need to succeed through the lecture material. However, make sure to pay attention to little details as anything is fair game for homeworks/exams. Some advice is to go slow through the lectures to make sure to avoid missing anything. SmokinNotes is helpful to review materials before the exam.

Could not watch her lectures because she had a very condescending vibe. However, the material itself wasn't too difficult and she gives you everything that you need to succeed. We are allowed one double-sided page of notes for each exam; however, the information is often so specific. There's a group project which isn't too bad.

Professor Phalin's class is straightforward if you stay on top of the work. Participate, take detailed notes, and leverage resources like Unstuck AI along with the lectures. The exams are fact-based, but she provides everything needed to succeed. Overall a solid class.

Not a good professor. She was so rude to students. Presumptuous, quick to judge, unhelpful, are but a few of qualities. It's almost as if she is miserable and wants to spread her misery to her students. Class was boring. She did allow her political leanings to come through whether or not people are aware enough to pick up on it is a different story

Capsim is a nightmare, but she's super lenient when it comes to grading it. My group was consistently in last place and I still ended with an A. Her lectures are good and actually helpful. The questions she writes suck sometimes and more than one answer could be correct. TONS of extra credit, make sure you do it all. Exams are okay.

Professor Phalin formats the class so you are able to do well even if you struggle on the exams. So many extra credit opportunities, but DO NOT FORGET to do them. Her exams are very specific, but if you watch the lectures she mentions everything that's on the exam at some point. Do not waste money on smokin' notes, just watch the lectures.

Dr. Phalin is very nice and her lectures were super engaging. I learned a lot from this course! Smokin Notes definitely helped me study for exams and organize my information. To succeed in the course, I recommend not getting behind in Capsim, taking advantage of the cheat sheets that you can make for exams, and study the Smokin notes.

One of the worst professors at UF. She is very liberal and it comes through during her lectures. She thinks she knows better than everyone else. Is extremely rude and abrasive. As long as you don't ask her any questions or interact with her, you'll make it through the class. Not sure why she has such good reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: participation matters!! TAKE SPECIFIC NOTES. The only way you get less than a B in this class is if you are lazy. You can use notes on every single assignment, but that's because she is VERY specific and detailed (i.e. what's the GDP of China in 2020, the growth post-COVID in USA?). didn't love her attitude, doesn't like to repeat herself ever

Dr Phalin is a great professor, she teaches the material well. Weekly quizzes and exams are easy, all the info is on the PowerPoints. The group project takes a while to get a hand off, but once you do, easy. Make sure to get a good group though! I spent ~2.5h on this class a week. 
Only downside is that she makes her political opinion clearly known

Professor Phalin teaches a completely useless course. The exams are almost entirely (80%) about memorizing obscure facts about a specific country. On top of that, she berates you with 4 assignments per week that are difficult to score well on. Overall, an out of touch professor. No one cares what the GDP growth rate is in 2020 for Canada...

Participate in the Capsims and study the lecture slides for the exams, and you should have an A in the class. She provides lots of extra credit opportunities and allows a full sheet of notes for the exam.

Dr. Phalin is great. She clearly knows the material and she's also incredibly kind. Lectures are clear and exams are very straight forward. She provides everything you need to succeed. Capsim is a little confusing at first, but you quickly get the hang of it. She also provides weekly extra credit. Would love to take another class of hers.
DO NOT USE SMOKIN NOTES SHE DOES NOT LIKE SMOKIN NOTES and she makes a point to give you all the materials you need, watch her lectures and exam reviews and you will be fine.

this was by far my favorite class. She is not a very good communicator, but the syllabus and lectures are so detailed that you literally don't need any other resources. Make sure to get a great team for Capsim; otherwise, you will be doing all the work.

This online class requires no interaction between the professor and the student. Make sure to submit CapSim and double-check because she will not give credit even if you've been a high-performing student. 

She has no empathy for mistakes, so don't make them.

This class is not hard nor are the assignments. The problem with the class is the professor. She takes way to long to make a point in lectures. The assignments and exams just promote memorization especially if you are not lucky enough to write the GDP of japan in 2021. She is very curt in emails. The simulation is the best thing in the class.

If you're going to use Smokin' Notes to prepare for exams, be prepared to get a B on the exams. The first exam is by far the easiest exam, get an A on 1st. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT, it's easy to miss just a few questions and receive a B on exams. Develop a competent CAPSIM team or your grade will suffer - build a diverse team of different majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Best Class in the business program. This is one of those classes you get the "A" in to boost your GPA.
Professor was also nice and super helpful.

Do all the extra credit! It will give you a cushion for the exams, which are super specific. Smokin notes is not as necessary as it is in other classes, but it definitely helps if you don't want to sit through lectures and assigned readings. The capsim assignments are pretty easy, just get a good group/carefully read through instructions.

Do not be overwhelmed by the massive syllabus and amount of material she provides. The team project represents a lot of the grade, so make sure you have a good structure to how you and your team handles the simulation. Make sure to do all of the extra credit, she gives a lot of it. As long as you do all assignments, should be an A.

DO THE EXTRA CREDIT. If you're planning on using smokinnotes for this class, be prepared to get a B on the exams. Smokinnotes leaves out crucial details, which results in getting a few questions wrong on the exams. If you do all the extra credit and form a competent group for CAPSIM, you'll have no problem getting an A+ in this course.

Two main points
1. Capsim: Make a text group chat w your Capsim team asap. If you set up just 1x weekly 1hr Zoom call together you'll knock each round out
2. Grades/Exams: Do all the Extra Credit opportunities. Also, review the answers to the HWs + Practice Exam for each upcoming exam as most of the Exam Qs are pulled directly from these banks

Overall a great class, Dr. Phalin approaches lectures with enthusiasm and updates the class with current events. My only complaint was that she makes a lot of effort to trick you on questions rather than testing your knowledge. She makes up for this with a lot of extra credit opportunities, really no excuse to get below 90% overall in her class...

The lectures are actually interesting. Capsim is relatively easy (once you figure it out), and if you have good teammates. There are plenty of assignments and extra credit opportunities. The exams aren't bad, especially if you do the practice exams.

Lectures are extremely long and boring, sometimes totaling up 6-8 hours a week of lecture. I recommend skipping the lectures for Smoking Notes, as it is unbearable to sit through one of her lectures. The content and homework is very easy, and the Capsim simulation is actually really fun.
Get ready for hours of lectures and her being extremely political.  She says she isn't, but lord, she is.  Just teach the class lady.  The Capsim assignments are a joke.

Course and professor are not too demanding. Lectures are straightforward and she seems very approachable and honest. Don't recommend if you are a snowflake republican because she cites facts relating to government history and operation.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class but terrible lectures. She's all over the place and included her political viewpoints way too frequently. The class felt extremely left leaning which was very frustrating. Keep your views out of the classroom. Easy to get an A though as long as you get a good group.
Easiest professor at UF. She gives so much extra credit and her practice exams are so similar to the real exam. Never watched a lecture and earned an A. She's also the sweetest human being ever!!

Dr. Phalin is a great professor. Her lectures are really interesting, but kind of long. She gives a ton of extra credit throughout the semester. The tests are pretty easy if you watch the lecture and you don't really need to watch the RMPF stuff, just look through the slides. Also, you can use the front and back of a sheet of paper on the exam.

I would say this was easiest class of the 7 business classes. The class is made up of a virtual business simulation with a group, 3 exams, and homework's on each country. She gave a ton of extra credit and the exams were pretty easy if you study the Smokin Notes.
Great Professor, Professional, very caring of Students. Class was fun and didn't stress you out. Loved my time in Professor Phalin's class.

Dr. Phalin was the great! This class can be a fairly easy A if you just do the work and she gives you SO MUCH extra credit. Capsim project was so much fun it barely felt like schoolwork. You don't even need the smokin notes.. just watch the lectures on 2x speed before exam time. Would definitely take again & highly recommend.

Best professor ever!! She truly wants everyone to pass & gives a lot of extra credit. Exams aren't difficult as long as you study the practice exams and homework questions. There are kind of a lot of assignments but all of them are simple & there is a group project but she makes it hard to fail.

Took Dr. Phalin's course due to a requirement but she is a gem. Class is very easy to pass, don't fret if you bomb CAPSIM. Tons of extra credit, exams are not designed to trick you, and she really tries to help students. Some students had tech issues with the third exam, so everyone got a perfect score. Not many profs would do that. She's a gem.

Dr. Phalin is the best professor I've taken at UF. She let's you have an entire page of notes for the exams, gives tons of extra credit, and quickly responds to emails. She truly cares about seeing her students succeed. Something many of the professors I've taken in the past lack.

Dr. Phalin is nice. She offers tons of extra credit; if you do all of it and get Smokin Notes you should be fine. Her exam and quiz questions are ridiculously specific but you get to use an 8x11 sheet of paper on exams and get 2 attempts on quizzes. Her lectures are pretty lengthy but watching on 2x makes them tolerable!

Dr. Phalin is super sweet and nice. She has tons of credits for you to make sure you are getting a good grade. She just change the business simulation to a group project this semester which is easier but it is still pretty annoying. She usually responses to emails quickly. She start allowing us to bring one print paper note this semester for exam

Hands down one of the best professors I have ever had. She gives tons of extra credit, her lectures are really interesting and exams are not difficult at all. If you actually keep up with the work, Its an easy A.

If you ever have the misfortune of having to deal with Phalin personally--even just in email--you'll find that she's the definition of condescending. On the other hand, her class is interesting and easy enough to do well in if you get Smokin Notes...

There is no excuse not to do well in this class. She gives SO MANY extra credit opportunities, and is very generous and understanding. The simulation is very straightforward, and she makes the material interesting and engaging.

One of the best professors at UF by far. She REALLY wants you to succeed in the class!! Throughout the semester she offered a ton of extra credit. Even at the end, she changed the pop quiz to no time limit, and she didn't have to! That was very nice of her. Definitely stay on top of the lectures and homework! Exams are similar to homework.

Prof Phalin is very understanding and provides plenty of opportunities for points besides exams, tons of easy extra credit too. I didn't watch many lectures but the ones that I did, she seemed very good at explaining the content. Get Smokin Notes for the exams and do the Capsim simulation and you should be good!

loved dr. phalin for the spring 2021 semester. she offered OODLES of extra credit, which really brought my grade up tremendously. do it all, even if you don't think you'll need it. second exam is much more difficult than the first, but if you pay attention and prepare thoroughly, you'll be fine. capsim is difficult, but fun.

Is it your senior year? Well, enjoy Hell, because this class was way harder than expected. She made the syllabus quiz hard just to drive the knife in. I swear to God she intentionally tries to trick you on tests, twisting the knife. Studied my a** off, got a decent grade, but most likely developed an ulcer from her test questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr Phalin is great! Class is relatively easy with simple quizzes for each chapter, 2 exams and the CAPSIM Simulation. I hated CAPSIM but as long as you do it, you get at least 75% and 100% for the training modules. I got 75% on almost all and still ended with an A. No textbook - Watch lecture and do sim without effort. Lots Extra Credit! Easy! :)

Phalin is passionate about the content and does a good job explaining it. Do not worry about getting the textbook or watching the lectures. You can pass simply by reading the powerpoint yourself. The majority of the class is completion points. Exams are useless Jeopardy style questions that don't test your actual knowledge. LOTS of Extra Credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Probably the easiest of the business 7 cores. 2 Exams (which werent bad), a bunch of easy quizzes/HW, a LOT of free points and CAPSIM make up your grade. There was A TON of extra credit, some of which was pretty random. PowerPoints and lectures were informative, the textbook didnt really help. Smokin notes also helped. Dr. Phalin was really good

I was surprised by the other rating here from this semester. My friends and I loved the class. Lectures were NOT boring. She gives tons of extra credit (even more than is in the syllabus so always be looking for announcements about other extra credit). AND she took a whole chapter off one test since she said everyone is stressed with covid.

Phalin's lectures are basically useless as she just reads straight from the PowerPoint. She also assigns a staggering amount of material that she wants you to read/watch outside of class instead of teaching it herself. She was also very rude via email to myself and a friend on separate occasions when we tried to ask her questions about lecture.

Loves international business and is invested in her students success. The only professor that can keep me engaged for 2 hours! Gives lots of assignments which are great for keeping your grade up. Get smokin notes and keep up with the many assignments.

Dr. Phalin was fantastic! Apart from the great course material she offers so much extra credit! She tells you exactly what's going to be on the exam and includes current events as well as lecture and textbook material. She does have ridiculously long powerpoints but her lectures are fun and interactive.

Her class was the only core business class in which I religiously watched lectures. She is an amazing professor. Exams aren't an easy A, but very easy to get at least a B. Pay attention to the deadlines! Also, do as much extra credit as you can! If you reach out to her she will help you however she can as long as she sees you put in effort.

Dr. Phalin is a great professor who is genuinely engaged and really knows her stuff. There are a ton of deadlines in the class, but it is not very hard work, and there are a lot of opportunities for extra credit. Homework, two exams and a pop quiz, Capsim and Pearson for extra credit. Good class, great professor.

Lectures are AWESOME. There's lots of them but mostly really interesting and she's so nice. Would've given her a 5/5-but she gave a pop quiz DURING EXAM WEEK. She made it seem like she was being nice by giving a quiz instead of a final exam, but gave it on a week when I had 3 other finals! So annoying. Left me w a bad feeling about a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easily the best class I have ever taken at UF. Don't waste your time on Smokin' Notes, they sometimes get the info wrong too. WATCH LECTURE!! For exams, print out the slides and review them. She really is passionate about what she's talking about. You have to earn this A, but it is 100% possible if you put in the work. She offers A LOT of E.C. too

You have group presentations every week so you need to really get the know your random teammates early on to be successful. The current event presentation is a good way to find a topic she likes and go with it to try to get extra credit. Must speak up in class to get attendance for that day. Very nice and learned a lot but you need to put in effort
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I really struggled in this class initially because I thought I could rely on Smokin' Notes, but you really can't. It's too much information and you gotta keep up with lectures and readings. The simulation is really tough but she offers extra credit for reading current events. Exams have a ton of information but are doable.
Dr Phalins International Business class has been my favorite at UF so far. She is fascinating and informative. Highly recommend!

Don't bother emailing her questions because she'll just respond "check the syllabus". As for the class its really not hard. Smokin notes for exams, for the hw look at the power point slides, nothings on google. capsim can be tricky at first but if you follow the strategy that the TA's use and the practice one that phalin shows you you'll get it.

Dr. Phalin is extremely smart and knows more than an average person could know. Lots of work, and exams/ homework can be confusing. She truly cares about her students, and is great help if you ask questions. Capsim stimulation can be extremely hard and she knows that so you can receive 15/20 points for just doing it. Keep up with lectures for an A!

Loved the class! Lectures are so interesting and I feel like I really learned a lot. Simulation is hard but tests are easy and questions are like the practice tests and homework. Also I emailed her a few times and she always wrote back right away. Some professors in these big classes dont reply so I liked how she did so fast.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class is very easy but Prof Phalin tries to make it as annoying as possible. Tons of assignments and two exams. All the answers to the homework are in the power point slides. Get smokin notes unless you plan on watching all the lectures and reading the book. Capsim program is hard at first but once you get the hang of it its easy.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I would definitely suggest watching the lectures rather than Smoking Notes. There were some errors in the smokin notes and she refers to the lecture in exams. This is a super interesting class and she's a really good lecturer. Biggest thing is to stay on top of due dates.

Dr. Phalin is passionate and a very good lecturer. She explains things very well and will make sure you understand the concept before she moves on. Her class is very well organized and her expectations are clearly defined. She was one of my favorite professors.

A class with a lot of assignments but not that hard to do. I recommend not reading textbook but takes notes during lectures, study the PPs for each chapter that is needed daily, those will help you. Homeworks are from PPs study those as well after you're finished. GLOBALDNA seems intimidating at first but once you start doing it it's very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Great class. Dr. Phalin makes you understand tough topics. She leaves no room for confusion, syllabus is clear. Group project is awesome.

Insightful course! You learn so much from all countries and Dr. Phalin makes the topics incredibly interesting. She is also accessible, she wants you to succeed! The group project is fun, my group always got first place. So, just follow the guidelines and you will do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I didn't expect to like this class. It's required. But Dr. Phalin totally opened my eyes to things happening in the world. Now I've decided to have a career in international business! Yes, lots of deadlines but the syllabus is really clear. I also liked talking to her outside of class. She's super nice and knows a lot.

Be aware of time management as her 21 page syllabus states there are lots of deadlines. She is passionate about what she teaches and you will be immersed in current events which effects the business world. Do NOT rely on Smokin' Notes she reads them and forms exams around them requiring true knowledge of the subject.

Not hardly enough time to complete very wordy questions, they are so bad they are almost trick questions. good thing I did well in the rest of the class or I would have had less than a B. Overall the class was ok, she over focuses on bad students from the past and tells you up front she has no compassion or flexibility. It is just a class...
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor really cares so if you put in the work it should be easy to get an A.
I really enjoyed this class. Very informative! Keeps you up to date with current events. The group project was time consuming and confusing at times.

Dr. Phalin's lectures are interesting, especially compared to other business professors I've had. There are a lot of assignments, but none of them are really difficult. The one thing I disliked was the group Global DNA simulations. I had a group that didn't seem to care, but extra credit can cover this part of your grade. I enjoyed this class.

I came here to say that Dr. Phalin's lectures are some of the best I ever heard at UF. She really does make you want to listen and learn, and I really liked the simulation. Yes there are lots of assignments and due dates, but I liked that my grade didn't just depend on a few exams.

I thought she was an awesome professor! There are TONS of due dates so stay organized and write them all down at the beginning of the semester.  Exams look exactly like the practice exams so you know what to expect. Smokin' Notes definitely helps but all of the information you'll need is in the PowerPoint slides. Gives extra credit.

You miss one detail and you are done. She packs on tons of assignments with loads of criteria to follow to a T. As a full-time online student (w/ a full time job), I don't think she understands that just maneuvering around all her loads of crap is hard enough. She treats you like a slacker if you can't keep up with it all and it feels demeaning.

I loved this class! Professor Phalin is really passionate and makes you interested. I would say go to her office hours too. She gave me great advice about grad school and internships. I agree with others about lots of assignments and staying on top of it all. You need to be organized for sure.

I got a job because of Dr. Phalin's class. She talks about current events and ties it all to what we learn in class so you can really use it later when you need to, like in an interview! Lots of assignments and dates to remember, though, so be organized.

Good lecturer but poor professor.  Focuses on route memorization of her materials almost exclusively.  She thinks route memorization of her materials is more important than understanding concepts.  Would not recommend.  I would change my major or drop out of school before I would ever take one of the classes again!

This class was challenging and forced me to learn. The tests were not too hard, you just have to read the book, do practice exams and homework. Your grade is heavily affected by the group project, and you compete with other students for the high grade. You have to do well on tests or you may not do well in the class because of this.
I love this class. Prof. Phalin is THE BEST.

Dr. Phalin is very passionate about the subject, making it easy to learn the material. She will not make any exceptions if you fall behind, so stay on top of your assignments. I enjoyed the lectures and learned a lot about the real world, gaining an interest in the subject. This class is making ECO3713 a breeze!

I liked her a lot. She is one of the few teachers who actually really enjoys the subject she is teaching. She truly wants her students to learn and become interested in the subject. I liked the subject matter. Tests aren't too too hard but if you want to make an A you better know your stuff. Don't get the book.

This was my favorite professor in my entire college career. She is just the sweetest, and if you're confused on something her office door is always open and she is so understanding. The material is interesting, she posts current events to make the material relevant to what's going on in the world, and just try and you'll get an A

Very fair teacher! Her tests are rather easy and then she packs the rest of the class with a ton of fluff grades. She is a bit rude and condescending at times but that really shouldn't matter. Put in the work and you will get an A!

Dr. Phalin was the best professor I've had at the COB! She was always so sweet. I loved the way the class was set up. MSM people reading: take her in fall! Don't wait to take MAN6636! The only class I actually want to go! Two group projects: one really long one, one really short one. But the stuff you learn is very interesting and applicable.

LOVED Phalin! Tests were extremely fair and she is passionate about what she teaches. Read the text, watch the lecture, take notes, study, and you'll get an A. Basically, just don't be lazy and you'll get an A. Would take more of her classes! She's also always quick to respond to emails.

I love professor Phalin. I saw on here a past student blaming that being married and and a mom for not getting an A. I am a mom and married and I got an A.  Watch the lectures, read the book , do the practice quizes and homework, there is no excuse not to do well. Also glad I took this before International Macroeconomics.

I only got a B- in this class, but that was my own fault. I'm married with a job and a baby, and didn't put enough effort into this course. With that being said, a full-time student should easily be able to get an A! Even with my minimal studying, I managed to pass all the exams. There's also 30 easy points of extra credit. I really loved her!

I really, really loved this class.  Dr. Phalin was super interesting and I thought the class was really easy.  People have written that she's difficult but all you have to do is take notes and listen to the lectures.  The final was a breeze and I got an easy A.  Great class, though.  Learned lots.

Since the first day of class she's had an unsettling "Not My Problem" attitude towards her students. She's one of those people that's very 'rules-based' and unaccommodating. This class is a perfect example of UF trying to make pointless classes unnecessarily difficult. Her lectures are not worth your time, Smokin' Notes are the way to go.

Honestly, this class is only difficult if you don't do anything. I watched the lectures on double speed and took notes, and studied by taking the quizzes and reading my notes a couple times. I have a pretty good memory, but you just need to know the concepts/ some details. Phalin interacts in class but her overall attitude is "Not my problem."
Class should be do-able but teacher totally kills it. Not helpful, and kind of rude. Everything is going to be YOUR problem, and there are lots of rules. Not willing to help, at all.

she carries herself in such an arrogant and unhelpful way and  makes her tests very VERY specific and seems like she is out to fail students. no extra credit and a 93 is an A. ridiculous for a business core course. she is the kind of person that if you asked for a recommendation, she would probably right something negative just to screw you over.

class is interesting and the material is simple/easy to understand, but her test questions do not reflect that.  I am microbio/finance double major and even though I got an A- in the class it was tough.  Based on the material and the text book this should be an easy A but professor Phalin is out to make it the most difficult class for no reason.

This was one of my favorite courses at UF. Professor Phalin made the lectures interesting with lots of personal examples and videos. Most of the lectures come straight from the book, so read the chapters a couple of times and you'll do well on the exams. I highly recommend this class.

This class wasn't difficult, but the way the exams were set up made the class harder than it should have been. Since almost all of your grade is from exams, you really have to do well on them, and the grading scale is pretty tough (93% = A). I suggest over preparing for the 1st exam, really focus on the small details, I was caught off-guard a bit.

As long as you watch/go to the lectures and study you can get an A. It really is doable. I finished with an A-. She does like to test on small details as opposed to major concepts (minute percentages, facts) so just be thorough. Use her practice exams as a guideline for studying. Textbook was kind of a waste, Powerpoints really cover all material.

I don't know what the people who have rated her so far are thinking. She is highly qualified to be teaching the class, her class is informative and highly doable. The 2nd test is by far the hardest, the first and 3rd are doable. Just read your notes, watch lectures and read the book and you'll do fine.

When I say this class is hard, it is only hard to get an A.  She doesn't test on concepts, is knit picky as can be, tests in a manner to try and prove she is smarter then you, and is irrational.  She teaches to the curve, and makes this class way harder then it should be, which has been confirmed by faculty.  AVOID class till her baby comes out.

Overall this class is not difficult so don't worry about it. Be sure to study a bit more for the 2nd exam. I am not a fan of her teaching style/personality, it is downright aggravating at times. Be ready for her to repeat herself again and again when she gets on her soap box about her "syllabus". FYI, quizzes are due in the morning not in the pm.

Never had such a bad professor with such autocratic behavior. Material is not hard but her tests are unnecessarily difficult and test on minor details of material instead of more general overall concepts
Frustrating teacher because she deliberately tries to trick you on the exam rather than testing if you know the material.
Pay attention to the lectures and reread your book.  She looks for the little things to test on.

Class was pretty easy, only frustrating part was teachers lack of clarity when writing test questions. Always had at least 5-7 questions on the tests that easily could have had multiple answers. Also was not helpful to students who had schedule conflicts.

the class covered so much content based solely on lectures and most of the grade came from exams. The exams would be 70+ questions and a lot would be expected to be known. Her lectures were okay but she would act pompous.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: don't be scared off first week, she's a great professor lol. very reading heavy with three textbooks. exams are all multiple choice, fair, and straightforward as long as you actually review. her TAs are all good and their review sessions are clutch.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tests are all multiple choice and heavily based on the three core texts. I only got a B because I did not want to buy any of the books, so I relied solely on the material covered in class.

Professor Kreppel is extremely knowledgable on the course content. Your grade is determined by two midterm exams, a final exam, and 11 short/easy quizzes. 300+ pages of reading per week, but it is doable as long as you spread it out and know what is important to read (which Kreppel makes clear). Exams are easy, as long as you did the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For those worried about this class being difficult I promise you it is not as bad as people say it is. Dr. Kreppel is extremely knowledgeable, easy to approach and genuinely cares about your grade and success. There is a decent amount of reading but if you pay attention in lectures and prep yourself before exams you should be totally fine.

I loved this class, I genuinely learned so much. The lectures are stellar and my TA was great. However, this class is not for everyone to say the least. There are more than a hundred of pages of readings a week (across three text books) which isn't not too bad if you pace it out. My tips: Listen to her test prep advice, go to the TA reviews,STUDY.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kreppel is a great lecturer and keeps your attention at all times. She uses three textbooks and all the material should be understood by the final exam. She gives out two midterms and one final (those are your only grades). The TAs are also very helpful if you don't understand any material. The exams are all multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible lectures, slides are messy and hard to take notes from, quizzes are too hard (trust me, she expects you to know every single thing about the EU), papers are graded too harshly.

If you do the bare minimum (read the textbooks, study, attend discussion, etc.) you will without a doubt pass. However, there is little room to boost your grade beside doing well on midterms so getting an A+ is doable but by no means easy. Poli Sci nerds should 100% take this class. Journalism majors ignore Kreppel's warning you will do fine 👍
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely love this professor. She's super passionate, funny, and gives great lectures. The content was tough and required a ton of reading, but I genuinely feel like I got something out of the course. Don't procrastinate, stay on top of readings, and don't be afraid to ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecturer and professor. Lots of reading and memorizing specific info, but prepares you well for other classes. Discussion sections with TA can be boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Dr.Kreppel is an extremely engaging lecturer who has the ability to convey information with personality. This class is a ton of reading spread across three textbooks. If you're not a political science major, this may not be the best choice.
Kreppel makes this apparent during drop-add week, and you should heed her warnings. But I did learn a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Yes, her CPO2001 class is very, very hard, but I got an A- by not reading most of the material and just being a polisci nerd. Defintiely doable to get an A by reading everything. Your grade is only based on pretty much three tests which are jam-packed with information. She is a very fun lecturer
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just don't take this class if you're a political science major, do the other 3 core classes. Ridiculous amount of material pulled from 3 textbooks, exams worth so much of your grade, 94 for an A and she doesn't round. The content is somewhat interesting but there's no room for fumbling.

This course covers a ridiculous amount of content for an intro level class, and the exams are quite difficult. Professor Kreppel is passionate about the subject, but the lectures weren't that helpful since they don't even fully cover what you need to know. If you're willing to put in the effort and do the readings, you can still do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kreppel is enthusiastic about the course. The workload is beyond extreme for an entry-level course. Reading the entirety of three textbooks is insane for a class at a 2000-level. The midterm questions are precise to the reading. The cumulative final includes too much information for one test. Overall, it is hard but doable if you read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible. Way too hard for an intro class and way too much information for the cumulative final. grades are determined by finals and midterms which are unbelievably hard and can be any detail on the 11 chapters of the core text, 13 cases of countries, or 20 academic journals which serve no purpose. Please take this class with a different teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not as bad as some people make it sound: if you go to the lectures and do the readings, you can secure at least a B. The threshold for an A is a 94% which is tough since it's 75% exams. Exams are very detailed but not really unfair. Final is cumulative, there's a ton of content. Lowkey got sleep paralysis from this class, but it wasn't the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lot's of reading, but I did like 10% of it. The quizzes were very difficult as they were "select all that apply" questions. However, you can get partial credit which saved my life. 3 essays throughout and i averaged aon those.. However, she is honestly the most entertaining professor ever. Also, she gave ec opportunities which saved my grade.

The class can be tough since the grade is mainly 3 tests, but the class is interesting for people who like politics. I would not recommend for people who aren't polisci majors since it is a lot of reading and you have to remember specifics to do well on tests. The class covers a wide amount of info. She is very no-games but is not mean.

Dr. Kreppel is a good lecturer, but the exams were a bit hard for an intro class. She warns you at the beginning of the semester, but it isn't helpful when you have to take it for your major. I did well in the class because I read the textbooks and took tons of notes. Be prepared to study a lot! My TA was also the goat and that helped too.

funny and snarky lady with engaging lectures and good powerpoints. tests are mcq and super hard and worth like 80% of your grade. a ton of content and reading and hard to get an A, but the prof is good and gets the content across well

my hardest class and my fav class this fall. Kreppel is engaging & entertaining, lectures are well-organized and I had a great TA. LOTS of reading and I also took notes for memory, but polisci majors should find material interesting. Tests are specific and 75% of your grade but generally fair. Study a lot and don't slack in section and youll pass
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is funny and her lectures are engaging, but pretty much your entire grade is dependent on 2 midterms and a final. The exams are SO tricky with wording even though they are all MCQ. Very few people get an A but if you want to learn and are prepared to read a lot you can get a B. My TA was mid, they kind of just read off a powerpoint.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Pros: lecture is based off structured PowerPoints taken from the reading, professor is funny and sarcastic, TAs are often knowledgable and intelligent 

Cons: be prepared to read 3-5 chapters a week (1-2 chapters from each of the three textbooks), midterm questions are often specific and detailed despite material being hard to memorize
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you're a political science major, I would recommend Kreppel for any polisci course. Granted, CPO2001 was a lot of reading, but she explained the info well and had good slideshows for visual learners. I barely read and only paid attention in lectures, and the exams were fair. I wouldnt recommend for someone taking this as an elective tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Keep in mind that the course has a lot of material to cover. Going to lectures was more helpful than attempting to learn the material on my own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class has no exams, but 60% of your grade comes from three papers. Two-thirds of class time is spent on lectures, and the remaining third is spent on discussions about your readings. Professor Kreppel gives a lot of feedback and has interesting lectures, but be ready to read around 100-150 pages per week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Literally do not take this unless it is absolutely required for your major! I regret.

Dr. Kreppel was an average professor in how she taught the material. She is a tough-love professor who expects her students to do the work and show up for their own good. The class itself was extremely hard to pass with an A because it was composed of a few tests on three textbooks worth of material. Would not recommend if you want an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unnecessarily difficult for an intro level course. Listen to everyone who tells you to read, as it is essential to your success. Go to discussions and ask questions. reviews.comment:
Unlicensed, no experience, no degree, doesn't teach, no care for students. She will punish you for medical, family, or personal emergencies rather than accommodating. Not only is she disrespectful to students, but UF staff as well.

She fosters an environment of fear and humiliation. 
There is not a single trace of good in Amy Freeman.
she doesnt even have a phd. find a god and pray.

> Incredibly strict with grading, nothing is satisfactory for her 

> Instructions and communications is always incredibly unclear

> Genuinely the worst, most inconsiderate teacher I've had

> “Art teacher” teaching a class about business and technology. Need I say more?

I can see why people don't like her. Her teaching style is very much so "there's always something you can improve upon." She's hard on you and expects good work, but when you understand that, her teaching style makes sense. I personally enjoyed having her for Catalyst preparation. You will not have a problem with her if you do honest/genuine work.

Part of the difficulty came from the course itself- its a lot of involved material, but she is unreasonable, unapproachable, seems to care more about the course than the success of her students. I would have done significantly better in the class if she was a more supportive instructor but going to her for feedback or answers was a waste of time

From what I have gathered, none of the professors for this course are great but I would not recommend her. For a two-credit class, it gets ridiculous with the amount of work given and it became my hardest course. The teacher switches up constantly and going to TA hours is your best bet to do well. The teacher doesn't do much but grade.
Should not be teaching this course

I was able to push through but I practically lived at TA hours. The TA's are helpful and the teacher is ok but very strict considering she can't help you when you need it. I think the way the course is made is not beneficial toward students but rather a large deterrent to people enjoying this course and encouraging others to take it. hardest class

for a first year class this class is unnecessarily hard and the TA's are your teachers for the large assignments. The course is pass/fail so other than presentations if you make the tiniest mistake you won't get a B you will get a 0. There is time to redo assignments but you need to go to TA hours constantly if you aren't tech savvy.

Dr. Freeman is the least understanding professor I've had. The class I took was Honors Sketchbook Development (not listed). This is a super easy, passable course, but there is a huge workload. The assignments will keep you very, very busy. However, the professor makes it unnecessarily difficult to earn an A. She hyper-focuses on all the details of your assignments. The grading criteria is unclear and often subjective, which makes it difficult to identify mistakes.
hate her she sucks, super mean and never teaches. not understanding even when sick

She is a very difficult grader. Hours of work put in to receive incomplete grades or low scores. Not understanding when it comes to difficulty with homework or with personal issues arise. Unable to explain the work herself so sends everyone to TA hours.
Very critical, very restricting on "creativity", and gives off bad vibes. BOO. there is so much work for a nonmajor class, all of my other classes don't have nearly that much work

If you ever approach her with a question or need help, she quickly rebuttals "you are not following the instructions" and sends you on your way. Her office hours were non-existent and she took days to respond to emails. Half the semester was over zoom since she went to an "art conference". 
Nobody gets an A, she makes sure of it.

Professor Freeman is an extremely harsh grader. I tried very hard on a lot of my assignments and she still found a way to not give me a good grade. Attendance is extremely important and if you miss a class you get points taken off at the end of the semester. (14 point deduction per class)

She is nice, but not very understanding. I personally felt like everyone in the class was infantilized. Very easy to fall behind and not easy to catch up. Asides that pretty chill, but not accomedating to health issues.

Had her for Art2936C. Literally so much work for a non-major class. Half of my major's coursework takes less time than this class does. She is incredibly picky and grades tough. I had fun at first but then it became repetitive and kinda overwhelming.
It's impossible for her to think that any of your work is good enough for an A and she makes you work sooooo many extra hours!

Ziggy is a great teacher. He is funny and genuinely wants everyone to learn and understand. Not everyone comes to class but there are several in-class exercises that are graded so attendance is important. The tests aren't hard if you pay attention to the lectures.

Honestly, do not recommend. Exams were ridiculously difficult and specific, and worth a huge percentage of your grade. Difficult to participate in class and participation is a big part of your grade as well. No rubrics for presentations so you don't know what you did wrong. Seemed way too difficult to be a 3000 level class.

reviews.comment: He was terrible! I took this class online because obviously the pandemic & although all teacher understood the difficulty of the different circumstances and tried to accommodate he did not. The class was not awful, but the online format was not fun. Ziggy was always kind and responded to emails quickly. The classes overall were a bit boring but could be fun at times, but the tests were ungodly difficult. Everything else he was a very easy grader on.

Ziggy was really chill and understanding. He answers emails pretty quickly and he makes sure that the class makes us think but that we also get a good grade. He curves tests if the whole class does badly. Just make sure you pay attention to lecture and you read the material he assigns. Also turn your camera on during Zoom projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Apraiz is amazing! She genuinely cares about your progress in the class and gives feedback on every lesson plan. By actually teaching a small group of students throughout the semester, this class will show you if you want to pursue teaching or not!

Dr. Apraiz is super caring about all her students and provides feedback on all of your lesson plans and debriefs. It is super important to attend every class because your grade is based on participation, but she is also accommodating if something comes up. Even if you're not in education, this course is fun and valuable.

Dr. Apraiz is truly an amazing professor who cares for all her students. Even if you are not an education major, I found her course to be very useful in seeing if I would like to work with children in the future.
Wonderful person and great class to take if you are interested in working with kids.

Loved my experience with Dr. Apraiz. She really cares for her students and the small size of the class allows for her to get to know you personally and thats awesome. 10/10 would recommend trying this class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He is clear, caring, and very personable. Really wants you to succeed. Readings are sometimes dense but he does a good job to make them understandable. He gives tons of examples from his job experiences. Overall a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Super helpful and easy to reach. He always made time for me after the class to answer my questions and responded to my emails quickly. He expects you to do readings and discuss in class. If you go to class and do the readings, you will be fine. I did learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: 350 characters is not enough to express all my problems with this man. He's nice, but that's pretty much it. reviews.comment: Aman is an amazing professor. He manages to pace lectures in a way that allows you to actually learn the material as you go instead of needing to do a bunch of outside practice to understand. He's really nice outside of lecture too. DSA is hard but 100% doable with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a super kind professor that is always willing to help. His teaching style was a bit hard to follow sometimes for me because of long and dense slides though. The exam multiple choice sections are heavily weighed so focus on that a lot, especially since the rest of the class isn't too difficult.

The best professor I've ever had, and probably ever will have. He was an amazing lecturer, and was great about slowly walking through examples. He always answered questions thoroughly. He moved back deadlines for projects and his policies were so lax. The class was difficult, it's DSA so it SHOULD be. But nothing unmanageable. 10/10 experience!!

This professor is of the kindest professors I have ever had by far. This class is very hard and I was struggling a lot (hence my grade) and he went out of his way to help me pass the class when I reached out to him. He knows how to accommodate students in a way that ensures fairness to everyone but is also gracious to those who are struggling.

Professor Kapoor is the best computer science teacher I have had so far at UF. His lectures are very informative. Exams are fairly difficult but you are given a cheat sheet. 3 projects all with clear grading structure. You will be asked to learn a lot but it is presented in a clear progressive order.

Great lecturer and he is genuinely the goat. Super understanding about technical difficulties and moving deadlines with projects, he pushed back 2/3 of our projects because ppl needed more time. We had some technical difficulties with exams this semester which was really frustrating, but it wasn't his fault. Also v responsive on slack!

He allows cheat sheets for exams, & he seems kind. However, he has us typing in the coding questions in a Canvas textbox on an exam, which is beyond frustrating because u can't view ur code as a whole while typing it out, & it's very unorganized. It'd be much better if he tried doing his exam coding questions w/ GitHub and Gradescope instead.

the absolute sweetest prof ive ever had. he is so kind, he cares so much about all of his students, and is always so lenient and understanding if you contact him outside of class. dsa is extremely hard imo, but he does his best to make it bearable. he deserves all of the kind words said about him. i wish more teachers were like him.

Aside from an understandable insistence that "this is important for you to know as it appears in interviews for big tech," his lectures are very focused and engaging (often a dozen people are able to raise their hand to respond to a spoken question and answer in a given lecture). Great professor who cares deeply about data structures common in CS.
The class is organized well and there are lots of resources that one can use when stuck. Lectures are useful and the course also preps you for technical interviews.

The projects and assignments in this class are incredibly easy but the quizzes and exams tend to have some stupid questions. Pretty hard to fail. Lectures were not all that. Watch the prerecorded videos and for quizzes always write down every time complexity mentioned and know how to do a pass through any data structures/algorithim mentioned.
Unc (Uncle Kapoor) is the best professor I've had at UF. Honestly the absolute GOAT. Do your work and he'll like you.
Pretty cool guy running pretty cool classes. easily the best prof I've had in college by a mile
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: GOAT. Super interesting lectures that covered everything we needed to know and Aman is a super nice guy in general. Project 1 is pretty hard so start early on that and the conceptual quizzes + exams can be tricky so getting an A does require some effort, but it is 100% doable and I loved this class and learned a lot.

Professor Kapoor is the type of professor that makes you grateful to be in college. He makes the material understandable and has his in-person/zoom recorded lectures as well as small online videos teaching the same material. Aman is also accessible outside of class, responds quickly, and is one of the kindest and respectful profs I've had.

This class involves a decent amount of work. Some of the concepts are pretty difficult but the class overall is not that bad. Aman constructed the class very well, it's a very good class. You can just watch the lecture concept videos but be aware that if you don't go to lecture, you may not learn of upcoming projects long in advance.
Banger class. Now Dr. Aman is goated.

professor aman is genuinely my favorite professor here at uf. his lectures were an integral part of my understanding and he also gives extra credit (3%). class does a great job introducing ds&a. aman is super caring and is always willing to help and answer questions in the slack. however, class is inherently HARD so stay on top of projects esp.

Best prof in the computer science department. Very clear on theory, great visualizations to help you follow along. Incredibly well prepared, organized class structure. Gamified lecture quizzes for extra credit. Responsive to questions. Open to feedback. Developed an arguably better version of leetcode for students. Actually the GOAT.
Best Lecturer in CISE
One of the best CS profs. Very clear, informative and relevant lectures; he's brilliant. Also the kind of guy you'd want to get a beer with

Professor Kapoor has assembled an impressive team of course staff that makes the class run incredibly well. Lectures can be dense but he will take the time to break things down and discussion sections can help clear things up. He was incredibly understanding with students and did whatever he could to alleviate unnecessary stressors in the course.

Amazing professor. He gave lots of helpful insights and always was accommodating to the student's schedule. He is also very good at thoroughly explaining the material to you. Overall, amazing professor and I would definitely encourage taking him as a professor whenever you get the chance.

This is the best professor within the computer science department. Simply with how the course is designed, it is challenging but not overly so, the material is in depth enough to retain what is important and introduces you to other topics that will allow you to explore more. He is also lenient and accommodating with external circumstances. #1

Aman was one of the best professors I have had at UF. He is super enthusiastic about the content and always goes out of his way to make accommodations (e.g. due dates) if students need them. He made the expectations super clear for the class so there were no major curve balls. DSA is hard, but Aman made it manageable for me!
Explains the concepts very well. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Still need to put in the effort to get a good grade. Learned a lot in this class.

One of the best professors in the Computer Science department if not the best. Lectures are extremely well made and presented in a way which makes following along very easy. Watch out for the exams, they were justifiably tough but if you pay attention in lecture you should be able to earn an A.

Great communicator, tough but fair course even in the condensed summer format. Heavy use of visual demonstrations and class involvement in lecture, records and posts everything done in class, gives ample detail for projects and exams. Friendly and responsive, good set of TAs, overall great class.
You will be a different person after this class. By that I mean, your coding ability will increase ten fold. BEST PROF.
He is the best.
Fantastic teacher, make sure you dont miss class.

One of the best professors I have ever had. He's super clear at explaining all the concepts and genuinely puts effort into teaching. Great class to prepare for technical interviews and you get genuinely learn a lot. 100% recommended!

Incredible professor. Enthusiastic, clear, and accessible. Large network of TAs and well-crafted Canvas make this the most organized course I've ever taken and the CS class (a) I've learned the most in and (b) I've had the most fun in. Consistent quizzes help with studying and make exam prep easier. 3 fun and fair projects. Plenty of extra credit.

Lectures are very informational and he does a great job explaining concepts. He is also very welcoming to questions, and makes an effort to learn his students' names. Each project has the opportunity to earn half points back, and exams are very fair. Also, you are given 5+ chances to earn 3% extra credit.

probably the best lecturer I have had within the CS department. He really knows his stuff and the class is formatted really well. Make sure to start early on the first project since that one will probably the hardest and longest for the class. Also, make sure you know your material for the midterm and final as these are worth 20% each. Do the EC!

He was a chill, great professor. No complaints there, but just be careful with the quizzes and exams. Pay extra attention to small details because there are many questions that want to trick or mislead you. Practicing problems is also so important for the class. You have to really understand it, and then be sure to review lecture recordings too.

Aman is an amazing and caring professor who cares about his students, DSA is just extremely difficult. I found in person lecture to not be the best for me, but I highly recommend watching his YouTube videos as they are to the point. Exams/quizzes are tricky if you find conceptual topics difficult. An A is a challenge, passing the class is doable.

Aman is helpful and a good lecturer, but his class is very hard because his quizzes and exams feel like they are there to trick you. He provides an abundance of review material only for almost none of that to be tested. He will mainly test you on niche details of the topic that were barely or never touched on in discussion and lecture.
Wonderful professor. The class is challenging but Kapoor is fair and seems very genuine in caring about his students. Respect this guy a ton.

Aman is clearly brilliant, but in a huge lecture it's sometimes difficult to get full use of the lecture. Exams are hard and each 20% and then there's the 3 projects that aren't so bad. He's really helpful and assessable outside of class. He really cares about his students, DSA is just hard in general so it reflects the same with him teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Aman was really knowledgeable on DSA topics but would often overestimate the knowledge of the class on topics not covered in this class. There are 3 big projects, 1 is a group one and 2 major exams. These are very time-intensive and the exams have a lot of trick questions on materials that sometimes were in the material but never discussed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Aman is amazing and very caring. However, the quizzes and the first project are really tough so you should prepare for those. Other than that, it is not difficult to pass this class (if you debug and try really hard on the mid term, it is possible to get an A).

Great prof! Discussions were really clarifying and there is so much review content to prepare you for quizzes and exams. Most difficult thing was def the projects, but Aman was very generous and flexible, extending the deadlines and allowing for regrades. So much extra credit offered. Hands down the only prof I would want to take for DSA

This year, Aman did only the Tuesday lecture. He would normally use this to give an overview of the project/lab due the next week and helped so much by explaining the base concepts we were learning. Zybooks was our online textbook which taught me everything. MAKE USE OF office hours! I would go in every week for projects and get TAs' help.

Overall Aman was the best lecturer I've had in a CS course so far. The only real complaint I have is how strange grading could be at times. If this course was graded the same way as prog 1 and 2 it wouldn't have been anymore difficult as those classes were. Not a lot of extra credit offered either.

This class is pretty difficult, but if you put in the work you will be fine. The lectures were really good. I highly recommend going to them, even if it's through Zoom. There are 2 quizzes every week (programming quiz and conceptual quiz), 3 projects, and 2 exams. The quizzes help you learn the material. Overall, great class. You will learn a lot.

If you don't like him then you got skill issue.
Better than most CS professors.
GG
GOAT. Need I say more? Like and sub if you agree

Fantastic professor and human. Aman is hands down the best CS professor I had at UF. He was so kind, caring, and understanding, which really blew me away in such a technically difficult course. I learned ALOT, pay attention as this class is uber important for OA's to land a job/internship. It is hard, but completely doable. Savor your time in DAS.

Aman is amazing. His lectures are really good, highly recommend you attend them. He is very helpful assisting in programming quizzes and projects so definitely speak to him or the TA's. He has study guides for conceptual quizzes which are helpful so check those out. Always pay attention to his lectures as he often gives tips on projects or quizzes.

The teacher obviously knows the content well. He was able to answer the questions asked and even offered to look at other resources if he was unsure of the answer. He was understanding and willing to adapt to difficult situations on the student. He also offered many options for additional marks.

This professor give plenty of chances for extra credit and is decently clear when giving lectures. The one negative I have is he will prolong lectures and fall behind in course content. The first project is around 20-25 hours of work and you are told you will have 3 weeks to complete it. This will fall to 2 weeks due to falling behind schedule.
Aman is a really chill and understand professor. He was understand of my situation and allowed me to turn in work late. I really enjoyed how he taught DSA.

Aman cares a ton about students succeeding in his class; he actually takes evaluations seriously and restructures his class around the frequently (ex. he now gives back 50% of missed project points if you correct errors after submission). He's got a YT channel of all his lectures too, so its incredibly accessible if you can't make it to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: aman def one of the top uf professors; COP3530 is a hard class for sure, but he does everything possible to make it easier for students while still enabling them to learn and be challenged. incredibly forgiving with his grading, and is currently working to make the textbook free + accessible. you'll honestly regret not taking his class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class online through UF dual enrollment. Pretty good professor, relatively easy class if you have prior python/programming knowledge. Make sure to find a good group for project 4 as it is hard without good coordination. Overall pretty good class and I found it interesting.

Most people will love Aman. He genuinely seems to care about his students and teaching, rather than just being here for research purposes. The class is really not that difficult as there are so many dropped assignments and ec opportunities, but if you fold on one of the exams it becomes an uphill battle to get an A (I got an 81 on exam 1).
