USE HER OFFICE HOURS. She provides important supplemental information that helps to better understand the topics at hand.
This professor gave a lot of study materials which was very helpful. The only bad part of this class was ALEKS because it does not relate to the quizzes or exams.

I did not speak to Professor Benjamin the entire semester. The class is fully asynchronous so if you're not someone who can teach themselves mostly, I would not recommend this class. However, I will say that Professor Benjamin provides an EXTENSIVE amount of study materials and supplemental materials if you're struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst course I have ever taken. The material provided, Aleks assignments, and quizzes are all completely different. Avoid at all costs.

This class is ridiculously difficult for absolutely no reason. No lectures are provided, and the class relies heavily on ALEKS and exams (which are both completely different from one another). tbh, "introductory" is not the word to describe this class. It's literally gen chem but for half the credits. Don't do it.

I had technical difficulties with my Aleks and it took a whole WEEK of emailing back and forth for her to fix it and I got super behind. You have to just read the textbook and watch videos from the 70s and then that doesn't even prepare you for the test because the material is so different. She seems so nice in person and then proceeds to be awful.

This class is basically a teach yourself class. there's no lectures, its read the textbook and do work modules. The exams can have nothing to do with coursework so it is confusing and very difficult to receive help. I wouldn't recommend unless you are required to take this course. I did it to prepare for Chem 1 and regretted it.
I can't even call her my professor because she literally does nothing at all and is barely reachable. Avoid at all costs!

She is honestly one of the worst professors. She purposely makes the exams so hard that it even tricks her and she ends up having to give credit back but then will take credit away from us when it's her fault on exams. Exams accumulate to over 80% of your grade so one bad exam faults you. She is inconsiderate much of the time.

The only reason this Professor "Good" is because I don't now how else to say that there is lack of relationship between her and the students in the class. The class is hw heavy but it was always doable. To me it felt like a normal virtual class where you teach yourself a lot of the material which is good or bad depending on your style.
Lots of work for a 2 credit class. Basically have to teach yourself through ALEKS. I had to take online as in person section was full.

If you aren't required to take this class, don't. If you do have to, I'd say take it online. Lots of self-study and grade is exam-heavy. She is basically unreachable. Not worth the time I spent for a 2 credit class that I didn't even need.

I loved Dr. B! Lecture was mostly doing practice problems together, which was the most important thing for exam questions, and her reviews were super helpful, too. If you take notes during lecture and do the homework, you should be fine on the exams. In my opinion, she's the best of the 2046 professors. Get her class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She wasn't bad but neither was she great. She was a little disorganized. ALEKS absolutely sucks but u just have to get through it, it will force u to learn. Tests are worth 60%, they were alright but need to study to avoid mistakes that can cost u. The lectures were fine, GET STUDY EDGE! Go in person to ask questions; she never responds to emails.

The class would definitely take effort if you were learning the material the first time, but it's doable. Many people complain she was not responsive, but I always received a response. TAs were helpful. Benjamin herself was alright, mostly aleks hw, decent answer explanations provided. Her explanations were not always the best but she was trying.

A LOT of homework for a 2 credit class. Exams go through honorlock and are hard as well as a significant portion of your grade. No lectures are provided, and you must teach yourself, so be prepared to read the textbook. Both quizzes and exams contain multiple-choice and free-response questions. Don't recommend.

Took this course Fall 2021. I think some of the reviews are a bit harsh. Yes, the course is very self-taught and professor Benjamin is not very involved, but the course itself wasn't terrible. Exams were a bit difficult, and made up a large portion of the grade. Lots of ALEKS, but not weighted heavily. Overall, pretty decent class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I HATED this class. The homework was on Aleks and it was so difficult and time consuming. There were no lectures or anything and I don't think she taught anything. Even the videos that were put up were not of her. I do not recommend this class online because you don't learn anything.

The ALEKS HW is the biggest problem with this class. Not only is it tedious, punishing, and sometimes wrong about answers, but it has NOTHING to do with the exam. In fact, if you try to learn from the ALEKS hw YOU WILL FAIL THE FIRST EXAM. For the first ALEKS assignment, MAKE SURE YOU GET EVERYTHING RIGHT, it will save you 20+ hours later on.

Chemistry alone is a hard subject, so the professor doesn't make the course "hard". Most of the work is done through ALEKS and can be time consuming, but the professor does a great of sending out announcements and reminding students of exams, quizzes, and ALEKS. Study for the tests because the grading scale is VERY test heavy!

I took this class online and the only downside was that sometimes Dr. Benjamin took kind of long to respond.  Definitely a doable course online though. Dr. Benjamin was good at reminding students about due dates and being straightforward about expectations. Overall, this course was a good intro to refresh from high school chemistry.

Dr. Benjamin was a really good professor! She was overall pretty funny and relatable. 83% of your grade in this class comes from exams. Only the final is cumulative. She really does try her best to help you prepare and is always there if you have questions. You just have to be prepared to put in the time and effort to succeed in this class.

Professor Benjamin really made you work for your grade. The lecture would cover the basis of the topics and you would pretty much be required to teach yourself how to solve them using the worksheets and practice exams that were given. The aleks homework and quizzes also took a very long time so it is recommended to start them early.

She's nice and answers promptly. I will say her lectures weren't helpful if you already read the textbook. Aleks had a lot of ridiculous assignments but the time frame to complete it was alright. I recommend StudyEdge to help you pass the exams, as they simplify things and make it easier to understand and they help with Alek. Would recommend her.

Dr. Benjamin is a good choice for Chem 2. The class is definitely challenging, but she teaches you what you need to know to succeed in the course. Her exams are beyond fair if you study properly. She uses iClicker, so attending lectures is necessary. I would also get Study Edge as a supplement to her lectures and the course materials.

This is completely a teach yourself course. There is no interaction with the professor, except if you attend office hours where she seems annoyed at your questions. The weekly assignments are tedious and usually do not correlate to the topics you are learning/the material that is tested on the exams. Get study edge and you will be fine!

She teaches really well and works to make sure every student actually understands. The material is tricky but not hard. This class requires a lot of studying and keeping up but thats expected. if you really study , you can get an A. Her practice exams and previous exams were extremely helpful because of how similiar they are to real exams.

- Self-taught through ALEKS
- HORRIBLE response times
- Unclear due dates

If the in-person class is available take it, if not prepare to teach yourself Chemistry with an uninformative and hard-to-use platform.

For CHM1025, you are teaching yourself. To complete the ALEKS homework assignments you need to read the textbook and watch the canvas lectures. The main issue for me was disciplining myself to learn the material on my own. If you are really interested in learning a good foundation of chemistry, I would take the in-person class instead.

Basically all on your own in CHM1025 online. You have only Aleks assignments, no lectures, and sometimes she will link some youtube videos. The class isn't necessarily hard or impossible, just confusing because you are all on your own and have to figure out what you need to know for the exams bc Aleks assignments rarely line up with the tests.

The class isn't challenging but for two credits it has a lot of work. If you lined up a group of people in a room and asked me to selected Stacey Ann, I wouldn't be able to because she never lectures. Focus on ALEKS and previous quizzes and practice exams and you should be fine. Chemistry is hard so just study to the point where you get bored.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures that I watched online weren't even her teaching, and they were all confusing and not in depth enough for the understanding that we were expected to achieve. She assigns reading in the textbook along with ALEKS homework that's a whole other problem in itself. The homework helps minimally on the test, you need to read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take online!!! Way too much work for a 2 credit class and is not worth the time! So much work on ALECKS and lectures that don't properly explain anything, and exams are way too much of the grade. She provides barely any way to review and takes weeks of studying to do well. Maybe in person she is better

Anyone who thinks Dr. Benjamin is a bad professor is not trying. She is very engaging if you actually attend lecture and she sincerely tries to make sure every student in the room understands the material. Her exams are beyond fair if you put in the effort to study a few days in advance. Study Edge helps too.

The exam material does not match the course content that is taught. Aleks Assignments also do not match the exam content so you are doing them for basically nothing. My B- is thanks to Study Edge only. Take with a different professor or take in-person if possible.

Dr. B provides no context for her exams & does not care about students. Decent person overall but her content consists of rushed lectures & only ALEKS. Not to mention, your grade is determined by 83% exams so if you are not a good test taker, I would look elsewhere. Do not take Dr. B if you care about your well-being!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: run. Aleks questions take like 40 minutes each and if u get one even slightly wrong it knocks u back and u have to do 2 more.For exam review,she gave a link to a zoom of a PREVIOUS STUDENT teaching everything on the exam. This girl was super unprofessional and was like "ummm just don't worry about that part I think" when she didn't know an answer
Grade discussions hard. Does not reply to emails. And does not accept late work

I took this class over the summer, so I did not have contact with Professor Benjamin, but she sent weekly updates and offered office hours. The class was very fast-paced and mostly done on ALEKS. Study Edge really helped me prepare for the exams.
I didn't really have much contact with Benjamin but she was not great at communicating. I had to reschedule an exam and it took her two weeks to reply.

Overly difficult for 2 credit class. There's a ton of work, so expect to put in 10+ hours a week. Although there's tons of work, your grade is calculated in categories. If you get 100% on the 1st HW assignment, 100% on the next 30+ actually doesn't help your grade at all. No EC. Tests mostly fill in blank & math. Your grade is really only exams!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My issue with this class is that it's done through ALEKS which is the worst online platform. You spend hours nitpicking answers just to try to get the assignment done. This class is not super hard but it's a huge waste of time just take chem 1 or take intro online.

I anticipated on this class having a light workload considering that it is only two credits; however, I spend more time on this class than my four credit calculus class. You're expected to put work into the class daily, which is way too much for a two credit class. Expect to spend a lot of time learning the material.

I took this class online so I didn't really have much contact with Professor Benjamin. She gives a study schedule that helps keep you organized that I liked. It's really just a lot of self-work: read the textbook, watch the videos, do Aleks, take exam, repeat. Not a horrible class if you need the credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not too difficult for an introductory class. ALEKs is what make the class a little hard because it is time-consuming. In order to do well on the test study ALEKS, quizlets, and even do the practice exams because they are similar to the tests. No extra credit so stay on top of the quizzes and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: professor benjamin was mainly a hands-off teacher. she posted her lectures but many of them were unnecessary to watch. i would suggest using study edge and completing the ALEKS because its a significant part of your grade.

In my opinion this class was too difficult to be an intro level course, the homework and (optional but necessary) notes take hours, they do help though. The exams and quizzes were very difficult and it seemed as though things were out of order, as I learned things in the last weeks that should've been taught in the first weeks. Not terrible though.

Took this 100% online, did all the ALEKS and read the textbook, and struggled. I guess I can say it's mostly my fault but, the ALEKS quizzes weren't anything like the quizzes and exams imo. Also I did not know that there were recorded lectures until the last week of class so yeah. Just make sure you're on top of the hw.

Dr. B does not even respond to her own TA's emails, let alone her students. She does not give points back even if you are objectively right. It was really easy for me because I took AP Chem, but I know people who are not doing too hot. That being said, in-person is 10x harder than online, so I guess this class is the lesser of 2 evils. Just avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: You will never see this woman throughout taking the class. Its chem, so its hard I was able to get an A with study edge and the practice tests, the lectures are taken right out of the textbook so i read the book and never watched a lecture. The ALEKS hw is useless busywork and is not indicative of the test. quizzes are 10 qs 2 attempts no honorlock

Professor Benjamin is awful at responding to emails. If you can teach yourself then I totally recommend this class as it was easy to learn from the book and get an A. However, if you need lots of help working through problems, this professor won't be a good fit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Exams were very difficult, I passed above average on every one and still managed to not pass. Class average score on the final was a 120 out of 250. ALEKS is also frustrating.

I was marked wrong for a correct answer on a graded assignment, so I emailed Dr. B to please adjust my score. After two weeks, she never responded so I emailed her a second time but still, she never got back to me (I double checked the email address and made sure it sent). Because of Dr. B, my final letter grade is lower than my true grade.

Many students complained about this class but no matter which professor you take chemistry with, it will be difficult and I think that Dr B did a good job of preparing me for our exams. I didnt use studyedge and only watched the lectures and was able to do very well in the class. If you work hard in the class it shouldnt be difficult to pass.

Chem 1 sucks in general, it's a lot of content and it's a weed out class so it wasn't entirely Dr. B's fault. Definitely be prepared to spend most of your time devoted to this class, Study Edge is nice but not necessary if you're willing to just do extra practice problems out of the textbook instead.

She was very new to online learning and she had quite a few technical difficulties. Did not like her teaching style, especially in large class settings. She responded to emails pretty quickly but Study Edge will help you understand the concepts much better than she or her TAs will. Also felt like she didn't give us enough practice problems
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No attendance, no homework, no assigned readings. Lecture then discussion, wants to know your perspective. Knowing INR and/or world events helps. Grade is based on a presentation and a oral exam at the end of the semester (optional term paper too).Pay attention in class and take good notes, you'll be fine. Class is very easy if you can talk well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clearly knowledgeable & his lectures are interesting if you're able to follow along with his meandering, rambling style. Does not utilize Canvas & didn't post grades all semester, vague about grades when asked. Cares about very minor details & frames every question as having one objective answer in a subjective academic field. Wouldn't take again.

The class wasn't hard because of the content but because the professor doesn't tell you anything about grades . The grade cutoffs were never made clear in the syllabus and there were no grades in Canvas. There were 2 assignments all year, neither of which were graded ahead of time. He cares a lot about minor details, but lectures are interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An amazing professor. Lectures were top notch. I will say he doesn't show many examples that'll appear on tests, so go in the textbook if you want ace exams. Very unique grading process… But don't worry, he'll take care of you. Only take if you have a love for math, mostly real analysis and lin alg. No prereqs necessary, he starts from the bottom.
Dr. Banerjee is the best lecturer I have had. Exams and homework were online through the textbook. Very enjoyable course.

Prof. Banerjee is as close to a deity as you're going to get.  He is an absolutely brilliant speaker and his lectures are SOLID GOLD.  I've seen some topics that he discusses come up as surprise interview coding questions.  He is a truly caring professor.  Brilliant scientist + exemplary soft skills = winning combination!

Professor Banerjee is very passionate about the course. His lectures are entertaining and many correspond well with the homework. However, he tends to go off-topic and talk about other entertaining math topics that have nothing to do with the curriculum. The exams are exactly like the homework. Overall, the class requires very little commitment.

Homework is 80% of grade. Other 20% is through online exams. The textbook/homework helps you really learn the material and understand everything. The homework takes a few hours each week so start early and you only get one submit so be sure to check. Lectures are not necessary but help if you are stuck
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked his lectures as I felt he was very enthusiastic about the material and always tried to give real-world examples of why we were covering what we were covering. The class is 80% HW so MAKE SURE YOU DO YOUR HW!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade consisted of 8 homeworks and 2 take-home exams, 10% each. He gave amazing lectures that tied the content into the real-world. I almost wish that we had in-person quizzes or mandatory attendance so that I would be more motivated to go. It's one of those things that you're not excited to go to but you're happy that you went afterwards.

He is a good teacher, he puts effort, but the maths is very different. I found the course super hard, the assignments are easier and people get mostly full in those but the exams are in class theory, and they are tough, It all abstract concepts and not formulas or practical-based, so take only if you truly like deep maths.

Develops very good intuition behind topics along with heavy mathematical background. Follows a bottoms up approach for complex objects.
Tests are difficult but are open book. Grading is very linient.

A great professor, hilarious too, and student supportive. He has strong knowledge(if you intent to learn) of the subject, and overall he is very kind and concernful towards students. Take the course, don't worry!

Very difficult class. I personally think the professor is very overrated. Strong lecturer but course structure isn't designed for you to succeed. Lack of assigned homework and problems to practice make it difficult to prepare for exams. Plus he has a very relaxed stance towards cheating which is frustrating to those who don't.

He's a fantastic professor. Very cheerful and enthusiastic. He taught MIS (Mathematics for Intelligent Systems), a topic that is notoriously challenging to teach. Reading the textbook is not helpful for comprehension. And far worse to explain to another person, yet he does it so effortlessly.
Only 10 grades for the entire semester, 80% of the class grade are homeworks, which are essentially take home quizzes, try your best to get 100% on them.
Class is 80% homework and two non cumulative exams which are both open book an unproctored. Nice guy, good lecturer but you won't care enough to watch after a while.

The class isnt challenging and prof Arunava really sets the groundwork to inspire an appreciation for th material. Down to earth and shows a contagious passion for mathematics. Contextualizes th material by mentioning th history behind th math, and somehow had me at the edge of my seat about "georg cantor's controversial proof." FANTASTIC lecturer.
The best Professor I've ever witnessed.

Comp. Neuroscience. Hardest subject I've learned about. The projects are straightforward overall but trying to figure out how everything ties in together is mind boggling and I spent far more time researching theory behind the project topics than the coding itself. You should be comfy with linear algebra & analysis or you'll be lost in the lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The professor is amazing, will give very deep insights on the subject. He teaches with great enthusiasm. The only problems are that his notations at times are inconsistent with the textbook and the grading is a bit tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gather around, for the story starts where we are taken on a journey through the efforts of entities before us, at understanding the most complex organ. Don't forget to get your math, compSc, biology lenses as you will need to see through them, a lot (You have other lenses too?, bring them!). Listen and think carefully, with a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Here's how you judge whether you should take a graduate class or not :- Uses black board  Knows how to teach and cares if you are learning. (ADD) Uses presentation slides  Lazy and needs to finish the syllabus quickly,you would learn better by reading the textbook yourself. (DROP)

Math (in all its forms) has never tasted so good. Few have Prof. Arunava Banerjee's ability to present the hardest material in the easiest form just so that we have a clear picture and understanding of what is going on.

It is challenging to condense years of research into an hour's worth of lectures. However, Prof. Arunava does a great job. The use of the blackboard instead of slides, his ability to pictorially represent mathematical concepts, his check questions to highlight the main concept are some of the best teaching methods I have come across. Sit and Enjoy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You may not find a teacher with his capability of rephrasing concepts again and again just so that you understand. (Do you want to waste your time taking classes under anybody else? I wouldn't. )

One of the best classes I have taken. Excellent teacher. Knows his Math and can communicate concepts clearly. Actively engages with students. Very approachable. Tries his best to keep class size small to meet above criteria. Have taken 2 courses with him. Will take more if possible. Tests could be brutal. Expects self-discipline.
Really inspiring teacher but will make you work for a good grade.

Few engage the class as well as Prof. Banerjee. His methods bring refreshing perspective to topics such as real analysis, topology and abstract vector spaces. I would highly recommend anyone to attend his classes, especially Mathematics for Intelligent Systems. Truly instils a new way of thought.
Awesome Professor. Recommended if you want to learn MIS .

The concepts could be explained in a much simpler way. His way of teaching makes the subject seem hard and lead few students to give up on it quickly. But the course is really good and professor knows what he is talking. this subjects needs to be given a little more time compared to other courses and you should be good to understand
Jumps from one topic topic to another.Makes the subject extremely boring and lacks clarity.

I took Banerjee for Comp. Neuroscience. Amazing course, he knows his material and presents old material (biology, circuit analysis, neural networks, set theory, topology, vector spaces) in a refreshing and clear way. Banerjee challenges his students with regular conversations and a casual friendly atmosphere. This is how ALL classes should be taugh
First part of course was rather easy, but the final was brutal. Not in line with the other tests

The lectures can be kind of brutal, but the tests are more than fair.  He does not talk down to his students and will try and expose you to a variety of topics in and about the book.  He knows his subject very well and I actually learned in this class.  Only downside is his handwriting.  Take this!
Brutally difficult, but an absolutely wonderful instructor.  I'll be going out of my way to take more courses with him.
Good professor.  Confusing at times but the tests he gives are a simplified version of the topic.

He confuses the students alot during lecture when jumping from one subject to another. He does have some very interesting proofs if you can follow him. He tries not to make the tests very difficult since we have to take it in class.

Great teacher. He does not tie himself to the book, and tries to get the student as involved in the subject as much as possible. He will teach you some mind-bending mathematical proofs, and he will explain at depth the subjects he thinks are of import.

I would never recommend this professor for a lot of reasons. I got an A in the class but i did not feel he needs to be a professor. One day i heard him talking on the phone in his office (i was in the hallway)  using the n word repeatedly. When i heard this being a black student i didn't feel comfortable entering and left. Racist professor indeed
Dr. Arce is a great professor! He truly cares about his students suceeding in this major!

Dr. Arce is a phenomenal professor that clearly has passion for the subject. Not only this but he is able to get students excited about all parts of Biomedical Engineering. His teaching style is scattered but I think without this his comedy would be dulled so I believe his tangents are invaluable.
Dr. Arce is a fantastic professor

When I took this class I was fighting cancer, and this man did not allow me to miss class. I had to go from my treatments directly to class otherwise he was going to fail me. I tried to talk to him one on one and he told me "life happens." In the end he passed me because he "felt bad." It's terminal, I have two months singing off ~ J

I don't have much time, I'm being hunted. I'm currently writing this from Anchorage because this is the only place I don't have to fear for my life. I'm getting on a plane tonight. Run away, you cannot fathom what will happen to you if you continue on this path. So much blood, there are only two of us left. Run from the old gods, he is coming...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Arce, a college professor, pushed to the brink of madness, wrestled an alligator with his trusted tail man, Andrew. The primal struggle symbolized their battle with inner demons. Through unwavering support, they emerged triumphant, rekindling Dr. Arce's spirit and reaffirming his passion for academia. #Resilience #Mentorship
Dr. Arce was not always the esteemed researcher that he is today. Early years were filled with dangerous adventures that most people could only dream of. So he was always too busy to grade exams

I had Professor Arce back on Fall 2015 and his class ran very well. He was fair with his quizzes and his two assignments were actually pretty useful if you continue on to become a BME major. His course gave a great overview of what the BME major entails without it being too hard to grasp. Overall it is an easy A to take

Its only once a week and every week he brings in a different professor to talk about their research.  I found all of the lectures really interesting.  Your grade consists of attendance, two writing assignments, and like 4 super easy quizzes.  The writing assignments were a resme (already had) and the BME admission essay, graded really lightly.
Great Math professor !!!! lectures are clear and he goes out his way to make sure you understand the topic if you express that you don't. He revi
He was very helpful if you had questions during or outside of class. Work was not difficult and he prepared you well for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was nervous about doing a 6-week math course. However, Professor Dhar truly changed my perspective on what a well-rounded professor is. Dhar offers exam review days before the exam, and the questions are similar to the exam questions. Lectures were clear and easy to understand. If you need to take a math course, take it with Dhar. SO WORTH IT!!

She is very sweet and very caring. Her lectures aren't the best in the world but she assigns readings which fill in the gaps. You get out of the class what you put into it and she will be very understanding of anything your going through.

She's great, class is run well. Exams are MC and have weirdly specific things, but they're almost always mentioned in lectures, so FILL UP your cheat sheet. "In Class Exercise" around once a week, so be there for that, but they're easy. My only complaint is some lectures were in person and some were online, making it harder to review for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A great professor who clearly cares and wants her students to do well. Tough class but definitely doable. Allows a cheat sheet on all exams, dropped the lowest exam, and offered a little extra credit at the end of the semester. Can be a little boring in lectures and attendance is somewhat required because of in class activities.

Dr.Saleem is a very caring and lenient professor but she honestly sucks at explaining concepts. It may be that the course tries to cover too many fields of materials science at a surface level without ever caring about a deeper understanding of the topics. You get a cheat sheet for the exams. FILL THAT UP because the exams get oddly specific.

No longer allows own formula sheet like others say, does a weird half in class half flipped lecture system that does not work out well making the class entirely on just you reading the textbook. Half the questions in exams are random facts that no one knows in the textbook.

Take Dr Saleem if you have to take EMA3010, you won't regret it. She makes her lectures enjoyable and is generous with grading. Genuinely wants students to succeed and allows a page front and back of notes on exams, which eliminates the stress of memorizing formulas. She is amazing, and I always recommend her to my friends who have to take EMA3010.
She is a great professor, she is very helpful, and explains things well. You do have to read the textbook a lot, and watch lectures, but they it is also basically a free 40% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very nice professor but can be a bit unclear at times. You get a comfort sheet for exams which, if you plan accordingly for each exam, pretty much guarantees at least a B. Content is objectively easy in terms of engineering, just really boring which makes it hard to pay attention during lecture especially since she just reads off slides.

Dr Saleem is the best materials professor. She allows a full page front and back of notes on every exam, is generous with grading, and will always be excited to answer any questions. She is accessible outside class, and picks amazing TAs. If you have to take materials, definitely try to have her.

Awesome professor, really wants you to do well and provides you ample opportunities to earn an A. Most exams have extra credit and if you study and do the readings, you shouldn't earn any less than an A. She's also always accessible by email and doesn't restrict academic questions to office hours. Lectures can be dry at times, but she tries.

Aroba Saleem was a very good instructor. She cares for her students and wanted us to do well. I have to admit, the course is not easy and it requires effort and lots of studying to do well. But there are 5 exams so there is not that much material for each and you get to drop one. The In Class Exercises / Kahoot are helpful for the exam.

Sorry but I honestly would avoid taking her. Lectures are extremely boring and she goes very fast through each slide. So hard to take notes. She doesnt explain the material very well and reads off the slides most of the time. Her heavy accent doesnt make things better at all. Be prepared to want to doze off before half the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not especially suited for online learning but did decently well given the circumstances. I never bothered watching any of Dr. Saleem's lectures as the textbook seemed to cover the material better anyway, but her grading was very fair and she did a fine job reviewing concepts you need to know before the exams.

Saleem used Perusall for all reading assignments which was just a joke. Recorded lectures are heavy, she struggles to explain subjects during live calls, and she takes forever to explain topics. For every live class, she would have us do activities then demand a student answer it which wasted a lot of time. Connection between topics is lacking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Saleem made excellent PPT slides to go with her lectures but struggled to explain much beyond what was on the slide. She always made an effort to engage the class, which if you are eager to participate, will go a long way for you. Her PPT slides are enough to study in order to pass the exams, but you MUST attend class for exercises.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures are useless. DENSE material. Uncaring, unenthusiastic, reads directly off PowerPoints and if you ask for more detail, she gets annoyed and sends you to the textbook. Nothing in this course is connected, be it the HW, quiz, or exams. Google is your friend for the former two. Stuff your notes and you'll nail concept questions, GL on math.

Very mediocre. Lectures are boring. Her accent makes some stuff harder to grasp. Messy handwriting. She sets the bar low though, so you don't need to be that good in the subject to get an A or B. Exams are pretty fair. Class is very boring and we went from 60 people coming to zoom lecture at the beginning of summer to about 10 by the last week

Solid professor, teaches with powerpoints which is fine for this class. she gives plenty of examples and practice. The tests are fair and she gives reviews and a sample test. As long as you keep up with the lectures and homework and quizzes its a pretty straight forward class.

Professor Saleem was an amazing teacher. She was very adaptable to the new online transition and readily scheduled meetings outside of her normal office hours to meet with students. The exams are not very difficult if you pay attention to lectures and go over the assigned homework and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take her for upper level courses. She is horrible at teaching and spends way to much time of things that are taught in beginner level courses. This is a senior spring elective and she spent over an hour on level rule, an hour on the difference between solids liquids and gasses, multiple hours on basic phase diagrams, etc etc

Participation is mandatory because there are in class exercises that count for your grade, but her lectures are very hard to follow, her accent makes her very hard to understand, and her hand writing is impossible to read. I taught myself this class through the textbook.

Her teaching is pretty average. She basically reads the lectures. However, pay attention to the lectures or you won't pass. She also comes off rude and blunt. You can honestly teach yourself with the lectures and textbook.

Good professor. Her lectures are somewhat dry since she just goes off a power point, but she knows her stuff. Attendance is mandatory because she will do in class exercises that are worth participation points. The class isn't that hard, just study the powerpoints in depth before the exam and do the quizzes/hw problems and you're golden.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Saleem is the most average professor I've ever had. Her lectures are boring and not engaging, and she talks very quietly along with her handwriting being completely illegible. The class isn't that hard and its totally doable if you put in effort, but you do have to put in effort to learn the material outside of lecture.
Great powerpoints teach exactly to exam, great professor.

Dr. Saleem is a great professor, everything she tests you on was well covered in class. She has engaging lectures where she asks questions for the class and expects a response, if the class doesn't give a good answer she'll make sure to emphasize and review the answer. She's eager to hear from her students and take their suggestions seriously.

She has no reviews on here, so I decided I'd leave one. Dr. Saleem is a great new professor. She cares very much what her students think, and is receptive to feedback. She explains the tough concepts very well.

Dr. Ardelt is very passionate about the material she is teaching, however, her lectures are 2 hours long and they feel like forever. Attendance matters a lot and you absolutely can't miss any classes. If you can, try to avoid taking IDS2935 with Dr.Ardelt.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Ardelt for my Quest 2 class and it was one of my least enjoyable experiences. She was acting like a high school teacher during her lectures, even though there were more than 100 students in the class. Attendance is all that matters for her, if you miss a class, she will ensure you don't end up with an A. Take a different Quest 2 class!

reviews.comment: Interesting topic, her hatred of technology in her lectures really threw me off. Otherwise a kind an good prof, you can tell she really loves what she's teaching about and is excited to participate in discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Way too much work for a quest class. The class was interesting, but harder/more exhausting than it should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Getting an A in the class was easy bc of two weekly 500-600-word writing assignments. The TA graded everything, and she (Bhavna Sharma) never knocked off points. Attendance is graded. The professor uses iClicker to track your location during class. The lectures become dreadful to endure as the semester goes on. The discussion section was alright.

I took wisdom and human flourishing for quest 2 with Monika Ardelt and to be honest, it was the freest class Ive ever taken. You have to write twice week, which you can bs everytime, but honestly I didn't want to because I actually learned a lot about myself and how to grow as a person. Final paper light asf. Easy.

I had Prof. Ardelt for an uncommon reads course, and it was a great experience. Philosophy for Life gave me a good opportunity to reflect on my week and learn a little bit about real applications of philosophy in the process. The writing assignments were reasonable, and she was very receptive to questions. Overall low-stress, interesting course.

This class depends on the TA you get because they're the ones who will be grading all of your work. Professor Ardelt did an amazing job with this class, even though her addition of the Jules Evans book added a few more readings. Her lectures are engaging, but she assigns the work the day before and in lecture the next day she goes over it.

Dr. Ardelt is an inspirational teacher. Our discussions in class were relevant and interesting, homework assignments facilitated students' participation in class, and the term assignment was clearly designed to achieve course learning outcome goals. She is organized and her expectations are clear. One of the best classes I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Ardelt was very good and enthusiastic at the beginning but then became sort of boring. Many of my friends would just sign in and skip every lecture. The lectures helpful about half of the time with understanding the content but if you wanted you could easily just look online at the power points. Her bias in class can be irritating
She makes lessons very interesting and engaging (you will need the top hat app). Tests can be hard, so reading the textbook several days in advance is a must

Great teacher! She makes it easy to follow along in class and is great about using examples to help you understand the material. While her test questions can be a little tricky she gives a lot of extra credit to make up for it. Lots of reading and attendance is important.

Dr. Ardelt has a heavy accent and she talks about personal experiences during the entire class. She applies sociological theories to her personal life stories and random Russian events. Participation MATTERS, you have to go to class!

Her tests are tricky but most of the question is "common sense". Getting an A is pretty easy so long as you complete all of the "extra" assignment an earn curve toward your final grade. Her assignment are extremely easy but can be tedious, its a  completion grade. Her lectures are not that boring, she try to engage the class into an open discussion

She is my favorite instructor so far. Hilarious. Go to class for attendance grade, read the book you will do well on her exams. Read the book starting the first exam, the easiest of all exams, don't procrastinate.

Go to class and read the textbook a few days before the exam, and you'll have an A. Most of her lectures are actually really interesting, and she's pretty funny too. It's just really easy to fall into the habit and not go to class because she takes attendance randomly but go! It's fun.

She's extremely nice and teaches the material in an engaging way. While attendance isn't mandatory, it's helpful if you go to class because she puts questions from her lectures on her tests. Reading the book will be your most helpful tool.

She is very friendly and funny in her own way. If you read the book then the exams are very easy because she uses a lot of examples that come straight from the book. Her homework is very easy. If I had read the book then I would have done better on the exams. Attending class is not mandatory but is does help you memorize the book.

She is very engaging. If you read the articles and go to class you'll do great. Her tests are not tricky and pretty straight forward. I enjoyed it and learned a lot from her class. Very knowledgeable and her accent is understandable.
Absolutely love her! As long as you participate in the class & attend class you will be fine; the exams are kinda hard but she is there to help if you need; just ASK

I don't know what these other people are talking about; her German accent is not thick at all. Her V's sound like W's, but other than that, she is perfectly intelligible. Go to class, read, and participate in class discussions and you will do great.

I loved Dr. Ardelt's class. She encouraged discussion and enjoyed getting feedback from students during lecture. The homework assignments were really easy and fun. I didn't think that the exams were that difficult. Glance through the readings and the course pack and you will definitely do well in the class. Highly recommend taking her class!

Easy and interesting.  Dr. Ardelt encourages discussion and very much wants you to share your opinion, even if she doesn't agree.  Sometimes the wording on her tests are a little unclear, but you can ask her about it.  Highly recommended!

Great teacher, very interactive and keeps class really interesting, accent isn't a problem at all. Have to read the assigned reading for the test. 3 tests and homework assignments. highly recommend her!

she is a great prof who is excited about what she teaches, even if she is the only one. she has a slight accent, not hard to understand. I only went to class days before test and test day. read book and power points. got a b+. for soc majors she is a cake walk. for others u might need to go to class but that's as hard as you have to try.
Loved her! One of the best classes I have taken at UF! She was very clear with concepts and helped a lot when you did not understand. You simply just had to ask. Taking another class with her soon!

Classes are pretty boring, kind of hard to stay awake most of the time. Usually spends the whole class to discuss one or two slides. The class itself is not too hard. She gives you a chance to get some extra credit by doing some extra assignments. Teacher is nice and she laughs at herself. Overall, not too bad, it'd probably take her again.
Snooze fest! Lectures are brutally boring and her exams are mostly from her opinins... The books and powerpoints are useless.

i didnt like her, her acccent is impossible to understand, she talks forever about useless information, it'll take her 30 minutes just to see if you're sitting in the right seat, some classes we'll only go over 1 slide the entire time, borrrrrring class, tests are impossible to pass, not an easy A
the lectures are incredibly long and boring.. she will spend a two hour class on one slide.  exams arent too difficult. her accent is annoying and makes it hard to pay attention

The test are mainly from the book, which is longest most repetitive book ever. Such a boring class. if you dont go then she gives you minus points. Shes a nice lady but her test are so confuing. if you dont read the long boring book you will fail her tests. Also she gives your assigned seats like your in 5th grade.

She is such a nice teacher and tests are so easy because she practically gives u the answers 2 the tests in the powerpoint student packet.  So many opportunities for extra credit.  You have to try hard at doing bad in this class!!!

i thought that she taught a very fair class, allowed you to get extra credit although the 2 page papers can be tedious.  dont listen to complaints, really a good teacher who is interesting to listen to. not a difficult class an easy A

Dr. Ardelt is very helpful, intelligent and understandable. She is extremely articluate and does her best ensure that every student understands what is being discussed. She is always willing to meet with you and is very approachable. She is a wonderful professor and I hope she gets tenure.

True her accent is quite heavy but she makes up for it in her enthusiasm for the subject. She appreciates students' opinions, although she plays devil's advocate sometimes, and encourages students to voice out their thoughts. If you don't take the class for the teacher take it for the content.

have taken this prof several times.  her biggest failing--i think she's more intelligent than the material allows her to be.  most students are morons, and she has to pass a few, so i think she dumbs down, and it doesn't work for her.  raise the bar, monika and fail the idiots--they'll catch up!
No Comments

People who criticize her are just xenophobes, who probably grew up so sheltered that a little bit of an accent scares them off. She is one of the nicest people - very helpful and insightful if you make the effort to succeed.
1/2 the time i am trying to copy down the powerpoint slides.. the other 1/2 of the time, i'm trying to make out what she's saying cuz her accent is very heavy!!
you cannot understand a thing she says. her tests make no sense and do not apply to watch she teaches in class. her grading is horrible too. she doesnt round.
The absolute worst professor on the face of the planet!  Run and hide here.  She is impossible to understand and conveys material like a blind-emu.

Very long and very boring lectures that are extremely hard to follow along with. She never gives any assignments, no group works, no discussions so I have not retained a single ounce of information. When the midterm came, she only gave us two days to prepare and 85% of the information given on her “study slides” was not used on the test at all.

This class is the most ridiculous thing I have ever taken in my life. Extremely boring lectures and very harsh grading on papers. I HIGHLY recommend dropping this class if you were forced to take it for Quest 1 credit like me. The title of "magic" might sound intriguing, but don't be fooled, this class is just art history and is horrific.

reviews.comment: Very long monotonous lectures. Combine that with a dark room and its lights out. Fun quest class and awesome TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not difficult at all, but make sure you actually attend class because participation brought my grade down to the point where I had to do extra credits to get an A. The actual lectures are so boring and uninspiring due to how monotonous she speaks even with interesting topics, but she is generally nice. The TA was great however!

Do not be lured in by the title of the quest class. She is an Art History professor and will make whatever class you take only about art. Most boring lectures of my life and they wasted so many hours I won't get back. It is not a terribly hard quest class but there are way easier ones out there. Overall, don't waste your time if you have a choice.

Lectures were tough to get through but the class was pretty easy to pass. I wish it was easier to take notes but it's difficult to tell what's important from what she's saying. The slideshows only included pictures that weren't helpful. Each week was predictable and attendance was necessary. The exams were weird but there was some extra credit.

I'm in STEM but I enjoyed lectures and found her approachable during office hours. It's lots of reading, but easy to pass: exams were not very challenging, advanced notice on big assignments, easy points via participation/discussion posts - just pay attention!

Recommend looking @ syllabus for a better idea of the course objectives and expectations
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Take another Quest 1 if u can. The lectures were dull with Prof Jones presenting in a dark hall using PowerPoints with only pictures & no real content, making studying hard. However, both Professor Jones & the TAs were nice. I just wish the course had a more engaging structure & captivating lectures. 30 points ext credit tho. Participation graded.

The professor herself was great; not super captivating but clearly passionate about her topic. My TA, on the other hand, was incredibly unhelpful. I had points docked left and right for reasons unclear to me, even when I asked her about it. Other students were shocked when I told them what I was losing points over. Exams were fairly easy, though.

Most boring class I've ever taken in my entire life, no hyperbole. The lectures are mandatory, but it is difficult to pay attention to her lectures as she runs on monotonously. reviews.comment: She is very sweet. I took her for ENC-1102. She encourages thoughtful exploration of literary and visual art, which I am always a big fan of. I recommend.

Amazing! She's extremely nice and legitimately cares about you. She also grades easier than a lot of other TA's which is always nice. Basically everyone hates Good Life, but if you take it with Asmaa you will hate it much less.

My absolute favorite TA ever. Definitely made my first semester at UF feel a lot more like home and got rid of the "no one cares about you in college" stigma. She genuinely cares, is hilarious, and will sit and guide you through absolutely anything. Definitely take her if you can, for anything!

Asmar's class is the most fun class I have ever been a part of. Asmaa is the best teacher I have ever had.  Not only were the lectures easy to follow, but they were also filled with fun activities such as playing online games.  I 11/10 recommend Asmaa to anyone that plans on taking a literature class at UF.  She is such an inspiration to me that I am going to dress up as her for halloween.  The class is LIT!!!!

She is a great teacher that made this class interesting. She doesn't make you write her certain way which makes it very easy to write and get a good grade in her class

Super chill professor and exams are very similar to his practice problems. You don't need previous experience using R, he teaches you in class and it's easy to pick up. Overall similar to undergrad stats.

We were able to practice supply chain skills with increased repetition in creative ways. So it wasn't monotonous, but it also wasn't completely overwhelming. Very easy grader. Clear grading criteria, would love to take his class again.

Great teacher!  Listen to his lectures, he literally spells out the answers to everything you need in order to accomplish the assignments.

The only assignments were a few written-responses and one class presentation. As long as you are present and participating, you will finish with an A. Very caring professor and very passionate about what she was teaching.

Dr. Baysal is clearly very knowledgeable of the course content, which came across in her lectures. Dr. Baysal is very knowledgeable, but EXTREMELY disorganized. Did not follow the syllabus at all, grades are due tmrw, & I still have a "N/A" for my grade. Don't take this class if you like an organized professor or one that gives you your grades back at all. I know that sometimes professors don't give their grades back on time but I didn't get a singular grade back the whole entire summer and readings were never posted until the night before

Amazingly intelligent Professor. Very nice and caring...people sometimes complain about her disorganization but honestly, she's really not that bad, she's clear on expectations if you take the time to ask her. Dr. Baysal offers great perspectives on EU politics. Just make sure to do the readings.

Dr. Baysal is a Great Professor! She really cares about her students and is very passionate about her students and her program. I 100% recommend you take this professor!

She explained the information very well and created a warm discussion environment. Excellent instructor and accessible for questions. Lectures can be long, but she's good at being clear and understands that some students are not in the CJC. Professor Asorey is definitely knowledgable about the subject. However, her lectures can be stale and drag on. Unfortunately, there is a semester long group project that massively impacts your grade. Grading is super tough in this class, but feedback on assignments is helpful.
Such a kind professor! Her experience makes her an amazing role model for us as students. Wish I had more classes with her.

This class could've been fun and valuable, but Prof. Asorey is condescending and a harsh grader. Wouldn't take her if I could do it over again. Final project is a team project in a group of 2-3 people. Textbook was interesting...

I cannot recommend Prof. Asorey's PR Writing class enough. Easily the most valuable course I have taken in the PR major. She once brought a live chicken to class and bit off its head in front of us to assert dominance. Would take again.
She's smart, but evil. Type of professor that I would not be surprised if she likes to go kick stray cats on the weekend. Get ready to fight to pay attention over her ramblings.

She is a nice person but on attempts to help you she cannot offer any guidance.  Her practice exams have incorrect answers and her homework so it makes the class even more confusing. Her lectures are all over the place and it is hard to learn during class because lecture is so unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE ANN. I do not like her.  class. She taught like she was in a hurry. She was no help when I asked what I can do early in the semester. She stands in front of her work so I can't write this down. gives little time to develop questions. MOST of the time she gets her own stuff wrong Her exam practice and homework answers were often wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are incredibly difficult to follow and understand. Even going back and looking at notes after class is confusing because you have no idea what's going organizationally. Exam/homework keys have incorrect answers. Office hours are regularly cancelled, or you can even get kicked out! I had to teach myself basically the entirety of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's nice. However, she is by no means a good professor. Her grading is ambiguous and her lectures are full of infinite rambling. Exam material often does not reflect what we are taught in class and she makes constant errors. The answer keys are often wrong and there are very few resources available outside of practice exams and few homeworks.
Absolutely awful, take anyone but her. Her lectures are overly complicated and the class material doesn't match the exams at all. She does the math incorrectly and gives limited study material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have had in my academic career. Constantly makes mistakes when providing answers for PRACTICE EXAMS and homework, making a difficult class more difficult. When asked about materials to use outside of class for extra help, she has none to offer. Will ramble for 30 minutes and then say it is unimportant for the exam.

take anyone else. seriously i'm warning you. virtually no exam prep, no outside resources to help, consistently gets the homework/review wrong and doesnt explain. Lectures are full of rambling and she'll test on topics barely covered at all. She doesn't post notes and expects us to study on the 3 practice questions provided right before the exam.

This professor is very kind, and I have seen that sometimes she does try to make sure we understand; but she is terrible nonetheless. I go to office hours to ask for help on homework problems that she then does incorrectly, then tells us that the session is over. Does not elaborate well on topics at all. Practice exam keys are incorrect, etc.

Pretty lenient in terms of homework and quizzes, and exams weren't crazy difficult. Struggles in the lectures, doesn't explain a lot and makes mistakes consistently. Everything clicks towards exam time, so don't worry if the HW makes no sense because that's how it is the whole semester. You'll live if you study, but I wouldn't recommend.

Poor lecturer who overcomplicates the subject. Condescending responses when questions are asked, and has little to no available resources outside of the infinite rambling they do in class. TAKE ANY OTHER PROFESSOR.
Horrible lecturer, didn't explain any topics. Very little review material. Exams did not cover material in lectures.

There was some drama in class with students but I found him funny. He taught good and the exams weren't impossible, just difficult and required a lot of studying. I wouldn't recommend taking it in the Summer but he does try to make it a bit easier since it is rushed. I'd recommend him but he's not for everyone

Teaches the material as if we are PhD students with familiarity in advanced statistics with some critical topics such as log likelihood being glanced over. Too many political tangents, takes up limited class time for 6 week summer term. Advisable to shove STA4322 in a normal semester if you can avoid taking it with Demetris in Summer B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extra credit is only possible if you show up to class and I found the lectures to be instrumental to passing so even though it's not mandatory it lowkey is. He made sure to integrate the use of LLM's which I personally didn't like. Overall, avoid this class in the summer because it's hard and proof heavy!

Worst professor I have taken at UF. Impossible grader, Impossible exams, horrible lecturer, makes fun of students, super long homework. Do not take him. Should have been an easy A, took way too much time.

I'm in STA3032 online. Professor Lindberg is the facilitator, but I presume Professor Athienitis organized the content. It's overly verbose and organized poorly. Simply finding the content to study is a big time sink. For a supposedly curated online class, it's inexcusable that the professor doesn't just present the content with relevant examples.

Overall solid prof- lectures consisted of him reading off slides (posted on canvas) with occasional supp. videos thrown in. Was almost always willing to make adjustments to due dates and was attentive in correcting any mistakes he made on exams/quizzes. Sometimes gave EC to students who attended class. Defo doesn't deserve all the hate he gets lmao

Class was 8 units and he lectured off slides. Slides identical to book, so you can learn from home. However, offers EC/offers incentives to show up to class (points for exam review class, told what was on final on last day, etc.). 8 HW, 8 Quiz, 3 exams. He's generous, and took off 2 Qs from one exam that was hard. Final was 87% MCQ too. Very kind!

Do not take this class with him, especially in the summer. 60% of the grades are exams which are hard, where most of the class failed and he still blamed the class. He spends 40% of the class on tangents and talking about politics. The course material isn't too hard but he makes it way more difficult then it needs to be. Please avoid this professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Tough course, but your grade is proportional to the amount of work you put in thanks to cushioning.
Pros:
- Gives lots of cushion with extra credit, homeworks, and quizzes.
- Quizzes were through Lockdown browser (no cameras/microphones)
- Super caring/approachable
Cons:
- Exams can be harder than you expect
- Will veer off-topic during lectures

His exams don't match up the notes he gives in lectures and he's pretty tough when it comes to grading quizzes. However, since this is summer he's willing to readjust final grades by allowing us to do exam corrections on Exam 1 and curved Exam 2 since almost everyone did poorly. Attendance isn't mandatory since it's extra credit.

Loves to tell jokes, to the point where class starts 10 minutes late everyday. Material is boring and not taught well. Class should be optional for both majors and minors, learned nothing. The good professor died over winter break so we got stuck with him unfortunately.

Takes his class to be a stand-up comedy bit, with large portions of class dedicated to jokes. He is funny, and a nice guy, but it takes away from the learning of the course. Exams always have too many questions to answer in the time, but at least he understands course concepts well, teaches them relatively okay, and doesn't take attendance.

Very respectable person, basically carried the course on his own. The overall class structure and complex material, however, make for an unpleasant experience. I just narrowly managed to pass and still have frequent nightmares of having to retake this class.

On the plus side, I did learn that the letter "mu" is very fun to scribble out.

Stats theory is a hard class, but he is entertaining enough to make coming to class fun (just don't take some comments personally). His teaching style is a little unconventional, but if you pay attention you will have a deeper understanding of stats concepts than other classes will give you. Tests are hard, but represent the course material.

Lectures are very confusing. He is too conceptual and doesn't show concrete examples with the concepts he is teaching. He clearly is a brilliant guy and I liked him as a person. However, he seems like he lacks awareness on how to teach effectively and communicate complex ideas well so that it's manageable to understand the material being taught.
Gave two sets of homework and two quizzes throughout spring break. Unbelievably terrible.

Athientis is kinda like the soggy French fry in the bottom of a McDonald's bag, no one likes it but if you were starving you would eat it. That being said, if you HAVE to take a class with Athientis, do so any try to trudge through it. Otherwise, just wait until another professor is teaching the course.

Rambles on about random things like politics, TikTok, and his salary during class. Uses terribly unclear slides made years ago. Homeworks are extremely unclear and take forever. Just wait until someone else teaches the class.

Overall, a pretty terrible professor. Lectures consists of him reading from a PowerPoint made a decade ago. Quizzes and homework are extremely difficult with no guidance given. Do not take for any reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: STA4183- started the class saying he had no background in the subject area and that he wanted to get rid of the actuarial science minor which this class was specific to. Would get off topic and ramble about his own political views. Lack of background knowledge was evident throughout the course and most of the class was failing. Avoid at all costs

Atheienitis is by far the worst professor I have ever had. His lectures are completely incomprehensible, and his notes aren't reflective of the content at all. I would try to get help in office hours and he was always unbelievably rude (talked down to me, make snide comments, etc.). The class was so unnecessarily hard and he was an awful teacher.

Dr. A is funny, caring, and easy to talk to. Exams are a little weird and don't reflect hw that well, but there is a curve and he grades reasonably. Lectures can go off topic and be a little confusing, but he is very accessible. hw usually is not bad. I actually like Athienitis as a person :) and learned stuff. Alright choice for 4504.

This man is a mediocre professor at best. He is very childish though and throws a tantrum when people dont show up to class, even though when we go to class he just reads off this note document and talks about politics no one wants to hear. Tests arent math at all and are just on trivial points about regression. Learned more in 5 online videos.

A painful but doable class. Some people make it out to seem like this is "the hardest class ever"-- it's not. Professor is structured but material is just difficult. For quizzes and tests, in addition to book/online, re-do the problems in the notes as practice (since those problems are the closest to quiz/test problems, not the ones in book/online)

The course was not that difficult, but the lack of clear explanations during lectures made the course material much harder than it actually was. You also have to learn how to use the program R for a majority of classwork, but he does not teach students how to use the programs and tells you to "Google It" if you have any questions.

It's a lot of work. The good is he gave extra quizzes to boost grades and moved deadlines when needed. The bad is that between the class notes, lectures/slides, and the book the material can seem very disjointed. Also you can find youtube videos that are much more concise, tell you what's necessary, and what's going on, than his lectures.

10/10 do not recommend. You have to learn R for this class, but he hardly gives instruction on it and tells you to google things you don't know. he had pre-recorded lectures but they were not very helpful. The textbook doesn't use R so it's not helpful in solving hw problems. And his notes do not provide clear examples to help with hw.

Terrible disconnect between lecture content, homework, quizzes and exams - it often felt like completely different material. He deleted student Teams comments expressing frustration at his course, and the final average was a 58.

Dr. Athienitis is accessible and caring. He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities that students who put a lot of their time can get a A . For ESL students this course can be hard because he creates original problems but I made it! For native speakers might not be a problem. Data science is not my interest but Dr. A is amazing! Thank you! YM

I don't like Stats at all. But given that, I like this class. The professor is extremely organized. The exams may be hard, but the grading is extremely fair, (almost one dropped exam). Yes the class is a lot of work, but the professor is always there to help. He really cares about his student, and he puts a lot of effort in making this course.

Possibly the hardest class I've ever taken, but it's because of the sheer amount of material covered. However, he truly wants us to learn and succeed. Dr. Athienitis was always available on MS Teams and in his office hours and was very helpful. He clearly knows the subject very well, so if you want to learn, take him. It won't be easy though.

Terrible professor. I spent way more than the recommended 9 hours a week studying for this class trying to do well, but the material is spread way too thin. Quizzes/Exams don't represent the reference material at all, and the professor would say things like "well this course is on par with other top institutions, push through and be patient."

This professor was a nightmare. He would pick the smallest thing from his notes and put it on his quiz. Conceptual quizzes with the expectation you remember something he skips over, the material did not match what we were tested on, and he seriously refused to bump my grade when I was 0.06 away from an A. He seems kind @ 1st... but he is ruthless.

I'm not sure if this was the circumstance due to COVID, but I found his pre-recorded lectures super unhelpful for quizzes, homeworks, and exams. The first two exams were fair, but the final was super hard and did not reflect the material given. However, this professor is also kind so if you are struggling, make sure to reach out to him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor does not care about his students. His expectations are never clear. The material taught in the lectures is not the same as the material youre expected to know for the quizzes or exams. I studied tirelessly and never was able to make a passing grade on a single quiz, and when I asked for help he recommended I get a tutor.

Gives a ton of extra credit and clearly cares about his students. The problems are mostly with the course itself. What you learn from the book is different from what you learned from the other book which is different from the other book which is different from the lectures. Not too tough, and a decent intro to data science.

The exams are only 30% of final grade, and even those are broken down into highest to lowest. Overall, professor is pretty lenient grader with a lot of opportunity for extra credit. MyLab exercises helped me understand the topics best. As well as the assignments. Few short lecture videos per week. Using R made the course real easy. Not hard 2 learn

Hard class, but he breaks it down pretty well. The lectures are in 20-30 minute snippets and you watch 2-3 a week. Main complaint is you kind of have to teach yourself R. Between extra credit on nearly every assignment and extra credit for participating in the discussion posts, you can bump your grade up 10-15%
Very helpful, hard to understand materials just from lectures though. However, he is always on slack answering questions. Understanding and accomodating, several extra credit options too
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This man has a very weird sense of humor and lacks compassion. His lectures are incredibly boring and dull and all he does is basically read straight from the book which I can do at home. He doesnt provide reviews for the exam, and sometimes random concepts we havent learned show up on the exams. Make sure to do well on quizzes, they help a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Need: basic stats knowledge and R programming. He made a custom book, which isn't internally hyperlinked, and it is poorly organized. Thus, his lectures in which he reads his book also jump around. We were supposed to have a formulas for a test, but it wasn't linked on the page. Too bad, so sad. Begs for good reviews so he can get a promotion.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I think this instructor is fair and above average overall. I actually learned a lot. Especially Liked his videos.

I took him during summer B and had to drop, but not because of the professor. The material is just too much for a condensed block. But he does try his best to make sure the students are able to succeed, and even if his jokes are lame they're still able to catch attention and help to foster a good atmosphere. Take him any time other than summer B.

Dr. Athienitis' teaching style is very unfocused and disorganized. It's difficult to follow him, and he jumps between concepts that aren't even part of the course. It would be helpful if he had a lesson plan and explained what he's going to teach beforehand instead of just reading the notes to us, and he needs to save stories until after lecture.

Took this online and this class is challenging. However, there is tons of extra credit, office hours everyday, and you can also argue for partial credit. A lot of conceptual quiz questions are from his lectures. Prof. Athienitis is a great guy and very knowledgeable, will walk you through any stats questions you have. Be prepared to work though!
He totally rocks this class.  I learned so much in his class.  You cant miss a class because of the pace but he explains well and gives good examples.
If you really want to learn take Dr. Athienitis.  He makes stats fun and easy to digest.  He clearly lives his job!
Awesome professor who cares about his students and is passionate about statistics.

He's funny and kind as a person. However, his teaching doesn't match up to his personality. He doesn't pay attention to non-Stats majors, and pays too much attention to a few students he's familiar with. I wouldn't recommend him to students who doesn't have an established base of knowledge of statistics due to his style of teaching.

Worst professor I have had here so far. The Lectures are awful and completely unprepared and there are no guides for what material and how much material you need to know for the exam. Avoid this professor at all cost.

It is currently the fourth week of the semester and I can say without doubt this will be the worst class I have all semester. Dr. Athienitis comes to class unprepared, spends most of class rambling about off topic subjects, and expresses utter disregard for students. I love statistics but am not thrilled about this professor.
This was by far my favorite professor. He was funny, kind, and caring. His lectures and notes are thorough and if you put in the time you will learn a lot.

Athienitis is the worst professor I have had not only for a stats class but any class in general. He obviously has tenure because it's clear that he doesn't care about teaching or his students which he has even said. His exams are hard and the lectures are ill-prepared and not worth attending. AVOID at all costs. You will have to teach yourself.

His online class is great! He takes the time to explain everything thoroughly and you feel like you are sitting in an actual class. He does not rush through the material, giving you time to absorb the material before moving on. He takes his time in office hours to explain any questions to you and is very much invested in his students' success.
He is outstanding and tells jokes during lecture which keeps it interesting. He has a passion for statistics and is very helpful.

I took this class in Fall of 2017, but forgot to rate him on here. Hes one of my favorite professors. He tells a lot of jokes, so it makes it fun to learn the material. If you go to his office hours he will take as much time as needed to help you understand the material. If you do the homework you will do really well on the exams. Great professor!

Online Class. The lectures were low quality and lacked. He talks slowly, and he reads the handout to you for most of it. The class is very textbook heavy (all homework comes from it).
