I am an extremely poor listener so I decided to take this class. Very engaging in her lectures. She can be a little critical in her tone and can be a little harsh in her grading but nothing too serious. She gave all the questions to the midterm and final and I actually learned a solid amount of material on listening. Def worth for the com minor.

She is so wonderful, you do need a textbook but halfway through I stopped reading it because her lecture covered the chapter. You get a chance to meet some new friends because there are two group projects, which are relatively easy. I really enjoyed the class, If you thought you knew everything about listening think again!! Loved this class!!

If you are more of a nervous, introverted person, you will likely receive a low B to D on your speeches. She randomly takes off points on delivery, even after approving your outline. She may embarrass you in front of the class for asking questions. She displays favoritism towards the male athletes in class through her demeanor and attentiveness.

Professor Ataga is wonderful! 100% recommend. The course has very clear grading criteria and several opportunities for extra credit so it was extremely feasible to maintain a good grade.

She is the most unforgettable teacher. Her lectures are always interesting. She encourages and motivates every student to be better.

I would totally recommend taking a class from her to everyone. Her lectures are AMAZING. You don't notice how the time has passed when you are in her class. She explains a subject with such a great balance of humour and education. That way, you always remember the most important things about that subject. DEFINITELY THE BEST TEACHER!
Great prof! Would definently take a class her from again. She is the reson I have any interest in neuropsychology. DO TAKE A CLASS FROM HER IF YOU CAN!!!

She is the one person who has most greatly inspired me throughout my life. She was always there to give me the motivation I needed. The lectures were understandable, and her way of teaching encouraged me to learn more. I truly missed her class a lot. If you are her student, be thankful for that.

I enjoy every second of her lecture. She has a unique way of presenting the concepts with humor which helps you to learn by heart. Her English is perfectly fluent. She is a smart, open-minded, fact & data-driven scientist. She is a caring person who listens & empathises you. She is always there for you to motivate and inspire. Missed her lectures.
She is a great teacher with her interest and relevance, and the way he teaches. I wish I could take all my lessons from her. The interactive nature of her courses makes them fun and informative.

Worst professor of my undergraduate career. Doesn't care if students get the material or not. Don't take her classes, ever.

Possibly the worst instructor ever - poor concern for students, incomprehensible, and 200+ pages of text per exam, covering perhaps double the total material taught in another section of the same course. If you need a course taught by her, AVOID IF AT ALL POSSIBLE.

HORRIBLE! I'm not a lazy student who doesn't go to class and wants to get an A - I am a double major with a great GPA and this woman is honestly the worst prof (she's a grad student) I have ever had. pathetic as far as professors go, her lectures were nothing more than her copying and pasting pieces from the book, which in turn she would only use 50% of the time on exams. might as well not even bother going, just read the book.
READ READ READ and GO TO CLASS!!! her tests are tricky, but ask for a study guide and she might give you one.It's a hard class if you don't REALLY STUDY because it's A LOT OF INFORMATION.

She is an absolutely horrible teacher. She teaches out of the book and gives you the test from the book. She prefers to argue with you instead of trying to help you and don't try emailing her. She was such a great teacher. She cares a lot about her students and does everything to explain the best that she can. She is very helpful and she's adorable! Definitely take her course if you can!

She is a really great teacher. I ended up with a really good grade in her class and I didn't even have to study that hard because she covers everything in class. She is very down to earth and she makes the class fun and interesting. I'm glad I got to take this course with her.

Yes she has an accent but it's more than understandable. She knows her information and explains things very well, she uses real life examples which help to understand the material. Professor Austin was my first ever class as an incoming freshmen. His class is very fun and very easy to get a good grade. Roger is the best professor that I have taken in my time at the University of Florida. He gives great lectures that will keep you entertained while learning the material. Took Mr. Austin summer 2024 and was one of my favorite teachers at UF. He is a practicing attorney and infuses comedy and personal experience into his lectures to make them fun and engaging. He is very descriptive and makes harder concepts easy to pick up and very easy to understand. As long as you somewhat care you will do well! Take him!

Took this class over summer b and it was ridiculously easy. Lectures were funny and entertaining while promoting class discussions and participation. Super easy grader with very few assignments. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Roger is a hilarious guy and a very caring professor. He always made time to talk to me and my fellow students every lecture, and he was never angry if you came in a minute late. Just a super awesome guy.
Best professor in the political science department. Insanely smart and knows his concepts.

Amazing professor, super accommodating and kind

Best professor at UF. I wish he taught all my courses. Knowledgeable, great at explaining things, engaging lectures. TOP. NOTCH.

By far the best professor I've had at UF.

His lectures are always really good and he is there for the students. His class talks about important concepts and as long as you listen you will be able to do the papers and exams for the class
Pretty sure this class is only taught during election years, but it's a real gem. Prof Austin kept it interesting and I wouldn't hesitate to take another class with him.

BEST professor at UF by far! Take this class even if you aren't a political science major, you will not regret it. He is hilarious and so interesting! Even if participation wasn't part of the grade I would come to class, best lectures ever. I will surely miss Dr. Austin's "good morning" at 3 pm. Workload is fair and he gives great feedback!
One of my favortite Professors to date, easy to talk to, informative, and interesting.

roger austin's a cool teacher who is pretty lenient about most things. deadline's are generally flexible and the workload relatively low. don't bother reading the textbook for his random quizzes. just skim it for the important info and make sure to come to class..and pay attention to federalist paper 10 b/c he's obsessed w/ it. interesting class!
Extremely chill and respectful guy. Very clearly passionate and super knowledgeable about the material he teaches. Couldn't recommend him enough. 2018 Lebron of MoM.

Some of the exam questions were pretty tricky, and there are lots of homework assignments, but the TAs go over all the homework assignments in office hours. It wasn't an easy class, but Dr. Moss is a great lecturer and a great guy overall, I would highly recommend taking him.

Why does he write lightly and his back covering the board every single lecture 😭 and messy handwriting too okay dude but come on

he's a good lad

She doesn't have lectures, so every assignment is done via self-study. It's unfair to expect students to learn everything themselves, then take so many points off for the most minor flaws!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely hated this class. Only took her section because I was taking it with a friend. This professor's rubrics were extremely unclear and she would take off points for things that did not deserve to be deducted. Who even takes points for not citing your opinions? 10/10 do not recommend. Save yourself if you can

You are expected to teach yourself by reading the text. There is not a clear rubric for anything, yet assignments are nitpicked for any imperfection. Any feedback is often not helpful. If you think youve included everything you need in your paper, no you havent. Take this with literally any other professor if you can. Its not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE SYG2000 WITH THIS PROFESSOR! If you have another option, take it. This class is absolutely horrible and unfair. The grading is extremely subjective and you will get docked off points even if you follow the rubric because you didn't say it how she wanted. Way too much writing, average discussions were 3 pages every week
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting class. There's a discussion post due almost every week and three papers, one of which is the final. McClellan is nice and open to answer everyone's questions during office hours. She likes talking to students and helping them out. You definitely need to read the textbook or at least know the vocab to get points on the discussion posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You need a 95 to get an A, but the only assignments are 8 discussion posts and 3 papers, including a final paper. Doing the readings makes the assignments pretty straightforward to complete. Prof. leaves insightful comments in the textbook readings/supplemental lessons. I currently have a 99%, put in the effort and you will do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is extremely difficult for absolutely no reason. There are no lectures, just a textbook. The grade boundary for an A is a 95 with no room for error and she and her TAs will mark off for any little thing, even though the rubric is extremely vague. Definitely the worst class I have taken at UF and I wish I took it with another professor.

She and her TA Troy are very kind and helpful. Class is based around labs on Wednesday and exams every Monday. If you study hard for the exams and go to every class youll get an A or B. I never studied on a test and cheated on proctored test and got a C but Cs get degrees. Overall study and youll pass.

Worst teacher I have had thus far at UF. Does not care or have any empathy towards her students. There will always be something wrong with your paper. TAs are just as equally inconsiderate. Save your time and dont take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The prof does not have a mean or bad teacher bone in her body. I was lowkey afraid the class would be boring and hard, but it's not hard at all. Read and DO the study guides and you will get an A, her and her TA are super understanding and give clear grading instructions. Really a breeze and has good lectures
Doesn't have a empathetic bone in her body

The class is structured very poorly for an online class. You pretty much have to rely on the book solely for concepts since she doesn't have any lecture videos or review material for papers. She only had annotations in some parts of the book. The papers were also graded in a tough manner which made it hard since that is the majority of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Stressful because of relatively small margin of error for earning an A. Professor is super helpful though if you are willing to email and/or show up to office hours. Interesting class and because it is asynchronous you can really just spend one day of the week working on it except when working on the essays that take a little bit longer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class itself seems like it should require a lot less work than it does. Weekly discussions and 3 papers. Grading was very specific and there definitely are "right" answers.

She made the online format of this class harder with 190/200 the lowest you can get to have an A which is impossible. The TAs and professor were very strict on the rubric which most of the time was vague. There were never lectures and everything was self-taught through the reading and then they expected written assignments to be extraordinary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The grading scale was ridiculous and you can only miss a total of 10 points out of 200 to still get an A. The only extra credit offered was Gatorevals which was nothing. TAs and the prof as well were very picky on all the written assignments with the rubrics being very vague as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class has ONLY 8 discussion posts and 3 papers. All written assignments. No lectures. Self taught. The rubrics were so vague that it was impossible to get a good score because TAs would take off points for anythinggg. An A is a 95 and the class is out of 200 points so once you miss 10 points you literally cannot get an A and theres no curve.

This class is supposed to be an easy A. Other sections with different professors had a mix of exams/quizzes and their grading scale is much more lenient than hers. Her syllabus says a 95% is the minimum for an A and although I'll have the discussion question and rubric for reference, she takes points off for hidden reasons. Don't do it.

I thought this class would be an easy A. The grading scale is only based on Discussion posts and 2 papers. Those 2 papers tanked my grade in this course. This class is online and theres no lectures. You teach yourself the sociological paradigms and they expect you to go above and beyond. Harsh grading by the TA. Thanks for messing with my GPA!
Supposed to be an easy A. In the online version (due to Covid) she graded like a monster. I wish I chose a different teacher because it was insane. The harshest grader I have ever seen.

Really easy to get an A. There are exams every two weeks that are straight forward, really simple, and to the point. All you need to do is watch the lectures and do the worksheet. You can also read the textbook for clarification and she provides a free pdf. She is really kind. If you ever need anything (extension or late assignment), just email her
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: sociology class was based off of about 10 discussions and 2 papers. i did not think the papers were graded too tough. the discussion forums required use of the textbook and another article provided. i did well on the m by incoroporating personal opinions as well. overall i liked the class but you have to do well on discussions and papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a great professor and is super helpful when it comes to learning the material. The material can be a little boring but she makes it interesting and explains things well, giving lots of opportunities to ask questions. There are tests every other week but she helps prepare you well. Would take her again!

this class was a lot of work but the topics were interesting and the professor was very nice. you definitely need to read the textbook and supplementary materials, most of the grades are discussions and papers which require a lot of writing
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took her this past Summer A semester. Sometimes we had to watch hour long documentaries which were interesting, but required a lot of time. Some of the grading criteria was iffy since I got 8/9 twice without much explanation. As long as you cited info from the textbook, you were fine. TA graded much of the work. Fast grading A 95+ was an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: The grading rubrics/instruction for the papers are not clear, and when there was a misunderstanding that cost a lot of students points, they were unwilling to admit their mistake and give the students their deserved points back. In order to get an A in the class, you have to get a 95% which is ridiculous when the grading is not clear.

Professor McClellan is great! The material is boring, but if you're required to take this class, take it with her. The only thing that I don't like about this class is that you need a 95% to get an A and you don't know what your average is until the end of the semester. Just pay attention in class and do all the worksheets and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great Professor! Smart, helpful, funny, and sweet.
Not a hard class if put in the work she asks you to.

Professor McClellan is one of the most caring teachers at UF. If you need to take Methods, take it with her. While the lectures and homework (which is just doing chapter study guides) can be a little boring, she tries to make it fun. She genuinely wants you to pass and will help you understand the test material and group project work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Group projects

reviews.comment: She's a great professor and tries her best to have the class enjoy it, even though the content of the class is pretty mundane. She genuinely wants to help all her students understand the concepts. There are four exams total and one group project which are all fairly difficult so attendance is important if you want to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I feel weird giving this professor a rating when essentially everything was handled by TAs. The prof gave 1-2 sentence feedback which was often "what [TA] said." Expect lots of papers and group discussions. This class isn't very difficult, I think the hardest part is knowing how to format papers since the grading rubric is practically nonexistent.

Dr. Austin is a very understanding and in my experience she responds to emails within 24 hours. She grades things fairly and you can make corrections on assignments before they are graded. Her lectures are also very concise. Just be ready to write, all the assignments are discussion posts and essays. I highly recommend this class.

Dr. Austin is amazing. I had her for my entire four years at UF; her classes are very straight forward and it is easy to get an A. She's very understanding and flexible, and her classes are never stressful. Grading is clear, and so are her expectations for papers. Very chill, responsive, and helpful thesis advisor too.

Kind professor who is super caring and understanding! The four 8-page papers were based on the readings, which are reviewed and summarized during lecture through powerpoint presentations, and were straightforward and did not take super long to complete. Format is important, so be sure to utilize office hours and you'll walk away with an A

Dr. Austin is incredible. Her African American Politics class was one of the most engaging, relevant, and empowering courses I've ever taken. She's passionate, organized, and deeply supportive. The readings, discussions, and international exchange made this class unforgettable. Take her!

Class is overall informative and easy. Dr. Austin does a great job of making the expectations clear to do well in the course. If you do a proper job on the essays you will have a good experience in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So great and very passionate about what she does. She keeps her class material interesting and relevant. The class is not super difficult, only graded on a few papers and instructions are clear. She is very understanding if you have something going on and cannot submit on time. I have taken her 2 of her classes and cannot recommend her enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: I took this course because it was super interesting to me, but the professor definitely made it that way. She is super clear about the way she wants your work, an interesting lecturer, and very passionate. There are a lot of papers, but it's difficult to do bad on them if you did the readings. Definitely recommend her!

There's a lot of reading and class participation is important. I don't remember extra credit, but I didn't really need it. The work is individual, and her lectures are great. She leans politically one way, so keep that in mind. No multiple-choice exams—just essays with clear grading and great feedback, especially if you visit office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The greatest professor I have taken at UF. She is very kind and understanding. The class is made up of 3-4 papers overall in the entire semester and that is it. The papers are really easy as long as you answer all the questions she asks you to. The class can get a bit boring at times but she incorporates videos at times. Overall, very easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, one of the easiest classes I've had to take. She's really easygoing, and as long as you do the bare minimum, you should be able to pass with an A. As far as what I actually learned, though, it is not that much. The lectures can be very long, and I was zoning out half the time.

Her requirements for her papers are very unclear. Ive gotten many points taken off just for the smallest things, even though Ive compared with classmates and they got full points with the same mistakes. She doesnt ever accept late submissions so dont try. The workload is light but she makes it way harder than it should be.
Honestly, I enjoyed the class. It was good to learn some background with race at UF. Dr. Austin grades very easy, in my opinion. As long as you reference the sources required then you are good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Austin is an easy grader, but my main issue has been her instructions are NOT clear. When she says "required materials" that means you source those materials, not just read them. There are multiple places in the syllabus/assignment details where she fails to tell us that completely. She has taken multiple letter grades off because of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
I took this for my Quest 2 option and it was one of the most interesting courses i have taken.
I highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was one of the worst classes I've taken at UF. She makes you do a THREE-PAGE PAPER + Bib EVERY OTHER WEEK. Most of the time it's an essay tho. I have never done so much work for a class in my life with hours of videos and lectures and 5 hours a week just dedicated to writing that essay.  No late work either. DO NOT TAKE THIS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing prof. Exams are super easy if you attend and do the readings, but long (minimum 8 pages). Some readings can be very boring, especially the pure research papers. Super understanding about potential mishaps. Rewarding lectures and makes subject matters easy to understand. Definitely take her, no regrets.

Only one assignment due per week and a zoom on Friday where you only have to speak once for full credit. As long as you answer the question, meet the page count, and use all the required sources, you'll get a 100 on every assignment. Material was very interesting.
Had her for Quest! Super interesting material and she obviously cares a lot about her students. The essays were easy and I learned a lot, just be prepared to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took her for my Quest 1 class, she is a really easy grader, and the class was straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: Easy course (WOC + the Law), lots of writing. Assignments easy A, just quote a bunch to prove you read and she'll accept it. Quizzes are easy and straightforward. Workload each week very manageable. NEED textbook, but you can just "buy" it from the bookstore and then take pics of the pages you need (on syllabus), and return it the next day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures are very straightforward. She rarely put her political beliefs into what she taught. Her papers are quite long (8 page minimum) but very manageable if you start on time. Fun and very informative class overall.

Dr. Austin is an awesome professor. Allows students to be independent thinkers without criticism for doing so. She is very approachable and makes herself available to help outside of the classroom. Take her classes!

I took Special Topics - Women of Color & the Law. Dr. Austin grades with a little bit of rigor. The class is not hard as long as you take notes on what she likes early on and the kind of detail she expects. The class itself was incredibly interesting. Not an easy A but if you do the extra credit (6 Page Paper) it's not difficult to get an -A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: African Americans in Paris was an amazing class and the best I've taken at UF.  We wrote 5 papers, but I learned a lot about the black experience in Paris and the differences in American and French racism.  We went on some awesome field trips in Paris and Dr. Austin was very knowledgeable and nice.

I went to Paris with Dr. Austin as part of the African Americans in Paris class.  It was the best class I've taken at UF.  We wrote papers before we went to Paris for spring break.  I learned a lot about the topic.  She is very helpful and knowledgeable about the topic.  I highly recommend her and loved going to Paris.  She is a very nice lady.

Dr. Austin's class is incredibly easy, yet very informative. She teaches in a straightforward, concise manner and respects her students more than almost any professor I've had. Attendance is somewhat mandatory, but she's incredibly lenient. Easy A if you can write a decent essay, which is what her tests are completely comprised of.

Rude, sends RA to show movies in her place AT LEAST once per week, says to email her with questions and gets back to you late at night right before deadlines, unclear, disinterested in teaching, and didn't even come on first day of class. Avoid. She is the worst professor I've ever taken at UF.

Dr. Austin is a great professor.  She genuinely cares about her students and she consistently helps us gain real-world experience(she always tries to get us to apply to internships/fellowships, etc)...and she is neutral when lecturing..you have to do work of course and know your info(exams are in class essays)

Very interesting class.  Discussions were hilarious. I was impressed with her ability to remain objective and encourage everyone to speak regardless of their views. She really enjoys the topic and spends time investing in her student's future by giving them information about internships and scholarships.

Awesome class.  I wish it fulfilled gen. ed. requirements so more people could know about it.  We discussed a lot of policy issues and read/summarized basic gov. info.  It was interesting because of the discussions and her interest in the class.  She seems to really care about her students and goes out of her way to help them.

No complaints except one: The class materials do present an obvious bias. Many times, she focuses on one side of an issue, and presents that as the truth. She does not do a good job masking their views. Conservative students be warned. Also, many of the issues she presents are not related to federal govt.She focuses too much on state social issues.

one of the best at UF.Very well structured class, organized syllabus, unbiased in her views. I took two classes with her American Federal govt and Latino Politics...im looking forward to her African american politics this fall 2010. S

Dr. Austin is great.  I took her for POS2041 and it was enjoyable.  The class consisted of 3 exams each counting for 30% of the grade and attendance/participation counted for 10%.  Her exams are very fair--mostly based on lectures and very little came from the book.  I would take another class with her again.  Highly recommended.

Definitely one of my favorite professors. One of the only ones who can present very contoversial info without any bias at all. Her classes spark great discussion, are fun, and you learn a loT. I would take her again in a heartbeat!

I took the presidential inauguration seminar from her.  We went to DC for a symposium on the media and the presidency for 10 days, to historic sites, and to Obama's inauguration.  It was an amazing experience that I'll never forget.  She worked hard to put the trip together and help us when we were there.  It was a lot of fun and I learned a lot.

Dr. Austin is an awesome, nice professor.  The black politics class is the most interesting one I've had at Florida.  Times passes quickly and she is committed to helping her students find internships and scholarships.  If you're a polisci/prelaw major, you'd be crazy not to take her class or just meet her.  She truly cares!
She is a great teacher, class is fun if you make it fun. Lots of disscussion She is pretty unbiased and presents many views. Awesome class take it with her if you can. Tests easy!!!
Great Teacher.  Class was discussion based, but she was a great moderator and added a lot of information.  I can't wait to take her again!

Race, Gender and Politics: Interesting subject matter. Class revolved around class discussions She's an expert in this field, and I wish she'd done more lectures. The few that she gave were very informative. I would have learned more from her directly than from the musings of the other students. She's nice, approachable, and an easy grader.

Excellent Class.  I had little interest in this topic, but the information and discussions were good.  I can tell she enjoys what she does for a living.  She makes all of the students feel comfortable and keeps in touch with many after they graduate.  Very friendly and caring.

Easy class. Discussions keep class interesting. Dr. Austin shows she really cares for her students by announcing scholarship/internship opportunities before class. Study the lecture notes and read the readings and you should do fine on the tests. Some complained that the class  was too focused on social issues and not government structure.

Cultural Diversity was a great class. Discussion was the best part, there's never a dull moment. Lectures are interesting, she usually shows a film or has a guest speaker. The test is pretty horrible, you look at it and wonder when you went over that material. I suggest reading all the assigned chapters and online readings. She doesn't tell you tha

This class is VERY easy. The exams are a piece of cake as long as you copy everything she puts on the board (not much), go over your notes, and read the reserve readings. I used to study for this exam the day of. BUT watchout, the paper is a HEADACHE!

The class is extremely easy and the discussions are very lively...and then when you get to the test, it's kinda like, "wait, what?"  She gives about a 5 minute review the week before the test, and then nothing on the review was actually on the test.  READ THE BOOK! 3/4 of the test questions are from the book (something she doesn't tell you)!

African-American Politics--TAKE THIS CLASS! She is an amazing professor, very dedicated, knowlegeable, and attentive to students. She had to go on maternity leave 3/4 through the semester, and she STILL made lecture videos for us, with accompanying notes while she was gone. The class itself was very interesting, great lectures, discussions, videos
Awesome teacher. Really liked her class. Learned a lot. Tests were a little hard, but overall highly recommended

She helped the Asian American students tremendously in this class by simply offering it.  We were able to get a certificate in Asian Am. studies approved because of her hard work.  The class was very interesting and she was a jewel.  She also was one of the most well dressed pregnant women I've ever seen.  She wore the cutest maternity clothes.

awesome, awesome class. she is one of the few poli sci female professors, so if you get the chance to take her class, DO IT. you learn a lot about inner-city politics, but you also learn a lot about poverty, racial issues, social welfare, and public schools. in addition, she is always showing great films in class. her tests are hard (all essays, and she demands a lot of info) but just go to class and study and you'll do fine.

She is the most helpful professor on campus.  I think that she works too hard because sometimes she's out of breath at the beginning of class.  She's very professional, dresses well, smiles, is always pleasant, is entertaining, and seems to care a lot.
Very personable and approachable. Loved her class and would like to take some more with her. Her tests were fairly easy and she will always give points back if you talk with her about the questions.
No Comments

I really enjoyed this class. The professor's passion is contagious and it makes studying less tedious than other course when the information is fascinating. Would 100% take again. Never a boring day. The course is set up very scheduled, one review assignment each week, the TA grades difficult and kinda slow so be mindful of that.

This is one of the most interesting courses I've taken at UF! I've learned a ton and it completely changed how I think about biology. Class is discussion-based and very interactive. Dr. A is amazing and does a great job of encouraging questions He also seems to truly care about students. Exams are long but the questions are fair. Highly recommend!

Professor is a great guy and the content itself isn't hard, but the way exams are graded is insane and It took over a month for them to grade. Very slow graders on everything. Lectures are not very helpful, more of a flipped class with lectures being "discussions" where people just ask questions. Do not take this if looking for an easy elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I wanted to do research and genetics coding. I did not. Felt like a waste of time. The first 3 months we did nothing but discussions, basic biology is, etc. Soo many reflections with harsh grading. Could be 3 assignments 1 week then 0 the next. The last 2 weeks we did ALL of the data analysis and posters. Slow feedback (day before due date)

This professor is passionate about entomology and the lectures are well structured.  The weekly quizzes and the exams are awful. The quizzes are misleading on purpose. The exams are graded extremely hard; your written responses are deducted heavily even when you get it right for not including some words. Spelling is law. Overall class is alright.

(I messed up the ratings in my last review) Dr. A is great! There's a lot of material but he explains it clearly and encourages us to ask questions. I love how passionate he is about bugs! The one downside is that he can go on tangents causing us to fall behind schedule, but its all interesting so I don't mind. I always look forward to this class!

Dr. Auletta is a great teacher! There's a lot of material but he explains it clearly and encourages us to ask questions if something is unclear. And I love how passionate he is about bugs! The one downside is that he can go on tangents causing us to fall behind schedule, but its all interesting so I don't mind. I always look forward to this class!

Dr. A is the BEST! I've taken Insect Research, Principles of Entomology and Social Insects with him so far. He expects hard work, but if you make an effort and show interest he will go above and beyond to help you. Dr. A is also one of the kindest profs I've ever had. You can tell that he really cares about his students and wants them to do well!

DONT take this class. This is the hardest classes I have ever taken, with very missleading questions on super difficult tests. Very confusing weekly tests, strict on spelling even for scientific names. Densest textbook I've ever seen. Just trust me do NOT take this class I wish I had a time machine so I could go back and take another class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Truly one of the best at UF! Has high standards but if you make an effort, he will go above and beyond to help you succeed. I learned more in his class than any other at UF! Take Dr. A's classes if you want to learn, and avoid if you want a class that you can sleep through and still get an A. Also, I wish I loved anything as much as he love bugs!

Dr. A is an amazing teacher! This was my first entomology class, but he made me feel so welcome and never made me feel stupid for asking questions. He also gives a lot of feedback on assignments. You can tell he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. The class is a lot of work but worth it- I learned a lot about how to be a researcher!

Do NOT take this class if you are looking for an easy elective. The class is content dense and definitely more than the 2 credits it gives. Dr. A expected us to know material he didn't finish teaching and was an unfair grader with confusing essay questions. He marked off for spelling. Exams are written & in person so theyre hard to finish on time.

Dr. A was a great professor and was absolutely the best person to teach this material. This was the first class I have ever had related to insects but many of my classmates were already well versed, so this proved to make the course a little more challenging. If you take this class just to get the science credit, this may not be the easiest class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. A is one of the best professors I have ever had. He cares about his students and wants to see you succeed in his class. He’s very passionate about entomology and it really shows in his lectures.

Dr. Auletta brings an infective enthusiasm to lecture and discussion on a consistent basis. His passion for both Entomology and education is obvious in both the quality of his presentations and the level of engagement he offers to his students. The course assignments were graded fairly and exams were relevant to lecture topics. Great prof!

He is so kind! Exactly the professor we needed this semester. You can tell that he really cares about his students and he goes above and beyond to help you learn. You will need to put the work in tho (lots of readings and discussion posts). The class was amazing too, Dr. A and the other professors make the subject so interesting. Highly recommend!

Amazing class, one of the best at UF! He's so passionate about bugs and will make you love them too. I think the other reviewer is too harsh: grading was slow but the feedback was so helpful when you got it. Never had another professor write so many comments. Dr. A cut us a lot of slack during the pandemic so I'll cut him slack too about grading.

He took over our class in the middle of the semester after our professor got sick. He's more intense than the other prof but he loves spiders and will do everything he can to help you learn about them. I hope he teaches the class again, if so take it with him!! Also seems like a genuinely nice guy who cares a lot about everyone in the class.

does NOT grade and give feedback in a timely manner. you have no idea where you stand for the entire semester. when questioned about his professionalism, he makes excuses... dude. I'm the student, you are the professor. get it together.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Auletta was my favorite professor this semester. He is passionate about bugs and all his lectures were super interesting. His tests are fair but you will need to study for them. He writes study guides that are very detailed and helpful. Also ask him questions, he was always happy to help when I asked. Definitely recommend Dr. Auletta's class!

LOTS of group work - a very picky grader but does offer in class help. tests can be tricky so be prepared to study. she will NOT round up grades even by a point. i would take her again but be prepared to be on your A game

A great professor who is extremely engaging and approachable when it comes to sociology. Lots of group assignments that are graded strictly. If you are unsure of something, go up to her and ask so you can get as many points as possible. Overall very straightforward class with chapter quizzes and readings. You'll do well as long as you go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I love Dr. McClellan. She really cares about her students' learning and is always available to chat (about both school and personal things). I've had her for 3 classes and she is one of my favorite professors at the university.

I took Dr. McClellan for SYG2000 in Summer B of 2023 and had no issue doing well in the class. Although this won't apply to everyone, I was able to get by with little effort & still perform extremely well on exams and quizzes as Dr. McClellan is able to structure a class very efficiently. Very collaborative class. Lots of group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She uses a free online textbook to teach from. As long as you do the chapter readings you're set. She is very eager to help students, even if it's not related to the class. Attendance is mandatory and your grade will drop if you don't attend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He served as a visiting professor and taught Multivariable Calculus last semester at Bucknell University. He teaches really well on this course as he have taught it multiple times. If there is a seat in his Calc 3, don't hesitate to get in. It is really easy to get a A in his class.

Great professor, and very good at teaching. He explains the material very well. Be ready to take lots of notes during the lectures. His tests are a bit hard, but he always explains everything in the lectures. He also curved the final exam, because it was for many students. He also gave me an extension for the homework once. I took him for fall 22.

He teaches well. However, his test is really difficult. We have 3 midterm tests and 1 final test. The first test has an average is 55%. The third test has an average is 40%, and a maximum is 80% with no curve. Don't skip any class. Homewords are 25% grade in the total grade, and it's easy to get a full grade.
His test is really hard
Really great guy but a bad professor. He does not explain the material very well. His exams are horrible. I do not recommend this professor.
felt like I was being talked down to when I was in his class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Augat is a great math professor although he goes a bit fast. Writing down everything you possibly can is the best strategy in his class because it will all make sense later when you go back and read it slowly. He does take time though to stop and answer everybody's questions and is generally a fun teacher.

Prof. Augat is a wonderful calculus teacher. He always takes time to answer students' questions and moves through the material effectively. The only downside is he does go through material fast (due to the course's nature).

Meric is a great mathematician and a good teacher. His office hours are amazing if you ever get the opportunity to go - this guy is clearly super passionate about math. Homework is generally pretty easy; however, his exam questions are pretty difficult and highly theoretical. You'll have to work for an A, but it's super attainable.

Meric is very smart. He definitely knows his stuff. In fact, he really isn't bad at teaching, I did understand a lot of the concepts he taught. However, the tests are IMPOSSIBLE. They are ten times harder than anything we learn, or any of the homework. The tests are also (mostly) multiple choice, so no partial credit. I don't recommend.

Professor Augat is so cool! I had him for Calc 3 and he made the lectures fun and easy to understand the difficult concepts. Very laid back-- his philosophy is that if you don't go to class, do homework, etc. you're setting yourself up for failure, he isn't there to babysit you. Very intelligent yet able to teach the material well.

He's a nice guy and clearly passionate about math, but his lectures are often proof heavy and hard to understand. Go during office hours we will make it much easier. Book is useless, Do the HW and practice exams and you'll be fine, watch out for the final its way harder than the other 3 exams

Meric's lectures aren't well structured. He spends lots of time proving concepts at the beginning of lecture, which is great until we run out of time for examples at the end. We are consistently .5-1 lecture behind Huang's sections, and his explanations could be clearer. However, he is a funny guy and clearly is passionate about math, which helps.
Reasonable guy. Very laid back and makes funny jokes. Easy to talk to after class. HITT points are given out for free. No accent. Overall good lecturer. Would definitely take again.
Pretty good all around.  Sometimes can get going really really fast through certain lectures but other than that solid.
Awesome professor! Best Calculus professor I've had here at UF.

Augat is down-to-earth, funny, and clearly passionate about math. Calc usually isn't a very exciting subject but he makes lectures as interesting as he can. If you don't understand something, he does a really good job breaking down the material for you in terms that make sense. Probably my favorite professor at UF so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: i didn't really go to class much because calc 3 is really easy, but you need to go for clickers which is annoying.  tests 1 and 2 are easy, but 3 is super annoying.  you definitely need study edge for all of them, but especially for 3 and the final.   augat is pretty nice and not a bad teacher

Very passionate about what he does and incredibly knowledgeable. Lectures were good and I enjoyed listening to them. I had a great experience in the class. Professor has clear grading criteria and is willing to explain things to you, and work with you, to succeed in the class

The class is pretty boring, but he is the sweetest man ever. He is very intelligent in what he does even if he goes on little tangents sometimes. You really won't be able to get through the papers without going to a few lectures & skimming the textbook. He lets you pick your topic for the term paper & asks everyone to share their work at the end.

OC was my favorite professor this semester! I had such a great time in this class, and he made the class very simple. I feel like I learned a lot but there was so much less pressure than in other classes. Going to class is somewhat mandatory, but it really is beneficial to go for the purpose of exams/papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: *** CLASS I TOOK WAS ANT4403*** This class was extremely easy. You didn't have to read the readings or pay attention to the lectures because you are graded solely on open note essays. He is very enthusiastic, kind, and understanding. Really wants everyone to do well in his class. Participation and attendance are graded so be sure to go to class.

The lectures are 90% photos with no captions. It's often hard to understand him because of his accent and quiet voice. Tests are based more on the book than his own lectures and usually include minute details no one focuses on. You have to teach yourself everything if you want to pass. Didn't communicate with TA and hard to reach outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Excellent teacher, very nice, compassionate about his work. Tests were easy, if you read all assigned material. All his lectures/videos were very interesting. Most people who did not regularly attend class got less than an A, due to the occasional attendence "check". I highly recommend his class and I too will take him again if I can.
Go to class. Very nice guy. May go on tangents.

Took him for a few classes. Mostly because I would learn so much every lecture! Its easy to do well with him.The tests are easy if you read the material and DO THE REVIEW. However, he does count attendance. You can have the best papers/tests, but if you don't go to class don't be surprised if you don't get your A!

i thought id clarify oc's reputation. he does have an accent, it does not get in the way. attendance is taken periodically and people usually leave after signing which is RUDE. he makes the material interesting with videos and if you don't pass this class with a b or better, you don't belong in college.

For the Fall '07 semester of Intro to Archaeology, there was a sporadic attendance sheet a couple times a week. So, showing up is important.  It is hard to understand the professor due to his thick Colombian accent.  He's nice, however will make a spectacle of you if you pick up and leave during the middle of lecture.

OC is pretty fair and intelligent professor.  Yes he has an accent, but that does not reflect his ability to teach. He uses powerpoints and TA's reinforce main points in lab. You do use the book to study the main points. Tests are fair and reflect exactly what you are covering. If you can't do well its your fault. Show up - succeed.

The first few weeks I didn't know he was speaking english. The tests are based on the book not lectures but  attendance is taken randomly. The class isn't that hard if you do all the reading but you have to teach yourself because you cant understand anything he says. The lectures are painful and dont help with learning. I suggest another professor!

I took INtro to World Arch with this prof and he is the so awesome! I love this guy. He has a Hispanic accent that people complain about but it's not bad at all. He's super funny and will prance around imitating monkeys and even shows ****erectus**** movies. He's a funny guy, the class was easy The lab with Jamie was awesome!!!

He is the sweetest human ever. All he wants is for his students to be as passionate about the class as he is. After class just ask him a question about astronomy and he will light up when answering you. His class is very lecture focused. What helped me was not taking notes, but rather sitting there and absorbing the info. Didn't really use textbook

Very nice guy and easy A with studying; however, the lectures are tough to get interested in. When you ask a question, more often than not, he asks your question to the class to see if anyone else knows instead of just answering the question, which can make it somewhat scary to ask a question without feeling like everyone knows more than you.

Very caring on reopening assignments, seems like a nice guy but... lectures are a slumber fest attendance is recording randomly based pop quizzes. Accent can be difficult to understand. Tests are the worst does not give back scantron from tests its impossible to know what you got wrong. I surprisingly difficult class to get an A in.

lots of problems accessing/submitting assignments. 2 tests that were alright, although some information was not clearly explained in the already tough to follow lectures. he wanted class participation, but shared his disappointment when people couldnt answer a question. attendance is taken through in-class assignments that are graded on accuracy.
Lectures clearly explained all concepts but some questions on the exams were not clearly discussed in the lectures. Lots of homework but the assignments do not take very long to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Avery is awesome! The class was heavy on AI and technology which was not what I was expecting but overall a good experience. The class was two big group projects, weekly canvas assignments that were super easy, and a written final exam. Extra credit was given at times for in class participation.

Easily the best professors I have ever had. He is dedicated to his students and is more than willing to help with the course work or career aspirations. I would suggest him for any of his offered courses.

Brian is one of the best professors I've had at UF. Assignments are short and simple but are meant to help improve yourself professionally. His weekly yellowdig discussions are pretty interesting and help the class engage with each other. Takes time to meet with students and help fix resumes, cover letters, or network for internships.

attendance isnt mandatory but i loved going and highly recommend going. amazing for prepping you for career and professionalism. hes super engaging and great for connecting and networking. Highly recommend.

Class was just completion grades for some easy online assignments, his lectures were super interesting and actually gave a lot of helpful, real world advice. He seems like a nice guy who looks out for his students. Def worth taking if you can go in person

Brian is as intense as it gets, but he could not be more helpful with career prep. He is entirely devoted to helping any student who shows him that they really care. You can choose to not put in much effort and you'll still get an A, but what's valuable about this course is the wisdom you'll walk away with. Only knock is he's super hard to contact.

Really smart with a lot of experience in the industry. Provides great advice and tools to better prepare you for a career in sports. Was great helping find internship positions in your chosen path. Easy to talk to.

Brian is super knowledgable and he knows it, but he's not a jerk about it. The actual class itself was a 1-credit cake walk, but going to class every week was where we really learned a whooolllleee lot about setting yourself up for success professionally.

Incredible professor. Works hard to ensure all students understand material and are actively involved. Made all students (regardless of interest in topic coming into class) interested and knowledgable.

The Best professor I've had in 4 years of college. Brian knows everything about the industry. You will walk away from his class feeling like you actually learned something. His exams are difficult and he tells you this at the beginning of the semester but if you ask the right questions on the review day you will be good. add on snap for test ?
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Always helpful and willing to break anything down on a one-on-one basis. Tests are challenging, but do the HW and study the review. This will make things go much easier on exams. Labs are mandatory to attend and are well explained. Help is always there when needed.

I think this is his first time teaching a class, so I will cut him some slack. He needs to like be better at things...like ya know...like better...this class is so hard but like he makes it even harder...like oh my god. Like seriously...I can't like not even. You know??
Luis is the most helpful and easy going TA I've had. The material is difficult, but thats hardly his problem. Go to class and always ask questions. He's always happy to help!

Luis is like the best teacher ever. I had no interest in the class, actually I took the class for fun. He is super chill and his exams are fair. Homework on the other hand can be tough but you're in college after all. :D
This class was very interesting; I learned a lot about Israeli culture. If you pay attention to the lectures at all, you will do well in this class.

He is absolutely adorable. I couldn't agree more (previous comment) ..that he cares more that you understand the reading rather than grades. The reading can be overwhelming but you you over it thoroughly in class so even if you don't understand it he will explain it! Hebrew Lit is very interesting! Highly recommended.

Probably the nicest prof. ever.  Grades very easily and is more concerned with making sure you understand the material than grades.  Always helpful and gets to know students well.  I really recommend you take his class.

I had little interest in the topic before entering class, but left wanting to read more Hebrew Lit. He is very knowledgeable on the topics. We read mostly short stories and one novel. Not too many papers, maybe one per two weeks. The readings were all interesting. I loved this class and would recommend it to anyone interested in literature.
he really is adorable. will help you if you need it. really loves literature.

This guy is adorable, and extremely understanding. He can read a bit too far into things when he really gets going, but it will open your eyes to literature you probably would have never read otherwise. Highly recommended.

Stories all short, interesting, and well-chosen. Balaban knows his stuff but is very approachable and not condescending. Great respect and concern for students, VERY understanding. Inspired interest in subject. Wish more teachers were more like him. Highly recommend for a fairly simple yet interesting course.
Really nice and flexible.Take home midterm and final.

She was a horrible lecturer and very scatter-brained.  She would go off on tangents and never return to her original thought.  The class material was interesting but she was so unorginized that it made the class a nightmare!

Overall, I think she is a good professor.  I found it hard at times to follow her lectures, but the PowerPoints are posted through E-Learning.  There isn't any in-class time devoted to group project, so coordinating is challenging.  Subject matter is very interesting and she is REALLY helpful and understanding.
Cut her some slack. She's a great professor. The only thing I don't care for is her TA. Lasseter knows her stuff, I think she is just nervous teaching.
I took this last semester and it was not very good. She said ummm a lot.  But it is an easy class if youre not looking to learn much.

At first the course seems demanding, but shes a very easy grader. Ive turned in complete trash and have gotten high As. She is definitely new to teaching and it shows, but the class is usually interesting and she can be very helpful if you need it. I needed this class for graduation and just sort of randomly took it, but its an easy A for no work.
I've had some bad anthro courses but this is the worst by far. She doesnt seem to know much anthropology and I do not think she could even handle an intro class and this is an upper level class.

He teaches the class like we're all software developers. If 1 person knows a topic in class he'll breeze over it. The exams are hard but he gives a study guide that is accurate to what you'll see on the exam. The homeworks are very challenging. He and the TA are SLOW graders. You won't know your true grade until the very end.
I really enjoyed his classes.

Though it is said to be the hardest course, I really enjoyed it. The process is tough, as he talked too fast and too much in class. But he prepared a lot of materials to help learning. And whenever asking him questions, he's there kindly to answer.
He is really smart. And a really kind and helpful teacher.

He knows a lot more than what he teaches. He tries to make it simple so that everyone in the class can understand. He is one of the best professors I have had, who can teach a programming language so well. And also, the snippets he uses in the examples are too good to explain the concept.

Good guy. Programs were built for a DOS console which was strange but, oh well. The last program took a lot longer than the first four. The 2 quizzes were pretty tough, b/c I think it's hard to test programming knowledge on paper - didn't like that. Def harder than Seema.
He is very good and he really puts a lot of effort into teaching the course. He does give a lot of work but he is very helpful. You will learn a lot from him.
Good professor and he's very helpful.   However, he does give a lot of work.
not bad in this class...perhaps more in his element.  stay away from him in ISM 6236 for sure, but this class wasn't too bad.  he's still a stickler and it's lots of work though, so be prepared.

please don't take this course from him, take it from Kohler at all costs. he taught this class as if we had all worked for MSFT for 10 years and is not one to try and adjust the class schedule when 85% of the class can't keep up. he does try to help thoug
Amazing Teacher!
Very chill professor, showed a lot of passion and seemed like he genuinely enjoyed what he was teaching
Azim was by far my favorite lecturer this semester! I loved and his enthusiasm. He knew how to teach all of the concepts very well.

Truly the best professor I had this semester, Azim was unapologetically himself and a true joy to be around. His lectures were pretty helpful as he went over code step by step and helped you see his process for writing code. Everyone loved Azim, and you will too. Go AI!
Very optimistic and enthusiastic prog 1 lecturer.

Took this class online and it was incredibly disappointing. His "Lectures" consisted of him reading a PowerPoint slide word for word. So sad because I genuinely felt like I learned little to nothing in this class. Everything I learned; I could have gotten from one video of crash course on YouTube. I spent hours reading book/doing hw all on my own
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Genetics is definitely a tough class, no doubt about that. The Exams were difficult and lecture specific. However, the professor offers a lot of extra credit (my grade ended up being boosted about 5% because of it). He's a caring professor that offers an exam drop, as well.

I was super excited to learn genetics from this course but this professor made the material as uninteresting as possible. His lectures were boring and exams were more specific than what you learn in the lectures. The only grades you get are from Exams (80%) and homework (20%). He does make the final optional and it can replace a lower exam score.

AGR3303 With this professor was the worst online experience I've ever had. Take any other genetics class if possible. PCB is a much better option. I thought I was taking the easy route but I screwed myself taking this guy. AVOID!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely Awful. Exams are 80% of your grade and he does not curve even when the test averages are D's and C's. His lectures are a joke, he reads off of the slides and lecture notes at the bottom. Homework was only able to be done using outside sources (Chegg, Course Hero, etc.) He offers extra credit quizzes but they barely help your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Wow. So, when I first signed up for this class, the professor didn't have any reviews on RateMyProfessor. I didn't think TOO much of it at the time, but now I realize why he didn't have any. This MUST be his first class. He is seriously the worst professor I've had in my ENTIRE LIFE. He doesn't know how to lecture at all and tests are impossible

Absolutely terrible professor. This class was a waste of time and money. Far too difficult, overly specific, WOULD NOT RECOMMEND WHATSOEVER. He doesn't put the time and effort into developing the course to make it understandable or digestible for students. I would give him 0/5 if I could. DO NOT ENROLL IN THIS COURSE!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His exams are way too specific &difficult given the amount of material to study. The averages were usually a D on every exam. He gives so much homework using Sapling and the questions are impossible unless you use outside resources. The lectures are just him reading from the notes he types at the bottom of powerpoint presentations. Very unsatisfied

Smart but not a good lecturer. He often skipped concepts or explanations because "they are straightforward." Physics 2 is not straightforward. Also, he often did not finish the slides and, as a result, just never explained a part of the required material. The class is curved, so you can get a good grade, but you need Study Edge or something similar
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Last exam WAS A COPY of phy2054 Spr 2014. U get 3pg notes. A student used this exam on their formula sheet and shared it on GroupMe. Lost of people used it and got every answer on the exam literally handed to them. Not fair to students who wrote their own notes. Don't take ALL questions from ONE EXAM change the #s at least - ur just testing luck...

Prof Avery is one of the better faculty in the physics department, but that's a low bar. He knows what he's talking about, unlike other professors, but he struggles to explain material clearly. Avery is engaging but offers very few examples an often skips explanations. Exams are unreasonably tricky and having a solid understanding is not enough

Every engineering major said they failed their first try at uf or took it somewhere else. Easy way to destroy your GPA and not learn a thing at the same time. Avery tries to cram so much material in each 50 min lecture- making it hard to grasp anything- and then expects you to know all the material in the text. 40% is the average on every exam

He doesn't explain the topics well and goes very fast. He always skips over the math so you probably won't be able to follow it. We also don't do any practice problems and we just have to figure it out ourselves in the homework. I gave up paying attention to lectures and just focused on doing homework and practice exams the night before.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Avery is an amazing professor. He does an excellent job at explaining difficult physics concepts with the allotted time. His only drawback is that he moves very fast, but that's necessary. As long as you take the time to fully understand the homework, you'll do well.
lectures are useless; textbook is necessary to do homework but class does not follow it closely. you will have to teach yourself. all around useless guy
He is there if you need him. Test are pretty hard though.

Worst lecturer at UF. Dude cant teach, he just rambles on and on and on and expects you to know it. Youll learn nothing at his lectures so just expect to teach yourself. Oh yeah and the exam averages are usually 55-60 so have fun with those

Obviously very intelligent, but just cannot explain concepts or get the point across to students in a way they'll understand. He acts like you're an idiot if you ask a question during office hours. Honestly seems like he truly doesn't want to be here and it's like you're an inconvenience to him. Exams are very hard but come right from the homeworks

Avery was a decent professor, however I only mainly went to class for the clicker points and never really followed his lectures. He was the better of my two lecturers the semester I had him though though. I mainly relied on study edge to learn and study the material and never paid attention much attention class and was able to get an A.

Physics 2 w/o calc is a super difficult class and you dont get too much help from the professors to succeed. If you're looking to do well in the class and dont feel like youre too good at the subject, I suggest checking out study edge. Their reviews are pretty much the only reason I did well in the class and I recommend it to everyone.

Solid choice. Class is graded in more lenient manner. Exams would be tough, except you're allowed to make a double-sided crib sheet which simplifies things tremendously. Exam questions come pretty straight from the notes/HITT so study those closely and you will do well. Overall very nice, reasonable guy who's willing to help and invest time.

Rude.. pretty much repeats on a daily basis how much he enjoys making his tests impossible.. bad jokes and boring lectures. And no you don't need Study Edge to get an A all you need to do is do all the old practice exams because they are too lazy to make new problems so they grab them from there.

Welcome to Episode 2 of the Physics weed-out classes. Much like PHY2053, this class is extremely test heavy. Study Edge is a MUST for this course, especially if you want to know what is actually going on in lectures and homework. Most importantly, the three main keys to this class: Study Edge, Practice Old Exam Problems, and a solid formula sheet
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Avery was very fair to say the least. Physics 2 is no joke but if you put in the work you will do well. Go to class, read the textbook, understand the hw, do the old exams and do Study Edge. It's important to get exposure to as many problems you can since they ask variations, Study Edge was very helpful for that.

Avery isnt that bad of a professor, however I'm pretty lazy and either didnt want to go to class or didnt pay attention if i did. I didnt even buy the textbook. Just use Study Edge and stay consistent with them and you'll pass this class no problem. I got a 93 on the first exam and barely went to class.

This class is difficult no matter how you look at it.  The HW helps to prepare for quizzes and exams but it is hard.  I Used Study Edge for the class and it made it a lot easier to understand how to do problems and it gave a resource bank of problems solutions for old exams.  Overall my friends that didn't use Study Edge got about 1 grade lower.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not too tough, but you definitely have to do the homework and it helps to read the notes he makes for each chapter.
Not the worst, but not the best. Exams are insane. I really don't feel like I've learned much this semester.
He was very helpful during office hours and made physics actually interesting. He was very clear with his expectations about the class, and the clicker questions helped reinforce the material better.
He's a nice guy and a decent teacher, but his exams were what made the class a poor experience. 50 minutes is not enough time for 10 questions.

I took this class with Avery and Hershfield.Avery was the lesser of the two professors, but he wasn't too bad.He seemed to have a unique sense of humor most of the class did not get. Uses power point in conjunction with chalkboard. Sometimes skipped important material, in assumption you read ahead. Overall not the best, but certainly not the worst.

terrible!i had him for an upper level course and thought he would be great. he turned out to be very rude and not helpful at all. his class unorganized, he made the subject boring, homework didn't correlate to classwork at all. felt totally helpless in the class. a joke and waste of time. i dropped it. he is not good at teaching!
Great, great, great. Made class interesting. Definitely the better half of the lecturing duo. Very funny, but also very good at explaining the material. Best physics prof I've had.

Avery was such a good professor. I really enjoyed his lectures. Granted, I'm not sure how much of my respect for him comes from Rinzler being awful, but regardless, I really enjoyed having him as a professor; he really explained the concepts well.

Dr. Avery is a very easy to listen to in a lecture, is very nice outside of lecture.  He was not particularly good at explaining ideas, but he is unfortunatly one of the best physics teachers I've had.

Dr. Avery has been using the chalkboard more often instead of powerpoint slides, making him easier to understand. He's also very friendly and approachable, and he makes the topic exciting. Best physics professor I've had so far.

Between him and Rinzler, Avery is SOOOO much better! Literally the class cheers when they see Avery, because he actually teaches the material on the board through example, not just powerpoint. Hard class, but all physics is, and Avery makes it easier to understand.
Avery co-"taught" physics 2 with Kumar, and he actually was the better teacher.  Unfortunately, he was always gone traveling or something so he taught very little.  This duo was horrible.

Of the Kumar/Avery duo he's the better teacher in my opinion. He's not as bad as the others put him to be. To be successful just do the practice tests and homework problems. I thought the 1st exam would be impossible but I ended up with a 20/20 with the curve. Watch out for the 2nd test though.
u will need help outside of class. they don't teach anything

Avery is not a good professor.  He is cocky and unclear in his lectures.  Him and the other professor were so bad, that at the end of the semester they had to lower the grading scale ranges, because the exam scores were low.  Obviously if half of the class gets a 5 or less out of 10 questions then there's a problem with the professors.
Pretty bad teacher/lecturer, but not that hard.  You will have to read and study the book hardcore.  Try not to look for the online hw answers online, doing it yourself helps a lot for tests.

I hate this man so much, he is a jerk and cocky guy. He thinks he is a geniuswhen trying to teach, and goes very fast, doing mental math, and stuff, but he does not really care about his students. Kumar was better, so he wrote an easy second exam. But Avery is so hard, tries to complicate everything in Physics. Study like mad for exams for an A.

Avery is very very cocky. Do all the practice tests you can... Lot of logic, not necessarily physics on his test. Beware of "none of these".. often they are actually the answer. His tests are ridiculous, keep your head up and you'll be fine!

Avery is very kind, and after speaking with him about a grade, I found out he cares about students. However, caring about students will not earn you a high grade. His class included RIDICULOUS exams...go to class and do homework to earn all the available points that are not test-related

Horrible! The tests are way to hard and do not compare the the old tests. He told the class to study old 2054 and 2049 tests...I did along with all the chapter problems and I still failed the tests. It seems like he wants you to fail. Avoid if possible!

Dr. Avery always seemed a little unclear while teaching. He would often go off on random tangents about things that have absolutely nothing to do with physics. It's my personal opinion that physics is the most useless science, and he pretty much lives up to that. Exams are ridiculous and he does not prepare you for them. Avoid.

Horrible teacher, just like every other physics teacher at UF.  Dont bother going to class, it doesn't help at all.  Tests are unfair, since less than half the questions  are from Webassign/practice exams. Average on first exam was an 11/20, considered "better than last year."  pray that you get a good TA for quizzes or you'll never pass. no curve.

He's better than the other guy(kumar) teaching the class. But he is a jerk and treats the students like they are stupid. He said that he try's to make the test average be a 50%. A total jerk, unfair test questions (they are not in the homework or webassign) and an overall bad class. (but he can teach ok)
the class was hard for me. do all the chapter problems and web assign!!!!!!!

I got an A, but it was extremely nerve wracking.  It's possible to never show up to class, just study the book, and do well.  You don't miss much from their lectures, but they do put problems from class on their exams to encourage you to come.  My saving grace was the cheat sheet they allowed us to have for the exams.  In short - very hard.
Just Okay

Well professor Avery is pretty much useless. He's so ridiculously smart and doesnt really bring the necessary concepts down to a students level.I had a private tutor and went to all review sessions offered by SI and this class was still ridiculous. Pretty much I would suggest avoiding taking this class w/him i wish i hadn't.

Professor Avery is the better of the 2 professors in the Dunnam/Avery duo. He is very straight-forward and far more comprehensible than Prof Dunnam. The powerpoints give hints as to what will be tested. He has a quirky sense of humor and always emphasized how much faster calculus solved everything. Study the book/past exams/do the homework.

the exams are not terrible but they will kill you if you are not alert and misread.read all the "remarks" in example problems and all those other small random notes.if he ever uses book problems, they are usually the black and easy blue, never anything too difficult. do all the concept questions too, they find their way on tests

I just fell one question short of an A on the final... So take this bias into account. Anyways, main thing here is that the exam questions are not too difficult to get tricked with when you're deprived of sleep. Sleep 10 hrs before each exam and know concepts. Don't get anything wrong on the TA quizzes and that should get you an A.

"The average was 11.2, which is pretty good, in our view." That is out of a possible 20 points. Exams are 66.6% of the course grade. Assuming you hit this average every exam, even if you has perfect clicker, quizes, and online homework points, you still cannot get a B. Avery + Dunnam has to be the worse combination ever. NO CURVE.

Not a good teacher at all, boring, and not clear. Didnt go to class for the second half of the semester and I did better in the class. Do webassign, know how to do them, many questions for tests come from here

This class is really easy...not as easy as phy2048 but close...all you have to do is webassign and that is 70% of the questions...final was all repeat questions and hw...got a 100 on the final...dont listen any one else they just didnt put in time to ACTUALLY DO THE HW and complain cuz they copies from the solutions manual

This guy is really terrible. He is confusing, refuses to work out any problems by hand, flashes through slides of stuff you wouldn't know if you aren't a physicist. Don't bother going to class, it won't help and you'll just end up reading the alligator because he's boring and just really terrible in general.

This is probably not a fair assessment seeing as he only taught like 6 or 7 lectures all year. Took like 3 weeks vacation. Wrote the harder of the test questions.
