Not very clear in lecture and would much rather teach PHy w/ calc. Refused to curve a class that needed curving. rumor had it the other professor did want to curve and he wouldnt have it.

HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE!!!!!!!!!!  Never did ANY example problems in class..they tell us the only way you will learn physics is through practice, yet they never actually DID any problems in class.  Exams were ridiculous and class was not curved as much as it usually is when other prof teach it. AVOID!!!

Avery was just like many other UF professors, brilliant and only into their research. Not enough emphasis on problem-solving, given he previously taught the 2049 course. He could've given more in his lectures, instead of just reading from the slides.

This guy stutters really bad and moves through power point slides at a million miles an hour.  Not a good way to teach physics.  He is a bad teacher and his tests are very hard, the average grade being no higher than 50%.  Avoid him.
Very bad. Makes you even want to see Rinzler teaching the whole semester.
All he does is dervive formulas... TEST are not what they teach and pray you are good at guessing on the test or you better be ready for anything.
Boring to listen to. Don't learn anything from his teaching.
He is very nice and tries to improve the class material, which is very dry.

Avery's powerpoint lectures do not cover the material in enough depth to be helpful for the exams, not to mention that he doesn't write most of them himself.  Dr. Acosta was the much better teacher between the two.
Wanted to kill myself after taking this class but didn't because then, he would eat me.

Avery tends not to explain things very clearly, though his powerpoints are decent. Woodard, Hill and Acosta are all better and more interesting teachers. Avery knows his stuff well enough, but is very boring and doesn't teach well. Anyone who disagrees has not had many PHY prof. Acosta got me thru.
Not bad by any means but not anything special either. Uses powerpoint to teach => boring lectures but then, there are few ways to teach outside of lecturing for a class like physics.

HORRIBLE TEACHER... this is his part time job for when he is not traveling.... I dont think he genuinly knows the material just teaches out of the book, dont take it unless Prof. Thorn also is teaching it, hes the good one that pulls the weight.I got an A
Most of the stuff he does in class is worthless for preparing you for the test. Its pretty boring as well.
He is pretty lively and you can tell he's into the material, which makes it much easier to learn the information.
Makes physics fun!
The content of the class was brutal, but his lectures are clear.  He is easliy distracted and loves to talk about himself (some explicit stuff).
Was very rarely present.  Went off on many tanegnts related to advanced physics instead of focusing on stuff in book.  Promised short answer section on final not there.

He is a better teacher than the other one Dr. Thorn.  Uses powerpoint presentations a lot and does many demos.  A fairly good teacher but probably one of the best I've seen in the physics department.  Overall I would suggest this teacher.
I've really been enjoying this class.  Prof Avery, along with Prof Thorn, explain things fairly well.  You have to put some effort into reading the text, but it's not excessively difficult at all.
He makes even the simplest parts (which are few) of the class difficult.
Goated prof

The lecture is equivalent to reading it from the book. They use most of their time doing derivations that could be seen in the book or looked up on personal time. They do not provide meaningful insight to the material and they are monotone causing class to be uninteresting. I recommend taking it with someone else. Bad homework feedback & grading.

Very bad professor, seems to be new and it shows in their teaching. All of the material that they lecture is in the textbook and he waste most of the class time doing the derivation problems that are already in the textbook. He does a bad job at making the derivations clear and he is quite monotone and uninteresting making the class insufferable.

there were a ton of typos and other issues in her slides/lectures and homeworks and exams. also 1st exam was a trainwreck mostly due to her fault bc she made multiple attempts allowed and said to use to advantage then later penalized those who abused it... overall class isn't too bad its mainly just using excel. join the groupme!!

Some of these reviews are exaggerating, not the worst professor to have but probably better alternatives. Excel HW assignments and open quizzes due every Sunday, HW could be time consuming but it is doable within a day. Watch office hour recordings as she reviews HW problems, she's fairly helpful. Overall manageable workload but not the easiest A.

Prof. Basinger-Ellis frequently came to lectures unprepared and made mistakes often. During the midterm, she first allowed infinite attempts after messing up, then threatened to penalize students for using them, creating a ton of confusion. Her quizzes and HW constantly needed changes and were not proofread. Take this class with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In Intro to ISE, she was a great mentor to go to. She answered any personal questions regarding ISE, gave great advice (even about classes and when not to take them), and made me feel much more connected to the ISE department. She & Dr. Kirli worked hard to make this new class engaging & beneficial to ISE students. No idea why everyone's hating.

Dr. B is awesome - either she got better or the previous reviewers are nit-picky. HW is checked via OH & you can guarantee a 100% that way. She goes over quiz questions/answers before it's due and you can ask her for ones she didn't cover. She also goes over how to do HW problems and sets them up for you. Very straightforward class; def recommend.

Excel heavy, and assignments are pretty straight forward. Go to office hours for homework checking! Very easy to make simple mistakes on exams but if you really focus on the class it wouldn't be difficult at all.

The one thing that irked me about this class is that the homework assignments didn't have any grading criteria, and after I did bad on the first assignment I went to office hours seeking help to make sure it met her standards and she told me she wouldn't help me with that. Felt a little ridiculous for a 1 credit class.

She is very unprepared to teach her material. Many times I would be watching a lecture and she would begin to say something, confuse herself or just make something simple confusing. A lot of her lectures went over very simple problems while the homework and the quizzes/exams asked the material in a more confusing/convoluted manner.
Class is kind of disorganized. Exams weigh 40% of grade, which sucks because sometimes they have grammatical errors.

I watched a single Organic Chemistry Tutor video and within 12 minutes, I knew more about the topic than I learned from her in 2 hours. Her lectures are all over the place and she makes so many mistakes during lectures. She sends announcements about mistakes that she made on the homework that SHE wrote. She also makes a lot of grammatical mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super rude and snappy on email responses. Lectures and classes seemed pointless and ill prepared. Honestly, they expected too much out of a 1 credit class. Would avoid if trying to see if ISE is something you would be interested in. If it is a requirement, it isn't horrible.

She wasn't bad. You have 2 quiz attempts. Start the homework in advance. The midterm and final aren't too bad if you review the material, previous quizzes & homeworks. Between her and the TAs, there was good feedback timing. The only thing that bothered me was something in the grading rubric that wasn't in the prompt on 1 Excel assignment question.
Avoid at all costs. Her tests and quizzes seem like they were written up last minute with many typos and conflicting information.

Definitely not the world's best professor, but gets a really bad rep on here. She was totally fine. Watched all the lectures online and was totally able to apply them to the homework assignments and quizzes. As long as you stay on top, you can get homework help and quiz help during TA or her office hours which are offered a ton throughout the week.
The homework assignments make up a substantial part of the grade, which is unfortunate because the instructions are always so cryptic.

Dr. B isn't the greatest professor of all time, but she's definitely better than Amini for eng econ. Lectures are relatively straightforward and the assignments are related to what we learn in class. Currently doing well in the class without ever reading the textbook.

Didnt mean to take this class, needed 3 more credits for bright futures and it fit w my major. Didnt watch lectures or put in a ton a work into the class and got a B+/A- depending on the final grade. Posts videos walking you through homework and quiz problems. Met w me to go over homework and even gave me points back. Sweet prof class worth taking

Dr. BE organizes the class agenda well and has a clear canvas page with recordings of lectures and her weekly office hour. However, she oftentimes is not well prepared for lecture which causes many hiccups including lots of mistakes with grammar and the example problems she solves. Weekly office hour is very helpful for quizzes and HWs.
Lecture notes and assignments always have typos. Grading criteria is unclear. If she is in a bad mood, she will make no effort to cover it up or hide her annoyance with you.
Reading the questions for this class makes you think you had a stroke.

She is a very nice teacher but there is a real lack of ways to study for the tests asides from going over problems you've already done. Also all homework, quizzes, and exams are definitely not proofread as although the material is absolute cake, all of the homework and exams are difficult because they're worded horrendously vague.

She was constantly lost on lectures and the wording of exams were RIDDLED with spelling errors and painfully vague to the point where many students would get wrong answers due to pure confusion. The content is not difficult and honestly would probably have done better if I learned out of a textbook instead of watching her lectures. Avoid this prof.

Extremely disorganized course. Every single lecture had some sort of error in it, not to mention the typos on quizzes, HWs, and exams. The HWs were insanely difficult and had nothing to do with what we were taught. The content itself isnt that hard, but it was presented so poorly that the class became more of a frustration than anything.

I had Dr. B for Lean. Powerpoints and HWs all have typos. Every single class (not exaggerating AT ALL) she made some type of mistake. Which made learning easy material way more difficult than it should be. Exam 3 she gave an immense amount of work in way too little of time. Had an A on Exam 1 & 2 and the 3rd exam caused me to not get an A overall.

I had NO interaction with this professor throughout the semester so I'm mainly judging by the content that was set up by her. She gives you everything you need to do the work but it usually has issues like typos, incorrect solutions, or confusing wording of questions. The class was more of a nuisance more than anything but it's not impossible.

Not as bad of a class as everyone is commenting here. Dr. B is helpful during office hrs, you also get to check hw problems and see if your answers are correct before submitting during office hrs. There are a lot of typos in the lectures so make sure to go to office hrs every other week to confirm your understanding, but not a bad class at all.
DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR

Absolutely the worst professor I've ever had. Actively tries to trick you during exams with ambiguous wording, is awful at explaining content, never responds to emails. She is absolutely awful at her job. Shouldn't be allowed to teach.
Never answers her email, every homework has a typo in it. she sucks

This class is hard for no reason. Macro and Micro are much easier but her lectures are not bad, but once you begin the hw, the hw is much more difficult for no reason. Use office hours for sure but this class shouldn't be so much work. There is an expectation that you know a ton of accounting knowledge which many engineers don't have.

I felt like the professor did not want to teach the class. She never answered any of my emails properly. If I would ask a question, she would just have some short reply without any helpful information. The TA's were great but the professor is definitely one of the worst I have had. Only reason I gave her at least a 1 is bc quizzes were open notes.

Very low maintenance class, maybe 5 hours a week max. Weekly quizzes (2 attempts) and 5 HWs throughout the semester. Sometimes questions are worded horribly so just go to office hours if you get something wrong. She's really bad about answering her emails.

She does not know how to explain concepts and makes everything a lot harder than it should be. Please rely on online calculators and youtube videos to help yourself. She is one of the most incapable professor I have ever known. Jesus Christ please save me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A really bad teacher teaches the class as if we are economics or accounting majors, not friendly for people with no prior econ experience. She really tries to make the class more difficult than it should be and I would take something else if I were you.

Ignore the previous rating that says she is bad - in the beginning the class is a little rocky and the quizzes don't correlate with lectures. however, it gets very straightforward very soon and all I did was redo homework and quiz problems and got an A on midterm and final - plus you get a notecard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: probably the worst teacher ive ever had in my life. its all online and she doesnt explain anything she does, she just writes stuff in the lecture and leaves it to you to find out how to do it. the quizzes dont correlate to any lecture so chegg is your best friend. this class made less sense to me than physics 2 or programming.

Cool and really smart professor. There are times where it seems like she doesn't know what she's talking about, but I'll give her the benefit of the doubt with all the work she's balancing. Study the slides before an exam and pay attention in class for labs, then you should honestly be fine.

The first half of the class was a bit of a train wreck, but after collecting feedback from students, she completely turned the class around. The addressed every major concern students had, and even dropped low grades to make up for past mistakes. Her exam prep is also extremely helpful, she has been a great professor.

The class is relatively easy IF you have taken an accounting class or understand basic accounting principles. Although she is now making her own lectures, they have mistakes that someone who is new to the concepts may not notice. Only a few hours of work per week of work, but be sure to take the time to fill out your 3x5 note card for exam.

Absolutely atrocious at explaining any topics in detail or accurately. Lectures often have 3-4 numerical mistakes made during them, prompting you to go back and re-do your notes. I emailed her asking how to prep for the midterm and she referred me to the date and time it was on. Terrible "professor". DOES NOT CARE ABOUT STUDENTS OR THEIR GRADES

Easily the worst professor I've ever had. Even in office hours nothing is explained thoroughly and she does not give much to work with before the midterm or really in general. Definitely would not recommend this course.

She's technically the instructor but really she isn't. The lectures are used from another professor and the HW is graded by a TA. There was nothing really given to prepare for the midterm. The solutions for the HW which was about the only thing to study was given out right before the exam so it didn't really matter. Would not recommend.

When I took this class, Basinger was the "instructor" but she didn't make any of the lectures. She just reused the lectures from an older professor who could barely speak English. She rarely answered emails and did next to nothing on the part of preparing us for exams. The first 3 chapters are worth way more than the rest so hit the ground running.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Homework and quizzes are relatively easy, and the exams are related to the lectures and assignments. However, the exams are significantly more difficult, which makes preparation challenging. The final exam seating was also arranged based on midterm rankings, which felt unnecessary and created extra pressure. Not respecting students' privacy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have a background in CS you'll be fine. Otherwise, good luck!

Only graded on the midterm, final, and ZyBooks assignments. She walks through how the compiler runs code on board to help you understand what's going on, so her lectures can feel a bit slow. YMMV with her teaching style but I liked it. Her lectures were clear and helped me understand the basics. Do the practice quizzes. Overall, pretty easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ChatGPT does a better job of teaching the material than she does.

This class was extremely hard. It seems like you are moving backwards from the first mod. Then on the exams there are answer choices a,b,c,d,e,f,g making it nearly impossible to use process of elimination. If you take the class learn it her way even if that is not how you normally could learn, thats the only way you'll be able to pass.

Awesome professor. She can come of as very strict, but in reality she really cares about the success of her students. Her lectures are fairly long but they're well structured and informative. Don't skip class.

Teaching appears to be more oriented towards someone who has taken Java previously in Undergrad or worked with Java. Teaching is not tailored to a Java novice. 
Professor expects that after doing 1 assignment per topic and listening to her class, student becomes exceptionally good without any adequate practice.

Professor Bandyopadhyay gets a lot of hate, but people don't seem to understand that she's strict for a good reason. Java is a difficult software and she wants you to grasp the concepts, which is why she wants you to complete practice quizzes and complete homework in the right format. Her lectures are very helpful with examples. Be sure not to cram
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Weirdly strict about the smallest things which I could get over if she wasn't so awful at explaining the concepts of Java. If I didn't have previous Java experience I don't know how I would have learned anything from her.

For a first time programmer, Java is a language with many ins and outs to learn about and can be quite stressful at the beginning. Seema is a breath of fresh air when comes to learning Java in the ISOM department and will provide you the best environment to grasp the fundamentals. Some policies may be strict, but is totally fair about it.

I failed Java when I took it in high school and was incredibly stressed to take this class again. I heard Seema had a reputation but she is by far the best professor in ISOM. She explains things very clearly and starts from the absolute basics. I recommend sitting right in the front so you aren't distracted by other students.
Amazing professor. Well structured, knowledgeable, and amazing at explaining hard concepts.

You know when you are in a group presentation and one group member didn't contribute and they now have to present a slide that you made for them. That's how she teaches. She truly doesn't know how to explain anything and just says definitions over and over again as if that will help us.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful class and chaotic schedule. Ask students to download the app required for the pop quiz five minutes before the quiz begins. The whole class downloads the app, and the downloading speed is different, some have to do the pop quiz while others are talking, and she starts a new lecture! I HAVE TO DO THE QUIZ WHILE SHE IS TEACHING THE NEW LESSON.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bandyopadhyay is a great professor. She is accessible multiple hours each week via office hours and takes the time to provide great, constructive feedback to students. There's plenty of practice that ultimately helps for the quizzes and exams. Just do the practice quizzes and attend office hours with questions and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Seema is my favorite professor I have had. She truly cares about her students and their understanding of material. I cannot wait to have her again.

Slides are vague and often missing components to help with assignments. Weird explanations. While the midterm practice was good, she had poor time management for the final and made us attend class on reading days. Some questions from practice exam are similar, but the ones worth a lot of points aren't. Seems like she wanted to tank grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Loved the class & professor as it challenged me academically, the end result was worth it as I knew little about it before and now i do. I recommend 1. Thoroughly prepare for any quiz by looking over her practice questions & slides. 2. Pay attention in class. 3 Always do homework on your own &review it as similar things will be on your exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Tough Class , I feel very rushed to say the least
Her classes are good, but her respect for students is close to nil. Hope she understands.

I think Professor Seema is the best CS instructor I've had here at UF.  She explains the materials really well.  I have to admit that some of the projects are pretty hard because we have to match the outputs, but that's what actually made me learn a lot. Highly Recommended!

Beware, Seema is tough! Vauge, barely helpful lectures, very difficult projects that practically require you to get help from the TAs unless you have a good understanding of Java and/or great Logic skills, no test reviews or practice questions, and if you're lucky she'll drop a project and exam. Discussion are helpful and an easy grade though.
Not bad, though actually expects interaction from the class.

The subject matter was often hard to stay interested in and focused on, but she taught the material well.  Discussion sections help.  She assigns a lot of homework and gives a lot of quizzes, so if you don't stay on top of the material your grade will suffer.  Put effort in this class, and you should be fine.
Not the most interesting of subject matter, but presented decently. I strongly recommend attending discussion sessions.

She is pretty cool. Teaches well, presents a significant amount of information, but makes it easy enough to understand. Tests were fair, and she even has a bit of a sense of humor. Not a fan of the class itself, though. It seems like just a hodge-podge class somewhere between EE stuff and Operating Systems.
Super nice, helpful.She does give regular hw and quizzes but it helps keep up with the material. Tests are fair. Seema is approachable.
Super nice lady. She will read the faces of the students during lecture and if everyone looks confused, she will go over the material until the majority of the class understands it.

Great Professor - Seema actually wants you to learn the material and really cares about the students and if you understand it or not - if the class looked like they didn't understand something, she would ask us, and try to explain it again. She makes jokes in class sometimes that are rather funny. Just an awesome class and professor.
newer teacher at UF.  Tends to give more assignments than really necessary.  Almost weekly h/w and regular quizzes.  Tests aren't too difficult though.
Seema was very willing to help any students that came to class and asked for help.
It seemed that Seema had not taught the class before, and she had a bit of a problem dealing with student laziness. Also, for code listings she really needs to use a fixed-width font.
Taking Intro to Sociology with Dr Beck was life changing to say the least. Really fun interactive exercises  in class. Definitely the best course I've taken at UF.
Legit, best professor I have ever had at UF. If you do not take him, you are missing out.
Dr Beck is amazing. He kept the class fun from beginning to end.

Engaging and respectful professor! He's very insightful and made the class enjoyable. He's well educated and talks about his experiences with sociology on hand. Definitely recommend him for any class you take with him.
Dr Beck made sociology come alive. He really stretched us to debate hard topics and appreciate diverse perspectives. Definitely five stars.

Dr Beck is one of the most amazing professors I've ever had. I'm not really a religious person, but I'd say this course was a kind of spiritual experience. I genuinely learned so much. His lectures are funny, engaging, & conversational. He takes time to really explain everything you need to know.
Dr Beck is the goat. Best professor I've ever had. I literally thought about changing my major to sociology, but there's not much money in the field. Take every sociology class you can with him.

I LOVED Dr. Beck's class!! He was passionate about the class, and you can tell that he cares about his students. He doesn't give out too much work, the quizzes and exams are super easy, and he prepares you very well for them. His lectures and activities were genuinely engaging. I definitely recommend him for SYG2000. 10/10 would take again.

This professor was incredible. I took him for SYG2000, and his fair grading and engaging teaching style made the class both easy to manage and genuinely informative. His in-class activities were fun and kept us interested. I highly recommend him for SYG2000.
Best professor ever! Exams are easy, he's very flexible, and he believes in AI like many Gen Z. Highly recommended.

Great class overall and assignments were pretty easy and straight to the point. Please be advised that the Exams are hard and are heavy scenario based. You will not have enough time to ponder on any of the questions as you have very little time to complete the exam with so many scenario based questions. So be prepared for that...
Not too bad of a class. Pretty easy to manage but some of the assignments were annoying. Tests were not too hard, but I would do the extra credit at least at first just in case.

1000% take this class. Dr. Beatty is awesome and wants everyone to do well. Weekly work is so doable and takes about an hour. The quizzes are directly from notes. Projects are actually helpful for your future and don't take long. Exams are application but are completely do-able if you study notes + quizzes. TAKE THIS CLASS

Professor Beatty is a good professor. He gives fair exams and doesn't require material outside his lectures. However, I found the content of the material to be a little dull. As an online course, it may be hard to stay on top of the material, and there is little room for error as his class is exam heavy and graded on a >94 = A scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this professor!! His tests are very straightforward and you can pass all exams by just using PowerPoints so don't get the textbook! He grades on quizzes and tests but nothing crazy. He also gives more than enough time to complete everything. Do your work and you will pass :)

He explains the things in his lectures clearly with examples. I never looked at the book at all since his exams are based on the lectures. Review the module quizzes before the exam. Pretty easy class if you study the lectures.

Professor Beatty is one of the best professors I've ever had at UF and one of my favorites. I had unforeseen family circumstances during my summer semester with him and he was extremely understanding, patient, kind, and empathetic. He was very responsive and gave me so much support when I needed it. Highly recommend & would take him again!
The class is not hard at all just a lot of reading on exam questions. The two assignments take really long to be graded and require a decent amount of time to complete.

Dr. Beatty was great for exercise psych! You definitely have to perform well on both of the projects (which are graded somewhat harshly) as well as the midterm and final to get an A. He offers substantial extra credit for doing optional discussions (which are horrible, but helpful). In addition, he was super kind and flexible surrounding COVID.

Wish the class was in person as I think the material would be better delivered in live lectures, but aside from that Beatty is an encouraging and enthusiastic professor who designs a course that facilitates learning and self-application through the two main assignments. An A is very attainable if you watch the lectures and do the assignments!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Beatty makes it easy to succeed if you stay on top of the 2 big assignments and study before exams. Although there are few assignments and only a midterm and final, there are many opportunities for extra credit.
This has to be the worst APK class I have ever took. He takes a very long time to grade assignments. If I did not need this class for my major, then I would have droppedd it!
Overall his lectures are pretty good and the subject is interesting. The only downside is he takes a while to grade projects.

I loved taking Sports Psych with him! The assignments he gives are a little longer than I'm used to, but he gives you the information weeks in advance so they are very do-able. Gives you all the resources you need to get an A, you just gotta do it. His tests do a good job reflecting content given. Overall, fun and easy class.

Absolutely loved this professor. Such a helpful and knowledgable guy. The assignments aren't too bad and the quizzes and tests are easy. Ultimately, it's a relatively easy A. Definitely one of my favorite professors at UF thus far.

Quizzes for every module, easy 100%  2 exams, not difficult if you watch the lectures and pay attention. Class is not mandatory, only if you want to discuss the lectures for clarification. Professor is extremely helpful. Highly recommend this class, especially if you are taking harder classes and need a break.

Quizzes are easy. There are only 2 exams but they are straightforward, as long as you study. You don't need the textbook as long as you watch the lectures diligently and take notes. The assignments are hard. They are a lot of work and he really does expect you to be an expert in the field. He's a tough grader. The class, ultimately, isn't too bad.

Avoid this class unless you are very interested in the topic. I expected to really enjoy the topic and class, and its arguably the worst class I have taken at UF. Through the 5 assignments he expects you to be an expert in the field based off of his lectures, it doesn't work like that. If you do take the class, I rarely opened the textbook.

Exams are half MCQ half FRQ. FRQ is 99% stuff seen before, easy, tougher MCQ from book.

Boring lectures, he reads off of a powerpoint, it's hard to follow without any visual stimuli. The powerpoints are super vague, expect to study off the book. Lots of focus on less-tested topics

Expect to walk out of a 2 hr lecture knowing barely anything new
His lectures are pretty bad and boring. He talks so slow and tests you on stuff that were only briefly mentioned. The first exam's mean was a 59 and he said it was our fault.

The mean on the first exam was a 59. No one scored a 100. His slideshows have little to no information on them and he does not explain anything well. I often leave class more confused than before. Do not take him for this class if you don't absolutely have to.

Hauser's lectures are bad. They are so boring and he often tests you on things he very briefly says that are not mentioned at all in the slides. I spend so much time strictly dedicated to this class, where content seems like it should be fairly simple, but he just makes everything so confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class is difficult, but not impossible. Hauser complicates things by providing less-than-understandable lectures. Anything he mentions in class is fair game on his exams, but he does outline specific things that will be on the FRQ portion. There are weekly in-class group quizzes and homework. Prepare to read the textbook religiously.

He's a nice person and is pretty generous with exam curves and extra credit, but his lectures are pretty boring and you'll have to spend some time drilling the vocab with flashcards since a lot of the exam questions rely on vocab. Besides that, most of the exam questions can be solved with basic logic, and the iclicker questions are similar to them

His lectures are extremely boring. His exam was okay, definitely need smokin notes. I remember he mentioned to not memorize the names for the amino acids just be aware for properties but we were most defintely tested on naming. His exam consists of the tiniest details that he barely covers in slides so basically you have to know everything.

He was the most boring lecturer of the three, but not the worst (second best, actually). He told us that his exam was super easy but really some of the questions contained the most random smallest detail from slide 37. He honestly made the class unexciting.

Don't be scared by the reviews- he truly isn't as bad as they make him seem. As long as you go to lectures, take notes, and give yourself enough time to study, you will do fine on the exam. He pulls some questions directly from Achieve quizzes, so study those. My only knock is that his voice is monotone, which makes it hard to pay attention.

He's a very straight-forward professor. Everything on exams he goes over in his lectures. Nothing crazy, a very steady, monotone professor. If you pay attention and take good notes, you will pass the class.

Very boring lecture, assigns a lot of homework that doesn't even wind up being on the text. Told us to study on Achieve, but the stuff we studied on there (and his ppts) was nothing like the test. I'm not sure what we were supposed to study then?? Average was in the 60s, which seems wrong for hard-working UF students in an intro bio course.

boring lecturer. exam was so hard for no reason, questions were based on minute details rather than what he actually extensively talked about. the average was around 60%. had to email him 3 times before he responded.

Dr. Hauser's lectures are long, boring, and hard to understand. Even though he is a slow lecturer, he assumes you know certain things about biology and summarizes concepts more than he should. The grade on the exam was sad and largely because he was not engaging. He tried to be nice and accommodating though. Responsive too!

Dr. Hauser's lectures were extremely boring. I had a lot of trouble paying attention. I spent at least 2 hours a day working on the material (with Smokin'Notes), and I still struggled a lot on the exam. Our class average for his exam was 65%. I was glad that he was only professor for one part of the course (Cells).

Hard to understand what he says because when he talks, it sounds muffled. However, he was nice & he tried to be funny. Doesn't rely on the textbook. The exam is based on lectures. The Smokin Notes was helpful, but you can survive without it. You need 80% of the iClicker points so you can miss a few classes.

Hauser lwk put me to sleep because of his voice, but was professional, accommodating, and humorous. To do well in his section of the course, GO TO LECTURE! Take lecture notes, listen to his explanations, and spend time going over what you don't understand right away. He gave out extra credit on exam 1, and you can tell he wants students to do well.

Great professor, I forgot my UFID on my scantron and he responded back within 10 minutes and a grade. With the curve I got a high B on the exam, but I also didn't pay attention too much during lectures and crammed the day before. The lectures are dull and make me fall asleep. Bringing snacks makes it better though. Do the practice questions.
The class was super interesting content wise. Make sure to review notes after class. Smokin' Notes was a game changer when it comes to doing well in the class

Professor Hauser was engaging and interactive with students during lectures. He provided tips on how to succeed on his exams and what to expect. I highly recommend reading the textbook to learn the material. I also used smoking notes for this course, which broke down the material to be more understanding and provided different resources to study.

Some people might find his talking voice a bit slow, but he has a good sense of humor and all relevant material is posted on the slides anyways. The exam is mostly class content but some homework questions may appear there. Exam is entirely manageable without studyedge or other paid services, just use Achieve and class slides + your own notes

Prepare to self-learn the material, because personally, I did not find his lectures helpful and he is not engaging. I also wished the exam was easier; it was definitely harder than the practice exam and iClicker questions :(

Expects you to know biology before you've taken the class. Does not do a good job explaining the lecture topics. Reads word for word off of the slides without doing a good job explaining. Smokin notes helped me prepare for the exam.

This lad's exam is like the final boss of the Elden ring dlc before it was nerfed for being too difficult. Every attack can only be evaded in the nick of time and each is intricately crafted to boggle your mind. There is no moment of reprieve say for 2 or so questions that actually come from previous assignments.

The lectures, while informative, were slow and boring. The practice test is nothing like the actual exam. He said multiple times that the questions on the exam would mirror the iClicker questions, which they did not. The exam was made to trick you and included almost all high-level questions and the SmokinNotes did not help in the slightest.

He was very kind to his students and provided help when we approached him. Make sure to use his study resources when you are preparing for your exams. I recommend using Smokin Notes as well to solidify your understanding.

This feels mean but I literally had to stop going to class because I was falling asleep. This man has got to be the slowest talker I've ever met. I can't tell you anything about his actual teaching because I could not pay attention to him when he spoke. The test was incredibly easy though, literally half the questions were from the practice exam.
Yes, this prof was a bit monotone. However, he was knowledgeable and gave us a great practice exam and review session. One of the harder tests in the class, but very doable.

I really liked all three professors who taught BSC2010. Each professor teaches one unit and there is no final exam, just 3 unit tests. All of them had interesting lectures and were super clear about grading criteria. Read the textbook to do well on the online quizzes. Sit near the front because he talks kind of quiet.

I don't know if its because I took his class at 8:30am but I found him to be so boring. He also talks in a monotone voice which makes it harder to care what he's talking about. The content itself is not that difficult to understand and he's pretty helpful if you go up and ask him questions.

Very slow, monotone voice during lectures, but he always took the time to explain the topics we needed - easiest exam of the three bio 1 teachers, has mandatory Learning catalytics questions for attendance and most of these questions end up on the exam - smokin notes makes it all easy!

Yes, his voice is so, so dull. If you have trouble focusing it is def a struggle with him. That being said, he does a really good job at covering material & making sure everyone understands it. He can be a bit condescending  but oh well. His exam is the easiest out of the 3 profs. The textbook gets confusing, so his lectures are worth attending.

Hauser is a very caring professor. People overexaggerate his monotone voice, you just have you try to focus a little harder in his lectures.  I personally wrote questions during the lecture and he would always answer them clearly after the lecture. His test is very fair, look at the practice exam! Smoking Notes also helps a lot :)

Dr. Hauser does have a boring, monotone voice, but he explains things in a way that makes difficult material easy to understand! I thought that his test was fair and pretty easy. If you study the material, you should do well on the exam. I would recommend Smokin Notes to help condense the information, because it is a lot of material!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He goes into great detail about the topics where if you focused more on what he was saying instead of the pace of how slow he was talking, he really does share great info. In office hours, he tells you whats on the exam but read the textbook for more info and study the vocab, the learning catalytics and achieve problems to prep as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Hauser provides a lot of assignments to buffer out the exams and tells us what to know for the exams. However, his exams are pretty difficult (MC and written response) and his lectures can be difficult to sit through. Definitely go to class for the in-person quizzes. Overall, the best professor to take at UF for Genetics in my opinion.
Took him for the 2nd part of Bio1. His monotone voice and tangents are very distracting, but the material isn't bad. Smokin Notes was a lifesaver. The first professor was way better

Read textbook to pass this course because going to the lecture is useless! He don't explain topics in detail and most importantly he mumbles and speak really very slow that you can not understand what he is says. He just run over the PowerPoints quickly to finish his lecture notes fast rather than giving qualitative explanation.

Lectures were long and disengaging. I would look around the room and several students would be on their phones and doing other work because the lectures just weren't all that helpful. Professor is nice and very approachable. Tests are not super hard but are very essay/short answer based.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a very bad lecturer, hard to understand and boring, tends to ramble.  The quizzes in this class are long and hard.  It also seemed no matter how much I studied for exams, I always did poorly anyway.  But the thing that really makes him a terrible teacher is that he changed the grading rubric A FEW DAYS BEFORE THE EXAM!

Professor Hauser talks extremely slowly and with a monotone voice, unfortunately, attendance for lectures was necessary as he uses learning catalytics. I had to take a makeup exam due to scheduling conflicts and he made my exam 50% short answer and 50% multiple choice, while the rest of the class got all multiple choice, which I thought was unfair.

Ignore bad reviews! Dr. Hauser is a great choice for PCB3063 - lectures are easy to follow and tests are based on very clear learning objectives (sometimes giving you FRQs beforehand). Class is significantly easier than Braun, who my friend has. In-class quizzes on Wednesdays, but he's promised a few drops. Attending lecture is the best way to prep

NEVER again. So disorganized. Would say you would get a certain grade and then not give you that grade. Had to grow a plant from a seed but the seeds were old and most didn't grow. When going home for spring break our plants died and he said we shouldn't have brought them home???

He's lectures are so long and boring. but he teaches everything that's going to be on the 3 exams. no final. Do the DMS, study guide, read the chapters and the hw. he doesn't curve the test. just stay on top of the chapters, go to office hours, and email the TAs if you have questions. He's a good professor, it's just a lot of memory-heavy content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is terrible. like watching paint dry trying to listen to his lectures. His exam was impossible.

Dr. Hauser really cares about your understanding of the material. When students were struggling with learning catalytics questions he would walk us through how to solve them. His lectures were good, but you definitely need to read along with the textbook to do well on the exam. He covers a lot of material, so make sure you don't get behind.

Great professor who really cares to help you out and wants you to succeed as long as you put in the work. There is a lot of reading and assignments, but they are all very useful and helps you learn the material well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly, he doesnt even teach the course, and the video lectures (not by him) are not useful for homework problems. The TAs dont give any meaningful feedback on assignments either. I hope this class gets better because I genuinely find the material interesting and I wish it was presented in that way.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Hauser took a very laissez-faire approach to teaching this course. The lectures were all "UF Online" lectures from god knows when, and there were assignments throughout the week (which do cushion your grade if you study as much as you need to) through the same program as the textbook. If you read the textbook and do the HW, you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The most understanding, empathetic, and best professor I have ever had at UF.
Selfish, lazy, doesn't have the ability to teach, and tough grader. 3 exams define your final grade. NOT recommended at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE any class with this professor. He can care less about your success in the course. He doesn't answer questions. He gets annoyed when students try to reach out to him. He's extremely difficult to work with and he doesn't even teach the class. If you take his class, be ready to do it on your own, and if issues arise, there will be no help
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class has a lot of small assignments that can be tedious at times. However, they really add up to pad your grade. Exams have easy MC straight from the textbook and difficult free response questions. Dr. Hauser was very helpful in office hours to explain any questions you have.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class can seem really overwhelming, but make sure you do all of the assignments (Chegg/textbook helps). Professor Hauser is good about keeping his exams in the same general format -- MC questions are straight from the study modules/practice exams, and the FRQs are based on concepts on the study guide (he did review videos for exams 2 and 3)

He doesn't lecture, he uses lectures from a professor who no longer works at UF. He expects you to know how to do many genetics problems without ever explaining it so you are teaching yourself. I did not learn anything from him. He did some review videos for exam 2 to tell you what to know for the exam. MCQ on exams are similar to hw. DO NOT TAKE.

There are lots of assignments for this class, the workload can be frustrating sometimes bc quiz/hw material didn't always align with what was provided in the lecture and textbook but the assignments really help pad your grade as long as you do them all and put in some effort. If you study for exams and do practice exams, they aren't too difficult.

Good course! Took it Summer C, so the timing was crunched. As long as you do the HWK (DSMs and quizzes), discussions, and prep for the exam, you should be set. The discussions were fun but lengthy, and make sure to stay on top of everything. We had one grade drop for each section (DSM, Quizzes, HWK, Discussion, NO EXAM DROPS). Exams had EC too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really loved this class, overall. Initially I was very frustrated as a lot of the problem sets require a ton of individual research to figure it out, but I ended up learning a ton that way. Gives little mini question quizzes during class for a few points, and they add up. Overall great experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Hauser for Bio 1, and he was a decent professor. His lectures were a bit difficult to follow, but reading the corresponding sections in the textbook helped me to understand the material a lot better. His exam was not written very well, as he tested some very minute concepts. Its possible to do well, you just have to work for it.

completely disorganized notes, hard to keep up with, be ready to teach yourself because you won't learn in lecture, he's very boring and not very engaging/lively in class. exams are hard because he tests you on little details that were not on his notes but apparently are "fair game" avoid.

Prof Hauser is OKAY. not great, but okay. His delivery of material is SUPER boring, makes you easily doze off and want to sleep. Yet, he's a pretty nice guy when you ask him questions. Now the exams, are tricky. try getting someone else who is more engaging and lively in class because this man definitely is not. too passive in class

His delivery of the material was a little boring but he taught the section thoroughly and tried to make it interesting. I studied purely off of Smokin' Notes 5 days before the exam and ended up getting an A; you can definitely do the same.

Took him for plant PHY lab, and he is the worst. As an example, he handed back 4 assignments with material from them that where on the final the day of the exam. He is unprofessional, rude at times, disorganized, and the worst person to take a class from. If you are in his class, expect to teach yourself. Most of my classmates agreed with this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Very math based for two of the three exams. Practice exam helps a lot for the math part. The first test was the hardest among all, second one just a lot of memorization and third one I would say quite fair. Get ready to read the textbook and do book problems for review. Not a great lecturer but class is doable. Study the quizzes and eoc problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Just read the book, and do the problems.

Dr. Hauser is a beast of a professor who won't let genetics get in the way of a good time. Lectures are important for the group quizzes he recently started doing. Read the book, do the practice tests/problems, Bada-bing you got a good grade. Sometimes he'll give extra credit on a test. Overall, great guy
class is tough but overall great teacher really knows his stuff

Hauser is a great professor.  Pay attention in class, follow his lecture slides while reading the book, work old problem sets and do some book problems too.  Genetics is a demanding class, but you can get an A if you just put forth the effort needed to succeed.

This is the WORST professor i have ever taken during my entire college career. Truly does not care about his students at all. Took forever to return email. Pointless  to go to lecture to say the least. Reading the book helps a lot !. Lectures are not helpful so are his TA. Notes are unorganized.First test, 38/100 is a lowest C. STAY AWAY !

A really lousy lecturer. Gets off topic very easily and does not explain things well. He really doesn't prepare for class. Most of his lecture notes are not put up in advance. Same goes for assignments and their due dates. HUGE curves are used because he has to. 40's are common test averages.

Great professor! I loved the lectures. Exams are hard but curved! Problem sets are extremely helpful!! Dr. Hauser is VERY kind and overall a great guy! Understanding too!! If you genuinely are interested in genetics TAKE THIS CLASS!! If not, take AGR3033

Hauser exam was very straightforward. Spend an hour or so readng each chapter, do and understand the problem sets. He was a very interesting profesor, he kept the class very interactive unlike most lecturers. One of the best professors I had so far and I'm in my fourth year.

Great professor. His lectures were helpful for the material but you do need to look over the textbook. His Problem Sets that are due each week help a ton for the exam (although I think he said he is doing Mastering Bio for fall). Quizzes each week were easy because he let you discuss it with people around you. Overall a great professor

Taught the plants section of the course. He's a really nice guy, but he's not very clear when teaching the material. His exam was really specific and difficult. Make sure you read the book. A lot of people expect a curve in bio 2 bc there's one in bio 1, but usually they dont curve, so be cautious.

Genetics can be a difficult class, but he made it very interesting.  The weekly homework problems were EXTREMELY helpful for the tests. Although sometimes he will make a point in class that something will be on the test, and then not actually have it on there. I didn't read a thing from the book and passed with an A-. GO TO LECTURE. VERY IMPORTANT.

Dr. Hauser is teaching; he just seems to have the hormones of a high schooler. Seems that his favorite topic is sex, or sex related. Often it pertained to lecture, but he would present it distastefully("who likes sex;isn't it great")often vulgar. Can't comment on academics b/c havn't had a test yet, but will leave another comment after the semster.
Whoops, I accidentally gave him a sad face rating in my review below. This is the actual rating I meant to give.

Physiology is very difficult, but Hauser is always there to help. Tests are hard (all short answer) but he supplies old practice tests which he recycles questions from, holds review sessions (don't miss these), and curves generously. Go to class, you will learn. He gives 2.5 point HW questions everyday of class, so don't forget. I pulled a B+

Friday debates are fun. This means you have to always show up on friday's though. Miss more than 3 classes it stars affecting your grade. Tests 2 and 3 are pretty far off then what he tells you to study. Not understanding. He makes a mistake and you suffer for it on your grade.

I enjoyed this class mostly because on Fridays we had debate on bio-ethical subjects. So he facilitated really interesting class discussions. However this also meant that he rushed through a lot of his lectures, or got distracted during lecture, so he didn't always cover all the material on the test.
No Comments

This man made me question my life choices. I got a 28% on his exam, the avg was a 44%, he said it was only a little lower than the usually 50% avg. I ended up graduating with a major in biology, but his test made me almost switch my major. I am currently a PA student and took this class ~5 years ago and I am haunted by that test.

It's somewhat astounding that a course like this even exists. The lectures are just walls of text with no care put into them, they are difficult to read and often don't get the point across. "Tests" are open-response exams where you are given hypotheticals and you must give an answer and explain yourself. Answers can easily be a paragraph long.

While the professor may have been knowledgeable about his subject, it did not translate into his teachings. He failed to teach basic concepts and rambled on about seemingly unrelated things - 27 point curve; Tests were similar to practice tests (The only hope); Lectures essentially useless
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Baer was my least favorite of the 3. The lectures were not helpful, the majority of my learning was done via the textbook. The only reason I did well on this unit was the crazy curve he had to put in place because of a very low average he claimed was normal for his unit. Hard but study and you'll be fine.

His lectures were extremely unhelpful; I had to rely on the textbook + Smokin' Notes to learn the content. The exam for his unit was horrendous, and I ended up with a 60% that was curved to an 87% after weeks of studying. I finished with an A in the class, but that was mainly due to obtaining As on the other two exams. Be prepared to study.

Genetics is definitely the hardest unit of the three. Baer was funny but lectures were boring and confusing and the exam was very difficult. BIG exam curve (like 30%) though which was really nice. Smokin Notes saved me for this exam. Best part of the unit was that he gave away the learning catalytics points for free.
such bad lectures... exam is so hard and the average is so low. smokin notes did not help me for this exam

I won't lie the second unit was rough. I love biology but this had be second guessing my major. Buckle down from the start!! Go to class!!  It's boring topics that are very hard to understand. The exam was just like the practice exams he provided so DO THOSE and learn why you got the questions wrong. He's a nice guy tho and is pretty funny.

Definitely the worst professor out of the 3 for Bio 1. The lectures are disorganized and hard to sit through since he makes everything so confusing. His exam was very poorly written and consisted of paragraph long questions meant to trick you, but I think it was his bad attempt at trying to be funny. Curve was crazy, but won't save everyone.

Baer's class was a wild ride. Exams were nightmarish, but if you stay on top of the material and use tools like unstuck AI, you can pull through. Lectures were hit-or-miss, but worth attending for the laughs.

Dr. Baer taught Genetics. Definitely the most difficult of the three units, exam had to be curved 27pts. Slides weren't very organized and lectures were not the most helpful. No LC questions, guaranteed 10pts. Take good notes and do a lot of external studying. Be ready to crumble if you procrastinate (don't)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor had good intentions but he was a horrible lecturer and his exam was a NIGHTMARE of disorganization and confusion. The questions were indecipherable and unclear, making the average for that exam a 50 or something. The curve was 27 points! Let that do the talking. The other profs were good but Baer's one unit tanked my grade to a B.

Sigh. His unit is by far the hardest of the 3 both content-wise and because of the lackluster quality of his teaching. STUDY THE PRACTICE TESTS a lot of questions were very similar. Very good curve since the average is 50%. Smoking notes help but the practice questions aren't very similar. Get ready to study just to receive a lackluster grade ;(

Dr. Baer himself is a lovely person, however, as a teacher, he did a terrible job of teaching genetics. He often made multiple mistakes either verbally or on his powerpoint presentations. While he did give us a study guide, he made a mistake on the answer key. His test made absolutely no sense, BUT he did give over a 15 point curve.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH PROFESSOR BAER!!! He reads off of the slides in lecture, is not helpful, and gave the hardest/weirdest exam in the world. My mental health really suffered for the entirety of Unit 2 and I will never get my happiness back. SAFE YOURSELF!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures don't make much sense, and whenever a question is asked in class, he never truly answers the question. The exam was difficult and was purposefully trying to trick you, so make sure you know every definition (tedious ik) Plus, he made some vulgar joke about his wife and trashed on his mom for getting a B in her college class. Avoid!!
The lectures weren't the best for preparing for the exams, they were scattered. Test was curved over 20 points for this section, reading through the textbook carefully will get you the A

Test did not match with anything that was on the exam. Boring lectures. Don't go to the lectures because he strictly reads off of the slides and gives no other information. Got a 65 on the exam. Only had a 10 point curve.
All I'm gonna say is that if you have a 27% curve on your tests and that the average grade before a test is between 40%-50% then you must be doing something wrong.

He gave the most difficult test I have ever taken in my life. He was very boring in lectures and the test had such hard questions that even after using Smokin Notes, I did bad. The curve was OK but the test was so bad that I don't even care about the curve.
Terrible. Would NEVER take again. His tests are so difficult (10 times harder than what he taught in class)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Baer didn't use learning catalytics at all but gave everyone a 100 for it as a grade booster. He answers any and all questions in class. Some of the practice questions on slides and old exams had the wrong answers that students had to call out. His exam has a very low average but a really strong curve.

I learned little to nothing from the lecture and slides, relied primarily on random YouTube videos to teach the material. That being said, the exam was fair but difficult and curved 27% which really meant anyone that put in the time did well. He is extremely caring and privately helped me with material when I was struggling.

His lectures are absolutely horrible, so I stopped going and solely relied on smokin notes. The exam was nothing like the material we learned, and it seemed even he didn't know what he was giving, as he had to revise the practice exam he sent out multiple times. Only good thing is the exam was curved very heavily so I was able to get an A.
Tests are written very poorly but he makes up for it with a strong curve. Honestly just study smoking notes and do your best to get around a mid to high 60 on the test (curved to high 80 to low 90).

This professor could not be any less clear with his exam questions. His lecture slides were rife with errors. I knew the material very well & still guessed on many exam questions. I ultimately earned an 88, but the exam average was a 48. At an institution like UF, that doesn't sound like a student problem--it sounds like a professor problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he's really funny but the exam is pretty awful. somehow pulled an 85 without the curve (which was like 27 points by the way), but only by sacrificing my happiness for a few weekends. would recommend smokin' notes and really look over his practice exams if he provides them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Be very prepared to read the textbook and use tutoring services because his lectures are hard to follow and incohesive. He's incredibly nice and funny, but I fear that is the only thing he has going for him.
Bottom 5 professors at UF. Lectures are absolutely useless, and he doesn't know how to teach the course. Test is extremely difficult

In class bro literally just reads off lecture slides, which gives minimal information. There was barely any homework, but the exam was the most difficult I have EVER taken. Bro needs to stop teaching because there's no way anyone learns anything from him. Exam average was a 30%. You have been warned.

Dr.Baer was very disorganized with his slides and they would NOT follow the book's curriculum so reading was not even helpful. Most of his lectures made no sense at all and everyone seemed to be scared to ask any question, when they did he would give such poor answers to the students. Honestly, I even lost motivation to keep going to his lectures.

This man has a specific personality. He really jumps into material and I often felt lost for big gaps. He is a math person, so he uses math to teach the material. He is a population geneticist, so he teaches ~1/2 the class as pop gen, which is kinda whack? Exams are hard and open response, he gives former exams for studying. Bad rep but I learned!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: most inconsiderate and horrendous professor I've had at UF. Was out sick for two weeks w a doctors note AND my grandma died, he approved my extension. Emailed him a week later to reopen my assignments, said no and fought me over email as to whether I exhibited 'extenuating circumstances', said I should've asked earlier (I did, w/ email proof) 0/10.
The exam Baer gave out did not correspond to what we learned in the class at all. It was extremely difficult and had to be curved significantly. I would avoid him at all costs regarding BSC2010.

Baer's lectures didn't correspond to the test at all. I had a 94 in the class after the first two tests and needed like a 75 to get an A in the class and I studied way above the average amount. He literally dreamt up the test and I don't think that I was confident in a single answer on the test that he gave out. Avoid him at all costs.

(Population Genetics - Graduate Course) While he can be unorganized, I found the class extremely interesting. He is kind and interesting and always available for additional explanation or help understanding the work. The tests were difficult but, fair considering the purpose of the course. A mix of reading and lecture. Tests were math-heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although I do credit the man for attempting humor in his lectures, the exam was extremely difficult. The average was so low despite that the evolution unit reportedly is supposed to be the easiest. He seems like a good, decent guy but be prepared to read morse code on the exam!! The lectures are very disorganized and not helpful too.
This professor had a class average of 53% for his exam. At an institution like UF, this is clearly a professor error rather than student issue. This man is a horrendous professor.

Dr. Baer was a fun guy who clearly loved evolution. However, his exam is by far the most difficult exam I have ever taken. The mean was around 50, but the final grade was heavily curved. I studied a ton and still didn't do great.

Baer was the definition of having a funny professor does not mean they do not suck. At the end of the day his lectures were so disorganized that they seem irrelevant to the actual course matter. His exam for evolution was the worst ever. Brought my high A(VERY HIGH A) down to an A-. His exam was full of terrible questions that made no sense. HATED.

BRO his evolution exam was the worst test i've ever taken. Had nothing to do with the lectures or the textbook, and made me feel like I was reading a different language. I did well on both other exams so I'm not making this crap up. He should stick to graduate courses or something bc him as a BIO 1 professor is terrible.

Worse teacher of my entire life. SO RUDE. SO ARROGANT. he literally told a kid that was asking a good question to "SHUUSSHH" cuz only what professor Baer matters. i literally have never been so repulsed by a teacher, their demeanor and let alone their desire to bring tears to each and every student. He made an exam  that felt like a literacy test.

Worst professor ever. He made me hate bio class. I would never recommend him to anyone. Avoid this teacher at all costs. He doesn't agree with what the bio textbook says and tells the class the textbook is wrong and he's right. So stupid. I walked out of the exam yesterday laughing instead of crying because of how big of a joke that exam was.

As someone that just came out of his exam 3 for bio 1, I can say with my whole chest that his ability to correlate the exam with what we actual did in class is virtually non-existent. Not only was the test nothing like what we learned- but it included outside concepts that we just weren't ready for or just barely skimmed, with no warning. Yikes!
Test wasn't anything like the practice exams or any of the prior assignments.

I made this account specifically to rate Prof. Baer. I did the readings and homework and studied for a week. It made no difference because the exam was all over the place, asking things we never discussed and couldn't even infer. I've never had a professor with such negligence when preparing the students. also his snarky lectures are useless.
Extremely difficult test. Otherwise had only okay lectures at best, and the test did not feel like it reflected the lecture content, it more reflected the book content

A nice funny guy but the lectures made no sense and did not line up with the textbook. The exam was absolutely horrible and it is the only one I have ever failed but luckily the curve was really big. Just not a good teacher or experience.

I have never failed an exam in my life and I got a 50 on his. The average was a 45. However he curved it 30 points so I guess that makes up for it. If he is the only option for Bio1 then you will survive I still got an A in the class but you will probably do really bad on his exam even if you feel prepared. Get smokin notes.

Professor Baer (Genetics) is a very nice professor and will answer any question you have, but lectures are not great and definitely require outside support. His test was terrible and everyone in the class did not perform well, but the curve saved us. Overall this professor should stick to teaching upper-level students, not underclassmen.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Baer is probably one of the worst professors I've had at UF. He's a super funny guy but he's not very good at explaining genetics to anyone taking a general biology course. His lectures make no sense and do not align with the textbook or genetics in general. I got a 60 on his test which was curved to a 92. You're better off not studying at all.

Professor Baer is a really nice guy, but not very clear in his lectures. He is very dull and does not explain things well. His test was unnecessarily difficult but, the curve saved the entire class. I would recommend taking his class if you already have a STRONG knowledge of genetics, or if working in a lab with him, but not as a Biology 1 teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was absolutely mind bogglingly awful. Absolutely nothing that he lectured about was on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Lectures don't make sense in the absolute slightest that so many students have resorted to not going to class at all. He admits that we're tested on things that aren't on the exam and the exam was impossible. The average score was in the low 40s and so many students got even lower. This section was ridiculous and no amount of studying could help.

He has this relaxed, almost carefree personality that, coming from a professor, is worrisome. None of the material he bases his test on is taught by him and honestly, getting a good grade on his test is purely luck. Do not take BSC2010 with Dr. Baer, you will regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Okay... throughout the lectures he was fine. His slides are a hard to follow but if you read the textbook you will understand the concepts. HOWEVER his exam is ridiculous. I studied for a week straight, I got a 59. Average was a 44. Just beware you will probably fail his exam but the curve is astronomical. Good teacher, bad exam maker. Just beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Funny guy but gets too distracted from his power points. His exam is super hard and our average was 44% out of 800 students. The curve was +30 points which really carried everyone's grades. Honestly, if you have this guy start studying immediately and don't rely on him for what's on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This guy is a nice guy, that's what sucks. His lectures have no goal, and aren't reflected on the exam. He loves: A+B, A+C, none of the above, or all of the above - he likes trick questions. Studied really hard for exam and got a D, but 30% curve got me that fat A. This man sucks at making tests, and his lectures are meaningless, but he is goated.

Lectures were unorganized and fast and it was so difficult to try and keep up with the material in the lectures as well as in the textbook which was practically ignored. Not a bad guy and knows his stuff but not a good teacher/explainer. The exam was a nightmare with about a 45% average. Beware.
HE IS AWFUL his exam is nothing like anything we ever covered. smokin notes doesnt help, lecturers dont help, nothing helps. AVOID AT ALL COSTS

Where do I even begin??? Powerpoints are pretty useless. He tells us what to study but doesn't correlate to anything on the exam. Not even smokin notes could help me with this God-awful exam. It has to mean something that a 900 plus class, not one person, could achieve an A on the exam; the average was 45%.

Deserves more bad reviews. Clearly passionate about Genetics, but passion does not equal skill - truly the worst lecturer I've had in a while. Cannot get a single straightforward thought out without digressing with random and seemingly unrelated tidbits. You'll depend on the textbook way too much, and even then you won't reach much success.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Truly awful. Does not know how to teach whatsoever and I'm convinced that this man lives for the pain of his students. Grammatical errors everywhere, useless lectures and tests that don't correlate to the stuff you study. When the average grade for an introductory biology class is 44% you know something's wrong.

Words cannot describe how insane the exam is for his section of the class. I got an A on the first exam, so I was feeling pretty good with my study habits. I took the actual genetics class during bio too, so I expected the genetics exam to be easy. Boy was I mistaken. I failed it and the test average was a 45%. Avoid at all costs!

I am going to lose my scholarship because of this man's exam. I studied for WEEKS and I got a 46 on the exam, which was ABOVE AVERAGE??? I currently have a C+ in his class, but I doubt I could really pull up my grade all that much considering this exam is 60-70% of your grade. Lectures are NOT helpful?? They are random tidbits he puts on slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Test average for my class was extremely low and test was only 23 questions so one wrong is a big hit to your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Does not care for student's success.

THE WORST PROFESSOR OF MY LIFE. He jumps to whatever comes to his mind in class, does not give good lectures, and the exam was nothing like what we have learned even with textbook or smokinnotes. He should be very ashamed of himself with his teaching. Hands down THE WORST.
READ THE TEXTBOOK. This man is useless and the exam average wasn't even a passing score. The worst professor I have ever had and UF is not short on them. Good luck
The exam was the most poorly written thing I've ever seen, studied over 8 hours for the exam and got a 60%. Lectures are confusing and poorly written. Doesn't use the book.

His lectures are just what he thinks is important and it makes everything more confusing you are better off just reading the book. Worst teacher I have ever had and the exam was horrendous. Lowest grade I have ever gotten the average was extremely low.

Get ready to teach yourself everything because he's an impotent and useless lecturer, and then fail the exam anyways because he barely covers the textbook material and picks his answers based on his warped logic. Easily worst professor I've ever had.

I had a surgery right before the second exam in Bio 1 - this man told me I didnt meet criteria for a make up exam. I was in bed recovering for two weeks unable to move yet my situation wasnt worthy of a makeup exam. If you can skip this course, do it. The most non sympathetic professor alive.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only good thing about him is that you don't have to go to class. His lectures are beyond confusing and feel disorganized. He rants about nothing and changes subjects out of the blue. You just have to read the textbook on your own and be ready for a super hard exam.

Was a nice person and made good jokes, but really just a bad teacher. His lectures were out of order with the book and he would ramble on and overly explain things that didn't matter that much. Just made everything so confusing, you're better off reading the book.

Dr. Baer filled in for a professor when I took this class, and his exam was the most unreasonable exam I've ever taken. It didn't correlate to any of the lectures or the textbook. He also messed up the forms of the exams, resulting in half the class being at an advantage. I don't recommend taking a class with him.

This was the hardest class I have ever taken. The lecture notes are just lines and lines of him deriving equations that have no meaning to anyone but him. He just reads off the notes so there is no gain to coming to his class. The exams are a free for all & have "many different answers" but only his in his mind are right. Confusing and frustrating

Hands down worst proffesor I have ever had. He filled in for another professor who was leaving the country in the middle of the evolution unit. Terrible lectures, test was completely ridiculous and was not reflective of any material covered or in the textbook. The average on the exam was an F, the curve saved everyone.
