Baer taught the second portion of the evolution section. He did not have very clear powerpoints but they were fine. His exam however included concepts not covered in class, nor in the textbook readings. The exam was curved, but it still did not sit well with me.
Lectures detailed, but barely according to the book. He takes genetics and reforms it his way, making things complicated for a student to understand when we have to read the textbook.

I didn't listen to his lectures because he was confusing, but I took notes on the LaunchPad book to learn the material. Go to the SI final review, it is EXTREMELY helpful. He gives practice tests that have questions almost identical to the test. A lot of people go into his test with a bad attitude and fail, which helps the curve.

He was overall very confusing. The pictures on his exams were hand drawn in case the question wasn't clear enough (and they're not) you now have a bad drawing to make it worse. Let's just say the curve on his exam had to be substantial bc otherwise I wouldn't have passed.

He taught the genetics portion of Bio 1 and I was really excited for this portion, but he made it very hard. Even after reading all of the chapters , the exam was VERY difficult with many test answers being all of the above, or answer choices A and B. Basically, very tricky and avoid if you can. The exam is significantly curved but still hard.

Awful. Just awful. Avoid at all costs. May have to retake Bio 1 because of him. makes his exams so that there are multiple right answers, so he has to go in and regrade everything. Exams are tricky.  I studied 100+ hours for his exam, have received As in all my other classes except of this class.

So you're here because you're wondering if it's worth taking Bio 1 with Baer, well it isn't. He's horrible at explaining things, his powerpoint slides are impossible to follow, and his tophat questions sometimes go against general rules of biology (lovely). More than 80% of the class couldn't finish his impossible exam full of trick questions.
He taught the genetics section of this class. He makes trick questions that only he understand. I highly recommended waiting a semester to take bio so you don't have him.
Moves vary fast through lectures like most bio teachers, but he likes to take concepts and try to add his own touch on them resulting in impossible tests.

Had him for the genetics portion of the class, AVOID AT ALL COSTS! Very unclear when teaching, constantly contradicts himself, tests are impossible, and Top Hat questions unnecessarily hard. Based on his testing style, wants students to fail.

Avoid him at all costs. He contradicts himself and teaches material that isn't supported by any journal or textbook. He makes Tophat questions where he knows what answer everyone will put (the right one) then explains why the wrong one is actually right using his faulty logic. Bad at lecturing, very boring, and can't figure out how to do anything.

His tophat questions  have right answers but every single time he proves that the right answer is actually wrong with some ridiculous way that goes against the textbook or general biology reading WHICH IS HOW WE LEARN WE DON'T KNOW THE SPECIFIC STUFF YOU KNOW DUDE. avoid at all costs he's ruining my grades

Doesn't make any sense in lecture. Goes against what some textbooks and scholarly articles. Cares more about how smart he comes off than teaching the class. Avoid this man at all costs. Purposely tries to trick you on everything.

He is the worst bio teacher!! I don't know why I even went to class because his TopHat questions are so difficult. He doesn't explain anything well and he always goes off topic in class.  Avoid taking him at all costs. I haven't learned anything and he can't ever keep my attention during class, his lectures are very boring and too long! AVOID.

You can guess on the exam and still get the same score, if not better than you would if you studied for weeks for his exam. He structures his exams so that when he takes it, he can't get an A on it. Average was a 48. Listen to me when I tell you this, avoid this man at all costs. Put back taking Bio 1 for another semester if you need too.

This guy is incredibly smart but not so great of a teacher. He reads directly off of his notes that will be posted online anyway. Gives only two tests that are incredibly difficult and the discussion and group project don't do much to help your overall grade. Weird curve makes a 50 a C but there is little chance to get a B or an A.

Nice guy who legitimately enjoys his work and material. I learned A LOT about evolution and I'm sure that he does well with research, but honestly, his grading scheme needs a revamp. He just needs to have a GOOD course percentage for homeworkdiscussion, not have students rank each other based on a group project, and express exam expectations more.

This class is titled "Evolution" but it really is "Population Genetics". So open a population genetics text book and you will find that it is very math heavy. There is no assigned textbook but there is a weekly book club meeting for Darwin's Origins and Nick Lane's Life Ascending. Without a textbook to reference you will have no idea whats going on

Worst professor I've ever had. He "taught" the genetics component of BSC2010. I had no idea what he was talking about so I stopped going to class. Average on the test was a 48, and he was happy with it. He has TAs write his test so that when HE takes it, he can't get an A on it. Whole class was curved so that a 33% was passing. AVOID THIS GUY

Unnecessarily difficult. This course was split into 3 parts and Baer taught the second part (Genetics). His notes are hard to follow. Buy Smokin' Notes and start studying early. Huge curve for overall grade, minimum for a C was above 33% in my section.

One of the worst instructors I've ever had. Had no idea what he was talking about in class, and most of the time, neither did he. Posted corrections every other lecture. There's no way to study for his test - average was a 48 and he said that it was no big deal. Admitted to having bad questions on the test and didn't care.

Avoid at all costs. Baer doesn't care about his students' understanding of the subject matter, just about proving how smart he is. Though clearly a genius, he doesn't transfer information well. His exam was unnecessarily difficult and didn't reflect lecture AT ALL. No point in studying; praying for a decent curve at this point.

His exam was unnecessarily long and difficult. I came to class daily and studied notes and it helped slightly. Some of the material on the test did not reflect his  practice exam and lectures. Overall, I was disappointed with this professor.

His exam was out-of-this world difficult.  Studied like crazy, and it didn't help one bit.  Longest test I've ever had to read and didn't even know what some of the questions were asking.  He didn't use powerpoint, only scribbled drawings on an overhead, and his lectures were extremely hard to follow.

The subject matter is difficult but the tests are mostly conceptual. They're not impossible, but are pretty challenging. His communication and planning for exams/project has much to be desired. The group project is a pain mostly because of vague requirements and large groups. Overall would recommend.

Professor himself was very nice. Lectures are boring and difficult to get through but if you pay attention everything will make SENSE and the course will be fairly easy. Unfortunately, he made us go through an extremely frustrating group project that took up half the semester.
Impossible tests along with a group project with 6 people. Good luck coordinating that many people. Pretty unhelpful and unsympathetic. Curves like hell because he has to.

Dr. Baer was a decent instructor on the surface. Granted, the subject material was difficult, but he made it unnecessarily difficult with his brand of insanely hard questions, and misleading practice test. If this was a 4000 level genetics class, I wouldn't be as frustrated. But since this was a general biology 1 class, inappropriate. Avoid.

He is the worst. I'll admit, I wasn't as prepared for his exam as I should've been, but I made sure I was for the final. I studied for days, and got a 70 on the final. I missed about one from the other sections, all the others were from his section. He makes questions confusing and his thought process for answers is convoluted.

If you can, avoid at all costs. He is a very intelligent man, but his lectures are kind of difficult to follow. Also, his test (well, when I took the class) was ASTRONOMICALLY hard. I took notes in class, made notecards of the important info, the test questions were either misleading, too long, or just plain difficult.
His test was very difficult. You absolutely should read the textbook and be sure to understand everything. I wish I had gone to his office hours. Be sure to attend class.
tests........ummmm dont bother studying it wouldnt do you any good

Best class I've taken .. You are only responsible for understanding concepts because tests do not require any sort of memorized material. Go to all the classes. doesn't feel helpful but it  is. There are only two tests and they don't cover much material. He loves what he does. Ask stupid questions. he'll answer them. Got an A. easy, useful class.

Very good teacher; I learned a lot.  The lectures can be boring at times, but it is very important to continue going to class.  Tests were challenging, all essay questions; but if you study hard, they are certainly passable.  The curve is very generous.

Like the last reviewer said, Charlie is a good in advanced courses. He is a population geneticist, so a lot of the class is taught in math terms, which I didn't expect. He is a fair grader and pretty flexible.TAs were fantastic & very helpful. There wasn't a textbook, which saved $ but a general evo textbook is kind of necessary.Overall a good clas

Sorry to u guys in bio2, but this course was good, and he's a really cool guy. good personality and a great course. tests require a good bit of studying, but is great at testing ur understanding rather than memorizing obscure facts. definitely recommend it unless ur the lazy type (and if u r, get out of biology)

never went to a lecture but read/memorized/lived the book two weeks in advanced. ended up with a 64 on his exam. so basically i got a little less than half wrong but the average was SO low that my grade was considered an A...thats how horribly hard it was. study your ass off from the book and you MIGHT be ok. he really needs to reevaluate his exams

He was... pretty bad. I couldn't pay attention in class, and this is a problem I rarely have. I'm not exactly sure what we spent 50 minutes talking about every day. Test questions came out of no where, I thought, but maybe I didn't study enough. He asked for too many useless specifics! At least bio is divided into 3 sections.

His practice exam was nothing like the midterm he gave, granted his computer crashed 3 days before the exam and he rewrote questions. Almost all of the questions were choices: A, B, A & B, or A/B/&C and very specific.Definitely go to lectures for his class. Power Point is not enough.

He's a very intelligent guy, but can't teach.  His test are ridiculously hard.  Only advice is to attend class, read and highlight the text, do the practice questions, and GET THE SMOKIN NOTES.  I got an A, but not without a ton of studying.  His test is almost all " A and B, B and C, none of the above, all of the above. Go fast on exam (Time)

Dr. Baer is the worst teacher I've had at UF because he has terrible lecture notes that don't have much to do with the test he's ridiculously boring, and his tests are the most terrible incomprehensible, ambiguous tests our there.

I am a Biology major who has credit through the AP. I love Biology, specifically genetics. And all I can say is, Dr. Baer, who teaches the genetics section in BIO 1, is possibly the worst teacher to have ever taught at UF. Avoid him! Take it in the fall, the summer, the spring, whenever, but do NOT take Baer!

Worst professor I have ever had.  He somehow found a way to make his lectures boring even though genetics is interesting.  His exam was impossible with the most ridiculous questions imagineable.  Put off this class if he is teaching part of it.

Don't take his class.  He taught the genetics section of 2010 in spring 08.  His lectures are clear and genetics isnt particularly hard, but his test was impossible.  I took organic 1 concurrently with this course and didnt make less than an 80 on any tests, but just about failed Baer's exam which was on MUCH easier material.  Avoid this guy.

Not a professor I would recommend. He has a hard time lecturing and his exam was extremly HARD. It was one of those exams where you go in feeling like you studied everything possible, but come out of feeling like you knew NOTHING. He needs to learn how to express himself better, if he wants to actually teach his students anything.
If possible, avoid this man at all costs. His lectures are boring and his tests are impossible to say the least. My best advice: if you don't have to, DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!!!!!!
The worst test maker imaginable.

For the spring 08 semester, he taught the genetics section of BSC2010.I must say that he is one of the worst teachers I've had here at UF. Compared to the other biology teachers, his lectures put me to sleep and at times he seems unsure of what he's doing. His exam is nearly impossible, with the average being around 50%. Avoid him at all costs!

Teaches the genetics section of Biology I and does a terrible job at it.  I tried going to class the first few days but couldn't help falling asleep.  His exam was full of so much uncertainty that it was impossible.

The class is very intense.. during the lecturing you know that.  I studied for about 25 hours total the week leading up to the test and felt extremely confident.  Then I got the exam and nearly died.  I know a WHOLE lot about genetics from this class.. but my grade definetely didn't reflect that because his test questions are absolutely ridiculous.

WOW! I never knew someone who seemed so down to earth and nice could be so mean and evil on his exam. Hard doesn't even describe him. He seems so nice, until you take the hardest exam in your entire collegiate career.

At first, I had heard a lot of warnings not to take his class and I must say I thought I had a chance. However, it's all true.....BEWARE OF BAER! he is not a mean guy, BUT tests are manipulaive and unclear and i studied over 10 hours each day for a week and still feel as if I got an F. Try to take another professor if you can!!!!
No Comments

He teaches the genetics part of Bio 2. Genetics is obviously not easy so don't expect to do well if you don't take it seriously. His tests are quite hard though, and you need to know EVERYTHING he puts in his notes in order to do well on the tests. Take Herrera instead if you can.

Bio 2 is a hard class, it's meant to be.  I wouldn't say Baer is extra hard though.  I studied using his slides (they're online) and from the book.  Pretty much what is required in any science class.  I'm shooting for an A if there's a generous curve, but I'll probably end up with a B+.
Tests were horrible. Found ways to trick you on purpose. Who does that?!? Changed the syllabus several times and screwed me over on a test day (moved it up, NOT BACK). Had to drop him.

Avoid him at all costs!!!  I have been a straight A student all my life and received a 5 on the AP Biology Exam.  I thought this would be fairly simple since I had taken the course already in High School.  Boy was I wrong, I received low C's on both of his tests.  Even if you know the material well, this guy will find a way to trick you on the test
not a good teacher.  moves way to fast through lectures, tests are full of vague and trick questions.  i don't think he knows what he is talking about. avoid him

Pretty good teacher, but his tests are extremely hard and very confusing.  He's willing to help you if you ask, but it's hard to figure out what to ask him.  However, the biggest problem that I had with him was his tendency to make jokes about people who didn't think like him...
Not a bad teacher...he's easy to understand in lecture and he provides powerpoints to study off of...his exams are somewhat difficult...but if you study enough you'll get an A
Horrible professor.  Goes really fast in lectures and does not explain things very well.  I had to read the book for the tests, but I still didn't do that well.  Very monotone and boring.

Great teacher - tests are REALLY HARD. He will help you if you go see him in office hours. If you don't study, you're screwed - so study and you can pull off a C or a B. You can get a better grade with someone else maybe? I dunno.
If you havent got the hint yet, i will spell it out... DONT TAKE HIS CLASS...!!!

tests r hard!!  he says theres a curve, but guess what, theres no curve! i was 1 test question away from a higher grade before a "curve" and did i get that higher grade? NO!  this guy is extremely boring nad doesnt really explain well at all...beware
very very very boring! hard to keep awake in that class!  and for bio 2 they dont even curve it, even tho they say they do so get a teacher that u could actually pay attention to

Avoid him if you can.  You can pull off a good grade if you study and such.  My problem with him was not the difficulty of the course.  It was his COMPLETE LACK of caring about helping his students.  He goes too fast in lecture and is not very available (or willing) to help clarify subject matter.
im not adding anything no one else hasnt said. Boring and tests are damn near impossible. Try getting ANYONE else.

Hes an alright teacher. Reads straight off slides from powerpoint but he puts them up online so u dont hafta go to class. Key is to just study everything off the notes since everything is from there. He cant teach much but hes nice and tests were alright.
just plain crap- he can't teach and also can't answer questions. reads directly off the slides, soooo boring!

This man is a professor who points to the projector with a laser pointer and simply reads. He posts the notes online; a plus. I got a 5 on AP exam, so I thought I would take BIO 2 for an easy A, which is now not going to happen. I went to his office hours, and he knows absolutely nothing. . .

Pretty good professor. Extremely helpful if you talk with him after class.  Just study his notes that he gracefully puts online and you're set.  Studying is the key to success. (but that is true in any class)
His tests are hard and class is boring, I went to class for the first half and did horrible, did about the same for the second half. I studied a lot and still got low C's on the tests.

iritating Professor. Difficult material which he reads verbatum from slides in such monotone (that you inevitably fall asleep) and at the same time (dont know how its possible) goes to fast for you to write anything down. Well i can see how, since your asleep after he turns down the lights...

What a moron.  Doesn't know biology and gives impossible tests full of trick questions.  I got a 5 on the AP exam in HS and retook it for an easy A, but I have a B now.  He can't even answer the questions I have in class about his vague notes, but rather skirts around the problem and keeps going.

Hes alright, lectures are boring and all he does is read off slides. Hes nice and a pretty cool teacher if u need help. Tests are tricky but if u study ull do good. Good thing he posts notes online cuz i dont go to class. Have a medium A so far.
He goes too fast, is boring, and makes me fall asleep every day in class. The best way to learn is to print the notes and reinforce those notes with material from the book

Dis dude races thru the slides on the computer in class and thinks we are Superman who can keep up with him. On the good side though, he posts the notes online. He's very intelligent but he does not know how to present material at all. Not very good!

the class is pretty easy, lecture can sometimes be boring but over he is really good. I had a bad experience with my TA which is why I rated this class lower but prof Beddor has a very strong understanding of philosophy and explains/teaches well.
Dr. Beddor's great. He's a great lecturer and knows a ton. The class isn't hard at all. Just put in effort. Also, the TAs are amazing. Ask for their feedback on your papers!

This professor was extremely accommodating and very understanding. The class can feel boring, but that is primarily just the material. It is not Bob's fault, he definitely tries to make it more fun. Didn't give much work and isn't a harsh grader. Overall, great experience.

This professor was the goat. Super understanding. Super accommodating. Love this guy. Lectures are kind of boring, but that isn't Bob's fault. Would take this class again if Bob were my professor. Unforgettable experience.

The professor was incredibly nice, however, the subject matter is super boring. The TA is an unreasonably strict grader. I asked for feedback on my draft, and he said it looked good and provided no other feedback. However, I received a poor grade. Would not recommend.

Professor Bob was very laid back in lecture, but he isn't the one who grades the 3 papers that are 75% of the grade, the TA is. Often times, points are taken off for no reason and until the last paper, no one had gotten a 100 on one. The feedback on the papers were never helpful and the TA was stricter with grading but was chill otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class, incredibly boring and essay's are subjective until they do not align with what the grader believes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Beddor is a really great professor who makes lectures interesting. I particularly liked how he had the course structured, with 2 major essays and weekly quizzes that are worth 1 point each (with the lowest quiz dropped). If you are engaging with the course material and active in class, then you will succeed while also having a good time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Beddor is phenomenal! Lectures were incredibly thought provoking. Very emphatic and engaging. Weekly readings with 1q quiz. 2 papers. Very forgiving in grading. Anytime you have a chance to take him for anything TAKE IT! He makes the course worth it.
Super understanding. Made class interesting and would let the class lead the conversation. Would give extensions on the paper assignments and would grade very fairly.

Bob is an awesome professor. He is so enthusiastic, his lectures are great, he grades pretty easy as long as you put in effort, and he genuinely wants to give everyone an A. Highly recommend taking a class with him.

Professor Beddor is really nice and the way he presents the topics of philosophy is so interesting since you get multiple opportunities to discuss your thoughts of the current topic with the people around you and with the whole class as well. Only three papers that are pretty simple to do and he's very lenient marking them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures can be very dense but they were easy to follow for the most part. He gives a lot of practice problems that often show up again on quizzes and exams. It is a very difficult class in terms of material but I think he's a very fair professor.

I took him for STA4322. Sohom is a great professor. He lectures are clear and easy to follow and he's great at explaining things. If you go to every one of his classes, you shouldn't have to do too much outside of class to get an A. Overall, I'd highly recommend.

Professor Bhattacharya is a very clear communicator and provides very helpful example problems. The class material is not particularly difficult, but a 95 (coming exclusively from 2-question quizzes and 4-question exams) is required for an A, making for a thin margin of error.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: New professor, I would gladly take again. Did not assign homework, tests and quizzes had no curveballs. Only issue was that there was nothing on canvas except handwritten notes that were posted a week after lecture, and that an A was a 95 with no EC. But it was doable.

She is VERY kind and willing to grant you points if there is a mistake, but be warned that your grade is based on relative standing (which curved the A to a 97.2 and above). She posts completed lectures, but they can be disorganized and don't necessarily help in completing HW and exam questions. USE all three suggested textbooks for exam practice.

Challenging class. Quiz questions are often weird versions of what she told us to study for, grading for homework is inconsistent, exam questions involve proofs, and lecture notes are scribbled and difficult to read. Professor is not a bad person, but the class itself could be much better.

I am really enjoying her class. I believe her notes are very thorough and make sense, you just have to do the effort of coming to class and engaging. It's not that it's "her" that makes the class difficult, but the content. This means you have to come! also go to office hours, she is SO helpful and very good at communicating, would take again
Extremely hard to follow her notes and lectures. Most of the grade is based on pop quizzes which quiz you on absurd concepts. Office hours barely helped
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She has the makings of a good lecturer, however there is one massive flaw to this course. I received a PERFECT score on the first exam, but I'm still almost failing. The class is mostly graded based on pop quizzes over highly specific statistics trivia & ungodly long homework assignments with bizarre questions and horribly inconsistent grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I found her a bit of a hard grader in the first reflection assignment with a lot of feedback. But then after talking to her, I understood why I lost points. Just a suggestion: if you have time, share your assignments with her before the deadline. If she has any observation, then she tells beforehand, and it really helps. She is very knowledgeable.

I took her classes twice, and I really enjoyed them. Then I became her research assistant for multiple semesters. It was an awesome experience. I really learned how to conduct international research. You don't need to beg her for a recommendation letter. She wrote a very strong one, which got me a scholarship in the grad school.

Sharma is a great professor, but like other reviews she's great if she likes you. Attendance was pretty much mandatory as she would take it at random time so go to class. There are no tests but you have to do 1-2 discussions a week and you will be working on an essay throughout the whole year. She gives great feedback but sometimes can be unclear.

Bhavna is the best professor I have had at UF. She is caring and extremely understanding of students' busy lives, etc. Writing one-two discussion-like entries per week which are super easy and come straight from the TB.  Final paper is broken up and submitted in sections so at the end of the semester there's no stress for this class. A must take!
Congrats to her for winning the best teacher award.  Most approachable instructor when I am applying to a Graduate school. work and occupations class was so helpful! Nice person.

Bhavna cares! She has industry experience which gave me information that helped guide my future career. She works with you on assignments which helped me when I was struggling in the initial weeks. Expect a quick response and an easy person to deal with. I took this course in my fourth year, so quite helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is nice as long as you're not on her bad side. Unreasonable amount of writing with ~1000 words of reading responses per week and two long midterm papers + final paper. No meaningful feedback on writing. She did not seem to accept opposing opinions well. Wrote all the good reviews herself. Class was easy, but tedious.

If you don't attend classes, your grade drops. Expect to write 1-2 journal entries every week. No exam, instead two long essays. I learned a lot through final paper related to my intended career. She is a very good teacher, and her work experience reflects in her teaching. quite approachable and flexible with deadlines.

I am taking her work and occupations class. She explains old and new economy, globalization, professionalization, Wisdom well. Final paper is research based and helping me refine my thinking about my future career. Attendance is compulsory. You can expect A but lot of writing. Textbook Readings are tough but she explains well during lectures.

CHOOSE 'work and occupations' with her. It is an upper-division course, so expect a level of difficulty. She does not just impart knowledge, she gives you experiences:) Every week is an eye-opener. Different modalities, a lovely game on bureaucracy, guest speakers & final paper is milestones-based, so no pressure towards the end of the semester.

I just finished her work and occupations class. it is best to take this class in ur third year so that you are more clear about your intended career. Readings are deep but Bhavna is a rock solid facilitator. I struggled a bit initially but she is a super helpful if u r honest. I have signed up as her Research Assistant for next year.

Not at all a theoretical professor, thus classes are engaging. Attendance is mandatory. Be prepared to write and read a lot. Loved her energy. No strong opinions, non-discriminatory, stays in her lane, her political opinions not known even if you ask her... she just smile and skips the question. Take her class and enjoy the ride!

She was a TA for the course and led the tuesday discussions and most grading and was an amazing professor. She truly cares about her students and targets lectures to personally relate to us while still effectively conveying the information in the course. Best teacher wish i could take a class with her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took her classes previously. She took an upper-division course this time and is teaching super. Nice person, indeed. Don't miss her classes, and be honest. No exams, but be ready to write a lot every week. Lectures are exciting and discussion-based. Term paper is research based on my 'intended career,' so you can take away something tangible.

I am taking her quest class in Spring 2023. Although she teaches her own class, this time she is a TA. She leads our Tuesday discussions. She makes such an impact and augment our deep learnings. We get theoretical inputs on Thursday lectures but then she consolidates beautifully on coming Tuesday's. Ardelt and Bhavna makes a great team.

She was the most helpful and understanding Professor we had. She provides two attempts to all chapter end quizzes. Group Project turned out to be better than writing the group final paper. She is very fair. I got enrolled in her quest class as well. Takes random attendance. inform her in advance, if you plan to miss her class.

The course is elective for me but very key for medical school exam. Theory explained well. There are 10 chapter end quizzes, 4 reflection essays, 3 exams,1 group project and only 10 attendance grades. shows lot of research and data as evidence of making inferences about social issues in America rather giving her opinions. Adaptable, easy, helpful.

She wrote all of the good reviews herself. Her class is an absolute waste of time. She takes what could have been an interesting, easy class and makes it awful. Petty and rude. Asks for student input and then completely disregards it while pretending to care. Asks for student opinions then argues with them, very uncomfortable. Do not take her class

Ms. Sharma provides a rubric for assignments and group projects, yet does not adhere to it when grading. She is an extremely harsh grader, especially for the final assignment. Even though she responds to emails and is very flexible with deadlines, the overall structure of the class needs improvement.

Last minute changes to syllabus, wastes important class time with meaningless discussions about group projects then complains about being behind, and does not do a good job at teaching such easy curriculum. Pretends to care about students but is unwilling to compromise with individual students and class majority. Stay far away.

I am targeting Law School. I took her class in Fall 2022. She has gone through huge personal problems, but she kept the interests of the students first. Always reply to emails fast. She keeps her exams online and as per dates suggested by students. She shares her mobile number with students. Very knowledgeable and compassionate person. Top-class

Be sincere and open in her class. There are reflection assignments and chapter end quizzes. 3 exams and a group project. She balances the workload as she is very flexible with deadlines. Group project became stressful as we are not very used to work in groups but the assignment itself is very good. If you are sincere you can surely get an A+ or A.

Proff is quite structured and her material is very organised. She is quite planned and handles practical issues fast. She is responsive and flexible. Provides great examples during lectures. Exposed to multiple cultures. The best modules she teaches is around work and economy, Social stratification, Marxism, capitalism, social movements.

The course is quite structured. The class material goes beyond the textbook which is good. Quite an understanding and knowledgeable teacher. I am targeting medical school so what she teaches adds to the necessary attitude needed in a Physician. Her global perspectives are valuable. Her assignments are thought provoking and unconventional.

She is very understanding and compassionate but never lie to her. She is too quick to understand any trick. Her  global knowledge is superior. Her personal ideas are very strong but she always present multiple perspectives and views. So she is very balanced. She takes random attendance, so inform her in advance. Best international faculty.

Ms Bhavna is a great human being first and then anyone else. She is one of the best international faculties In the UF. Her practical experience is enriching. Very flexible person who does not take unilateral decisions. Always ask students to work on dates and deadlines. Her assignments are tough but highly self reflective.

You need to be extremely honest and transparent with Proff Sharma. She really makes you think and reflect a lot. She is very grounded and simple to understand. Expect quick responses on your emails. Extremely knowledgeable.

Ms Sharma magnetises you as soon as she walks in the room. Although she is an international faculty, but it seems she knows America more than any of the American faculties taught me previously. There is subtle aspect of spirituality in her aura and I think she loves her job and has only one end goal - how to develop her students. She is so caring.

She is highly knowledgeable, has global insights, extremely helpful, clear thinker, caring and have great communication skills. Her practical experience provides great examples and therefore helped me understand lot of abstract concepts easily. Superb human being!

She’s a very sweet lady with a lot of unique life experiences. She’s a fair grader and is flexible on due dates if the class requests an extension. The content she teaches is interesting, relevant, and good for anyone looking to be more socially aware. Assignments are focused on application rather than memorization and exams are open note.

He is a good teacher and a chill person. He is also easy to reach out and is responsive to email. However, his class is test-heavy and the second exam was way different and difficult from the rest of the exams, including the past exams.

Be aware- I took this class with a decent amount of prior knowledge. I transferred and just barely didnt meet the course requirements from my last college's class. Yet, this man managed to MAKE ME CONFUSED ON A SUBJECT I KNEW VERY WELL. absolutely horrendous professor. you're better off guessing how it works than taking his class.

I thought his teaching was alright, but he definitely didn't explain a lot of concepts efficiently or clearly. If you don't have a good stats background or struggle to learn stats, you might struggle a little bit, especially with grades being composed of quizzes and exams only. Easy material to learn, but I love stats.

Very responsive to emails. Exams are 75% of grade, and there are weekly quizzes but no homework outside of that. Very important to go to lectures as he does not post his filled out notes. Lectures are very clear and he provides everything you need to succeed on exams. Exams were fair and representative of what we learned
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a very chill and smart guy, but does not seem to be efficient at teaching. It's hard to understand his handwriting and hear what he says even if you're seated at the front (he just got a mic so that's good). Also, his exams are worth 75% of your grade, which makes it stressful. Overall, this class was harder than it should be.

Low amount of work, as long as you understand the key concepts, the exams aren't too bad. Lectures are decent, and the feedback on assignments are helpful.

(took this class in spring 2024)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Somnath is great!
Compared to the other classes, especially math classes, the workload was incredibly manageable.

Two exams, 65/60, and 62/60. 
1 HW per module, 6 total, lowest drops. An avg. of 90% and above is an A! 
The HW is 2 to 5 questions 

1 R Project (20% weight, and easy!). 

He made it as easy as anyone could make this class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really caring professor. Will give partial credit if you show your work. The class is not difficult to pass as long as you complete all the assignments. Plenty of practice problems provided to prepare for exams.

He's a really nice guy, new to teaching but he's very forgiving. There are 6 homework assignments (40%) and 3 exams (60%). The class was apparently easier than a lot of the other professors at the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's really nice, the class was just hard because there were so many readings, She really tried to help.

Best professor I've had so far at the University of Arizona. Her RELI160A1 course was easy and straight forward. I never used the textbook and never read, I would only read if I needed quotes for discussion posts. Her class is lecture heavy and attendance is required. She is a very nice professor overall, do the work and you'll get an A.
This class was great and so was the professor. She is very knowledgeable in her subject.

This professor changed my life for the better and I highly recommend that you take her course and take it seriously. She is incredibly knowledgable, kind, and flexible. This is the sort of professor who spends time thinking about how to make the experience both enjoyable and informative for you. I couldn't possibly recommend her enough.

Dr. Mamtora is a very caring professor and also is very flexible with her deadlines, she is very understanding if you have an event coming up or are struggling through some material. She gives great advice and always tries to open discussion in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: the best and nicest teacher I have had. very accommodating to students' needs and willing to compromise. sweet, but not a pushover. her class was enjoyable

She is super nice and cares. Go to office hours if you are stuck. She is actually invested in making you a better writer. Lots of writing, but it is a writing class. As an engineering major, I would not choose to take this class but it is required. She makes it better. It is just awkward in class when she asks questions and no one answers.

Easy A, no need for textbook. Class consists of discussions and tests that are easy to do and do well on, there are no additional assignments. One big research paper for this class that is easy as well, I wrote it the day it was due and I got a hundred percent on it. This class is very very easy.

Took this for my Summer A elective as a Public Health major. There was a minimum of 300-500 words for every assignment, discussion & journal. This class was interesting but added unnecessary stress. Communication and grading was divided between the professor and 2 TAs making communication with the professor difficult for me. I would not retake.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: As an anthropology major, this was the most difficult class I have ever taken. Even though the material was interesting, the expectation was unrealistic as she doesn't give clear instructions at all. We had at least 3 hours of homework every night (including holidays) and I wrote more in this course than any of my English classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: 6-week class, so it is understandable that this would be a lot, but this class was horrible in the way it was structured. Just because it is an online class doesn't justify giving us assignments on the weekend. Grading is unreasonable and completely random. Teacher is not clear and then rude? Take it with someone else.Topics are great, teacher isnt
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst class I've taken. This class requires an assignment due every day for 6 weeks, plus 100+ pg readings, lectures, & videos for each module with 2 modules due a week. The professor's instructions are sometimes unclear and contradictory. I got an A on every assignment, but I dedicated between 5-10 hours to each one. Interesting, but not worth it.

This is the worst class I have ever taken.There was an assignment due every single day that would take hours.The TAs are awful and the professor is not helpful.They grade incredibly hard and are not clear on the requirements for each assignment.If your happiness means anything to you DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! At least the information was interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst class I have taken in 3 years of college.A gargantuan amount of writing assignments due nearly every day of the week including weekends. On top of that, grading is inconsistent, incredibly strict, and nonsensical. This is the first review I have ever left for a class and that speaks for itself. If I could leave 0 stars I would.Summer A ruined
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Save yourself from wanting to drop out because of this professor. Take's off points for things that weren't even clarified, then is passive aggressive in emails and quite literally stops responding when you bring up a genuine argument as to why you deserve credit for something. An interesting class that is ruined by an absolutely horrible teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you don't have to take this class DO NOT TAKE IT. I took this class during summer A and we had assignments due EVERY SINGLE DAY. These assignments took me 3 hours minimum per day due to the extremely strict grading and the large readings and lectures required for each assignment. You are only given 1hr 40min to complete 2 essay exam...

Professor Bhushan is nice enough, but oh my god is this class so much work. If you can avoid this class, just take something else, especially if you're taking it over the summer. There was a 500 word minimum assignment due every single night (though you'll receive points off unless you go 200 words above the word count). Take something else! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Global Health Culture is by far the most work I've ever received from a class. I took this in 6 weeks over summer so I understand that this naturally entails a lot of work, but this is brutal. I'm a 4th year Mechanical Engineering student (taking this for gen ed) and I have never had so much work from a class. Super long readings and tough grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A very solid lecturer who did many helpful practice problems and always made himself available outside of class for extra help. A bit lazy with making exams, but that actually works in the students' favor. Was pretty sensitive to questions that may contain some criticism and would look to turn them into an annoying life lesson.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is probably one of the most straight forward professors I've taken at UF. The exam and quiz problems are just problems taken from the book, and so there are not really any curveballs. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lectures are clear with a ton of helpful practice problems. He does the homework problems during OH. He picks problems for homework and exams from the textbook, so I HIGHLY recommend doing practice fundamental problems and reviewing HW questions when preparing for tests. Expect most communication to be done through TAs. Overall pretty fair class

Good guy, interesting class. The exams were very fair, and the homework could be challenging but he always helped us out if there was something we were really confused on. Quizzes throughout the semester were also fair, and you get a drop. Solid choice.

Dr. Sankar's "APPLIED ELASTICITY AND ADVANCED MECHANICS OF SOLIDS" is the best class I have ever had. He is a true expert in this field (also in Fracture Mechanics and Finite Element methods), which shows in his lectures, assignments and exams that are very well designed to help make your fundamentals rock solid.
Heavy homework is true. But I think it should be like that. If you are not hardworking enough, do not blame your professor!

I give 1 not because he's so bad but just let you guys come to see what I write. Sankar may looks too high of some of his students, especially some international (Chinese) students like me. I don't think it is a good idea to pick his class in the first semester if you are not so good at your English and understanding of engineering stuffs.

He was  my Master's adviser, I consider himself one of the greatest influences in my life. I teach his principles to my kid. An encyclopedia of knowledge, knows your weaknesses very quickly and awesome communicator. Need to understand his point of view. A great original thinker fantastic human being.

Professor Sankar is a great professor. I took him for aerostructures which is just re-emphasizing mechanics of materials. You have to pay attention in class because he is a little soft spoken and sometime hard to hear. Otherwise, I think he did a great job. Helpful both in office hours and during class and very knowledgeable of the subject matter.

Lots of Hw, and its graded very rigorously. His accent is thick and he doesn't communicate with the students very well. He's very interested in the material hes teaching, just doesn't realize that were new to the material. Its just MOM on steroids.  Not much involving actual aircraft strcutures

Sankar is AMAZING. Fair warning: He moves through the material kind of fast and has a quiet/accented voice. Other than that, Sankar cares tremendously for his students. One time, I completely forgot to make a formula sheet for a quiz, so he took another person's formula sheet (with consent of course), photocopied it, and gave it to me for use!
WORST PROF. KNOWS HIS SUBJECT BUT ASSUMES STUDENTS KNOW AS WELL. IS IN HIS OWN WORLD WHILE TEACHING. DIDNT UNDERSTAND A THING AND MANAGED TO SCRAPE THROUGH. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS
Pretty good teacher. He explains the concepts, then does a lot of examples. Class is based on:3 exams and Hw (10% of grade). A Hw assignment of 2 problems is due every class.

Dr. Sankar is smart.  So smart that he forgot how it was to be a student.  No one said Statics is easy but he make it 10X hard by his style of teaching and by not answering question.  I can understand such thing for a high level class.  Now tell me why when I had Dr. Dickrell statics was a breeze but when Sankar replaced her it was hell?
Very good professor. As long as you are in class, you will learn what you need for the tests.

Prof. Suman is hands down the WORST, teacher I could have ever had. The Fall 2020 semester was one of the worst I've ever had at UF. There were several occasions where he treated students horribly, at one point demanding from a student why they needed to know stuff for an exam. Would refuse to help students, never showed where we went wrong

The curriculum isnt that difficult if you are good at math. There is always a way to get more practice or help. A few projects, but the grading criteria is very understandable. Youll get a good grade if you just put in effort.

Do NOT sign up for this class! Suman gives way too much work, and doesn't make any effort to connect to or provide aid to his students. Expect multiple quizzes a week, with 3 projects throughout the semester that are harshly graded. If you want to pass, seek outside help.

I was super involved in the course, yet did terrible on every exam. He does NOT curve, even when one of the mean grades was below passing. I literally follow his mini projects verbatim and still don't get a 100, yet he never explains why. I do not suggest this class
Suman does not teach, instead, he just links the students to pre-recorded videos which are confusing and difficult to understand. Avoid this class at all costs...

I studied for every single quiz and exam for this class. I passed every single quiz but somehow manages to fail every single exam. When I emailed Suman, he very passsive aggressively told me there was nothing I can do and to try harder. He also refused me from seeing my exam questions from any of the previous exams. Do not take with this man

DON'T TAKE! This teacher was unreachable. If he did respond, it was to direct you to the TAs (who were no help either) or passive-aggressively ask you "Why do you need this?", refusing to answer your question on the material. He drops 3 quiz grades which is nice, but there has been absolutely NO EXTRA CREDIT and most of the students are failing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The easiest A I've ever received. I only showed up to class once other than the exam days and I aced the class without issues. He gives tons of extra credit which makes the class a breeze.

Goes deep into statistics,gives a good amount of homework but the tests are based on them, and is very caring towards his students. Truly passionate in his profession and only wants to share that passion with his students. Book not required, 7 biweekly quizzes, 3 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: HE IS AMAZING. HE REALLY WANTED HIS STUDENTS TO SUCCEED. He had no idea what he was doing in the bebgining of the semester (he was teaching discrete math type material that wasnt even related), but the students helped shape him in to a decent lecturer. Tons of extra credit.

This course was an actual roller coaster. The first couple weeks were brutal, and the material being taught was way beyond the scope of the curriculum. Everyone failed the first quiz, but everything went uphill from there. Tons of extra credit (and Im not exaggerating). You could fail all the exams and still end up with an A.
You have to take the initiative to do the practice problems but they really help explain the statistics.

I received an A in this course, and I learned zero statistics this semester. Difficulty of assignments, quizzes, and exams was incredibly inconsistent. If you want to get credit for STA3032, take this class. If you want to learn statistics, look elsewhere. Suman is a bad teacher and bad lecturer.
Legendary. Dude's way nicer to students than he needs to be

I would say this class is really fast-paced. Although he usually just reads off his well-made notes on the topic, I wouldn't suggest skipping his lectures. You know how you were just given the pythagorean theorem in the past and just accepted how it works? That's basically what I feel like it he does with statistic ideas. Def need to self-study
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: the nicest professor I've ever had at UF. He genuinely loves the subject he teaches and makes it so so interesting! Grades pretty easy as long as you literally just go to class and listen to him.  Anyone who says he grades hard probably just never went to class because his essay prompts for the exam are so predictable.
If you memorize the slides and listen to lectures you will be fine. There are readings but you do not need to do them at all. The exams are straightforward and straight from the slides.
pretty chill class, exams are written and he's not a harsh grader

Teaches extremely well. Easy to talk to, will listen to any questions you have and will help expand on them. Extremely smart and informative, does not judge students differently based on beliefs, but rather allows them to expand on their beliefs and demonstrates the importance of learning about all sides of a political conflict.
Can be hard on you if you're not prepared.

He is an ok professor. Clearly passionate about what he teaches but he does not grade exams well. He will not give clear feedback on exams and grades somewhat subjectively. I do not really recommend, take another class if you can. I don't want to be unkind but thought I would share my experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, if you think he's some hardass professor you either use chatgpt
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: James was honestly a terrible professor overall. While the class information was interesting he honestly made it feel boring. He would just ramble in class and then grade your essays based on his personal opinions. He has no rubrics and uses participation to tank your grade. Don't take this class and tell everyone you know no to. Have a nice day :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Thorough lecturer, offers a plethora of case studies to support theoretical concepts discussed in class, and provides a list of the names these case studies on his tests to make sure you have something to write about if you draw a blank. A confusing grader due to illegible handwriting and the lack of a clear rubric, but a great guy and a fun class.

James is a bad teacher. He only accepts answers if they align with his personal views or follow exactly what he wants them to say. However, he doesn't tell you what he expects and instead gives poor and unhelpful feedback. Also his lectures are not good as he just rambles about random things. Overall, I would not take this class.

Be warned, this class's grade depends heavily on very few things, attendance and exams only. With this in mind, if you are not the going to class type, I would hold off on this one if you can. James however is a great lecturer and clearly is passionate about the material. Go to office hours if you want better grades on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a good professor, just make sure you attend office hours to make sure your paper and exams contain what he is looking for. He is definitely a bit picky with grading but as long as you show interest and participate you will be able to secure a good grade in his class. I would definitely take him again.

He's kind, caring, and genuinely wants his students to do well. The only grades were the exams, which are timed essays. The grading seems pretty confusing but you'll do well if you know the content. The content itself is extremely easy to understand. Attendance and participation are tracked.

Extremely nitpicky. Whenever you write about class concepts, it has to be worded exactly how he expects it to be. This was stressful at first, but I did a lot better in the class when I came to terms that he will critique whatever I write, so I couldn't care as much. He's a good guy and willing to help you. Lectures are convoluted but OH will help.

2 essays/2 exams. He's passionate about the subject, but in an obnoxious way. Goes on a 50-min rant about the content, then asks if we have questions when no one grasped what he said. The course content is interesting but if you don't read his mind on what he wants you to write, you won't succeed in the assignments. Take smth else if you can.

This is my second semester in a row with James, please take his classes! This class is super interesting...highly theoretical. Dives into security studies, theories, and current examples. Graded on 2 written exams, 1 paper, attendance, and participation. James is kind, funny, accessible, and cares a lot about his students. Go to his office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Glen succeeded in making what should have been a manageable course unnecessarily difficult and frustrating. Not only did lectures lack any coherency or structure, important concepts were too often explained in a confusing way or not at all. He also rarely gave assignment instructions that were complete.

He is an amazing professor. He truly understands students, and is a great lecturer, even though it could be heavy on some days. It's a required class for Sustainability Majors, and I really enjoyed it.

I had Glen for the Fall 2023 semester for American Political Thought, and he was a very informative and kind professor who truly cared about the material he chose and the student's involvement in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A fantastic professor and a great person

Glen is a great professor that is extremely responsive to his students. He did require us to keep physical versions of the books we read, but it was definitely useful. His lectures are amazing and have a lot of information. Participation does matter but his class structure makes it so unintimidating.

Professor Billesbach is hands down one of the best university professors at UF! His lectures are fun, easy to understand, and he really tries to break down the content so each student understands the material. He encourages participation, lectures are great, and the readings are super interesting. Take this professor for any POT class at UF!

He's the best! If you're looking for a passionate professor with clear grading outlines, great office hours, and an overall happy demeanor: TAKE HIS CLASS. The texts are super interesting, not too difficult to understand, and he's super understanding if you have problems in class. Just listen in on the lectures and you'll do great on the essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is so entertaining and easy to approach. He cares about his students and he loves when they participate. Graded by weekly worksheets based on the books we read, discussions, and two essays. He loves to relate to things outside of political science which makes the class even more fun. great lecturer and amazing professor!

One of the most caring professors I've had. After doing poorly on the first exam, he helped me a lot and I was able to improve my grades significantly. The quizzes can be challenging and interesting but they're doable. I really enjoyed the class overall and don't agree with the negative review. I would definitely take this course again.

Although he is a really nice guy himself and he is lenient, you won't learn anything. He is really confusing and expects you to know the content without even teaching it. Whoever gave him a 5 is lying to you and praying on your downfall. Just don't take his class if you can avoid it.

The course itself can be dry but he is 110% productive in class going through problems. Course is graded on four exams each 15% of your grade. Another 25% are homework assignments and the rest 15% are random quizzes that include attendance.
His class is super easy and he really cares about his students. He's really approachable and funny. He can be rather repetitive and the class has a lot of reading.

This class is an easy A, especially with Dr. Bird. I overslept and missed a quiz, and he let me take it later with no penalty. He is very considerate and tries his best to keep the class engaging. The weekly discussion posts are annoying but very easy. Dr. Bird is the most far-reaching, grassroots, and consequential professor at UF. iykyk.

I took his class as a senior engineering student and actually found the class to be interesting and not just a waste of time. I did feel slightly unprepared for exams due to the fact that he did not give us a guideline of what to study. There were too many questions about dates of events and also small facts that were mentioned once.

This professor has great lectures and very passionate about the subject matter. He doesn't require that you attend but has in-class practice quizzes on most lecture days to make sure that people come. The class is not test heavy, just a midterm and a final. Also, there are planned quizzes throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Exams aren't hard but you need to study for them, essays aren't too bad either. Don't save the discussion readings for the last minute, some of them are long. Dr. Bird cares about what we need to learn from this country's history and why it's important; highly recommend giving this class the time of day, even if you only take it for gen ed credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Bird's enthusiasm for history is contagious. Even as a STEM person, I genuinely looked forward to this class. The material can be heavy, but he always handles it with respect. You can tell he really cares about the class and about his students and values learning over grades- grading was super easy and most stuff could be resubmitted.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bird is so entertaining and a good lecturer. This class is super easy as long as you study vocab words before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Doctor Bird is absolutely amazing, and I could not recommend him enough. He enjoys teaching, and his students can tell. He requires weekly discussion posts, attendance quizzes, 50 states, 12 countries, amendment and timeline quizzes, two papers, and two exams. The tests are easy if you study for about four hours. Overall, they are super doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class was not as easy as other people had said. The TA you are assigned grade the essay portion of the exams. Bird doesn't give clear guidance on how the essays are graded, and the TA gives no help and expects detailed writing. The multiple-choice section of the exams had no study guide, and he just said to read the textbook. Not worth it.

Dr. Bird is an excellent professor, his knowledge and passion made his lectures really engaging and the readings are great. He was graceful at navigating the hard questions of American history and engaged with students who disagreed instead of shutting them down. 

He gave me an extension on an essay when I emailed, super approachable and nice.
Genuinely such a dynamic and engaging individual. Unafraid of confronting uncomfortable history and does so with tact. We had reading (from an onand discussion posts

Dr. Bird is one of my favorite professors that I have had at UF. His lectures are interesting and engaging. Dr. Bird is extremely knowledgable and provides valuable insight on many topics. While this class is not attendance based, there are pop quizzes most days that require a daily code to access.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: It's clear that Dr. Bird cares a lot about American history and about teaching students about the less comfortable aspects of that history. He handled a lot of these sensitive subjects with care and he was very accessible. I think a lot of people who aren't as interested in history will still get a lot out of this class.

Love this professor. Even though it's history and has nothing to do with my major, he makes the class very interesting with how passionate he is about the subject. He also listens to the class about feedback and is willing to push back dates on quizzes and assignments based on class consensus. Only about 1 discussion post per week for assignments.

THE nicest person, quirky guy. Really cares about your wellbeing, is super accessible & accommodating. I took his Uncommon Reads course, "Democracy in Black and White"; he's clearly passionate & knowledgeable about the subject. Facilitates great discussions, readings aren't too heavy, graded on weekly discussion board posts & a final essay.

This theoretically should've been a very easy class, but the quizzes, speeches, and outlines made it somewhat difficult at times. Professor Bitrus is very nice and understanding, and his passion for public speaking made the class enjoyable. As long as you follow his instructions exactly and don't get super unlucky on the quizzes, you'll be fine.

If you're not religious, pick one and pray. Hes a villain, he'll take points off your speeches for things you didn't do, then when you ask for clarification he won't give it to you. You don't have to buy a textbook, but there's one provided and if you don't wanna fail his million quizzes then you need to read them. He has no idea how canvas works.
Great class if you show up it's pretty much an easy A, awesome and kind professor. He isn't great at canvas or technology but it's ok

Awesome professor, a super nice guy he remembers my name 2 semesters later and greets me like a friend when we run into eachother on campus. Easy A, he's still got some of canvas to figure out but overall super easy to work with.

Awesome professor, great attitude and connects with students. At times the instructions are a little vague but he is more than happy to clarify. Overall easy class if you put a little bit of effort in

I gained nothing from this course. Professor Bitrus was very unorganized (constantly changing due dates, not updating the canvas, etc) and often put in the wrong grades for me (which I had to request him to fix literally 6 times until he did). The class is a stupidly easy A, but it might test your sanity.

Prof. Bitrus was unorganized and the class wasn't well structured, but he is genuinely the nicest and cares about his students. I think this was his first semester teaching so maybe he will get better with Canvas in the future. Super easy A and almost zero homework. He is so chill with the speeches, I basically put in zero effort and did just fine.

Professor Bitrus cares about his subject and wants students to succeed. The course structure was a challenge. Assignments are not difficult, but there was always poor communication about due dates. Additionally, Canvas was not set up in a way to easily understand and also lacked due dates. I learned a lot from the course but beware of organization.

Would highly recommend taking SPC2608 with professor Bitrus. Though the class is not organized, it was still a chill and easy A. The speeches are super relaxed and he genuinely wants his students to do well.

History of Film pt 3 was one of the best classes I've taken at UF. Prof Bianchi does a great job demonstrating the continuous themes of this era of films and provoked me to think more deeply even about films I'd already seen before the class. He gives very thorough feedback on all assignments and is accessible outside of class.

Bianchi did a great job of emphasizing the historical context of the films we watched which enhanced my enjoyment; the films themselves were interesting and easy/fun to discuss in class. You are required to informally present about 1 film he assigns to you, he permits 3 unexcused absences. Covers important readings in class that will be on quizzes.

ENG4135 - Italian Cinema

Professor Bianchi is kind, cares about his students, and is clearly knowledgable on the subject(s) he teaches. His knowledge of Italy's history and appreciation of film is evident. He wants his students to succeed and is not a harsh grader. Watch the films, go to class, and you will succeed. Entertaining and educational.

I had Professor Bianchi for both ENG3125 (History of Film Part 3) and ENG4133 (Cinema of the Global South) and he is for sure one of the best professors at UF. He's passionate about what he teaches, picks awesome films, and gives great feedback. I recommend taking a class or two, or more, with him, you'll learn a lot!

One of the best professors you can have at UF! He is truly passionate and always interested in what you have to say, no matter the topic. This was my first-ever film class, but his directions were clear and easy to follow.

Professor Bianchi is the best professor I've had in college thus far. His classes are fun, inspiring, and extremely educational. He is clearly passionate about film and that transpires into his lectures. Pay attention in class, do the readings, and participate every once in a while and you will be successful!

Bianchi is an awesome Professor. He cares about his students' and wants to see you care. Attendance is mandatory and your grade will go down if you don't go. If you watch the films and post the discussions, everything is easy. Two quizzes on the films, main grades are attendance and discussion posts. He's my favorite professor i've had.

Prof Bianchi is actually THE best professor I have ever and will ever take at UF. Seriously. He picks super cool films, some you'll like some you won't (personal preference). There isn't much else to say honestly he is just the best. The one class I was never bored in.

Professor Bianchi is easily the best instructor I have had the pleasure of taking a course with. He is kind, empathetic, and gives fantastic feedback on papers. I wish I could take another course with him, because I learned more in the two classes I took with him than I did in many other courses at UF.

Pietro is one of the best, if not the best, professors I've had during my time at UF. He is so engaging, and genuinely cares so much about what he is teaching. He's also always willing to work with you and offer help. I've taken 3 classes with him and loved each one, definitely worth taking!

Great lecturer and course was not a heavy workload. He also offered extra credit, pretty easy to do well in his class. The course I took was very philosophy and theory heavy so may be hard if you're not interested in that. Also he loves David Lynch a lot, he came up so much. Class was very film heavy, not a lot of books.
literally one of the best. super well-read and really accommodating. very interesting to talk to and his class was pretty easy.

This professor has brilliant things to say about the most profound ideas found in media/film/philosophy and culture. The assignments are straightforward, complete the readings, arrive for him to explain the context, and then post a discussion about whatever you want to talk about. He encourages critical thought and leads discussion off students.
Love him! He is nice, smart, and respectful. His lecture won't let you disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bianchi is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is beyond helpful and encouraging, I genuinely enjoyed learning in his class.

One of the best instructors Ive ever had. I took him for both psychoanalysis film and colonial/poco film, I learned an extensive amount of history, geography, philosophy, science, and film analysis techniques in both of his classes. He is so knowledge in his areas of study and shares info in a way that gets you very excited about it.

I love Dr. Bianchi. A very kind person and is a great facilitator of discussion. Welcomes questions and always aims to answer them extensively. Quizzes can be daunting because they are open-ended but trust me you will do well if you have moderately participated in class work. He is very understanding and loves talking to his students. Recommend!

I love Professor Bianchi! I took his psychoanalysis class on desire this semester and it was amazing! He's genuinely one of the most caring professors at UF. His lectures are always really fun to attend and active participation is encouraged. This is the only class that I actually enjoyed doing discussion posts for!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Bianchi is extremely passionate and knowledgeable of the information he teaches, but he doesn't come across as condescending. He loves what he teaches and I loved learning from him. The class was formatted around weekly film viewings, two brief writing assignments, and 3 written quizzes + final. Fair grader, be aware of deadlines. A+
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took his critical theory course, and it was amazing. The concepts he focuses on and fosters discussions with are extremely interesting, and I constantly refer back to them. If you're in one of his courses, I highly recommend joining the discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Absolutely love this man. This class was super theoretical and not my usual cup of tea, but Professor Bianchi made it so interesting and enjoyable. 100% recommend this class with this professor- he has such a passion for this subject and it's super evident throughout the lectures and assignments.

Prof Bianchi's class will literally blow your mind. He'll teach you about a concept in psychoanalysis, and then you'll begin to see that concept pop up in life everywhere you go! He takes great care to ensure that his students fully understand the class material, and he never hesitates to elaborate further when necessary. Very passionate. 10/10!!

Simple grading criteria (attendance, participation, midterm paper (5 pages), final paper (5 pages), discussion post on the weekly film). Easy to get an A on the course, very educational and nice professor. No textbook!

Dr. Billups is a great professor, and this class was top-tier. The best class I've ever taken. Super interesting material. It's a ton of reading. Attendance mandatory. Classes are mostly discussions related to the readings, with the occasional lecture thrown in. A good number of essays that are graded firmly but fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Primarily a lecture and class discussion based class, with essays and written work for at home work. Gives lots of take home reading but most of it can be skimmed and/or read right before class to participate in group discussions. The first half of papers use readings but the last half is independent from the readings.

Dr. Billups truly cares about the students. He will schedule half of his week for office hours. I've heard most of the TA's can be quite tough. Please take Charlie Davidson as your TA. He is not only easier, but he will make you think and contemplate history in a different light during discussions.
Took because it's required so definitely didn't enjoy it. Made it easy for someone who didn't want to be there, but I needed to focus on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Billups is very passionate about teaching history. However, if you do not like engaging with LOTS of dense literature and participating in class discussion, do NOT take Media in American Democracy. Compared to other history professors, Dr. Billups is a moderately tough grader, but he genuinely wants to see you succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had. He is very understanding and truly wants to see his students succeed. I have taken two of his courses and more than half the students from our fall class ended up taking his spring class because we liked his style of teaching so much.
Billups is my thesis advisor. Be excited for a professor who is genuinely interested in your success.

Dr. Billups is AMAZING! He is my favorite history professor I have had at UF and would 100% take his class again. He is very knowledable on his topics and cares deeply about the success of his students. Class is very reading heavy but the readings are extremely interesting and relevant. Could not recommend DR. Billups enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor! If you are interested in taking a history class at UF, make sure it is with Professor Billups! He is super knowledgeable on the subjects at hand! Yes, the classes are more discussion-based and somewhat reading-heavy, but they are totally worth it! One of the best history professors at UF without a doubt!
He is so knowledgeable on his topic and the classes were always interesting which was impressive considering it is pretty reading heavy. Dr. Billups is so nice and funny WE LOVE HIM

Dr. Billups is AMAZING! He is super knowledgeable and passionate about the subject, which is great. Class is discussion-heavy, so doing your reading is important! However, he makes discussions interactive and pushes you to think about what you know in a new light. Has some major papers, but he gives amazing feedback and lets you resubmit one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is not the professor in 2018 and 2019.
