Great name, makes her memorable. Just goes by Dr. Raga. Very smart and a great professor. You get the sense she cares for her students. Also she is doing (or did in the past) informatics research I believe.

Raga was great. I've had her for two classes in my graduate nursing program and enjoyed both. She certainly cares about her students, is easy to talk to, and her assignments are reasonable and relevant. It can sometimes take time for her to get back to you, but she works hard to ensure everyone has enough time to finish their work without stress.

I love this lady. She is just soooo sweet and really engages with class. Show up for class and you're gonna get an A. I never had to worry about my grade in this class. It was so refreshing to just show up, talk about conservation, and just learn.

Dr. Bjorndal is the best! She's been the head of the Archie Carr Center for Sea Turtle research for years and has so much knowledge, wisdom and passion. She loves and cares about her students. Class is geared toward real learning, no exams just group projects and journal club each week but she picks the papers and they're pretty short and simple.

Dr. Bjorndal is so passionate in her field of sea turtle ecology and biodiversity. I recommend taking this class if you like sea turtles and if you don't! She lectures/traches based on learning and with group participation. Great GPA booster, learning experience for research presentations in a group, and amazing subject material. The best class.

By far the best professor I have ever had. She is one of the few professors that take the time to connect with every single student. Always a joy to go to class and she was so passionate and knowledgable it made you want to learn more. I really wish she had more classes because I would take her again in a heart beat. If you like turtles take it!!!

She always made sure to take our feedback to heart and check in that we were enjoying the material. Grading was primarily based on attendance and discussion classes, with a research project ongoing through the semester. Class can drone on a bit unless you are 100% passionate about sea turtle conservation, but still was an incredible class.

Had a great time taking this class. Bloom is definitely sweeter than a lot of the other French professors. I did feel like I wasn't getting as much French practice as I would have liked taking this class, but other than that, had a great time. Readings were interesting.

I've had Dr Bloom for three classes now and she is interesting to say the least. She is not flexible with new ideas/different approaches to prompts, but is a very nice woman. She will eventually give you an A if you participate, but if you are used to AP Lit style writing where you go beyond the prompt, be prepared to be flamed for it at first.

While this class interesting I cannot recommend Dr. Bloom. Her grading criteria was completely random and she did not give clarification when asked. She only has like four assignments the entire semester, so one error was detrimental, I asked her for help and she refused, then failed me anyway. If you need any type of accommodations, she will hate.

She is definitely passionate about the subject matter, but her grading criteria for essays was very confusing. There seemed to be little room for subjectivity within essays, resulting in lower grades for points she personally disagreed with. Not to mention essays took up nearly the majority of our grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took her fairy tales class and her enthusiasm was contagious. She is somewhat of a tough grader without super clear expectations, but she does an excellent job of teaching course content. 50% of the grade is made up of 2 essays, each with 1000 words, the rest of the grade comes from discussions and participation. I would def recommend for quest 1

I was nervous about class, but she was so kind and encouraging, really willing to help you succeed. The course has a lot of different assignments but not different from other lang classes. If youre unsure take with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This professor loves what she teaches and explains everything so clearly. I definitely recommend this class. At first, I thought she was a tough grader, but if you go to her office hours and ask questions she will help you get the best grade in papers and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great fench professor. Takes the time to actually get to know everyone in the class and about our lives. This class was about 70% essay-based, but she graded them fairly leniently. Most of the times it was points if we used specific verbs and phrases, etc. Was pretty strict on grammar though. I felt I improved a lot, and she lectures well.

I took Bloom for French Fairytales and she did really well with the course! Your grade is composed of strong participation from class discussion along with 2 mini presentations and 3 papers, 3pg length. I am not sure when this topic will be taught again but I would recommend this prof as well as the course content! Good relaxer for French majors!

For a grammar/comp class (boring content), Dr. Bloom did her best to liven up the class. I think she went too easy on us, PP slides emailed, grammar explained to the T. Normally you'd have to come 100% prepared. Compositions are not bad, even if you mess up the first draft, you can make up for it. 8 quizzes/tests, not too much pressure.
Fantastic.  I admire her, but she expects hard work from her students.

Bloom makes most of her assignments clear. But I don't really like her, her lectures are pretty dry and her grading is sometimes arbitrary (which is strange since her guidelines are pretty clear). I would not take her again there are much better profs in French who are much less two faced. Only take her if you don't have better options.

I've taken 3 classes with Madame Bloom and she's the best. You definitely have to go to class and participate, but she makes it really easy to understand what she wants and to get an A. If you speak French well, you'll be fine.

Of the 3 classes I've taken with her, this was definitely the worst. A lot of reading and not an easy A, but it probably would have been a lot worse with someone else. If you have to take it, take it with her. If you don't, avoid it.
I highly recommend this professor.
She was very helpful and clear about what she expected. Take this class with her!

I had mixed feelings coming out of this class. She is pretty nice if you get to know her. She gives the questions for the test before hand, but since she does she expects thorough essay answers on her tests. Not an easy A but it wasn't too bad. Some homework (reading). Important subject matter to learn (IMO) if you are a french major.
She's great.
excellent professor

Interesting material and I can only say good things about this professor for her teaching. Most UF professors are easy A's, but this is not one of them.Fortunately, the curve will save you and your final grade will turn out to be good.But trust me, you'll be worried every minute until you get that final grade.I guess she likes to motivate her stude
She is a great teacher, but everybody thinks she is a hard grader and her expectations are too high.

She is a really tough grader. She explains the works really well, but her rubrics are out of whack. She has extremely specific expectations for essays and tests, which doesn't make sense for a literature course (in my opinion). I loved the material, but open discussion of the material was almost discouraged because of her specific expectations.

I have had this professor twice now and strongly recommend her.  After taking her classes, you will see literature a new way.  She is just so inspiring.  The last time I had her, she was a hard grader all semester, but then surprised everyone with decent grades at the end.  Don?t believe the myth that she always grades so hard.

This  professor instills an incredible passion for French literature in every student.  You walk in not caring and you walk out with a new passion.  She is amazing! She comes from the Ivy League, so expects a lot and grades hard at first.  But then she brings everyone's grades up at the end, so don't worry about her hard grading reputation.
Impossible to tell what the professor wants. Seeing her in office hours doesn't help either.

In the beginning of the semester, I was really apprehensive about her because of some of the comments I read on ratemyprofessors, but it turned out that she's a really great professor.  I learned so much.  She's very nice and very intelligent.  Her instructions are clear, and her grading is fair.  I would definitely take another class from her. =)

Ok, I don't know why anyone says she is difficult.  She literally gives you the exams beforehand so you can prepare your answers.  You can even bring your tentative exam answers or papers to her to review. You don't really have to read everything she assigns because she goes over it in class. She does tend to grade on the harsh side.
Boring, boring, boring... and she will give a B as a grad student, FOR SURE! Useless. You will not learn anything with her. Waste of time.
By far my favorite French professor at UF.  She is tough but I've had her for 2 classes and I've learned a lot.  Always encourages Office Hour help and genuinely seems to care how we do in class.

Avoid her like the plague if you have any interest in keeping your GPA up.  Some professors teach so much, the learning experience is so enriching, that it is WORTH the bad grade, just to take a class with them.  Rori Bloom is NOT ONE OF THOSE PROFESSORS.
Difficult grader, but not impossible. Her class isn't the most exciting, but could be worse.

People tend to stay away from her classes at the 4000-level with good reason. She is soft-spoken in person but ruthless as a grader. I don't think she is intentionally unfair, but don't plan on coasting to an A...or a B..or a C...Besides, she is unenthusiastic and thus the class is boring.
Nice teacher, very helpful. Not the most exciting class ever but did get to do some fun stuff.
interesting class, cool selections.
She's an ok teacher. The class is kind of a pain in the ass.

My goat. SO entertaining, really values participation and getting to know her students. Values ideas over grammar. Let me throw a backpack across the room as part of a scene (this class was 20th century french theater) and gave me extra credit for it. Love her down.
Dr. Blum is amazing! She genuinely wants to help you and is super flexible. She's funny in class too. Go to office hours just to talk to her! I wish I had taken her classes sooner!

She is  truly passionate about fashion and film. I learned so much, and it was genuinely a pleasure to attend her class. The structure was well-organized you watch the films at home and discuss them later in the week, which allows for better time management. She is also also very understanding and approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took this my 1st sem & was worried I wouldn't keep up - she speaks French 95% of the time. Felt way more comfortable by a month in. Truly cares abt her students, gives lots of not-that-hard small assignments, generous grader. 5 "major" essays, 1-2 pages, interesting topics. Very French & endearing humor. Discussion participation matters. Love her!

Professor Blum is a fantastic professor who cares about her students. You must do the homework and be prepared to speak in class. She randomly calls on students to speak which is intimidating at first but it leads to great improvement. Just be ready to be called on 1-3 times each class. I would totally recommend her if you have the chance.

Prof Blum is a super chill professor. Basically just watched a movie every week, answered questions(she actually reads them so don't troll), and discussed it in class. Yes, there were some bigger project assignments, but not much effort is needed for full credit; it's an easy A. Cons: class sometimes feels disorganized and the instructions vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: We watched funny and cute french movies and talked about them in class. It was easy to get an A and she likes when you participate, of course. I would take her again but some of the lectures were a little boring, but I did take it online when it's supposed to be in person so maybe that's why.

Dr. Blum was SO funny and so helpful. I took this class as a freshman after taking IB French and it was pretty easy. She gives 5 major compositions throughout the semester (1-2 pages each) and then short homework assignments, overall not too much work but be prepared to participate in class discussions.

Had her as my prof for French Senior seminar and would hands down take her class again!! She makes you read novels and plays instead of textbooks so you feel like you're actually learning something real. My French has improved so much and when she corrects you she never makes you feel bad. She's super funny and cares about students.

Dr. Blum is very passionate about French cinema and it shows, she is a very sweet professor who loves to communicate with her students. She actively posts reminders and content to her Canvas course page, so it shows that she is engaged. There is not any wrong answers with her, she is open-minded and accepts open discussions in class.

Definitely not a class to take lightly. You have to prepare in order to really follow along and understand. She is very French and won't hesitate to correct your every error, but it leads to a significant improvement in your French over the course of the semester.

Dr. Blum is not easy, but she is wonderful if you are willing to make an effort and show that you are trying. Homework is rarely collected, but you will be severely disadvantaged in class if you don't do it. I learned tons from her and became much more comfortable with French. I'd love to take her again.

this is my second course with the professor and she is awesome. participation is a must and over rides most other assignments. weekly quizzes based on a lot of reading, but again, if you participate it won't matter what you get on the quiz. lovely person to talk to and very compassionate. great professor!

She's great! she almost never gives you a complete 20 points on any assignment but is relatively easy. she is also very understanding of personal issues and has great taste in film. overall, excellent.

I've taken two of this professor's courses and she is delightful! she is very cool and fun to talk to. She is very French, sophisticated and classy. She is also very knowledgable and willing to assist you, whether you are that great at speaking french or not. Her courses are stimulating and interesting. I took french cinema and french theatre.

Pretty good teacher.  I had a bit of a problem with the way she favored students who were already fluent.  But all in all a good experience with her.  you have to make a little effort to prove yourself to her, though.  I am looking forward to taking her french cinema class.

Wonderful teacher. More interested in having her students learn, than assingnig them grades. European Cinema was a joy to behold with her.  Unstructured lectures, but really fun nonetheless. Short papers, 2 exams, and a 15 page final project. TAKE HER!

Most of the films were pretty dull. Although, there were a few I enjoyed. Expectations for exam was unclear. She can also be a bit disorganized. She often changes her mind about assignments. Overall I'd say she's an alright teacher.
She was great! Very friendly and helpful, always made the class very interesting.
Love her!  She's crazy and challenging.  Recommended.

Highly recommended prof. Clever lady. Eager to respect persons. Student-friendly & so much fun to pester. Her classes can be hilarious when the right gang is signed up. My French improved dramatically with her. You must have proper attitude: If you're boring, unready for interm-adv French, or like to be spoon-fed grammar, don't take her classes.
Dr. Blum taught my favorite course at UF, and I would have taken many more courses from her if I hadn't graduated immediately after turning in my final.

i once plagarized a short paper and a week later she was standing behind me and started talking about how plagarization is awful and how this specific class is above that, so that i knew she knew. but she never did anything and i gave me an A. she's very funny and clever. but for her french film = post-colonial french film/ no new wave.
Be prepared to turn to your classmates and whisper: "Do you understand what she's talking about, because I sure don't....?"

The only grades for the course were three exams, but they weren't particularly difficult. He rambles a lot, but he is very knowledgeable about the matter, and textbook chapters are posted online if you don't attend class. The class material revolves around monopolies/monopsonies and Anti-Trust Law.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Blair is extremely knowledgeable and always willing to help if you're genuinely interested in learning the material. Don't skip lectures or you will fall behind!

He is very kind, however, he doesn't use powerpoints, he provides a couple sheets of graphs at the beginning of lectures and then just talks. Most of the time the graphs aren't detailed so you have to make sure you're following along to make your own notes on them. Class is only three exams, he is very nice to talk with and very intelligent.

This class should have been miles easier than it was but this guy never failed to impress me with how quickly he overcomplicated simple subjects, how subjective he made the exams, and how ridiculous the grading structure was (your only grades are the three exams, no curve btw & completely subjective grading.) Lectures are also slow and monotonous..

I really enjoyed Dr. Blair's course and he is very knowledgeable and willing to explain anything from the class in office hours. Be prepared to study hard for exams and make sure you use all the materials he gives you. His lectures are very important for the exams, so be sure to stay on top of the content and ask questions if he is not clear.

To say he's qualified is an understatement. It's obvious that he cares a lot about the subject matter and his experience is vast. But as a lecturer, he often rambles and for an economics class, there's rarely any visuals he utilizes. The textbook is free but parts of it are incomplete (no detailed mention of Bertrand in the textbook).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please avoid taking his class when you have a choice. I understand he is old, but this does not mean I can accept his unplanned teaching. Don't expect him to explain the concepts clearly in his classes. This course requires much time to read his out dated textbook. Preparing for his exam is undoubtedly a difficult and painful process.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were unorganized and dragged on way longer than necessary.  While attendance isn't mandatory, many exam questions require that you mention things explicitly stated in class. Exams were only a few written response questions each and I would often lose points on questions that I thought I nailed because of the subjective manner of grading.

Prof. Blecha is universally beloved. Mech 1 is a super easy class if you were good at Physics 1. Blecha makes it even better with spectacular lectures and great posted lecture notes. Quizzes are super easy and last one (ALC) is extra credit. Exams give back 20% of missed points via corrections (i.e. 80 goes to 84). Python hw helped me learn SciPy.

Professor Blecha has been one of the most understanding professors I have had. She truly wants to see you succeed. So accessible outside of class (spent an hour going over gravitation with me). I took this class as my first physics course ever, and I got an A. She is so kind, will offer help when she has time and is extremely considerate. 10/10

LOVE. THIS. WOMAN. She is the nicest professor you will have and you can tell she cares about both her students and what she is teaching. Only 12 quizzes and 12 homework assignments AND she drops the lowest 2 of each.

Professor Blecha was amazing with our Enriched Physics 1 class. She was very accommodating and understanding of the stressful events happening this year (COVID-19, election). Instead of a few big exams, our class had weekly quizzes. I prefer this format greatly and feel like I learned more. Textbook homework is challenging but helpful.

I ACTUALLY TOOK THIS CLASS FOR AML2070 (American Lit)! However, I truly loved both the class and the professor. She is a kind and caring person who genuinely wants all her students to succeed. Attendance is mandatory, but she understands if you miss a few classes. I am not a big fan of poems or American literature, but I truly loved this class.

Amazing professor! She is very chill and understanding, doesn't expect you to be perfect and provides lots of resources to help. Attendance is mandatory but you can miss two classes without penalty. She truly cares so much about her students and making sure they are doing well. Can't recommend her enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is sooo sweet and understanding. Attendance is mandatory but you can talk to her if you have any issues. She is so good would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. WHAT A WASTE OF MY TIME AND EFFORT. IT'S AN EASY CLASS, HOWEVER, THIS PROFESSOR IS SO UNFAIR AND IMPULSIVE WITH GRADING'S ABSURD. RUN SO SO SO FAR.
I would not wish this class on my worst enemy.

I would like to point out that she did not give one single 100% to anyone in the class on the discussion posts that she decided to choose 2 of from the whole semester. Lazy and unorganized professor. My discussion posts followed everything. DO NOT TAKE THIS DUMB CLASS AND TANK UR GPA.

I just cannot believe a class about old people is going to be the reason my GPA drops. Don't waste your time in this class. Seems like you need be to Edgar Allen Poe to do good on the two random discussions out of all 13 during the semester. Unfortunately my major is not english and my answers to every part of the discussion is not enough.

What a terrible and unorganized professor. It's almost as if she wants her students to do badly. I thoroughly discussed every point in detail, yet I was robbed of my grade because she is too lazy to grade every discussion, so she chooses only 2 from the whole semester to give horrible grades on.
Beyond awful class. do not take. I would rather take astrophysics than this class again... It really was just horrible.

Don't take this class. This professor is ABSURD. She randomly tanks the grades at the last minute and gives no care about it. This class is a waste of time. I spent my time making discussions THAT ANSWER EVERY QUESTION ASKED IN DETAIL; yet, she gives a 42/60 and this is the only grade that is worth over 20 points. What a scam of a class & professor

Just absolutely awful. Don't waste your time in this disgrace of a class. Take a class that you don't have to worry about your GPA dropping. Crazy that I currently have a B in a class about old people... This isn't a writing class so I'm confused how a singular discussion grade counts for this much. Honestly I am horrified.

DON'T TAKE. The last week of the class, WHEN WE barely have ANY MORE ASSIGNMENTS TO BRING OUR GRADE UP, she dropped a major grade bomb. NO discussions are graded throughout the semester. She chooses 2 random ones to grade and PICK APART. I participated in each discussion every week and answered all questions just to get a 70%. absolute BS!!!!!!!!!!

Online class - She was an amazing professor! I took her this Spring (2024) for a gerontology psychology class and I ended up loving her and the class. she's understanding and willing to help. Her exams were open note, there are discussions every week but they are easy. Take her!!

I would have liked to hear more from Dr. Bluck instead of random videos but the material is still pretty interesting. The weekly assignments are a bit tedious and the quizzes are pretty hard. Dr. Bluck is very understanding, but this class feels pretty disconnected as an online class.

Horrible. Do not take this class. It is an endless amount of homework, especially videos that are very long with tons of points, then a locked down test with many questions, confusing answers and not enough time to finish. If you want to keep up your GPA, take something else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The material is extensive and the tests are unnecessarily difficult. Tough grader to the point of discouraging the students. I would not take this prof again. I was excited about this class but now I'm just trying to through it without withdrawing.

Unreasonably difficult. Inconsistent deadlines. She assigned homework due over Spring break. She's a "nobody's perfect" grader so even if you follow the rubric to the "T" she'll still mark something off. Majority of the grade was based on a MASSIVE group project with 10 separate assignments. Lectures & text are from a previous year and not current.

This course was extremely informative. The semester long project is a great and a practical way to apply the information learned throughout the course. Her feedback is above and beyond appreciated, although it takes a while for her to return graded assignments. She offers lots of extra credit options throughout the semester. I highly recommend her!

Brianna is an amazing professor who really cares about her students and takes the time to help them succeed. Her class is very straightforward and as long as you come to class and pay attention you will do well. Brianna took the time to give helpful feedback on every assignment and even took time to help me find somewhere to gain event experience.

I'm Brianna's first class and it has been a joy being in her class. She has a lot of background in the hospitality event industry. She is a very caring and kind person with a good personality. She gets back to you via email very promptly and wants you to succeed.

I'm Brianna's first class and it has been a joy being in her class. She has a lot of background in the hospitality event industry. She is a very caring and kind person with a good personality. There aren't exams- 4 module assignments in groups with quizzes, 2 site visits, and an easy 5 points if you do the active learning assignment in class.
Professor Black's AMH2020 course is not bad if you do the work. There's one or two 15-20 minute lectures per week, a chap
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Way too stressful for a gen ed. Ridiculous workload. Lectures were from another prof and discussions were student led, so he never taught nor prepared students. He gave no instruction leading up to the exams, so no one knew what to expect. He graded insanely harsh. Doable, but way more effort than it should be. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The workload is insane even for a summer class. Professor Black lacks professionalism and was extremely rude when I tried to meet with him.

Do not take this class. It was his first year and it showed. Rude and not interactive with students. This was like any literature class that you will take at UGA and he just wants you to tell him his own opinion back to him. He was not knowledgeable about the field and it was detrimental for the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lecture slides were vague but packed, and the professor seemed to be reading off of his own separate outline that he would never upload. His lectures always felt disorganized with how much he goes off on tangents. I had difficulty keeping focus in class, but easily did assignments since you can honestly ignore the lecture and just know the readings

The class was to substitute what is a good life because I heard so many people say they hated it. Well, I highly disliked this class. He barely knew what he was talking about and talked too fast, didn't even explain the slides he was presenting, and went on tangents every 2 seconds. He is a really nice guy and he really cares, but the class is bad
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: His lectures revolve around class discussions, but he'll never call out on a student or make them look dumb if they give the wrong answer. A LOT of required reading and reading the recommended reading is sometimes necessary if you want to understand certain concepts better. Cons: he's vague with assignment details and student expectations
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took his Intro to Law class which consisted of guest lecturers who spoke about their specific areas of law. I would highly recommend taking this class to anyone who has an interest in law. It is only one credit thus it is super easy essentially one must just show up and do a 100-word response to the reading each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was not very difficult imo, but was occasionally frustrating because of his unclear descriptions of basically any assignment in the class. However, he is very nice and passionate about his subject. His teaching style is mostly discussion based, with pop quizzes interspersed throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Black is a nice guy and a good lecturer. You can tell that he's very passionate about law and he's great at transmitting his knowledge of legal history. He does speak a bit quickly, which makes it occasionally difficult to take notes, but I didn't find this to be that big of an obstacle. Overall, Dr. Black is a great lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. History is not my major but Mr. Black made it interesting.
Excellent teacher!

Go to class, follow his outline... these are the main points that'll appear on the identification portion of the exams. He definitely stutters and says certain words like "century" weird. Overall, not a painful class.
He's a good professor, however he does speak fast so its kinda hard to understand sometimes. Its an "ok" class. Most of us ended up with a B.

Anyone who complains about him being not helpful or not being clear is obviously one of those people who has to strictly memorize their notes and flips out if they are thrown a curve ball. He kept lectures interesting and his tests and papers left alot of room for your own opinion. Talks with a stutter, so sometimes hard to get. GREAT TEACHER!
His lectures went off topic but were interesting.  Hardly used the books at all, studied from my notes and did well.

He speaks way too fast for anything to be understood, his directions on assignments are ambiguous, he does not let students know important facts/persons during lectures, and he is unavailable during office hrs. I am a great student and I did bad in this class even though I attended almost every class. DO NOT take his class if you can avoid it.
wonderful TA. Really helpful.
this TA had no idea what he was talking about and many times contradicted what the professor said in lecture.
Excellent class.
not helpful

Joel is engaged with his subject matter and his students. Underlying his somewhat rumpled and confused appearance (think Hugh Grant) is a sharp wit. Although just embarking on his teaching career, it is clear that Joel has the potential to be a professor of substantial caliber.
Helpful, knows his stuff. Sometimes off topic, but made the subject interesting and fun. Super hot, for what its worth.
No Comments
Professor Blanchard is an excellent professor!! Class has a flipped classroom structure.
Not nice at all. Blanchard is racist.
Free A if you show up, pretty disorganized but he was really nice and accommodating so in the end no complaints.

Professor Blanchard's class can be challenging, but he's passionate and accessible. Use unstuckstudy and the free textbook to stay on top of the material. Lectures are engaging, and as long as you attend and complete the work, you'll do well.
This class is not difficult at all. All you need to do is do some weekly reading/video and quizzes in class (very easy). Also, Dr. J is one of the best professors at UF.
Ofc we love Dr.Jei. Just show up to class and you'll get an A. The weekly videos for the quizzes are 20min MAX so super light work. Definitely recommend this class even if you aren't TA'ing.

I also had Dr. Blanchard under other several courses not currently listed - my experience with him across was always exceptional. He is a very caring and accommodating person, and shows genuine interest in the success of his students. For many classes his teaching style is open ended in terms of assignments, leaving room for creativity.
He is awesome. Super knowledgeable and always ready to correct his own mistakes. He will be tough on you, but you will learn a lot. Great course.

His tests are very dependent on incredibly specific edge cases. If you're taking him for COP3504 I would recommend having more experience then AP CSA. Also if you are going to take COP3504 with him, make sure you know you can co-rec it with COT3100.

Dr. Jei doesn't receive the flack he gets. No other Professor has shown such personal interest in my success, and if you truly care to succeed in his class, you will do so. COP3504C was a little chaotic towards the end, mainly because of how new the class was, but Dr. Jei was fair and deliberate, and I can't wait to take a class with him again :)
I lost interest in coding through this class. But the professor was nice.

Took this class my freshman fall and my prior CS experience includes APCSA and basic python. Blanchard is knowledgeable, easily accessible, and clearly passionate. Lectures can be fast and hard to follow at times, class structure was sometimes disorganized. Read the textbook and PLEASE start projects early. Overall it was challenging but rewarding.
class was disorganized this semester but the grading and pacing of the class was fair

Grading projects and exams took a month, but other than that the material itself was pretty self explanatory. One thing I did not like was that the projects were ALL individual, so if you didn't know how to do something, you could only go to office hours and ask the TAs. Quizzes were open notes and as long as you attend the lectures, it wasn't hard

He made the lectures very engaging by using funny references and memes, so you never got bored. He's not a harsh grader, and as long as you attend the lectures and complete the projects and labs, you'll do great in the class. He makes the quizzes open notes, but notes need to be handwritten, which was a pretty helpful offer in my opinion.

Grading for projects would take a month or more, lectures were information packed and not very clear, and the course felt disorganized with lots of errors/ambiguity in test questions and assignments. He clearly cared about us, the content, and making the course better(so I think it will be better in future iterations), but this semester wasn't it.

For tests we did not receive any practice problems or exams and everything was disorganized.  We were not even allowed to look at previous quizzes unless we went to office hours.  Things took forever to grade even if they were just multiple choice canvas quizzes. You will not succeed unless you are already a proficient programmer.

One of the worst professors I've ever had, he literally does not teach or interact with students. His assignments are not clear, and useless in my major - CpE. They require an unnecessary amount of time just to decipher what he wants us to do. His TA's mainly teach rest of the course. He just sends videos of old lectures.

Professor Blanchard's class was honestly the toughest class I have ever taken. He doesn't really answer emails and rather tells students to visit office hours where you can coinflip to see if your TA really knows what they are talking about or not. Do not take this class if you are not an extremely proficient/knowledgable coder, you won't succeed.
He's really good and pretty nice. Also quick on responses. Class is difficult but you learn a lot

Professor Blanchard is a cool guy but a terrible teacher. He doesn't teach so much as give you a bunch of random facts and expect you to put everything together on your own. He is definitely nice and easy to access outside of class, but he just really doesn't know how to teach. I suffered through OS and learned nothing.

Professor Blanchard is an interesting guy. When you talk to him he seems nice and cares about you, but his class is mentally taxing. It is a lot of work, and very disorganized. Lectures are either too slow or too fast, and his examples dont make sense unless you have prior knowledge. There's also too many errors in the labs and projects.

Unless you're an amazing coder, able to debug anything and everything- this class is not for you. Dr. Blanchard seems to be a good lecturer but when it comes to assignments and tests- he's very lacking. The projects are incredibly time consuming and so are the labs. It's almost as if he expects us only to focus on this class and have no life.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Blanchard is a wholly disorganized professor. His assignments are chock full of errors and his exams are written last minute. Corrections are not clearly defined and are only available sporadically dispersed among class general chat messages. He will give you a zero and almost insultingly, allow for correction in a short window without notice.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. J is a great professor, probably among the most passionate I've ever seen in CS but with that passion comes struggle lol. He does care and wants to see every student succeed, but he WILL push you. Learned a lot, even though the course got pretty hectic towards the end. Start early and stay on top of projects, cannot stress this enough!

Dr. Blanchard is single-handedly one of the toughest professors I have ever had. He is extremely immature, sensitive, childish, and demeaning and is constantly complaining about every little thing he has to do as a teacher. He does not accept DM's and will rarely answer emails. Honestly a manchild. Avoid his class at ALL costs and if not, GOOD LUCK
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class was not bad except for the final robocode project which I found really difficult, make sure to get a good group. Rest of class was medium chill imo. Blanchard cares and the class is pretty interesting. Decent amount of work, but overall not too bad.

Everbody is right. He cares, knows what he is doing, is super responsive, etc etc. Go ahead, email him right now and I bet he responds in .25 seconds. Also, make sure you get a good group for the project!

Spring 2021. Great guy, and really cares about the students. One group project, 2 exams, and some smaller coding assignments. There were some organizational problems which I didn't like. He had class materials in a repo but didn't have clear instructions for how to mirror it (another student found/posted them). Overall the pros outweigh the cons.

Professor Blanchard is my favorite teacher at UF. He is a fantastic lecturer, sets clear expectations, and is reasonable. This is the only class I look forward to this semester. This class is way easier than OS or Performant Python. I'd compare it to Programming Fundamentals 2 with him in terms of difficulty.

This was the hardest class I've ever taken at UF, but also the most rewarding. I'm not interested in the topic, but professor Blanchard is a fantastic teacher. His teaching style isn't for everyone, but I purposefully seek out his classes to get the best learning experience. The class is lecture heavy, quiz heavy, exam heavy, and project heavy.
Great lectures, very useful. If you aren't planning on watching, another professor might be better.

Blanchard is one of the best lecturers I have had at UF and he clearly cares a lot about his students. I just wish that would reflect more in his management of the course. I found the amount of work unnecessarily overwhelming and tedious so be ready to work. The exams are doable but tough and take a lot of cramming. ATM he is the best option for OS
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is majority attendance-based and is very easy to get an A in. You have short weekly reading and easy 3-question multiple choice quizzes on the readings. The other reviews for this class were joke reviews; I can't imagine anyone actually struggling for an A in this class.

This course is a mixed bag -- I learned a ton from Dr. Blanchard, but the coursework also had me questioning my sanity for most of the semester. Be prepared to spend 50+ on a project just to have an okay grade on it. He was good about providing EC and being fair with his exams, but expect to spend full weeks dedicated to this class.

OS is one of the hardest classes you'll ever take, but I think Blanchard is a great professor to teach it. There are A LOT of projects, but you actually will learn something from them. His instructions are more clear than I usually see in CS, but you will still have to teach youself a lot. Exams/quizzes are hard but fair. Lectures are pretty good.
Blanchard makes off color remarks. He has no business speaking for professing for the university of florida.

AI for Games with Blanchard was an amazing experience. If you put in the effort you will genuinely learn the material and know it. As someone who has experience with programming prior to college there is a lot to take away from his courses regardless of your experience. Workload can be hefty, so judge your schedule ahead of time.
One of the best CS profs at UF

I have taken 3 of Blanchard's classes so far. They are never easy, but I've learned so much which is more than I can say about any other CISE professor at UF. If you want to get an industry job as a programmer, take his classes and you'll be adequately prepared. He cares so much for his students.

Blanchard is a great lecturer. He cares about students and wants you to succeed. However, the grading criteria for the project reports is ambiguous and seems to be unfair. The report is supposed to be a brief summary, but you are basically expected to explain everything you did to get full credit, which is nearly impossible to do in 500 words.

CS Teaching and Learning is no doubt the hardest class I have taken in my computer science curriculum. I needed one elective credit to graduate and Professor Blanchard requires at least 10+ hours outside of the class for this one. Super hard quizzes every week. The only reason I didn't fail this course was the extra credit 10 page essay I did...

CIS4930 with Professor Blanchard has been the hardest class I have taken at UF. His frequent exams often go beyond the scope of this class and don't have enough time. I thought I would succeed but this class really crushed me :(

I took the CS teaching and learning class with him and it was so hard :( Class was super test heavy and none of the material on the slides were on the quizzes. I have a 3.8 GPA but man I got destroyed by this class

He's a good professor who cares about his students. He wants you to succeed. However, you won't pass COP4600 if you aren't putting in effort. His projects are not meant to be tutorials -- You gotta figure it out on your own. Learning via Self discovery > self exercises > taught visually > taught verbally. Blanchard wants you to discover solutions.

He is great in terms of teaching. He puts a lot of effort to make sure everyone is on the same page. However, he encourages students to ask WAY MORE question than it needs to be asked. In a 2 hour lecture, at least 1 hour passes away student asking irrelevant and frankly sometimes very stupid questions. Some of the projects are poorly written.

Does not provide exercise and project solutions. Hide exam and quiz solutions. This lecturer lectures well, but he puts more effort into preventing cheating than helping the community to learn by making answers public. Projects are vaguely constructed and rubrics change last second. As a result, he can irresponsibly make new projects every semester

This class is tougher than any other intro course (even physics 2), but Blanchard has incredibly clear lectures and is always available to help. Very fair grading. Projects and labs are time-consuming, but you will learn a lot from them. The class is about half its original size at the end of the semester, and the average grade is a C+.

I learned more in one semester with Dr. B did I did in four year's worth of programming experience. He throws you in the deep end by forcing you to use your creativity to build cool and complex programs put of seemingly simple concepts. If you put the work in, your skills will vastly improve.

I respect Jeremiah Blanchard and his methodology for teaching, however, I don't think it works for every student. Even if you do have programming experience, prepare to dedicate at least 10+ hours to the labs and projects in this class per week. If you have any other obligations such as a job, you will struggle a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The best professor Ive had for any class ever. His tests are hard, and his programming assignments will force you to put in work, but his lectures are absolutely unmissable. Also, hes probably the sexiest man on UF campus. Take this class.

Blanchard is truly one of the best teachers I've ever had. He clearly loves teaching and seems to genuinely care about students. His quizzes and exams are extremely fair: most of the knowledge he tests is actually pretty intuitive if you have studied the material and paid attention to lecture. You need to work a lot for projects and labs, however

Professor Blanchard is a great teacher, hes extremely knowledgeable about programming and is honest when he doesnt know an answer. You can tell he truly believes in the importance of improving teaching. He does go quickly in lectures and theres a lot of work to do, but you learn a lot. He clearly says in the beginning that the average is a C.

He's a great lecturer but exams and quizzes are oversimplified to true and false questions, which doesn't really encourage you to learn material. He gives a ton of assignments, a lot of which have poor descriptions, especially for projects. He's definitely a better CS professor than average, but not a model of perfection.

I took him for operating systems and he was a fantastic professor. Probably the best in the CISE department. His projects are hard and are a lot of work. But his lectures are very interesting and easy to follow considering how hard the material is.

Prof. Blanchard was super funny, I loved the jokes he'd make in lecture. The biggest problem is that so much of the content you have to learn yourself on ZyBooks and you have to spend a fortune of time on it. Grading criteria for the projects is pretty stringent too: if it doesn't match EXACTLY then it's no credit for that sample output.

He is really funny and relatable. When teaching code, all of his examples are meme-related. Although, I have never really learned much from his lectures. But, ZyBooks is super helpful (and time-consuming). I spend more time on his class than any of my other ones because there are 5 projects per semester and a mini-project every week.

As someone with no prior experience, I need about 12 hours of work per week to do well in this class. You can't expect to learn how to program just by watching lectures. You have to read and do your non-mandatory homework on Zybooks. Labs may have flaws, but you just need to read the specs carefully and match the output. Grading criteria is fair

Professor Blanchard is a very likable guy, however, his tests and quizzes are VERY difficult and his lectures do not prepare you for them at all. His project/lab specifications are very vague and ambiguous. If you are taking this class online you must really on other students and TA's to help you. The problem is that only the students are willing.

Hands down the best professor in CISE at UF. Not only does he teach well and spend time to clarify concepts that are confusing (only if you speak up), but also makes himself extremely accessible to students through Slack. It's a challenging course but you're provided all the resources and support you need to succeed.

Professor Blanchard is a very likable guy, however, his tests and quizzes are VERY difficult and his lectures do not prepare you for them at all. His project/lab specifications are very vague and ambiguous. You must pester him for clarification or get points docked. Overall however, this is an great class to introduce to you to programming and CS.
He's so great! His lectures are great and entertaining. My only complaint is that his project and lab specs can sometimes be confusing.
Amazing Professor! His explanations were on point and was always happy to clarify the fundamental concepts in class. Learning with him was a great experience :)

Blanchard was extremely caring for his students and he wanted them to not only succeed, but also to actually learn the material. As someone with no programming experience, the class was very challenging. I practically lived in the TAs office. When I asked him for an individual tutor, he found someone for me. 10/10 teacher, but not an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Blanchard is a really good professor and I am glad that I had the opportunity to take a course with him. For someone who had no prior programming/cs experience, yes - this class was quite challenging . I think that Blanchard did a good job at teaching a tough course to teach and made it manageable to understand and learn for his students.
He's my best CISE professor yet, I really liked the layout of the class. He was nearly always available on slack for any questions you had and the TA's were there too.

This class is tough, but extremely beneficial. I had previous programming experience and it was still challenging, but its possible to do well without experience. You will definitely have to work for it, but Jeremiah truly cares about his students success and knowledge, which is why its a tough course! I definitely came out a better programmer.

Honestly, the class was challenging, but if you put the work into the class and take the challenge, you become a better student as a result. The grading was very fair, even though there were a lot of quizzes and exams but the more you test the better chance you have to do well.

One of my favorite classes ever. Blanchard truly cares about all of his students and teaching, which really shows. The class isn't easy, especially if you don't have any prior programming experience, but with effort your work in the class will pay off. Blanchard is easy to get a hold of outside of class, as well as many other helpful resources.
The professor's cirriculum does not prepare students for what is on the tests. The programming assignments have several significant errors.

The professor uploaded lecture videos and slides onto Canvas, but not timely sometimes. There is much work including weekly quizzes, exercises, and homework. Projects are time consuming and the TAs gave few hints to help you with the projects. I think people need to read slides, take lecture notes, and understand them to do well in exams.

I'm betting the awful reviews are salty they didn't pass. Blanchard is one of the very few who actually cares about his classes. He makes his own power points and his lectures are actually good, a rare occurrence at UF. OS is easily passable but it did require a lot of work on projects. These kids are in for a shock if they think Blanchard is awful

Blanchard is extremely caring and accessible (but follow his rules about no-contact/tagging periods). His class is concept-heavy: watch his lectures, ask questions, and make sure you understand. Tests are TRICKY, very difficult. He is slow to give back grades (needs more TAs). DO NOT try and cheat/copy code. Respect him, and he will respect you!

The class was a lot of work but it was a blast. The tests can be difficult but the hardest part is adapting to a different style. You can't just memorize lecture slides like with some classes, so it can be frustrating if you are used to that. Once I started studying differently I did much better, and the projects are fun!

I am finishing up my online semester with Professor Blanchard. Assignments and materials are manageable, a lab & quiz weekly, 5 projects, and 3 exams. If you need help Professor Blanchard and his team of TAs are always available. If you do the assignments and readings you will pass. Clear expectations at the start of the semester.
He is a nice guy, but not a good professor. His lectures don't prepare you enough for the projects and exams. He also constantly changes assignment instructions and confuses students.

He was a cool guy but his teaching style was not at all near what it needed to be for a class that supposedly did not need prior experience. I had coded in high school and was still oblivious and blown away by how hard the exams were. I don't really know what I learned from this class but ended up frustrated with the overall experience.

Professor Blanchard is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. He truly has a passion for what he does, and cares about his students. His lectures are very informative and entertaining, and his projects are a great learning tool as well.

At UF, he's one of the best computer science professors. I took COP3502 with Blanchard, and I personally had trouble on his tests; I feel like the questions he asked were much harder variations to the concept he taught us. I still did well overall because of the multiple coding projects, where I learned the most, but just beware of the tests.

Professor Blanchard is an example of how a professor should be. Too many professors only care about their tenure/research and do a crap job at teaching. Professor Blanchard's class isn't easy but he makes the class entertaining and a great learning experience. He has inspired me to do much more with my life. I am so grateful for Blanchard! :)

An excellent professor who actually cares about his students! His lectures are entertaining with a lot of good information and he is overall just a great character. I learned more in this class than any high school coding course that I have taken. The class is not super easy but you will learn a lot and it has been my favorite class in college.

I've started a class without any previous programming knowledge and I have learned a lot with Blanchard. Get ready for a lot of work and studying and you'll make a great progress. His lectures can be boring, but you shouldn't miss them because they are really valuable and exams are based on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took Programming Fundamentals 1. Because I didn't come in with a huge history of programming, I found the lectures to be difficult to follow, so I just read the online textbook and did the challenges and I still earned an A- without attending most of the lectures. He's super easy to reach outside of class and a really nice guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Awesome professor who knows what he is talking about and makes a difficult subject seem more fun.

Great professor and an even greater person. He truly cares about his students. The class was easy if you actually read the online books and studied. His exams are difficult, but he gives plenty of extra-credit to balance it out. If you put in the work you will easily get an A in the class.

Great guy and makes the class pretty fun. However, not a great lecturer. I think I learned a lot more going through the textbook then in class. As someone who did very poorly on the exams (like only one digit numbers on the free response section), it didn't really matter because your project grade kind of balances out.

Best programming teacher any student could ask for. The quirky jokes and memes actually made you look forward to lecture. The exams were hard, but the projects were extremely fun and challenging. Had a great time.

Cares about his students and if very accessible online. Added multiple EC opportunities throughout the semester. Class isn't hard even if you have no programming experience, which was my case. Just do good on the projects and you can get by. I got C's on the first 2 exams (haven't done final yet), but A's on projects on will probably get an A-.

He is such a goober! As a women in computer science I am one of a few, but I can say I never felt judged by anyone. The class is so inclusive to everyone that I could yell out about how I am a vegan and nobody would be mean about it. Blanchard is a great teacher with a sweet personality. Excellent memes and great lectures.

Blanchard is the commander lord of all memes. If you cannot stand him (which I have met some) you are most definitely the issue. His jokes are quirky and nerdy and I cannot keep the smile off my face. I have never learned as much in a class as this one. I never coded a day in my life but after hard work and effort I enjoy it. Cool guy!

I really enjoyed this class. Blanchard is the funniest teacher I have ever had and his jokes are amazing (if you are a nerd like me). Blanchard really cares about his students and gives them plenty of help. Anyone who dislikes his class most likely does not even try. Blanchard has been my most favorite teacher in all my years of schooling. :)

If you have previous coding experience it's really not bad. Lectures are very boring and often go off on tangents. Quizzes and exams are based on tiny details that don't test for knowledge on the topic very accurately. Not necessarily difficult just annoying for the most part.

He is really cares about the students in his class. The class I had him with had 500+ students and he would respond individually to everyone. He is very active on the class Slack and would answer questions is a timely manner.

Great professor. Projects are pretty tough and requires effort, but the prof is always available and willing to assist students even outside of office hours through email. The prof explains concepts really well for students to understand.
Awesome professor. Helps you whenever you need and loves his job! He always encourages us to go outside our confort zone and become better programmers! 10/10

Dr. L is the best professor! He is supportive and accessible, and he is willing to help with anything ID related. His assignment feedback is extremely personalized (and often is in video/audio clip form). I marked average difficulty, but I really mean, he is fair. I had a wonderful experience in both his courses I took. Would 100% recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. L is amazing. He is accessible through email and truly wants to support students. Also, his courses' designs are great. He is a fair grader and very kind. Ask him anything EdTech and he will certainly help!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As long as you submit your assignment by the deadline, you're going to be fine. No busy work. Everything is planned with a purpose. Dr. L is really good about leaving personalized video feedback and making an effort to know students. I have taken three classes with him and he is by far one of my favorite professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor, very understanding!

The professor is amazing and always responds within a reasonable time. He is a super fair grader and always leaves great feedback on assignments and posts. The course work is not difficult as long as you read the instructions and understand the topics you should do great.
he is a great professor as long as you do your assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. L is a very respected professor at the University. His modules can be wordy and uninteresting at times, but he explains everything very thoroughly and assigns lots of in-class assignments for credit. If you need help with something, he is always willing to go out of his way for his students. I highly recommend any of his classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: i found this class to be alright (taken post course change), though the labs can really surprise u with work if ur not prepared. start early on them. its cool to see all work come together to make a cpu. bobda is really nice and understanding, the class is insanely unorganized though and studying for exams was annoying.

Taking a class with Bobda is like a Kitchen Nightmares episode: everything's in flames and he has no idea. Lectures cover anything as long as it's NOT relevant. The labs have two sentences of instruction, no further elaboration necessary (it's very necessary). And nothing works... ever. I go thru the 5 stages of grief, every time. Do not recommend.

Really hard to grasp the material during lectures. I found there was a lot of unnecessary information on the PowerPoint it is a lot of confusing information and isn't very organized. You learn best in this class through doing the labs and quizzes and asking for help from PIs!

Most unorganized class I've ever taken at UF. Homework assignments are consistently unclear yet graded on accuracy. Labs are more about debugging VHDL code rather than learning Digital Logic. Lecture content gives very little help with labs.TAs aren't on the same page. Very caring professor but he simply does not know how to properly run the class.
Very boring in lecture, and class seems a little disorganized. It's easy to do well in the class and not learn much, but if you apply yourself you can learn a lot too.

Dr. Bobda reads off of slides that he seems barely familiar with and often rushes through. The content of these slides often is lacking and doesn't provide any help with the assignments. Much of this course seems like regurgitation of other courses such as Computer Architecture. I would recommend avoiding his courses if you can.

Dr. Bobda's lectures and assignments tend to be disorganized. Provided skeleton code and instructions often had unintended errors that made assignments a bit frustrating. I didn't learn much about SoC design (ignore the course code) in his class, as much as I learned how to deal with miscellaneous software errors. He is a very easy grader

Dr. Bobda is the most caring and understanding professor I have had at UF so far. I have taken him for DL and am currently taking him for Digital Design. You can tell he is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about the material he teaches. At times he seems too smart to teach but he is always willing to help if there is any confusion occurring.

Dr. Bobda is a great guy and clearly knows his stuff but because of his accent he can be a little hard to understand during lectures so don't be afraid to ask questions. The labs are very straight forward and not that bad at all other than lab 5. He also gives lots of extra credit in labs and will give you an extension if you ask him.

He has a very thick accent which can sometimes be hard to understand, but he is overall very caring and if you asked for a extension he would give class wide extensions, plenty of extra credit available. Labs are difficult and unclear but overall there is plenty of help for it. Better then Shwartz anyday

Despite being fairly enthusiastic about the material, his lectures often felt boring and unhelpful. Expectations and directions were extremely vague. Due dates changed on a whim, poor communication, but there was decent extra credit. Exams did not match much of the lab or homework assignments. Lecture recordings were bad and often unhelpful.

Oh boy, this class was a mess. Bobda's a nice guy and wants everyone to succeed (you could submit labs a month late and still get over half credit), but there's really no structure to this class. Even the TAs were confused about what went on here. Wanna age 10 years but understand digilog? Take Schwartz. Wanna pass with little effort? Take Bobda.

Bobda is a caring professor for logic but the class is awfully structured. You definitely learn less than schwartz kids but it is easier to get a better grade and get through the semester. Labs are very unorganized and your TA can make or break the class for you. If you care about grade only, take Bobda. If you want to learn mateiral, take schwartz

Bobda is really kind and wants his students to do the best. Despite this, his class is extremely unorganized and very confusing. You spend hours trying to teach yourself the material because there are limited resources online. Would strongly recommend taking Digital Logic with a different professor if you want to actually learn material.
I did not enjoy this course, the lectures were impossible to follow, and this is possibly the most disorganized course I have ever taken. Avoid this class unless you need it to graduate.
Honestly didn't learn too much from Bobda. I don't think he's the right choice if you want to take uP or are majoring in EE. Bobda helps you get that A and that's about it.

Professor Bobda is a super nice and understanding professor. However, I was unable to learn from him or my TA. He will go through about 40 slides in the 50 minutes and will occasionally scribble something on the board. The only person I learned from was the main TA who's labs I attended on my own time. I received an A but I do not understand DL.

Prepare to code VHDL and few MIPS. Exams are open book and internet. Prelabs are due before the lab period. Don't take it if your lab period is on Monday or Tuesday. Because people are not very active during the weekends and you have to spend weekend on prelabs. **Someone should asks the professor to make labs due on the same day for everyone.**
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very hard class. Bobda is an ok lecturer but teaches a lot of outdated material. Hard to find resources to help you online. He is pretty lenient, will extend deadlines and release helper files for labs if you wait a few days to start. Labs are hard and need 20+ hours a week. Tests are hard. Seek out the good TAs for help. Hardest class ive taken

If you want a good grade in 3701 take Bobda, if you are willing to sacrifice your GPA for knowledge in this field, take Schwartz. Bobda actually wants you to get an A! He curves grades, extends deadlines, gives extra credit, and will work with you outside of class/OH; but be warned, he's not a great lecturer and will stumble over his own examples.

Bobda cares about his students wants us to learn the content and gives plenty of opportunity to get the grade we want. He does read off the slides but he does a lot of work on the whiteboard as well. All activities outside of the class are relevant and if you do all of it then you will do good on exams. Very understanding prof. You should get an A.
Great professor.

This class was 100% participation! You are given a proof from "Proofs from the Book" and, as long as you give a reasonable presentation of this proof, and attend all other presentations you will get an A. Bona, after the presentation will give a few words on it and, I must say, the man is a genius and just listening to him is enamoring.

Tests are 80% of your grade and tests are hard. The test is hard not because the question itself is hard, but because the homework is unrelated to the test. You do not have questions to prepare for the test. And the test requires you to have a very thorough understanding of the concepts.

Dr. Bona is a no BS professor. A very talented mathematician and in my opinion extraordinarily fair. I would highly recommend this course if you are interested in building a strong set of higher mathematics fundamentals. To be successful: Do NOT miss lectures. Ever. When he recommends reading ahead, DO SO. And lastly, DO THE TEXTBOOK Q's.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was the worst experience of my life. He changed the course to something it was not supposed to be, and seemed to be completely out of touch with reality. His expectations were completely unrealistic and he was the first professor Ive ever had be actively discouraging. He offered no support or help of any kind. Avoid him at any cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great at answering questions and explaining the content. Grades are based solely on exams (6 progressive, and 1 final). Partial credit is given on exams, but its out of 4 points per exam. Study hard, and though homework isn't "assigned", it is best to actually use the textbook and practice questions from there. SUPER HELPFUL TECHNIQUE TO PASS EXAMS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Your grade is based on 8 tests, and each test is only 4 points, but he gives a lot of partial credit. He's super smart but sometimes moves too quickly through the material, but it's easy enough to keep up if you do practice problems every night.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall, not bad, but unless he is the only teacher left, choose someone else. Goes through a TON of material very quickly, and doesn't let up. All exams are out of 4 points, so if you mess up, your grade drops quickly and severely. Overall, smart and dedicated, but a lot of work and time to pull off a great grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took him for a simple credit honors class, and it was pretty easy, but worth taking. I learned a lot about the proofs behind many math principles. I can tell that Bona is an extremely intelligent man, and he KNOWS his stuff. I don't doubt other reviewers who say he make his classes challenging, but that you learn a lot.

Took this class online, terrible decision. Used study edge and got Bs on all the exams and a C on the final.  He gave about an extra 5%  in extra credit which got me to an A-. It was hard but I actually did learn the material. So close to an A though :(

Bona is a great professor. He's probably the best math professor I've taken, however his class was still extremely challenging. The class was structured in a way that required constant studying, but in the end that made studying for the final easier. Great class overall, but not for someone who isn't willing to put the time and effort into it.
I really liked him as my professor. Whenever I asked a question, he was willing to go back over what he just said just so that I would understand it.

I respect Bona, I really do.  I'm a math major here at UF and have done well up until I took set theory with him.  He's possibly the smartest person I've ever met, but when it comes to teaching he is difficult to understand and you never know what is going to be on his test.  BEWARE OF BONA, you might have to drop, like I did.

While occasionally it may seem like he doesn't have proper teaching skills, but rather that he enjoys standing there just "talking to himself," he actually really knows his stuff and proves theorems. Going to class is worthwhile, and doing the optional homework is the most beneficial thing possible. Hard teacher, but learned a lot.
He's a good teacher but the class overall is hard. He's pretty funny, if you appreciate extremely dry humor. Good luck with the true/false, that's all I'm going to say.
One of my favorite professors. UF is lucky to have him. He's tough but fair, and as a result you'll learn a lot.

Ridiculously hard for the subject. This was my second time taking Diff EQ and it was no less than 10 times as hard as the last time I took it. I feel as though he was teaching at an Honors level, whereas this is simply NOT an honors level course I signed up for

One of the best teachers I have had in any subject. He may seem a bit gruff at first, but he is truly interested in helping you learn the material as long as you are willing to put in the effort. Pay attention in class and do the homework (which is optional but very helpful) and you will not only do well but will actually develop an understanding.

One of the best math teachers I have ever had. This is the hardest I have ever worked in a math class, however anytime I went into office hours, Dr. Bona was eager to help. If you want an easy A, do not take this with him. However, if you want to learn the material Dr. Bona is the best math teacher I have ever had.

Bona was very unforgiving when it came to grading. I put everything I had into this class. I studied countless hours, attended every lecture, and went to office hours but still had to drop it, along with quite a few others. Effort doesn't matter to him. Yes he may be a pure genius which I respect about him, but that didn't help me understand.

Definitely not an easy class but Bona is brilliant. Very inspiring and makes me want to continue my mathematics career (which I will do) and he makes you think way beyond what you have been expected to before.
Very difficult class.  The material/homework seems easy enough, but the tests are ridiculously hard.

One of the most difficult courses I have taken at UF, and quite possibly some of the best lectures I've had as well. There's no better way to learn Combinatorics or how to think like a Mathematician. If you are a serious math student, take Bona's class.  You won't regret it.
I worked my butt off but now I actually understand the stuff. By all means, if you just want at an easy A and do not care to learn the material, do not take a course with him.

Professor Bona makes this class extremely hard, he is unclear as to what material you need to know for the exams, but he also does not understand partial credit. Your grade is based on the exams, so you cannot mess up. To study for the exams, practice all the problems in the book, as for the T/F questions, read and pray. I do not recommend Bona.
DONT TAKE DIFF-EQ WITH THIS PROFESSOR IF YOU WANT AN A. He is very dedicated to making sure you know the material thoroughly with all the exceptions. 6 exams +final(27% of grade) that is CUMULATIVE.
He makes the class hard. There is True and False on the tests which sucks. He isn't very clear on what is going to be on the tests. Find another professor
It's not so much the material that's hard, just his tests. He really tries to get you on trick questions, and make the simple stuff as hard as possible.

He will take any material and make it as difficult as humanly possible. Do your best to avoid this teacher. I study all the time for this class and get bad grades when people with other teachers are much more successful with little energy. He gets pleasure out of failing students. Although he explains well, he doesn't understand partial credit.

The class went from 30 to about 10 people.Bona is one of the toughest teachers in the school, but if you want to learn math he will smash it into your skull,you will understand.His tests rely on genius(its more about how quick you are compared to how prepared) but he precurved the class, but its still wierd to be happy with a 70(an A in his class).

Bona makes any class insanely difficult.  If you truly love math, and are AMAZING at proving things, he can be inspiring.  Otherwise he will be your worst nightmare.  I currently have an A by the skin of my teeth, but would still recommend against taking him unless you have supreme confidence in your mathematical abilities.

Bona's exams are really tough. only 3 questions, and very little partial credit. He explains really well though, so if you are willing to put in the work, you will do OK. The grading scale for abstract algebra was 70-100 is an A, and in 10 point increments afterward. 25/40 students dropped the course. To keep up, I did every odd problem in the book
sucked beyond sucking
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Dr. Dorr's class is extremely valuable. She is extremely competent and has been doing research for decades. It can be hard to reach her outside of class, but the TAs are very available. If you study, you'll learn everything you need to know.

Every assignment/exam is open-everything so its ez to pass with a good grade. Projects are kinda pointless but considering most special topic courses are always full, this is a great alternative. Slides werent downloadable which was kinda a dealbreaker for taking notes but its wtv considering how free this class was

Very chill class, easy assignments and projects, and Dr. Dorr is very passionate and knowledgable about NLP. This semester she implemented BLADE which is an AI chatbot specific to the class and it helped a lot. The lectures/quizzes/exams are straightforward with no surprises.

Always impossible for her to be wrong. "Some of you guys call advanced concepts trick questions." Honestly, if you need a good understanding of grammar to get a good understanding of the course. Projects are easy as hell, but quizzes will mess you up. 3 hour class, but the whole time is for reviewing the weekly quiz and answering general questions.

Prof Door is a good lecturer, very intelligent, and I thought the content was interesting. I did not, however, appreciate the projects and overall wish we spent more time going over the low level theory of NLP. I'll admit though, this partly come from my dislike for Python, and my general unwillingness to sink too much time into this elective.

She's not a kind person. For some reason even though she's teaching a class, she has a general animosity towards students. If you have any issues in her class, be prepared to be blamed because she can't be wrong about anything
She also doesn't teach actual NLP, just gives you the esoteric textbook explanation. Too lazy to host her whole 3hour class
