Burt is awesome. He's not the most energetic guy, which may put some people off, but he knows his stuff and he's interesting. He's also very forward with his opinions, about politics, the class, or anything.

I didn't learn very much at all in this class. You have to come with questions for every film and class reading and then you discuss them. Historical accuracy of films is brought up a million times. Very boring... The only thing I enjoyed was watching all the different Midieval films.
Dr. Burt is probably one of the best professors at UF!  He's very relaxed and open-minded, and most of his classes are roundtable discussions.  He also assigns great readings and films.
cared more about himself then his students. hard to follow- not particuraly nice. Do not recommend.

Super easy class if you just work on the flashcards, the assignments are easy and interesting, and the tests are the quizzes but longer. The professor was kind and nice, and overall present for an online professor! Would recommend!

This class is a great, easy elective. There are weekly quizzes that are not honor locked, and a midterm + a final that are honor locked and you have a week to take. There are also extra credit opportunities. The class was interesting and assignments are easy with most answers being found in the textbook.

Super easy class. You can finish the course (other than the midterm and final) in probably less than a week. Easy A and helpful for pre-health! The prof was very clear in her grading, though did not always respond to emails.

Great class. Super helpful if you're prehealth and very low maintenance. Midterm and final were super chill and if you do extra worksheets you can get extra points put towards ur midterm and final. Never had to worry about my grade in this class. I strongly recommend it!!!

Very easy class that provided me with a lot of practical knowledge. Memorization based, so tests were very straightforward and easy to ace. A lot of extra credit provided, 12 points per each exam. Only two exams, a midterm and final. Professor seemed very nice and caring. She wanted the students to understand the content.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class is very easy yet really insightful. It took 30 minutes to get through the weeks work and I studied starting two days before the midterm and got a 100. Apply yourself and you will do well. DON'T get the textbook - you will never need it. 24 points of extra credit is offered throughout the course. I highly recommend!
This was an awesome class. She made the class fun and enjoyable and it was for sure an easy 3 credit class. She was the best and offered extra credit on the midterm and final. LOVE HER

This class is an easy A if you study lots for the midterm and final. The assignments during the week are super easy and took me max 30 mins to complete. I reached out to the professor a few times and she was great and really cares about her students. I enjoyed this class.

Taryn is awesome! She is so funny and she makes the monotonous material interesting. I definitely learned a lot and enjoyed going to class. Attendance is mandatory because she does random sign-ins. She has great guest lecturers and movies to supplement her teaching. She is great and I highly recommend this class if you want an easy A.

Taryn is very entertaining and funny. However, the class is nothing bu regurgitation. She basically gives everyone all the answers. She joked about her tests being middle school level, which is almost an understatement. I wish the class would have been a little more challenging. Make sure you fill in the powerpoints and DON'T buy the book.

Taryn is a good instructor. One problem is communication. She NEVER responds to emails and doesn't offer much help. When you have a problem, you might as well suck it up. Take this class for an easy A. You won't really learn much and it's not a challenge. She tells you exactly what's on the test. She's more of a friend than a teacher.

Taryn is very funny, helpful and interesting teacher. Just make sure you have the blanks filled in for her power points. Tests are super easy. I studied the day of the test and got a 95%. Don't buy the book because she tells you what is going to be on the test.

I found this class pretty boring because of the 3 hour lecture but none of that was Bridis's fault. He's a great professor and knows a lot about reporting. I would miss class from time-to-time, and it was no big deal. Lectures were online and the weekly quizzes or homeworks were simple to complete.

Prof. Bridis knows his stuff and his class is extremely useful. He's a funny guy and the class went the full three hours maybe once or twice. Tests aren't a cake walk, but he will go out of his way to let you retake them to help you at the end of the semester. Would highly recommend.

I loved this class! Definitely super useful and I was a big fan of his lectures and sense of humor, you could tell he's lived! He's always there to help so don't hesitate to reach out. For summer A we only had 6 quizzes and 4 assignments, so not many grades. The quizzes are really specific so have the lectures out and read the questions carefully.

Very professional and knowledgeable professor. Also very flexible. I was out for a while with a serious illness, and he was very accommodating. Lectures never went the full 3 hours. Weekly assignments are not hard, but they are not engaging.

Incredible professor!! He is incredibly knowledgeable about the journalism world and left every class wanting more. Every week consisted of a Packback assignment, and a quiz based on the lecture plus a couple of other assignments throughout the semester and some extra credit. Very easy to get an A. 100% recommend and can't wait to take him again

Best professor ever. If you want to learn how to be a good journalist, he's your guy. If you want to hear the craziest stories, he's also your guy. If you want a brilliant source of knowledge in the field and true guidance, he's amazing. Overall, attend his class, it is one of the most valuable classes I've ever taken.

I absolutely loved Professor Bridis for JOU3110. He is one of the most down-to-earth professors I have ever had. He is always open to help you, and you can tell he truly loves what he teaches. The course content isn't that bad, some of it can get a little tricky. He makes sure to post the PowerPoints, which can be a great resource.

THE BEST. The lectures are SUPER long but are worth watching, exams are not proctored and the lecture really is a cheat sheet for the exam bc he goes step by step how to find the info. Weekly backpack questions (stay on top) and maybe a small paper here and there (easy grader). 100% recommend!!

I've had Dr.Brown for both ISM3254 and ISM3255 now and I think he is incredible. I've had many coding professors in the past who can't seem to grasp the fact that coding is a new subject for many students. Dr. Brown walks you through Java so clearly and the assignments all have purpose. He is a gem of a professor.

The class itself is challenging without a textbook and in such timeframe (8wks), but he gave us soo much material to review even without a textbook. He also makes himself available to help students through regular office hours or you can just schedule a teams meeting with him. I would say it's a lot for a 2credit class but he's a good professor.

Poor course structure across all his classes. With such a bad rate my professor at his previous school it's a mystery why UF hired him. He seems almost panicked teaching and gets himself always behind which puts us at risk consistently. Doesn't look out for student success at all.

This course has way too many assignments. There are quizzes, labs, discussions, and two exams. He covers way too much material in 6 weeks. For the quizzes and exams, I felt very overwhelmed with the amount of material I had to know. I would have to constantly study to keep up. If there is another professor, take the class with them.
He assigns convoluted assignments and never grades them so you do not know how well youre doing in the class. It is a 2 credit class that takes like 6 hours each weeek
He will change assignments on you last minute and only update through announcements.

Professor Moraski is a great guy, very knowledgable. Theres a lot of readings, and the class is only really graded by attendance and the exams, which aren't too bad, but he likes to throw a couple curveball questions in there about niche things, and that can really mess your grade up because of the lack of any other assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Moraski was the best professor I had at UF.  He is insanely approachable, and his lectures were always interesting.  His classes require a good bit of reading and work, but it ultimately made me a much better student as a result.

Very interesting class but is difficult if you have no previous knowledge of Russia. Very informative but his slides are bare, so you have to pay attention and take notes. He wants students to succeed and be engaged. The class can attract strange people but he handles them. It's important to read and study. The tests are specific but managable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Moraski is a great professor and CPO3633 couldn't have been more informative.  His classes are a bit faster-paced than some political science classes at UF and in a good way, after a class or two you realize the importance of coming in completely prepared to break down the reading assigned for the day and it makes everything easier.

Please do not take this professor for your own mental health. He is very specific with his exams and participation. His paper was not hard to write but he is a tough grader. There are far easier classes to take as a poli sci major. Attendance is mandatory and he does not share notes or his power point at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's passionate about teaching and means well, but his exams are highly specific to lectures & readings. I had to study at least two hours a day to keep an A, and he doesn't share his slides. Paper was tough, and he's really strict about attendance and participation. He can seem timid when you ask for help. There are easier classes.

Amazing professor!! 3 noncumulative exams but they're doable if you do the class readings (PDF style, 10-15 pgs max). Asks questions in class straight from readings & answering counts towards participation. One paper - good grader on it and has great office hours to help. Totally recommend!!

Amazing teacher!! Has 3 exams based on class readings but they're not bad if you do the readings (PDF style, max 10-15 pages); no HW besides reading. Asks questions in class but they're easy if you read before & that counts towards participation. One big paper but good grader, great office hours to help with it. 

Totally recommend!!

Professor Moraski is an amazing lecturer! Every class was super engaging, with interesting readings we discussed in-depth. The course content was fascinating, and I learned so much. I'm really grateful I got to take this class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: For your own mental health, do not take his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tough class but very interesting and you learn a lot. If you work for it, you can definitely do well. Would highly recommend making a study group and attending office hours.

He is a pretty good professor. If you are interested in Russian politics, I recommend taking his class if you need a quick PoliSci credit.  A lot of reading, but honestly I didn't even do most of them and just wrote notes on the discussions of the readings during class because he ends up telling you what was important during the lecture anyway.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class won't be easy if you don't give the material the attention it needs. Get ready to read A LOT, and make sure that you understand the content. Class was based on five exams and two papers. If you procrastinate, and if you do not show up for class, then you will struggle in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Moraski makes his classes very easy to navigate. Everything is organized and provided for you for the most part. His classes tend to be very lecture and reading-heavy, but the readings are not difficult at all. The quizzes can be tough, but if you do the readings and review you will be fine. Participate in class if you want a good grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He makes you read a ton, but he split up the final into 5 or 6 short quizzes which I liked. He obviously knows a lot and his lectures show it, I just wish he wasn't so hard to follow. He doesn't grade harsh on essays but the quizzes are pretty hard and will make you study your notes once or twice, but they are open note. Overall he seems nice.

Slow grader. With only four grades for the semester it was nerve-wracking. Graduates walked without knowing if they actually passed the class. Three weeks to grade an exam is no different than a student turning in late work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the hardest PoliSci professors at UF. He makes you work for your grade but as long as you go to class and put in the work you can get a B or an A. MAKE A STUDY GROUP
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Moraski is very articulate, entertaining, and knowledgeable. As long as you have some interest in recent Russian history and contemporary Russian politics, you will enjoy this class and learn a lot. There is a fair bit of reading, but most of it is interesting and even if you skip some of it but still attend class you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Moraski is definitely passionate about Russian politics. I would advise anyone considering this class to first take Russian history. Have some basic knowledge of Russia from the Bolshevik Revolution to the present. Otherwise, you will spend a lot of time explaining more history to yourself than anything else. He's a good teacher, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher. He keeps the readings interesting and is very good at keeping anyone's attention in lecture. His test are only hard if you don't study. He has funny jokes and is worth taking the class. Also try to start a study group makes studying easier. Make sure to come to class, could be the difference between a 10 or 9 on an essay.

First of all he's funny as hell, which I appreciate. lectures are extremely fascinating (for people who like politics). But, do understand what you're getting into. Expect 60 pages a week of dense articles + short-answer/essay questions on exams that are hard to get full points on. You need to be an expert at studying this kind of stuff already.

I took Politics in Russia summer A and he was a great professor. It was a condensed class so keeping up with readings is a must. If you participate and show effort he'll recognize it, which is extremely helpful in a class with few assignment grades.

This was an extremely helpful class to take as a poli sci major.  Comparative elections is rarely taught at an undergraduate level, and I enjoyed it. The reading materials were a little difficult, but overall the information was very interesting. Go to class, do the readings, participate, and you will be fine when it comes to the test/papers.

Had him for the Intro to Comparative Political Analysis, the first graduate course in the subfield. Outstanding Prof who does an excellent job fostering discussion and keeping comments on topic. He is an A type personality and has high expectations, yet do the reading, participate, and you'll earn an A.

His teaching style in class was fair, but the way he approached "constructive" criticism on papers showed he has absolutely no business teaching undergraduate courses. Rather than providing ideas for how to better a paper, he writes from a negative place. He should stick to teaching graduate courses.

This class was challenging but it was definitely worth it. I have a much stronger understanding of politics in other countries and I feel that it enhanced my understanding of things in my other polisci classes. Basically: if you put in the effort you'll get the A.

TAKE THIS CLASS WITH MORASKI! Many complain that he is "difficult," but honestly if you do the readings and show up to (interesting) lecture, you'll have no trouble in his class. I'm a freshman, non poli-sci major and got an A in his class without doing any additional classwork than what he gave. Very helpful for understanding current global events

I LOVE history and politics but this class was awful. The TAs finally asked him to slow down during lecture but he verbally brushed it off. He puts one phrase on the powerpoint and then just goes off on random tangents. I brought my computer and I type super fast....yet it was still extremely hard to keep up. You have to go to class every lecture

Don't take his class!!!! I was very excited to take this class, but I was disappointed. He mumbles too much. He is very intelligent, but he doesn't know how to communicate with his students in a large lecture hall. He sometimes seems like he is talking to himself. Take CPO2001 with someone else :) His exams and weekly assignments are hard.

Moraski is a nice guy and loves what he teaches. However, he is not used to teaching undergrad courses, and his intro level course is a killer. Prepare to do insane amounts of gradlevel reading and to study obscure details for his tests. It's good practice if you plan on taking higher level poli sci classes, but way too much work for an intro class

Interesting teacher and seems like a nice guy. Class was compelling and the readings were advanced, but informative. If you want an easy A this is not the course. A lot of reading and you should attend class to expect an A or B on the exams.

Intro to Comparative Politics. It's really not that bad, I don't know what everyone's complaining about. All you have to do is read. There's a lot of readings but all you really need is the gist of the stuff,no real tough analysis; all you have to know is what concept goes with what reading. And Moraski talks fast but he's good. Got jokes too.

I would have been much more interested if I wasn't weighed down with so much reading. He spoke many times of his role as a teacher in our learning but never actually came through. Also, if you have a Mac, one of the textbooks (MicroCase Explorit) won't work for you unless you have Windows emulation software.

If this course is offered, take it with someone else. I would think that he would want people to become (and stay) involved in Poli. Sci. Instead he makes the class extremely hard and difficult :( Anybody else but Moraski!

really fascinating stuff. unfortunatly, unless you already have a degree in poli sci, chances are it will be a struggle. tests are unbelievable difficult, several dozen pages of dense reading every week, and lectures were often hard to follow and involved irrelevant tangents. obvious weed out for poli sci majors

I like his class. It is really interesting and Professor Moraski knows his stuff. I actually spoke to him during office hours and he was really nice. :) He actually challenges you to think about politics which I think is a great idea.
pretty hard class for a 2000 level. he goes off on tangents a lot, makes a lot of references to russian politics, and doesn't tie in the material together for you.

This was one of the better professors I have had so far. Took Russian Politics in Fall '07. Definitely must keep up with readings and attendance to get an A, but overall not bad. And he takes the time to learn everyone's name. Very approachable and fair.

Democratization Global Perspective. I was surprised to read over some of these ratings. I thought he was one of the nicer more approachable professors I've ever had. He's definitely tough and expects you to be caught up on the reading every class, but his notes follow very closely with what you read. Very helpful on essays and tests. Recommended.

very hard class and very hard grader.  i went to class every day and studied for hours for the exams which are very detailed and challenging.  despite all the effort i put in no A.  very hard class not worth it

Dr. Moraski is one of the best profs i have ever taken. He succeeds in his aim to be 'challenging but fair.' study guide he gives is a life saver. must go to class and do the readings, but both are normally interesting. one decently sized paper and three tests. highly recomended if interested at all in Russian politics, not for the slacker, however

Loved the class but not for everyone, you must be interested in Russian Politics or ready to work really hard. Attendance was important, a lot of reading but very interesting articles. 3 exams and one 10pg paper. I would take another class with Moraski. He is not as mean as he appears to be, very nice and funny guy.

I had him in his first year. You could tell he was nervous, but he tried really hard. It was an introductory course, so not particularly fascinating. He prepared very well and the lectures were very sturctured. I prefer less structure, but oh well. He was very nice and approachable and understanding when I complained that my TA was an idiot.

I loved this class because I learned so much in it.  He is very fair, the exams are very straightforward, and I am glad I took the course.  The paper helped me so much in terms of understanding post-communist transitions and was very interesting.
If you don't go to class you will not do well.  Exams are are not easy, there are pretty fair though.  Pretty forgiving on the essays if you spill your guts on the writing
Tough but fair
He has no structure. He knows everything about Russia so he jumps back and forth in time and topic to the point you don't know what he is talking about. Still, he is interesting but very, very hard.
He's interesting and fair. He's never vague and if you do the work, you'll be fine.
STAY AWAY
JUST DONT.
he is new so he is hard... not super friendly. trying to make tenure.
Aloof--a researcher first, he teaches as an afterthought. Very structured, so take careful notes and do all the reading assigned. Ultimately, he is tough, but fair.
Tests are hard, just do the review sheet.  If you work hard, you will do fine.
Extremely difficult tests, not very helpful.
Knows his stuff.
had for east euro politics; hard tests
not cool...tough tests

Lectures are not particularly useful, exam reviews basically go through every lecture compactly. Homework takes forever to do and is not super related to exams at all. Exams do require a lot of studying but very manageable. Interesting teacher, but definitely get the textbook and read it over a lot of the lectures to save time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Probably the best lecturer at UF. The info he gives in lecture stays with you more than other professors. He test are ... different, but in a way that aims at understanding rather than simply going through the motions, hes the engineering goat fr.

He seems to confuse a good student with someone who laughs at his jokes rather than does well in the class. Good at teaching, but has an ego. Just because you do not like his teaching style does not make you sad and boring. You are just different! If you don't like a teacher pushing 40 acting like a teen, don't drop the class just be yourself!

Numerical methods is honestly a pretty conceptually difficult and boring subject at times but Brooks' lectures are great. His jokes and quips are hilarious and make it easy to stay engaged during class. Consistently gave out homework extensions and extra credit. You can tell he really cares about his students. Great class overall

Brooks was probably THE BEST professor I have had at UF so far! His lectures were not only helpful in learning the material but he's an inspirational man who taught us many things about whats to come in life. Numerical methods is hard, the homework takes a lot of time, and the exams are manageable if you study! Take Brooks if you got the chance!

Numerical methods are a hard material. Dr. Brooks makes it fun and bearable. The homework can sometimes be difficult but going to his office hours made them significantly easier. 10/10 prof never a dull moment. Highly recommend taking numerical methods with Dr.Brooks.

DO ALL THE EXTRA CREDIT! I got 80s on first 2 exams and 104 (locked in) on the final but its doing all that EC that got me an A. The TAs are the best Ive ever had for a class, GO TO OH, theyre so helpful! Exams are fair, im just not a great exam taker. He makes class very engaging and explains hard concepts like we are 'simple monkeys', so helpful!

The best engineering prof I have had so far, and probably ever will have. His homeworks really help you to fully understand the concepts and the material is really interesting. His tangents are funny yet purposeful.

If you have the chance to take Dr. Brooks you 100% should because he is a pleasure to have. The class is hard and will require a lot of time but Dr. Brooks is very easy to work with and easy to ask questions to. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but if you want to do well attend all the lectures. He genuinely cares about his students learning.

Lectures are great, funny, and easy to follow, despite his tangents and some comments with slightly controversial racial/political/religious undertones. Severely lacks in organizational and communication skills. Very unclear grading criteria, including extra credits (take advantage of them). Better than the alternative.

Brooks is super caring but the HWs take a long time so START EARLY. You get a cheat sheet on exams which is awesome and the TAs are super knowledgeable too. Also, he is very committed to the bit, so if you're not into hijinks then don't take him. But if you are (like me) then it's a breath of fresh air. My fav Twitch streamer.

Very funny and easy to talk to. Really good at breaking down concepts and explaining them in simple terms with analogies, and wants to make sure you understand. Values your education and his tests are fair. Do your homework and this class will be a breeze! Plus, his tangents make the lectures interesting.

Dr. Brooks is in every sense of the word, exceptional. From his energy, knowledge in the field, and commitment to his students learning, I cannot think of any educator in my entire educational career that was as great as him. He is the type of professor that you seek out as you will no doubt learn so much, while still having a great time doing it.

By far the best professor that I have had at UF. The class is difficult and homework's are very long and tedious; but if you don't take Dr. Brooks for numerical, you are making a mistake. Very funny and makes his lectures very engaging.
Abnormally committed to your success. Lots of homework, but lots of help is available. Writing this from my chalet in the alps, reflecting on numerical methods.

Brooks is the best prof I've had at UF. He almost always responds to messages immediately, is willing to walk you through homework problems or any other questions you have at any time of day. Numerical is tough but Brooks makes it so much easier to understand. Exams are fair and there is so much extra credit.

Dr. Brooks is the best professor I've had so far. He is super knowledgeable is his field and always willing to help. He would answer my slack messages at 3 am. Exams were easy if you paid attention to his lectures, which were entertaining and easy to pay attention to. The homework was pretty lengthy but manageable with office hours and slack.

I never go to class but I did for this man. He has one of the most engaging, funny, and overall enjoyable classes ever. He always talks about how the education system has failed you, but he is writing a different narrative. My most favorite professor since I have been at UF by far.

DUDE TAKE HIS CLASS!So funny, and so involved. He doesn't just teach you numerical methods but he also teaches you about how to think and act like an engineer. Not to mention he has so much EXTRA CREDIT but he's also such a fun guy. Don't believe his warnings to not take the class if you want to enjoy your life. If you don't like him you're boring.

One of the best professors UF has. Amazing lectures, he clearly knows very well what he's teaching about, the homework are hard but you actually learn a lot and it's not that difficult to get through with them, but more importantly, he's an amazing person. LOADS of extra credit opportunities and he's very understanding in any matter. 10/10

Dr. Brooks makes Numerical Methods (a crucial piece in understanding advanced Mechanical Engineering Curriculum) extremely digestible and easy. He is also an amazing human. If you do bad in this class, it is your fault.

Just an overall good dude who puts life and personality into his lectures. Controls can be very confusing and while he didn't explain it perfectly, it mostly made sense. Tends to waste some time with lecture stories and second exam had too little preparation, but he stands out in the engineering department as friendly, approachable, and available.

Brooks took so much time outside class to help guide my learning. He honestly cares so much about his students. He is a gem and a blessing to the UF department. Refreshing to see a professor care so much

One of the best professors in MAE. He cares about his students and is very accessible and understanding. He really breaks down his problems into small bites that are understandable. He is concept focused and only does derivations where it is absolutley necessary. You definitely walk away knowing more than you would if it were a different professor

Literally won an award this semester for being one of the best professors in the college of engineering. OH are engaging and beneficial, available at 2:00am, genuinely friendly. Taking one class with brooks means going down a rabbit hole of semesterly begging the registrar to let him teach one of your classes. Homework takes forever and is hard asf

Dr. Brooks is an amazing professor. You can tell this by the way he is. Incredibly knowledgeable, engaging, and hilarious. Homeworks are quite difficult but he provides ample resources to help students succeed, including tons of office hours. Exams are fair, even fun. Overall, best professor I've had and made learning genuinely fun.

Best professor at UF. He devotes so much of his time to teaching, it's insane. Constantly on slack and many office hours to help us. If you don't get something, ask him for help or look through slack. The class is difficult to grasp at first, but it's not hard to look for/get help. You can tell that he has a passion for this. Enjoyable lectures
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I haven't been excited to learn in a while. But considering he doesn't teach any more of my future classes, all hope is lost )-:

Brooks is a great professor for numerical methods. The class itself is very difficult, no matter who you take it with. Brooks gives lots of extra credit and makes it very manageable to succeed in the class. Homework is very important and is weighted just as much as an exam in the end. Exams are fair but comprehensive, review everything!!

GOAT favorite class ever and I took in the spring 2022, homeworks are hard but fun and exams are very fair based on hw and quizzes and he makes sure we know everything we need to before the exam, if you can't take dynamics with brooks just add as many semesters as you need to get it with him, you won't learn anything as well and deeply

Best professor in MAE> cares deeply> gives everything we needed to do well> engaging lectures> posts his notes> busy office hours, but he made sure to give time to everyone present> handcrafts the homework, so you learn what you need to know for the exams> exam reviews go back through the notes, were very helpful> makes himself available over slack

Dr. B is the best professor I've had at UF. He goes out of his way to help students and uses so much of his free time to answer questions and host extra office hours. He is always helpful and is understanding when he notices we are stressed and adjusts the class accordingly. My only qualm is that he picked god-awful TAs. I hope to have him again.

Brooks makes numerical very accessible and bearable even for students who don't feel confident with programming or math concepts. VERY approachable and helpful in slack/office hours. Overall very challenging but very rewarding class.

Tries to be quirky in everything he explains and it really subtracts from your ability to understand material. Can never give you a straight up answer no matter how lost you are in an assignment, just repeats the same useless line over and over and you arent able to ever understand it. he is an engineer's nightmare, we just want concrete answers!!!
OG DR. B IS THE BEST

I normally don't write RMP reviews, but I just had to after taking his class. One of the best profs I've ever had. Teaches you how to think versus just plug and chug. Class was always entertaining, too. Learned a bit of grammar, Latin, and Survivor trivia along the way. Taking him again for Numerical (and any other class he teaches in the future).

Simply S tier, one of the few outstanding MAE professors. It takes a while to get used to his... style. But at the end of the semester you will realize that its probably the most fun you have had within a class. Homework is a lot in quantity, but an experience to solve. Very good at explaining concepts.

Dr. Brooks has an interesting sense of humor but it is quite hilarious. I think he is one of the best professors I have taken so far. I thought the class was going to be difficult because it is entirely made up of variables. However, Dr. Brooks is always there to help and he teaches in such a way that it helped me understand the material.

Dr. Brooks is hands down one of the greatest and most inspirational instructors at this school. I took him for numerical methods, dynamics, and controls and I can definitely say that Ive learned more in his classes than any course offered by UF. His homework and exams test your ability to think critically and not rely on mindless use of formulas.

Dr. Brooks is easily my favorite teacher of all time. His lectures are a great combination of informative and fun. While Controls is very conceptual, he is very understanding and offers plenty of office hours with him or with the TA's. He makes every exam easy enough so that they have 85-90% averages. I cannot recommend him enough.

He really does care about his students and puts time into the class. regardless, his teaching is very confusing, he never gets to the point fast making it hard to stay focused. His exam 3 had such a low average that he gave us a retake. The project took everyone so long to figure out, even with lots of office hours, it made finals week even harder.

Dr. B really gives a d-mn about his students & wants them to succeed. He's personable, tries to make dry subject matter actually interesting, and is singlehandedly the reason why I know how to program in MATLAB. Has great TAs. The exams are weird and conceptual, but not unfair or too confusing. I've taken 3 classes with him and hope to take more.

Dr. Brooks is the best teacher I've had at UF. He consistently explains things in a way that makes sense and also feels like you came up with it. He likes to reference pop culture during lecture and some find it a little distracting but it didn't take away from the lecture for me. His office hours are essential and taught me twice as much as class.

I really don't understand why people rave about Dr. Brooks. He's knowledgeable, but he also has to explain everything in the most confusing, pretentious way possible until it's clear no one understands what he's talking about, and only then does he bother to explain it reasonably. Really don't understand why people enjoy this kind of teaching.

He's a good lecturer, but the class and tests are hard. Homework and exam questions were often unclear. Exams consisted of 5 true/false questions with explanations worth 40% of each exam grade and 1 long problem worth 60%. Slow at grading exams and we had to take the final exam without knowing our exam 3 score that was taken before thanksgiving
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: great lecturer and nice person who truly cares <3 however, exam grading took awhile and nothing was returned apart from the points earned on each section. when asked, he said he did not have marked copies of the exams to return. i get that his focus is on learning but the lack of transparency with grades was alarming. he will admit to his flaws tho
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hes good at lecturing but his overall class organization is pretty awful. You have no idea what your grade is till it pops up on the transcript. Exams were kind of disastrous and I have no idea how he grades anything. He insists you trust him with it but its not generous. Homeworks were really unclear and required you to go to office hours a lot

I cannot put into words how much I loved this class with Dr. B. Lectures are hilarious if you understand his pop culture references and he explains things well. This class reminded me why I like engineering after contemplating dropping out. Focus on learning the material slowly instead of cramming. Also, you will get solid laughs from his memes.
literally just go to his office hours and you'll see... he's gr8

best professor I've had. his lectures are well structured and he is very passionate about the material. Numerical definitely takes some brain power, but Brooks will literally drop anything on his plate if you need some extra help outside of class. truly cares about his students' success and well-being. wicked smaht. what a guy.
what a guy. charming and witty and really cares for his students. go to class and office hours and you will be gr8

by far the best, most empathetic professor ive had at UF. by no means are his classes easy, but hes always available to offer extra help if you just ask. you can tell he truly cares for our well being and success as students, and he offers a good amount of extra credit as well
Incredible professor. Probably the best professor I've ever had. Extremely caring. Makes class fun. I love this man!! 11/10 would recommend

Dr. Brooksis brilliant, can speak intelligently on a plethora of topics, and REALLY wants you to do well in his class. I also took him for Numerical. His homeworks can be difficult, but going to his office hours gets you in a small group where he will work through everything with you. He wants you to learn. He also tends to go on tangents and meme.
This class was somewhat chaotic, but ultimately I learned how to solve dynamics problems pretty well. Expect lots of typos and Survivor trivia.

Dr. Brooks is my favorite professor at UF to date. He is absolutely hilarious during lectures, relatable, and is incredibly caring towards his students. He also has a very down to earth teaching style that simplifies difficult to understand concepts and makes them feel incredibly easy. If you have the chance, take Dr. Brooks! PS Memes Galore!

In my opinion Dr. Brooks is easily one of the greatest professors I've had the opportunity to take classes with. He is great at teaching the material and he is very passionate. In addition, Brooks cares about his students and is always more than glad to help you in office hours. He makes class a joy to go to and is always cracking jokes.

Brooks/the TAs take forever to grade HW/exams (literally over a month). The lectures are half relevant/half random tangents. The homework is very time consuming, but exams are fairly easy. You can tell Dr. Brooks is passionate about the material, but I wouldn't say he's good at teaching it.

reviews.comment: Dr. Brooks is a good choice for numerical methods. I enjoyed this class with him. The material is dry, but the class isnt that hard.
Great professor, best i've had at UF. very passionate and made light of very dry subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Brooks is the best professor I have had at UF! He puts lots of effort into making class as engaging as he can and making himself available to students outside of the classroom with lots of office hours. Go to office hours. He gives plenty of time to complete homework assignments, but they can be overwhelming if you wait too long.
Take numerical methods with this hero!!! He's awesome! exams are easy and conceptual although the homework are hard and time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He's just an overall cool and interesting dude that makes the boring material kind of interesting. The material isn't really that hard and exams are doable. The biggest issue with Brooks is that his classes are highly sought after and fill up immediately during registration.

His lectures are very enjoyable if you pay attention and really try to understand the material. The class requires a little more MATLAB than students are taught in COP2271, but the homework is doable, and sometimes enjoyable if you have a good understanding of the concepts being taught. Exams are mostly conceptual.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Brooks does a good job of teaching a pretty dry subject in a way that is entertaining while in class. His homeworks take forever but that is the nature of the class. Overall great teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Brooks is compassionate, personable, and very knowledgeable. He was not once stumped by a question asked in class. He is a solid lecturer and usually had a few "when are we going to actually use this" examples. He makes a notoriously dry subject relevant and as interesting as it can be. Great guy, great teacher. Take him for numerical!

He's a really good teacher who cares a lot about his classes. He gives hard homework but he gives so much time to help his students understand it. His exams aren't bad if you pay attention to his lecture and he gives a lot of hints about it. The topic is kind of dry but its not really his fault. If you put in the effort you'll get an A.

This professor has a very structured, understandable lecturing methodology and is able to keep me entertained despite an otherwise dry, seemingly inconsequential subject. This class will require a lot of effort, however that effort will pay off as the subject matter is very practical with respect to mechanical/ aerospace engineering.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He seems like a good guy who is passionate about the subject. However, the class is much more difficult than it really needs to be. Like someone else posted, the quizzes were focused on obscure details rather than key concepts. The essay assignments get longer and longer throughout the semester, and the grading is abruptly hypercritical.

I took Black Popular Culture online. It wasn't bad, just more work than some other quest 1 courses. It does give you words which is nice, exams aren't hard at all, lecture videos are alright. The topic is a little boring and the professor isn't super engaging. Overall, medium-level course. If you want to take a quest online, it's not bad at all.

ABSOLUTELY DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! The TAs are incredibly picky with grading, and papers just get longer each week. This is listed as a 2000 word class, but you definitely write more than that. Although extra credit is offered, your grade is dependent on 5 measly questions based off hours of reading and lecture material. WARNING: NEVER TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Initially when choosing this class, I wanted to fulfill my quest 1 credit, but then after being enrolled into the class, I realized just how difficult the class is. The quizzes are only 5 questions that test you on at least 3 pieces of large media, and the papers and presentations are graded very strictly. I would never take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Class is handled terribly. I took summer b so the fast pace was to be expected but each weak had a paper that was longer than the last up to 1.5k. TAs graded everything which was good at first, but randomly some assignments were nit-picky. everything is graded late so you get feedback after you submit the same mistakes. manageable class tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Class was disorganized and the amount of writing you have to do is absurd. Doesn't feel like the professor cares at all about his students and just assigns these huge papers to keep students busy rather than actually learning anything.

Dr. Brown took his class, Why Sports Matter, way too seriously. I thought the class was going to be easy, but no. The quizzes were 10 questions which you had 5 minutes to complete, and the questions were on very specific details from readings that took hours. In one assignment, you had to record yourself march/chant for a political issue in sports.

Dr. Drew Brown was very enthusiastic about the topic. However, he failed on numerous levels to effecivley teach the class. He was extremely vauge on instructions and very harshg on grading, espeically on assignments/essays that were worth a large percentage of the grade. Although enthusiastic about the topic, professor seemed to dislke students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown, though very knowledgeable on the subject at hand, was an awful professor. This is due to the obscure nature of the class the class was difficult, and Dr. Brown's inability to convey his thoughts in one coherent thought led to this class feeling dragged along and lacking a key point. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS by Dr. Brown.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr.Brown's class is very unorganized. He assigns readings that are HOURS long and even if you break the readings up into a little bit each day, he does quizzes every Tuesday that ask about the most irrelevant details , so you'll get them wrong if you dont remember it. Do not take this class if you're looking for an easy A quest class.

I took this class over summer B as a newly admitted freshman and man was that one heck of a start at UF. We had assignments due frequently and were given so many materials (texts, pdfs, videos, articles) for each chapter all for 5 question MC quizs. The papers were long and unconventional. TAs were make or break for your grade. Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Please do not take this class. Maybe it was because I took it online over Summer but the class's workload is insane. There would be hours of videos, 50+ pages of readings, lecture videos, a quiz, and then occasionally a 1000+ word essay per module. The TAs are horrible graders, giving little feedback. The professor is extremely passive-aggressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
-required textbook "sports in African American life" never used (he wrote the book)
-hours of reading for 5 question quiz about miniscule details (or not mentioned in reading)
-more Black history that Black popular culture
-assignments due next day, even over weekends
-passive aggressive
-canvas unorganized so some essential things are inaccessible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown's class was incredibly disorganized with many in the class not knowing what topics out of the many twenty page articles and hour long videos we were assigned would be on the exams. Assignments had unclear and often changing instructions. We had five different papers each up to 1700 words long for a six week class. Do not take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Brown is extremely intelligent. But he is very unorganized, often times changing the grading rubric after the assignment has been submitted. He will also ridicule you for your opinion making you feel inferior when he thinks he creating an environment for critical thinking. He will also cut you off and talk over you. DO NOT TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Takes forever to put grades in, no resources available for tests, an excessive amount of reading for a five question quiz, unapproachable, and rude. The class is set up for you to struggle and possibly fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown has amazing and engaging lectures where he fosters class discussion and open debate for critical thinking. This is a reading and writing heavy class, but it's worth the work you put in.

Absolutely awful experience, class was super unorganized, grading criteria was unclear and was received after next parts of sequential writing were due. Class assigns over 120+ pages of reading per week to loosely related material, then has a quiz on small unimportant details from the passages. No resources given to study for exams. DO NOT TAKE!

Quizzes were based on the 5+ readings. The quizzes did not give you any more than 30 seconds per question. If you have issues retaining information from ALL readings, or reading quickly this class will not be for you. The exams are hard, however, the papers saved my grade. I don't recommend this course. Professor is not approachable either.

Exams are pretty straight forward and align with the study guides she provides. Weekly in-class group assignments. Mandatory attendance. Goes on tangents and is adamant about participation during class. Tedious international project. Extra credit provided. TLDR; average difficulty, fair professor but really annoying format-wise.

This professor rambles a lot and her lectures are usually just asking students to read/watch things outside of class. She cares A LOT about participating even in big lecture halls. You really just have to teach yourself the information outside of the class. She tracks attendance and sometimes twice a class. Also won't believe you for tech issues.

Such a bad lecturer. The whole class is poorly organized. She's a nice lady, but she does not know how to use technology at all, which makes it literally impossible to navigate the course. Also, the iClicker is so annoying bc she literally stops it after 30 seconds and then gets upset when not enough people have answered it.

She rambles a lot in her lectures which made me lose focus even when I was actually trying to learn. If you want to do well on the exams focus on reading the textbook and doing the adaptive quizzes. While I wouldn't take her class again, she is very kind, responsive and helpful when I messaged her. Do the extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Records attendance based on chat and iclickers, up to 7 absences. The subject isn't hard, but you do need to study to do well on exams (reused parts from practice). 5 min assignment due Sundays and discussions. Expects posts to be college level, kinda strict but doable. Likes to ramble in lectures but interesting! Old fashioned and expects effort.

I'm not sure if Professor Brunnig thinks this is the only class I have, just based on the assigned readings and lectures. Basically feels like I'm doing her job and reviewing completely on my own. Exams are heavy on small details. Very unorganized, and half the time I feel lost. If you HAVE to take this class, good luck, you'll need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Brunnig is a very nice and caring and takes time outside of class to talk to you and host multiple office hours per week. Each class was structured lecture + group activity for last 20 minutes. She gives study guides (recommend doing) for the exam, along with practice questions. Recommend the class, especially if you are going into healthcare.

This class was definitely all over the place. I would not say it was necessarily difficult, but you will not succeed if you do not do the study guides. Her TA was extremely helpful, and not as difficult of a grader as she was. She goes on tangents, but overall a nice professor. There is extra credit that helps with your grade too.
take the other professor..

One of the most annoying classes ever; lectures are ramble sessions; group activities are a waste of time for no reason; grades assignments harshly; exams are not terrible, but may take a long time; 10 pts extra credit is very helpful; studying for exams is just doing the study guides the night before and memorizing them; sweet person, bad teacher

To call her a doctor is a disgrace to all doctors. She is so scattered and unprofessional. She treats students terribly and cannot believe them when they say they have a problem. If you can take this with anyone else, do it. If you cannot, dont take it.

If you take this professor, be prepared to be confused. The slide shows are all abbreviated terms that only she can understand, the lectures are frantic and unorganized, and the whole class just feels disorganized and all over the place. She talks a lot about the trump administration. Both her and the TA grade harshly so be ready for that.

Took class fully online, attendance was mandatory through iClicker. The iClicker questions were not graded by accuracy but just whether you participated or not. She does give options for extra credit, but the exams are ok. Lots of questions are taken from practice quizzes/adaptive quizzes.

Lectures are 50 minutes of incomprehensible  rambling at 9:35 am, complete with mandatory attendance. Class is harder than you'd expect. Everything about this class is unorganized and messy. I absolutely dreaded going to the mind numbing zooms.

Very disorganized and you never really know what to expected. Was kind of annoying that attendance was mandatory. An A is achievable if you study a lot of the content by yourself because you won't get much from class time. There are 4 main discussion posts and 4 main exams. Discussion posts were fairly easy and the TAs graded them.

A lot of work. She's a yapper. She grades harshly but her TA wasn't as much of a stickler. My essay responses on the exams were always unnecessarily picked apart. She is very unorganized, most people were confused about assignment procedures the whole semester. Id pick a different professor, not worth it.

If you can take another professor, do that. This class is incredibly disorganized and the material is not taught properly, she just rambles and goes on tangents. Class is mandatory, but it is a waste of time, just focus on the notes and study the material for yourself. There is a chance to win 10 extra credit points. She is incredibly political.
Great professor. She really is understanding and knowledgeable. The lectures are what's tested on mainly. The book isn't needed.

Be prepared to dedicate way more time to this course than you would think. She doesn't really emphasize what you need to know in the lecture; you really just need to complete the study guides to do well. The Canvas page is really disorganized, and she has trouble believing students when we tell her anything at all. Beware; she gets political.

Dr. Brunnig is a great professor overall. She makes lectures very interesting and you can tell she knows what she's talking about. The tests are pretty difficult, as they focus on small details, but they aren't impossible. As long as you listen in class and study, you will be fine. She offers extra credit. I didn't do any of it and still got an A-.

Overall, not great professor. She definitely over complicates this class for only being worth 2 credits. Very tough grader and gives very unclear expectations for the two projects. Exams are 50 Qs multiple choice and expect trick questions. Do the study guides days in advance and pay attention to lectures. EC is offered but is time consuming. 3/10

Lectures consisted of clicking through slides, rambling, and telling us to read articles outside of class time. Exams were not impossible if you fill out the study guides. Assignments are harshly graded and expectations aren't made clear. Extra credit is available and VERY helpful if you need to boost your grade. Too stressful for a 2 credit class.

Dr. Brunnig is so sweet and the lecture slides were basically the exam. If you just listen to what she says in class and take the time to fill out the study guides then you will be fine. She's a great professor and it is clear she loves nutrition and wants to just teach us more about it so we can make healthy choices.
Very stressful class.

Very kind lady but canvas is disorganized. Lectures were average. If you fill out her study guides for each chapter then you should do fine on the exams. Attendance is required which is annoying. She offers extra credit that really boosts your grade towards the end. I almost got a B+/A- but the extra credit saved me since its heavily weighted.

Professor is nice but seems a bit disorganized at times and she can be a bit of a harsh grader sometimes. Lectures are okay quality. Attendance is mandatory but you have some free skips. She also offers extra credit. She emphasizes the textbook but it isn't necessary to do well.

Dr. Brunnig was super sweet, and the lecture slides were basically the exam. Our final wasn't cumulative. She made us study guides (obviously you would have to fill them out, and those helped me do well on the exams. I paid attention to lecture about half the time, barely took notes, and still got an A, all just by starting on the study guides ASAP

Probably has the most disorganized canvas page ever. Forces everyone to do group projects every other day that don't really help with information retention. Study guides and test questions are worded very confusingly. Every time we take an exam she spends the first 20 minutes rambling on and its hard to concentrate. Too much work for 2 credits

None of the lecture material appeared on the exams. I read every chapter in the text and did the study guides she provided, and I still averaged a 65% in the exams. She made the exams so that there are two right answers per question. Prof made the class much harder than it had to be. Assignments aren't bad, however they are a little time-consuming.

She really likes breakout sessions which I didn't find very helpful. She takes attendance but gives you some leeway. Her exams were easy but textbook heavy. I suggest getting the textbook problem bank and going over the study guide after reading each chapter. I honestly don't feel like I learned a lot in this course because it didn't require me to.

Would recommend taking the other professor. Tests are hard, specific, and lengthy, and require very detailed studying of the textbook. You have to participate in the zoom chat and do assignments with other students on zoom which can be challenging. Some assignments were interesting, but the class was harder than it should have been.

Brunnings class is doable if you have no life. You have to attend lectures and comment to get credit but all the exams are strictly based on the book so you have to really read and study... dont wait until the last minute because it is again very specific. She offers extra credit max of 10 point, make sure you do it!!!!

Her exams are only based on details found in the textbook. These exams are extremely difficult because the answers and answer choices are vague and there are usually two answers that seem correct. She has said in lectures that she aims for the exam average to be in the C range and purposely designs her tests to be difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
-Difficult exams
-assignments are long but not too bad 
-Very inconsiderate when it comes to asking for help 
-Rambles way too much 
-The only way to pass is reading the textbook

I am currently taking nutrition through the life cycle, a 2-credit course, and this is probably the most annoying class I've ever had to take. Brunnig is kind and she wants to help, but the structure of the course is just not effective for true learning and absorption of the material.

Sarah Brunnig isn't a bad person by any means, but, she does not teach this class well at all. For rambles and includes her opinions in the majority of the lectures. Her assignments are not difficult and are weighted high; however, the tests are very difficult (mostly due to her lack of talking about actual material).

She wasn't the worst, but I recommend taking someone else if you want a clear understanding. She rambles a lot in class and her tests make no sense! She will often put two correct answers and it's not select all that apply. The only hard thing in class is her tests, but do the study guide and you will pass!

Exams are incredibly difficult, her study guides are essentially a stream of consciousness that make little sense, talks in circles in lecture, does not know the science behind nutrition enough to be teaching this course, would choose a whole other elective over taking her as a professor ever again.

Mrs. Brunnig is super sweet, but she is terrible at lecturing. She is unable to be clear on what is on her tests and you have to be very dependent on the book in order to get a good grade. Attendance is mandatory and classwork is not as bad, tests are brutal though. She has a really bad way of wording things and it is always super confusing.

Ms. Brunnig is not a bad professor at all, she is a really good person as well! My critiques of the class are about the test and the "study guide." She works very hard on the study guides, but they do not explain what to study. The tests do not accurately reflect what is emphasized in class and are worded in a confusing manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is a GREAT teacher. She offers extra credit, keeps her lectures engaging and interesting, and tells you exactly what you need to know from the text by uploading her study guides for each chapter. Only a few 300 word discussion posts and two 100 word replies for each one.Assignments are easy and she lets you be creative with the discussion topic

Exams are slightly difficult since the questions are made by her. Her exam question is very specific, sometimes they aren't clear at all. Class is mandatory, it is also graded. She offers extra credit points as well. Overall, not a bad class but you need to put the work in to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are all over the place and wont help you on exams. You have to read the textbook to get a decent grade. Very specific exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Brunnig is very nice and understanding. Her class is graded by a few assignments and it is test heavy. Make sure to read the chapters from the textbook and take notes to do well on the exams. Her exam questions are very specific. She offered extra credit throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is the most non-self aware, annoying person I've ever had as a prof. "oh yeah memorize that too" "oh read that too" "you're gonna want to know that" as she rushes through a lecture. Unorganized slides. Tries to be positive but everybody hates her. Needs to learn to be more concise and respectful of students' time.

Exams arent easy, although she does cater to the students and she reflects later exams on how well students did on previous exams. The Diet assignments are what saved me. Put your work into those and you should be good. She also offers extra credit and definitely do those.

Brunnig is overall pretty nice. I barely went to class and still passed with an A-, her lectures aren't the best because there isn't enough time to cover all of the info. You NEED to read the textbook for any chance to pass the class. Long chapters but not too bad, taking notes helps signfiicantly. Do any available extra credit, it helps a lot.

Ms. Brunnig was my instructor for HUN2201 during the Spring 2021 semester. Ms. Brunnig is very caring and extremely passionate about nutrition. The course is extremely textbook heavy as Ms. Brunnig encouraged my classmates and I to read the text before and after each class. The course itself is challenging but very enjoyable.

Professor Brunnig was sweet and cared about her students. She offered office hours in the beginning of the semester to allow us to meet with her and get to know her beyond the classroom which was refreshing with the online platform. Her class grades on few assignments but they are relatively easy and interesting at times.

She definitely cares about what she teaches is very nice but unfortunately her lectures are not great. Would recommend reading the textbook to understand the material since test questions are annoyingly specific. However she does give tons of extra credit and the other assignments are easy and worth a lot so they boost your grade. Very doable class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Brunnig was honestly the best prof i've had since being at UF. She was so sweet and caring and really tried to make even the hard concepts interesting. The textbook is your best friend as there isn't enough time in class to go into heavy detail. The tests are pretty tough, but the other assignments and extra credits help level that out.

The tests were pretty hard because need to know specific facts. The other assignments are worth a bunch too though so it balances out. The assignments were not that hard. Multiple easy extra credit. Only the tests stressed me out.

Her tests are tough, but the other assignments (discussion, diet project, etc.) are easy and help your grade a lot. She gives multiple opportunities for extra credit. Sometimes she skips over stuff in lecture due to time, so read the textbook, do the study guide, and/or watch youtube videos (professor makkieh's playlist) for studying.

Take this class! Dr. Bwenge is maybe the most caring professor that I've had at UF. His style is "untraditional," but in a good way. He mixes readings and films for an interactive conversation rather than a lecture. I was always excited to come to class and I surprised myself with how much I learned as the class was essentially a completion grade

He is very unorganized. He speaks very quickly and rambles often. Additionally, the work that he tends to give seems like busy work rather than valuable knowledge. This class is not very flexible and needs and online option as well. Everything he gives out is printed and in person which is difficult for when unexpected emergencies come across.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor is really passionate about the class and loves to hear what students have to say about the different topics that are explored. There are only 3 short papers you have to write, 4 reading quizzes (the readings are short), and a group project at the end. He gives very clear instructions for all assignments and answers all questions.

reviews.comment: Please take this class! There is little work, mainly four reading quizzes, a presentation, and three short papers. He is very passionate about what he teaches, and structures the class well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: A really nice, and caring professor. Class is really easy to pass. Mostly really short writing assignments. No tests, midterm, or final. Only reading quizzes that mostly have to do with common sense.

One of the best/most interesting professors I have had at UF. Bwenge is amazing. He has a true passion for the subject, and he cares about his students. Assignments are easy, and the projects help you learn a lot about Africa. Take this class for a requirement or just for fun.

Please please take him!!! I loved how he structured his class. I learned so much and it was not stressful at all. He is so sweet and is so passionate about what he teaches. BEST HUMANITIES CLASS EVERRR!!!
great guy, super nice, super funny, actually learn in the class
nicest guy ever. easy and interesting class. very little work involved. totally recommended.

the best humanities class ever. He is the most entertaining and lively teacher. He has a strong accent, but hes SO flexible. NO exams. easy quizzes on like 3 pages every now n then. gives out A's like no tomorrow. 2 papers and 1 group project. LOTS of movies. BUY THE BOOK, you need it for the quizzes.

Bwenege is a very nice teacher! Don't let people fool you. The class is very EASY! I suggst pruchasing the books, thats where the quizzes come from. He tells you what is on the the quiz. Watch movies and give reflections, very easy and simple class. And hes very nice!
No Comments
Class was engaging but I would not take it again. I found the professor to be a little overbearing and would frequently interrupt students.
Ethical Leadership is a very easy class and fun class! The professor cares about students and does not grade harshly at all. This is one of the only classes I actually enjoyed attending!
Best professor I've ever had. Actually learn things that will help you in your career and in life in general. Very inspirational.

Loved Professor Ray! I had a back injury midway through the semester, and he accommodated me instantly! 9 Assignments, 2 exams, and 3 papers for the ENTIRE class! He gives you plenty of time to complete all the assignments, just make sure not to procrastinate! Work gets graded by PAs, you'll be making your resume, LinkedIn, and autobiography.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ray is one of the most inspirational and easygoing professors I've had at UF. He truly cares about his students and looks to make an impact on them in the long run. Class is very straightforward and clear on what is expected, would definitely take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ray is the best! Most engaging lecturer I've had, and one of the only classes I've felt compelled to pay attention in and actually see myself referencing what I learned after the class ended. Definitely a TON of reading. One book was good, but the other was boring and unnecessary, as were most articles. A ton of work in a short period of time.

Brian Ray is one of the best professors I've ever had. He clearly loves what he does and is super accessible outside of class. The course was just one credit, but all assignments were clear, the grading was fair, and if you participate, you'll get an A. He's an inspiring lecturer and a great resource for students.

Dr. Ray is an amazing teacher. The quizzes in the class are kind of difficult and there's quite a bit of reading; however, you can use your table's notes and they're only 20% of the grade. He promises everyone an A or an A- in the class, and the difference really just depends on your quizzes. Overall, really good class. I HIGHLY recommend it.

Professor Ray is amazing - one of the kindest and most helpful I've had. His class can be challenging but he provides great feedback and extra credit to ensure you succeed. Definitely use resources like unstuck ai alongside the readings to ace this course.

It is a lot of work, but it is genuinely worthwhile. He is an easy grader who allows for creativity in assignments. Set up your interviews in advance! Some people never got back to me. Exams are easy if you read all the content. Lectures are good for reviewing before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Read the grading rubric and complete all the written assignments. There isn't really any test prep, but if you read the book, listen to all the lectures, and use the Quizlet exam reviews, you will do fine. Do the extra credit for the occupational interviews. It is worth 30 extra points and can bump up your grade a letter.

Dr. Ray is honestly awesome. Don't listen to the people who said it's hard. I genuinely enjoyed this class a lot. Yeah, the writing assignments are long but they are fun! The exams are honestly really easy. Extra credit is good too. This is a great course. I highly recommend it! Dr. Ray is so caring and is genuinely passionate about this course.
Great class! Learned a lot about leadership. Make sure to do the discussions at the right time and study for the exams. There are not a lot of assignments, so make the most out of each one!

Dr. Ray is a fantastic and caring professor. His classes contain a lot of information, but it's not hard material to learn. Highly recommend doing the extra credit assignments to pad your grade in case you don't do well on the exams, like myself! Assignments aren't hard; they're just time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You can tell Dr. Ray deeply cares about his students. The class is not extremely difficult, but it is going to make you think. There is a lot of writing. Do yourself a favor and stay on top of it. I did not purchase the textbook but still managed B's on both the exams. You get out of this class what you put into it. Make it worthwhile for yourself!

Brian Ray is one of the kindest professors at UF that I have ever met. His lectures and course gives extremely valuable information that helps start a successful leadership journey. 

This course is based on 2 papers, 3 discussions and 2 exams. The exams are tough, but he provides a lot of extra credit (30 points).
Fluff on fluff on fluff. Dr. Ray just rambles about things that are not relevant to being successful in the workforce. Extremely boring lecturer.
Not the best at explaining topics. Was left confused most of the time. Seems to care about memorizing definitions rather than learning.

Dr. Ray is very passionate about what he teaches. His class was very engaging and he's not a tough grader. As long as you read beforehand, the CRAs shouldn't be difficult. I highly recommend completing assignments a couple days beforehand; they're not hard but can be a little time consuming.

reviews.comment: There is 2 writing assignments you have to do but they aren't all that hard. Easy grader

reviews.comment: Legitimately my favorite class and professor I've had at UF so far. I strongly encourage all business majors to take this class, you'll learn things that will last your entire career. Dr. Ray is the epitome of a caring professor, and he strongly believes in what this class teaches. He makes every class enjoyable.
Very caring Professor and a helpful class.

He's truly one of the most caring professors I have had yet. Dr. Ray is understanding that life happens and he tends to be very understanding. His lectures are also really interesting and as long as you keep up with the readings then you will easily receive an A.

Dr. Ray was one of my favorite professors at UF. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He is very fair and grades papers amazingly fast! I enjoyed his personal feedback notes he provided on every assignment submitted. I really appreciate his efforts this semester!

This class is almost identical to GEB3017. He is a very lenient grader and gives personalized feedback to every student. The interview paper is incredibly easy if you start early. Don't get scared by the example papers. The class was actually very helpful for trying to figure out a career path if you don't have that figured out yet like me :)

The lectures are a little boring, but necessary to watch for the exam. 2 long papers are required, but I hate writing papers and they weren't bad at all. I didn't read the books, just read summaries and that was enough. The class was easy overall and easy to manage.

Professor Ray is awesome! This class is an easy A as long as you don't fall behind. There are a lot of reading and writing assignments but he's not a tough grader. Two exams that are easy if you just watch his lectures and read all the assigned articles. I personally didn't read the textbook but I think this depends on how you learn best.
Great guy

fluff on more fluff. nothing concrete learned in this class. most of it is common sense and does not even apply in the modern work force. waste of my tuition and time. UF cheats its students by requiring classes such as this one.

reviews.comment: Dr. Ray is a great professor. If you meet the requirements for the discussions and papers you're guaranteed full credit. The exams are fairly easy. Review quizlet and you'll be fine.

Dr. Ray is a very nice, respected, and intelligent man. He tries to do everything in the best interest of his students and is very accomodating and accessible outside of class. Do NOT take this class if you have the slightest understanding of career building, the workforce, or how to brand yourself. I felt it was a very tedious, bore of a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Ray is a great professor. He really wants his students to improve their professional development and provides assignments that encourage students to think about their career goals. Few assignments, but lengthy. Heavy writing assignments but worthwhile. I would definitely take the course again and encourage all students to take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: literally the most understanding professor I've ever worked with. I asked to have an exam window moved because my job scheduled me outside of my availability and they wouldn't work with me. he changed my window without any question. he also allowed me to make up 2/5 of a major paper past the due date. amazing guy, pleasure to work with.
