Great professor. He challenges you to be introspective and the readings he assigns will stay with you long after the course. You can't breeze through the class, but workload is balanced and the grade is spread between papers, discussions, and exams. For exams, he loves big ideas and lists. Focus on those when studying, and read everything.

Do not listen to any of the reviews. This class is hard, be prepared to write until you're ready to cry. I have had English Composition classes that are less writing-intensive than this class. Exam covers way too much material, not only are you responsible for lectures and the textbook chapters but he assigns about 15 articles for you to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Ray is hands down one of the best professors I have taken at UF. He truly cares about his students, and makes an effort to get to know each one individually. His lectures are inspirational and have true real-world applications. The class itself was very easy; he offers extra credit opportunities and is not a tough grader. Take his class!!!

Great class with real world practicality. There is a lot of reading, but I found the textbook unnecessary, the test come from his lectures. Exams could be a little tricky though because they covered a lot of info.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would recommend Dr. Ray and GEB3017 to anyone. I thoroughly enjoyed this class and the assignments were easy to pace out and complete. He explains the books very well and leaves you with a great understanding of what a leader should be. If you can, TAKE THIS CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ray is one of the best professors I've ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Instead of textbooks, you'll read about 5 books that are actually really great reads. Don't procrastinate on finding your leaders to interview as there's an opportunity to earn extra credit if you do more than the required amount.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ray does a great job preparing you for the exams and makes the class a fairly easy A. There are a couple big writing/research projects but the grading and extra credit make it worth the effort. There is a good amount of reading throughout the course but the exams are not overly difficult. Do the extra credit and reading and you should get an A.

Five assignments and two exams. He is a very generous grader on the assignments. Some say the tests were easy, but I never received higher than a B. Be sure to read the articles because they are definitely on the exam. I never read the book, so maybe that is why I didn't do well on the exams. Overall, he is a good professor that cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Ray made going to class fun and enjoyable. His passion for the topic showed through in the lectures and was contagious throughout the classroom. Favorite teacher at UF so far.

One of the only professors I have ever had that truly cares about your success. Email him, talk to him in person, he's there to help you succeed. Absolutely a positive force in this universe. Class was organized, easy, yet intellectually stimulating. I learned to be a better person and student here.

Dr. Ray is amazing. He genuinely cares about students. You don't need the book if you watch the lectures because he goes over everything you need to know. Assignments are not difficult, and there 2 exams which are easy if you watched the lectures/read the assigned articles. Dr. Ray will take the time to speak to you about your career & advise you!

This is my second course with Dr. Ray and he is phenomenal! I could not recommend him more. If you are looking to get motivated to learn new things and grow as an individual, Dr. Ray can help you! Watch all his lectures and take notes! Never opened the assigned books and got no lower than 90% on tests solely studying the notes from the lectures.

Taking his class was very beneficial to me as well as eye-opening, I was able to learn how to solve real-life practical issues in business. This class is actually something that can be applied in the real world and it teaches you how to navigate tough situations in the industry. His lectures were always inspiring, keep an eye out for his quotes.

there are very few lengthy assignments that you receive great feedback on from your "career coach", meet the requirements and you should get an A on them. Two books were required but I wouldn't say they were necessary as you can look up info on them. Overall, great professor and helpful class!

Dr. Ray is a great professor. This class should be an easy A, as long as you do all of the assignments (there were only five assignments, some lengthy, plus two tests). Beyond the grade this is the course that I have gotten the most out of in my entire time at UF. The reading material is very inspirational and helpful.

I have a love-hate relationship with GEB3035. Dr. Ray is an amazing professor and spent the time speaking with me on the phone about my career, which I really appreciate. The exams are, for some reason, extremely difficult for me. For most assignments, he doesn't provide a rubric so that's kind of annoying. Overall, the course was useful though.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I loved taking this class! When I saw it is an easy A, I mean it. I did like 1/5 of the readings. He gave one extra credit assignment but honestly there wasn't a criteria for it. You literally just had to do the assignment and answer the questions he wants you to include in it. 4 easy quizzes. Downloaded pdfs for the longer readings to use on quiz.

Lots of real world benefit in taking this class, so when you finish you'll have an updated resume, linkedin page, etc. Exams are not difficult but since there's only two and since they cover a lot of content make sure to do all of the assignments. Score well on the assignments and you'll be fine.

I feel like this class tries too hard to earn its 3000-level. There are only two exams, which is fine except that you never really get to learn how he and Guffin test. Lectures are crazy long, but most of the exam questions come from the books and articles. The papers probably saved my grade; they make up most of the points in this class.

Dr. Ray was one of the best teachers in the business school. His class went threw different ethical dilemmas you might face in the work force and how to go about them. He is very inspirational and impactful when it comes to his teaching. A class that I would recommend and it's not that hard to get an A in either.

Dr. Ray is a really great professor. He is inspirational and very passionate about what he teaches. He is a great professor and very understanding. This course was interesting but there are 5 required textbooks and lectures are quite long. Honestly, I bought the books but never read them because Dr. Ray's lectures cover the material just fine.
Not an easy elective. There is weekly assignments. Long lectures. Need the book. Not too bad, but was more work than intended. Very tough grader.
Nice guy, but very unclear on assignment and exam expectations.

Oh my goodness the lectures are entirely TOO long. i just read the book and took notes and got a 90 on the first (hardest) exam. For the outside book i watched the lecture.. 3 lectures that are at least 30+ minutes long 2 times a week. The content is kinda interesting but the expectation of watching these long lectures kill the experience for me...

Took this class thinking it would be a relatively easy elective, seen as it is taught by two guidance counselors.  Awful tests and lots of lengthy assignments. They try and justify the difficulty of the class to other 3000 level business classes, but there is just too little substance for how hard and specific the tests are.  Really time consuming

Projects are pretty easy but time consuming. there are 4, autobiography, career analysis report, doing a resume &cover letter, and interviewing 5 people from careers your interested in. Two exams that are easy as long as you watch lectures. If you don't get an A it cause you didn't try.

This is a good class for someone who has never had a job before and still lives at home...However, for the rest of us who have been working since High School, the "useful" info is stuff we've already heard before. Tests are mere memoriziation of random facts, and not really about concepts discussed. If I didn't have to take this class, I wouldn't.

Great class for anyone not sure of what they want to do after graduation, recommend to younger students, fun, simple assignments, tests based off lectures (slides available online) and text. The text is entertaining and informative, make sure you read all of it. Ray is an inspirational guy and grade is dependent on TA/career coach

GEB3035 is a very helpful class for those who have NO CLUE about internships, jobs, resumes, inverviews, etc.  It helped me SO much with what to do.  If you just read the book, the class is simple and helpful.  Very low maintenance, just read right before the exam.  Dr. Ray is a great professor and is always willing to help. Take it junior year!!!

GEB 3035 is an absolutely amazing class - I owe a great deal of my success in finding an internship with a Fortune 500 company to this class!! The course helped with building my career successfully, creating a great resume, and properly communicating your ideas during interviews.  TAKE THIS CLASS - you will be very happy that you did!

This is a an extremely useful class because it assists you with resume writing, interview topics, and networking tips. The professor and TA's are great with meeting with you one on one to provide specific feedback or concerns that you may have.

This has been the most practical and valuable class I have taken in my college career. Every college freshman should be required to take this course, as I believe it would help a lot of students figure out what direction they want their career to take. The class has a lot of information that can be applied to the the "real world".
I took this course in 2005 and found it to be very useful. During the progression of my career, I have applied many of the tools learned during this course.

The class is not an easy A, but you will learn applicable and useful tools for your job search. Helped me getting an internship. Despite the online lectures, the class is personalized and assignments receive individualized feedback. Dr. Ray and the TA's really care about helping. Take if you need some help picking your career and finding a job.

Dr. Ray is passionate about the success of his students and will reach out to anyone to provide career management advice. As dean of the school of business, he makes it a goal to improve the professional development skill sets for his students. You have to study for his tests, but everything you learn for them can be applied to the real world.
Great class and great teacher! It is extremely useful but does require effort. The assignments really help prepare you for the job search and I would recommend this class to anyone.

The class requires a lot of reading however the assignments are quite useful. You learn a lot of skills that will help you in the real world but you have to put forth the effort to see the results. By no means an easy A but it is a class that is worth taking.

I registered for this class thinking it would be an easy elective and an easy A. I got an A alright, but easy it was NOT. Required assignments were time intensive, exams were not too bad. Be ready to memorize the text book. I was determined to get something out of the class because of all the work I had put into it, and I did.

HORRIBLE. Brian Ray reads directly from slides with no substantial commentary. Tests are on random facts. Took it at the recommendation of a counselor & realized later that they promote the class to everyone. Brian Ray created this class to weasel his way into being a professor. This class is part of the reason UF can't be a top school.

The only positive reviews on this page are probably Ray himself. The class is not only useless, but requires a surprisingly high level of rote memorization. Avoid if you're looking for a course to further your education. Take this if you enjoy memorizing useless facts and spitting them out on exams.

I have no clue why this class is a junior year class in the online business program, where most students are already mid-career and in their 30s.  The final assignment is to write a resume!!  Tests are on generally useless material such as "who authored this theory?"  no opportunity for appeals, no exam review, terrible class as a whole

This class is very difficult.  The tests do not test your understanding of the material but rather test minor details (e.g. "which of these words were not included on the list of 10 career moves").  The assignments are generally helpful but are long and don't make up for poor grades on the test.  A in ECP and a B in this, somethings wrong!

Terrible class, you basically have to memorize the textbook, and thats not just the concepts,  but details.  Considering each chapter has about 60 names, it sucks.  My friends and I struggled through the class to earn Bs.  I also had a very tough TA, would grade my paper hard.
It was a good subject... I guess, the tests were utterly ridiculous though, it is not as easy as the name may imply.

A single poster wrote: "Requires a lot of effort into the material."  "Do not take this class if you expect it to be a breeze." "Must read textbook in order to pass his test." I'm sure that was a nightmare for a slacker like you.  Spend less time whining and more time studying and you might realize what a great teacher Dr. Ray is (doubt it though)

This class is utterly useless and a waste of time.  Requires a lot of effort into the material. His lectures are boring and brags about himself a lot.  Do not take this class if you expect it to be a breeze.  Again totally useless course and mostly a memorization course.  Must read textbook in order to pass his test.

Lectures are very boring, but the class is easy.. I don't know what these people are talking about.. I did all of the assignments the day they were due, pretty much made all of them up, and got 100% on all of them! Class is very easy just very boring.. must read the book and sorta watch lectures..

This class was completely boring and completely useless. A lot of psycho babble in a text written by 4 academics from FSU, then a lot of memorization on stuff like the CASAVE cycle that is completely unimportant in the real world. My only advice is memorize the book. Half of the tests come directly out of the book.
i like that course. I thought it was helpful.

this class is irritating.  The assignments are really easy but sliightly pointless.  Just make sure you use the right format on webct.  The lectures are never the whole 2 hourse.  If they are then they're not on the test. Dr. Ray talks about himself ALOT but thats not on the test so just tune it out.  Tests ask very specfic questions.

What are these people talking about? This class is an easy A. I never watched one lecture. Just read the entire book (boring but easy) and you will get atleast a B on the test. Autobiography, interviews,  and Resumes are explained well. Not a hard class just put in some effort.

This class is straight up memorization. He talks about himself the whole time. His resume reads like a book...just wait you will see it. Don't take this class if you have trouble reading the textbook, he will ask you names from the examples on the test.

this class was a waste of time! I thought it would be helpful but it was merely time consuming and the lectures were pointless. Tests mainly on memorization and useless facts, even watching lectures and reading I managed to only pull a B. Felt more like a reason for Dr. Ray to sit infront of the camera and brag about himself.

I don't think this class should be grouped into business as if it's specific to this major. It probably doesn't get many of the students who probably could use it for this reason. If you don't have interview skills, don't know how to write a resume, or aren't sure of your career - take it. Don't expect it to be easy, though. Very time consuming.

Academic Advisor said it would be an easy A... busted my behind for a B.  Very time consuming, boring assignments.  The layout he teaches for the resume and cover letter for the final project was WRONG.  CRC tore mine apart after... tedious, useless dribble. have fun

I was really looking forward to this class, unfortunately it was a total waste of time. There was NOTHING practical until the third unit. Textbook is boring as hell, nothing but straight memorization for the tests. Dr. Ray is a little stuck on himself (you'll learn ALL about his accomplishments). I was fortunate to get a decent TA.

The assignments r time consuming 1 u r supposed to do like 10 occupational interviews thats like 30 pages of work. Its easy but it takes a long time. The book is SO boring.The test are super easy but u have to read the book which is torcher, the lectures just review the book but 1 test i didnt read n i got a 72. thers 1 online exam thats an easy A
Extremely easy, and fairly useful class. Main qualms: Classes filmed WAY in advance, assignment 2 is tedious, tests require a lot of memorization.

Dr. Ray's career development class, while easy, is practically valueless given its poor design. To echo a previous review, Dr. Ray is not a teacher -and it shows. The tests quiz you on unrelated minutiae. It seems like the class is an excuse to pad Ray's resume, as most of the lectures were filmed months ago and disconnect noticeably. Unfortunate..

Dr. Ray has NO teaching experience and it shows! He talks all the time about being a "good fit" with your career,maybe he should rethink HIS career. I have a high A and I still think this class is a joke. Lectures taped over a year ago, MANY errors in spelling and inconsistencies with lectures/online material, busy work. EASY but a waste of time.

Dr. Ray has zero teaching experience, and therefore the class is not presented or taught very well.  The tests are ABSOLUTELY AND COMPLETELY useless and a pain.  The first two tests cover over 250 pages of useless memorization.  The assignments are a pain, and really do not help.  Study book and defineteyl get A or B. Class was a pain, not expected

Get ready for a good grade and an easy class! You should watch lectures, although you are not tested on all of them! Reading the book, watching lectures, and doing a few EXTREMELY easy assignments will result in an A! This semester (fall) 77.4% of students ended up with an A or a B.
learned a lot of good stuff but as far as the papers and tests are concerned, it was a waste of time.
Some of the lectures were extremely long when it could have been a whole lot shorter. A little boring but should be an easy class.
No Comments

Don't take this course if you plan on not watching lecture and instead purchasing smokin' notes...there are no smokin' notes! I was lazy with the class, and thus I will probably not get an A, but if you watch lecture you should easily obtain an A.  There are 3 assignments, not too bad though.

Professor Byrne is an overall a nice lady. For IUF1000 you deal with your TA for discussions and they grade your papers, so make sure to develop a connection with him/her. It seemed that Byrne did have harder DBPs than other professors, but they still weren't that bad. If you buy the smokin notes you will pass the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Kathy is a great teacher! Easy grader, although the class is basically passable by anyone. She makes the class fun.

I had Prof Byrne for my Good Life section, which means she didn't really teach, but instead reviewed the online concepts we had already seen. IUF is an essay class but there are a lot of papers and short writings, so I was glad she was my grader. She grades fairly nicely and often gives good feedback. Overall a nice person to be around.

I took her for TPP2100. At first glance the semester seemed like it might be horrible. However, she taught us to get out of our shells, especially for those who had no prior acting experience. The class we had became one of the most close group of friends I've seen in a classroom setting. It was truly an honor. Take this class. You never know. :)

I took the online section of this class.  It was the most time consuming class that I had the whole semester.  While the assignments were easy and I got an A in the class, each assignment is only worth 10 points out of about 400 points possible.  You end up doing a ton of busy work.  If you want an easy A, go for it, but be prepared for busy work.

Dr. Byrne is nuts! But the class is ridiculously easy. In class is much easier than online though. Like everyone else said, test reviews almost guarantee an A without reading the book. Only downside is they take attendance so you have to go to class even though you don't have to show up mentally. The plays were also actually pretty good.

I took this class online and no joke spent probably ten minutes a week on work. It was so easy and the assignments are such a joke. There are no tests just weekly quizzes and discussion board posts. The final is just a group project. I spent no time on this class and ended up with close to a 100.

easy easy class. really boring and strange but almost no work. u do have to go see 3 plays though. test review with all the answers right b4 the test so go to that. the teacher is not the best but just bring something to do during lecture since they take attendence. ta's not hard graders. group project at the end. good way to get a diversity credit

She's really passionate about theater but she doesn't know how to communicate ideas to her students. She mumbles stuff and goes off on tangents that has nothing to do with the class and she thinks we are laughing with her when we are laughing at her lol. Just be there for the review days and you'll do well in the class. Try to get a good TA!

This is such and easy class, dont even buy the book. Its an extremely easy A. The problem is that I really like theatre, but there is not passion in this class. Take acting for nonmajors if you like drama and actually want to learn about it-its not a hard alternative. I didnt learn anything from the actual teacher, but the ta's showed passion. :)

Very easy class. Grade is based on tests, an easy group project, ridiculously easy online quizzes, and attendance. Do yourself a favor and don't take any notes during the lectures. She has the lecturing skills of a second grader and gives you the answers to the tests the class before.
one of the most scatter brained and unorganized teachers i have ever had. get a good ta and its an easy a.

She is strange and can be a little scatter-brained sometimes. But, don't let that discourage you from taking the class! It is super easy. Attendance is supposedly mandatory, but if you get a good TA then the only lectures you need to go to are the ones before each exam. She goes over the questions and basically gives you the answers!
Horrible teacher, she is all over the place. Luckily I had a great TA.
No Comments

She is a little quirky but I loved her class. It was interesting and funny. What she goes over in the lectures is on the tests so attend them. If you can't, make sure to attend the review sessions because those are hands down the most important days (next to the tests themselves). Have fun with her and get to know her. You'll love the class too.

She is a moron. Lectures her opinions and experiences, rather than what will be on the exam. Attending her lectures are a waste of time, just skim through the book and attend discussions and performances and you will get an A easily.

Unclear on assignments, refused to answer some reasonable questions unrealistic expectations, made 25% of the midterm on a question the class was confused about and told us she didn't have time to go teach it to us easily upset & often perceived as rude not helpful with any solutions when I reached out for help Worst scholastic experience to date
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: One of the worst teachers I've had at UF, and it is not because the class material is challenging.  Her attitude is the worst, she thinks that because she has a PhD in neurology she is better than everybody else.  Directions were never clear until papers were graded.  Also, she bases particpation grades pretty much on whether or not she likes you.

Believe me when I say this woman is insane. I am certain she has anger management issues because she screams at people for no good reason. NEVER have anything out unless its related to her class because if she sees even a planner she will embarrass you. Do the readings and take detailed notes because she asks for very specific answers on quizzes.

This class was HORRIBLE!! She is very unclear about what she expects from the assignments until after they're graded. Her grading is very inconsistent among different students. She never gives clear answers to questions either. Good luck in this class! I don't know how, but I somehow managed an A, so it is possible.
His helpfulness in office hours helped me pass. Personally I think Fred is a really cool guy.

Summary: Take the class. And Go to his office hours, people.   The Backstory: I've always sucked at math. But The Byrdman was really helpful.  I was intimidated by his beard at first, but he's actually super nice. Knows a ton about math and worked hard to help me understand. I feel totally less mediocore now.

I loved this class a lot. He was very helpful and understanding. Just study your notes and complete the H.W. assignments and you'll be good. He was the best math professor that I experienced at UF. I finished off with an A.
Mr. Byrd was very helpful. It's clear that he likes what he's teaching and wants you to do good. I took Trig and Precalc separate and recommend it. I would take his class again.

I was pretty nervous about Calc 2 coming into this class since I was never really great at math, but Professor Byrd made it easier with his discussions and notes. I also used study edge and that helped a lot!

Don't take his classes ladies! It was evident that some students received preferential treatment, while others were often dismissed or criticized harshly. It's crucial for educators to foster respect and professionalism in their interactions with students. I observed him harass a student employee. UF did the right thing in firing him. Toxic!

He is a horrible professor, one of the worst at UF. He constantly makes really big assignments all due on the same day and then more big assignments due right after that without any kind of break. He can also be really mean and patronizing, especially if you are trying to advance yourself in the field. If you do not have to take him, then do not.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: He does't show any empathy towards his students when they bring up their concerns with him. He sees students as replaceable and just doesn't care about anyone. If someone is struggling, he honestly doesn't care. He knows a new student will just replace them. I strongly recommend avoiding taking a class with him and just avoid UF overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was the best class I have taken. Dr. Byrd is the best professor. He has so much experience which makes his lectures so much more interesting.  He's incredibly intelligent and hilarious. Definitely go to class! It's necessary to be able to pass, plus it's just great to listen to lectures. He's not bad to look at and crush on either.
Great class, and after this semester I am changing my major and entering graduate school to become a forensic scientist.  Certainly one of the best professors at UF!
Amazing class and professor. Would take again. Dr Byrd has lots of field experience and tons of interesting stories to share. Forensic photos of crime scenes not for faint of heart.
Great professor and a very interesting subject.  Take this class if you can...one of the best at UF!

I took both of Dr. Byrd's classes and they were by far the best classes I've ever taken at UF. Dr. Byrd is extremely helpful & honestly cares about his students. Class is easy and interesting. You don't really need the textbook. I highly recommend his classes!
Dr.  Byrd's forensic science class is one of the best classes at UF.  Take this class if you can...interesting and fun!
Byrd is by far the best professor I have had at UF. Incredibly interesting, clear, humorous and such an easy teacher. Obviously loves what he does and he is actually world-renowned. Take him!
Great professor.  Really has an interest in the subject matter and wants his students to do well.  One of the best classes at UF!
Great professor.  One of the best at UF!

Very interesting class. Easy A as long as you go to lecture. Dr. Byrd is extremely helpful and sweet, and definitely not bad to look at. ;) Highly recommended. He's the only prof I've ever had a slight crush on!
Great teacher, very interesting, incredibly intelligent, and funny. I have already switched my major because he made me want to become a crime scene investigator. Take this class!
Great forensic science class!  Probably the best professor at UF, and one of the most interesting courses I have ever taken!!!

Great professor.  He responds to e-mails quickly and teaches the course effectively.  He has to travel the world but still takes the time to care about his students.  I highly recommend this class because it is interesting and it is easy to obtain in A if you attend lectures.
He was okay.  Not that easy, and not always that interesting.

he's a great teacher and knows everything there is to know about forensic anthro.  But he gets very specific and you need to know the notes, which add up, backwards and forwards for exams.  it's not a piece of cake.

Prof. Byrd is an amazing teacher and has incredibly interesting stories. He actually taught Grissom everything he knows about entomology and even set up his office! Interesting class material - attendence necessary - but made even better by his personal anecdotes. Class is an easy A as long as you go.

Professor Byrd is one of the coolest people I've ever met. He's a great teacher, is very funny even when he's not really trying, and presents what might usually be boring material in an interesting way via his lectures. My only regret is that he only teaches two classes at UF! :(

I enrolled in his forensic anthropology class.  It was probably the best class I have ever had at UF.  I stongly suggest the course.  He is always help and he cares about his students.  Always responds to questions promptly...rare for a prof. at UF.
Dr. Byrd is awesome, really knows his stuff and has some cool stories to tell. Take the class if you can!

The coolest professor I've had. DEFINITELY knows what he's talking about and makes the class interesting with his anecdotes. Very helpful, always answers emails promptly. If you get the chance, take his class!

He is such a sweet guy. He answers your e-mails promptly and always asks if there's anything else he can do for you. The class was very entertaining and he has a lot of hilarious stories. You don't need to read the book at all, just go to his lectures. I highly recommend his classes. Plus, he's a looker! ;)

Really great class and a really great teacher.  We covered lots of cool stuff, and he really knows what he's talking about since he has done pretty much everything he teaches about. It's  pretty easy to get an A, so theres no reason not to take a class with him
Absolutely amazing professor.  Very qualified.  Very helpful, interesting, entertaining.  Always makes exam material clear.  Highly recommended.
Excellent!!!  I have enrolled in his general forensics courses and his forensic anthropology course.  One of the best professors at UF.  High suggest this class.

Amazing. Quite possibly the most qualified professor I've ever had. He's seen and done it all; his lectures are so cool and you have to ask about what he does outside of teaching, he's got some really crazy stories. Great sense of humor and he's definitely not bad to look at.
No Comments

Excellent class, and great teacher.  Probably the BEST teacher at UF.  He gives LOTS of information but makes it very clear what he wants to you know for the exam.  Forensic science is a hot topic, and he's also kinda hot.
No Comments

If you're looking for an easy and enjoyable honors course take this one.  He uses powerpoint a little too much, but on days where he's telling stories about his job, it's VERY fascinating and definitely worth taking the class.  He's done so many cool things in his life.  Just don't bring your friend to class on autoerotic death day like I did.  ^_^
Great teacher; made the class enjoyable and interesting.

I loved going to his class! He is such an awesome teacher! The subject itself is interesting... but he makes the lectures so much more interesting! I never really read the textbook... studied off of my notes from class.. and still pulled off an A! He's also very helpful and nice.
Dr. Byrd is simply amazing. Always willing to help, busy but you can email him. Funny, intelligent, easy. Talk to him, he's led an amazing life and is willing to help you do what you want.

Class is easy if you go to lectures - he'll tell you what's on the exam. He's got an awesome/morbid sense of humor, perfect for his field. Great for those interested in forensics/pathology/etc. Best not to eat lunch before the class though.

Great course for someone trying to decide if grad school and forensic science is the thing for them.  Excellent lectures, and probably the best class I have ever had during my 4 years at UF.  Highly suggest this class!
Excellent class.  Exams are easy if you attend lectures and take notes.  Skim the chapters for main topics and key words.
Pretty Easy class as long as you go and take notes. Skim through the chapters for key words on tests
I enjoyed taking the class.  You have the opportunity to see an autopsy if you arrange it with him.

Excellent professor.  THE best class I have taken at UF, and would take him for any other class he teaches.  He makes sure you understand the material before the exam, answers any questions you have on the exam material, and holds reviews.
Great introductory course for forensic science.  Easy "A" if you come to class and take notes.  He lets you know what will be on the exams.

VERY introductory course on forensics. if you like this stuff, this class is great to take just to learn about the topic and doesnt get that deep into anything. Easy A, dont even need to read the book in my opinion. puts notes online.3 hour lecture sucks cuz he can only make it to campus once a week
very interesting class, information wise. he makes sure to tell you things you need to know for the test but they can still be a little tricky.
No Comments

When going to/watching the lectures, thy to understand the main idea he is describing. He likes to include many specific details about everything he discusses but he does not require you to know them so don't feel overwhelmed.

If you have taken BCH 4024 then this will be extremely easy for you. If you have no prior knowledge of biochemistry then you are going to be utterly lost  but the textbook is written in very simple language so just read it and you'll be fine. He gives extra credit for coming to class. Study the practice questions and you will do well on the exams.

This class is easy compared to the other electives such as parasitology or immunology. You will pass if you study the practice exams, use garlandscience quizzes. This professor was aware of his accent and he wrote down important notes before class. He actually teaches! Hard to find now days. He is very nice to his students too.

Hard to understand at first. His tests are very detail oriented, so be prepared. The book saved me and his practice exams are an enormous help. It's a difficult class, but he gives extra credit homework and quizzes and drops your lowest regular exam. Use that to your advantage, not as a crutch.

His accent is pretty thick I spent half of one lesson trying to figure out what this mysterious 'veggie-co' was that he kept mentioning, only to finally figure out he was saying 'vesicle'. However, I didn't find his exams to be very hard. He was clear in class and in his powerpoints what he wanted you to focus on.

This class turned out to be way more difficult than I expected. Dr. Kang's dialect of what I assume resembles the English language to him is pretty much unintelligible. I feel like most professors are more concerned about the big picture when it comes to a class that covers a lot of material, however this guy wants you to know every little detail.

He's really bad at teaching the material. Read the book, memorize practice questions. Not only does he fail at explaining things, he makes exam questions very detailed and difficult. Don't underestimate this class...

One of the worst professors at UF. Should have been a simple science elective, turned out to be my worst class of the semester. The material itself isnt that bad, but the teacher thinks hes teaching at Harvard.The questions are so convoluted, you dont even understand what it is asking. Must teach yourself everything, forget understanding him speak.

Not a typical biology class, make sure you actually understand the concepts, rather than memorize. Dr. Kang is extremely helpful during office hours. Be prepared to work your butt off. Also, the latest version of the book is not necessary, the professor himself bases his questions off the second edition. Study the sample questions!

His accent isn't a big deal and he's actually kind of funny.  As others have said, his tests are based off the practice problems he gives,a few might be verbatim but most he gives a different twist to the question and it can be really tricky.  Reading the book is really helpful need to make sure you UNDERSTAND the CONCEPTS not just memorizing.

This reviews make Dr. Kang sound so bad! Yes, he has an accent but you can definitely understand his statements. DO THE SAMPLE PROBLEMS. About half of the exam are exactly these questions or these concepts. He may rewrite the question, but its NOT tricky, its to see if you know your stuff which you should.

This guy is definitely the worst professor I have had at UF. I've never seen such detailed and tricky questions in my life on a test. Going to class and practice questions don't seem to help, and keep in mind that this is from a guy who has kept a 4.0 GPA through college...

I thought this class would be just like any other Biology class where you put in the time to read the book, go to class, take notes, and do the practice tests and you would be fine. Wrong. I study so much for this class and still get low grades on the exams. Questions are extremely tricky. You should probably read the book twice to do OK on them.
This should've been an easy class, but his accent is very difficult to understand so you just feel yourself zoning out during lectures because you can't tell what he's saying. Tests are tricky.

Very difficult to understand professor. 40 percent of the test come from sample questions for tests but he changes them so much that you feel like you are being tricked. third exam is hard. Talks very very fast and it is hard to understand. do yourself a favor and just read the book a couple times.
He made an intimidating class way less scary and very passable. He's the best! Take him for sure, he is super funny and nice

I have Dr. Cano for CCJ3701 as well. He is so kind and funny. His lectures are interesting and he is knowledgable. He gives review days before exams and tells you exactly what to study. He also has extra credit days just for showing up to class. He tries to make his classes as accessible as possible and is very understanding.

Amazing class! He is really knowledgable about court cases, so he will tie that into what is being taught. Exams can be challenging, but if you study the material you will get an A. Exam reviews are extremely helpful. All of the essays I actually really enjoyed writing and they were short. Read the textbook as well since that is what the test is on

Dr. Cano is amazing. He is flexible, caring, helpful, and understanding. He has clear grading criteria, good lectures and offers lots of opportunities to do well. If you attend class, read, and put in effort you will do great. He is so nice and funny and really tries to make class interesting.

Dr. Cano is awesome! I took his courts and sentencing class, and I would highly recommend it to any pre-law student. As long as you read the textbook and make sure to stay on top of the case brief assignments, you should be good to go. Lots of extra credit and clear expectations for written assignments. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gives engaging lectures and demonstrations, assignments are interesting and not too much work. However, she gives no grades or quantitative feedback on assignments, which is absurd for a class specifically about receiving feedback and iterating.

Although Cantrell is a kind and engaging lecturer, the course lacked organization. Assignments were graded very late, making it hard to track progress, and grading felt harsh with little explanation for point deductions. She also NEVER answers emails, so concerns are almost always never seen. Overall, she made the course structure very stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: NEVER EVER grades ANYTHING!!! Made's students do strange things to get her message across. For example, when the class wasn't participating enough, she asked everyone to stand up, everyone did, then put their right hand out, then pat their head. Cantrell "~Oh good, so now you can hear me, and you are using your brains." Just super disorganized.....

Mixed feelings, she is very nice and caring, her lectures are entertaining and interesting. She also gives very personal feedback on all the assignments. However, the workload is a lot, if you are taking other classes with this one, there is constantly a lot to do and it takes a lot of time. Don't take it with other time consuming classes

She definitely grades harder in the beginning of the semester, but if you put in the effort than it is very doable to get an A. She is also just great to listen to. She does grade very late though, so its a while to get feedback. You'll be able to redo assignments you did bad on to boost your grade. You'll learn so many cool things from Cantrell.

Cantrell has a great personality and her lectures are entertaining though the class structure and grading are some of the worst I've experienced at UF. The final project assignments at the end of the semester take forever (with too high of expectations imo) and also grading in general is very harsh.

Cantrell is passionate and brings humor to class, but inconsistent expectations and sudden changes made it stressful. The lack of structure and feedback is frustrating; with one week left, there's only one grade in Canvas. Beginners should consider another course, as this one doesn't teach enough foundational skills. (Worst teacher I've ever had.)

Chelsea Cantrell is amazing, so kind, however, her course is difficult and unorganized. At the end of the semester I hadn't had a new grade in two months. For a class that you need feedback in, there was little to none. I didn't know if I would get an A or C at the end honestly. Very interesting material, make sure you like this type of class.

She is super nice and cares about students. She is very funny and very talented definitely recommend BUT she and TA take forever to grade things that's my only complaint!!! other than that the class wasn't too difficult i took DIG2121.

she does not put in grades until the last week. she takes points off without reason. guidelines are vague. rubrics are missing, assignments unpublished, with no accountability taken. feedback is minimal and schedules fall apart immediately. email 3+ times and talk in person before getting an answer. my 3rd class with her and its always the same.

I really REALLY wanted to like Ms. Cantrell. She's a pretty good lecturer. However, her class has been a nightmare for me because she lacks total responsibility for everything grade-related in her class. She consistently doesn't upload assignments and rubrics and blames it on Canvas. It is past the halfway point in the semester and IDK my grade.

She seems like a good person so I feel bad to be this annoyed with her classes. She doesn't grade most assignments until the course is over. The assignments are often incorrect on Canvas and the instructions make you feel like you're solving a riddle to get full credit. You must go above and beyond to get full credit, and how is never specified.

If there was a worst class to take at UF this would be up there. So disorganized, never know what is assigned, her homework is long and tedious, and she grades things at the last minute. Oh and, if you email her, expect it to be never answered or answered by the time you graduate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Cantrell is a good lecturer and always entertains our class. However, she was extremely bad with grading assignments and providing feedback. Our class only had around 3 assignments (out of 8-ish) graded by the time the semester ended, and then she batch-graded the rest in one day, and none of them had any feedback. Harsh grader IMO.

Pt2
Assignment descriptions are unclear, she will put a standard for B in the description, and will have the rubric to have something extra for an A. So if you have done multiple assignments doing what it was described, then congrats you get a B the whole time (even worse, you won't know if you did it wrong bc she has not graded anything until then

Pt1:
She is a nice person, lecture have good flow, the quizzes were easy. But she is too busy to respond emails and grade the assignments, so any question you should ask the TA that is very attentive. She had only graded 4 assignments when final had come and finished grading them until the final day. Only the final had detailed feedback.

She's knowledgeable and gives helpful feedback.. eventually. Has multiple aids so your work can be graded by any. Grading is harsh it would've been nice to get grades sooner. In class students seem to be favored. Check info for the final well in advance its a ton of work in a short amount of time. Check Discord a lot or you'll miss important info.

Ms. Cantrell is one of the nicest, funniest professors you'll ever have at UF. But, she NEVER grades anything, her lectures aren't valuable, her assignment instructions are never clear, and the course is just a big mess. She also never provides any feedback for the projects. You'll never know if you're doing the assignments well until its too late.

I've had her for almsot 3 years now.  Her lectures are hilarious and very relatable. She understands how it is and has real-world experience and shares everything with us not so much as a professor but as a real person who understands you. If you need anything ask. I really appreciate the experiences and how clear expectation and instruction is.

Assignments & due dates were out of order, it was near impossible to communicate with the TA in a timely manner, grading made no sense, rubrics were different than the assignment descriptions, and my submissions were being mixed with other students.

I feel bad since Ms Cantrell is passionate about the subject but the course itself was a mess.

This is the third class I've had with Professor Cantrell and I am incredibly lucky to get to continue learning from her. She shares her industry experience, gives detailed feedback, inspires her students, and is highly passionate about what she does. I'm excited to take more classes with her in the future.

Ms. Cantrell is an amazing instructor. She is very dedicated to her students and always give amazing feedback. I have always been intimidated with 2D art but Ms. Cantrell has been very encouraging. I love that her lectures are created in order to expand students artistic abilities no matter their level of artistic education.

I am a former student of Ms. Cantrell and alumni of the digital worlds program where she teaches. As a professor, Ms. Cantrell offered a curriculum that was enjoyable for both news bees to digital programs and students who already may have a handle on the program. In addition to offering extra credit and being understanding with grades she always
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ms. Cantrell is an engaging, educated, experienced, and passionate young professor whose primary interest in teaching is to set her students up for success in an expanding career market. She is funny, understanding, and gives her student all the help she can.

She does not grade on time, She does not give feedback and if she does (rarely), She batch grades assignments before the class ends. DO NOT expect her to be fully committed to class- she is too busy on TikTok or Twitter and SCAD. Her material in class taught me nothing I couldn't have learned from YouTube. Her classes are all the same.

Professor Cantrell was amazing. For 2D Animation, she made sure to hit all the points needed to help us succeed in class. Lectures and feedback were clear and constructive, and she had an amazing personality! Our assignments and final project were fun and truly utilized our knowledge that we learned from the course.
An excellent professor who teaches a hard subject very well. Always does her best to keep students encouraged and inspired.

This was one of the only classes where attending lecture actually mattered and made sense in real time. I didn't feel like I had to reteach myself the material afterward.

That alone puts him among the best professors in the department, in my opinion. I highly recommend taking this class if you have the opportunity.
He was great would 100% recommend over pretty much any of the other math professors
Quizzes are attendance-based and exams are straightforward with no tricks or surprises. He's also really funny and lighthearted. Take for a chill math elective

What a gem.  His lectures are interesting and super easy to follow, and he does not give trick questions on exams.  Is super accomodating and understanding.  The class itself is not difficult at all, and although you go over formal proofs in class, he never makes you write a formal proof.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Di Cerbo's Complex Variables class a year ago, and I realized that I should leave a review. He is passionate and energetic about teaching as well as being easy to talk to. Only bad thing is his accent making some words unclear, but it only happens 1-2 times a lecture. You won't get a more relaxed higher math class, so enjoy it while you can.

Very fun professor. He will sometimes take too long in the beginning of the lectures, so he does not cover as many examples. But the concepts and the material sticks very well. He is extremely nice and office hours are very helpful. 10/10 would recommend.
Probably my favorite math professor that I have taken at UF. Interesting and clear lectures, and assignments and exams were very fair. Highly recommend!

Di Cerbo is one of the best math profs I've had. His lectures are very clear with the right amount of rigor, and he is charismatic and easy to talk to. Quizzes are for completion and exams cover things he talks about in lecture and hw. His grading system was generous. Frankly, this was the easiest 4000 math elective I've taken. Highly recommend!
He isn't the best but at least he knows his stuff and is pretty good at lecturing.

Very simple class structure with few assignments, which was welcome. Lectures were very clear and educational, if sometimes boring. Extremely personable and approachable. One of the easiest classes I have taken, but I still learned a lot. Highly recommend.

Good professor who encourages questions and tries to help you. However, between him and Huang, I'd opt for Dr. Huang next time. Not a big difference though and you can just attend Huang's lectures if you don't like his style. She also makes the tests.

His accent is hard to understand so I end up watching Ian Manly's lectures on YouTube. I also had to go to Study Edge to make sure I was understanding it better. The lectures give more practice problems than conceptual knowledge, so Study Edge really helped in that department.
Di Cerbo was an average teacher. I Had him for calc 3 and he knows how to explain concepts really well. Besides the Lectures, I didn't really need him that much.
Dr. Di Cerbo is a funny and caring guy who provides great lectures and notes. His assignments and exams are very fair, aligning well with the lecture content. I recommend him for Complex Variables.

I'm not gonna lie, Dr. Di Cerbo was behind the main professor in lectures for the whole semester and he didn't explain the material quite as well, but if you happen to make your way to his office hours, he his very good at helping you understand the material. Only 75% attendance required for a 100% in the grade book. Beware of the tough final.

Lots of class resources and a big cushion with extra credit. I had a very low attendance grade but still got an A. Final is much harder. Homework takes long but very few points. This professor was consistently behind, so I watched Huang's, but he explains it well and answers questions thoroughly. The study guide n practice exam are really helpful!

I enjoyed this class. It was the first time he taught calc 3 and he explained the material very well. He answered everyone's questions thoroughly and is a very caring professor. The final is very difficult. I got high As on the first 3 exams and failed the final, the material got exponentially harder. But I am a freshman, and I am glad I had him!

Good professor but lectures are slow and consequently doesn't cover all the class material and never does all the examples. Get Huang instead if possible, or maybe just click in to his lectures at the end and then watch Huang's lectures.

This class was okay. Dr. Di Cerbo rarely finished his lectures, but the concepts that he did explain, he explained well. He has an accent but it's easy to understand, and he's a relatively good speaker. I'd come to class for the clicker points and watch Huang's lectures online. Overall good, but get Huang if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult to work with regarding medical accommodations. Communication is passive-aggressive, inflexible, and stressful. Questions legitimate telehealth notes and repeatedly emphasized missed exams, making students feel unsupported. Not ideal if you need flexibility.
do youself a favor, take this class online.
This guy didn't input too much time in class preparation, which is very obvious. You should not expect to learn too much in his class. The course is boring and useless.

Lectures are pretty boring, there is little room for class discussions, and Ceobanu will not hesitate to talk down to you as if you are stupid. The "study guides" he provides are literally just a list of every bullet point from his PowerPoints, and the tests are probably 20% of what's on the study guide. The tests are also worded like riddles.

Not fun to participate, usually treats you as if you don't know what you're talking about. Study guides for tests are very convoluted. Tests are confusing and lectures are hard to follow. Reads off PowerPoint that barely makes sense for the entire class. also gives paper with very vague instructions. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ceobanu is a very fair grader and always willing to help out. He seems to genuinely care about his students. I will say the lectures can be a bit dry and repeat the textbook a lot, but the tests were very predictable and it is a good class to take to be an informed citizen.

Class is mainly taught through student presentations so be prepared to learn on your own. He is willing to offer extra credit when necessary. Very nice guy and wants you to succeed, as long as you show up to class and participate. Other students didnt like the format of the class but I truly didnt mind. Fine for me but not for everybody.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Literally the hardest class I've ever taken with the worst professor possible. He's nice but truly terrible. He had the students teach every class and sat in the back grading the presentations meticulously. The exams were hard and impossible and there was nothing to cushion the grade. Didnt give much resources so you teach yourself. Don't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is the hardest class I have taken so far for literally no reason. The only assignments we had are 3 exams that are all worth 90%. During lecture he talked the whole from start to finish reading off of the powerpoint. The class was just too hard when it shouldn't have been.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Labs: use google and watch the linked tutorials on the lab pages. He has a TA and this semester she's been amazing in the GroupMe we have with her. This man is beyond kind--giving extra credit on exams, extending labs, and he just MOVED A TEST for us. The material is essential, just read like he tells you to and pay attention. Great professor!

Someone who truly cares to help you with your grade and learning. Is very flexible with exam dates as he wants to be doing whats best for the class. Just show him effort and respect and hell do everything (and more) that he can do to help you get the grade you want. Material on labs can be tough, but again hes flexible and helpful with that also

This class is just hard in general, but he is very understanding especially with covid, and tries to help out his students. He lectures the entire time and the information is often dense but he is not a bad lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoy this class but considering taking this course means reading and showing up-every day. He's super detailed and particular with lectures- ask questions when you need to, not only is it welcomed but it makes the class more interactive and the material easier to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wonderful person, okay profesor, youll be okay..
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor ceobanu makes his class much harder than it should be. His lectures are unclear and he doesnt delve into the material. He wants you to form your own opinion and interpretations of the readings but will then tell you youre wrong but wont say or explain what he deems as correct. He wants to do the least amount of work he has to
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy. Not all nice guy's are great professors. However, he's not the worst i've had. He genuinely cares about our grades and isn't out to get us. He bends to your needs and tries to supply you with what you need. But, his tests were tricky and based on the textbook and lecture. Notes aren't posted-no electronics, he will call you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Although, yes, his lectures may be long and his grading a little tougher than most- he is an amazing professor that has a true passion for what he's teaching. There are only three exams the entire semester that dictate your grade, each worth 30%. Attendance is mandatory and is taken at the end of every class- so DO NOT leave early!

He wasn't too bad, but the subject is very one-sided and liberal. You HAVE to go to class and take notes because he won't put them online, a lot of the test questions come straight from his lecture slides. Quizzes are straight from the book. But overall, he is a nice guy and trie to give a lot of bonus points.

Class was fairly difficult because the teacher refused to put notes online. He expected us to take notes quickly and somehow listen to him at the same time. I only got an A because he had to curve the class's grade by over 4 percent. His tests didn't really correlate with the book and neither did the quizzes

This class was very interesting and the professor taught the material in an easy-to-follow manner. At times he was argumentative with students, but the debates kept the course interesting. He occasionally provided real-world examples and videos of past social problems. Overall a great class and professor. I would recommend taking this course.
This is the worst class I've taken in my 4 years at UF. He was incredibly haughty, one-sided and argumentative.

Professor Ceobanu is such a nice guy. His lectures are easy to follow. He will do everything in his power to help you get a good grade. If he sees the class is getting bored he will give a quick break. He is very knowledgeable and entertaining.

Such an amazing professor!! Even if you aren't interested in the subject I would recommend taking this course. Ceobanu is sociable, interesting, and keeps the class entertained. The exams are harder than expected but he will help in whatever way he can.

Class is tough, but enjoyable.  If you do your readings, attend class, and participate you should make a B+ or an A.  I thought he was a pretty easy grader, but his tests were very detail driven. And...I agree about needing background knowledge to keep up at times.

At first Ceobanu can come off as an arrogant SOB...but as the class goes on and you actually get to know him you realize he's just different. However, don't be fooled by this, he expects a lot of BACKGROUND KNOWLEDGE so if you want to take this class better pick up a history book RIGHT NOW or you'll end up crying in class...yep, it's that bad.

He really likes feedback and questions.  You MUST do the reading, and it really will help you for the tests.  Kind if anal about attendance, make sure you go.  The class seems boring, but at the end you'll be amazed at how much you've learned and how much your understanding has deepened.  Can take a lot from the class if you try to.  Prof is nice 2

Awesome dude. He's passionate about what he teaches. As long as you keep up with the notes and the reading, you'll be fine. He gives fair curves on quizzes and tests. Warning: DO NOT bring any electronics to class, they really annoy him.

took him for nationalism in europe- COPIOUS AMOUNT OF NOTES, tons to write and he talks too while u try to get the notes down so i felt like i missed stuff. difficult tests, attendance is mandatory, be careful if u like to skip classes. readings suck and so do the required note cards every day. stay away unless ur interested in the topic!

Im a junior..and i took him for 2 classes. Best professor ive had at UF. His tests are straight forward..and he tells you the main concepts he wants you to learn. Tests are easy if you take notes and go to class.
He is not a difficult professor, but his tests are definitely not simple and straight forward, so be ready to do a lot of boring reading.

i definitely did not like the topic of nationalism. he talks a lot. the class is not too bad if you are able to zone out.  his exams are kind of tough.  but he's almost a fair grader.  if you are interested in the topic of european nationalism, this class is definitely for you

Culture and Identity in Europe. Interesting reading material and class lectures. Only 11 people in my class. Take home essays.  Go to class. It's interesting! Romanian accent is easy on the ears. Liam Neeson look-a-like.
Takes attendance through a system where you turn in daily index cards. On your index card, you write questions pertinent to the reading assigned the previous class. Class wasn't diffcult.

This class is incredibly boring. There are 2 exams which mostly consist of short answer and essay questions. Usually that would be hard but his grading is so lenient and easy that any fool can do well. He just wants you to show that you have an opinion about something - anything (even if it has little to do with the given question). Highly reccomen
Yes, he is good looking and that accent is amazing.  Besides that, he is very informed and makes the class very interesting and relevant.  This class is actually useful.
Great teacher and great Romanian accent that makes you want to listen to what he is saying.  Plus he looks like Liam Neeson.

A great professor whose really engaged in what he teaches; really knows his stuff.  Very willing to help outside of class, and works with students as far as exams go; very willing to change formats in order to accommodate the class.  A lot of reading, but all relevent material.  Truly awesome!

The grading criteria is awful, which then leads to picky grading and points off. Takes a long time to grade and the group project is annoying. Group projects should be banned; I support this idea from my experience in this class.

AWFUL!! She is the most nit picky professor i've ever had at UF which is ridiculous for a class about social media. Grades so unfairly no matter how much time you put into an assignment. She takes a week to answer an email, I had to follow up twice before getting a response. Avoid her.

she does not know how to communicate. i had to email multiple times for a response. not accommodating or understanding. takes points off with no explanation? she just proctors the course (online summer b), I honestly don't think she even knows anything about it. she couldn't get Hootsuite to work for the longest time.

I took PUR3622 online with Martinez and if you can get a different professor, do it. She is an incredibly harsh grader and awful about responding to emails. She gave me a 0 on an assignment because of a misunderstanding on her part but didn't answer my emails trying to fix it, which unfairly brought my final grade down to a B from an A.

Lots of work for this class, including a FOUR PART group project. The individual assignments, discussions and playposits were fairly standard, and she gives many opportunities to get extra credit. But - this is a very work heavy class, and I can't stress how annoying the group project is.

The course itself is not difficult, although a bit outdated. The professor is the issue. It isn't that she is a tough grader - that would imply she has standards. It is that she makes up her grades on the fly. No clear instruction or rubric. Accuses students with proof of their work that they used AI. Unreachable for feedback or any discussion.

This professor is based remotely in Puerto Rico and as you will quickly perceive, this is a side hustle for her. The syllabus is incredibly blunt and harsh, and the course is painfully outdated and unclear- steer clear of this course unless it's required, which is how I got stuck with it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I will say that I was scared to take a class of hers because of the ratings, but I believe that the course was not difficult overall. No exams, weekly work, and asking for more than just "I agree" is not asking much of students. Many complain that she asks for more, but if you use other info you may have from everyday life she gives you credit.

This is my 2nd time around with this professor and I can assure you I didn't select this class based on the instructor. As is often the case, UF will work with some lackluster professor based in another country who could not care less. The curriculum is full of technical issues that should have been fixed long ago- highly unprofessional.

Although she isn't an easy A, she is fair, kind, and knowledgeable. I will say that many of the assignments were so intimidating. You are often being pushed hard to do things you have never done. Do not slack for the group project. It is a huge part of the grade. Stay on it, and communicate well with your team. Reporting is way harder.

This professor is a very tough grader and extremely strict, with little room for flexibility or accommodations. She doesn't even hold lectures at all and grading was harsh and didn't always reflect the effort put into assignments. I didn't feel supported, and it was difficult to get clear answers when issues came up.

PLEASE just listen to Rate My Professor and take this class with another prof/wait til next semester. She has no idea how to use Canvas & uploaded assignments wrong/had technical difficulties nearly every week. I had to email multiple times to get a response/she is really hard to communicate with. Also a harsh grader for no reason. just don't lol

I do NOT like to leave negative reviews but I feel like I have to. I just got a 0 on an assignment for saying that I don't have original responses or analysis. She has been great at communicating with me in the past. For one, I don't even know what that means. Thankfully, the class drops the lowest grade.
So much unnecessary stress for a class that is meant to be enjoyable. Dislike sooo much dont take!
Dont take. Marks off for anything and I have so much unnecessary stress for a class that is supposed to be fun.

I wish I would have paid better attention to the reviews. I though "How hard can social media be?" Let me tell you- this professor sucks the fun out of this course. Good luck communicating with her- one of the worst experiences I've had at UF.

Worst teacher I've had. Emailed 7 times for points taking off for things not specified or even MENTIONED in rubrics or instructions. Took half my grade for lack of capitalization of two words. For students wanting to learn & succeed this professor tanks your grade for no reason/ without explanation. Discouraging: unresponsive, uncaring, unjust. Bad
She gives a lot of work and she's very harsh at grading your work.

What kind of elective class grades this harshly? Absolutely nonsensical to try tanking people's GPAs over what should have been a light course. For how hard she grades, you would anticipate this is a critical tracking course. Also should be a fun class considering it's about social media, but she sucked the fun out of it completely.

She's not great, but tollerable. She does things a little differently than other professors as far as Canvas organization and communication, and we all felt like she gave tedious unnecessary work. For a social media course, it was a lot of work.

Professor Martinez was impossible to reach. After three unanswered emails, I finally resorted to DMs on Instagram and Twitter. Assignments were incredibly confusing, grading was inconsistent and there was a lot of work that felt random and off-topic. Our group project was a nightmare. Professor Martinez was the worst teacher I've had at UF.

I don't know about the experiences from Fall '18, but Spring '19 professor Martinez was great. She offered ample extra credit opportunities, listened to feedback from students, and generally gave good advice concerning homework. It's always nice to learn from a teacher who cares about what they're teaching. No group projects.

I have tons of respect for Professor Martinez because I can tell she is genuinely passionate about social media management. However, her class is one of the hardest classes I have ever taken! I am a straight A student taking five classes, and thought that social media would be a light course load. WRONG! She is unclear, unhelpful, and intimidating.

She was not made to be a teacher. Unorganized, unclear with directions and grades on what is not included in rubric. The rubric will show you did A+ work but she will give you a full letter grade off for kicks.

Recep's lectures were engaging, but make sure to write fast because he doesn't stop going once class starts. He was pretty funny and kind, and wants his students to succeed. Make sure to go to office hours if you are struggling because he does randomly call on students during class for answers, which keeps the class engaged.

I took Calculus 3 with Professor Recep Celebi in summer 2024. His enthusiasm for mathematics and willingness to provide additional support outside of class significantly enhanced my learning experience. I highly recommend his course to anyone looking to deepen their understanding of calculus.

Mr. Celebi cares about his students and is happy to answer questions in class or office hours. However, he is exceptionally particular about the take-home quizzes, to the point where he would critique my handwriting and formatting of my work. This was my first math class at UF and I hated it, but it also prepared me for my future classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I honestly did not struggle to get an A in this class but I know that was not true for most of our class. His tests were really hard but he awards a majority of the points for the work and the tests have bonus points, so I found it easy as a non-math inclined student to get A's on them. He gives EC + weekly at home tests. He's also really funny lol

I'm not going to lie, Recep was a tough TA. However, I wouldn't have any other instructor for Calc 2. He genuinely cares for his students and wants them to succeed. His lectures were so clear and easy to follow. However, he did single out students sometimes, which is the only thing preventing me from giving him a 5/5.

Calc 2 definitely isn't an easy class, but I wouldn't have wanted any one else as my instructor. I can tell that he wants his students to succeed, but that he doesn't want to compromise the value of what we are learning by making exams/quizzes super easy. Definitely go to office hours.

Had as a TA for MAC2312 and I am fairly grateful for it. He is a bit of a tough grader, yet very fair. He is always willing to help explain what you did wrong and why it affected your grade. Insanely helpful during office hours and is very accessible outside of class. He often would send additional optional work to help prep for exams.

I had the pleasure of having Celebi as my TA for MAC2313. He is a great lecturer, a fair grader, is easily accessible outside of class, and above all he really cares about his students. Be aware that the homework, quizzes, and tests are hard, you will have to work hard to succeed. I would highly recommend having him as your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Definitely would take him as a discussion teacher for calc 3 again.  He was super nice and had a good sense of humor, along with knowing the material for the class really well.  Loved my time with him.

Because this course was 100% online, there was not much interaction with Recep. He seemed pretty nice though the exams were very difficult for non-math people. Had a bad time during this course as the online lectures were from Professor Knudson and our homework and exams were often different than what we were taught in the lecture videos sometimes.

Professor Celebi is an excellent educator and a kind person. This was an online course so the lectures were prerecorded, but Professor Celebi remained in contact during the semester and held office hours, which helped. When I got stuck on a problem I used the tutoring center and would sometimes meet with Professor Celebi there, which helped so much

I took him for calc. Hardest class I've ever taken, he made all the exams maximum difficulty. this class was impossible for me to pass. My other classmates are having to drop their entire pre med tracks or engineering whatever it may be. If you are not one of the sharpest tools in the shed with an uncrackable math foundation do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Celebi always came into class frantically, but was so sweet. I took him in summer B, which I do not recommend, because of how fast-paced it is. The midterms were pretty hard, but the final was easy, so it made up for it. He offered a few extra credit assignments at the end for those who wanted to boost their grade a little bit.

Having Recep as a TA made the class far more difficult than it needed to be. During discussions, there would be many times where he'd get sidetracked on unrelated proofs of concepts rather than helping us with the actual problem itself. He grades super harshly, is very strict, and only ever has time to answer a few questions during office hours.

I actually had the pleasure of having Recep as my instructor during my Summer B semester. Recep was an awesome lecturer, and always sought out to make sure every students questions were answered. I had a hard time grasping pre-calculus at times, and he always helped me get a better understanding. I am still not a fan of multiples of 7 though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Recep is a great TA whose discussion sections really improved my understanding of calc 3. He always responds to emails to help clarify anything about the course and is a great resource for anything related to the content.

Professor Celebi was so fun to be taught by. He was hysterical but you could tell his passion for Math was there. While there is a lot of homework, it genuinely is there for the purpose of helping you. Im not gonna lie, it was hard, but he made sure to explain why everything happened vs just telling you to do it. I recommend him greatly to all.

Recep is a great professor. Attendance is crucial for success in the class, but Professor Recep's humor makes attendance all worthwhile. He gives lots of supplemental material to help prepare for tests and is also very understanding in general. Get ready to do so homework though. Class is great for those looking to strengthen math background.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly this class is a lot of work but if you're willing to put in the effort, Professor Carmichael will meet you halfway. He's funny and makes the lectures enjoyable. The homework also isn't too bad, it's just a lot of questions.
