Patrick is a good professor; however. The workload for this class is just insanity, multiple homeworks per week consisting of 35+ questions, so much material. Class average on most exams was near-failing. Genuinely it's easier to teach yourself trig whilst in Calc 1 than take this class. Don't do it, you'll thank me later.

Carmichael is an amazing professor. I took his MAC1147 class (algebra and trig). The schedule is heavy. He explains the material very well in his lectures. I didn't need to use the textbook or anything else to understand it. Staying on pace is key! Overall, you should have no problem with him, but learning the material is on you!
Pretty boring professor in my opinion, also, I didn't think the past exams were similar to the online exams.

Professor Carmichael did a great job lecturing and making the class feel personal even though it was online. Although the class can be difficult at times he explains topics well and has an easy to follow system for homework, quizzes, tests, and extra credit. I would easily recommend taking his course.

LOVE CARMICHAEL!! Make sure to actually use the past exams he provides and STUDY ON YOUR OWN TIME! Study these exams over the homeworks/quizzes because those aren't as accurate (learned that the hard way...).  Make sure to make it to your discussions because that's the only attendance that's actually mandatory :)

Professor Carmichael is an amazing lecturer who explains concepts clearly and thoroughly. There are 3 HWs a week with around 30 questions each, long but great practice. Exams are almost identical to the past exams he posts, so use them to study. Extra credit for attending class and answering a live question can add up to 2% to your final grade.
Tests are weighted so heavy and are nothing like the tons of homework you get. No rounding in the end either i had a 76.99 that if rounded to a 77 would be a B and he refused to do it.

Professor is chill and good at explaining the content and expectations. Homework 3x a week but definitely manageable if you stay on top of it. Provides past exams that are exactly like the ones he gives and he drops your lowest exam. You can redo quizzes and hw questions until you get a 100 plus extra credit every class. Overall great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If Professor Carmichael didn't teach this class, I definitely would've done horrible. His lectures are actually amazing and very informative. I've never been a math person, but I enjoyed learning from him. As long as you follow the lectures and make an effort to do the homework on your own, you'll go great!
Lots of homework and quizzes, but very good instruction overall and always willing to help students understand
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I cannot gas up this man enough, his lectures are the only ones I've ever understood so easily (even though you might have to go back in the recording if you miss something, but the explanation is really good). If you do your homework and the practice quizzes & past years tests, the tests are easy and are pretty much the same.

Practice exams are not similar to the real exams. Lots of homework, frequently includes difficult questions not discussed in lecture and cannot be solved by peers/TAs. High percent of grade is based on exams, this class took a LOT of effort between exams, homework, and lectures because of the content. do not take as an easy refresh class.

Do NOT use AI to do your homework. Actually study and do all the HW assignments (even if they're a lot). He's a great professor if you go to his office hours and utilize all the resources you are provided. It's a harder class, but attend lecture and don't cheat. Also, his exams are almost identical to the practice exams he publishes!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was such an incredible professor. I love him. Yes the class is hard, but if you show up you will be fine. Do your homework don't use AI and study.

hard course. I had previously taken college level precalc and gotten an A but wanted an easier first semester so chose to take a math course I knew and severly regretted it. Exams are practiacally all of your grade and are not the same as hw or quizess. Met with proffessor in office hours to try and get help and he made me want to cry and drop.

Carmichael is stellar professor, BUT this class requires a LOT of work. It is precalc and trig, which is offered as 2 separate courses at UF, but MAC1147 are both smashed into one. Ended up using Teachmezach to help solidify the content, really affordable tutoring service.

Carmichael reminded that I actually like math. One of the best professors and lecturers I have ever had. He explains topics in depth and never shys away from a question. The class is very clearly laid out no surprises, EXTREMELY fair has extra credit and dropping of an exam. HW heavy and a decent amount of work not a snooze class, work is required!

I absolutely loved Professor Carmichael and I think he's a great professor. He is intelligent, caring, funny, fair, and humble (not pretentious). The exams were very similar to the practice exams/exams from previous semesters, which he readily provides. He is the only math professor I've ever had who records and posts all of his lectures.

Carmichael is a great professor, but the class is naturally hard (and I mean it is TERRIBLE). He had generous late passes and drop grades. If you show up to class you should be fine (I never did). I mostly got high D's and low C's on the exams, but for the final I locked in and got an 88% so I ended with a B.

While Carmichael seems to be very kind, this class in unnecessarily difficult. The exams are nothing like the quizzes and HW. They also account for 40% of your grade so they will tank it. No type of curve on exams despite class averages being borderline failing. Be ready to do a lot of HW that doesn't help on exams. Has EC & drops. TAKE ONLINE!

Honestly way harder than it needs to be I had to study 2 weeks straight for one exam to get an A, most ppl get Cs on them, no curve, lots of HW and pointless quizzes. He posts past exams but questions change and he likes to throw in curveballs. Exam 4 is one week away from the final so start studying before then bc it's a lot of content

He is a very nice teacher and gives lots of examples to help you understand. The only complaint I have is that you have a 25-45 question homework assignment due 3 times a week. If you're a procrastinator on that kind of stuff you are going to have a hard time.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS unless you have to. If you have ANY sort of illness or emergency, he won't care, even if you present him with doctor's notes. I had a serious illness and had to go home to the doctors, but he forced me to take his 8:30 PM exam on Friday stating "If you can make it to class to tell me this you can make it to my exam on Friday".

I absolutely loved Professor Carmichael and I think he's a great professor. He is intelligent, caring, funny, fair, and humble (not pretentious). The exams were very similar to the practice exams/exams from previous semesters, which he readily provides. He is the only math professor I've ever had who records and posts every lecture he gives.

Carmichael's MAC1147 is challenging but rewarding. The course covers a lot of ground quickly, so active participation and resourceful study habits, like using unstuck study, are key. Exams can be tricky, but his teaching style and available support make the effort worthwhile.

Professor Carmichael was very fun to learn under. His lectures were thorough and explained concepts in their entirety. Not only did I learn how to utilize new concepts, but I also learned how and why they work. Although a lot of work, effort, and time management were required, his class was pleasant and straightforward.

He's a great teacher who likes his job. He often goes into WHY the concepts are the way they are and their importance. Every lecture has homework of 20-40 questions but is relatively easy to do. I didn't do very well on any of the tests but scored highly on homework and quizzes and ended up with a B+ so an A should be achievable with more effort.

Class moves at a very fast pace. Each week there are 2-3 hw that are 15-40 questions. There are many opportuities to use "late passes" though. Exams are heavily weighted and questions can be "different" from hws. Quizzes every Monday are based on hws. Cumulative final. Look at previous exams+do practice questions from them to review for exams!

Great prof but the class was hard. 3 lectures per week, 1 homework per lecture (25-35 questions each), and one quiz a week (10 questions). Lots of extra credit. 4 exams plus a final. Lowest exam, quizzes, and homeworks dropped. Study past exams, not the quizzes. Quizzes are way more difficult. Discussion attendance is graded. My TA was terrible.

Prof is nice, but the amount of work either forces you to understand the material fully or use artificial intelligence to complete it. LIT215/Office Hours were probably most helpful way to get problems explained.

The main pro of having so much homework was that it acted as a much-needed balance to exam grades, which had low averages and no curve

TAKE PROFESSOR CARMICHAEL!! I liked precalculus in high school when I took it, and this class, although it was a lot harder, was still a fantastic class to take. There were about 34 lectures and a quiz every four lectures, five exams, and the last was a cumulative exam. There were discussion posts as extra credit. Overall a great professor!

If you struggle with math, this class may be difficult; however, Dr. Carmicheal is rather considerate.  There is pretty much HW every other day and you need to either attend the lectures, or watch the recordings to complete them.

3 days to finish hw & 20+ late passes for the semester. quizzes on mondays based on last week's content, but u have the entire day to do it online & questions come straight from the hw just diff numbers. exams are harder than hw but thats a given in any class. review past exams & you'll be good. this class shouldnt be your most difficult one at all

Professor Carmichael is one of the best math teachers I've had. Has a lot of extra credit opportunities (DO THEM ALL!) and uploads lectures online. Difficult because of its nature, insanely fast and you will rely on self-re-teaching for exams. TAs were super helpful. For those not confident in math: I feared this class and got an A-, you got this.

Lots of work.30-40 questions each hw and VERY time consuming. My TA wasn't helpful at all with answering questions, but it depends who you get. Exams way harder than the homework or quizzes, use the past exams Carmichael posts to study. Prof Carmichael is a good lecturer and chill, funny guy, but the class is a lot. One exam dropped, saved me

Definitely harder of a class than I anticipated. Lectures are 3x a week and you have 3 homeworks and a quiz per week. Each lecture homework is 30-40 questions and very very time consuming. Felt like I spent way more time on this class than others. Exams do not match homework, but do match past exams. The professor himself is really funny tho.

GPA BOMBED. I didn't need the credit but took the class to get some extra practice. There is so much homework that is 30-40 questions every other day and a quiz once a week. However, the assignments were manageable but the tests were NOTHING like the quizzes or past exams and were very tricky. DO NOT take this class unless you have to.

This class is war. Moves incredibly fast, and homeworks take FOREVER with little application to actual exam questions. Get ready to study for hours consistently with a lot of self-teaching if you want a half decent grade. Carmichael understands that the class is hard, but there's very little he can do anyway that improve anything about it.

The professor is good and is really nice when you reach out to him. But the course is WAY harder online compared to in person with the in-person exams being significantly easier being multiple choice compared to the online ver which includes none with small mistakes such as forgetting in include including a deg/pi value costing the entire question.

I found this class to be incredibly challenging and frustrating. He mentioned putting things you have learned on the test and putting things never seen on them, which turned out to be the theme of the semester. Simple concepts made difficult. Went to tutoring and office hours, and was defeated and confused most times. Avoid if possible.

Take in person. Online exams are harder in-person students get easier, multiple-choice tests and free points on the final. Lecture videos are outdated and miss key topics, I had to look up how to solve problems for homework. The course is a lot of work so consistent studying is a must. He's not a bad teacher, but the online course feels unfair.

If you watch the lectures you will do good in the class. He gives examples and the homework is very manageable in regards to feedback. This was my heaviest class workload-wise but it's expected when taking pre-calc. He gives a lot of leniency with turning in assignments. He gives two attempts per exam, unlimited attempts for everything else.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this class if you dont need to. The exams are excessively difficult in comparison to what he lectures and assigns for hw/ quizzes. Around 30 question homeworks three times a week, due every other day. hw is manageable but the tests will completely drop your grade.

This class is a total GPA killer, and shouldn't be as hard as it is. Students get an average of 50-70% on tests, and those weigh 40% of your grade. A ridiculous amount of homework with content not applicable to the test. The test are difficult due to them having different questions he's doesn't go over. My best piece of advice use the textbook.

Professor Carmichael was not a good professor. The exams were SO difficult and did not correspond with the homework. I spent so much extra time doing this class just to barely get by. Pre-calculus should have been a refresher for me because I took it in high school, but he made the class so much more difficult than it had to be. TAKE THIS ONLINE.

Around 2 hour length homeworks for every lecture, so 3 times a week. Must work hard to keep up with this class and if you can't keep up, you'll get buried and won't have time to go back to what you really need to review. Material isn't necessarily hard, there's just a lot of it. If you have a basis of knowledge in the topics, skip. 4 exams -> final

Do not take this class. If you have a basis in calc 1, skip this. Lectures move incredibly fast, which is understandable for the amount of content that needs to be covered, but the exams are far more difficult than any of the homeworks or quizzes (which take forever). Carmichael is a cool guy but the exams are awful. GPA killer.

Professor Carmichael has a challenging course, but he is kind and gives good tools to help study. Exams can be kind of tricky and are sometimes a little bit different from the review, but this is coming from someone that struggled with math. There are quite a few lectures and homework assignments, but he gives out lots of late passes and attempts.

very time consuming class; about 3 hw assignments due per week (20-45 questions each). fast paced covering over 34 topics, and 4 exams as well as a final. however, chances for EC, lowest exam, quiz, and homework assignments dropped. this class required a lot of self teaching and looking for resources outside notes. very passionate professor though.

The professor was really great but this course is very intense in the amount of work it requires each week. I think the structure and organization of the course is all really good but just be ready for the effort it requires. Lectures were helpful as well.

I would highly recommend him. Go to class, you'll understand a lot more that way. He is nice and does his best to help students understand. Uses a lot of memes in his lectures, and will talk with you about things besides math. He is a great choice. Class will be a bit tough if you didn't do well in math in high school, but it's like that for anyone

As someone who took precalc in high school, I found this class fairly difficult. I still managed to get an A, but it required quite a bit of studying for someone who was already familiar with the material. He also assigns 30-40 questions per homework assignment, but this practice is pretty much useless for exam studying. Use past exams to study!

Class was pretty easy and lectures went over everything you needed to know. Did the homework and did the past exams before each one. Lowest of the four midterms gets dropped. Decent amount of extra credit offered.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Carmichael is a good lecturer but the course is very difficult. DO NOT take if you are not strong in math OR if you don't need to take calculus after. The lectures are very fast and there is homework after each one. The exams covered a lot of content and were difficult. Passing is possible if you're good at math/have time to study.

I am naturally pretty good at math and have always gotten high exam grades, but this class taught me something different. I feel like the professor makes the exams harder than they need to be. He lectures SUPER FAST. I stopped attending class because he would over the material too fast. I watched the lecture videos he posted. Be prepared to study.

Professor Carmichael is a very understanding individual, and I can tell he is passionate in teaching. However, I would not take another class with him because of how difficult his exams are compared to homework material (which there is a lot of). I do not feel like my grade reflects my understanding of the content within this course.
Worst professor. This course is required for liberal arts and sciences majors and he expects you to be an expert at math to do well. Getting a B on his Exam was

Taking it for practice for calc 1? don't. It bombed my GPA. TA's suck, you're lucky if you get a good one. He teaches differently then HS pre-calculus so just bust out your old notebook for Calc 1 instead of wasting you're money. Don't study for practice quizzes.

he offers zoom and recordings so lectures (3x a week) aren't mandatory. homework after every lecture and sometimes the questions aren't really covered in the lectures but he has a discussion open for students to ask and answer questions which was super helpful (and sometimes there are videos attached to the questions that are also helpful).

Half of HW/quiz questions weren't covered in lectures AT ALL. Sometimes he doesn't go in depth on certain topics and also some HW question topics come up in later modules. Very time consuming as you have to scour the internet on how to solve half of the HW questions. Takes me the whole day to do this class. Lectures are 3 times per week.

Lectured very quickly on a lot of material. Do not take if you don't have a good base understanding on what the lectures are about. You will spend a lot of time doing homework and quizzes, but you have multiple attempts, so they should be easy grade boosters.

This man gives homework until you can't breathe. His tests are nothing like his homework assignments like he says they are, and learning through a bunch of lectures and an insane amount of homework is not the way to go. Please choose another professor who will make your life much easier in terms of homework and tests.
Good lecturer, and fair professor. Practice exams are very similar to the real exams. The majority of the course is fairly simple algebra.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His lectures were really good at explaining the material. If I ever got confused at one topic it would be fine because he uploads his lectures after class. He was very nice and approachable, and really seemed to be passionate about the lecture material.

EXTREMELY hard class if you aren't good at math. Difficulty ramps up rapidly throughout the semester. However, Carmichael is an extremely clear and good lecturer and cares about students. The tests are fair but very difficult. As everyone has said, study previous years' exams. Do not skip lectures. Very long but useful homework, do it all and try.

Carmichael is a very good professor but you will need to be ready to put some work in for this class. There are three lectures a week and a homework after each lecture and a quiz once a week. Attendance is not mandatory but I would highly recommend going. This was a good class and I learned a lot.

I really appreciate how he tried to make this course as fun as possible through the lectures. I have never liked math, but this course made it somewhat enjoyable. The coursework is pretty easy if you watch the lectures, and if not the videos on Canvas cover almost everything regardless. Would definitely take another one of his classes.

Great professor! It is a fast paste class but he did a good job of teaching. Seems like he actually enjoys his job. Exams can get a little tricky but using past exams to help study works well. You can take the quizzes online up to 20 times and you get a good amount of late passes for hw (I forgot how many). Discussions are mandatory attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He did a great job of being there for you even in a huge lecture class. The class was difficult (very easy at first) and there is a lot of homework and quizzes (that you can retake 20 times) so there is a lot of outside work. The exams were hard but he puts up past exams which definitely help. He was great but I didn't love the class.

The class was difficult (easy at first) but Professor Carmichael was definitely a great teacher for a huge lecture course. We didn't get to interact with him much because of how big the class was but he always responded to emails and office hours quickly. The tests weren't easy but studying past exams definitely helped. He is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Carmichael was a great professor and really boosted my confidence as a student who struggles with math. I felt I got a better grasp from his teaching than ever before on trig and precalc concepts. There is a lot of homework but I found it helpful. Quizzes may be retaken many times and the lowest test score is dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Carmichael is a pretty likable teacher, although this class can be a lot of work. Three homework assignments a week which can be lengthy, as well as a quiz once a week. There are four exams and the lowest score gets dropped. He also gives 20 late passes to use on homework. Overall, this class isn't too bad, but it does take a lot of work.

I enjoyed his humor and lectures and discussions are mandatory to attend. As far as the course goes, it is hard. There are 2-3 HWs due each week along with a quiz. There are 4 exams that are 50% of your grade and the lowest one gets dropped. I recommend studying past exams rather than just the material. The material gets harder throughout the semes

The professor is extremely nice and provides students with 20 late passes to submit late homework. The number of quizzes, tests, and homework can be overwhelming for some. He provides two attempts on every test and many more on quizzes and homework. One of the quotes he uses from students is that the class made them cry every day. It was accurate.

Prof. Carmichael was a great professor during the lectures. He always seemed to have his information prepared and rehearsed which made the topics easy to understand during class time. However, the exams were always a struggle. I only managed to get an A on one exam throughout the whole term, even though I spent hours each day studying. Be prepared.

He is a good prof but there is a large amount of homework which is doable if you manage your time. Recommend going to office hours and tutoring more often for trig portion of the class because that's when it gets more difficult. He is good at explaining things though and very helpful and kind in office hours

Attendance to lectures were not mandatory; however, attendance to math breakout sessions is. Professor Carmichael lectures relatively fast but he does send a video recording and the notes after class. A lot of the homework is nothing similar to what he lectured in class and makes it very hard to complete. The exams get harder as the course goes on.

Prof. Carmichael has a decent sense of humor, but beyond that, I wouldn't recommend this course for the online section.  Although it is fairly easy and doable if you stay on pace, his exams for online students (even those of us that live 100s of miles from Gainesville) is free response, while in-person is easier w/ multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There is lots of homework but it is pretty straight forward if you pay attention to the lectures. He explains the topics very well and always sends the recording after if you need to go back. Lots of studying for the exams but there are no suprises.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class was decent, exams were heavy material based and lectures were really important. My TA was AWFUL. Hated mandatory TA discussion attendance because it was a waste of time and didn't help at all!

Took diff eq with him over the summer, pretty good prof overall for this class. Super fast paced but he did a good job with uploading lectures + notes and being accessible for questions. Funny guy and good at explaining difficult math concepts

This class is HARD, especially since I already struggle in math. The in-person courses get multiple choice exams, but the online students have free responses for all exams. I understood the lectures, but quizzes were HARD, AND EXAMS WERE EVEN HARDER. However, retake exams are similar material for the retake which sort of saved me. HARD CLASS
Great professor for this class! Very helpful.

Professor Carmichael's lectures are very informative and really had you understanding what he showed you. However, the lectures are nothing like the homework and even more so the test. Really the key to this class is to study previous exams to get an overall good exam score. The tests get difficult so do your best early on to keep your grade up.

One of the hardest precalc classes ive seen. Tons of homework and lectures although they only count for a small portion of your grade.The exams are a majority of the grade and are difficult. Best way to review is to study the review quizzes as much as possible. And if you are taking online do your first take of the exam and study it.
I took him because I didn't feel confident enough to take Calc 1 at the time. If you are thinking of the same make sure to really pay attention to the parts of MAC1147 about logs and trig.

Proff. Carmicheal made me lose my motivation to learn. I started to struggle on his tests and when I went in for help he was no help at all. He answered my question and did not give any guidance nor tried to help me understand the material. I would not recommend taking his course. He treats it like a weed-out class and felt he wanted me to fail.

Professor Carmichael seems like he likes his job and I understood his lectures well, but I always felt like the exams were 10x harder than the materials we studied with. I never really did well. That being said, his course is very fast paced. Also, do the extra credit because it brought me from a B+ to an A-. Mandatory attendance for discussions.

As a student with a disability being away this prof mad emy life very easy. He was always prompt in emailing my advanced lecture slides (he wont do it for everyone but he posts the slides after class) the exams are tough but he was always available for questions. Go to office hours and do the homework without cheating and you will do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is so sweet and so funny BUT this is quite literally the hardest math class Ive ever taken. Only passed b/c drops lowest exam score and pulled a B on final. I put HOURS on end into studying/going to tutoring for each exam and still did poorly due to how different his exams were from the resources he gave us to study with. So hard.

Great professor who teaches well and really cares about his students! His tests are much more difficult than anything you see in class or on the homework, so make sure you practice with more difficult problems and go to the teaching center for tutoring. Gives lots of opportunity to succeed (EC, drops lowest exam score, drops quizzes/hw). 10/10 prof

Study for his exams, they're a lot harder than the homework. Otherwise, he's kind and tries to connect with his students despite the large size. He explains things well and gives passes for homework. Probably better to take it in person than online though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is homework on every lecture that is due 2 days after the lecture. You will have 3 lectures and homework assignments every week and quiz at the beginning of each week, it's not too bad though because you get 20 late passes to use on homework and quizzes. He has 4 exams and a final exam, his review quizzes tend to be harder than his exams.

Professor Carmichael is an incredible professor and you could tell you knew what he was talking about, but the tests were nothing like the lectures or the practice quizzes he gave us. They were incredibly hard and the average was always around a 50-60. The worst part was the TA. The TA knew nothing about the course and made mistakes every time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Carmichael is a good prof but the course itself is just a lot. The exams are hard, his quizzes to review for the exam are nothing like it. The exams are more about applying what you learned. It also really depends on which TA you have, some suck and others actually give you real exam practice problems. This class is hard but Carmichael teaches well
do not take this course the exams are nothing like the practice problems and lectures and the averages on all our exams was an F.

If you want to take the online class, don't. The online class exams are all free response, meanwhile the in-person get multiple choice. Seems highly unfair to me. On the final exam the in-person people also get free points while us online people don't. Material was fine, I just found it would be easier to get a better grade in-person...

Prof. Carmichael is extremely respectable and a very good teacher. There was so much homework that it was hard to keep up sometimes but he offers 20 late passes on both the homeworks and the quizzes, which each have unlimited tries. The exams are super difficult though, with super low averages and no curving. Hardest math/precalc class i've taken
His lectures are great, and he explains well, but his exams are really hard. He also doesn't curve despite the average being a D.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was probably the most difficult Precalculus class Ive ever taken. Lots of homework after every single lecture and extremely complex and advanced tests. No extra credit besides the fact that he drops one grade. Easy to fail and difficult to get an A. Only take this Math if you HAVE to.

The course's content is difficult, but Prof. Carmichael made it easy to understand. His lectures are thorough and hilarious. There is a lot of HW - the problems on the HW can also be a bit challenging, but I found they helped me better understand the material. I also had a great TA, but I know others who've had bad ones.

TLDR: Good prof. Hard class Prof. Carmichael is actually a really cool guy with a great sense of humor. He gives a quality lecture, which is good because you better show up for them if youre not great at math. Full disclosure: your TA will probably suck, you'll do a lot of homework for very little credit, and your exams are hard and at awful times

Great guy in general and shows he does care about students. Not sure if it was this semester being back from COVID but exams are really tough. Not at all like the practice exams or even old exams from previous years. The second exam the average was a D and everyone complained it was impossible.

I had the luck of having Professor Carmichael for my first math class, MAC1147. His lectures were really good at hitting at both common cases and edge cases for math. It is thanks in large part to him that I had a solid base for upper-division classes.
Reviews before every test which helps a lot. Pay attention in class especially on zoom or not you will be lost. Get study edge if you can helps a lot.

He was very helpful during office hours and always kind to students. He seemed very knowledgeable on what we were being taught and was always prepared for class. Just do the practice quizzes and reviews before exams and pay attention during lecture and everything is pretty easy.
king.
Great professor! Offers a ton of extra credit opportunities to post grades. Tests are fine since you have access to previous quizzes to review. Lectures have little funny sayings in them.

It is very important that you stay up to date with the lectures on the homework in this class or you will definitely fall behind. He does lectures and TAs work with you for the rest of the stuff. The material is not too hard but there is a lot of it and you will have to make sure you are accumulating knowledge and not just studying for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Carmichael is easily one of the best if not THE best math teacher I have ever had. His lectures are entertaining and he cracks little jokes to make them bearable. He understands that the class has a lot of work and is very fast paced so he tries to help his students as much as he can. He makes math a lot easier!
Great in detail descriptions of everything and did a great job of breaking things down.

Professor Carmichael gives many lectures throughout the course, but if you pay attention and take notes you will learn a lot from them and do well on quizzes and exams. To prepare for exams I would recommend doing the review quizzes he posts before each one and watching the teaching center reviews.

Online lectures were really funny and very informative; Carmichael was very kind and very responsive to emails. Workload is heavy but manageable since this is basically 2 classes in 1, stay on top of it and you'll be fine. Gave 20 late passes, unlimited attempts on quizzes, and 2 tries on all exams except final. Lots of extra credit.

You could tell he put a lot of effort into the online course. It was a lot of material but I felt that his lecture videos were extremely helpful. Its is definitely a difficult course and you have to constantly be on top of the work because it adds up and it is a lot. Also dont leave studying for the last minute like I did and you should be fine!

It's math so of course it's going to be difficult, but Mr. Carmichael is a very funny, understanding, and enjoyable teacher. He tries to make learning fun, and gives you lots of late passes. His exams are the same as the practice tests, and he's very easy to get in touch with outside of class.

His class was extremely organized. The prerecorded lectures were detailed and helpful. The class is pretty straightforward if you put effort into learning the material in the lectures. Professor Carmichael also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities.

Made online math bearable throughout the semester. There was definitely a sh*t ton of content that was reviewed, (it's trig and precalc) but I think I can survive calc now because I had Prof. Carmichael. I wish I had his class in-person.

Super funny guy, I find math incredibly boring but he made it interesting in the lectures. Class moves very fast (60ish homework problems a week on about 12 lecture videos with a weekly quiz and a progress exam every two weeks). Definitely feel more prepared going into calc 1.

Carmichael is super cool and really funny. He is fair and answers questions quickly. However, the homeworks are very time consuming and difficult compared to the lecturers. For a UF math professor, this guy is amazing.

I found him to be an okay professor. He is very willing to work with students if they have a conflict. Just be prepared to work your butt off. I, personally, didn't think his lectures were great. He seemed to explain things in a more complicated way than needed. Also, failing exams will kill your grade. It's 48% of your grade.
Hes a good professor. He answered my emails quickly and answered all of my questions. He tries to make it fun and it is. Very fair professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Carmichael is a great professor; you simply just have to work a lot in his class which is expected. Be dubious of other reviews saying this class is extremely hard - it's not and Carmichael is super reasonable and generous. I had great TA's and a great time in the class.

Prof Carmichael is an amazing professor. The class moves fast. I definitely felt like I was drowning, but that was completely my fault. Everything makes sense, but I procrastinated A LOT. If you have an asynchronous section, keep yourself on track, and you'll be fine. Super great and helpful guy.

Very detailed lectures with plenty of examples. Responds to emails very quickly and will offer any help you might need. Cares about your grade in the course and offers extra-credit for each lecture. Actually sent me an email reminding me to take the first exam after I had forgotten about it.

Lectures and homework sometimes take a lot of time to complete, and you do 3 modules a week. Carmichael is amazing though, really cares about his students and explains concepts well and is always there to help. Quizzes are open note, just pretty frequent. Exams are like the quizzes, but doable if you study for them. Made me like math more.

Prof. Carmichael is an amazing professor who clearly cares for his students and for math. He explains everything in detail and is always accessible at any hour and usually responds in 30 minutes. His quizzes are very similar to the exams, and he gives us plenty of resources to prepare for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's math at UF. That's all that really needs to be said. It is way harder than it should be. You're going to have to put in a lot of work to be successful and get an A. The exams can make you or break you.

MAC 1147 is a very fast paced course due to its nature, so ignore anyone saying he goes too fast. Prof. Carmichael is an amazing teacher who explains things in a way that is super easy to understand, and if you have any problems he will help you after class or in office hours. The exams he helps make are very fair. Highly recommend him.

He is a funny guy who clearly loves math. He makes fair exams and I didn't mind this class. Math is not my thing and I better than I thought. Study edge is a must in my opinion because they teach tips and tricks Carmichael dismisses in lecture.

Learned a lot and he is good at explaining things clearly. Tons of homework but its very helpful to prepare for exams. Discussion period is very helpful but lecture attendance is not super important. Sometimes gives extra credit for showing up to lecture so it never hurts. Hes a very chill guy and this was an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I didn't go to lecture after the first week and just copied notes from the uploaded slides and did the homework (I did go to discussion periods though- that's necessary). I already knew the material from high school so it wasn't that hard. If you don't know the material, go to lecture. And use Broward's resources to help study for exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He goes through his lectures VERY fast, so watch the recorded lectures if possible. He makes the material super complicated, and he does not give any shortcuts or tips to help understand the material. He does not do a great job preparing his students for his exams either.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't mandatory, but if you don't go, you probably won't do well. The tests and quizzes aren't too hard if you study and go to discussions. Weekly homework is assigned, which pretty accurately reflects the test material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Carmichael is a solid teacher. I already knew the material but didnt score high enough on the ALEKs test so I had to take it. If you prepare for the exams it will not be too hard.

Gives extra cred on random lecture dates. Often will not be able to cover all material within the period, but always uploads his slides after. If you're confused, he'll pause lecture to go back and explain stuff. Exams are tricky, so make sure to pay attention, do tb hw, WA, and watch Teaching Center practice exam vids to get an idea of test q's.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures are okay, he goes through them fast so if you are taking notes leave space between but he wont upload the notes until days after :/ Use the lectures to supplement textbook and WA hw but be ready to learn stuff outside as well. Hard exams in the class, make sure you go to office hours and tutoring, you're gonna need it!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Went to every lecture in the beginning of the year, but he overcomplicated the material, so I started watching the online lectures which helped more. Very content heavy. Lots of work and time in order to get an okay grade

This is a really hard math class so you will have to go home and teach yourself a lot of content. The exams are really difficult and the professor doesn't do a great job of covering what will be on there.

Lectures are extremely detailed and very helpful if you go, but you dont HAVE TO. Very accessible outside of class. Helpful during office hours. Sometimes gives extra credit during lectures, so you should probably go.

I absolutely loved Dr. Cenko! She is one of my favorite professors here at UF simply because of how kind she is to her students and her passion for public health is clear. The class is simple (I took it in-person) and the requirements to get an A are clear. She is also always open to feedback, which I love in a professor.

Cenko is the best professor I've had at UF! I took two classes with her in Fall and she was amazing in both. She cares for the students and wants us to learn. I messed up an assignment and instead of giving me 0 points she offered to meet and review the module together to make sure I understood. She was also very helpful with a rec letter. 10/10

Great professor. Things felt a bit disorganized but it's obvious she cares about her students and the subject matter. Basically everything involves a group-project, which wasn't my favorite. It is such an easy class, only 2 quizzes are graded and there are no exams. Grading was a bit slow at times, but that was mainly the TA, not Dr. Cenko.

Dr. Cenko is AMAZING! She truly cares about her students and you can tell she really enjoys teaching. Class was super easy with very few assignment outside of class even though the class is hybrid. This class was heavily based off of group projects but grading was very easy as long as there was effort.

Dr. Cenko was amazing for this course and I'd 100% recommend her. She gives very useful study guides and genuinely listens to student feedback. Class is mainly easy group projects. Tests are very easy as long as you do the study guide & watch the lectures online.

Dr. Cenko is a wonderful woman. She replies to emails quickly and is super helpful with questions. I didn't care much for the subject of the class, but she made it interesting. Grades very fair. I recommend her!

Dr. Cenko is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about public health and teaching it understandably to her students. We had a hybrid class that met once a week and made our semester-long groups at the beginning of the semester. If you're looking for a light workload class that you'll enjoy, this is the one. Would definitely take her again!

This was a hybrid class meeting once a week. We often had very easy group project assignments every week that we would talk about in class. Dr. Cenko is very passionate about public health and genuinely cares about her students.

If I could take another class with Dr. Cenko, I absolutely would. She is hands down one of the nicest and best professors I've had not just in PHHP but in my entire time at UF! Probably one of the best decisions I made was taking HSC3502 with her over Hanson. Everything about this class from tests to projects was handled so great. 1000+/10 for sure
Best option for this class! She is so kind and caring!!
Love her! Super sweet and super easy tests! Wants everyone to get an A and will talk with you if you didnt do good on an exam! (took HSC3502)

Dr. Cenko was very kind and professional. She answers emails quickly & you can tell she genuinely cares about her students. Weekly quizzes and 3 exams that are pretty straight forward as long as you keep up with the readings and material. The rest of the coursework is mainly group assignments and then occasional individual assignments. 10/10 !!!!

I am so sad that she left UF. She is honestly one of the nicest and caring people I've met. Her class was full of discussion where people could freely say and think without judgement. You can tell that she put a lot of effort into her lectures and the assignments were simple enough to teach the material without overwhelming you.

Prof. Wagner was such a joy. I think the class would have been better if more people responded to her questions, but it was pretty easy and she made her assignment expectations clear. She did always take a point or two off on the group projects but she left feedback on ways to improve that I think was valid. Definitely the best option for MMC2604!

She's one of the sweetest people ever! She's incredibly accommodating, understanding and flexible. She gives really good and interesting lectures and tries to engage class discussion. There's a lot of readings, supplemental materials but if you find your way to more easily go through it you should be fine. I'd definitely take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The difficulty of this class honestly depends on the TAs. I got stuck with very harsh graders, so understand what their expectations are. Dr. Wagner is great and tries to keep students engaged. She listens to the needs of the class and adjusts her lectures based on that. I'd recommend going to the office hours before exams and the short essays.

Lectures are enjoyable and workload is minimal. 4 exams that primarily cover the content from the online textbook on Connect. Do not skip the short "lecture extensions" as it is common to be asked about them on an exam. Do the extra credit and you should get an easy A

Probably the worst class I've taken in the business school. Professor Schulz only reads off of a script during lectures and does not provide any of her PowerPoints to the class. She gives 4 exams for some reason despite there not being enough content to warrant it. The class is not difficult, it is simply a waste of time.
She was so great! Cares about her students and keeps lectures fun, up-to-date, and relevant. 10/10 would recommend. Always responded quickly to emails and is very helpful and kind.

Cece is one of my favorite professors because she puts so much effort into her lectures and really make the experience fun (if you have a good attitude). I would say most people can get a B or higher simply by watching lectures. I would say it is pretty hard to get an A in the class because so many of the exam questions are tricky. I learned a ton!

I can't say enough about this professor! I loved her class. She's enthusiastic, funny, and kind. You can tell that she cares about you and wants you to succeed. Probably the only professor with enjoyable lectures. Exams were straight forward. Assignments were very reasonable. Wish all classes could be like this. Thanks, Professor Schultz!

Cece's exams are pretty straightforward. She keeps her class current and I highly recommend watching the lecture, lecture extensions, and doing the LearnSmart. If I could do one thing differently about the class, I would definitely pay more attention to the lecture extensions instead of treating them as an afterthought.
Poor delivery. The content is redundant, lectures poor and she's more concerned with her political views than with preparing content. Reading from a powerpoint is not teaching.

This class is super interesting, fairly easy and the professor is funny and very kind. Exams aren't super tough but are written off lectures so don't skip those! also exams and some zoom meetings are scheduled in advance which can be a pain if you are 100% online and need the flexibility.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a great professor. This is my favorite class I've taken at uf because she's so passionate and funny. read the textbook before taking the exam. Group project at the end of the semester not too hard. If you arent doing great on the exams make sure to do the Extra credit paper

Just read the chapters 1 day before and make sure you know the vocabulary. There are 4 exams (50 questions each) composing 200 out of the 300 possible points. There is a presentation about a current event article(10pts), a group project(30pts) , 3 pop quizzes (5 points each) and 40 points ( 10 each) of online HW and attending retail bash (5pts)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: I never know what to expect! Every day in class is something completely different. You can tell she puts in a lot of thought and effort in making her lectures interesting and FUNNY! Youll definitely learn a TON about he retail industry in this section. I know I feel more prepared now to head out into the field. Worked hard but definitely worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cece is a great teacher who tries to make every topic fun and interesting. She really knows so much about the retail industry so you know you are getting correct information. There are only a few assignments and pop quizzes but overall not too difficult!

It is a good class. Attendance is mandatory. I recommend going to any workshops available to make up for absences. The speakers are there for the most part to recruit people so you mostly learn about their companies than anything else. If you want to get an internship in retailing this is the class to take.

Great one credit class and great if you're interested in retailing.  There are guest speakers every class and it's easy to get an A.  All you have to do is attend a luncheon (great food), write a paper on one of the speaker's presentation (3-5 pgs) and attend a focus group.
Course is a total waste.  Amazing that someone with no apparent qualifications other than thinking she's funny is allowed to teach.
I got a lot of this course. It's really beneficial and an easy way to get an A. Cecilia is very friendly and really cares about her students.

Doesn't have much direct involvement in teaching the course, but Cece finds great guest lecturers and can set you up with some truly great opportunities.  The Seminar is a very, very useful one-credit course, and you'll get out of it ten times what you put in.

This was probably the first time I actually enjoyed a Spanish class and it was all because of Hadder! He was hilarious, and always made it a point to get to know everyone in the class. He was also a super fair grader. The only reason I got an A- instead of an A is because I didn't really study for anything in the class, so I'd recommend practicing!

My favorite professor at UF by far. He is very laid back, loves teaching, and is very in tune with his students' lives and interests. He is very understanding if you miss class and will do everything he can to help you learn tough topics. He makes learning Spanish so easy and fun. I looked forward to going to his class every day!

This professor is the best I've had so far. He's so helpful and caring. Spanish can be difficult but he makes it fun and I actually looked forward to going to class. 100% recommend. Thinking about continuing further with Spanish. This prof makes getting an A very doable.

Prof Ceballos is one of the best teachers I've ever had at UF. He genuinely cares about his students and wants to see us succeed. He goes out of his way to make class fun! I honestly can't say enough good things about him.
While this class has a major online component with quizzes that werent very enjoyable, its fairly easy overall. Professor Ceballos was great! I loved going to his class.
Very reasonable prof - chill class and wants every student to succeed. He's pretty funny too. Definitely a no-stress course overall and easy to get an A if you study.

He offers little to no explanations; one time he literally said no when I asked him to go over a problem. His lectures are all over the place and impossible to comprehend. I have to rely heavily on the textbook, yet it's not enough and he doesn't offer supplementary learning besides that, classwork, and homework. Avoid him if you can.
Isn't very good at explaining concepts, easily frustrated when students ask questions.

He seems to be a nice guy, but he is definitely not a good teacher. His lectures are unorganized and sometimes incomprehensible. Since he is not much of a help, the course becomes unnecessarily more difficult, especially if you are new to the concept of mathematical proofs. Be prepared to grind the textbook. Please avoid him if you can.
His teaching makes the class fun, but the course itself is slightly confusing.
I did well in the class. He is a good professor, however, the class will take work and a lot of studying and is not easy.

Cenzer makes this class very easy!  Don't read the book, it will just confuse you.  Cenzer's lectures are very clear and show you exactly how to do the test questions.  At times he loses himself and stands muttering to himself, but this minor flaw is greatly overshadowed by his greatness as a professor.  Take Cenzer for Differential Equations!

Cenzer is a really nice guy.  Keep up with the HW and you'll be good.  He doesn't try to trick you on tests and he grades fair.  He drops a test so you can escape the final.  You lose 1 of 300 points each day you miss class.
he is a very nice guy. exams are easy. almost the same as review.  but his teaching is different. he confuses me sometimes.

if you are going to take this class, you better make sure you have this teacher, he has been one of my favorite teachers so far. VERY VERY clear with his lectures, made this class really easy, 4 exams (final optional), exams questions come exactly from suggested HW problems, knew every student's name, very kind and encouraging!
Excellent professor. Explains material very well, no surprises on exams. Easy to get a B or B+, harder to get an A. Very understanding professor.
Easy if you go to class, but never terribly exciting

Seems like a normal guy compared to many in the math department. Nice and helpful person, but one of the worst lecturers. He isn't prepared, mutters to the board, you can't understand him, searches notes frantically, forgets how to do proofs, just stands drumming his fingers on the desk. Each lecture is improvised with him.
Cenzer is very confusing in his explanations. However, the homework helps a lot and his exams are similar to the practice ones he gives. Final was really similar to practice exam.
I had him for both linear algebra and abstract algebra.  His lectures were often impossible to understand, but his exams were, with only one exception, pretty simple.  He gets my recommendation.

Nicest professor I have ever had. Really cares about his students, explains material clearly, and you can tell he enjoys his career. Exams are from the homework and study problems, no surprises. Fair grader and there was an awesome curve at the end of the course. Would take another course with him.
He's a very nice guy. Very approachable. He is still the typical math person, who fumbles with words. He did a good job, and wanted everyone to get an A, but you had to earn it. Highly recommend him.

I really liked the class, but I would have enjoyed it much more if he weren't the teacher. He had a hard time explaining things to the class because he understood it and we didn't. SUPER nice guy though.

Very intelligent, very nice guy.  However, sometimes it seems that he's so smart that he can't understand why the class isn't following the material, and seems to get frustrated if we don't understand.  But, his grading is very fair and the exam questions consist of some of the more simple concepts.

he is a really smart guy and pretty nice in class but he honestly teaches like he doesnt realize that he's been doing logic fo 40 years and this is our first. the homework is hard because there is no solution manual to check it with but he tests on the easiest stuff from each section. fair grader
Very fair, and usually lowers the scale.  He's very smart and sometimes thinks too fast, but he's a good teacher.

Definitely a lot of HW but it was all very relevant and useful. I feel like I've significantly improved my french language skills. Quizzes are pretty easy if you study and she gives many opportunities for extra credit. Gives half points back on all writing exams.

I would strongly discourage anyone who is not genuinely interested in learning French from taking this course. To those who are, however, I would highly recommend it: Professor Ciesco designed a really efficient online system that covers a lot of material for just one semester. The assignments can get pretty tedious but there's plenty of groupwork

I was scared by the reviews here but this class was great. Yes there is a lot of homework but it certainly did not take up 5 hours of my week. I have a very intense class schedule and this one is the least of my worries. VERY accommodating whenever I emailed her for an extension.  In my opinion, if you have to take a language this is the way to go.

Expected to learn a couple of months' worth of content... in 5 days. Absolutely unbelievable. If you actually want to learn a language, this is not the way. Taking this made learning seem unbearable. Avoid if you can.

This is a very intensive class, but the professor is very accommodating. You have to do 5 talk abroads and I think 5 group assignments a semester. The homework is very intensive and the tests are difficult, but they always address what was taught in class. You will pretty much be doing homework everyday for the semester, but it's a 5 credit class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: A+ in both Beginner French classes. Ask if you need help. She always gave extensions if I needed, just ask before the due date day. Yes, there is lots of homework, but its not bad. Most of the questions have a "check my work" button. 4 exams w one drop (+2 oral- try to lead the convo) first 3 cover 2 chapters, last is only one- its the easiest.

This class was genuinely insane. The amount of work was too much in a way that doesn't work for a beginner language class. I couldn't actually learn any french because I was too busy doing 15 assignments each week. Of the very few assignments she has to grade, barely any of them have been graded thus far (class ends next week.) Avoid if possible!

I wanted to take french so that I could study abroad, but instead of actually learning and digesting the material, I find myself having to rush through the homework just to complete it on time. There's just an overwhelming amount of work, that I can't even focus on my other courses. Take another professor if you can.

Bro, this class is beyond measurable in the amount of work she has us doing. 13 homework assignments in a week plus an exam due Sunday? She makes it very clear that its a 5 credit course, but come on. For a beginning french class, there's absolutely no way to manage your time properly and still maintain an A average. Avoid at all costs if possible.

First off, professor Ciesco is a very kind professor and she is passionate about what she does. My complaint here is the ridiculous amount of work being given on a weekly basis. The whole formatting of the course and homework load is unbearable and almost impossible to learn at a pace for beginners of two chapters per week with 10 homework
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The amount of work she gives us in the online class is downright insane. 13 assignments due in a 3 day period plus a paragraph essay in french, an audio recording of us speaking french for 2 minutes-and its only the first week of beginning french. Be careful if you're taking other classes, you may fall behind if this isnt your main priority.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Ciesco is an incredibly kind and funny French teacher. I had a great experience in high school and was afraid I wouldn't find another teacher as great, but Prof. Ciesco met all my expectations. There is a lot of textbook reading due before each class, but other than that, the class is easy if you study and participate in lectures.

Madame Ciesco is the nicest french teacher I've ever had. She is super funny and very interested in the student's life and making sure everyone is always doing well. She is super helpful in office hours and loves to see everyone succeed.

I took her for 3rd level French Grammar, so she spoke in French the majority of the class, but she was still a very understanding/caring professor. Mostly graded on inclass compositions, discusssions, and quizzes. Very kind and even brought our class macaroons on our last day. One of the best professors I've ever taken here at UF

Madame Ciesco is incredible. Her classes are difficult and she expects a lot out of you, but is very caring and fair. It's true that sometimes she can come off harsh, but it's because she's more interested in helping you improve than coddling you. She is just an amazing person in general, and even brought in French snacks for our class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: This professor was awful! She doesn't teach material. Study the book. If you have the option, don't take her section!

Definitely my favorite french teacher so far!! Nathalie is lots of fun and very entertaining. She's also VERY willing to help outside of the classroom, and will work with you to help you succeed. She does expect a lot from her students though, so come prepared to class- and be ready to participate! :)

A truly great teacher. I have learned so much from her. She is very accessible to students and helpful. Not an easy A, but not too hard to get an A. Make sure to be prepared for class, though. I highly recommend her!

Her course is hard, but that's because she expects a lot from you. So far, I really enjoy this class, and she is pretty energetic and really amusing. I think she is one of the best professors you could have for French. You'll learn so much! :)
This class was tons of work, but my French improved dramatically.  Shes one of the nicest professors I've had here and though she's tough it's worth it.

Mademoiselle Ciesco is one of the best french instructors I've had at UF, next to Madame Cesar-Lee and Abdou Yaro. She is very helpful and easy to talk to. She may seem tough in the classroom but all she wants is for you to succeed and be more proficient. I highly recommend her!

I was used to really easy french classes in high school and this was the first time that i had to work me ass off in french.  I think I'm gonna get like a B but still, when you're used to gettign A's this is a rude awakening.

I'm taking her class right now, and I hate the class! The class is so boring, everyone hates it! It takes her AGES to return any graded work, so that when you get an assignment back with a C on it, you don't even remember what is was about! All we do is GRAMMAR, and you'd better understand what all those grammatical words, because if you don't she
Not a very nice lady. Maybe it's just the french thing but I know lots of pleasant french people and she is not one of them.
Nathalie is awesome.
No Comments

M. Ciesco expects hard work and doesn't take well to slackers.  However, if you give her a chance, you will find that she is very intelligent, helpful, engaging, and understanding.  She is always available outside of class if you need the help.  Certainly not an easy class, but worth the work!
Hardest french course taken!  Excessive amount of work! If you don't fit as one of her pets, BE AWARE of your ability to get a passing grade.
Very nice, engaging, and fun.  Learned alot in that class.  If it was challenging and unclear, well, hey, she's French so that's to be expected!!

She is very funny, but can be unclear at times. She made our syllabus easier then the required coursework so that was good, but she won't ever switch in to english, even if something is highly difficult, which can be frustrating.

Best professor I've had at UF. If you have the opportunity to take her at a decent time slot, do a favor for your GPA and take FAR 2 with Dosch. Very tough exams, but extremely fair and she prepares you well. Everything you need to know is in her lecture slides and in the assigned homework problems.
Best teacher in UF choose her 100%
A simple Pass/Fail class, definitely not difficult at all, just show up. Dosch is lovely and very charismatic, clearly cares a lot about working with students.

Great public speaker. Nice. Funny. Goes above and beyond. Very caring, if you're going through anything personal she will help A LOT. Amazing at explaining content. Very fair. Takes one week to grade. Send you an email if shes concerned about you not passing. Simply deserves every award and raise out there FR
Pass/Fail Course; Very much geared towards accounting majors only; Prof is great

Professor Dosch is the best! I am an accounting major who took the ACG2391 elective for fun, and it was extremely worthwhile. I am actually looking forward to FAR 1 in the future, since she is the professor. If you have a chance, definitely take Exploring Careers in Accounting and get to know Professor Dosch.
The ratings speak for themselves, 10/10 professor who goes above and beyond.

If Cindy Dosch has a million fans, then I am one of them. If Cindy Dosch has ten fans, then I am one of them. If Cindy Dosch has only one fan then that is me. If Cindy Dosch has no fans, then that means I am no longer on earth. If the world is against Cindy Dosch, then I am against the world.
Best FAR 1 professor at UF. Exams are definitely hard but her lectures/practice problems are very representative of the exams and make sure you are prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Dosch is the best professor I've had at UF. She is incredibly good at explaining, very knowledgable, and truly wants you to succeed. Take advantage of Piazza, she answers all questions very thoroughly. The key to doing good on all of the quizzes and exams is to do all of the homework problems at least 2 times.
Go to every class and definitely do the optional homework, which is not really optional if you don't want to fail. Great lecturer and cares about her students' learning.

Professor Dosch is the reason why I switched into the Accounting program. Haven't had a better professor in my life. Taking her for FAR2 right now and it's great as well. Do the homework problems and her lecture examples over and over again and you'll do fine. Get Automatic Tutoring if you need some extra help. If a seat is open, take it.

This is a difficult class but Dosch is very clear about the exam content and gives you everything you need to do well, no outside help necessary. Her class lecture example handouts were the most helpful for me, and doing the homework before each quiz and marking the most difficult ones to study for the exams will help tremendously.
She's sweet, funny and really wants you to learn. I was worried having not done the best in Financial Accounting, but it is completely different, and if you pay attention in class, you will do well.

Dosch is the best professor in the business/accounting tracks. She cares about students, teaches incredibly well and is very fair. Having had her for FAR1 and 2, I can say if you do the homework, pay attention in class, and study, you will be 100% prepared. No trick questions, expectations are extremely fair. FAR sucks but she makes it tolerable.

Professor Dosch was definitely the best professor I've ever had. I am a finance major but am required to take this course, and the material is extremely tough. However, she offers partial credit and teaches you how to understand a problem incredibly. Achieving an A is doable, just takes a lot of extra work. She is super goofy and can make acg fun!

This class was super challenging. The material is a nightmare. Prof Dosch was very open to helping outside class and understood we have issues... like the hurricanes. I was worried that she would not curve or adjust any grades since she was new. Thankfully, she did curve and most of the class ended with a C or better. Take this professor!

Great professor! She made challenging topics understandable and created a course that allowed you to secure an A without making it impossible. Her grades are based on three exams, with half of the exam being free response questions, and quizzes. The exam MC is pretty difficult.

Cindy Dosch is the go-to lecturer for accounting at UF. She is very kind and makes as much time as possible outside of class to help students with their academic needs. She is clear and detailed when explaining material in her lectures. If you are concerned with accounting and worry about taking the wrong professor, taking Dosch is the best choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was Dosch's first semester at UF and in comparison to other professors, I thought she was a great lecturer! DO THE HOMEWORK PROBLEMS. I also used Automatic Tutoring to nail down the conceptual parts and obtain more practice. She is a fair grader and is willing to help you outside of class if need be. Quizzes and 3 exams are your only grades.
She was great at explaining concepts. Quizzes and exams were fair. Provided great examples in class especially excel sheets that exemplified concepts. Definitely try to secure a seat in her class.
Amazing lecturer

Professor Dosch is new, and already likely the best professor the Fisher school has to offer. Her lectures are clear, her exams and quizzes fair, and her office hours helpful. She goes the extra mile in providing excel sheets that run certain problems for you, or explain concepts in greater detail than what was allowed in class. 

Do hw as practice

This class was very tough in the beginning and had a harsh learning curve, but Spence made me such a better writer in the end. She will be very tough on you, but listen to everything she says, and you will become such a better writer because of it. I started the class with a 58 and ended with a B, and three papers were published! Go to her for help
Really tough but you will learn a lot from her. I went from a 44 in the beginning of the class to a B. Do Not Give Up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was by far the hardest class I have taken. Spence gives out 2x more assignments than other JOU3101 professors. I recommend Ross. Spence was difficult to communicate with; more than half my class dropped out.

Prof. Spence is the best. I am so happy I had her as my lab instructor. She is so encouraging and really cares about the success of her students. She is also super accessible and willing to help outside of class. She gives great feedback and honestly just wants to see her students do well. Don't let this course intimidate you!
told me i was incoherent and when i begged for help he refused. i did good on everything except the final and i failed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's alright, test can be easy if you payed attention in class.

He's a really nice guy, but a bit of a pushover so his class is REALLY easy. Go to reviews before the tests - he'll pretty much give you the answers. If you participate in class and go to his office hours, he'll go easy on you when grading your papers.

If you are a poly sci major or you are going for the Political Campaigning Certificate, TAKE THIS CLASS! There is no easier class at UF. All the lectures are on powerpoints that he emails you. He takes random attendance. All his tests, including the midterm, he reviews the class before. In his reviews he practically gives you the answers! Take it!
Take him! you learn a lot and if you put in a little effort you can get an A. He does go over everything before the exam. Takes random attendance so go.

Boring teacher but easy class and very helpful.  Gives random attendance so you should go to class.  Before every test he gives a review and basically tells you every question that will be on the test as well as the essay question, so it is very easy to do well if you just study for 15 minutes.  Definitely recommend taking this teacher!!!!

Likes participation. takes random attendance. tests are multiple choice, gives good review though. really listens to students and is open to debates and concerns. really easy class and cool professor. Attend class to get participation points.

Good class, first half was great but second half was not my favorite. Tests are ambiguous and difficult. Study hard; be ready for anything and give as much detail on free response questions (70-90% of questions are free response on exams).

Course was hybrid, with lectures recorded online and discussions in class once a week. It's an interesting course and I've come to like it. The book is a must because the lectures are based on the book. It's very helpful in clarifying concepts because the lectures do not cover everything.
Great teacher! She is very nice and her lecture notes are mostly from the textbook.
Dr. Prins is an incredible teacher! Epidemiology is awesome to begin with, but she mak
Good epidemiology professor. Helpful, and cute too.  Overall satisfactory.
Not a huge fan of this woman, but the class was okay!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Keeps my interest and brings clinical life experiences to her teachings. Highly recommended if interested in becoming an Adult Nurse Practitioner at UF in the College of Nursing. She is a faculty who truly listens & understands her students! Glad to have Dr Figueroa-Haas as my advisor & looking forward to continuing in this program. BSN-DNP student
Dr Haas is very knowledgable in so many fields of nursing & personable/kind to all her students. So glad I had her last term.

It was a difficult & disruptive class for Dr Haas to teach, but she did the best she could with what she had to deal with..a new unprepared,cooker,lab professor in 3067L,who did not cover the required objectives for her course and the multitude of rude, immature students that kept talking while Haas lectured. Hands up to Dr Haas for getting us out!

I learned so very much from Dr Haas, my experence on the Unit was unbelievable & life long rewarding. I hope Dr Haas nevers leaves UF/CON...she is such an asset to the college. She is so smart, caring & fair to all her students. You can tell she loves teaching & working with us. Thank you Dr Haas for working so hard with us, We ALL love you!
I had her for clinicals and she was awesome.  She's funny and very nice.

Dr Haas is an exciting, enthusiasic,awesome professor that keeps your attention at ALL times during lectures. I've learned so much from her...love the stories! It's obvious that she loves her students, faculty & job. I hope to be just like her one day! Thank you for being such a great role model for me. I will never forget you. YOU ROCK MY WORLD!
No Comments
Dr. Haas is super helpful and enthusiastic about everything! She makes the class super fun and interesting. Awesome professor! =]

Do not take GLY1102 at UF. The structure of this course is incredibly confusing. You are required to download an archaic software to your computer, on which all of your assignments are located. None of your grades are recorded on canvas. Information about the course is hard to find seeing as it is spread out in various places. This class is a mess.

Don't take this class if you want an easy A; you won't get one! The software is so outdated and ridiculous to deal with. The professor is non-existent and makes it clear he does not want to be bothered. Beware! I strongly urge that you take something else!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Easy A class. the program he uses is a bit difficult at first when you don't know how to use it. once you figure it out you're set. i did all my work ahead of time. chapter quiz weekly (you can google), 2 projects that are small but you google everything, practice midterm and final and actual midterm and final (again found online) Definitely take!

By far the worst class (with the WORST professor) I have taken at UF. I took this class because it met the requirements for a credit I needed, but it was such a mistake. The program used for this class is literally impossible to figure out, and Dr. Ciesielski makes it very clear he doesn't want to offer help or be bothered. Don't take this class!!!

The Faulkner software he uses is super outdated and hard to use. It's very obvious that he doesn't like to be bothered, and the customer service for the software is the worst I've ever encountered.
