Her lectures could've been better in several ways but overall she wasn't a bad professor. I would just recommend going to Tutoring Zone to prepare for the exams.
Worst teacher ever, she is terrible at explaining new concepts and she goes 1 million miles an hour! She is very hard to understand also bc she has a huge accent!

I dont know what people are talking about on here. SHE IS HARD. No one i knew was doing well. the stuff she taught us, was WAY easier than what she actually put on the test. and if you get a crappy TA, your SCREWED. Take someone else, she makes its harder than it needs to be!

Just turn everything in! Lots of material but not impossible. You cant understand her but it doesnt really matter as long as you copy the notes. DONT MISS DISCUSSION! she take random lecture attendance, just make sure youre there or someone you know is that will turn a quiz in for you
Chui was really sweet and helpful, but I learned the most by making use of her office hours, not in lecture.
Chui is a crazy lady who you just laugh at sometimes. She is a pretty good teacher and knows her stuff. The tests are not too bad if you just study the review posted online and do the old exam.

Quirky woman who can make students laugh without her knowing.  Slight difficulties with presentation materials.  Emphasized hers and TAs' office hours.  Lectures had random quizzes to check for attendance.  TA does much of actual comprehension for students.

HATE pre-calc,LOVE Prof. Chui! She's aware that her class is a pre-req for most majors so she tries to keep it simple. Extra credit if you complete all but two of the quizzes, and your lowest test/quiz grade is dropped. I'm terrible in math, but with the drops and (free) private tutoring, I pulled an A-. TAKE THIS WITH HER!

Can barely understand her during lectures so I would rec. sitting up front. If you are decent at math you will do fine in this class. You can drop your lowest exam, quiz, and HW assignment. Definately would rec. her for Precalc.

Chui is a very good teacher. Any type of math at UF is hard, and pretty tricky. You have to stay on top of the work, and really study if you want to get a good grade, but excellent person and teacher!!! Tutoring Zone is very, very, very helpful for this course!!!
She is super nice and explains everything very carefully. Her accent isn't that bad if you listen. She's very fair

I had no clue what was going on in her class. She made a lot of mistakes and had students correcting her, she usually makes odd comments, and she has little empathy. She has poor classroom control but likes to call out students for talking.
She teaches the material well, but sometimes she makes it more difficult than necessary. She was nice in class, but her accent sometimes made it hard to understand. She's fairly nice.
Not easy to understand through her accent. Not very helpful at office hours.
Ms. Chui's class is extremely easy...partially because I already know the lectures lol.  She is so nice and friendly.  Amazing teacher and person!!

Prof. Chui is the coolest. She is fair in her grading and as long as you don't try to get away with anything she will give you a fair grade. And she always gives a review sheet before the exams and some questions are very similar or even the same.

She just follows the lecture notes. You can buy the whole semester's notes for about 30 dollars but she leaves some blank spaces for you to fill in during class just so you attend. Never had to use the book. You actually have to put in a few hours a day of your time and effort if you want to get anything higher than a D in this class.

I love chui! She is really nice and a great teacher. Her tests are fair and she gives a review sheet before each test. Do the review sheet and you'll get do well on the tests. Go to class for the participation grade and before tests for hints on what to expect. Take any math with her and you won't regret it.

Best calc 3 teacher at UF. For the first time she puts her class lectures online for you to print prior to class. Go to class, take the quizzes seriously, and copy down her examples and you will do fine. Her test are almost always some variation of an old hw or lecture problem. I missed a B+ by half a question but most of the class got A's.
Best Calc3 prof at UF!

She's amazing.  She's the sweetest lady and she always takes the time to stop if anyone has a question.  She makes sure the material is very clear and her tests and quizes aren't hard if you go to class.  Definitely recommended.

She is very nice and very helpful. She explains the material very well and goes over a lot of examples in class. She allows one test drop. Her quizzes are very similar to the examples in class so pay attention. Going to class is highly recommeded since she sometimes uses similar examples on test as well.

Chui is a great teacher. My recommendations to you is jus tod practice problems as much as you can from the book. Go to class because she takes problems from her notes as well. Most importantly is take advantage of her office hours, and any questions you have go to her, she will do anything to help you understand. Just put time into the class.
Two words - the best.  Very clear, makes calculus 3 so easy.  Exam questions come from the notes or homework.  And she's just so nice!!!

Mrs. Chui is one of the best professors I've ever had. Calculus 3 can be tricky during certain sections, but Mrs. Chui is fair in her curriculum. Her tests often follow her examples in class and the homework she assigns. The best tip I can recommend to anyone who takes her class is go to office hours for assistance, she's always willing to help!

Chui's a great teacher. Her lectures are very clear and she gives plenty of examples to help with the homework. Her tests are fairly straightforward and, while they aren't exactly easy, if you study they're very manageable. The only complaint I have is that she writes REALLY fast, so it's hard to keep up in your notes while paying attention.

Ms. Chui is so amazing!  She teaches so well and clearly you don't even need to read the chapter to do homework.  The quizes are there just to make sure you come to class, but you get so many drops, they really just help boost your grade.  Her tests are pretty easy, she grades fairly.  And the most important thing--she's SO nice!

Ms. Chui is the best calc teacher! Her lectures are clear and straightforward.  She gives 10 quizzes instead of test, and then a final.  If you do the homework and attend class, then no problem.  Also she gives extra credit at the end for attendance.  GO TO OFFICE HOURS! She is so nice and will help with any questions you have, and hints for quizze
Shes really nice and the class isnt too hard.  Put some effort into the quizzes and youre good to go.

Very helpful, puts aside a lot of time for office hours.  She takes attendance but it only effects your grade for extra credit in the end.  Her quizzes are easy if you study before hand.  But the mandatory final was wickedly difficult.
everything was easy and fair in her class, best calc3 prof by far. easy A
Best professor ever!  Had a wonderful time in her class.  She grades fairly.  Tests were not too hard.  Always willing to help.  Would def. recommend taking her class.

she is a great great teacher. VERY helpful. her office is always packed with students during office hours. very nice. just make sure you go to class everyday. she takes attendance for bonus points and doesnt have sympathy for those who dont show up. very fair, very reasonable. she is the best calc 3 teacher ever!
Just awesome.

Email sent from her after her third test because there's no partial credit: The drop date is coming up soon, someone told me it's this  SUnday.  IF that is true and you need to make a decision, please  come get the test and if you need to, you can discuss it with me  if there are not too many students waiting to do the same  already.
Her quizzes can be tough.  Good overall professor.

Mrs. Chui is awesome!  So nice, go to class because she'll give you extra credit.  All you need to do is do your homework and pay attention in class, and you're guaranteed an A.  Missing a few classes is okay, but its best if you go.  Tests are not hard either, a lot of the same concepts in the homework shows up on the tests, so do the hw!
total hottie! and she's very very nice very fair grader
She is awesome! She always makes sure everyone understands and is really nice.
she's awesome, and kind of gives really nice exam reviews.....hint hint
These comments are right- she really is a great teacher! She is so helpful and makes sure that you understand what you are doing as you go. If you can, take her for math and you will be very happy.
BEST MATH TEACHER EVER!!! Sometimes goes fast, but she makes diff eq easy for anyone!

Chui is the best math teacher I've ever had, probably the best teacher ever.She is incredibly good at what she does, which is communicate complex mathematical complex with a clarity that almost makes it fun to attend class.Her incredibly warm and caring personality shine through despite the rather dry subject matter.  Make every effort to take her.
She's and incredibly caring teacher! Probably one of the nicest math teachers you can have in gollege.
Chui is the best math teacher you will ever have in college. Take her if you can.
most amazing teacher ever. she is such a sweetheart. she cares about her students. she is like an elementary school teacher teaching college math. TAKE HER OVER ANYONE ELSE!
AWESOME...the other ratings are NOT AT ALL exaggerations. Actually teaches the subject unlike some others and has good focus.
SUCH AN AWE$OME TEACHER!!!! TAKE WHATEVER SHE TEACHES!! She makes calc3 and diff eq look like algebra 1. god i wish she taught all my classes.

Thank god she teaches diff eq now.. and I wish I had her for calc 3.. but im stuck with some other guy. Oh well. She is awesome and if youre going to take mac2313 or map2302 then you better get her section. she's so nice and makes other professors look like dimwits.
She's amazing.
She was an amazingly helpful and caring teacher. She is one of those teachers who you can't help but like. She is kindof easy, but you learn most of the stuff you need to. Overall A+

I'm still in this class but I know I will get an A. Except for the 2nd and 3rd quiz (I got 0 and 5.5 respectively) I got a perfect score on every single quiz/test.(28/20 on test 2) That doesn't mean you can slack off though. I study a lot! wait...test 3 is tomorrow. oops
She is amazing. Nicest professor i have had. She holds reviews before tests so there is no reason not to do well. she leaves no one behind and always takes questions
Loved her, nicest person I have ever met and the best teacher. She'll make you love calc and want to be a math major
she was the best teacher i've ever had. so helpful, it'simpossible not to grasp the concepts!

Mrs. Chui is by far one of the best Calc teachers at UF. Her lectures are very thorough, she's always willing to help in and outside of her office hours. Her tests were challenging but not impossible. Do the homework and you'll be fine!
Very helpful and explains material well.  Helps you out w/ the upcoming test material and tells you to "make life simple"...GO CHUI GO!

She was a great teacher. Went way above and beyond to help me out. She came in on a day off. She definately graded pretty easy. But she was starting to grade harder near the end so not sure if it's still and easy A. The nicest person I've ever met.

I love Mrs Chui.  I learned a lot even though her class was really easy.  Quizzes and tests come directly from homework problems.  She will tell you that you calculated a problem wrong on a test, and let you redo it!!  It's an easy A class!
very helpful!!!
Professor Clarke is very enthusiastic and supportive of her students. I really enjoyed her International Business course and the group projects in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I found Dr. Clarke to be a joy. She is a demanding professor, but I can't believe the amount of OB knowledge I'm walking away with from this class. We probably read every page of that book, but I don't see how anyone can hope to be a good leader without having the information she imparted on us. This class was A LOT of work, but learn we did!!!

One of the worst experiences I have ever had through 6 yrs at UF. Lectures were awful, so awful that even though attendance & participation is technically graded, only 10-20 ppl/65 showed up to class.
Criteria for assignments is both unclear and used against you with confusing wording. Group project heavy w/ no safeguard for problems. Be aware.
Literally had to fight for my A so hard. I dreaded her class even though it was fully online. Avoid at all costs

Professor Clarke is very straight forward with her materials. The class is made up of three open note exams and extra credit. The exam questions are very basic and have no tricks. I would recommend reviewing her lecture slides and tabbing the textbook for main topics. SmokinNotes is also extremely helpful to use as a condensed textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Professor Clarke for BUL4310 and was pleasantly surprised! The exams were easier than expected and came from the lectures.I watched the lectures, took notes, read the book, and used Smokin Notes to study for the exams and so far am doing well in the class!
Still saying insane things about trans students on the first day of class, a woman of tremendously flimsy moral fiber.

She is terrible. She does not care about her students at all. Her lectures are incredibly boring and tests include material that was never discussed. If you have any type of flag during an exam she doesn't even look at what the flag was and just sends you straight to honor court and then proceeds to ignore your emails. Avoid her take someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Clarke is an amazing professor! I highly recommend her classes. Her grading is very fair and is always open to help. She is also passionate about what she teaches. Highly recommend her classes. I took 2 of them and was very satisfied.
This class is very easy and the professor is really nice as well. There are group projects but nothing too hard. There are 2 quizzes as well that are not hard at all.
Would not take, puts way too much into rote memorization and is not very progressive in educational development.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very little guidance by the professor throughout the course. I recommend purchasing Smokin Notes to prepare for exams. Do the extra credit opportunities because there are a lot and they will boost your grade at the end of the semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 100% avoid this professor! Her lectures are boring and she just reads off her powerpoint slides. It is next to impossible to get ahold of her for literally anything except for makeup exams. Her tests are absolute trash and 90% of your total grade. Exams go over stuff never taught in the textbook or in lectures. Don't even bother trying to appeal :/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall not a great professor and horrible lecturer , however the course itself is not extremely difficult and one can get an A simply by reading the book and using smoking notes. Expect for exams to have some poorly written questions. Extra credit is offered and I recommend to do as much as possible as it can make or break a grade.

Great lecturer, very thorough with the course content. I would recommend doing the smartbooks and other assignments before quizzes to ensure a good understanding of the material before taking the quiz. Would also recommend Smokin Notes for this course; they provide great study material and the value you get is amazing.
get smokin notes and call it a day, lectures are useless

I got an A in this class and felt the material wasn't bad, however the exam questions at times felt poorly made where answers weren't clearly the right choice because of how vague they can be. I didn't go to the lectures because Clarke didn't add anything. I wrote my own notes on the chapters and consistently did the smart books to study for exams.
Dr. Clarke bring great expertise to class from her experiences prior to academia.

Dr. Clarke made it feel uncomfortable to be in class. If she was so uncomfortable with the pandemic still, the course should have been fully online. You must read the book & watch her video lectures. I ended up being .21 away from an A- & despite all of my effort this semester and no final exam curve. She did not foster a positive environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you are in the MSM program, you'll have to take her for Organizational Behavior and International Business Law. She provides study guides for all exams and most of the work is in group projects. She replies back to emails very quickly. If you read the textbook and watch the lectures you'll be fine. It's not easy but it's possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR IF YOU CAN AVOID IT. The Master's of Management requires you to take two awful classes with her; International Business Law and Organizational Behavior. She makes you read a 600+-page textbook and then gives you vague exams on it. She is the worst professor I have had at UF.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: A few group projects that take a lot of extra effort so make sure you pick good people to work with. Exams are easy if you have the study guide to go off of. Must go to class every day for attendance credit, but do not need to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The worst professor in the entire graduate school of business. If your time is valuable, take another class.
drones on nonstop, often to the point of exceeding class times

Prepare to remember 10-11 chapters of definitions and concepts to murder your brain. easily 250+ definitions and other random concepts. Each test is almost 40% of grade, not an easy A. Easy to pass, but not "easy" to get an A. Harder than marketing class because you have 6 more chapters of material.
Her lectures are very boring, don't bother watching them, or buying the book for that matter. Get Smoking Notes and study the hell out of them before the exam.

I took and passed this course online. It was hard watching the lectures, as her presentation was usually dull and she read directly from the PowerPoint.  My advice: read the book, Smokin Notes, do the homework. Unless her requirements change, there's no need to watch or attend lectures. She seems like a nice lady. Just not a great public speaker

Literally, the easiest class you will take in the business school. All you need is Smokin' Notes. I didn't watch a single lecture or read the textbook, and I got a very high A in the course. You only need the textbook to look up HW answers.

she just seems so afraid, depressed, hopeless, weak all the time. i feel uncomfortable staring at her. reminds me of an abused animal. so i just didnt watch the lectures nor read the book and i came out find. read smokin notes. she is a nice lady tho dont get me wrong.

Not sure why everyone gives her a bad wrap; maybe she has eased up this semester. I'm in the online section, so I watch the lectures on my computer. If you double speed it, her tone is less dull. Do the homework, and review any concepts you don't understand in the book. Easy A/B if you watch the lectures.

Got an A in the class by: 1) Doing all the online HW assignments 2) Reading every chapter THOROUGHLY 3) Smokin' Notes for second and last exam and 4) Taking advantage of every extra credit opportunity.  No benefit in going to class; prof just reads off of PowerPoints that come directly from the book. Just read and/or use Smokin' Notes.

She is pretty much useless. As long was you keep up with the readings, study exactly what she tells you during the reviews and do your homework you'll be fine. I ended up with an A-, pretty easy class if you study but she is very boring and only reads directly from the slides during class.

All I did was read the book and do the aplia assignments. I didn't watch the lectures or purchase Smokin Notes.  Most of the material is common sense. Watch the exam review lecture(s) and keep up with the text to get an easy A.
The class is boring as she only reads through the powerpoints almost word for word. Do the online homeworks, read and outline the book (of get smoking notes) and you should do fine.

Her class really isn't that hard. Just buy smokin-notes and you'll be fine. Make sure you do all of the online homeworks, they really help boost your grade. She also gives a good amount of extra credit opportunities. I took this class over the summer and received an A- with minimal effort.

I really like Dr. Clarke.  Honestly, all you have to do is read the book and watch lectures. I didn't find her tests tricky at all. I work full-time and have taken much harder classes at UF. I loved this class. Very interesting and I found her lectures helpful. Good stuff!

Idk why people think she's a bad professor. I took her class online and learned a lot. I'm an exercise physiology major and I greatly enjoyed learning about management. Yes her exams are a little tricky but she makes you think. I got a B+ but considering I'm not a business person I did rather well compared to other students. Read the book!!!
I own a successful small business in Gainesville, FL and got a B- in this class.  Real world application equals zero relevance
Took online didnt watch lectures. GET SMOKIN NOTES and memorize every line. Each test is worth about 45% of your grade so study. For the first/second test make sure you read the book its emphasized.
She pretty much just reads from the slides and there are not enough exams. Each exam is worth so much of the grade that if you mess up on one exam, you're done.
She is not a very good teacher. Class isn't difficult but you also don't learn anything though.
She doesn't seem to know what's going on in her class. tragic.

The class focused on management theory and she brought in few real world examples or anything outside of the textbook. I watched lectures, though could have just read the textbook and followed along on the lecture slides. Memorize concepts and watch her reviews before the exam. The homework seemed irrelevant. Not the best intro to management.

Lots of memorizing so constant reviewing of material helps. Watch lectures and read the textbook for the constant exposure and review. Especially pay attention when she goes over old exams because usually she reuses questions. Don't expect to have your grades up when she promises or anytime soon after you take the exam.

She never responded to a single email of mine all semester, even though I took special care to email her exactly how she asked. Lectures are a complete bore. Just read the text and the notes a couple of times before the tests and you'll be fine.
Not a hard class at all. Prof is not overly enthusiastic and energetic, but she is not bad at her job. Easy A if you study the highlighted stuff and definitions in the textbook.

I've only watched a single lecture and I have a 100% in the class. I had a management class with a REAL professor at my previous college, but was required to retake it at "UF's Level" of course...what a joke..how pretentious..The lecture I did watch, she stuttered and tripped over her own words constantly. She seems very incompetent and unprepared.
Not all that bad of a professor. She does come across as very timid.

Easily the worst professor I have seen at UF. Shows no enthusiasm, uses terrible examples, contradicts herself constantly. Seems to be making it up as she goes. Takes forever to grade exams, and doesn't respond to emails. All in all, a terrible professor. I have no idea how she was hired.

Horrible teacher. NEVER responds to emails. I wanted to go over one of her HARD exams and she didn't get back to me until a month later when it was already too late. Very boring and very hard. You have to keep up with Smokin notes and the book to do well in the class.

One of the worst teachers I've ever had. This class was supposed to be easy, and I was so excited to take it, but she killed it in a single lecture. Lectures drag on, and she has no enthusiasm whatsoever. The tests are vague and take forever to get graded. Terrible class, terrible teacher.

The first test was very confusing, the second was much easier. The biggest problem I had with this class is that it took weeks for test grades to be posted. I ended up with a B, it's not a hard class just EXTREMELY frustrating as the teacher doesn't have strong communication skills. Which ironically is an important skill for a manager.

Probably the worst teacher I have had so far at UF. Monotone voice and reads word for word off of the slides while contradicting herself in lectures. For a management teacher, she is clueless in managing a class.Tests are vague and confusing. She doesn't respond to emails; TAs are nonexistent. Grading takes weeks and inconsistent with the syllabus.

Tests are ridiculously vague and have multiple answers. Never watched a lecture. Her 1st semester teaching. Read the Smokin Notes obsessively 3 or 4 times and memorize them, but no amount of reading will get you an A on a test. EC, optional tests, and quizzes save you. Don't bother with the book. Management got 10x harder this year because of her.

2 words... Smokin Notes. i didn't use it on the first test and watched all the lectures and read all the book and only got a 43-59 but I used it on the second test and didn't even finish watching all the lecture and never cracked the book and I got a 51-60

This teacher is horrible. She was boring and hard to follow at times. This class was supposed to be the easy class , but it wasn't. I definitely do not recommend this professor. Management should be a fun class, take someone else.

This woman is by far the worst professor I've had. She is horribly monotone, and stands there reading word for word off the ppts. She makes irrelevant side-comments during lectures, and tries to make jokes that just come off as tired, ignorant, and pointless. She honestly seems incompetent. Tests are not based on lectures, but the book alone.

I hate everything about this woman. For one she is comically ****. I don't mean clan **** or anything, but she is by far the most ignorant teacher I've had at UF and blatantly stereotypes cultures. The best part is that she actually thinks her asinine examples like, "If an Asian person calls you fat it's just them being nice," always apply.lmao

Although my course was 100% online, Michael Clark always responded to Canvas emails and resolved issues incredibly fast. During the one mandatory live meaning, he provided great career insight and seemed genuinely interested in mine and my classmates' futures. I'm now taking DIG2121 with him this semester, highly recommend!

The course was being remodeled in real time so there were a couple of bumps along the road, but overall the class was really easy. Lots of drawing, fair bit of typing, but it is very straightforward especially if you already know how to draw digitally. The quizzes weren't too difficult, discussion boards were straightforward; easy class.

He seems like a good guy, but his instructions for the assignments can be weird and confusing. Also, he will give you 2 days to complete a quiz on canvas, but if you take it on the second day, you will have a late penalty, which would not be a problem if he clarified.

He is very nice with students, and he clearly has a passion for what he teaches. However, homework instructions can get very confusing; he will post a lot of documents and not post what they are for. Also, takes a while to grade your assignments ( 2 weeks average)

He is very caring and enthusiastic about his subject. He let students have a say in what rules were put in his syllabus. We do fun assignments during class and have little homework. He makes the class enjoyable, but his assignment instructions are often very confusing, and he has a lot of problems with Canvas.
She was great. Very open to student involvement. Easy A just a lot of busywork. Very flexible.
Format of online class is confusing, disorganized, and tedious. Communication is not good. The class itself is interesting and easy!

The main problem stems from the fact that she is entirely unresponsive to any concerns students have - emails or discussion boards alike. Lots of busywork assignments that aren't necessarily hard, but are so tedious nonetheless. Easy enough grade, but the class is so frustrating to deal with that it doesn't feel worth it.

This class was terrible DO NOT TAKE IT. Dr. Clark could not be reached by email or office hours at any time during the semester.  It was about 10 hours of work for each module. 1 module was due weekly. Instructions on ALL assignments were lengthy and unclear. Content was understandable but the way it was "taught" was unbearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
This class will have you working up to 4 hours per day for one lesson...3 lessons are due weekly. This does not include the lengthy discussion posts and assignments. Though the content is not very difficult, this class is very time-consuming. 
This professor isn't the best at answering emails, I recommend emailing a TA and finding a GroupMe.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Oh boy. Took this class as an economic requirement and she has been the worst experience. You get randomly bombarded by ~8-12 assignments on a Wednesday at like 7 pm. Which is just a bunch of busy work and the LONGEST guidelines for discussions and specific assignments. Just not an enjoyable class and takes up too much time. Choose someone else.

Such an easy class. Though there's a lot of tedious assignments with the world's longest instructions (not exaggerating), they are not by any means difficult. If you follow the instructions for the discussions/projects you'll be fine, plus most of the textbook assignments can be found on Quizlet. Definitely would recommend this course

I had to take this economics class as a degree requirements. Every three weeks we could have a dozen random assignments, along with an insanely detailed discussion, along with a project. This class has been the most annoying class of my college career. They grade your projects and discussions very harshly. I learned nothing in this course.

The class itself isn't exactly difficult as long as you know APA very very well. She gives good feedback and overall seems like a good professor...Just don't expect to have free time with this course there is so many assignments, weekly bookwork and a 750 word discussion response w/ 250 word student response due weekly that needs APA cited sources.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
This professor is very strict, even for an intro class that should be more about learning. Small mistakes can drop your grade a lot, & feedback often feels discouraging. Assignments are timed & locked. Overall, not the best experience for students still adjusting to journalism basics.
If you value supportive teaching, I recommend someone else.

The comments about her being condescending are very much so true. She is not approachable, her criticism is not constructive, and she is not there to help you learn. Her assignment are locked so you can't work ahead, and some of her writing portion are timed. For your mental health sake & grade please stay far away from her.

If there is any glitch with your course shell DONT expect help or for her to give you grace at all; it's always "ask IT." Had a glitch with one of the big projects "Gator Professional Series," did all the worked, PROVED I DID IT, and still got a 50%. New professor let this slide and took my screenshots as completing the work, unlike Cleland.

Assignments were relatively easy to understand and do. Some of them were time consuming to finish and two of them were timed assignments which I wasn't a fan of. It would be easier to manage if the assignments weren't locked.

Mrs. Cleland is nice but also the kind of professor that can't fathom the idea that students have other classes to work in. The amount of busy work in this class is ridiculous and she can be a tough grader. The text book work is super time consuming and her discussion posts are needlessly difficult. Be sure to follow her instructions to the letter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Fav professor ever. Class was super easy, same with the work assigned. Communication is great absolutely loved it.

I had Professor Cleland for 2 classes during spring semester. She is amazing. She is very knowledgeable of the material and was welcoming when speaking via zoom on how I can improve. She provided activity examples to help better understand formatting and expectations. WRITE NOTES FROM THE LECTURES!! This helps, she wants you to learn and grow!

Class was VERY easy. Didn't watch lectures and the quiz/activity answers came straight from the textbook. Discussions are your pov as long as you used evidence to back it. Yes she is a stickler for APA, but she provides a lot of resources to help. 1 essay but it's not hard if you are passionate for your stance. She gives a lot of time to prep!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm not sure why the reviews for this professor are bad. All you have to do is watch the weekly videos and complete the weekly assignments. She is not one to let a late assignment go by, so make sure to give yourself plenty of time to submit assignments. The class was actually pretty interesting and I learned a lot.

Dr. Cleland's course is pretty easy. It's mostly just short (5-10min) videos with a quiz. The final project is the most difficult but she was really helpful in assisting me with it. She's really sweet and cares about her students.

I have taken numerous journalism classes with Dr. Cleland at UF and she is by far one of my favorite professors of all time. She is passionate about the topics she teaches, pretty lenient and flexible with her grading, and always provides actionable feedback when applicable. I've really only had very positive experiences with Dr. Cleland.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is the type of professor to say "I don't want to fail any of my students, but..." and proceed to grade very harshly. I personally enjoyed reading the textbook content of the class, but for the amount of busy work you have to do with different dates to meet and different specifics for each assignment its almost impossible to get an A.
Her lectures are not good and she can be overly condescending in her grading.
My favorite professor every.

Dr. Cleland is obsessed with APA.  Follow her instructions to the tee and you will be ok. However do not expect to learn much about your course material as it seems her entire focus is to make people learn APA even in non English/writing classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I learned a lot but she is one of the harshest graders I have encountered at UF.

Prepare to write, abuse APA style, read tedious instructions, and receive elitist commentary/feedback. Expect subjective grading with high writing expectations. Quizzes had no time limit but are long and tedious with an annoying amount of requirements in each question. Capstone project was a 10-page essay. She makes things needlessly complicated.
Constantly told me that I didn't know how to write at the college level and always "expected more." All feedback was condescending.

I made an account on this website just to warn you about Cleland. I was so let down by this class . Cleland is an impossibly hard grader giving feedback that doesn't make sense and is overly critical. On top of that, it takes her forever to grade things! She is rude, snarky and doesn't answer questions properly. She sucks DO NOT TAKE THIS

This class is one of the easiest courses I've taken so far at UF. I like writing and I have an interest in the field in which this course is designed for the assignments were no big deal. There's about 6 quizzes total, very easy -- just watch videos she posts. Weekly assignments and she grades pretty quickly.

This professor is the antithesis of what a teacher should be. She singlehandedly made me question if I want to stay in school. The combination of ego, sarcasm, condescension and confusing assignments and tests makes this experience frustrating and counterproductive. I know less now than when I started this class. Take a different class!

If you have to take a Cleland class, RUN! If I could have given her a 0, I would have. She lives for the GOTCHA! moments to throw unnecessary wrenches into your plan, she creates convoluted projects, assignments aren't released early so you can work ahead. College is hard enough, this prof makes it harder with surprises. DON'T take her class!!!

Shes a tough grader but shes willing to proofread your assignments before submission to help you improve. Her criticism is constructive and actually helpful. Her quizzes are based around the video lectures, not the text or discussions. Its worth taking her if you put a lot of effort into your assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great Professor!!! She cares about the well being of her students and their grades. Supper accessible by email and almost always gets back to you within the day. Gives a three day grace period for each assignment where she only takes off 5 points per day. Easy A if you stay on top of things. Would definitely take another class with her!!

If you want bizarre, off-topic, research-heavy assignments masquerading as tests, then this is your class!!! The "critical-thinking" questions are really just an exercise in frustration, and it seems like she keeps trying to get television show ideas from her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I wanted to love this class, but was very disappointed. Some of the feedback seems overly critical and illogical. Assignments are outside of the reading. Tests are not based strictly on assignments, a lot of subjective influences with the grading. I would not take another class with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is honestly awesome; she's very sweet and really tries to relate to the students. Her assignments are fun and it's not a bad class at all. Her announcements are usually pretty funny and sweet, she's an easy grader, and gives great feedback. This being online, though, is lecture intense and she isn't the best with updating grades.

Cleland is the instructor that communicates with the students. She is super fun and sends news and current events she finds interesting. She is also a big fan of emojis in her emails. The class is easy but test heavy. You have to read and understand the techno-talk of the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is a complete waste of time - you learn nothing, you hardly do any writing, and half of the class time is spent waiting for him to come up with something for us to do. He is extremely disorganized and confused with his other classes at UCF and has a difficult time working with technology/Canvas. I would not recommend this professor.

He has unclear expectations; the class is 2 hours of nothing. He refuses to help or guide you, because "you don't learn if you don't get there yourself." As a student with a high gpa, this class is a waste of time, and stress that was completely avoidable. Do not take. If other class is full, wait a semester. It sounds harsh but it's true. Trust.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is awesome in almost every aspect of the course. He is not great at elaborating when you do not understand what he expects. I think the disconnect is that he thinks elaborating on a subject is holding our hand and the students (me) think of that as teaching... which some would say is Clarks job.

Professor Clark was by far one of my favorite professors I had at UF. His grading is very fair, and he really cares about your work and will let you know if he thinks your work will have a real-world impact. Clark prepares you for the job market in the industry ahead of you. His lectures are rooted in his 30+ years of experience in the industry.

He is super nice and provides good feedback. Assignments were easy and exams only required light studying. During lectures, it could be hard to tell what was important to know for exams (also, slides didn't have much info and weren't posted), but I took notes on everything he said and used the textbook to fill in missing info and I did well.

Very nice professor and for the times I turned in something late I was simply honest about why I did and he always understood and didn't take points off. Lectures were lowkey boring, exams are straight from study guide and weekly reading assignments that you do. Overall, should be an easy A.

The class covered basic high school history material. Lectures were boring, but attendance made grades easy. Content and tests were simple, with light workload (1 assignment per week, occasional book reviews). Cline was patient and understanding about hurricanes affecting deadlines.

You won't spend too much time learning new material in this class if you payed attention in American History in high school, the main thing is getting through the lectures, which Tyler can make hard to do specifically because he seems unenthusiastic about the subject itself. If you can stay on top of attendance, the class is a breeze.

Dr. Clark was a great professor. She was very knowledgeable about agricultural policies. Her in person class is entertaining and informative. Attendance is expected but in person is easier than online with her and there's less work. 
I would definitely take her again.

Easy A. Was not the biggest fan of her in-person lectures, but the good thing about them was that you never had to do the online discussion assignments. All of the assignments, homework, and quizzes were straightforward. She's also very nice and flexible.

Professor Clark in AEB2014 was very clear in her expectations for the class. If she says expect to work 9-10 hours a week on the class she truly means it. Work load is heavy and grades aren't posted for a few months. However she is a helpful and positive teacher who truly has students best interests at heart
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is very knowledgeable about agricultural economic concepts. However, she is not very responsive, which is a big deterrent for me when looking for a good professor. Her assignments, quizzes, and lectures are well thought-out, just sometimes difficult to get adequate feedback on why you got points off. I don't dislike her though.

Dr. Clark is incredibly kind and available to students, her class was pretty interesting and not very hard.  The reading material was often provided in class.  The group projects were easy.  Overall Dr. Clark is an amazing professor, I very much enjoyed this class and her teaching
Lots of busy work, but manageable if you stay on top of it. The professor can be tough to reach, so utilizing Unstuckstudy and TAs for support is key. Put in the effort and you'll likely get an A.

Accessibility issues with most course modules, resulting in modules released late. Discussion board was supposed to be monitored to help with issues, but professor/TA's did not respond. Tons of busywork and reading in lectures and assignments. I've never seen instructions that long. Too many issues to discuss in this rating. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You will not interact with this professor even once throughout the semester. She is super hard to reach, and does not post all assignments ahead of time. The problem with this is she often forgets, then when she remembers; she assigns 2 weeks worth of assignments on wednesday, due that sunday. Class is ran by TAs that grade weeks later.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: chill class i took it online as a dual enrolemt course, it was my first and it was a good start. Lots of reading and McGraw hill assigments. Besides that most of the class was discussion post and a final project work. But there was no final exam so that is a bonus
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She was a whatever professor, I honestly didn't need her for the course. Her directions on assignments were SO long to read. It's an easy class but she uploads assignments kinda late, especially for being online. The course is just busy work; you can chat GPT almost everything.

This class was terrible DO NOT TAKE IT. Dr. Clark could not be reached by email or office hours at any time during the semester.  It was about 10 hours of work for each module. 1 module was due weekly. Instructions on ALL assignments were lengthy and unclear. Content was understandable but the way it was "taught" was unbearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Other reviews are pretty much right. Easy class, but a lot of busywork. Never actually interacted with the professor, it's all graded automatically or run by TAs. TAs grade very harshly, but that could change when you take it. Overall easy grade, I didn't even do some of the assignments and I got a B. I'm avoiding this professor in the future.

Very understanding, set expectations and met them throughout the course. Assignments built on each other throughout the semester so there wasn't busy work. Would highly recommend the Quest 2 class Valuing Circular Food Economies. Very interesting class to take.

Absolutely awful professor. She gives out way too much work, and at least for the semester I had her, she would release the module with about 15 assignments every week the week it was due. You have no time to breathe, and if you want to get it done while being a busy student, you have to cheat and not actually learn the material.

The class was straightforward with open-note assignments. However, it can be time-consuming. The professor made the class difficult by assigning assignments late, which left limited time to complete them alongside other classes. The professor doesn't respond to emails, so attend office hours or ask a TA for help. Easy class but bad professor.

A great professor and has been more available this semester for help. You have about 20 things due a week. Not hard assignments just a very time consuming class. No exams though, so overall I rather do the extra work and know I get an A then take the other economic classes where exams are the only thing your grade consist of.

Don't let the reviews scare you the class is not that bad. Their is a lot of instructions but as long as you do everything for an assignment you will get a good grade. No exams and quizzes are open note. You have to do two discussion post a week or a bunch of story book assignments, they switch off each week. I think I will end up with an A.

The assignments weren't challenging at all but they were very time-consuming. The instructions for all the assignments were very tedious but the grading wasn't that bad so you can definitely end up with an A as long as you follow all the instructions. The professor was bad at responding to emails but if you just join office hours she will help you.
Class was very simple, 6 modules each with discussions, homeworks, and quizzes, there was some extra credit and assignments were overall pretty simple.

I highly do not recommend this class. The professor is nearly impossible to contact. Emails from the beginning of the semester have not been answered. She does not show up to her own office hours. The assignments take like 4 hours each, and it is way too much work and unnecessary stress. Take a different professor, or a different econ class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is run by the students and not in a good way. She never answers her emails and every assignment has a dissertation of instructions that takes you an hour to read. She takes off petty points and overall, the class is run like a middle school english class. We grade each others work so she doesn't have to do the work. I don't recommend her

Looking at the other reviews I expected worse, but the class wasn't that bad. The instructions are lengthy and hard to comprehend sometimes, but as long as you do the work assigned and semi pay attention you'll get an A. She's also really nice, and very willing to work with you if something comes up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you value your time and sanity, don't take this class. The syllabus contradicted itself repeatedly, she never responded to emails despite saying she would, she put in 4 grades out of 19 with three days left in the class, and 3 of the assignments were literally to just copy and paste sentences from an old assignment, just in a different format.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The instructions for each assignment is like two pages long and there are way too many assignments in one week for a summer class. No lectures.Since shes not doing lectures you would think the professor would have plenty of time for grading, but I guess not because it is the last week and I have one grade in the grade book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I did not interact with the professor in any way throughout the course. AEB2014 is online asynchronous, so I was expecting to watch recorded lectures. Instead, Clark put in 0 effort and did not create a single material used in the course - it was all from the textbook. This was sincerely the worst experience of my life and I learned nothing.

THIS CLASS IS THE MOST FRUSTRATING CLASS EVER. OVERALL, ASSIGNMENTS ARE EASY, BUT HER INSTRUCTIONS ARE SOOO LONG AND COMPLICATED FOR EVEN THE MOST SIMPLE TASKS. IT WILL BE AN EASY A, BUT THE AMOUNT OF FRUSTRATION IS NOT WORTH IT.

As long as you follow instructions carefully you will do well, but she lays everything out, (like how to use Canvas) so it gets exhausting. The work is easy enough, all open note quizzes and the project builds upon itself all semester. Pay attention to deadlines since many discussions and assignments are multi-part. Good for STEM major freshmen.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There were about two assignments per week and some of them were rather time consuming, but the quizzes were all open book, open note, and open internet, and there were no exams or a final. The due dates were always 5pm, so that added a bit of stress, but if you need an economics credit and you don't mind doing a little extra work, take this class.
No. Too many lengthy assignments to the point it's hard to keep track. The assignments have annoying instructions as well. If this class is not required, dont take it.

There are no exams. There are 6 open note quizzes (internet search allowed). There are also 6 discussions, projects, and online homeworks. It is INCREDIBLY REPETITIVE AND TIME CONSUMING. It feels like busy work and honestly a huge waste of time. The instructions are really clear and as long as you follow them perfectly, you will get a good grade.

I did not expect the amount of work load that I would have with the class. The work is relatively easy, but the amount of it is insane. Make sure to look at your assignments, usually there are multiple parts to one assignment. You can meet with Clark and Ta's to review your assignments to get feedback before submitting. Willing to help you learn!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The other reviews that talk about the annoying instructions are true. If you want an easy A this class is NOT worth it. She is not involved and makes her students and TAs grade everything. In my opinion, it wasn't worth the tuition money. I say find another class you are interested in.

First I would like to say this class is easy but she has the MOST tedious instructions for her assignments. The instructions span pages. It takes me an hour to finish a discussion post but half the time is spent reading her instructions. Unless you really like this subject I say look elsewhere there are easier classes with less frustration.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark had zero involvement in my course. Her assignments were repetitive and tedious, and added nothing beneficial to the course past the first assignment set. Most of the answers to hw and quizzes are on quizlet so its not hard to do well, but her meticulous format instructions make the work much more difficult than it should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was extremely easy. If you can follow directions, you will make an A. I wouldn't say you get much out of it, but it is required for CALS.

Class is a lot of work but very manageable. Easy A if you do your work correctly and on time. Reach out to the TA if you have any problems and they will report back to Professor Clark for clarification. Interaction with her was really nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class is not hard to get an A in. You just need to be willing to put in a ton of work. Every module (6 total) consists of the lessons, homework, quiz, discussion post with two responses to classmates, and an activity. Her instructions for every assignment are super specific and detailed. This makes clear what she wants but can be annoying
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is honestly a joke. I was told it is a required elective for transfer students entering the CALS program. She is more stringent about what you bold, how you source, and what "defines a paragraph" than the ideas you convey. You can sail through this class with half a brain cell as long as you follow the knit-picky instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You will most likely have zero interaction with Professor Clark while taking AEB2014. There is also so much homework in the class that is due each week. If you don't follow the format of the discussion posts or assignments she requests (which are oddly specific), then you will lose the majority of your points. DO NOT PROCRASTINATE ON SUBMITTING!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Anyone looking for an easy A look no further. The grades are not determined by the substance of your work, but by how well you can follow her seemingly arbitrary formatting instructions. The class doesnt seem to have been updated since 2012, and she doesnt answer emails. Im so glad I paid $1000s for this class!!! :)

Never have I ever been so glad to be done with a class. If you want to be treated like a second grader for an entire semester, I highly suggest this teacher. Seriously, the formatting instructions for discussion posts and assignments were longer than the assignment itself.

This class will feel like a lot of work if you wait until the last minute to do the weekly assignments. Stay on top of it and this class is an easy A. Clark's way of formatting doesn't make sense sometimes but follow the instructions exactly and you'll be good. You'll get used to it as the semester goes on

No exams. Discussion, assignment or quiz twice a week with very clear directions. Follow directions and write something meaningful to get full credit. Interesting/easy if you like economics (micro & macro) and/or like agribusiness. TAs grade everything. Online lectures on economic principles that are useful for quizzes.

There is a lot of assignments but they are not hard. The grading criteria is described in great detail for every assignment with guidelines and if you follow the instructions you will get a 100 on almost everything. Quizzes are a little more difficult but they are open note. No exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I wasn't a fan of this class. I felt the information to be pointless, you can look up most if not all of the infromation. I only took it because my advisor said I would get rid of taking macroeconomics and microeconomics. I dreaded every assignment I did in this class. Would not recommend, even though I got a good grade. It's a waste of time.

Course assignments and discussions were unorganized; the directions would tell you to do one thing and then the rubric below would say something different. You're graded more on technicality than content so take that how you will. Unless this class is specifically required for your major, don't bother.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Out of all the 5 classes I took this semester, this was the most tedious, annoying, pointless class I took. I didn't learn one thing in this class. she doesn't respond to emails and doesn't care how you are doing in the class. I would take this class with any other professor other than her.

Your adviser will tell you this is an easy course that helps the department, for your own sake, ignore them and take micro. Her class is the biggest waste of time, spent hours just to do a discussion post . Her lectures are useless after module 1, as you can look up all the terms you need to know for homework and quizzes. The class is a joke.

This class is the most disorganized mess I have ever been through. I should have dropped it immediately during drop/add. It's unfortunate there isn't another prof that teaches it. Clark's attempt at organization are flawed, and ultimately result in confusion and stupid specific instructions that are so messy, you will have no idea what to do.

I cannot emphasis how stressful this professors disorganization is. Trying to figure out what information is crucial and what is not, just forget it. The descriptions for discussions, assignments or even announcements are very lengthy and unclear. I have to summarize and breakdown discussion questions so I can answer them, ridiculous.

very tough grader. Her discussion post instructions are extremely unnecessarily lengthy, confusing and she is a super tough grader on them specifically. Doing her discussion posts take longer than the quizzes themselves. As a straight A student, I was surprised when I received a 73/100 on the first discussion post.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was a lot of work and all the due dates were consistent which made it pretty easy to stay on track. If you complete all the assignments and follow all the parameters an A is easy but you do have to put in the time and effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was the easiest class i've ever taken. The only reason i can see some people not doing well is because it has a lot of work associated with each module. Do each assignment as the instructions say and you will pass with a high A. Each module drops your lowest "category" of grade, so just stay on task and you will pass with a 98 honestly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Be prepared for a ton of assignments. They are all pretty easy content wise but it is definitely time consuming. All the assignments are due biweekly so you basically have 2 weeks to do everything but be prepared to write a lot for most assignments and discussions. Textbook is useful for the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Be prepared for a ton of assignments. However, it's all biweekly so very easy to manage with appropriate planning. The textbook helps for assignments and quizzes. Definitely time consuming but relatively easy.

This was such an easy class, but it is important to work ahead because it can get overwhelming if not (projects due at 5pm). TAs grade more on technicalities rather than the content itself. If you do everything she wants you to do format wise you should get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: AEB2014 was the easiest class I've taken at UF. People say it's a lot of work, and I genuinely have no idea what they're talking about. Each module takes about four hours to complete, I literally sat down and did work for this class once a month, finished the whole respective module, and forgot about it. Not just an easy A, this is an easy 97%.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: AEB2014 was not a hard class but it requires a lot of work. Some nice things about it are there are no exams and work is only due every other week. With that being said, the assignments and HW are all SUPER time consuming and all assignments are due at 5PM not 11:59. If you are in CALS and need to take it, take it during a light semester if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class is about what you'd expect. There's a lot of reading/lecture-watching/work involved but assignments have VERY clear criteria and she's an easy grader. As long as you keep track of when things are due you should have no problem doing well.

The only thing I enjoyed about this class was that there was no final. However, Ms. Clarke's lectures were so long, boring, and the readings that were assigned were like full on novels. I do not like economics, but this class made econ so painful. I did not enjoy the class or the teaching style because it was so time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Interesting and easy course. She gives you plenty of time to work on assignments. I usually could finish everything early. She was also very helpful during office hours. Extra credit opportunities and no exams!

Honestly one of the easiest online professors thus far. Assignments are extremely straightforward and she's extremely fair with grading. All quizzes are open note and open google search, and the majority of the answers can be found on quizlet and coursehero. EASY A, just apply yourself!
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: Not even finished with the semester yet and I am so fed up with her that I have to write a review. She takes FOREVER to grade assignments so you cannot get any feedback to improve your assignments. Simple assignments have multiple pages of instruction. She has discussion boards open for each assignment, but never replies to any questions. Avoid.

Easy class but a lot of things due every week, one of each: quiz (do the practice quizzes before) based on readings, project, assignment, and discussion with two responses to classmate's discussion post. Each of these take some time to do because you have to read long and specific instructions (VERY important) to follow. Easier to manage over time
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class wasn't hard but she made it hard. VERY unorganized, never managed to post assignments on time or stick to course schedule. Even had syllabus for wrong course posted on Canvas, had to ask dept. for right one. Very slow grader and sometimes picky. Quizzes and assignments open book/Google. Did give one drop for lowest quiz/work grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: AEB2014 is a very easy class. You don't have to use your brain for this class. However, it is very hard to get in contact with Professor Clark. It would take days to get a response. Also, she releases the assignments pretty late in the week.

I would never recommend this professor.  She doesn't answer emails.  There are 12 modules but she uploads assignments each week.  Sometimes she uploades on Wednesday and assignments are due Monday.  Sometimes she uploads them on Friday and due Monday.  Would never take her again!

Though Professor Clark is very lenient in grading and allows multiple drops for assignments, quizzes, and one exam, the online class is very unorganized.  Honestly you just have to check Canvas early in the week and hope that at some point that week's material will become available.  There is no option to work ahead.

I hate that I have to take Dr. Clark for so many classes in my major. She is the most unorganized professor I've ever had (that's saying a lot) who doesn't follow the syllabus, doesn't know how to use Canvas, and posts assignments/quizzes last minute so if you have work or other classes to worry about you are out of luck. Easy class, bad professor.

This professor is so specific on what she wants there is NO room for creativity or critical thinking. I felt like this was the college version of kindergarten where the teacher holds your hand through every sentence she wants you to write. Get ready for constant BUSY work on top of it; A never ending flow of tedious assignments. I do not recommend.

Very disorganized, never managed to post a single lecture after module 1. We had to teach ourselves and take quizzes based solely on readings. The class is essentially reading comprehension. Very slow grader, bad at responding to student questions. Never released modules, did not follow syllabus.

She's very nice, and the class is pretty easy. There are 12 modules, each containing one homework and one quiz. Most of the quizzes can be found online. The homeworks are annoying and time consuming, but not hard. She grades SUPER slowly, but she's a pretty easy grader overall. Lots of powerpoint assignments, no papers. Take it for an easy A.

It is the same routine every week: discussion board, quiz, assignment (usually a short paper). Super easy class as long as you do your work on time and follow directions. Easy grader, no exam, good lectures and readings (that you don't even have to look at since the assignments are easy and the quiz answers can be found on the internet).

This class is not difficult pretty straightforward. Same thing every week. Assignments due at 6 PM which can be hard to keep track of. Don't expect replies. I've sent her 4 and no response. I sent one once and she didn't reply and then sent one to the entire class. If you have questions you're on your own. Emailing her just wastes your time.

Terrible!!! Clark was late in releasing every module and she rarely responds to email. The TA almost never responded to inquires on the Chat because questions pertained to when (and if) the modules would be released or Clark's poor instructions. Currently, less than a week left of classes, and two modules (4 weeks worth) are yet to be released...

I didn't enjoy this class at all. It's not difficult but things are due at 6pm on random days so it's hard to keep track of. She doesn't teach. She gives a topic for the section and assigns "find an article that relates to it." The only things I've learned in this class are from finding news articles, not her. She also NEVER answers emails!

I had to WORK for my A-. 3 assignments per week.  Contrary to what others on here say, she doesn't give much extra credit.  Organizational skills are terrible. Tries to make the information tricky by embedding core information in paragraphs of text. Obtainable A, but beware she will try to trick you.  100%s on everything is necessary for an A.

I took this class online and it was one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. I do the assignments on the weekend before it is due and only takes me about 2-3 hours a week to complete. She gives tons of extra credit, so always take advantage of those.

AEB2014 is the easiest class you will take at UF!! As long as you turn in the work on time it is impossible not to get an A. All the quiz answers can be copy and pasted straight into google and the answers will pop up.

One of the worst classes I have ever taken. Professor Clark set up every exam differently from how she told us it would be. She would also not answer questions from students appropriately.  All directions for most assignments are very unclear. Would ask students clicker questions that were for a grade that even the TAs did not know the answers to.
This course is easy to follow and do well in. I don't have much interest in economics, but did gain some after this class.

This is an Easy A if you do your work and don't miss assignments. It is designed for you to do very well in. There are two quizzes, no final, most of the grades are discussion posts and writing assignments. I would take this class again in a heartbeat!
She responds to questions pretty slow. The class is easy if you do your work and don't miss any deadline. The was no exams. I got an A and she gave work but it was very doable and easy.
Ms. Clark is VERY slow at returning grades. Tests are very straight forward. MUST GO TO CLASS. Remember that you must study. You get a formula sheet.

This class is EXTREMELY frustrating! ZERO organization! This lady can't get her stuff together! She constantly moves around assignment open dates, deadlines, and sends (not exaggerating) at least 10 emails a day! She will drive you INSANE if you like to plan. It will be the most annoying A you ever get in your life if you take this class. UGH!

Excellent professor!! Crystal clear about what she expects and very well organized course! The final project is actually fun and interesting. work was graded on a timely manner... offers some extra credit but you really don't need it! :) Overall I was happy with the course and keep up the great work Professor Clark. She cares for her students .

This teacher lacks any effort nor knowledge. She teaches of a textbook and retrieves questions from a test bank. Probably why she is teaching a low level economics class (to match her low level economic class?). Easy class.

Clark was wonderful and responded promptly to emails. I would def take her again. If you want a solid A here is what you need to do: Read the chapters, watch the lecture, and spend time on the hw. I did that then bombed the midterm and final (they are very hard) still made an A :)
Easy class. Easy A. You don't need to watch lecture or read anything. Google "AEB2014 Easy A" for a guide on know how get an A on this class without lectures or anything.

This is a semi-easy class. All you have to do is watch the lecture notes and do the online quiz and online homework assignment. The key is to watch the lectures and skim the book. Quizzes are open book and you get an hour to do it. The concepts are easy and it is a good class
Very easy class. One hw and one quiz a week. Easy to read textbook and look up answers. Definitely recommend taking this.

VERY EASY CLASS! I took this course while taking 3 core science courses and a science elective. I would highly recommend this course to anyone that's planning on taking an overbearing semester. The material was easy, she lectured well, and what she didn't lecture on was easily Googled. You can drop 2 aplia assignments and 1 quiz. Easy A!

SUPER easy class - read the few pages assigned, do the quick homework, watch the 30 min or less of lectures and take the open book quiz. I only spent ~3-4 hours on this class every week, skipped the last test and got a 96%. Lowest quiz grade is dropped and 2 lowest homework grades are dropped. Grade = 40% quizzes, 60% homework. SUPER easy.
GREAT professor, very informative. 99% of the quizzes questions are online, however, APLIA sucks. she gave EC for it. overall, lovely...

Online course. Answers 95% of quiz q's can be googled. APLIA HW comes straight from the book. Gave us a chance to retake the majority of the quizzes. Offers extra credit (good amount). I hate economics, but this class became easy once I got familiar with the quizzes/HW. definitely get an E Book, makes searching 4 quiz answers easier.

This was an online class.  Mrs. Clark is great lecturer and follows the book to a T.  Quizzes and homework are really easy if you read the book. She ended up giving everyone a second chance on most of the quizzes this semester.  If you aren't required to take macro/micro but still need an economics class (i.e. CALS requirement), take AEB2014!

This was the online version. Ms. Clark is an exceptional lecturer who knows her stuff and cares about her students. She makes every effort to ensure her students have every opportunity to succeed. Mankiw's textbook rocks. The APLIA online learning tool was fantastic.  If you don't pass this class you didn't even try and should just leave school!

Very good lecturer. However the tests were all from a test bank that came with the book. So the tests would have questions that were not talked about at all during class, and also would be maybe 2 sentences in the book. Also she has some issues getting back to people through email. Sent her 4 emails and received no responses to any of them.
Tests come straight from the book. Homework is pretty easy. Her notes are a good summary of the chapters but they exclude some stuff. You only need to show up for class if you want extra credit.
This class was so easy, I didn't buy the book and still got an A!
Very nice lady, has some issues with getting back to students. Overall, nice,hot, and helpful.

I had Dr. Coombes for my first APK class at UF. I do not have a sports science background and he made my first class at UF go smoothly. The lectures were great and informative, he is funny and caring, I loved listening to his accent, and there is not a lot of busy work. Watch lectures and take notes. I learned a lot and it was an interesting class.

Dr. Coombes was a pleasure. I took advantage of e-mailing him and he provided great feedback.  The labs were short but important. Liked the yellowdig approach which gamifies engagement.  Limited discussion ecological dynamics, but that was ok, because we dove deep into information processing theory. One request: more on attentional awareness.

Dr. Coombes class is a hybrid (online lectures and in-person quizzes and discussions). He loves research and is a very thoughtful and kind professor. Although there is little room for error as he only grades with exams, quizzes, and a tiny bit of participation, the material is really interesting and challenging enough to enjoy the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures were all pre-recorded and put on canvas,. Each chapter is between 1-2 hours of lecture and they're simple and clearly explained. Quiz at the end of week on lecture with straightforward questions. Tests similar to quiz. In class time, we do a group project that we work on whole semester and get feedback each week. Very cool and nice guy
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Coombes has been one of my favorite professors at UF. The material is challenging but he presents it in a very organized and digestible manner. The way he teaches with research applications has been a huge inspiration for me to pursue research and consider grad school in a similar field. You can do well if you attend class and study powerpoints
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Coombes is a funny and caring professor. You are graded on mainly quizzes with a midterm and final exam. As long as you pay attention to and study his lectures, the class is relatively easy. Take him if you can!

Dr. Coombes is by far the best professor I have had at UF. He is a very caring, funny and knowledgeable guy. The material is really interesting and he makes everything exciting with his humor. Study the quizzes and his slides and you shall do very well on the exams. He is always ready to help and really cares about the success of his students.

Dr Coombes really cares about the material he is teaching. The class is 10 quizzes and 2 exams. The quizzes are relatively straight forward if you go to class and study your notes. The exams are mostly quiz questions so very easy to study for.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Coombes is great. I loved his class and he is so nice. We even had a full day of lecture where he explained his whole life story to show up that things don't go as planned and never to take life too serious. Midterm and final are 75% the exact same questions from the quizzes. Highly recommend.

Dr. Coombes really seems to care about his students doing well and succeeding. He gives dynamic lectures that really teach you the subject. His quizzes are easy if you go to class, take notes, and read over them the night before the quiz. Exams are heavily based on quiz questions. I'd highly recommend him!!!!

Dr. C is a really cool prof and he knows what he's talking about. He definitely cares about his students. The only part about the class that sucks is your entire grade depends on 10 quizzes and 2 exams. If you screw up one quiz you won't get an A, but he doesn't make them overly difficult as long as you go to class and somewhat try.

I really liked this professor, and his lectures. It is a bit hard, but it's not much material... I would suggest to come to class everyday and get help if you need it. I enjoyed being in class because he made it enjoyable to be there. He really knows what he's talking about and makes it easier to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He was an incredible lecturer. I was never bored in class. Quizzes and tests were fair as long as you paid attention in lecture. We had a group presentation and my group had one member who was not prepared the day of the presentation. My grade on that presentation was the difference between the A and the A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS
