Out of 3 exams at least 7 questions got overturned on appeal because the questions are just that difficult. I recommend doing the extra credit and the Smokin notes it will save you! I had to take this class twice!!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fair professor with an appeals process for bad exam questions. Do all the extra credit you can because you may need it in the end. Smokinnotes is a godsend for this class, wish I had it for all 3 exams. Overall, good prof and interesting class.

Organized, fair, friendly, and inspirational. I recommend reading the chapter, then watching the lecture (2x speed), then doing Smartbook. There is a lot of information, but he gives you notes to add to, as well as practice exams. Lots of resources. Guidelines are very clear; you know what is expected of you! Great professor, nothing bad to say.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exam heavy. I read the textbook and watched all the lectures, and studied with SmokinNotes (which definitely helped with studying). I did the worst on Exam 2, but extra credit got me an A. He's an interesting lecturer, and a good grade is definitely possible if you put in work. Some test questions could be confusing, but he has an appeal system/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do all the extra credit if you can -- this ended up adding about 5 percentage points to my grade. The class is test heavy, so do the practice exams to prepare for them. I did not have Smokin Notes and I got an A. I would suggest watching his lectures as they can be interesting and they are relevant to the exams (watch him in 2x). Cooke is great !

Cooke's exams were confusing and out of the 3 exams we took he dropped about 12 questions total because they didn't make sense. Some exams were more bloated with the material than others. During exam 2 the power went out in my room and he offered my roommate a chance to make the test up but did not allow me to which I thought was odd.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Cooke was great! You are mainly graded on exams, but there's plenty of practice exams to get a good feel of what to expect. I attended all lectures and got smokin' notes. As long as you do some practice exams and give yourself about 5-7 days to study for each exam (depends on how slow or fast you like to study) you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class, lectures were actually interesting to watch (1.6/2x speed) I would watch them to get a general idea of the topic and then do the smart book assignments. 3-4 days before the exam I would read smokin notes and take all of his practice exams. Got high B low A on the exams, but the extra credit is the reason I got an A, add 5% to my grade

The three exam grades in this class are 80% of your grade. He writes his own questions on the exams and allows us to appeal because they are so difficult and most questions have multiple answers. I got 100% on my homework and quizzes, but I struggled with the exams which got me a B. I was actually with the class average though. Do not recommend!
The material seemed straight forward and id do well on practice but then Id fail the exam. Struggled so bad I had to withdraw and take again later.

Professor Cooke is AWESOME! You MUST watch the lectures, but they are super interesting and applicable to marketing today. He draws on many examples of articles, ads, videos, etc. making the class easy to understand. The hw and quizzes are easy, just make sure to read the book!

Class was definitely more difficult than I expected, but getting an A or B is definitely doable if you put in some work. I highly recommend his lectures and smokin notes notes to do well on the exams. He is very passionate about this class and it shows through his lectures! Also do the extra credit!

Alan Cooke is often unfairly hated in conjunction with the challenging course he teaches. He is actually a very reasonable professor who will help you if you are proactive enough to ask. He posts old exams which are super helpful for studying the material. Marketing is super tough, but he really tries to make it interesting!
Smartbooks is the only thing textbook is used for you don't have to read it. Do the extra credit marketing research things they are so easy. All info comes from lectures

This class is not difficult if you memorize the smokin notes and take all of the practice tests for the exam, you will do well on the exams. 6 questions are computational on every exam and are free points as long as you learn to do them. He often gives back 4 questions per exam through his exam repeal system as well

Alan Cooke is not inherently a bad lecturer; however, the course is graded based on smart book assignments, quizzes, and exams. The smart book assignments and quizzes are each one point, and the exams are 56 points, so once you do bad on one exam it is hard to bring your grade up with the other assignments. There are extra credit opportunities.

Professor was straight forward in lectures. Weekly quizzes and lecture 2x week. weekly smartbook assignments. Lots of concepts so study and get smokin notes to help as well. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I am terrified of learning a different language for credit but I highly recommend Professor Marull. She and her TA's do a fantastic job of giving feedback. LinguaMeetings are fun and definitely will help you learn and pass this class.

She really cares if you are understanding the material. You do have to really try and participate. She gives tons of resources and is always available if help is needed. Go to your Linguameetings, do Contraseña, and pay attention to VoiceThreads and you will do fine. If you are lazy you won't pass, simple as that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class was easy, but you are required to meet with a linguameeting coach every week. A lot of homework assignments and only 2 exams that are worth basically nothing. There was also voicethreads and a final oral project. I did this class as Pass/Fail, but definitely could have just gotten an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Weekly Spanish homework, weekly recordings of yourself speaking Spanish on Voicethreads, meetings with a Spanish coach once a week. Extra Credit opportunities! Spent about 15 hours a week for the course, but that's expected for a 5 credit course. Professor expects you to speak like a first grader so don't pressure yourself over the course!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Marull was fantastic! Her course is geared towards success, with homework and class assignments counting as almost the entire grade. Exams and the project are formatted to test learning without putting your grade at risk. I truly felt this class taught me more than 3 years of HS Spanish ever did. She is always available. Great person!

Profesora Marull teaches Spanish the way all languages should be taught. Emphasis is placed on production of language in a natural setting, some with videos you create and some with a native spanish speaker. She gives great feedback, is always accessable, and her TA's are professional and kind. You will really truly learn spanish in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Marull is honest about the time required to do well in her class - 25 hrs/wk. Lots of homework. Not hard but very time consuming. Dr. Marull cares about her students, is very accessible for help, and responds quickly. Majority of grade comes from weekly homework. Do all the homework and get good grades on it and you should get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Her classes are not an easy A and she uses a lot of different platforms to teach. But once you get the hang of her class her class is fun and very educational. She is a top-notch online educator. I wish all professors knew how to create online curriculum like she does.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took Professor Marull for both Spanish 1 & Spanish 2 consecutively and both were online. Professor Marull is an AMAZING teacher. She puts her students first and is always ready to help a student in need. She makes the class entertaining and really encourages the students to take ownership over learning the language permanently.

Sweetest professor ever. She cared enough to get to know each one of us and was very quick to respond to emails and give feedback on our work. Regarding the work for a 5 credit class, the workload was fair. She gives you plenty of practice for hw, projects, and exams. 100% would take again if I could. So passionate about her work and teaching

All college language courses have lots of homework but Professor Marull is also a really tough grader on the little things that aren't automatically graded by Pearson (which is the worst platform for learning to begin with). Lots of money thrown away on programs that suck, I've learned more from outside sources. Defeats purpose of paying for class.
Best professor I've had at UF!
Best professor I've taken at UF!

Offers a multitude of different platforms, but unequally grants credit for homework. Not good at speaking Spanish? Not a good test taker? You probably won't pass because she grades almost solely on the recorded activities and tests. Very accessible for extra help, but feedback comes off very short and condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Marull has a background on understanding how second languages are learned which to me is extremely impressive and useful as a second language professor. The amount of assignments are reasonable, easy grading, and you will learn Spanish. I recommend this online class

Very tough grader. Does not like students to achieve higher than she believes they should. Lots of homework. Lots of different platforms that require specific software. Not a timely grader. Feedback is not helpful.
Excellent professor, but so many different platforms to keep track of, especially if you are taking this online. Lots of busy-work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Really tough class, but Dr. Marull is kind and tries very hard to help, but you have to ask for the help. It's a roller coaster of a class, and you will progress if you do the work --- and it's A LOT of work. If you get behind, it can become overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Even though I found Spanish at the college level to be very difficult due to the massive amount of information you have to learn in a short time, this professor is very accommodating and understanding. There is a lot of homework and there are video requirements and live meetings. There is a midterm and a final with oral interview.

This is coming from a failed math major. Professor Crew is the only professor that taught linear algebra in a way that I could grasp. The majority of your time is spent doing homework while the majority of your grade is determined by exams. Make sure you've seen every proof at least once as the exams are proof heavy.

Nice professor, lectures were hard to follow at some points, but the book would cover when everything else failed. If the lectures were more organized then I'd rate a 5, but they aren't bad if you can follow through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Crew was a decent professor. His lectures were quite messy and made on the spot, but the tests were relatively easy. He doesn't go over all the material in the course, so if you want to learn the stuff well, I'd advice seeking another professor. Regardless, he was charismatic and sometimes funny, making the lectures confusing but not boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Why is this professor's rating so low? He's very flexible. Sure, he's a boring lecture, but you could just stay home and read the textbook because everything's in there. Memorize all theorems, do all assigned homework, and attend his review lectures, and you'll do just fine. Loved the class structure. I never attended class and still learned a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Crew is an earnest professor who wants to see his students succeed. However, he is the worst lecturer I've had yet from the math department as a math major. He wings each lecture, goes extremely fast, explains the concept as if the audience is already familiar, and covers the chalkboard with his body as he writes.

Enthusiastic about the material. Fast, rather messy lecturer. Lectures would generally follow the textbook, but he would sometimes sidetrack into topics that were beyond the scope of the class. Exams were extremely true to the review lecture. Graded on 5 4-question exams, but plenty of partial credit was given, so it wasn't terrible.

Crew's lectures are basically repeats of the textbook. Each class before the exam, he would do a 'review' that was a question for question coverage of exam content. Class was graded entirely on 5 4-problem exams. Topics covered were unusual for this class, being more controls oriented. He gives a lot of partial credit, but lectures felt worthless
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very fast lecturer and makes so many mistakes but expects students to be perfect. Never fixes the mistakes he makes while posting new class material. Horrible for students who aren't incredibly strong in math and should be taken as the last option for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His class is not as useful as the book required in his class. He made mistakes and explained a little about the material. His class is a burden for all the new learners.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Group theory is not easy and he doesn't make it easier. His lectures are fast and often unclear. He's oblivious to his audience being lost, but if you speak up he will explain again. Lots of HW which I learned much from. 3 exams instead of 2 which is good, but each exam has 4 questions and only 50 mins. Grades toughly while sloppy himself.

Horrible. The man made each class a speedwriting contest, jotting along the board as quickly as possible. When he finished on the chalk board he would turn around, gasping for breath, and ask if we understood what he had vomited on the board. The man has weekly quizzes, and grades very strictly. Only class I failed at UF.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Crew graded fairly and had a lot of enthusiasm for the class. He cared to learn all of our names too. His lectures were alright, and the tests and quizzes mostly came from assigned problems. Going to his office hours was not as helpful as I would've liked because he doesn't work out the problem with you, but it was still helpful.

I am pleasantly surprised with this class. It's like any other math class where understanding the material requires simple repetition. His exams/quizzes are based on HW questions (he'll definitely use the harder ones). Show up ready to ask and answer questions. Practice writing proofs because those can be time consuming and they must make sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class was fairly straightforward, three exams on three separate chapters with graded homework. Homework was tough, but seemed to be for participation. Tests were based on examples straight from class. Lectures are a bit slippery, but you should be fine if you just read over the textbook and complete a few examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class topics are really easy. What doesn't help is deriving the general solutions and never working examples (heat equation, wave, in last section). HW posted, and hopefully you have enough time because doing the HW takes forever. 15 pages for one of the HW's. The exams, 50 minutes, 4 (ish) problems. When you sit down you have to GO GO GO.

Very difficult professor, relative to other MAP2302 professors. Class relied on 3 or 4 pop quizzes, and 3 or 4 exams. The exams were very difficult, and twice he said a certain topic we had yet to study would NOT be on the exam, but he ended up putting it on and saying "oops, sorry about that".  No good, especially when others grade much easier.

Lectures are useless, he is impossible to follow and doesn't care if the whole class has been lost for weeks.  Often uses messy or even incorrect proofs.  Homeworks often contain mistakes and ask you to prove things that are false.  Does not attend his own office hours.  Avoid him.
Dr. Crew is a very friendly, energetic person. His lectures are very interesting and I really enjoyed having him as a teacher. The material was difficult but if you work hard you can easily pass.

This class is hard but if you do all the homework and study you can pass. Office hours saved my life. He often rushes during lectures but if you write everything down and then read the book later it makes sense.

Grades based on quizzes every friday (10 points) and three tests (30 points) and final (50 points). If you're good at math, you'll do well. If you're not, then study. I know that many were struggling to hold even a C by the first test, but by the last test average was a high B. He gets into the topic, great if you like Math.

Professor does not lecture and expects students to learn everything from the book. Homework every night and he makes students present their work in front of the class. Basically you go to class and watch some kid fumble over his answer, which takes the whole class pd. Tests are hard, no partial credit, and he is very particular. AVOID PROFESSOR!

This class is awful!! By far the most boring class, and this teacher does not make it any better. Be prepared to present problems, which are difficult as it is, in front of the class while he sits there and critiques you (no lecture!). If you're a genius you'll be fine, otherwise you will be pulling your hair out all semester. he's not approachable
Grades with no mercy, don't expect much partial credit. Homework everyday, drops nothing.

Loves the material, very intelligent. You'll need to invest quite a few hours into this class. He loves to assign a lot of homework problems. Make sure you know just about everything about the class. Can be harder than most other professors.

He's an interesting guy. Kind of weird, but amusing, even during 2nd period. Occasionally he races through the lecture making it kind of hard to understand whats going on, but you can ask questions during lecture. Finds a way to make tests a bit difficult if you want an A. If you're willing to study for a couple hours a week, he isn't that bad.

Abstract Algebra is probably the hardest class in the math department, but he made it very manageable. He does go very fast at times, but it's not so intimidating. I would recommend him for this or other upperlevel math classes.

Great professor if you enjoy the material. Can be hard if you don't understand. If you don't understand - GO TO BROWARD TUTORING! Has funny comments. Also has a strange relation with coffee. Favorite quote: "Are you all comfortable? How can I make you uncomfortable? Where is my cattle prod?"

very knowlegable but not helpfull at all. his grading scale is rediculous, u could get a highest grade or lowest by knowing the same thing! very unclear at times and but overall good introductory class for mathematics majors.
Great professor....but you better like math, or he will ruin your****.

Taken for Honors Calc III. Avoid! Most difficult Calc 3 teacher. Knows his stuff but has hard time sharing it with students. Extremely hard tests, doesn't like talking about grades. At least he is enthusiastic...

I really liked Crew but I can see where his teaching style (which often skips "redundant" steps in problems) would confuse non-math-oriented people.  If you love the subject, you'll like his class but you may want to avoid him if you struggle.

He's nothing short of a genius. However, that does not mean he makes a great teacher. He assumes students know advanced mathematics and will fill the board with equations that might have nothing to do with the class "just for fun" kind of thing.

I don't know if Dr. Crew has a life outside of class, but he seems to assume his students don't.  He's very knowledgable, but doesn't pass this knowledge along very well; he's so orgasmic over it that he covers it in a flash.  Just not my style.
Highly recommended for serious students pursuing mathematics. His high paced lectures keeps the students engaged as well as providing for a large amount of knowledge outside of normal text books.
A serious mathemetician. Not for the faint of heart. You'll like math with Crew about as much you like math in general. Well-paced (a little fast sometimes), doesn't get behind, and enthusiastic.

Prof. Muñoz is fantastic. His Policy Process class is theory-heavy but super engaging, and he explains complex frameworks clearly. He's approachable, fair, and creates a respectful, thoughtful environment. If you want to actually understand how policy works, take this class—you'll come out smarter.

You can tell he cares about the class and makes class interesting and easy. It's a pretty easy class for being so abstract since he started using slides(Fall 24). The in-class essays are not too bad since you see the questions before and the other projects are not crazy. It's worth attending lectures because reading everything is tough.

I love this prof so so much. He sounds a little like Gru and his lectures are funny and very helpful. He is super knowledgable and the readings (though there are a lot) are interesting. He cares a lot and prepares you well for the two tests. He gives you 10 questions before the test and picks 2-3 for the written exam.

There's only 5 grades but the paper, presentation, participation, midterm, and final are graded easily. Grades are reliant on the TA. Wallie was a great TA and taught more than the professor did. Professor was funny, lectures sometimes random but he posts the slides and you can use those to prep for the exams which are written essays. Easy A.

His lectures were decent, there is no required attendance but I definitely recommend going anyways to stay on track. There are 5 grades (a short paper, presentation, midterm, final, participation), but as long as you have a good TA it isn't hard to do well on those. Be prepared to read a lot, but the content is pretty interesting so its fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
graded on 5 things, but most TAs aren't strict on grading (I had Walle)
you don't need to read the assigned readings if you go to the lectures and not much work
content is not very fun and kind of hard to grasp but if you study you will get an A 
professor is hilarious so lectures are enjoyable
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Excellent professors & TAs. 5 grades: discussion attendance/participation, short paper, short presentation, 2 essay exams (in-class). You're given 10 prompts based on PowerPoints & chosen 2-3 on exam day. Content is not challenging but not very fun and takes a lot of time to grasp because they're very extensive. Professor is very engaging in-class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are really engaging and teach you basically everything you need to know about readings. Kind of assumes you have some background knowledge going in. He genuinely loves the subject, and the lectures are pretty interesting. A lot of your grade is TA dependent, but it was overall an interesting and fun class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's knowledgable, but his lectures lacked any visuals when I took it (Fall '23), so it made following him very difficult as it was just verbal talking. Don't take this class if it's not required-- a lot of reading and u only get graded on like 3-4 things, which is a paper, discussion, and presentation. Imo, my TA did most of the teaching.

Prof. Munoz was a fair professor, but the class is entirely dependent on your TA. His lectures are kind of hard to understand sometimes, I think most people stopped going after the first couple of weeks. But assignments and exams are manageable as long as you have a good TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Graded extremely easily. There are not many assignments for this class. There are a few "required/recommended" readings per week, but you will be completely fine if you do not read them. His lectures are sometimes engaging but often confusing (there is no powerpoint or outline), but they are explained well in the discussion section by the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Munoz is funny, passionate, and smart. BUT, my TA, Hassen, was not. He bickered with me (yelled at me once in class for asking a question??) and was harsh on random things. Also, I find it very distasteful that the syllabus was edited 1 day before the term ended which took out attendance (supposed to be 20% OF YOUR GRADE!) bringing grades down.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Munoz is a hilarious guy, and his lectures tend to be engaging but don't have any structure. He doesn't use PowerPoints, and pretty much just goes with whatever is at the top of his head on any given day. He knows a lot about the readings and Political Theory, so you will learn something in this class if you attend regularly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cristian is a funny dude and is passionate about his teachings. His lectures range from incredible to completely out of the text on some days. Great lecturing abilities, it just only seems to be on certain days. What's great about him however is that he doesn't emphasize grading, and focuses on making sure students get something out of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Munoz was super passionate. There were only two presentations and the midterm and final, along with a participation grade in discussion sections. He wants his students to learn and not be concerned about grades. There are multiple long readings every week but you can get away with not reading all of them. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Munoz is an amazing teacher. His lectures are engaging and he tries his best to include students in discussions. Overall, you are graded by a midterm, final, and discussion/presentation in your TA section. There is a reading assigned every week. If you can take him for POT2002, definitely do!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, not much work but he isn't very clear or responsive. I learned next to nothing.

Professor Cretul is the best instructor I have ever had in college. I loved this class and was disappointed when it ended. Cretul kept the class nimble, mixing online lectures with interviews, group discussions, and videos. In addition, he was interesting and was clearly invested in his students. Fantastic professor.
tough grader but gives good feedback, about one assignment per week plus a midterm and a final
He's a bomb teacher. Like I loved his class and always was willing to give me advice when I needed it. Hard grader, but gives you good feedback.
Loved Cretul! Great teacher, very patient. He makes you want to go to class
Very helpful, but not the easiest. Funny.
Awesome TA, helpful, hilarious

This was actually my favorite class I have taken at UF. He provides critical, yet very helpful feedback on all of your writing and really takes the time to read through all of the work you submit. If you work hard and care about the work you are submitting, the course is not hard at all. He is also really funny, and  cares about what he teaches.

The content of the actual class isn't hard at all, but dealing with the professor makes this class so aggravating. He is such a bad lecturer, with no enthusiasm and zero student engagement. He is so rude and dismissive, answering any of my questions with "Check the syllabus." Spoiler: my answers were not on the syllabus.

This class is relatively easier than his other classes, but I don't think Craig was that bad. His lectures were kind of boring, but I think you can do well on papers if you figure out early on what he is looking for. For this class specifically, he really wanted to see a connection from films/literature to things going on today. Blunt over email.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I thought he was alright but politics in film and fiction is an easier class.

Boring class but not bad at all. Everyone is complaining about there being no rubrics, but every paper is just to write about any political subject of your choice that relates to the film. With such free reign, obviously there's no rubric. If you're a generally decent writer, this is an easy class.

Although somewhat fair in terms of grading (is a harsh commenter but doesnt necessarily take away too many points), he is extremely rude. Constantly interrupts students during discussions and is extremely condescending, especially within written replies. Doesn't even have a clear grading rubric. Extremely disrespectful.

Horrible professor with very unclear grading criteria. He is rude in his email correspondence and does not even attempt to understand his students. He will continue to nitpick your work even when you fix what he tells you to fix from previous assignments. His lectures are way too long.
Beware of this professor, he will berate students with disabilities and then gloat when they end up not doing well in his class. This man has no business being a professor, he needs to be fired.

Honestly one of the worst professors at UF. He is not straightforward in how you fulfill all the requirements of the essay rubric and basically is just assuming you know what he wants you to write about. His class lectures are boring and basically just him throwing his opinion at you, nothing of substance or value. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.

Genuinely a horrible professor. Condescending at best and rude at worst, both in class settings and in emails and private feedback. Took him for POS3233 and there was no clear instructions for any assignment. Comments on assignments were often out of the scope of the assignment (grammar, punctuation, whether it was novel research, etc)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My experience wasn't AWFUL. He's decent to listen to and I think he means well, but he doesn't provide any feedback unless critiquing grammar, and we made it halfway through the entire fall semester without a single grade in the gradebook. It's not an easy A which is okay, but it's way too easy to do poorly without even knowing it, which is not.
He makes you write your essays in single-space. Enough said.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Craig was not as bad as people made him. I took him for public opinion (his first year teaching the class) and it was fine. Class is a little slow but the assignments (5 in total) make up your whole grade. If you're interested in the topic you should take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Save yourself. Do not take this class. Does not care. Mental health gone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely rude and not understanding of when students are sick or if students don't understand a topic. He never gave defined feedback or a defined rubric and would administer exams that students did not even have the time to complete since he expected essay answers and works cited. Horrific class, learned nothing valuable

Listen to me. if you take this class and want to succeed on the exams, you HAVE to compile your resources before hand. go through the slides and readings, categorize it and have data and citations ready for everything. his exams are essay-format and theres very little time to find what you need. i regret not doing it for the midterm. gamechanger!

One of the worst professors I have ever had. I have never had a professor be more degrading and give less constructive feedback in my life. Everything that he does seems to be built to belittle students and feed his own ego. Took this class as an elective because it sounded fun, and it quickly became one of the hardest classes I have taken at UF.

Home boy literally grades based on how much he likes you. If you speak in class you will be the higher grade, if you don't follow one thing on his syllabus man will never give you a good grade on the few assignments there are. Comments on papers are brutal literally every single time. Looks for things wrong with paper rather than a single positive.

IF YOU ARE GRACED WITH GOOD CRITICISM THEN YOU MIGHT AS WELL PLAY THE LOTTERY CAUSE YOU HAVE HIT THE JACKPOT. I HAVE NEVER MET A MORE RUDE PROFESSOR IN MY 3 YEARS IN COLLEGE HE DOES NOT OFFER FEEDBACK BUT INSULTS. I recommend you take another professor or ignore this class altogether, his lectures are unbearable online. also, he doesn't care.

Worst professor I've ever had. His criticism is never helpful nor does he answer questions well. It seems like he is here to research and show off how smart he is, not to teach. His grading is so unpredictable and there isn't a rubric. He only gives letter grades in the comment section so you never know where you stand in the class. STAY AWAY!!!

Dr. Craig is a very smart man and he provides good insight into the topics that he himself researches. However, while he is a good researcher, the man is an absolutely horrible teacher. I found the class material fascinating, but it seemed as if Dr. Craig did everything he could to make success impossible. He is short, rude and frankly brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Craig assigns weekly two-pg single spaced essays and grades/criticizes every single detail (make sure you use qualifiers!). He gives letter grades instead of exact percentages, so youll never know where you stand until after the final. Hes not that approachable for questions; hed much rather correct/scold you than help you. Please stay away.

Professor is knowledgeable, but exams are extremely tough, does not provide rubrics and doesnt grade in consistent manor. Most of his feedback is harsh and unhelpful. Spends a significant amount of class time having you discuss political topics that have no relation or benefit to course knowledge. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely bad. Criticism was bad nasty. NOT HElpful. Would NOT RECOMMEND!!!! STAY AWAY ����
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: This man is the worst professor I have ever taken at UF. Not only condescending towards students he also clearly does not know what he is looking for when grading. All of the feedback I received was extremely harsh and unprofessional. He does not provide a rubric for grading scales so he will determine your grade on how he feels that day. AVOID HIM
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor is clearly not at UF to teach students, and only there for accolades, books, and research. He is arrogant towards his students, and many of the assignments he told us up-front were to find articles that he would enjoy for his professional work. He is a very harsh grader, and due to his focus on his career, most people won't make A's.

I missed class because I was admitted to the hospital for an emergency appendectomy, had a note, and this prof still refused to give me an excused absence... so good luck. Course and materials were very interesting, essays (if you include A LOT of relevant outside sources) weren't too hard. Don't take this class if you don't enjoy writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Unprofessional, makes no effort to helps his students. Lots of reading but does not cover out of class work during his long boring lectures. Interested in topic but uninterested in the success of his students. Really just there for the grants for his research and books.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: *STAY AWAY FROM THIS MAN AND ANY CLASS HE IS THE PROFESSOR OF!!* Probably the worst professor Ive ever had the displeasure to take. His opinion of you is all that matters. I went to his office once to get help and he told me he was too busy he was literally on his phone. Hes a true disgrace to academia.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is by far the rudest professor I have had in my entire life. Every respectfully worded email I have ever sent him he has responded to with a short, rude, insulting response, and other people in his class have said the same thing. He grades essays harshly, and has class discussions where he just explains in detail why your opinion is wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: In my senior year at UF now, and this is the worst professor I've had here by far. His politics in fiction class includes an inordinate amount of "caveats", each of which he will deduct a lot from you if you miss one. Worse than that, it seems like he actually enjoys making life more difficult for students. Avoid like the plague!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He's not a bad person but the class grades are ridiculous. Wrote 8 essays, in which the first week I got a B and using the same skills every week he graded an automatic C with the same feedback, "start learning how to write essays." The class is fun but don't take it as an easy class. TAKE ALTERNATE ASSIGNMENT FOR FINAL
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Easily the worst professor I've had at UF. How did he become the department chair? I can only assume he is better at office politics than he is at teaching, because he doesnt merit it based on his sneering, arrogant attitude in class towards his students. He has no social skills, can't teach, makes fun of students, can't effectively manage a class

WORST and RUDEST Professor I have ever had, period. He grades papers on how much he likes you, not joking. I just don't understand why he became a teacher if he is so bitter about it in every way possible. AVOID AVOID AVOID AVOID AVOID AVOID AVOID PLEASE FOR THE LOVE OF GOD AVOID.
Rants on during class. No nonsense kind of guy. Surprisingly helpful during office hours. A lot of short papers but he isn't a hard grader.

He really was not that bad. He grades the essays easy if you follow directions and exams come mostly directly from the notes. He tries to throw in a few textbook facts,  but I did not read one article or chapter and got an A in the class. Study notes THOROUGHLY for exams and you'll do just fine.

The guy seems to have no interest in getting along with the students at all.  He rambles  through lectures that are tough to follow, and gives you no clue as to what's on the exams.  Don't expect second chances, humor, study guides, clarity or any significant amount of useful knowledge.

He does drone on and on, I once actually fell asleep in class and started snoring.  You can't anything he writes on the essays  and will later say you should be doing something different after already turning in a couple of assignments and not saying anything.
mean spirited guy

Despite receiving an A in his class, I must say that Craig is the WORST professor at the University of Florida. He is highly conceited, egotistical and cares little for his students. It blows my mind that this man is the department chair. AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE.
Still hasn't changed since 1980's. Took him on-line and in person.  He pushed me over to another prof and then decided to take the class back. Very unprofessional!

This guy is honestly the worst professor at UF. He is terrible at teaching and grading and would win in a landslide for most conceded professor. If you're an overachiever like everyone who takes the class and plan on writing a thesis, do yourself a favor and either take the class in the spring with Martinez or don't do it all. Not worth the torture

Honestly, all you have to do is the work he requires of you and you end up with a good grade.  I missed three quizzes and did my final paper on Battlestar Galactica and still ended up with an A.  He cares about his students and will always discuss papers/grades/other stuff at his office hours.

All of these people are crazy! Not only is he easy but he's a really nice guy. You have to do the work but honestly you are in college and having work shouldn't make you that upset. This class was so interesting. Learned more than in most poli sci classes! I should have an A.

I thought it was me...he gave me the "dirty old man vibe too"...but I ended up getting a "B", I swear he looked for every possible way to give me the lowest grade he could.  He is the WORST prof I have ever had.  I had to document EVERYTHING I did in there since I knew I would HAVE to PROVE my "B", which I ended up HAVING to do.  Guy is a JERK!
No Comments
BORRING

Do not take this course unless you absolutely have to.  He does not care about his students.  Reviews cover nothing relevant.  He is boring, his class is useless to most students, and everyone I know hates him.  A lot.
You know...I got an "A" and it was basically b/c I figured out how to boost his ego.  The man is insane.

I cannot believe they allow people with such limited social skills into classrooms. Additionally, he gives all appearance that he is bitter in his choice of profession.  Shouldn't teachers at any level desire to improve students on the whole or play a role in motivation? HORRIBLE. AWFUL. AVOID.

The worst professor I ever had at UF.  Not only does he drone on and on for the entire semester, but he gives no guidance whatsoever about what the test may cover.  Just a bad professor and bad course all around.

This teacher makes you buy $200 worth of books that he has articles in just to bring in royalties. He's totally boring and in a 4000 level course he talks to the class like they've never read an academic research paper. Only take this course from him if you actually haven't.
No Comments
No Comments
Was the only C I ever received in college. So boring and his tests are too hard in comparison to how simple the class should be
Avoid
so boring it made me change my major

One of the greatest professors in the Arch department and one of the sweetest human being ever!! D3 work is timeconsuming regardless but she was always super understanding with deadlines and provided great in-class feedback for each assignment or project!  Workload at times could be difficult but that's just the major, it was never too overwhelming
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Cronin is a kind soul and any Design 1 student with her is in good hands. Architecture is a tough major and like 10% of students switch majors by the end of the first semester, but it definitely won't be because of her. She is a down to earth person who is passionate about architecture, and will always accommodate for your needs.

She's amazing, I loved taking d1 with her. It was a great introduction to architecture. She's incredibly nice and patient. Great professor, wish I could take her class again!!

Studio is hard but it's just bc it's studio, Cronin made it as easy as possible .

Professor Cronin is honestly a blessing to teach architecture. It is extremely daunting at the beginning, but her friendly and caring nature guided us through the whole way through the semester. If anyone is considering to major in architecture, having at least one class under her is a must.
Amazing person and the perfect professor to teach you the intro foundation of architecture.
She's amazing and anyone who doesn't have her good luck🥰.

Professor Cronin was very caring and supportive to our projects. She never said anything negative but instead told us how to improve and what she liked about our projects. I definitely want her as my professor in the future.

Architecture in itself is an extremely hard course and therefore so is D1.  However, if you have decided this class professor Cronin is awesome.  She is so positive and genuinely understanding of the amount of work you are being given. Would definitely take again.
Great professor, super understanding and accommodating. He made the class so simple and I learned a lot, he really cares about his students.

You can tell he enjoys teaching and wants students to do well. Not a ton of homework and everything was super fairly graded. Group projects throughout the class and for the final. Nothing was super difficult. Have to put in some outside work to really succeed but not really homework, just watching tutorials and such.
Great Professor. Makes you work for you grade but you learn a lot. He is by far the most helpful professor I have had at UF. Great lectures and keeps your mind into it. Best professor for this class.

Great Lecturer looked forward to class. And knows you're in college to get a job not be an academic. Test, quizzes and homework are challenging but not impossible. Make sure you know how to do all of the homework well and you will do alright on the exams. His exams are similar to past semesters try to get a hold of them. Helpful guy but challenging

Great Professor, doesn't like to teach anything he thinks is a waste of time, so he skips a few sections in the book. Attendance is optional, but he likes to give pop quizzes every once in a while. He will give you hints to what will be on the test, so take note of those hints and study them well before going into his tests.
Excellent teacher. Tests are very straight foward and what to expect is given before the exam. Best person to take for MOM.

This guy is the BEST. I wish he taught more classes; I would take them all if I could. Makes you think critically, gives real-world problems, wants you to truly understand the material, always super helpful, funny, connects what you know from other classes. I enjoy going to class! Wish there were more profs like this.

Totally AWESOME professor. He is generous with grading and genuinely cares for his students both inside and outside of class. Best prof @ UF yet!! He makes statics seems easy and understandable. If you can, take this class only with him!!!
Really awesome i took this class before and didn't pass but some how everything becomes clear with Dr. Taylor. I don't think he should make the hw so difficult and worth 30% of your grade.

Mechanics of Materials can be a very easy class and Taylor makes it that way. His quizzes are usually easy with big bonus points to be gained by simply showing up to class on his special days where he goes off on tangents. His tests combine PE probs and fairly easy examples similar to class/hw. If you did well in statics you'll do better here.

Literally stated that he purposely wants to humiliate students. Can't teach, incredibly rude, and the opposite of accommodating.Clearly favours and is incredibly rude to students, laughs and humiliates at projects and calls it "criticism."Obviously, IA doesn't care about qualifications for teachers, but even as a person,Charlie is purely unpleasant

He picks favorites, if you are not a favorite you will be harshly graded and given absolutely no grace. You will need to go to TA office hours every assignment. Attendance is MANDATORY. Every project will have you up front speaking. He will grill you in front of the class. I think this is the worst class I have taken.
Really harsh guy
He praises one group only. If you aren't in the group, the class is extremely hard. He won't answer any questions. You need the ta for every assignment.

Prof. Cummings facilitates a unique environment where students complete both independent and collaborative work with foci on brainstorming, innovating, and prototyping. There are no tests or quizzes and you can get a high grade by showing up to the biweekly meetings and engaging with the rest of the class.

Charlie and the whole Innovation Academy Program should be shut down. Completely ignored our group while working on the project and did not bother to speak to us during catalyst. Praised one group for the whole project and gave no criticism to the group. Very unclear on standards for projects. Uses his pottery "business" to claim experience.

Mr. Cummings gives you exactly what you put into the class. If you slack, don't try, or cheat, you're going to get a bad grade. If you do the homework, work on the projects with the group, and don't cheat, getting an A is all but guaranteed.

As for Mr. Cummings himself, he is direct but fair, calling you out on the work but also providing feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He has a very tough love attitude and will tell you straight to your face that your idea sucks. But, your grade is a direct reflection of your work. Procrastination and slacking will get you a bad grade and be prepared for group work (basically the entire semester). Show up, listen to what he says, complain about it, then do it.
He makes fun on students projects in front of the class. I would not recommend having him as a professor
Very harsh and super critical of students and projects. He was vague with what he wanted for assignments. Did not respond to emails.

Do yourself a favor, sign up for your IA classes as soon as registration starts. All of the other professors classes get full right away, and then you're left having to take an already challenging course with Charlie Cummings, who's a major jerk and an unhelpful, demeaning and inconsiderate professor with a bad attitude.

If he didn't like your ideas, he was rude and would make fun of you in front of the class. When students got frustrated with projects or during the pitches in class, he would do nothing to deescalate the situation and if anything he would make it worse by saying that students were "being too sensitive" and that this was "constructive criticism".

Had to take him for my IA minor. Felt like he was harsh and didn't explain projects well but he gives you the chance to fix assignments you did bad on. There is extra credit and I would definitely do it. Just follow his comments and try to be prepared for any type of question about your prototype.

Professor Charlie Cummings is a professor for the Innovation Academy at UF. As long as u show up to class, submit the assignments he assigns early or on time, and actually show interest in the class it will be an easy A. I currently have a 98 in the class. It's not hard. Don't halfa** ur assignments and don't act like you're still in HS.

Her lecture videos are kind of long and repetitive. I honestly learned nothing but she's nice and an easy grader. Papers aren't hard at all. There's textbooks but I literally never opened them. Very experienced in her career and would probably be a great connection if this class was in-person. Wish I could say I got something out of this class.

Great professor! She was funny, laid back, and very experienced in the field of media and politics. Gave good extra credit opportunities. Not a lot of assignments but they're all very doable, interesting, and relevant to the current world of politics. Three exams but the study guide has all the answers in it so if you use it, you'll do great!
This is the type of prof everyone wants to avoid.

Prof. Cunha is clear and easy to understand. Her classes are interesting and provide a lot of context, according to current political events. Do all the assignments and you should be OK. Overall, she CARES.
Amazing and experienced professor! She gave awesome feedback and was very willing to help students in real-world situations. She is extremely hilarious and makes lectures worth attending.

Very easy class. The professor gives clear guidelines for assignments, and all test questions can be found in the lectures and material. Make sure to actual listen to the lectures before quizzes, because the questions are quite difficult otherwise.
She is an awesome professor, and I loved her media entrepreneurship class. She really wants to teach her students real-life skills and help them succeed. She made me more confident in my writing.

Darlena is an excellent professor. She has a lot of real-world experience and incorporates that into her teaching. She's very outgoing and laid back, and makes her classes fun as well as educational. She is also accessible whenever you need a question answered.

This was a great class and decently easy. There are a few main quizzes but she gives you study guides that have all the answers on them and they aren't proctored. She gives extra credit opportunities that boost your grade a lot. There are a few discussion posts and written assignments but they were all relatively short and interesting. Great class.

I absolutely loved Darlena. She actually cares about every one of her students and goes out of her way to help them succeed. She gives amazing feedback and teaches you stuff that is applicable to the real world. She is pretty lenient on late work and is understanding about outside circumstances. If you get the chance to take a class with her do it!

Darlena is a great professor. She tries to engage the class by using relevant examples (Beyonce was part of our PR lecture) and is enthusiastic when it comes to the material, even when she knows it's boring. My only complaint is that she tends to a little too free with her political opinions in class. However, none of the tests have bias in them.

Mass Media and You was my favorite class this semester because of her! Attendance isnt mandatory but there are 4 exams which make up your grade. Just go to lecture or see the powerpoint slides when theyre uploaded and you can get an A. She was really funny and laid back. Would definitely have her as a teacher again in the future.

Darlena is really energetic and funny! However you can tell she's still a bit new at teaching, so sometimes her lectures are all over the place and she makes grading errors, but she's always happy to correct them and work with you. She's passionate about her field and is always eager to help students succeed by sharing her contacts. Love her!

Darlena is by far my favorite professor here at UF! I loved attending her class. She is so funny, outgoing, and really passionate about her job. Always down to help her students get stories published because she has many connections.. Her exams and quizzes come straight from Powerpoints and grades mostly come from lab.

Darlena is so funny, unfiltered and interesting. I looked forward to attending her lectures. Never missed a class! It was an honor to take class from a woman who has articles published literally EVERYWHERE. You don't need the textbook  quizzes and exams are straight from PowerPoints and lecture. Be aware that lab counts for most of your grade.

Super tough grader with very few assignments. She does "first draft" assignments but does not grade and offer suggestions until it's past the due date of the final draft, so you lose points for the same mistakes twice.
She was more concerned about being your friend than teaching.

She was very nice and accessible. Would definitely recommend her if you need to take public speaking. Not too harsh of a grader if you actually put effort in. Exams are pretty easy, she basically tells you the exact questions during the in-class review.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher! I really enjoyed her lectures and she never failed to give us the help we needed to succeed!

This professor made me question my entire degree. He put me down when he graded my work and in front of my classmates. I would get my grades with no feedback. When I asked him what I did wrong and how to improve, he would tell me that I just didn't understand what he was trying to teach. Whatever you do, do not take his lab.
Lots of assignments per week, thorough grader but can be nitpicky

Reporting was definitely the hardest class I've taken at UF so far. Cunha was one of the better TAs in my opinion. He is a very tough grader and will give you honest feedback that is ego-crushing but ultimately in the end, you will learn more than you thought. This is the class I've learned the most in even if it caused a lot of gray hairs.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Cunha made this class unnecessarily difficult. There were a lot of writing assignments, and there was no schedule for the class just random due dates that changed each week. He is very nit-picky when grading assignments. I recommend taking this class with another professor.

Multimedia Writing with Carlos was somewhat difficult. There are several writing assignments that have to be completed each week along with reading/lecture quizzes and discussion posts. His feedback is very detailed and thorough but he can be rude and obnoxiously nit-picky at times. If you aren't a good writer, definitely don't recommend taking him
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cummings is a super good prof to have for a core credit in ethics. She knows what she's talking about, and addresses it to you in an easier way then you would get in the reading. Just show up to lecture and take notes and you'll know what you need to succeed. Only based on two papers and a presentation which is iffy for some but worth it.

Even though there are a lot of readings it is so worth it. she is an amazing professor and she's my favorite class. I feel like I am well prepared for anything in her class, and in each class, she will go around and speak with everyone and make sure we understand the topic. she is very funny and outgoing and if I would take her for more classes.

Cara was extremely nice and accessible and very laid back. She also understood the material very well and was able to explain it fluidly. She is a nerd at heart and makes quirky jokes which keeps the class fresh.

I loved her. Her personality was great and she used interesting examples instead of the usual boring ones to explain logic. Her class was not hard if you paid attention and did the homework. She was always helpful if you didn't understand. Great teacher!

She had a great personality, really nice but her test are WAY harder than what the HW are. She just started teaching and its clear she needs to learn how to.  I would take a more experienced professor so your grades wont drop.

She is extremely passionate about what she's teaching and taught very relevant information that was interesting and applicable to our lives. She didn't teach to prepare you for an exam, she taught for the sake of learning. The exams are easy and she lets you use study guides, and the rest of the time she taught whatever we wanted to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Is this an easy A? Yes. Is this class a pain to get through? Yes. Every lecture in class will be different and will have nothing to do with the subject of the course. The classes will always go over and they will sometimes be cancelled right at the start of class. The professor is pretty condescending and will snap so be careful with what you say.

If you asked me what this professor's name is, I couldn't tell you. She also goes by Jennifer Murphy, or Curtis, or something. She is very pretentious, she gives lectures on the wildest topics, unrelated to what will be tested on the exams, and the instructions for the group project were so unclear. Easy A, sure, but a headache to deal with.

Prof also goes by Jennifer Murphy/Curtis. This class is an easy A. You can pass by only completing the exams, but everything she discusses in lecture or offers you to read is interesting and can only help you. It's up to you. She is talkative, class WILL go over time. And check your Canvas inbox frequently, this is where she mainly communicates.

She's very passionate about what she teaches and provides lots of information and examples on the topics. There's no homework except to go over the material. You're only graded on 3 exams (she posts study guides) and a group project. Not too hard, easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: I got points off for missing commas. Professor has army of TAs that grade extremely hard in a class that shouldn't be this difficult. Expect a challenging time and a terrible one
I got points off for missing commas? Professor has an army of TAs that

Class was not hard but you'll definitely need to know someone in the class to get through. The lectures were long and boring and consisted of a lot of reading. Assignment instructions were often unclear and had 2-4 peer reviews each week. Asking her questions always resulted in a snarky response. Textbook is only available in physical form.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Simmons's class was enjoyable. It was a pretty easy class, & her grading criteria was very clear. There is a good deal of writing as there are weekly discussion posts. Overall, it wasn't bad and it was doable. If you do the assignments, you will get an A. Her videos are a bit awkward, but they had important information. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The lectures were so boring and the quizzes are difficult for no reason.  Mandatory peer reviews on the weekends (open assignment on saturday and due sunday) which was very frustrating.  There are no exams which is nice, but many of the assignment instructions were confusing.

NO EXAMS! But weekly quizzes! Discussion post due weekly and peer review due each sunday on 3 classmates. Her pre recorded lectures were frustrating, but got the point across. I don't think she was comfortable recording herself. EASY A if you turn work in on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: I was scared to take this class due to the comments; but the Professor turned out to be the opposite! I loved her!

Profesor Simmons Is amazing!! My only reason for not getting an A was my fault for not trying hard enough and having to deal with personal problems but she is very understanding and willing to help out any way she can. Feel free to email her if you have any questions and she will email you back pretty quickly!

Very passionate teacher w/ interesting & stimulating material. I truly learned a lot in this course including useful technical skills (Google Earth, Word Cloud, etc.). Grading criteria is extremely clear & fair. The quizzes can be a little tricky, at times. But Extra credit & a few fun assign. counterbalance any lost points. No exams either :)
Dr Simmons is a great professor that uses hands on skills. Loved taking her class!
Do not take if you have a choice. She doesn't care about students and thinks her class is the only class. Wayyy too much work for the course level and word count.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is only for 2000 words, but it is harder and more work than a 6000 level class. The professor puts in absolutely no effort to make the class interesting. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Annoying group projects, many tests and assignments, and too many readings, but still pretty easy. The teacher puts little effort to make lectures interesting but the class is easy so there is no reason to give too bad of a review. Half of the readings aren't needed for the quizzes and usually you can go into the quizzes blind and be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class is taken for the writing requirement. You will have a quiz and a discussion every week, but discussions sometimes are "group discussions" which can be inconvenient. The only problem I encountered is that she waited until the last week of classes (after drop to time) to grade all 3 essays, and those essays are worth like 60% of your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. T is a true GEM!  Her enthusiasm for the class is undeniable, turning short discussions into two hour debates. Her grading is like playing the lottery, thrilling because you never know if you'll hit the jackpot or go broke, despite the quality. She wasn't everyones cup of tea, but definitely is a flavor to remember.

Dr T is a true GEM. She is passionate, caring, well-spoken, and very approachable. She cares about making genuine connections with her students. A few essays that were easy to write, and her grading approach was like playing the lottery, unpredictable, and effort occasionally paid off! She has taught me so much about the subject and about patience.

The lectures I never watched, the quizzes are open note, but the PAPERS. omg the papers are nuts. She uses 3 different online platforms for the class which is annoying and just busy work. Every week there is a discussion in class, a paper of some kind, a discussion online, and a quiz. A 3-4 pg paper a week for an undergrad intro class is heinous.

This class is easy, but it just sucks to complete because of how it's structured you don't actually learn anything in it. The actual work you do in this class is just brain rot because discussion posts, perusall, and yellowdig all suck to do. Essays are ight but the TA who grades it tends to nitpick at your work and just doesn't elaborate on it.

Assignments were not difficult but time consuming and there was a lot to keep track of. Prof. Thomas makes the canvas dq's and responses due on different dates but the canvas to do list only has the date responses are due so it is easy to lose points for lateness. Quizzes were open note, but specific to the textbook.

Lots of assignments and writing. She requires discussions to be incredibly long. Nearly every module has a writing assignment, one assignment being no less than 4 pages no more than 10. Quizzes are honorlocked but open book so they're pretty easy. I feel like I would get more out of this class if it ws in person rather than online.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is very straightforward but the GRADING IS AWFUL. They consistently take points off for the smallest things and they take them in bunches. They give little to no feedback on what you did wrong and don't even bother trying to dispute it. They grade this class like its a 5000 level class when it is literally a 2000 introductory class.

You will not have to learn much to pass her intro to sports management class if you have decent knowledge about the sports world already. The class is a pretty easy A if you just do the work, but it is not the most fulfilling. I had no real problems passing the class, I just also did not learn much from it.

Class is not too awful but lots of annoying assignments. She sets the weekly discussion posts due on canvas a week after they're actually due to trap you into submitting late. Actually try on the quizzes and keep up with the Yellowdig. TAs grade the long assignments arbitrarily (got a C with only one comment?). Overall, eh.

The class was designed poorly. All you do is read the textbook and then do discussions. I have learned nothing in this class. Her test questions are random and will be about a topic that has little to do with the material covered in the textbook. Grades are as follows: discussion, quiz, and essay. You do that on repeat for the entire course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, she assigns pointless assignments that she doesn't give any feedback on other than your score. This class should be way easier but she makes it so much work for no reason. Her lectures are useless because all that matters is the textbook and its 80 pages a week of reading at the minimum of dull sports management introduction topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class was designed poorly; difficult to know what to do. The GroupMe for the class went off constantly with students confused about assignments and projects. Dr. Thomas said that assignments for each module are due every two weeks, but some assignments have tasks due the week before the rest of the module, which are NOT listed in the syllabus.

The class was easy, but Dr. Thomas had nothing to do with the class. Throughout the entire semester, I never once received feedback on any assignments/papers. On top of not receiving feedback, I never received any replies to emails when I had questions about papers, assignments, and quizzes. Easy class, but don't expect any help from the professor.

Dr. Thomas was the most compassionate professor I have had in a very long time. My mother passed midway through the semester and she offered to give me an "I" for the class and an entire extra semester to complete my assignments so I had time to grieve and deal with my mothers estate. Additionally, she is very responsive and fair.

Persuall was horrible, at least the discussion boards on canvas don't sound as fake as communicating with peers on this site. Her lectures were ok, but what I found confusing was the papers, and how they were graded. Will give credit when a question on a quiz is wrong, she will change it without hesitation. No exams, all open book quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Manages to make something as engaging as sports and business and have it seem like watching paint dry by the end of the course. Perusall is one of, if not the worst, softwares I've encountered for reading textbooks and keeping on top of course content.

Just put effort into the papers and read the textbook chapter THOROUGHLY and you will be fine. Pretty light workload. Each module probably has about an 1 to 1 & 1/2 hours of reading, and every other module has a paper/assignment. Not graded too tough, but I recommend getting a hard copy of textbook. Makes taking quizzes much easier.
Material is not updated from 3 years ago. Honestly not much learning in the class, but an easy A.

Took this in the fall last year. Easy class. 4 quizzes, discussions, and assignments. The quizzes are all on Quizlet (most of the questions). Discussions are straightforward. The assignments do take some time to complete. I would suggest doing the first part of the 4th assignment early as it requires you to interview someone in the sport industry.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Thomas is an awesome professor. Anyone complaining did not study and use time management skills to do well in the course. Only thing I can say I did not like was the I felt as if some of her teaching made students teach themselves. That is not a bad thing, but some students rather have the professor teach them all the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: UF just needs to get rid of this lady. Unnecessary amount of busywork. Her lectures just end up with her going off on tangents about something that is not related to the class material. Tough grader with little feedback. Three exams for this class is also unnecessary. The only positive thing from her is that she drops the lowest quiz grade.

Unfortunately, this class is required to get a degree in Sports Management. She takes her job seriously, therefore she isn't the easiest grader and the exams are hard but they are fair. One big group project at the end which helps your grade out, but other than that its a few homeworks and exams. If you hate studying, not the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Get ready to read the entire textbook word from word bc she will pull out the smallest detail you would never think a professor would use but nope trust me she will. Shes terrible. Her lectures sound shes talking of a script. Assignments make no sense. I love sports and its ashamed this class was complete garbage. Basically teach yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I don't know why the rating is so low for Dr. Thomas. Her class wasn't particularly difficult. It's a matter of following directions and completely tasks on time. The material is interesting to people who like sports. There is no reason you should have anything less than a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bad! Most of the grade is based on the quizzes each module that are wildly unfair. Quizzes are based on such small irrelevant details from the textbook. I read the textbook every module and took detailed notes on the lectures yet still failed multiple quizzes. The only thing that saved my grade were the assignments because I did well on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This teacher is so inconsistent w/ her grading policies. The class is strictly discussion-board based. You literally are graded on your performance in the online discussion groups. Be careful with the discussion leaders' assignment. This class is basically how often you post on the discussion board. It's baffling how little material is taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was not easy for an intro class but I did learn a lot. Professor Thomas is great! She responds to emails fast. I suggest going to her office hours and introducing yourself! It helps your grades. No tests but assignments are pretty complicated. The quizzes are EXTREMELY hard! Be prepared and do not expect to find any answers on google.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class is some reading and if you like sports the projects are not bad.

She is awful. All of her classes are centered around her stupid discussion posts. Terrible. You will not learn a thing with her teaching you the material through superficial, busy-work type discussion posts.

Pretty easy class overall. Timed quizzes, discussions, few papers and thats the class. Most if not all the questions to the quizzes can be found on quizlet. Discussions are easy and the required word count is low. Easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor, was aiming for a B minus and above, final was pretty hard in my opinion but provided lots of resources.

Dr. Czyz is an amazing professor. His exams are exactly like his reviews and lecture videos. It took a LOT of studying and hard work but it was a very interesting class. He reuses quiz questions, and offers easy extra credit assignments. Anyone complaining the class is too "content heavy": it's a 4000/graduate level class what did you expect lol.

AMR is a really cool class. LOTS of memorization and tests are about 75% of the grade but there's a drop score and if you put in the work, you can get an A. The lectures are super thorough and everything on the exam is in there. Dr. Czyz is obviously very passionate on the subject and makes the lectures super interesting and enjoyable.

I hate this man and his course. The first 3 weeks you must learn every class of antibiotic, function, side effects, MOAs, structure, etc. For this insanity he provides 100+ pages of AI slop "mneumonics". The rest of the course is nothing until the last 2 weeks we repeat for anti-virals, fungals, malarials, and cancer drugs. The final is cumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take another elective unless this is your only class. 4 total exams, 2 and 4 are cumulative. Tests are unnecessarily long, the final is 150 questions. Not allowed to go back and review old exams. They are basically worth your entire grade. He drops either exam 1 or 3 to boost your grade. Slides are easy to follow but way too much info to study!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Czyz has put together a great, and very informative class. Stay up to date on what is expected of you, study, put in the time, and you will succeed. He responds quickly to requests from students, is very well informed, and cares.

Dr. Czyz is passionate about AMR, but the course is much harder than needed. Exams are 600/775 points, with two cumulative tests. The final is 38% of your grade and tests on everything. Doesn't allow review of exams or practice exams. Study slides marked by a peptide gator logo—but almost all slides have it. Too much memorization hurts the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Czyz is amazing. Material is not easy and requires heavy memorization, but is very interesting. Offers extra credit. Cares for his students and responds quickly to emails. One of the best classes I've taken.
The exams are long and difficult. But he teaches everything in a way that makes the concepts easy to understand and his TAs are amazing.
