He is a great lecturer and his tests are very fair. He is engaging, knowledgeable, and makes the material interesting. His assignments were very reasonable as well. It is not an easy A but as long as you actually take the time to try the class is very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Please listen to the other reviews. I wish I did. The lectures were bloody awful. The tests were even worse. I did like how there were other assignments to be graded besides exams because if you failed an exam there was a chance of regaining a good grade. The downfall for this class is really the cumulative exams. too much stuff to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Requires a lot of memorization/time. Slides are marked to help for test but anything is fair play which makes studying a little bit hard. Midterm and final are both cumulative and very long. Assignments are simple but sometimes they are not very direct and graded a little roughly, hard to get full credit. Lectures vary from 10-30min. EC offered

While AMR was a tough class and required a good amt of memorization, Dr. Czyz made the lectures super interesting and the class super doable. He was clear on what would be on the exams, offered EC, and was very caring towards his students. Also a super interesting class

Tough class. 10 quizzes, 13 assignments, and 4 exams. Final is cumulative, 150 questions, and 300 points (worth >30% grade). There are hundreds of slides with gator icon to memorize. Some TAs are unqualified, and you have to deal with them throughout the semester. Grading on Canvas is unclear. Choose your elective wisely, and not this class.

Not an easy elective. If you did not like organic chemistry and applications, do not take the class. The professor requires you to remember all organic structures, mechanisms of actions, etc. and that is not even a 1/10 of the material needed for exams. Exam are extremely hard, with 2 being cumulative. Everything is pre-recorded.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Passionate/caring prof. & interesting lectures. Class not difficult but is annoying- SO many slides of content + excessively long midterm/final. Very wide scope, you have to memorize A LOT of only tangentially related concepts. If you are not good at memorization, you will probably not do well. Regularly do Anki for all drugs + focus marked slides!

Dr. Czyz is a very good lecturer, and the class is very interesting. However, there are four mandatory exams, two of which are cumulative: a midterm and a final. The midterm was 97 questions, and the final was 150. The exams are worth about 75-80% of your grade, and the final is 30%. Take another elective if you can.

The assignments for this class are very unclear. he makes a video on how to do it but if yo choose the wrong thing then the whole assignment goes sideways. Exams suck and he claims that slides with this figure in the corner are important but anything is actually fair game. If everything is fair game why bother with the figure in the corner?

The first cumulative exam is on 585 slides, ill let you decide what to do with that info. He states that slides with this weird figure in the corner are important and then doesn't actually use most of the marked slides for questions on the exams. There is no study guide, no sympathy from this man despite claiming he cares. its a rough semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome class, very interesting and valuable for everyone. lectures, weekly quizzes, perusal discussions, 4 exams (2 are cumulative), and multiple extra credit opportunities. I liked that this class emphasized the chemistry of the concept of AMR more than the bacteria. Czyz is a good lecturer everything you need is on canvas. LONG final and midterm

This course is not easy but it is definitely doable. I took it as an upper level elective and expected to be able to get an A but ended with an A-. The material is very interesting but was personally difficult for me to memorize all of the information, as the midterm and final are cumulative. The professor is very caring and offers extra credit.
He is a good lecturer and the class content is interesting but the overall class experience is ruined by his nightmare exams. 140 questions final is just ridiculous and unnecessary.
Its the last day of the semester and he still hasn't told us our grades because he won't just use canvas normally.

Dr. Czyz has very clear lectures and leads an interesting program but none of that matters because he makes the experience miserable. No exam should be 150+ questions and loaded with select all that apply. He's sassy in emails and just not a good vibe.

I really enjoyed this course and Dr. Czyz! If you watch the lectures and take notes on the slides with gators on them, it's doable. He reuses exam/quiz questions for the midterm and final which makes them easier; averages were in the 80s. He's very nice and cares about his students and the course content. Exams are worth a lot though which is tough

DO NOT TAKE. The final alone is 150 questions and 40% of your grade which is absurd. He offers no material to study for the exams and his exam reviews are utterly useless. He will just tell you to review the slides. His exams are extremely specific. You are tested on exam 1 material three separate times. Dr. Czyz ruins a very interesting course.

Dr. Czyz teaches a tough class, but I think he explains the concepts well.  This course was a little tricky because all of the information comes from lectures and there is no supplemental study tools.  The tests are hard and I do not test well, which can be bad because the majority of your grade is exam scores.

I don't fell that he gives enough to really prepare you for exams (that are most of your grade) despite the amount of tedious information that you have to remember. Not worth the elective credit at all. Take something else if you can. The class in general is just kind of pointless - the information is in the course title.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy but he falls short compared to other professors. Not one but two cumulative exams. The last exam covers 40+ lectures. And he doesn't let you see the questions you got wrong in previous exams! The extra credit and the drop are nice but it won't help if you get a subpar grade on the final. If you can, take another elective.

He has good lectures but they are eclipsed by the fact that his exams are a chore. Cumulative exams encompassing 20-40+ lectures. You can drop an exam but not Exam 2 or 4 which are the ones with 70-150+ questions. He gives extra credit opportunities but his exam reviews are lacking.

He is super passionate about his field, and his lectures are short. His tests are veeery specific though. Mandatory cumulative final was 150 questions and worth just under 40% of the grade which felt like just way too much for an elective. Class is super heavy on pharmacology. Great if that's your cup of tea, but not the best for a casual elective.

Dr. C is funny, loves to teach and truly cares about his students. Although the thought of AMR can be intimidating, Dr. C manages to make it concise and fun. I wish he taught more classes as his lectures are beautifully structured, amazing lecturer, offered extra credit and even asked for volunteers to tutor students that needed help in the course.
Friendly, supportive, hardworking and enthusiastic Professor.

Dr. Czyz is very passionate and caring. This class requires personal interest, you have to understand concepts, mechanisms of action & resistance as well as applications. He doesn't push his students to memorize the material but their critical thinking skills. Not easy A, hard work/effort is required. Exams can be tricky if you dont study well.

Took antimicrobial resistance. He is a good teacher, cares about the students, and communicates well. But the material is hard and theres a lot of to remember. 4 exams including midterm and cumulative final. Lots of questions on exams but all multiple choice. He gives lots of extra credit.

If you are pre-med, I highly recommend this class! You learn in-depth info about antibiotics, mechanisms, and AMR, and this class complemented my biochem class. 4 exams (exam 1 or 3 dropped), 10 quizzes, and 1 EC opportunity. I recommend studying the lectures for quizzes and exams. Dr. Czyz is passionate, accessible & an amazing lecturer! :)

Dr. Czyz is a wonderful professor. You can tell he cares about his students. However, his tests can be very specific making them quite difficult. Other assignments have clear grading criteria and he always gives timely feedback. Quick responses to emails as well. Would take him again just for his personality!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great Professor! Wants you to learn. The material is hard, but he breaks everything down well. Great structure and feedback.

Dr. Czyz was a great professor, by far one of the most interesting ones I have had. He cares about AMR and reflects it in every lecture. THIS IS NOT AN EASY CLASS. Good effort is required but an A is attainable. He is a wonderful educator. This class is great for pre-meds since most of the content taught here will be needed for medical school

Dr. Czyz tries and overall the class was not bad. However, he doesnt like to be corrected and wont admit when hes wrong. He also will say one thing and end up doing another. He definitely made everything way more intense than necessary. He is passionate about science, but I wouldnt want to do research under him.

As another reviewer said, Prof. Czyz genuinely cared about his students. That must be challenging as an online instructor, but he made it work. For a new course especially, it was very well organized. Expectations and deadlines were clear. Excellent 20-30 min lecture videos. His exams were tricky, but he might tweak them for future semesters.

When I took his AMR course, it was the first time the course was being taught, yet it was organized well. He had so much interesting/useful information to share, especially for pre-med students. Definitely have to study a lot. He was also extremely kind and despite it being an online class, was very present and reached out to students frequently.

Dr. Czyz is an amazing professor and his online class is extremely well organized. You will learn a lot of material in AMR and find new ways and tools that are available to help understand the microscopic world that is around us. Great class!

Classical Chinese 2 was really a great course. The workload was manageable and relatively easy. The lectures were really interesting, so I looked forward going to class. Overall it was a great follow-up to Classical 1, and I highly recommend anyone who is interested in classical texts to take it. I only wish a Classical 3 would've been offered.

I had her for Classical Chinese 1 and 2.  Classical 1 is relatively easy and interesting, but Classical 2 becomes much hard and way too specific, hard and detailed.  I recommend Classical 1 if you are moderately interested and Classical 2 if you are only extremely interested.  She is very helpful and approachable though.
Though prone to favoritism, she really knows her stuff!

Shen Laoshi is the best!! She is very sweet and understanding. Show her that you really want to learn Chinese and she is absolutely thrilled to help. She is one of the nicest professors I've ever had, and she's pretty funny. There's something due all the time but it's not too difficult as long as you stay on top of it. Would highly recommend her.
I had her for my First year Chinese, and I have to say that I was very lucky to have her. She's the sweetest and extremely helpful! TAKE HER! And you will learn so much from her.

Absolutely amazing and very sweet professor. After two semesters, she treats you like her children; is always extremely accommodating. Definitely still a course that you have to keep on top of, but as long as you do, it's very hard to not do well in her courses. exams are totally do-able if you go to class and study the textbook. highly recommended

Shen laoshi is a great teacher. She is so nice, funny, and most importantly helpful. Her class is not easy but you can get an A. You just have to stay on top of everything, something is due nearly everyday between hw, quizzes, and situational responses. She also tells you pretty much exactly what will be on tests so they are doable. I loved her!!

She's very nice and very helpful. Homework and tests are worth a lot. Her class is very verbally based--2 group oral projects, 1 individual. Her tests are pretty simple. She's willing to help you on your homework (take advantage), the test questions come from homework. I got B+ both semesters, but for native chinese speakers, A's are not hard to ge

Overall, she is a great teacher. Some of the assignments she gives in class (and for homework) may seem like busy work, but it really does help you to understand the language better. She is very accommodating to students and will help you if you ask for it. Be proactive and study the text before coming to class - it will help immensely!

She's very accomodating to students, i forgot my homework a couple of times and she let me hand it in late, don't whine to her about how u got a -1 on ur test on some stupid**** cuz that's just rude and annoying, she already gives very reasonable grades in the first place. Highly recommended

Professor Shen is very knowledgable of the subject matter and always willing to help students on their grammar or pronunciation pitfalls. The class is pretty easy as long as you remember the expression and grammar rules from the book. Her grading is fair but sometimes questionable. There are daily quizzes on characters and straightforward tests.

learning Chinese is not easy, and you can expect lots of quizzes, homework, weekly tests, and oral presentations.  The workload will exceed that of your other classes combined.  Shen is extremely nice and very helpful.  Go to her office hours and she will help you to improve your pronunciation. Take Chinese if you are very serious about learning.
Excellent professor. Very kind and understanding of student's needs. Lots of homework, oral quizzes, and exams, but if you're interested in the language, you'll have fun.

She is a very nice and helpful teacher.  I didn't know any Chinese at all going into the class but have made A's so far.  Intensive homework and many exams but she tells you exactly what is on the exam before you take it.  Great teacher.
Great teacher, had her for two semesters. Exams are frequent but not very difficult. Grading Scale is very fair
Class is easy to those who have a passion to learn this language. Her tests are fair.
class is easy only if you're a native chinese, or know chinese very well.  if not a lot of work.  overall, she does her best to help student with anything.

Shen laoshi is an awesome teacher!  I love going to her class, she always has fun ways of learning and speaking.  She will always help you on an individual basis and grades very fairly.  By far the best language class!
She is a great Chinese teacher, and also the only one who teaches Beginning Chinese.  Everyone seemed to do really well in this class, and she grades very fairly.  Anyone can do well in her class.

I went into the semester hesitant but overall, Professor Willming was great. There are two tests, a few group papers that are only 250 words max, and a few quizlets online to help with both exams. Easy class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Willming is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students. She provides engaging lectures. Course is just a weekly online quiz and two exams, with no assignments. Attendance is taken about once a week. She provides a study guide for the exams and if you know that you should be good.

Professor Willming is amazing to say the least. She is super kind and she actually cares about her students. She makes the effort to learn your name and things about you, which is super rare these days. There was a lecture everyday with an activity every so often. If you engage in the lectures you'll be just fine.

Dr. Willming is amazing. Super thorough and engaging lectures. Attendance is required once a week and there's no homework, just discussion posts and quizzes. Class is lecture heavy but it's easy. She's great id take it again

Dr. Willming is one of the best professors I've had so far at UF. Her content makes sense and it feels like I learned valuable information from the class that I can use in the future. Weekly discussions and vocab quizzes but they are very helpful in understanding the material. You earn a FEMA certification from this course which is good for resume.

Several group assignments throughout the semester. You earn two certificates in this course which is awesome for your resume. Tests are pretty straight forward and she provides a study guide. Shes thorough and understanding. Would def recommend!

Very easy class that I took this past semester. 2 quizzes (Honorlock), 3 discussion boards, 5 group assignments, and 2 certificates you earn by completing online training courses. Study guide given for both quizzes that extremely help. Make sure to carefully read all instructions for each group assignment. Drops lowest assignment grade as well.

Dr. Willming was extremely sweet and genuinely cared for her students. She was extremely accessible outside of class and there were only 2 exams which were extremely straightforward. Group projects were easy and as were the individual papers. Lectures were not recorded, but attendance was not a grade and she posted the powerpoints. Great professor!
good class. not a ton of work.

She is a tough grader to the point that she will grade you on things that were not specific on the assignment. Almost like she thinks it is common sense even though a lot of us have not learned this subject. She has a lot of assignment, but you won't know what you are doing wrong until your first graded assignment regardless on the instructions.

Professor Willming is amazing! She is super nice and the class is pretty easy if you somewhat pay attention. There were 2 exams, but she gives you a study guide that really helps. Took her for 2 classes and it was a breeze

I've taken Willming twice and would take her for every class if possible. She is a great professor who knows the material and wants students to succeed. She clearly defines instructions on all assignment and is quick to answer questions. Her exam reviews are a very clear depiction of what will be on the exams. Be sure to participate in class.

Sometimes lectures get a little boring. She doesn't let you use your laptop or phone during class, only handwritten notes. Overall this class isn't that difficult and she is very sweet. Your grade is basically 2 exams, one presentation, and one written assignment. Attendance is taken 10 times randomly throughout the semester so you have to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She does not post assignments online, only tells students in class. She goes on random rants often that are off-topic. You must follow her formatting or you will fail. She will not correct grades even if she grades an assignment wrong. UF could easily find a better professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is SO sweet! She's super picky about grading criteria, but she makes it very obvious what she wants and it isn't very hard at all. There aren't a ton of assignments, one big presentation/project and a couple other big things, but nothing is too hard and overall it's an easy class. She's very kind and I'd for sure recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very nice professor! it's easy to get an A in the class, but it will require a bit of work. Takes random attendance, don't miss class. She doesn't post lectures but does provide about 15 extra credit points. Lectures can be a little boring sometimes, especially towards the end of the semester. Follow the study guide for exams!

I definitely recommend attending every lecture since they summarize a lot of the textbook. Read the textbook and complete her study guides to get a good grade in this class. Willming rambles on quite a bit during class but her stories are quite enjoyable so I didn't mind them too much. She is such a lovely person, would recommend to anyone!

Always Lectures, 2 exams, do the extra credit (it'll help get you the A), work with other classmates on study guides, material can be boring so I skimmed the book, go to class, she takes random attendance, cares about you but can be v boring in class

Professor Willming is very nice and I would take her class again. Her lectures can be fun if you interact with her, otherwise it may be pretty awkward or boring to hear her talk. She's a sweetheart and grades on attendance, two exams, and two projects that are pretty cool. 8/10 overall and I recommend her to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Willming is so sweet and is very clean on her guidelines for projects and papers. She clearly defines what she wants and she is always there to help her students. She wants to get to know each of her students and always asks how their day or week has been. Class is normal, attendance is taken randomly. Not a big workload, very doable.

Willming is great. Very positive and nice. She's a little picky on some things but she's always available for help. Class material is not hard at all. Attendance isn't always mandatory but she picks 5 random days to count attendance points. Overall great though!

Very particular and nit-picky.  If it's not exactly how she would do it, then you need to change it.  The content is easy enough and she gives you the opportunity to do corrections and earn back points but she takes off for the stupidest things.

Amazing professor. In class pop quizzes were scheduled so you really didn't have to be at class until those days. However, those are graded pretty strictly and are open note and collaborative. Would suggest going to class instead of asking peers for the notes. Exams are extremely fair, do the practice exam and you'll be fine.

There was a lot of work in summer engineering stats. I felt like it was a bit unreasonable. That's why he doesn't get a 5/5 from me. He wasn't the lecturer - he was the course coordinator. I felt like the exams he designed were super fair.

For such a large topic, Lindberg teaches the class very well. Attendance is required bcs pop quizzes, but they are open-note/collaborative. The exams are easy and he has prep sessions, examples, and formula sheets for each. He is a very specific grader, but if you show your work he gives full points on all assignments. Responds good to email!

Professor Lindberg is easily the best professor in the Department of Stats and one of the best professors I have ever had. He knows so much and teaches so clearly; The breadth of my stats knowledge became so fleshed out after taking his class. He uses a lot of materials and does video reviews before the exam. I would take any class he teaches.

Difficult class, but the professor was fantastic. The syllabus was incredibly in-depth with grading expectations, so I was never super lost when calculating my grade. He does NOT tell you your grade while you're completing the class, so you have to do it manually (he gives you the formula). If I need to take more math, I will absolutely choose him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly a very nice guy. Very acommodating with deadlines as long as you email him. Attendance is definitely a MUST if you want to pass because the material is quite difficult and it all continuously builds on previous lectures. Also there's 13 mandatory in class assignments that you can't make up. Overall a great explainer too.

Professor Lindberg was an amazing professor. He was always lenient with deadlines if you reached out and would always be super responsive by Teams and Email and he always had office hours and useful links to resources that helped for learning content. He provided formula sheets every quiz/exam and always had grades posted very quickly.

very kind and eager to answer questions. lectures were very clear and posted after class. we were required to complete 10 out of 15 in-class assignments & 5 coding homeworks in r markdown (all open note). later homeworks were a bit time consuming, but none were graded harshly and all answers can be found in the lecture notes if you look hard enough

Took Summer B. Weekly quizzes, R assignments, & homeworks; two exams. Quizzes & exams were video-proctored. Says 1 wk turnaround for assignments, and it's typically exactly 1 wk (or a bit over). Rubrics unclear, but reasonably graded. Dr. Lindberg is great in OH, but that's the only interaction with him. Lectures (by Dr. Athienitis) are… strange.

Really kind and friendly. Gave out 15 in-class assignments making attendance mandatory for most of the course, but only required 10 of the 15 to be completed. Also assigned 5 homework assignments to be completed in R Markdown. Excellent lecturer and posts all his lectures on Canvas. Straightforward class. Hope to take him again for a future class.

Actuarial GOAT fr- I had him for both Theory of Interest and Actuarial Math and Stats and enjoyed both classes. Relevant weekly homeworks and quizzes and 3 exams- exams are tough but passable with some effort, especially with the practice problems he provides. Sometimes curves exams.

Took him for STA4183 & STA4930 (Actuarial Mathematics & Stats), & would take him again. Very knowledgable professor in the actuarial field & provides clear lectures of class material. Exams for both classes mirror the lecture examples, quizzes, & HWs, but be sure to do his exam practice problems beforehand for clarity. Kind & accessible!
Very kind and wants everyone to succeed. Exams are out of 105 and very similar to the practice exams so make sure to do those. Homework can be lengthy but is mostly straightforward.

Dr. Lindberg always responds back to emails and truly wants people to do good in his class. His exams can be difficult, but they are straight forward. I personally just took his class because I needed the credit, and I expected the worst, but he was very helpful and willing to answer all my questions not to mentions he posts all his lectures!
Needs a raise tbh..
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Needs a raise tbh
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures can feel long but the examples done in class help with homeworks. Exams almost always felt too long and some problems were hard for the time allotted. Actual FM exam felt easier. He does seem out of touch and  not as understanding for extra credit opportunities or making adjustments to exams.
Exams rather lengthy. Lectures are dry bur straightforward somewhat out of touch professor.

Exams can be a bit hard, but you get a cheat sheet so write down every formula. It's easy to get a good grade, but you should spend time doing the exam review and homework problems. He teaches very well so attend the lectures. He's a very nice man and understands the subject very well. 100% taking him again.

Very well-structured class with well-paced, easy to follow lectures that are posted after each class. Exams can be difficult but he allows the use of a one-sided formula sheet and plenty of practice problems. He is a former actuary so very knowledgeable about the actuarial exams. Definitely would recommend.
Pretty easy class, the class material is very straight-forward and you can always ask questions

Very enthusiastic about the material and explains concepts extremely well. Class structure is very fair and the consistent homeworks and quizzes helps you prepare for the exams, which are slightly more challenging but still straightforward. Supportive and accessible outside of class. Great experience for anyone interested in act. sci. and exam FM.

Dr. Lindberg is a fantastic lecturer, and is able to even make very dry content enjoyable to learn. The homework assignments merge the lecture content with R programming in a way that is not difficult, but actually very educational. In addition, the exams are based on clearly-established content taken directly from the amazing lecture notes.

All in all, I loved this guy. Lindberg clearly loves math which makes this class more rigorous than some (i.e., me, a stat minor) would want. Lectures have lots of proofs, homework in R, quizzes conceptual, and exams a mix, so feels a bit disjointed, but you will certainly gain a deep understanding of regression taking this course. Bit boring tho

I liked him! At first, I was a little bit nervous because of the R programming, but it wasn't that bad. He was really helpful in making sure we could use the software. Very good lecturer and very willing to help out during office hours. Quizzes and tests were fair. Overall I learned a lot and would definitely take a class with him again!

Took Regression Analysis for summer A 2018 and he did a great job! I went to office hours with some theoretical questions and he did a great job at explaining them. He taught R very well and was always willing to help us if we were confused. He was enthusiastic and I really enjoyed the class!

Took regression with him Summer A and getting a 97 in the class so far. Only barely harder than Stats 1 and Stats 2, just with some R coding and basic linear algebra thrown in there. He is helpful in office hours, quizzes and tests are also easy if you study the notes.
Easy to understand during lectures. Offers many opportunities to raise your grade, but try to start with getting A's on everything. That makes life easier.

Not a bad professor. Teaches in a no-BS way; always on-topic. Unfortunately that makes the class pretty boring, and that's coming from someone who's really into numbers and statistics. Lowest two quiz grades are dropped. Study hard for tests and you'll do okay.

Pretty easy class. He's not the most interesting lecturer , but he does break everything down to make the material easy to pick up. You really don't need to attend class as long as you stay caught up in the material. Grades only based on weekly quizzes and the few tests. I didn't find either challenging at all. Overall very easy and I hate math.

Dr. Lucier is so sweet. You can tell he cares about his classes and he wants you to succeed. He's a great professor and is very helpful. You get what you give in this class and it's very important to show up.
Really enjoyed my class with this professor. Greatly recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Lucier had so many examples from his experience in the industry. Each module had an assignment or a quiz. He is a quick grader with good feedback. There is a midterm, final, and big group project due at the end of the semester. Most of the grade comes from your own part of the project, with a smaller portion for the overall project.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lucier is an incredible professor, he makes class enjoyable. I wish he taught more courses because I would take him a thousand times.

I was David's first class that he taught and he was absolutely AMAZING! He cares about the students and incorporated a lot of his experiences that he has had into his lecture. It may say to get a textbook, but he gives you all of the materials to do well. 2 exams, 1 group project and presentation, about 10 small assignments. He is such a great guy.
The methodology used by this profesor is meant to make you feel. Not approachable to receive feedback. I would recommend to avoid this profesor.

Not approachable at all, tests were extremely complicated and hard to understand and when asked for feedback she denied completely. Lectures were too heavy and time demanding, makes it complicated to understand one lecture, takes hours. It seems as she wants her students to fail.

Half the class will get a 60 or under on an exam but the class is "graded on a curve" so its okay? Lectures are very very tedious, and when you're working 40 hours a week, how can you expect me to spend a minimum of 12 of your class alone, as if I'm not attempting other courses as well. Don't like the grading style, 3 exams worth 70% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not only a terrible class but very unprofessional. Would say exam grades would be given by a certain date and gave no update when she provided them well after the given date. Multiple people including myself after surprisingly bad exams asked for feedback on how to better prepare and were ghosted. It felt like she actively wanted us to fail.

45-50 min lectures that take you 3.5 hours to get through on a fast day. Tests were FOUL, unfairly made and poorly written. Perusall assignments are not worth your time. Overall very disorganized and some of the lectures you cannot even understand. Class average for exams was around a 68%. Heavy curve but it doesn't get you an A. Deb is the worst!!

While the use of medical acronyms can be a bit confusing at first, once you get a handle on them and understand them better, it becomes easier to understand the lectures and content. The first responder brand of humor is also a big positive for me.

Super cool guy and actually does what he teaches in real life. Online labs are kinda annoying because they're pretty long, but they drill in information pretty well. Everything in this class is super applicable to real life and it feels like I'm learning actually useful things. Highly recommend taking this class for kicks and giggles.

He's been in the field a long time and has the stories and expertise to show for it. Your learning depends on how much effort you put in. You can skate by as an easy course, but if you're willing to, there's a lot of fun, important info to learn. Highly recommend attending his lectures on Zoom if possible.

I am an engineering major, this class has nothing to do with my field, but what a cool learning experience. From the beginning, there is so much you wouldn't even imagine you could learn in a 99 percent online class (only 2 labs in person). So much fun and boy does he have stories to tell.

Hunt is an amazing professor. He loves what he teaches and loves his students, even though online. He makes all quizzes open note, and gives you study guides to tell you what to know for the midterm and final. He eliminates A-, so anything 90 and above is an A, and he wants absolutely everyone to do well. He is overall an amazing guy!

He is very passionate about the class and wants to help you succeed. The lectures are easy to follow and the study guides tell you exactly what you need to know. He makes the class fairly easy as long as you use the study guide for the exams. Note that he will not give an A- and instead has a bigger range for an A that goes directly to a B+

Derek is a great professor! He is passionate about what he teaches, and has great labs which are optional to get EMR certification. As someone who tends to slack off when it comes to watching recorded lectures, I have no problem watching his lectures because he is engaging and entertaining to watch. If you are pre-health, this is a must-take class.
I was very engaged in the lectures. Very informative and reasonable class!

Dr. Hunt is very kind and genuinely wants students to succeed. EMS certification is optional—if you opt out, focus on weekly quizzes, the midterm, final, and patient assessment. The TAs are helpful. The class is lecture-based, but labs give you a chance to apply what you've learned.

I really enjoyed this class and I found it very beneficial. You just have to watch the lectures (live or recorded) and do one weekly quiz. If you keep up with the class you should do fine. It is very manageable and not too work-heavy. If you want to get the certification be aware that you will have to do a lab in the afternoons (Tue/Wed 6:15-8:15).
Greatest professor I have ever had. Teaches very efficiently and the class, although work heavy and a little bit challenging, is very manageable.
I highly recommend ems1055. Derek provided a lot of real-world knowledge on emergency medicine, and the course offers you certification opportunities.
He's the best
Great lectures, entertaining, doesn't give busy work, recorded lectures allow people to work around their schedule. 10/10

EMS1055 is very interesting, not particularly difficult, and great if you are interested in joining GEMRU, but do not be fooled into thinking an A comes without work. Other than that, Derek is a great guy who knows his stuff. He gave a point back to me on a question because he found my logic for an incorrect choice reasonable, which I appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Incredible professor with lots of experience the field. He outlines what you need to know for exams, and makes the class as easy as he can so you can focus on learning and not on grades. Allows for flexible schedules. Provides labs that can feel long but are incredible for practicing and retaining material. Most perfect professor I've ever had

He is simply perfect. Love his enthusiasm and knowledge. Quizzes are so easy and the exam is very manageable with a generous study guide. Optional labs to get AHA BLS certification and EMS certificate. If pre-health so interesting and an amazing into to medicine as he combines medical and emergency situations!! Fav professor and class!!!

Midterm, final, weekly quiz, and one assignment. There's about an hour long lecture or two each week, but Derek keeps them entertaining! Learned a lot of information that would be valuable to anyone pursuing any career in the medical field. Exams aren't bad, just study. The zoom labs for the EMR certificate are tedious and 3+ hours long though.

Such a fun class learning practical things. Labs are optional earning you an EMR certification but are so helpful for reviewing course content. It's definitely not just an easy A but as long as your interested and put in some work to study you should get an A. I found lectures super interesting and loved his stories. Wish he taught more courses!!

Super helpful as a Pre-Health class, but by no means an easy A. I took it over the summer online and you have to travel one day to UF to take the BLS course to get your EMR certification. Go to the optional Labs, they are very helpful for studying for midterm and final. You get to pick the time slot you want to take the exams during a week.

Derek is a great guy! I took this class because I heard it was an easy elective for someone pre-health, and I don't really agree. The class is cool, and you learn a lot, but I had to put in a lot of effort studying for the midterm and final. I ended up doing well and enjoying the class, but it is definitely not a "free A"!

Derek hunt is really great at teaching. The class is pretty easy overall, only graded by quizzes and two exams. You will learn a lot about emergency medicine. The lecture slides have everything you need. He doesn't do A minus and rounds up from 89.5 . Overall, great class.

Literally the best. Doesn't believe in A-. Majority of the quizzes are on quizlet and the final/midterm both repeat quiz questions. Only grades are a weekly quiz and then the midterm and final. Such a cool guy!

Amazing class. Lectures twice a week and records it. I would say the lectures took me 1-3 hours each time due to me taking notes (which is reasonable for only lecturing twice a week). His slides are interesting and I would take this class again if I could. Make sure to not procrastinate the patient assessment assignment and you should be good! :)

Prof Hunt was great! Very down to earth and clear, a breath of fresh air different from many other professors. Gives great examples from his life experience during lectures. Lectures were synchronous as well as recorded for convenience, with 8 lab sections to complete your EMR degree. If you're pre-health, take this class!

Highly suggest taking his class. On top of getting BLS and EMR certified, I have genuinely learned so many applicable skills in medicine. Basically a guaranteed A with the weekly quizzes and midterm/final, so you really get to enjoy the lectures instead of worrying about your grade. Great class and very personable professor!

Derek is by far the best professor I have ever had! Every single one of his lectures is engaging and interesting. He is a very down to earth person, and I could listen to him talk for hours. He also provides really cool opportunities for his students, like BLS and EMR certifications. He helped me realize how much I loved medicine; Take this class!

Derek is an insightful, passionate, and intelligent-looking professor. He has a lot of experience and imparts his wisdom in a straightforward manner. While class isn't easy, he cares a lot about his students and gives you all the resources you need to succeed. Show up to all labs and lectures, you'll learn a lot and get BLS and EMR certifications.

Derek Hunt has been my favorite professor at this university. This course is a subject that he has a lot of passion for and that is clear through his lectures. As long as you go to the lab sections and pay attention to the lectures, the course should be an easy A and it also gives you two certificates - one for BLS/CPR and an EMR certificate.

Derek Hunt is probably my favorite professors at UF. He is knowledgable, is straight up about the reality of emergency medicine situations, and you can tell he's passionate and cares. His lectures were recorded over zoom and never boring. Highly recommend his emergency medicine class!

Derek is such an amazing person and professor. He is extremely lenient with assignments and is always willing to help out when he can. Besides the class being an easy A, it's very interesting and he does a great job engaging everyone. Definitely take this class, you won't regret it!
Derek is an amazing professor. I has so much fun in his class and he really cares about his students. Definitely take his class if you are interested in medicine!!!

Dr D. gets so much hate. i was terrified to take this class but if you watch the weekly lectures and actually do the hw & quizzes his class is super managable. i spent 3 hours a week typically& around 5-6 the week of the exam which is less than typical in person lectures. i would reccomend if you are able to hold yourself accountable each week

Dr. Dickrell is a great online lecturer. I took statics over the summer online. I never put in more than 5 hours a week total—(hw, quizzes, lectures, reviewing). My guess is 25-33% earned an A or A-, and it is not difficult to do so if you just do the assigned works. He is not rude, just straightforward. Tests were fair and easier than HWs.

Lectures were fine, but grading was extremely unfair. Over the summer semester there was no partial credit on quizzes, which are 40% of the grade. Later on, he gave the occasional partial credit question but most weren't. The content was difficult but doable with a lot of effort.

Has incredible lecture videos that helped me understand the content better than any other resource outside of the class. Most of his hate is unwarranted but the grading in the class is definitely unbalanced. Even getting a single problem wrong on the exams can make getting an A unattainable. I think the emails he sends out are real more than rude.

has the best lectures I have ever watched. Conversely, this class has the most god awful grading ever. An example is me getting a 0/30 on a quiz because it was 1 question with no partial credit. reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes were often 1-2 questions, significantly harder than the homework, and graded pass/fail. His favorite activity was mocking the students in the canvas announcements for bad score distributions and refusing to self-reflect. Managed to carry an A into the final and ended with a C for getting two questions wrong (one of which for units).

Absolutely atrocious. Incredibly rude and degrading professor who loves to belittle students for making mistakes that can be explained by the poor structure of his exams and quizzes. I got an A on the final but I still feel compelled to warn others because the lengths I took to get it were unreasonable for what should be a very easy class.

So hard to get an A, but I feel like I learned statics. He sent out demeaning messages saying that we will not be needed as engineers. I know options are limited, so if you need to take it with him just remember that professors only put students down so they can feel better about themselves. Avoid if you can!!!

His lectures were fine, but the way he runs the class is honestly a joke. The final exam is worth 50% of the overall grade, and best part is he isn't going to post our final exam scores. I felt like I understood Statics well,  went from having an A to a B- because of the final.

Horrible professor, has a huge ego and is unbearable. He's strict with grading and its basically impossible to get above a B with how he grades things. Would not take him again, avoid him for every single class he teaches!!!

The problem here is that he will grade tests and quizzes incorrectly and sometimes unfairly. Also SUPER rude when you try to communicate or if students do poorly on a test.

DO NOT TAKE THIS ONLINE CLASS!!! This class is an absolute joke. Lectures are useless and the homeworks and quizzes are made by the TAs who have NO idea what they are doing. Almost every homework has errors or incomplete/wrong information. You will do everything right and think you made a mistake when it was actually just faulty grading. Waste of $

This man should not be a professor! He's isn't clear about what he's looking for and grades things to his made up standards he doesn't specify. He gives great lectures that are very easy to follow. Other than that I'm embarrassed that this guy is a professor I've had nothing but bad experiences with him. How does he have a job here…

Final exam is worth 50% of your grade, its insane. This man is extremely egotistical, stuck up and genuinely one of the rudest people I have ever met.When majority of the class is failing he blames the students and taunts them. Horrible grader as-well he doesn't make instructions clear and blames you when you don't meet his unspecified criteria.

An easy class in terms of material, but it was made overly difficult by the professor. I spend equal time formatting the assignments to his specific requirements as I do actually solving the problems. He took 30 points off on a quiz because my drawing didn't look good enough. Blames students when almost everyone fails. Very disrespectful in emails.

Do NOT take this guy if you want to pass. His only goal is to give you overly difficult quizzes that feel like they are intended to bring your grade down. 65% of the class made a zero on the quiz and his response was "this should be a wakeup call to the students." DO NOT TAKE. I would've rather put myself a semester behind then take this guy.

Sends a weekly email complaining about students and said those that did good on his quiz will be successful in the future and “There will be no need for the rest”. The class material is super easy. If you passed PHY2048 at UF the material will be a breeze. However, the way he grades is downright horrible. Expect to be loosing crazy points every assignment for miniscule shit (sig figs, formatting, file type). I spent every assignment doing the work then spending an hour re-writing it in the correct format.

Took his online asynchronous dynamics class for Summer C. As someone who took his Fall statics class (hybrid), dynamics was similar: we were graded on 2 exams and several HWs. Flexible for summer internships/jobs bc the exams were open for 24hrs. He can be hard to reach and his emails can be informal/blunt but overall his lectures are informative.
Tough professor, with engaging lectures but very challenging exams. Utilize unstuck AI and the free textbook to get the most out of the class.

His lectures are amazing, and his videos are very engaging. However, he was almost never accessible and didn't have office hours. Some quizzes (which were weekly) were overly challenging and felt like it was meant to bring your grade down. Very annoying that there's no partial points given anywhere on these quizzes too.

I am almost done with this class, and I can say by far that this is the worst professor I have ever taken. He's a good lecturer and overall I felt that the tests were mostly based on the homework. 75% of your grade is your tests so be sure to not neglect them. Homeworks are the best practice and also doing practice problems from the textbook if you need extra practice. Overall good teacher I would take him again.

Very frustrating exams, very heavily weighted. It's not fun to have 30% of your grade hinge on your ability to solve two problems only. Otherwise a very engaging lecturer, though not very kind to students outside of class.
